review_text:
First of let me start by saying I have stayed at almost all of the upscale hotels in the Galleria area. This hotel is my absolute favorite. 
Parking is great and you can't beat free. I have paid $25 a night for parking in the Galleria.
Check in was easy and fast. Staff were very friendly and helpful. Decor is different then most but I loved it. 
When I walked in the room it was so refreshing. Extremely clean and bright. Bed was so comfortable, I slept great. Have read many review complaints about the blinds but I had no issues with them. The shower was my favorite. It is huge, it has great pressure and the temperature was easy to adjust. I loved it. I took 
about 4 or 5 showers during my 2 night stay. I never had water on the floor either. The room was smaller then most but it worked for me.
Location is great. Maybe a 5-7 minute walk to the mall. 
Overall my stay at The Indigo was extremely enjoyable. Like I mentioned at the beginning I have stayed at almost all the Galleria hotels and this is my favorite place. I look forward to my future stays with this Hotel.

I have stayed at a couple of Marriott's in Houston, and this one is the best so far, the hotel was very clean, excellent location, awesome room service the food was awesome, and the staff was great, especially the overnight staff Samantha who was very helpful. I will stay here again for my next trip.
hotel_name: Houston Marriott West Loop by the Galleria

review_text: I went to a conference an the people serving us stole my heart. They were very helpful, friendly and happy.
hotel_name: Houston Marriott West Loop by the Galleria

review_title: Took a risk, it paid off... And continued to pay off.
review_text:
I took a risk after reading some of the negative reviews and opted to stay at the Marriott West Loop instead of the JW Marriott which is located down the road. The JW is top notch and by no means did I expect this hotel to be on par.
The good:
- The hotel is conveniently located around 3 miles from the galleria, close enough for an evening shopping trip yet far enough to not having to fight that area's morning traffic.
- Rooms were clean albite on the small side
- Staff service was on par and sometime exceeded JW Marriott's service, I did not come across any staff member that was not smiling and greetedly warmly as if they had known me for years !!!!!!
- Heavy presence of both uniformed and non uniformed security personnel was always a welcomed sight especially in the parking garage area which is a bit of a walk from the hotel and is not very well lit.
- Food was better then I expected, restaurant staff were friendly.
- Bartenders were friendly albite not very professional with a distinct "bar lingo" such as babe, sweetie instead of sir or maam, it was also hard to get their attention, they were focused on what appeared to be a VIP and I had to make several gestures to get a drink.
Finally, I did get a chance to experience the "after check out" service of the hotel when to my dismay I discovered that I had left my pro error bag behind. I called the hotel and I was transferred to their security office where I had to leave a voicemail. (yes usually that means you will never see your item again). However to my surprise, around 2 hours or so later I was called by the director of security who informed me that they found my item and that that he would be sending it to me by FedEx at their expense since he felt like it should not have taken that long for someone to get back to me !!!!!!! This is impressive considering I am no longer a "guest" at that time.
This gesture and all the rest of the helpful staff earned my permanent business, as the title says, I took a gamble and it paid off, the substation savings off of the JW Marriott rates will also keep paying off for me.
Well done Marriott, great location, good rates, clean new rooms, excellent staff, excellent staff, and excellent staff.
hotel_name: Houston Marriott West Loop by the Galleria

review_text:
My boyfriend and I stayed here as a business trip for him. We are both young and pretty "middle class" since the time we arrived, we were treated like we didnt belong. We arrived late monday night with our 2 little dogs. We were told over the phone that we would have complimentary dog beds with our stay. They never mentioned anything. I finally called and asked after our 3rd night. Nobody has come to clean our room or ask if we need anything. And, they put us in a room thats at the very end of the hotel next to the stairs rm 301. We felt like we were in a closet away from everyone else. Everytime I call to guest services for something, they come up with an attitude like ive disturbed them. 
We usually stay at the La Quinta but everything was booked due to the NCAA weekend. We would of preffered La Quinta over the Sheraton anytime. They have very comfortable "king" beds, and a wonderful complimentary breakfast and always treat us nicely. The rooms are always clean. The bed here by the way was a queen, and so uncomfortable!! I highly doubt we will be back. Atleast not anytime soon.

As always a great stay at a Ritz Carlton property. The location on Central Park is central to everything! Surrounded by great shopping. Everything was terrific except breakfast at the hotel....over priced and the food was not good. The service atbreakfast was, however, very good. My husband an I love staying here.
hotel_name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park

review_text: So nice to treated so wonderfully. Jenny at the desk was very hospitable. Every employee we ran into whether it was housekeeping to any staff member in the elevator & the manager was ALWAYS very courteous & concerned about our stay. Staying @ The Ritz was a treat!
hotel_name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park

review_text: This is a beautiful hotel in a great location- across from central park and a few blocks from great shopping. It was a bit pricey when I stayed, but thankfully was able to use AMEX points to pay for entire stay. Online photos do not do it justice. I was slightly hesitant to book this hotel because it t looked "old- fashioned" and dated from the photos online. When I arrived, i was proved wrong. Its very elegant (just what youd expect from any ritz) yet still very fresh. The lobby/entrance way was smaller than i had expected, but that was great because it prevented tourists from walking in and just "hanging around". I stayed in one of the smaller suites with one bedroom, living room w pullout bed, 2baths, and a great view! The room was spacious- perfect for 1-4 people. I had clothes pressed and they did a great job w turn around time- needed it within a couple hours. Room service was great. The staff is wonderful. I arrived at 9am, check in is not until 3, but i called ahead and asked/ begged if I could have my room early since I had an event to attend at noon. They told me they would do their best but if I needed to shower and get ready and A room wasnt available when i arrived, they would give me access to they spa facility to use. That was very nice of them. When I arrive it was ready! If you are willing to splurge on your trip to NYC, this is a great hotel. I wouldnt even think twice.
hotel_name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park

review_text:
Excellent location and good welcome received for a frequent returning guest. Noticed lower numbers and accessibility of Club Level staff on last visit - although staff when available were very good.
More worrying was the refusal of staff to address or acknowledge recent well publicised shocking health reports on the hotel's hygiene. As a result of this we have a reluctance to return to the hotel or recommend it until this situation is sorted satisfactorily.
hotel_name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park

review_title: what you would expect from Ritz but pricey
review_text: The Ritz sure know how to pamper. My wife and I stayed in early October. The room was outstanding though didn't have a view of the park. Clean, spacious (for Manhattan) and an excellent bathroom (including speakers for the TV). Also, very quiet for a midtown hotel both inside and outside. Only drawback was the smell when the doorman opened the door. This is due to the number of horse drawn carriages just outside by the park. While an awesome property and excellent service, not twice as good as lower ranked properties at half the price in my book. For a splurge or Marriott points, don't miss it.
hotel_name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park

review_title: You ain't stayin' for value baby!!
review_text:
Again, this place is fantastic. This was our 4th stay at the Central Park Ritz and of course it was as fabulous as always. But of course, I post a new review with each visit because there are always updates!
Remember - this gorgeous hotel is not cheap. The lowest rates I have ever seen were for 595 per night. So if you count your pennies stay somewhere else. But keep in mind - I did not hear the word "no" even once. My husband, 3 kids, sitter and inlaws came and we all had a blast. There were some snafus at check in - not sure if this was the fault of the hotel or Amex but they worked it out. The locationnom central park is great. For families, hit the m and m store, the bike rides and victorian gardens in the Park, serendipity 3 (of course), Dylans candy shop, etc.
Also, if you can afford it, purchase club lounge access. The food is top notch and the service can simply NOT be matches anywhere. Carmelinda the club concierge is wonderful. Lazar is the man with the most. He is an amazing server in the club lounge - he will anticipate and meet your needs. And I imagine he has stories we could not fathom.
This trip I did find that housekeeping and room service were both not as responsive and speedy as usual. With summer, maybe they are short staffed?? Also the spa is good, small but with well done services. The La Prairie products are exorbitantly priced. Seriously - 495 for a moisturizer? That's ridiculous. But then again if they can get it why not??
hotel_name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park

review_title: Wonderful location and perfect choice for our special visit to New York
review_text:
You have high expectations when you book into a Ritz Carlton Hotel...even higher when you picked it as special treat for your sister and brother-in-law birthday and anniversary celebrations. Overall we were not disappointed! The start started a little rocky when our rooms where not ready at check-in...which was after 4pm in the afternoon. So we were invited for free drinks and to wait in the bar/ loune. It did take even longer than we expected (90 mins) and as we were jet - lagged....we were dsaapointed! The rooms though were large and sumptuous.
The location was perfect ...wonderful launch pad to all the sights! We chose not to have breakfast in the hotel but to experience all the different options on offer very close to the hotel...having pancakes was quickly ticked of the list of must dos! The concierge was very helpful in solving a dilemma to find a restaurant that served fabulous steaks for my in-laws ( another must do for them!) AND served vgreat veggie food (for me and my husband). It also had to be within walking distance as we were tired from sight seeing (The Met, staten island etc.). So, very knowledgeable! With central park on your doorstep, no stay would be complete without a lovely evening stroll in the park to see all the activities going on there.
On leaving the hotel, the hotel surprised us again. They realised that we were disappointed aboit the long wait at the start of our stay and decided to comp all our drinks over over the time of our 4 night stay.
hotel_name: The Ritz-Carlton New York, Central Park

review_text: Its a new hotel, walking distance to financial district, soho, battery park.the rooms are clean and efficient, staff is friendly and great way to see an ethnic neighborhood in New York. It was nice to see Chinese ladies practicing tai chi in the morning in the park.

When you book a refurbished junior suite do you expect a bathroom ? Well this hotel evidently doesn't feel the need to tell it's guests that a tiny shower with a basin is what's on offer .... Oh and of course we'll move you but to a dirty and depressing smoking floor which stinks . So we cut and ran ... Across the road to the Mark , a wonderful modern clean friendly hotel . 
The Carlyle is a disgrace and they had the gall to send us a computer generated letter thanking us for staying there!

review_title: Ideal to get about to most places
review_text:
Went with a friend for 3 nights this june
Was pleased by the rooms with 2 big double beds, go for the terrace as the cost isnt a lot more, we didnt but i wish we did as the weather was great. Staff were friendly and answered all questions we had. 
Will prob be back here again at some point this year
Little italy 2 mins away, china town your in it but away from the smell and a park outside with people doing tai chi every morn, brooklyn bridge & courts 5 mins, tube station just round corner and lots of food shopping nearby
This was my 2 nd time in ny and this hotel was far better than the last

review_title: Well located modern hotel ideal for tourist
review_text:
Very well managed hotel. Clean rooms, Vera good beds. Breakfast had to be taken in a separated building (only 4 doors away).
Close to China Town en Little Italy.
Subway only 3 minute walk away.
Try to have a room @ the frontside of the building. Those at the backside are sometimes a little bit noisy due to ventilation systems at the outside'

review_title: Very enjoyable, very helpful staff. Good location and safe. Will recommend.
review_text: Free internet so thats a bonus. Great staff very friendly, enjoyed the free breakfast around the corner. room size was adequate. whenever we had a request it was answered very well.
Fast check-in, helpful smiley staff, fairly spacious for NY, hot breakfast around the corner, 2 min walk to several subway lines, super clean. A recommended option.

My wife, 2 daughters ages 7.5 & 6, and i stayed here Dec 27 & 28. We arrived around 11 am and were surprised that our room was ready and we were able to check in early. They do offer bag check if your room isn't ready and have a lobby restroom. We had a king bed w a pull out sofa. The room wasn't big, but was large enough to accomodate us comfortably, it was clean and NO beg bugs! The front desk personel were all very nice and helpful. A breakfast is included, which is more than just juice and danishes, and included fruit, juice, bagels, cereal, coffee, belgium wafels, yogurt, and probably a few other things. The dining area is rather small, so you may need to wait for a table or take it back to your room. The location is great for exploring downtown or escaping from midtown. The seaport is right next door, the brooklyn bridge is just a few blocks away - great views of the bridge just a short walk away, the world trade center, wall street, battery park - all within walking distance. We started our day with coffee from Jack's Stir Brew a block away. There is a good italian restaurant almost right next door - "Acqua" - good food, reasonable prices, nice atmosphere. I will most likely return here in the spring for another visit.
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Seaport Inn Downtown

review_text:
Very caring staff when checking in. 
They offered me an upgrade to a deluxe room which was very enjoyable when travelling during 12 hours.
My room was nicely decorated, had a beautiful entrance corridor and a full mirorred bathroom(which was great by the way)

This hotel is grossly overpriced for a three star type place. We were charged an additional $80 per night for our two kids pushing a four night stay to over $2000. Nothing is included here. They wanted $14.95 per day for Internet. A petty rip off.
We won't stay here again.

review_title: Great hotel and very good location
review_text:
If you don't like walking around and explore new things then chinatown is not for you and try a hotel downtown.
Hotel overlooks Columbus park, 3 rooms per floor, 12 floors. Very friendly staff and very clean and new. Breakfast is at a cafe nearby, it is also very popular by the NYPD so it can get crowded around 9am.
Be sure to get a room not ending on 03 as 01 and 02 overlooks the park while 03 is on the backside.
Chinatown has THE cheapest good food and you can get sweet fresh fruits from the street. Taxi to empire state building is around 20$. If taxi driver asks the crossing street, say mulberry and worth street as bayard st is more unknown to taxi drivers.
Hotel can also provide taxi service, it is a bit overpriced, specially to Newark (cost 70$ + tip +12$ toll). Bett to hail a taxi from the street if possible.

First time ever in NYC. I was shocked by the cost of hotels in the city but found the perfect fit for a quick stay. Very clean rooms with private bath. Provided nice shampoo, cond., shower gel, lotion. Shower is hot and powerful. The beds might be the most comfortably ever. Direct TV on the flat screen. Very quiet despite its location. 10-15 minute walk to WTC area. Unfortunately did not make it to times square so not sure how far away?
Staff is very friendly and helpful. Can not beat the price!

review_title: A good, clean hotel if you want to stay in Chinatown/Little Italy
review_text:
I stayed in this hotel for 2 nights with my husband. We had a room on the top floor and it was large by New York standards (we stayed in another hotel in midtown for 8 nights). Request a room on the top floor - it was quiet (for New York). 
Good location if you want to stay in Chinatown/Little Italy. It's about 2 blocks to the little Italy part of mulberry street.
Hotel is close to SoHo. However, I preferred staying in the Flatiron/Gramercy park area. It is more expensive to get a taxi from broadway to hotel mulberry (about $15) compared to about $8. Still, Hotel Mulberry is a lovely and clean hotel, it just depends on what you want to do in New York.

My husband and I just spent 6 nights at this l wonderful hotel. The location,shops, restaurants and bars were great and we loved the cobble stone streets. It was quiet and very clean and the staff was very helpful.
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Seaport Inn Downtown

review_text:
I got an amazing deal on the private sale site, SniqueAway, and stayed at the Carlyle over Valentine's Day weekend. I found the Carlyle to be the epitome of old New York style and grandeur. From the front desk to the white-gloved elevator operator to the cleaning staff, everyone we encountered was helpful and polished. 
The suite was the largest I've stayed in New York City. It had a large bedroom, living room, separate fully-enclosed kitchenette, full bath off the bedroom, and 1/2 bath at the entrance. It was larger than my 2-bedroom Back Bay Boston apartment! 
The location is wonderful, conveniently located one block from Central Park in the gorgeous Upper East Side.
The few downsides were the kitchenette was very dated. Also, it was stocked with a few wine and champagne glasses, but after we used them the first night, the maid staff took them to be cleaned but never brought us a clean set.
Full disclosure, if I had paid full price, I would have expected a more updated kitchenette and a better view. However, I feel I got a great value on this amazing hotel.

review_title: Okay Hotel, a bit shabby but Great location!
review_text: Okay Hotel, a bit shabby but comfortable. Great location!
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Seaport Inn Downtown

review_title: Keep this as your last option
review_text: The rooms are extremely hot and stuffy it claims to have heating and cooling yet they refuse to have both on. Even outside when it is 5 degrees whilst sleeping the room temperature without heating ever turned on is 26 degrees goodluck try to sleep in that. The add comfy except they are a thick latex pillow top and are very hot. I feel the cold and love the heat but these rooms were ridiculous. Lucky we had a balcony and would leave the door open for hours before we went to sleep. Just beware you will hear people flushing toilets, using hair dryers, there tv. For the price l would book somewhere else. Although the location is great l would never stay here again.

review_title: Fantastically comfortable accommodations that is peacefully located across from Columbus Park in the heart of Chinatown.
review_text: This is a wonderful hotel chock full of comfortable amenities, including spacious rooms, in-room refrigerator and free breakfast for two. It's location across from Columbus Park offers a serene setting, considering you are in the heart of Chinatown. Three adults and one 13-year-old big stayed comfortably together in one room for four nights. I highly recommend this hotel!

review_title: Superb neighborhood hotel with great customer service
review_text: Close to grocery store and multiple subway stops. Staff was helpful and kind. Great place for families, as we are a family of 5 and our room was wonderful! Loved all the philosophy soaps in the bathroom! Good light contol, with blinds that kept the room dark when sleeping. A/c worked great and noticed no outside noises. We will stay here when we come to NYC again, with or without kids!

Unfortunately we picked one of the cheapest options on ----. Unfortunately because the experience felt like THE cheapest hotel a respectable website would advertise. Even cheaper. I call the Mulberry a recession hotel due to the low budget decor and lack of comfort. We were requested to move rooms several times due to their incompetent booking system. Of course I refused to play 'musical rooms' on my vacation. Our air conditioning unit packed up the last night in the middle of the 2011 July/August heat wave. SPOIL. Uncapable of fixing it, the 'technician on call' was unable to answer his call. All in all a two out of 5, one star for cleanliness, one for being in close enough to Soho (although the stench made us rub past the fish stall en route every morning)

review_title: A cead mile failte in NYC
review_text: First impression of this this hotel was fantastic and it continued to be a great hotel with a great suite on the 16th floor, ( great for a family) I would strongly recommend this hotel with true Irish hospitality! Staff were very nice and a credit to the greatness of this hotel. Will book this hotel again on next trip to NYC.

review_title: A perfect value, clean, comfortable and reasonable.
review_text: The staff are very warm and friendly. The room is cozy, bathroom small but extremely comfortable bed! Location... Not the greatest but close to subway.

review_title: Great find! Wish I could keep it a secret.
review_text: The other reviewers were spot on. This hotel is a gem in the heart of Chinatown and only 2 blocks to little Italy. Beds super comfortable, marble bathroom with strong shower pressure to ease away the pains of a long day sightseeing. Staff could not have been more helpful....especially Jackie, Kelly, and the young man on at night. We are in NYC frequenlt and will return to the Mulberry again and again.

We stayed for 10 days over the Holidays. As a family of four we booked 2 Luxury suites, one with King bed and the other with 2 double beds. Both Suites were AMAZING! What was even better was the staff at the Kimberly! Highly recommend!

for the first time in New York I chose this hotel recommended by a friend who knows the manager so I had a great price, is wonderful and beautiful large rooms, the service for the things I asked was impeccable and the area is perfect with the metro will turn out.Sure Ill come back 'I hope to find some deals because the price is a bit 'high!

I love Affinia hotels. This last trip I wanted to stay closer to Central Park and I got my wish. Affinia Gardens is clean, rooms are spacious, and hotel staff polite an helpful. My only suggestion is an update on the wallpaper. I will continue to stay at Affinia hotels when possible.

review_title: Very large rooms, good location, but poor service
review_text:
I visited New York for work and the Kimberly Hotel is only a few blocks away from my firm's Manhattan office. A colleague stayed at the nearby Omni and the rooms at the Kimberly are far superior.
My room was, I believe, pretty standard for the hotel. There was a large separate living room with a couch, coffee table, desk and dining table. The separate bedroom had a king-sized bed, frette linens and a very beautiful chest of drawers.
The bathroom had a jetted tub, was covered in lovely white marble and had double sinks. Though I usually prefer a more modern style, this hotel did old fashioned luxury well. Given the age of the building and the location, the size and quality of the room were very impressive and if I had received better service, this hotel would have received a higher rating.
However, these are the service issues I encountered:
1. At 8:30 am I left my room and placed the maid service sign on the door. When I returned at 2:45, the maid was in my room on her cell phone. She didn't fully service my room (which I realzed after she left) and I had to follow her down the hallway with the bag of garbage she left behind. This should never have occurred.
2. I planned to meet two of my colleagues to go over a project in the afternoon. All of us were guests at the hotel. Two of us were told we couldn't work in the sky lounge because it was closed for a private event. I asked several employees if there was another place we could work in the hotel. I was told no. All the while, a third colleague was working in the sky lounge. Eventually, we were able to join her but only as a result of our relentless persistance. I found the business center later and realized we could have worked there.
3. After dinner, a few of us were going to the sky lounge to have a glass of wine. Again, we were told it was closed. We took the elevator nonetheless. In fact, it was open and the bartender was happy to serve us.
4. I have been trying to get an invoice for my stay. Despite several requests, I still have not received it.
The service issues are very unfortunate because the hotel is perfectually situated in midtown.

We stayed here the first weekend in December and were really looking forward to it. Last year we stayed at the Gansevoort in the Meatpacking district and we loved it, however we were a bit disappointed with this one. We booked our room through Magellan Vacations months in advance, and the week of our trip we were notified of a room upgrade that the Gansevoort was offering. We thought this was great! Once we checked in and got to our room we realized that we hadn't received our upgrade. I called the front desk and they notified me that as of that day they were no longer offering the upgrade (even though they acknowledged the fact that they were indeed offering it when it was promised to us). They then told us that there were no rooms available to upgrade us to (but their website showed rooms available) and gave us a small discount on our room. I didn't feel like they went out of their way at all to accommodate us. The front desk staff was very mediocre, you would've thought that it was everyone's first day on the job! The rooftop bar has an amazing view and our bed was super comfy, but overall not a great experience. We would return to the original Gansevoort before this one.

review_title: Perfect location, great deal, clean, okay condition
review_text: We chose The Kimberly because of the price and it's location. The staff was nice and helpful, the rooms were clean and big, BUT what stuck out to me during the visit was the day we checked in. As we were at the "mini" front desk (if that's what it was) they were either repairing or renovating the area, where constant drilling was going on. This made it hard to hear the Front Desk person - I thought this was a little tacky. After checking in, we were waiting for the (what we thought was the guest elevators) elevator to go to our room, and when the door opened, there were (6) housekeepers & (2) room service wait help inside going to the level below us. When I saw this, I had to ask if these were the "service" elevators or "guest" elevators. Overall, I would recommend this hotel for it's location & staff.

I stayed at the Gansevoort Park Hotel over the weekend as part of an anniversary celebration. Having put a lot of thought into choosing the right hotel in New York, I was thrilled to discover the amazing quality and service we got. Because of the occasion, we received a complimentary upgrade to a Grand Deluxe room, which was super spacious, clean, quiet and comfortable. The king sized bed was so plush and downy! The famous rooftop pool was a really unique feature and one of the reasons I was drawn to the hotel in the first place. We got to go swimming under the stars in New York in December with the Empire State Building in view. Definitely recommend it for a romantic getaway. You don't even have to leave the building since everything is right here. I couldn't have asked for a better experience.

review_title: Chic Hotel in NYC would definitely stay again
review_text: My daughter and cousins stayed here 1 night when we went to jingle ball. It was very chic. Beds were very comfortable and staff was very nice. Decor is very cool & chic. Roof top pool is very cool. We would definitely stay here again.

We stayed 6 nights over thanksgiving, and overall had a very nice stay,
The room we had on the 10th floor was massive for NYC standards, kept very clean and the bed was amazing. And I mean amazing I don't think I have slept in a more comfortable bed away from home.
Some other reviews said that they had an issue with the fact that there was bars on the roof, but we used the main enterence so there was no trouble and didn't hear a thing in our room.
There are two enterences to the hot one for bar/ one restaurant and one for the hotel.
We were greeted with a smile and with complementary champagne and breakfast vouchers which was a bonus. 
The hotel is modern, fresh and quiet racey, perfect for a naughty break away with a loved one. 
The staff did go out of thier way to be helpful, I had an issue with a broken lock on my suitcase and an engineer was in my room in minuites and even got a call another 5 minuites later to make sure all was sorted.
I picked this hotel due to the reviews on trip advisor and glad I did as would recommended it to anyone.

review_title: Hampton consistent quality in the heart of Manhattan
review_text: Neighborhood is ok, rooms are good sized by Manhattan standards, noise from ice machine, doors and street can be a bit much. Staff and cleanliness are excellent, which I greatly appreciated!
Everything about the stay was superb. The hotel spends it's money on the important things.

Walls are paper thin. Can hear casual conversation in room nextdoor. Service was poor. Ordered toothpaste and it did not show after 45 minutes, so we left. Called concierge 5 different times and got voice mail. Left message with front desk to have him call back, and ge was "on break". He didnt call back.

review_title: Great location, great rooms, good value.
review_text: I have stayed in this hotel for two weeks in August / September for the past five years. It is in a great location for exploring N.Y, you can walk to Times Sq, Central Park or 5th Avenue all within 15 minutes. The rooms are huge, and are all being refurbished at the moment, the room I had was cleaned daily to a high standard. The beds are queen sized and very comfortable. The staff are very helpful and the doormen always greet you with a smile. There is no Restuarant in the hotel, but this is not a big problem as the are hundreds of places to eat within minutes of the hotel. If you looking for somewhere different then you will love this place.

The staff were very friendly & helpful. Buffet breakfast was the best way to start the day. Such a huge variety, something fir everybody. Room size was ample by New York standards.the extra touches such as mints of a morning & warm chocolate cookies at night made the stay. Location was very handy, easy to get around with Penn station less than a block away. Will definitely stay here ahain

Excellent personnel and location. The room was very small and with thin wall, you will be hearing noises from inside and outside the hotel.
If available will be staying again.

einfach fantastisch.... kann ich jedem empfehlen!!
Zimmer sauber, personal freundlich, fÃ¼r alle sonderwÃ¼nsche offen, super ausgangspunkt fÃ¼r shopping touren,...........
preis ist ok... ist einfach mal was
besonderes! gibt sicher preiswertere
 hotels, aber der flair ist unbezahlbar!!.â€¦

Well my first time in New York and to be honest went on a deal with British Airways. Checked reviews before I went and was not disappointed when I got there. Check in was easy, staff were great and could not do enough for you. Rooms were good, clean, everything worked and the free wifi was great. Good breakfast and taking a hot drink 24/7 from the restuarant was a good touch. Me and the wife stayed there from 28th to 31st October. Now here is the only concern. You check put at 12 noon and we had the maid knocking on our door from 8 asking when we were leaving. On the third occasion she got the message not till 12 noon. Only cplaint and hotel had easy access to all main attractions.

Great location. Hotel very clean, room small but comfortable for 2. Good King-size bed. Nice breakfast with many choies. Tea/coffee machine available 24/7 for free. Helpful staff. Ask for a room as high as possible in the floors! One bad aspect: you hear a lot when people go in or out the rooms next door. But we REALLY enjoyed our stay there a lot and would definitively recommend this hotel!

Having had a bad experience staying in a similarly priced hotel in New York before I was cautious in my expectations of this one (booked as part of a group booking). I needn't have worried. Hampton Inn Madison Square is a great hotel to stay in if you want a central base for your New York trip. The rooms are a little small if more than two folks are in them, but they are clean and comfortable. The staff are what really make this hotel a pleasure to stay in. They are fabulous to a man clearly taking their lead from the excellent manager.

review_title: Rooms large and clean, great location, very comfy beds!

review_title: Residence Inn Times Square - Great Location, Nice Rooms!
review_text:
The Residence Inn Times Square is a perfect hotel if you're looking to be near Times Square but not IN Times Sqaure. It's located on 6th Avenue a little away from the action but close enough to Rockefeller Center, the Diamond District, the Theatre District and Bryant Park that you'll still feel very much part of the action. 
The rooms are a very nice size for Manhattan, clean, efficient and come with a very workable and comfortable little kitchen. This feature allows you to save on meals if you wish. 
They also have a small bar in the hotel and an ample breakfast in the AM. One caveat about breakfast. Get there early. We got there near closing time and the eggs were cold and the French Toast was hard. 
All in all a pleasant stay just a little out of the fray!

review_title: Central and comfortable for a couple or single person
review_text:
I stayed with my sister in law in august for 2 weeks amdfound it initially small and it was however we were mainly there for sightseeing amd shopping. We managed quite well. Didn't really use much of the kitchen except the microwave and the fridge which was very handy! However the kitchen was better than I expected:)
Now I loved the bed so super comfy even though me and my sister in law shared it which we were not planning on as we were under the impression and was told by someone at accor we could upgrade if a room comes available ....well this is not an option at this hotel as the only have one size room. But it worked out fine in the end we managed and we were always so tired from all the walking and touring we did. 
Great location central to everything you need in manhattan. The port authority is super close.
I found our floor really quiet too for such a big city.
The free wifi was great. 
All in all I would recommend staying at the candlewood suites however it would be even better if it was a little cheaper but most accommodation is expensive in NYC 
Thanks for a pleasant stay:)

review_text:
My family and I arrived on October 23 very early but couldn't check in. The front desk member called a bellman and two actually came!! They were so welcoming and helpful and told us different places we could go and see while our room was being made. The two bellman were mostly always together and helped us throughout the week we was there. I was very thankful of Lido and Willy helping us in almost everything starting from the valet to up to the luggage and city attractions. The front desk manager or supervisor( not sure which one) was very kind and also welcoming. I would definitely be staying here again and would recommend it to all!! Breakfast and wifi was terrific and the location is perfect to go almost anywhere. My family enjoyed our first stay and more to come in this marvelous hotel. 
P.S. Very small rooms but very clean and comfortable.
hotel_name: Hampton Inn Manhattan / Times Square South

review_title: A very good and pleasant stay
review_text: I have nothing negative nor have any complaints to say about this hotel. Staff are pleasant and overall hotel experience was very pleasant

We couldn't have asked for anywhere better. The hotel was located right in the centre of everything we wanted to do. The room was lovely (very comfy bed) and the staff all very helpful - recommended us some great places to eat that weren't expensive and also helped us out with finding different tourist attractions. Very clean, helpful staff, ideal location, what more could you want!

The Sofitel NYC, located in mid-town, with easy assess to the subway, short walk to Rockafeller Center, Saks, 5th Ave and Macys. The room are small but not as small as other NY Hotels. The front desk, bellman, are all really helpful. The food this visit was not great. While the maids are visiting the rooms several times a day, the rooms are not extremely well cleaned, nor were the amenities such as soaps, evening evian bottle of water, q-tips etc refreshed. With the exception of the garbage pails being emptied I was not impressed with the maid service. Regardless, I would still stay here again. Its convenient, the staff is very helpful and polite and its across from the Royalton hotel - a great to stop by for drinks or dinner.

My husband & I have just returned from 5 night stay at this hotel. On arrival we were greeted with friendly & helpful staff who advised us that our room was being inspected....after a little wait (with free tea & coffee) we were allocated our room on 22nd floor. The room was lovely & clean, not massive but big enough for the 2 of us, nice shower & bathroom area and very comfortable bed! Rooms very also inspected by housekeeping each day which we thought showed that staff were making sure standards were being met & each time we were asked if we were happy with the room.
Yes, as other reviews will say there is construction work across from the hotel but this does not generally start til 8am and as you are going out and about in New York during the day by the time we got back it was either finished or finishing so it never bothered us and our room was opposite it! Street noise is also at a minimum due to how high up we were.
Hotel is in a good location to times sq, port authority bus terminal and times sq subway Stn. Times sq is only 3 blocks & 1ave away and could be walked in just over 5 mins 
Full breakfast served everyday which is a bonus and saves you $ in terms of food bills....hot and cold options for all and nothing is too much trouble for breakfast girls who were polite and accommodating to our requests. Weekends were busier esp as we were guests over NYC marathon weekend but we were still able to get seats in dining area.
Reception were always on hand if we had any questions or requests and Jennifer was always particularly helpful and friendly, welcoming us back to the hotel every evening with a smile asking us if we had had a nice day & where we had been.
We will definitely go back to both NYC and this hotel! 
Thanks Hampton Inn!
hotel_name: Hampton Inn Manhattan / Times Square South

review_title: Good choices, a few improvements could help
review_text:
A good choice to stay in Manhattan, it's nice to have a kitchen for these evenings when you want to have dinner at home.
It's in the walking distance to Times Square. W 39th St between 8th and 9th Ave is however not a posh address and there are often trash bags on the sideway. 
Of course, hotels in New York are expensive, but this one comparatively has a good value for money.
Much appreciated:
Use of washing machines and dryers is complementary
Wifi is complimentary
Free coffee and USA Today in the lobby
The personnel is helpful and quickly solves your problems
Comfortable bed
A small kit to start you stay (tea bags, coffee, sugar, salt, pepper, detergent...)
Could be improved:
Lack of tableware and cookware: 4 plates, 4 knives, no colander... That's not much when you like cooking. Also, you need tu run partially filled dishwashers because of this lack of tableware (not environmental friendly).
The scheduling of housekeeping could be improved (it was performed after 8 days of stay but 2 days before our check out). 
The sofabed is absolutely uncomfortable to sleep: you only feel the springs! Forget to use it to accomodate an extra guest.
You cannot select a low fan speed of the air conditioning (e.g. to generate less noise at night).
Tip: do not choose an accessible room if you do not need it. The no-step shower pours a lot of water out of the shower onto the bathroom floor and you constantly need to wipe out. 
Second tip: consider the hotel loyalty programme. It allowed us to postpone the check out time at 2pm. Other advantages are also available. 
Last tip, for European people. Select "warm" on the washing machine when you are used to washing at 40â€¢C.
Please apologize my poor English, this is not my native language.

review_title: So small you will go insane!
review_text:
My partner and I recently booked to stay here after reading some of the previous reviews and the reasonable price. While the hotel was very tidy and has a fantastic location it is small and so are the "rooms". I don't just mean a little bit pokey I am taking Harry Potter under the stairs small. There is no where to put your luggage which makes it very interesting when you are travelling as a couple. You are literally on top of each other the entire time. I think this would even still be too small if you were travelling on your own. We found the pictures to be very misleading. Kudos to the photographer who took the shots, the room looks spacious and you cannot see the hideous window mounted heater/aircon unit. majority of the staff were friendly some more so than others. On a number of occasions we were greated with a grunt by the ladies at the front desk only to walk behind them to get into the elevator to discover them doing a spot of online shopping for shoes and dresses.Â 
The max time I would recommend to stay in this hotel would be no more than 2-3 days it was a nightmare with how small it is. In a city as crazy as NYC your hotel room really needs to be a sanctuary, where you can escape the hustle and bustle of the streets. Unfortunately this hotel room only intensified the feeling of constantly being surrounded by people. Next time I would spend slightly more on a larger hotel room as it wasnt worth the stress if being in such a tiny room, with no where other than the bed to sit. While we thought who cares after reading other reviews about how small the room is, your in NYC right who hangs out in their room? But honestly with what little time we did spend in it with a room that small we couldn't wait to leave!

We stayed in this Hotel for 6 nights , in the last week of august. Rooms are small clean and comfortable. Nice friendly staff. Great location. We will certainly stay here, on our next trip to NYC.
And we thank the Hotel for the free breakfast they provided, on the morning of Hurricane Irene. Much appreciated. Would recommend to friends.
I would not recommend this hotel to anyone staying longer than one night. Rooms too small, and aircon too noisy.

This was my friend and my first trip to NY and we were recommended the Washington Square Hotel for its location and price. 
It lived up to its reputation in that it is a good price and a fabulous location. 5th Ave starts just under the arch in Washington Square Park!
On arrival to the hotel at 2.30pm (after a long day travelling) we were met by what I can only say as an unfriendly moody receptionist who didn't really look at us when we spoke to her and said our room wasn't ready. We had to prompt her to say when it may be ready and were told 3.30pm (half an hour later than it should be). We were not offered an explanation or ideas of what to do in the mean time...NY is rather daunting when you first arrive! However the lovely guy on the door offered to take our cases and suggested we make the most of the beautiful weather and go to Washington Square Park, which we did. 
We arrived back at 3.20pm to be met by another moody receptionist who said our room was ready and asked for a credit card in most rude manner. I'm afraid to say at this point after 10 hours + travelling I did say that I was tired and irritable and was likey to snap back at her at any moment and after this, she became helpful and friendly!
We finally arrived to our room and had to wait as the cleaner was still vacuuming! He didn't take long though and we were in. 
I have to say we were both a little disappointed on first glance. The room was very small and dark (view from window was a brick wall) and was in need of a lick of paint. However, it was immaculately clean and the bathroom was more than adequate with nice thick heavy robes for our use. The wardrobe is a joke for 2 women sharing! We had to stuff clothes in bedside table drawers etc!
The room did its job though, we were only there to sleep in any case as NY has so much to see and do. 
We did go to the breakfast buffet once but it was rather dull. Cold pastries and cereal. We wanted pancakes!!!!
I would stay here again but would request a better room with a view if possible.

review_title: small rooms but clean with comfy bed and good location for people who love to explore a city by walking everywhere!
review_text: I expected a small room but this was tight! no worry though, as it was clean and the bed was very comfortable. the location- great if you like walking- most of the interesting stuff is within walking distance. even the subway is a couple blocks away. but the problem is that none of the interesting stuff is nearby either. the location lacks character and feels a bit like a no mans land in between the interesting bits. it was also a real mission trying to find good coffee each morning if you don't like Starbucks!

review_text: We booked this hotel after a recomendation from a friend. It was everything we hoped and more. I spent ages looking at rates and with the advance booking discount this was a bargain. It was clean, well maintained and the staff couldn't have been friendlier. The Hotel is in a great location in what felt like a very safe area and we can't wait to go back.

This ones hard to beat. Seriously great location in midtown, clean and good price. Drawbacks? This is New York - rooms are smallish, mini-gym insufficient, postage stamp lobby (can get hectic during mass check-in/check-out). - otherwise, for less than you'd pay at a La Quinta in Ft. Worth you're in the heart of the worlds most exciting city!

review_title: I think this will be my NYC hotel from now on
review_text:
I can't say enough about the location of the hotel. Right near Washington Square Park, great restaurants/bars & shopping. What more could you ask for? It has a neighborhood feel instead of a touristy feel which I enjoy. 
Otto (one of Mario Batali's restaurants) is right around the corner. It's not only delicious but very reasonably priced.
Bars like the Four Faced Liar & Slaughtered Lamb on 6th & Fat Black P****cat on 3rd are all great neighborhood bars. 
Shopping is only a handful of blocks away on Broadway!
The hotel is clean with decent size rooms & bathrooms. I have nothing negative to say about this hotel. I loved it and will definitely return.

We stayed here for eight nights over st patricks wk. We'er seasoned travelers n have stayed in many hotels in USA n Europe. Rooms are very small but very clean n modern, ensuite was nice. I'm over six foot n slept in the bed fine, street noise doesn't bother us but remember it's on 5th ave! We were in ny to sight 
see n shop so didn't spend any time
 in hotel only at night, which is good cause there's only the small room n starbucks to hang out in but we knew this when booking. Location is fantastic, we looked out on empire state from bedrm window! Macys n time sq 5 min walk, central park 10/15 min walk n hop on off bus tours pass across the st! Hardly used underground n only taxi twice! Staff were friendly n helpful. If your looking for large reception area, restuarant etc stay elsewhere. But for great location n very clean rooms for little money then 373 is the place. Ps not easy find the building for the first time even standing ar the street corner, small sign on glass door. traveled from Ireland n would defo stay here again n recommend.
