review_title: Great service at mid price manhattan
review_text: Stayed at Marcel. Rooms are designed in funky style but clean tiled bath rooms. Pillows seem shabby and ceiling light is clothed and not bright enough. I am neurotic about bed bugs and checked under sheets and around mattress. Didn't see any but did get one bite that I think was bed bug bite. Wished beds and pillows had bed bug covers.

Best hotel we have stayed at. Staff are friendly, patient and beyond helpful. It was really nice that they all remembered our names when they saw us. It isn't your usual anonymous, robotic chain hotel 
Rooms are 'european' size but we were too busy exploring to mind. Decor is fresh and modern and there was a complimentary tea and coffee station on the 10th floor. Although we popped over the street to bagel express for breakfast. 
Hotel is within walking distance to all the touristy bits, if you are fit and have good footwear! 
All in all we loved it and can't wait to return.
Great hotel for the price you pay. Very clean, good beds, great service.
Stayed for 5 days in August 2011. Room was good, I hear they can be hit n miss. But the location, value and service were faultless, would stay again.

review_title: Friendly hotel in an excellent location
review_text: Having never been to NYC before, I was unsure where to stay. I wanted to be able to get around the city easily but be based in a quieter area. This hotel gives that. The local area is great; plenty of good restaurants and coffee shops, easy walking distance to many interesting places in the Village, and very close to metro stations which give access to a number of different lines. The room was small, but very comfortable and the bathroom had a tub and shower which is unusual in a hotel of this size. Breakfast was included which was great, although if you're looking for the archetypal American breakfast cross Sixth Avenue to the Waverley Diner. There is a Starbucks at the end of the block; perfect for buying a coffee in the morning before sitting in Washington Square Park. The staff were friendly and helpful and the hotel's retro styling is attractive. I'll definitely stay again!

review_title: Great location, unacceptable service for the level of hotel
review_text: This is a hip hotel in a great location with a good restaurant. The rooms are extremely small and have a poor layout. I was here on a business trip and had no where to work beside essentially sitting in the bathroom. On that note, forget room service unless you want to eat it in your bed. My biggest issue is the service. A hotel at this price point should have flawless service all the way through from the doormen( which there was often none and the ones when there didn't want to help with bags and were noticeably irritated when they had to help get a cab) to the desk to the room service. None of these people were terrible but none seemed to be trained as to the level of a superior hotel.

This hotel is in a great location with Madison square park a 100 metres up the road,stunning at night.
I found my room to be very comfortable,the bed being especially comfortable,the room being very spacious with a well set out bathroom.I found the house keeping staff to be very friendly and thorough in cleaning my room, always a pleasure to come back to.
The front desk staff were also very friendly and helpful with anything.A great hotel
hotel_name: Wyndham Garden Hotel Manhattan, Chelsea West

review_title: Excellent hotel in excellent location attentive and friendly staff
review_text: Stayed here for 4 nights in december , loved the hotel with great views. Lost my wallet first night I was here and staff found it on the sidewalk and made sure I got it back completely intact . Hugely greatfull of the honest and helpful staff . Visited New york for last 8 years around christmas and stayed in soho in several boutique hotels .The Mondrian rates amongst the best. A definite return visit for me next time I am in town

We stayed for 5 nights at the Mondrian Soho and had an amazing time!! The rooms were clean with a huge bed and equipped with iPad and free wireless which really helped!! The staff were amazingly polite and helpful - best service I have experienced in NYC! Location is great for shopping in Soho and easy access to the subway. We received a great deal via booking.com. Thank you for making our stay so enjoyable!! T&P

review_title: Average tourist-class hotel; very nice staff.
review_text: Stayed here on a 2-night business trip. The staff was very nice, friendly and helpful. The location is not great but alright. The room was quite small and hard to move around in, as others have said, but the bed was comfortable and everything was very clean. Noise problem with the air unit, but without it you hear everything in the rooms around you.
hotel_name: Wyndham Garden Hotel Manhattan, Chelsea West

review_title: Avoid this one, not clean and outdated.
review_text: I stayed with a friend who has a time share; my daughter and I have stayed at beautiful hotels worldwide and are not snobs, and we hated this place. The rooms were dirty, the carpeting, upholstery, countertops etc were dirty as well. The staff unhelpful and unfriendly. Rooms are dark and dreary. Filthy would be a better word when it comes to the upholstery! When we walked into the lobby late at night I did not feel safe and felt like I was in a very sketchy place. The halls were dismal and dark, some areas were VERY narrow, could barely walk through without banging luggage against the wall. Luckily, I was not the paying customer, I would have been furious and appalled at the conditions. You could not pay me to stay here again. My friend offered me the place for additional days but we could not stay any longer than one night. I didn't sleep a wink, the fold out was uncomfortable. I would rather pay $500/night somewhere else and feel clean and secure than stay at the Manhattan club for a second. I don't write reviews normally but felt I had to in this case. Trust me you can pay less and have a significanly better experience!!! Previous reviewer was right Howard Johnson's or a Holiday Inn would be a better choice! You can pass on this one!

I've been meaning to write this review for months. We stayed at the Mondrian end May/early June and loved every minute. 
The rooms are amazing. We stayed on the 20th floor and had great views. Loved the cool blue/White decor. The whole hotel was spotless and oh so cool. Some people have commented about the 'trendy' clientele but we didn't feel uncomfortable for a second. It was our first time in NYC and we pounded the streets making sure we saw all the sites. We were returning to the hotel rather tired looking but the staff welcomed us & treated us the same way as guests at a champagne reception hosted by Susan Sarandon (yip, that was just one of the snazzy events while we stayed).
The bar area is lovely, we enjoyed a good few cocktails there but didn't get around to sampling any of the food.
 If you're lucky enough to be planning a trip to NY you should definitely consider staying at the Mondrian.
love this hotel.from the entrance to the postcard on my pillow, perfection.

The Mondrian hotel was an oasis of calm, quality, and service in the middle of soho. The food was seriously the best prepared and presented and of course the best tasting ! The rooms are spotles and ver funkyly decorated and yea the are reall small, I mean closet size small but they are very nice, comfortable and unheard of in New York they were not noisy at all.

review_title: Great location and more than adequate rooms.
review_text: For us this was a great value because we rented from an owner for three nights over thanksgiving weekend. The costs would have been much more if we hadn't. We stayed on the 20th floor in a Junior Executive Suite and were very pleased with size. We stay in the city several weekends a year and this is the largest we've stayed in. The location is awesome, subway is real close, plenty of food choices. I have 2 complaints although not significant to us. The elevators were slow a various times during the day. Many people were willing to ride up the elevator just to get back down. And do not attempt to use them during checkout time (11 am). The guest directory is a little misleading when it talks about the club lounge- the continental breakfast is not included with your stay, it is $14.95. The tv in the room was even more misleading. We are going to stay here again in March in the one bedroom suite.

review_title: Nice location, high price for value.
review_text: Had to call to have the heat turned on 2 of the 3 nights we were there. Missed our wake up call. Had everything we needed though and quiet. Overall good.

I stayed at this hotel for 8 nights with my husband in September 2011. The first night our room was very small. The air con was loud and right next to the bed. I was worried as it was so loud but the hotel staff offered to upgrade us to a bigger room for the next 7 nights. 
The second room was much better! I agree the rooms are small but the room we stayed for the rest of our trip was bigger and had room to unpack our bags. We stayed on level 5. I recommend asking for a higher floor if you are a light sleeper as the traffic is a little loud. 
The location is great! Close to so many restaurants. 3 blocks to a laundromat which was handy. About $10 by taxi to broadway. We could walk to west village (half hour stroll). The hotel also had a lounge on level 10 with free Internet and great view of empire state building.
Overall, I recommend this hotel.

A special thanks to Raoul! The last day, before arriving at the airport, we forgot the iPhone and Raoul stopped our taxi and gave it to us. The hotel is in a good position, near the center, but the rooms are too small. Un saluto dall'Italia, consiglio a chiunque di visitare New York........................................â€¦â€¦

First time in NYC and this is the place to stay! It is clean, beautiful, and centrally located. The staff is so helpful, and Manuel is fantastic. Being tourists from out of state we didn't have a clue how to get anywhere or even what to do. Full of suggestions, and always patient and helpful, Manuel has made our stay memorable!

review_title: Great staff, great location, great stay
review_text:
I read other reviews complaining about the front desk staff. I don't know what they did to those people, but I have nothing but excellent things to say about them. They were helpful in every way and went the extra mile. 
Room - we stayed on the 8th floor facing the museum of natural history. The windows did nothing to block the noise from street. I'd recommend an even higher floor. Other than that, room was sufficient.
Overall, no major complaints, convenient location, great staff, good room.

review_title: The best service I've experienced at a hotel anywhere.
review_text: From the moment we arrived, the hotel staff went out of their way to make our stay as comfortable as possible. Our original room did not accommodate the 3 of us well, so we asked for an alternate room. The front desk manager personally showed us several other rooms available and let us chose the one we wanted! Amazing service! Any time we had a request, the staff responded immediately. The location was convenient, rooms clean, and hotel trendy. They even have a nice lounge with refreshments open all day on the 10th floor.

review_title: Great location, the rest is average
review_text: We used rci points to stay here and not sure I would pay to go back - was all ok just not amazing. Our room had no natural daylight which made you feel like you were sleeping in a dungeon! Made it really hard to wake up. Service from staff was ok but not that friendly.

review_title: The most courteous staff of any hotel I have patronized centrally located in manhattan.
review_text: I have already stayed in this hotel four times within this last year. The employees are courteous and friendly as well as helpful. The rooms are very clean, and it is located a few short blocks from grand central station. With all this hotel has to offer, the price is more than competitive. Great value without sacrificing quality. 2 THUMBS UP
Perfect location and wonderful staff all wrapped up in great price
hotel_name: Wyndham Garden Hotel Manhattan, Chelsea West

review_title: One of the best "boutique" hotels in NYC and great value
review_text: I have stayed at the Roger Smith hotel about 17 times over the last 10 years and every time is better than the last. Seems that every time I come to NYC and stay somewhere else I end up saying "I wish I was at the Smith". While some of the rooms are small, the suites are great, like little apartments. The staff in this hotel is top notch and is incredibly helpful in every way. There are fantastic restaurants and good deli all within a short walk. Also Grand Central is just a short 5 block walk which is super convenient. The place is very clean, food is good, staff is always great. If they have rooms available you should stay here, . . . Joe Sloboda

I had a very nice stay here over a weekend. The staff during the day are extremely helpful and friendly. The night shift crew a little less so but they werent rude.
The rooms are small. This is partially expected due to location but don't expect to bring and be able to fit more than a 2 large suitcases with you.
This place is in a great area with lots of parks and easy train access to things like empire states building and times square. 
Room was clean and cleaning staff were very friendly.
hotel_name: Wyndham Garden Hotel Manhattan, Chelsea West

review_text: This hotel is amazing it has the nest location of any in SOHO. The staff is very helpful but definitely a little hipster which we enjoyed! If you are wondering where to stay, this is your place!

review_title: Affordable NYC hotel near Central Park
review_text:
The Manhattan Club's location can't be beat. Two blocks from Central Park, one from Carnegie Hall, and close to the MoMA. The online deals right now are fantastic. We booked a junior suite with kitchenette for $250/night. 
Rooms are clean and comfortable. Bath and Body Works tolietries. Free wifi. The only disappointment is that the living area of the suite is not actually separate from the bedroom. It's small for a jr suite, but the more important part is not having a door to separate the two rooms. Thankfully this wasn't a big deal for us. 
Valet parking is $28; standard for NYC. Overall very pleased.

review_title: A very welcoming, non-corporate atmosphere wher I always feel at home, very reasonably priced!
review_text: My favorite place to stay in manhattan. Lots of personality. Great rooftop bar in warmer weather. Great bacon! Interesting art! No cookie cutter decor here. Close to Grand Central. Always clean, great service, free wifi!

review_title: This is more Mondrian Chinatown and not Mondrian Soho
review_text:
I decided to book Mondrian Soho with the idea to walk around Soho, but sadly we are not at the heart of Soho but rather on the edge of Soho, borderline to Chinatown.
The room is rather small.

Stayed for 4 nights with my friends in October. We booked a triple room with 3 single beds but on arrival were given 2 doubles so I had to share with my friend. Room was very small especially for 3 adults sharing. Found the staff throughout our stay VERY UNHELPFUL!!!! The only good thing about hotel is location. A few minutes walk from central park & the subway. Lots of restaurants & a supermarket nearby. Plan on going back to New York but wouldn't stay here again!!!

Seriously, the only good thing about this place was the location. My bathroom is bigger at home than the entire room we stayed. Every time I showered, there was a major drainage problem, so my feet were in a foot of standing water. The heater never worked & mgt said the boiler goes on & off every 20 minutes. Was it coincidental that every time I tried to use the heat, the boiler was off? Half of the power outlets didn't work. The concierge was snarky from the beginning. The bell boy was either clueless or just simply rude. Maybe both. I would NEVER stay here again.

Stayed here for 3 nights prior to a QM2 crossing. We enjoyed our stay, though we only used the room, not the bar or restaurant, but these seemed popular. Our room was clean and well presented, with two flat screen TV's! 
The staff were helpful, though the car booked by the hotel did not appear and a taxi was hastily summoned.
My only, minor, criticism is 
we only saw two small lifts servicing 16 floors and quite often had to wait several minutes during peak times.
The hotel is well located in a pleasant area of town with several good restaurants nearby, 
particularly on Broadway. 
Access downtown is simple. If you're of reasonable fitness it's a pleasant stroll through Columbus and Times Square. There is a subway station close by outside the Natural History Museum, with 
access directly onto 81st Street.

review_title: Trendy Soho hotel with great service
review_text:
We got a great rate on booking.com so despite the critical reviews we decided to give it a try. 
PROS:
Staff is really friendly and helpful.
Super comfortable bed & pillows. 
Great soho location- shopping & close to the subway.
Cool entrance, lobby and restaurant
Nice Complimentary breakfast 
Hip blue and white themed rooms. 
Nice smelling bath products.
IPads in all the rooms.
Con.
No free wifi and you pay per day & per device ( how hard is it to make this free)
Taxis have no idea where this hotel is- make sure you have the 
address. 
Shower head aimed right at door- could not adjust it so it got water all over the bathroom floor.
Small rooms- but where arranged to maximize the space.
Overall we had a great stay and loved the trendy design and friendly service.

review_title: special thanks to the Marcel staff!!
review_text: My family and I stayed at the marcel in early july for a mini family get away and boy wasnt It amazing! The staff made us feel right at home upon our arrival and gave us amazing resturant suggestions throughout our stay! As for the rooms they were decent sized for a nyc hotel cant complain! Deff will be returning to the Marcel.

We discovered the Excelsior via Travelocity and expected "discount" quality accommodations. We couldn't have been more surprised when we were shown our mini-suite, complete with all imaginable amenities. The staff were also extremely friendly and helpful. The location is ideal, with the front of the hotel facing the "dog park" alongside the American Museum of Natural History, and Central Park less than a block away. We plan to make the Excelsior our place to stay every time we visit NYC.

review_title: Great friendly hotel in an excellent location
review_text: Stayed for five nights on business. Room was comfortable and very clean. Happier once I found the thermostat on wall by wardrobe. Room was at back of hotel and very quiet so great for a good nights sleep. Coffee making facilities, iron and board was a nice touch. Reception staff were only too pleased to help and nothing seemed too much trouble.
hotel_name: Wyndham Garden Hotel Manhattan, Chelsea West

review_text: Great location, excelent peopme attending and fair cost.

review_title: This was one of our best picks in nyc hotels!!
review_text: We were so happy with our choice of hotel! The staff was friendly, the room was spacious and clean, and the location was great. We'll definitely return! The only negative was that the rooftop bar is not open on the weekends. The accommodating staff did let us take drinks from the bar onto the rooftop, though!! We LOVE Roger Smith Hotel and we'll definitely return!!

review_title: This was one of our best picks in nyc hotels!!
review_text: We were so happy with our choice of hotel! The staff was friendly, the room was spacious and clean, and the location was great. We'll definitely return! The only negative was that the rooftop bar is not open on the weekends. The accommodating staff did let us take drinks from the bar onto the rooftop, though!! We LOVE Roger Smith Hotel and we'll definitely return!!

This hotel was a great price and great stay!!! This was my first time actually staying overnight in New York and I would definitely go back and stay again! The hotel staff was very friendly, great location( not too far from times square), the rooms were very modern and clean (bed was super comfy). The restaurant in the hotel is amazing (try the shrimp). Overall very pleased!
hotel_name: Wyndham Garden Hotel Manhattan, Chelsea West

review_text: Great hotel. The bartender Errol was awesome! (Definitely made the dining experience entertaining) Errol was friendly and he made the hotel stay that much better! Affordable and the beds were comfy. Great location too.
hotel_name: Wyndham Garden Hotel Manhattan, Chelsea West

review_title: Quiet location, close enough to the action.
review_text: 5 nights stay at this hotel, we got some flavor of living in NYC. Visited plenty of the sights using the subway just up the road. No issues with the staff, but we were not in the hotel room long enough anyway. Quiet room on the 11th floor, so slept soundly each night.

spend some time in the lounge and do yourself a favor, order a mojito, Number Eight and Number Nine from the cocktail menu. You will not be disappointed. 
A big thank you to the staff who made our newly engaged stay absolutely perfect! We'll definitely be staying here next time we're in NYC!
What up Mondrian SOHO!

We really enjoyed our stay at the Mondrian SOHO over the past four days. The hotel is beautiful, the location is great for SOHO shopping, the food in the restaurant is creative and amazing, and the staff has clearly been hired for their positive attitudes and love of customer service. 
Quick note: the restaurant/bar is rockin' well past 2am so make sure your room is at least on the 5th floor or not on Crosby Street or you'll hear the subwoofer pounding. 
We're definitely staying there again.

Having visited New York several times, I have to say that the Excelsior is by far the best hotel I've stayed in - the main reason being it's fabulous location.
I love New York, but sometimes I need a break from the constant crowds and hustle and bustle you find in midtown. The Excelsior is far enough away to offer a haven from this, but being on a subway stop means you're not far from anywhere either.
The hotel is situated on West 81st street, directly opposite the American Museum of Natural History and Central Park. The fabulous bars and restaurants of Amsterdam Avenue are two blocks away too and offer much better value than the tourist traps of midtown.
The rooms at the hotel are spacious, with two double beds and en suite. Safety deposit boxes are in the room and are free. There's also a tv and iPod dock/radio in the room. Staff were also friendly on check in.
The hotel offers a pretty basic $17 breakfast and has a bar (pricey) and restaurant just off the lobby. There's also a gym on the second floor which is also pretty basic.
The only negatives I would give it would be the lack of coffee/tea making facilities and no free wifi - but these are minor as there is a Starbucks around the corner on Columbus Avenue which served my needs.
Overall, this hotel was a great place to stay because of it's location. I would 100% stay here again.

Albergo in posizione fantastica davanti a Rockefeller Center a due passi da tutto...perÃ² la camera di dimensioni 'normali' era fredda (non funzionava il riscaldamento) con vetrata non isolata sia dal freddo che proveniva dall'esterno che dai rumori...colazione non compresa e abbastanza cara...personale gentile e disponibile.

review_title: Was happy with our stay at the Excelsior Hotel
review_text:
My son and I came to NYC from NC to take a look at Columbia University.
Took two cancelled flights from RDU NC to reach hotel a day late. Lost one night of prepaid reservation due to airline delays. Manager took off $100 on hotel bill when asked.
Unlike some reviews we found both the room and staff most acceptable. Even had doorman stand in down pour for 15 minutes getting us a cab.
Hotel is not luxurious but a very good value in NYC.

I usually stay in the Meatpacking District near my office but I wanted to try the new Mondrian Soho as they have fun properties elsewhere. I called to make my reservation as their booking system wasn't working and I was arriving on a redeye and wanted to have a room ready that morning. They didn't note that properly and cancelled my entire reservation when I didn't check in the prior night. Reservations couldn't help, the front desk couldn't help get me into a room so I could shower and change for my meetings. They were inflexible and generally unhelpful, especially considering it was their fault. Not even close to the level of service expected from such a luxury hotel. I will never stay again.
Great location for access to tourist sites by day and local neighborhood feel at night. Nice location across from museum park and very spacious room. Will definitely stay here again.
The location and value of this hotel is hard to beat. Rooms are typical Marriott, but are clean and roomy enough.

review_title: Great location but otherwise average Marriott
review_text: Although one might think being on the east side would not be accessible it actually is located in a very opportune location to Madison, 5th ave and times square shopping and tourist spots. Concierge club was one of the nicest but service was lackluster otherwise from the front desk to the concierge. It ended with me asking for an envelope for my bill and they just handed me one. Food was barely edible. This is NYC and its clear there is no attention to detail here. Bathroom was dark otherwise everything else was standard issue. They did not change out our playpen sheet even though it was clearly stained. We'd stay again for location and for not being in a super busy area like times sq but that's it.

We have been staying here forever and the improvements are amazing! The staff has stayed very constant over the years which is a sign of a good employer and makes the returning guests feel like they are coming home. All but three of the floors have central air conditioning now. The bathrooms have undergone updates...( apparently nothing much to be done about the fluctuating water temps). The continental breakfast is just enough. BTW I usually go down for that very early and never have a problem. Today, I didn't go until 9AM and there was a line of people waiting for tables. Because I bring it up to our room, I was able to skip that line...why wouldn't everyone do that? We really wouldn't stay anywhere else in NYC unless the Milburn was full!
Clean, spacious, and free wifi! Couldn't get a better deal and in a great location. Definitely heading back very soon.

review_title: Great experience but request bigger room.
review_text:
Our family chose hotel belleclaire because of the value and reviews. It was overall a great experience. We arrived very late and we given a very small room. For a family of four, we would not be able to walk. However, once I requested a bigger room, they accommodated us and moved us the next day while we were out. The location and cleanliness were top notch. 
Even though the cable was out for two days and the heating was funky, we had a great time. I also recommend visiting Big Nicks.

I stayed in this hotel for 2 nights this past week. We stayed on a friends hotel discount so I certainly won't complain about the price! It couldn't have been better. The hotel was clean..the views sucked but that's new York for you! All and all it was a great trip and the hotel staff was super nice.

Am still staying in the hotel as my company did a block booking of about 30 rooms for 2 weeks.note that basic toiletries like shower caps, toohthbrush or toothpaste are not provuded. Housekeeping did not clear the leftover hair in the shower stall. My room is small, with barely any counter space at the sink for toiletries. Massive long wait for elevators. Forget about the buffett breakfast, eat elsewhere. Internet acces is charged at $10 per 24 hours, which is atrocious for a financial district hotel. Will not recommend to any friends.
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel New York City-Financial District

review_title: Good value hotel in an excellent location
review_text: Myself and my wife have just returned from NY having spent 5 nights at this hotel. Like most of the other reviews on here, we agree that the best thing about the Belleclaire is the location. The hotel itself is a lovely old building with not so lovely plumbing keeping the rooms warm. The clanking and knocking coming from the radiator kept me awake on our first night but after walking miles around Manhattan on the subsequent days sleeping at night was not a problem! What we liked most was coming out of the mayhem of Midtown and walking up from Columbus Circle and up Broadway which got more and more sedate the closer we got to the hotel. We also got the Metro to and fro Midtown using the station at 72nd Street on Broadway. We felt safe walking around here late at night and there are some great restaurants nearby. We had breakfast in Big Nicks which was virtually next door - don't expect posh but do expect decent New York food served in a true New York style! Our room was very small and we had a view of a brick wall, however, we didn't spend much time in the room so this wasnt an issue for us. The bed was very comfy and the room was kept very clean. All in all this was a great place to stay for a short break in this wonderful city.

I just checked in to The Marcel and felt right @ home! Ricky, Chris and Juan got it going on:) I am looking forward to an amazing stay! So hurry up and get here and see what I'm talking about! More to come on this lovely place:)

I recent decided to try the UWS for a try to get away from the usual tourist crowd- Hotel Belleclaire is in a great neighborhood, and amazing close to the 1 train! There are places around to eat, drink, and shop.. And if not just walk to the 1. The rooms were good, the only criticism I have is the elevator smelled strange and that the rooms were clean but maybe because the hotel is older they had a musty not clean feeling. The staff was super helpful and kind ( I had a flower in the room and the staff placed it in a vase). The only criticism about them is ther person I shared a room with said someone came to the door about a possible leak without the front desk informing us so we were a little annoyed! All in all a great stay, a good price, and they leave copies of timeout NY in your room everyday!!!

review_title: Great New York value and great location...small room...yep you're in New York
review_text:
The best thing about this hotel is the location. Nice safe area on the upper west and close to the subway, with neighbourhood restaurants all around. The second best thing is the price, very reasonable for NY and a lot cheaper than the usual chain hotels.
Originally booked a standard room but was told on arrival we had been upgraded to a queen room. The rooms are small, I wouldn't have like to have seen the standard room! However it is no secret space is a luxury and at a premium in the big apple, so this was expected. The floor on which we were staying had some renovation work going on. This was neither communicated to us before or on arrival. It wasn't noisy, but walking on cardboard (placed to keep carpets clean and the hallways), wasn't the best impression along with furniture littering the halls where they must have been stripping out rooms. Perhaps this was the reason for the 'upgrade'. However, a simple mention of this at checkin wlild have been polite - i tend to expect more than a one word 'no' answer to a request for service. They get a point back for organising a car for check out to take the airport..but as this is not a standard taxi, and you pay the hotel...they are glad to be making some money from you I expect...but it was easy and on time, and thats all I are about. 
Stay here and you will not be dissapointed, and you will not be grossly out of pocket compared to staying closer to Times Sq. Being a more neighbourhood type area yaou will also find some hidden gems as restaurants.
How could this property be better? Better people skills from frontline staff (excluding housekeeping who were wonderful).
I would stay here again, for the value and the location, just not the staff...but then if they want to be indifferent, I'm happy for them to get on with it, whilst I enjoy my day.

review_title: Big city, big promise, small rooms
review_text:
Can't go wrong with nyc, but this hotel was a bit disappointing. The lobby and building are very impressive but we were bit surprised that the rooms didn't meet the expectations set on their web site.
For most the tourist hot spots the excelsior is a bit too much of a walk but sub way nice and close and this area has a few places to eat and drink.

review_title: Staff is top of the line
review_text: I've stayed here on 2 separate occasions and both times the staff did everything possible to make my stay enjoyable and to get the best rate available. They are very personable and made me feel very comfortable when they remembered me from my previous stay and helped me get a room during a snow storm when the hotel was full.

The location is lovely...close to the park, cafes on Columbus Ave., Hayden, walk through Central Park to the Guggenheim, subway close by...Our room was large with two beds, nice bath, and was very clean. We had no need for interaction with staff except at check in and that was pleasant. 
I look forward to returning on my next trip to NYC.

review_title: Our home away from home when we come to NYC!
review_text: This is our second extended stay at this hotel and we feel right at home. Hotels in this city tend to be ridiculously expensive and add insult to injury by charging ala carte for a miriad of additional services. Not here. The rooms are fresh, clean and ample in size, particularly for NYC. The wifi is free, the gym is free and I expect no extras on my bill. We will continue to visit this friendly small hotel as long as we come to the city!

I was most disappointed with this hotel. My room was a shoebox and the bed linen had seen better days. The sheet and the bed cover both had holes in them.
The carpet was quite soiled.
The room needed a deep clean and a total overhaul.
The staff were just ok - they could have benefitted from a training course in customer service.
The only positive was the location.

We spent 3 nights at this hotel and I must say the service was excellent. The location was within walking distance to Rockefeller Center, Times Square, Shopping, Central Park and Grand Central Station. I would definately stay at this Marriott again.

review_title: Wonderful location. Long waits for elevators.
review_text: The staff at the DblTree were very accomodating. I had gotten a great rate by booking online and using a Hilton Honors code. I saved about $60 a night. The room was on an upper floor - very clean, totally what I expected - the wait for the elevators was crazy though. Thirty minutes to get from the 15th floor to the lobby. Would have taken stairs had it not been for luggage! They have a concierge service that gave pretty good directions. Overall the location was ideal as we weren't very far from a subway and battery park was within a quick walk for ferry to Statue of Liberty
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel New York City-Financial District

review_title: Stay away from hotel belleclaire if u want quietness
review_text: I was attracted by the photo in hotel.com. The deluxe room looks nice with reasonable price. I was so disappointed when I check in as the receptionist required us to pay 25US dollar for extra bed each night! I was mislead by the photo as it showed two separate bed!! The room is spacious and even we suited at the 9 floor, it's still noisy. U can request much in this old buidling but the window cannot close and the air conditioner is super noisy! We could only turn off the air con and open the window. But there is a fire station and a construction site near the contner which are so noisy and make u can sleep! The location is ideal but its just too noisy

Stayed here for business because of the price and location to Wall Street. There is not a lot to do after dark but a cab ride and a few blocks later young some great places to eat. The hotel is pretty low key and on a quiet street. There is a hole in the wall across the street that sells awesome lobster rolls for lunch but get there early because the line is huge. If you know about NYC history you are in the oldest part of town. Cool stuff if you like that sort of thing.
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel New York City-Financial District

review_text: The room was so small you could hardly move. Staff so unhelpful and they seem to be on a commission for certain businesses. We wanted a taxi to the airport and the concierge told us that we had no chance of getting one but that he could recommend a drivers service! We passed on his offer and walked out to a waiting taxi at the required time. Messy areas, only 1 lift working. Very poor hotel.

review_title: Our home when we're in NYC
review_text:
My wife and I grew up in New York, and lived in the city for forty years. We make frequent trips back however, and now that we no longer prefer to sleep on friends' pullout couches, we always stay at the Belleclaire. The rooms are always clean, the wi-fi works well, and we like staying in the Upper West Side in a real neighborhood. (First time visitors to NYC might not, however. The only close by tourist attractions are the Museum of Natural History, the Planetarium, and Central Park, and Lincoln Center is a short walk. If you want to see things in Lower Manhattan, you'll have to take the subway, a bus, or a cab.). 
We also like the staff a great deal; they're both friendly and helpful. Although we've never needed their help to get around, we've seen them offer good advice to others. The fitness center is nothing special, but at least it exists: if you're a runner and the weather is not terrible, you can run in Central Park, which is much more fun.
In short, unless this is your first NYC visit-and maybe if it is-stay here. You won't be disappointed!

Disclaimer: I'm an impatient new yorker and extensively travelled, so my opinions probably aren't in line with most likely clientele of this hotel.
Background: I recently moved to the burbs so needed a night in the city for a friends wedding, and grabbed this hotel off priceline ($150 w/ tax). - the negotiator didn't pull through for me on this one guys.
Complaints: Service was quite terrible for the following reasons:
1. Called the night before and requested early check-in bc wedding start time was 3pm (normal check-in being 3pm). Was told "no problem - plenty of free rooms". I understand there are no guarantees for early check-in, but upon arrival (at 230pm), was told that rooms were fully booked so early check-in was never possibility. Avoid "Lenny" at front desk - less than helpful.
2. Maid opens the door to our room at 930am on a Sunday without knocking. Acts like my wife and I are incoveniencing her, cuz she can't clean the room according to her schedule.
3. Am told that there is breakfast included. Went downstairs to eat the garbage breakfast buffet instead of having a respectable NY brunch, since it was free -- of course then told to pay for said dumpster food. At check-out, told by "Sam" at front desk breakfast charge would be removed from bill. "Mike" the asst. gmÂ  and "Marshall" the food and beverage mgr disagree. - I guess they thought i was lying to score a free meal at the doubletree.
4. Only 3 elevators on a 44 floor building hotel? You can do the math on that one. Its like they are trying to upset people.
5. Then waited 20mins for my car to be pulled out of the garage. (in fairness, parking garage is not operated by hotel, but that's where you have to park, and its also horrible.)
Conclusion: Lesson learned re: priceline -- just spend the extra $100 and avoid the dumps like this one altogether
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel New York City-Financial District

review_text: Stayed 2 nights in July in this hotel. Firstly the room was not clean the bedding was dirty and had hair in it-that wasn't ours. The air conditioning roared all night I appreciate that all ac units make a noise but this was like a low flying plane. The staff are false and not interested in helping- the concierge look at you like you are something he trod in and grumbled about people using the 'free' wifi-it's only free in the lobby. The only staff who were friendly and helpful were the doormen who were able to tell me where to eat and which subway to get after the concierge was too busy chatting to the reception staff. I'd promote them any day!
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel New York City-Financial District

review_title: Typical friendly Marriott welcome, hotel well located and appointed.
review_text:
Marriott people do seem to try that bit harder and this hotel was no different.
Facilities correct , nothing special. Locality quite mixed ,as near Grand Central Station . Views on Chrysler building spectacular,at night.

stayed here for our first trip to NY, compared to the other hotels within NY, very reasonably priced. Stay very friendly. Room very clean and snug! But everything you need as didnt spend much time back at the room. Few mins walk from bronze raging bull, Battery park, which is where the boats leave for Liberty and Ellis Island trips. Hotel also near the
 metro. Near to Wall street (which has a tiffany's half way along) and Trinity Church. Only a 10 min walk from World trade centre site. Great american breakfast in georges, which is rector/greenwich street. Yummy. Loads of starbucks so if your a coffee addict, then yr in heaven. Would stay again at the hotel. When you check in you get a free warm cookie which was lovely.
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel New York City-Financial District

review_title: Perfect location, clean, tidy and helpful staff
review_text:
Had an excellent week stay at Hotel Belleclaire. Room (Deluxe Queen) was perfect size for the two of us. Recently renovated and very clean. 
Only comment is the one extremely small elevator! Made for some interesting conversations though! :)

review_title: Great budget hotel in the Upper West Side.
review_text: Charming hotel in a lovely neighborhood. Friendly staff, helpful concierge service, and extremely convenient location. One block from the subway, and cab service within minutes. Central park, The Museum of Natural History, Zabar's Market, and the iconic Big Nicks Diner just around the corner. We will be back!

The location is outstanding as is the service from everyone in the place. If you believe there are 200 better hotels in NYC I'll sell you some resort land in Florida. The wireless internet is spotty but everything else was perfect

The rooms were clean and beds were comfy. Bathrooms were nice as well. Not an overly fancy hotel but if you are looking for a great location and a clean place this is great. Elevators are slow on lower level floors.

My only complaint is that the elevator was slow--otherwise loved the decor. Was pleased with the clean modern room and the front desk staff were courteous and gave us an upgrade for no apparent reason. We will return!

review_title: Clean, above average, hotel in a great location
review_text: The rooms were clean, the location was perfect but this hotel didn't "wow" me. I can't say exactly how good the service was because I never really came across any workers. I noticed all the security workers seem to congregate in the lobby each time I returned from an outing. I guess the one thing that does stick out, is that I was never once greeted with a "hello" by any of the Marriott staff. Other than that, our room was comfortable and met an above avg expectation. The room was nice and clean too!

review_title: Close to subway 1 in safe part of new york
review_text: The hotel is clean, has smaller rooms, small fitness center, and kind workers answer any question. 5 minute or less walk to the subway.
We stay at this hotel for a week we had only one thing bad to say is that the safe in the room didn't work so we had tk lock all passport in are suitcases

review_title: Clean, comfortable, AFFORDABLE rooms in NYC
review_text: I visited NYC for the first time in July with my daughter and a friend. We reserved a deluxe room with two double beds. When we arrived, the room we reserved was not available. We were given two seperate rooms with queen beds for the same price. Although the rooms were very small, they were clean and comfortable and a perfect place to rest and sleep after sight-seeing. The staff at the hotel were warm and friendly and very helpful. My initial decision to stay here was affordability. The rooms are about half the cost of most hotels in NYC. Now, even if I could afford a more expensive room, I would choose to stay here!!!

Spent Christmas here; Soho Grand has a unique 'NewYorkish' aura around it, room size included. The staff is very professional and friendly, keeping you company even when you go outside for a smoke (thanks, Jose!). I would recommend it to anyone who can value location & feel, versus name and brag rights. A very good launch-pad to Big Apple.

I have been to Manhattan several times and stayed in a variety of places, but Belleclaire has been my favourite!
We settled on the Belleclaire because it seemed a lovely hotel with great value prices! It delivered!
On the upper westside we had lovely shops, a short walk to central park and two minutes to the subway, everything about this place was great 
Inside was amazing, the most helpful and friendliest staff and truely welcoming rooms! Clean, stylish and comfortable!
I know where I will stay on my next visit!

You know you're in SoHo when you pull up to a hotel that's discreetly marked and you are greeted by a handsome young man dressed in business casual, all black attire...across the street from a bodega.
The SoHo Grand is decorated with the urban chic-meets converted industrial loft style that New Yorkers have been overpaying for since the 80's. The room looked great but had a few notable drawbacks: the bed was hard, the water pressure in the shower also. I also noticed the sink dripping and found the TV far more complicated than a TV in a hotel room should be. To the hotel's credit, I did not report these problems--the visit was short and in true NY style there just wasn't time.
Pleasant surprises: each floor has a common area with ice machine, magazines and a FilterFresh coffee maker. Smart alternative to in-room coffee. And the doormen are friendly and helpful in a way one would expect from a luxury hotel. And if you want to shop SoHo, you will not find a better location.
Clean, well priced, friendly and helpful staff. The whole family enjoyed our stay. We would recommend to friends and definitely stay here again.

For how much I spent on my suite - the hotel was a good value. The rooms were very clean and despite what I'd heard on some of the reviews, our room was very quite (we were in a corner, so maybe that made a difference). We arrived to the hotel a few hours early, and they let us check in without a problem, which was very nice. The free filtered bottle water and the refrigerator and microwave in our room were very much appreciated. However, I'd booked my room for four people and they only gave us three towels. When we called down for more, we received a little bit of attitude about it! We stayed over a weekend, and I'm not sure if it was temporary construction or a normal weekend thing, but a lot of the subways weren't running and we had a bit of a hard time getting around. The hotel felt kind of out of the way for what we wanted to do, next time that I come to the city, I will try to stay closer to midtown. The bed was kind of uncomfortable, I had trouble sleeping on it the first night. The TV had a very limited amount of channels, and the one in the bedroom we had to watch without volume because it was really fuzzy. Also, I was charged a $90 security deposit to my bank account, which was returned to me in full after I checked out, however, nobody told me that I wasn't going to have that charge on my account which felt kind of sneaky to me.

review_title: Hip and comfy, a rare combo
review_text:
I stayed at the Soho Grand for a week and loved it. The atmosphere was exactly what you'd want from Soho with a stunning lounge/bar, great food and good drinks. Upstairs the room was biggish for NY, comfy and well appointed for a stay that long. 
My one niggle was that the lobby was such ad estimation it could've hard to get a seat as a guest but I hope to be back.

review_title: Great value, good location, helpful staff.
review_text: We had a Family suite for four of us, two adults in one section with a king size and two kids sharing a large sofa bed. Great room. Air con noisy but it was 36c outside. The staff very helpful. Coffee in the foyer. Plenty of places to get breakfast. Easy walk to Central Park. 5 mins stroll to Metro. We loved this hotel

If you want to be in the soho area, this is a great option. The rooms are very nice and small. I don't reccomend eating there because it's not fantastic food and the prices are high, but it's soho! there are many options for food! The hotel often has good deals so try to get one ;) over all it's a good and cool place.

This is the only hotel I know in New York. The rooms where OK, location close to the subway, walking distance from Central Park.
I had booked a room for 4 but when checking in there were no more left but the staff after asking if it was ok gave me 2 rooms for the same price.
Overall good experience, but I might try to find something more budget friendly in New York next time (if possible at all).

The staff was great, super friendly and helpful. The location is superb. Close to the metro, close to parks, museums, restaurants, supermarket... Just great location. The hotel is ooold, so rooms show it, even with the new renovation, our bathroom was especially old looking and a bit dingy, but nothing major.

review_title: Not bad, but definitely not 3 1/2 star
review_text: Good location and clean. Staff typical for NYC (rude and in love with themselves). Good deal, but no way is this a 3 1/2 star hotel... time for Priceline to reconsider.

review_title: Service was a 10. It's an older hotel. If you know that going in then you will love the place. Those who are older think of the
review_text: When I arrived 3 things were not working in my room. I talked to the front desk and the head of repairs and within 2 hours EVERYTHING was fixed or new. The service was OUTSTANDING!!! if you want Times Square area it's a fast 4 minute subway ride. Walking to Lincoln Center. One minute walking to the Beacon theatre. I would stay at the Belleclaire again!!!

I stayed here over labor day weekend and got a good rate. I was in town for a wedding and most of the events were nearby, so it was convenient. Overall this is a fine choice. The decor is definitely dated- from the '90s and there was obvious wear in places. The rooms, as others have noted, was small. There were some stains on the carpet and I was definitely nervous about bed bugs, but didn't see any evidence of them. That said, the bed was very comfortable and the shower had great Water pressure. I also liked that there was free wifi. As far as I'm concerned, all hotels should have this. Public areas of the hotel were nice but again it just feels very '90s. I had a drink at the bar- nice and strong. All staff I met were great. Friendly and accommodating. One weird thing- one enters the hotel on the ground floor and has to go one floor up for reception. There's no sign indicating this and when I arrived there was nobody to direct me. I stood there for 5 minutes before a fellow guest advised me of this. Overall, this is a solid choice. Good not grand, great service, and I think it's due for a facelift.

This was our first time staying overnight in New York City and I'm so glad I picked Club Quarters. The room was immaculately clean and we loved the whole look & vibe, it was super modern. The pillows were the most comfortable I've ever felt and there is a touch screen monitor next to the bed to control your room temp + a flat screen tv. From the moment we walked in until checkout the staff were very friendly. We ate Valentines Day lunch at their rooftop restaurant and it was delicious, very pretty and there was even a view of the water from our table. The only not so perfect part of our experience was the fact that it's directly next to the twin tower construction site so it was a bit noisy in the morning after 9am but since we had to wake up early anyways it didn't bother us. This is a beautiful, comfortable and convenient hotel especially for the price and I'd recomend everyone to give it a try.

review_title: Good location, lots of character, central park so close
review_text: Hotel staff were always very friendly, staff member Crysta put us in room 805, it had a great view of broadway. Close to the subway, either 79th or 72nd street. We loved walking through central park to get to all of the museums and art galleries on the upper eastside. Westside market was in the base of the hotel, very convenient. Only problem were the elevators, one was not working and the one the was, was small and slow. Other than that, great staff, great location and good value.

We stayed 4 nights. They're renovating out front but not a problem entering building. Prompt check-in service. Room is small but normal for NYC. Neighborhood is nice. Rooms are clean. Has fridge and own bathroom, flatscreen TV, iron/ironing board, hairdryer. Shower stall not a bathtub. Full length mirror and some closet space. There was only 1 elevator functioning at the time we were there but we were on the second floor and the wait was longer than taking the stairs. The microwave is at the bottom of the staircase. Internet is free but at times couldn't get on b/c too many hotel guests were online. No public computer for use and if you want boarding passes printed you have to email the info to the concierge (they'll give you the email address) who then prints it. I thought that was a hassle plus I don't need them to have my info so I didn't use that service. Location is about 4 subway stops (10 - 15) from Time Square. Very convenient. Just watch the rates per night as they fluctuate frequently.

Has fridge and own bathroom, flatscreen TV, iron/ironing board, hairdryer. Shower stall not a bathtub. Full length mirror and some closet space.
