review_text: My wife and I stayed here a few days before Christmas for four nights. We are in our late 20's and this was just enough for us. We have stayed in four-five star hotels before and I would say this hotel rates about a 3. We had a couple minor issues that we more or less bit the bullett on and just went with it due to the fact it's NYC and we got a great deal. Going into our trip I had read some horror stories and been a little nervous before getting there but was relieved when we saw the room. The location could not have been any better. Literally 2min walking to the heart of times square and subway stops within a couple blocks to anywhere. It was 15 degrees with the windchill and we were happy the entire time. The lobby staff were receptive to our needs as best they could and were very friendly most of the time. The only issues we had were #1 the thermostat in the room seemed to blow hot air constantly....I quickly figured out setting the thermostat to ON and turning it on 70 would keep the room a little cool at night but the auto function was wayyyyyyyy worse....set it to on and 70. #2 we ended up being on the second floor and I read about the noise close to street level so we downloaded white noise apps on our phones and ran one through the iPhone docking station(turn it on airplane mode or it'll pop off and on) and sat the other on the other side of the bed and used earplugs at night. In four nights we never we're woken up by a car horn or sirens. #3 if your going for the free wi-fi....go elsewhere or live in the lobby. Our room on the second floor managed 1-2 bars intermittently, if any at all, but towards the center of the building and the lobby we had full service. But you're here to take in NYC; not look at Facebook and keep up with the world right?lol. #4 our shower curtain in our stand up shower was too short by about half an inch so when we showered the tiny bathroom flooded due to the curtain passing over the ledge and water running off. I made a complaint and asked for a longer curtain and immediately the front desk staff notified housekeeping to come down via walkie talkie. When we came back I could tell they switched the curtain but it was the same as before. So we took the metal basket in the bathroom and sat it on the ledge at the back of shower for the magnet in the curtain to stick to....rolled a towel up and sat it on the middle of the ledge and that kept the curtain from passing over the ledge. Honestly these were very minor problems that were manageable like i said. If you expect a 4-5 star at the price you're paying.....wake up Alice. If you're wanting to stay some where at a price that real people can afford with just enough ammenities... then stay here and experience NYC. I was was very happy with our stay. If this were any other city I would have been slightly aggrevated with our problems but this is NYC, look at the prices of the hotels surrounding this and realize you can sacrifice a little and gain a lot. Location was excellent, people friendly, and a great price. My wife and I would def stay here again. Had an amazing trip and a good stay. Thank you best western.

review_title: You get what you pay for on Times Square!
review_text:
If you're looking for somewhere cheap to crash in a great, central NY location, this 'no frills' hotel is a good bet.
As two twenty-something girls from England, we were worried by some of the reviews on this site but we were pleased to find the hotel wasn't nearly as bad as described.
The rooms are basic (and on a par with some youth hostels we've previously stayed in) but they were clean and convenient for a four-night stay in a city where there's so much to do, it's a crime to spend any time in your hotel anyway!
Good points:
The location is excellent, steps from Times Square and the 42nd St subway. 
The hotel reception staff were friendly and we were given a free upgrade on our room on arrival.
The rooms are spacious and in our experience were bug free!
The hotel felt secure for two girls travelling on our own.
Bad points:
The bed sheets and towels were threadbare and some had holes in (but were clean).
The hot water in the shower was intermittent.
No soap, shampoo or hairdryer in the room (though reception lent us a hairdryer when we asked for one).
The decor was very old and desperately in need of an update. No bed side lamp, the smoke alarm had fallen off the ceiling and was stored in a cabinet (unsure if it worked!), peeling paint work, a carpet which looked as if it was from the Victorian era, furniture which might have been picked up in a garage sale etc, but it was 
functional.

review_text:
I found the Beekman to be a charming hotel with its art deco style. The furniture fits in with this theme so don't expect modern furniture. The rooms are massive with a kitchen and eating area and plenty of room to sit and relax after long days of exploring New York. The room was clean and the bathroom and towels were spotless and staying here in February when it was still very cold, the room was always lovely and warm. The only minor point I can find with the room was that the sofa bed was a little worn, but this was not an issue as it was still comfortable and no sleep was lost. The staff were very friendly especially the bellman Ayman who always went out of his way to greet us with a smile and warm conversation (thanks Ayman this really did add to our stay). 
I really enjoyed staying here on my first trip to New York and will stay here again on my next trip whenever that might be. I would definitely recommend this hotel to family and friends. Great hotel, great staff, great location with good value for money. Thank you all at the Beekman for making my first stay in New York a good one.
If you plan on staying here make sure you check out the nations cafe across the road which has good food and service and is good value for money. Also make use of the big Apple greeters to show you around you will need to book this in advance before you arrive on their website, this is a free service with fantastic volunteers, the best way to see the city with a New Yorker.

I stayed 4 nights in the Milford plaza from nov 3rd till nov 7th.We booked it mainly for the location I did stay here before and did think it was quite grubby and in desperate need of a renovation.
When we were looking at hotels for our trip I noticed that there were newly renovated rooms so I went ahead and booked it .
I was extremely pleased we did as from check in to check out I wouldn't have one bad comment to say about this hotel .The staff at reception were quick and friendly .When we got to our room I was so surprised the room on the 28th floor was bright and airy 2 big windows with fab views. The room and bathroom were absolutely spotless ,everyday we had plenty of clean towels and clean bed linen .I would definitely recommend this hotel (renovated room)for the service and location and I will definitely book it for myself again .

review_title: Don't listen to all the negative reviews it's not that bad...
review_text: I read many reviews on here before my stay and I was worried about the hotel, especially as this was stay was to celebrate my husbands 40th. Yes the hotel is undergoing a large renovation, and yes the room we were allocated was tired and in need of work, but having been on holiday many times to Europe, I have stayed in much worse hotels! If you are expecting the ritz then don't stay here, well not until the rennovations are finished anyway. Our room was always cleaned and the bed comfy. We were hardly in our room it was just a base for us, and location wise you can't get much better than the Milford. Don't let the bad reviews put you off!

review_text:
I read countless reviews before my stay at hotel Penn 12/28/10-1/2/11. I was scared. 
We stayed here during three shows at Madison Square Garden, which is literally four feet from the hotel, really amazing location, very easy to explore the city and make it back without using any public transit, no need for taxi either. Check in had a long line, about 40 minutes, even at 11pm. There was not enough staff on for the holiday, however our guest agent was funny, friendly, and helpful. Be prepared to pay in full for your stay upon check in. 
Our room had a working refrigerator, very comfy king bed, clean sheets, clean carpets, clean bathroom with a funky old new York feel. The place is a hundred years old and by FAR the cheapest of it's location, it's only rational that the carpet and hallways were a bit outdated. (but VERY clean.). I received mail that was sent before my stay in the mail room with ease from a very friendly and helpful 
man. The housekeepers were sweet and friendly. I left a key at the desk for a visiting friend with no problem, not even having to wait in line. I was able to go to my valet'd car and get some items no problem. Extra pillows were brought within 
30 minutes. Check out was a breeze, the car showed up promptly. 
I'm sure there are some crappy rooms in that huge place but my new years eve with Hotel Penn was an A+++

review_title: Nice place to rest your head.
review_text:
When people say this hotel needs updating, trust me: that is all they mean. The kitchen and bathroom tiles and fixtures are a little worn. Nothing was broken or dirty or in disrepair. The only complaint I had was with the dirty, threadbare ironing board cover. The room was spacious, bright and clean, and the bed was very comfortable. They charge for Internet usage, but you can print your boarding pass with no charge. As everyone has said, the doormen are very friendly and helpful. All in all, it cannot be beat for $125 through Priceline.
I was not crazy about the location, although the 51st & Lexington Metro station is nearby. Many nights after the theater, I simply walked down 45th, then up to the hotel. Greenacre Park nearby is lovely and peaceful, and several restaurants and drugstores are nearby.
I only go on at length because some of these reviews make the Beekman Tower sound like a run-down dump. That is very, very far from the truth.

review_text: My wife and I stayed in one of the new rooms. We have stayed in Manhattan before and are used to small rooms but these are minuscule. The tv didn't work four out of five days, we had to ask for more toilet paper after it ran out in the room, they told us the room had a queen size bed but it was really only a full, and I don't think they ever vacuumed the room once. Our friends stayed in one of the old rooms and they are even worse. Plaster was falling from the ceiling all over the hotel. This place needs more than fresh paint and a new carpet. If you are looking for the cheapest hotel you can find close to Times Square then this is your place. If you are looking for any of the usual comforts and conveniences of a decent hotel, stay somewhere else.

review_text:

The neighborhood is riddled with tourist traps, including the electronics store across the street, although the proximity of theaters and restaurants would be a positive point if the hotel was not such a horrible and dirty place.

I stayed here 6 years ago. And the year after that. This hotel was brilliant. Gorgeous lobby, great security (couldnt use elevators without key card) and the little bar downstairs was great. Loved the jukebox in there. There was lots of elevators so never had to wait too long and once you where in your room it was big, clean and very comfy, just slightly old fashioned. Also liked the gift shop downstairs that did amazing hazlenut coffee The only thing i had to complain about was the long queue to check in and all the static shocks you got when touching lift buttons and things in the room. Would love to stay there again and see what its like now.

review_title: Location excellent, hotel... Not so much
review_text: We booked this hotel through an agent and when reading the reviews on here, it did worry us. But I'm aware from previous experience that some people who put reviews on here do just like to moan and so we decided to give it the benefit of the doubt. The service when we first arrived was reasonable, we didn't have our bags picked up and taken to the room but I did see concierges roaming around so I believe they do it. Our room was on the 15th floor, there are plenty of lifts, no waiting around and they were quick. We were given a free upgrade to a 'deluxe' room as there were no standard doubles free. This was still tiny, dated, shabby but we had a flat screen TV and the beds were clean and comfortable. The air con worked, the shower was tempremental and you either had to shower in boiling water or freezing. Having seen through the doors of the other rooms when being cleaned, we realised that we had actually done quite well with ours so just stayed rather than ask to be moved. Location wise it was great, right on the doorstep of Times Square and Broadway, next door pretty much to a subway. We still had a great time, but this hotel didn't add to that. If you're just looking for somewhere to put your head down then this will suit you but anything else and you're better off going elsewhere.

We stayed at the Milford Plaza for our honeymoon. It fulfilled our needs perfectly. We were looking for something cheap in Times Square. We got a great deal and the location was superb. RIGHT ON TIMES SQUARE!! Yes it is going through renovations but we didn't notice and weren't disturbed at all. I do think once renovations are complete that the price will go up, but right now this hotel offers value in times square and comfortable basic rooms.

review_title: Inexpensive and convenient, but don't expect luxury.
review_text:
I have stayed at the Milford twice, and was very satisfied with the location and price. It is a historic hotel with very small rooms and tiny bathrooms, but boasts an amazing location in the theater district within easy walking distance to TONS of fabulous restaurants and is a block off of Times Square, so it is close, but less crowded. The package included a continental breakfast, which was very good. We noticed that there were quite a few international guests staying in the hotel both times we stayed there. 
I would definitely stay here again, and would recommend it to friends who can appreciate affordability over luxury.

I am so glad I stayed at the Milford Plaza in Times Square. I knew from previous reviews that they are under construction and there would be noise from it at night. I figured it was worth it to be in such a great location for $200 a night. I slept just fine despite the hammering. The shower temp was a little cold. Other than that, the staff was very friendly at check in and at the bell desk. The room was super clean. I spent very little on transportation. It is a great option if ur on a budget and willing to put up with a little noise and be right near Broadway,Times Square and Restaurant Row. It's all right outside the front door of this hotel.Two thumbs up.

The street is quite but within a block of Union Square and all that action..plus several great little bars and eateries within eyesight. The hotel is quaint, yet elegant. The hotel staff friendly and helpful but not chatty or intrusive. It's a very intimate experience being a guest here..much like a B&B, but better.
I would recommend the Inn at Irving Place to any travelers jaded by over hyped hipster joints or large commercial hotels.

review_title: This little hotel has stolen my heart
review_text: If you love intimate, warm, delightful, quirky, deliciously comfortable and being in the middle of everything that is wonderful about NY look no further. If you are looking for elevators, business centers, spas, gyms, concierge desk and everything branded this hotel is not for you. But the flip side is a handful of rooms, Frette linen, breakfast (included) in the famous Lady Mendel Tearoom, free wifi, warm and wonderful staff, a hop to Union Sq and a skip to everywhere else you will love The Inn.

review_text: This place needs a major face lift. They are in process of renovating, but only so much you can do with a property like this. Rooms are small and bathrooms are old, but they keep it clean. Stayed for one night and had a restful sleep. Needed a place near Times Square at last minute so this was best option for the price. It is no frills and worn so not for everyone. Not the kind of place you would pick for an extended stay.

review_title: In the heart of the theater district
review_text: My friends and I booked two rooms for one night at the Milford Plaza on July 22, as we were just in town to see a show on Broadway. The location could not have been better. The theater was literally on the corner! This is a no-frills hotel, but the front desk service was great (they gave us adjoining rooms which made it more like a suite), the room was clean (if a bit old) and the bed was comfortable. Most important, the air conditioning was blasting on the hottest day of the year (115 degree heat index)! No, the best part was the room rate. With the Trip Advisor discount, we stayed in the heart of the theater district for an unheard of price. I will stay there again is the price is right.

If you're willing to look past the raggedy interior, it is in a great location near times square. It will meet your needs if all you need is a spot to drop your bags, sleep and shower while you play tourist all day...but that's it.

review_title: Good value for the location, given the high price of Manhattan rooms
review_text: Stay here if you want to save money on accommodation so that you can go to town on sights, shows and shopping. We could not find a cheaper en suite room in Manhattan with this central location and it was more important for us to be with in walking distance of the city's attractions. However, this is a impersonal hotel with zero customer service (we asked twice for the bath to be unblocked and nobody came by). The whole place is tatty, dated and scruffy and we found dust in our room. Having said that, we slept soundly in a comfy bed and were out each morning before 0900 so we didn't mind the cosmetic shortcomings as much as some travellers might. I'd like to hear from anyone who found a better, cheap en suite in Midtown Manhattan.

I booked this hotel ( superior room) over the internet for my stay in New York during August 2011. After 23 hours of traveling i arrived at the hotel at 1 pm and was not allowed to see the room before 3pm as this was the rules and they were not prepared to make any exception. I requested to see the room as it looked nothing like i imagined or what was advertised. The furniture is old and tacky, only certain channels of the "flat screen" tv worked, the shower was broken, the bath plug was not working, the flushing mechanism of the toilet was broken, the safe was left of the dresser table (not even mounted). When i brought this to the attention of the front office manager i was offered another room for the next day. Honesly, if you want to waste your money on this dump with yello hand painted stars on the roof and walls, be my guest. I eventually checked out the next morning and checked in at the Gem Hotel 300 W22 for $40 a night cheaper, with room service, coffee, tea in the room, clean linen and most of all professional, friendly staff... A full package and far superior than this rat hole. Its nothing what they advertise it to be... Be warned!!!!!!

review_title: Great location, great staff, no kitchen!
review_text:
Chelsea Star was a truly pleasant surprise. The staff are professional and friendly. The rooms are clean and secure- although my bed (top bunk) was a little wobbly. My room had air conditioning and a very clean bathroom. In fact, as far as hostels go, 'clean' would be the best word to describe it- a very important budget travel factor! Free wi-fi, nice deck area with power connections, umbrellas and deck chairs. Guest lounge is tiny- really just a room with a coffee machine, washer and dryer but what more do you need- there's enough to do in NYC without needing the hostel to entertain you! 
The only draw-back is that there's no kitchen, which makes eating a slightly more expensive venture, but if you don't want to go far, there's an incredible deli across the road.

review_title: Read the reviews, then look elsewhere....
review_text:
I travel to NYC approximately 20 weeks a year for work. This was my first stay at the Milford and it will be my last. I'll try keep this brief, but there is a lot to describe:
1. Matress was just worn out. I could feel just about every spring.
2. Wallpaper peeling everywhere.
3. Furniture old, dated, and very worn out. This is stuff I'd expect to see at a tag sale or goodwill. 
4. Carpet, hallways, worn and dated. 
5. Lobby entrance very oddly laid out. 
6. Nonexistent security. 
7. Indifferent, weary staff. I expressed my dissatisfaction to several of them. They all apologized, but really couldnt offer any solution. One flat out told me that the hotel was not the nicest one around and that they wouldn't recommend it to their friends or family. That should tell you all you need to know!
8. WiFi is an additional $14.95 per day and the quality is poor at best. I tethered my laptop to my cell and the Internet connection speed was significantly faster. In NYC, in this day and age, this is an expected amenity for a business traveler, not a luxury. Extremely poor. 
9. Tv is a 19" Zenith circa 1980??? WAY out of date. 
10. AC unit could barely keep the room cool 
11. Bathroom very dated and not clean. In defense of the cleaning staff, it seems as if they try, but like any older porcelain fixtures, these have reached a point where they can no longer be effectively cleaned. Grout lines in the tile are dirty, etc. It looks as if a renovation was tried at one point perhaps, but it was a half hearted job at best. 
12. Paint work is terrible. Door trim has been recently painted perhaps, but they didn't bother to prep any of the surfaces. New paint was simply applied over old layers of peeling paint. 
13. Only 3 outlets in the room. All behind furniture and low to the floor. 
14. Convenience/gift shop in lobby closed at odd times with a be back later sign in the window. I know, I'm in NYC, I could get anything I wanted on the corner. However, sometimes I just want to get a diet coke or cup of coffee without going out in the rain. Also, the clerk couldn't take any cards because the cc printer was out of paper and there were no spares rolls in the store. This condition has been going on for two days. 
15. Coffee. Really? No complimentary coffee? Anywhere? Makes me wonder if the management of this hotel has ever stayed in another hotel ever before?
I'm sure there is something that I missed, but that should paint a good picture for you. Sorry to be so negative, but this is one of the worst hotel experiences I've ever had. I travel for a living. I spend 200 nights a year in hotel rooms. This is hideous. Please stay away until the mgmt here rectifies these issues. Based upon other reviews here, the mgmt will likely respond with a canned letter below. I really don't expect anything else. 
For the record, my dates of stay were 6/9/11 to 6/12/11 in room 1630. My observations are based upon what I experienced in this room, but other guests expressed similar dissatisfaction with their stay.

We arrived late 1030pm after a very long tiring journey. 1st impressions were large impersonal hotel. Typical of a major city. Check in was fairly quick, And we went up to our room to drop bags off and go get a bite to eat....
The room was fairly small and a little disappointing. We kept hearing a swooshing noise every 2 seconds. We then realised we were backing on to the 4 lifts! I decided to phone reception to see if we could change. They said yes but not till morning. We decided to put our personal belongings in the safe. Ie money passports etc. It was broke, so I phoned down again and was told they would send somebody up. When he arrived, he immediately told me that this safe was broke, and to phone down to change rooms. I did as he said and was told that there was no king bed but we could have a double. Fine! We gathered up all our bags and 2 large cases. We were then given the key to another room. Soon as we walked in we were hit with a strong smell of urine. The furnishings were very old and tatty. The lampshades had stains on them. I phoned again and was told to get another key. I was not too happy by this stage. Carting bags up and down long corridors and up and down floors was really annoying! Our next room once again had no working safe. The man came up again and told us that it didnt work in that room!!!! I was furious by now and went down to reception. When we got to the desk the receptionist said shall I get you the manager before I had even opened my mouth. 
He was a very quiet, unapologetic man. He gave us another key and off we set, bags and all! My husband tried the card in the door, it wouldn't open? After 2 or three attempts a women opened the door to ask us what we were doing? We had disturbed them in bed! 
As you can imagine I was now ready to blow. When we got there we asked to see him. " is there a problem" he said. We told him somebody was already in the room! All he said was " oh somebody must have forgot to book it out" and proceeded to phone the room up and check all her details, leaving us still with out a room!
I told him it was not fair that we had originally booked in 1 and a half hours earlier and were still waiting. He never even apologised.
 Our last room was ok, nothing special maybe a 3 star at a push. Knobs missing off drawers, not particularly clean and a bit dated, but the safe was new! 
It was now too late to go out so we decided to have a drink and go to bed. First we had to phone and request tea making facilities, as there wasn't any in there. My husband then went to get ice. Every floor had ice making. He went from the 11th to the 2nd to find a machine that worked! It seems that this hotel is very much lacking in maintanence, and customer service. We have stayed all over the world and never come across such couldn't care less attitude. 
On a good note, the hotel is very well situated and we did only sleep there. The bed was comfortable and with earplugs we slept ok.

review_title: This hotel is a scam! Do not stay here!
review_text:
Upon our arrival, an irate woman was at the front desk complaining about her reservation the hotel would not honor, which was booked through a third party company. This woman was with her young daughter very late at night. The front desk staff were not helpful, rude and inflexible. It was shocking that there was no manager on duty the week of new years in a times square hotel. They bullied the woman into booking a room for full price, regardless of the price she booked b/c they could not find her reservation in he system b/c she only booked it an hour ago. 
Fearful this would happen to us, it certainly did and to 5 people total that night. Our experience was shady at the least and an unsuccessful scam attempt because we watched and listened to every move. Our front desk attendant, Natalie Garcia, was the epitome of poor customer service at the mercy of her management to scam customers into paying full price for a room. 
We booked through booking.com. Natalie said they couldn't find the reservation in the system. About 30 minutes later, it appeared but the dates they had were incorrect ( one night off). I confirmed the correct dates shown in my Droid email confirmation. That should have stopped right here and we should have checked into our room. Then we had to wait while they called booking.com to discuss. Booking.com wanted to fax a correction but THE FAX WAS BROKEN! Booking.com then offered to email the new reservation to the hotel email. Natalie then provided her personal gmail account to receive the email. When questioned she didn't see anything wrong with this. she was aslo going to take another customers information home to fax to England bc the fax was broken! Are you kidding me! Natalie never did check her personal email and I started to smell identity theft. Natalie then offered us a "quoted" room for the original discounted price per her managers approval who was now taking calls at home. However we still had to deal with booking.com to cancel our original reservation. We declined thus quote and called booking.com and they told us the front desk needed to give an ok to cancel the reservation! We then dis ANOTHER go around of them now not being able to find us in the system when we were just up on the screen and they could not reference anything to give the ok to he woman on the phone. After pushing the new staff attendant, Chris, he miraculously found us in the system to cancel the reservation. 
What a nightmare! It's was like they were trained to use 3rd party reservations to scam for a full price hotel, not to mention Natalie who was sending info to her personal email....identity theft?

review_title: Great hotel for NYC visitors on a budget
review_text:
This hotel is a hidden gem in my opinion. Ok, the rooms are small and basic, BUT people need to realise that you get what you pay for. If you plan to spend that much time in your hotel room whilst in NYC, why bother going!? The rooms and facilities were clean, staff were very helpful and location superb. If you want an affordable hotel in Manhattan that isn't amongst the crazy pace of life in areas such as Times Square etc,this is the one to go for.Â 
You will get most benefit from this hotel if you are prepared to make use of the subway. $29 gets you a 7-day unlimited metrocard and the 72nd St stop (C or B line) is hardly any distance from the hotel at all. Download the free subway app onto your iPhone and you're laughing.
The free breakfast is a superb bonus, though we found that we started noticing how 'beige' all the food was after having eaten it for a week. Healthier options are available in the way of fruit, yogurt, wholemeal bread and cereal... but you WILL find yourself indulging in the waffle making machine and muffins at least once during your time there!
Only one negative would be the walls in our room (not sure if it applies to all the rooms but ours was like this). It appears that when the hotel put in the air-conditioning systems (as an afterthought it would seem) they didn't seal the gaps up and as such we could feel a draft coming from the wall! In fact we could see several small holes around the aircon unit where it hadn't been filled! A quirky feature but it didn't bother us that much, especially as the mercury didn't rise that much while we were there.
This wouldn't make us hesitate recommending the hotel to our friends.

review_text:

The staff were lovely and really helpful, we checked in easily and our bags were brought to our rooms. 
I was a little disappointed with the rooms, on the website they look great but in reality they are tiny and our bathroom was dingy with paint peeling from the Walls in various places. However it was clean and the shower was great! 
The main things that annoyed me about this hotel were: 
The lift to the rooms took absolutely ages to reach us, we were waiting almost ten minutes for it. 
And also our key cards never worked! Even the guy bringing our luggage had trouble with his key in our lock. We had to get them replaced twice at reception and it only worked the second time because we jiggled it around in the slot for a few minutes. 
I was also surprised that given it's in NYC, this hotel had no free wifi in rooms. It was free in the lobby but I had to pay $10 to access it in my room. 
Overall this hotel has a perfect location but I do not think I would stay here again.

We stayed at Holiday Inn SoHo from 9/30-10/4. We landed at 10pmÂ at LGA and took a taxi to the hotel ($26 plus tip). Check in was very quick and easy.Â 
Our room was on the 4th floor and we got what we reserved-- standard double room. It was small, modern and updated. The HI website had outdated pics. We were pleasantly surprised! The bathroom had very nice granite counters Â The shower had nice water pressure and the shower head was removable and you could change the height too. They also provided Bath and Body Works shampoo, lotion and bar soap. Overall, we were very pleased with this hotel and would definitely stay here again.Â 
The location was excellent. We were just around the corner from the Canal St./Lafayette or Canal St./Broadway stations. We took the Subway everywhere (7-Day Metrocard was well worth it, even though we only got 4 days use from it). We also walked to the Soho shops, Little Italy and Chinatown. All very close. There are also little gift shops down the steet from the hotel. We preferred the ones closer to Chinatown/Little Italy, where we could haggle/bargain. :) Even my 13 y/o sister was getting good at it. :)
All of the staff members we talked to were very nice. We mainly interacted with the bellman staff. The main entrance takes you by their stand and to elevators and the front desk is a short ride up the escalator, on the second floor. We didn't eat at the restaurant or order room service. One thing we would have liked to see --indoor pool or hot tub, but no biggie. We did utilize the luggage hold area. We checked out at 10am and our flight wasn't until 8pm. The bellman put our luggage in the locked storage area just behind the bellman counter. He gave us a claim ticket and we were off to explore more of the city without luggage in tow. We came back around 4pm and picked up our luggage.
Overall, the hotel was great. The location was perfect. Service and cleanliness were excellent. Would definitely stay here again!

Bedford hotel hints at a former grandeur that has slowly faded like it's decor, couch stains ruining presentation, needs update. As most new york hotels go the space is small but adequate. Service was good. Price reasonable for the location it provides, 2blocks from grand central station, 10 blocks from empire state bldg, 14 blocks from time square.

Finding an affordable hotel {that isn't roach infested} is not an easy feat. Holiday Inn popped up on Hotwire and was cheaper than a friend's employee discount at Starwood Resorts. Location is great, rooms are remodeled and clean but of course they are small. That is my only complaint.

I could have upgraded to a motel 6! 4 stars-really! No bell desk, no late check out. Crazy blaring music until 3am. SLOW/NO bar service. View of nothing. At least they were rude to round out the scuzzy gross room experience. Recommend, not no, hell no.
For sure not a 4 atara hotel. Good location, but terrible service, and in front of the hotel had an alert of bugs and rats in the hotel. Rooms without a temperature control.

review_text: Holiday Inn Soho is really close to little Italy, china town and of course soho which makes it convenient to pretty much shop for low end stuff high end stuff and eat good stuff!! On the downside of this hotel is the upgrades so desperately needed. The room was less than average with no space for much. The windows are filthy and the bathroom is need of a scrub down. The amenities ... Well there aren't many ... I didnt even find soap nevermind toothpaste in the bathroom. If it's for a one night stay and don't have any options stay here as long it's for sleep. Oh and by the way you'll be paying for less than 24 hours when you stay here they don't allow you to check in until 3 pm so if your flight comes in early and you want to take a nap think of something else cause they will make you wait in the lobby!

review_title: Great Hotel, but the staff is even better!
review_text:
I just returned from a two night stay at the Time Hotel, and it couldn't have gone any better. 
I arrived at the hotel around 12pm on a Tuesday, the doorman greeted me at the curb, assisted me with my luggage and escorted me to the Front Desk. On the way he spoke about the restaurant, introduced me to the GM (who was exiting the building) and the Front Desk Manager who checked me in. 
Upon check in, I was given a complimentary upgrade into a suite and a late check out at no cost. The manager described the hotel and amenities it had to offer including a $10 wifi fee. I stated i was use to free wifi and without hesitiation he comped the two day charge! You could tell he was a charmer! 
I was escorted to the room by Gilbert, and on the way he introduced me to the concierge, the housekeeper on the floor, and housekeeping manager in passing. I felt right at home.
The room was clean, modern and big for NYC standards. Turndown service at night, and a complimentary NY Times in the morning. 
Check out was quick and easy. Gilbert assisted me from the room, Charlie was there to check me out and Ed hailed a can like a pro.
Great job Time Hotel! You have won me over, this is my new hotel of choice!

My brother and I stayed at "The TIme" last night and I have never felt more compelled to share my experience. We are both in the music business, so we have stayed almost everywhere in New York and this trendy, low-key, hot-spot, is hands down the place to stay! Upon arrival we where greeted by an extremely well spoken doorman who led us through the impressive High-design entrance into an all glass elevator that brought us up to the lobby. The front desk attendant Andre, or Andrewi think than quickly checked us in while providing us with a play by play of all of the hotels many amenities.Â  I couldn't believe the level of professional as well as the suave ambiance projected by the hotels staff. They moved quickly and efficiently, without forgoing service. Something most hotels in the heart of times square are incapable of achieving. The time it took us to get in the hotel, check in, and get to our room couldn't have been more than 10 mins which is quite the feat and something a person like myself who is constantly on the road appreciates. The professionalism and competence of the employees with out a doubt stems from the hotels hip gm, Kanvar Singh. I have never had the gm of a hotel actually make himself known, let along approach me and introduce himself, offering his personal knowledge of the property and the surrounding area. The room was perfect size, we had two full size beds, a fully stocked mini-bar with drinks and snacks, and a flat screen high-deff TV! Again, for a hotel in times square I was expecting to be one of countless guests without any personal attention and the time completely blew that expectation away. I cant recommended this hotel enough. If you are traveling to the city for any reason and want a hip, stylish, personally accompanying stay than this is the spotfoRbear guys are killing it, and if you don't wanna feel like another abused tourist in times square, than this is your sanctuary on west 49th! street!

review_title: If you are only interested in location, then this could be the place for you!
review_text: The hotel has a nice enough lobby. The lounge and restaurant are very trendy. The service is lacking. There was no help with bags to our room. Hallways are dark, elevators are tiny, and the rooms are not clean. In this place, it looks fine at first glance, but then you notice the towel rack looks dirty and the edges of furniture pieces are torn off. I liked how the music was playing in the room when we entered, but that was the only thing I liked. The bill for one night was $419. If we had not arrived at 7:30, with an important dinner reservation that we had to make, I would have left and spent more for a nicer hotel. They need to get better furniture, wipe down and clean everything, and improve service.

Dirty. I know it's NYC, but for $229/night--such a rip off!!!! It's in Chinatown, not Soho. 
Rooms are gross- filthy carpet that needs replacement, dirty walls (I don't even know what that is on the wall) with wallpaper that's peeling. Bedding worn and falling apart, and one bed had little hairs in it. GROSS. Room is small but that's expected in NYC. I don't want to lay in bed much less sit on it and forget about going barefoot on this carpet. Sooo gross!!!! Such an expensive ripoff!!!

Great location and value for money but you get what you pay for....a very old out of date hotel with old bedrooms and everything else that goes with it. The hotel is one of the cheapest to stay in in new York...under Â£100 a night and we had a massive room on 10th floor. Its all you need for a city break when u are out all day exploring the great city.

review_title: Location to value can NOT be beat.
review_text:
Location can't be beat, service top notch, decor a little dated, 1br suite is spaceous and decent price, deal with parking for $23.00 24 hr/overnight was a pleasant surprise.
The price and location trump the minor flaws the space displayed. I came to walk around all day and night and travel on a budget, not sit in the room all day anyways. If this is your criteria as well this place can't be beat.

While the hotel isn't as swanky as some others in the area it is close to public transportation, reasonably priced and a comfortable place to rest after a day of playing tourist in NY.
Just beware the WiFi. The hotel doesn't have it ( or so they said) but there are "Bedford" hotspots. They may be counterfeits, so be careful.

Great hotel! The place is great And also especially the service!! Everybody here is so kind an is always willing to find another option if one isn't possible. Also I wanted to say many thanks to Kenneth, so overall this hotel is great and I would stay here another time also if I have to compare it with other hotels in New York (been here two times earlier).

review_title: A suprising hotel in a great location
review_text:
This was my second visit to New York and decided to stay a little further away from times square. The hotel is set a block from grand central and park ave so close to all transport.
I stayed in a suite on the 7th floor and even had a partial view of tje empire state building, which at night, was beautifully lit up. The room consisted of a small kitchenette, large bedroom, plus walk in wardrobe, and cupboard with safe. The main living room had 2 arm chairs, and sofa bed which was comfy enough to sleep on and always made up every day. The bathroom was clean and had a constant supply of towels, soap etc. It wasnt noisy at night at all. 
The staff were all friendly and helpful, reccomending resteraunts, and easiest routes to get to places.
All in all, a great hotel, with no complaints.

Before staying at The Manhattan at Times Square I was abit worried about the reviews about cleanliness and bed bugs but when we got there we were really surprised how great it was!! We had no bed bug problems at all and the rooms were clean and homely! The staff were really friendly and helpful and not to mention the great location!!! NYC is cold in December and it was so nice to come back to a nice cosy hotel room!!! The rooms are a little dated but this really didnt put us off the only one thing is the Walls are abit so you can hear everything happening in the next door rooms but please do not be put off by any bad reviews as we absolutely loved out stay here and NYC is amazing and we will definitely be returning to The Manhattan at Times Square!!!! X
hotel_name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel

review_text: Stayed here three nights and I was apalled with the service I was getting. I read the reviews and thought hey it's a Starwood property how bad can it be. It wasn't that bad until my last night. When I called for a wake up call I was waiting on the phone for a good three minutes and I guessed they were busy so hung up and tried again ten minutes later. When I called again I was greeted with a rude voice, when asking for a wake up call she rushed me and then hung up on me. When I come to new York I will never stay here again.
hotel_name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel

review_text: Stayed there one night and could not go to sleep! They put me next to the service elevator room 2128... They should not rent this room, worse noise than NYC traffic all night! They sent up a tech. After complaining and he said "oh well" you can't help machinery noise. Thank god used price line,,,,,this hotel is a 1/2 star!
hotel_name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel

review_text: We only stay for the weekend icame from london to new York With my mum it's a very good location if your two girls on yur own and you go out at night and don't want to get the subway home. Very close to time square which is always handy and very close to bordway. Staff were friendly and helpful rooms were a bit small but we didn't mind as it was only 3 days I would stay here again only for location bit to much for 4/5 star hotel as it doesn't exceed expectation. There a Italian restaurant next door don't go there it over price for such little food. Apart from that great trip.
Had an awesome stay last week. Service was excellent!

review_title: Great location. Could do with more facilities.
review_text:
Stayed for 6 nights end of Nov/early Dec.
The location is superb. Right off Times Sq and 5 min walk to Rockefeller Centre.
The rooms are comfortable and good size. We did get awoken by noisey guests in the early hours several nights.
It's a shame there is no bar, restaurant or coffee area. There's a good Internet / computer access area, but the hotel really misses out on the non availability of food and drink. Surprisingly they do have a breakfast restaurant (pricey!) but this area is not available for other times.
Overall, we did enjoy our stay at the hotel.
hotel_name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel

review_title: Great location, basic amenities (eg no in-room Wi-fi, No room service). Wait till it has been properly "Sheratonised"
review_text:
I had been wanting to try this for a while, since it joined the Starwood Group. 
It is a great location, but expensive for a totally 'no-frills' hotel: basic, but adequate rooms (bigger than the neighbouring Sheraton and Towers), no charm or style, no room service, patchy Wi-fi only in the lobby, need t go round the corner for the Coffee Shop (the local Deli).
Despite these negatives, after a busy work week, it started to grow on me - a bit of a facelift and a facility or two, and this has good potential.
hotel_name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel

review_title: Great hotel for young couples and groups
review_text:
My partner and I stayed at the Hudson hotel between Xmas and new year. Upon arrival we were greeted with a friendly warm welcome at reception by a top guy James. 
If you do your research before hand you know the rooms are going to be on the small side..... But that's to be expected for a good location in the city. I've stayed in smaller in Mayfair, London. Our room was clean and decorated in cool decor. There is room for you to store stuff and move around. My only downside would be if you keep the curtains drawn the room can be a little dark for getting ready. The bed was extremely comfy and you get a dovet which many other hotels don't offer. Location was brilliant- opposite central park, the subway is 2 minutes away and time square is only a 5 min walk. The best part of this hotel for young people in the cool and funky Hudson bar. It has a neon floor, plays good music and offers an array of drinks at a reasonable price ( remember this is ny so $25 for 2 drinks is acceptable)
I would recommend the Hudson to any of my friends visiting ny who want a clean hotel, good location and nightlife at their doorstep.
If you're unsure about booking this hotel visit the Morgan hotels website and it provides details of room sizes. 
You won't be disappointed. Hudson hotel and staff thank you for your part in making our visit to ny so enjoyable

review_title: An awesome hotel in every aspect
review_text: I can not say enough good things about our stay here. First, the location was amazing; 1 block from central park and a 10 min walk to times square/rockefeller center. The staff was so friendly and helpful and the hotel is gorgeous! Spend the extra money and get a room other than the standard. That room is way too small so we upgraded and was well worth it. Seriously, this was my first trip to NYC and the folks at the Hudson helped make it the best trip. If you want to save money on food there is a whole foods across the street that has great prepared foods

Besides being given a room that backed up to the elevator bank so that we constantly heard the up & down of the cables, the room was small & bathroom was one of the smallest we've experienced in a hotel. We won't be back.
hotel_name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel

review_text: Definately not what I expected for a Starwood property. Location is great but hotel is dated, expensive, and employees not very customer focused. Would not stay here again.
hotel_name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel

review_text: Zimmer sind sehr klein, aber sonst ok. Wir hatten zum GlÃ¼ck keine Bettwanzen. Es gibt fÃ¼r 14 Stockwerke 1 Lift, so muss man manchmal etwas Geduld haben. Der Fitnessraum besteht aus zwei KonditionsgerÃ¤ten. FrÃ¼hstÃ¼ck war gut, leider gibt es nur 24 PlÃ¤tze, was manchmal zu Stau fÃ¼hrt. review_title: Really friendly and helpful staff conseirge very useful overall pretty nice place to stay
review_text:
After reading some of the reviews of this place I felt very apprehensive after booking to stay for four nights. However upon arrival the security staff at the door took our bags to the bellman who took them to our room while we checked in. A good start we thought. Checking in was nice and simple although they wanted to take a $100 a night deposit and a credit card, tell them you have neither if you don't want to pay this as we did, they weren't too bothered, just means you can't charge anything to the room but don't reccomend this as hotel service is normally well overpriced anyway. 
The room on the first night was as expected enough room to fit a double bed and an en-suite and not all lot else, the room was however clean the heating worked the bathroom was newish and the tv had all the channels you could want there was free wifi but don't expect to stream a film only get limited bandwidth. Having said this didn't go to New York to stay in watching tv or a film on my laptop was good to be able to find places and to book things to do (recommend to beat the crowds). 
On the second day we were happily upgraded to a suite which was double in size had a bigger bathroom with a bath and again room was very clean and tidy.
As mentioned earlier the conseirge desk was very helpful and we were able to print out pre booked tickets using iPads they had at the desk they also told us where good places to go were whilst we were looking around.
Can't review the food at the hotel as we never ate at it. There is a bar which on Friday and Saturday nights gets quite busy and if you are on the lower floors can be heard but this wasn't that much of a problem as we were on the 11th floor.
Checking out is at 12 on the day you depart and was easy but as our flight wasn't until 6 the hotel was able to keep our bags in safe storage until we were ready to go to the airport they security guy hailed a cab and loaded our bags.
All in all brilliant hotel undergoing a bit of a makeover hence probably some bad reviews before but seem to have got it together now definitely recommend for a weekend break

Nice hotel in a good location, short walk from times square. If you want to spend alot of time at the hotel when visiting new York this hotel is no good for you as the rooms are stupidly small. Staff are helpful and friendly. The inside is so dark you can hardly see anyone, several Guests tripped over stools because they couldn't see them as it was so dark. We mainly used the hotel as somewhere just to sleep rather than for anything this else as we spent 12-15 hours of the day out exploring and really only came back to sleep. For this purpose te hotel was good. However the rooms were still very small and didn't deserve the price they were charging for them. Overall, if you want somewhere sleek, fashionable with a close proximity to major attractions in new York and you don't mind having a tiny box room then this is the hotel for you. Although there must be thousands of other hotels out there with a similar location but better rooms.

First time in New York and the hotel was tremendous!
Situated on 7th avenue, it's location was perfect. Reception area is big, clean and the staff were extremely helpful and always smiling.
Room was big and spacious, couldn't hear any noise from outside which meant we could sleep easily, bed was comfy too!
Highly recommended!
hotel_name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel

review_title: Start Spreading the News it's a great hotel
review_text: After all the bad reviews on Tripadvisor I must admit I was sceptical. What a great surprise - love the hotel. Best location , great staff and very happy with room and the fantastic rate. Don't listen to all the negative not sure why folk been unhappy , our stay has been fantastic and will be back. Thanks Ginelle and Jerry at reception

review_title: Super cool hotel but rooms too small
review_text: Loved the Hudson bar and the roof terrace. Both super cool. And the location is great too. However, the rooms are ridiculously small, even though we got upgraded to a bigger room on arrival (I'd hate to see the original room !)

First room had loud banging pipes and right next to elavator even though I asked not to be near elavator. After hearing what sounded like a hammer on a pipe every 15 minutes we moved rooms next day. When we got new room it turned out to be a handicapped room. This is the first time ever I wasn't asked first if I wanted handicapped room. Shower was horrible. Would flood entire floor. This place was just gross.
Great location and clean. The rooms seem a little outdated but that did not take away from a great stay at this hotel! We will be back!
hotel_name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel

review_title: The Hudson was a lovely hotel, I'd stay again
review_text: We stayed for 9 days it was our first trip to New York, the Hudson was busy and sometimes waiting for the lift or to be seated for breakfast took a little time but I didn't mind, check in was a breeze she gave me a large room that I'd requested as the box rooms in the pics look awful it didn't have a view but in a city like that being in the room wasn't on my to do list, the bed was comfy, a tad harder than my own but ok, nice decor and lovely bathroom, the shower pressure wasn't great but mine at home is very high so I'm always disappointed with other showers, the food at breakfast was yummy, I had a ham and cheese omelete most days, which my other half was massively pleased about, I tried the chocolate pancakes also, again lovely, watching everything being made was a huge highlight, that and one particularly friendly waitress, she smiled and chatted like she enjoyed her job which I appreciated hugely. The location is great, 5mins walk from times sq 2mins from central park... If I stayed again I'd look for somewhere lower down as we hadn't time to explore lower manhattan but that's my fault not the hotels, we got a great deal as we booked in advance 25% off so the price was great, it was what I expected.. One problem with the safe, it broke and getting someone to come fix it was a pain and took forever but that's my only negative point and perhaps security was very busy at that precise moment you just never know! Overall the staff couldn't have done more for me, it was clean and warm and exactly what we needed, ignore other negative reviews as it reflects on the person they are as well and give the Hudson a chance to show you how nice it is!! P.s the entire hotel was hugely classy and architecturally beautiful, it took my breath away to walk in the first time, go up the elevator and there onwards have the satisfaction and prestige of being it's guest. That and a very good looking doorman, great smile, the rest were all arrogant but this one guy was calm and polite I liked him very much!

review_title: Great and enough for NYC travelers
review_text:
Me and my wife visited the hotel for one night. The hotel located 2 minute walk from Central Park.
The lobby is nice, with interesting design, and the service was kind and nice. The hotel is abit dark, but not as you will feel uncouftable walking there. It's part of the design. 
The room was very clean but small. It's really enough for couple who stay just for traveling in the city and do not stay in the room for working etc. Also, we were on the 18th floor and still heared the noise from the street..
We visited the city for traveling, so for us the hotel was excellent and actually more then expected after reading the reviews.

review_title: Small rooms and room service now removed
review_text:
Here are some of the positives:
- it is in a good location - minutes away from Columbus Circle and Central Park
- cool bar and cool "library" where you can get drinks and chill
Here are some things that are disappointing:
- the rooms are the smallest I have ever witnessed. It feels claustrophobic with two people in a room
- the bathroom is even worse!
- they have decided to stop room service now
- breakfast is daylight robbery!
Some tips:
- if you are staying here, then make sure this is just a place to sleep - make sure you are out most of e time
- I got a load of breakfast items from Whole Foods which is in the basement of the Time Warner Center - for three days stay, I got all I needed from there for less than what you would spend for just 1 breakfast in the hotel 
- if you don't like hotels with little lighting etc, this place is not for you

The hotel has a noisey popular bar on the reception floor which goes until late. Music travels up the floors. We stayed on the street elevation the first night and might as well have put our beds out on the road....single glazed windows throughout do not block out extremely noisey outside so could not sleep. Ended up moving to the 19th floor courtyard side which was better and quiter. Rooms crampt and bath or bed not even standard size. Hotel very dark and dingy throughout. Breakfast pricey, average and poor service.

review_title: Its right where you want to be!
review_text: Always a pleasure staying here. Great location. Can get anywhere in times sq easy.
hotel_name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel

review_text: We booked this trip for a special celebration. Our stay exceeded all our expections. Service was excellent from our check in staff were pleasant, friendly and very helpful.Nothing was a bother to any of the staff. The location is brilliant, very close to Columbus Circle Subway. So easy to get to all the sights from there.I thought our room was very clean, but bathroom on the small size but how long does anyone spend in there ? It was small but useable. Bar area very cool but expensive, but glad we availed of the experience. I would book to stay here again, really made our special stay in New York one to remember, thanks to all the staff @ the Hudson.

I wanted to surprise my wife with a NYC Christmas holiday weekend, 
Looked at different locations and read trip advisor reviews. Some of the reviews go on and on about the noise from the club if you are on a 
 high floor, the street noise if you are at a low floor, small rooms etc. 
People love to complain, this is a very nice boutique hotel very close to central park, Columbus Circle, Lincoln Ctr. Very friendly and helpful
Staff at the front desk. I upgraded my room to a 10th floor overlooking Lincoln ctr, and yes you will hear some noise but people have blown this out of proportion, this is NYC! It is a very active city and at the Empire the location is the best; great lobby, best burger in town at PJ Clarkes...I will be back, I recommend the Empire

review_title: In the middle of everything to do in Manhattan New York.
review_text: Convenient location to all the main attractions. Walking distance to Radio City Music Hall, Rockefeller Center, Central Park, Time Square, Broadway Theater District, The Metropolitan Musuem, and The American Musuem of Natural History. Easy access to transportation to all other New York tourist destinations. Had a spacious room with all the comforts of home. Friendly hotel staff through out the hotel!! Would love to come back!
hotel_name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel

review_title: Cool Design..great location...let down by arrogant service
review_text:
Having just come in from the Delano in Miami. I was keen to try another Morgan's hotel..and I was not disappointed. 
Rolling up to the entrance which has two escalators up to the reception it was certainly a world away from the traditional hotels of New York like The St Regis and The Pierre.
Intial greetings were frosty and there was no one around to carry my bags up and when I eventually checked in my bags took nearly 45 minutes to get to the room.. Was this a indication of what was coming later. 
The penthouse was delightfull with a wonderfull outside terrace and all the designer bits that i expected were there in full affect. The views over lower manhattan was spectacular, and the real fire was a great touch.
The various areas for drinks and dinner were packed with beautiful people of New York, although it was hard to find a space just to find your thoughts and have a chat. waitress service was a non existent in the library bar and we finally went to the Hudson bar and waited ages to get served. Weirdly I was unable to sign for drinks and food to my room and was asked to pay everything straight away which was a hassle. 
Dinner in the Hudson hall was slow and totally over priced. Service is a bit issue, questions went unanswered, food and drinks never arrived and the overall demeanour of the staff was that they could not be bothered. Which was a shame as the food is great and the atmosphere outstanding..
The rest of our stay was marred with non existent service from housekeeping to concierge. 
Although an outstanding location right next to central park and walking distance to some amazing restaurants in the time Warner center
Will return once I hear they have their service and attitude right.
Really nice hotel. Located right by central park and a short walk to times square. Pleaseant staff, lOvely roof top bar. Highly reccomend

review_title: Get rid of those old and harmful mattresses. Video
review_text:
I spent three nights here recently. The place has the potential to be a great hotel for NY standards due to its privilage location, its interesting design and price range, but they ruin it all when they make you sleep on a very old mattress, the kind of mattress people dump in dark alleys.
We complained the same day we arrived but they didn't give us a solution until next day.
I can put up with the lack of space, but the main reason to pay for a room in any hotel is to have some rest. That will never happen with those old mattresses. 
Not all the rooms in this hotel have mattresses like the one you can see in the video I made (link below) but as long as they keep any, guests may be forced to sleep like fakirs, liying on a bed of harmful and noisy wires.
I sincerely hope this video encourages the managers to get rid of the old mattresses.
http://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1LQjL3R3S4Y&feature=youtube_gdata_player

review_title: Beautiful hotel hugely let down by the rooms.
review_text: I stayed at the Hudson for 5 nights, the hotel itself is beautiful, the bars are amazing and the lobby has been decked out wonderfully. The rooms however really let the experience down. Other than the fact that they are tiny, the telly has been positioned so you can't view it properly but I also found a cockroach crawling around which left me feeling very uncomfortable for the rest of my stay.

This is a great hotel. Probably needs a little money put into it but overall great value. Everyone has to have one complaint though, right...one thing I dislike are miniature ironing boards. If you have an upgraded/larger room can't you at least have a full size ironing board? Fast and easy checkin check out which is great after 3 hotels in 6 days.
Dark,dank, not kept up, tiny rooms, needs overhaul, 2 star at best, never return

The hotel location is perfect, behind it were the theatres.. And a walking distnace to the shops and all the attractions in times square, clean rooms but a bit tiny but thats normal for nyc hotels:) the staff were very friendly , their business center wity free internet access is a smart move it was very useful .. Id definetly come back!
hotel_name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel

review_title: Friendly and helpful staff, great location, just ok rooms.
review_text: We had a one stay while in town to see a show and do some shopping. The lobby and the library bar were cool but the room was small and not that comfortable. The staff were great, which would be a reason to return if not for the room.

review_title: Worst hotel stay EVER will never stay here again!!!!
review_text:
Uncomfortably small rooms - no amenities and for $350+ per room this experience was inexcusable and totally unacceptable. Standard room fits only the bed, no room for 2 pieces of luggage so we had to use the very narrow and short hallway for luggage and changing area. No mini fridge or water in room. No bathrobe or slippers. Window from bed into the bathroom - odd - cheap sheer curtains covering window. Bed linens cheap and uncomfortable - down comforter without a duvet, instead covered with a scratchy sheet. A/C unit extremely loud with air blowing onto our faces when in bed. 
Bathroom so small that knees hit wall when sitting on toilet, painted tub with peeling paint, terrible quality towels and space for barely even one person. No q-tips or cotton. 
Hotel hallways are dirty. Room service dirty dishes remain in hallway ALL DAY long. Carpet is tired and hallways are drab. 
After marathon only one bar open because the hotel didnt staff the other bars. Lines were inexcusably long and guests and runners were requesting they open other bars given the high demand. Went up to room and found a note under door saying the hotel was discontinuing room service beginning tomorrow, Monday 11/7 due to lack of demand. This is after this morning learning the hotel would not be offering room service supposedly because of too much demand due to the number of marathon runners staying at the hotel. 
Overpriced miserable experience. Would never stay here again. Oh and when we arrived we waited 20 min to check in - again understaffed. Common theme here all 3 nights 4 days. Do not stay here. There are plenty of similarly priced hotels in Manhattan where you will be happier!

review_title: Can't complain, overall very good stay.
review_text: Stayed at the empire hotel for 1 week over the time of the marathon. We stayed in a superior double double room on the first floor and were more than pleased with the size. Bathroom was fine, and yes the floor did get wet but we were given plenty of clean towels every day. We didn't have to get in contact with reception for any reason so can't comment on this. Location is amazing! So close to everything..Eds chowder house is a must!! Food was amazing! Would definitely return!

tiny rooms, trying to be too cool but not that comfortable. Have had larger rooms on most cruise ships. No sign or address out front so if the door man hadn't greeted me would not have know I was at the hotel. Not sure how they fit a toilet sink and shower/tub in the bathroom. BUT the show pressure was outstanding.

Wen we arrived the room we were given was an express queen which is what the travel agent booked for us, it was extremely small if staying here I'd stay away from them rooms. We upgraded to the junior suit for an additional $100 a night but it was worth it!!! The room was amazing with great views and you couldn't ask for a better location. Nearly everything in walking distance and subway just down the road, central park is right across the street! Staff really polite and friendly. We will be back again sometime in the future! We had a great honeymoon!!!

review_title: Excellent location. Great value especially with SPG Points.
review_text:
Location is excellent. Walking distance to Times Square, but not too close so it's quieter and less crowded on the street. Very good service at the desk and concierge. Had breakfast here daily and waiters/waitresses could not have been nicer. 
Easy walk to the best pizza in Times Square at John's. Also liked Junior's and the Cake Boss Cafe (same place as the Harry Potter exhibit, which I highly recommend if you're a fan). 
Great place if you want to see theatre while you are in town. TKTS and all the theatres are very close. 
Taxi from museum row very reasonable (~$10). Taxi from LaGuardia good too (~$30). 
One tip: Taxi drivers didn't know the hotel name, but they knew the Sheraton at Times Square which is right across the street.
hotel_name: The Manhattan at Times Square Hotel

review_text:
Super small rooms, but that is not unusual for a city. But it was dark, poorly lit, and very worn. Hall carpet is dark grey dingy and worn. The whole place needs an uplift. And I will vouch for reviewer below complaining about smoke...they may claim it is smoke free but I too smelled smoke up and down the hallway. And the room had an ashtray or else it was a creepy soap dish. I can also vouch for the reviewer who complained only 3 out of 7 elevators work. Very annoying and very slow.
I was here by myself for work but would I come back with my wife? No. For $350 per night I think you could do better. Wait till they actually do some of their claimed renovations then try again. This place could be really cute. It's in great location and has a lot of potential. But it needs improvement.

review_title: The best hotel and location in NYC.
review_text:
Of all the hotels I have stayed at in NYC, this one has been the best. The location is amazing. The rooftop bar great. The atmosphere at the hotel puts you in a great mood. 
The room was spacious for NYC, view of Lincoln center was awesome.
 I have stayed at many hotels usually based on price, I got a good deal on my stay. I am returning to NYC in dec. And booked this hotel not based on price, but because it was such a great stay.
The easy access to the rooftop bar was a great way to jumpstart the night too.
Romeo at the front desk was extremely helpful as well.

We were concerned because we've read mixed reviews about this hotel, but we're very glad we took the chance. 
Location is great for Lincoln Center and Central Park. Checked in at 1:00am and had no hassles with the process, in fact they upgraded us without needing to ask. We asked for extra towels and toiletries so that we wouldn't need room service and someone from housekeeping arrived at our room within 10 minutes. Housekeeping came the next day and gave us more toiletries just because we like L'Occitane products and put a magnetic sign on the door so we wouldn't be disturbed. Nice touch since the door hanging signs fall off. 
Very busy high-end nightclub on Weds, Thurs, Fri and Sat but no noise reached our room at all. Rooftop pool is nice and bartender up there is very friendly and helpful. The elevator doesn't go all the way up there so you have to hoof it up several flights of stairs, though.
 I will say that the design of the shower is a broken hip just waiting to happen. It's only partially enclosed and no matter how careful you are, the floor will get flooded so ask for extra bath mats. Hot water is plentiful and water pressure is great.
Bedding was nice and mattress has down-filled topper. Duvet is changed with every guest and bedding is sparkling white.
We had a bizarre experience with a nightclub patron one night, but clearly this isn't commonplace because the hotel management couldn't do enough to make it up to us, but hey - it's New York and weird things sometimes happen. I won't hold it against the hotel, they handled the situation beautifully.

review_text:
We stayed here at the end of a trip from Vegas before flying back to England. We arrived about 11pm - there were bouncers on the door for the rooftop bar but didn't feel threatened or anything. Check in was problem free. I had booked a budget room - it had a double bed without a great deal of space around it but was adequate for our needs and nicely decorated. There was no view - just the back of other buildings, but again I knew this when booking. The air con was noisy - it didn't bother us too much but others may find it annoying - people we spoke to in the hotel asked to be moved. The bathroom was also pretty small. 
The hotel lobby is dimly lit with almost club music playing. It is also where the bar is based. We liked it although it may not be for everyone. 
Unfortunately hurricane Irene hit when we were there. Our flight was cancelled and we needed an extra 5 nights. We initially moved to a bigger room for an upgrade fee as we were going stir crazy! The superior king is lovely - much bigger bed, lots of space and a bigger bathroom. There was also a view of the Lincoln centre - a much better experience.
One thing we were not happy with is that it would cost an extra $100 per night for our original room to stay in the hotel. We couldn't afford it so had to change hotels. Talking to other couples who had also been stranded, it seems that the hotel charged everyone different rates varying from $170 a night to the $300 we were quoted. Some had been upgraded. It was just disappointing to note the inconsistency especially in the circumstances.
Overall the hotel was nice, quite trendy, and in a good location. Central park is a couple of mins away and times square is about 15 min walk. There are endless choices for places to eat no matter what direction you head in.

Being that the hotel is just a five minute hike to Central Park in one direction and a five minute walk to Times Square in the other direction, the hotel is in a great spot. The rooms aren't that clean and the building is rather old. Another downside of this hotel is that the wifi wasn't free. Thankfully I had a smartphone to get the Internet when needed, but wifi is a huge selling point.

review_title: Would not recommend to anyone - stay clear!
review_text:
I stayed at the Empire Hotel last week for one night during a quick trip to NYC to go bridal gown shopping. Since I was hitting the big boutiques and department stores along Madison and Fifth Avenues, it was important for me to be relatively close to that area. I booked the Empire Hotel because it was available last minute (literally, booked the room the day before I arrived) and under $300/night. Now I understand why it was still available the day before. 
There were many issues with my stay at the Empire. I had relatively high expectations given the hotel's popularity with the media, but also because my close friend had chosen the Empire as the hotel of choice for her NYC wedding a few years ago. The room I was given was about the size of a cinder block, and had absolutely no view at all. The window looked straight into another room on the opposite end of the hallway, which was awkward. Needless to say, the drapes remained closed the entire time.
The bathroom is TINY - no bathtub, just a shower stall, which oddly enough, has no door. L'Occitane toiletries were a nice touch, but I would have appreciated more if the bathroom had been clean. I found a few hairs on the sink upon arrival. Gross. 
My fiancÃ© was on a work trip to Chicago at the same time I was in NYC. He tried to call me in my hotel room five times, and four of those times, the front desk of the hotel did not pick up the phone. The other time, they directed him to the wrong room. (Unfortunately, a friend misplaced my iPhone charger, so my cell was turned off to conserve battery.). Incompetence, anyone? 
Lastly, I requested a morning wake up call that went ignored. I received no such call at any point during the morning, and I was frustrated by the hotel staff's negligence of its guests. 
I would never recommend the Empire to a friend (or anyone, really). I will go out of my way to make sure my friends do not stay here - EVER. This was my worst hotel stay in recent memory.

review_title: Friendliest and most accommodating staff in New York.
review_text: My daughter and I just left New York and we are both raving about the Hudson. The ambiance in the lobby and the bar was captivating. Our room was spotless and chic. Having Starbucks and Pinkberry right next door made us both so happy. But most memorable was how accommodating and gracious the staff was to us. From the moment our cab pulled up to the hotel we were treated like long lost friends from the bellhops, the front desk, the manager and even the housekeeping staff were engaging, helpful and friendly. review_title: Great hotel if you can afford the upgrade!
review_text:
I stayed at this hotel at the beginning of July with my girlfriend.
We booked a standard room and were allocated one on the 1st floor. The room was very nice and clean if a little small (which is what we expected) however, looking out of the window all we saw and HEARD was the air conditioning unit. We asked to be moved and were moved to the 7th floor where we could still hear it and were looking out on it. We complained again and were told that all the standard rooms looked out on this area. 
We had no choice but to upgrade our room which cost us $350.
The new room was excellent and money well spent, it was very big and looked out over the Lincoln Centre. 
All this aside the hotel is good and we enjoyed our stay once we had a nicer room. We tended to get used to the good staff on reception and the not so good, so waited until the good staff were working before we asked for anything
All in all I would stay here again and anybody going shouldn't be worried.

The best placed traveller friendly place in NY for those on a budget. Close to central park, quick walk to times square, broadway & 'hop on. hop off' bus just across the road. While the rooms are a little small they are clean, beds soft & service good and your in New York - 7th Ave! Bathroom clean with all ammenities. Access to lift & stairs. Diner downstairs provides a good option for breakfast bit dont go past 'fluffy's' for a great coffee & food at a reasonable price. Will definately stay there again
