review_title: Eccellente rapporto qualitÃ  prezzo in una location eccezionale.
review_text:
Se provaste a comprendere in un cerchio tutte le attrazioni di Midtown a New York (MoMa, Carnegie Hall, Metropolitan, Guggenheim, Museo di Storia Naturale, Central Park, Fifth Avenue, ecc.) probabilmente il centro di questo cerchio coinciderebbe con il Manhattan Club. L'ubicazione di questa multiproprietÃ /albergo Ã¨ sicuramente straordinaria. Certo, ci sono altri hotel nelle vicinanze, ma sono molto piÃ¹ costosi (Mandarin, Essex House, Trump, Plaza, Pierre, ecc.) o sono molto piÃ¹ brutti (cito solo il Wellington, reso famoso dal film Borat). Il Manhattan Club nasce dal taglio di circa 500 camere all'attiguo Hotel Park Central. Le camere, unite due a due, sono diventati mini appartamenti (camera da letto matrimoniale, soggiorno con divano letto matrimoniale, due bagni, angolo cottura) che hanno dato vita una dozzina di anni fa alla prima multiproprietÃ  della cittÃ  di New York. La struttura non ha ristorante, ma dispone di un lounge al 28mo piano dove si puÃ² fare colazione o prendere un the o un drink durante tutta la giornata. Vi Ã¨ inoltre una palestra e un centro business con sale riunioni che si possono affittare. Portiere 24 ore e bravissimi concierge nelle ore 
diurne per dare informazioni o prenotare teatri o ristoranti. Il tutto regge bene l'etÃ . La manutenzione Ã¨ frequente e curata. Gli ascensori, Ã¨ vero, sono sempre occupati, ma recentemente ne sono stati aggiunti altri due. Insomma, sembra di stare un po' a casa, con i vantaggi di un grande albergo, anche se non bisogna aspettarsi lusso sfrenato.

review_title: Excellent stay at the Empire - rooftop bar & pool deck made it!
review_text: A great hotel for a trip to New York - modern, clean & a great location for getting about. Rooftop club (weekends) & pool deck made it perfect for a summer girls NYC trip. Only downside was that the hotel charged $1200 to my credit card as a security deposit on check in & didn't advise me - subsequently mu card got blocked by the bank. An apology from the hotel but no more - I would have expected at least a bottle of wine from the bar as a token gesture. Would stay again in the summer but will definately by asking at check in for clarification on security deposits!

review_title: Won't waste my time looking here for my next NYC trip
review_text:
I reserved a standard queen room on Expedia for $190/night. The website notes that these are queen beds, but our room wasn't even large enough to fit a queen bed. Instead we had a full size bed and a bathroom where you could barely open the door. I've stayed in NYC plenty of times and have never paid so much for such a small space with a view of the interior building furnace. 
The good news is the location is good and staff was friendly. However, this room should have been further discounted because it is about half the size of their normal queen rooms and didn't include a queen bed. Maybe this hotel simply stiffs Expedia travelers. That would be pretty terrible if that is the case. 
I will not stay at this hotel again. There are plenty other places with friendly staff, nice locations and rooms bigger than a closet. 
Good luck.

review_title: Excellent location, good value, but you pay for all the extras
review_text:
I stayed at the hotel for 5 days. From checkin to checkout service was great - reception and bell hops were very helpful and friendly. 
Rooms are clean and fitted with flat screens, but quite drab and outdated in design (looks like the last facelift was in the 70's). The room had a view of the brick wall and very little natural light. Rooms are air conditioned, but the ac is very loud even at it's lowest setting - I asked front desk to have someone take a look it at because I couldn't sleep with the noise - he told me that's just the way they are. I ended up getting earplugs from the pharmacy down the street.
Location in midtown walking distance from central park, times square and 5th ave shopping is unbeatable. There is a subway stop on the same corner and a hop on hop off stop about 100 yards from the door.
I got the room on priceline for $150 / night after taxes - but found out wi-fi was an extra $10/day and breakfast wasn't included in the priceline rate. 
Hotel overall was quite good if a little drab and a reasonable value for money.

Perfect location in Tribeca: the hotel literally sits above a subway stop, which is very convenient to move around NYC. Rooms are rather small but very clean, elevator is v. v. slow...
Highlight of our stay were the two lovely cafes downstairs, we had breakfast there on the first morning and were so pleased with the delicious fresh food that we went back many times for lunch and dinner (or for a sweet crepe :) )

We found a great rate for the Cosmopolitan on Hotwire, and we were pleasantly surprised by the quality of this little hotel in TriBeCa.
Everyone on staff was friendly and eager to help. After we checked in, the front desk manager, Jaime, even called up to our room to make sure that everything was satisfactory.
The room itself was unusual, but fun. The double bed was accessed by climbing a spiral staircase up to a little platform. (If you are over 5'10, watch out, you won't be able to stand up in the loft!) The hotel thoughtfully provided a remote control for the well-functioning, downstairs air conditioner. 
The neighborhood was busy, but not overwhelming. There were two subway stops nearby, and The Village, SoHo, and lower Manhattan were all within reasonable walking distance. 
The only real con was the noisy construction on Chambers St. (Could this be why they sold the room at such a low rate on Hotwire?) Also, the loft may not be for everyone, but the hotel does have other options. 
The Cosmopolitan was a very clean hotel, with a very conscientious staff. We would definitely stay there again, if the rates continue to be within our price range.

review_title: Don't think you're different to those who didn't like this hotel, it's awful
review_text:
My husband and I ignored the reviews and desperately regret it. We figured that we're young and cool and live in London so this sort of place would be fine for us.
The public areas are lovely. The rooms are small but they're fine. However, there's no quiet public area, only lots of loud music and loud people and the rooms are so noisy it is beyond a joke. It's like being in a nightclub. My husband had some really important unexpected work to do and it's just impossible to do anywhere.
But the really serious issue is the amount they pre-authorised on our card. Hundreds and hundreds of dollars more than the room and tax, including a second transaction on day 2 of our stay which they had no right to take, which seriously impeded our ability to have fun in New York. And the staff whenever we needed anything whether it was help with lost property, demands to get our money reimbursed or just a coffee were mostly rude, unhelpful and at one point practically lied and treated us with no respect. 
Do not stay here.
Seriously, stay anywhere other than here.

We stayed in Cosmopolitan for 10 days in april/may. Check in was easy, staff kind and helpfull. Rooms are nice and clean, roomy and comfy. Bathroom is small but you have everything you need. The pipes don't make any noise. After about four/five days the cleaning lady also left in our room an iron and desk which was very kind and thoughtfull. This hotel really helped make our stay in New York beautiful! The only complaint would be the noise from the streets...there is quite a lot of holes between the window and AC so you can hear everything from the streets, so long sleeps in the morning weren't possible. But this didn't bother us much..there is so much to do and see in NYC!!!

Rooms are very small for the price, but location is great. We had a one double bed and private bathroom but overall felt like you were in a closet. There was also no view from the window but it's very clean hotel.
The hotel was comfortable. It could have been a little cleaner. Great Location!

review_title: comfortable and clean, close to subway, and in a trendy but not so exciting area.
review_text: this hotel was very comfortable considering the room was a bit small. plusses - clean, free wifi, subway station at doorstep, trendy area, posh bars/restaurants. minuses - no good cafes/coffee nearby, no good casual dinner options (apart from 'kitchenette'), construction work outside, expensive shops, not such an exciting area if you have not been to NYC before. could improve - need to top up the soap after a couple of days and a full length mirror wouldn't go astray. also, the lift really is very slow!

review_title: Great location for visiting the city.
review_text:
When I first went to check in to this hotel I thought I was going to hate my stay thanks to a mix-up with my reservation and a rude staff member. I reserved a king suite but the reservations rep mistakenly put double at first but cancelled that reservation and sent me a confirmation for the corrected one. However when I went to check in the lady at the front desk said the reservation still had double and of course my phone was dead so I couldn't pull up the confirmation. Thank God for Maria who was working the desk and took over when she sawy frustration with her co-worker, who was insisting I had to take the double. Maria couldn't have been more helpful. She found me a king room, but unfortunately it was on a smoking floor, and the next day no other non smoking kings were available, but Eric, who was at the front desk at the time gave me a credit my bill.
The rooms are small and the shower takes some getting used to, but it's in a great locale. I was able to walk to Central Park, MOMA, the Time Warner Building, Rockefeller Center, the MET, and the stores on 5th Ave. There is a Starbucks and a 24hr pharmacy next door to the hotel. All in all I will be staying here again when I come back to NYC this summer.

This is a great hotel for visiting NYC. We stayed for 8 nights. The room was a nice size, had a wardrobe, desk and flat screen tv. Was very clean. The bathroom was small but had all you needed. The view from the window was great. Looking at the Woolworth building. Staff are nice and helpful when asking questions. Be aware that the hotel is lovely but there is a good bit of street noise. You can't fault the hotel for this as it's NYC. Bins are collected on the street in the middle of the night every night during the week. I slept with earplugs so barely heard a thing. Location is great, nice restaurants and bars nearby. Lovely coffee shop below and a Starbucks. Subway outside the hotel or a short walk to city hall will get you to most places in manhattan. Takes about 10 min to get to midtown by sub. Would stay here again and recommend it to friends.

review_title: Great location, close to subway, food, downtown shopping
review_text: Clean and good location. Nice staff. Pls ask for a room away from theroad. I paid a good bit to stay a night and did not sleeep a wink. The noise from the road was too bad..soundproofing anyone?

Arrived at hotel 8pm long check in line, probably 20 min wait. Looks like all rooms weren't ready and had to check what was available.
Saw reviews prior and expected small room- yes is small but clean and great bath products.
Restaurant is great I ate there several times- it's buffet but dishes are cooked fresh in single serves.
Concierge always helpful but were always so busy had to wait a bit but ok
Location close to central park and can walk to 5th ave, times square, subway nearby also
Would recommend to anyone staying in NY

review_title: No complaints and a great value hotel
review_text: My family just returned from a week in NYC during one of the busiest times of the year. I was a bit nervous booking a 'value' hotel in NYC. But we wewre thrilled with our stay. The staff were extremely helpful. The rooms were spotless, and the staff could be seen cleaning the hotel throughout the day. There is a Starbucks and two cafes practically in the lobby. And our room was ready when we arrived 4 hours early. We could not have been happier. We had read complaints of street noise, but you are in NYC people! We loved hearing the sounds of the city. We could also walk to more restaurants than we could hope to sample and were close to the tour bus stops if you are interested in that.

review_title: Clean hotel across from subway! Great location!
review_text:
Don't usually stay in the city because I live so close, but family was in from all over for a party in TriBeCa. The location was really great - directly across from the Chambers Street l but not for NYC standards. 
The room was small but not small for NYC standards. Most importantly it was spotless - and I'm a really bad critic with that. 
The only bad thing I could say was that the elevator was not the best - my inlaws got stuck!! So we took the stairs the rest of the time since we were only on the 2nd floor. 
All in all - I'd recommend this hotel staying in the area.

review_title: Good location, Walking distance to central park and Has numerous eateries / pharmacies / super market in the neighborhood.
review_text:
We spent 3 nights in the hotel. We made our booking thru hotel.com. The location was good and the room we stayed was fine as we got upgraded to a suite as the room we booked thru booking.com was not available...still not very spacious for the money spent.. But I think by NY standards this room was spacious.. The rates are on the expensive side.. However,Room service took a long time to get food
 and the kids slept off by the time dinner came! The place was teeming with guests and it looked like a popular hotel!the lobby was dark and had a medieval look and the funny thing was I don't remember seeing a name board outside the hotel! The sound proofing is poor Coz u can hear other doors being closed thru the day!! We were traveling with small kids and the restaurant didn't look like they expected guests with small kids...

I am amazed they can make a room this tiny. You are greeted on entering with painfully loud music. Service is for bar drinkers - not hotel guests. This is no place for rest. Maybe a good hotel for people to sleep off a drunk from the hotel bars. Otherwise not recommended.

review_title: Great way to experience a true spirit of NYC!!
review_text: I came to NYC to work for fashion week, and found that Empire Hotel is the place to be at- to see and be seen!! As I arrived I was pleasantly surprised with an upgrade of my room to deluxe! Mariana Mero was at the front desk and I have nothing but the best comments about her- helpful, knowledgeable and efficient!! My stay in the hotel was amazing, loved every second of it and would highly recommend to all my friends + business partners!!!

review_title: Clean hip hotel in perfect location
review_text:
In town for 20 hours on busines and this place was great. Good value, clean sleek rooms and best of all a super comfortable bed to sleep in. Staff was helpful especially the bell/doormen. Romeo at the front desk was also very pleasurable. 
Only complaints would be not enough outlets to charge gear the bar closed very early and other than that great place I'll be back in three weeks

Just arrived at this so called hip and happening hotel and to be frank, it's awful. 
The rooms are beyond small and with an arthritic mother, it's not an ideal situation to be in. Also we have been given a queen room, despite requesting a twin at booking over a month ago. 
The room itself is small, which having been to NYC before I fully expected, however, this from cannot fit two adults' suitcases without one of us falling over it. There's an ironing board, goodness knows where to put it up without being double jointed!
The bathroom is beyond a joke. Hardly any room whatsoever and it's filthy. Otter people's dirt which turned my not so sensitive stomach several times. 
The owners of this property have concentrated with putting mod-cons in the room such as stereo, HD TV ( which I walked into too many times to mention) iPod dock and a clock radio, however the essentials in my opinion are not here, eg tea/coffee facilities (brought a travel kettle, asked for cups and spoons only to be charged $5 for the privilege which is normally free in most hotels). There is no mini bar, so stock up well. 
Im only grateful for the fact we will be out of the room all day and only here for the sake of showering/sleeping. Simply not good enough

review_title: Modern and clean hotel near the Lincoln Centre and Central Park.
review_text: Overall the empire hotel was very good. We had a standard room which, although a little on the small side, was very clean and well decorated. The hotel is well located opposite the Lincoln centre and is near to the subway and central park. The staff were very helpful and the hotel has a great cocktail bar on the 12th floor.

The Wellington has an amazing atmosphere, the staff is friendly and timely with service. Always willing to help or answer any questions. John C was an amazing help and thanks to him our romantic getaway was worryfree and comfortable.

review_title: Horrible stay. Don't even bother to come here. Service is awful.
review_text: We only stayed for a night but it was more than enough. Our rooms were an hour delayed upon check in. Then we get to our room and we realized that the Tv does not work. There was a light on the screen that resfused to shut off. We tell our bell man about it and he said they will send someone up. Wait for an hour, no one comes. Call front desk and they said they were sending someone up. Wait another hour, and no one comes or calls. We then decide to leave for dinner. We also tried to figure out how to shut off the AC as it was like Siberia in the small room. Could not find the thermostat. We come back later that night, and stop by again at the reception asking for help with the tv and the AC. Again they say someone is coming up. We had to pretty much disconnect all the wires to the tv ourselves as the light on the screen was so bright we could not sleep. After nearly an hour of trying to locate the shut off valve for the AC, we found it hidden behind the bed. My husband was so furious about the lack of service that we had. The rooms are expensive and tiny. If we had gotten someone to address our concerns, that would have been a lot better. Addressed the issue the next day to the guest relation manager and knew she was only giving me lip service. Will never ever stay there again. Horrible experience!

I had stayed at the Hudson more than 5 years ago, so I knew the rooms were small. But after reading Tripadvisor reviews, I was nervous when we got it via Priceline. At check-in, we received an upgrade (from Sabrina, who was very friendly & helpful behind the front desk). The room was small, but about average for boutique hotels in NYC. The room was clean, the staff was helpful. I brought earplugs after reading reviews about the noise, but we had no problems at all! The Sky Terrace was great for after-dinner drinks. And there are many subway lines right down the street.
Overall, it was a nice trip. It may not be a place where I'd stay in the most basic room with a family, but perfect for two people to rest after a busy day in the city.

The junior sweet that my brother and I shared was clean stylish and spacious. The view was not the best but you can't have everything the location was great. short walk to the metro Drank at the bar in the hotel on Sunday night great service from the guy working that night I would recommend this hotel to anyone

review_title: There are better hotels than the empire!!
review_text: Mold on the shower heads, maids walking into the room when we are asleep, key cards stop working, insisting you pay for wireless connection when it was stated that it was included......................the fact that most of our visit was spent away from the hotel doing the sites, eating etc. Means our stay wasn't spoilt..........we will go back to New York, we won't go back to the empire

This is NEW YORK!

review_title: An excuses orientated hotel when you have a problem. Stark design with poor maintenance
review_text:
We checked in at the Hudson yesterday 19th February after a 12 hour journey from the UK. We had contacted the hotel 2 months in advance confirm our booking with a request for a bath tub. The request was clearly stated for medical reason and we assured that this would be no problem.
Once we got to the room we found the bath tub to be 2/3 the size of a standard tub when you can just about sit in it. The guest experience team told us all rooms contain the same bath size but other hotel staff claim to be untrue. 
We have had to change rooms due to a faulty window and draft in the room to now being in a room with a faulty shower head. After a long journey and a bad start to our trip, we have no choice to accept these poor standards.
The hotel have offered a refund via British Airways which will take another of weeks but this would mean we would have book another hotel. We have 5 days and a full itinerary so this isn't an option. However, if we had known about the tub, we would have booked elsewhere 2 months ago.
The air condition comes on with a racket in the middle of the night than switches off and the blinds mangled on the window.
Don't be fooled but the Pillipe Starke design. This hotel is poorly maintained and managed. We have not even been offered any compensation as guest experience manager is away for 2 weeks!

review_text: I stayed here for my brothers wedding in April 2010. Travelling with a small baby we did have our reservations but nothing could prepare us for the nightmare that would follow. Arriving at the hotel at 7pm we were keen to get to our room and get our baby to sleep. We had emailed a request for a cot to be present in the room and also rang ahead to confirm this was the case. We were told that there was no record of this on the booking. However a cot would arrive straight away. 2 hours later following 10 visits to an empty front desk and having been repeatedly been told "it's in the lift" or even better "they are in the corridor" (whilst I walked around the corridor unable to spot the invisible cot). Eventually it arrived with a now hysterical child beyond comfort. We had booked a king size room - no such booking available and no room available. As other reviews the room was so small that it we were barely able to unpack our suitcases. We had stayed in NY the previous year and had no so such problems. No offer of compensation until we complained for the 10th time to the manager - free breakfast! Brilliant. We then got moved to a new room on the 11th floor - the whole floor was like a sauna and the room even hotter! Window wide open / closed -air con on full blast - no difference and no support from the hotel. All in all a dreadful stay and one which ruined our time in NY. This place is great if are happy to sleep in a box room and have as poor service as you imagine. Returning? You must be joking!

Really bad front desk help. If you are staying there for the pool, it not opened the hrs. Listed.

review_title: No frills but good basic alrounder
review_text: We stayed here end of october, staff very friendly and helpful. Cafe breakfast lovely, hotel worth the money for sheer location, very clean and tidy. Value for money it's not the Hilton but we didn't pay for that!

I'm actually in the hotel bar now waiting for taxi and just a few notes, this hotel is great, the location is superb, the hotel is very clean and nicely decorated, the breakfast is very good and rooms are very nice. We had the empire state building as our view from room! I just wanted to add this review as I honestly can't figure out why some people give it a bad review, I would recommend this hotel and would use again, forget you get what you pay for, this hotel is great for the money, you will enjoy a stay here.

review_title: really great location, close to everything
review_text:
the hotel is very clean, we had new towels everyday, the beds were great, the pillows the same. there is internet acces on the 2nd floor for free and payable in the rooms. printing is payable.
the hotel is close to times square, macy's, 5th avenue, empire state building etc really easy to go, by foot, by metro or by bus.
the breakfast was awful, only bakerys, very sweet and not baked enough. no fresh vegetables, eggs, cheese or anything.

review_title: Maybe great for vacation, horrible for business.
review_text:
Zero reception in these rooms. Wifi drops in and out. Television never worked. Three business partners of mine had the same experience. Made it very hard to work. 
Location was great though.

review_title: Expected cleaner, more contemporary room for the $$
review_text: Nice amenities, fantastic location, disgusting bedding. It was probably clean but the stained bed skirt squished me right out. Overly aggressive early morning room service loud enough to disturb anyone on the floor regardless of privacy requests was also extremely annoying. I would expect this in a cheaper hote. Not worth the money.
A great value at a great location great staff nice bar overall a real find

Near 5th Avenue and Times Square, it's a bargain! Rooms are small but well-furnished, great for a solo business traveler. Breakfast buffet had good food, but it took them a while to find someone working the dining room - the only time that the service was less than excellent. One nice touch - though checkout was at noon, my business in the city kept me until after 4pm, but the hotel provided a free baggage check service.

What a joke this hotel is so overpriced its actually laughable. Too start is miles away from everywhere you want to visit, u have to pay for taxis or get the subway unless u want very sore souls on your feet, the rooms are tiny I mean the littlest I've ever stayed in, the bed is obviously little in the small room, the sockets don't work to plug ur iron in then when u balance it in that does not work, with sockets not working you can't dry ur hair with the hair dryer or anything, moving on to the shower an bath oh the fun of them, the plug doesn't work in the bath an as for the shower you have freezing cold or burny hot take your pick. So to summarise, this hotel is overpriced, out of the way, very scruffy, the shower an bath don't work also the sockets oh and just to add the view is awful looking into other peoples apartments because there's a big cloth blind, if you want to be ripped off an sorely disappointed then the Bentley is definitely for you!!

One stay has made this my first choice whenever in NY. Serene lobby and staff were a pleasant welcome after a long day. But, even better was our room's view of the Queensboro bridge at night. Beautiful! Thank you Bentley for a wonderful stay.

I was in New York for a quick vacation with my wife, in February 2011.
Finding a hotel with a better position, at the same price in New York is almost impossible.
Actually the rooms are not that big, but they are very clean and the position is perfect: two steps away from times square and broadway.
But most of all I would like to spend a few words about the staff: everyone was so nice with us and everyone did his best to make our visit as enjoyable as possible.
Especially our new friend Walter, at the concierge, since he did everything for us! He told us where to go, booked for us tables in the best clubs and restaurants etc... And everything at the last minute! I will be back for sure, strictly recommended! Marco & Irina From Italy

We selected this hotel after an internet search. There were mixed comments on TripAdvisor but the negatives (parking costs, restaurant promotion and distance from Central Park etc) did not concern us. Other comments were positive.
We confirmed our booking as suggested by the manager responding to a tripadvisor comment. Arrived at 3.10 pm as advised to find the room was not ready. After a few minutes I mentioned the previous email conversation with the manager and a room was available with upgrade.
The hotel is older and the external appearance is a bit off-putting. Inside is better but the need for refurbishment is evident. The room was spacious and everything worked OK. The A/C unit was noisy but we put up with it in case a relocation meant the original room which we were certain would be much smaller.
The bed was comfortable and the room roomy enough to enjoy a meal in the room at the table. There is a good food market close under Queensboro bridge that sells prepared salads etc. 
The bathroom was very small.
Stay here again? Probably not. The crowning point was when I asked for help to get a taxi to go to Penn Station at 6.00 am. Response was basically my problem. The doorman was more enterprising and earned his tip.
Having tried many hotels this is now my place of choice. Small but lovely rooms. Great service with a personal touch and an ideal location. The bar (Aspen Social Club) makes it even better

Between rockerfeller center and broadway/times sq. Very convenient to subway. Crowded area. Clean rooms and friendly staff. Internet is in the lobby only. A bonus during our stay is the complimentary loaner umbrellas
You know how some hotels can have an awkward smell? Well this one doesn't. It stayed fresh my entire stay. I love this place! The beds are comfy and rooms are stylish and functional! I love it here!

If you are looking for an hotel on the east side, this could be a good option. It is far east at York, so if you have business on the west side, it is far. ($13-14 to Javits Center. I had an upgraded suite room (thank you) with fantastic views of 59 St Bridge and up/down York ave. Lots of amenities in room typical of 4 star hotel. Robes, sewing kit, shaver, toothbrush, nice soap & shampoo. NO coffee makers in room. Coffee bar downstairs in morning, not included w/room. Walls a bit thin if you have noisy room neighbors. I liked the room decor w/ zebra stripe carpet and hounds tooth pattern pillows. Small bathroom - but this is typical in New York. Pleasant staff. I'd consider this a 3 1/2 star hotel with some 4 star amenities.

review_title: Awkward rooms, not much care for the hotel guest.
review_text:
I had a reservation and quaranteed my late arrival with a credit card. I noted in the reservation that my flight would land at 11:30pm (JFK). They called cell as I was disembarking the airplane to ask if I were coming to the hotel - I said yes, of course.
I arrive to be told that there is only one room left, and not the king I had reserved. Its midnight and I'm tired having flown from west coast for business. I'm now told I've been "upgraded" to room with two fullsize beds - what? I'm 6 feet tall (only) and yet my feet hang off the end of the bed with my head against the headboard. Not comfortable. Furniture so tight its almost impossible to sit at the desk. The bathroom is a different story. Lets just say your entire bathroom kit fits in sandwich bag or no room.
Last, the Aspen Social Club which adjoins the lobby and under my "upgraded" room (and many others) is hosting a private party wherein the DJ (a very unimaginative, and simply put, not very good DJ) was allowed to crank the volume well past their small lounge "loud music" threshold and put the music loudly in my room. Yep, cut right through the sleeping pill.
I called the front desk at 11 (wasn't upset) and was told an hour more...fine. 12:30am comes and it gets louder. I call back to the front desk - no hotel manager on duty (pretty common in the evening here) So, with no adult on deck to take care of business, its left to the bar manager to think about the hotel guests this magical Thursday night. Oh, not to be.
I am now told by the front desk at 12:45am that it will only be another 5 - 10 minutes as there are hardly any patrons left. Ok, cool. What?! - now the music gets even louder...until 2am. 
I've stayed here before, put clients up here and recommended ad infinitum. Well , I truly regret those days are over. The management has lost customer quality control. I love music and hotels with DJ'd lounges, but I've never been to one that totally disregards its paying guests. Sad and not a great business model.
But hey, the front desk called me to say that for my inconvenience, they would comp my to little bottles of water that I drank in my room. I'm always ready to see the phenomenal customer service reach-out and Rocky-like comeback. This restores my faith and I am inevitably happy because of this great, we-care-about-our-guests effort. Hmmm, well two little bottles of water was their master stroke.
I'll not stay here again, and rather than recommend, I will instead actively refer friend and clients elsewhere. Shame really. And to all a good night.

I travel frequently to NYC. I live in an extremely quiet town so I typically only get a couple hours of sleep due to the the noise of The Big Apple. Not so with this hotel - lights out, awakened refreshed! The room was very clean and all of the staff were exceptionally helpful, courteous and friendly. I will definitely be staying here more in the future.

We stayed at Hilton last weekend for 3 nights and really liked it. No bed bugs, that was the 1st thing we asked about and checked ourselves! Very nice contemporary hotel, in a great location! I would stay there again!

My husband and I have been at Stay. for the last 3 days. The rooms are small, but comfortable and efficient. It was exactly what we needed because you don't spend much time if your room in NYC. The room was clean and absolutely prefect except for the border rod sticking out of the mattress seam. 
The hotel itself was very nice and trendy. We were on the 5th floor which was perfect. The elevators are INCREDIBLY slow when you're traveling down (on the way up, it's relatively easy), so if you're going to go with anyone elderly, you might want to request staying on a lower floor, unless you don't mind waiting 10 minutes to go up and down. Also, I wouldn't recommend staying on the 2nd floor. On the weekend, the restaurant turns into a nightclub and it's loud.

I didn't actually stay here so maybe their rooms are a whole lot better than their Rooftop Restaurant and Bar. I was in the city for work for the weekend and I got a Travelzoo coupon to check out their restaurant. I thought it was a pretty good deal, four drinks and two appetizers for $39. The decor was nice but the service was horrible and the food...not worth the price and I'm glad I had a deal. We were seated in what they call their lounge area of the restaurant only to wait forever to be waited on. We had to flag a server down and multiple people would come to the table. Weren't really sure who our server was. After we finally got served, no one really checked on us. We had asked the server for our check and then decided to step outside for a minute to check out the great view. It is a rooftop now....but not a very safe one. Appears to be under construction. While we were out there, we noticed new people sitting at our table. When we came back in to ask the server, she said "oh, I thought you guys left". Um no, we were waiting for you to bring the check. Unless you have a deep discount deal, I would recommend this restaurant for anything.

Modern and hip with great service and free Internet. The location makes it easy to get the best Broadway tickets at the tkts queue and good shopping and eating. Staff helped us locate laundromat and hairdressers v good. Only downside v small room, even for NYC but if you are out and about lots like s less of a concern. Best service we had in NYC.

review_title: Modern hotel just off Times Square and very near Rockefeller Centre
review_text: I got really good deal via lastminute with the Stay Hotel coming up as one of the cheaper hotels. Based on tripadvisor reviews booked this. The reception area was very impressive fish tank was amazing, very modern. Reception allowed us to check in early. Our room was on 9th floor, can't complain on size enough room to sleep, shower and move around. Given the amount of time you spend in room it's completely functional. Location is great, just off times square, near a subway and close to rockefeller centre. Would definitely stay there again.

review_title: Nice clean hotel with a good location
review_text: This was a nice hotel. Not fabulous, just nice. We stayed here for 10 nights whilst travelling. The rooms are tiny...and I mean tiny. But we were only sleeping in them at night so it wasnt that big of a deal. The one complaint I would have is the female concierge. She was terrible. Very rude and not interested in helping guests at all. I think she was on facebook everytime I went to the desk (which was only about 4 times) but everytime I went there to ask for some information it was if I was inconveniencing her. Didn't make it any better when the 3 times we asked for directions of where something was she sent us the complete other way?? Anyway we learnt our lesson and started asking the staff at the front desk for things and not concierge. I would try and stay a little closer to 5th ave next time but still on 42nd st...

This hotel has everything a traveller needs: a great room with a great view, a terrific bed, an LCD tv and a nice bathroom. Moreover, it is located at the eastend of 42nd Street, which makes for a nive walk towards midtown. 
The only thing I didn't like were the rates for wireless internet: $16 per day. That's a little steep..
But all in all a great hotel !!

review_title: Excellent location but not worth the price
review_text: Only good thing about this hotel is it's location. Right smack on time square. Room is very small, price of this room can get a better hotel around the same location. House keeping service is bad. They knock on your door every early morning to check on whether they can come in to clean, the hotel dont have any thing to hang at the door for house keeping or do not disturb. Basically they will knock every couple of hrs to check starting from 9am which is very disturbing when you asleep still. Hall way sound proof is very lousy, basically u can hear everything. I stayed at the 5th level and I can hear the hotel bar banging with music and crowds almost every night until 3am. No ice no hot water. Basically very simple small room, good location but won't come back again

Bon hotel, pas mal place, assez tranquille, rapport qualite prix honnete pour la ville. Un bÃ©mol, la climatisation fort bruyante dans la chambre qui impose un changement urgent de ces appareils, intenable la nuit en fonctionnement. Le personnel est reactif et attentif. 150 euros la nuit du 16 au 19 aout 2011.

review_title: Good but a little noisy and dark rooms
review_text: A very centrally located hotel with nice employees and good cleaning. On the downside: Dark rooms, irritating elevators (to small and extremely slow) and poor noise isolation towards hallway. The location makes it unavoidable that there is trafic noise, but that is only to expect. Relatively stiffly priced rooms compared to i.e. deals offered at Intercontinental Times Square at 44th and 8th where my friends stayed. So i am not tempted to come back. All in all.

The stay was a great hotel! It is just around the corner from time square. Everything you want or need is in the area. The staff members were amazing. They were friendly and helped me with every issue I had, including a parking ticket. They went above and beyond in assisting me with that. I also liked the fact that there was a lounge down stairs. Great hotel for those who love to party! The stay is the place where I will literally stay every time I visit the city that never sleeps. Keep up the good work.

I stayed here for one night. The lobby was nice, and the staff was friendly. The room was cute, had a retro feel. I was told that my room would have 2 queen sized beds, they were the smallest queen beds I've ever seen. The shower didn't close in the bathroom which was incredibly inconvenient and made the entire bathroom very wet! Also, there was no heater in the bathroom so it was pretty cold getting out! The view of the river and the bridges were very nice. The giant water stain on the top of the curtain however was not. Also had some trouble operating the television, we could only seem to get one channel! I did not get a chance to see the rooftop bar, the breakfast seemed a bit over priced, and we found a delicious diner just one block away. It served its purpose if your looking for a cheap place to sleep, but did not do anything to achieve above and beyond in my mind. I booked through a discounted site, so I am satisfied and feel I got my moneys worth. However, I wouldn't recommend staying there for full price, I feel there are better options in the city to get your moneys worth.

I stayed at the Bentley Hotel in January 2011 when my dog needed surgery at Animal Medical Center. I wasn't going to stay overnight but his procedure got bumped so I needed a room in a pinch. The front desk clerk was helpful, kind, and polite to a Vermonter in the big city. The room was classy, clean, and very comfortable. The hotel is right next to the animal hospital and he could even have stayed with me if he hadn't been admitted overnight. I'd recommend this hotel to anyone from out of town who has a pet at Animal Medical Center, or who is just looking for a nice place to stay on the East Side.
Sentralt plassert med gangavstand til Central Park, Empaire State, Time Square m.m. Fine rom, trivelig bar og lobby. Bra belldesk. Rimelige priser.

review_title: I need to Stay. again here Real soon!
review_text:
Stay. Hotel caught my eye as soon as I came across it online, and guess what? Stay. was SOLD out. Ready to have purchased my 5 nights, I decided to room else where for my first night in NYC.
My second night I passed by it, I walked in and asked if they had any availability, and they did, I told them I would get back with them, I did at 4am, luggage in hand. The Courteous Gentlemen by the name Amaury was very kind and assured me that there was a room for me that night and helped me book my 4 remaining nights with them.Â 
My room (single queen bed) was perfect for my modern taste, small and very CLEAN. The bed was soft and extremely comfortable (4 Pillows)! I enjoyed the 4 different light preferences: Dimming Celling lights, Lamps, Desk Lamp and table Lamp where the BOSE Radio with AUX for your iPhone/iPod/MP3 player is set. Flat TV Screen. Digital A/C. The extras such as: "Green" Earth Friendly Soap, Facial Cleanser & Shampoos. The Vanity Box, which includes Q-Tips, safety pin and needle with different threads. An Amazing Conair Professional Hair Dryer. Many & Plenty of Towels. Two Robes in the closet with iron & ironing board. A Safe for personal belongings. A mini-bar :) Â Nancy my housekeeper always had a smile on her face. She was happy to help me with anything I requested. I also noticed how she updated and changed out my magazines on the Desk!Â 
After Midnight on the weekends, I went downstairs for a surprise. The Hotel's Restaurant turns into enjoyable entertainment, bringing it's daytime lounge image into Life at Night!
Amaury and Sangbo (the door man) were always present late night and assisted me with any questions a night owl and/or tourist could want answered. Fantastic Service!

review_title: You'll either love or hate the rooms, some problems with this new hotel
review_text:
Stayed here for one night while travelling on business. The hotel is very cool with an excellent rooftop bar.
However, you'll either love or hate the rooms. Super modern with an iPad to entertain you in every room. But the concrete floor, bean bag for a chair and somewhat dark atmosphere even with all the lights turned on won't be to everyone's tastes. The bed is low down and more like a fouton but was reasonably comfortable.
Biggest problem was a few inexcusable issues with this new hotel. No rail or hangers in my cupboard left me with nowhere to hang my suit! No hair dryer in the room. No coffee in the room, although there was a mini bar. These glitches were pretty annoying for the price but hopefully they will sort them out.
The staff were very friendly and helpful, but the rooftop bar closed at 11pm which for such a trendy hotel was a bit annoying when coming back from dinner.
Overall, you'll only like this place if you are into super modern hotels and can put up with some of the glitches.

review_title: A good value in the very heart of the theatre district.
review_text:
I've stayed here many times over the last 30 years, mostly for business but sometimes, like this time, for a theatre-going vacation. This time we saw 8 shows in 5 days...great fun!
Older hotel but well taken care of. A beautiful Art Deco lobby. For security one must show their room key to get onto elevators or stairs. 
The 4 of us had a lovely 2 room (plus bath and huge closet) suite with windows facing both the Hudson and 47th st for $239.00/night. Compare that to the Marriott Marquis across the street! The living room has a pull-out sofa bed that was comfortable. Bath small but fully functional. 
Entrances on both 46 and 47th (47 the main one) both are loaded with theatres. 1/2 a block W of the TKTS discount ticket stand. A covered walkway from the 46th st door to 45 and 44th St. At 45th and the walkway (on that block it's named "Shubert Alley") is "Junior's" Resturant with a very complete take out counter with (usually) no wait, then it's one block back to your room to eat. On 47th is "Danny's" Deli with 24 hour buffet food and sandwiches. 
In the hotel is the "Edison Cafe" AKA "The Polish Tea Room" for informal B-L-D meals. At the 46th St end is "Sophia's" a nice upscale Italian Resturant with a piano (sometimes bass and sax too) bar. The location of the loan-shark garrotting scene in the Godfather. 
I'll try to attach a pic I took out the West window. 
Have a nice trip!

The bathroom was so small that the condensation from the shower clung to the ceiling and you got a little rainfall after you got out of the shower if you didn't get out of the bathroom fast enough. We had called ahead and asked for an early check in and a remodeled room. We got neither and when we arrived and asked if we could check in early the desk person was quite rude. The Empire State bldg is a block away, as well as Macy's. The location is excellent! Yes, it is on a street that has many Korean shops, banks, restaurants, but we liked that it was not on a busy street and there are many fancy bakeries and expensive Korean restaurants open 24/7 if you're hungry late at night.
The area had a very safe feeling. And we had NO problems with bugs, as one reviewer said. We have actually stayed here annually as tourists 6 years in a row and love it. 
Minuses are the room lighting like most hotel rooms is a bit dim and during busy summer months or times the elevators can be very busy and are slow, or 1 breaks down. No hair conditioner is included FYI but thankfully there is a 24hour CVS down the street.

review_text: This hotel is along walk to Times Square action, but access to the subway and Penn Station for airport travel was very convenient. The room was very small and the door did not tightly seal; therefore, hallway noise was not blocked out. The staff was courteous, however, the room did not seem quite clean (maybe it was the old bedspread and thin towels?). I did check for bed bugs and did not find any thankfully. Overall, I would try another hotel next time.

review_title: One week stay great price. Close to every thing
review_text:
My daughter and i stayed Here for a week. Great price on room. Breakfast every morning roof top bar. And right behind the empire state building. The subway is a block away and Starbucks macys it was great. Never felt afraid. 
Nbc studio is a must. We went to the jimmy falon show and were selected to dance behind the band. Awesome. 
Went to battery park, statue of liberty, walked on wall steet. Took in a broadway show, central park. And trinity church. Is Just one of the many church we saw. They are all wonderful. We have to return. One week is not enough. FantÃ¡stc city and. Great hotel. Will stay Again
Although the rooms are small, I found this to be a lovely small hotel in a good location

review_title: Great location. Service and facilities could use some work.
review_text:
The good: location! Close to everything I needed and wanted to do and to subway. Room layout was good for a NYC hotel. I got the King room. Very small, but design and layout was practical and appealing. Exception was no full length mirror except inside closet door. The door did not open so that you could actually see yourself. Lost opportunity on not making the over-the-desk mirror taller so you could see yourself when standing. Stayed there because rate was better than most in location. 
The not so good:maintenence and service issues. 2 light bulbs and sink drain control were not working at check-in. Fixed promptly, but took 2 trips. Was not offered or given newspapers or turndown service despite being Wyndham Rewards member. This seemed to be just a random occurance. A colleague received both without asking. Charged $10/day for VERY slow internet service. Room service errors resulted in cold coffee and toast waiting for a return trip for 2nd person set-up (they were told twice that we had 2 diners when order placed). Work-out room is gloomy, hot, poorly designed and equipped and water cooler was empty. Apparently you can get a pass to a nearby Golds Gym and if you have time and want a real workout, that would be a must. Regardless, it was not OK.
Rooms are small, great location but beds were uncomfortable. Would not stay here again

Location is great, lobby is beautiful and staff is friendly and efficient. This was a girl's long weekend that had been planned and anticipated for months. The room was a disaster, frayed carpet and general run down appearance. Calling it a "suite" was a wishful thinking on their part. They were also renovating so it was very noisy. I complained to the front desk and we got a slightly better room. I told the desk clerk that the rooms were not what was depicted on the Internet. She apologized and said they were undergoing renovations. I asked for a renovated room and was told none were available. If I had asked for one when I booked, they would have made every effort to accommodate us. Who knew to ask!? So now you all know. Great location but there are many hotels in the area. I would not stay here again

Old buildings have flair and character, but they must be maintained. The first room my sister and I were in had a broken hairdryer, a heater that only occasionally worked and a leaky pipe that caused a bulge in the wall. When our room was changed so maintenance could take care of the leak, we had a leaky shower head that sprayed us in the face everytime we showered. Lastly (in both rooms), I don't think the matresses have been changed since the hotel was built - they were like sleeping on concrete! The hotel is in a great location, the staff was nice and the lobby was nicely decorated, though. I just hope the owners care enough to provide the rooms the TLC they need.

review_title: Might as well have been sleeping outside
review_text: AC window unit let in all the street noise and cold air. Couldn't believe a 4 star hotel would think this is acceptable. Don't stay here.

review_title: Good location hotel, friendly staff but no luxuries.
review_text: Stayed here recently with a friend in a twin room, the hotel staff were friendly but the room was very small the bathroom even smaller. Clean and tidy but no tea or coffee facilities no in room safe there were safety deposit boxes in reception which were available but somehow we didn't feel as comfortable using these. All in all we were out all day so really only used the room to sleep in. Value for money...yes ,for the location but don't expect a luxury stay or a room with a view!
From reading the reviews I expected a somewhat unpleasant room but convenient location. I shortened <!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC

Very nice stay. The well equipped kitchen is welcome if your stay is more than a day or two. Amish market across the street is convenient for stocking the fridge and pantry. The staff is very friendly and helpful. Good food in the restaurant, Ringo. Comfortable bar. Good midtown east location.

review_title: Beautiful, attention to style and a perfect location- and somehow reasonably priced!!!! A great place
review_text: The Alex hotel is definitely a place I will return to. It is such a Nice, unique hotel with an ambience that is unparalleled to any other hotel stay I have experienced. Modern and quiet, it is in a location that allows quick access to anywhere in the city-it's almost across the street from Grand Central- and it is just far enough from time square and the crowds to enjoy a very quiet nights sleep. The staff is beyond polite and attentive, and the bar is awesome. I look forward to staying here again! Also, I stayed in a very ample room for what I felt was a fair price.

What a dump. The photos online are very misleading. The room was nasty. The woodfloors looked like they hadn't been cleaned or finished in 50 years. The window would have been nice if a walmart window air conditioner hadn't taken up most of it. There was a lovely fabric bench in the window that was cover with stains and the seat was broken away from the frame. When they dropped our bags we asked I'd this was the upgrade... The bag guy said there were 'worse'. We checked out without staying more than an hour. Dont stay here unless your other option is a shared bathroom hostel on 95th street.

We stayed here for 6 nights and booked in advance on booking.com - a one bedroom suite was cheaper than a standard room in many of the other high end hotels nearby. Our suite was great - amazing views of the Chrysler building, spacious living room/kitchen area, v comfortable bed. We ate in the restaurant one night which was good if a little pricey. Only downsides were the plastic covered sofas - not the most comfortable - also no i pod dock - bring your own. Wifi is additional $15 per day per device - however the diner opposite has free wifi and also serves a good brunch. Location good - short walk to central station and also to shops on 5th Ave and Moma. Overall would highly recommend.

I have been to Europe, if you have too then you know what I am talking about when I say the hotel is European style. First off, the check in is nice enough, service was ok with champagne upon receiving your keys. Kinda snobby, but ok. The elevators are made for two people, very small. The room we had, 804 is the equivalent of a shoebox. The bed is small, a queen but I am used to a cal king. Tv was smaller, mounted on the wall... Carpet a little worn, bed was great as well as the pillows. Might I mention that this hotel washes all bedding between guests, no stinky comforters here! 
On to the bathroom... The door to the bathroom was frosted glass which is ok, but the door seems like an afterthought, there was a huge gap between the door and the door jamb. This created an awkward environment for those wishing to use the toilet in private because this gap allowed people in the room to see your rear end.
 The sink was as wide as my toothbrush, no storage whatsoever. Very trendy fixtures, soapstone counter. The shower had a rain showerhead and four wall mounted heads. Again, European style where you adjust temperature and intensiy separate from each other. The problem here is that the drain didn't work well so soon enough your were standing in a pool of your own dirty water and there was no vent in the bathroom. 
The ac in the unit was a little loud but tolerable. The windows opened with no screens. Our room faced other rooms so yes put down your blinds. 
Would I stay here again? Absolutely not.

review_title: Overrated, tiny room, bed and bathroom
review_text: Nice location, fashionable but very tiny room, tiny bathroom and tiny bed I prefer to walk a little further and have a larger room, a larger bathroom and a real bed

review_title: Better to be found in NYC
review_text:
Being a big fan of boutique hotels I decided to give the Dream a run for it's money on a recent business trip to NYC.
The hotel has a great location, just off Broadway and very close to the subway station. On check in the staff looked put out having to great me and check me in, I must have disturbed their conversation Â on what they had for lunch.
Â I was not asked for preference on a preferred floor and was accommodated on the 3rd floor, if you have trouble sleeping ask for a high floor as noise outside can be quite load and it was, especially during the weekend.
The rooms are tiny, we all expect small rooms in NYC but not this small. They also looked old, slightly grubby and lacked attention to detail one would expect from a Boutique.Â 
One big plus is the quality of the bed, it was extremely comfortable and I would rate it as one of the best I have had in any hotel.
The F & B is outsourced and both bars in the hotel are well run, the staff are extremely friendly and go out their way to make you comfortable.
I requested a late check out, the receptionist looked at me as if I was asking for a weeks free stay, after deliberating she gave me an hour extra. To wrap it up there is better for your $ in NYC.

review_title: Nice hotel with a great location
review_text: I stayed there for 4 nights. The room is very nice and modern. The bathroom is a bit small but clean and has a great shower. The only downside of the room is that the window faces another room of the hotel so the blinds need to be down all the time making it necessary to have the lights on. The staff at the reception were excellent and very friendly. There is a cool bar at the ground floor where you can have a drink. Free wi-fi.

Had a dinner to attend on one of the busiest weekends of the year in New York and got a great rate at the Shoreham. I was pleasantly surprised with an upgrade to a one bedroom suite. Good sized living room, huge bedroom. Tiny bathroom but had everything I needed. The bed was amazingly comfortable. I did use any of the hotel facilities but they looked good. The only problem was my room, which faced 55th street, was a bit loud. Lots of traffic all night. Otherwise a good value. Friendly young staff.

Great hotel, fantastic location. We had a two bedroom suite for us and our two teenage sons, which was very roomy, had lots of clothes storage space (four wardrobes) and three TVs, including one in the bathroom! We stayed on the 23rd floor which had amazing views. We had breakfast in the hotel once, which was great, but most mornings left early to try breakfast elsewhere (Comfort Diner across the road was great). This was our second stay here, and we'd definitely stay here again.

review_title: Poor value for money, could try harder
review_text: I don't mind the small room, which you expect in New York. But for $260 I found it a little tatty in places, with not enough attention to detail. My main complaint was the window-mounted aircon unit, which was very noisy - but with the summer heat there was no alternative. There are better options - e.g. The Pod Hotel down the road, which is also small but much better value.

Super cool hotel. Beautiful room. 
Ours was located on the 32th floor - with a view of the Chrysler Building. Large bathroom, big fridge with a lot of good stuff and a nice bed. Flatscreen tv in the bedroom and on the toilet? A bit american, but what the h*ll, you're in NY...
Restaurant was a bit expensive, but the food was good. Staff was very helpfull, and very serviceminded.
I would stay again, and I would't hesitate to recommend.

The rooms have varied greatly in size the three times I have stayed there, but the service and location is excellent. The only drawback for me is the lack of news channels available in the room, no BBC, al jazeera etc. Bar downstairs great for a quick drink. Lunch at Amish market nearby a bonus!

Stayed for one night to see a Broadway show. The location of the hotel was perfect. Just a couple blocks from all the shows. This hotel is definitely for the younger crowd. It has a roof top bar with great views of the city. Walking distance to central park and shopping on 5th Ave. Would definitely stay there again. The bed was absolutely wonderful. The staff was helpful and nice.

The hotel has the most perfect location. Right on 55th and broadway, most of subway lines are around the corner. Times square at your feet! What more could you ask for!
The rooms are small, don't expect otherwise. Minimalistic, great bed, small bathroom but practical. Do not take clothes to hang, there's almost no cabinet to put your stuff in. 
No view also, the windows are on the other side of the hotel (you basically see the other rooms or the wall opposite the hotel). 
What matters is that you are in a boutique hotel with a wonderful club on the rooftop and you can go up, drink, dance, and go to bed in a minute. The music is great, the ambiance and the view on Times squares' lights are amazing. The hotel is adjacent to one of the best italian restaurants in NY: Serafina. 
You will also find tons of places for breakfast just around the corner on 7 and 57 for example. 
Now go and live your dream!

We were welcomed with champagne. A machine was available free 24/7 for espresso, cappucino, latte, and coffee, reg or decaf; teas, and hot chocolate. Nice touches for a nicely renovated modern feel hotel. Our room was very large with a very comfortable king bed, flat screen tv (limited channel selection), desk, and very very unusual good lighting. The bath was small, but this was totally offset by the awesome shower. It had the usual overhead spray, but also four others that were adjustable for direction and intensity. Best of all you could adjust water to very hot, afeature so many hotels simply do not have. Our only issue was room temp, which was too warm. It is possible we could have adjusted the a/c, but we opened the window instead, so I don't know if the a/c would have solved the problem.

My boyfriend and I stayed here for four nights to celebrate our two year anniversary. The hotel was in a great location and the view from the rooftop bar was amazing. The room was small but that is expected in New York. The sound from the hallways carried into the rooms and the bratty little teenagers that were across the hall from us made so much noise that it sounded like they were in our room with us. The free breakfast was fine for me but my boyfriend wanted waffles because the pictures in the elevators advertising the breakfast had waffles in them lol. The staff was friendly when we checked in and out. The room was practically a steal at $106 a night. I would definitely stay here again.

Everyone was excellent at the La Quinta Inn Manhattan. My husband and I wanted to spend a few days in the city for his birthday. I had a cake delivered to the hotel the day of our arrival & the front desk was very helpful in keeping it a surprise. I must say, I was really surprised that the hotel was very clean and perfect location for an excellent price. The only problem with the hotel are the elevators..very slow & not enough of them. Overall I would definitely stay there again and would recommend the La Quinta Inn manhattan to all of my friends.

review_title: Don't expect good old fashioned customer service.
review_text: A basically good hotel. It's biggest plus is location which couldn't be nearer to times square, though noise should be expected. Staff are not the friendliest & didn't get the welcome I had heard Americans were proud of. My party & I often felt we were an inconvenience.

review_title: Wow must be New York's hidden gem
review_text:
Just spent two nights at The Alex. I am a Leaders club member and got upgraded to a one bedroom suite. The rooms on the 32 have 180 degree views of the city including of the iconic Chrysler Building. Suites are comfortable with kitchenette all the electric mid cons except a coffee maker!
Staff are superb and all so helpful. A great stay and great value for money.
Nice place, stayed there 6 nights. Visit from Argentina. They charge 10 dollars for wifi. Too much!

I've stayed in enough poor quality or faceless hotels in manhattan. This was a refresher. Good sized rooms, attentive staff, good location and unique enough to separate itself from the usual clone chain hotels which a lot of people seem to love. 
Restaurant onsite seemed a bit pricey especially when there's so much more around. 
It is expensive but then what hotel isn't round there? The points are knocked off for value for money. Otherwise a great place.

This is 2nd visit to the Alex. Once again, the staff is too friendly, we received an upgrade, and the room is great. It is more like staying in an apartment. Who needs a spacious lobby with an ever changing staff - it is like coming home to my old apartment in a doorman building. Had to leave my car in front for half hour - no problem. Comfortable bed and luxury linens. Bathrooms are large and functional. No problems with water pressure. Any electronic device you could want or need. Also need to mention the wine glasses - perfect! And ice in the freezer. Plenty of storage space. Finally, L'Occitane products. Only negative is the noise produced when flushing toilet. Will only stay here in NYC.

Stayed in the hotel in early October. The location is good. 2 min walk to Times SQ. 
The hotel needs refurbishment. My room was 634 and was poor. It was a small twin room, very little storage and needs updating. 
The staff are helpful. The bell boys Larry and his brother Bobby were brilliant as were the concierge and reception staff. 
Overall if your looking for a central location at a budget it would be ok but it's no 5 star and needs updating.
for the price in that area, I thought it was a good deal. The Guy at the front desk was really nice. I did find a few crumbs in the room though. (didn't complain about it) overall, it wasn't too bad.

After reading the reviews I was skeptical about the hotel we booked. Loved loved the staff, great locations and fabulous bath products. Anyone who says they had a bad stay, clearly expected the four seasons. Fabulous studios for a great price.

review_title: Great location, not so great service
review_text: This hotel has the perfect location, it's literally round the corner from Times Square so right in the thick of things, in easy walking distance of the majority of New Yorks greatest attractions, however that seemed to be where the positives ended. My friend who booked the trip called the hotel before we arrived to find out of there was any other information we needed to know before arriving to be told no everything is ready. When we got there they tried to tell us we had not paid for the room when we had paid in the previous January. They then asked for a credit card for security details without making us aware they actually wanted to put a hold on 100 dollars of our spending money. We had to agree to this to be able to stay in the room but under the agreement that this would be released upon check out so we were able to spend the full amount we had saved. Check out comes around, told the money was back with us automatically, tried to spend and card was declined! Went back to speak to the hotel and suddenly the money will take 2-3 working days to go back on the card! The staff were not helpful and got angry with us when we tried to explain that the communication between staff and customers was appalling. Add into the mix that there was no hot water on the first night, their suitcase scales werent working and we didn't have the best stay! Make sure u ask all the above details before staying here!!

Great price, we got an amazing deal for 7 nights!! Great location, great roof top bar! Rooms were small typical for NYC but spotless and the bed was super comfy! Great linens/ robes & toiletries, no iPod doc tho :( . Most of the staff were great some didn't seem to notice guests unfortunately! All in I would deffinately stay again, great smell of insence in the lobby at night... Worth a visit!

I found this hotel to be great location wise. I found the food and service in the cafe to be not great. Food not tasty and service very rushed. The staff in reception was lovely however the key would not let us in to the room on 3 occasions. And on the last nigh a letter was pushed through our door at 2 in the mornin I found this very disturbing. Other wise it was perfect and Wu recommend it to others

Stayed here a few times and have to say it has never failed me! The location is spot on. The rooms are great and spacious. A fantastic bar is situated within the hotel also. If your going to New York for the first time or have been before then try this hotel, you won't be disappointed!

review_title: I will Stay again. Excellent location and value for money
review_text: Spent a week here. Really central location for shows and within walking distance of lots. Rooms big enough and beds comfortable It's right in the city so it's all part of the atmosphere and that included a little street noise and I had expected that, but I slept well every night. It's a bustling place and breakfast was in the cafe downstairs or in the Deli next door. Porters very helpful as were all staff I experienced

review_title: Excellent location you could'nt get it better.
review_text:
This is an old hotel when you just are going to spend the nights there. The location is excellent, I came with my niece from Mexico we felt always very safe.
This is a huge hotel with 53 floors and 10 elevators you never have problem getting one. Breakfast is served with a wide variety of choices.
Highly recommended.

review_title: Excellent place to stay in NY!!!
review_text: This was one of the best trips that our family has taken. The location is perfect. We could look out of our room window and see Ground Zero. It was amazing!!! We were at the entrance to the subways, a lot of eating places in the area and different places within walking distance. The staff were very friendly and helpful and the rooms well kept (even though they were remodeling downstairs). I would recommend this hotel to anyone who is going to that area and I am looking forward to going back :-)

I am currently staying at the hotel until Sunday. Checking in was no problem although when we arrived in our room- the down comforter had either urine or seeman stains all over it & the bathroom had not been cleaned. Today we went to times square around 10 am as the maid was coming in. We arrived back into our hotel around 6 pm to find our door had been left open all day from house keeping. Called just to give a heads up to the office to let them know and security acted as if it was our problem, not theirs. Leaving the situation alone, we left again for times square and when we returned- we were locked out of our room due to the latch somehow closing on it's own. Waited 30 minutes for security and have yet to receive an apology for THEIR inconvenience to us. Very disappointed.

review_title: Good value for money in a central location
review_text: I stayed there dozends of time, and when staying close to Times Square this is a convenient, clean hotel with a modern timeless look and design, good for business travelers and tourists. The checkin sometimes can be a zoo, and there was no turn-down service with fresh towels last time I stayed.

This hotel is in the heart of Manhattan with its Times Square location. Good for sightseeing and Broadway. Staff were polite & helpful and the rooms were clean. We in fact had 2 stays here and both rooms were equally well kept, the second being a free upgrade to the Premier section of the hotel. We were a little apprehensive after reading previous reviews about bedbugs but we saw no evidence of this and slept well.

Great stay in this perfect located hotel.
This hotel has a great front desk team taking care of guests

review_title: Do not stay here they have bed bugs!!!
review_text: I stayed at this hotel because I got deal thru hotwire. I had requested non smoking room and my room smelled of smoke, when I asked to change rooms they basically didn't care and said no rooms available. Decor was awful and rooms weren't very clean. I spent 4 nights at his hotel by end if my stay I noticed red dots on my legs, back, and arms thought I had allergic reaction to something but came to find out when I got home they were BED BUG BITES !!!!!! I'm currently being treated and very upset, I will never stay at this hotel again rather pay extra 100 dollars and stay at Marriott in times square.

review_title: Perfect location, shocking rooms and disinterested staff.
review_text:
The best thing about this hotel is it's location - not even 30 seconds from the top of Times Square. However that is the only positive comment I can make.
I booked a 'Deluxe' room. Their understanding of deluxe and mine vary greatly. It was deluxe if the definition of this is shabby, dated and cheap.
The room I booked was for three people - a queen bed and a sofa bed. It took three requests and eight hours to get the sofa bed made up. To call the reception staff disinterested is an understatement.
The attached cafe was also shabby and dated. At least it offered consistency. The deli next door (Danny's) was by far the better option.
This hotel has an excellent location. Other than that, I can sadly recommend no more.

Could not have been happier with our recent stay. Everyone we had contact with exceeded our expatiations. The front desk staff were very efficient and helpful. The rooms, while not what you could call large, were very adequate and clean. Best of all was the location. Just 1/2 block from Times Square. It does not get any better. The next time we visit NYC, this is where we will stay.
Spent 5 days in this magnificent hotel. Its right on times square. Amazing place to stay.

review_title: This is a terrible hotel with extremely rude staff.
review_text: The room is a hotwire mystery hotel and it is in a good location if your a first time tourist to NYC . Otherwise the service is horrible and the hotel is old and gross. The lights went out 5 times during our 4 night stay. The staff took about 30 minutes to fix it everytime because apparently it wasn't a big enough issue to them. We selected a room for 3 people and they gave us a room with 1 full size bed. We had to battle them for a roll away, because they weren't going to give us that. To top it off when were leaving the baggage guy was extremely rude and refused to give us our bags. Overall this is a great hotel for you if you don't care about service ,cleanness, and comfort!

My wife and I celebrated our 10 year anniversary at this hotel from 6/28-7/2. The front desk guy was great at check in. He hooked us up with a great view. The guy working at the concierge was decent. The lady at concierge was great and gave us directions. The room was great and the bed was ok. The location was awesome!! Overall had a great time and experience at this hotel. Try the Times deli across the street its awesome.

review_title: A very comfortable hotel in the heart of Times Square
review_text: I had read mixed reviews about this hotel. I found it was very comfortable and clean. Rooms were large with good sized bathrooms. Price was excellent for New York. I had a great view of Times Square. All for $250/ night. Concierge was very helpful as were the porters and desk staff.. I would definitely stay there again

W0W-this is fantastic place close to Times Square-they provide breakfast and happy hour drinks!!!make use of happy hour as the prices in Times Sq are exhorbitant! Will stay there again! Great Value! Location in a very Gentrified Location!

review_title: Great location. I'd stay here again.
review_text: Just got back from New York vacation. We stayed at Milennium Hotel Broadway and it was just fine. The location is outstanding. Just a few steps off Times Square which is nice because you can get through the doors without having to fight through a crowd. But you are really right there where the action is. Hotel was clean, nothing too fancy or really anything special but definitely a decent place to stay.
Great hotel! Amazing location, best staff at any hotel I've ever stayed in.
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City

review_title: Busy location with easy Subway access
review_text: I stayed for one-night on business and was upgraded to a suite. The bed was extremely comfortable and the gym was larger than average with quality equipment. There is a subway stop directly outside of the hotel and food options are plentiful. The hotel seems to have recently completed renovations, which were well done. Ask for lounge access - there is warm breakfast and drinks available.
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City

review_text: I was going to give this place 4 stars for service and accommodations but on our last morning in the hotel my husband and I noticed our legs were itching and covered with red bites!!!!. You can draw whatever conclusions you want from this review. I have painfully swollen bitten legs that itch like crazy!.
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City

review_title: Bell hotel al centro di NY a 2 passi dalla fifth avenue

This is a great hotel in a great location. The only downside was the building work that was taking place while we were there. It started early at 7am, however it was useful to get us up early for sightseeing!
Staff were excellent, as was the room; would definitely stay here again.

This hotel was within perfect distance to the subway, grand central, park & Madison ave, and central park. I thought the rooms were a little lacking particularly because my room had the empty space for a mini fridge but no fridge! In addition I had a few issues with the cleaning but the staff promptly responded when called. Bell hop was super nice!
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City

review_text: Stayed from 14-18 December and were pleased. Good size room, clean, helpful staff and amazing burgers! The bed was also very comfortable. We were on 28th floor facing the construction and the noise really wasn't that bad, although it was incredibly loud in the lobby and bar areas during the day. If your looking for real luxury, don't stay here, but if you want a decent hotel in an excellent location, you can't go wrong with this place.
