Tienes cafe y leche gratis. Ideal para el desayuno. NO desayunes aquÃ­, solo coge el cafe (en la maquina gratuita) y luego busca lo que te apetezca por los alredores

Ubicato fra la quinta e la sesta strada, quindi nel centro della grande mela. Sevizio impeccabile, estrema pulizia, personale sempre disponibile, la colazione non Ã¨ inclusa ma a disposizione dei clienti una macchina automatica per caffÃ¨ cappuccini e cioccolata. A pochi passi dalla fermata rossa della metro. A pochi passi da central park, apple e tutti i principali negozi. A pochi metri dal moma, rockefeller...se volete visitare manhattan non sbaglierete scegliendo questo stupendo albergo. Buone vacanze.

Stayed at this hotel room for 4 nights and had a pleasant stay. This hotel has a superb location with loads of sight seeing and shopping trips within a short walk.
Slightly disappointed with the standard of the rooms but they were clean and the maid service was good. 
Staff were very helpful and friendly especially Rafael the bell boy and Juan Carlos who served me every morning at breakfast.
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City

review_title: Good service, but did I wake up in Ikea?
review_text:
We live in the area, so we have been to the hotel's restaurants, but had never stayed in the rooms. During the holidays, we needed a place to stay and figured we should give it try since I could pay with Starwood points.
We have been to Norma's, which has been a consistently great brunch spot. This time was no exception, as the service and food were exceptional.
So why the low ratings? If you like Ikea and amenities from 2002, enjoy. The rooms, while large, are severly outdated with seemingly cheap appointments, CRT TVs, and desperate need of bathroom updates. 
I suppose nobody stays here for the rooms, as the excellent location and service make it worthwhile. But the rooms just bothered me. If you are spending your hard earned money or points and are very picky, this hotel may let you down.
Oh, and please avoid the Burger Joint. It is a joke and not worth the money. Save yourself the cash and head to Burger Heaven, Five Guys, anywhere.....just don't buy into the hype.
So positives: Norma's, location, service.
Negatives: Outdated decor, very expensive, a bit of a tourist trap.
If you are a travel snob, you will appreciate my sentiments and may want to look elsewhere. But if you can get over the rooms and get a good deal, the location and service may overshadow my claims.

review_title: Disappointing value, do not stay for business
review_text:
I travel for work and stay in nice hotels at least 50-60 times a year. This was by far my greatest disappointment. While i know NYC hotels are expensivea at $650/night I expected a hotel on par with the Four Seasons in LA or Seattle or the Mandarin in SF, boy was I wrong. I'm ok with small rooms which it was, but it was old and outdated. It had a 36" old CRT tv that was in a huge cylinder taking up half the room. The bathroom is something you would expect in a motel for $49/night. I was scared to sleep in the bed as it appeared dirty. And they wanted to charge me $17/day for in room wifi. 
What really got me was after staying three nights and dropping $2k for a crappy room, there was no paper delivery so I asked the front desk for a paper and they said that will be $2! With that I walked out and will never go back again. I would suggest to look elsewhere for your business stay.
Stayed during restaurant week. Employees very friendly. Location in Times Square is amazing. Great value too.

The hotel has a charm and elegance worth the price. The location is convenient to almost everything around central park. The bar invites intimates converasations in a lux environment. A great experience!
Concierge will get you anywhere you need to be and the service is second to none

review_title: In a good spot for Midtown Manhattan
review_text: I come to Manhattan for work and always stay here. It's conveniently located to many favorite tourist spots as well as my work, so it works out well. The hotel bar is really nice, always packed and serves up a good drink here and there. Right across the street kitty corner is a starbucks for the diehards. The rooms are decent sized for a New York hotel (some can be quite small) and comfortable and clean. Convenient gift shop for snacks or quick souveniers. Shopping is within walking distance in just about any direction.
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City

review_text: Well located but dirty and with unpolite staff! This is certainly the worst hotel I have already been! Old furniture, bad beds, terrible A.C. the bathtubs are always dirty and there are not refrigerators for every room. The worst of all is that they are very disorganized. We made reservations for two rooms with twin bads and when we alrrived they wanted us friends to share a double bad! When we checked out they tried to overcharge a friend of mine for calls she didn't make. And ir you are looking for a charming place Times Square is not the place!

All the previous reviews are correct- the rooms are 'cool' but tiny and hotel offers no creature comforts; bathroom (nothing beyond soap & shampoo etc, paper cups), very basic breakfast (on paper plates), we took our own bags up etc.
However the hotel was the best value I could find in the area. The subway is metres away, round the corner bars that are opened till late (cool east village types), the main strip of Broadway shops is 5 mins walk (chainstores: zara, topshop, h&m etc) soho is about 6 mins away (where I preferred; you get the unique boutiques, cafes, Lomardi's- best NY pizza, MoMa design store) I wish I found how close it was earlier! You have to walk through some barren areas first, but like most of this area it's part of the charm.
The area was perfect for what we wanted out of new York for the 4 nights (catching up with friends in nearby bars/restaurants, shopping). The city is huge and it is best to pick 1 area and explore it well. I was told by our friend in NY that the room size is pretty much standard for the price & area but a few more creature comforts would have made up for it. If you want to be closer to all the sites perhaps midtown is better, but we enjoyed the culture that this area has.

I must start this review by saying that the hotel looks lovely and has that boutique feel about it, but from a practical point of view it is a terrible hotel if you are traveling with large suitcases and are staying a long time.
We had a room on the third floor in the very corner of the building. Â We had been in NYC for over a week already and had 5 nights at Hotel East Houston. Â Our room was tiny. There was virtually no hanging space for your clothes. The space provided was a corner cupboard that has what could be best described as a clothes hook with five coat hangers on it. We had two large suitcases which we had to put close to the door. Â We were always tripping over the suitcases to try and get out of the room. Â There was just no space.
My partner decided to go for a walk within 30 minutes of being in the room, because it was impossible to try and unpack with 2 people in the room. Â As he was standing in the lobby looking at the tourist pamphlets, a male guest approached the front desk demanding a refund. He had just arrived, went up to his room, saw it was tiny and not what was described on the website and wanted to leave immediately. Â When he asked to speak to the manager, he was told that the manager was on leave and could not be contacted. He did not receive a refund, but still left.
Back to our room....
The bed (very comfortable and clean) takes up almost all of the room space. You can barely walk from the far edge of the bed to the other side. I had to walk over my partner at night if I wanted to get up.
The room was exceptionally dark at night. Â There are two reading lights mounted over each side of the bed and a light in the passage between the door and the tiny square space the bed was in, which did not really help. We had to turn on the tv to get further light. The bathroom lighting was good.Â 
I called down to reception to ask if they had any other rooms. Â The woman told me they were fully booked and that we had one of her 'favorite rooms'. When I told her it was very dark she told me that we had a good room, and the rooms at the back of the property had less light.
We were on the third floor and on East Houston Street. Â It was very noisy. There is a lot of night life on East Houston Street many nights of the week so be prepared for this.
On the second day, we returned to our room to discover that our room had been cleaned, bed made, but they had not replaced the hand towel, bath mat, plastic drinking cups or the shampoo and conditioner.
On the plastic drinking cup thing, this hotel is too cool to offer any sort of creature comforts, aside from the bvlgari shampoo, conditioner moisturizer and soap. Â No kettle, coffee, tea, glasses, iron, safe, minibar. Â There was a hairdryer.
On the third day I approached the receptionist about checking out early and what the cancellation fee would be. Â I was told that our total for the five nights stay would be charged regardless of when we checked out.
This hotel would be okay for people traveling to NYC for short stay (one or two nights at most) without any large luggage. Any seasoned traveller who is familiar with good hotels will find Hotel East Houston a big disappointment.
Hope this review helps.
Located within walking distance to most all the sites. My daughter was playing in he Macy's parade and we were able to walk right out the door and see the parade

review_title: Great location, ideal place to stay in NY
review_text: Our second stay at this hotel in the past 18 months. Yes the rooms do need updating but the location is perfect as a base to explore NY city. All interaction I had with staff was really positive.
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City

review_title: Good for tourists and business travers
review_text:
Location great - subway stop right next to the hotel.
Service: Friendly.
Lobby perfume smells too strong.
Room was clean and modern,Â Air conditioning unit outdated.
Good toiletries - Crabtree & Evelyn, including a Sewing kit which i ended up needing.
Hair dryer not good.
Shower has the curved shower rod which is great, but the shower curtain smelled skunky.
Trash bins have a receptacle for recycables.
Complimentary newspaper.
Wifi is chargeable but reasonable (15-17$) compared to other NYC hotels.
Limited dine in hours 6-10 AM/PM.Â Several Room service trays were still left out more than 12 hours - that can bring bugs.
Can buy tickets to shows right at the hotel.
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City

review_text:
The hotel is next door to a huge construction project. The whole hotel literally shakes from the jack hammering. You can't rest at all between 7AM and 6PM which is a huge issue when you are traveling with small children. I asked if anything could be done. I was offered nothing in compensation for the annoying noise. In addition, it wss rather warm jis weekend for standard NYC standards. Good luck trying to sleep In a room that is 80+ degrees. They Dont have the abaility to change temperature In each Room!!! Either everyone gets heat or cool. This weekend it was heat only!!! 
So if you enjoy resting with the rattle of a jackhammer in 80 degree heat, this is the perfect hotel for you!!
Management is put off by asking for special requests and their only response is "I am sorry sir.". This hotel is way overpriced an the service is very I accommodating and rude.

The overall hotel was great, the location is very convinient and close to a subway. The room service was quick and the food was good. 
The only issues were the breakfast that could be improved but apart from that the service is efficient and the bar at the hotel is very nice.

review_title: TrÃ¨s Moyen, Hotel Bruyant, Chambres non chauffÃ©es.
review_text:
Hotel trÃ¨s dÃ©cevant.
Chambres a la propretÃ© moyennes.
De trÃ¨s petites tailles.
Chambres bruyantes et mal placÃ©es.
Vis a Vis laid ( donnant sur mur intÃ©rieur).
A EVITER !!!!

Brought a group to stay at the hotel for one night only. Sales dept was great! Loved Knave and the burger joint. Positive, smiling staff despite the horrendous drilling and construction going on next door. Will definitely stay there again!

review_title: Gradevolissimo hotel ubicato in posizione ottimale.
review_text: Abbiamo soggiornato per 8 notti. Studio suite molto ampia, cosa non comune negli hotel di New York, e confortevole. Posizione decisamente ottimale. Dovendo trovare un difetto, trovo eccessivo il costo totale di una colazione servita in camera per due persone, richiedendo items tipo: caffÃ¨ cappuccino croissants yogurt succo d'arancia+tasse+servizio+altro addebito, diventa quasi il costo di una cena. Considerando l'offerta disponibile in giro.... in fondo credo sia controproducente per l'hotel.
La verdad es que tengo muy buen recuerdo, estaba reciÃ©n reformado con todo muy nuevo y limpio. nos atendieron muy bien y estÃ¡ muy centrico.

Estuvimos alojados el aÃ±o pasado y lo mas destacado de este hotel es la ubicaciÃ³n, a dos pasos del times square y de gran central terminal, sin olvidarnos de la gran quinta avenida. La habitaciÃ³n era pequeÃ±a pero confortable, ah! Y no tiene moqueta!!!!!

review_title: A bit rough around the edges, but has character and served its purpose.
review_text: We stayed at this hotel last week, and were quite pleased with our stat. It is an art deco style building, and the lobby is fantastic. The valet service was so convenient - except that when we checked in, the girl at the desk took our valet ticket! We thought this was weird, but figured that since we said we wouldn't take it out until leaving, she was just going to keep it in a room file or something... We were wrong! We did get our car back but it was a hassle. Our room was a king and a pullout couch (we took turns). When we got in, the room smelled very smoky, and the air conditioning didn't work. We bought some febreze which helped the smell, but there was no solution to the a/c. That week was so hot, we really wish it worked. Nevermind, though - we had a cold shower every night which really helped. The location is great. So close to times square (closer than we thought) but we couldnt hear it. There was construction across the street all night, but we wore ear plugs anyway, so that wasn't a problem. It was clean, and the bed was comfy (the rollaway was what you'd expect). The bellhop who helped us as we left was so kind, and told us all about the hotel's past famous guests. We ate at Cafe Edison every morning, which was perfect for what we needed!! We'd return, but only if we weren't going in the summer. The lack of air conditioning made the room too hot!

Hotel was living a little on past glories, and trying to be a little too cool, I was lucky upgraded my colleagues not so and they had some bad tales, on the negative my fridge didn't work, safe was locked, toilet blocked, on the plus good size room, prett good service bar reception and great location.

This hotel is located right next to times square with fairly close access to the subway as well. We had a special deal on this hotel which made it worthwhile value. Overall our stay was good, the room was clean though a bit outdated, no fan in the bathroom. If you were paying $300+ a night I would expect a much larger room. Staff were friendly apart from one at the front desk that was extremely rude when a friend had dropped off a parcel for me to collect. If you are looking to be close to times square there is not really anything closer, but definitely get out and explore the rest of New York

review_title: Great location, not so great hotel.
review_text:
We recently took our kids to New York for the first time. We wanted to be close to time square. The hotel Edison is in a great location, close to all of the shows. The rooms however were very poor. Very thing in the hotel looked like it hasn't been touched in 50 years, the 
carpets were filthy, electrical outlets were jerry rigged with extension 
cords, and the service at the restaurant was interesting to say the least. For $300/night, this midwest girl was far from Kansas.

review_title: Great location. No wait perfect location!!!!!
review_text: When you visit NY you don't come for the hotel you come to see the city. The Edison hotel is a good hotel. It's not perfect but the room are a good size and are clean. The beds are somewhat firm but I had no problem passing out from walking the city all day. The staff was awesome!!! Out first 2 nights we had a jackhammer taring up concrete below us at 7am the staff moved us to the other side of the hotel right away. The LOCATION IS PERFECT!!!! your right on times square. Stay here!

review_title: Love Noise? This is your place!
review_text:
Astoundingly awful stay of six nights where ever weekday started out with outrageous pounding each morning at 7:30 AM. The room was 80 degrees we called engineering. They came and -poor guy - had been to like seven rooms before ours and each time he had to explain that there was no AC but he could open the window. $400 a night and no AC. Amazing. He opened the window a bit and the room did cool off. The next morning the pounding started promptly at the noted time and continued ALL day. We were here for six nights and luckily two of the nights were Friday and saturdayl so we did get a slight reprieve. I don't know why the front desk staff hasn't quit en masse the pounding, is even worse in the lobby. The rooms were not that nice given the price and the spigot in the shower was hanging by the pipe and made an awful noise when you pulled up the thing to turn it into a shower. 
I would NEVER recommend any one I liked to stay here. Seriously - really really bad noise problems. Really!

review_title: Other than location and being part of the Starwood Family, this hotel has little going for it
review_text: I have stayed at this property at least a dozen times for no other reason than it is part of the Starwood Group. However, the rooms are very small, the beds and pillows are rock hard (NOT the heavenly beds), and their idea of an upgrade for a platinum member is to go from the 12th floor to the 30th floor. Additionally, there is major construction that starts with a pile driver at 7 am weekdays and eir is no warning posted on the website to warn of these conditions like so many other Starwood Hotels post.

We were a little dubious about staying here from all the reviews! On arrival for 8 nights we were told that the only room they had booked for us (we booked back in Jun 11) was a double bed.....um there are 2 adults & 2 children. It wasn't looking good but in the end he rearranged & we got 2 doubles - phew!!!!! The rooms are like a matchbox but hey we are in NYC & we only sleep here! The free breakfast is great, limited seating but we have not had trouble getting one & the hotel is completely dull! Location is good we are walking everywhere & it's about a 10 minute walk to Times Square (kids are 8 & 5!). The diamond district is interesting & if your not interested I suggest u avoid as they all stand outside trying to hustle u in. It's an absolute must to do the 9/11 memorial but make sure you book your tickets online that's the only way you can get the tickets. Also we used a go pass which yes saved us time buying tickets but there wA no express line as promised for any of the attractions! Also as we were here for so long we were desperate for a coin laundromat which noone could help us with - if you go to 9th avenue between 50th & 51st there are heaps of them!
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express New York City Fifth Ave

review_text: Myself and my boyfriend have recently visited New York and stayed at this hotel. Everything about our stay was excellent. The service upon arrival and check out, the cleanliness of the room, the helpful and friendly attitude of all staff. Not to mention the efficiency of the room service. Its location is between times square and central park off a busy and loud street, however the room was quiet and provided us with a peaceful sanctuary when we needed it. Rooms on the small side, but doesn't matter as you're in new York, who spends too much Time in their room anyway! Highly recommended. Enjoy,!

Stayed at Le Parker Meridien for the first time in over 15 years. This NY gem is better than ever. Fantastic gym and a pool. A POOL in New York. This is a rare find. Rooms are very nice, beds comfortable. 
Burger restaurant is among the best in Manhattan. Do not miss this!
I arrived late in the day in the heart of rush hour. Took the Q subway to 57th street then a 1 block walk. It was just all so convenient. Met the hotel owner while waiting for the elevator. Good to see attention to detail comes from the top. Overall a strong recommendation for this property.

Really enjoyed our stay at this hotel, the location was great, the rooms were clean, everyone was polite. 
If you want a nice clean hotel that is reasonably priced then look no further then this hotel.
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City

review_text: We stayed here for 5 days, no dramas. The hotel is located just across the Times Square. If you require basic accommodation just for sleeping in new york city, this is the right hotel for you

This is my first trip to New York city and I didn't really know the areas well but from the reviews that i read about this hotel, it has a good location and quite good priced at that time so I chose this hotel. 
When i first arrived i thought i chose wrong. The streets are a bit quite and i was shocked to see the size of the room. It was very small for the two of us. It was even small for just one person and the door made a noise when we opened it. So i was a bit stressed out especially since we already paid in full for 7 nights stay. 
But the room was surprisingly clean and quiet. I hardly hear any noise from the street the whole time we stayed there.
The best part about this hotel is the location. It's only about 2 blocks away from Times Square and it's convenient, we never have to take the subway or taxi. And the nearest subway station is alo not far from the hotel.
I would consider staying here again the next time i'm in new york if i get a good deal.

Absolutely no complaints!! Room was clean and quiet!! Complimentary breakfast was very nice.
Would definitely stay again!!
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express New York City Fifth Ave

review_title: Needs to be upgraded and cleaned - stay away from this tourist trap!!!
review_text: Why don't they invest some of the profit into rooms? Our room had old ripped carpet, lamps with holes in the shades, mold in the bathroom.

review_title: Pay in full at check-in = buyer beware.
review_text:
I would like to state first that small rooms are not bothersome, as we are accustomed to boutique hotels. Room size is not this hotel's problem... At all. It is, however, everything else. The website advertises "cheap" as a hallmark, to which I will personally attest-- an undoubtedly and unfortunate Freudian slip, dooming our stay from the get-go.
Though the hotel is located along the lighting supply retail hub of SoHo, the owners/designer have missed the mark in lighting design in the lobby. I have read reviews describing it as bordello-esque. I see it as kitschy Village-wannabe New Jersey trash: too many themes to even be considered designer chic or eclectic. Note to the management: cute chairs, cute lighting, awful paint palette, ALWAYS REMOVE THE PLASTIC FROM YOUR LAMPSHADES... What are you- Fran Drescher's family from 'The Nanny?'
The check-in process was streamlined, though please keep in mind: you pay in FULL at check-in. Buyer beware. They have you by the cojones should you encounter an irreconcilable difference (the plastic covering the lampshades JUST about did it). Staff are helpful enough and a solitary, hard-working bellman will help you with your bags to the best his slim frame can muster. Note: this hotel requires stair climbing (read: no elevators), which is also not a deal breaker for us. Good exercise and easy staircases to climb. 
Let's discuss the god awful rug runners down the hallways. Management- you've covered your poorly laid laminate floors with the most awful and poorly laid oriental rugs in Chinatown. And you've apparently left them there for 10 years with not so much as one shampoo!?!?! The horror! Folks. If this is SoHo chic, you will find me in the Upper East Side next visit. 
Moving to the room. Small quantifies size appropriately in most rooms here but not bothersomely so. What bugs me is the management will upgrade you to a room with more beds than you need for free so you're "more comfortable." Actually, no. I'm not more comfortable. You've put me in the same size room crammed with more beds. We sleep together, we are not amoebas, we do not divide into more guests, therefore more beds with less room WILL NOT be convenient. The rooms are bland, poorly designed (as in no esthetics), and unrefined for a self-proclaimed boutique hotel. The television wires hand from the wall as tackily [sic] as the plastic covered chandelier in the lobby. The furniture looks as if it is trying to be antique eclectic (God, I hope) but fails miserably. It's dinged and it's plywood and it's awful looking. That seedy hostel I stayed in in Germany was furnished better. The A/C, bless its heart, rattled worse than my grandmother's dentures. The artwork was hung on a fabulous exposed brick wall. The paintings were hideous and likely from Wal-Mart. It was a disservice and slap in the face to that gorgeous brick wall. The brick wall was glazed to prevent crumbling mortar (I assume). Well, the mortar crumbled... On my bed... Under the bed sheets. Either housekeeping didn't take note of this when they made the bed or they simply didn't care to brush off the abrasive pumice treatment before I got into bed. P.S. The beds are divitted neatly where previous bodies have lain. Management: invest in nicer pillow top mattresses or change out your el-cheapos more often. 
The bathroom was well appointed and marbled, well, mostly. My problem with the bathroom: nasty dust bunnies clogging the exhaust fan and grout that was in bad need of a toothbrush scrubbing or regrouting all together. Call me a prude, but boutique hotels are known for using neat, obscure toiletries for guests. Not here... As hohum as the artwork. 
On a bright note, morning coffee was killer. Nicely roasted and great temperature. I'll forgive the cheesy micromini styrofoam cups. They dim in comparison to the plastic lamp shade covers surrounding the coffee service. 
We didn't get mugged. We didn't get bed bugs. We didn't have to shower with cold water. Some might say this was a success in NY, NY. Pshaw. I know great boutique hotels are out there. The SoHotel (aka the HohumHotel or the SoHostel) is not among their ranks. My vote is to keep driving and find another bordello to snuggle into.

This hotel is overpriced for what you get. There are no elevators. 
The rooms are small. In some rooms there is hardly any room to walk or put your suitcase. 
The rooms are sparsely decorated and crowded. 
There are no phones in the rooms. If you want to call the desk you have to use your cell phone. 
The Internet is slow and undeniable. 
There is only one plug in every room to plug in any equipment or appliances. 
The hair dryers in the room are slow and hardly put out any air. 
We had to change rooms twice. One room the fan didn't work and the next one the toilet stopped up. I asked for a disount and did not get one. 
I will never stay there again.

review_title: Great location and very cool hotel
review_text: This hotel is located in a great part of town! Right by Soho, Little Italy and Nolita which are all very trendy. Great places to eat out at near by. The hotel is very cool and the rooms were great! Clean, comfortable beds and quiet.
From the super friendly staff to the great location (only 5-10 min walk to Times Square) you cannot go wrong staying at this hotel. Would stay here again in a heartbeat.

This hotel is in a good location on w51st so definitely walking distance to times square. 
The rooms are extremely tiny though and the girl who checked us in advised that we had been upgraded to a slightly bigger room...would hate to see what the smaller one looks like. 
The service wasn't good, the check in girl seemed like she couldn't be bothered and the doorman was no where in sight, which was a bit annoying when the entrance is only stairs and you have big suitcases. 
Apart from that it is a good budget hotel if you want to be in the thick of it all. Although I'd recommend booking something like airbnb where you actually stay in someones apartment - we did that for the remainder of our trip and it was amazing. For the same price we got an apartment with a kitchen and computer with internet.

review_title: Very nice hotel in great location
review_text: My husband and I stayed in Sohotel in june for his birthday. We had a wonderful time. This hotel is in a great location in Chinatown. The room was cozy and clean and had its own bathroom. (We loved the decor) We were impressed with the friendly staff who went out of their way to make us feel welcomed. We will stay here again.

review_title: Would not recommend Herald Square Hotel
review_text: Room, including sheets was dirty. Not worth staying here.

review_title: FOUR WORDS: INFLATABLE RAT, BED BUGS!!!
review_text: FOUR WORDS: INFLATABLE RAT, BED BUGS!!! I don't know how I'm going to survive 3 night here. Ny is.gross but this welcoming was by far a bit much! The room.is totally run down and dingy. Bathroom is awful! Yuk!
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City

review_text:
Stayed here recently for 4 nights and could not really fault it.Here to see New York and not moan about the hotel rooms.The hotel does need an uplift which is now taking place.did not use the cafe but the recently refurbished bar was excellent.Hotel can get very busy but never had to wait long for service,Donna and Youseff on reception were a credit to the hotel. Location is perfect for Times Square and shall hopefully be returning next year
.

review_title: If you love Chelsea, this is the perfect location.
review_text:
Two of my friends and I stayed here during NYC Marathon weekend as we were here to cheer on a friend who was running. The location was great for us (between 6th and 7th), half way between downtown (we visited the 9/11 Memorial) and the Theatre District, so we were able to get to both with less than a $10 cab ride. 
The room was a good size, especially for a Manhattan hotel. We stayed on the 7th floor facing the street, which was not surprising, quite noisy on Saturday night. I would recommend asking for a room on the back side on the hotel. 
Also, there is great food and bars one street over on 26th. We ate at Tre Dici (I think that's the name) on Friday night and it was amazing... And we could easily walk (stumble) back to the hotel after a fun night out.
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan Chelsea

review_title: Can't beat the location or the bar downstairs.
review_text: If you are not familiar with the city but want close access to great food then this is the place for you. Have great happy hour tequila specials in the bar and whole foods around the corner. Need to pick up a baby shower gift so try Schneider's Juvenile not too far away. Lots of access to Zipcar too which makes touring the city fun and easy. Rooms are basic and a little tight but fir 1 person it is fine.
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan Chelsea

review_text: Stayed there for four nights to explore entire Manhattan. We did not have a "new" room and ours was to the street. What should we say? The hotel itself did have an athmosphere rather like a hostel than a hotel. The floors were kind of smelly. Our room was clean and o.k., however, should be redone soon. It was quite loud since the window to the street was not shut entirely because of the a.c. Still, what is perfect about the hotel is the location. Many sights are in walking distance and you can easily access several subway lines in a couple of minutes walk. Also, there are several dining and breakfast choices around, especially at Herald Square. All in all worth staying if one gets a good deal, does not need more than a clean room and a bed and might wanna choose a "new" room.

Das Hotel ist nahe des Times Square. Zimmer sind klein, was nicht weiter stÃ¶rt. Nervig sind die schlecht isolierten Fenster. Man hatte das GefÃ¼hl bei offenem Fenster zu schlafen, so laut war es. Es ist kein "Traum" mÃ¶glich, da Nachts zu laut? Durch die NÃ¤he zum Times Square, Subway und Central Park, ist das Hotel aber zu empfehlen.

Great hotel in great location. Rooms have been refurbished and we had a queen room which was very big with a massive bathroom which had aveda products which was a lovely touch. This hotel is great value for such a good hotel considering what new york charges for its hotels. Second time to this hotel and will always use it as it is right around the corner from macys and a lovely deli called speedys.
Great location and friendly staff. We will be back.

review_title: All you need, some of what you want.
review_text: In early Dec I took a school group of teenage boys to NYC from Australia. The Travel Inn was a good choice for a home base whilst there for a week. It's inexpensive, in a great location and the rooms are a decent size. There are no frills but the boys thought it was a cool place. The staff at the front desk consistently looked annoyed whenever you fronted there and paying for wireless was a daily pain in the butt. But really all this wasn't enough for me to not recommend this place when wanting a cheap place to stay. I'd be booked it again.

I thought that because this is part of the Hilton chain, the rooms would be good. I was wrong. 
The foyer of the hotel is nice enough, with a decent bar, but I'm here to sleep, and the rooms are awful. I stayed in a room which had connecting doors to the rooms either side. These let through the noise badly (they leave ear plugs by the bed!). The bed is strange and very small, and although the room has a sofa, you can't see the TV from it. The room layout is bad, and unattractive. 
There's no fridge/mini bar and no tea or coffee making facilities, which makes for a more expensive stay and less convenience. 
The location is good, but there are plenty of other better value places. Don't risk staying here. 
The final straw was the bed bug scare. They've apparently had an issue with bed bugs but don't think this affected us. We found out about this after we arrived which made for a few phantom (or maybe real) itches.
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City

review_title: Great if you're not staying in too much
review_text: The Edison Hotel is in a superb location in New York literally seconds from Times Square. The Lobby area is stunning with a concierge service, baggage and transport service, cafe, bar and gift shop. The overall service was excellent although the transport service were reluctant to help as much as others in the hotel. The hotel has 22 floors including rooms and a free fitness suite. Our room was very dated and not very clean and on complaining the cleaner said if we didn't like it we'd have to move rooms. The heating in our room was extremely loud when on so we had to keep it off overnight. Overall a lovely hotel but poor room so perfect if you're not staying in much!! Refurbishment is however going on and the newer rooms do appear to be very nice!

Surprised to see that the room was much better than the lobby area. Room has a nice comfy bed, and everything is clean. A/C works well. Name brand toiletries is a plus. Location is within walking distance to Empire State Building, Penn Station and Times Square.
One more thing I did not like when you shower the water does not go down fast so you are standing in s pool of water which is nasty and the sink water also would go down very slow too

This hotel is decorated in the art deco style and was probably once quite smart. The public areas look to have been refreshed recently and the bar was closed for refurb when we were there but our room was pretty shabby. Great location though and all you need if you're doing the tourist trail. The diner downstairs is good for traditional breakfast (cash only!) and the guys on the door are really helpful

I stayed here for the weekend of dec4 to dec5... It was one of the cheaper hotel in NYC, we got to our hotel the front person was nice. The rooms were small but clean! But it was too hot we turned the heater off but still was hot!!! That's the only thing i didnt like about it. The hotel was close to great restaurant and 8 min walk to time square close to great shopping stores!! Next time I go to NYC again I will stay here again!!

review_title: This is a good place to stay in Chelsea
review_text: Located on a relatively quiet side street, this relatively small hotel has reasonably nice rooms (medium-size by NY standards) and is clean. The elevators are slow because there are only 2 and 22 stories (each floor does not have many rooms). There is an outdoor cafe/restaurant which is nicely situated as it is in a recess from the street. The front desk service can be slow as the area is small.
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan Chelsea

review_text: It was a good hotel, we were on the fourth floor at the front to start with and it was a bit noisy as there is a mexican bar directly below (which has very good drinks and nachos!) we asked to be moved and they did this straight away and they put us on the 7th floor where we could not hear anything as it was at the back of the hotel. The maid cleaned our room everyday very well. The only thing would be that the wardrobes and furniture need updating but it was not a big deal. The beds were very comfortable and overall we were pleased with this hotel.
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan Chelsea

review_text:
We stayed at the Four Points for 13 nights in August and absolutely loved our stay. Â We had a standard room with 2 double beds. Â The rooms were a bit small as they all are in NYC but the location and hospitality of the staff makes up for it! We had a 1 yr old with us and they provided us with a portacot & a microwave which was great. The location is fantastic! It's a 15 min walk to Madison square garden & about 25 mins to Times Square. If you go south, it's about 30 mins to soho and all the shopping on Broadway St. If you don't want to walk its close to a subway on either 23rd on 6th or 7th ave. There's a Wholefoods across the road on 7th and a massive baby store on the other side (for mums it's like a toysrus but better! Lots of cool stuff for babies in this store). Â  The Wholefoods stock everything from groceries to cooked food. Â The hotel didn't have a fridge in the room so storage in the hot weather was an issue. The rooms had air conditioning which is a must in the hot weather.Â 
There's no place in the hotel for breakfast but being NYC there are coffee shops everywhere (Starbucks)! There's no shortage of places to eat or have a coffee. Â We found a nice place on 23rd street called RUB for ribs one night. Also the hotel is near the fashion schools and bridal boutiques.Â 
Our room 702 was towards the back of the building directly above the bar downstairs. It can get quite noisy up until the bar closes around 10 or 11pm but after that it's pretty quiet. We had no issues with street noise since we were in the back of the building.Â 
Our rooms & beds were done daily and the beds are nice and comfortable. Transfers to and from the airport took about an hour. We used a private car (Golden Limo) when we arrived and a shuttle (Super Shuttle) when we left. Â Both good services. Â 
We would definitely stay here again!
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan Chelsea

review_text: Stopped at the travel inn while running the marathon. Great location just a 5 min walk from times square. Great deli next door, clean and tidy room just a little dated. No kettle in the room but we improvise microwaving cups of water. The lift to the second block had a mind of its own so expect to hang around a few minutes each time you use it. Outside seven floors down roadworks seemed to be going 24hrs but they do say it's the city that never sleeps, cant blame that on the hotel though better quality windows may have helped. All in all a good location at a fair price

I have stayed in a few NYC hotels and this one was by far the best ever. I stayed in a queen size new room, loved the hardwood floors! I didn't have to worry about whose been on the carpet! Bathroom was beautiful and spotless! Only problem was it took awhile to get warm water but it's an old building. Bed was defiantly comfortable and amazing! Brand new tv with great channels! Close to subway also!
We had a Nice stay here. There was construction going on at The time of our stay so The rooms were noisy during the day. Otherwise a wonderful time at this hotel.

review_title: Good room for the price being close to subway, grocery, diners and Time Sq.
review_text: Overall good stay. Most inexpensive we found on the mid west side. Closer to Times Sq than you might think. Was in the theater district and is only a few feet from the Emporium grocery store and a CVS pharmacy. Theater Row diner was a good place for us for breakfast each day. Overall there isnt alot to do at the hotel but we didnt spend alot of time in the room. Room was clean and quiet. I would recommend.

In the midst of wholesale decorations and designer businesses, this hotel is my new NY oasis. At $160 a night, in August, I can't imagine a better deal in the city. Our room on the 11th floor was quiet and super-comfy. Great location in Chelsea, a Whole Foods to eat virtuously and scores of good places to eat less than virtuously. Highly recommended!
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton Manhattan Chelsea

review_title: Pretty good for a reasonable price in NYC! Handy location
review_text:
Stayed in a double double with my mum for three nights. 
Can't complain about the location at just 10min walk from Times Sq.
Rooms were generally clean (although could do with a good scrub and Hoover behind chairs in the room) but looking on the tired and dated side.
Nice to have a fridge and microwave in the room.
Rooms open onto open corridors, which surround a courtyard and the swimming pool so can be a bit noisy. 
The hotel offered the best rate room we could find in NY which is generally hideously overpriced, so on that sense it was good value, although it was expensive compared to the 4* we had just come from in Philly. 
No breakfast facilities, but a deli next door and a supermarket just a block away.
If I couldn't afford any more money, this is a good choice for couples, but next trip to NY I might see if I could afford tp push the boat put s bit more. Previously stayed in the sister hotel the Belvedere, which is a bit more plush, but also not wow. 
It's a hotel in New York- so get out of the room and enjoy the city!!!

The best parts of this hotel are the location, the 2 hotel restaurants Norma's & The Burger Joint, the service, & the pool & sun deck. 
We stayed here on points & might not return if we had to pay full value for the room. This is just because of other hotels we love that are a bit cheaper. However, it's by far the best starwood hotel in NYC if you are looking to cash in some starwood points.

review_title: Room smelled of terrible body odor
review_text: Nice hotel in nice location. Bit room smelled of terrible body odor which ruined the stay.
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City

review_title: Very good location and very clean
review_text: This hotel is in front of a police station, the rooms are very clean and comfortable. If you are looking for a hotel within budget, this is the one. Many good small restaurants are around which is always conveinent.
Location was excellent. Beds were very comfortable. Nice linens and toiletry line. Loved the longe! Very friendly & professional environment to be in. Would stay there again.

This hotel is extremely easy to get to and the staff is excellent. No coffee in rooms or hotel but deli next door is very nice. My only comlaint is the pool hours. It is only open 10-7 and I stayed there four nights and was not ever there to use it. Rooms are great for the price.

review_title: Great hotel. Avoid the Burger Joint.
review_text:
Stayed here several times. Love the location. Quiet location but still close to many spots. Very clean and quiet rooms. Great service. I always try to stay at Le parker meridien if available. 
But stay away and avoid the Burger Joint. Saw it on tv and wanted to try it. Burgers are ok. Buns are ordinary. Fries are worst. Nothing great. The service was the worst. Most unfriendly and rude service I've ever had. The cashier I had was so rude and had the worst attitude ever. 
Hotel recommend but don't bother with the Burger Joint.

Everything was perfect. My wife wanted tonswim in the pool on the top floor but we didn't have apt costume. We planned to purchase but the cheapest in that area we found was well over 50 bucks. Bring yours along if you want to take a dip. 
Checkin counter was extremely busy but it was still understandable considering the fantastic weather and also was a Saturday. Everything extra is charged and is pricey and

review_title: Quite perfect, especially the concierge service
review_text: Question: why the persons who work for conciergerie service have to be stand up all the time? It's very "derangeant"! Why don't you just let them a "bar chair" to assist us efficiently behind their desk ? You know, you have such a great concierge service, give them more comfort !

Yes the location is convenient but this is nothing special. Check in kind of unfriendly. Lobby dark utilitarian has the ambience of a train station waiting area. Hallways narrow and dark. Rooms ok size but tired.
Real negatives- no thermostat. They determine whether you get heat or cold depending on the month. Not great on a warm day in April to have heat or nothing
$15 for internet access? In 2011? Are they kidding? And difficult to even make the connection when you pay. Internet should be like electricity- a basic part of being in a hotel- like electricity or television. This is a dated policy
No coffee maker in room. No coffee in lobby. No way to get a cup of coffee but room service for $6 + service. Or walk somewhere
No refrigerators- waitlist offered but clearly that was a joke
Big inflatable rat on the sidewalk warning of bedbugs made me itch all day. I hope it was not valid but it is not a positive
Doors are tired_ locks don't work right. Bathroom door won't close or lock. Closet room right up against the bathroom door. No laundry bag. Tv awkwardly located taking up desk area. 
Outlets poorly planned
Bed was decent- as long as it does not turn out to have bedbugs!

review_title: Over all rooms where poorly kept not up to date and smelled horribly
review_text: I recently stayed in this hotel for 4 nights. The front desk was of no help and very unpleasant. The hotel hallways had a repulsive smell and where always cluttered with maid carts. The room it's self were small. Not enough space to comfortably stay with another person.not enough drawer or closet space. Most hotels I've stayed in have a coffee machine in room and complimentary bottled water this did not. It was a big inconvenience especially when you walk to the vending machine located in a smelly dirty stairwell just to find out it is not working. The bathroom sink constantly clogged. The room tempature was not able to be Controlled. You could also hear noises from outside and noise in the hallway. The only thing this hotel has going for them is the location.
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City

review_text: We stayed at the Doubletree for a six days. Without any extra fancy a normal hotel service: clean rooms, proffecional staff, free Internet in a lobby, parking right next to hotel. For my personal taste beds are a little to firm but it works anyway. Overall a good experience
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City

review_text:
We stayed at the hotel from the 7th to 11th May and had a lovely stay!
Before we left my husband emailed the hotel to request a room with a view as we were celebrating his birthday and an anniversary, we were given room 1602 which looked straight down Lexington! The room was clean, ample in size and the bed big and comfy! There are no coffee/tea making facilities in the room which was disappointing given the cafe next to the hotel commits highway robbery with their prices and this would be an easy and standard addition to the room! There is a fire station on 51st next to the hotel but in honesty this didn't keep us awake any more than the incessant taxi cabs beeping! We didn't have any problems with bed bugs and there is a hotel policy on it! We saw the blow up rat (think it's meant to be a bd bug) outside the hotel on a couple of mornings but we saw this outside hotels in the city, was more amusing than anything!!
On our first night we were delivered a conplimentary bottle of sparkling wine and a pudding to celebrate our anniversary which was a lovely touch, and shows that the staff do go out out of there way to treat customers!!
The hotel is a 5 min walk (2 blocks) from 5th ave and there is a tube stop right outside the hotel so for us was conveniently located as tourists for us!
All in all a good hotel in a convenient location and good value for the price we paid! 
Thank you to Jasmine for making our stay special!
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel Metropolitan - New York City

review_title: Perfect for a week in NYC
review_text: The only negative aspect is the tiny room. Perfect location, Clean, breakfast included, reasonable price and good staff. Perfect for a single or a couple without kids. Walking distance from all major attractions.

review_title: Great value -especially if you have a car!
review_text: This hotel might seem a bit out of the way but it is an easy walk to Times Square and the theaters. The rooms were modest and very clean. There are no in room coffee makers which is annoying but there is a deli next door and a Dunkin Donuts across the block. Small lobby area but nicely furnished.
We loved it as much as our boys (8 & 6). Great room and amenities.

The travel inn was located at an amazing location. It was right around the corner from times square. The hotel was excptionaly clean and that's including the lobby and room . But the service was alright, every day the cleaning lady would come in and try and get in when we were still in bed so this is pretty early in the morning. And I wouldn't say the lobby staff were chirpy. The room wasn't very spacious but it had a nice clean bathroom, but the tv had many channels but was very fuzzy at times. Overall I'd say it would be a comfortable stay over a long stay especially considering it location which I believe is the big seller.

Starbucks across the street, good central location, fantastic breakfast/lunch place (really surprising dishes) that is great for business meetings. There is a ridiculously loud jackhammer starting at 7 am as of the time of this review though so beware.

review_title: Good location, great burgers and a comfy bed
review_text:
Checked in on the the 26/8 for 7 nights. Check in was was reasonable although offered no help with a large bike bag from the doorman however the staff at check in offered porter service. The hotel is close to everything, central park
, subways, times square. The hotel room was pretty average considerin the asking price (we booked through expedia). When told that the going room rate was approximately $400 a night before arrival I was expecting something alot better. The air con was set to 71 degrees and came on intermittently through the night which would result in the room becomming cold enough to put the quilt on and once the thermostat kicked i woke up covered in sweat several nights. There was construction on 57th street which meant that at 0700 every morning during the week we were woken by either a jackhammer or drilling noises and could not get back to sleep, not exactly what you want when when you're on holidays (I understand this is out of the hotels control but it would have been nice to have been notified). I was in town for a cycling race and when I arrived back to the hotel at 0830 I was promptly told that I was not allowed to have my $10,000 bike in my room and it had to be stored in the garage for $15 a day. I was checking out at 1300 and told security that I was going straight up to pack it and almost had to argue the point with him. It is a little hard to understand how a hotel that is pet friendly will allow a dog or cat to releive themselves, malt and possibly chew furnishings to stay in the room but won't allow my bike to sit in the room, I can see the point if it was covered in mud but it was spotless. The charges for alot of the hotels services where exorbitant such as $17 per day per device for the net. Starbucks is across the road and offers free wifi. If you want a burger from the burger joint order it yourself and eat it in your room I think the room service charge is something like 7 or 8 bucks on a $7 burger. Staff at the hotel were helpful especially during the "hurricane". The doorman was rude and arroant just because I was wearing shorts and a t shirt and not Armani doesn't mean I'm not going to tip for hailing a cab. I told the doorman we needed an suv type taxi for my bike bag indicating to the one parked without a driver. He proceeded to hail a sedan and tried to force my bike into the boot with me telling him it would not fit, he then expected a tip after almost damaging my bike. He then ignored us for about 10 mins and when the driver of the suv came back he took the bags of another guest and put them in the boot when there was a sedan waiting knowing we needed an suv. He is you're first and last impression of the hotel.

Although your staff was very friendly, the rooms were way below what I had expected of your establishment. I was disappointed with the noise level. In addition, your coffee bar did not open until 7:30 am? I heard it was the best in the city? Oh well. I stayed at a boutique hotel around the corner from you last year. A much better experience in a much smaller property.

review_title: Nice hotel, but not the best !
review_text: We've stayed for 10 days and definitely not having free "continuous" wi-fi service is a minus, the rooms are good but the amenities are less than the average, the hotel is located in an excellent place near to Central Park and in a quiet zone. I will need to admit that having a pool at the top is a plus, despite the small size of it. Another thing you shouldn't miss is the Burger Joint which gives you the opportunity to taste an excellent hamburger.

review_title: Great remodel job for right before flat panel TVs came out.
review_text:
Park view tower room views are the best of 
NYC hotels, but rooms (especially bathrooms) are tiny even by NYC standards. Take some room design Inspiration from le meridian Philadelphia or others. Bar was great, lobby and other common areas: thumbs up. Good service - bell, door, getting cabs, etc.

review_title: Great location, impeccable service, comfortable rooms, delicious food options in the restaurants.

I could go on and on. When we left, my 7 year old said he wants to stay at this hotel every time we return. I agree with him!

review_text: Awesome. Everything from the service to the restaurants in the hotel was perfect.

Loved our stay at Le PM. It was a magical weekend. Emailed ahead about a birthday and got an upgrade to the 40th floor - Park view. Even though we were using points. Room was huge for NY. Norma's was amazing - pricey, but hey, it's got to be the best breakfast in NYC or at least one of them. Staff accommodated a last-minute suit press for the theater without a blink. We stayed with our two yo daughter and it was great. Silence is gold in NY and we all slept like babies. Penthouse floor pool and the awesome secret Burger joint in the lobby are worth the stay.

review_text:
A gorgeous little hotel for the traveller on a budget. We stayed here for two nights at the end of our US trip. It compared very favourably with the other hotel we stayed at at the start of our trip. Clean, cute little rooms. Lovely atmosphere and character. Clean, shared bathrooms. Free wifi in rooms. On a lovely street in Greenwich village, close to the subway and some lovely little restaurants. Nice European style exterior and staff were friendly. 
For this price in NY ($130ish a night), this was fantastic. Highly recommended!

Our room had complimentary toiletries, small flat screen tv and bathrobe and slippers.
Our bathroom was in the hallway, but we had a sink and a hairdryer in the room.
The staff was friendly. Place is very clean and conveniently located.
Breakfast is euro style. Pastries and bread.

I've stayed at the Larchmont three times previously.
Their rates are excellent for the location (Greenwich Village). Subways and PATH are a couple of blocks away. The only handicap accessible train is a little too far at 14th and 8th so trekking through the neighborhood with large, heavy bags is a mild annoyance but I like being cheap more and refuse to spend money on the cabs and airport shuttles.
The quality of rooms is average - flat tv is tiny, no irons or ironing boards. The shared bathrooms are usually clean but make sure to pack your shower shoes. Haven't had any issues with waiting to use the bathrooms but I shower at odd times anyway. I like a firm matress so the beds are too soft for me.
I've never tried their continental breakfast because there are so many places in the neighborhood or close by with good food.
Staff is friendly and were quick to tidy up my room after Housekeeping failed miserably one morning. I'm not a messy guest so cleaning my room shouldn't be a problem. One morning, I piled my dirty towels, hotel robe, and hotel slippers into one big lump as usual. No bed linens in the lump this time. I ventured off into the city and returned late afternoon/early evening.
I found my room in a state of "somewhat serviced". The bed was made but a little sloppily in my opinion. The carpet was not vacuumed so bits of food and random pieces of trishy trash greeted me. My old slippers were placed neatly beside the drawer and a robe was hanging on the hooks near the new towels. This scene was suspicious. Since the carpet was in disarray, I inspected other items for cleanliness. The old slippers should have been carted off with the dirty towels. I had a spare pair as the room came with two clean sets. I eyed the hanging robe and noticed yesterday's stains. I ran my hands across the robe and noticed it was wet.
At this point, I was livid and rang the office for service. They're response was prompt and very apologetic. The bellman vacuumed and presented me a fresh robe. He speculated the housekeeping ladies were probably on their phones blabbing with their boyfriends and became absent-minded and hurried. I chuckled imagining his scenario. He apologized once more, asked if the room was to my liking then returned to the office with a promise to notify Housekeeping oof their epic failure.
I'll continue to stay here but I will be triple-checking housekeeping's work. I rated Cleanliness a 1 strictly due to my last vist otherwise it would be a 4 as would the rating for Service.

review_title: Fine, for just a bed, but they need to get their act together.
review_text:
I stayed here with part of a bachelorette party. Overall the hotel has decent facilities, but the service leaves something to be desired. 
Check in was at 3pm, I arrived at 4:00, and was told my room was not yet ready. At 4:30, the room was finally ready. The elevators require the guest keys to go up and down, and everyone seems to have trouble with them including the staff. And the pool did not open on time either. The guest services book in my room said it opened at 8am, at 8:30am I called to ask why it was still locked. I was told that it didn't open till 9am. At 9:15, when the pool still wasn't open, I went down to the front desk, and was told the lifeguard had not yet arrived, and they couldn't open the pool till then. It's 9:30 and I'm still in my room waiting. I understand these things happen, but I feel like it's a bit of a pattern here.
I will say the rooms are nice, albeit small (but it's a boutique hotel in NY, so that's to be expected). And the lobby, and pool look nice. My only other complaint is that the hallways are pretty dimly lit. I probably wouldn't stay here again, unless the service changes, but it's a nice hotel in a decent location.
Rooms are amazing, large and comfy! Bathroom I dream about. Service was insanely good. Will stay again! Skip the restaurant. Over priced and many better spots around!

review_title: Hip place at a hip location
review_text: The place will get you in the real NYC mood in notime. Classy, but not over the top, modern but not inpractical, this place has it all. Go foe the LES, it is the place to be now!

The Jane is probably one of the most valuable hotel right now, at least from my experience in NY. The service is excellent, all staff friendy and always ready to assist. Even if the rooms are SMALL (buy who will be in NY to sleep) and there is shared showers, the value of the hotel is in the service and the staff. 
One simple example: instead of standing waiting for your taxi, take a drink in the neighbor bar and the staff comes and get you when the taxi has arrived. Another example is that the baggage storage, including Alia me stuff get stored at the office.

review_title: First trip to New York - can't wait to stay at Thompson LES again!
review_text:
The hotel is a bit more minimal than we would usually go for but fitted New York to a T. The room was on the 15th floor and had the most amazing which started at the Brooklyn Bridge and finished past the Empire State building. The floor to ceiling glass and wrapp around balcony ensured that the view could be enjoyed to the maximum. 
The shower was amazing and the Kiehls products were also very nice. The bed was huge and made it hard to get up was very welcome after a hard day sight seeing and evenings out.
The hotel has a gym area and spa which were able to use before going to the airport as our flight back was at night. 
Finally the staff were brilliant. Very friendly and helpful. 
Would like to stay at Thmpson LES again in the summer to use the roof top pool and to see that view again.

review_title: Just what I wanted from my accommodation.
review_text: The Jane is situated halfway between midtown and downtown, ideal for getting about. 5 mins walk from 14th Street subway or $10 in a yellow cab to Times Square. If you don't intend to spend a lot of time in your room, want somewhere clean, secure and friendly I would definitely recommend this place. Free wifi, tv and iPod docking station are a bonus. I would definitely recommend and i will stay here again.

I just spent one week here in a cabin and I loved it. The room had everything I needed, the bed was very comfortable, the showers were hot and the staff were friendly and helpful. Yes, the rooms are small but are you coming to New York to hang out in your hotel?? I requested a quiet room and it was perfect; the first time I haven't needed earplugs in New York. I'll definitely be back and will be recommending it to my friends.

I booked a suite for my family,reading the reviews everyone said that it was small, but I figured it couldn't be that bad, they were right! Two people cannot walk in the room at the same time. The elevators can not accomadate the high volume of people using them. Even the staff with their carts use them. The wait is unacceptable. They charged my card a few times by mistake, which was a nusence dealing with my bank! 
Way too expensive! Not worth staying there! You will get more for your money by staying at the Doubletree suites in times square!

review_title: A room with a view !!! ( chambre avec vue)
review_text: We ( a couple with a teenager) enjoyed everything : the location ( next to Grand central station, the Chrysler building, the public library...) the view ( East river, UN building, the Empire and the Chrysler from the 38th floor!!!!)and the kindness of the staff ( some of them speak French). The beds are confortable, you may hear some people in the corridors or the clicketing of the heating but frankly we were so exhausted with the jet lag and our visits that we slept very well... We had a very Nice breakfast at the hotel on our first day ( fresh fruit, cooked or continental breakfast...) and then we went out everyday to a different place in the neighbourhood.
Feels like you're on a ship - narrow halls, tiny rooms, great front desk. Incredible location - close to river, highline, west village, etc. Very quiet. Really nice cafe.

The hotel is fine. I was there for a conference - in that instance the location was convenient. The neighborhood is residential - so it's a little quieter, but there are plenty of good restaurants within walking distance. If I were coming to NYC for fun, not sure would be the ideal location.
The rooms are nice - fairly roomy for big city standards. Beds are clean. TV reception was horrible, but I wasn't there to watch TV so I didn't care. 
If you need a hairdryer - bring your own - the wall unit one is brutal and totally old school.
The exercise room is really good - one of the better ones I've seen fir hotels. Apparently there is a pool as well, but I never saw it.

review_title: Always a welcome place with friendly people!!
review_text: I have stayed at this hotel on several occasions for business trips. The rooms are clean and comfortable, and the staff is super-friendly. You are always greeted with smiles but an attentive staff, at the door, front desk, and at breakfast. I would definitely stay again!! The only downside is the same as many newer NYC hotels-it can take a longer time to get an elevator on weekday mornings around 8 or so as there are three elevators.
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel Chelsea New York City

review_text:
The Millenium UN Plaza has fantastic views of New York City and a great location on Manhattan's east side. It's a 5 minute walk to Grand Central Station and an easy walk to the Museum of Modern Art, Bloomingdale's, and some excellent restaurants. The UN is across the street. 
I've stayed here twice in the last month for a total of 5 nights. On both stays I needed a room change. During the first stay the front desk clerk couldn't have been nicer or more accommodating. He moved me to a room with a fantastic panoramic view on the 36th floor. On my most recent stay the front desk clerk seemed offended and put out that I would be unhappy with a wet carpet and a foul-smelling room. She grudgingly moved me to a room on the other side of the hotel after offering two smaller rooms with less-than great views. No A+ for her customer service. 
The doormen and bellmen are friendly and helpful. The elevators are sometimes slow and not functional (get in, push the button, wait, get back out, try again). Some things in the room didn't work (phone, hair dryer) but were replaced quickly. 
The rooms are clean and comfortable with minimal amenities. Don't expect fancy little shampoos and bathrobes; it's not that fancy a place. I don't watch much TV but noticed less than clear reception when I turned it on to check the weather. The beds are very comfortable and the room lighting is excellent. The bathroom lighting could be brighter and some drawers would be helpful for those of us who like to unpack. 
The lobby is beautiful and modern and there are places to sit and relax there. I did not eat any food in the hotel so cannot comment on that. 
I was able to get what I consider a very reasonable rate for Manhattan and consider the UN Plaza Hotel to be a great find. It could use a little sprucing up and someone should go around to all the rooms and make sure things work. The management should also encourage all the front desk staff to be as friendly and helpful as they can. I know they have to deal with a lot of jerks but at least try to fake caring that your guests are happy. You want them to return.

review_title: Great value, good location, small room
review_text:
I have stayed at this DoubleTree more than 10 times in the last 2 years. Every time I stay, my room and bathroom are spotless and the rate is always very competitive for NYC. The rooms are small and the lobby is almost non-existent but who cares when you have a very clean room, comfy bed and CHEAP!!
There is little atmosphere here but it's such a great value and the staff are always pleasant. You can walk to almost everything and it's so nice to be near broadway without all the craziness. This DT is tucked away on 29th and 6th and is actually pretty quiet, which is an anomaly for a locale so close to all the action.
If you are looking for a good, clean room and don't care about bells and whistles and resort-type amenities, then stay here. It's small but such a good value.
hotel_name: Doubletree Hotel Chelsea New York City

review_text:
I had a great time at The Jane Hotel! Located in the cultural hub of the MePa district and a short stroll into Chelsea and Grenwich Village, there was always something happening in this exciting part of NYC. Although a little far away from the nearest subway stop and even buses, there is so much to see as you walk there, you hardley notice. Staff are friendly and the rooms always clean. Be warned, as everyone has mentioned, the rooms are tiny, and if your the sort of person who likes to spread your things out then you may want to opt for one of the larger rooms or another hotel. My experiance here was the best that I had in NYC and I will definently recommend this to any single traveller!
Thank You Jane Hotel!!!
Very convenient, because we're near times square & rockefeller. Staff were very good.

We spent a day during the holidays. The hotel rate was excellent considering the location. Few blocks from Time Square and Rockefeller Center. Steps from 5th Avenue. 
The room was small , clean but a little noisy. Well, but nothing is perfect. The breakfast was included, not too much variety but good to start the day. Staff was really friendly.
We will definitely return to this hotel.

review_title: Amazing location and foyer...Shocking room and service

My room, though had lovely views had a bathroom that had some bodily hairs in the bath, untidy room and little to no amenities. The hotel was a black hole for mobile phone reception and the breakfast was shockingly expensive for what you get.

review_title: Style over substance - and not even that stylish
review_text:

The room was TINY as stated - and very hot. You could hear your neighbours every move/ word. And the worst part was you could hear the music from the bar - which went on each night till 4am. So I got no sleep what so ever. 
This is a great hotel if you want to be out till 4am partying. The location was fantastic. But it is not for someone looking for a boutique hotel experience!

review_title: Great location, good price, ok stay.
review_text: This is one of the cheapest places I could find to stay in New York in a reasonable area- I love to stay in the Meatpacking district as it is close to clubs and shopping. Only thing is if you pay less you stat in a tiny room and share a bathroom which is new to me but I found it ok. The hotel has a popular bar downstairs known for celebrity spotting. The staff are incredibly helpful- the airport lost my luggage and they did everything they could to help. The hotel is very close to shops and clubs but about two blocks from a subway stop which was slightly inconvenient.
Room was small but come on it's new york. Nice helpful staff upon check in. Didn't spend much time in room traveling throughout the city.

review_title: Shabby rooms overpriced breakfast and valet
review_text: For the price of the room I expected a more updated hotel. The rooms and hotel in general was shabby. Bathroom didn't have a decent shower. No water or coffee machines in the room. Breakfast very overpriced!! Staff were friendly and the location is ok.

My wife and I took another couple to New York City recently. The other couple was visiting us from Brazil and this was their first visit to the United States. Imagine our surprise when we discovered the street on which the hotel is located (46th) is nicknamed Little Brazil. The street had several Brazilian restaurants on it and many Brazilians stay in the hotel. Needless to say, we felt right at home. First off, the name is a misnomer. The hotel isn't at Times Square, which is two blocks away. They don't normally allow you to let check in before 3 p.m., but they already had several rooms cleaned and allowed us to check in at 1:30. Our room was on the top floor, which meant a long, slow elevator ride up. There are two elevators, but only one that goes all the way up. The room was very nice and really clean. It was a little small, but very comfortable. It had a huge walk-in closet with a programmable safe for our valuables. There was also an extra pillow. The TV was a flat screen that telescoped out from the wall. The bed was extremely comfortable. The climate controls on the air conditioner kept our room the perfect temperature. The bathroom was a little cramped, but clean and adequate. Only one person at a time can really use it to get ready, so plan accordingly if you're on a schedule. One really nice feature is that the maid service doesn't come banging on the door at 9 a.m. like most places. We never saw them on our floor, but our room was always cleaned and the towels replaced. They left more than enough towels each day, so that was never a concern. There were two cordless phones in the room, with clear instructions on which numbers to dial for specific services. Now, when we wanted to go out, we had to wait for the elevator to come up to the 14th floor from the lobby, which was very time-consuming, especially if you're in a hurry. You could take the stairs if you don't mind descending 14 flights of stairs. One nice little unexpected bonus was the second-floor bar. Dubbed "the biggest little bar in NYC" by the management, it stays open late and offers just about any libation you could desire. The sign out front promised $3 drafts, $3 shots and $5 cocktails. We went two different nights. The first night they were out of draft beer. The shots were the smallest I've ever seen, but what do you expect for $3? The bartender was a friendly young American girl who kept our glasses filled. The place is tiny, with only enough room for six two-seat tables and three chairs at the bar, but has all of the high-dollar liquors. The second night couldn't have been more different than the first. A different bartender, who sounded like she might have come from Eastern Europe, never did get the prices right. She tried to charge me $6 for a shot and had no idea what the actual prices were when I questioned the prices. She was playing this Euro techno-pop music very loudly, so much so that it made it difficult for my wife and I to talk. She also had her boyfriend sitting at the bar, and between drinking shots with him she went downstairs and out front with him to smoke, leaving the bar completely unattended and several people's glasses empty for an extended period of time. The next day, even though we'd checked out, the hotel alowed us to leave our bags there while we explored New York City some more. They locked the bags in a secure room until we returned to pick them up up. It was extremely cordial of them to do that even though they were under no obligation to do so. I recommend this hotel and would stay there again.
