review_title: Great location, nice lobby and bar, room is tired
review_text: My first trip to the hotel. It is ideally located for so many things. Service was great. Bar had a fun evening atmosphere. The restaurant is a destination, so they ask for reservations even at breakfast. Without one we were still seated. The room. Bed was comfortable, room was clean. Flat screen TV. Bottom of bathroom door was chipped, dirty. The inside rim of the sink was lined with mold and made using the sink less than desirable for $400+ a night. Charge for Internet in the room, free in the lobby. I went to the lobby; they do give free Starbucks coffee in the lobby, so some consolation. All in all, I still give this a 4.

I come to NYC regularly for business and am well acquainted with many of the city's hotels. For this trip I was coming in for an evening memorial service and I wanted to be close to where it was being held. I could not have been treated more rudely by the staff; was told my room would be ready by 2; came back at 2 and was told by a horribly rude woman at the front desk in her snootiest tone, "check-in is at four; come back then." I explained I was told my room would be ready by 2 and she just shrugged and began to speak to someone else. NEVER in all of my years of traveling have I been treated so rudely. I will never consider coming back.

review_title: If you have can pay $50 more, Do it!!
review_text:
I always book the cheapest flight I can find and cheapest hotel in the best location I can find. Last year after a trip with China Air I decided that if I can afford it I am paying for a better airline when I travel next. Hotel 17 is convinced me that I should do that for my hotels as well. Look! there is nothing fundamentally wrong with this place. It is one of the cheapest priced for its cathegory, it is definatly clean, and in a good location. 
But, it is not in excellent location. the real place to stay south west of Unnion square ( closer to Washington square park as possible) or slightly north in the meatpacking district. So the location is good but not excellent as it is claimed. 
Rooms are so small that I can not fully open my luggage. I am sure not all of the rooms are like this but in my room there is no place to even stand. I had to wear my socks in the hall way sitting on the floor once since my travel partner occuppied the only avaliable standing room while he was dressing up.
I am a very heavy sleeper, I have never thought that I will be complaining about noise in any place ( I slept 15 hours on the way to NY from sydney in the plane- NOthing wakes me up) but apparently hotel staff vacuuming the hallways 6:15 am on a Sunday would wake me up. I thought it was a bit much. 
Rooms are awfully hot and there is AC but it is so noisy that you can not leave it on and sleep. Not just yours every other room also have a noisy AC that every time your neighbours turn theirs on you wake up as well. I managed to get max 4 hours of sleep each night.
So if you have to stay here stay. But if you can afford 50 more dollars a night i am sure you can find something a bit better where you can enjoy the place you are staying a bit more.

I had booked this hotel through Priceline and we were looking forward to our 4 night stay with them. Great location for us to get around by foot as we were taking the train in from Toronto. No problems with checking in and room was spacious and clean. Our problems started when our train was cancelled for our return trip on Mon Aug 29 due to the "hurricane". My husband and I went to the front desk to explain the situation...we were basically stranded and could we extend the stay until Tuesday. Sure no problem we were told but the rate would be $429 for the night. So with taxes it would be almost $500. REALLY what with the situation and all you think they would have been somewhat sympathetic and at least charged us the rate we had on the previous nights even $100 more than that rate would have been alright. We asked to speak to the Manager who was understanding but it was the powers that be that were telling him that he was not allowed to give discounts...yeah right. He offered to give us his lowest rate so since we had no other choice we accepted and went out to salvage what we could of our holiday. When we returned we found out his "best rate" was only $20 less. Considering the circumstances I think more could have been done even a free meal in their way way overpriced restaurant would have helped. We will not stay in a Loew's property again.

I've visited NYC from the UK four times and I've only ever stayed at Hotel 17 or the sister hotel 31. It's such good value for money, and I love the Gramercy park location of Hotel 17. Anyone who has wasted money on overpriced hotels down in the noisy touristy Times Sq area will wish they'd known about Hotel 17. It's ideal for those who don't require extra frills from a hotel, they just want clean and good value for money, with a nice room and a comfortable bed. Sharing bathrooms is never a problem- they're always unfailingly clean, you'd never know you were sharing them. 
Nearby is Union Square with great shopping, farmers markets, and the subway which is ten minutes to Central Park area. 
I also recommend Gramercy Park Cafe just nearby where you'll get the best eggs, and Bar Jamon for spanish tapas. It's restaurant next door is also excellent but more pricey as its Michelin starred! 
Hotel 17 is perfect for those who would prefer a quieter more surburban neighbourhood, which is nonetheless only minutes from the main tourist attractions.

review_title: Love this hotel. Been to NYC 5 times & wouldn't stay anywhere else now.
review_text: Great value for money, affordable with a perfect location for people wanting to experience a bit more real NYC culture rather than the tourist bustle of Times Square. The hotel itself feels old & its decor outdated but that's what's charming about it! It feels deliberate. I have stayed in 5 star hotels in NYC before but genuinely wouldn't swap this hotel for them. I feel at home here. I feel like I'm living amongst proper New Yorkers. The surrounding streets look residential yet it's just a quick walk from Union Square and perfect for exploring Lower Manhattan on the East (or, if you like walking) the West side. This gives you access to great bars, restaurants, shops and culture in Gramercy, East Village, Little Italy, Chinatown, soHo, Chelsea, Tribeca, Financial District and even Brooklyn. I would recommend it for people who have been to NYC before and stayed around Times Square or Midtown and now want something a bit more real. Good luck and hope you enjoy it as much as we did!

review_title: Beautiful stay, beautiful rooms, great service.
review_text:
I love this place except for the location, not ideal for weekend stays but that is when you get the deals at this w location (kinda far from soho, times square, tourist spots). Not too bad of a cab ride though and door people will hail you a cab promptly. Excellent location for business travels. Very clean, super comfortable, very friendly staff. The bars and restaurants at the hotel are good with great service (but when you run out of olives and someone orders a $25 martini, please have someone run down to the corner market and grab a jar!).
Rooms were surprisingly big for Manhatten, very modern, everything you could need or want in the room. Would definitely be a top choice if traveling to NYC for business.

Nice hotel in middle of manhattan .. 2 miles each way to lower and midtown manhattan.. Small rooms but clean.. Even though bathrooms are shared I found always cleaned and prepared in my 4 days except once when someone had just used it.. Found good deal at orbitz for little over 100 bucks when I booked 2 months in advance for the memorial day weekend... Very good value for money in NY

We stayed here to be strategically in place for the 5 Borough Bike Ride, New York's nod to spring and the great outdoors. The hotel is gorgeous, with a front row seat at Groubd Zero but the staff was absolutely spectacular. Spec-ta-cular! They ferried our bikes up and down to and from th front door, hustled us cabs, sent drinks to the room and in general, acted as if they were personal assistants instead if desk clerks, doormen and oom attendants. Unbelievable! We had a wonderful wonderful time and now, irrespective of what we're doing in New York, we'll never stay anywhere but The W Hotel Downtown.

Do not stay here unless your room does not overlook the world trade construction area. Unfortunately, at least half the rooms do. It is all night construction and my two colleagues and I all were awake by 3.45 to 4 AM and had no chance of getting back to sleep. To make things worse, the lobby is essentially unlit so that at 7 AM it is too dark to read the paper or talk to anyone. Looks like a bad Vegas show room

review_title: Watch your wallet at the W
review_text: This hotel charged me $500 for a reservation adjustment five minutes after making the original booking. I got nowhere with the staff over this. A complete fraud. Also the neighborhood surrounding is devoid of nightlife . So many other hotels to choose from.

Great hotel, right across the WTC site. I got the 15th floor, so got a hgreat view of the monument and the site. In spite of the work going on, it was very quiet inside the room. Very spacious and well furnished. Will stay agin if visiting downtown. Will definitely recommend it.

review_title: Great location and clean. Overall reasonable hotel.
review_text:
We got very small room and it felt quite uncomfortable (with two big luggage cases taking a lot of space) but to be honest we only came to the hotel late in the evening and left early in the morning.
Bed was comfortable, lcd tv in the room and relatively reliable wireless internet are worth mentioning.
Main thing is location though. 5 min walk to Union Sq which is one of better subway stations in Manhattan (in terms of connections).
There is also Whole Foods shop on union sq which we can thoroughly recommend for breakfasts as it has breakfast salad bars and seating on first floor with views over union sq.

review_title: Luxury in the Upper East Side
review_text: We usually stay in a king room but upgraded to a large king room. The extra $40 for the larger room and bath was well worth the money.

review_title: Trendy modern hotel looking down on ground zero.
review_text: An enjoyable stay for our family of four with pre teen kids. Not really a family hotel but v cool and rock n roll. We all liked it. Great rooms, service. Not a very big hotel. Reception on 5th floor. Complimentary taxi to uptown whilst we stayed. Complimentary coffee and wi fi in lobby. Location is a little away from the hustle and bustle of 5th ave and time sq. But we liked that. It's virtually on wall St, near the ferry terminal for station island and statue of liberty. Plus you can explore all the places in between downtown and central park. great stay overall.

review_title: Buon rapporto qualitÃ  prezzo... Ma ricordatevi le TASSE
review_text: Per essere un hotel di new York le camere erano pulite e di dimensioni accettabili. RumorositÃ  nella norma (noi eravamo 9 piano)!alla recepito non brillavano per gentilezza, ma neanche maleducati..soprattutto dopo la mancia! Colazione abbondante! Nel complesso buono anche se aggiungendo tasse varie non era poi cosi economico

review_title: Excellent, trendy hotel in downtown New York
review_text:
We spent 3 nights here while our daughter was on film camp. We booked through discount website and got a room with a view over the 9/11 heritage site with 2 double beds. The beds were very comfortable and the room well appointed. No bath but great shower and the best shampoo.
Nice flat screen Tv but problems with signal feed meant that we weren't charged for the film. Staff were all greaty and patient with NYC first timers. Nearest subway 5 minute walk. The area is under development so is noisy in the day but quiet at night. A great hotel. - really. Shout out to Nicole and Kareem on the front desk in particular. Just remember - get the lift up to the lobby to check in; it's not on the ground floor. The lobby is more like a nightclub than a hotel - you'll feel most comfortable wearing black!

Checked in on Friday evening 9 p.m. Restaurant was closed.
Had dinner on the terrace overlooking Ground zero, a hole with mud and noisy construction work...food tasted good but my daughter was sick with the hamburger she ate. Sat. breakfast at the hotel restaurant was a excruciating experience! Rotten service with very obnoxious waiter and manager. We left without eating our meal after waiting 50 minutes...gentlemen that were having breakfast at the next table said that we were right to leave because they were also unhappy about the poor services...
Concierge did not know anything, nice but not helpful at ALL!
Last and not the least, the shuttle rides that they promote were never available during out 3 days stay there. I say, they really need to
Get their acts together!

Positives-good location for downtown business, good value for money for NY, very friendly staff. Negatives-interior is in dire need of an upgrade; it is dated and feels run down. If you decided to stay at the hotel, ask for a room away from the elevators, it gets noisy in the early hours of the morning as people return from their night out.

review_title: Not a good place to stay w a family - in my opinion
review_text: Just a quick review for now, while I am kept awake in my room that is above the lounge. Unbelievable that they would put a family in this room (especially one that is a rewards member of their program). The noise is so loud - we are hearing both the din of people and the music. This room should be used for young "hip" people that won't be in their rooms until later. NOT RECOMMENDED if you want a good nights sleep.

We had a great stay at the new W Hotel Downtown NYC. The hotel is beautiful, the rooms spacious and comfortable, and the staff exceptionally helpful. Of special note was the desk clerk Jason who made our check in fast and welcoming (and made sure we knew all about the property), and Anari the concierge who was well connected and set us up with fun activities for our Saturday night in the East Village. Despite these two shout outs, I would say that all the staff from housekeeping to doormen were excellent and always made us feel welcome.
As it is a W Hotel I would caution people who don't like a lively hotel atmosphere that this may not be for them. But anyone who appreciates a bit of fun, a supremely comfortable room, great views and chic interiors should definitely stay here!

This hotel may work for only 2 people. However, we had 4, two adults and two children. We rented a small 1 bedroom suite as it came will a pull out sofa. Unfortunately the mattress on the pull out sofa was discolored, worn, tattered and uncomfortable, and could not sleep one or two. The hotel sent up an air mattress which could sleep one, and our other slept on the sofa not pulled into the sofa bed. 
Temperature controls were bad, with the air conditioner fan blowing directly onto us the entire night. We checked out of this hotel after one night and went to a different hotel.

We had a week in this hotel and couldn't fault it at all. Great central park location, rooms were very clean, food was lovely. Just round the corner from fifth avenue, and close to the tube. Would be happy to recommend this hotel to others.

review_title: Very good value for money, great location and very friendly, helpful staff.
review_text: We booked 9 days in December 2011 over Christmas and were pleasantly surprised at the quality of the hotel. A block away from Soho meant we had the best stores and restaurants in Manhattan within walking distance. Hotel is very warm, inviting and a welcome respite from a cold New York winters day.

review_title: Overall, it was a wonderful hotel
review_text: Im from south carolina and I stayed here for 4 days recently, and it is not in the best location in the city, its a bit far from times square and other attractions, but the hotel was nice, the front desk was helpful and tony, the concierge had great restaurant suggestions and tours for me and my wife.

review_title: Great Service---only caution is taxi situation
review_text: Service truly great--not the I'm cool young hipsters I've had at other W's--truly helped-car service good but you need to reserve that free Acura--- only problem is getting a taxi --because of location they are not going by and note since it's new several drivers didn't know it and I had to supply address. Staff works hard to get you one but it's tough

review_title: It is very good and deligthful
review_text: We have a very unexplained entrance to this date but after we talk everything get very well.after all we just traveling 4000 miles to stay one week and we were trap in the heat wave that day only. The rest is very good and the breakfast and service are excellent.

I stayed in room 2206. The too wasn't terrible. It seemed clean enough even though half of the lamps/lighting didn't work. The 9.95 per day wifi didn't operate well, and I was triple charged for mini bar items. The worst was the bathroom, which was so filthy I was compelledto take photosto show my corporate travel agent why I will never stay in this hotel again. Tub, toilet, basin, wall and fixtures were dirty. Not just "oh you missed a spot" dirty, but like homeless person looking dirty. I realized after staying here that it primarily cates to foreign tourists, but shame on you for showing tourists such a dirty representation of NY at the prices you charge.

review_title: For 120 dollars the night this hotel would have begoo fine but not more!
review_text:
For 350 dollars without breakfast, without safe deposit in the room and without free wifi, this hotel is a rubbery ! Way too expensive for what you get ! Taking into account it is on Canal Street which is gross !! Of course if you close your eyes on canal street and turn left you are not far from Soho, Mondrian hotel etc but still it is too pricey ! 
Won't go back !

The staff was super helpful - directions on how to use the subway, finding a neighborhood cobbler (Stanley's on Thames - excellent!), comping my cab ride when their complimentary car service was down for the day (what a great feature). Everyone there was so helpful - Sam was amazing & so friendly. I was also nervous about the location being so far downtown & it really wasn't a big deal at all - it's 2 subway stops from soho & 15min max to times square. Room & bath were clean - no bed bugs! I will definitely stay here again!

review_title: Surprisingly decent hotel given the Canal Street location. Don't miss the rooftop lounge area.
review_text: Very clean, pleasant and efficient. (Tribecca is a great neighborhood but Canal Street is gross.) Nice decor. Very comfy beds. If you're a light sleeper avoid the corner rooms because the doors open and close loudly. Free wi-fi in the lobby but not in the room. Great roof deck on the 18th floor but you have to ask to be let up unless you have a club key.

I brought my family here for the week between Christmas and New Year's. The good: Location at Grand Central couldn't have been much better, as subway lines to everywhere were within easy reach. Check-in experience was fine. Found out on arrival that my room rate (booked thru American Express) had a "business upgrade" that I was told would allow for free wifi, and free breakfast at a designated hotel restaurant (for the entire family I was told). The room size (2 double beds) was generous by NY standards, and had been renovated recently. Room was clean and water was hot, with almost everything in good working order.
The bad: I was skeptical of the free breakfast claim, so I ran my folio after the first day, and sure enough, breakfast for only one person was covered. To the hotel's credit, they backed out everyone's breakfast charge due to the miscommunication. Housekeeping gets a B-/C+, as the proper, omplement of towels for a family of 4 was missing until the very last day in spite of our specific request for same upon our arrival. One ofmthe room phones was in very bad working order for the duration of our stay(in spite of my repeated requests to fix). The worst (and near fatal) flaw was that upon our checkout, the bell desk charged a per-item fee to hold our bags until our airport transportation arrived. This is a ridiculous charge that I have never seen before and hope I never see again. Besides taking tip money out of the hands of some hard-working employees, it puts Hyatt into the RyanAir bargain basement...not very becoming. 
In short, the physical plant was fine. Better than that, actually. The issues here were service related. They can and should be fixed.

review_title: Nice hotel, friendly staff, great location, would definitely stay there again
review_text: I took my two daughters to New York for a 4 day, 3 night shopping trip. The hotel was clean, the staff were always helpful, and the location is great. I was concerned after reading previous posts about the Canal Street location. There are other streets to go outside this hotel to avoid Canal, even though we were out until midnight and had no problems. Walking out the front of the hotel, you can walk straight down Wooster,( a really trendy art studio street) and turn at any of the cross streets, which are lined with cafe's, retail stores, etc. It's about a 15 minute walk from the hotel to Greenwich Village, on streets lined with restaurants, clothing stores, and the like. We had a great time, and would definitely stay there again. The only negative is having to pay $10 dollars a day to have Internet in your room, I think the Sheraton could do better
Great location and new grand club staff. However, If you want a glass of cheap wine, go elsewhere and avoid the Grand club,a rip off as compared to other Hyatt clubs.

review_title: Great location by Grand Central and Bryant Park
review_text: This is the first time I have stayed here since the completion of the renovations. The lobby appears bigger with a contemporary feel. The staff was welcoming and helpful. They could of done a better job of decorating for the holidays. The new Regency room is beautiful and offers great snacks, hors devours, etc. Unfortunately, alcohol comes with a charge. We stayed in a suite and the accommodations were great. The room was large and comfortable. The gym did not make any changes, but there really was not a need to as it is an above average gym for a hotel. The locations is great and walking distance to Times Square and Bryant Park.
Had a great overnight. Club floor great - especially breakfast. In particular like to commend Michael the doorman. He is awesome!!

Paid a lot of dollars to stay two nights here. 
Bad points: 
 1, They placed me next to the maids store room. The door was banging on a regular basis. Sound like nothing but after a few hrs of trying to sleep it kinda gets on your nerves. Good job this was vacation and not business. 
2, Went for a shower in the morning only to find it was lacking no facilities to wash. 
3, The elevators require your key card to work. Not a bad idea if it works correctly. Unfortunately for most of the people I spoken to found it a complete pain to use. Sometimes taking 5 mins to get to your floor. At one point I used the stairs. 
4, The wireless connection. Only worked 50% of the time I was there. I was told to go to Starbucks. Nice! I pay 100s of dollars, only to find I have to visit Starbucks to check my business matters. If this was a working trip that would have made me check out! 
Good points:
1, Nice friendly staff
My advice is to find an alternative to this place. Your get more for your money! 
Russ McCulloch
Andrea Holt

review_title: Worst hotel staff i ever stayed in
review_text: Thinking that Hyatt is a world renown institution & famed for its reputation & great hospitable service in ASEAN locations. I was truly & genuinely disappointed wt many hotel staff, very cocky, very snobbish, aloof, unfriendly, unapproachable, condescending, obvious racial discriminations toward Asians. Having travelled the whole world, i've never encountered such despicable attitude by a reputable hotel wt such ugly treatmemts especially the concierge white guys & when i collect my lost baggage by that 2 unruly black guys, damn rude. I find staff in Minneapolis & Orlando are so much better & sweet & heavenly than these dumb New Yorkers. i truly give good credit to Danny, the concierge, who has been the most outstandingly helpful, pleasant & resourceful personnel to our 5 day stay. NYC Grand Hyatt has significantly lost all my respects for Hyatt group completely.

$450 a night and not even a coffee maker in the room. Mildew growing on the shower curtain, stinking up the room. 
Checkin was a disaster - multiple lines, no signs as to where to wait.
It was obvious the hotel cares mre about its new chic bar than the guest experience.

review_title: Watch out - they charge extra for everything!!!! Is this just a ripoff?
review_text:
Two examples
.my wife and I wanted some wine glasses and corkscrew brought to our room ( in our experience they are usually in the room when you arrive at any decent hotel, but not here!). The Hyatt wanted to charge $38 for delivery!!
. My wife and I have iPads,iPhones,computer - in fact 5 wireless devices. There is no free wifi in room so we paid the $16.95 a day to connect to premium service. We then found out this covers only one device - the 5 would cost $85 a day. 
Buyer beware !!!!

Esta a una cuadra de times square, es relativamente barato comparado con los hoteles de la zona. El hotel esta limpio y los cuartos estan chicos pero bueno. Lo recomiendo para los viajeros que pasaran mas tiempo en la ciudad que en el hotel

This was the 5th hotel we stayed at at the end of a two week holiday in USA, and was by far the most disappointing. Don't get me wrong - the room was ok, clean and comfortable, but it was the smallest of the three rooms we'd stayed in in NYC, and the most expensive. We thought we'd book something nice for our last night - so splashed out on this 4star hotel and expected something special. Wished wehad gone back to the Yotel or Thirty Thirty.

New hotel, but very small rooms, even wardrobe can fit just few things...
Despite i m a spg platinum they didn t gibe me a suite saying it was sold out, but it was available.....
And any welcome amenity in the room. 
Doorman offered us a private trasportatiom to' the airport wirh a suv for 7 pax when i asked for 8. 
Unprofessional!!!!!

review_title: Am I a guest or a number?
review_text:
I nornally like Hyatts but this one frustrated me. The hotel is very cold (colors and attitude, not temp). With automated check in we were here three nights before ever having a hotel employee acknowledge us (at check out... and barely... and after a 15 minute queue.) I understand it is a large convention type hotel, but not exactly any hospitality. Better hotels are able to bridge this gap.
Hotel recently remodeled, and rooms were nicely decorated, but we had two basic problems. One, tv picture was very fuzzy. Two, one day copious amounts of smoke came in through the bathroom fan (nasty neighbors I guess.) Ick. Ick. Ick. (On n/s floor).
What really ticks me off is the 12.95 per day for internet. This is unacceptable and a blatant rip off. For the rate charged for the room, inclusion of this now basic service is expected. I hate getting nickel and dimed. Also a charge for storing bags... again, usually a basic service I am more than happy to tip for but don't expect having to pay up front. Yes, I know this is NYC but that isn't an excuse.
Location is pretty good. Hotel is adjacent to Grand Central Terminal and there is a back passageway so can get to the trains and several subway lines. Also there is a market in GCT. This was very nice. We did lots of exploring by foot and didn't see a lot of hotels with significantly better location. Happy with this.
Breakfast at hotel was 60 for two. Yeah, we found better for much better value the other days. My bad, but still rip off for rip off's sake. (Don't get me wrong, I am not cheap, but I can tell when I am being ripped.)
Beds very comfy. No complaints there.
All in all, this is the first time Hyatt has let me me down. It just... should have been better in a couple of basic ways. You know, any of these little things I could probably overlook if I felt they appreciated my business at least a little. Glad my employer was covering this one :)
Oh, and get the TripAdvisor NYC app before you go. This was extremely helpful to our explorations and restaurant choices.
Good location. Nice inside and rooms are lovely. I'll be back

review_title: Nice room, don't pay for club floor
review_text:
Nice new modern hotel on Canal Steeet, on the edge of Chinatown and little Italy. Perfect access to subway and all the boutiques on Broadway and SoHo. 
HOWEVER, we had paid for an executive floor and were disappointed. We arrived at 4pm only to be asked to wait 15 minutes which turned into 30 minutes more. The lounge was poorly stocked and not clean. The fridge supposedly with soft drinks was empty and never regularly stocked. Coffee and tea available as well but no tea bags.
Evening appetizers consisted of samosas and chicken skewers of average quality. The fridge still was not stocked with any additional soft drinks and the tea still absent.
Breakfast in the morning was less than average, no breakfast pastries for those who didn't want eggs and bacon. The hostess present, however, was nice to go get a whole wheat croissant, that's all that was left downstairs. Silverware and plates were coffee stained ... Just an overall dirty atmosphere.
We brought this to the attention to an assistant front desk manager who asked us why we didn't talk to a food and beverage manager !? 
We can only hope our feedback has been taken seriously. We were not expecting 5-star service but it can be a good club level lounge if there is attention to detail. For us the rate difference for the club level was not worth it.

review_title: Good value, great location in New York
review_text: My husband and I stayed the weekend here in May 2011. The hotel is pretty much brand new and you are walking distance to TriBeCa and SoHo. Several subway stops are close so we were also able to venture around other parts of New York. The room was small but very nicely appointed and comfortable. But hey, it's NYC so why stay in your room except to sleep!

I recently stayed at the Sheraton TriBeCa while on a business trip. I found the hotel to be conveniently located to both the Financial District and SoHo. The staff were extremely nice and outgoing. A great place to stay while on vacation or on a business trip.

review_title: Close to metro, far from the tourist hubbub.
review_text: My husband and I stayed here for a week. We enjoyed being away from all the tourists, and several metro lines were close by. If you want a quiet area with good restaurants stay here. The room was clean, cool, and comfortable.

The hotel is in a prime location with two different subway stations just a few blocks away and the much quieter south end of town. The hotel was spotless all the time. The employees were polite and went above and beyond to be helpful at all times from the desk clerk to the housekeepers. The rooms were absolutely imaculantly clean and perfect. Good sized rooms and the most comfortable bed I have ever slept on. Will stay here again.

Booked this hotel as part of a flight/travel deal. I chose it due to the central location as I was travelling alone. On the doorstep was Grand Central Station, Park Avenue, 5th Avenue, Bryant Park. So much to do within walking distance (Times Square 10 mins). The hotel itself has just had a remodel and is very impressive. Efficient check-in, good size room with massive bed.

review_title: Bonne situation, cher pour le confort drs chambres
review_text: Hotel situÃ© tres pres de Central Park et du Rockfeller Center et de la 5th Avenue. tres bonne prÃ©sentation et trÃ¨s bon service. chambre relativement petite et salle de bain peu Ã©quipÃ©e et relativement petite pour le prix de la chambre. Personnel de rÃ©ception trÃ¨s poli, qualifiÃ© et serviable. vue depuis la chambre mauvaise si situÃ© en dessous du 15eme Ã©tage.
Not terrible, but you could find something in a better area for the same price. Also, the floors were dirty, both in the room and the corridors, and the air conditioning was loud.
bellman michael v. was knowledgable courteous and helpful and should be considered an asset to your organization.

My husband and I stayed for two weekend nights in Novemer 2011. We loved the spacious room and the very comfortable king sized bed. We were within walking distance of great theatre and restaurants and Grand Central Terminal, of course. We had a relaxing stay and would certainly like to return for a longer duration.

Stayed here 1 night right before Christmas. Although its a large room, that's about the only great thing.
There's a kitchen, fridge, etc which I'm sure is handy, but we didn't really use. Large seating area, with old dingy furniture. Bed was awful, with a dip in middle. Bedding was just a sheet and blanket.
Bathroom was tiny. Heat had no thermostat. It was either hot or cold.
Overall there is potential but needs a major upgrade. Location is decent. Not in tourist area which is nice.

Not impressed To be told on arrival at 11pm at night that the room you had booked 9 months in advance was not available after a 14 hour journey from the uk! Although somewhat expected after various recent reviews.We had booked a standard room with 2 double beds to accommodate myself , wife and teenage child. We were offered an upgrade which seemed acceptable, however it was the same size room with a king size bed and a roll out bed, which didn't exist! We had a quiet chat with another receptionist, went for a walk till midnight to return to a room With a newly delivered bed with a poor mattress and no bedding! Another trip to reception and this was resolved along with vouchers for complimentary breakfast( value apprx 80 usd). Following morning I informed yet another receptionist that we expected our bags to be moved to the room that we had booked upon our return that evening. The error was resolved and the room we booked and expected was supplied, along with a further complimentary breakfast. Apart from early mishap, great stay, great location, good sized room, views over chrysler building and no noise from other rooms/corridors.everything clean and in order, breakfast staff excellent, doormen will magic you a taxi in seconds! Hotel is as busy as grand central station, continual functions/ conferences in reception areas, don't expect to be recognised after a few days as way too many people.

review_title: Not for people with small children - but great location!
review_text: I guess in New York one can't expect too much of hotels, but with a brand name like this one I certainly had some expectations. The location was great, right next door to Grand Central and within walking distance to Times Square, 5th & 6th avenues, Top of the Rock, Central park etc. But service left a lot to be desired. The rooms were quite small even though we were at a super deluxe king sized one ( or so they told us). Housekeeping never answered the phone and the room and bathroom only got cleaned after 3 days and that too on my insistence. Amenities like shower cap, shoe shine, cotton, coffee maker etc. are only available on request (even b&b's in UK provide these). But what irritated me most was the refusal to heat up baby's food stating the reason that outside food is not allowed to be heated! Seriously, baby food?!!! We stated there for 5 nights. I didn't find the staff there very friendly or helpful, though I have to say that room service were quite efficient. I guess the hotel is ok if you are travelling there on business, but is definitely not convenient if you stay with a little one! or maybe it could be down to the New York culture...

review_title: Total Rip Off and terrible staff and service I ever experienced in any hotel.
review_text:
I stayed at Grand Hyatt Hotel, New York for one night along with my wife and my 2 daughters. One a 3 year old and other a 4 month infant.
The stay was terrible just even from start. The moment I entered the hotel, and the bell boy got my luggage and I told him to give me luggage tags which he refused to give saying that I can't give you tags until you check in. It was hard to believe that once he got the bags, he was supposed to give me tags. Of course after that I have to check in.
I had a 4 month infant with me so for her feed I asked for an electric kettle for warming water for her feed and was shocked to hear that they said they dont have electric kettle in hotel. They send me a coffee maker instead, which even wasn't working. At last I placed an order of a bottle of hot water at room service number and when I got the order w shocked to see I was charged $25 for that bottle of water, which includes water cost, delivery charges, gratuity.
Then I placed an breakfast order for my 3 year old daughter, scrambled eggs and the lady taking order I told her I don't want bacon it it and when order came, it again had bacon along with the eggs. Upon complaining , it was replaced.
For using business centre I was charged extra and even a black and White print out I was charged $1 per copy.
Even when checking out, asked concierge to send bell boy to take the luggage down, he charged me $2 per bag, in total of $12 to take the luggage down, saying that we have been doing this practice for last 5 years now.
Totally pathetic and total rip off hotel. I wouldn't ever stay in this hotel ever ever again. I would prefer staying night on roads rather than staying at this creepy and rip off hotel.

Stayed here for 3 nights with my family. The location is fantastic, central for all the famous NY landmarks. Yes the rooms are small but you come to NY to see all it has to offer, not to sit in a hotel room! The staff were friendly and helpful and nothing was too much trouble. Breakfasts were hectic but ideal for busy tourists.

review_title: The service level at this Holiday Inn is excellent
review_text:
We stayed at Holiday Inn through the Hurricane Irene weekend. We were in Manhattan for a long weekend and booked a standard room (2 double beds) for 3 nights. While the room was smaller than we are accustomed to, it is normal by NYC standards.
Where HIE distinguished itself is with the level of service during the Hurricane. Management communicted very early on with a printed note in each room regarding their preparations. That simple communication to customers is so often overlooked. Management was on property the entire weekend, brought in extra food, made sure we understood that a generator was available in the event of electrical interruption, etc.
The staff were all very friendly and most helpful throuhgout our stay. I can highly recommend this hotel.
Also, the location is really good, only 1 block from the 28th Street MTA station for lines 1, 2, and 3. Walkable to Times Square in decent weather.

I stayed at the Grand Hyatt for ten days. First of all how any half decent hotel has the audacity to charge for wifi is beyond ridiculous. They need to move on with the times!
The Grand Hyatt has one very obvious plus point working for it, it's location which is adjacent to Grand Central. Ideal if you need to travel to Greenwich or Connecticut.
The room we were given had a innocuous view, builders working on some kind of extension to the hotel. Not ideal especially when you want to open the blind to find some noisy builders looking in!
The room was OK, it's New York, so guess we need to be realistic in terms of expectations of size. However, there is no excuse for a room to be kept untidy (found some bottle lid on the edge of the bed and hair on the cupboards). 
Lastly, they had the cheek to charge a fee to leave bags after checkout. That just seems petty and in a sense sums up the value they place on customers.
Would I stay here again....I think there are better hotels that offer greater value for money!

review_text: Had an excellent stay at this hotel over new years. The staff are so polite, hard to fault this place.

The Grand Hyatt met and exceeded my expectations. Very classy and conveniently located next to Grand Central Station it lends itself to anything the traveler needs. The staff was very professional and knowledgeable. 
There is a 24hr 'market' in the lobby. Prices for most items were $8/$9. The coffee was good. You can get better selections in Grand Central's food court when it is open. It is connected via covered walkways. There is also loads of shopping there. 
Times Square is about 5 blocks away. NYC Transporter shuttle picks up/drops off across the street. Super Shuttle does this at the door on the first floor. 
The only minor complaints: While the room was larger than expected for NYC, the bath/toilet was cramped with a very generic utility-style toilet that didn't fit in with the classy decor and the shower curtain had mold on it. 
Overall it was a great place to stay.

We arrived during a heat wave & our room was sweltering. We immediately turn down the temperature as low as it could go & turned up the fan. We left for 6-7 hours & upon our return the room was still sweltering. Couldn't sleep because of the heat & woke up sweaty & dehydrated. We stayed on the 34th floor & thereist have been maintenance going on becuase starting around 7:00 a.m. It was outrageously loud. The only positive about the hotel is it is located next to Grand Central making it very easy to get to & around from. However, in the future I will stay At a nicer hotel that is less convenient.

Some of the front desk staff were not very helpful, I asked on two separate occasions for recommendations for a restaurant (breakfast and dinner) and was recommended to the same place twice. I went there on my first day for breakfast as I didn't know any better but there are lots of amazing places close by that I event to over the 5 days I was there. Compared to other hotels we have stayed in across the world, this felt very expensive for what it was, although it's a peak time and so guess this affected the price.

review_text: Great spot near Times Square. Family friendly (with a bunk in the room that really went over well). Clean and stylish enough. TV could use updating. 10th floor was still loud - but it is a block from Times Square. DVD player and small fridge in room. Would (will?) stay again...

I really, really wanted to like RMG. I tried hard. Unfortunately, the only thing this place had going for it is location - 1/2 block from Time Square. 
Customer Service: very disorganized. Appalling. The left hand doesnt seem to know what the right hand is up to. We had 4 adults and 4 children with us. We reserved 2 quad bunk rooms about 4 months in advance. We stored our luggage at about 10:30 and were assured our rooms would be ready promptly at 3 PM. After touring the city we had some very tired, small children. And adults! We arrived at the hotel at 3:30 finding that only one room was ready. The other would be ready in "20 minutes". Well repeat this scenario for another 2 hours. We repeatedly called checking on the status of the other room. Each time we talked to someone different and were given a different story. It was ready and the key was being sent up. 30 minutes later oh it's not ready it's still being cleaned. 20 minutes later it's being checked by housekeeping and we're bringing the key to you now. At 5:30 I stormed downstairs ready to check out completely. The two at the front desk acted as though this was all brand new information, they argued about what room we were to have, and then assured us the key was being sent up. I demanded a key in my hand before I left that desk or I was checking out completely. Needless to say I received the key and we went up to our room, after demanding a lower rate as well. Also, everyone had very thick accents. Which is fine, I have no issue with that...but not one single American is employed by this hotel in any regard...? Seems a bit strange an makes me wonder about their business practices.
Rooms: clean but in need of repair. The wallpaper is gashed and peeling. The carpet is worn. The TVs are mismatched and broken. Lights broken. Requested that a broken light and tv be repaired - neither were. Asked again and were told it takes several days to put in a "work order"...? Stayed 2 days and never addressed further. The shower is all tile and while clean, the grout is stained. Also, beware that only a thin shower curtain Seperates the shower from the rest of the room. Kinda weird. The beds are comfy. But know this room is functional and that's all. 
Noise: be aware this hotel has a club scene and plays bass laden music until about 3 am 5 days a week. Problematic for lower floors.
Overall: if you plan on just sleeping in your hotel while NYC the RMG will probably suffice. It's not a luxury hotel. It's not even a fun boutique. Another reviewer said its more like a hostel and I agree. But the location is excellent and for the price you probably won't find better in that regard. I think the RMG may have been neat and fun at one time but it is in swrious need of an overhaul in both appearance and customer service. So if you can live with a lipsticked pig, the RMG is probably for you. We, however, won't be back.

We didn't have any problems at all with the hotel, room or the service. The location is very close to time square. If there is an negative to the location it would be that there's not a subway station close to the hotel but that's not an reason that will change our mind on staying here next time we visit NYC.

I stay at this hotel a few times each year for work. I go out of my way to book the propery for a few reasons. 
First is the location. It's located right on the E line on the subway and it's very easy to get around the city. You are only a 15 minute walk from Times Square. 
Second is the service. I have been staying here for three years for work. I have yet to experience a rude staff member. 
Finally is the value. The few times I paid my own personal funds for a room, I found the value to be very good considering you're in manhattan. 
Yes, the rooms are small. But you shouldn't be headed to the city to live in your hotel. That is just my opinion.

It's a Four Points, so you don't expect the moon and stars, but this hotel is clean and well maintained, with efficient and friendly staff and good rooms. It's at the top end of the range of the brand, and better than many Sheratons I have stayed at. You're not staying on the greatest block, but it's about as convenient as you can get. I will stay there again with pleasure. The front desk staff in particular get a mention - super nice and a genuine welcome every time you come back to the hotel.

review_text:
I stayed at hotel grace for 4 nights in may 2011 for my birthday.

I had researched the hotel before we booked so i was aware of the crazy pool parties in the bar area so this was not a problem for me and my friend.

review_title: Totally recommended! Five stars all round.
review_text:
We loved this hotel so much we ended up booking an extra three nights here! 
The location is great, the staff are lovely and the rooms are terrific - excellent Starbucks coffee, good shower with nice products, lovely fluffy bathrobes and a good safe. 
We used the hotel restaurant too, which was very good, although a glass of pretty ordinary wine was $10 without tip!!
Don't bother with the Chinese takeaway a couple of doors up - it's rubbish- but Schnippers on Times Square ( about 2 mins walk) is brilliant, and Dean & Deluca good for breakfast stuff. 
A super hotel that's perfect for seeing New York. Can't wait to come back!

review_title: Unique hotel with funky vibe; great for a trendy couple.
review_text:

Party in pool area was great...DJ and all! However, the bouncer kind of pushed one in our group because we didnt "stop to get carded" at the door. If I pay that much for a hotel I dont want to flash an ID everytime I walk outside. The only other issue we had was that no one answered the phones while we called for a wake up call...also not acceptable for $500 a weekend
Other than that, we loved our stay!!

Had a wonderful 4 night stay at this hotel. The rooms are not massive but it's New York, and they are more than adequate. The beds really are very comfortable and the free wifi was a nice bonus - something that many upscale hotels do not offer.
The hotel is located just a couple of blocks from Times Square and directly opposite Port Authority which was really handy. There are some 'interesting' shops and buildings along the same street, but we did not feel any less safe than along many of the other streets around the Times Square area.
All in all, excellent value for money and a very nice hotel!

review_title: Solid, high value option with great convenience.
review_text: Our family (two kids ages 14 and 11) stayed at the Four Points for one week. Marcos the manager was great in accommodating our request for two rooms next to each other. The rooms had a view of the Empire State Building which was beautifully lit at night. They were large enough for us. Staff (particularly Alex the head bellman) were helpful and friendly. Small bar in lobby was nice respite for drink after day of seeing sights and was good place in morning for coffee. Biggest positive of this hotel is its location which was within two blocks of three subway stations that provided access to every line. It was also close to 9th Ave with tons of great restaurants. Yes, the block occasionally had some questionable characters but we always felt safe because there were always other tourists walking around (three hotels on block) and often a police officer walking a beat. Only minor complaint: our Apple devices had problems accessing free WiFi.

review_title: Only location is good that's all
review_text:
We were touring around USA for almost a month and stayed at a couple of hotels in few cities. This is what I have to say about Hilton new York:
Pros: great location for tourist as it's at the centre of every place of interest.
Cons: no matter which level of membership you are either walk in, gold or diamond, no difference. The waiting time for check in counter at hhonors or diamond counter was so much longer than the usual counter. I am a diamond member and believe me this doesn't mean anything at all. Upon check in we asked for a nice room and was told that the room assigned to us was nice. When we walked into the room, to our horror, it was so dim even we switched on all the lights and the bathroom was so pathetic. The furniture was so old that you can smell it. Looks no diff from any 3 star hotel actually. No upgrade at all.
So we went down back to the front desk to complain and she gave us a much better renovated room. Still the bathroom is so tiny. Don't understand why she couldn't give us this room from the beginning. Have a feeling that the staff will try their luck to give away the old ugly rooms first and hope the guest will just accept it without any complaint. It's wasting so much of our time on queueing to changing room etc.
The hotel is seriously under staffed as we had problem getting through our calls to concierge especially. The lobby was really busy and crazy. Morning breakfast was chaotic and we decided to take away from second day onwards.
On check out day, we were being approached by a man before the taxi queue to tell us that we can take his town car to JFK airport at $69 instead of the usual $85 cuz he give special rate to Hilton guest. We were made to understand that was hotel limousine so we took his car. As usual the taxi queue was chaotic. Upon arrival at the airport, he told us that total should be $69+tax+toll fee+20% tipping. We really felt that it was a rip off and the hotel staff should have control over this kind of crooks that hang around and behave like he is from the hotel limousine service. He seemed to know the hotel bell boy well and tipped him when we went into his car.
Overall, you should stay in this hotel only for it's location purpose, and don't expect anything else from them. We stayed at hyatt 48 lex at Lexington ave earlier and the service was so much better even though it's a small hotel. Their breakfast is complimentary and it's simple and nice. Room was nicer as well.

review_text:
I have just returned from a 5 night stay at the Hilton hotel in New York. I have to say this was my first time in New York and found the location of the hotel to be fantastic. You are just a 5 minute walk from central park and all of the places you want to visit are in walking distance or near a subway connection. 
Our bedroom was to a high standard with a view overlooking the New York skyline, all the usual facilities that you would expect to find in hotel rooms were there with coffee machines etc. 
The service in the hotel was very good as well. While we were there the hotel had some very large functions and conferences on but don't let this put you off. The hotel is very large but i would say you have to expect that in the states. Breakfast was ok, I would advise to get an early start as the que can be long once you get past 9am. 
We spoke to the concierge team a few times about different restaurants and places to visit and each time they booked what we wanted and left a message in the room. 
All in all, like I said this was my first time in New York and thought the whole holiday from start to finish was fantastic. I would recommend this hotel but be aware that this is a very large hotel and can get very busy.

review_title: The only thing that this hotel has going for it is the name... Hilton and that's not going to be enough to trick me again in the
review_text:
Let me try to be as brief as I can. We reserved guest rooms and conference rooms in this hotel because we assumed the Hilton brand is one you can't go wrong with. Man oh man, were we wrong. We canceled half of our meetings in the hotel because these people just couldn't get it together. No white board until hours later, even though it was ordered as part of the reservation. The room was freezing cold and it took countless phone calls and random personnel visits for that to get fixed, if it ever did. The internet NEVER worked even after we were given a special free access code. The conference room service was so terrible we canceled the second day after we talked to some manager that was absolutely out of touch with what it means to provide a decent service that one would want to use again in the future... Enough said about that aspect of the trip. Now the guest rooms.nothing super amazing, clean rooms with good beds but very small bathrooms. Our room had the toilet paper holder way way to close to the toilet to the point where it was uncomfortable to use the toilet. To make things even more annoying the toilet was slightly twisted towards the wall. Go figure. We used the laundry service and that was a nightmare too. The laundry was 12 hours late and was only delivered after 10 phone calls with incompetent employees which all had major attitudes. To make things worse a random cleaning lady literally walked in the room without knocking one evening, and when she realized the room was not empty she mumbled something about checking to make sure we are ok and then she more or less stormed out. A bedside lamp was broken, and no one picked up the phone when we called for service. We stayed on the Sunday the clocks changed, and we were told at the desk that all clocks in rooms would "fall back" automatically. Ours didn't, nor did half the clocks in the lobby. We were told wi-fi in the lobby was free--another lie. Worse:they had continental breakfast set up--for a price, of course--with Starbucks cups and napkins, but the coffee wasn't Starbucks and the tea was another (inferior) brand to the Tazo teas Starbucks uses. That seems like a blatant violation of some trust or contract, but whatever. The hotel is large, clean, reasonably comfortable, busy and staffed with polite employees. review_text: Esta claro que buscar un hotel bien ubicado, bonito y barato en Manhattan puede ser tarea dificil, pero dimos en el blanco con este pequeÃ±o hotel. Es muy modesto, las habitaciones son pequeÃ±as y compartiamos cuarto de baÃ±o (limpisimo, por cierto), pero su ubicacion compensa con creces. A tan solo 5 mins andando del Empire State, 15 de Times Square y 30 de Central Park, hay una gran variedad de restaurantes, delis, tiendas y servicios muy cerca. I was put onto this gem 4 years ago, and it really is an amazing location at an amazing price.
Most rooms here are shared bathroom, however you can (as we have both visits) book a room with private bathroom. To stay in a decent location in New York City will cost you, but this is one place that is cheap, and in an excellent location.
We stayed this visit for 5 nights, the rooms are basic, but clean, the bed mattresses are vinyl so make a bit of noise when moving around, but are still quite comfortable (we had no complaints/loss of sleep after 5 nights there!) the shower/toilet are clean as expected. The price you'll find hard to beat approx. $130/night with private bathroom, compare this to one star hotels in bad locations at sometimes double that price!
But the location is what it's all about! 2 min walk from Union Square (features farmers markets, is lively at night), which has a central subway stop that connects to the majority of the main subway lines which means you can get all over Manhattan (and Brooklyn!) with ease. As with everything in NYC you can walk anywhere too, but close by are SoHo & The meat packing district (some of my favorite areas).
I love NYC and cannot see me staying elsewhere on future visits the price for the location is just too hard to beat!

review_title: Used to be my favorite place to stay in NYC
review_text: I used to travel to NYC all the time, sometimes once or twice a week for weeks on end. When I did travel to the city, my number one choice was Hilton's flagship hotel, the Hilton New York. It has been about three years since I made regular trips to the city, so I have not stayed at this Hilton for some time. The years have not been kind to this property. It is still a great location for a lot of different things to see and do, this cannot be denied, but the cleanliness and appearance within the hotel has fallen off. First, I was assigned a non-smoking floor, which stunk of cigarette smoke one more than one occassion. Second, the hallways had broken wall sconces and trash in them. The room itself was fine, nothing extraordinary. This is the same hotel where I have had my biggest and smallest rooms in all of my many travels, so I have seen a lot at this property. The bathroom was not clean and the shower had a head which did not always work well and a tub which did not drain very fast, leaving you in a large puddle. I was going to give this a 3, but because of location and for old times sake, I will bump up to a 4.

review_title: Small, comfortable, well-located to avoid the mid-town madness but convenient to the subway, Greenwich Village, SoHo and Chelsea
review_text:
While this was admittedly a freebie courtesy of frequent flier miles, it was a pleasant surprise to discover this pleasant small hotel just a block south of the Houston station on the #1 line.
We were greeted by a very pleasant and courteous staff at check-in and, though an hour early, shown promptly to our room. The room was small but nicely appointed with a fairly sleek, modern aesthetic that was warm and comfortable. The bed was comfortable and nicely outfitted with fluffy comforters and equally comfortable pillows. The bathroom was modern and nicely outfitted. One quibble - the faucet in the sink was overly touchy and you can't avoid spraying the countertop no matter how slowly the water is running. It was a quiet and restful night's sleep, though it should be noted that some of the second floor rooms are above the restaurant, which was hosting a fairly noisy celebration of some kind that brought several calls of complaint to the manager while we dined at the bar. I would highly recommend this Sheraton for anyone wanting to sleep comfortably in a more quiet but interesting Manhattan location.

review_text: This was one if the worst Hotel stays of my life!!!On December 17,2011 I arrived at the Fairfield Inn with 10 girlfriends. This however was not an ordinary girls weekend. The trip was at the request of a very sick friend who always wanted to see New York at Christmas. We came from South Carolina, Virginia, New Jersey and Pennsylvania to be together to try and make this as wonderful for her as possible. We also requested a wheelchair so that we could take her to See the lights and decorations I was told no problem. It was a problem. No wheelchair. I requested 3 double rooms got 3 queens. We were told if we were not "ok with that we could leave" . 11 women 3 beds in a hotel that does not supply cots . 5 of us slept on the floors.As well as uncomfortable this was a NYC fire code violation. All for the low low price of $ 1300.00 . I have contacted the hotel management and they were as casual about our situation as their rude front desk staff and the unprofessional manager on duty. I checked with the Marriott Marquis and was told they had double rooms at the same rate we paid available that night and all it would have taken was a phone call from the Fairfield. This was a very emotional trip made so much worse by a staff that was well aware of the reason for our trip.

The staff were all pleasant and importantly not in an artificial way, they seemed happy to help and ensure my stay was pleasant. I've stayed in so many Radisson hotels and highly recommend you do the same, excellent hotel chain.
David
This has been the best experience I've had at a hotel in New York.

review_title: Cute Boutique, Perfect Location, Wonderful Staff!
review_text: The perfect location, reasonable price for NYC, over-the-top staff! The staff made the expensively, simple, small room worth it!! Very clean room. The thin windows give you the perfect sound of the busiest city in the northeast!!

Pros - price was right for a family of four making a last minute trip to NYC. $269 for 2 double beds. Location was great, room was outstanding (newly renovated) Staff was very helpful and friendly. 
Cons - street noise. May have been the corner room and the wall of windows (which was a good thing for the view). If you are a light sleeper may want to request a room away from street. 
Bottom line - We will stay there again

review_title: Were amazingly helpful during Hurricane Irene
review_text:
We enjoyed 5 nights stay here but unfortunately were due to fly home the day the hurricane hit. As a result our flight was cancelled and couldn't fly out for another 6 days. The hotel allowed us to remain in our room ( which had been upgraded on arrival to a king) for a reduced rate. Luckily we managed to get an earlier flight and only needed the two exta nights, there was no problem cancelling the extra nights we provisionally booked. They were patient as we tried to find the extra money to pay for the room.
The hotel is in a good location, close to subway stops. The Flatiron building is right near by, the Empire State Building is a five minute walk, times square a little further. We even walked to central park one day. 
The room had everything we needed including fast wifi! Parts of the room were a little worn around the edges but it was modern, fresh and clean. The room was a king size and an ok size but that's standard for the area. It was perfectly adequate but upgrading to a king would be worth the money. I can imagine the queen is a little small. 
The breakfast was a nice idea but didn't work for me, by the time I got there at 08:30 it was demolished. You either have to squeeze standing up in the Lobby area or take it back to the room. But it is complementary so can't really complain. Even though there is no restaurant on site they do provide room service from a nearby restaurant, never tried it but menu looked promising.
In summary the service was fantastic and it made a good base for exploring the city. Good budget accommodation.
Again thank you to the reception staff for being very helpful at a stressful time. It made things so much easier to know we at least had accomodation organised.
Would stay here again

review_title: Perfect spot for whirlwind city stay
review_text: We got a great deal on the room- 140 incl. tax on bookit.com- and all of the little extras were wonderful! The aquarium was beautiful and the rooms, though very cozy, had fun touches with a remote for the curtains, iPod dock w surround sound, a tv in the bathroom and a great shower. The location is perfect especially if you don't like being trapped in midtown- you're a short walk away from everything. I could see a longer stay being uncomfortable with the room size and the tv was spotty- a lot of channels didn't come in. I don't know if its worth the $300/night they ask but if you find a deal, it's a great getaway!

Our stay was wonderful. Room was very clean and bathroom was quite spacious. Shower was a bit noisy but it did not bother us. Everyone was helpful and friendly. Our room was upgraded and we had a late check-out. We hope to stay there again and look forward to the bar being open.

review_title: Stylish boutique hotel in good location
review_text:
We stayed here for 5 nights to celebrate my birthday, and I loved it! The communal areas were modern and very stylish; our room was the same, and surprisingly spacious for New York. 
I was paranoid about the risk of bedbugs so checked the whole room from top to bottom, and there was no sign.
Couldn't fault the facilities... Molton Brown toiletries, good hairdryer, flat screen tv, etc etc. The staff were always polite and helpful.
The hotel is in a good location in central Manhattan, with a subway station around the corner. It's very convenient for lots of the sights, with the Empire State just a couple of blocks away. 
The hotel restaurant was great, they specialise in seafood so i had some delicious oysters and they put a birthday candle in my ice cream for me! :o)
Would definitely recommend!

A girlfriend and I stayed 3 days at this hotel. The location was great for getting around downtown NYC. The rooms were a reasonable size for the city, the shower was small but fantastic, and the lobby has an amazing massive aquarium as a centerpiece. Service was well intentioned, if inept. Eataly is one block away, and the best coffee at Stumptown is 3 blocks north.

review_title: Few start-up glitches but enjoyable stay
review_text:
All good in general, just a few things needing ironing out in this new hotel. Staff helpful and friendly, rooms are nicely done and clean - only couple of issues were a fuse blowing which put out main lights in the room - we coped with bathroom lights though and we were offered lots of lamps. Also they need to invest in double glazing as room heated up quickly but got cold quickly too so that would be nice to find a balance.
Enjoyed our stay though as it's in an ideal location to get all around Manhattan. Just round the corner from places to eat like Eataly or the Shake Shack and great bars like the rooftop at 230 5th.

This hotel was clean and tidy room was quite basic I upgraded the room which was nice but still quite small good location two blocks from empire state good 10 minute walk to times square staff were really nice and helpful had a great time new York is amazing

review_title: Nice location...kinda trendy...a bit above average
review_text: Just completed a two night stint here. Paid for the larger broadway king (260sq ft room) and it was cool but cool in a way where you are trying to make something old look new. Floors were dirty. Windows filthy and a misty water smell was masked by a awesome bed, great bathroom and nice decor. Location was great as two subway stops were a block away on either direction and your on madison ave!

I was not sure about this hotel because it was still in the soft opening stages, but I am so happy my husband and I stayed here. Staff was wonderful, hotel was cozy and quiet, our king size bed/room was clean an comfy, and after a long day of sight seeing in the cold it was nice to come back to a wall jet shower. The hotel has no room service/ restaurant but that was no big deal because restaurants/delis were walking distance. This is our new spot when we come back to NY.

Stayed for 3 nights in unusually cold march. 
I loved this hotel. The room was surprisingly big and really clean! The bed was huge and very very comfortable. The hotel provides everything u need toiletries, coffee machine, maps etc. 
The reception staff were very helpful and even recommended and booked us a restaurant on our first night. 
The location was also brilliant we walked everywhere. It is very close to the flatiron building, empire state and times square! 
We wanted somewhere which was nice for a good price and I have to say that I was very very happy that we chose this hotel!

I stayed here with my Mum for a birthday celebration, her 50th my 21st. 
Let's starts at the beginning, we arrived 3 hours past check in due to our flight been delayed and were taken straight too our room and given maps of the area and the times of breakfast. 
The room was an ok size, 2 double beds with enough room to just about walk round in. The room was opposite the lift, this is something did not bother us at all. Over the 5 nights we stayed we never heard it. On the other hand the traffic noise was really loud, it seemed like the window didn't quiet shut properly and we could hear everything! BUT after our days out and about we were so tired, we didnt have a problem sleeping at all! 
Breakfast was ok, a deffinate grab and go. We took ours back up too our room too eat, which was a little difficult but we managed it! On a few mornings we went to the local dinar and had amazing breakfasts. 
The location was amazing, right on the corner of Madison Avenue, everything we wanted was right on our door step! 
We had a really great time and all the staff were fab! Even sorting out a coffee machine for my mum who wanted to pack a kettle.
I would defiantly stay here again!

Our teeny tiny room rocked from the noises on the street including the rumble of the subway and street traffic. The bed was on a platform with drawers for storing our stuff... the only storage space in the room. Really claustrophobic experience that cost a bundle. Don't expect complimentary breakfast or coffee. That said, I do appreciate the early check in by the cordial folks at the front desk.

My sister and I spent 5 nights at The Flatiron Hotel last week. While it is a nice hotel and the staff is friendly and accommodating it is not a four star hotel. The rooms were clean and comfortable. They brought us up a mini fridge and coffee pot. The beds were comfy. What would make it a four star? Added touches like stationary, NY magazines, double paned windows, bell men, and room service. The location was fine for us...a bit out of the rat race, but for some, they may find it too far away from the hustle and bustle (we love to walk!) Would we stay here again? No, probably not. Would we recommend it to friends? Probably, with full disclosure.

I came to this hotel in september for a vacation , i loved it so much i came back to it recently for another trip. Great hotel- very clean and updated. Its close to everything! Staff is super nice and helpful . Im always going and coming from new york and i wouldnt choose to stay anywhere else but here to stay.

review_title: Friendly staff with fun technology equiped rooms
review_text: This is a newly opened hotel and when we visited the resturant was not yet open. This is not a problem really as there are plenty of places to eat nearby. The staff was very friendly and we alwas had a good feeling comming back to the hotell after a day out. The twin double bed rooms were large enough for us with two adults ald two kids to fit w/o any problems. A fun thing was the technology in the rooms including integrated TV in the bathroom mirror! Not very necessary, but fun :-)

review_title: Wow! Amazing service particularly from Mayerlin & Maureen! Thank you my stay was great and would highly recommend!
review_text: Other than a small hiccup when I arrived (heating wasn't on/working) I was quickly moved (& upgraded) to an incredibly comfortable room, fantastic bed & WIFI, extremely clean and cannot fault the service. The hotel has this great "Desires" program and Mayerlin booked and researched tours for me before I'd even arrived! Extremely personal & knowledgeable front desk staff, nothing was too much trouble, great restaurant info and other helpful info for a traveller! Even a note from my room attendant wishing me a safe onward journey! I would highly recommend this place-make sure you ask for an upper floor though I was in 206 and it was a bit noisy early morning (briefly) and the heater was a little noisy but everything else was comfortable, warm friendly staff at every interaction-will stay again when next in New York.

Even though the hotel is just opening and working things out, I have to say it is a wonderful property. The views are spectacular I could see the empire states building. The rumble of the subway made me feel like hey I'm in the big city. Steve the manager was so kind and helpful I can't say enough good things about him. If you stay at this property you will hopefully get to meet him.

review_title: Nice hotel, but the service was so so.
review_text:
The rooms were okay, but everytime we asked for anything service oriented, it was either missed or done wrong.
We called for a toothbrush and was brought toothpaste instead. We called to have the sheets changes, but it was never done. We called to have our noisy neighbors kids stop slamming the doors, but hours later they were at it again. And the last straw was calling the front desk for two wine glasses and being told I'd be charged by room service for them. I said fine, but they were never delivered. Normally that wouldn't be an issue, but they have a bottle of wine for sale in every room, so it doesn't really make sense to me why they wouldn't have a wine glass in the rooms to begin with.
In their defense, we were given a new room and free wine glasses later when we complained, but I expected a bit more from this hotel initially.

review_title: Luxury hotel in The middle of Manhattan!
review_text: The perfekt hotell in Middle of Manhattan! Close to Metro and good restaurants. Walking distance to everything. Start with Ã  breakfast in madisson square park and walk up or Down! The surroundings are "calm" and you can easy walk to The shopping. Rooms are small, clean and designed.
It's a very nice hotel. I enjoyed the tv on the mirror.

I found this hotel by chance on the net. I have to say that all is just great! The room is impecable, confortable, great huge tv, and the staff is very freindly. The manager Vince knows his work and is there for you. The best of the best. We even had the chance to speak with the real owner of the hotel :-) rare thing in this big city. Enjoy
Special thanks to our housekeeper/Joyce :) .. Very nice caring lady who attended to all of our requests. What better location than Midtown East :)

East gate Tower is in a fantastic location and many of New York's attractions are within easy walking distance. Rooms are a little dated but overall very clean and comfortable.
Hotel staff were courteous and friendly.

Location and good quality. Prices are good. Some thing to improve in the hotel: the kitchen appliances are old.
The rooms have good sizes and the beds are comfortables.
