Art deco classic , amazing building that looks best the way it is without renovation! Only problem was banging from service room about ours, other than that very very good

I recently stayed here with my daughter and was very impressed with this hotel. The room was very clean especially the bathroom, 2 double beds were comfortable and there was even a fridge and desk. Not a bad size room for NYC, and it was pretty quiet on the 4th floor. Breakfast was good, lots of choice including waffles. The staff were helpful and check in and out was speedy and they stored our luggage on the last day.

On the west side of the theater district, a couple of blocks to major theaters. Cost efficient way to stay in midtown. Being near the port authority the neighborhood is a bit dodgy but two blocks over there is a very large nypd presence at the start of the theater district. Very clean but typical polyester bedding. Staff is very friendly and helpful. Could not find a way to use the shower head but no big deal. Breakfast is a gallon bowl of bacon cooked in the microwave - same technique for the eggs. Bagels and cereal available if you prefer. People staying here mainly foreign budget tourists. Overall not a bad alternative place especially booking at the last minute.

I am a 19year old female student and I travelled to NYC alone. This hotel has been awesome, good location, good value BUT it has a huge security problem. Anybody can just enter the hotel and there was a night (actually tonight. This just happened, im writing this review immediately because this experience was terrible.) at about 245am, a big burly man knocked on my door. I didn't know who he was, I didn't know anyone here in NYC. I was jusy lucky i could hide behind my door and lock it. He stood outside for a while knocked a couple of times and called out, "hello?" many times. That experience was pretty scary... I cant get back to sleep and I didn't know what to do. Would probably never stay here alone again. Hotel management, please do something about this. It's really quite scary. Especially when girls like me travel alone and unexpected guests turn up. It's terrible. 
The hotel is nice to stay in but it's security is a big problem.

review_title: Good value, great location but paper thin walls and really basic facilities.
review_text: Pleasantly surprised by this Orel in a really good location. A short walk through Manhattan to Times Square, 5/6/7th Avenues for shopping. There is also plenty to do in and around the hotel with good eateries and pubs a stones throw away.

review_title: Central location on a budget- would defo stop again!!
review_text: Stopped here 4 6 nights nov 11 for just over 725gbp with my hubby in a double pod with on suite. The price is very reasonable for central manhatten if u compare. The staff were helpful and friendly. The room and communal areas were spotless. The room is tiny but if all your after is a place to sleep then you'll be fine. The shower was hot and powerful but I agree offers little privacy if you are not close to your room mate. The look of the room is simular style to ikea but makes cleaver use of the limited space. Only thing lacking for me was full length mirror, the room was cleaned daily and towels changed etc, complementary toiletrees offered. Overall the hotel was contemapary with free wifi and ipad loan and resonably priced coffee and snack bar. Paying for location here walking distance to subway and most major tourist attractions. You reach rockafeller centre and 5th ave in under 10min. Plenty of cheap places to eat within a five minute walk. If u want to spend lots of time relaxing in your room then mybe not for you, a place to rest your head after a days shopping/ sightseeing perfect!

review_title: Not for everybody, but a reasonably-priced choice for Manhattan
review_text:
I spent the last four nights here so I'm working from a fresh memory. 
Now I'll admit that I was disappointed at first, and wondering if I had made a huge mistake. But most of that was due to the A/C not working in my room. Even in early November, the humidity was stifling, and other parts of the hotel were even worse, such as the bathrooms.
But once the A/C was fixed two days later, my perception of The Pod Hotel changed for the better. I appreciated its convenient location mid-town near the subway stops for the 6, E, and M trains. The room was not spotless, but reasonably clean. 
Yes the rooms are small, and unless you book one of the larger rooms with the en-suite bathrooms I would not recommend it for anything other than a solo traveler. I had my doubts about the shared bathroom facilities but I never had to wait as there are 4 on each floor and above your room door are lights to let you know which ones are occupied. Except for wet floors left by the previous and inconsiderate guest, the bathrooms are in good condition. 
Note that that on my floor (9th) bathroom #4 has a window which is fixed in the open position, exposing your naked body to windows on the opposite side of the building. I do not know if this is the case on other floors.
As I did not need to leave Manhattan until well after checkout, they graciously allowed me to leave my luggage with them during the day. You get a claim check so nobody walks off with your suitcase.
Besides the room size, another negative is that the hotel does not have an ice machine. However they do have a vending machine (Coke products only) and there are numerous cafes within walking distance. I highly recommend Pax on 51st and 3rd Av, 1/2 block from the hotel and on the way to/from the nearest subway stops.
Some reviewers complained about noise but I did not find that to be problematic, and my room was near the elevator and bathrooms. I would occasionally hear a loudly talking person in the hallway, but I still slept very well.
I would recommend this hotel ,but with caveats. If you can tolerate the sleeping compartment of an Amtrak train, it won't be a problem for you. But if you need a spacious room, you won't like it one bit.

review_text: Come hanno scritto altri utenti, l'unica pecca di questo hotel e' la colazione. Ottima l'accoglienza e la disponibilitÃ  del personale. review_title: Shocked to see how worn down and out of date this property has become.
review_text:
Had reservations to stay 3 nights at this property with my wife - she insisted we leave after one evening there.
Everything seemed worn out and dirty. They haven't maintained or updated this hotel in a long time. 
Our room was large but only had a bed , a small desk and a mirror in it. Therr was a lot of empty space - Felt like they didn't want to spend the money on an armchair or other furnishings. Room felt like a $80 per night hotel - but it was quite expensive. 
Location is very good and the staff seemed very nice - but can't make up for its shortcomings. 
We couldn't wait to get out of there. We won't go back until we hear the hotel has been fully renovated.

review_title: Great service, great location, but needs more lights
review_text: Our family spent two nights at the W, and mostly were quite charmed by the hotel and its staff. Every single staff person we encountered, from the doormen helping us out of our cab and into the hotel, to the front desk, the concierge, and the engineering staff (more on that later), were simply great: helpful, friendly, warm, informative. We loved the location and the general vibe of the hotel, as did our 11-year-old daughter. The room was spacious and comfortable, Â with a stellar view over Union Square. Our only issue is that the decorative theme of this hotel seems to be "dim." The halls are dimly lit and our room was so dark that we had to ask for more lights. The good news is the staff responded promptly and efficiently, and brought us both a standing light and a desk light. Â We'd Â love to come back to this lovely, attentive hotel.
Great place for the price..... don't get panicked from the shared bathroom. Its very clean. Would come back again.

This is the smallest room of my life. No kidding. Thank goodness I have a toilet. Not all rooms do. 
More like a prison. Cell.

We stayed here for a week and really enjoyed it. As has been well described already the rooms are small but have everything you need. We had a double room with an 'ensuite' shower. Don't share with someone you don't know really well - the wall between the shower and the room is clear glass. 
The location is great, just a block away from a subway station. The staff were really helpful and good at recommending restaurants etc. Free wifi in the rooms was an added bonus. Don't forget to check out the rooftop terrace - we took our takeout pizza up there and staff were happy with us doing so. 
The only downside was very noisy air-conditioning which we couldn't sleep through so had to turn off over night - not ideal in an oddly hot October. 
We would happily stay again and in fact have started to plan another trip for next year already...

The hotel is very quaint and a very high end boutique hotel. The rooms are designed fabulously. The service is fantastic. I rate it 5 stars and highly recommend the Thompson hotels as a fantastic value.

review_text:
My husband and I stayed at the Rebaissance 57 the two nights leading up to Thanksgiving. From the moment we entered the property every member of the staff treated us as special guests. We were upgraded to a room on the 17th floor which had a gorgeous rooftop terrace attached. The room was well appointed and extremely comfortable. The maid freshened our room at least twice a day and left goodies for us each night. We received a beautiful tray of cheeses and a bottle of wine the first evening as a gift from the manager, since we were in New York to celebrate my 50th Birthday! 
The location was fabulous and the concierge staff gave us recommendations for restaurants and activities that were exactly what we were looking for. 
The second night of our stay we had some issues with noisy guests next door and upon check out we were notified that night would be complemintary. 
If you want a fabulous place to call home in New York City and be treated as an honored guest, this is the spot. I can't stress enough how incredible the staff, location and ambience were. I will definitely be back as soon as I can.

Expensive like all Manhatten hotels.
On entering the small, casual looking lobby with noisy bar next door (after a tiring taxi ride from JFK) was off-putting. The rooms however are of a decent size, extremely clean....the bed was comfortable with decent pillows and silky sheets. There was no view to speak of from our particular room...luck of the draw on this one. 
I went against the advice of many in choosing the location...but was not let down by my decision. Union Square is central in many ways. The market and surrounding shops are a bonus. Chelsea, SoHo, TriBeCa are short walks away... Times Square and 5th ave shops etc are likewise walking distance....the subway station on the square is useful if you don't want the walk.

We booked 2 rooms, 4 teenagers happily shared one room. Free wifi and great breakfast makes a huge difference when traveling with this age group! Very quiet - great location as close to multi line station and easy walk to time square! Loved it!

review_text:
In the past I have always stayed here and it has been very good. Now it has changed. The bathroom had no soap. I had to request it be brought. The room cards repeatedly do not work and it requires you go back to the front desk to get a new card. This happened everytime I left the room. The wireless connection is spotty and slow and costs extra. The helpfulness and friendliness of the staff has deteriorated.
The location is great.
I will not pay the prices they charge to stay here again.

review_title: Compact funky place to crash in mid town New York
review_text: The Pod makes maximum use of the limited space available in New York. The rooms are compact but are cleverly designed with everything you need. The lobby provides good snack food and drinks, whilst street 51 itself has some nice French and Belgian restaurants. Cool art on the wall makes this a hip place to stay.

We stayed here a few years back it is in a Fab location in NY the hotel was clean staff friendly when leaving the front desk ordered a limo there is a fab little Diner just along from the hotel brill breakfast

We stayed at this gotel for 8 nights. Very well located if you want transportation to explore Manhattan and Brooklin (great subway hub). I got a bigger room, that was pricy but worth it. Comfortable, clean and trendy place.
Just finished a three day stay for business. The rooms were a nice size for NYC and the open shower was great. The location is awesome as is the service. Going back next week.

review_title: Stylish, Great location for Wall Street
review_text: Stayed here for a week and enjoyed the usual style of a Thompson hotel. Amazing location for Wall Street financial district, ten mins from Soho. Great service. Nice breakfast

review_title: Excellent hotel choice: perfect location, great service, nice decor, excellent value!
review_text: Stayed with 4 girlfriends in June for 5 nights. It was an excellent stay with no complaints. The price was amazingly cheap for NYC and the location and service couldn't have been better. I highly recommend this hotel to all my friends.
hotel_name: nyma, the New York Manhattan Hotel

review_title: Nice hotel, convenient to city attractions.
review_text: We stayed for 2 days in the suite for a wedding at south street seaport. Very well decorated and clean room. The price was pretty pricey, but I suppose it's pretty much the same anywhere in that area. The staff was very nice and attentive. The only complaint I have is the breakfast available for $10.00 a person was aweful because there was not much to pick from and no silverware or napkins were available and the coffee was horrible. But I didn't stay there for the breakfast so really not hardly worth mentioning. I would stay there again.

review_text: Our family of 4 (kids aged 3 and 6) stayed for a week. It was good value for money and had everything you needed. It is a little tired but is very very clean. It's a perfect budget option for NYC. If I were to return to NYC, I would probably stay closer to Central park, we spent a lot of time traveling uptown to see museums, broadway shows, children's zoo etc but you might like the location of Nyma literally around the corner from the Empire State building.
hotel_name: nyma, the New York Manhattan Hotel

review_text: Love this hotel. Great location, friendly staff. A special shoutout to David, a doorman, who particularly helped me out.

review_title: Eclectic but rooms a bit stuffy
review_text: This was a good hotel but the rooms felt old and a bit claustrophobic. On the plus side the bed was very comfortable and the service was excellent. We got this hotel on priceline and paid 170. We would not have been happy if we paid the full price.
hotel_address: {'region': 'NY', 'street-address': '15 Gold Street, Entrance on Platt', 'postal-code': '10038', 'locality': 'New York City'}

review_text: We stayed at Gild Hall this past weekend and have few complaints. The location is average, I have never stayed in he Financial District and found it is not my favorite neighborhood. However, the hotel is very convenient to the subway and I'd definitely stay here again. Other reviewers mentioned problems controlling the temperature in their rooms, but our room had a thermostat that adjusted easily and we were very comfortable. My one complaint would be the corrugated glass bathroom wall and door. It did not afford much privacy as you can see more than just the outline of someone sitting on the toilet! It was fine since I was traveling with my husband, but would not share a room with anyone else at this hotel! Overall we had a pleasant stay and felt the price we paid on priceline was fair. We would definitely stay here again.

review_text:
I stayed 4 nights/5days, and enjoyed it tremendously! The hotel has a very chic decor which fits in perfectly with the east side. It was a great location for shopping at bloomingdales, as well 2 blocks from the nearest subway station. The restaurant has top notch "free" entertainment with comforting menu.
The highlight of my stay was the friendly,helpful stay.The staff went out of their way to make us feel welcomed.
I will definitely return!

review_title: Nice location, nice hotel but for the price you'd think they could afford to throw in complimentary water and free wifi.
review_text: This hotel feels a bit like any Western airline. A solid pedigree and a polished facade, but that illusion of luxury quickly fades as you realize they'll charge you $9 for a bottle of water, and $15 for 24h of Internet access - PER device. That's beyond cheap. If you pay a premium to stay at a place like this you expect such things to be included. Sadly, this tarnishes an otherwise excellent experience so far. I would easily recommend the hotel if not for this. As it stands, I don't know.

review_title: Amazing experience that I can't wait to repeat!
review_text: My stay at the Pod was wonderful. The hotel was nicely decorated and though the rooms were small, they were clean and very comfortable. In the evening I had a glass of wine in the downstairs cafe and hung out in their courtyard. It was great to be in the city and still have the quiet and privacy they provided. The service was great. I will definitely be back.

I stayed in the hotel in 2006 before it had been refurbished on a school trip and definitely would he giving it a 1 if I could! Now that I've been there since it's a fab 5 out of 5! The rooms are small but the website doesn't boast about 50ft balconies and ensuites that you could run around in.
The staff were extremely friendly and pleasant in assisting us with booking cabs to get about.
Rooms were immaculately clean and the shared toilet facilities are always sparkling.
Well done The Pod! Will be seeing you again very soon

review_title: Ok for a night or two for the price
review_text: This place would be great if you were a back packer, however as an non backpacker the rooms were a little small and sharing a bathroom (4 small cubicles for the entire floor), although didnt cause too many problems, did get very old, very quickly

This was our third time staying at Nyma (formerly Red Roof Inn); you won't find better value in manhattan; great location, clean rooms, above average breakfast, friendly support staff, pleasant greeting, renovated front desk....it's no longer a hidden gem as savvy travellers have caught on (it was sol out the weekend of may 20) - only downside was ventillaion issue as some rooms do not permit the windows to be opened - bit overall a cant miss hotel
hotel_name: nyma, the New York Manhattan Hotel

review_title: Very nice hotel with a great location.
review_text:
We booked a wonderful room on a lower floor but got upgraded to a spectacular room on a higher floor upon check-in. They also let us check in at 11am. I assumed we would have to wait while they got our room ready.
I had been to Manhattan several times on the past but this was my first time staying in the city. Usually my visits had been composed of some combination of times square, central park, and a museum. That gets old very quickly. This time we wanted to get a different feel and see more of the city and the union square location definitely delivered. We walked everywhere- little Italy, across the Brooklyn bridge, Greenwich village, south street seaport, Madison square park, and others. When we got tired of walking, which we did, the subway stop fit the bill. 
We felt safe everywhere including walking from people's improv theatre at midnight.

The hotel is very uncomfortable. I have stayed at many boutique style hotels. This is by far the WORST! The pod doesn't tell you that there ate no toilets in the rooms. So you have to share showers and use showers that others use. So gross!!!!
There are much better options in NYC. This is crap and I wouldn't stay there for free.

I found this hotel through the Hotel Tonight app. We stayed two nights. The room had a full bed and was tiny. We had a forth floor room wiith no view. Check in and out were fast. Cool retro decor. Doormen were all very nice and helpful when we needed a cab. Room was clean. Bathroom had a heated tile floor which was really nice! Complimentary New York Times paper each morning. Starbucks right next door and a Pinkberry frozen yogurt place not far away. Right next to central park. I would defiantly stay here again.

Aa very tiny with a more tiny bathroom, but excellant location close to 5th street and madison and central park. Very clean, excellantservice, terrace for bagel and coffe u can buy in the lobby. At night go on the roof 14th floor its worth to sit theere a while and relax. Moderate price

If you want to feel like someone special, stay at the W Union Square. The staff there makes you feel right at home from the front door, to the front desk, to the bar and most impressive, the concierge. It truly is Whatever, Whenever.

Tries hard to match the Hudson further up the road (which is similarly priced)' but doesn't quite make it. If room prices are the same when you look, then go for the Hudson every time. That said, the location is great, and the restaurant is good. My room was tiny, and the aircon was incredibly noisy (and the control unit was broken).

review_title: Great things come in small packages!
review_text: This hotel was SO cute, and awesome value for the location. Walking, we were minutes from Times Square. It really is perfect if all you want is a comfy bed. Because the rooms are super small. We had a double bed, and there was less than 2ft of space between the bed and the wall. The shower was surprisingly roomy though, but the toilet area was not. Also, there's no fridge or microwave, so don't bring food back to the room. There's also no parking, you'll have to find and pay for a nearby garage. They recommend one, but it's not the best price. So look around. We only stayed one night, so we didnt get to see the balcony or cafe. But maybe next time - I'll definitely stay there again the next time we go.

Cool place with a nice vibe to it. Small basic room, but with everything you need. I was quit busy when I was there, but didn't even one time have to wait for the toilet or shower. Great location, good price and I would for sure stay again.
Stayed here with my sister over Easter rooms we had a double room which sleeps two but will be comfortable for one :) very nice hotel!!

review_title: Great location, great Hotel, rooms are small but perfectly laid out.
review_text:
Myself and my partner stayed here recently on our first trip to NY. The location is fantastic with lots of bars and restaurants all within walking distance. The rooms are small but very functional. We had a double room with private bathroom. I only ate breakfast once, bagel and coffee but it was very good, coffee was actually gorgeous. I would have no problem recommending this hotel and would definitely stay there again.
My only tip is, when you get to your room put your stuff in the pull out drawers under the bed and put away your cases. That way it won't feel so cramped. 
I didn't deal with staff much but when I did they were very helpful.

I stayed here in a single room in early 2007 and refurbishments were almost complete.
I chose to stay here to attempt to connect with my dad's experience when he lived here for a year in the early 70's (and it was previously known as the Pickwick).
My room was understandably small but quaint & gorgeous.
It was warm, clean & funky & served it's purpose with a sink, swivel wall tv, iPod docking station etc & very comfortable. 
The bathrooms were clean and it was a great idea to have the lights to indicate if it was occupied or not & I thoroughly enjoyed having a shower in a bathroom which looked out onto NYC. Breathtaking!
The wall designs & colour scheme were awesome & location was great.
There was a small bar just a few doors down which I also thoroughly enjoyed.
Staff were helpful & friendly helping me organise a town car to the airport and the whole vibe of the place resonated with so much character.
Thank you for a pleasant stay. This hotel is definitely on top of the list when I visit again with my partner & kids.

review_title: Great location, great value and clean!
review_text: I stayed here for three nights (fri, sat, sun) and would stay again. I had booked a single room with shared bathroom but upon checking in (3am) I was given a free upgrade to a double with my own bathroom! What a great start! The room was clean and I had plenty of room. If I was a 6 foot guy it would have been a bit squishy but who spends all their time in NYC in a hotel anyway! The location was great too. I walked to both Times Square and Central Park. I would stay again!

We had such a nice time at the pod hotel. The front desk workers were always so friendly and polite. We were upgraded to a double room at no extra charge. The rooms are tiny but they are so fun and who really spends time in the room anyway. Great location with subways close by. We took the train to the airport and it was easy.

review_title: Trendy, upscale boutique hotel at Central Park, Columbus Circle
review_text: In Manhattan, you expect small rooms. It is bed comfort, room design and service that set one upscale hotel apart from the other. On the counts of comfort and design, 6 Columbus rates very well. Beds are firm and new-feeling and the bedding is luxurious. Service from the front desk was spotty, but the maid was friendly, helpful and pleasant. Can't beat the location.

review_title: Great little hotel. Well located. Top service. Will definitely go back
review_text: If you are looking to stay near the UWS this hotel is great. It also is a comfortable walk to the theatre district. We got an upgrade to a lovely room with a deck. Very happy with the hotel.

review_title: Horrible and ridiculously over priced at nearly $200
review_text: Horrible hostel like hotel ridiculously over priced at nearly $200. Rude front desk bad rooms

A friend and I stayed here 3 nights in the bunkbed accommodation. Great staff and concierge. Nice lobby with drinks and breakfast. All together nice stay and very clean/eclectic. We were barely in the room during our trip- if you are looking for downtime and to spend time in your room, get something larger than the bunkbed option. Overall would recommend.

review_title: A fuir comme les punaises de lit
review_text:
Comment qualifier cet hotel, le plus pourri dans lequel j'ai sejournÃ© !!!
D'abord, je relativise la position geographique pretendument ideale. Que veut dire etre mal situÃ© a ny quant toute la ville est un spectacle. A moins detre au fin fond du bronx tous led hotels de manhattan sont a priori bien situes.
A peine arrives , on nous a demande de regler la totalite de la somme... Bizarre mais on sest pas mefies plus Que cela. Bien mal nous en a pris!!! On monte au 7e apres avoir traverse une salle de restaurant glauque et indigente, supporte des odeurs de desodorisateur bas de gamme et de renferme. On ouvre la porte et la quelle surprise, la chambre la plus laide que jai jamais vu. Moquette epaisse marron murs marrons meubles marrons rideaux marrons ... Un mobilier choisi dans les foirefouilles du quartier indignes d'un hotel a 180 $ la nuit. A ce prix la on a pu sejourner dans des hotels de reve a lisbonne ou meme en france. 
Ceci pourrait etre sans importance s'il ny avait pas le reste:
Apres une premiere nuit passable ( ascenseur bruyant... Portes qui claquent etc ), nous desendons prendre notre petit dejeuner.. Vision cauchemardesque, une bande d'ados avachis sur les tables en train de devorer les cereales en boites... Pas une place. Nous patientons et en trouvons enfin une. Je me sers un cafe, me sers de croissants et de pain de mie, le reste etant franchement repoussant . Mon amie a du recracher le croissant tellement il etait degueulasse!. A cela ajoutez la serveusr qui essuie son nez qui coule avec lanmain qui lui sert a faire les gaufres et vous aurez une idee du petit dej. Notez aussi que le menage de la salle est fait le soir!!bien sur nous avons pris notre petit dej ailleurs des le lendemain, notamment a lhotel intercontinental, a 100 m a gauche en sortant du taudis qui se nomme comfort inn! Endroit magique boulangeriende qualite et possibilite de prendre ce que lon a achete dans les canapes de l'hotel.
Deux jours plus tard mon amie se reveille en se demengeant. Plusieurs boutons rouges tapissent ses bras ses jambes. Figurez vous qu'il s'agit de punaises de lit!!! Franchement ne vous fiez pas a l'apparente proprete du lieu. C'est un hotel tenu par des gens sans aucune hygiene. 
Pour moi, ce n'est absolument pas de l'hotellerie, juste un minable pret a dormir qui vaut a peu de choses pres l'hotel de passes derriere la gare de nice dans lequel j'ai ete oblige de dormir une fois!!!.
N'allez jamais dans cet hotel. Preferz mettre un peu plus, ne pas forcement prendre unenformule avec petit dejeuner et regardez les bnb.

review_title: Great hotel but could improve how they deal with complaints
review_text:
I stayed here with my mother for five night in march and we were pleasantly surprised on arrival. The room, although small, seemed spacious by NYC standards, particularly given the price. We stayed in a queen room with our own bathroom, it was clean, modern& all the space is well used. 
The roof terrace is amazing, particularly at night, you are surrounded by skyscrapers, it's beautiful. The concierge service is also good, she checked us onto our flight online when we were leaving, printed our boarding pass&ordered us a taxi in about two mins.
The only thing negative we found, and it is quite a big negative, we cane back from a day's sightseeing to find our room door lying wide open and the light was on. We had not left it like this. We immediately checked if anything was missing but thankfully there wasn't. I phoned to reception to complain& was told someone would be up immediately to check that the door hadn't been forced open and to ensure it was locking properly, no-one arrived so I went to reception & spoke to a different member of staff who could not have been less helpful. When I explained to him what had happened he did not even react, he simply stood looking at me blankly. I then asked him to send someone to check the door & he said he would.( no-one ever checked the door to our knowledge.) he didn't apologise, offer any form of assistance or explanation, extremely disinterested and unhelpful. Which is a pity because it is a huge disappointment in an otherwise fantastic trip and a huge failing by the hotel, which otherwise would certainly have been receiving top marks from me&recommendations to friends.

Arrived here for 6 days, taxi to hotel was great however over eager concierge bet us to the bags! Tip 1 handed over b4 we started our holiday!
We stayed in bunk bed room, small but cool, air conditioning which was a massive bonus due to the hot weather. Ladder and handle rail were not the safest but could be moved around meaning that extra space got created. We had two very large bags and found no problem moving around the room with them. 
Room was cleaned daily, towels changed daily. Very eager maid knocking at 09.00am in the morning was not a bonus, considering their was no "do not disturb sign". 
Shared bathrooms were always spotless, showers were amazing. Their was always a toilet free when we needed one.
Lifts were annoying.. 3 lifts and they were not very efficient!
Reception staff were a little rude but nothing we couldn't handle.
Morning star cafe on 2nd avenue (around the corner) is amazing for both breakfast and dinner.
We will Definately 100% be staying here again.

My husband and I stayed here Dec. 30 with my sister and her boyfriend after a Phish concert. We had the largest suite with a large terrace and an amazing view of the Chrysler Building. The room was great until we opened the pull out couch and realized there were no sheets on it, and there were no blankets, sheets or pillows in any of the closets. I called down to the front desk and was told they will bring us up one pillow and some sheets but there were no blankets. Not that I was expecting a world of comfort from a pull out couch but it royally sucked. Moral of the story is this is a great hotel if you're sleeping in a bed!
hotel_name: St Giles Hotel - The Court New York

review_text: We had the junior exec room which is the size of 2 regular rooms. We look for size since we had 2 teenagers an brought an air matress for one and the other used the sleeper sofa. The king bed in the other room was nice and comfortable. When we asked for another blanket they only brought us bed sheets and said that is all they have which seemed a bit low budget. When we turned on the heater both heaters in both rooms made some noise but did not blow warm air which also seemed low budget. We called the front desk, the engineer showed up promptly and reset the heater and then they worked but continued to make some strange noises when the thermostat turned them on. The engineer seemed not very friendly, he did not say much, and seemed a bit tired from possibly resetting heaters?When this building got tuned into a hotel I suspect the heating and ac system was not replaced other than putting digital thermostats in the rooms. The location is great, not a far walk to most midtown attractions. All in all we give this hotel good value as the price was lower than most other hotels in midtown and the room was spacious.
hotel_name: St Giles Hotel - The Court New York

review_text:
Stayed here over a weekend, checked in but was on a floor with a group of 20 kids. As my roof was near a shared bathroom the door was continuously slamming.
Credit to the hotel they moved me straight away, the rooms are nicely fitted out with everything you need.
Being a few mins walk from the subway was great.
Good price for location and quality.

I wasn't sure what to expect from The Pod. I had never stayed in a shared bathroom hotel before, but my 10 year old son, who was my travel companion, was in love with the idea of having bunk beds. It worked out great! 
The Pod is located in an older building which has been updated to very modern stylings. We had a bunk bed room, which was quite small, but made good use of the space. The shared bathrooms were always readily available and in good order. They also have an open rooftop which made for a unique dinner one evening! The rooms were generally clean, however it seemed that the carpet had not been thoroughly swept. We had one one small maintanence issue with the in-room safe which was quickly attended to.
Overall, the stay was very nice.
clean, good service, close to all important transport links - and above all an amazing view on the empire state building!!!!
hotel_name: St Giles Hotel - The Court New York

review_title: Fine place to put your head at nite but not much else going for it.
review_text: Its a fine hotel for the price, but seems somewhat run down, especially the bathrooms. Not much of a lobby to it at all and the rooms are small - you dont feel comfortable being in the hotel other to wake up and go to sleep. The place is trying to be modern but just comes off as tacky. Area is close to mid town but definitely feel out of the main scene. Also both mornings house cleaning was very noise in the halls pre 9 am. No room service after midnite and the radiator clicked throughout the night.
hotel_name: St Giles Hotel - The Court New York

review_title: Holds $100/night on card in addition to reservation amount.
review_text: Only a few complaints...fridge didn't work. no coffee pot in room. asked for a crib when I booked the room and the hotel was out upon arriving, crib should have already been in my room. also, may/may not be a big deal for all, but in addition to your room charge they hold an additional $100 per night on your card.
hotel_name: St Giles Hotel - The Court New York

review_text:
I stayed here for a week in a bunk pod on the 10th floor. For the record, it's not a hostel. It's a hotel just with shared bathrooms. The rooms are spotlessly clean and every day they are cleaned by housekeeping. The rooms and small and compact but come on - this is Manhattan you're going to be out all of the time anyway! Each bed has it's own TV. There are lights above the door telling you which bathroom is in use which saves a wasted trip. The hotel staff are very polite and friendly and the hotel decor is very modern! Also the Subway is only a 1 min walk from the hotel and Lexington Avenue is a short walk away plus there are some great bars on the same street. It's only an hour on the Subway from JFK and a 30 min taxi ride. Plus the room has heating and air con so you're never too cold or too hot!!!!
Only downside is the hairdryer is pretty useless and housekeeping can be loud in the morning as they're often talking more than loudly in Spanish. Also sometimes the lift goes slow when housekeeping are doing their routine. But overall I would definitely stay there again!!!!

review_title: An absolute ideal budget hotel, in a great location!
review_text: Fantastic modern art deco hotel. Good location, helpful staff. Daily room service/ towels changed daily/very clean! Great location; fantastic Diner near by for breakfast, lovely chic Indian Restaurant on way to 5th Av, 'Mint'...overall a great, simple, no frills stay & reasonable prices for NYC!

review_title: Please beware... Do not stay here.
review_text: After reading the reviews on tripadvisor, me & my gf decided to stay at the pod hotel for our 1st night in NY. To sum up: receptionist grunted something and shoved a key over the desk when we arrived, room was so small that we could not unpack anything (we had reserved the double pod room) bed was filthy, room was very small, heating extremely loud. After paying $260 in total, talk about feeling ripped off. I guess if you make a hotel so hip & cool, you can forget service and all the rest. Believe me, don't stay here....

review_title: Bom valor para estar em plena Times Square.
review_text: Equipa atenciosa, cafÃ© da manhÃ£ simples mas suficiente, a poucos passos da Time Square e da Broadway. review_text: Good location. Small room. Get a room with a bathroom.

review_title: More than expected! Amazing birthday weekend!
review_text:
The hotel is very clean and the from desk day staff is great! They upgraded me from a standard to a one bedroom suite for my birthday! The suite has a private step out balcony with a table and two chairs - very romantic! The bed is SO COMFY and clean! NO BEDBUGS - I always check thoroughly! The AC blows strong cold air and there is an iPhone/iPod hookup in the room for louder speakers. The bathroom did not have a fan NPR could I open the windows so it does get steamy quick!
It's kind of hard to hail a cab because of it's proximity to Grand Central Station but walking up a few blocks helps. Nice convenient store on the corner, and the view at night of stars mingling with the skyscrapers makes for a great romantic evening while drinking chilled wine with your love!
I will be back here, definitely!
hotel_name: St Giles Hotel - The Court New York

review_text:
Excellent rooms, location and service, couldn't of asked for a better hotel, mini bar expensive but that's self fault, bar and restraunt very expensive.
Overall very good and well done

review_title: Fabulous Location in New York City
review_text: This hotel is in a most amazing location within easy walking distance of Times Square. My wife and I stayed at the hotel in August 2012 and we just happened to be there at the same time as Hurricane Irene. Our room was simple but clean and had all of the necessary hotel amenities that would be expected of a major chain such as the Novotel. Given that we were confined to our room for about 24 hours due to the hurricane we were quite comfortable. The staff were very conscious of the needs of hotel guests and did everything possible to make our stay enjoyable. There are hundreds of restaurants in close proximity of the hotel along with many iconic New York tourist attractions including Times Square, Central Park and the Empire State Building. I would have no hesitation staying at this hotel again and in my opinion it represents good value for money.

I booked this hotel because of trip advisor's advice. my room was spacious so I was able to pack all my things easily (I shopped a lot) it's a good location everthing is located within walking distance! staff are friendly:) it has everthing including kichen, spoon, microwave, refrigerager etc. it's not a fancy hotel but if you want to stay at reasonable price hotel with spacious room, definitely recommend this hotel

review_title: Indian spice smelled floor and room on 13th floor!
review_text: Don't stay at Eastgate if you have a choice and if you booked it already, make sure you have a copy of your confirmation. In my experience, my reservation was changed from a 2 bedrooms suite to a junior 2 beds. I had to go online and print out the reservation to prove it. After they finally got me the 2 bedrooms suite, it was on the 13th floor. Bad sign! After I got out of the elevator, pungent curry smell just overwhelmed me. Should have just went downstairs and cancelled the room. But, I thought maybe the smell would be gone once the hotel cleans it. Nope, the smell lingered and after one night, I was DONE. Checked out and cancelled the rest of the reservation. Can you believe it, the hotel staff didn't even seem surprised. They knew!! And the front desk lady didn't even bother to apologize for it. Unbelievable. Terrible experience. Don't stay at Eastgate Tower unless you can tolerate bad customer service, smelly floor and smelly room.
I think i was upgraded i have a huuuge room that i could live in. Great location and service. Booked on hotwire. I love the street noise. I love nyc.
hotel_name: St Giles Hotel - The Court New York

review_title: Perfect location , incredibly large rooms and great service.
review_text: I recently visited NYC on a retirement trip for my father with a party of 5 including my sister.having visited Manhattan on two previous occasions I was absolutely amazed at the space we found in our 2 bedroom suite.The decorations are dated but I honestly believe the prices are in proportion.having the second bathroom was perfect for the one female in our party.we found the location perfect for getting around the five boroughs as grand central station was a 10 minute walk so we were able to visit Yankee stadium in the Bronx and also the mets baseball game in queens within 1/2 hour.there are plenty of good value bars and restaurants that were within walking distance along with the usual fast food choices.But the biggest plus point of all were the friendly and helpful staff who could not have done more to make our once in a lifetime trip more enjoyable.

Everything about this hotel was great. Room service was very expensive but then there was a great diner round the corner from the hotel so no big deal. Conscierge service was great. 
Would highly recommend this hotel and I would be happy to go back there.
hotel_name: St Giles Hotel - The Court New York

review_text: Staff and employees were perfect. And very clean hotel. Room wallpaper could be renovated...

We were recommended Eastgate Towers Hotel by trail finders, our booking agent. What a great find! review_title: Beautiful, grand hotel, staying here helped make our special day perfect!
review_text:
We stayed here from 28/11/11 until 3/12/11 and got married 1/11/11(on the World yacht). 
We were allocated a large room on the 9th floor which was perfect! I had my very own dressing room and walk in wardrobe..wot more can a girl want! The champagne in our room on arrival went down very well also.
The commonal areas of the hotel are stunning and you can't help but feel special in some way amongst the surroundings. I had some wedding photos taken in the lobby which I'm sure will look very elegant:-)
We didn't eat in the restaurants as they were very pricey although we did enjoy some drinks in the bar.
The location of the hotel was great! 
Within walking distance of the Rockefeller centre, Times Square, Grand Central Station and the Empire and many more. There is a subway station adjacent to the Lexington Ave entrance also.
Went to Kenneth's salon within in the hotel for my bridal hair and makeup...expensive but well worth it!!
All in all this hotel is a special place to visit and helped contribute to an amazing wedding day!!

Love this place, great staff, great service and a fantastic location, make sure you pop down to Chelsea Market when you stay here and have a Fat Witch brownie ! Then grab an espresso at 9th Espresso . It's only a short cab ride up into Midtown and theatre land and it's a much nicer area to stay in . One of my fav places to eat anywhere in the World is nearly opposite the hotel , it's Scarpetta, a NYC institution! Make sure you go to Pastis for breakfast
Sitting on the roof sipping a cocktail has to be a highlight of any stay here

I visited here a few days ago with a friend and I was impressed at how lovely the setting was at the rooftop terrace! Luckily had some great weather! It also had a swimming pool which added a nice touch however I was put off when some other members of the public decided to jump in in their underwear! Not very professional! Also the toilets were pretty smelly! 
It is a lovely place to drink, not the cheapest of places but they do a mean mojito!

review_text:

review_text:

You can't close the black out curtains which means the occupants of the adjacent building - which in true New York fashion is almost close enough to touch - can see everything. I set the heat on auto and the target temp to 75. Aside from the fact that it blew so loudly that I could barely sleep, i also had to get up and turn it off in the wee hours of the morning because it stayed on non-stop pushing the room temp to over 80 degrees. The continental breakfast had travel coffee cups but no tops to them: useless. When I asked the front desk about a cab he told me "sure they're outside just grab one". Famous last words. 
The only silver lining: checked thoroughly...no bed bugs. I guess that's all you can ask for in a NYC hotel nowadays.

review_text:
I'm usually a pretty easy grader on hotels. If they are clean, quiet and comfortable, it's difficult to disappoint me. Unfortunately, my three night stay here found a way to disappoint me repeatedly. For a premium hotel that is bold enough to "suggest" a dress code on their website, my expectations were not met.
1. The staff deliberately overlooked an obvious issue with my room. When I checked in. The thermostat was on 65 and a window was cracked, letting in considerable street noise as well as plenty of 45 degree air. Of course, I closed the window and changed the thermostat to 72 before hearing out for a few hours. Upon returning to the room, I discovered why the window was open and the thermostat had been on its 65 degree minimum, the room was burning up at well over 80 degrees. I soon discovered that the thermostat was inaccurate by about 10-12 degrees. Why the staff decided to bandaid the problem rather than fix it is beyond me.
2. The bathroom sink stopper was not working. It would not close. How was the maid cleaning? So I used a wash rag to stop it temporarily, only to discover that the stopper was then stuck in the closed positin with a sink full of dirty water. Again, an obvious problem that should have been fixed before I ever walked into the room.
3. The tv had no picture. I'm not much of a tv watcher and I only tried it on the very last night of the stay, but still disappointing to discover at bedtime that the tv doesn't work.
4. The bill slipped under my door at the end of my stay had overcharged me by more than $200. The room rate was incorrect for the last two evenings. Luckily, I had my confirmation email with me and was able to sort it out with the front desk after showing them the email. I hate to think what would have happened had I not had my email with me. What is so hard about charging the same rate that is included in the registration confirmation?
Upon educating the front desk of the issues above, I got an apology.
Final notes... I was placed on a floor with both smoking and non-smoking rooms. On two mornings, a strong cigarette smell invaded my room very early in the morning (prior to 6am), waking me up. Obviously, there is a physical issue where smoke is leaking between rooms. If you want a smoke-free stay, insist on a floor that's completely non-smoking.
Room size was fine for New York. Typical for New York and Europe, small for most American cities.
Room was very clean. Bed was comfortable. Lobby was beautiful (as depicted in web photos). The rooms themselves could stand some refurbishment on some cases... Missing tile grout, slight mold I soap tray, peeling paint on havoc unit, tired desktop lamp shade, etc.

It was the first time we have stayed at the W-A and have to say I felt very privilaged. I would have loved to have stayed there in its heyday. I do agree with others that this hotel is resting on its history but hey they can get away with it because the place is like Grand Central Station.The atmosphere is buzzing. The entrance, the lobby, the reception area is beautiful, so elegant. Yes it is expensive but one expects that. 5 star hotels in any city are expensive. 
We booked a room with two queen beds but were given a king in a small room with a view of the scaffolding (no problem with the scaffolding, maintenance work has to be done at some time) Following day I mentioned it to the receptionist and she immediately changed us to a bigger room with two beds. Got lost in the pillows and have never slept in more comfortable beds in any other 5 star hotels anywhere in the world, it took a lot of effort to get up.
Of course the rooms are dated, its what makes it the Waldorf but I do think that Wifi should be available complimentary in the room as it is in many hotels these days. Nothing in this hotel is free except the toiletries. You pay for the room, breakfast is not included, there is not even cofee/tea making facilities. 
Most of the staff are friendly and helpful. The only issue I have is with regard to security. My husband brought an antiquated Nokia cell phone which he managed to lose between the cocktail terrace and our room around lunchtime on our second day. We retraced our steps 15 mins later feeling sure we would find the phone or at least be told it had been handed in as we felt that the type of clientele who visit or stay at this hotel wouldn't be seen dead with this old relic. It never did turn up. They have enough security agents there, maybe they should be looking a little closer at their staff after all this is NY not Dubai. Next, on checking out, we asked reception if they could arrange to have our bags brought down. They told us they could but someone would have to be in the room at the time. Kind of tells you something as this is a first for us. Never in all our years of travelling have we been expected to stay in our room and wait for the bags to be talen down.
I would love to stay at the Waldorf again but the security aspect makes me feel uncomfortable.
I do feel everyone should have the experience of staying there at least once in their life.

This is quite the grande dame kind of place where I've previously toured through the lobby as a tourist getting a taste of old New York. This time I actually got to stay here a few nights as part of a conference held in the hotel. First off, if you've stayed in other NY hotel rooms, this was huge in comparison (i.e. equivalent to hotel room sizes in other parts of the country), with a desk area and actual floor space and room around the bed. My corner room has a some view toward Lexington...nothing iconic, but enough to feel like you're in Manhattan. The decor was a bit old school (puffy chairs with no support, kind of worn carpet, patterned drapes and bedding, old wooden doors with many years of repainting), but what do you really expect from the Waldorf? The bathroom was a little snug, with the toilet, sink, and tub apparently at a slightly odd angle, perhaps to fit into the space. The shower was not a particularly water conserving head, with a blast enough to exfoliate, if you like that kind of thing. With that kind of flow, the annoying billowing of the shower curtain liner was hard to avoid. The main meeting area was the ballroom, where NY politicians have big events.
If you want to experience a classic high-end NY hotel where important folks like to stay, and aren't necessarily looking for updated interiors, clean lines, modern furniture that you get in most of the newer boutique and high-end chain hotels, you might want to give it a try. Then you can say you stayed at the Waldorf.

review_title: The way a hotel should be.
review_text: It's not often that you can stay at a hotel and feel like royalty. The Waldorf truly is a one of kind experience. The staff goes above and beyond out of their way to make your stay memorable. It's an older hotel, but the nostalgia and history you experience makes up for that. Also, the hotel is an excellent location. Everybody should stay at the Waldorf at least once!
