review_text:
I loved this hotel. It is an old school place- no temporary feeling here. Heavy maple doors, marble staircase, just beautiful. Slightly marred by some post modern renovation (fake granite pillars) and bad fluorescent lighting. As many others have mentioned, Matthew is great- welcoming and steered us towards an equally charming diner in the area: the Tic Toc. 
As far as cleanliness I didn't see any problems and I was a hotel maid for several years so I can be trusted on this matter. Maybe we lucked out with our room. But it was clean and up to date.
As far as negatives, only 2 things:
1) Room was too hot- much too hot. Desk clerk suggested turning on AC which is ridiculous in December but it did even out temp. Still, I wish the windows could have been opened.
2) Breakfast was deplorable. Don't bother. Don't bother with small cafe next door- equally bad. Wound up going to patisserie on 5th for a real bagel and coffee.

review_title: Living something of a dream! Coming to America style!
review_text: Stayed here in March of 2009 and was awed by how beautiful the setup inside was. The service was beyond expectations, as they went out of there way to hook a girl up for a birthday. Originally I booked a single double bed and they gave me a king size. They called me by name and made me feel very welcomed. The room was clean except for a few lint balls in the bathroom. The view was of the street, not extremely impressive but okay. The bar was definitely overpriced but the drinks were good. Upon check out which was like 3 in the morning, the wake up call was very prompt. And when I had to come back from the airport cancelling my flight, they put me back in the room at no charge and allowed me free late check out. I felt blessed being able to walk the halls of famous people before me. Thanks

review_title: Nice hotel in a great location
review_text: Stayed here for 4 nights from the 28th October. I booked this in March this year and paid the additional money for a Central Park view queen room so imagine my disappointment to be told the only room available was on the 3rd floor and there would be nothing higher until the next day. We went up to the room and were presented with a view of the tree trunks in the park which didn't fit with my image of waking up in the morning and opening the curtains and looking over the park. We complained and they miraculously found a room on the 6th floor which was also much larger. All that said you don't go to New York to sit in your room which was both clean and comfortable but make sure you ask for a higher floor when booking. The food and drink is expensive but if you go out of the rear entrance, turn right walk up to 7th there is a great organic bakery that does a fantastic breakfast directly opposite.
hotel_name: JW Marriott Essex House New York

review_text: Muito bem localizado, com metrÃ´ na porta, Macy's do outro lado da rua, vÃ¡rios cafÃ©s no entorno, alÃ©m de farmÃ¡cias Duane, Wallgreens e CVS no mesmo quarteirÃ£o. Isso sem falar que Ã© colado no Empire State Building. Internet gratuita, porÃ©m complicada, com muitas falhas de acesso. Bem limpo, com camas boas e chuveiro decente.

I was a little dubious about the reviews posted on here however I was very pleasently surprised!!! The room was huge we had a double double which was double the size of the room we had at heathrow prior to the flight!! The bathroom was also big and have everything we needed. The location was brilliant just 2 minutes from Macy's and 10 from empire state!!! The breakfast too was fine yes there were plastic plates etc but anywhere you went in NYC that's what you got. The only negative I had was that I requested a non smoking room and of course we got a smoking room we asked twice to move and each time they said it would be the next day in the end we left it but we were hardly in the room and just opened the windows. What a brilliant brilliant hotel. I'm already planning my next trip. Thank you so so so much comfort inn!!!!

review_title: Old lady but still with some class
review_text: I booked this hotel as a 40th birthday gift. Yes there are far better hotels listed on trip advisor but we wanted to see it for ourselves. Although our room was not ready for a 3pm check in when we arrived at our suite we were delighted. Granted its dated and I was surprised some areas were definitely past it's best but I think that's why it's unique. Everyone must stay at this hotel at least once in their life!!! Tips - unless breakfast is included in the rate then I wouldn't pay the extra costs. Starbucks in the lobby is very expensive and remember the front of the hotel is undergoing renovations so scaffolding is up.

Stayed at the waldorf recently,good location ,check-in took awhile ,our rooms not ready for hours.
had to walk out to use up time , not recommended after a 7 hour flight and 1 in traffic.
Rooms were ok although tired,no tea or coffee making facilities we asked for a kettle but received no milk just sugar ,no coffee & some Tea bags.
The foyer bars need a complete refurb ,must have been fantastic in its time but like alot of old girls need a little cut and tuck

We have stayed at the Essex House many, many times. It is always clean, quiet and the staff is very attentive. I suggest booking though Amex concierge to get the late checkout, $100 room credit and room upgrade. I admit the price of the hotel is sometimes steep, but it never disappoints!!
hotel_name: JW Marriott Essex House New York

review_title: Not prepared to help business travelers.
review_text:
My day started 2 hours earlier than expected thanks to the maids walking the halls and talking loud enough to wake a heavy sleeper behind a thick door. No coffee in the room - had to get dressed to walk to buy a cup. 
In the lobby I stopped to pick up the phone that was charged by the night staff. It was not charged and the only option is to leave it with the business center. This is not a workable solution. No apology offered.
On service it took two calls to have a toothbrush brought up.
Great location.

review_title: I just had such high hopes....then they were all dashed.
review_text: I really had high expectations of good service and a nice room. But the 2.5 hour wait when I was told the room would be ready in 15-20 minutes was just the beginning of a long night of rude staff ( probably tired due to tennis star watching ) and plumbing that knocked all night long like a "B" horror film. If you are in the area, it is a nice lobby to hang out in. But the room was so small I mistook it for the closet initially. We would have been better off sleeping in the nice wide hallway, it was wider than our room. This was just not up to snuff. There are better places in NYC with service & rooms that match price with value.

review_title: Shame about the Starbucks but generally a grande dame.
review_text: Still a great hotel with magnificent public areas. Our room was very comfortable and we enjoyed a couple of fine cocktails at the bar (though on that point, shame the bar isn't open later for a nightcap). We had difficulty working the lifts but we were given a new key which seemed to do the trick. Also Hilton Gold Card holders please note, your breakfast is a Starbucks pastry. Aside from the grottiness of the grub, it's disappointing a hotel of this renown accommodates a Starbucks concession. Overall though, we very much enjoyed our stay and can recommend.

review_title: There is No place like the Waldorf!!!
review_text: Excellent!! Clean comfortable rooms. Excellent location, excellent service. You can't find a closer feeling of comfort and calm!!!the beds are the best. Stay here, you won't be dissappointed.
stayed here for 4 nights, great location, easy to get to places, room fine stayed on 3rd floor food at brendan`s vice night recommended it.

Great location. It's very basic but when your staying in NYC why would you spend all your time at the hotel?!? It was clean, comfertable and only around the corner from Times Square! Great service & amazing view from my room window. Made my trip to NY even better :)

This hotel is fantastic. The location couldnt be better. It is located in the next street to the empire state building. Our room on the 11th floor at the rear of the hotel had an unobstructed view of the ESB.
The hotel decor is old fashioned classic luxury. Dark wood, cream walls just perfectly. When we arrived we were greated by a lovely concierge and receptionist. We were both tired from our journey and the receptionist pointed us in the direction of the free tea and coffee machine situated next to the extremely comfy sofa. Our room was lovely not huge but big by new york room size standards. It was big enough to fit a large king size bed, bedside tables, a small table and two chairs and a large chest of drawers. Yes the bathroom is small but perfectly formed and has a full size bath. The location is excellent. 30 second walk to the subway, 1 minute walk to Macys. Lots of shops and restaurants closeby. Brendans bar and restaurant adjoins the hotel. Eat there the food is amazing. We ate there 3 out of the 6 nights we stayed. Breakfast is served in the restaurant in the morning. It is free and has a huge selection. Waffles toast bagels every type of donuts fillings jams cheese eggs, tea coffee juice. U also have an option to update to cooked breakfast if you wish
I thoroughly recommend staying at this hotel. We are already saving up for our next visit.
We cant thank the staff enough for our fabulous stay

Hotel is in a great location, right near Macy's, Empire state and a Subway station. 5-10 min stroll to Times Square. Hotel comes with complimentary breakfast, this is fairly basic; toast, doughnuts, cereals and bagels. But great to fill up in the morning and will certainly save you a few dollars. Hotel is far from luxury, could prob compare to a UK travelodge! Can be quite noisy so request a higher floor, we were 7th floor and especially at the weekends there was a lot of street noise until approx 4am.... But then that's New York. Staff friendly, if your travelling with Virgin you get a big breakfast free on your 1st morning, however don't buy from your rep they RIP you off! Not for families, more suitable for couples who literally need somewhere to rest ....

You could not ask for a hotel in a better location ! , we stayed for 2 nights 23- 25th October following our cruise to New York .
We arrived just after 7am our bags was placed into storage and as we walked around the corner ..... Empire state building - wow ! , so close to many of midtown attractions & off course SHOPS ! , Macy's is left out of hotel & across the road ! .
Hotel quirky boutique style , our room on 8th floor lovely , spotlessly clean & really friendly staff , if we're lucky enough to go to the big apple again I would stay at the comfort inn again .
Continental Bfast is also included , we only had a few drinks in Brendans Bar which is attached to the hotel , but the menu looked good.
Couple of good Irish bars across from hotel & Keens Chophouse next street - fabulous !

review_title: An iconic hotel but needs updating
review_text: If you are looking for a hotel with all the mod cons then give this one a miss. But if you want a hotel that has character and a sense of nostalgia then this takes some beating. Perhaps the most famous hotel in New York, it is beautifully ornate and has a charm all of it's own. The staff were excellent and nothing was too much trouble. However, the room we had was basic with a very small bathroom. Better rooms are available if your budget allows. Friends who travelled with us said there room smelt like "old people" . Another couple were upgraded to a suite with dressing room and huge bathroom. It's the luck of the draw so ask.

review_title: Unfriendly staff, made us Wait 2 hrs for our room because it was a suite! We will NEVER stay here again!
review_text: We watch guest check in one after the other for 2 hours.... All the check in desk would tell us is it's because you have a suite. So Pay More Money to be treated like garbage!!!! NEVER again! Not worth the $$. Better treatment a Holiday In Express!!!
hotel_name: JW Marriott Essex House New York

review_text: Fantastic hotel, so helpful, great rooms and amazing hotel, ian on the front desk was so helpful and the doormen couldnt do enough for you, amazing location 110% spot on!!

This hotel is in a perfect location for Time Square, Empire State building & Macy's. The bedroom we had was very spacious but the bathroom was quite small BUT both bigger than any London City Centre Hotel we have stayed in. This was my first visit to NYC but my husbands 2nd and we both were very impressed with this hotel.

review_title: Weren't treated as equals by staff
review_text:
Stayed for 2 nights with 3 other groups of people and 1st impressions were good. Nice clean old fashioned style as you walk into the lobby. The receptionist was friendly and treated us with respect. Sadly, that's where it ended. Our room was nice at first glance, but when it came down to it, it was very average. Literally 10 minutes waiting for hot water in the shower, flimsy light switches, had to get out of bed to turn the tv off because the remote was broken, no fridge and no safe which should be standard in a hotel of this stature. The best way I can describe it is a 3 star hotel with fancy carpet. 
Talking to our friends in the morning, they too had problems such as cracked light switches, 1 toilet seat broke when lifted up, and the wardrobe door falling down when it was opened. And besides the receptionists, we all thought the staff were judgmental and rude. My friend went to the bar and asked for a drink and was told rudely to go elsewhere. Just because we weren't wearing suits like the rest of the guests, doesn't mean they can look down at us and treat us like we didn't belong there. The other guests did the same thing to us. 
The only good thing that came out of this experience was that I can say I have stayed in this world famous hotel. But I can safely say I will not be staying here again because of the obnoxious staff and poor room fittings.

We stayed in a suite which was lovely and roomy. The bed was very small given the enormity of the suite rooms! Furniture was quite worn.
Reception staff were not very helpful. When we arrived to find the minibar had items used in it , we notified reception immediately who promised to get someone to come up. 3 further phone calls to reception in the duration of the stay still resulted in no one restocking the minibar, and sadly we were charged for the items we had not used.
I would definitely stay elsewhere in New York for other hotels offer better service & quality accommodation for a smaller price ticket.

Recently stayed here as part of our honeymoon. Rooms arevtotally over rated, old and the tap was dripping all the time and also the shower was very poor pressure. It cost us $21 for water to be brought to be brought to our room! Breakfast in bed was Â¢107. Our view wasnlooking at a dirty roof top of the reception!! Did not float our boat. Location is the only thing going for this hotel sorry.

review_title: A pleasant stay, but it needs to come a little more into the 21st century.
review_text: My husband and I stayed here as part of our honeymoon (20th-23rd august). Upon arrival we were met with an extremely warm welcome. Cases taken straight off us, whisked up to our room to meet us there. We were checked in by such a friendly gentleman (but I can't remember his name :-/) who chatted to us about our wedding etc. He gave us spa vouchers (which we didn't have time to use) and asked us if we'd like a bottle of champagne or drinks vouchers for the bar. We chose the drinks vouchers, however, the next day we returned from shopping to find a bottle of champagne chilling in our room, and a card in our married name, even though I had booked in my maiden name - a very nice touch! The lobby and bar areas are outstanding, oozing the class and glamour that you would expect from the waldorf. It's also interesting to see the history of the hotel in the lobby, seeing pictures of it's famous guests! The only fault I have is the rooms. I was very worried after having read reviews, but I was pleasantly surprised. It was clean and well presented. However, it does still look stuck in the 1930s. It definitely needs to modernise it's furnishings now, it is looking a little tired :(

review_title: Great location, shabby decor, awful shower.
review_text:
Best things about this hotel are the breakfast and the location. Breakfast is continental which in America is refreshing. Location is along from Macy's, next to empire state and just off 5th avenue. Great really.
Staff were nice enough especially when organising transport to the airport.
Rooms aren't great, clean enough but looks like a 200 a day smoker had been in one we got. Shower was awful. Had to adjust hot and cold to get the right temperature which was aful and even then it would fluctuate between freezing and scalding. Really not good enough. 
If they had decent showers I'd recommend totally as the room decor is less important, however, with what we got as a shower in our room I'd current say no.

review_title: Great hotel in the perfect Central Park location
review_text: We stayed four nights and it was very enjoyable. Jogging in the park every morning, a decent gym, very nice restaurant with some excellent staff.
hotel_name: JW Marriott Essex House New York

review_title: beautiful hotel, in a great city
review_text: The Waldorf Astoria is a beautiful hotel, with all the original features of when it first opened, we loved our stay but if we were staying again in New York would go for a more modern hotel, that would have a more relaxed way about it.

Stayed here for 5 nights Aug 30- Sept 4. The location was great close to shopping and most of all the subway is only down the street. The room we had, had 2 beds and a real good size bathroom. My only issue was there breakfast. It had to be one of the worst I have had. Other than that the Hotel and the staff were all great. I would definitely recommend this hotel.

review_title: location good but dated hotel. ok for tourist who need a place to hit the bed after a tiring day .
review_text: excellent location for a good price..a bit dated but ok for a short stay. breakfast was included so good value .a good selection of muffins , donuts , breads n cereals but was crowded .empire state building n macys almost next door.subway station a few steps away and a very short walk to times square so all u r paying is for the location. 2 computers with internet n printer in the lobby was quite useful as we could print our boarding passes. beware of the front desk calling a cab for u to get to the airport . they charge a good $25-35 extra .better to walk out of the hotel n hail a metered taxi yourself.will recommend this hotel only for people who r planning to spend the whole day in manhattan n need a room closeby after a tiring day.

This Hotel is a good choice because it's in the heart of the island, close to lots of interesting places, but the staff are NOT friendly.
Their slogan could be 
"Do not disturb us"

The hotel itself was beautiful and very well maintained. The staff was helpful. The location was perfect, not far from time square and the shopping around it is great! Wouldn't stay anywhere else in the city!

review_title: Excellent location and would stay there again
review_text:
We stayed here on a 4 night NY trip. Its in an excellent location for everything With excellent subway connections and only 8 minutes walk from penn station. Macys is on one corner with the empire state on the other end. The room was clean and tidy and hardly any street noise and the staff were really friendly and helpfull too. Breakfast was nothing to write home about but it was adequate for a start to the day and free compared to other hotels for the same money. Brendans bar and resturant next door is nice for relaxing in after a busy day with a nice relaxed atmosphere. 
I would definately stay here again when i go back to the big apple.

review_title: Decent hotel with excellent location and breakfasts!!
review_text: The rooms are pretty small, what u would expect from a city centre hotel. The air conditioning isn't great so be prepared if travelling in the summer. It is perfectly located however, times square is 10 minute walk away and Macys is just at the bottom of the street and 5th avenue is jus around the corner. The complimentary breakfast is an excellent help and a huge bonus! I would reccomend for short stays (we were there 4nights)

We stayed during hurricane Irene and were very well looked after. Great location. Staff were very friendly and helpful. Rooms were very clean and comfortable. Only downside was the window looked onto a brick wall and air con was noisy. But we will definitely go back and stay there again.

review_title: They lie about your room and view.
review_text: You pay an upcharge for a room overlooking Central Park. We weren't in a room as high up as we were told we would be. Our view was two walls. One window overlooked part of the park. Don't stay here unless you like looking at walls of buildings for lots of money.
hotel_name: JW Marriott Essex House New York

review_title: Great location, no problems, would stay again
review_text: Booked with travel agent and after reading reviews thought it was going to be cheap and nasty, but actually it was nice and would recommend. can't comment on staying with children as we didn't have any nor did we eat there as we wanted to try others. When we arrived we were allowed to check in 2 hours early and staff were very friendly. Room was fine, tv with sat, money safe, cleaned good everyday, our room over looked times square. there's a information desk which is open all day which they reccomend places and give leaflets. Nice bar terrace which over looks times square with great views. Location is brilliant, 2mins walk to central park, 8 to rockafella, 20 to empire, we walked everywhere even to ground zero and back. When you check out you can leave bags at hotel for as long as you want, no problems, would stay again, don't let other reviews put you off

Grand entrance
From limo pickup at JFK through welcome,check in and room-everything was special
Historic hotel just like the movies
Highly recommended

I booked a double bed room for 4 adults. The room was cosy with a luggage closet and a decent size bathroom. Though quite small for the 4 of us, we managed to get around without bumping into each other. I enjoyed the buffet breakfast and free coffee and tea facility. The front desk staff were helpful and the bell boys were friendly. Best of all was the great location as Macy's and many other great shops and street food vendors were all nearby.

This is the fourth time that I have stayed at Essex House and it never disappoints. This time I took my daughter (8 yrs old) with me so was interested to see how or if things would be different. They were as good if not better.
On arrival we had our room upgraded because our preassigned room wasn't ready. The staff helped us book tickets for our bus trip and couldn't have been nicer to my daughter. 
The waiting staff in the restaurant were more than helpful after I explained my gluten intolerance and they made sure I had bread at breakfast. 
All in all an incredible stay at an incredible hotel.
hotel_name: JW Marriott Essex House New York

review_title: In the beating heart of the Big Apple
review_text:
The hotel is conveniently located in the centre of the City that " never sleeps", just a few blocks away from Times Sq and 300m from the Empire State Building . The building itself would need to undergo refurbishing, the rooms are small and so are the bathrooms. 
We requested a refrigerator to be put in the room ( as advertised on the hotel's website) three times, but never got one. It was so hot those days, it'd have been beyond useful to have cold water in the room to hydrate. The complimentary buffet breakfast was average ( I personally found the bagels not very fresh and the eggs had a funny taste). On the whole i would recommend this hotel and would go back again. 
On the whole

We stayed in this hotel while getting married in NYC and I simply cannot praise it enough. We booked a junior suite and were upgraded on arrival to a room with views of the Park and the City skyline. The hotel receptionist even sent complimentary champagne and strawberries to our room within half an hour of our arrival after we'd told him we were getting married.
The suite was elegant, comfortable and huge with sumptuous plush furnishings. We particularly liked the evening turndown service where you returned to find blackout blinds had been pulled down and numerous lamps were lit. 
The room service was excellent and the manicure I had in the spa was the best I've ever had.
We only had breakfast once and it was excellent.
This hotel really was something special and we were delighted with it. I only have 2 complaints - the first is that it took a little while to run the bath. The second is that we only stayed for 5 nights before heading to Mexico for our honeymoon. With hindsight, we wished we'd had a few more nights here and less time in the supposed 5 star place we stayed in Mexico, which just couldn't compare.
hotel_name: JW Marriott Essex House New York

review_text: Stayed on a 3 night holiday. This was my first time ever in New York and I was staying on the ninth floor with an empire state building view. The room was great hd tv, clean, warm, good bathroom, nice and quiet. Staff were very helpful in showing me the way to landmarks. Overall great stay. Definitely come back !!

The hotel is modern, clean and well functioning. there is a nice outside bar with a great view to Time Square. Our room was great, also with a nice view. The bed was big. If you want to stay close to central park and Times Square, this is a good place.

My husband and I stayed 5 nights. Location in Midtown was perfect. The restaurant food was delicious, and the bar was fun. Matthew and Gulbye at the front desk were so helpful and nice!!! We will be back!

The Essex House is my first choice of places to stay in NYC. The rooms are lovely & the bed is "heavenly". The location is superb for anything you're doing while in the city. The views of Central Park are something I always have from my room..because I can't get these from home, so pay the extra $ it is worth it. It truly is a jewel. I hope the renovations leave some of the old charm that make the Essex stand apart from the rest.
hotel_name: JW Marriott Essex House New York

review_text: We stayed 7 nights in this hotel n the huge plus about this hotel is the location, u can practically walk everywhere n for everywhere else there is subway stations close by...Times Sqaure, Broadway, Rockefeller, Central Park!! Perfect for the tourist. Rooms are neat n tidy, quite large for New York! Service hotel was fine however didn't have much to do with them considering you don't spend much time in your room! Also great value for money considering the prices of NY hotels! PS Pharmacy/convenience store right underneath which comes in handy..

sono stata in questo hotel in agosto. ottima posizione, si raggiungono facilmente tutti I luoghi di interesse e poi e' attaccato alla quinta. Buon rapporto qualita prezzo, abbiamo risparmiato almeno 300 euro rispetto ad altri hotel della stessa catagoria. La hall e' bellissima, I corridoi un po' cupi, le stanze abbastanza spaziose e molto pulite. Consiglio la superior room. Il nostro soggiorno e' stato davvero piacevole, ci tornerei!

review_title: Expected more from this luxerious hotel
review_text: I am hilton diamond vip member, and we only get room upgrade and breakfast in starbucks. I was surprised that there is no executive lounge like the other Hilton hotels.

This hotel is the best ive ever stayed in, the views of ground zero are that stunning we had the curtains open all the time, the room was on the small side but more than big enough, the bed was sooooo comfortable especially after a long day shopping :) the staff couldnt do enough for you and will help you locate directions or cabs etc

review_title: Avoid Get better service at a one star b&b
review_text: Absolute horrific customer service on arrival. Had to carry my own bags to my room. Rooms look slightly dated. No toiletries as they had run out. Incredible told to go buy some at CVS. The only plus is great concierge. Front desk and manager don't care less when you complain.

review_title: Recommended, friendly staff and great location.
review_text: A four day trip to New York was greatly enjoyed with thanks to the staff at this hotel! Very close to the subway, walking distance to Macy's and fifth avenue. Hotel has well stocked bar, comfortable rooms and a good restaurant.

This was our second time in New York. The hotel was in a great location. We had a room on the 16th floor at the back so there was no noise from traffic which was great. The room was fine although the bathroom was a little worn. It would have been great to have tea/coffee making facilities in the room. The big downside to the hotel was the staff, they were all miserable. The outside bar area was busy and on the two occasions we went for a drink, we had to ask to be served and the barman on duty was surly and rude. Unfortunately the rest of the staff encountered were not much better.

My friend and I recently stayed at the Millenium Hilton (Dec 8th to Dec 13th). This was our second stay at the hotel following our last trip in Dec 2009. My friend contacted the hotel prior to our recent stay to advise the staff that we were returning and it was my 40th birthday on the 12th. As a result, we were upgraded to a junior suite, room 5402. This suite is situated only one floor from the top of the hotel. I can't describe how breathtaking the views were. 
The suite was just sheer luxury; we had our own wee living room area and a massive bedroom with windows covering the front and side wall in their entirety. We never once shut the curtains as we didn't want to miss a thing with the views. We couldn't believe how much the WTC has changed in 2 years. It's just astounding!! I cannot understand the comments made about the noise coming from the construction sites as neither this time nor the last time when we stayed were we disturbed by noise.
The staff were just simply wonderful and so helpful. Even on our last day, a lovely porter called Jerry spent time with my friend and I explaining the proposed layout of the WTC. 
I honestly couldn't praise this hotel and the staff enough. Thank you for making our trip and my birthday so memorable.

review_title: Too expensive for what you get
review_text: Stayed during July 2011. Air conditioning struggled to cool the room. The bed was very comfortable. The drinks at the bar were incredibly expensive and bartender seemed bothered to be working. Lobby was beautiful. Very difficult to move bags from lobby to garage. I would not stay here again but I am glad I did so I know what it was like.

Die Bedienung ist soweit gut, jedoch nicht sehr persÃ¶nlich, was wir aber in dieser Grossstadt auch nicht erwartet haben. Die Lage ist gut. In der NÃ¤he ist die U-Bahn. Zu Fuss ist es zum Times Square etwa 20 Minuten. FrÃ¼hstÃ¼ck kam uns zu teuer vor, weshalb wir dieses in einem externen Restaurant eingenommen haben. RD.

review_title: Ottima posizione, camere nella media, front Office pessimo
review_text: Ho soggiornato al Carlton per otto notti con mia moglie e mio figlio. Abbiamo scelto l'albergo per la posizione e perchÃ© abbiamo trovato una tariffa molto conveniente grazie ad una promozione. L'albergo Ã¨ sito in una ottima posizione perchÃ© Ã¨ vicino a tutto ma Ã¨ fuori dalla caoticita tipo Times Square. Vicino all'hotel c'Ã¨ un parco con una bellissima area giochi per i bimbi. Il servizio di housekeeping Ã¨ ottimo, ma il resto del personale Ã¨ pessimo, quasi maleducato. Se non avessimo prenotato con uno sconto di circa il 45%, li avremmo mandati sicuramente a quel paese. Comunque lo consiglio se lo si usa solo per dormire e se si conosce giÃ  la cittÃ  (Ci hanno consigliato solo un ristorante in una zona che non conoscevamo e ci hanno fatto spendere 450$ per una cena mediocre anche se con ottima vista).

Working in a hotel myself I obviously have a bias opinion when it comes to hotels. However, a hotel is a hotel as far as I'm concerned....rooms, as long as they're clean and pretty are great, which here they definately were. The location is great and the hotel itself is nice, the staff hoever were incredibly robotic and cold. From the desk staff at check in, when we called regarding pool hours, the bartenders, and the lobby greeter( man standing near elevators in suit?) Everyone was incredibly cold and very unpersonable and for me that is the most important aspect of a hotel. So I rate the hotel itself a 4 and the staff a 1. I couldn't honestly even tell u one employees name because they didn't leave a good impression at all.

review_title: Hotel ok but stayed in better
review_text:
My boyfriend and I have just returned home after a 4 night stay in this hotel from Feb 23rd to Feb 27th. Whilst there we had a Few problems, when we entered our room it stunk of stale cigarette smoke so we aired it by opening a window. We are both non smokers and hate the smell of it so this was highly unpleasant, after having the window open for a while however the smell cleared.
The room was large and clean and u could request clean linen when u wanted it. Rooms and beds were clean daily and the maids did a good job so we tipped them well.
On the morning after our first nights sleep we found the toiled had been blocked. How this had happen I don't know. We told the front desk when we went out that morning and by the time we returned it was fixed. At the time we mentioned the toilet we also complained that the tv signal was rubbish and also that throughout the night the radiator was making really loud hissing so could they please fix that as it woke us up on many occasions throughout the night. Sadly these two issues weren't resolved during our stay. Another grumble is the water temperature of the shower and the hand basin. It was either red hot or cold u couldn't get a good mix on the temperature at all.
On the plus side the staff were friendly and always available at the front desk. The included breakfast was good enough to start off the day with and there was always enough choice of bagels, bread, cereal fruit and doughnuts and there was always a seat spare to sit down. There was also free wi Fi which was strongest when in the lobby and they also had a Pc and printer which was free to use for 15 minutes per guest at a time. This was a great help when we wanted to check in on line for our returning flight and print off our boarding passes.
All in all I would say that this hotel is in a great location with good staff. Personally we wouldn't stay here again though as we preferred the hotel Metro which is across the road and was in the same cost bracket ( we stayed there 2 years ago) 
If you would like any more info about our stay please PM me. Gem

review_title: Great gateway to a wonderful city
review_text: Location, location, location--we found this property to be very convenient to the subway. Both the bell staff and concierge were helpful with dining recommendations and attractions

This hotel is legendary and it's a hotel that you must experience in your lifetime. The service is faultless. They are so sincere in wanting to make you feel welcome that nothing is too much trouble. I had a problem with the blinds in my room that didn't get fixed before I left. I filled in my questionnaire which I gave to the porter on my way out to the airport. Two weeks later I get a letter of apology and an invite to stay in a one bed suite, open for a year!!! I was in a duluxe room! I was really pleasantly surprised at that. The hotel is a little dated but beautiful. You can't be disappointed at this hotel

review_title: Great location and comfort all round
review_text: We had a great time here. The room was comfortable and large enough for my husband and I and our 2 1/2 year old. The location is great and the views if times square, particularly at night are fantastic. We didn't eat at the restaurant but had room service a few times and were more than happy with the food and service. The rooms are cleaned well. The concierge wasn't all that friendly, which was a shame as all other staff we had dealings with were fantastic. No free Internet in rooms - which isn't the standard ant more - disappointing. Relied on Starbucks providing wifi during our stay.

review_title: What you would expect from novotel
review_text: The hotel was in an excellent location. The room was good, bed was comfortable. Sheets felt scratchy and there was alot of black mould in the shower. The bathroom floor looked like it hadn't been swept as there was glass on the floor. Service at Reception on check in was excellent- kind, patient and helpful. Atmosphere in hotel was good. Rooms were quiet and could be darkened, great for sleeping. Skyscraper view was nice with a view of river. Internet free in lobby. Porters at the entrance were nice and looked after our luggage, even got us a private driver to the airport for the same price as a taxi. Housekeeping could have been slightly more prompt with our requests. Overall though, good value and I would stay here again.

review_title: Good location but waiter, there's a hair in my soup!
review_text: We stayed here because of the location, and because of the brand name. Check in was prompt, the rooms are small but reasonably clean and modern and the views of Times Square are pretty nice. The 24 hour fitness centre is also reasonably well stocked out. The cleaning staff are pleasant. The concierges were unhelpful and generally just delegated questions (definitely not Michael J Fox). The only real complaint I'd levy against them is that while at breakfast, my wife found a (pubic) hair in her coffee cup that she'd been drinking from. When I alerted the waiter to this, he looked puzzled for a minite, and then, as though some divine light bulb switched on, he got the dirty cup, and swapped it with a clean cup with the unoccupied seat next to us, without another word. Nothing more was said, although I did catch another waitress on the same morning scowling at us (???). I'm really sorry to the waitstaff we offended in drawing their attention to a PUBIC hair we found in their coffee.

Soggiorno spesso a NY per lavoro o per piacere. Solitamente alloggio al New York Palace o al Le Parker Meridien. Stavolta volevo cambiare hotel ed ubicazione ed ho scelto il the Carlton. Pessima idea. La camera standard e' un buco di 12 mq, il bagno impraticabile con la porta che urta il vaso e non e' possibile aprirla del tutto. Lo staff Ã¨ rude e scortese e per farmi cambiare stanza Ã¨ dovuto intervenire il CEO della mia compagnia. Mi hanno addebitato anche il luggage storage. Sconsigliatissimo
Great hotel great food great location. Breakfast a bit expensive but good quality

Loved this hotel. Location on Broadway was perfect. Breakfast delicious!
No complaints!
Easily accessible location, close to subway, shopping and the magnificent 9/11 memorial.

review_title: Emotive location, but a great one for exploring all the sights
review_text:
We booked this hotel because we wanted a 4* hotel at a reasonable price, and we found it here. 
The rooms were great and the location easy for everywhere even tho you are down town not in the middle of everywhere. Use the subway right outside the hotel to get everywhere. Get a 7 day pass and it is quicker than taxi's. 
I called the hotel as soon as booking and asked for a high room and true to their word they gave us greatrooms on the 30th floors. It was our daughters birthday as well and they arranged for balloons and cake. 
Also we were delayed in getting to the hotel due to flight problems and the concierge phoned the top of the rock for us to explain we were going to be late for our scheduled slot. Fantastic service!! 
The rooms were good. Big enough for everything. Lots or draw space to unpack properly and the beds were amazingly comfy!! Their pillars were wow and they gave you lots!! The rooms were a bit chilly and we did not work out how to re set the air con but they gave us an extra blanket for each room and then we were fine. I'm sure if I'd asked about the air con someone would have helped! 
All in all a great hotel. Don't be put off by the noise from the WTC building. It is not too bad at all. The location looks a mess because of the building, and when we were the the wall street protesters were also just across the way, so eveywhere was barracaed around, but that adds to exactly where you are! The views were amazing!! 
Stay here!

review_title: Great hotel with lots of history!
review_text: This is a beautiful hotel! We had a great experience and plan on returning next time we are in NYC.

review_title: I'd stay again, if on a short trip.
review_text:
Chelsea Lodge is located within walking distance of Penn Station, which is one of the main reasons I chose it. A good pick indeed, as I was able to get out and about to everything I wanted to see with ease. 
The rooms are small, so I don't think you would want to stay longer than a few nights, but I knew that before booking. I found everything to be clean too. 
CL customer service extends to having a person near the front desk who takes your money and gives you a key - very transactional, and not going to win any awards here for friendliness. 
Also, I'm not convinced about the whole "character" thing, personally I think it is all rather old and needs some money pumped into for new wallpaper etc. 
Overall, I would stay here again though, but only if it were for a few days.

room was small but manageble. free wifi and sweets on the frony desk.
the heating broke the last night.but.there were guys fixing it when we left.

review_title: Fantastic,amazing nouns do not do it justice
review_text:
Fantastic location. We stayed for four days on a room only basis, and cannot fault anything as a professional employed within the service industry I found the the experience impeccable. 
If you are looking for a retreat not too far away, there is a great little bar called The Growler on stones street, just off water street. Which offers a relaxed atmosphere with a range of fine beers, wines and spirits, with amazing service. Definitely worth a visit!!

review_title: Great, modern hotel in good downtown location
review_text:
Had a lovely stay here, all the staff we encountered were very helpful and friendly. We went to get changed before leaving and there was a large, air conditioned cab waiting to take us to the airport without us even asking!
The room, although small was bigger than others we've had in New York, was spotlessly clean, had plenty of towels, much needed air con, great Lavazza coffee maker and lovely toiletries. 
The decor was generic modern hotel, nothing to complain about, and the bed was soooo comfy after days and nights walking around the city.
We were at the front of the hotel which had an amazing view of the World Trade Center site, having thought it would be eerie it was actually very calming to look down on the fountains.
We found the location great as this visit we were more interested in the Downtown and SoHo areas which are within easy walking distance and everything else is easily accessible by Metro (3 stations within easy walking distance) and the city sightseeing buses pick up just around the corner.
We got a price we were happy with through lowcostusa, and having read on here what others have paid think we saved a good Â£150 or more on a 2 night weekend stay.
The only very minor negative would be that there was no free WiFi, but there was a PC set up in reception so at least we could check in and print our boarding passes for our flight home.

review_title: Best service we have ever had at a hotel in 40 years of travel!
review_text: The staff made us feel warm, welcome and pampered. After 40 plus years of travel we have never experienced this level of exceptional service. It started upon arrival with Jim, the bellman, and held throughout our five night stay. History tour on Saturday was both interesting and delightful. Already planning a return stay!
Very nice place, excellent staff, the rooms are perfect. Breakfast is great. Definitely a worthwhile place to stay.

review_title: Worst reception staff we have ever come across.
review_text:
Nice hotel but geez the service is so unfriendly it is almost comical. The front desk staff don't acknowledge you when you walk in, and definitely don't smile or say hello. It certainly did not give a good impression of the city.
The hotel is in a good location to the downtown sites (9/11 site, staten island ferry etc), but only recommend a short stay since midtown has much more to offer in terms on eateries, nightlife and site seeing. The complementary breakfast was a good start to the day. If they improved their customer service this place would be enjoyable.
Good sized room, clean and cozy. Great helpful staff. We will absolutely stay here next time we go to New York. The back alley has some nice pubs, but the hotel is very quiet.

While I read many of the reviews on here before booking this hotel, I was still hoping that Hilton would live up to it's great reputation and surprise me with a beautiful hotel right at the heart of ground zero.
Maybe I was being too hopeful and a little ambitious and should have take the word of other reviewers on here wih a bit more notice, especially given that I was staying for 9 nights.
Upon arrival, the actuall building looked quite nice and well maintained. The foyer and lobby bar on entrance were well looked after and still appeared fairly modern which you would expect from a rather new hotel such as this in comparison to others in the area.
But that is where the compliments stop. It is very hard to describe how helpful the staff were as they were all extremely different. The men seemed to all be very helpful and always seemed more than happy to help while I honestly did not meet one female who could even afford a smile. I only dealt with 3 females on the front desk, and they were all very condescending in their approach and seemed to think that their job stopped at processing my payment. They really had no idea on the concept of customer service. 
When we finally got into our room(junior corner suite) I was pretty shocked at the state of everything. It looked like the hotel had been fitted out in the 80's and never updated since. The bed was very comfortable but probably about average for a Hilton bed. Certainly not as nice as those in Australia but still very comfortable nonetheless. We had wi-fi in our rooms but were expected to pay an exorbitant amount for it so decided against it. given the price of the hotel, and the fact there is a Starbucks downstairs with FREE wi-fi, there is definitely no need to fork out more cash.
The showers double as bath tubs which I believe is not acceptable in a decent hotel, especially when decked out with cheap looking shower curtains. 
The bedroom lighting is very poor with only two small bedside lights for the bedroom. There are other lights for joining rooms which suffice however.
We were extremely disappointed with the room service. We stayed during the recent hurricane/tropical storm and understand the limitations this placed on staff, but we were never even told that we would not have room service for the weekend. not that it really mattered, seeing though our room was only made up twice during how ENTIRE stay!!!! Not including the day we were checking out, where we had 2 staff cleaning while we were still in the room trying to relax before our long flight back to Australia.
The noise of the construction next door can be annoying at times but we were aware of this from other reviews on here and given the circumstances, it's hard to criticize the hotel for that.
During the hurricane we were forced to eat at the hotel restaurant. While I was fairly happy with the quality of food, the service was terrible. We had to wait 30 minutes before we were asked for our order. Then, before we could even finish telling him what we wanted he was off, without even asking for drinks or sides. We also had breakfast there which is ridiculously over priced. $6 for a small glass of orange juice or disgusting coffee? Who are they kidding!!!?
We arrived just as the renovations were completed on the restaurant so we were expecting something special. Well, weren't we in for a shock. I seen the before and after photos and i really have no idea why they even bothered. Whether they failed to employ an interior designer or whether they had a budget of $50, I'm not sure, but the renovations were a joke. Apart from the new carpet it didn't look any different. While we were there they started renovations on the lobby bar which I didn't think really needed one anyway and when I left it didn't look like that was going to change much either really.
The only plus side to our stay was the help of the concierge. He was a fantastic help and could not do enough to help us find our way around NYC. The only note I have with the concierge is that he finishes quite early and there should be an evening concierge as this is when a lot of patrons are in need of info for somewhere nice to eat.
I am a member of the military which entitled me to a great discount. Without this, I would have been even more disappointed(if thats possible).
I really hope that this hotel gets it's act together, especially the from desk female staff and improves because at the moment it's a scar on the Hilton name.

review_title: Ideal for young couples, good location.
review_text: Chelsea Lodge is no thrills, yet at the same time it is quaint, clean and well looked after. It is in hip Chelsea and it makes getting round very easy. The share toilet was not an issue and the shower in the room is not as odd as it first sounds, however I would only recommend this set up for couples only.

I have never stayed in the Wall Street Dist. so was puzzled about where to stay when I needed a room in the heart of Wall Steet. As usual Trip Advisor came through. OMG Shay a great place!,!! My wife wouldn't like it but for my needs. True enough the rooms are small, and if on vacation, might not work. For business they are perfect. All around the hotel are great places to eat and you are at anywhere on Wall Street in 3 minutes! This is a treasure go for it.

review_title: Great room upgrade, but too busy to really look after you
review_text: When we arrived our taxi couldn't get anywhere near the front door too many cars and cabs double parked. We were upgraded to a mini-suite because we were staying for 12 nights - that was fantastic! Room was clean and remarkably quiet. We did have the toilet back up - no real apology They just said it was due to "old pipes". We couldn't adjust the room temperature so we turn the heating off. The lobby was constantly crowded with a major conference on for 4 or 5 days, and the doormen were inattentive throughout our entire stay. The housekeeping staff however were delightful and did a good job. The concierge staff weren't eager to help and were a bit surly.

review_title: Great location for a great price
review_text: My wife and myself just came back from Europe and as far as hotels goes (along with everything else, of course) it is great to be in U. S. Better price, bigger room, wifi that works, great service, etc. The location is magnificent. The hotel os located in The heart of The Financial District. Minutes away from Battery Park, Staten Island Ferry, Brooklyn Bridge, many great restaurants And ample shopping. Friendly staff. Highly recommended.

review_title: This hotel offers apartment-like accommodation on the upper east side with few of the usual hotel services such as a cafÃ©.
review_text: Our one-bedroom suite was spacious and had a full kitchen - larger than we had expected. While comfortable, the suite needed updating, eg, the broadloom had seen better days. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The free wi-fi was great. Don't bother using the room safe; it's not bolted to the wall or floor. One downside about the location - it's on the corner of 2nd Avenue where subway construction has been ongoing for years, so not pleasant to walk along, as well as noisy.

We loved the room, the location and the staff. However the bathroom needed a good scrub down. There were urine stains on the toilet. The counter needed cleaning as well. I was only there for 1 night otherwise I would have purchased some Clorox wipes and cleaned it myself.
Great hotel,would definatly stay there again. Has large suites with kitchens.

review_title: El mejor hotel de NEW YORK
review_text: Habitaciones grandiosas y camas muy grandes. Nunca habia dormido tan bien en un hotel. Que relax y que gusto. Dormia tan bien que mi novia y yo nos levantabamos con mas ganas todavia de seguir disfrutando de la mejor ciudad del mundo. Sin duda si vuelvo a NEW YORK volvere al GRAND HYATT. Seria nuestra tercera vez. I LOVE NEW YORK, I LOVE GRAND HYATT

I booked Cooper Square hotel after reading the reviews on trip advisor. We certainly were not disappointed. On our arrival, we were given wine and asked to take a seat in the library/chill out area. We arrived about 2pm but our room wasn't ready, so we left our bags and went to explore Greenwich and the meat packing district- well worth the walk! We returned back to the hotel and were given our keys. When we went to our room we found we'd been upgraded from a Cooper 2 to a suite with a bottle of champagne waiting in the room to say congratulations (we had mentioned the purpose of our visit). The room was beautiful- big bed & very comfy, tv, desk, extensive mini bar and a lovely spacious bathroom. On top of this, we had a great view of Manhattan! 
What more can you ask for? A great location, great staff and beautiful hotel. We'd definitely return here.

I've stayed here for around 30 nights since May 2010 and this place always leaves me more relaxed than the last stay. The location is excellent and the staff is wonderful. The doorman are very attentive and keep up with the high volume very well. The front desk team has great suggestions and makes you feel taken care of. 
The rooms are beautiful and not too small for your typical NYC trip. I will say tho after staying in a corner junior suite, I don't think I'd ever not pay the extra for it. They are so comfortable! 
The breakfast buffet is great, but be careful if you're with your family. You can spend more than $100 for breakfast for a family of 4. The upstairs bar in the evening was a little quiet, and prices were to be expected. 
I love the close proximity to the R, N, and 4 trains. The location is wonderful in lower manhattan. I will stay every future trip to the Big Apple.

review_title: Best service, great location, awesome city view, and wonderful thoughtfulness.
review_text: My husband and I came here for our 1 yr anniversary and it couldn't have been any better. The location is perfect, close enough to soho to walk to and the subway is only minutes away. The people at Cooper Square are so welcoming, accommodating, and thoughtful- we received a complimentary gift for our anniversary when we came back from our day out! The lobby is comfortable with complimentary coffee and several flavors of tea. The view we had was amazing- I loved going to bed to the city lights. The bed is the most comfortable bed I've ever slept in and I was so tempted to ask what mattress it was lol. The bathroom was a great feature, heated floors, a great little bay window and bench area, huge shower stall and heavenly smelling toiletries. If you want to stay in and watch tv they have a good size flat screen with lots of channels which I appreciated after being in dingy hotels with 2 channels of news and infomercials. I can't say how impressed and happy I was on my first trip to New York, I hope to come back for every anniversary b/c it was a great experience. Book here and you won't regret it. oh and forget those standard back in the day mints, one day we got apples and the next cookies!!! Great for snacks while walking and strollin the city. :)

Great staff. Great views. Great rates. Great location. Will stay here again. The staff went above and beyond and the room was better than perfect. Heard no construction noise inside the hotel and room.

review_title: Excellent mid town location, first class service
review_text:
Myself, my husband and our 9 year old have just returned from a wonderful weekend to NY to celebrate my 40th birthday. 
When we booked the trip with expedia, we were asked if it was a special occasion and we confirmed it was. 
On arrival, a bottle of chilled champagne and 2 glasses was waiting in our room with a note wishing me a happy birthday! 
The service, cleanliness and room comfort was first class. Every day we were given fresh towels and a lovely turn-down service in the evening. 
The location is fabulous too, short walk to 5th avenue, central park, rockerfeller plaza, times square etc.
The concierge was very helpful and suggested a few good restaurants nearby that were very good. 
The lobby is absolutely beautiful, so grand and reminiscent of a bygone era. 
All in all, the Waldorf is 5 star all the way, from the reception staff to the surroundings. I especially liked the excellent zip check out, just dial a number and just leave your door key in your room and leave, no 
hanging around at the front desk. 
I would not hesitate to recommend this to a friend and might even ask if I could join them!

review_title: Another Great Visit to NY Waldorf
review_text: I decided to have a girls weekend to celebrate my wedding engagement and try to find a dress. We rented 4 rooms. Jackie at the Diamond desk helped us out (she is wonderful!) we had beautiful rooms facing park ave and was greeted with champagne and strawberries to jump start our weekend. I am a frequent for business at this hotel... I am now a frequent for personal.

review_title: It is in the middle of a construction site
review_text: Not a good choice. Go elsewhere. Anywhere. Noise. Bad lobby inadequate elevators. Bad expensive parking.

review_title: Location excellent, rooms ok, service no thanks
review_text:
We stayed in a room on the 30th floor and had excellent views overlooking the World Trade Center Site. Unlike other reviewers have pointed out we didn't get earplugs, so better bring your own as you will here some noise ftom construction work.
Staff at reception wasn't really friendly or welcoming and when asked about driving times to La guardia airport the receptionist insisted we would need an hour by cab on a saturday morning-it took us just a bit more than 15 minutes.
When we arrived there was no bellboy and nobody assisting with luggage- unusual for a city centre Hilton.
Our room was spacious with two of those comfortable Hilton beds, however room could have been cleaner like the whole hotel. Fitness centre needs maintenance and a thorough cleaning.
All in all not what we expect from a Hilton and are a bit disappointed

Get a corner room... After a night in the city, looking out over 9/11 memorial project, statue of liberty, etc... Just really beautiful. Far from the theater district - but close enough to little Italy and soho. Big, clean rooms with great views at a good value

I'm a new yorker but live in a shoe box ... so when my mom came for a visit I splurged and booked a room here. The staff could not have been more helpful and accomadating ... big rooms for nyc standards ... a Starbucks in the lobby ... every major subway within fifteen feet and peter Thomas roth products! plus ... a Lovely sun drenched pool and sauna ... if you have concern over the noise from ground zero don't ... we were in 3001 and heard nothing!

review_title: Disappointing- not living up to its heritage.
review_text:
My wife and I stayed for two days Valentine's weekend. I am a HHonors Diamond and we stayed on points- I spend approximately 225 days a year on the road, about 100 w/Hilton properties.
We both love historic hotels- given the choice, we'll frequently stay at an Embassy Suites vs. a Hilton or Waldorf because of the ameneties for our style, but we have enjoyed wonderful experiences at properties like the Waldorf Grand Waileia and found the flagship wanting.
When one arrives at the main entrance of the Waldorf on Park Avenue, there is a 18-20 step staircase up to the lobby level. There was one doorman and no bellmen working (the main bell desk is next to the front desk in the main lobby, 200 feet up the stairs away), but to his credit the harried doorman helped my wife with our third bag to the top of the stairs and apologized there was no one to help to the desk- functionally this was fine, as we are used to handling oour own, but the doorman at the WALDORF is having to apologize for being unable to help on a Sunday afternoon? 
Check-in reminded me of a Vegas casino hotel, with the line and line-minder, but they were very friendly and when our room wasn't ready offered to call me on my cell when it was and directed me to the 'Diamond Reception' when we returned to pick up our keys.
When we returned, we went to the 'Diamond Reception,' which was a two-desk room, only one manned, next to the bell desk at the end of the lobby. While waiting for the couple in front of us to be waited on, I got the pleasure of listening to the bell captain talk loudly into his cell phone in walkie-talkie mode as if he was yelling at his kids at home.
That said, we were given nice coupons for drinks and continental breakfast at the Starbucks at the base of the stairs (where a bellman desk would be great), upgraded to a junior suite, and the bellman who delivered our luggage (we'd left it with walkie-talkie boy when we first checked in and the rooms weren't ready) was outstanding in both service ethic and personality.
 Sunday night- we went to the Met for a concert, stopped at the lobby bar for a drink, great service. Two hours later, after we haad changed clothes to go for a brisk walk (from dress to casual), went back to the same bar, sat down, I ordered an upscale drink and a glasss of water for my teetotaler wife, and received a very snippy 'there's a two drink minimum at the bar' from the lady bartender. Responding 'Oh, would it help if I am paying with this?' and pulling out the Waldorf coupon with my name on it as a Diamond, she just turned around and made the drinks, no other response.
When leaving, at 5 am Tuesday morningn to catch an early flight, I had to stop at the front desk to fix our receipt- I'd been charged fro Internet acceess. Very friendly staff and no problem, but why? I have this problem 1 out of 20 stays- didn't expect it here.
So we head out, down the stairs, and come to find out that the flagship of the Waldorf brand, a hotel located oon Park Avenue in NY City, doesn't have a 24 hour door presence. The taxi drivers were nice- the one who took us to the airport helped my wife through the door when her bag was stuck- but REALLY? You're the Waldorf and you don't have a doorman?
Please understand- this is not overblown expectations. We spent the previous two night at the Intercontinental Barclay (also on points), and the service blew the Waldorf away. All things being equal, I had better service at the Hilton Atlanta airport I bought off of Hotwire last month during a snowstorm.
Have been NYC several times. Loved this hotel. Great service, good location and nice accomodations.

I was at a business meeting at AOL and they had a discounted rate for their clients at Cooper Square Hotel which is close to their office. So I was wiling to give it a try. The hotel was wonderful. The service was very personal and attentive. The rooms were clean and modern. The beds were so comfortable. The shower was large and included a steam shower. The views of Manhattan were terrific with floor to ceiling windows. The value was really terrific. I will be back with my family. And it is in a great location in Greenwich Village near terrific restaurants including Lupa Osteria.

We spent just one night there while attending a couple of Yankee games. The entire hotel was refurbished after 9/11 and was closed for two years. They got it right with the renovation - very nice and a good value. Not very convenient to Yankee stadium - unless you take the #4 train at Fulton (which we did)

review_title: Why is it so hard to get rooms ready?
review_text: Have been waiting at and around front desk for more than an hour, as the hotel keeps predicting (wrongly) when my room will be ready. What's so hard about being honest with guests, so they don't waste their afternoon sitting around the hotel?

Just came back from a great weekend and have to thank the Millennium for a big part of it. Everything from early check in to the fantastic view everything went without a hitch. Though we where on the eighth floor directly across from ground zero we heard no construction noise. Andrew in the lobby bar is not only a mixologist but also a great comedian and conciere. review_title: Great location, shame about the hotel.
review_text: Currently staying in this hotel and have to say that for the price we have paid, it has not lived up to expectations. We paid close to $300 a night having booked a couple of months before an early December stay. For that kind of money I would have expected more than a tired and dated room, no breakfast, a dysfunctional and noisy cooling unit (which is is required as the 16th floor rooms get seriously hot even though it's freezing outside), no black out blinds (or full width blinds of any kind for that matter) and no free wifi (which always annoys me greatly when expensive hotels charge you for this now basic service). It is in a great spot that is true and though the concierge was short and fairly standoffish the staff in general are friendly and polite. That said, we won't be staying here again and would recommend to our friends investigating others hotels first.

Staying on a last minute business trip with a budget, my original list of hotel selection was diminished but the close to $800 per night rates. I came across the Belvedere Hotel by the uncharacteristic high scores it had received from from various hotel recommendation sites similar to this one which listed it high even though only being a 3/4 star banded hotel. Well I can tell you that staying here really shows the reason for these ratings as the hotel is extremely clean and friendly with newly renovated executive floors/rooms with marble bathrooms and pillowtop mattresses. The atmosphere is very pleasant and the cleanliness is second to none.
The staff are very attentive as are both the concierge and doormen.
Executive rooms are best value for money with upgraded services/features and complimentary WiFi.
NB: this is a Mid December stay - so probably their busiest time of year - kudos to their service levels.

I stayed here in NYC fashion week. Hotels were sky high so I opted for an economical room. Well I was pleasantly surprised. The rooms were spacious and had a tiny kitchenette area with a fridge, sink, and microwave. I couldn't believe it. In New York that's unheard of. The beds were cozy and the staff was extra nice. I have had bad experiences other places where I have paid up to a thousand a night. For just under 300, it was a bargain and I definitely am coming back!!!

review_title: I'd rather stay in the subway...
review_text: I am a 25 year old educated understanding person. I use Expedia to book hotels all the time and have never been disappointed. Unfortunately this experience has changed my view. I booked the room for my husband and baby to stay there during a weekend tourist trip. This hotel needs a disclaimer. Those who aren't down for weed ( i heard a lady pronounce loudly how she forgot her weed in the room) and drinking all night don't stay here or expect even the smallest amount of respect for paying guests. This hotel is more worried about its image as a "club" or "lounge" then about the people paying 400 dollars plus a night for. Those people are treated second class. I heard THUMPING bass from 10-5am. I could hear the lyrics completely. Around 2 am I called the front desk and pleaded for them to get some control and ask the music to just be lowered not turned off just lowered. It got louder. I was offered to pack my baby and all my things up at 230 am to move rooms. The nit wit at the desk has clearly never had a child. I entered the room and the bathroom was filthy, with opened and used soap and shampoo and conditioners all over the shower. So that was never cleaned... Classy. Next I was trying to enter the hotel lobby/bar/lounge to go to my "bedroom" I use that term loosely cause you won't sleep on the 2nd 3rd or 4th floors, and was stopped by an idiot who asked me if I was on the "list" or if I had a reservation. I said I'm staying here he tried to give me a hassle. So again their own "guests" get hassled because entrance to their precious bar is more important then Hospitality. Last but certainly not least when I went down to complain the manager Carla who was the only half sensible person around and I had to wait in line because another disgruntled guest was doing the same. I know theyd like you to think most people are happy but that spoke volumnes. Poor Carla offered a free night in that hell hole, really I'm telling you how your hotel is a piece of crap and you offered me another stay no thanks. I'll take my complaints else where cause that poor girl was just reading off a script and offering no real apology. Next time I do this I'll make sure to do better research. These posts are all valid. Most of the reviews about the rooms are spot on, ie: mini bar, lights, prison bathroom, smell, attitude of staff and much more. I'm sure the raving reviews about the bar are true. Because that is what they are worried about. Not their PAYING guests. A night in this hell hole will only set you back 500 dollars. My suggestion, go uptown to a good resort, like the Marriott, Hilton or Hyatt and get real service. The times square Marriott is awesome!

review_title: Simply the best budget tip in Manhattan
review_text:
Located in Manhattan's Hell Kitchen the 414 offers the best value for your money. 
The rooms are well equipped with 37"-Flatscreen and are spacious compared with other hotels in NYC. They are all clean and quiet, one the other hand the Times Square is only a five-minute-walk away.
I was there for the New York Marathon and at the day before the race I found a complimentary race pack in the room with bottles of water and Gatorade as well as Energy Bar. On the race day the hotel offered a breakfast at 5 a.m.
To describe the Hotel 414 in one word, I would choose "perfect"

I've stayed at the Dream in midtown and other hip boutique hotels in NY. There is a lot about this hotel to like. The location is great if you want to be in Chelsea. The room isn't as tiny as, say, the Hudson, and there are actual drawers and a tiny closet. But there are several serious flaws. First, the walls are paper thin so you can hear every word of the tv or conversation in the next room or the hall. Every slamming door will wake you. The lobby is too hip and noisy to be occupied after about 5. And weirdly, the electronics are a genuine nightmare. We could not get the tv to work. All the lights in the place are programmed by buttons on the wall but there is NO WAY to turn off the overhead lights and still have a bedside or desk lamp on. All on or all off. This is insanity. We complained repeatedly but there is no solution. Also no way to turn the light off on the electric control panel on the phone. We had to cover it with a towel. At these prices they should have brought us a lamp to plug in but they said none was available. Also the euro style toilet is a good foot higher than a normal toilet. We won't be back at the Dream.

The metal bathroom fixtures are intended to be cool, but bear a strong resemblance to something someone might find in a minimum security correctional facility. Again, the key word here is LOUD. review_text:
We had our annual SISTER trip here in New York this year and stayed in this hotel. It was everything that we could have asked for in a hotel plus more at times. The staff was very professional and personal. We met a lot of personnel the four days we stayed and not from problems. They were always around and greeted you very politely. The rooms were small, you are in NYC, but we fit us 5 girls in there comfortably I must say, luggage and all. We didn't plan on living in this room the whole time while we were here anyways. 
There was almost always a doorman opening the doors for us or helping catch us a cab. The tv didn't work at first but they fixed it. The bathroom sink is designed weird and does not work but it is interesting to look at. And there is NO insulation between the walls. You can hear EVERYTHING that goes on next door. 
 overall, wonderful stay. We will definitely come back. Hotel look is awesome.

review_title: Do not stay here, they charge your credit card for services not used!!!
review_text: I booked this hotel through expedia as one of it's secret luxury hotels. I paid $500 for the privilege. I only stayed one night (and thank god it was only one night). It was a disaster from start to finish. Firstly the lift got stuck on the 6th floor, and if you think you will get a good night sleep for $500 think again. I was on the 10th floor and you could hear the music from the disco all night. But the disaster did not stop there - since getting home dream downtown have charged my credit card for an additional $400 and $35 dollars for an umbrella. These charges are fake and my bank is in dispute with the hotel. Don't be taken in by the friendliness of the staff. And make sure you check your credit card statement if you do stay here , they will try to steal your money!!! Do not stay here if you value your credit card and want a good night sleep.

review_title: Great hotel, if you don't want to think too much about money!
review_text:
Super trendy hotel with a great lobby underneath the glass bottom of the first floor outdoor pool. Rooms are not very spacious, but very clean and comfortable with all white minimalist finish and porthole windows.
One strange point is the en suite which is separated from the room by an opaque glass partition and has a hole in the door for some reason. Only share a room with someone with whom you are comfortable sharing more than sweet nothings!
The roof terrace is fantastic (if pricey) for cocktails with a great view of the skyline, it is guests only until 9pm.
Only real downside, and this may just be NYC generally, is that, as well as the room not being cheap, everything was quite expensive and nothing was complimentary. For example: the bottle of water they put in the room on arrival is $10! left feeling they were a tiny bit money grabbing - but still enjoyed our stay.
