review_title: Horrible hotel no matter what deal you get!
review_text: This hotel is the worst. The doormen don't assist you. You can only get free Internet in the lobby so you might as well walk down to Starbucks bc at least they have coffee. The elevators are so slow you need to leave an extra 10 min just to get down to the street so you are not late. God forbid you forget something in the room Just forget it bc it's not worth the 20 min delay. The bed is super squeaky and loud! Every move you make is a tsunami for the person next to you and you feel the wave of the person turning at night. There are barely any lights in the room so expect to dress and put makeup on in darkness and don't attempt to put your clothes in the closet bc you don't have a light in the hall or closet. At night you can hear everything from babies crying to the tv next door. Also, the AT&T wi-fi is blocked on your iPad so you have to purchase the $14.95 for access in your room and then can't get what you payed for on your laptop because it's 'per unit'. Don't bother complaining because the front desk has no sympathy! Even if you get a good rate it is not worth the money saved. If I wouldn't hbe prepaid I would already have checked-out.
We really enjoyed the location of this hotel, away from NYC's tourist hotspots.

review_title: Great, affordable, for New York, place to stay.
review_text: OTA was a great place to stay, particularly for the price and location. The staff went out if their way to be helpful. My one (small) complaint was there was no hotel bar and no wine or liquor in the mini bar, which would have been nice after a long travel day and late arrival.

review_title: Great place to stay, near everything!
review_text: Room was good-sized. Service awesome. Right near the subway and theater district. Will definitely come back!

review_title: Nice Biz/ couples Hotel steps from 79th st subway
review_text: Great place if ur looking for a biz or jumping off room. No idea if there's even a restaurant but here r so many in the neighborhood no need to stay there to eat. Views on the north side suck (7 th floor that is) but patios on 14 and 16 more than make up for it. Grab some take out and a bottle of wine and have a nice night. Only a couple min to subway (79th) and ab 5 to Columbia. If taking a flight from Newark give yourself ab 3 hours to go subway, NJ Transit and Airtrain (only 15$!) and thT will give u an hour to get thru customs etc (fly Porter if ur coming from Toronto! Great sevice quick flight (door (Oshawa) to door OTA was 6 hrs. Taking GO Train and shuttle fr Union.

review_title: Great place to stay in NYC!
review_text: Wonderful weekend experience! The staff were friendly, helpful and went out of their way to accommodate our schedule. The lobby and the room was neat and clean. Great location - right next door to the Shake Shack - walking distance to everywhere from Penn Station, to Macy's, to the theaters, all at a great rate.

From the very short-tempered, snarky guy who 'greeted' me on the front desk to the five phone call attempts that it took just to schedule a wakeup call, I did not have a good 5 night stay here. The standard room was incredibly small even by NYC standards but it was quiet. The TV was criminally short on cable channels which is really unnecessary in a modern hotel, there were wires sticking out of the walls and TV, there was no age in the room and I came back to my room one day to my smoke alarm having been removed and just left on the chair with no explanation. So odd. Really not a pleasant or comfortable experience at all, especially given the price.

La mia ragazza ed io abbiamo trovato questo albergo dopo averne visti moltissimi..era l unico che aveva un prezzo ragionevole rispetto alla posizione e ai servizi che aveva..allo stesso prezzo di una qualsiasi camera in un qualsiasi albergo abbiamo preso una junior suite (salottino, angolo cottura, bagno)..l unica "pecca" se cosÃ¬ si puÃ² dire Ã¨ che le camere andrebbero un po rimodernate ma Ã¨ un particolare al quale si passa sopra solamente pensando all ubicazione! A piedi si raggiunge tranquillamente la stazione centrale, l empire state building e time square, la libreria comunale e il palazzo delle Nazioni unite..facili anche i collegamenti con metro e autobus..ne vale davvero la pena!!

review_title: total not worth staying at, its over rated!
review_text: The room is tiny and smell like mold. Most of all, the toilet is broken. I'm very upset with the choice I have made. 4 Star is over rated for sure.
Thank you Antonio and Alberto!! You guys made our trip perfect. Loved everything. Thanks again.

This hotel is recently new which I value since it is always better to use a room that hans't been touched by thousands before you. The rooms are nice, clean and the space is acceptable. The location is OK if you are into theaters and times square area. I had a corner room located at the 23rd floor. The view was unremarkable. Office towers and old ugly buildings are all around this hotel. Some shady restaurants are near by. If you want the "times square experience" I would reccomend you to stay in a hotel just besides times square like the marriott marquis, otherwise I would stay in a hotel closer to midtown, like the plaza. I wouldnt pay more than $280 for a double room in this hotel.

review_title: Amazing service, great rooms, fantastic concierge department!
review_text:
We were there for the first week of our honeymoon end of June - beginning of July.
We had a King bed Sky View on the 35th floor with an amazing view directing north with a distant view of Central Park.
Rooms are clean and well equiped,
location is central, but we would have preferred a little more towards 5th avenue because you always jeed to pass by Times Square (which we knew in advance),
but the best part of the hotel is the friendliness of the staff and especially of the concierge department with Kat Bride being an amazing help to anyone having questions about restaurants, bars, places to visit and things to do!

This hotel was really nice and the staff went out of their way to provide me with exceptional service.
The rooms were updated with modern style but they were rather small, which I guess is the expectation for Manhattan.
The only real downfall that I had was that the rooms echoed from even the smallest noise in the hallway and that for the duration of my stay, te entire hotel had a really bad smell to it. I think the smell originated from the hotel restaurant, but was not a pleasant food smell. It also could have been the air freshener that was being used.
Overall though, it was a nice hotel and I would definitely stay there again.
For the best prices, check Expedia

review_title: Always Perfect , great beds and ideal location.
review_text: Our home in NYC, perfect location. Comfy beds with a nice tv to relax and watch some movies. Just beside Madison Square Garden, Penn Station and Macy's. Really great Irish bar next door called Tir na Nog. Great storage facility on your day of check out where you can leave your luggage in the hotel for $2 until your ready to go to the airport which saves you bringing it around if you have a few hours to kill.

review_title: A great location, great hotel, great ambiance, exceptional service equals a very happy customer.
review_text:
As soon as we walked into the hotel I was very impressed with the very friendly service we received. The lobby was very nice with a very relaxing feel. Sophia was very helpful and was just a genuinely nice person. I told her that my two kids were excited because they were having a birthday and we had traveled from San Diego to take them to a Blackeyed Peas concert (the concert was eventually canceled due to weather). She asked me for their names. I didn't think much of it. She gave us a great room with an awesome view. The room was very well appointed and had a very nice bathroom.
The hotel is very centrally located. It is only two blocks from Time Square. There are also great restaurants in the area. The subway is right at the corner. After a great day in New York, we returned to our room and were surprised to find two small birthday cakes for my now 8 and 11 year old kids. They have won me over in a big way and will recommend this hotel to everyone I know.Â 
I have stayed at great hotels all over the world but I have never had this kind of personal service. It really made my trip to see the look on my kids face when they walked into the room and saw the cakes. It really is the simple things that make the greatest difference. Thanks Sophia!

Stayed at this property for one evening and will defiantly stay here again. My assistant booked the hotel and I didn't even look where I was staying until arriving at the airport. It is near Time Square which is better than those directly in TS because it's not as crazy or loud. Room was big (for NYC), clean and staff was fantastic!

This was a very much delayed honeymoon for our civil partnership the previous year. Before we arrived from the uk, we emailed ahead for helpful info on things such as shows and transport etc. The concierge team were fantastic.
When we arrived, we were informed that our room had been upgraded to a deluxe king double. The staff were so pleasant and professional. We never minded tipping for the good service. 
When it came to leave NYC (we didn't want to leave) not only do we miss and crave the intercontinental but also the burger and cheese fries from shake shack burger restaurant which is on the same corner of the block. Don't get me wrong, you are in a great area for all types of food... But nothing beat a great evening out at the theatre (seeing Daniel Radcliffe in "how to succeed in business...") than sitting in our room very late night, with shake shack fries, cheese burgers and hotdogs. Watching Saturday night live on the rooms HUGE hd tv. It's the simple things lol.
We miss NYC so much (it was our 1st visit) and can't wait to go again. Hopefully stating here again. Afterall, there will be anniversaries.

very nice lobby but found some of the staff rude and sarcastic. Room was very small, the two of us barely had space to even open our luggage! No coffee machine and an out dated blowdryer which didn't work properly!

review_title: Excellent trip- felt like real new yorkers! Staff is great, concierge the best. Great location, beautiful room.
review_text:
We were very nervous to visit new York for the first time. Not speaking English very well and hearing bad stuff from people made us worry. We emailed the concierge ahead of time and got a quick answer everytime. Sonia arranged tickets for two shows and picked restaurants for us for all the days. 
When we arrived, everyone was so nice. Abu helped us with our bags and Nelson helped with our room. It was so beautiful, the view was amazing. When we went to concierge for some help everyone was so nice and helpful. Sonia recognized our name from the emails and had so much patience with us. She showed us how the subway worked and even went down to the station and showed us how to buy the card. All of the restaurants she picked were so delicious and most important we felt like real new yorkers and not tourists. 
We will definitely stay here again and dell our friends and family.

Extravagant lobby, helpful receptionist, lovely doormen and porters for the luggage. Doorman was especially helpful in hailing a taxi at 6:00 for when I was going to the apple store to buy an iPad 2.
Rooms are great, food at breakfast and tea was gorgeous.

We stayed here for 3 days and had a very pleasant experience. The rooms were clean, bed was very comfortable and the service was great! The price was reasonable as well. Only thing... I found the beverages available for purchase in the room were way overpriced, even by NYC standards. Kuerig coffee maker very convenient but real creamer to go with the delicious coffee would have been nice and expected. Shame to put powdered creamer in a good cup of bean:-)

My husband and I stayed here for 2 nights and it was very nice. Only a block or so from Time Square. The rooms were very nice and fully stocked mini fridge (very expensive though). The staff was nice and extremely helpful.

review_title: A good hotel lacking coffee and tea in the foyer 24 hours a day.
review_text: My family and I had a great stay and the staff were extremely helpful but as with most places in the US they are tip motivated. An early riser and with my wife asleep I couldn't make a coffee in the room. Nowhere in the hotel could I get a coffee and resorted to a trailer across the road. That was the only fault. I would definitely stay again.
A very nice hotel ideally located for Times Square. If you get one of the higher rooms you will have excellent views. Would stay there again.

review_title: Good hotel in a great location
review_text:
Stayed between 20th and 25th february for my daughters 1cth birthday. Even before arriving the customer service shown by Nima was excellemt. On finding out it was my daughters 18th birthday we were upgraded to a suite on the 33rd floor with fantastic views of manhatten and the hudson river.
The hotel is very modern with excellemt rooms. I would definitely stay here again

review_title: Great location and good room size (for NYC) marred by shoddy service.
review_text: This is my first Tripadvisor review ever. Usually I find the previous reviews to be accurate, but this time I am mystified by the praise of the service. I am a frequent business traveler to NYC averaging a week per month here. Never have I gotten such half-hearted service. Here is the rap sheet: No replenishment of toiletries or mini bar on either day of service during a three night stay. I called down and only three of four requested items showed up. The fourth item was the laundry bag so I could send my shirts out. I ended up walking them over to a local dry cleaners. I don't understand. All I need is for there to be shampoo/soap/lotion, the bed to be remade, some water and maybe a beer in the mini bar, and a laundry bag. Why is this not part of the service here? Why can't they make the bed so it looks like a pro did it rather than me at 6am? Where did my daily $5 tip go? Who knows. I am heading back to Eventi in Chelsea from here on out.

It was our first time visiting new york and we were really excited to see it all. Being 4 guys on vacation we didn't really do any planning on where to go/ how to get there. On a recommendation we decided to stay at the Intercontinental hotel in times square. The hotel is super nice and our rooms had great views. The front desk team was pretty rude all around. Anytime I asked for something they seemed bothered. What was weird about it was that all the other staff was friendly and helpful.
We spent a lot of time with the concierge. Sonia was the best. She was patient and listened to our rambles of what we wanted to do and turned them into reservations at the best restaurants and amazing tickets to a sold out show. It didn't hurt that she had the most beautiful smile.
I would definitely stay at this hotel again. The awesome rooms and knowledgable concierge make it worth every penny.

My partner and I stayed here in Feb for four nights and thee hotel surpassed all our expectations. The hotel is immaculate, clean, luxurious and very welcoming.
The staff at the hotel are very professional, yet extremely friendly and we often struck up a bit of conversation with the door men and they were all very funny and friendly.
The location is perfect for being a tourist and Times Sq is just two blocks away which has a great atmosphere at night.
Our room was massive and spacious and we had a view of Hudson River which was great. The bathrooms are modern, clean and the shower was huge with a waterfall shower head - bliss!
If you're visiting the Big Apple, this is definitely the hotel to pick!!!!!

On the avenue hotel is a perfect hotel for a business or pleasure stay. When I booked my room with Zenaida Latorre, a booking agent there I must say I was very satisfied with her knowledge in the hotel rooms and also with her courteous treatment. She accommodated my fiancee and I in 
a great room at a great rate.. Thanks to all the staff at on the 
avenue hotel for making our stay memorable and a special thanks to ms.Latorre for all her help..
I'm going back to this hotel in March! It's the best..

Expensive and old. Feels morn worn than classic. AC was broken, phones were broken, windows were old and dfficult to open (and not double paned in a noisy area). No WiFi anywhere but in the lobby. Room wasn't even ready for check in at 3:30 PM. 
Certainly not horrible, but with so many new, modern hotels that are cheaper, why stay here?

Very good. Stayed from Friday thru' Monday and wished I could've got the second weekend at the same rate.
Very good for 5th and Madison, Mid town anyway and I would stay here again. The restaurant ain't half bad either.
This hotel is one of the best hotels in new York by far. The hospitality you get as soon as you walk in the loby, is incredible. Best hotel experience ever.

This is the typical NY well located hotel. Expensive with average rooms and average service. The only thing that makes it attractive is the address. If this is essential, and the price not an issue, beds are comfy and that is just it. There are better choices in NY if you look carefully.

Ho soggiornato in questo hotel per una settimana: l'hotel e' molto accogliente e confortevole. Il personale cortese e disponibile. La camera molto spaziosa, con letto king, bagno spazioso, connessione wifi a pagamento (12.95 usd al giorno) ma free nella lobby dell'hotel (splendidamente decorata per in Natale). L'hotel si trova all'estremo sud di downtown, fuori dal caos ma anche fuori dalle zone con ristoranti e locali quindi per trovare un po' di vita, bisogna spostarsi col metro' (dista 15 min da times square). Proprio dietro all'hotel passano tre linee del metro' quindi per fortuna ci si puÃ² spostare senza troppe difficoltÃ . L'hotel si trova proprio davanti a ground zero ma il perenne cantiere non ha arrecato alcun disturbo. Le camere sono pulitissime, anche facendo la prova "dito sulla cornice del quadro"! review_text:
I've stayed in a few hotels in midtown manhattan and I've learnt never to set my expectations too high. If you do, you're often disappointed. So that was my approach with the Hilton Fashion Dist. What I got though was a really outstanding hotel with great service, great rooms and an overall outstanding experience. 
The rooms are a decent size, and the way they are furnished makes them better to use than many larger ones. Clean, modern, homely and quiet yet still really funky. Everything has been thought out well to make the best use of space. The housekeeping staff were fantastic and having little extras get such as the safe, iron and iPod docks really do make a massive difference (especially if you don't pack your iPhone charger!)
The bars were great and reasonable, and Rare View really does make you feel like you're in a movie with its fantastic views across downtown and midtown. 
The staff were all incredibly polite and friendly, and always looked to help in any way they could. They weren't pretentious or snobby as you can sometimes find. A really great assert to this hotel. 
I would stay here again, although I have two minor suggestions and one major criticism. 
The criticism - $15 a day for wifi is ridiculous. Seriously, this adds on to the price of the room, and I'll be honest, I will be calculating it in when I next look at hotels in midtown. It's a rip off and I've never paid that much for wifi anywhere. 
Suggestions - the mirrors could be better placed - having only one on the bathroom door away from a good source of light is a nightmare when getting ready. Also MORE CUPCAKES! They're lovely, but in four days I only saw them once!
Sort the wifi out and I won't give other hotels a thought.

review_title: Good stay, but not what was promised.
review_text:
We booked a package on the hotel's website that was supposed to include a room upgrade, late checkout, bottle of wine and cupcake. We received absolutely none of these things. 
The room itself was clean and comfortable. There was A LOT of street noise, so if you're a light sleeper you do not want a room that faces Lexington.

My boyfriend and I stayed here for 4 nights before heading down to Miami in October. Neither of us had ever stayed in New York before so we had no idea what to expect. Hotel is quite small but is clean and safe, staff were very friendly and gave us plenty of tourist advice. The room was also quite small but it was clean, modern, well equipped with a huge bed! We both absolutely loved New York and the hotel was a great base, we really weren't in the hotel much so was perfect for us but if you were planning on spending a lot of time in the hotel I would recommend going for one with a bar and restaurant. review_text: I normally stay at these Marriott Marquis which is beautiful with an excellent location. This year finding ourselves in search of a pet friendly hotel ended up at the Affinia Manhattan. We stayed in a suite w/ a kitchenette living room and 2 bathrooms walk in closet. Although for us the times square location of the marquis is more centrally located, the Affinia was clean, and beautifully decorated. Lots of room and very user friendly right down to the flattering light in the bathrooms. Here is one con: the rooms are not as sound proof as the Marriott and there is a fire station a few doors down. I however tune out the noise of the city...I actually enjoy it...although not the fire sirens in the middle of the night. Didn't bother me but if you have a noise sensitivity and do not care to wear earplugs, it may be a consideration. The staff was friendly. Just a beautiful hotel for half the price of the Marriott. A room so big 6 of us plus dog fit comfortably.
Stayed over night on a weekend. Very clean and spacious room. Service was great and the Sunday brunch was very good as well. Couldn't ask for a better location.

review_title: No temperature control in individual rooms
review_text: No ability to control temp in room. Was 64 throughout my stay and when I asked them to turn up heat they said it was impossible. Sent spaceheaters but they were clunky and ineffective. Cold in room, uncomfortable before and after showering. Not business friendly. Asked them to print out some documents. Acted as if it not only was illegal but frowned upon despite my offer to pay for it. No doorman, porter, or concierge available when I arrived at 5pm.

The hotel was in a good location for exploring New York, only 20 minutes to Times Square, 10 minutes to Empire State Building. Grand Central Station 5 minutes away. Elevators are a HUGE problem at this hotel so try to ask for the lower floors since you will be using the stairs a lot. review_text:
We stayed here for two nights as a result of finding what appeared to be a good deal in an excellent location. I ended up being taunted by the Marriott, Waldorf, and W hotels right across the street for two straight days. 
When we checked in we were greated by an unpleasant front desk staff that seemed more interested in getting rid of us than getting us the double room we had booked. The room ended up appearing very old, the sheets dirty, and the bathroom in need of an update. Overall we were not happy with the stay.

review_title: Excellent location, excellent service, excellent room, excellent value
review_text:
Did the Macy's day package... had an amazing room w excellent views. We loved the newly remodeled look very clean, nice comfortable furniture, loved the bed,very nice kitchen. 
 The staff was always very attentive.
When my family of 5 arrived via minivan, we pulled right up and Anthony was waiting for us. He took all our bags and then valet parked the car. As it had taken 1.5 hours to go the last 6 miles from the Lincoln tunnel to the affinia I was very thankful... it was simply put very nice to receive the kindness and attention. Our room was always promptly cleaned every day and we all know that w a 6, 4, and 9 mos old that can be a pretty crazy hotel room for the staff... Van (Vandat) one of the other doorman was always courteous. And very helpful w baggage on the way out. I also want to give a great review to the employee originally from Ireland who gathered our bags and brought them down for us. Lastly Jenny and Margaret did A fantastic job w all of our front desk needs. This was our 3rd stay. Every time we stay the affinia exceeds our expectations. That has always been why we come back. Thank you to the staff of this wonderful hotel for making our Thanksgiving stay memorable. All in all my extended family had 13 people and 3 different rooms over a 3 day span. My parents have always had a great experience at the affinia(they have stayed there 6times now)
Respectfully the Ternullo family

The +'s: Friendly staff, deluxe room size huge. King bed, sitting area with couch that could be pulled out-double bed size, large office area off of this with mini fridge. Excellent location across the street from Madison Square Garden and Penn Station. Easy to walk to lots of attractions. Onsite restaurant expensive but delicious. Has a safe in room.
The -'s: extremely small bathroom, no where to sit things, no extra mirror in outer room which would be extremely helpful. I was bothered by the fact that we had our do not disturb sign on the door and someone came in and made up our bed. We prefer no one in our room during our stays. NO control over heat! It was blazing in our room and the AC unit would only run for seconds at a time. After having to complain twice and waiting an hour and a half before we left again. Same with us asking to get a fan for our room. I would have rated this hotel higher if it wouldn't have been for this lack of service. For the high price we were paying per night I definitely expected better service from maintenance.
This hotel had a deal with Macy's for the parade and we had great grandstand seats.

Nothing that particularly wowed me about the place. The room was nice but not amazing, the service was reasonable, but again nothing that wowed me. The price nothing special. 
I don't feel anyone would be disappointed with the place, but it won't astound you either.

We arrived from Europe with a lot of dirty clothes and asked the desk clerk where we might find a laundromat. She told us we could use the laundry room in the basement and sold us a roll of quarters to use in the machines.
For $8 we washed and dried two loads in less than an hour. The laundry room was a bit grungy and noisy but had chairs and cell phone signal. 
What a nice service, and the staff didn't pressure us to use the hotel's more expensive laundry service!

Selected this hotel as it seemed to offer the best balance between star rating and price. I was worried that the room would be tiny and there would be no windows etc but it was much larger than expected and the bed was fantastic.
The location is great; just a short walk to Empire State, Times Square and 5th Avenue.
The restaurant was better in the evening than for breakfast. At breakfast an 18% gratuity was added to the bill but there still seemed to be an expectation to tip on top of that. This policy wasnt applied at dinner. The hotel provided a good list of local restaurants and all we tried were really good and also good value for money.
All in all I enjoyed my stay and would recommend this hotel.

review_title: A Studio with SPACE in NYC
review_text: Congratulations Affinia for a great stay. Staff with welcoming smiles and willing to go that extra distance to make ones stay that much more comfortable. Rooms with great appointments , good linen on the beds and windows that open 6 inches if you , like me, prefer to go without aircon. Had a studio which even had a view of the river in the middle distance. Utilized the kitchenette as a great deli , Delmonico's, was a couple of blocks away. And the location was superb, a quiet part of Manhattan but close to Grand Central. What more could one want?

review_title: NO FREE WIFI but a really good hotel overall.
review_text: We were on the 10th floor for the first few nights and the street noise at night and construction noise during the day ensured we went without sleep, we complained to the staff and they upgraded our room to penthouse with magnificent veiws and free breakfast for the remainder of our stay. Very nice. No free wifi but there are atleast options that arent too ridiculous price wise. And there is free wifi at Dunkin Donuts downstairs. The location of this hotel is great, right in the thick of the city and right on top of the subway. Staff are very friendly nothing is a problem for them. I highly reccommend this hotel if you can handle the full on bustle of New York.

review_title: Amazing unobstructed views of the beautiful city.
review_text: I booked the standard high floor king room for my husbands 30th and noted it in my reservations. I was prepared to ask the hotel manager if I can get an upgrade, but upon checking in they offered me an upgrade first thing. I went from booking a room on the 9th floor to getting room 195 on the 19th floor. MY jaw dropped when I walked in and saw the view! We had a balcony that just about wrapped the entire lengh of the building. It was amazing, the staff left a birthday card for my husband with red velvet cupcakes and when my husband met me at the hotel, he was surprised. He had no idea I booked a room here much less the amazing room they gave us! We had dinner at co-op and danced the night away at the lounge. There was Not too many pretencious people there which was good and the staff was friendly. I will def stay there again for two days instead of one so that I can enjoy the view of my beautiful city, that is New York. Living in queens, the hotel provides that dream apartment with gorgeous unobstructed views.

review_title: Amazing hotel in NYC that is great value for size and location
review_text:
I stayed at Affinia shelburne with my husband to celebrate his 30th birthday for five nights. 
The easiest way I have found to get to the hotel from the airport is either a shuttle bus or taxi (the shuttle is cheaper but takes twice as long so keep that in mind, and you get to meet other travelers too on the shuttle). The hotel is locates in a great central part of manhattan. As previously I have stayed at Affinia Manhattan which is next to Madison square garden. Also a good hotel which I believe they have just renovated as it was a little tired when I stayed there in October 2009.
Affinia Shelburne is in a great location as it's very Residental. I felt like I was living in NYC not a tourist. 
The staff were very helpful when we mad a request and the room. Well The room was huge for what we had expected in NYC. We had plenty of space for the two of us to spread out things out over the floor and move around comfortably. Also the bathroom was very functional and modern. There was an inroom safe too that was easy to use. 
Housekeeping cam everyday an we were sure to leave a small tip each dy of around 1 or 2 dollars as we were in a basic room and not made of money. Plus we are pretty tidy people. 
We were able to walk pretty much everywhere from here however manhattan is deceptively large. If you are wanting to visit any of the museums I would suggest getting a cab to the desires destination then making your way back on foot. As the best way to see NYC is to get tour walking shoes on and make your way all over the island. 
For those of you whom want to do some serious shopping you might hear people say that the beat shopping is on manhattan and I do wholeheartedly agree however the shops are really spread out over the island. If you want to do shopping all in one place and you at least 6 hours then head out to Woodbury premium shopping outlets over on new jersey. Seriously this place is so amazing. It does take at least a 1 hour bus ride but it is so worth it. One my second trip here we took and empty suitcase. Yes an empty suitcase as the shopping is that amazing. And the bus ride was while it was snowing. I come from
Australia and yes I have seen snow bur actually to be in new York when it's snowing and see new jersey covered in snow was so cool really it was a great sight but freezing. 
Overall when I go back to NYC city again I will definately stay at this hotel. In terms of booking I did this direct on the hotel website and made sure I signed up to affinia's website for any specials.

review_title: Great location but front desk needs improvement!!! Stayed12-17 to 12-19.
review_text:
Great smaller hotel, very big rooms very well equipped, within walking distance to all must see nyc spots!! We had a great time despite the service. 
However, every thing i requested from front desk was met with a NO!! Forget using the 'customize your stay' option on-line because it wont be in your room. ONE bellman only is in charge of locking- securing your luggage so plan to wait!! Of course, frontdesk will tell you they cant help ( dont bother asking)! Pushed my checkin to 3:15(front desk said nothing they could do, sorry charlie)! No bottled water on site so ' you can go to corner store to guy some' again, thanks front desk. 
I travel extensively and can honestly say ive never felt like an interruption to front desk like this. I paid rack rate 399 per night versus using hotwire: guess that made my lack of service even worse. 
By the way, major issues with heating in our room! During three day stay, two visits from maint man. Front room way hot at 80 degrees and bedroom couldnt heat up past 67!! Bring sweaters and flip flops.
The staff is incredibly helpful and kind, their recommendations for dinning were spot-on as well for sites to visit. This is one vacation I will never forget and already planning to come again.

Just returned from affinia manhattan and got to say what a fantastic stay we had. We were watching foo fighters at Madison square garden so location was perfect. It is also a great location for most other major attractions. Staff were always courteous and polite and the room was always clean. Having spent days reviewing various hotels in new York, I am delighted to have chosen the affinia manhattan!!!
We loved our stay here! Great location, great views, and spacious rooms. Highly recommended!

review_title: Fabulous stay at Hotel on Rivington
review_text:
Stayed at this hotel for labour day weekend 2011. My room on the 19th floor provided wonderful views of manhattan skyline. 
The room was relatively clean... Luxurious thick black carpet.... Bathroom was lovely with an amazing shower and the bed was huge and very comfortable.
Most importantly NO SIGNS OF BEDBUGS.....
Breakfast was okay but check out local places too there are plenty to have brunch/lunch or dinner.
Soho is literally down the road.... Turn left out of hotel and just keep walking
Loved it... Loved it ..... Loved it

You would think that a desk would be a standard piece of furniture in a hotel, and not just any hotel, one that charged me $515 a night (that's $590 with taxes). So, if you don't care about a desk, maybe you'd like a room with some light? Oh, sorry, you're also out of luck. The lights are very difficult to figure out, but once you do that, the room is dim at best. With all the lights on, it's lit like a bar. And this is true in the bathroom also. So, really not a big deal if you don't want to put in your contact lenses, or apply makeup. When you walk in off the street, the carpet is dirty. The carpet in the room is black, so good luck finding anything you drop that is also dark. I almost left a shoe there because it blended in with the carpet, and I had a black case that went to my iPad, but I couldn't find it--a combination of the low lighting and black carpet. Next time, I'll bring a flashlight. The hotel is in an area that is still a bit dicey, and it is filthy dirty--it does not look anything like the streets or sidewalks in the nicer areas of town. I'd have prefered to pitch a tent in Central Park.

Stayed in this hotel for 4 nights end of August/early September. The stay was great, we were given a room with 2 beds at no extra charge and the room and beds were huge. We had a view of the empire state building from our room which was great. I would reccomend the rare restaurant, the burgers are delicious. The best part of our stay was the rooftop bar, the views at night time are spectacular and the cocktails lovely. The hotel is only a 5 minute walk from grand central station which is very convenient. From there there is a shuttle straight to times square and you can get to all places easily from there. The hotel staff organised us a car for our journey back which was great and allowed us to enjoy our last day in the city knowing this was arranged. I would not hesitate to return to this hotel when I return to New York and would definitely recommend.

review_title: Very good but they lost my DVF flip flop.
review_text: It was a great hotel, with great location and an overall enjoyable trip. The only problem was the long lines for the elevators in the morning. Additionally one of my flip flops went missing which was brand new.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express New York City Times Square

review_text: A hotel decorated like we are still in the Nineties. Clearing living off past glories. Rooms still have TVs you would not buy off eBay and an AV system that continually broke. Avoid - lots better value in close range.

We stayed 4 nights the last week of August 2011. Our suite was lovely, bed was amazing, views terrific and the floor was very quiet, 9th floor. 24 hour doorman, room service a bit pricey but very good. Local restaurants are delicious, Mikeys and Tinys for vegetarian friendly, many more for sure. Great candy store across the street. This is a happening neighborhood. I will definitely stay here next time I come to the city.

The hotel on rivington is located in the hearth of lower eastside. The rooms are spacious and cleened twice a day. The bathroom is dark and luxurious with a turkish steem bath combined with the shower. A cute gesture is the home made cookies they serve you in the afternoon. The lobby is chick with a pool table.

review_title: Solid hotel but lacks some modern touches.
review_text: Have stayed at the IC New York barclay many times before and just stayed again this week. I always like it - great location, good breakfasts, great service, nice lobby. The rooms are comfortable and perfectly adequate my only main issue is that the hotel could do with some more modern touches to really make it a great hotel. E.g. Having wifi throughout the hotel, having more modern tv in the rooms and generally having a bit of a modernisation of the floors/rooms to bring them from 1998 into 2011.

We stayed here for 4 nights after getting discount tickets online. Our stay was not unpleasant, but at no point at all did I feel like I was in a 4-star hotel. 
The room size was quite decent for NYC (king bed, with some room to move around and use the table). The bathroom was very clean, but crowded.
The service was just lacking the finish you expect of a 4 star hotel. I had to call twice to get a second robe for the room, and every morning to ask what happened to our complimentary paper that was supposed to be at the door. The TVs in the room are OLD. I don't expect a 50inch plasma, but this thing buzzed so loud from its old tubes that you could barely even hear what was on. The elevators were slow, and for half of our stay only one was operational. The other days they had 2/3 working. But in a hotel that size, and staying on the 12th floor, you could expect a long wait and to stop on every floor until it was at capacity.
You definitely feel like you're being squeezed for every penny you've got on the services. For instance, I could have replaced most of my wardrobe for the cost of laundering (not even dry cleaning) it there. But it's not so much a money issue as it is one of feeling pampered, which is what you pay for at a place like this. I'm half surprised there wasn't a coin slot on the toilet.
Overall I don't regret my stay, but I wouldn't have paid a cent over the (deeply discounted) price I paid. It's just not a 4-star experience.

review_title: A wonderful hotel and great value
review_text:
I shouldn't even write a review on this hotel because in doing so more people will want to stay here and it will harder for me to get a room next time I am in NYC. This place is great for business traveler or even when traveling with the family. The rooms are big and very clean. I love the full kitchen. Roof top bar in the spring and summer are awesome with great views of the city. Staff couldn't be more helpful (be sure to say hello to Dennis at the door, he has info on everything)
Super convenient location with just a short walk to the NY Public Library, Grand Central, Bryant Park and the list goes on. 
Do yourself a favor and stay at this hotel. You won't regret it . . . Joe Sloboda

The Affinia Manhattan is an ideal choice for those who are taking the Amtak train which is literally across the road from the hotel. The lobby entrance is grand and the rooms are big and newly renovated. The only disappointment is the small bathroom where one has to squeeze in to get to the sink. As the work on the hotel continues, there was quite a bit of noise although I was probably too tired to notice after a 30 hour journey. Another contributing factor is the street noise which was not surprising for New York city. Macy's is within waking distance from the hotel but the rest of the shopping was not fantastic. While this was close to the train station, it did not feel unsafe during the day time. I will probably choose this hotel again if I needed to take the Amtak train to travel elsewhere.

review_text: Hotel has good location, room very comfortable,bad points breakfast and number of lifts available for the number of rooms.

Within walking distance to empire state, central station, Rockefeller, MoMa. Very helpful front desk staff. Beautiful lounge in the foyer where we could chill out & use the free wifi. Having informed and booked the hotel on the basis it was suitable we were disappointed that there is no access from street for wheelchair user, we had to use a side workers entrance! Restaurant is not accessible as down steps so we were unable to use! We moved rooms three times as first two rooms were not accessible and only had a bath, no roll in shower!.

Fab location! Was upgraded free to a junior suite! Rooms are bug and lush and clean! The bar upstairs on rooftop is stunning at night!

review_title: Great location, we got what we paid for - in a good way!!
review_text:
Stayed here for a week in May with friends; as a fan of tripadvisor I was fully aware of the good and bad with the hotel and have to say it didn't disappoint!
The good: central location meant we walked plenty even though our feet ached at the end of each day! Found some great restaurants nearby, Thai Select just a couple of blocks away on 9th is great and there's a great Italian place also on 9th (cant remember the name) where the staff were very accommodating. The breakfast was a great start to the morning, for all those worried about the elevator queue getting downstairs just take the stairs!! All day tea and coffee was great. Staff were friendly, when we requested more towels the front desk called few mins later to confirm whether they had arrived yet.
The bad: Room is small and it was a bit of a tight squeeze for three of us, particularly after we had done some shopping! Bathroom was clean but little space to put our toiletries, however we worked around this so it was fine. The room was equipped with an iron and hairdryer - however when we contacted the hotel prior to travelling we were told they didn't provide them so ended up taking both with us. On the last day we asked for a set of scales so we could weigh our luggage - lots of shopping im afraid! Initially we were told they were elsewhere and then finally we were told they couldn't find them. It would help if the breakfast items were labelled, some are clearly obvious but for those with specific dietary requirements a few labels would certainly help!
Overall we had a great holiday, this hotel is ideal if like us you want somewhere clean and safe to stay in whilst you explore the city. If you plan on spending a lot of time in the hotel and want the extras then pay more and stay elsewhere otherwise don't complain if you stay here and you get what you paid for!
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express New York City Times Square

review_title: My favorite hotel in NYC. I'm looking forward to re-visit.
review_text: I got an upgrade to a fantastic suite. The service is the best you can get and the overall experience is great!

We spent two nights at the Affinia while on an excursion to New York. The hotel is perfectly situated for those wanting to be near Madison Square Gardens and Times Square. We were given a premium room on the 21st floor (a Travelzoo deal), and it was so attractively designed, very spacious by New York standards, and very modern! Striking black-and -white prints on the wall, toiletries by Philosophy, fluffy white down comforter on a firm mattress, and a choice/ menu of pillow types are the appealing amenities offered. I stayed in three different NYC hotels while on this six-day trip, and this was my favorite. My girlfriend kept exclaiming, " I love this hotel!" I've stayed in many, including other Affinia hotels in NYC, and this ranks right up at the top. I'd definitely stay here again given the right rate.

review_title: Sadly not as good as it used to be!
review_text:
Having previously stayed here in 2005, when the hotel was a great deal newer, my second visit left me feeling a bit sad.
My two biggest moans are that the rooms (we stayed in a corner king both times) have not been touched in those six years. Cracked tiles in the bathroom, even a cracked window pain, and the tv and iPod dock now just seem old. On one of the 4 nights our bathroom wasn't cleaned.
Perhaps more sad is that the bar and restaurant are now almost completely estranged from the hotel. At the prices charged, it feels more like you are staying in a serviced apartment rather than a hotel, which the old Hotel didn't feel like. The new Co-op restaurant is a blatant attempt to entice the local population in, to the detriment of the hotel guests. I think this is a big mistake by the hotel, especially when the rooms are now so tired.
You cannot fault the location, the views and the surrounding bars and restaurants - but Hotel on Rivington have really dropped the ball here, and with hungrier and hipper places springing up nearby, you have to worry for the hotel in it's current guise.
Still good, but need some big investment and to recapture some of the original attention to detail. Overall a bit sad.

review_title: A hotel conveniently situated for business trips. Good service and friendly atmosphere
review_text: The rooms were a little bit old but clean. My family of five and I spent a 4 days in this hotel and we enjoyed our stay a lot although I would have prefered to be a bit closer to the park. One downside to the hotel was the absence of wifi in the rooms.

review_title: Room 701 is the one to avoid!
review_text:
Overall not very impressed with this hotel, room 701 is an accessible room which we were made aware of at the time of booking however it's either haunted or needs a maintenance overhaul! The door bell kept randomly going off at all hours and as the room is accessible this meant the bell was extra large with flashing lights! This woke us at least 4 times during the two night stay. In addition drainage was poor and a short shower would flood the entire bathroom and spill out onto the hall carpet which to avoid meant using the towels at the bathroom door as a barrier! 
Breakfast was very busy both mornings and not enough seating for guests.
Finally beware of the dry cleaning service, I checked a shirt and trousers totalling $16.50 according to the slip in the room, when collecting the cost doubled to $33 and the slip I had completed wad not attached to my cleaning but a totally new one with very different prices! It took a while but I did get the receptionist to agree to amend the bill eventually!
Overall poor hotel but good location.

review_text: Just came back from staying at this hotel and to be honest overall it was really good. As one of the other reviews said,we also experience some noise from traffic, but its nyc!! The hotel was ultra clean,but a little ruff on the edges, such as mastic peeling off in the bathroom and the odd crack in plaster, but nothing that would stop this fussy londoner staying again.the rooms are nicely decorated with lovely big beds,and staff were helpful. We did change our room as we were given a single and had booked a double suite, this was arranged the next day. Niles restaurant is well worth a visit and is next door,the food was out of this world amazing! !!
Good value. Excellent location. Staff were courteous. The restaurant was quite good with excellent selection. Very near Penn station for travelers.

After years of longing to vist NYC, my girlfriend and I finally went there last week and I must say the hotel was absolutely fantastic. It is in a very good location to lots of places, Grand Central, Empire State building and lots of really good dinners cafe's and restaurants.
The room was very spacious and very modern looking and had all the amenities you would expect. 
The cleaners did a fantastic job everyday also.
The staff at the desk were all very helpful and always greeted us with a smile and went out of their way to help us. One guy at the desk (sorry I can't remember his name) recommended us a few good steakhouses round the area and also said that one, Angelo and Maxie's was his favourite so we went there and had the best meal o the holiday. We're very thankful to him for that.
Also the man who calls your taxis and open the front door was extremely friendly and adde to the whole great hotel experience.
To sum it up, this hotel is perfect for anybody visiting Manhattan and I'd recommend it to anyone and would love to go back again.

review_title: Fantastic hotel in a excellent location!!
review_text:
I have stayed here twice on both my trips to New York and is a fantastic hotel.
The rooms are really spacious, clean and even had a little kitchenette which is such a little bonus for hotels in New York!!
Hotel is in a lovely location across from Maddison square gardens and only a 5 min walk to times square which is perfect cos only a short walk to the husstle and bustle but yet far enough away where you can sleep at night!!
I would highly recommend staying at this hotel and will deff be staying here again when I visit the big apple.

review_title: Not worth your money or time.
review_text: Rooms are small and uncomfortable. Noisy and slow elevators. Room we had wasnt cleanest for sure. Consider somewhere else if you are paying full price.

review_text: I stayed at this hotel for 3days in Oct 2010 with my husband and 1 year old son. I feel unbelievably ripped off by this hotel and I strongly recommend avoiding the Affinia Manhattan. I booked a suite on Expedia, and paid in advance. When I arrived I was told there were no suites, only rooms. I was offered a free breakfast or internet connection as consolation. (Do you really think a free coffee and egg makes up for not having a suite with a kitchen??)
However, it was late at night and I was tired so I said fine. When I got to my room, my jaw dropped. The door opened to a long dark (and yes, creepy) hallway. I walked in, bumping my bags on the walls. At the end of the hallway was a room roughly the size of a walk in closet. Now I have stayed in NYC a lot and am familiar with the size of rooms in this city. This room was exceptionally tiny. ALSO, it gives the feel of a tenement, or family shelter. The carpet is ugly and worn, the paint is chipped, the curtains were a dingy grey, not the white they were originally. Over the window was a fabric valance covered with visible dust and dust bunnies. In the window was an ac unit covered in a dusty cloth. The window, however, was wedged open at an angle and looked broken. And when I tried to close it I found it was, because it wouldn't close. Yes, that is right. The window was stuck open. 
The wood furniture was chipped and looked like it was from a thrift shop. The chair was a metal framed stacking chair with a dingy cushion, the lampshade was white with brown stains.
I could clearly hear my neighbors talking. And urinating.
I won't go on. Yes the ladies at the desk are friendly but that does not make up for how robbed I feel. They took my money for a suite and gave me a tenement room, with a "free" coffee and egg.
For that, I ask. Affinia, are you serious?

Rooms were very good and having stayed in many New York hotels over the years they are above average in size (well certainly the one I stayed in was). The beds have a comfort control system which allows you to select the firmness of your mattress - a nice quirky touch! The adjoining bar/restaurant was also very good with friendly staff and a good selection of drinks to choose from. My one and only real major problem with the hotel was its elevators. They have to be the slowest elevators I have ever, and I really do mean EVER, come across. My friend and I were on the top floor (6th floor) and we literally got to the point where if we were meeting our friends (who were on the 2nd floor) at a certain time in the lobby we would leave the room 10mins early to allow for travelling time! On one occasion we decided to go down the stairs and made it down to the lobby quicker (although a little dizzier) than the people from our floor that were waiting for the elevator! Other than that though it's a very good hotel to stay in and I would certainly consider doing so again.

I have to admit that this was originally not my top choice for our trip to NYC. I am used to staying in some very high end luxury hotels and was only talked into this one by my husband who did not want to spend exorbitant NYC prices since we were not spending much time in the room. After multiple fights on the issue, I finally gave in and agreed to stay in the HGI. 
While not luxury by any stretch, the HGI was a surprisingly good experience. The staff was very helpful and seemed like they wanted to assist guests in any way possible. They accommodated my request to be in a quiet location as I am a very light sleeper. The room was clean (and I am a stickler on this issue) and the bed was comfortable. The most surprising thing is that there really isn't anything bad I can say about the place. 
Bottom line is that the HGI made the weekend comfortable. Don't expect luxury coming in but you can expect good value for your money given what you usually get in NYC. Overall, I would recommend the hotel if you are coming to NYC and just want an easy no frills type of place. 
Damn, I hate when my husband is right.

review_title: Great hotel - great location - great price!
review_text:
I had a great stay at the HGI TriBeCa! Close to everyplace I wanted to go: we were able to walk to Soho shopping, Little Italy dining, Asian reflexology in Chinatown, and several train lines A-C-E right across the street and several others just a few blocks away (N, R, 1 & 2) TriBeCa itself had some cool cafe's and restaurants but We had to leave before I tried them.
We arrived on Sunday so we were able to park about 20 yards from the front entrance until the next day for free, though I believe valet parking is available.
We also had our bikes and were able to Ride the bike path down the west side of manhattan all the way to battery park. The bike path runs just a few blocks west of the hotel. We also were able to stop at ground zero about halfway to battery park.
The only negative with the location is the proximity to Canal st which is a nightmare, walking, driving, or biking. Wall to wall people day and night, so we went around it as often as possible, though it's hard to do with it being the nearest cross street.
The staff was friendly and helpful, and let us check in early. The hotel was very modern, clean and new feeling. There was a 'mini-bar' type set-up available in the lobby where you could save yourself a trip to the store for basic snacks and beverages. I think it makes up for not having a mini bar in the room which is expensive anyway. The items get charged to your room.
There was a Mexican restaurant on site but we never made it to that either. 
I felt safe in the hotel and neighborhood. Even at night. There was a fitness center and business center but I didn't have the need for either. I was there for less than 24 hrs, but would absolutely stay again for a similar deal ($199+).
Overall a great stay, in a great hotel. This is not the ritz, but great accommodation and service if you do not require the luxuries of a 5-star.

The windows in the Indigo must be made of extra thick glass - I didn't hear a peep. But what was a bit noisy was the AC - so I turned on the virtually silent fan instead and slept without the comforter, which was fine.

review_title: Very comfortable, excellent service, great location
review_text:
Once we were settled in, roughly 24 hours after our confirmed reservation, and 16 hours after we arrived at the hotel, we enjoyed our stay. I am not a frequent traveler but I know that hotels, like airlines, "overbook". 
It is not fun to be the family bumped out of a confirmed reservation, particularly when you have made the effort to call the front desk directly to advise the staff that you would be arriving very late. Alas, we were that family. 
We arrived after midnight to find that there were no rooms available. The Westin offered alternate accommodations and generous compensation and did so even before we asked.
Other travelers can decide whether I am being too kind, but I will only deduct one star for this inconvenience. Really folks, the Westin is a lovely hotel, with good sized rooms, an excellent location, good service, and all the amenities you expect from a hotel of its class.
In the end, althougth we were inconvenienced the first night, we were overall very happy with our stay.
Hotels should not overbook, but they all do it, and we all know that they do. You can tell a good hotel from a bad by the way this is handled; the Westin handled this extremely well.
hotel_name: The Westin New York at Times Square

review_title: A great hotel on a budget
review_text: Having researched budget hotels to death we took a chance on this one. Trying to find a hotel in any city that is cool, local, a decent size but within budget is hard for any city let alone New York but the Indigo met all these criteria. We got a great deal online (less than Â£100 per night per room) yet were still upgraded to a larger king. The room was a good size with a huge bed (probably one of the comfiest hotel beds I have slept on) yet still room for a chair, 2 bedside tables, a huge decent LCD TV and a dressing table. Smallish shower room but clean with a walk in shower (yes the water gets over the floor but the bath mat helps!). Some nice touches (other than the bottle of fizz left for my birthday by the staff) were the Aveda products (shower gel would be nice though) and the great coffee machine in the room. We did not have a view but when you are in New York there is always a view from somewhere (here it's the cool hotel glass bar). The heating is noisy but even in January when it was -7 we didn't need it on for long. The staff were truly friendly especially Sam on the front desk and Mohammed the doorman. The free comedy show in the bar on Thursday night (6th Jan) was surprisingly good. The location is central and although not a picturesque area like central park or 5th Avenue it was very handy for walking/running and for the subway. We took the train from JFK (air train via Jamaica beach then train to Penn station) which cost about $17 each then it was less than a 10 min walk from Penn to the hotel. We walked to Times Square, the Rockerfeller centre, central park, TriBeCa and even ran to Battery Park from the hotel. The bar drinks are a little expensive but so is New York generally and the fitness suite is tiny but adequate. Whilst this hotel is a hotel intercontinental it feels like a boutique hotel because of the friendliness of the staff and the little touches (including a docking station in the room for iPods). I would definitely stay here again on a trip to New York (for the right price!)
