The quality of the room was great, the only issue was when we booked we were assured the price was for four people not two. Once the confirmation was received we noticed it only said two guests. When we called back they said the price would be an outrageous amount higher with two more people. After some long phone calls with various hotel personnel we did get the price we locked it when we booked since the service rep did say it was for four. If booking directly through the hotel just double check your requests. Overall great place to stay!
hotel_name: The Westin New York at Times Square

review_text: The sheets were disgusting and the service was terrible.
hotel_name: The Westin New York at Times Square

review_title: Decent trendy place not so good service
review_text:
Location is nice and the hotel has a nice design. The rooms were ok after staying in two different ones. One room the bathroom light didn't work and the other the tv didn't switch away from the initial channel. The room with no street view is much quieter.
The service here was really an extreme. Some were nice and courteous, but several were downright rude. Two @ the front desk and one waitress. The waitress in particular was terrible and non apologetic. The manager had to apologize for her. This was the first time i have ever walked out before being served. Front desk people two in particular were rude. It just wasn't a very professional feeling. I would not stay there even if offered a free room. Good luck fellow travelers!

Ilike the Ace for what it stands for, but it is just not my cup of tea. It seemed like a space for youngsters to transition into adulthood. 
Decorated in hipster nostalgia, the space seemed a cross between a prison and college dormitory. As cool as it wanted to be, I just wasn't feeling it. Dark, small, cramped rooms.
A few pros: great staff, great location, cool energetic lobby, great restaurants, excellent wifi and Internet services, cool concept in theory
Cons: dark gray floor halls (prison-like, disturbing), dorm-like accommodations (I didn't even like dorm rooms when I had to live in one), large sized toiletries which are meant to be shared from guest to guest (big no for me, I didn't touch those things), scratchy wool blanket.
Wouldn't knock it for the many others who love the Ace, just not my cup of tea.

review_title: Great big room, great location, good value.
review_text: Stayed here 10 days ago and got a great room (thanks to an upgrade i have to say), which was big for New York standards, had a sunset view, and was high up to avoid any noise from the streets. The room was modern, had the famous great Westin bed and was a pleasure to come back to in the evenings. Hotel location is great: in the middle of Manhattan, at a corner where you can get taxis easily or have a choice of subway lines close by, and you are within walking distance to many great restaurants. A bit in a busy tourist area but to be expected around times square. The only negative point is that WiFi for 24h costs $15, which i think is ridiculous.
hotel_name: The Westin New York at Times Square

review_title: for fashion victims that don't understand value or quality and are prepared to pay through the nose for comparative rubbish
review_text: seriously, I don't get all the good reviews. Judging by the amount of time the staff seem to be surfing the net, i would't be surprised if they hadnt written a number of the reviews. The rooms are overpriced, and way below the standard and quality of a typical room for NYC. In one way it's clever; you made your concept an industrial/utilitarian theme, and fill it with minimalist furniture and attach funky labels to the odd thing, and therein lies the beauty, but it's cheap rubbish all dressed up as part of the concept, and it doesn't work. And you pay for it. The rooms are cold and uninviting. Harsh clinical which walls interspersed with pages of books stuck on the wall to create a look, but they have yellowed with time, and just look odd. I had a bunk room, which had a piece of cheap wood placed under it as an afterthough to firm it up. The room was close to 300 dollars (their smallest room), but had no space to sit or relax, and you couldn't sit on the bed without hunching over, which just left sitting on the floor. The A/C doesn't really work, which means you leaving the windows open all the time, and the furniture looks more like it was stolen from some college dorm than be though through. Seriously, if the furniture in the room cost more than 100 bucks, you can call me susan. Note that all the 'bunk' rooms are right next to lifts on every floor, and the room doors have huge gaps underneath them, so expect aural excitement for as long as people keep returning during the night. I woke constantly. I even asked them to move us, but all such rooms were by the lift. The rooms, are cheap with harsh colours and bare bulbs, and the bathrooms look like they used to be college dorm rooms. Theyre not dressed to look like that. The cracks in the floor tiles (room 400) make it seem like they actually were. So, you charge 3.50 for a bottle of water, put a funky sign on a bathroom wall, and tell people if they take the, frankly awfully tacky bathroom robes, they'll be charged 150 bucks for the priviledge. And that to me, is this hotel in a nutshell, it's tat dressed up as funky because they think you're too stupid and unwise to know better. From the 100 dollar 'retro' polaroid camera that youre invited to keep, to the art project youre invited to take pictures in, but then you pay 25 dollars for the priviledge of using the black and white film provided. Seriously. You are so much smarter than this. Stay in a decent hotel, warm hotel with warm comfy rooms, ni stale air, with a/c that works and have a good time in new york. You worked hard for your vacation time. You need to go somewhere where you can relax and enjoy it.

Wow. If David Bowie and Mazzy Star had a baby and it was a hotel, the Ace would be it. Retro meets mod, with small but spacious rooms, terrific amenities and a ton of style. Great lounge and restaurants down stairs and NYC at your fingertips, for way reasonable prices. Book it, chief :)

review_title: Overrated, noisy facing broadway and loud music
review_text: The ace hotel is the place to be for hanging out for hipsters and .com people. Lobby is chill and coffee at Stumptown is a treat, as well as Breslin restaurant but the location sucks. We complained about the noise and when we were there, the water pipes burst due to someone accidentally doing something. They did not tell us and I was stuck without a clean shower. To top it off they did not refund us. Seriously??? All a hotel should offer is a clean bed and hot shower. If that can't be provided we shouldn't pay. Even landlords in NY have to provide hot water! The management did nothing until I wrote a scathing review on yelp.
Nice place to stay and the location is great. Little things like internet and using the business center are extra though.
hotel_name: The Westin New York at Times Square

review_text:
Vous me direz, c'est pour cela que l'on choisit un Hotel. Et bien si ce n'est que pour cela, a choisir sans hÃ©sitation!
Pour le reste, l'hÃ´tel est un peu Ã©trique sur la 28th pour prÃ©tendre offrir les services d'un Hotel de catÃ©gorie supÃ©rieure.
Une note un peu moyenne au personnel de l'hÃ´tel, pas forcÃ©ment aux petits soins.
hotel_name: Hotel Indigo New York City, Chelsea

review_title: Enduring the hurricane in the lap of luxury
review_text:
I ended up staying in the westin while Irene was around new York, and was pleasantly surprised that only a little bit of food service was disrupted, otherwise the hotel was operating 100%.
What can you say about this hotel? Well everyone knows that Westin is known for its beds and showers, but I really appreciated the little touches, such as complimentary umbrellas for guests use. 
The room was spacious and comfortable, with the centerpiece being that king size heavenly bed (which i am considering buying after my stay).
The staff is top notch, and are more than friendly. 
Overall, I would recommend this hotel to anyone, with one exception... There is a halfway house or something across the street, with some interesting characters that come out. You really only bump into these people if you go out for a smoke, so keep that in mind. I know from working in the area that there isn't much the hotel can do to stop these people from bothering its guests, so I'm not knocking the hotel for it in ANY way, but it is good to know.
hotel_name: The Westin New York at Times Square

review_title: Puzza di pesce crudo appena usciti
review_text: L'hotel e'ben servito dalla metro,a me han dato una camera con due tv al plasma e un bagno molto grande, ma non c'Ã¨ nulla x la colazione salata e neppure yogurt; la pecca piÃ¹ grande e'che trovandosi a chinatown appena usciti dall'hotel si e'investiti da uno sgradevole e vomitevole odore di pesce venduto dai cinesi su banchetti scoperti

review_title: Groovy place to stay and eat
review_text: Loved the unique rock vibe. Definitely not stuffy or pretentious. Friendly staff, unique rooms. Amazing coffee! Great location for meeting friends for drinks and dinner!

We stayed here for four nights during 
Easter weekend. We are very satisfied with the hotel. The location was excellent. within walking distance to the theaters and a lot of restaurants. We had a great room on the 44th floor. Great view and no bed bugs!!!!! The concierge was very helpful and friendly. The only complain is the wifi is not free. It should be free at the lobby. We got free wifi at Starbucks across the street. I would stay here again.
hotel_name: The Westin New York at Times Square

review_text:
We recently stayed at Ace and took advantage of the "cheap" room rates, not really sure what to expect. My husband and I were impressed with everything the room and hotel had to offer! The room was always clean, the bed was very comfy and they even provided us with a free laptop to surf the web with during our stay. Although the room was small, we expected that, and we had a great view of the Empire state building!
We loved Stumptown coffee downstairs and enjoyed our daily morning visits. The lobby bar is really cool, and we never heard any noise from it or anywhere else in the hotel.
We would definitely come back to stay here or visit another Ace location
This is not a chain hotel or upscale place, but the location and size of the rooms makes it worth it. It was older but clean. Great choice

Good location, worst smallest bathroom of all time. Sinks looked like prison sinks. Felt like I was under assault. Last day we were there, I fell in the shower trying to get out of the way of the water and thought I broke my toe!! Hobbled all over the city that day. Just ligament damage!!! UGH never again just based on the bathroom. Room was typical NYC size and clean. Bed was nice. Doormen were great.
hotel_name: The Westin New York at Times Square

review_title: Embodies the best of New York
review_text: My wife and I stayed at the Westin Times Square in early August. As an SPG member, we were upgraded to a Deluxe room on the 44th floor with a view of the entire skyline and the Empire State Building as its most magnificent spire. We hadn't told the clerk that it was my wife's birthday so was a sort of last minute surprise. As it was our first trip to NY, we didn't actually get to spend much time there but it's strategic location made it a welcome respite from the madness that is Times Square. We'd highly recommend this hotel to anyone visiting NY.
hotel_name: The Westin New York at Times Square

review_text: Great location that is within walking distance to Times Square, Fifth Ave shopping & Central Park. Staff is outstanding! Room decor is a bit outdated but very spacious rooms for New York City.

My family enjoyed our stay at the Salisbury. The rooms were a bit old and in need of some renovations but the location could not have been more perfect. We were in town for the Macy's Parade and could not have lucked out for the location and price. We got a fabulous deal on Expedia and had a fabulous vacation with the Salisbury serving as a more than suitable home base.

Our recent stay for 6 days in December exceeded our expectations. We were a family of 5 in a suite for 3 days and of 3 in a single room with 2 double beds for 3 days. Rooms were large and clean. The location is excellent for walking or subway travel. The staff was helpful and friendly. There is a little store that is 4 doors away and has inexpensive breakfasts and lunches. It is very convenient. I gladly recommend this hotel

My husband and I stayed for one night (8/5) and had a fantastic experience. I read some of the negative comments/complaints and I would like to encourage readers considering this hotel not to hesitate. Our experience was flawless. We were treated with the utmost respect and courtesy from the front door to room service. We booked our room through priceline and got a phenomenal deal! When we checked in, the clerk upgraded us to a deluxe corner suite with panoramic views of times square on the 33rd floor. We paid a fraction of the retail price of a standard room and ended up staying in what proved to be one of the finest rooms of all our travels. They even gave us free access to their health club and we have no membership affiliations. Needless to say, we were thoroughly impressed. Please understand that the negative reviews/comments are isolated occurrences and book your stay! You will not be disappointed.
hotel_name: The Westin New York at Times Square

review_text: We have stayed here 3 times over the past 8 years. Always clean & always a smile from all the staff. Food is a bit costly in the hotel but quality is top notch. Located in the middle of theatre land.
hotel_name: The Westin New York at Times Square

review_title: You think it's all about location?
review_text:
To be honest Times Square is the last place you want to stay when visiting New York, next time I'll stay just out side. To say it's inflated is an understatement. 
Westin, not cheap, nice looking hotel (in the pictures, who ever took the picture photoshopped the life out of it as the place is surrounded in buildings, view = 0, but it's manhattan the moat vertical city I have ever been to. 
Back to the hotel, location fantastic in the morning around 7am, no one about, after mid day nightmare. Piles of rubbish outside which never seems to go. Staff terrible, our welcome was a 'Give me your credit card in case you break something, after we found out the hitel had blocked the whole card!!! I went nuts, it took several hours to transfer money from one card to another just so we could buy something. Not a good start. 
Room was more like a YMCA room, food was bad and drinks expensive and time consuming to actually get one. 
All in all not a good experience for a supposed 'special 5 days trip' for the wife and me.
hotel_name: The Westin New York at Times Square

review_text: First time at a fairfield inn.What a great hotel. I have stayed in 5 star world class luxury hotels all over the world and the service at this fairfield inn was equal to or superior to those! Perfect location in the flower district close to union square and the village area. The rooms are small but then again so are most NYC rooms. Rooms are very clean front staff could not have been more accommodating. My only "complaint" would be a softer bed. I would highly recommend.
hotel_name: Fairfield Inn & Suites New York Manhattan/Chelsea

review_text: My husband and I stayed here on our honeymoon in New York. Our room was clean, comfortable and had a fantastic view. The staff were really helpful and all our needs were met, including providing umbrellas when it rained. It was a peaceful haven from the noise and bustle of Times Square.
hotel_name: The Westin New York at Times Square

review_title: I'm not hip enough for this hotel
review_text:
Wanted to like this place and got a good last minute rate here, but would not have been happy if I had paid regular prices. I have most of the same complaints, lobby crowded with hipsters, no room for guests. Front desk staff like a Junior Achievement project, no greeting, most responses were "yeah" or "cool". Wish I had brought my skateboard.
Room awkwardly laid out, strangest shower control I've seen in 30 years of travel, commode jammed in a corner, almost no to left there and no spare roll, shower curtain leaves a big wet mess. Room service prices were astronomical.
Went to brekkie at restaurant, took more than 30 minutes to get a grilled cheese when the place was empty. Staff wander around looking hungover. When food finally arrived they all swarmed and wanted to know how it looked. Hilarious, I wasn't there to look at it (greasy gut bomb by the way). Can't believe they have a Michellin star.
Overall professional prices with amateur service. Also, good luck finding their checkin desk, it looks like a shoe repair shop.
Excellent treatment platinum club room was awesome. Rooms clean great location. Would stay again
hotel_name: The Westin New York at Times Square

review_title: Good hotel in a good location
review_text: Stayed four nights across two rooms. Hotel busy throughout but service never an issue. Bar good. Restaurant average. Wifi a bit hit and miss. Good location, friendly and helpful staff. Rooms: corner one on 44th floor good size and great views. Other one (not corner) a bit smaller but fine with good views.
hotel_name: The Westin New York at Times Square

review_title: Can be a good option in Manhatan.
review_text:
Positive aspects:
1) Location,close to Central Park.
2) Room and bathroom sizes.
3) Cleanability.
4) Breakfast,good value:Usd 9.00 per person,despite wrong information.
5) Close to several restaurants and stores.
Negative aspects:
1) Old construction,but in good condition.
2) Terrible staf,rude,unpolite.
3) Very expensive,but is NY.
4) Charged internet in room: Usd 10.00/ day.
5) Some days before my arrival I ask them regarding breakfast price,they told me Usd 6.00 but it is Usd 9.00 in fact.

The beds are amazing. The location for a tourist is first class. It's clean and the staff are helpful. I went with my wife and two teenagers and enjoyed saying here. Just two things to watch out for are the minibar which for a can of coke costs around $8 (Â£5/6) and there is no price list in the room. The other thing is excursions booked through the concierge desk. The key point here is that they are a third party outsourced service not directly linked to the hotel. So if something goes wrong, the hotel cannot directly instruct them or refund moneys, etc. We booked two family tickets to the Harry Potter and Pompeii exhibitions on Times Square and was told they were discounted because the hotel was running a promotion. Turns out they were $80 more expensive than the door price and made getting a refund very difficult and were very rude. Use the concierge only for a good recommend (Westway Diner was great for breakfast with the locals), just don't part with any money.
hotel_name: The Westin New York at Times Square

review_text: Mancanza di connessione WI FI ad internet.Bagni scomodissimi.Prezzi eccessivi negli extra.Carenza di accessori in camera ( pantofole, spazzola etc. )Camere senza doppi vetri e molto rumorose. Hall grande ma poco ricettiva. Prima colazione inclusa cara ma buona e abbastanza ricca. Personale gentile ed efficiente.

The Ace is more about hobnobbing with your hipster brethren than a hotel stay experience. Tiny rooms are still pleasant and functional. Bathroom is minuscule with huge showerhead requiring you stand an inch away from the soap dispenser. 
Still, the lobby, the corridors, the bar, the restaurant - all fun. Location is cool as well. Staff is attentive and committed to the overall experience. 
Aim for rooms on as high a floor as possible. 3AM garbage collection outside felt intimately close from the 7th floor.

review_title: The Salisbury is not new but very comfortable, clean & ideally located.
review_text:
We stayed in a junior suite and compared to what we had heard about NY hotels were very pleased with this hotel. The room was large with separate living area and kitchen.
The hotel had old world charm and is only 2 blocks from Central Park and a short walk to the Times Square precinct.
We had a great stay & would stay here again.

Just like many prior reviews stated, it is a modern hotel in a terrific location. We had the AAA with breakfast promotion and thus made for a great deal. The room was in a corner on a higher floor.

review_text: Used our points at this hotel. Front desk staff was super friendly and informative (needed help shopping). Everyday I went downstairs, they recognized me and said hello. Rooms are NY size small but clean and modern. Right in between the subway lines= awesome location!
hotel_name: Fairfield Inn & Suites New York Manhattan/Chelsea

review_text: Stayed with husband mother in law and toddler in a 2 room suite which turned out to be huge and perfect for our needs. Hotel is a block down from central park, 5th avenue shops, FAO schwartz etc so location is excellent. Accessible by subway. Couldn't fault it! Not luxurious but very good overall

I had a surprise I was updated to a pent house st. It was very clean and large. Front desk leafy was very helpful, and welcoming. Location 1 min walk to timesq 
Will go there again 
Very funky decore

Great location. Quiet clean rooms. Would have given this an excellent rating if it wasn't for the poor advice we got from the conciergie who told us it would take 45 min to get to JFK airport in the rain. It took almost twice as long, we missed our flight and had a 7h wait at the airport. Not happy!

Just checked out this morning from this lovely little hotel. Firstly thank you to Patrick who was just brilliant on the desk. 
Lots of reviews on here talk about the rooms being dark, I expected to have to walk around with a miners helmet on!!! Not at all, yes it's not the brightest of rooms but in no way was it a hindrance! No problem at all getting my make up on as some people have complained about!
The bed was the most comfortable I have ever slept in!
The robe was superb to use after having a lovely shower. 
The position of the hotel on Times Square was perfect. 
The only downside was the noise level on Saturday night. Was told music would end about 1 but actually it got louder and went on til about half 2! But still it was only
One night. 
Just like to thank everyone at Night Hotel for making our first trip to New York a great one. Would defiantly stay here again.

review_title: Party All Night Sleep All Day Package is a winner!
review_text:
Great hotel! Romantic setting where everything is black and white and dimly lit. One block from all the theaters, restaurant row, times square.. Short walk to rockerfeller center and tons of shopping.. Bryant Park is also in walking distance. 
We booked the party all night package because the 3pm check-out was intriguing. We got in at 12pm and check in was at 3pm. They had our room available..we were upgraded to the PENTHOUSE!!!! We had a balcony with lounge chairs and a decent size room with dressing area and large bathroom. The bed was amazing, down featherbed, perfect down pillows! 
I gave it an overall 4 because there was a downside. The walls are thin and our neighbors were obnoxious so we heard way too much when they came in at 3am. Also the shower is odd. There is a drain in the center of the bathroom and no separation between the shower and the main part of the bathroom...so when you take a shower EVERYTHING on the floor gets soaked! You can't blow dry your hair in there because it is hazardous! The restaurant/bar area is very nice, but completely dead.. Our package came with a $50 bar credit so we felt compelled to have a couple drinks.
We went for our anniversary and they sent a bottle of champagne up! The staff was incredible! Everyone from the front desk to the doorman, to the maids to the bartender They were very accommodating and sweet!

Excellent hotel! I absolutely recommend this to everyone. The staff is extremely friendly and eager to help - I needed to locate a sprint store and the gentleman at the front desk looked up the location, called them to verify, and wrote me directions, even said if I got lost or couldn't find it to call him and he would te ll me how to find my way from where I was at :) one employee gave us parking tips during the weekend and week so we wouldn't get ripped off while we were out and about. They have a smoking area which is nice, I thought it was just an included room like in the airports at first but you look up and you can see the buildings and the sky and lights so there's no actual roof-its really neat. Room and hotel is super clean. Rooms are small and a wee bit overpriced but that's new york for ya - I'm from cleveland, ohio and used to paying between $50-$70 for a room that's 4x's the size of theirs'. Overall this place is awesome and I will be staying here again when I come back for an adventure to the city.

We hebben hier vier nachten geslapen. Schone kamer, mooie entourage, locatie is top en personeel is erg behulpzaam. Maar goed dat mag je voor dit geld ook wel verwachten. Al met al heerlijke dagen gehad.

Excellent costumer service.. The front desk people were amazing at helping out, but the only problem was that they didn't clean our room :/ besides that it was awesome! The whole night/gothic theme was super cool

review_title: Location great, room great - just don't order room service!!!!
review_text:
So we arrived in NYC for the 1st stint of our honeymoon, we were welcomed by a larger than life New Yorker who was lovely. He gave us an upgrade as we were a honeymoon couple. The room was great, a corner room with views of the hudson, also very spacious by NY standards. 
All was going well, we made a coffee in the room but only had that creamer and wanted some milk so I called room service and ordered a little cup of cold milk for our coffee. When it arrived I had to sign the delivery slip, my mouth dropped, $11 + tax....for milk. We're not tight people but that takes the biscuit. 
The concierge is poor, we asked for fine dining recommendations and he suggested and booked us into a Japanese resturant. Without boring you with the details, it wasn't what we were looking for and ended up standing on the street scrolling through trip advisor to get a fine dining restaurant. 
This was a small thing but annoying that he clearly didn't listen to our requirements. 
Couldnt beat the location, was perfect.
hotel_name: The Westin New York at Times Square

review_text: Fantastic location, 2 streets from central park, a 10-15 walk to Times Square/Rockefella Centre and bang in the middle of two subway lines serving lower Manhatten. Rooms are spacious and well equipt and service was great. For the price you can't ask for more.

Ci siamo fermati 8 giorni, in camera doppia.
Bell'hotel: camere ampie, pulite, con bagno spazioso, in marmo, dotato di vasca e doccia separate. Molti accessori in dotazione in camera.
Personale cortese, forse un po' invadente: continuano a bussare alla camera per chiedere se serve qualcosa.
La mattina giornali gratuiti a disposizione degli ospiti.
Ottima posizione centrale a Manhattan. Ben servito dalla metropolitana.
Unica pecca, che ritengo non trascurabile: il wifi a pagamento. Personalmente trovo questa soluzione in un hotel di questa categoria, francamente inaccettabile. We stayed at the Westin for a week as we were getting married in New York as part of out holiday. Our room was on 22nd floor with a view of the edge of Times Square. The room itself was a good size, well equipped and clean with a free safety deposit box. We advised the hotel we were returning visitors and getting married during our stay. We didn't ask for freebies however some recognition of our happy event would have been much appreciated. It cost $20 to press my dress which was a bit pricy. The bathroom door was also a sliding door which if we weren't a couple may have caused some discomfort as it didn't close properly. The mini bar was also a bit pricy too. We didn't eat in the hotel but there was the bar and shulas steakhouse which did have a good reputation. 
Times square was seconds walk away as was a subway station and cabs could be hailed anywhere. There are plenty of bars, restaurants, shops and takeaways extremely close by. 
We had an amazing time in New York and would stay at the Westin again but more down to location and facilities than the service.

review_text: Rooms are small but it is spotlessly clean, the service is exceptional, and the location is unbelievable.

Close to Central Park, Broadway Theatres and Times Square this hotel did not disappoint. Helpful staff do well with a product which is looking tired. Only disappointment was breakfast, following the latest trend of disposable crockery and plastic cutlery. Much nicer to eat out.
Amazing place, fantastic location and awesome staff. Well worth a visit.

review_title: Great location, but expensive for what it is.
review_text: Booked based on other reviews. The location is hard to beat. Admitted, I have not stayed in nyc for a few years now, but it seemed very expensive for a very basic hotel. Clean and quiet, yes. Excellent location. Would shop around a little more next time for a better rate somewhere nearby.

Although one pays almost a grand per night for a standard room, one recieves the treatment of a second class citizen in an occupied land. The HVAC system is so old--you'd swear you were in an airplane rather than a 5 star hotel. A call to room service leaves one feeling verbally abused--yikes!

review_text:
Don't be fooled by it's modest frontage. This little gem will he my families preferred destination while in NYC. Minutes from Central Park, subway, and Carnige Hall, this hotel is in a great location. My wife felt completely safe walking from Fifth Ave to the Sailsbury on her own. 
We had a suite which broke all stereotypes regarding room sizes in NYC: IT WAS HUGE! 
I must admit my biggest fear with traveling to NYC was bed bugs, and I was quite pleased with the cleanliness of the Hotel. 
Part of me wants to keep the Sailsbury all to myself, but that would be doing a disservice to all the hard working and friendly staff who work hard to separate themselves from the larger big box hotels.

review_title: Nice touches at this boutique hotel.
review_text: Stayed in November with partner and friends. Room was very small but expected. Bedding, amenities, and toiletries all very nice. Great view of Empire State Building from our window. review_text:
As we were four adults, we had a spacious room - bedroom, dining with kitchenette and large lounge unfortunately it was serviced for only three.
The room was old and tired and could do with a makeover. The two double beds were uncomfortably hard which took time to get used to. If you were using the hairdryer you couldn't use any other appliance in the room or it would short circuit and it would be lights out!
The staff were very good and friendly but those behind the reception desk made us feel we were an imposition. Watch any accounts put under your door as we got one on the last morning for laundry etc that wasn't ours! When queried, reception didn't quite believe us!
All in all it was okay, a bed after a long day, but it really comes down to the location - close to everything!

All I can say about this hotel is that the location is amazing! Right near centeral park, times square and a 5/10 min walk to 5th avenue!! Our room was huge, think it was a family room but lots of room. Decoration quite dated but clean! One minor irratation was that every time we got the lift we had to wait at least 5/10 mins!! Overall would definately come back

As a first-time visitor to New York, I was overwhelmed by the logistics of a safe yet affordable vacation in New York City. The Salisbury Hotel exceeded all of our needs! Our room was clean, the staff was prompt, friendly, and professional making us feel valued and important. The location was perfect! It was easy to access the subway, Times Square, and Central Park. The parking was only a block away and our voucher made it affordable. We will book our next New York stay at The Salisbury!

A package arrived after I checked out and Kevin, concierge, was kind enough to contact me and offered to send it on. This kind of service from all of the staff is to be commended.

review_text:
My girlfriend and I (or I should mow say FiancÃ© as we got engages out in New York) stayed at The Salisbury for 5 nights this past week. 
Upon arriving at the hotel we were checked in very quickly and shown to our room. The hotel itself as others have said is on the old side, but it's very quaint. 
Having never stayed in New York before we didn't know what to expect for a standard NY room, but the rooms here were huge for a standard room! 2 double beds, 2 large wardrobes, air con, flat screen TV and a kitchenette area and a decent sized bathroom. The best thing about the hotel is the location!! Central to everything. 5 minute walk to Central Park and 5th Avenue, 10 minutes to Times Square and a subway station with easy access to Wall St and Ground Zero. 
If you need any recommendations on where to go or directions for anywhere then the staff there will be more than happy to help! Or like my fiancÃ©, if your case starts to split then the bell captain will come to your aid with lots of Sellotape!! (if you read this thank you so much again, the case arrived back to the UK in 1 piece!!)
We will come back to NY, and we will be staying at The Salisbury again!

I attended a conference in Manhattan. I booked the Hotel 70 because it was a Kimpton property, close to the conference venue, and was offering a good rate. When I checked in I was provided a queen deluxe room on the 11th floor. There is an odd layout to the rooms on the floors, with my room being directly across from the stairwell, but I did not have any additional room noise because of that. The room was huge for NYC standards and very nicely decorated. There was plenty of storage in the room and the double window allowed a lot of light into the room. The bathroom was small, as said in other reviews, but again not excessively small by NYC standards. 
I did have several issues with the room, but all were probably maintenance issues. With a hotel of this age I can imagine how difficult it must be to maintain everything. The most problematic issue was the temperature of the room. Even with the thermostat set at 65 degrees the room never got below 72. At this temperature it was very difficult for me to sleep. After the first night I opened the window in the evening to cool down the room for sleeping. I did not report this issue to the hotel staff as I felt there was little that could be done about it. On my first morning I had no cold water in the bathroom. I reported this and it was repaired by the time I returned that evening. I rolled down the window blind and it would not roll up the next morning. Also fixed within hours. Because it is an older hotel the hot water does not get above tepid and it took a long time (10-15 minutes) for it to get to the 11th floor. But it was sufficient to have a comfortable shower.
All of the staff were exceptionally helpful with a special note to the concierge. She went out of her way to provide all the information I needed. As with all Kimpton Hotels the evening wine hour and morning coffee are extremely welcome after a hard day and a good night's sleep.
The hotel is extremely well located just over 2 blocks south of Grand Central Station and within walking distance of Times Square. It qualifies as an Oasis in the middle of the city.
hotel_name: 70 park avenue hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

If you are going to the airport from the hotel take advantage of the private car service! For a very competitive flat rate of $60 (which includes toll and tip) you in fact have your own limousine to take you back to the airport!

review_text: We were lucky enough to spend two nights in the plaza hotel in new York. Our kids wanted to stay in the "home alone" hotel and after a week in the west village we decided to move uptown for our last 2 nights and to surprise our 3 boys who are 9, 6 and 5). From the moment we arrived at the front door we were treated like extra special guests. Our room was not quite ready so they treated us to a drink in the champagne bar while we waited. It was my sons birthday and about an hour after we arrived a yummy chocolate cake was delivered to our room. The bell captains were outstanding and took the kids for rides around the lobby on the bag trolly... Breakfast in the palm court each morning was made even more fun by the brilliant waiters. The rooms are huge for new York and we loved the decor, the super comfy beds, divine pillows and they were quiet (amazing given our location) on the corner of 5th avenue. Every aspect of our stay at the plaza was a delight and hoteliers world wide should take note. The staff are brilliant and although the hotel is very grand we felt extremely welcome and at home. Well done plaza a triumph!!

review_text:
Stayed during the first August weekend. Arrived at the hotel around noon, after arriving from La Guardia via the 7 train to Grand Central Station. The station is a close 3 blocks away from the hotel. I was able to check into my corner King sized room right away. The room was definitely bigger than most NYC hotels I've researched & stayed at. The room fit my needs including a flat screen TV, a chaise, a work table & full length mirror. The air conditioner was great which was very fortunate as the humidity in NYC was scorcher. The room has large windows so there was a lot light. The room was also very quiet & I barely heard any noise from other guests. There was free wifi only in the lobby & any service in the room had to be paid for ($14.99 for 24hrs I think). I was mostly very impressed with the top notch service from the staff at the hotel. They were always courteous & genuinely willing to help. I didn't try the cafe/bar downstairs as I've always enjoyed visiting Penelope's for Breakfast on E. 30th & Lexington. 
I found it was a great location. Close to Grand Central w/ it's numerous lines including the shuttle to Times Square. I enjoy walking & found it convienent to walk anywhere. & it was safe, even at night. 
The only complaint I had was the bathroom shower. The shower needed an update as the water was spraying every else but down. Was told that the rooms will be getting updates including the showers. 
Overall, I'll return again the next time I'min town. It was such a great value as well.

review_text: I was put in the Blakely due to other guests extending their stay at their partner hotel, the Wellington. I believe this was to my advantage though as my experience in this hotel was perfect. The room was very nice, the staff was very friendly and helpful. My only comment was that the breakfast could have had a few more choices and maybe some hot dishes like eggs or bacon.

review_title: Great location, large rooms, friendly service
review_text: We had spent way too long deciding on where to stay for our "girls week" in New York. I am happy we finally decided on the Blakely. It is a cozy, boutique hotel in a great location only a few blocks from Central Park and subway around the corner. The suite with separate lounge area gave us plenty of room to handle all our shopping bags we came back with each day. The construction noise outside kept us awake the first two nights so we asked to change rooms and they were happy to do so. Unfortunately our new room was even noisier so we moved back ! Staff were helpful and understanding. I would recommend a room at the back of the hotel and as high as possible to escape street noise. Lifts were slow as others have commented but if you are on holidays you should be able to spare the extra few minutes to wait. Continental breakfast and free wifi are excellent inclusions and although the breakfast was the same each day we were happy not to have a decision about where to eat each morning and just go downstairs to the small restaurant connected to the hotel. Overall we were very comfortable at the Blakely and would recommend it as a boutique style hotel experience.

review_title: The golden pip in a big apple!
review_text: Me and my (now fiancÃ©) have just returned to the uk after staying in NYC for the first time. We chose this hotel based on the reviews and let me tell you we weren't let down! The location is brilliant! 5mins from times square and a few mins more to all the other excellent tourist sites. Every member of staff there were extremely professional, friendly and hold an extensive knowledge of the area. Our stay was made even more special as after proposing to my girlfriend in central park Eric from concierge arranged a chilled bottle of wine sent to our room compliments of the hotel and a card! I mean that's great customer service, they really do make u feel welcome and will do there upmost to make your visit memorable. Room was always very clean, excellent bed and large flat screen tv. So to summarise, great location, great rooms and excellent staff at a low cost price (by NYC standards). Hope this review was helpful, and if you do chose this hotel I think you have made a good choice. Have a nice stay in NYC!

Ginnia welcomed us the second we walked in the door. The entire staff was super friendly and accommodating. Everything in the rooms are nice and new. We had a great view of uptown. The breakfast is decent. If you just want a place to crash from sightseeing this hotel is perfect and clean. Rooms are a little small just like the rest of NYC so be mindful of that. Also bring your own water bottles because they don't sell them at the hotel.

Was surprised how dated the room was. Stains on carpet, furniture ripped in places and walls stained in areas. Tub chipped in multiple areas, etc. in other words, this hotel in major need of renovation. Service wasn't great either. We asked for extra towels and pillows. They didn't arrive until we called a few hrs later. Bed was best part of room....

After staying numerous times at the Benjamin, this stay was a disappointment. I travel 50-60 times a year and stay in many hotels in NYC, Chicago, Miami and other big cities so I have an extensive sample to compare it to.
The Rooms are getting old and the service has deteriorated significantly. The suites are rare in NYC so we always choose the Benjamin despite the poor location for tourists. However, the service has deteriorated so much that it is not worth it. Examples: multiple calls for towels, bed sheets with no response and poor housekeeping. It is not a 4 star hotel anymore. 3 at best. The doubletree in Times square, renaissance, waldorf, W, and hilton garden in in NYC (all of which I have stayed in this year) are cleaner and more responsive to guests.

Great hotel! Friendly and helpful staff, makes you feel very welcome! Nice and clean rooms, and a decent complementary breakfast. Have stayed there for 4 nights, going back in a week!
The location is close to Soho, and with subway stations a couple of minutes away by foot you can get to anywhere in a blast. A good place to stay when exploring the Big Apple.
A boutique hotel in a great mid town Manhattan location. It's Friendly staff and understated charm made my stay very enjoyable. I would stay here again.

We just complete our stay. We had a wonderful time - the staff was great and the room was outstanding. A little on the pricey side, but at this time of year not completely unexpected. Our package included a credit in The National, we had a really great meal there.
The only glitch occurred as we were leaving. It took over an hour to retrieve our car from the valet parking. When it finally appeared the sun roof was open as well as the driver's window. Unfortunately it was also raining. The hotel staff was apologetic and immediately removed any parking charges from the bill. They brought out towels to dry the car seats and driver's door.
They claimed that the parking garage was responsible - not sure it makes that much of a difference.
Otherwise, it was a great stay.

review_title: Our family's Thanksgiving Holiday at The Benjamin in NYC was magical.
review_text: My family spent five nights at this hotel over the Thanksgiving Holiday and we loved the location. Our one bedroom suit on the 16th floor was spacious and had an awesome view. Gina and Sara at the concierge's desk were spot on with our dinner reservations, theater tickets, and activities for the day. My kids want a repeat next year.
We came back to our tiny room after a nice long walk to find a huge cockroach in the closet. The staff was sorry but basically said they could not do anything. It was disgusting.
Well appointed room, fantastic restaurant, great staff. Perfect location mid- town east.

review_title: Plenty of other hotels in area, avoid this one!
review_text:
Don't stay here. There are Plenty of hotels in the area. Find someplace where the staff have hotel experience!
We asked the "concierge" to get tickets to see "How to Succeed in Business" for that evening. He told us theaters are dark on Monday. He said this was a "hot" ticket"! We told him we knew that, but we also knew there was a performance that night. He supposedly called the box office and found out there were 2 seats left in rear mezzanine for $250 each. He also told me that he had just gotten tickets for four people for the following night for $350 apiece. (poor, unsuspecting souls). A half hour later we walked over to the box office and got sixth row center tickets for face value (of course we did, the show was that night and not sold out)
The concierge either takes a pretty hefty commission or he's working with a sketchy secondary market!...watch out.
The second thing that happened was that the housekeepers threw away my daughter's retainers which she left in the bathroom (where would you leave them?)
The hotel launched an investigation even though we weren't assuming a crime was involved! We only wanted them to check the garbage and laundry and to reimburse us the cost of replacement.
This should be called the three stooges hotel!
Oh, and the bathroom was so small and laid out in such a bizarre fashion, it was almost unusable. That would have been ok if the people weren't so useless!
Don't stay here. Old rooms, slow elevators, and poor service. They also got the bill wrong twice and when I called to get it sorted out was hung up on by the front office manager.

I treated my BBF and myself to a spa weekend at the hotel. Needless to say we were impressed from check in to check out. The Wellness Spa was extremely accomadating and the girls gave us a great treatment. The breakfast was great: the orange was freshly squeezed and the syrup was real maple. 
I would recommend the Ben to anyone!

I stayed at this property for one night. My concern was I would be checking in at 8am and not checking out until 2pm the following day. I was tired from travel as well as jet lag and had been given an extensive shopping list by my wife and kids. I needed the late check out as I was ferrying bags back to the hotel when there was too much to carry. I emailed the hotel requesting arrival and departure times but did not receive a response. When I checked in there was no problem with the request. All was sorted by a male receptionist. I had received an email some days earlier offering a complementary upgrade if I made a comment on twitter or Facebook. I did this and at checkin they had no record of this but still upgraded me to a fantastic room with seperate living and kitchen area. The bed was really comfortable and the sheets like silk. The location was another huge plus as I only needed one cab which was to Macy's and everywhere else was walkable. I booked a bed and breakfast package and due to my early check in the receptionist offered me breakfast that morning also at no extra cost. It was a great experience and I will be back. 
Stayed October 7th 2011
Stephen

review_title: Perfect location for Radio City / Rockefeller sight seeing.
review_text: Paid 400 for premier room and was a nice room. Very 50s decor but in a vintage fun way. The room was spacious (yes spacious) for NYC. Bathroom is marble and clean -- bed was outstanding (very comfortable). There was very mild street noise considering we were so close to a very busy area. review_text:

But no worries nothing here is dated .I have already booked another stay next month.

review_text:

review_title: Yes, stay here but there are some (very) minor issues.
review_text: As business travelers, we picked the Warwick Hotel in NYC because of its location, reputation and TripAdvisor reviews. Good decision based on good tools. The bonus is that the place is very clean and the rooms are very fresh. Some staff that standout include Jamaal at the front desk, Daniel the bellman - who just may have the best attitude for a bellman EVER - and Ray in the package room who is all about doing a good job for his guests. Oh, and the servers and manager in the hotel bar (did not get their names) did a nice job as well. ---- my only minor complaints are with a couple of things that are missing: charging your phone in your room is not easy with the very limited number of outlets, there is no coffee maker and this may be the last hotel on the planet that has not yet installed the curved "heavenly" shower curtain rod. All three seem like very simple fixes and each would elevate this lovely hotel to a preferred status. Thanks Warwick, we enjoyed our stay.
If you have the chance to stay here, all other things being equal, try this magnificent property at an unbeatable location. XMas in the city never wads so special!

review_text: Very nice hotel. Our room wasn't ready when we arrived so they upgraded to a king size suite at no additional charge. Great service and the price wasn't bad compared to similar hotels in the same vicinity. We drove to N.Y. so the Benjamin parked our truck in a parking deck for $60 a night. I would definitely recommend this hotel!

We are just about to spend our 4th and final night in the great hotel. It is located in a perfect spot, very easy walk to Times Square, restaurant row, shops and public transport. Small hotel and do not expect a view from your window. How much time to you spend in your room though? All you need is a comfy bed and a good shower. This hotel has both, extremely comfortable beds and a large over head rain shower with excellent pressure. The staff at reception are friendly and very helpful. Thank you Teddy for the friendly NY welcome, you are a wealth of information. Would definitely stay here again.

review_title: Amazing staff, they really make you feel at home.
review_text:
The Moderne is a great little hotel 5 mins from time sq, central park and 10 mins from 5th Ave. The convenient location is also close to the underground.
The biggest point of difference was the staff. Victoria on the front desk is amazing! Welcoming and friendly. Teddy and cj are able to offer many restaurant and bar suggestions. If you're looking for great service, a fab location and a boutique feel then I would highly recommend the Moderne

review_title: Totally recommend this cute hotel in a perfect location.
review_text: Great hotel. Perfect location in NYC. Clean, nice employees. Upgraded us to a suite because it was our anniversary.

We stayed for three days and had the greatest time. The staff were exceptional ... So friendly and very helpful.a special thanks to Victoria and CJ for all your help .you made our stay! this hotel has the best location and we totally enjoyed the second floor lounge.

review_title: Almost did mid town, SO glad I didn't!
review_text: So we planned to take our 5 kids and 2 nannies to Ney York for Thamksgiving week which would be our first time int the city! We had booked a very posh upscale Hotel facing Cental Park but we felt uneasy. We didn't want the total tourist experience but wanted to see and feel the real NY. Thru a friend we were able to secure the Penthouse and 2 additional rooms on the 8th floor! The terrace was amazing, the Keihls bath products were great, but the stand out was the staff who were always kind and helpful in every way. The location seriously was perfect for us. Subway right outside the door, great Resturants within 5 blocks (Mr. Chows, Nobu's, Gianni's, and Bubby's where we had Jake Gylnenhall 1 table away enjoying breakfast with his mom). Anyway the food was great and easy to get too. We did a walking tour of the city Where we discovered so much history and culture within 15 minutes of our hotel. Little Italy, Chinatown, World Trade Center, and SoHo were all within easy walking distance even for my 5 year old. TriBeCa was a great place to start and finish our day and I highly recommend The Smyth for your stay!

review_title: Great, luxurious and good value for money!
review_text:
My friend and I wanted to have a luxury NY trip and looked at the Waldorf before we found this hotel. We stayed in a 2x double bed room on the third floor, with walk in closet, tv, marble bathroom and did I mention the 2 double beds?! It was excellent, you couldnt hear other guests noise (although a little st traffic, nothing major though), cleaned every day, so close to central park and other great sights. Close to metro line 57f, there is a great shop on about 58/6th which sells dinner and snacks. Beds so very comfy, shower high powered, staff nice and door man got us a taxi for our plane ($50 flat rate). Would definately stay again! 
One point to be aware of, you need a card with $100 free on it for check in, which they will refund you if you dnt have films room service etc.

We stayed her for one night. Hotel is in a great location. We were in a king superior room which was relatively spacious (especially for NYC) and meticulously clean. The service was great - within 5 minutes of calling for things (like an iron or more towels), they were delivered. Everyone we came into contact with was so friendly. The bed was super comforable and the shower was great too. The only downside is that the bath towels are not good (too small and barely absorbent) and there aren't enough of them in the room. Also, it grossed us out that there was no top sheet between the bed and the comforter...we assumed they wash the duvet cover after each person's stay. We booked this hotel thru magellan and got a better rate that so-called discount internet tavel sites.

I stay at the Smyth for a few days every month. It has unusually spacious rooms for NYC, which are squeaky clean and with a pleasant, minimalist design featuring quality fixtures. The place feels stylish and hip without being painful. Staff is genuinely nice and helpful. Any hickups are always dealt with swiftly and efficiently. Good dining options in the neighborhood, also a Whole Foods.

review_title: What a great hotel great staff great decoration and style great restarants and bars full of life
review_text:
This is not my normal type of hotel I usually stay at uber modern minalmalist places but they were full 
Thank god loved it at gramercy,don't book here if you want isolation and piece and quite this place is full of life at the weekends great bars great restarants great staff great management

review_title: Perfect New York winter home in great location
review_text:
Gramercy park hotel
I spend six months of the year staying in New York hotels, including hotels such as Trump Soho (3 months), The Crosby Soho (6 weeks) but none compare to the warmth and ambience of the Gramercy Park.
The huge
Â open fires, roof terrace, rose bar, Danny MyersÂ Maialino restaurant on the ground floor, Â the lighted candles in the room as part of the turn down service, Â Gramercy park and some of the best retaurants Â in Manhatten make this hotel so comfortable you don't want to leave. Definately going to be my home whenever I am in New York.

review_title: Great hotel. Feels like a modern boutique hotel.
review_text: Best thing is the service. Everyone is so nice, friendly and helpful. Rooms are super modern and clean. Not huge, but big enough. Quiet, double-paned windows. It feels like Hyatt's boutique hotel. The only downside is the virtually non-existent lobby, but this is more than made up for with their incredible 2nd floor lounge. The staff there is truly wonderful. It's modern and spacious. They offer coffees and teas whenever and also sometimes have top notch snacks.

review_title: From whence cometh the star ratings? There must have been a sizable payoff for this Place to get 4 stars! Small, dark, and chinc
review_text: From whence cometh the star ratings? There must have been a sizable payoff for this Place to get 4 stars! Small, dark, and chincy, this place rates 3 stars at best. The designer must come from the Munsters. The surfaces are all dark brown and dreary. The furniture- if you can call it that is dark laminated (starting to delaminate) plastic. The hardware is vintage Lowes, and failing, and the "standard" room has a full size bed an reading lights for one. It is not really a two person room.

review_title: Ok. Not a good representation of brand.
review_text:
I travel a great deal for work, and almost exclusively stay at Hampton Inns around the US and Canada. I have noted that Hilton is making an effort to update and modernize the Hampton hotels, and have stayed at both per and post updated hotels.
The Chelsea hotel is in sincere need of update. The original room I was given (1401) was shameful. The shower stall was patched and cracks ran from the ceiling to halfway down the stall. The toilet overflowed on the first flush covering the bathroom floor with waste water. The staff immediately placed me in another same sized room that was in better repair. Great service, but it should not have been required.
Beds are strangely uncomfortable, and must be different than then brand standard.
Rooms are small, as are most in NYC.
Room was clean.
Overall, a good location. I booked with rewards points (although in hindsight I wish I had used them at a better finished brand hotel), but I felt the regular price was fair.
A modernization and refinishing of the hotel is definitely needed.

My wife and I stayed here with our 2 sons, ages 9 and 7, for three nights the week before Christmas. We've previously stayed at the Excelsior and at the Beacon, and we can easily say The Lucerne is the best! We stayed in a large suite on the 12th floor - it was perfect for a family. They let us check in when we arrived around 11 in the morning and they were always accommodating - they even helped print out our boarding passes. The location can't be beat. You're near the park, near the Nat Hist Mus, and Lincoln Center and the Met are just a brisk walk away. A subway station is nearby and so is Zabar's (don't miss it). Also, don't miss the restaurant next door, Nice Matin, and Coppola's across the street. Nothing's cheap, but it's NYC!!!

Everything at the Hampton Inn was wonderful for our stay during the Thankgiving holiday break.
The staff was great including the assistant general manager, Kevin. We couldn't have asked for more.

We apologize to the avid trip advisor review readers who expects a balanced review because we just can't come up with anything but positives about Gramercy Park Hotel. It's hip, it's well located, and the rooms are perfect. We had great experience in the Rose bar. The front desk staff are the most professional around. Quiet. Well located. Walking easy to good restaurants.

review_title: This luxury hotel feels like home away from home.
review_text: I love this place! The staff is very friendly and accommodating....I feel like I'm in a little town somewhere when I'm here than you step outside and you are in the heart of nyc....I love it! I stay here all the time. The front desk staff is amazing!

review_title: Was scared to stay after reading reviews, but they have listened and made changes!
review_text: At first I was scared to stay. I had read some negative reviews. I believe that they fixed some issues that I had read about earlier. The staff couldn't be nicer or more helpful. They were eager to assist. The front desk check in was a breeze. As posted before, the elevators can take a while if you want to use them during peak times. The longest we had to wait was 5 minutes. We were fine with that. The room was nice. No tub, but nice hyatt showers(big). The bed was very comfortable. Room overall was not huge, but that's ok. There is a lobby bar, but we didn't go there. It's seemed nice. If you are looking for a huge hotel like feel, you won't find it here. There is no grand lobby. It was a 10 minute walk to Grand Central, Rockafeller Center, and 5th Ave shopping. I would recommend to anyone, and I do believe they have ironed out any issues that negative reviewers posted.

The service received and the room met and surpassed our expectations. The location was exceptional with respect to all the activities and attractions we had hoped to see and do. We have recommended the hotel to friends that are planning a trip to New York within the next few months

I had a very pleasurable stay here at the Hampton Inn Manhattan Chelsea. The hotel staff was very helpful and curtious. The location of the hotel was perfect for me because it was only a short subway ride away from Times Square. So it put me close enough to the city but still far enough away from the most busy sections. The room was very pretty and had a modern look to it. The beds were extremely comfortable too. I was overall very pleased with the time I stayed there. My only complaints were that the rooms were kinda small, but this was my first time to New York, so for all I know, that could be a very common thing. Also, the majority of the rooms don't really have any kind of good view or the city but I didn't mind that too much since I didn't spend too much time in the room. Also, the common area/breakfast room was kinda crowded and cramped, but the fact that they had a full service breakfast bar with plenty of hot food compensated well for that.

Lied to by restaurant/room service staff about their opening hours and when we complained the restaurant manager did little more than shrug and suggest we eat elsewhere!
Amazing how easy it is to be sucked in by a good tripadvisor ratings. 
Needless to say we moved hotels the next night never to return!

review_title: very happy family!!! stay was great!
review_text: We decided to take a last minute trip to NYC! we were able to check in early! room - was designated as a smoking room- we don't smoke and it smells fine!!! staff fun and friendly! would def stay here again!!!

Spent 4 wonderful nights here for New Years eve 2008 with some friends.
This hotel blew me away, the decor, the art work, the service, the ambiance, the martinis, and even the smell in the lobby (thanks to GPH specifically designed candles). 
This is easily the best hotel in NYC, and I've stayed in all the competition (Hudson, Royalton, W hotel etc). 
The only negative is the standard rooms are a bit small, but that's typical for NYC. 
Had the time of my life.

Just spent four nights at the Lucerne, our fourth time staying there. What makes the stay at this facility so special is the caring staff. The bellmen, doorman and housekeepers go out of their way to make a guest feel at home. The rooms are immaculate, the hotel is located in a vibrant upper westside neighborhood with small shops and a variety of restaurants. Some of the rooms are small but the TLC lavished by the staff more than makes up for that.

Uber cool, unpretentious, decadent hotel with friendly staff and chatty permanent residents and guests. Much friendlier and more relaxed than you would generally expect from a high end hotel. Loved it. And it's within walking distance of so many great places.

The hotel is still undergoing some construction, but The staff more than made up for it. I was traveling for work on valentine's day and shortly after I checked in, I received a complimentary bottle of wine. About 5 minutes later I received a hand written thank you note from the general manager (nice touch). I felt like the room decor was a little tacky and cheap, but the tv & bathroom made up for any of the room's shortcomings. Also the hallway from the elevator to the room was a bit dingy, dark, and cheap. Overall, for the location, value, and friendly staff, I would recommend this hotel. However, next time I'm in NYC, I will probably try a different place just for the variety and to be able to compare.
This is my favorite hotel in Chelsea. Staff is great, location has lots of food choices, and it's a nice value.

review_title: Beautiful hotel in a beautiful city
review_text: Unique and comfortable, close to all. We really enjoyed our stay

review_title: Exactly what you need for a visit to NYC
review_text: Hotel was extremely clean and front desk staff were very helpful. Breakfast was good and there were plenty of places within a short walking distance to eat at as well. Subway station was right around the corner. I'd definetly stay here again.

review_title: A hidden Gem in New York City
review_text: A excellent hotel. The rooms are of a good size and lovely and clean. The hotel is in a good neighbourhood. The staff here are both professional and courteous. If you don't want to stay in the middle of the city, this is for you. Subway station close by so travelling into the city is no problem. Ideal location for central park. We loved our stay here and definitely recommend The Lucerne.
I stay there regularly as I visit NY regularly. It is hard to fault it except to say it would be great if they could serve wine with room service. Crossing the street to a liquor store is annoying.

review_title: Clean but very basic with poor service
review_text:
Here for four nights, I had booked several months ago making room request for a bar fridge then. With the hurricane last week, the front desk had lost Internet service when I called the night before arrival to confirm reservation details. The could not confirm anything, let alone my special requests. 
The rooms here are very clean which is the best part of this hotel. There are no frills at all in the room, barely even pictures on the walls. 
They do NOT have room safes which meant carrying everything around of value, such as my iPad, extra camera lens etc. With all the walking in NYC i have learned not to book somewhere without this feature again! They do have small safety boxes downstairs but they did not ell me on the phone when booking that they are very narrow and useful only for jewelery and money. 
Breakfast was fine but simple. Nice touch that some mornings (not all) they had bagged breakfast you could take with you with an apple bottle water, cereal bar and muffin. Just like cookies in the lobby, this "perk" was inconsistent and not always available.
I would say that the most disappointing part of this hotel was the apathetic attitude and lack of knowledge of front desk staff. Service was lacking for a Hilton chain hotel! We didn't get a bar fridge until the night before we left, were unable to get a late checkout beyond 1pm, and repeatedly had to seek general information about city attractions and directions via the Internet or other hotel guests!
Good restaurants are limited in this neighborhood. Nice to have a whole foods at the end of the block though if you want fruit on the go, and the eataly on 24th was a cool grocery store with neat eating options cafeteria type style but high quality
If you are a starving student or on an extremely tight budget this hotel will do, but if you can alternatively book last minute on hotels.com and don't care about Hilton points, and can spend $50-80/ night more, I am sure there are much better alternatives!

review_title: Poor service and poor quality for an expensive place
review_text:
My stay at Cassa portait as a luxury hotel has been a forgettable experience.
The place has a great location but that it's as far as it goes in terms of appreciating the place.
The hotel has not a breakfast room that still undergoing construction, you can have breakfast on a bar on the 10th floor that clearly cannot accommodate everybody. An the choices of food are pathetic.
Cassa is not a cheap place to stay, and if you come for business as I do, you expect a wifi service and 2 days the service was down although I still got charged for it.
The business room where you should have the alternative to use a computer was also down however I lost money twice trying to access Internet there, because no one said the service was also down
Laundery was delivered late and they forgot to deliver more than half of the items I sent to get cleaned.
The answer to my complained was go to block down to an Internet caffe'. 
Charging a full price for something it's not up running it's simply unacceptable.

review_title: Great location, beautiful area, nice overall vibe to this hotel.
review_text: The staff was great. Love the atmosphere! Definently staying here again.

review_title: Style over substance! Get over yourself
review_text:
Had a 2 night treat with my husband and booked a loft room. Really impressed when we first walked inside the hotel and sadly this is where they have clearly invested money and creative resources.
The room was fine, a bit outdated and plain. The bath was the big attraction and was pretty cool but the rest was totally impractical and not cosey.
Don't get me started on the ridiculous price of everything- water for 8 dollars is shocking and pathetic and you might day hey it's NY but Soho House is much better all around and more reasonable for a stylish hotel.
The in-room IPad was cool but is outdated now, with no music on the iTunes and the restaurant recommendations including ones th no longer exist, poor attention to detail.
Loved having a fire in the room and the bed was very comfy but the rest of the room felt a bit corporate, strange considering the warmth and style of the reception. The noise caused by having the fire was terribke! Must have been from the flu and we regretted ever turning it on! How can a hotel in midtown a few blocks from Times Square not have double glazed windows? This was the worst part, we could here trucks and sirens all night, awful.
Service was truly hit and miss? Waiting 20 minutes for my bag when I came to collect it was frustrating while checking in the first person we met chatted away with us and really welcomed us.
We were in such a hurry to leave so didn't complain (how British of us, I know) but we were truly unimpressed.
Overall I'd say not worth the hype at all, for the price there are now so many more interesting options and next time we're in the city or friends ask where they should stay, I won't quick to recommend this hotel.

review_title: Simply the best place to stay in NYC
review_text: I had the best stay at the Lucerne. A quiet, well appointed room, free wi fi, helpful concierge who recommended and booked restaurants and shows. The bistro Nice Matin downstairs was open all day and night. Friendly staff who provided pillows and document printing. The location is great, 2 -3 blocks from Central Park and 1 block from the subway. And bargain shoppers, Filenes Basement is 100 Metres away.

review_title: Perfect location in Manhatten, perfect hotel.
review_text: Simply a fantastic stay! Upgraded to a suite as it was a special occasion with champagne and strawberries! Staff could not be more helpful, everything was just so easy. The bar area is stunning - will be back!

This Hampton Inn is predictably like most Hampton Inns - clean, safe, helpful staff, no restaurant, nice breakfast included, rather rigid about checkin times, etc. The Hampton Inn on 24th is almost a clone of the one on 34th near Madison Square Garden. Great location in Chelsea in easy walking distance from flower district, many nice restaurants, High Line, etc.

review_title: Not a fancy hotel, but has everything you need for a great value.
review_text: Big room for Manhattan standards, great free breakfast, free wireless. The only thing I missed was a fridge in the room.

Girls weekend 8/25-8/29. First I'd like to thank the hotel staff for making our comfort and safety a priority during Hurricane Irene. Your sacrifices made a real difference. Highlights of this property were proximity to theatre, Times Square and metro. I've stayed at the Algonquin acrossvthe street and like this location for solo travel because it is close to everything yet quiet and safe to walk to even late at night. Comfy beds and contemporary decor. Great shower and bath products. Awesome cheese plate and the lamb burger with fries were a delight.

review_title: This hotel is just PERFECT, staff is super nice (especially Jenny and Natalia at the front office), and we were treated like kin
review_text: The location is great (walking distance from eveything), staff is super gentle, the hotel looks good (the carpet at the entrance is so fluffy, it feels like walking on clouds) and the rooms, though a little tiny, are really worth it. Ask for the soaking tub!

review_title: Hotel full of surprises and all good too.
review_text:
We had booked a Superior Room based on the website so did expect everything that was on the website. The hotel has a distinct look from the outside with its pillars. The doorman provided excellent service from the onset. The check-in was in the middle of a dark lobby which looked absolutely amazing. Check-in staff was really nice and professional and as complimentary provided me with free Wi-Fi throughout our stay. We were located on the 9th floor opposite the elevator. Was a bit worried by this but was never affected by any sound disturbance at night throughout our holiday. 
We were fully surprised on entering the room as it provided a lot more than we expected. There was a room that was like a walk-in cupboard with shelving and hanging space in which our suitcases and shoes lived in during the stay. Additionally there was another dressing room which we did not expect. The room was walled with mirrors, had a dressing table and stool. The bathroom was of top standard too with a wet-room shower.
The hotel staff were never hesitant and were always on hand to make the stay pleasant. We were provided with slippers and additional bath-gown on request.The room was cleaned daily even if it meant being cleaned mid-afternoon after you left the room. 
Overall an excellent hotel that I could not criticise in any way.

review_title: Fantastic stay in a beautiful hotel with an amazing location
review_text: Our stay was to celebrate my husbands 40th. After reading some of the recent reviews I began to feel a little anxious and considered changing hotels. However, to my relief the hotel was beautiful, the staff were extremely helpful and the location was perfect!
If it's not too expensive for you, I recomend you to try this place. I like this place very much, hope you will like it too.

This is third visit to New York but our first at the Peninsula. 
Having done my research on the hotel, we weren't disappointed!
The room did lack a view but was well equipped and the lighting was a very clever and nice touch!
