review_title: A perfact stay at the perfact hotel
review_text:
We came to new York for two nights, my husband our 17 years doughter and myself, on our way to Dallas for our daughter's surgery. We stayed at the 4 seasons for the first time. 
The room was unbelievably large. The bathroom is the most beautiful I have ever seen. 
Food was so good, and above all was the service. Just perfact.
The price was high, but I guess it comes with the hall package. There is no daught: we found no 1 hotel in new York city.

Nice hotel just should be cheaper overpriced
Wish the price was cheaper and
Hotel was not an inch form apartment overpriced expected better from the four seasons

In New York you get what you pay for... I have tried to find deals in Manhattan and have never experienced the service, quality and class as I have at the Four Seasons. Kudos to management and staff. This hotels rocks!

We went for my sons birthday and woke up first morning scratching and with blood on sheets. We were covered in bites. Hotel mgmt shown bites and changed our room. We are miserable and just went again to dermatologist who verified diagnosis. Hotel said not their problem. We paid 3000 dollars for 5 nights. They refused any reimbursement of this fee.

review_title: It was not the best, but not bad for a 5 star hotel!
review_text:
One of the best hotels that i have had the privilege to stay in. The positives are 1) Our room was very, very clean and spacious. The bedding was changed every day, complete with towels, etc. 2)The staff was the very polite and attentive to your needs, 3) Great food, served fresh and hot and served by the waitstaff in your room if you desired, 4) The hotel is located in an excellent location close to Central Park and more shopping you could possibly do in the time you will probably have.
The negatives include 1) In building the shower, somehow, the shower door seal does not prevent the water from running out on the floor. There was a drain in the middle of the marble floor for the purpose of water runoff! Strange! We spent five days mopping up water each 
time we took a shower! 2) We did not receive the daily paper as 
promised each morning.
Although they need to fix these two negatives, I would definitely come back again and recommend it to my friends.

review_title: Best NYC stay in the price range
review_text:
My wife and I stayed here while we where in NYC to get married and find an appartment (we are moving there from EU in jan.)
The staff was the best, so friendly and nice. I have stayed with 3 different top hotels during the last year in NYC, and the staff here is so much more friendly then any other I have meet in NYC. There was a real "anything is possible" respons to any request. They even let us shoot pictures at the roof top bar for weeding photo.
We had a corner studio, which had a great view and was very nicely decorated. I would recommed this to all people below 40 who are looking for a top hotel. Not sure it would be right for my parents, but younger or single, then no one beats this.

I had high expectations and Four Seasons exceeded them. Stayed for the Easter long weekend, 3 nights, booked through the internet and saw they had 3 nights for the price of two. When we checked in we got upgraded 3 levels to a 1BR suite. Complimentary Wine and Champagne because it was our birthday (how thoughtful) the service, food, location, amenities, the overall experience was definitely worth the price. Especially if you have a special occasion to celebrate- 4 Seasons will look after every detail. Janet, Toronto

The staff are very friendly and helpful! Love their hip uniforms. The rooms and housekeeping is amazing. The rooftop lounge has amazing views. 1st time in Soho. One of the best hotels I've stayed at! Young, hip and very chic! Would come back and definitely recommend!

review_title: Loved the location,the vibe and all the hidden included bonuses!
review_text: We stayed for 8 nights over thanksgiving for our first visit to NYC after being recommended SOHO by some fellow Aussies! This hotel is fabulous! From the arrival and the great sky elevator to the included pastries/coffee in the Morning and wine and cheese in the evening! An the wifi! My only criticism would be the wifi occasionally blocks at night due to too many people using it-presumably due to those in the awesome rooftop bar JIMMY. You get what you pay for at the James-it is worth every cent!

review_title: Awesome location with great service in a contemporary boutique hotel!
review_text:
The staff at every level was accommodating, from the doorman to the manager! Chris, Claudia, Christina and Michael to name a few. They are so attentive that within a day we were on name basis! We had two rooms for 3 nights on the 14th floor with amazing views! We traveled with 2 teens and an 11 uear old. The neighborhood is teeming with restaurants and shops. The subway is close by and taxis are easy! The rooms are compact and no problem
For us. It is a new and clean place to stay with trendy style and comfy beds!

We stayed 3 nights from December 8-11. We were very happy with the hotel, particularly the value. Location is central to all major attractions and within walking distance of macys, times square, Rockefeller center etc. The rooms were small, although clean and nicely decorated. Continental breakfast was a plus, although not much variety ( muffins, toast and yogurt, and a few cereals)
We were overall very pleases with our stay, staff are very friendly and helpful. The only negative aspect of the stay was on our final day we waited 15 minutes for an elevator and finally had to take the stairs down 6 flights so we wouldn't miss our flight. Staff were apologetic, and I realize these things do happen, just frustrating.

review_title: Nothing a New HVAC System Wouldn't Fix
review_text: We loved the location of The James. It sits right on the edge of SOHO and Tribeca. Great shopping, restaurants, coffee shops, services all around. Not the craziness of Times Square and Mid-town. We walked almost everywhere. The James has real potential. It's cozy and personable. The rooms have delicious glass walls of windows. Our room was small, but that's standard for NYC. Making it feel not-so-small was a very cool glass wall between the bathroom and bedroom. High ceilings help too. Bed was comfie. But what other reviewers describe with the HVAC system is true - or else they have a serious poltergeist issue! It sounded like someone was dragging steel cabinets across the floor for two minutes at a time every 10 minutes or so. All night. We're good sleepers, so it didn't really impact us too severely, but it gives the place a weird vibe. I'm assuming the issue was the HVAC...

Our weekend visit was exactly what we anticipated for RC standards. The staff were friendly, yet impeccably professional. The food & beverage offerings in the club lounge were great. The club lounge staff went out of their way to accommodate a late evening special request. Room was terrific & bathroom sublime. I had to purchase the Bvlgari bath products after coming home. Heavenly! Can't wait to return!
Modern hotel, professional staff make for a great stay

Stayed at this hotel from Monday the 14th til Sunday the 20th November. The staff were fantastic, extremely helpful and polite. They showed a real interest in how our stay with them was going, and also how we were enjoying the city. 
Hotel very very clean, room service staff very polite. Always someone available if assistance required. Roof bar also very nice. Would most definitely recommend staying here, literally a 2-4 minute walk from broadway and times square. Food available at both ends of street. 
Excellent hotel, was very pleased and got exactly what we wanted from a hotel in NYC. 
Rooms are fairly sized, plenty room to store 2 big suitcases and 2 adults. Bathroom good size. Shower nice and spacious. Lighting and heating very easy to use and great quality. 
Well done - a reasonably priced hotel compared to others in NYC with great standards.

Had a Liberty views room. It's great being away from the hussle and bussle of times sq and the like. Great gym, didn't use room service or restaurant so cant really comment on these. Would stay here again without question.

Had a Liberty views room. It's great being away from the hussle and bussle of times sq and the like. Great gym, didn't use room service or restaurant so cant really comment on these. Would stay here again without question.

review_title: If they could only get the checkout correct . . .
review_text: My go to place in NY. Love the quiet location. Rooms are spacious and well appointed. Great value if booked through Virtuoso so rate includes continental breakfast and $100 hotel credit. Downside is that checkout is always screwed up.

Staff more bothered how they look than how they treat their guests. Small rooms. No evening turn down service (should do but do not bother. Complained twice.). Only 1 bar (bar upstairs with pool is only open after 9.30pm and only if your on the guest list). Usually stay in similar boutique hotel, but this is the worst I have stayed in and would recommend you chose another.

review_title: Reasonable price trendy hotel in soho
review_text: Hotel perfect for soho shopping trip. Hotel is very modern and has a great rooftop gym and bar. David Burke restaurant was ok. The concierge gave great dining recommendations.

Modern, metropolitan and minimalist. Impeccable as few are able to consistently be, effortlesslyÂ luxurious with a genuinely attentive service. If you learned to appreciate this recipe at the James Chicago you will be pleased to find it in New York too.Â 
It's all those little unexpected touches that get you to L O V E the James New York. I won't list them because the discovery journey is part of what make you smile.Â 
Whether you have been to NYC many many times and you want to breath Soho in or this is your first visit, the James is a MUST.
The Strand is a good hotel for a reasonable price. Rooms are nice although a bit small. The breakfast is average. Not a lot of choice.

review_title: A great all round hotel! From food-service to all those special added extras!
review_text:
we Booked this hotel as a package deal through Virgin and it was our first time in new York.
We got a taxi straight to the hotel which was cheap and as we arrived our bags were taken straight up to our room for us and doors to the hotel open for us with a warm welcome!
We checked in and arrived in our room to find it was clean modern and a good size with everythingwe needed. The beds are amazing here! We were on the 4 floor and there are 21 floors at the hotel, 21st being the roof top bar.
This was handy to take the stairs wen the lift was busy.
As we were at the back of the hotel our room looked out on the back of buildings so our intention was to keep the curtains shut(bad view)
the hotel is in a prime location for the best shopping on 5th ave, Madison and 42nd street. Also right by the rockafella, times square, grand central station, empire state!
We walked for miles but cabs are so cheap and staff at the hotel will hail you one on request.
Breakfast starts at 7am- get in quick to have the best choices of continental. It does run til 10, get replenised and I free!! Love it!
Restaurant and bar really classy and Great quality, this will pull on your purse strings but so does everywhere else!
After afew nights we noticed we were being woken by a constant banging of music coming from a building over from our window. Starting at 2am and stopping around 7am.
If you were a heavy sleeper this may not bother you.. We are not!
I complained to staff at reception, was told there is a salsa club and that they have put in noise complaints but I was not happy with this and asked to move.
I went out for the day having packed my bags and when I returned I was greeted by name, given a new room card and told it had all been sorted...
I was now on the 18th floor facing out on the empire state building 
with a larger room and couldn't believe it! My bags had all been taken to my room for me and the curtains remained open for the rest of the time.
Staff here really care, they are weloming and go out of their was to make sure their guests are happy.
Only other thing, if you can be bothered the gym is really nice! And when you check out you can leave all your bags in a safe room and use the hotel facilities or go sightseeing until that sad time you have to return to the airport!
I'm saving for my next trip and I'm staying at the Stand!!

review_title: Great hotel , in less touristy noisy areas!
review_text: The hotel is on the bottom tip of manhattan , the hotel seems very small , however the rooms are massive for new York standards. The bathroom is also very nice!! We stayed on club so the food Presentations were great! However the club lounge and our room had city views ! The statue of liberty view was amazing and we should hav payed the extra 40 dollars to upgrade!! Overall a very nice hotel!

Muy buena ubicacion y servicio. La habitacion confortable y me encanto que tenga cocinita, puesto que podia preparar mi propio desayuno a gusto. El lobby demasiado pequeÃ±o para mi gusto pero lo compensaba el bussines center, que era grande y muy completo, con sillones, tv, maquina de te/cafe, wi-fi free, etc.
El personal de lo mas atento y cordial.
Stayed during Irene and the staff handled the situation great. Location good -- on the edge of SoHo. Outdoor bar looked fun. I will stay here again.

review_title: Trendy NY hotel, good for business traveler.
review_text:
Rooms- Standard Ny room size=small. Clean, nice tiled shower, took a while to figure out there was a curtain that slides over the clear glass in the see through bathroom. Mini fridge with STD bar drinks & snacks. Couldn't find the price list so didn't want to buy a $20 pop just in case.
Happy Hour- the free wine & cheese
 was nice. 
Continental Breakfast- that was a waste. Strong coffee & cinnamon 
buns. That's all I saw.
Room Service- ordered pizza. It was
 good & quick. 15 minute service.
Rooftop Bar- very trendy & nice. 
No complaints. Very dressy, noticed all the women wore a little black 
dress including the waitresses. Expect the Std. $20 NY drink. I was at the hotel for work.

The hotel was perfect, the service and the staff were so nice and warm, they took care of everything we asked and did it with alot of caring. The location was perfect. The hotel have a nice pool on the last floor. We really enjoy every minute of the the staying. Highly recommended !!!

What a fantastic hotel. Went with 6 friends. Staff is the nicest in all of NYC and made all the difference. Rooms are very nice and well appointed. Food was great. JIMMY rooftop bar is cool (get in before 9, the doormen are jerks and don't want hotel guests up there). Location is great for soho, TriBeCa and wall street. I'll definitely stay there next time I go to NYC.

review_title: An expensive high end hotel that does not cater to it's guests
review_text: The hotel is very pretty in a great location however the management and staff have a long way to go before they have perfected a truly world class hotel experience. It is very clear that the focus is entirely on their "coolness" factor with their facilities and very little on making their guests happy. Upon check in I was not informed that to utilize any of the outdoor spaces, pool, Jimmys, greenhouse etc, you must reserve through front desk and still not likely to be accomodated. The attitude of employees at these locations was terrible. David Burkes breakfast is delicious however. Additionally, the cleaning continued to forget to replace my filtered water bottle they emphasize nor did they remember to replace towels. All in all a fine stay and pretty nice room, but there are many better options in Soho and TriBeCa at this price range that are focused entirely on their guest experience rather than press for how cool they are.

review_title: Wish I could reside at this hotel permanently.
review_text: The Strand Hotel offers excellent quality in every area. Staff is friendly, breakfast is great, bed is sooo comfortable, towels are sooo plush, restaurant has great food and you are close to many eateries and souvenir stores. Would definitely return there if in NY again.

What a complete disappointed this hotel turned out to be. On the website it all looks great, big, wunderfull, bright, modern etc but these pictures are enormously deceiving! In fact this was the smallest down town NYC 400 usd per night room I have ever seen. The floors were already damaged in the room and instead of a luxury feel of a new hotel it already looked 10 years old. The pool upstairs is not a pool but a large bathtub and if you want 1 of the only 3 double beds you really have to reserve (!) like 6 weeks ahead. The pool is actually a rooftop bar so when you like to dip the pool after a days work it is not possible, it closes at 5 PM. Actually the hotel restaurants and bars are not really for the hotel guests but more for outside visitors and allthough staff is trying, you don't have the feeling you are actually a guest of your own hotel.

We stayed here for my wife's 40th birthday and found it to be a small, discreet and vibrant hotel. We were welcomed by the hotel staff at reception who were very friendly and efficient. The room was small and at the back of the hotel but suited us as we didn't plan to be in the room much.
We had breakfast in the hotel each morning which was adequate but not great... There was little choice and the same things each day which became tiresome after four days.
We found the rooftop bar to be a fabulous place to enjoy the evening as it offers a fantastic view of the empire state building but at $23 for a beer and a glass of wine a bit expensive. 
The day we were due to leave the hotel we found out JFK was closed due to hurricane Irene and our flight was cancelled. The reception staff were excellent in arranging things so we could stay in our room for another couple of days (which we paid for). 
Without boring you with details of the horrendous service provided by Aer Lingus we had to return to the hotel after we had left and they were happy to secure our cases until we left (again) for the airport.
Overall I found the staff there excellent, very friendly and helpful and I would recommend this hotel to anyone as it offers an ideal location for anyone wanting to be close to Times Square etc.
PS - the Concierge arranged two tickets to see Billy Elliott and for them to be brought to the hotel for that evening.... Excellent
I stayed 2 nights to enjoy Christmas in NY. I never even needed a taxi cause the location is perfect. Hotel rooms are lovely & spotless. Can't wait until next time!

review_title: Awful - ruined by a manager who simply thought we weren't cool enough to speak to him.
review_text: The rudest hotel manager I have ever met in any hotel anywhere. Arrogant, patronising and aggressive.

I was preparing myself for the fast-paced, Ã¼ber-efficient, transactional process of a check in and stay at a Times Square hotel that really comes across as rude. It is New York, after all. What I found was an incredibly friendly, service-oriented lady at the front desk, Vicky, who really did dispell my prejudices about NYC. Rarely do you find someone who goes above and beyond like she did in any industry, much less at a hotel. I will stay at this hotel again for future meetings because she and her colleagues.

I have stayed in them all around times Sq (double tree, Marriott, W)
And the CP out does them... Sorry but true... Great room (large corner king) but what made me write this review was the service and workers there... I decided to take my son to NYC for the weekend and they all treated him so good and so nice always making sure we were comfortable and happy... I will def be going back numerous times and I will always stay here!!!
Thank you all, well worth the money...
David...

Stayed in hotel for three days due to a business trip in your York and had a very nice time. 
The personnel is very cooperative and friendly, rooms are clear with big tv sets and nice view. Free wifi also provided.
Hotel location is a must as you can explore the whole soho area on foot. Definitely recommend David burker kitchen restaurant.
My fiance booked a room for us an hour in advance and Louis and Ahmad did a great job with accommodating us and making sure our stay was far beyond or expectations. I will definitely be back.

review_title: Will return. Very clean, modern, comfortable, good value.
review_text: I come to NY for business and will tack on some leisure. This hotel is in a central location, is very convenient to Penn Station, and has been updated recently. The room is generous for NY. Closet space is very limited so more than three suits and four shirts hanging would be tight. There were three decent size drawers so plenty ofnspace for non-hanging items. Tabletop ironing board was not easynto use but functional. No space in frig for your own stuff - it is all mini-bar. Continental breakfast is excellent with fresh fruit, cereals, yogurt, hardboiled eggs, cold cuts (truly continental, although Europeans will be disappointed by the American style cured meats).

Bar longue sul tetto dell'omonimo hotel. Posizione da sogno, prezzi da incubo...ma NY Ã¨ cosÃ¬. Se vi avanzano 100$ un aperitivo in due ci sta ! Scenografico. A un passo da Central Park 
Very cool. Tra grattacieli e la 5* strada proprio sotto. Bandierona USA che garrisce nel vento... Ci sono stato ed era Dicembre, la magia delle feste in una cittÃ  dove succede tutto e tutto succede!
Da provare una volta nella vita!

review_text: The Crowne Plaza certainly lived up to our expectations. The location, friendliness of staff, and rooms (spacious) were excellent. We really enjoyed our stay and definitely will be coming back. The location was perfect for shows , restaurants and shopping.

Stayed here for 5 nights. Lovely room with view of Empire State. Cocktails on Roof are a must. Good breakfast set us up for days walking the city. Very quiet room (good nights sleep) and good facilities incl free wifi. Dinner in restaurant also very good, although wine quite expensive. Would definitely recommend.

review_title: VERY SAFE and honest employees at the Crown!
review_text:
I checked in and left my laptop case laying down and Emron the front desk person took care of it in a very professional manner and turned it right over to head of security and security guys Abdul and Rueben were right on top of the situation. 
What a blessing to still have honest people. Thank you Crown Plaza for hiring people of integrity. Hard to find anymore but I found it at your hotel. 
Very thankful and blessed.
Tom

We stayed at this hotel a couple of nights in April. If this is your frist stay in New york City, you will be overwelmed with the location and the view over Times Square. If you have been in New york several times, you might wanna find something less touristed. Be sure to get a room with Times Square view. Overall a nice hotel.

We stayed at the Metro for 6 days in December for my daughters 21st birthday.
Hotel rooms were very clean and comfortable, the bed was very comfy, flat screen tv, fridge, air con coffee maker etc. Tasteful decor.
Bathroom was very small but shower was large and powerful.
Complimentary breakfast was great, just enough choice and plenty of everything. Tea and coffee available all day and night in lounge was a real bonus.
Managers cheese and wine on Tuesday evenings is a very nice touch, loads to eat and drink if you want it and a chance to chat to managers.
Location was brilliant. Round corner from Empire State Building, and what a sensational view from the roof terrace, and about 50 yards from Macy's front door and all the shopping around it. Felt very safe and friendly area.
Very short walk to Times Square and can walk to central park if you're in the mood for the walk.
Would recommend this hotel, not the cheapest or the largest but good value when you consider breakfast is included and excellent location for most of tourist areas.

We stayed for 7 nights in this hotel in Dec 10 through to Jan 2011. The hotel is situated slap bang in the middle of everything. It was a 10 minute stroll to Times Square, 5 mins to the nearest subway and had a 24 hour deli around 2 mins away. The hotel served a full continental breakfast between 7 and 10 every morning and the bar on the roof is a must with great views of the city. Very helpful staff. Only down side was no room service. A+

This is a perfect location, 10 minutes from Central Park walking and 10 minutes to the Empire State. Ask for a corner room when you get their to get a panoramic view of New York. The staff will do anything to help. The food is very expensive in the hotel but you have lots to choose from near you. I spent hours trying to decide what hotel to stay to book in New York, I'm very glad I choose this.

review_title: Good value for manhattan. Great location
review_text: Location walking distance from times squares, broadway central park and shopping areas. Staff very helpful as well

The location of the hotel is fabulous, the rooms are quite good and clean, free wi-fi at the lobby, nice view to the river, good prices at the restaurant. The cons, is that the lobby is always crowdy, no bellboy available to assist.

This hotel is absolutely gorgeous, it is clean, modern and very stylish. 
The rooms were more than big enough, the bathroom and the shower was divine. We had a massive flat screen TV and plenty to watch. The bed was big and soft, trust me I did not want to get out of it.
We got woken up the first night by noise outside, but that was not a fault of the hotel, but it didn't take us long to get back to sleep.
The breakfast was delicious, a good choice of cereals, bagels, muffins, yogurts juice etc, it really kept us going way past lunch, although we had a coffee machine in our room tea and coffee was available 24/7 in the breakfast room.
The gym was refreshing and handy, and very neat. The rooftop was breathtaking, as we couldn't get out on the street for the thanksgiving day parade, we took loads of pictures from the roof top. The weather was really warm for November so we were out there most nights, the empire state building was right next to us, it's amazing at night.
The staff are all extremely accommodating and nothing was too much for any of them, this hotel is absolutely outstanding.
I cannot recommend this hotel enough, 3 stars is totally unjustified, more like 4.5 - 5 star easliy. When I return to NY I will definitely be staying here, and I recommend you do to.

review_title: I'd forgotten how great this hotel was
review_text: I haven't stayed at the Hotel Metro for about 3 years and had forgotten what a little gem it is. The rooms are very comfortable and the breakfast is great; particularly the red velvet muffins, they're huge! Thank for a wonderful stay.

Really great hotel in the heart of it all. Walk to Central Park, Fifth Av, Times Square, etc. Modern room with a great view, nice lobby bar and great breakfast. I would highly recommend as you don't feel like the hustle and bustle and sometimes obnoxious T'S is right outside the door!

My honest preference for location would be somewhere a bit quieter and less packed, such as the meat packing district. However as we were going to a few shows, this location was great as we could just walk right out. 
The hotel itself is spotless and remodeled, so it is very modern. The bar is great and the restaurant has a delicious menu, as we did eat there one night. The room a good size. And the gym! Wow. A real gym with a real weight room, absolutley huge, for that reason alone I would return. 
The reasons I did rate this place higher was mainly due to the plumbing. There was practically no water pressure in the shower and hot water was a bit of a crap shoot. The tap turned in two directions and both were "cold". There was a sweet spot that if you hit it just right (depending on time of day) where we could have a reasonably warm shower. That was a bit of a drag. Our toilet also had issues flushing and then it finally just stopped. So that morning we had to go to the lobby to use a restroom. We left a note for housekeeping (right on the toilet, pretty hard to miss) and went out for the day. We came back for a short break around 3pm and the room still was not serviced, so again we had to use the lobby. We went out again and got back around 9 pm and the room was serviced, and the note was still sitting on top of the toilet. So housekeeping neither cleaned the toilet, nor requested maintenance. So unfortunately we learned if you have an issue contact maintenance directly - and they did respond when we called but at 9:30 pm at night it was a drag. 
The other caveat is I do not suggest breakfast there! There are many great, clean, affordable, non greasy diners around. I went there alone my first day as my husband was working. I ordered oatmeal , fruit, coffee and a side of eggs. I was told they could not give me a side of eggs I would have to order a complete breakfast, so the buffet would be a better choice $$ wise. Which it was but with tax and tip my eggs and oatmeal cost 40$!!! Geez!!!! Even for New York that's nuts. I realize I only wanted very specific items, but even looking at the less than stellar other choices it's really not worth it. It's a mediocre at best selection. Go to a great diner instead. 
Other than those 2 caveats, which for me are lessons learned for next time, it's a very convenient place to stay.

review_title: Very nice with a few caveats
review_text:
We stayed here for a week. The location was central and easy to find from train station. Rooms were extremely clean and well appointed. We staed in a superior queen room on the 12th floor.
Downsides for us: room was always stiflingly hot even when noisy a/c unit was running and the room was very loud. We were there in October and the days weren't all that warm. From the a/c fan, to the street noise (windows need to be weather-stripped), to the housekeeping cart parked outside our door, the loud noise meant we didn't sleep very well. It's unfortunate, because everything else about the hotel worked well.
This was an expensive room that provided a clean and comfortable stay, but with a lack of sleep. Oddly torn: high marks, but hard to recommend.

review_title: Nice, but for the price you expect more
review_text: The room was nice, recently redecorated. For 300 plus a night would have expected not to have a cleanliness issue with the room,or to see my neighbors room service outside the door when i checked in, and again the same tray there the next morning. Location is great and rooms are prettier than Marriott Marquis. Just be on the lookout for service and cleanliness.

Situato downtown,l'albergo ha un'atmosfera molto "cool" e moderna. Frequentato da gente giovane, le camere sono molto luminose e abbastanza spaziose( cosa non comune a New york).Belli i bagni e la "rain shower". Il plus e'sicuramente la roof pool, benchÃ© piccola e' eccezionale nei mesi estivi. Divertente anche il roof bar e molto buono il ristorante David Burke con tavoli anche in terrazza.

In the middle of everything, this very old hotel provide little service. Just TSquare and nothing more. Rooms are very tired, toooo looooud from the elevator and other rooms!!! Avoid it for long stay!

review_title: Typical Times Square chain hotel - average but incredibly expensive relative to quality!
review_text: Great location but absolute average at top end prices

review_title: Very comfortable and wonderful service. Clean!
review_text: Great hotel. Staff was very nice and the rooms were clean. I loved the bed, fell asleep as soon as I got in it. The bathroom was nice with a really great shower. The only thing to remember is to ask about the counter space in the bathroom. Some rooms have no counter space and as a girl I had no where for my make-up and hair stuff. Otherwise, I loved it!
Very comfortable, lovely staff friendly and helpful. Amazing location. Brilliant breakfast.

After coming from a bad hotel in another state, this hotel was refreshing. Clean and surprisingly friendly cleaning staff, small but well thought-out rooms with everything that you need. Great showers. Quiet even tho near Times Square
Stolen my iPad and Mac book air in 5/october/11 and the hotel don't reimbursement yet.

review_title: Good location.. Won't be back though!
review_text:
All in all a disaponting stay. My girlfriend and I headed to NYC with my brother and his fiancÃ©. We had been to the city a few times before and always like to try new hotels. As it was a first trip for my bro we stayed in time square which if it is your first time the only place to stay. 
The hotel this time was very disappointing. As we were on a flying 4day visit from ireland we upgraded to the concierge level for what I was hoping would be more comfort. As it turned out there didn't seem to be any added value for the expensive rates we paid, nearly 650 dollars per night. 
I know most rooms in NYC can be small and this lived up to that. 
The breakfast room was not exactly equipped with a lot of options and was not worth the extra money. The concierge was helpful when required but all in all I would say we all left feeling a little ripped off. 
3/5 at best and the location counts for a big portion of that.

review_title: Great room, wonderful service, and perfect location
review_text: The hotel was beautiful, the rooms were large and well appointed. The staff was beyond helpful. The only problem we had was that they serve before dinner drinks on the entire lobby. When we returned to meet our car we had no place in the lobby to wait. The staff was very accomodating, however, and made arrangemements to wait in another area.

I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone visiting the big apple! I very much enjoyed staying in the quirky soroundings of the Royalton hotel & would definitely go back. The staff here have a laid back attitude but do go out of their way to deliver excellent service. The rooms are small but the layout and design more than make up for it. Super comfortable beds and luxiourious bedding was heavenly...complimentary use of an iPad in my room made contacting staff easy and was very useful indeed for accessing the Internet which was free!! Yay!

I'll start by saying rooms in NYC are expensive, so my review accepts that fact and doesn't punish the hotel for it.
Great location with subway station on the block and one stop away from Times Square. Subway is best mode of transportation here and having it on the same block, and three blocks from Penn station, is a good thing. Grab a pass for how long you're staying, it's worth it.
One block away from Empire State Building, Macy's.
Rooms are clean and comfortable, but they are small, at least the one I stayed in. Although, NYC is like Vegas; you dont come here to hang out in a hotel room:) Nice shower stall with multiple shower heads.
Bed is comfortable, slept really well.
I'd recommend it.

We were upgraded to a suite and shortly after settling in a porter arrived at our room with a bottle of cava and two glasses, very nice touch. The staff are helpful and friendly and really looked after us. The room is fabulous, the breakfast is great and the Metro Grill looks great, we didn't eat there though as we didn't have time. Location wise, couldn't be better, literally around the corner from the empire state and a ten minute walk from Times Square.
If you're looking for a good hotel that won't break the bank in central New York, Hotel Metro is it.

Stayed here my last trip to NYC. 
Great hotel, stunning decor, especially in the lobby. 
Would certainly consider another stay here.

review_title: Overpriced, rude staff and small rooms.
review_text: This hotel is right in the middle of the action which is far too busy for me. The rooms are quite small for the price, I struggled to fit a bag next to the bed. Some of the staff, particularly the security staff, were quite rude. The room for which I paid $300/night went up to $560 for 9/11.

Hotel squeaky clean. Staff super friendly. Location terrific. Subway lines on both 6th and 7th Ave. Talk about convenient. Also, the street was really quiet. 
If there is one knock, the breakfast selection is really limited. Then again, you GET breakfast. Of course, I really hate that they serve pre-packed bagels in NYC. With all the great bagel places you'd think they would use a local purveyor. Oh well.

review_title: Great location, friendly staff, good food!
review_text:
Got there and offered a free upgrade which is always nice but that aside the location is great - right on times square 
Only ate there once for dinner on the first night and thought it was really nice with a relaxed atmosphere at a reasonable price and added bonus overlooks times square( hint I'd eat here over the view resteraunt at the Marquis any day! Better food food better price better view) 
Anyway good place will stay again big thanks to hotel for great time

This hotel was great. The room was big and clean. Good breakfast and the rooftop was awesome. The only negative thing was the elevators didn't have AC. Otherwise this was a great place and I would come back.

review_title: Excellent choice for quality accommodations and excellent location.
review_text:
We stayed here for 4 nights at the end of July with our 2 sons ages 10 and 14. It was their first trip to NY from LA. I found the Hotel with the help of an agent on Newyorkluxuryhotels.com. They got us a very good rate and helped us choose the right accommodations. We had a corner room on a higher floor with wonderful views and a quiet atmosphere. While I agree with some reviews that the rooms are small, they are actually good sized for NYC. The staff was very friendly and helpful, the rooms clean and newly renovated with comfortable (but small) double beds. The restaurant was good and the location unbeatable if you want to be central and in the action. Everything is just outside - you are steps from the theater district, restaurants, Rockefeller Plaza and the subway. The bathrooms were nice and well stocked although our bathtub needed some refinishing. 
I would highly recommend the hotel and I would stay here again.

My first impression has not been great. The room across the hall is under construction. The mess from this is all over the hallway. I requested this to be cleaned up, but nothings been done. My room was alright. A bit cold actually, with no thermostat to be found? 
Tonight we tried to order a movie. Upon placing the order, I receive the message that says I need to speak to the front desk. It took me 20 minutes just to speak to the front desk. They actually would not answer the phone. I used the button on the phone labeled Guest Assistance. When I did speak to them, they decided they have to come to the room. My wife and have to get dressed so that we can have a midnight stranger just so we can watch a movie.
Since that call, we got dressed. I downloaded the trip advisor app. I wrote this review. This all took about 25 minutes. They have not arrived yet.
(To be continued)

review_title: Wonderful stay from checking to checkout
review_text: We had a corner room very roomy and looked out at the New Years Eve ball in Times Square. Service quick and efficient. Ate in restaurant which was very good. Elevators state of the art and fast. Very cool would stay again anytime.

review_title: Fantastic stay! Well worth the wait!!
review_text: I stayed in the Hotel metro from the 4th may 2011 for 5 nights with my parents for my mum's 60th! I have to say it was absolutely fantastic! We booked a double room and got upgraded to a family room which was fab :) it was huge! It was in prime location and walking distance to everything! Times square 5 to 10 mins away! Subway on your doorstep! Empire state perfect view especially from the roof terrace which was also great! And Macy's on your doorstep! Where I spent lots of money :) continental breakfast was great we looked forward to that every morning! Staff were fabulous even reccomended places to eat!! All in all it was great! I will definitely be returning to this hotel! Hopefully with my friends next time :) thoroughly recommend it!

review_title: Great location, nice finishes, some flaws
review_text:
My wife had a two day class at the AMA building attached to the hotel, so her company was more than willing to generously put us up in the Crowne Plaza for a night. We arrived well before check-in time, but the front desk was willing to let us pre-register and we were able to store our bags with the concierge. I came back at 3 and the room was ready.
We had a king corner room. There is an ample size bathroom to the left of entrance with a big shower (no tub), toilet, and sink. Straight ahead from the door is a desk and then a walk-in closet. To the left of the closet is a dresser with an HDtv. Opposite the dresser is the king bed. To the left of the bed is a chez lounge and to the left of that is a huge window with a view of the West Side.
The main flaw was that this was a non-smoking room on a non-smoking floor, yet there was a smell of smoke in the air. Apparently, this must be a recurring issue as were provided with a little kit that included "linen spray." The smoke smell was even more pronounced in the bathroom, where there is no smoke detector (btw - if you have to smoke so bad that you are doing it in a hotel bathroom, you have a problem). The smell was even more intense when you opened the toilet! Later, my wife went to put in the bathrobe hanging in the bathroom and it reeked of smoke! My conclusion is that the previous guest was smoking in the bathroom and used the toilet as an ashtray. As for the bathrobe, the housekeeper probably never changed it out since the previous guest likely did not use it.
Normally, this kind of thing would warrant a lower rating for the hotel, but we had a good night's sleep and the room was otherwise clean and in good repair.

Very much enjoyed my trip to NY, and even more so because of this hotel. Right in the heart of everything but safe and relaxing. All meals especially breakfast were outstanding, staff were so polite and helpful and couldn't do enough for you. Bedrooms were spacious and comfortable and I slept soundly. Would defiantly return

review_title: Better then I expected. Location,location, location.
review_text: We had to attend a formal Gala and I just didn't want to have to travel around town in a floor length gown. We sucked it up and splurged on a room for two night at $500/ night. It was totally worth it. The location can't be beat. The room was spacious and clean. Even being right a Times Square it was very quiet in our room. The staff was okay. Could have been more helpful and knowledgeable about subway, but we managed. If you want to splurge and have some fun I NYC it is worth it.

review_title: Luxurious, but a few issues overshadow the good parts
review_text:
Hotel is gorgeous and luxurious. Very clean. Nice linens and comfortable beds. Restaurant was good as was room service. 
A couple of issues overshadowed the good parts, and I probably would not stay there again. Within ten minutes of checking in, someone from the hotel knocked on the door and before i could answer they just barged in. Once she saw I was in the room she turned and left. Same thing happened in the morning at 8am! Then AGAIN at about 10:00, but I yelled at them not to come in that time. WTF?! In my view there was no legitimate reason for these people to be coming in my room and that is evident by the fact that they turned and left immediately. They didn't say oh, we're here to fix this or that. Also, the towel bars in the bathroom were missing; just the brackets were on the wall. One of the closets had about 7 or 8 pair of old shoes in it. Weird.

review_title: If you must be in Houston ...
review_text: It's a boutique hotel in Houston. The people watching in the lobby is priceless. The rooms are sweet if small. Ask for a room with a patio and you can let in the fresh air (Houston air mind you). The restaurant has great coffee and pancakes. The shuttle makes this a great choice over staying near that big mall (nightmare traffic over there). Cookies and candy in the lobby plus free wi-fi. Yippie y'all.

review_text:

If your after a cheap stay this may not be the best option, wouldn't call it expensive but cheaper is available in NY but if your anything like me you wouldn't really care where you stayed, it's New York, give me a card board box n I'd be happy.

review_title: Location is the only good thing
review_text:
Being In Times Square, that is the only good thing about this hotel. The propery is way too big to get really good service. The rate you pay to stay here is not worth the lack of amenities. 
The rooms are pretty small, and the fee for wifi is also pricey. You are just paying for a name here. There are better deals out there.

This hotel is massive at nearly 2000 rooms, the level of service, personal interaction was surprisingly good. The location of Times Square is key but be prepared for a lot of energy at all times of day and night. We did not experience much noise from the street but I would imagine the lower floors might be a factor. We had a great view of the square from our room too. While here, try Juniors for cheesecake right across the street and Johns Pizza and 44th street (a 2 minute walk) Elevator system was great but expect some wait (not too much) at peak times. The lounge on the 8th floor had good appetizers and was a great place for nightcaps!

review_text: We booked a room for Thanksgiving (and the parade is great). The place was full-up and yet the staff were friendly and helpful. There is a significant up-charge for staying during thanksgiving, but it did not seem to translate to service. review_title: THE ONLY PLACE TO BE IN NEW YORK!!!
review_text: I searched for weeks prior to booking a hotel, because I was desperate to find a hotel that would be very quiet during the night. I understood that for New York, that was a near possible expectation... I persevered and found it! Crown plaza hotel guaranteed that they had double glazed sound proof windows, and for a times square location they were certain that I would sleep soundly! For a light sleeper like me, I could have sworn I was in a hotel in the middle of the country side! Not a sound!! I booked through a company called Magellan vacations and they were able to guarantee me a higher floor room, including breakfast and free wifi. The standard in cleanliness, service and quality was way above excellent. My experience was completely PERFECT. I stepped out of the hotel and was in the middle of the buzzing energy this amazing city exudes! Once inside, I had peace tranquility and luxury with Hudson river views to die for.The best of both worlds and more. Nothing could possibly beat this hotel, it ticks all the boxes. I have already recommended it to many friends and colleages because I am certain it is the best in times square. DO NOT STAY ANYWHERE ELSE!!!

Could you really ask for a better location? Right in the heart of time square! This was our second time and let me tell you the speedy elevator is fun among itself. It's super fast and get you to your room like a coaster ride. Guest service and check in are very kind and friendly. One guy who checked me in was nothing but great! He hooked it up on a weekend and upgraded our room for free! The rooms set up are a little weird looks like your on a cruise ship! Many many rooms! Our room was pretty until when we wantedto sleep! We asked for it, time square ball beaming into our room haha but worth the site. Totally a new year eve's room.
Right outside is the action love it!

Unica pecca non ci sono i pancakes a colazione che a NY mi aspettavo di trovare. Ma in generale veramente consigliabile e da riprovare in un prossimo viaggio.

We recently stayed here as we have in the past. The rooms are very nice. The bed was comfortable however the pullout sofa my kids had a flimsy mattress. Check in & check out was quick however retreiving our luggage after check out had an unacceptable wait (1/2 hour). The hotel is close to uptown & times square. Also near the subway & NY Penn station. Room was clean, comfortable, and quiet. Did not try the restaurant..too many other good places to eat close by. Try Hells Kit hen area only a few blocks away for some very good food.

Nuestra estancia en nueva York fue increÃ­ble, empezando desde el hotel. L ubicaciÃ³n es muy cÃ³moda, sobre todo si viajas con niÃ±os, dos estaciones del metro cercanas e infinidad de cosas por hacer yendo a pie, caminar por el area es muy agradable! El hotel nos dio un excelente servicio, definitivamente es EL hotel para quedarse en Manhattan.

I would have given this hotel a very good review, but for their elevators. First, let me tell you about the good: Location, location, location. This hotel IS Times Square. You are in the middle of everything. We did a Broadway show and the theatre was literally right next to the hotel. The hotel is huge. The room are at least adequate and some have great views. The fitness room is great with views over Times Square. 
Now for the bad: We stayed during Christmas week. The hotel was obviously busy. I stayed at the hotel many years ago and there were issues with the elevators. They installed a new, supposedly technologically superior system. It is a failure. We literally had to wait 15 to 20 minutes or more almost every time we attempted to take the elevators down to the 1st floor. To go up was much of the same. It is simply outrageous to pay the money you pay to stay at this hotel or any hotel for that matter and to literally feel trapped on your floor because you can't get an elevator to take you down. This hotel knows full well about this issue. The answer is simple. Don't fill all the rooms to avoid this issue. It is obvious the hotel is putting money far over the comfort of its guests. Sad. I am a Marriott Gold member and this is the worst Marriott experience I have ever had. By the way, while the concierge lounge is nice, the lines a horrendous when the hotel is busy and there is simply not enough seating. Once again, unacceptable.
I would recommend staying here in any remotely busy time if you enjoy spending your valuable time waiting for elevators for hours on end. Such a shame.

review_title: The hotel is old and not up to date clares to The price
review_text: Dont visit The topfloor lounge. Too expensive and no information about extra fee for view. The view is bad compared to other places NYC

Superior dubbelkamer aanrader. Elke dag lekker bijkomen van dagje NY. Metro downtown op 5 minuten lopen, giga supermarkt aan de overkant, ontbijt naast de deur, diners overal, comedyclub om de hoek. Echt super

review_title: Depends on what your looking for
review_text: Stayed in a suite for 2 days. If you are looking to stay in the heart of Times Square then stay here. If you are looking for a nice hotel that is clean and well maintained then stay away. The room was worn down and old, furniture looked beat up. The bathroom vent had so much dust on it that the hair barely came out of it. Housekeeping does the minimum when they clean. Not my type of hotel but it sure does attract a whole bunch of ppl.

I stay in hotels 60+ nights a year and am a huge hotel snob. The CP was amazingly quiet--the quietest hotel room I've ever stayed in--despite it's location right in Times Square!! The beds are great, too. Would definitely return.

We have just returned from a family holiday staying at the above hotel for a week. We found the location fantastic just off Times Square opposite the M&M's store. 
As we had our 13 and 10 year old with us we didn't use the bar or restaurant but they both looked lovely.
The swimming pool is very good but small (you will need to wear a swimming cap - you can buy one at the gym reception). The gym was being refurbished but still very good with great facilities. 
I would definitely stay there again.

review_title: Location, location, location, the place to stay in the City that never sleeps.
review_text:
Wow (overused phrase for the visit)! Â Location, location, location, right in the heart of the action; welcoming, safe, clean and comfortable. Â We, daughter (14) hubby and me stayed for 4 nights early April (a stop over on route to Florida) and had a wonderful time. Â My husband had booked it as a birthday treat for me (recommended by a colleague of mine). He contacted the hotel before we left England and they were kind enough to upgrade us to a higher floor (38th) with a spectacular view of the square (very little noise no disturbed sleep). The room was immaculate and spacious enough for our needs (plenty of space for 4 should you need it, 2 double beds, Â bathroom toiletries supplied, no fridge in room). We ate breakfast once at the hotel and the variety, portions, quality of the food, service and ambiance was excellent however expensive (couldn't justify price for Â 3 each day expect more would eat there if a better deal for guests). 
Reception and concierge desk were helpful, efficient and friendly. 
We ate breakfast at Mama Sarbo (buffet style) across the road which was ok but limited on choice and somewhat chaotic. Â Try Appleebees which was much better both in terms of food choice, quality and service (free coffee too) - a good price. Â Dinner at Mama Sarbo's was better and something of an experience (you help yourself and pay by the weight of your plate).
We bought the Citysights 2 day hop on and off bus pass (plus additional day added free). Â You save $5 on line but we bought from agent in blue jacket on the street outside the hotel and stepped straight on to the bus. Ticket included all the bus tours, ferry trip, cruise and we chose Empire State ticket. Â We paid separately for Rock ticket at the venue (picked up a $2 discount flyer for each of us at the tourist info bookcase in Applebees). 
Uptown and Downtown tours were great and guides very pleasant, helpful, knowledgeable and proud of their city. Â The audio system on the buses were a bit hit and miss which was a shame when it didn't work. Â Buses were frequent. Â The Brooklyn tour was poor as no stop and our guide didn't seem that interested in the city and was somewhat sarcastic and morose for the 50 mins. Â 
We didn't take the ferry trip as the queues were huge (tried Sat and Sun am). The 2 hour harbour cruise was well organised, comfortable and very informative with excellent photo opps of the city and Statue of Liberty (so didn't need to try a 3rd time for the ferry). Â Only qualms were no bus direct to the port so you have to walk (15 mins) from nearest stop and from 1 April there is a 5$ admin charge for each Citysights voucher (which we were not told about when we bought the tickets).
Empire State ticket worked well although did queue for security checks Â for 20 mins it wasn't too long (map and audio additional expense). Â The Rock was brilliant, much better organised, fewer people, panoramic views of the city, river and central park; map only 2$ and seating area if you want to dwell a while.
We stayed over a weekend and the Tks booths were really busy - though probably less of a wait than at immigration at JFK (see last para). We purchased tickets for Wicked from the Theatre box office - fantastic scenery and show. On Mon evening on a whim at 5pm (as no queue) we asked at the booths what shows they had tickets for and got 3 for Sister Act for less than we had paid for 1 for Wicked. Â Seats were ok, show lively and good fun which we throughly enjoyed. Â Â 
We loved New York - so much to see and do for all ages and interests (next time the museums). Â I can honestly say it was cleaner and felt safer than many of the cities we go to in the UK. Â WOW as the teenager said again !
One word of warning expect to spend 2hrs plus clearing immigration on your arrival at JFK. Â Insufficient staff to cope with volume of people (we counted 8 to 10 unmanned booths). Â Very poor conditions - no seats, Â 1 water fountain, Â toilets (though people worried about using them as might lose their place in line), extremely hot and uncomfortable and this was Spring hate to think what it's like in Summer. Felt really sorry for young and older people who were standing in line for such a long period (worst than any Disney Q). Â Staff were fine and doing a good job, just not enough of them ( we complained to the airline as we understand they can influence the situation). Don't let it put you off visiting just allow 3plus hours from landing to getting to your hotel if in Manhattan.
The front door guys are so friendly and helpful they make you feel like your visiting old friends! Not to mention that everything else was awesome too! GREAT TIMES

review_title: Great location and my travel will take me to New York several times and this is definitely where I will stay
review_text: This hotel meets all the criteria for a luxury hotel along with great staff and location. Will definitely stay here again

First, let me say that I am grateful to have had a room for the night. We were comped a room here by another Starwood property when we arrived at that property to find that the room that we had reserved (not a specific room, but ANY room) was not available. 
This property lives up to its trendy marketing and those travelers looking for what is advertised will not be disappointed.
Travelers requiring privacy in the bathroom should stay elsewhere. The bathroom walls are translucent glass and offer no privacy unless the bathroom is completely dark. There is no curtain or shade on the window walls and no obvious way to improvise with a sheet or blanket. So, plan on using the bathroom in the dark if you are a mixed sex two generation family that is used to privacy in the bathroom.
Travelers with aging eyesight, i.e. anyone over 40, and/or with depth perception issues, should also look elsewhere. The walls, carpet, furniture and glass are all the same color gray. There are no visual clues to help you find your way around the room and through the the hotel. 
Plan on feeling lost and/or walking into walls, windows, and furniture.
Travelers who prefer to avoid elevators should stay elsewhere. The lobby is on the 7th floor. There are no escalators and the stairs, I was told by the "whatever" desk, take you through the kitchens of the restaurant complex that occupies the floors below. There are only three elevators, so plan your time accordingly.
Be sure to ask for your coffee maker when you check in. And check to be sure that the paper cups they send you with it fit under the drip spout. Otherwise, you will be without your first cup of coffee while you are waiting for an elevator to get you out of the funhouse. Or, you could ask in total exasperation for a comped pot of brewed coffee and a real cup to be delivered to your room. I got the coffee and cup quickly, but do not know yet how much, if anything, I paid for it. The speed with which the coffee was sent up is why I gave the W a 4 star rating for service.
So, if a trendy bar and trendy decor are what you seek, by all means put the W on the top of your list. If you want bathroom privacy, don't like elevators, like your coffee in the room, and prefer not to feel as if you are lost in a carnival funhouse, stay elsewhere.
Can't say anything more than 5 stars across the board. Easy friendly check-in, great room, friendly employees. Can't wait to return next year.

review_title: Great location, but you pay for it
review_text:
The Marriott Marquis is right in the heart of Times Square, so you cannot beat the location.
We paid $549 per night for rather small rooms, but beyond that it was a clean, will maintained property.
My only large issue was the elevators really goofy, and we lost done vacation time waiting for them.

review_title: Visit the lobby bar - choose an other hotel!
review_text:
1. Rediculously small rooms
2. Hot water if lucky after 5 min wait
3. Tiny bathrooms toilet 10cm from shower and 2m from bed
4. Worn down rooms
5. Wannabe design - but old fashioned
6. Staff friendly, slow and helpful
7. Location, great for broadway shows
8. Noice from street coming to rooms even high up- old fashioned glassing not sound proof
9. Restauratr blue fin- good food, but due to air con problem felt like an outdoor skiing lunch
10. Don't go with kids, reception noicy, great if you want to party with friends
Finally: Cannot recommend a stay to anyone used to staying in nice hotels!

If you are going to NYC for fun and you want to be at the heart of Manhattan in a cool hip place....this offers it all.
Excellent Bluefin restaurant and hip bar in the 7th floor lobby....and GREAT location.
We will stay there again for sure.

review_title: Wow! This hotel has it all & great location..
review_text: Wow this hotel is not only in a great location, 40 ft off of Times Square but also is very clean and nice! I had never stayed in a W before, but look forward to it again. 5 star all the way-

review_title: Cool Hotel but needs some renovation quite urgently to really deliver the W promise
review_text: Very good location and very trendy, excellent restaurant. Service can be improved and the whole interior should be renovated to be truly W like. Nevertheless definitely one of the better hotels in new york. Alternatives could be some of the boutique hotels in meat packing or lower east side. But overall we enjoyed the hotel and ofcourse the city

Great spot to stay while visiting NY! It's like a mini city inside 4 walls!! Lobby is a lovely place to sit and just people watch! Fab bar with fantastic water feature, two Starbucks within the hotel so handy to pop down on the elevator for breakfast without having to put your shoes on. You can book broadway plays, use the media centre, go to the gym, have dinner in the View restaurant and get a 360 degree panoramic view of NYC while u eat, all without even stepping outside the front door. Only drawback is that it's a bit expensive.

Right in the center of it all on Times Square. It can best be described as crazy. Bar scene is young hip and (im?)posing. Service at the front desk is good but overwhelmed. The rooms are adequate. Bathroom walls? Slightly see-through. But? Well worth the averages for the best location if you want to experience Times Square, Broadway, The Rockettes, The Frick Museum and Central Park all within steps or walking distance of this controlled madhouse of fun!
