The Check in lobby is horrible but pales in comparison to what W refers to as a "Spectacular" king room. The room was small, even for NYC, with a bathroom that barely has enough space to place a hair brush. The shower was a cruel joke as I had to crouch down to get my head under the shower head that spit out barely a mist. The walls shake when other guests closed their doors. The room lighting looks "cool", but you can't get enough light to even read a room service menu on the bed. I honestly felt like we stayed in low income housing. 
Things in NYC are expensive and small but this hotel is horribly overpriced with ZERO attention to basic services.

Staff friendly and professional. But rooms have deteriorated substantially from my stay last year. Dirty carpets, non-functional fixtures, peeling paint, wallpaper and stained tile equals intentional poor maintenance. I asked for different room and it was worse....all that luxury for $600/night.
I would strongly urge readers to steer clear of this hotel until they realize how badly theur reputation becomes when they don't maintain quality of the rooms

El personal es muy amigable y dispuesto a ayudar. Todos los hoteles en NY son de alto precio y este hotel quizÃ¡ tambiÃ©n lo sea si lo comparas con otras ciudades. Pero para ser NY y para su ubicaciÃ³n, el precio es muy conveniente.
Un poco antiguo como los demÃ¡s hoteles de esta zona pero en los Ãºltimos tres aÃ±os he visto que estÃ¡n renovÃ¡ndolo poco a poco, lo cual estÃ¡ muy bien.
Definitivamente mi elecciÃ³n en NY! y si necesita taxi para que lo recoja o lleve a cualquiera de los aeropuertos de la ciudad, el hotel puede enviarle uno. Personalmente prefiero que me recoja Ramiro, un amigo ecuatoriano muy trabajador, buen carÃ¡cter y atinado en su comportamiento.

Just stayed here for the first time and was sorely disappointed. The only redeeming points were the Bliss toiletries and that I was on business travel and didn't have to pay the ridiculous rate of $459/nt. (I would also be remiss if I didn't acknowledge the Concierge who gave an excellent recommendation for sushi in the vicinity.)
When I arrived mid afternoon, the room wasn't ready so I opted to leave my bag with the bell staff who seemed to be struggling with the lobby full of other guests also wanting to check their bags. After a twenty minute wait, they finally took my bag, only to get a call that my room was ready two minutes later.
Other challenges were the darkly lit lobbies, hallways and elevators (which I missed half of the time because there's no bell signaling they've arrived) and the incessant club/hypno music that follows you around the hotel. Perhaps the most disappointing was the baby roach who settled in on the pillow beside me as I prepared for bed. I was so tired that I threw the pillow on the chaise and tried not to think about the little roach (and his friends) partying up in my very expensive hotel room. 
Will not be staying here again.

It's a very busy hotel in the heart of times square but theres nothing like it. Its the amusement park of all hotels.certain Floors have restaurants, bars, gym is huge! All and all the rooms are clean and huge! The beds of course are phenomenal enjoy your stay! I know I did!

Perfect location in midtown Manhattan , walking distance from Central Park over looking Times Square. Impeccable friendly service. Extremely clean very spacious rooms. Very reasonable rates. THE BEST HOTEL IN THE CITY!!!

Room type not available had to stay in a room, change rooms the next day! No fitness centre, they have a gym run by another company $10 a day to use it! They gave me a conplimentry buffet breakfast and $60 in bar vouchers for the room stuff up. Everything else pretty good

We stayed here dec 18 2011. Very nice hotel and I am extremely fussy. Very clean rooms and very very comfortable beds. Would definitely stay again! My only complaint would be I wish they had a little more lively bar area.

review_title: Awesome if you don't mind a view of brick wall.
review_text: We stayed at The Michangelo the first weekend in Dec. The location of this hotel is perfect. Walking distance to everything ie times square, bway shows, Rockefeller center, 5th Ave, central park. We were given an upgrade when we checked in. Absolutely beautiful room, very spacious, well decorated, 1 1/2 baths. Just no view. Service was excellent. Answered every question, assisted when needed. We didn't eat in the restaurant or room service. We did use the mini bar in our room. Of course it's pricey, but it's there if you need it. The Duke store is next door, if you need snacks, or a meal, they have everything! $12.99 for Internet I felt was a little cheesy considering what you pay for the room. Overall very good experience!!

Can't beat the Times Square location. Nothing else stands out as being better than just good. Room was hot (75 degrees) upon check in. Thermostat had a hand lettered note taped to it that said "no touch air". Since I was heading out for a couple of hours I stopped by the front desk to ask them to take care of it. Upon return, no change, note still there, so I "touched air". Only made the slightest of differences. Irritating.

review_title: I felt like a character out of Madmen.
review_text: And that is a very good thing! The 50's/60's elegance appears heavy, but is actually a warm and cozy welcome and change from the more modern bland hotels. Large room with 3 sitting chairs, huge tub, spacious bathroom. Excellent location for any NY agenda. Close to 5th ave shopping, 9th ave international cuisine restaurant row, and literally ON Times Square (saw Mamma Mia theatre from my window). Staff the friendliest possible. (and i got a great deal on the Booking).

review_title: The Michelangelo Hotel: the best stay in New York!
review_text: Guests are so well treated, that you never want to leave. Courtesy and professionalism are cornerstones of this magnificent hotel.

review_title: Fantastic location, helpful friendly staff, and clean rooms.
review_text: My husband and I stayed at The Crowne Plaza for my first trip to NYC. It's literally in the heart of the city and where all the action is. It's within walking distance to all of the broadway attractions, and any restaurant you can think of. Our room was very clean, and the staff at the front desk were friendly and attentive. We asked to change rooms because our original room was too close to the elevator which would have likely kept us up all night, as we're light sleepers. The staff gave us another room far from the elevator which was just as nice as the first room. We noticed the rooms were spacious ad clean, an provided a wonderful view of the city. It was so quiet in the room, it was difficult to believe we were so close to Times Square. It took us just five minutes to walk to a Broadway show. And just ten minutes to the subway station, or Central Park. We will definitely stay here again, and would highly recommend to anyone looking for a great location to stay while in NYC.

Great boutique style hotel. Good for those that have never been in NY 'cause it's located in times square near every most tourist attractions.
Very clean.

I thought the hotel was great the room was clean and rooms was surprisingly big. The location was great it was very close Central Park and Times Square. The only problem we had was with the bathroom door it is a sliding door and was very difficult to open and close. We called down to the lobby and they were on it right away.

review_title: Old world charm in central location
review_text:
After arriving jet-lagged and exhausted, was relieved to receive a complimentary room upgrade and even managed to successfully extend our stay by one night upon check-in. Room size was surprising large for such a very central location . Appreciated the little touches like nightly turndown service (weather forecast and chocolates), bath-tub to unwind after a long day of sight-seeing, separate vanity dressing table outside the bathroom and the complimentary warm scones/fab coffee to start the day. A pity that there was no complimentary wi-fi and the daily paper was only delivered on the last day of stay. overall, it was a generally good hotel stay. Close proximity to key sights and good base to start exploring
NYC.

The hotel was very quite. The lobby was very nicely decorated. We even got upgraded to a JR. suite. It seemed perfect for our marathon weekend. However, we were very disappointed when we got to out room. It seemed like it had not been updated since the mid 90s. Also we had a few of a wall/rooftop (not a big deal). For the price we paid it seemed like the room just have been more modernly decorated. The room was clean. The gym was decent but nothing great. The best part about the hotel was the location (close to Times Square, 5th Ave, Roc Center and Central Park). Also the younger doorman(did not catch his name) was extremely helpful. Maybe we got the older room bc we booked via Expedia. Regardless, I woul ask for an updated room when checking in.

We were more than pleased with this hotel, we had high expectations after hearing good things and we weren't dissapointed! The location is perfect, walk out of the hotel and you are right on Times Square.
Very modern and clean, comfy beds, good view from room, high up so heard no noise at night.
When we come back to New York we will definitely stay here again and I would recommend this place to any one.

Great hotel in great location,staff very friendly rooms amazing got upgraded to a spectacular room on second to last floor if building was fab.Recommend this hotel for any special treat as no not the cheapest but a big WOW factor can be had at the W

I travel a lot and stay in hotels very often and this was one of the WORST. How can this be a four star hotel! It should not be more than one star! I returned to my room now to see that the bathroom was not cleaned. They only changed my towels and left the floor unwiped, kept the used shapmoo and conditioner and did not care to put new ones, the floor was not vacummed and there was white dust on the carpet and the bed sheets were not replaced! I called the room service immedietly and conplaibed to the manager who refused to give me the name of the person who was incharge of cleaning my room. She told me to call tomorrow morning and speak to someone else who might be able to give me the information I need because I won't let them after paying more than $ 1400 for 2 nights!!!!! 
So, the manager send two housekeepers to clean the room and guess what! They didn't even care to replace the used shampoo and conditioner with new ones. I called the house keeper immediatly and she went to get me new ones!!!! I have taken photos and will certainly reach the manager early morning!!! They really ruined my vacation!!!! What a waste of money. 
And by the way, if you request a cup of hot water, they would charge you $2.50!

review_title: Hotel made our stay in New York perfect.
review_text: We stayed 5 nights in the hotel paid for with reward points and had two rooms. As a gold card member our rooms were upgraded and were amazing. They were both on 30th floor and were newly refurbished, one was an enormous corner room which looked down onto Broadway and the lights between the two sides of the street. The other room was a regular sized room which was large enough for two double beds and a sofa. The view was stunning it looked towards the clock and police dept and because of its position you could see time square with nothing blocking the view and no.other tall buildings nearby it really was awesome (room 3035). We had free breakfast in the concieege lounge which included a good selection but was only available Mon - fri. We also ate breakfast in the hotel restaurant (expensive as you would expect but good food) and juniors (across the road) which was also good. We did not go to the view restaurant but the newly refurbed bar overlooking time sq was nice. Overall the stay was excellent the rooms were stunning and the hotel was big but nicely done. We stayed over the same weekend as hurricane Irene so the hotel was full and people had to stay in more than usual due to no subway and most shops restaurants and bars were closed. The hotel coped with this well and it did not feel overly busy especially considering its size. We had a fantastic time I would love to return.

I stay in NYC often; a few times per month. I try out different places in a search for the best value. This is my second room after checking in. Upon entering my initial room, there was a pair of underwear hanging from the lampshade (an obvious remnant from a prior guest). I am not a prude but that was just a little unappetizing. Staff was nice about it...gave me a new room...promising a free breakfast buffet voucher under my door in 5 minutes. Well, two hours later, I still didn't have one. I did call and they delivered it. In my new room, the television is not working properly. After two phone calls, somebody finally came up. He saw that it was not working and told me that somebody from the front desk will call me. I was called and told that I would be moved to a 3rd room. It is now midnight...and that's where I am in this narrative.

review_title: Top locatie, maar overall teveel tekortkomingen
review_text:
De locatie was werkelijk prima. Dicht in de buurt van Central Park, Time Square, Empire state en de betere zaken op 5th AV. 
Helaas was dat wel het beste van allemaal. De kamers waren bij aankomst niet helemaal schoon (haren in douche en wastafel). Kamers zijn zwaar aan vernieuwing toe, gaten zaten in de deuren en verf bladderde van kozijnen af. Daarbij waren de kamers (en het hele hotel) zeer warm en moeilijk koel te krijgen.
De enorme kakkerlak op de laatste dag was het toppunt. 
Locatie maakte veel goed maar niet genoeg voor een aanbeveling.

It was our first time staying at a W hotel and we were not impressed. Our room was supposed to be fabulous, but was lacking in all categories. Nice getting passed the facade of the glitz and glamor of the hotel lobby, you realize quickly that it is no more than a La Quinta in disguise. The room was dirty at best with dust on the window sill, fingerprints on all the glass/stainless steel and cracks in the glass trashcan. The room is very small for the price and the view isn't anything to brag about.

review_title: Monolithic hotel, great location, poor service
review_text:
We stayed here on a package deal with the QM2 transatlantic cruise from Southampton. 
Hotel is right on the middle of the action so fantastic if you want to be at the centre of manic NYC at it's best, but not great if you want a quieter stay.
Staff civil , but not overly helpful. Room was dated but spacious.
Corbetts Ln, Caerphilly, UKgain, great location, but there are better hotels for less money in New York.

review_title: Great location, a hotel to sleep not to stay
review_text: Location is fabulous. Just around the corner of Times Square. Hotel interior design is trendy but as a result light is very dimmed and gives you the feeling to be in a cave. Rooms are okay (small and missed the coffee maker) but not great and the promised spectacular view is so-so. Service of rooms was very good. The staff was very helpful but as well very young. The facilities of the hotel are limited. The bar is not very inviting and the one and only restaurant rather small. As such a good place to have a bed down town in NY but not a hotel to spend much time in.

Times Square is reviled by New Yorkers, but for first time visitors like us you cannot beat the location: broadway at your steps, the park within walking distance...
You could say the same about the W: my NY friends never set foot in it, but NFL rookies and out of towners are bound to love it. It is far from perfect, actually quite filthy (but so is the city), and it drools cheesiness, with neon lights and translucent toilets ( sexy until you have an upset stomach), but if you want the country chic of the village, why not visit Europe? This is NY, and you are a tourist. 
The view from our corner room screamed New York: a forest of skyscrapers, Top of the Rock, the Hudson if you try and, literally at your feet, Times Square (we woke up at the sweet voice of Jessica Alba starting a marathon). 
It is not cheap but with good promotions it places itself at the minimum price in Manhattan for some comfort and location. Service is good, including that disconcerting American habit of asking 'how are you' to complete strangers. 
I'd probably not get back: been there, done that, and I'd probably like to stay somewhere quieter, but for my first NY visit it could not be beaten.

We recently stayed at the Marriot Marquis for 5 nights. It is in an excellent location but it is extremely busy so be prepared. But everything is on your doorstep!
The rooms were comfortable and of a good size. 
I was impressed by the gym. I like to exercise when traveling and would have to say the gym here would be the best hotel gym I've seen.

Very central for all the sight seeing. Service is just so-so!
Room curtain is very weird! We got a corner room and to draw the curtain is such a hazzle. No place to put the coffee machine On the table as there is no plugs except by putting the machine on the floor!

review_title: Great location for first time tourist.
review_text: Staying at the W Times Square for 2 weeks, we were extremely excited and the W exceeded all our expectations! The location was perfect for us 1st time NYC visitors. Riht on times square meaning we were extremely close to transportation and attractions. Service was some of the best that we had on our trip, although we did have to ask for extra towels everyday. The room size was bigger then I expected especially with three girls with too many bags and lots of shopping going on. We didn't have too much of an issue with the bathroom frosted glass but I can understand why some people might. Overall I would recommend this hotel to my family and friends because of its location and the helpful staff that helped three clueless girls around NYC.

I traveled to new York in august for leisure and chose the Marquis for its location, price (I was able to secure a corporate rate) Â and positive TripAdvisor reviews. Â  I arrived into new york via JFK airport and took the AirTrain ($5) to Jamaica station. Â  I originally planned to take the Long Island Rail Road to the hotel, but electrical issues cancelled all inbound trains to mid town. I took the E subway downtown which took around an hour. Â The hotel is a few blocks from the 42nd street station. Â There is an elite check-in counter on the ground floor, which I took advantage of (the primary check-in desk and lobby is on the 8th floor). Â I was given a corner room on the 44th floor which was extremely spacious with a view of Times Square. The room was recently renovated and contemporary. Â My only complaint about e room was the size of the window compared to the size of the room. Â The room also contained a very large safe. Â The bathroom was a fair size and had two bottled of complementary water (Not sure if this occurs in every room). Â The morning of my checkout, I stopped by the front desk to get a later checkout (normal checkout time is noon). I was hoping to get a 3 or 4pm checkout, similar to Starwood, but the latest checkout time I could get was 1pm. Â At checkout I requested that the hotel hang on to my luggage, which they will do until 10 or 11pm at night. Â When I came back later that afternoon to get my luggage, there was a wait of 10-15 minutes for my bag. Overall I was very satisfied with my stay at the Marriott Marquis and would definitely consider returning.

review_title: Typical Marriott hotel in a great location
review_text:
I spent 3 nights in the hotel traveling on business to Manhattan. Overall I would say the hotel is a typical Marriott hotel in an awesome location. The room rates have nothing to do with extraordinary amenities of the hotel but more to do with where the hotel is located....Times Square is literally right outside. The hotel is current under construction but that aspect didn't have any affect on our stay other than the escalators on the lower floors aren't working. 
There are several reviews complaining about the service & staff. I could see how these are true....I think it's the charm of the city more than anything else. 
I would stay here again for the location more than anything else. I've also stayed at the double tree across the street - very similar but at least they included breakfast.

review_title: Completely satisfied and would come back
review_text: We are sitting in the hotel lobby getting ready to leave and wish we were staying longer. The hotel upgraded us to a gorgeous one bedroom spacious suite. The staff was very accommodating for a quite late checkout. The location is excellent as it is walking distance to the theaters, 5th and Madison ave shopping, central park and eateries. We would definitely stay here again.

review_title: Construction ongoing if you want to sleep go elsewhere
review_text:
This is our third visit to a Klimpton hotel, second to the Muse. When we checked in they told us about the construction, but since it was not near our floor(7) we shouldn't be bothered. This is our second day we are up at 0545 two days. I have complained but apparently they are full and will not move us. Usually I wait until I get home to write a review cut I feel I must warn others to go somewhere else if they want to sleep past 6 or have any peace while in their room during the day.
The hotel is in a great location, is clean and for the most part staff are friendly. Still had I known about the noise I would have gone elsewhere.

Our first trip to NYC and wasn't sure where to stay...we got lucky with the Muse. Everything was beyond our expectation! Yes there is construction next door but we turned our fan on and it blocked the bulk of the noise. Close to everything we wanted to do and see. Staff was friendly and extremely helpful. Will definitely stay here again!

This is a very nice hotel located in midtown and great if your trip centers around shows and shopping. It is close to Times Square but far enough away to not be loud.
Rooms are small but very comfortable and the staff couldn't be any nicer or more helpful. If I return and need a central location I will choose this hotel again
We had Ã  wonderful stay. Ver large room, best location, just wonderful!

First of all, I love the Kimpton brand of hotels. I have stayed in Kimptons in Portland, Seattle, San Diego, and Arizona. NYC was no exception. The location is fabulous. A block from Times Square on the "Little Brazil" street which is smack dab in the theatre area, and sooo many nice restaurants and pubs around. I wish my stay would have been longer. As all Kimptons do, they host a complimentary wine happy hour in the lobby lounge each evening at 5. Love this. The decor is contemporary yet homey. My husband and I traveled with our two boys, 6 and 1, and my mom in tow. For NYC standards, are room was nice and roomy (we stayed in the double double) even with a crib brought in. They also brought in 2 child sized robes for the boys. I will DEFINITELY be coming back to the Muse on my next return to the city!
We had a corner room with amazing views all over central park and Hudson. Loved bar, rooms were bit old here and there, but great place on average

I was not impressed by this hotel st all!!!! Bathroom was dirty!!! So grose for a suite! I have stayed at other Starwood Hotels in NYC, such as Four points Chelsea, Four Points SoHo and W Hoboken. I would go back to any of those! They were way better and didn't have a suite!! Oh, and staying in times square forget it!! Too many people!!

review_title: Too expensive for what it really is
review_text:
We payed too much for a small renovated room.We asked for a rollabed, they said there wasn't enough space for one but we had a convertible sofa in the room.
When we opened it up it was filthy, there was a kid's note from two years ago and it was so uncomfortable we could feel all the springs!
The hotel is very well situated and we loved having breakfast at the starbucks in the lobby.

I booked this vacation to the city for my mums birthday. 
Unfortunately 4 weeks before we arrived I fractured my ankle & has painful surgery. 
I was concerned that this would hinder our experience in New York & I worried that the hotel would struggle to accommodate me whilst on crutches. 
However, it was quite the opposite. I emailed the hotel just a week before I arrived & explained my accident to them. I received an immediate response to my email from the Area Reservations Coordinator (Lulu Elkerm). As well as being so kind & caring she was exceptionally professional & made sure that I had a spacious room & that everything was at hand to make my mums birthday an amazing experience. I can't thank her enough for that & I've promised the staff that we will definitely be returning very soon! 
On anther great note, the hotel was beautifully decorated & so clean. Every single member of the Muse hotel team went out of their way with kindness. 
Myself & my mother took a great loving to one particular member, that was one of the concierge/bell staff (Michael Miskulin). He truly went out of his way to make sure we safely arrived to our destinations by getting us cars very efficiently & quickly. Even to the extent of getting me a larger car which made it easier getting in & out of with my crutches. We both agreed that of there was any promotional opportunity he should definitely get it for his professional manners. 
This was an amazing trip & we will be returning very soon. 
Thank you again. 
Caroline Curry (room 1003)

After our stay I feel compelled to write my first review. After a fantastic cruise, I thought our stay here might be anti-climatic as rooms in NY generally are! The staff on check in were so friendly and welcoming and our room (lead in type) was so big with wonderful views over the river for 4th July! Will look no further then this hotel for next trip to NY

I emailed ahead requesting a room in a high floor and questioned if they could do something nice. They gave us a room on the top floor with a balcony and had a bottle of bubbly waiting on ice. A great hotel and a perfect stay.

Hip hotel and bar is good but it's like walking into a nightclub every time you come back to hotel. Not suitable for older travellers.
Bathroom wall is see through so nit suitable for those timid, families or sharing. Check in staff friendly but concierge. Ok but overall disappointed.

review_title: Hurricane Irene at the soho courtyard!!
review_text: Waiting out hurricane irene at the soho courtyard and couldn't be in a better place right now!!! The staff is so over the top friendly and accommodating. Everything is so organized and there is plenty of communication in prepping us for an emergency situation. The hotel even organized dinner for all the hotel guests--- what a pleasant surprise considering almost everything is shut down in lower manhattan! Definitely always staying here on my future trips! Thank you soho courtyard!

Just got from NYC and stayed at the Michelangelo and me and my daughter loved it. Great room, clean, decor is lovely bathroom was wonderful. Croissants and coffee in the morning is complimentary and was a great way to start the day. Staff was friendly. Would stay here again!!!

review_title: Location good for tourist but very expensive for services
review_text: Good hotel with approximate to all the tourist locations. Good rooms and great layout. Heart of broadway and times square and phenomenal view from windows

Recently stayed here on a business trip & found it to embody a good value. This is a new property and the rooms are well appointed. 
The location is good and near to many restaurants. Also I felt safe walking in this area (as much as possible in NYC!). 
Overall a great stay.

Stayed for six nights booked a superior room which was spacious very clean the bathroom was very spacious with fluffy towels and bathrobes.The hotel was a few minutes from grand central station it also had an adjoining Irish bar next door ate there once and enjoyed my meal a good place to relax after a days sight seeing.I will stay again at this hotel on my next visit to nyc I would highly recommend it

review_title: Fantastic location, room, and facilities...poor service.
review_text:
I am a huge Marriott fan. I even own a Marriott vacation club property. As a single dad I either trade my unit in or use my rewards points to take my 8 yr old son on a 2 week vacation every summer. Last year we did San Francisco and Santa Monica. This year its NYC and Boston. 
We just arrived home from NYC. What a fantastic holiday. First the good. If you have children this hotel's location, and unique lobby is the best in times square! The elevators are fine and exciting. Many of the rooms have fantastic views of times square! For NYC they are spacious! The 1,2,3,7,A,C,E subway lines are all within 3 blocks. 
Now the bad. I don't think I've ever said that in a review about a Marriott or affiliated property. However, if they are going to receive my endorsement then they must endure my criticism as well. 
With the exception of the housekeepers...who were great...I honestly felt as though every employee was either hired last week, or simply too burned out to care anymore. Marriott runs an add on the in house TV about how incredibly competent and gracious the "at your service" folks are. I found them to be annoyed and put off by simple requests for a refrigerator and missed newspaper. In both cases it took 2-3 calls.
I worked as a concierge for 5 years when I was younger. I found the staff to be unprepared or disengaged. I asked for simple things like direction via subway to La Gaurdia airport. These are the types of things that you have printed sheets for. They knew the numbers of the trains and busses but couldnt tell you small details that are needed in a city like NYC. The same thing happened for the fireworks show. In this case there was a standard form, but the concierge got the details regarding viewing areas and street closing completely wrong. This was THE big event of the weekend. How do you not discuss it and prepare?
Finally, the luggage storage system is rediculous. There are 4 guys standing at a counter willing to take your bags. They are very pleasant and efficient. The problem is when go to retrieve the bags at street level, there is just one bellman. I waited for 20 minutes while a man kept ringing a little desk bell. Nobody came. Finally, my son started to ring it. When I complained, the employees immediately made excuses or just stared blankly at me. 
This sums up the staff. Rather than acknowledge your issue and offering to help, they either make an excuse or pass the buck. 
Marriott does better in Bueno Aries, Rio, Atlanta (Marquis) San Francisco (Marquis), LA, and Chicago. They can do it in NYC as well!

review_title: Great location in the theater district.
review_text: We spent a week in New York attending Broadway shows and we wanted to stay at a smaller hotel in the Theater District. The Muse met that criterion and we had a wonderful experience. The staff was outstanding and made our stay a memorable one. The room was very comfortable, and it felt like being at home. We'll definitely come back again.

Loved this hotel location brilliant bar over pricey but we were on a special trip, sheets and bed were gorgeous. Only down side was static shocks we kept getting ... Funny but made you wary of touching anything!

What can I say!! Everything was so Perfect! Before we arrived I receive the help of Patrick Armano to create the dream weekend for the birthday of my 17 years girl. He was so helpfull and did all our wish come true!!! When they say; whaterver whenever, believe me that is true!!!
The Hotel is wonderfull, classy and modern, on the right spot in Time Square to shop all night, and the restaurant in the Hotel is so good, I will definitly go back there for my next visit in NY. W staff are incredible!!! Thank you to all of you, because this will be a weekend to remember...

review_title: Great hotel in a great location friendly helpful staff
review_text:
A really lovely hotel in a most convenient location to visit all tourist attractions in New York. Lovely spacious room and beds extremely comfortable. Lovely patio restaurant at the back of the bar which could easily be missed if you weren't the inquisitive type to roam around !
Greg the concierge helped to make our trip a great success with his New York sense of humour which I love !
I'll be back !

We stayed in this hotel on our HoneyMoon, it was fantastic! It has a revolving restaurant on the top floor too which gives great views over the city. Expensive place but what do you expect? Take lots of money but well worth it. Can't wait to go back.

Arrived at 4 pm, but still had to wait 2+ hours for a room - then another 1.5 hours for bed to be made. Asked manager for compensation the next morning: he replied their outsource laundry had flooded causing delays and they wouldn't compensate because it was not their fault ( notwithstanding they had nearly doubled prices for fashion week), and then he blamed it all on hurricane Irene which had been over 2 weeks prior. Somehow other hotels were able to recover from the hurricane and work with more reliable laundries. Never again. 
,
Room has a spectacular view of time square. Service is superb. Very friendly. Great location. You are near everything.

review_title: Absolutely Brilliant from start to finish
review_text: Stayed here for five days and I cannot find any fault. The location is great, the staff are very helpful (especially the 2 concierge )and the rooms and food ate just great. Would recommend without hesitation.

review_title: Believe the reviews, great hotel in top location
review_text:
This hotel is just far enough North of Times Square to miss the crowds, and an ideal spot for walking to 5th, Central Park, nice Restaurants or a Broadway show. Staff were nice (but could have been cheerier), and the room was fantastic. Great shower, large bath, heat lamp and small TV in bathroom, Bose radio, good sound insulation and heat. No safe or ironing board in the room, but hardly an issue. Housekeeping staff were fantastic, and we has a European breakfast in the lobby each morning (great coffee and a couple of pastries). Would highly recommend this hotel - it's not that much more expensive than others in the area, and you defo won't regret the extra expenditure. 
I never write reviews, so that is something in itself.
Well I stayed with my wife and daughter on the 16th floor in 3rd & 4th june. It's a neat place but service is poor. It's basically for short stays. I changed my hotel to renaissance for 20th June.

For first timers traveling to new york city, this would be a great place to stay at. Hotels on NYC are pricey to begin with and there are really so many options. I chose this because we were traveling with a group of friends, most of whom were first timers. We were allowed to check in early, which was great after a long day of traveling. It is right in the middle of times square and you can get a room with a view of times sq, if you price is not an issue.
My only complaint is the bell service. It took 30 minutes to get our bags ready while waiting on the cab ride line. (we dropped off our bags after checking out the last day to go around and shop before our flight that evening). I thought that wait was not acceptable. Otherwise we enjoyed our stay here.

I know people have commented on the size of the rooms but this is NYC where you expect smaller rooms. The rooms at the Muse are average-sized, but well proportioned with the right amenities. Staff have been extra helpful and anything I have ordered to my room has come promptly. 
Not my prefered location, but I'm here for work so not much choice on where they book me. Good amenities close by.
This hotel is right where you want to be! It was clean, the doorman were very helpful with info we needed; it was the perfect stay. Convenient to all the attractions.

review_title: Favorite place to stay in NY, and anywhere!
review_text: We keep coming back to stay here! Best value, great place. Very clean, great beds!!

review_title: I will recommend the Fitzpatrick Grand Central to any traveler to NYC
review_text: We stayed on the 9th floor and there was hardly any city noise. A good proper old style hotel with none of that impersonal franchise feel of the newer and larger hotels in the area. Large clean rooms and good service. Everything you can want in a hotel. It was our quiet haven after busy NY days

review_title: Great location, central to pretty much everything you'd need.
review_text: Really good location, especially for everything we'd planned to do - sight seeing up and down town, shopping, times square, theatre and central park! Very clean room and common areas, and helpful staff. Didn't eat at the hotel so cannot comment on the food.

Really amazing location. We could see the electronic billboards in Times Square from our bedroom window. Usual lovely bedroom and bathroom that you get from Kimpton plus the cute leopard print bathrobes! Really helpful staff. If you go you have to check out the amazing ground floor bathrooms - they're themed, really great fun! If you stay here you'll have a fab time in NYC.

My daughter and I stayed for nine nights at this excellently located hotel. The staff were welcoming and helpful. The rooms were to a really good standard - nice size and with a spacious bathroom; comfortable beds. The hotel was busy during our stay but there was little in the way of noise reaching the bedrooms. 
We spent the last night our trip in the Waldorf Astoria and, whilst we really appreciated the sense of history and the beauty of the place, it was far less welcoming than the Fitzpatrick; there were no tea/coffee making facilities in the rooms; room service was ridiculously expensive; the maids made a great deal of noise outside the rooms quite early in the morning and the bathtubs were not entirely clean. I should have saved my money!

Had a great stay at this hotel! Room was clean and comfortable, bathroom was spotless and the location by Grand Central couldn't have been better! The room was tiny, but that was not surprising in NY. The staff was more than eager to help out with anything asked, whether it was to hail a cab or give dining recommendations. Would definitely stay again!

review_title: Great boutique hotel close to the bustle of Times Square
review_text:
We stayed here three nights in suite with terrace. The room (1504) and it's fittings were great the only problem was the noise due to the fact that the extractor vents for the whole hotel seemed to be located directly outside our window - the noise made the terrace unusable.
You might think that would have been enough to put me off but the hotel is so nice in other ways that I'd still recommend it - just make sure you don't get that room.

review_title: First Timers Best Place To Go
review_text: What can one say this place is smack dab in the middle of TS...this was awesome and the staff was great...a must as it was out first time in NY and this was awesome....
Great hotel in great location right in the heart of times square.

review_title: Not all that's hyped is as good as billed
review_text: Although the aesthetic was pleasant the finishes felt cheap. The room was large by NYC standards but the shower temperature was difficult to control. The towels were rough to touch.

We stayed at the Muse this past Tuesday night while in the city to see Mary Poppins. The whole trip was a surprise birthday present from my husband. The hotel had known about my birthday and shortly after check-in they sent up a lovely plate of cupcakes and a bottle of champagne! The rooms are very modern and posh and just add to the whole experience. I am a huge fan of Kimpton hotels and this hotel just added to that love! Every staff person encountered was overly friendly. We also had the pleasure of eating dinner before our show in the hotel's restaurant, NIOS, and it was equally as amazing as the hotel! I look forward to visiting this hotel again very soon!
PS... the restrooms off the lobby are amazing! there was a 'lobby' like room with several doors, each with a different description on the outside and each individual bathroom was totally decorated to fit that word (I know, I looked in each one)! Definitely something you have to check out!

review_title: We have recommended The Muse to everyone!
review_text: Large rooms for New York, well furnished. Great value accommodation for Jan/Feb. Close to everything and to subway, very friendly staff. We loved it all

review_title: The hotel gives you a feeling of importance and makes you feel like you are home.
review_text: The front desk was extremely friendly and helpful, and the restaurant was the best you could hope for. The management was great and the Bar was immaculate. Peter was a great help in our stay and the bartender Lisa was the warmest and friendliest person we met. It was nice to not have to ask for something to drink, it was always there. She really knew how to make you feel at home, we will always remember her warm smile. Thank you nios and the Muse, we will be back for another round.

review_title: The friendliest atmosphere and great bar
review_text: The front desk was extremely friendly and helpful, and the restaurant was the best you could hope for. The management was great and the Bar was immaculate. Peter was a great help in our stay and the bartender Lisa was the warmest and friendliest person we met. It was nice to not have to ask for something to drink, it was always there. She really knew how to make you feel at home, we will always remember her warm smile. Thank you nios and the Muse, we will be back for another round.

Wang bang in the middle of Times Sq! Perfect location. The hotel bar is great, whether I was drinking a Bud Light or a Champagne Collins cocktail, it was great as I you were overlooking Times Sq!
It ain't cheap, but where is in New York?
Our room was on the side of times square with an ok view but I'm sure some of the views from the most expensive rooms are spectacular.
If you want to treat yourself or have the cash stay here!

review_title: Great for a break in New York
review_text: We stayed for 3 nights in a deluxe king room which we found to be very comfortable with enough room for moving around. The bathroom was compact but clean with a good shower & quality Aveda toiletries. We appreciated the complimentary breakfast & cheese & wine offered in the evenings to compensate for the renovations in the lobby. We had a fantastic break in New York & the Chandler Hotel helped make it great.

review_title: Great location and room but don't expect too much sleep!
review_text:
We stayed there fro 3 night in Nov 2011. 
It's a great hotel for NY weekend. Just off the 5th, so only 15 mins walk to Penn station and Port Authorty Bus Terminals. There are a few cafes around the hotel, a Thai and a Korean restaurant just opposite the hotel, so quite handy. 
The only down side for us is the noise of NY city. Both of us are light sleepers, we were on 6th floor, 5th if you are British, but we woke up but noisey rubbish truck every morning at 4:30is. Not something the hotel can help, but maybe they should think about getting the double glazing.
The staff are friendly, the lobby is getting work done as other reviewers said but doesn't affect the stay of the hotel. Oh, when we were there, the larger life kept on breakdown! Management need to sort it out soon!

review_title: Great place close to everything and great service
review_text: Staff was very attentive to all our request. They go the extra mile to make your stay very comfortable. I am already making this place my home away from home. Looking forward to the new restaurant and bar next year. Thank you :) !.

review_title: Very good for New York but not one of the great hotels in the world
review_text:
I stayed Monday to Thursday ( three nights) in early November for business. 
The hotel itself, the gym, bar, amenities are all very good and the location is excellent. However it just didn't have the same "wow" factor that I enjoyed when staying at some other top hotels in other cities including the St Regis in Singapore a few weeks earlier. 
I did use the complimentary Bentley just to try it. However it is more of novelty value as it only goes 10 blocks and my meetings were mostly in the 12 to 20 block range. Within 10 blocks I would always walk in any case. I gather it is mostly used for advertising value. Having it go 15 blocks would be far more useful as it would get to 42nd street and upper east and west sides.
The internet performance varied a bit and was not working for a prolonged period of time when I needed it. 
Bell desk was great. Butlers were not as proactive as some other hotels but did everything requested so no complaints. But no "wow" - that is exactly what I needed being offered.
Bottom line is that New York hotels are different. The base cost of simply operating in a good location with good size rooms is so expensive that there just isn't the budget to be great and still fill up 
occupancy.

review_title: Best hotel and location on earth
review_text:
We have stayed at this hotel 4 times and have always looked forward to our next visit with great anticipation. The location could not be better, it is extremely quiet for nyc and the rooms are extremely confortable, it feels like you are staying in a castle not a hotel. The service we have received has always been superb, especially kristel in the front office. The unpacking and packing by the butlers is an excellent service which we always use. The king cole bar is one of the best hotel bar i have ever seen/been in.
The service of the concierge, bellmen and doormen is always friendly and helpful. We have stayed in over a dozen nyc hotels of all calibers and by fsr the st regis is not only our favorite but by far the best. My wife loved the spa and the room service is excellent.

review_title: Good location, clean and small room
review_text:
The staff was friendly and helpfull. 
There is a renovation around the reception but it didn't bother us at all. 
Deluxe queen room is very small. It can not accomodate 2 large luggages. 
Overall it was a good experience, recommend chandler hotel to all.
It was not cheap but it was great! Improved the quality of holidays because it is very good and you do not get bad surprise! Good staff, good location! Strongly advised.

review_title: Friendly and attentive staff, chic rooms, comfy beds in a central location!
review_text: I have continually stayed at Hotel Chandler for the past two years. I was drawn by the location near the textile building for business reasons but I have come to find out that this location is great for other reasons. It is close to the Flatiron building, Times Square, Murrey Hill restaurants, "Curry Hill", Fashion District...It is also easily accessible by subway. Place is clean and the staff always remembers who I am even months later! Only gripe is the food. No restaurant but they are remodeling and will have one soon. Anyway, I dig this place. You should try if in the area.

We stayed for two days after Christmas. It is the first time we have stayed here. It is a great location and quite nice rooms albeit not large. The room has a small kitchen. Breakfast is included. It was busy when we were there so breakfast was very busy so plan accordingly. We will stay there again. Close to 9 th st and many excellent Restuarants of modest cost.
hotel_name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City

review_title: Needs improvement to really deserve its accolades. Could be better. Customer service would be a start.
review_text:
We have stayed here many times including a recent two week stay. The front desk staff continue to cater to certain people and be rude to others. Dont ask for anything because you will be told to pay for it or be told by the front drsk that it cant be done Some front staff walk you to the elevator upon check in 
and some butlers wait to welcome outside your door But thats only for
 certain people Treating everyone 
with equal respect and class. Though we were on a nonsmoking floor, people on our floor were smoking and when we checked in there was an air freshner/dehumidifier in our room which should have been our first clue that they already knew there was a problem before we got there. Unless you are an Arab prince or are paying by cash, as a Starwood member, there's nothing special for you unless maybe you're a platinum member and even then there's really no guarantee and they love to remind you of this. This hotel is cozy but they need better seating in lobby and library which are not at all welcoming. It's very tacky to constantly see tons if luggage in the middle if the Lobby with people checking in and out. They have a house car which they are very stingy about offering up to you unless of course you look extra wealthy or tip generously and in this city, who knows how much greasing it takes to get noticed. Housekeeping and butler service are generally excellent but we had a horrible turn down service where it appeared that the housekeeper spent time in our room looking through our things rather than turning down the bed, placing down the slippers and refilling the ice. The butler followed up
Immediately but it left a bad taste. The female conceirges are much nicer then most of the male ones Not sure why but we have noticed this on the last three visits. The conceirges also need to get out and discover more restaurants that they have actually eaten in as well as see all the top shows so they know what they are talking about. We hope some customer service classes will be offered to the front desk. The butlers could probably conduct them. Don't go here with tremendous expectations because even a top hotel will disappoint you 
St Regis work a little harder and you will be deserving of your accolades. Also stop charging for everything including mailing a stamped letter. That's just a bit absurd.

review_title: Great room at agood price for Central Manhattan
review_text:
We searched a number of alternative centrally located hotels before opting for Staybridge Suites and we weren't disappointed. One needs to get over the fact that centrally located hotels will be expensive in NY - but no more expensive than, say, London.
The hotel is only minutes from Times Square but that short distance translates to comparative quiet.
The hotel lobby doesn't quite compare with the pictures on the web pages - I expected more spaciousness. However, what was important was the room and it couldn't be faulted. We had two queen beds, a kitchenette area and a very acceptable bathroom. Our room was on 22nd floor and was quiet with a good view of some skyscrapers. The room was clean and neutrally decorated. All the appliances in the kitchenette including a large fridge, dishwasher, mcrowave and double hob appeared to be new and certainly clean. 
The bed was very comfortable.
The minor downside was breakfast. The hotel was very busy during our stay and simply finding a place to sit was tricky. There was a mixture of hot and cold options that were acceptable but nothing to write home about. However it could not be challenged given it was included in the room rate.
Overall I'd be surprised if this hotel can be topped at the price.

After searching around for a hotel in Manhatten the reviews led us to this small hotel in the heart of midtown. 
The welcome by the staff was excellent and the front desk were always polite and helpful when we had questions. The cleaning staff however could do with checking the do-not-disturb sign a bit more closely. 
The room wasn't massive but well equipped with everything you need (including an umbrella which was a massive bonus in the storms). 
There was some road noise and plumbing sounds from adjacent rooms but nothing that you couldn't get used to.
Would stay there again and recommend to a friend.

Just back from a 6night stay. Could not fault, location, room size, cleanliness, staff all first class. Only a short walk to times sq, drug store on corner for beer, dollar pizza on the other. Staff were excellent, polite and couldn't do enough to hell. Breakfast was good and only ever had trouble one morning finding a table which can be expected with a hotel this size. Even so tubs provided to take back to the room. Lifts can be slow with only 3, but we had a low floor so we could use the stairs, but with a max 5min wait for a lift when we did need one we can't complain. Overall definitely recommend with high praise to the dedicated staff.

review_text: This hotel made our trip even more perfect, from beginning to end! The location was so close to everything- the port authority was literally across the road (perfect for going to the Jersey Gardens Outlet for shopping), the subway was located at the end of the street which is really handy too if you're planning on making your way to Soho, etc. Because the hotel was so close to Times Square, myself and my boyfriend walked everywhere as it was dead quick and easy. The breakfast is included in the price, and believe me it is worth it! Bagels, bacon, eggs, muffins, cereal, fruit, yogurts- you name it! And you can take as much as you care to, with take away bags available too! The social evening tues-thurs 5pm-7pm is definitely worth a go, with hot food appetisers a and alcohol for free and in abundance. Beds were amazing, rooms spacious, spotless and fitted with a kitchen and everything that you need. Will definitely be back!

review_title: Very comfortable, clean and modern hotel.
review_text: We stayed on the 29th floor for 6 nights. Not once did we wait more than a couple of minutes for the lift/elevator ! Room was lovely. Breakfast was great, cereals, fruit, yoghurt, bagels, toast. Hot food was a bit limited ie scrambled egg, potatoe, ham but no tomatoes, mushrooms, beans. Eat as much as you like though and even take away if you wanted. Wifi in hotel was great and you could print off boarding passes at the business centre for free. Went to the free drinks and nibbles evening once and had a nice chat with other guests. Used the free washing machine, dryer facility day before we came home so no big suitcase of dirty washing:) When eating out in NYC look out for the hygiene rating displayed on restaurant windows - A being cleanest ! In Macy's we got 10% off with a visitor pass, so ask at the tills about that. We liked the restaurants on 48th street, between 8th and 9th street loads of them.
hotel_name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City

review_text: The room was clean, new, and bright. Service was speedy and so helpful and cheerful. Location could not have been better, steps from every train! Seconds from shops and restaurants and night life. We could not have asked for a better way to spend our honeymoon and start our new life together!

Ok, the location (next to the Port Authority Bus Station) may seem not ideal. When we googled the location before arriving in NYC it looked drab etc. However, in reality it was absolutely fine! Everything on your doorstep in terms of transportation and eateries etc. 
My husband and I were in NYC for 6 nights, celebrating our anniversary. We asked for a high floor, having read other reviews on TripAdviser, and were pleased with 31st floor! We could lay in bed and see the Empire State Building! Fab! The lifts were not a problem either! Breakfast was fine and we always managed to get a seat in the main dining area. To have the facility of a free breakfast was a real bertie bonus and set us up till lunchtime each day.
Staff were great - always attentive and helpful when we needed.
Free computer access was another bonus.
We got a tube to JFK when we left ($7.50 instead of a $70+ taxi fare!) and it was a great journey! Don't waste your money on the taxi fare!
Would definitely recommend this hotel!
hotel_name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City

review_title: Clean, affordable, great location. Perfect place to stay for a visit to The Big Apple.
review_text: Everything was great about this place. Nice staff as well. There are only two things that I feel the need to mention. 1. The breakfast clears out fast, make sure you go early. We went late, and only had an apple, and an orange. 2. The elevator at peak times were a long wait. It wouldn't bother us, if I didn't need to use the washroom at the time. But overall, a great affordable stay, I would definitely come back again.

review_title: One of the best I've found in NYC!
review_text:
Fantastic hotel in the heart of midtown! This was my seventh trip to NYC and I would consider this one of the best value hotels I have stayed in to date.
The staff on the front desk (most especially Dan) were incredibly helpful and friendly. Rooms were of average size but usual for NYC and beds were extremely comfortable. Only downpoint for the room was the size of the shower... It was a little small compared to the bathroom. It was very handy to have kitchen facilities, especially the fridge. The included breakfast was also great, and the hotel has excellent wi-fi throughout the building. During peak times there was often delays in waiting for a lift, but I have found this is common in any bigger NYC hotel so it didn't really bother me much. 
The location is exceptionally central and access to most subway lines is at the corner (also very handy). I wouldnt hesitate is recommending this hotel, and would definitely stay again in the future.
hotel_name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City

review_title: Two major flaws at this nice hotel
review_text: 3 elevators for 32 floors. Waited 20 minutes then walked down 8 floors. Breakfast and happy hour included but mobbed and no place to sit. Worst, no taxis available in morning or dinner time, reported cheerfully by doorman.
hotel_name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City

review_text: We had a week at the Staybridge Suites. I travelled with my husband and sister and we stayed in a triple share room. The room itself was small but housed the essentials. The room had 2 double beds, aircon, TV, mini kitchen with all essentials. Mostly we were thankful for the full size fridge. The bathroom was of adequate size however the shower was small. It was no problem for us but if you like a roomy shower then it may be. The location is excellent. Right across the road from the Port Authority Bus Station which is where the bus for the Woodbury Common outlet departs and arrives. There is a food emporium (supermarket) only 2 blocks away and subway stations only a few blocks as well. Breakfast was included in our room rate and was the perfect start each day for us. With cereal, fruit, muffins, yoghurt, bagels, and hot breakfast (scrambled eggs, then each day either bacon, ham or sausage) juice coffee and tea there was plenty to choose from. I loved that they even had take away containers which was perfect for taking a muffin with you. The service was friendly and attentive, Dan on reception while he appeared to work every day was happy, smiley and full of willingness to please each time we saw him. While I feel the room was expensive for what it was, in a big city like New York that plays host to so many tourists I imagine its a case of you pay for what you get. I was happy with our comfortable stay at Staybridge Suites and would easily recommend this place to family and friends. The hotel also had free reliable wifi.
hotel_name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City

review_title: Excellent location - home away from home
review_text:
We stayed from Dec 30-Jan 2 and used the hotel as a first stop upon arrival from Australia.
Check-in was painless, and we were in the room quickly.
Room was clean and comfortable. Bed was clean and sheets were crisp :) bathroom was a little poky but you don't live in it! Was fine for us :)
awesome location. My partner and I walked to central park and without realizing, walking past empire state building, times square and rockerfeller on the way!
Some great little food places in the area too.
Hood service and drinks in the hotel bar too - gotta love the happy hour prices!!
Would definately come back to the Chandler.

We went there with our daughter and were very surprised by both the location and the size of the room. We had the kitchenette and used it a lot. From the hotel you can easily go by walk to fifth avenue, timesquare. Definitly a good bet in the pricey Big Apple!

Bit worried at first coming here but have had a fantastic stay at the hotel - truely superb value - better than some claimed 5 star hotels... Great location to times square and the rest of manhattan.
The bed is too comfy..... Come back from a good days shopping and youll find yourself sleeping in after a power nap.... They were lush.
Great staff... Just great....
hotel_name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City

review_text:
Great value for it's proximity to times square, only a block and bait away from the bright lights.
Great value in that breakfast and PR dinner drinks and snacks were complimentary, as well as free wifi.
Staff were great at reception. don't let the swanky looking lobby fool you, the rooms do not look like that, but still serviceable.

review_text: This hotel is in a great location in proximity to the theater district. The rooms are clean and the staff was very friendly. Good buy

We got a great deal on this hotel so we were slightly skeptical but it turned out to be great! Several members of the hotel staff were very outgoing, polite, and helpful. Rooms were clean and the location was perfect for sightseeing everywhere around the city. Bed was very comfortable, especially after a very long day of walking. Slightly noisy because it's beside a fire station but not terribly noticeable, especially when you're tired. Definitely not enough to deter from staying there, and we were in the section of rooms closest to the station. Overall, great place to stay, especially for the price we paid for it.

Negatives: Dark room. Waiting for lifts for 25 mins. Waiting for a table at breakfast. 
Positives: Location is great for Times square. Don't worry about previous reviews - it's perfectly safe! We used the Grayline bus tours and were able to pick up from Port Authority. Room is modern and clean. Breakfast is great (even if you have to queue) and free. The bed and bedding is as good as any 5 star hotel I have stayed in. I slept like a baby!
Overall: My wife and I stayed here for 3 nights I would recommend this hotel as a low cost modern hotel in a great location.

review_text: warm welcome,quick and straight forward to check in.breakfast was good,lots of choice other comments say busy which true but always got a table food constantly refreshed.rooms lovely,not huge but more than fine!could self cater with modern kitchen best was coffee maker-thinking of buying one!important is a hotel bathroom - shower warm,powerful lots of fluffy towels and bath to rock my feet!very clean,maid service everyday.odd duvet cover was a sheet wrapped around duvet that came off in night!going back next year to see Christmas lights
