review_title: Happy to have returned, Waldorf you are forgiven
review_text:
Following our stay in January in the main hotel, which was not very good the management contacted me to ask that I pay a return visit and stay at the towers. 
We have just come back from a four night stay, which was fab. The room was clean and well appointed. The views amazing. We were looked after from the moment we arrived late on Saturday evening, until we left on Wednesday evening. Being 3 girls who like to shop the staff were always ready to store our bags as we were in and out all day long.
We will be back, soon I hope
hotel_name: The Towers of the Waldorf Astoria

review_text: What a nice feeling is to meet the expectations I had from an institution like Waldorf Astoria in NYC! I had an incredible stay. The suite I had was breath taking, the staff at the Front Desk, Lounge and of course the Concierge ( best I ever experience) made the best possible welcome I could ever got to NYC. Highly recommended!
hotel_name: The Towers of the Waldorf Astoria

review_text: I stayed at Morgan's from the 14th to the 19th of December 2011, and found the hotel to be awesome! Everyone there was so friendly and went out of their way to make our trip feel special, and it did! I'd definitely recommend it to others looking for a great location, and lovely rooms. We could see the Empire State building from our room! My only small criticism is that free wi-fi was only available in the living room. Other than that, I can't fault Morgans. I hope to stay there again when I visit New York next. Thanks for a memorable stay!

We're currently staying at the Morgan hotel for Christmas and we couldn't be happier. The hotel is great - we were upgraded to a suite on the 8th floor. Spacious and beautiful. The hotel is centrally located and the staff is super friendly. The free breakfast is great - fresh croissants, fruit and coffee - what more could you want?
We'll definitely be returning. One night left and sad to leave.

I stayed at the Morgans for a few nights when I was in town on business. The staff were very friendly and even gave me a free upgrade upon check in! The rooms were fairly spacious for new York. The only complaint I had was that the radiator was a little too loud when it was on. The stay came with a complimentary continental breakfast with a variety of options. I would stay here again.

We have just got back from a 5 night stay over thanksgiving . Where to start. Let's start with your hotel all I can say is what a gem. Small and friendly and the staff where excellent nothing is too much trouble . Can't mention you all but you all where brill. The hotel rooms where spacious and very clean yes the bathroom was small but how much time do you send in there. What a great idea the living room is free coffee and tea and a relaxed area to meet people . Breakfasts we good too it kept avery one going till lunch time . Bravo . We knew the restaurant was shut before we came but there are loads of eating places on or just off maddison ave. would I recommend Morgan's NYC . You bet
We got a fabulous room with an amazing view of the crystler building. The staff was by far the friendliest I have ever come across.
hotel_name: The Towers of the Waldorf Astoria

review_title: Great hotel in a great location.
review_text: We had a great stay at the morgans hotel. The hotel room was a good size, clean and the staff was very friendly. We would definitely stay there again!

This is a clean hotel that's trying too hard to be trendy. The rooms are nice and comfortable but the bathrooms are horrifically small with terrible fixtures. Worse part, the "free" continental breakfast doesn't open until 7am on weekdays and8am on weekends. Though it's nice, the times are not posted anywhere in addition to being so horribly late for a business hotel. 
I doubt I will stay here again or recommend it to others.

This is the 3rd Morgans group hotel I have stayed at and they continue to impress me with their service and attention to detail. A great location if you are looking to be in a quieter part of mid-town yet still close to major attractions. The staff are very friendly and helpful. Their concept of creating the feeling that you are at home in NY rather than a tourist in a bustling hotel is fantastic. No hesitationl to recommend to others.

review_title: No aircon, no movies, dated, what's not to like at $550 a night?
review_text: I've stayed at the Waldord a number of times, but now old has gone from acceptably elegant to simply shabby. Aircon on high floors can't keep up with the heat, i couldn't get it cooler than 24c/75f in the room, indifferent restaurant service, though roomservice remaina excellent.
hotel_name: The Towers of the Waldorf Astoria

review_text: Morgans is a small quaint hotel with a personable staff. (I was tracking this, front desk staff greeted with "welcome back" everytime I came through the front door.) But there's no old world charm here. Design is modern, clean and clever (especially the smart bathrooms) and the beds are devine.

I have just returned from my stay at the towers and couldn't have wished for better. We originally had booked at the waldorf but got upgraded to the towers when checking in and said we were there for our anniversary. This in itself was fantastic and made us feel very welcome and valued as guests. The room was amazing with ample room for two and a gorgeous view of the Chrysler building. Everything was immaculate and the bed was the most comfortable I'd ever slept in. The hotel was stunning and very old fashioned glamour. Every day walking around was a treat with beautiful decor and intricate design to take in. The staff couldn't be more helpful. Very friendly and approachable. It's not every day you get to stay in such a fabulous place and i enjoyed every second. Within easy walking distance of the major sights but if some are a bit further than you'd like, the doorman arranges a taxi and we never paid more than $12 to get anywhere even in rush hour. If anything to trip this place up it is the price of food and drinks but staying in such a grand and historic place it really should be expected and we still paid it rather than go elsewhere. Thoroughly enjoyed my stay and would definitely go back. Gorgeous!
hotel_name: The Towers of the Waldorf Astoria

review_title: Out of this world, luxury, classy and a once in a lifetime trip.
review_text: Hotel was amazing, suite was so luxurious, the service was so attentive. The hotel is out of this world and has such a history and splendour. There's no doubt it's not good value and is very expensive.
hotel_name: The Towers of the Waldorf Astoria

review_text: We booked on Expedia and got a very reasonable rate. The room was big by New York standards, clean, modern and quiet. The included breakfast at Asia de Cuba was a good perk-the coffee was good and there was a big selection. The front desk service was also good and what I would expect of a boutique hotel-attentive but not intrusive. The only thing I was not expecting was how dark it was-there were no public or private areas, even the living room, that seemed to have natural light. The location was perfect-close to mid-town but far enough away that it was quiet. The bed was very comfortable and I liked the Malin+Goetz bath products.

This was our first time in New York .So we wanted to make sure we had made the right decision when choosing a hotel. The staff are very friendly and made our stay enjoyable. Loved the location we could see the Empire State Building out of the window. We will be back soon. Clarebirty and family

We found Morgans Hotel in Trip Advisor and booked it on booking.com. We got the suite with a very special price and with breakfast at Asia de Cuba. Stayed there for 9 days. Perfect room, perfect bed, perfect location and perfect service. Loved the Living Room area too. I strong recommend this hotel. It was like to be at home. Calm area too.

The hotel was beautiful if you like contemporary style, but do not stay there if you're bringing small children with you!!!!!!! 
Their rooms have gorgeous floor to ceiling windows but there are ground level windows that easily open outward about 6 inches with no locks! My 20 month old went right for the windows and could easily open them. It was extremely frightening, so I asked for another room or a refund. Thankfully, we were upgraded to a suite with balcony that had doors that could lock because I would not have been at all comfortable staying in a room where my baby was at risk of falling 15 stories! I can't imagine how it is legal, honestly. There really should be a disclaimer before booking that the rooms are not at all child safe. 
For those without kids though, Yotel is a clean and trendy hotel at a good price if you dont mind being a few blocks from Times Square.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text: We stayed at the Yotel in December for our Christmas trip to New York and it was excellent. We would really recommend paying a little extra for the corner rooms as the views are fantastic. The windows go from floor to ceiling on two sides of the room-we had a view of the Hudson River on one side and NYC on the other. On a morning we laid in bed and at a press of a button the blinds opened and we could see the sights from the comfort of our own bed! The complimentary tea and muffins on a morning also helped us start the day great. We will definitely be staying here on our next visit to the Big Apple.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text:
We only used the room to sleep in and spend our time out about in the city that truly never sleeps. Shame it looked out on a brick wall and the room was small, but space isnt everything.
Staff were great and were accommodating when we had a late flight out kept our luggage whilst we ran amock in Manhattan.
Tips:
buy 7-day transport pass works a treat whilst using buses & tubes. (nb it doesn't work on the jfk train or the new jersey system, but they're cheap enough)
Buy 7-day NYC pass even if there for a short period (we had 3-days and packed the attractions in, be sure to pop down to NBC studios to book the tour and if you're there now Circus de sol is on at radio city)
see a yankees game - fantastic, amazing atmosphere.
Head down to Hells Kitchen / 9th Avenue for real food, but down forget the pizza slices.
It was my wife first time and I made sure we saw lots and she came back with plenty of stories.

review_title: Excellent location and very helpful staff!
review_text: Good value for money - very helpful front desk staff (helped get tickets to Broadway shows that were sold out) - leaking wheelchair accessible shower (not great drainage) but otherwise good room - no bedbugs!
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_title: Outstanding boutique hotel in a prime Manhattan location!
review_text: From the moment we entered this discreet hotel on Madison Avenue we were met with friendly and courteous service. We were on the first leg of our honeymoon and had been booked into a twin bed room by our agents, unfortunately there were no double rooms left but they organised one for the next 3 nights with a fantastic view of the empire state building. The rooms were modern, nicely decorated and furnished, had great toiletries and fantastic aircon! Breakfast was included which is a novelty in NYC, there was fresh coffee and juices, cereals, fresh fruit and yogurts and a selection of croissants/pastries/bagels etc which was right up our street! We usually stay at the Waldorf-Astoria but went here on recommendation and were very pleased! Will definitely stay here on our next trip to NYC.

review_title: Nice design hotel but not extravagant
review_text: Nice hotel but compared to its relatives, like the Morgans hotel on Miami beach, this hotel is more "normal". For ordinary, modern people with a feel for contemporary design it is great. Location in mid-town close to all attractions. Not luxurius, but homely.

review_title: This place should be called the YoUtel.
review_text:
Because it is very You-centric. The service is awesome from the get go. Even with a self-check in the guests services are very friendly and helpful. Not to mention they have a freakin' giant robot arm in the lobby. 
Once you get to the room (or pod as they call it) the fun continues. You feel like you've stepped into a room from the 5th Element, only without the dirt and grime and annoying Chris Tucker. 
Even though the room I stayed in was a tad smallish, although more like a suite at The Waldorf, they more than make up for it with a retractable bed. 
The price was unbeatable. $174 for a night is very competitive for right of of Times Square.
I will definitely stay there again if given the opportunity.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text: My wife and I used Yotel on our recent long weekend in NYC. Perfect if your the travel type that are there to experience the city but still want a little cleanliness as part of your stay. Staff are great, room is small but perfectly adequate. Shower is actually better than most! They are also more than happy to keep your luggage at no extra cost allowing for a full final day without the hassles of luggage. I would recommend is hotel to anyone.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_title: One of a kind! Yuppie Paradise!
review_text:
Young, 20-something, traveling w/ no kids for shopping and partying in NY...to keep it short and sweet, clean, small, and modern...like being in crew's quarters aboard the Starship Enterprise...unlike any other hotel. Bed is more of a bunk, but at 5 in the morning after partying all night in manhattan, who's complaining? 
Don't bring your kids; this is a boutique hotel that caters to a young (or young at heart) trendy clientele that loves to check themselves in at a kiosk, drop their bags off with a robot, snag a cappuccino in the shared galley (one on each floor) and dance to the iPod you've plugged into the TV (plug provided). No spacious Ritz Suites, here, but it's fun, functional and the staff rocks! I'll be back.
*guess that wasn't so short...:)
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text: December 15-19. Wonderful hotel with extremely clean rooms. Only concern was the firmness of the bed on my wife's back. Good food at Dohyo and good service. Will definitely stay here again!
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_title: the best big hotel in manhattan 2011 (and amazing value for money too);
review_text: unbelievable design, friendliness in every department, great music atmosphere (no muzak nonsense), small but perfectly accommodating rooms full of brilliant details, free wi-fi... almost too good to be true;
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_title: I had the BEST BIRTHDAY EVER because of my stay at Yotel....
review_text:
I stayed at Yotel the night of November 12th to celebrate my 22nd birthday. As a full time student, and full time employee, along with other "burdens" (lol) of life, Yotel was such a breath of fresh air of the daily struggles of I endure constantly! The hospitality of the employees were truly amazing! Anca, made sure I had EVERY SINGLE THING I needed to enjoy myself. I think she sympathized with my tiredness when she greeted me upon my arrival. Lol. She was such a sweetheart. I must've told her I LOVED her a million times during my couple hours there! My room wasn't ready and she upgraded my suite at no additional cost. She didnt have to, I didn't ask but she wanted to make sure I got my rest before I went out for the night! She's great! I also had the pleasure of meeting Chad, I believe he was the manager of housekeeping? Great man as well! Word got around that it was my birthday, and on behalf of the hotel he brought me up a slice of cake from the restaurant .... I was elated!! He was so warm and welcoming to me and my guests. Who would have thought someone from housekeeping would have gone out of their way for little ol me :-) I used to believe I had a birthday curse but the staff there broke the chains of misery lol!! I had a group of friends meet me at the hotel for a little Pre-gaming into the city life. Although they couldn't come up to my room (it was a lot of them) Anca and Justin (the manager of the clubs) agreed that it would be okay for us to occupy one of the cabins in the club at no cost! Talk about accommodating!! Just writing this and reminiscing on that night is getting me excited. Justin was super cool! My overall experience was more than I could have ever thought would be granted to this 22 yr ol girl at a hotel. I'm no celebrity, I'm no big time NYC sociliate. I'm just a girl satisfied with a good time. Yotel, it's staff and employees showed me a GREAT time. I tell people to stay there ALL THE TIME! I, myself live right in westchester county. But I can guarantee I will be staying at Yotel every time I need to get away. I love it!! There are some more names I have written down of staff members I didn't write about. Quick S/O to Robert (baggage) The security staff, Dana, Simone, Adam... And, let me not forget the manager of the hotel!!! Forgot his name but he was also very accommodating and warm!!!!! I have all of their names written down but I left them at home. If I have to write a second review, I will! Look out for it! <3 
-Danielle Owens
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text: We had so much staying here, from the elevator music to the wonderful views (which you can see from the shower). The cabins made excellent use of space and the multiple outlets were much appreciated.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_title: Do yourself a favour - Just Book It
review_text: We stayed for a total of eight days as part of a 40 th birthday celebrations. Throughout our stay we found at all times the hotel staff to be incredibly helpful, the room, which was upgraded on check in fantastic in size and the breakfast included more than adequate for our days activities.

review_title: One of the best hotels I've stayed in.
review_text:
I travel to NYC on business regularly, and have spent a while trying to find the perfect hotel near to Times Square. Finally, I found the Yotel!
It's comfortable, beautifully designed, with friendly helpful staff, and creative touches that make all the difference. It's also incredible value - about 2/3 the cost of the Hilton Times Sq and so much better.
Tips: bring ear plugs as the doors are quite thin so noise from the corridor is an issue; and make sure you pull your door properly shut as it's surprisingly easy to leave it unlocked.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text: This hotel is fabulous, fantastic and just plain awesome. The head concierge Jeffrey is the best and will make sure you have a great time in NYC (and that you "live like a local"). The rooms are just to die for: best room I've had in all my NYC trips over the years. Fabulous view and great patio on the rooftop. Would stay here forever.
Any where you go, the kimpton hotels are the best, wether its the staff or the rooms its all great!

review_title: Perfect sanctuary in the midst of a busy city!
review_text:
Amazing location. Right snap in the middle - close by Grand Central Station, Rockerfeller, Koreatown, etc...
Staff was friendly and very accomodating. 
Stayed 10 nights and no dramas at all. Will be back real soon.

It was a great rate for NYC. I especially enjoyed the Yobot that stores ur luggage. The only thing I did not like was not having the ability to print from my laptop. The robes and shower gel/shampoo was amazing and a nice touch.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text: I really like the location of this hotel but I do not like that some areas were closed.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_title: Elegant hotel with a great attitude.
review_text:
We loved our recent stay at Ink48 and we were pleasantly surprised with the size of the rooms. Great modern fixtures and a staff that went out of their way to make sure our stay was exceptional. 
Jeffrey at the front desk who also ran the complimentary wine happy hour went over and beyond his normal duties to ensure all the guests he came in contact with were treated like "friends". We will be back! Don't pass this hotel up.
The staff was extremely helpful and kind. Everyone had s smile and was willing to help. The rooms were clean and the view was amazing. I would definitely refer my family and friends here.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text:
We have not long got back from our long weekend to NYC! I'm a frequent visitor and this is the best hotel that I've stayed in here!
After a very swift check in and the staff on entrance were always very helpful with any questions we had. 
A little unguided to our cabins as you do need to take 2 lifts. But we did find our way eventually. 
The room was great we were very pleased on arrival clean and very modern. Easy to use everything in it. 
A short walk to times square in a perfect location close to the action but not too busy. Only 2 blocks and your in the heart of it. 
The map the hotel gave was very helpful. And the free tea/coffee was very appreciated. 
The staff in the lobby (floor 4) were not as helpful as they could have been. And were difficult to talk to always seemed to be in a rush!
The complementary breakfast was lovely muffins (very fresh). 
Overall a great stay will defefinitely use this hotel on our next trip to NYC. Very pleasant experience.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text: My sister and I planned a getaway to new York for the weekend of 12/9/11. We had prior superior experience at the palomar hotel in Chicago and based on that we booked ink48. According to the kimpton website our best deal would be to pay in advance which we did. Subsequently lower rates were found for equal rooms. I contacted the hotel and was told to provide proof which I did. They then told me to call them to discuss my options which I did. A minor adjustment was made, but I was told not to expect such things to happen in the future, because when you pre pay, that's the chance you take. Upon our arrival, there was no doorman or bellman to help us with our luggage. We were also informed that the lounge was having a private event and we could not go up. We went to our rooms and ate at the hotel restaurant. Food was delicious. After returning to our room we noticed that an 18% gratuity had been added to our check automatically. I never saw that and added 20% on top of that. Next morning was the same thing. 18% tip added to our breakfast for two. The lounge was closed once again for a private affair. We wanted to sit in the downstairs area for a drink but were told that that area was booked. We could not have felt LESS welcome at our hotel. We found a couch to sit down and asked if someone could please get us a drink. Got our drinks AND 20% tip included. There are not options for breakfast in the area so once again breakfast at the hotel. Food is very good I should say. My sister saw they had free coffee in the lobby so stopped to get some. Manager would not let her bring it into the restaurant. Said it was not affiliated even though you can charge directly to your room. Instead we had the privilege of paying $18 for offer for two. This is only the second time I have complained about a hotel. I travel extensively and I think/hope I have an awareness of when I'm treated as a welcome guest and when I'm not. I will never stay here again and I will never recommend it to anyone. Next time it's back to le Parker meridian...my favorite

review_title: Felt like i was on a bottom floor cruise ship.
review_text: Hotel was clean, good location.. They double charged my debit card on a Thursday, called Friday and no one was available until Monday to issue a credit?! Got xfered on the phone 4 times until it reached someone's voicemail. Won't stay here again
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text: Nous avons eut la chance de dormir 5 nuits aux towers. Absolument fantastique!! Nous avions une suite exÃ©cutive, chambre 39m. Elle faisait environs 90 mÃ¨tres carrÃ©. La literie est juste fantastique. La salle de bain est bain est grandiose. Petit dÃ©jeuner et thÃ© de l'Ã¢pres midi inclus dans le prix. Que Dire de plus, le waldorf towers fait partie des meilleures adresses que je connaisses et pourtant je suis habituÃ©e Ã  voyager.
hotel_name: The Towers of the Waldorf Astoria

review_text: Terrible service! Concierge incompetent. Requested res which was booked by the staff at the wrong restaurant even after confirming with the staff. Then when asked about the mistake, the staff member stated that she "googled it wrong.". Are u kidding me! I forgot to mention that she laughed at her mistake as if it was funny that we had planned for weeks to fly 800 miles to eat at a special restaurant to us and not have the requested res that she had confirmed was done. Very disappointing experience.

review_title: A wonderful Kimpton hotel with a great concierge!
review_text: My sisters & I had a sister's getaway weekend in NYC and we loved this hotel. I really liked the location because it wasn't in the thick of the craziness. It had lovely views because there's space between buildings & there's a building height restriction in this area. It's close to great restaurants, a few blocks from the subway. The concierge, Jeffrey, was fantastic. Very welcoming & very helpful. He sent us to two great restaurants & nailed it! Our room was beautiful. Upscale & contemporary. Comfortable beds & lovely linens. Huge bathroom. I love Kimpton hotels - they never disappoint. I didn't make it to the rooftop bar, but it's supposed to be a lot of fun with great views. Quite the hotspot. Highly recommend to those who want to enjoy comfort, style and a more local neighborhood feel.

Upon arrival this was everything like I've read about.Super fast checking on the ground floor with plenty of helpfull staff around at all times.You then go in the lift up to Four.Mission control,the lounge,the bar,the restaurant,meeting booths & access to the outdoor terrace are all on this level.I never needed mission control for anything but they'll help getting transfers to the airport or tickets to shows if needed.From Four you get into another lift(there's four lifts)up to which ever floor you are on.Theres a galley on each floor with microwave,fridge,cold water & crushed ice dispenser & a hot drinks machine which are all free to use at any time of the day.The rooms are spotless with everything you could need.Soap dispenser at the sink & two in the shower so no need bringing your own adding to the weight in your case.Theres a hairdryer,iron + ironing board great tv with iPod connection and the bed can be made into a sofa at the touch of a button.Free wifi & air con aswell.When checking out if you've got time to spare before your flight as we had then you can leave your bags or cases with the Yobot a fancy robot on ground level.Our cases were to big in height so the porter took them off upstairs for use while we made the most of our remaining time in this wonderful city.The guys on the ground level will hail you a cab but this really is only a 10 min walk into times sq.Go out the hotel doors turn right then right again.Also if you want the subway then you'll pass the port authority subway on the way to times sq.Also if you get chance go to TIMES SCARE down in times sq.If you love scary movies & don't have a weak heart you will love this place.Also the Magican there is awesome he got to the semi finals of Americas got talent.His name is Dan Sperry!Hope you have a wonderful time like we did!!!!
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text:
Stayed at yotel for my 40th birthday in mid October. 
Checked in via screens in lobby and helped by a friendly staff member. They took our bags to our room on the 21st floor and showed us how the gadgets worked and explained about breakfast and the galley. The galley was a room which had complimentary tea coffee and hot chocolate. Breakfast was served from floor four - mission control at 7am. Only muffins and coffee or tea but it was free so that was a bonus!
It was only 10 minute walk into times square with lots of restaurants, diners and convenience around. 
The only negative point was I found the bed too hard and asked for a pad or mattress topper only to be given a quilted mattress protector type thing that didn't really help. 
Checking out was easy on the screen in lobby. Didn't use YOBOT but it looked cool!
Yotel was a bit of a party scene over the weekend we stayed. Loud music on floor four but it didn't bother us but I can imagine slightly older folk may not like it! I was given a $20 gift voucher to use in the bar or restaurant I think as they knew it was my 40th. Nice touch. 
Rooms were small but the expert use of cubby holes and gaps to hang clothes and put bags and suitcases made room feel bIgger.
I d definitely go again and stay at yotel!
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text:
I booked Yotel for 2 nights on hotels.com and got an awesome rate. I arrived at Yotel really early--at 9AM the day of check-in. My room was ready, so they let me check in right then. So awesome!
The location was great for everywhere we ventured to--easy access from Port Authority and Penn Station, the theatre district, museums, great food options and anything else you can think up. 
The room was quite spacious by NYC standards and was super comfortable. The elevators were quick and the staff was friendly and accommodating. I'd definitely stay at Yotel again. 
Coffee and muffins for complimentary breakfast, food and drinks available in the hotel, a sweet view and helpful little map of the city. 
The music at Yotel was really cool and changed with each environment--lobby to elevators to hallway. 
Bed folds up to make more daytime space in the room, nice lighting and nice entertainment wall with iPhone/iPod plugin. Overall great experience.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text: Yotel was clean and good value for the location, but some of the mod looks sacrificed simple functionality. The shower drained onto the bathroom floor creating an uncomfortable puddle, the bed was hard as a rock because of no boxspring, the lights and window shades were hard to work, and our reservation had a glitch when we checked in. The lobby is a row of computers which makes it feel impersonal. That being said, it was clean and a good value for the proximity to Times Square. I wouldn't stay there for more than one night because of the uncomfortable bed and how awkward the modern service and atmosphere was. Depends what you like, but yotel is pretty much a watered down version of The W hotel.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text: No hot water for showers on Nov 20 with no notification, reason or alternatives. Prevented from bringing all guests to rooftop to take in spectacular views as advertised. Extremely disapointing experience.

review_title: Expensive for an impressive, unique view
review_text:
This hotel has everything to be a great hotel, incl. an breathtaking 360 panoramic view of the city skylines from the terrace.
Very large bedroom with all facilities.
However, the service let's the hotel down! It says in the handbook that the hotel provides an experience for every guest to feel unique during the stay whereas the reality is that we were restricted by the rules and security procedures (!). For example we were enjoying the welcome drink at the bar and was asked to move by the barman because the hotel has a separate licence to the bar... In the evening, while we were going from the terrace to the lobby for a cigarette outside (the only authorized area), 2 people politely requested (like in military operations !) not to take our glasses...
So it is a great hotel but the constraints are excessive and prevent you from having a relaxing experience.

Stayed at Ink 48 for 3 nights on business. Beautifully decorated, comfortable, very clean and spacious size guestrooms for the city. Only a 10 minutes walk to the Javits Center and right in front of the cruise terminal. View from my room to the Hudson and saw a NCL ship arriving very early on Saturday morning. Go up to the roof top bar and check out the view - amazing! More out of the way location for Times Square or Central Park areas. Really liked this property! The only negatives I can think of were the drinks in the minibar were Luke warm and it can be quite difficult to get a cab between 5-7 pm.

review_title: A superior example of what hotels need to be... Especially in NYC!
review_text: Believe it or not, I was at a Springhill in Lake Charles, Louisiana. It had a new generation theme with superior design and functionality. It was a real conceptual surprise and it gave me hope for a realized comfortable stay. Now, put that on steroids and add a huge helping of humanity. Yotel is near perfection. And to top what they've done at any point in the future will take some serious vision. It's that fine of an experiece.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text: We chose this hotel for a combined business/leisure stay also coinciding with our wedding anniversary. Chose it based on tripadvisor reviews and have not regretted this for a single second! Location is perfect, far from the crowds and noises but close all the city centre attractions. We looooved the funky and stylish atmosphere of Yotel, appreciated friendly, relaxed and service-minded staff and loved the food and drinks both for breakfast, lunch and dinner. We really loved the fact that the hotel style is so complete - from staff uniform and behaviour to the music, decor of rooms and names of dishes in the menu. Great job, we'll be back!
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text: If you like modern with hi-tech, that is the hotel you will enjoying stay. Great location, just d block to time square. Early check in usually not a problem. But the stuff not so helpful when come to early checking.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_title: Nice staff, big room, terrible view! Too far from the subway
review_text:
My boyfriend and I stayed Hereford our week long holiday and booked a junior suite. I think we were given the worse room (718) as we obliged one window and the view was terrible. Having advertised the room on the basis on having a view of the Hudson I expected more. 
The staff were pleasant, if sometimes a little snooty at reception. 
Wine hour was a nice touch. 
The room was nice and comfortable and house keeing did a good job. It was very quiet so we slept well. 
As we were sight seeing the hotel was a little too far away from midtown or subway as we were walking so much everyday as it was. If I went back to NY I would stay more central midtown.

review_title: Excellent hotel, Fantastic value and great location
review_text: Stayed for 5 nights with my wife and couldn't recommend it enough, check in was easy, we were in the room 5 minutes after walking in, room was spotlessly clean and plenty big enough for the two of us but clothes hanging space is a bit limited,that was the only fault we could find with the room, this is New York so you don't spend too much time in the room.Times square is about a ten minute walk up 42 nd st. And the main bus terminal is 5 minutes away.all in all a great hotel and we would stay there again and have no hesitation recommending it to anybody
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_title: All glitz and glamour, no substance.
review_text: Worst hotel ever. Automatic key check in didn't work, Yobot was broken, rooms are sooooo small and the service was awful.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text: Great location with great restaurants in 3 block radius. Jeffrey the concierge was fantastic. Got us reservations at 11 Madison square when booked for months. Free bikes to borrow and circumnavigated Manhatton in 4 hours in bike paths from front door.

review_title: Great if all you want is a basic room in a funky hotel
review_text:
YOTEL is ideal if all you need is a bed and basic necessities. It is not for people who like lots of space to relax or entertain in their rooms. 
The automated check-in was simple. Even though I arrived at 10:00 am my room was ready. 
The room was small but efficiently laid out. Everything I needed was there, but not an inch wasted. It was spotless. Everything in the room is whiter-than-white so that's a bit overwhelming when you turn the lights on. 
The bar happy hour is great value. $4 each for wine, bar and a good selection of appetizers. I had sushi, beef sliders and two glasses of wine for $16. 
The location is handy to Times Square, but verging on the sketchy. In the 5 blocks from Times Square you go from bustling tourist and entertainment district to the fringes of a seedier industrial area. The area seems to be gentrifying so in a couple of years it may be a great neighbourhood. 
All-in-all excellent value if all you want is a place to lay your head.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text:
Stayed here in November 2011.. The hotel has about 10 minutes walk to Times Square/broadway. 
A great bar on fourth floor, free coffee machines on each floor, free wifi and free breakfast.. Rooms are small but very modern, and you don't come to New York to stay in the room.. But whilst you are here there are no complaints, great views of the city, friendly staff, decor very modern.. Perfect place...
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text: Down by the USS Intrepid, this Kimpton hotel has a very friendly staff, clean room, very quiet location and good value for the price.

Rooms are huge for NYC. Rooftop bar is spacious with amazing views. Be sure to meet Nandi at the front desk. She is pleasant, engaging, and patient! The staff, in general, is great but Nandi definitely goes above and beyond!

What a massively overpriced place it was. I could have stayed in the Waldorf Astoria for the same money. Such a mediocre hotel, position wasn't that great either. Do not get suckered into the boutique hotel thing, its just not worth the money, in fact stay in the Edison, much better placed and cheaper. I booked Ink48 because of reviews on here, how surprised was I when I found out what I was getting for my money.

I travel to NYC frequently and found ink48 by accident. And I love it! The view, service, space and aesthetics are all top notch and so outstanding that you can overlook the loud music in the lobby. It's been so fun to introduce new Yorkers to the hidden gem in their own city. Every new yorker I've sent their has fallen in love. Be sure to ask for a city view when booking. You can't get a view like that in NYC for the price!

I stayed at Yotel for 1 night. The room was very interesting, specifically the layout. Good use of space. It had everything a hotel room typically should have. It suited me, myself and I - though had I been with my husband, it would have been very cozy and somewhat lacking space. 
The bathroom lacked privacy, if you are into that. It was very modern and had a glass sliding door. 
The bed was very unique, as it came up and down with the touch of a button. Though the novelty of the sliding bed was a hit, the comfort was lacking. The mattress was very firm and uncomfortable. 
Other small details were there was a cable to connect your iPod, iPhone which would allow you to play music through the TV.
Downfall was where my room was located; directly adjacent to a stairwell. The stairwell was constantly used by staff - as I could hear the door opening and closing regularily.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text: The room is clean and cute. Great location, and the staff is super nice. I had a wonderful time n definitely will stay again!!
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_title: Wonderful integration of energy efficientcy & artfulness. Very modern.
review_text: We stayed here during a convention at Javits Center. Easy walk to the convention & times square. Very modern rooms & lobby. Loved the hotel, it reminds me of flying on Virgin America. Very friendly staff. The weekend private parties seemed a little wild though.... The club loung was closed during these parties.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West
Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City

review_text: I was so impressed by the quality of customer service and the care that the great people working at Ink 48 had for their guests. I was asking for help trying to find a good restaurant from a great guy named Jason working at the front desk, and I noticed that one of the fish in the fish tank on the desk seemed sick and I was sad it might die. Not only did he recommend an amazing restaurant, he got a fish bowl and brought the sick fish to my room so I could take care of him during my stay and try to help him get better. He even brought up fresh fruit and a bottle of wine for my mom who was sad from visiting the world trade center memorial. I cannot thank him and the people who work at Ink 48 enough for their generosity!!!

review_title: Modern, clean hotel in a great location offering great value in NYC! Excellent hotel!
review_text:
Great location, very easy to find, easy access to times square and rest of Manhattan.
Check in process is very quick and simple on the computers in the lobby, the guys there will help and show you to your room, giving you some useful info about the hotel on the way.
The room is small compared to other US rooms but has everything you need and the bed slides up to create more space and it has everything you need - big tv, iron, hair dryer, large shower etc. 
The galley is a great idea - free water, ice, coffee and fridge on every floor which is very convenient.
Concierge on level 4 are very helpful. The free wifi in the rooms and computers in reception come in handy for researching attractions or checking flight details.
We booked on last minute .com and saved 25% with the advance purchase offer which made it even better value.
All in all a fantastic hotel!
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text: I was very pleased with my stay. Amanda couldn't have bEen nicer and was excellent in recommending things to do. She was able to recommend the most spectacular places to visit and met all our needs. Will definitely be coming back.

review_text:
I enjoyed my stay. It was unlike anyplace I'd been before, with automated check-in and a small, easy-to-hose-down but slick and chic room. The robotic valet in the lobby is an eye-catcher and sets the mood. 
I typically prefer DIY to excessive service pushed in your face, so this fit my likings nicely. I was concerned that the barebones service approach would mean that maid service wouldn't be prompt and comprehensive, but thankfully it was. No complaints there. 
The room itself is just fine -- small but comfortable, with smart design decisions making up for the lack of space. The adjustable reclining bed is especially good, making the room more usable during the day without sacrificing comfort during sleep time. 
Two things I missed: a shower door (water splashed out into the toilet area) and a small fridge. I know a fridge would be a relative luxury for such a stripped-down place, but it seems like exactly the kind of targeted smart luxury that its guests would appreciate. As it was, I used the ice maker on my floor quite often. 
On my way out, I forgot to check out. Calling the main line, the person I spoke to rectified this immediately and without issue. So real people DO work there and are helpful. 
I didn't try the breakfast but instead walked to the nearby Sullivan Street Bakery for its pizze bianca, which is delicious and almost exactly like what you'll get in Rome. Mmmmm.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text: Although this hotel offers a good location to times square, the value for money is compromised in lack of space in 'your cabin'. There is no door to separate the bathroom, and the extendable bed was cement hard making the floor an attractive option (not that you could lie on floor due to lack of room). The corridor noise outside the 'cabin' also made for no sleep.

review_title: Efficient new hotel in a great district.

Rooms are small but efficiently designed. We brought two huge suitcases with us and found places for both of them
Staff was very friendly and helpful.

We arived in to the city late due to a delay in our flight and we were extremely tired and just hoped that check ing in wouldnt be a hectic process, from reading that its a self check in kiosk. review_text:
When we arrived we were greeted by a very helpful gentleman who helped us check in. The hotel design is very impressive and I loved the contemporary look.
Our room was quite small but very clean and I liked the moveable bed quite a quirky feature. The toilet/shower room is separated from the room by a glass partition and curtain so not an awful lot of privacy but we didn't find it a problem.
On each floor there is a galley kitchen with free coffee machine (and the coffee was good!), fridge and microwave. 
The light breakfast was a nice touch, just muffins and coffee/tea but was great for us.
Downsides: was difficult to get the lift in the mornings as they were all so busy! Breakfast was pretty crammed and had to push your way through to get a muffin!
All in all a good hotel. The rooftop bar was definitely my favourite part, don't miss it. The guests seemed like a good crowd too.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_title: Nice budget hotel in good location
review_text: Though small, room is very well organized. Bed was comfortable, linen was of good quality.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_title: Great hotel, wonderful service (esp. Yannick & Nandi)
review_text:
This was my first trip to New York, and I can't think of a better hotel to stay at. The staff was very attentive, had wonderful attitudes, and the hotel was awesome. Loved the rooms, loved the bar upstairs, loved everything. 
Yannick and Nandi were particularly helpful. I was in NY for a business trip and they took the time to tell me where p to go and what to do to best treat my clients.
I would highly, highly recommend Ink48. Many of my colleagues have also stayed at Ink48 and I know they are equally pleased.
Great hotel, great service, great experience.

Luved this place!! I get the idea its a love it or hate it place. 
It has a cool location, walkable to times square and lots of 9th ave restaurants but not so close that it was overwhelming (as times square can be)
I know people complained of checking in problems, but I had none. The doorman held the door for me & whisked me to a computer, told me to type in my last name and # of nights. Had I not spelled my last name wrong the 1st time, it would have taken a whole 30 seconds to check in and have key in hand. (Early too- before noon.)
They did have complimentary breakfast each mornin - yes it was just muffins but it was free and this is nyc!! Each floor had a communal kitchen with an espresso maker that made awesome free lattes, chais, mochas, etc.
I stayed in a room alone, but the bathroom DOES have a sort of sliding glass door and a curtain.
Lighting was awesome- you could make it really purple and soothing. The bed was like a futon. Very firm mattress but very supportive pillows. Personally, i like having good pillows overly soft mattress. You could raise and lower the top of the bed. 
Overall, it wasn't big but well laid out and very functional. No tissue, but come on! You cant improvise with toilet paper?
Other perks: very cool outdoor bar/ patio. HUGE with beautiful view. I didnt eat at the restaurant but i t looked good.
Also, the main club Lounge is free to hotel guests and had celebrities and djs while I was there. That's a huge plus right there. 
I'm not in my 20s so not necessarily in the main age bracket, but I found all the employees very friendly. A few went out of their way, giving me bandaids for my blistered feet (bring comfy shoes for walking!) without me asking.
I didn't see the yobot work but no big deal. There is a convienent 24 hour cvs across the street and a grocery store (fridge and microwave in the galley) around the block. 
This was not exactly a budget hotel, but it was nearly the lowest price decent hotel around midtown for the weekend I stayed. 
Loved the yotel!! Very fun place.
**Oh yea, qtip dj-ed and ashanti was at the club 
:))
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_title:
Especially welcoming and attentive staff plus an unexpectedly top notch locavore restaurant and rooftop
lounge with spacious s
review_text: From the moment we arrived until our day of departure we felt welcomed and served at just the right level. The concierge, Jeffrey, poured great complimentary wine from 5-6 and made several great restaurant reservations for us. The entire frontline staff was gracious and accomodating. Highly recommend Print the hotel restaurant that sources food from family farms. Will definately stay here again.

Awesome hotel super close to Hells Kitchen & Time Sq
Clean White and utterly modern. Compact but fully equipped rooms. Easy check in and out. 
Perfect. Would really reccommend.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_title: Yotel is unlike any hotel you've ever stayed in before.
review_text:
I found Yotel on the web. The pictures on the website showed that it was definitely different from the old-line hotels of New York. I loved the look of the hotel in the pictures, and was not disappointed to find that the actual hotel matched up to the pictures. Sometimes you can be fooled by a wide-angle lens picture. 
My cabin was small (which I knew from the website that it would be) and pristine.The layout of the cabin/room was designed to maximize the available space. 
I had a great view of the city and the location of the hotel is great. It was about a 10 minute walk to Times Square and the theaters. 
The restaurant was trendy and the food was great. I loved the "small plates/tapas" presentation of the food. 
My one complaint was the staff on Four. The young man that checked me in on the first floor could not have been nicer. However, at no point during my stay did anyone on Four acknowledge me in any way. I never even got a cursory "Good Morning" nor the traditional "Have a good night, sir". In fact, no one at Mission Control even made eye contact with me. Their attitude and aloof mannerism prevented me from even asking about the great smelling body wash products.
In summary, new and trendy are great, but don't forego tradition when it comes to common courtesy to your guests. 
I will stay at Yotel again, and the next time I hope the Four staff are a little more humble when it comes to the treatment of the guests. 
Remember: no guests, no paychecks. 
David Atchley
Johnson City, TN
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_title: Beautiful view ,clean crisp cabins. Great service.
review_text: I'm from queens and it was my anniversary ,wanted to get away for the weekend . Aubrey was great in helping book a room , and remembered us when we walked in the next day. Yotel has a very nice and warm staff I would definitely stay there again and also recommend to friends.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

Les chambres sont tres spacieuses moderne et extremement bien equipÃ©es! Petit dejeuner tres copieu variÃ© et de tres bonne qualitÃ© ainsi que les apero servient du mardi au jeudi! hotel_name: Staybridge Suites Times Square - New York City

review_text: We moved to NYC recently and stayed in Ink48 for two weeks! The service is amazing and it is the little things they do that makes them shine! They sent up dog treats for our dog. They remember our names and have made us feel like family. I am a Kimpton regular and this is why!

review_title: Great week spent at Ink48, even my dog had fun.
review_text: I spent a week here at Ink48. The rooms were comfortable, the service was excellent but the real star treatment went to my dog Jake. He got a really cool gift basket, he went for walks in the park nearby and everyone welcomed him. The complementary wine glass between 5:00-6:00 was a nice touch and the rooftop terrace, amazing!

review_title: The best hotel in New York!!!
review_text: We stayed at the hotel for two days during our hmoon trip and felt that was the best experience ever. We got a free upgrade with amazing city view. Also got a free champagne and brownies. Great rooftop bar not to be missed. Will reconmend this to all my friends.

This is a very cool hotel with an ingenious room layout. Rooms are small but very well-designed and comfortable. Location is very good, right next to 9th Ave, Hell's Kitchen, which has lots of good bars and restaurants. 
However, I found the staff on the Floor 4 'mission control' desk rude. No eye contact and a dismissive, unhelpful attitude even when they were at fault for losing a package. And lots of big, security guys glaring at everyone. 
On the plus side, the staff in the lobby who help with check-in were very helpful and friendly so the first impression was a really good one.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_title: Excellent service from a wonderful group of staff
review_text: My teenage daughter and I travel to new York 2/3 times a year and have stayed at many of the hotels around Times Square. This was our first visit to Yotel. We were there during the Hurricane and whilst the rest of New York closed down the staff and management insured that life continued as best it could for the guests. Yes the rooms are small but that's New York. Yes the breakfast is muffins and hot drinks in paper cups but it is free and if you want a proper breakfast that's available in the restaurant. Special mention must go to DJ and Emmanuel who always were on hand to help with my daughters fencing kit and to Ricky who looked after us brilliantly. Don't think we will stay anywhere else now.
hotel_name: YOTEL New York at Times Square West

review_text:
This hotel was great! It's about 3 blocks from times square and the subway stations. The rooms were very modern and pretty spacious for nyc, but the only thing wrong with it is the bed. I would definitely stay here again. 
One tip I would give is to try and get a room as high up as possible to have a better view of the city.

The ambiebce and technology used is like sci-fi meets trendy. The terrace is really relaxing and the rooms are European standard size (US small). The price is on the mid to high for NYC however its still reasonable. The pantry on every floor is nice and offers great Lavazza coffee. The only downside is that the mattress are as stiff as a board, more stiff than US standards and may be even than European as well. The owner as for feedback and did mention they would be adding some mattress Toppers to meet domestic clientele requests.

review_title: Very clean hotel 15 steps from subway. Very easy to get around
review_text: I really liked this hotel-clean, close to the subway (15 steps) so its really easy to get around the city. Also, the huge shower and hot hot water was very nice. Invest in a good map before you go and spend the $30 for a 7 day unlimited subway pass. This will pay for itself many times over. Only thing that irked me is they give you a bottle of water at check in and refuse to give you water any other night of your stay and they are $2 to purchase. Grab a bottle from the vendor just outside the hotel for a buck. Also do NOT eat the hotel breakfast. Yes it is convenient but you are 10 minutes from 2 excellent diners (N or R train downtown to 23rd street)-try Johnny's Luncheonette or Malibu Diner. At Johnny's you get 2 eggs, sausage or bacon, toast, coffee or tea AND potatoes for ONLY $6!!! Amazing deal. The only thing is that for $350 a night you can pre pay and stay at the W midtown for a few dollars more. Just something to consider.

review_text:
My husband and I stayed at this hotel in late August and after reading some more reviews now we are back home in Australia, I don't feel so bad that I ultimately did not like this hotel at all. 
The hotel is good value for it's location to times square and access to the train station but that's about it. 
The hotel is dirty for something that is supposed to be brand new, the only staff who understand the concept of customer service are the lovely gentleman on the ground floor ( not to be mistaken for 'mission control' ) the construction next to the hotel starts at the butt crack of dawn, the hotel holds terrace parties until 4 am, the housekeeping staff walked in our room twice without knocking - once when I was on the toilet. We also stayed across the wekend of the hurricane - we had a bad one in Australia earlier this year so knew what to expect however, I felt for the other guests when it took the hotel until late Saturday afternoon to stick a note under the door which said " there is a hurricane warning - shut your windows" and pretty much nothing else. 
I expected the rooms to be small so no issue there. Overall the hotel should have spared their guests that useless robot on the ground floor and spent more money on facilities.

review_text:
This review is based on my experience last week at Yotel as an attendee at a party.
A friend of mine from out of town decided to celebrate his birthday at the party DJed by Q-Tip of the legendary hip-hop group A Tribe Called Quest. I called ahead to find out the dress code and cover charge. I was given the information, but when I arrived at the venue, I discovered that the cover charge was $5 more than I was told it would be. I was upset and complained to a manager that I was misinformed by a staff member. She issued an apology immediately and kindly offered me a complementary drink from the bar to make amends. I appreciated the gesture.
Overall, I had a positive experience. The entrance, lobby, terrace and bar room are designed beautifully. I enjoyed the outside terrace elegantly set-up with bars and seating for guests.
I spent most of my time in the bar room which was somewhat small but tastefully designed and set-up. The space was very clean and, coming from a music and sound background, I was impressed with the sound system. I thoroughly enjoyed the party. Q-Tip did a good job DJing mixing both classic and new Hip-Hop and R&B and keeping the crowd moving. The drinks were a tad pricey (I got a gin & tonic for $13), but I guess that should be expected of a venue of that caliber so close to Times Square. The crowd was comprised of mostly mature music lovers and celebrities.
I would go back for the nightlife experience and, though I haven't stayed in the hotel yet, would consider it an option if I needed a hotel.

review_title: The Lowell is understated, elegant, and becomes your personal pied a terre in a lovely and convenient east side neighborhood.
review_text:
I believe we've been staying at the Lowell for approximately 15 years, usually visiting in the spring and fall. My wife and I have a favorite one-bedroom suite that we request, which is particularly nice in cool fall weather with its wood-burning fireplace. The suite has been totally renovated with a beautiful and spacious white marble bathroom and granite topped kitchenette. We use the Lowell as our base on these 5 night trips for forays to the theater, museums, restaurants and socializing with friends who are lucky enough to call NYC home. The Lowell is a welcome and ultra-comfortable respite from busy days and nights. We have also used it to host small cocktail gatherings in our suite, or order pizza up and watch a movie with friends. As I said, it feels like home and it's a tranquil and inviting respite to busy days and nights in the city. But above all, the real gems of the Lowell are its staff. 
These people are there to serve in a friendly and professional manner. They're down to earth, but exacting in executing your wishes and making you feel welcome and very special. From desk managers, to doormen, to bell men, to waiters and housekeeping, we see very little turnover from year to year. I assume the Lowell personnel are treated well, enjoy their jobs, and therefore reciprocate to their guests. The concierges, John Mark and Philip, are outstanding resources, well connected, and eager to advise and facilitate. The Lowell is a small hotel with approximately 4 rooms or suites per floor on 17 floors. It is an old building, but gracious and elegant. If you enjoy your hotels large, sleek, and bustling, this isn't what you're looking for. If you want highly personal attention, elegantly timeless ambience, and a stellar east side location between Park and Madison, this is your place. However, like most things dear and unique, it comes at a price, and it will get your attention depending on what type of accommodation you 
choose. But, that is a matter of choice, personal prioritiy and most likely frame of mind. The Lowell offers my wife and I everything we're looking for in NYC and we always look forward to coming back.
