review_text: Beautiful hotel! Not a big chain hotel, yet not as small as most boutique style hotels in NYC. I comsider myself pretty picky when it comes to hotels, and i loved it here. Pros: spacious rooms, clean, unique decor, beautiful fitness facility w city views, great staff, and perfect midtown location! Cons: small TV in room, no fun lounge or bar at hotel, had issues w our room in particular with some vent noise. They sent someone up to fix it and ended up giving and upgraded room to me. Awesome stay... If i cant afford four seasons and dont want to stay at the marriott or W, the London is where its at!

review_title: Good Location | Large room | Otherwise Average
review_text:
Although the London NYC has received many good reviews, we failed to witness same. We booked through AMEX FHR program with an high expectation level set and unfortunately wished we had not. Yes, the location is excellent: Columbus Circle, Broadway, Fifth Avenue, Subway... All good. And Yes, rooms are larger than many in NYC, but overall we would have opted for a smaller room if the details were taken care of. Check in was like having your Miranda rights provided. I did ask for an upgrade which is available with the AMEX FHR, subject to availability, but no... this was not available... surprising for a hotel with some 500 rooms on 54 floors. We were given a room on the 15 floor. I was hoping for a room with a good view. We were told it was a larger room and, too, was a corner! So be it... Turns out the room was not a corner, not larger, and to disappoint even more so must have been the poorest view vantage available. We were just some 20 feet from an old residential building that wraps around the north and east corner of the hotel. So what are the odds of getting a low floor out of 54 and to worse view of which maybe only 20 out of 500 get. To add to the disappointment AMEX includes a promotional item explaining how we have received $450 with of benefit through booking with this program. What we got was an average well sized room, on a low floor, zero view and a "pardon me you are interrupting my day" check-in. We did receive complimentary breakfast (cold buffet) and "high" tea. The tea... not devon or clotted, but whipped... They provided one pot given we order the same English Breakfast and when asking for some more, provided more hot water with the same single tea bag. How many cups of tea do they expect to get out of one bag, only made more shocking that we were at a Afternoon Tea? And the scones... so dry they crumbled into many many pieces when trying split them to add jam. Not what I would have expected from a chef regarded as always seeking perfection. We decided not to make a reservation for his restaurant given this experience. The room... In need of some attention... Damaged furniture, worn carpet, needed new batteries for remotes, etc. Last item... Inconsistent "service" at the restaurant especially form the hostess.
We have many gold and platinum hotels loyalty cards... Shame we decided not to use them on this trip and settled for the London NYC. The problem is obviously not the staff, but the management to allow such mediocracy! It should be removed from the AMEX program and personally I would not choose to stay here again.

My husband and 9 year old daughter just returned from staying here. The entire staff was fantastic, polite and nice-probably the best hotel staff I have ever encountered. They even had cupcakes for my daughters birthday upon check-in! The rooms were up to par with most NYC sizes, and beautifully decorated. We were able to walk to all plays, shopping and Central Park. We will absolutely stay here again!

review_title: Great location and suite style rooms, but little else
review_text: Right on Times Square so location could not be better. Hardly any other facilities. However, restaurant served tasty food. Room was a sitting room and bedro with two doubles. We were badly advised on booking that it could accommodate 6 of us and as a result it was very cramped. We needed two suites and would have happily paid for it had they been available.

First trip to NYC! We had a blast and the hotel was awesome. Location was right in the middle of all the action, breakfast was yummy, and the service was terrific. Drinks in the bar were expensive but so is everything else. 1/2 price ticket booth right across the street from the hotel, subway right next door and the red line bus tour was right across the street. 1st time New York visitor stay here! And..having a suite was great for our family. Thanks doubletree!!

review_title: Amazing staff! Blanche, Whitney, Lenny and Rafael were excellent.
review_text: I have never wrote a review when I stayed at hotels in the past but i feel I must for my stay at the Sanctuary. I've stayed at many hotels but the service at The Sanctuary was second to none. The cocktails at the bar made by Whitney and Blanche are dangerously good, Lenny knowledge of the local night life and food recommendations were excellent and Rafael on the door was first class. The rest of the staff were also excellent. The rooms are clean and well designed. The prices are very reasonable. The only thing I would like to see is a restaurant and room service etc as much as discovering NYC is great food around times sq isn't great and a quality restaurant with the level of service provided by the staff at the hotel would be an instant success. Highly recommend to anyone. Will be back. X

I stayed in a king room. It was on the 12 th floor facing the highway. It was quiet and very clean. There is a shower only but it was large. My room had a refrigerator and microwave. There was also a separate living area with a couch, desk and additional flat screen tv. 
My bed wasn't as comfortable as I hoped but it wasn't horrible either.
There's a 24 hr shuttle that takes you within five miles. You will need this shuttle if you don't have a car because there are no places to eat within walking distance.
The hotel does not have vending machines with food. They have a gift shop where mist items are about 2.00 each. I picked up a small bag of chips there during my stay. The other option is the hotels restaurant. I didn't eat there because I thought it was highly priced.
Valet parking is available. I didn't find it necessary as there's a parking garage right next to the hotel. The parking spaces are tiny so for my suv it was tight.
The staff was very professional and kind. 
This hotel is located on a toll road so keep that in mind. Going anywhere is going to cost you 1.50 each time you go through one of the tolls.
Overall I was happy with the room and hotel but not with the location.

What an amazing hotel! Great rooms, super location and fantastic staff and absolutely amazing bed! (Trying to work out if they will notice me pushing it out through resection so I can take it home to London)
Joanna, front of house manager was great and everyone at the hotel, from door man to the ladies servivinging the continental breakfast were super friendly and could not do more to help you.
This is a new hotel, and if Jeremy (the GM), Joanna and the rest if the team keep this up, this hotel will be the IT place to stay in NYC!

review_title: Luxury accomodation for a Great Price...
review_text: I stayed at the London for my bday.... It was a wonderful experience ... Staff very friendly .. Excellent service..... Room was big.... Nice , clean and comfy..... Romantic and Classy..... Bathroom very clean..... Loved it... Will definitely go again... This is for folks who love the finer things in life ....

review_title: In the heart of it all!
review_text: We stayed here for 5 days with out late owl 2 year old. Fantastic location. The staff could have been friendlier. Our room was clean and had all the ammenities for kids. I requested an allergen free room, but didn't get it.

review_title: bueno,bonito y barato... good,beautiful and inexpensive
review_text: excellent hotel ,great service, super clean.front desk reps were kind and helpful. i will surely return. lovely place and so many stores and restaurants near by.

Arrived around 7 on a Friday night, just in time for the manager's reception which lasts until 730p. Great drinks and snacks! Can't beat that! Kids loved the huge seating area around the atrium. 
Ate dinner in the hotel restaurant. Food was very good and not too overpriced. Only downside is that they were not busy at all but the wait for food was very long. That being said, after having a few drinks driving to another restaurant was not an option. 
Check in was quick and easy. The room was very nice; two queen size beds and a pull out couch. Rooms have refrigerators and a microwave. Coffee maker in room stinks, but it didnt matter because there was plenty of coffee in the morning at breakfast. 
The living room and bedroom area are separated by a heavy door, which means privacy. 
Shower was standard with the usual toiletries, nothing special. 
Breakfast in the morning was fantastic. We stayed because of a gymnastics meet that started early. Usually on Saturdays they open the buffet at 7, but they had it up and running full speed for 6. It is the usual Embassy Suites fare, but there was a lot of food and it was good. My favorite is the made to order omlettes...definately a nice touch. 
We didn't use the pool, gym or business center. They do have a sundry shop with snacks, drinks of all kinds and other things. 
The parking is great; a nice garage behind the hotel. They do offer valet parking but you really don't need it because the parking is convenient. 
All in all, it was a great stay and I would both recommend it and stay there again. 
Our price was $99 for two adults and two children, booked by calling the hotel.

I stayed at the sanctuary for 5 nights with my girlfriend in September this year. 
A lot of reviewed slate the hotel due to ongoing works. This really wasn't an issue. The lobby was having a bit of work done and our floor had been freshly decorated but none of this was a problem. 
The staff couldn't have been any more welcoming or helpful. The massive doorman was great and full of hints and tips. The reception staff were great, they made reservations for dinner on a couple of occasions and were always on hand. 
The room was well appointed and very clean. The shower was great and I loved the sliding toilet door. The mini bar and snacks withing the room were eclectic and a welcome break from the norm. 
I would absolutely stay here again and look forward to returning in a couple of years, not sure I will be able to afford it though as I'd imagine rates might rise once the word gets out!
Chris & Ruth from Scotland

review_title: Beautiful boutique hotel in the most amazing location.
review_text:
My Husband and I stayed here for 7days from 22nd to 29th September. This trip was to celebrate my 40th birthday and we paid extra for deluxe king room however when we booked we where advised that we had been allocated a deluxe queen, the reception staff where very helpful and advised that we could be allocated another room but suggested that we review our room first. We agreed and once in our room where very happy as we had a lovely view (which is very rare in NYC) another nice touch was that when we got into our room I was welcomed with a lovely card and bottle of wine to celebrate my birthday!! The hotel is absolutely gorgeous and will be even more amazing when completely finished - still to finish restaurant though we where not disturbed by any building work. The hotel is decorated to a very high standard and is absolutely spotless, the service was amazing and everyone was always very eager to help you. We only had one small issue with the hotel bar as opening times was quite inconsistent - I think this was due to new staff and would imagine would now be resolved! I would also make sure you get the price of your drinks as the prices where a bit expensive, though we did enjoy a few drinks during happy hour!!
All in all this has been our best trip to New York and I would say this has been one of the best hotels we have stayed in and we are currently planning our next trip and will definitely be returning to the Sanctuary.

review_title: Airport hotel with a family atmosphere
review_text: We stayed here in July 2010 and enjoyed it very much. The staff is extremely friendly and welcome you with a smile. After a year we decided to fly to Miami through Houston and booked a room for a night. They recognized us immediately. Incredible! We stay in 5 star hotels quite often but hardly ever wittness such sincere hospitality and recognition as a returning customer. Outstanding!

review_title: I did not want to come home!!
review_text: By far the best hotel I have ever stayed in. The staff were among the most friendly people I have encountered and went above and beyond the call of duty to help us with absolutely anything (if we didn't ask they volunteered). They made us feel so welcome and are a credit to this hotel. I would agree with other reviews that the rooms are not massive but it's location more than makes up for this plus in NYC your hotel should only be a place to rest you weary head at the end of a packed day! The hotel was a bit dark but this created a boutique ambience. I cannot Find anything to criticise this hotel and it will definitely be my first choice when I return to the big apple. I would definitely recommend to family and friends.

review_title: Heart of NYC Great Value and Spacious Comfort.
review_text: We ( 4 of us) booked Doubletree Suites Times Sq for a Friday night as we had theatre tix. The location is ideal, walking distance to show and dinner. Reasonable valet parking ($45) for 24 hrs-amazing in NYC. Smooth check-in, warm cookies, immaculate, luxurious 2 room suite with lovely amenities, awesome view, superb beds. What more could one want???

review_title: Best hotel mattress I've ever slept on.
review_text: Stayed here for Big East tournament and definitely will again. Most comfortable beds ever, even the extra cot/bed we had sent up was great. One note if the safe shows all 888's it's the gfi button in the bathroom. We waited 30 min for an engineer who pushed the button and fixed it.

This hotel is an old building with a makeover. It looks nice at a first glance but when your laying in your bed trying to sleep and the floor above you is non stop squeaking because instead of updating anything real they just put down new carpet and paint. But a lot of the cuteness of this hotel is how old the building is. So you get what you are thinking. I would stay here again if no newer hotels are available. Internet is painfully slow and the elevator only holds two people at a time.

review_title: Great location, friendly and helpful staff, perfect room for the money.
review_text: I loved our room in this centrally located, well-appointed, well-staffed, friendly, lively-yet-intimate hotel. It's exactly where we wanted to be and how we wanted to stay the night in Chicago. I am relocating to Chicago soon, but, until I do, whenever I plan on being in the city, I'll be checking availability first at the City Suites Hotel before anywhere else. I highly recommend this wonderful little hotel!

Stayed for 3 nights,front desk ignored all requests,I.e high floor,view of times sq. Etc.
Travelled with 2 small children who where very disappointed.
It's the little things that matter and make your stay a brilliant one.
This hotel only makes money from it's location,customer service leaves a lot to be desired.btw I am an Hilton diamond member and was ignored.
Spend your hard earned
 money elsewhere

review_title: Labor Day weekend stay at the City Suites Hotel
review_text:
We booked the CSH based upon the mostly positive Tripadvisor reviews, it's proximity to the "L", as well as being close to the Halstead area.
We checked in and were given a room on the "quiet" side, but once we got to the room, we realized we were on top of the yogurt shop which plays loud music, and is open past midnight, and heard the music below us. We requested another room, and we relocated to another room, on the "quiet" side, but it was at the south end of the hotel which was still close to the train. The noise wasn't too bad, especially with the air conditioner on. 
We had a queen suite, which was nice and big. The bed was soft and plush, and had a good nights sleep.
We didn't partake in the free continental breakfast,, so can't comment on that.
Parking was $22/day, and it is in a secure garage about a block away, with in/out priviledges. 
Staff was nice, and accommodating.
Went to a few places around the hotel for breakfast or lunch. Sinbad's Middle Eastern food a few doors down was good for lunch. Ann Sathers for breakfast was OK... not quiet as good as all of the hype.
Overall, the CSH was a great place due to it's proximity to the train which was a great benefit, and would stay there again.

review_title:
Good hotel, good location and great service!
Walk to restaurants and convenience stores and feel as you were in your own neighb
review_text:
I booked this hotel after searching something close to downtown but everything was busy or extremely expensive!
After all, i found a great experience, the location, a bit far from my business destination (15min taxi to the McCormic Place and 10min from dwntown) but the hotel has everything: free internet, spacious rooms, good TV and programming, etc... The best part is the service attitude from the personnel, they gave me some advises on how to maximize my visit, where to go around, how to leverage offers and deals for saving money, etc... And taking caee of my luggage until very late!
The bad: they cleaned my room late but they done quicly and silently.
So if you want to enjoy Chicago as local people do, this is a great option... Very close to the Cubs stadium, theaters, 1 block from the bus stop and the lake. Actually this is the Lake View area (or also called Wrigley Viile).
I will come here next time for sure!
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Plus Hawthorne Terrace Hotel

review_text: We had a king suite ( it was all that was left). It was a bit pricey but you can't beat the location. Great restaurants all around and 5 minute walk to the Boystown clubs. Great location and great restaurants in the area. I liked the laid back feel to the area and this is the best hotel in the area. I'd recommend it.
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Plus Hawthorne Terrace Hotel

review_title: Great room/suite, unbelievable price, perfect location for a visit/mini-vacation, we'll be back!
review_text: We normally stay at the Hilton on 6th Ave., but decided to try the Doubletree at Times Square as it was a little better price and closer to our planned venues for this trip. We were very pleasantly surprised to find a much larger two room suite with a prime Times Square view. We had a large flat screen HD tv in the living room and a second large flat screen tv in the separate bedroom. The room was spotless with a minibar, microwave oven, privacy safe, sink, coffee maker and refrigerator. We have definitely found a new "home-away- from home" when in NYC.

Such a perfect spot for visiting friends and misbehaving in Boystown. My 2nd stay in 5 years and still impressive: big rooms and new baths this time around. Friendly staff, and within comfortable walking distance of bus, el, restaurants, etc. If you need to stumble home after a great night out why stay anywhere else?!
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Plus Hawthorne Terrace Hotel

review_text: Big trucks. Loud clanks. Revved engines. Beep beep beep. I wish I had known they were building something right outside my window. Forget about sleep if you face the noise.
hotel_name: Springhill Suites Chicago Downtown / River North

review_text: Shares a building with a Marriott Residence Inn. As plastic hotels go it's fine but not exceptional Best attribute is location.
hotel_name: Springhill Suites Chicago Downtown / River North

review_title: Sutton Place-Chicago. Nice, maybe a bit over-priced
review_text:
I stayed at Sutton Place for one night in July of 2011. I walked in at about 1AM looking for availability (visiting someone in the hospital and needed a place to crash) which thankfully they had!
The location is actually excellent. Very convenient to all the sights and sounds of the magnificent mile. My first impression was that the lobby was rather small and it smelled of cigarettes. This made me a bit apprehensive about what the room would be like but it was just a place to crash for the night.
The single bedded king room was $199 for the night plus tax and the 24-hour valet parking was $45. Not horribly expensive especially for the location but you can definitely find some cheaper options in the area.
The room itself was small but nice. Modern amenities and in-room movies. Bathroom was actually quite large and well stocked (bathroom could have been smaller with a larger room).
I was exhausted and enjoyed a good nights sleep. Room was quite and the bed was comfortable. The staff was very nice and polite and responsive to our needs/requests. They only had one bedded rooms available but they quickly brought a roll away bed up for us.
Checkout was quick and efficient and the concierge kept my bag so that I would not have to lug it around the city.
I am a big fan a larger, chain hotels but overall, I can recommend Sutton Place Chicago. Relatively reasonably priced with nice (though small) rooms and polite staff.
Dated. Dirty with stains on floor. Room was smoked in and all my belongings stunk of cigarette smoke. Don't plan on coming back. I have stayed in 4 star hotels and this is not 4 star worthy.

review_title: Good, but only worth it only if you get a good rate or need to be in area.
review_text:
I stayed at the Wyndham Blake for business and it has all the basics for short-term travel: rooms are smallish but they make the most of it with an especially comfortable bed, a generous desk and an open glass stalled shower. 
Location is not prime for shopping but great for the park, museums and colleges. A little on the fringe of the main area so I wouldn't walk at night, but no worries during the day.
Very agreeable at $150 price I got for for a conference but stayed beyond 1 day and got hit with a $250 rate! I would stay again only if convenient for business but unlikely for personal travel. Not enough personality or perks to be a favorite in Chicago.

The overall experience was good but nothing great. We had two rooms book for a business trip however we did not realize that one of the rooms was book a day early. The hotel charges us a nights room which is understandable and listed in their cancellation policy... However they also cancelled the rest of the reservation and gave the room away. 
I would just expect a hotel listed in the top 50 on trip advisor to go the extra mile and contact the one who made the reservation prior to cancelling the entire stay. For that reason alone i can only give this hotel an average rating. More effort and consideration could have been shown.
Stayed here for 3 Nights and had no complaints. Good price makes it even better!
hotel_name: Springhill Suites Chicago Downtown / River North

review_title: Buen hotel un poco alejado del centro
review_text: Hotel muy completo, buenas camas, buen servicio y buenos precios. Por poner alguna pega diria q esta algo lejos de los dos metros mas cercanos. Con el bus 36 llegas bien al centro y la parada esta en la puerta dl hotel, lo unico q tardas bastante mas. El aire acondicionado hace bastante ruido, pero creo q compensa.
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN Plus Hawthorne Terrace Hotel

review_title: This hotel is in a great location.
review_text: Our family stayed here over the Christmas holiday. Weber Grill restaurant was very good. The staff was helpful, our room was spacious, and just steps away from shopping. We will stay here again.
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn Chicago Downtown/Magnificent Mile

review_text:
My friends and I were coming here for a convention. Because we are all students, our budget was limited and we couldn't afford the $400/night rooms that other attendees were staying at. It took me awhile to did a place that was in our price range, close to a bus line that went to the convention center, and that had availability during the time that we were there. I was pretty happy when I found Amber Inn, because there were so many positive reviews and seemed like a great deal. Being that the starting rate was so cheap, we even decided to upgrade to the "hotel suite" for $91/night. 
Our experience there was summed up by the text message that our friend who arrived there first sent out: "OMG this place is sooooo ghetto!"
It was in a very unsafe area of Chicago. We didn't even feel comfortable walking out to the bus stop and just decided to take cabs everywhere. The room was run-down and smelled like musty BO. The bathroom had some sort of voyeuristic red light that was reminiscent of a low-budget porn film. We stayed there three days and they never cleaned our room. When we asked for extra towels and pillows, the response was..."we're in the process of looking for them." Ugh-they never ended up bringing our pillow and my friend and I had to share one between us. One of our cab drivers, upon learning where we were going, commented that it was 'the hooker hotel' and asked us if we heard screaming at night. Our room was two girls and one guy, and our guy friend already had plans to stay in another hotel for the third and fourth night of our trip. I was very close to begging him to stay because I didn't feel safe staying there with just us two young girls. Thankfully, us girls also had a chance to escape by the third night and did that as quickly as possible. 
The good thing is that the staff was nice about refunding my money for the last night, and the owner/manager of the place seems like a really nice lady. She asked us why we were leaving so early and we were just like,"I'm sorry, we gotta go..."

review_title: Perfect boutique hotel in a great part of downtown Chicago.
review_text: We just returned from a trip to Chicago, and we were so thrilled with our hotel, the Wyndham Blake. The room was a very good size. Our friends stayed in the Palmer House Hilton and their room was a closet compared to the Blake. The bathroom only had a shower, which was fine for us but may not be for other people. Nice little gym (2 treadmills, two ellipticals, some small free weights) overlooking the city. Great food at the custom house, right next door to the hotel (lemon grits that they serve with breakfast were so great!). Great friendly service at the front desk, and the maids were excellent--they didn't cut any corners when cleaning. A few blocks from shopping on state street. It is a bit on the outskirts of the loop but definitely still close to everything. Loved it and would go there again in a heartbeat.

I stayed at this hotel but unfortunately they missed cleaning my room for one day. The location is good either their food at the restaurant.
Their shuttle was unable to bring me to pick up my rental car, because it was out of their way. They charge you for the newspaper but you should pick it on the front desk daily.

My family and I wanted to find a reasonable hotel down by the Michigan Mile for a quick weekend getaway. We selected the HGI and were very happy with our choice. The staff were excellent, the room was clean, comfortable and well appointed. I've stayed at other Hotels in Chicago and this was one of the best values for the money.
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn Chicago Downtown/Magnificent Mile

review_text:
This is an older Holiday Inn that could stand another round of updating. But - the staff is very friendly, everything typically works in the rooms, and you cannot beat the location for the price. They have a free airport shuttle, plus it is in walking distance from the Blue Line Cumberland Station. I have used this hotel many times when flying into O'hare and having business downtown, when I did not want to spend the $$$ to stay at the O'hare Hilton. 
Not a four-star property by any means, but clean and reasonably priced with a great airport location. This is one of the few hotels that is an easy walk to the Blue Line as well.

DO NOT STAY HERE if the streets are being worked on!!! I am currently in my room and it sounds like a marching band is in here with me!! It is a Wednesday night and they said all the rooms are totally booked and they can't move me. It's midnight. Guess I won't sleep tonight. They don't seem to care.

We stayed two nights here and had a lovely room with a city view in this vibrant part of Chicago, north of the River. We had lost a suitcase at the airport and all of the staff went out of their way to help us retrieve it. The atmosphere was very friendly and everything worked well. The bed was extremely comfortable, with a gadget to change its softness/hardness -- just what we needed after a long flight. Also near some great restaurants, and across the street from a supermarket/drugstore, which was very handy. Would definitely stay here again.
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn Chicago Downtown/Magnificent Mile

review_text: Loading and unloading the car was easy, the staff was friendly, our room was large and clean, and the bed was comfortable. The is free wireless with a reasonable speed. We were very pleased and would return afain

The appearance of the hotel upon arrival was not as good as it looked on the website. We were led to room 101 which was neither on the first floor nor the second and involved taking an elevator to second floor and steps down to the room (we had several suitcases so this was not convenient).
Once there, however, room was large, clean and well appointed. It was also incredibly quiet (caveat: there were 11 dumpsters outside and below the window not emptied by a beeping truck while we were there). Bathroom amenities also complete but the shower curtain gave us the choice of soaking the floor or having it constantly blow in on me as i showered. It was too light.
Location was pretty good but it was mile from the main shopping area. we like to walk so it wasn't a problem. Adler Planetarium, Grant Park, Art Museum, south side of Michigan Ave were all easily accessed. 
We would stay there again if looking for a reasonably priced stay.

Reception is on the 1st floor and hotel starts on the 12th floor. Everything is excellent, including the rooms (although the bathroom was unexpectedly small), the furnishings, internet, fitness equipment, Weber Grill Restaurant on site, and service. Room also had a microwave and refrigerator (with a Jewel Grocery across the street). Location adjacent to the train and across from Nordstroms is great. Stayed 4 nights and was very pleased.
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn Chicago Downtown/Magnificent Mile

review_text: I was referred here by manager at greyhound bus terminal. It was the most awful hotel I have ever seen. The room even smelled like urine. I did not stay. I gagged as I ran away as fast as I could. This place was breaking every health code in the book. Nasty nasty nasty!!!

When I checked in I was told I was upgraded to a deluxe room (that just means it's a bit bigger than a standard room). Lots of street noise out my window and a rattling heat/AC vent - even though I asked fir the quietest room they had when I checked in. 
Having said that, the bathroom was large and nicely appointed, and the rest of the room was nice. Roomy, too.

The hotel was in a good location, the subway was really close by. The rooms were large but the space lacked furniture. There was free internet, and complimentary breakfast. I would have to say that was my only critique. If you wanna call a muffin, coffee and banana a breakfast then you will be happy. I was not impressed! Overrall If you dont care for breakfast and want a close location to the subway, then this is the hotel for you!

Great location near Magnificent Mile. Walking distance (about 20 mins. to Millennium Park, Navy Pier and Oak St. Beach.
Staff was really pleasant and helpful. During my stay I even received a call inquiring if there was anything else needed. There was a small but nice and warm pool, very clean, and great spa tub. I went during the day when few people were there. Weber's Grill was conveniently located downstairs.
I enjoyed the Wendella Boat Tour, with great architectural views from the Chicago River and Lake Michigan.
This was an unexpected stopover in Chicago due Hurricane Irene but it was a wonderful weekend in a fantastic city and a very nice hotel.
Enjoyed the
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn Chicago Downtown/Magnificent Mile

review_text: I've been in alot of motels / hotels in Chicago but this had to be the nastiest place I've ever seen... They only have six channels on tv... No fox, abc,cbs,or nbc so I couldnt watch any football games... I asked for some clean linens and she came back wit some stained ones.. There was blood spats on the ceiling, found a condom under the bed and some poor girl (who had been unfortunate enough to stay there) ID... I wouldnt recommend this place to my worst enemy... Or would I... NAW it's gross!!!!

review_title: Thin walls, no sleep. Stay away.
review_text: This place seemed like a good value and the room was in decent shape, but the walls are so thin that you can hear everything from the room next door and even the restaurant area. We moved rooms because the neighbors were so loud, but we found the same problem even after we moved to a new room. Being from NYC, I can deal with noise, but this was absurd. I would avoid this hotel at all costs.
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown Lakefront

review_title: Well, we did have reservations but.....
review_text:
Looking at the reviews we were a bit apprehensive. We went with our gut feeling and canceled them. We found another hotel exactly one block away the wasn't much different in price. 
I sure am glad we did too!
Out of curiosity, my friend and I walked down just to see what it looked like first hand. 
Dingy walls, unswept floors, elevators were very small and even saw dried blood on it's floor. Hallways extremely narrow. 
We don't spend a lot of time in the rooms when visiting Chicago, but we expect cleanliness anywhere we are laying our heads... Period.

review_title: Holiday Inns are there for consistency -- this one isn't
review_text: Holiday Inns, especially airport ones like this one, are like supercuts -- you're not expecting anything special, but you are looking for a level of consistency and basic service. This one needs a visit from corporate QA. Made a reservation online for a non smoking double. Had the confirmation with me. Alright, we got there a bit late, 10pm... this ain't a resort, we're here to see the city. When we checked in, they said they couldn't honor the reservation and all they had was a room on the smoking floor (yes, floor, even the floor reeked of cigarettes and broken dreams). "It wasn't a reservation, mr concierge, we prepaid." "Sorry sir, youre SOL." Staff was unfriendly and unforgiving of their screwup. Find another airport hotel unless you enjoy Reservation Roulette.

Very messy hallways with wet carpets. Romm with a backed up bathroom sink. Called for service 4 times before someone showed up. Could not use the bathroom for all night.-
I will not stay hereagain and will highly recommend to all to not stay here .I have never seen a hotel where staff is so ignorentand irresponsible.

review_title: VIP Treatment without the VIP Prices
review_text:
As a former customer service trainer, I'm always observing customer experiences. The Downtown Chicago Red Roof definitely earns an A+! 
Since I started my current job a year ago, I'm back and forth to Chicago often. We stay at the Downtown Red Roof for the value and the proximity to our office. The staff has always been extremely friendly and accommodating, and they always knew my boss by name, which was nice, but expected seeing that she stays there sometimes 3 weeks out if a month or more. The rooms are always clean, the beds always comfy.
It was my last visit which blew me away. I had not been to Chicago for probably 3 months. Even when I came regularly, unlike my boss, I was only there maybe once a month. When I checked in, I wasn't surprised that they greeted me as if they were really happy to see me. I wasn't even surprised that despite the hundreds and hundreds of people who are in and out of the busy hotel, they recognized my face. What shocked me was as I reached in my purse to get my ID, the clerk addressed me by name. She knew what kind of room I liked. She even knew to use my Redi Card and corporate code to get me the best rate...all without me saying a word. I felt like a celebrity.
In addition to the five-star customer service, the hotel provides the most affordable and covenient valet parking in downtown Chicago. They offer free bag checking for those who arrive before check-in or business travellers like me who need a place to stash their luggage after check-out while they conduct their business in the city. There are great restaurants just steps away, and the hotel is just a block from the Magnificent Mile.
When I'm at the Red Roof in Downtown Chicago, I feel like I'm in a home away from home.

review_title: Great location and service in Chicago
review_text: Took a family trip to Chicago and this was a perfect location for us. Close to Michigan Ave. where buses to the museums can be caught - walk to Michigan via Ohio. PF Chang's less than 1 block. Navy Pier Reilly 1 block. Jewel market across the street. Extremely friendly and helpful staff. Only improvements are fan in bathroom and MUCH less chlorine in hot tub.
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn Chicago Downtown/Magnificent Mile

review_text: A great value! Excellent location, very friendly staff. Bed was not king size as reservation stated, but that is really the only negative thing I have to say. Nice view from room. Very reasonable parking. Would stay again.
Everything fine except that the internet did not work in our room. Had to go down to the lobby to get it working (still annoyingly slow speed)
This place looks ugly. The hallways look terrible. If it wasn't because of spending these nights with my friends, I'd kill myself.

We were driving in from 3 hours away to fly out of Chicago. Since we were going to be getting in late and flying out early, we decided to book an "economy" hotel. Worst decision ever made! 
First of all, we booked the hotel through a website. We were told that they had a park and ride and it was only going to cost us $20 for the duration we were gone. We arrived into our room to find both of the beds missing a leg and leaning to the side. We asked to move to a different room, which they were accommodating. The new room didn't have fitted sheets on the bed, the pillows smelled musty with stains on them (we covered the pillows with extra t-shirts we packed and just layed on top of the sheets without any covers...I wasn't about to use the bedspread with holes in it), the shower curtain was covered in mildew, i was scared to look at the rest of the place,and I woke up early the next morning to find 3 extra guests in our bed (looked like small roaches). The only reason we didn't go to a different hotel was because it was late and the kids were cranky. Plus, we figured we could handle a few hours. 
When we ended up leaving our car there (surprised to find it was still there when we came back on our return 10 days later) we found out it was $30 more than they originally told us. What could we do then since we were already there?
Once we got back from our vacation, as soon as we landed, my husband called the shuttle to let them know we needed a ride. After about 30 minutes my husband called them to find out where they were in case we were in the wrong place. They told him the driver tried to call us but we didn't answer. This wasn't true because my husband had his cell in his hand the whole time and there wasn't a missed call notice. My husband confirmed the phone number with the guy dispatching the driver and was told the driver will be calling us soon. We never received a phone call. This went on for another 2 hours! We were finally told to just get a cab!! We already paid them for their service!!! By this time, it was 3:30am and we had been sitting on the curb for 3 hour with 2 very cranky kids (a 2 year old and a 10 month old). We were literally the last people out of the airport. We ended up having to pay an extra $15 to cram into a cab. 
When we got back to the hotel of course my husband had something to say to the manager. We were told the manager wasn't available and to call back the next day. Of course we didn't want to stay at that rat hole again and since it was so late (ER...early) we decided to just drive home 3 hours. When we called the next day, the manager said there was nothing he could do to accommodate us.
 We paid an extra $30 dollars for the park and ride than we were originally told, waited for over 2.5 hours for the shuttle to pick us up to be told to just get a cab, then paid an extra $15 just to get back to the hotel, then told they wouldnt reimburse us for the cab fair!! Mind you, my husband was very courteous (unlike i would have been) while dealing with these people. By this time, we could have stayed in a MUCH cleaner place for a cheaper price.

Can't believe people slam this hotel over a printer, small elevator, and an air conditioner. My family spent four nights here and have nothing to complain about. Yes the building and pool area is showing it's age a bit but for those who don't care for this, there are plenty of newer and much more expensive places to stay. The location and price can't be
 beat. Staff is top notch. Yes parking is at a minimum at the hotel, I agree they should have one spot per room but this is out of their control.

review_title: Value on Michigan without te glitz and glamour
review_text: Great hotel on south Michigan avenue. Great value for the location. There isn't anything exceptionally remarkable about the hotel but my expectations were met. We stayed there the night of te lighting of the magnificent mile and had a great time and were able to walk anywhere. For the money the room was satisfactory. Nothing more. Nothing less. And be advised that this hotel is close to soldier field and thus very busy saturday night before Bears home games - usually full of the opposing teams fans!

I spent a night in this hotel 2 times now and each time ive had my room upgraded becuase they have had an extra larger room free. I dont have a lot of money, but this place is perfect for me and my partner when ever i travel in chicago. :)

review_title: Great location, awesome price, fun place overall!
review_text:
I'm sorry but if you booked here and complained you're an idiot for booking here in the first place. This close to so much for $70 a night? What do you expect?
The lobby has a nice appearance and the staff was very friendly. Our room is small but clean and perfect for what we need-a place to sleep in Chicago. It's close to the red line where you can park your car and have quick access to downtown. We walked back from the red line at night and that is definitely a little sketchy but well lit and close. 
We read the reviews so we were prepared for parking and the no elevator situation. We paid to park out front for an hour, loaded our stuff and headed out to find parking. The Walgreens near by is helpful too. 
Chinatown and Chinatown Square is a lot of fun shopping during the day! Definitely recommended if you're looking for cheap, fun, and convenient!

review_title: Good value, decent staff, great location
review_text:
A visit to the Inn leaves you with a
number of impressions. The staff is very friendly, professional & considerate. The immediate impression of the quality of the facility is very mixed. Some areas have been modernized & updated.. My room was not. This is a very old building & cracked & repaired tiles
& age old sinks & such don't leave one with a sense of luxury. There was some newer furniture, but I was a bit taken aback by old draperies which seemed like originals from the 1920's. But the place is kept very clean, nice towels & toiletries. 32 inch lcd tv, comfortable bed with a not too new bedspread. I have stayed in far brighter & more modernized facilties but for the price, staff, & cleanliness this is a Chicago steal. If you are thinking Palmer House.. I recommend you go there, but I would stay in this location again. Ah yes, the breakfast is a convenience, it's not House of Pancakes, but there are places nearby where you can safely walk to get a variety of foods at different prices.

review_title: Very good hotel to stay in Chicago downtown...
review_text:
Very well designed, very nicely located hotel.. The staff was very well trained..
The only problem was during the reception hours there was a huge line to get the drinks and they were offering very basic snacks- not suitable for a low-carb fan.. Also the enterance of the hotel was a little hard to find while driving-very small sign...
But they had a nice breakfast and a nice location..
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown Lakefront

review_text: My stay is not yet over but, I've already had such a great experience that I'm writing my review. When I pulled up to the valet, someone was right there to send me on my way to check-in. At check in, I was quicky greeted by the bellman with an offer for bottled water. After a quick check in and look-up of my HH number, I made it to my room which was clean and comparable to any other Hilton Garden Inn. I ordered room service from the Weber Grill. My only gripe was a long hold time but, I called at peak time. Here's the great part: when my meal was delivered the staffer asked how my night was going. I responded that it was good except that I forgot my iPhone charger. He then offered to find me one to borrow and a short while later came back with a cord for me to use. This saved me the effort and expense of buying another one or going a day without my phone and contact with my wife, kids and work. Sounds a bit dramatic but, it really meant a lot to me. Well done Hilton Garden Inn Chicago on Grand.
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn Chicago Downtown/Magnificent Mile

review_title: The location of this hotel is the ONLY good thing about it!!!!
review_text: I'll try to keep this as short as possible cuz I have a big list of complaints! We stayed 1 night in a lake view,double bed,nonsmoking room,4th floor main lobby section which I decided to go with cuz I read all the reviews n decided it would be the best choice. The lake view was the only thing nice about the room. Smelled horrible! beds were comfy but blankets were not. Tv was old. Not a flat screen, pic fuzzy, and the remote would only change channel going down, not up. I can almost guarantee the smoke detector didn't work. Looked about 100 yrs old and about to fall of the ceiling. No a/c or heat! There were knobs on this panel thing nut nothing happened. No vents in the room either but it was cool enough outside it didn't really matter. Reviews are right about the thin walls. We didn't hear much until we went to bed..for a good hour ppl were stomping, talking loud, slamming doors! That sucked! The noise from lake shore dr out front is pretty noisy but u get used to it! I loved the view! I didn't watch any tv but stared out the window watching boats on the lake and ppl running etc. Other then the view, the free parking and the closeness of the museums we visited( MSI, Shedd, and Field) everything else pretty much sucked! The restaurant next door is HORRIBLE! Had to send a few things back n waitress kept getting our order wrong. We ordered pizza from gordino's which was sooooo good, only the service messed up and we waited over an hour cuz they put pick up instead of delivery. Well this isn't so short so I'll sum it up......choose this as a last resort..and if u have to choose this ramada stay only 1 night!
This hotel is in a good location in downtown chicago. Room are fine, service is ok. The location is perfect, good price for this location
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn Chicago Downtown/Magnificent Mile

review_text:
I stayed at the Embassy Suites for a conference. Overall, it was a nice hotel-great location, clean rooms, great made to order breakfast options, and a wonderful reception every evening with free beverages and snacks. However, I was most shocked at the wireless Internet. It costs $15/day to register one device. Normally, that wouldn't be an issue-there had to be a starbucks nearby. However, I was away from my kids and wanted to video chat with them. Additionally, there was no wireless in the conference rooms, and this particular conference had all their materials online. I fault the conference organizers more here, but still find it a touch odd that there is no available wireless in a hotel con fence room. Additionally items in their shop (soda, snacks, etc.) were insanely priced. These things may be the norm among many hotels, but this was the first hotel I'd stayed in that charged for wireless, especially per device. 
All in all, a good hotel, but definitely not for people on a budget. If this weren't a work related trip, I probably would not have chosen it, purely for the cost.
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown Lakefront

review_text: We were looking for a hotel near Michigan avenue shopping that was reasonably priced. We had the room reserved at the rate of 184 a night. It was not worth 50. It was tiny, dirty, old and the service from the staff at the front desk was atrocious. The air conditioning broke and after the room hit 82 degrees we complained and got out of the room. Bottom line do NOT go here.
This is an older hotel but very clean. Everything worked just fine. We did not have any issues. Basic hotel met our needs just fine. Breakfast at the cafe next door was great.

review_title: Good location to pier. Good for families.
review_text: Nice hotel. Would recommend to others. Pretty close to the shopping mile and the pier. Extremely pleasant staff all around. If I had one issue the pool is almost so tiny you may laugh. Good place for families.
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown Lakefront

review_title: You have to be kidding me
review_text:
This place is a glorified shooting gallery/hot sheet motel. The fact that reviews cite the location as a saving grace is preposterous. We were checked into a room with an unmade bed, the ironing board out in the middle of the room, trash in the garbage including a condom wrapper...etc. The decor is barely maintained. When my wife and I went immediately backdown to the desk, the clerk said "you're checking out right?", as though she knew .
If you want to stay in a dump that's close to attractions, more power to you. I also find it somewhat suspect that negative reviews on here are always commented on by Heidi the"general manager" while the conditions remain third world. Maybe the priorities should be fixing the red roof...

review_title: Great hotel very clean but busy free Breakfast and managers reception
review_text: Stayed here with kids over spring break. Really nice clean comfy rooms and beds. Sleeper was okay Wonderful views of downtown buildings like the Tribune from our room. Used the pool and sauna small pool like 3 lap lanes, but great sauna. The breakfast was very busy and it was a long wait for the made to order food. Separate lines for self serve which helped. Entire lobby area was packed and it's a big area! That said they never ran out of food and staff cleared tables quickly. Good food when you found a place to sit. Maybe not as busy at a different time of year Valet parking was fast yet expensive like other hotels in area. This is a beautiful clean hotel.
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown Lakefront

review_text:
This is the worst 'hotel' I have been to in my life. Checked in on October 20th, 2011 with my husband and sister in law and her husband. When we got there about 6pm we were immediately creeped out. The rooms and hallways were something from a horror movie!!! We changed out of our traveling clothes never left anything out because the place was absolutely disgusting. We left the room for few hours to go eat came back about 12:30am to go to bed. Well when my husband was climbing into bed he noticed a small bug in the bed he called for me and sure enough a bed bug!!!! We pulled the sheets back even further to notice that the sheets did not fit the mattress and the padding under the half sheet was full of probably every pubic hair from everyone who has stayed in room 812!!!!! I immediately called the front desk the desk employee sent up security to come check it out. They said they would upgrade us to a suite. But my sister-in-law checked her bed also at the same time and the same creepy crawlies were in her room as well!!! We then went down to the desk employe and said we wanted our money back but since our reservations were through Expedia they could not until we spoke with them. So we got them on the phone and they called this said desk employee he hung up on the Expedia employee!!! The most awful customer service I have ever seen! The desk employee never seemed concerned about the situation was more angry that we disturbed him reading his book! So at one in the morning we had to pack up our things which took no more than 5 minutes and started calling other hotels in the area. Luckily we found one or else our only other option was sleeping in our car because we were not sleeping there! We were finally refunded our money sometime late afternoon the next day after Expedia repeatedly calling the hotel to speak with the manager... will never go back! Instead of the Teddy Bear as their logo it should be a bed bug having a good night sleep on your bed. 
It was a horrible experience and we just got home today and everything was directly put in the dryer to make sure to kill any little bugs that could have possibly hitchhiked home with us. DO NOT STAY HERE!!!

I've never written a review on TripAdvisor before, but felt the need to with the Travelodge. Although the hotel is in a fantastic location in the loop, it is not worth the money. (Plus it's right next to the train tracks which makes for a lot of noise.) A few major issues: 1. the elevators. There are 3, but there were only 2 working, and on one night, only one. One of the elevators would stop on a floor, doors would open, then a few seconds later the elevator would rise another foot before finally settling. Very dangerous. I can't imagine how many people have tripped. I sure did. And that happened every time with that elevator. The inspection notices are from 2008. I'm shocked they are able to still use them. Secondly, the condition of the rooms/beds. My bed/linens as well as the shower curtain had a strong odor of stale sweat. Just really disgusting. Plus there were stains all over the carpet. I strongly recommend you spend a few more dollars and stay somewhere (anywhere) else.

review_title: Biggest ripoff I've seen in years
review_text: This place charges you with hidden fees. We were charged for parking at the hotel we paid to stay at. We left and came back and they tried to charge us to park again. Check your bill is all I have to say.

review_title: 2nd worse hotel stay ever and I've been traveling for over 15 years-national and international
review_text: Staff and service was absolutely miserable. Towels and sheets were NOT clean. We left the notice to receive breakfast in the morning and it did not show up-the notice was still hanging on the door. Called up room service and they were slightly rude, and then they called back because they did not understand the order the first time. When breakfast FINALLY showed up, the employee said someone didn't do there job(no kidding). They still got the order wrong. Even the service in the restaurant was bad, even they could not get the order right. I would never recommend this place to anyone, it was a miserable experience. DO NOT go here.

My breath was taken away as soon as I stepped into the "sky lobby". It was phenomenal. It was a great experience. Rooms where great, so was the service. I'd delightfully come back to stay there. The pool was great, the sauna and hot tub was great too. I hope to come back there soon.
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown Lakefront

review_text: Having stayed at a number of Embassy Suites, this was disappointing. The room was in serious need of repair. The service wasn't great; the valets, bell staff and breakfast staff were great, but the front desk staff gave the impression they didn't give a hoot about any issue we had. The managers reception was way too crowded and the line for beverages made the whole event pointless. The location is good, with public parking nearby for trucks that are too tall for the garage onsite (6'8"). Overall, it was a 3 star stay, but compared to the other ES we're used to, it fell short.
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown Lakefront

review_text: Best doorman in town especially Yasir suliman he really helped me during my whole stayed.
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown Lakefront

review_text: We were only there one night but it was in a great location and our room had a great view. The people at the front desk were very nice and helpful. The only complaint was that there was gum stuck in the carpet by the couch but I assume the can fix that.

Stayed 3 nights in August with husband and teenager in one of the suites, very well appointed and clean room. Friendly and quick check in, especially for a Friday . One block from The Magnificant Mile so a great local if you will be shopping. Walking distance to Navy Peir and all the beautiful parks!
Coffe, espresso and pastry in lobby for a quick breakfast was nice.

The hotel is in a great location, close to the parks and close to the shopping. The rooms are very comfortable and clean. Service is also very good. I would recommend this hotel for business and pleasure.
I stayed here for one night on a last second business trip. The staff was great. The room was a nice size and clean. Great location. I will stay here anytime I'm in town.

review_title: Okay for a couple of nights
review_text:
We stayed at the Travelodge as there was literally nothing available for less than Â£500 a night over graduation weekend.
The hotel is dated and there were very basic amenities.
The towels and bedding were all clean, however around the edges of the carpets had a thick layer of dust.
The location is this hotels redeeming feature. It is right by Grant Park and located a block away from Harrison on the Red CTA Line. 
Breakfast is not provided but there were a few places to eat across the road and a 7 Eleven around the corner for sundries.
For what we paid we would ordinarily have been able to stay in a four star hotel, but we were so grateful to find this affordable hotel so it was easy to look past it's minor flaws.

We stayed at the Union League Club hotel as a guest of our daughter's boyfriend and found it to be a great choice in disturb Chicago. It is located in the business/banking district, but is walking distance to the Chicago Art Institute and Millenium Park, and a longer walk to the shopping district. The rooms are business hotel small, the beds and linens are excellent, bathrooms are marble and updated, and the hotel diningroom and food are wonderful. A great and inexpensive choice in Downtown Chicago at approx $140 per night.
Very cheap, right in the heart of Chicago. Walls are a little thin, but who cares? Nice little greasy spoon attached.

If you want to stay in a 1960s motel then Ohio House is for you. Reasonable rates for an expensive city. Central downtown location, tho some might find corner location noisy. Clean rooms. Comfortable beds. Breakfast not included. Poor wifi. Friendly and helpful staff.

Just stayed here last night and rooms are newly renovated and was very clean...we walked everywhere from here! Great price for being in the heart of downtown! & free parking! I would definitely stay here again!

Came in for a convention and was one of the best options I could find. The room was clean but there were stains on the chair, floor which kind of creeped me out. Location does not seem to be in a good area. We felt safe but didn't want to leave the compound of hotels to go elsewhere.

review_title: Our family of 5 had a great 4 days at the Essex
review_text:
The hotel was very nicely redecorated. Our room was very clean and comfortable. Very stylish even! And didn't smell like a hotel/motel. Most seem to smell like cleaners and soap. This hotel smelt like home. Clean!
Service was excellent. The pool was large and clean. Huge surrounding deck with an outdoor patio. Not a cramped room with an undersized pool and a few tables squeezed in. The fitness room was well stocked with all the major tools and ran the full length of the pool room. Yes, the sink was small but cute and plenty functional. Bathroom, not huge but average and also very well kept. Located right across from Grant park with a Starbucks one block away. Beautiful morning walk for coffee every morning!
I would recommend this hotel to anyone!

review_title: Check your room for clean sheets before you commit...
review_text:
Location - Fantastic
Room was very dirty. Sheets, bathroom.
Staff were very friendly.
Bad need of remodeling
Will charge you card 75 a nightt for incidentals and will not tell you.
$37 a day to park your car.

We had to move rooms on morning one and request a full refund on day three. We had massive bed bugs and received over 50 bites from the critters. Staff responded fantastically gave us a full refund n paid for the antiseptic stuff we needed to buy. We found four bed bugs,(one squashed) varying from big to little in our bed....disgusting!

review_title: Good location, if that's what you look for
review_text:
Staff are unkind and they don't even look to the face in check in/out dialogue. 
Rooms are like the hotel, they are old. Newly furnished but even the doors are seems like one hundred years old. Don't expect a fridge or complimentary water.. You have your tv, bed and coffee machine..
No free wireless Internet. 
Average hotel with average price in a very good location. Close to "bean" , "loop" and Michigan avenue.. All in walking distance.
For a short stay, I recommend this hotel but not for long..

Stayed here based on the reviews and the close proximity to McCormick Place Convention Center.
Many years ago this place must have been magnificent but now it is badly in need of an update.
The bed was comfortable enough, but that was the high point of the stay.
The bathroom was tiny and in my opinion inadequate for the price point.
The service in the restaurants was mediocre at best and the food followed suit.
I would not stay here again.
