review_title: Welcome to the Hotel from The Shining Movie---am I a ghost?
review_text:
Did I see a ghost? This place is old and creepy. Yes it was built in the 1800s but a little word called upgrade goes far.
In the room; blood burgundy, ratty, creepy old carpeting. How unsightly. 
The 1930s wallpaper matches the drapes. I mean it's the same ugly antique pattern. 
The doors don't close because they've been painted over and over and I think they're the originals from the 1800s. Bathroom door wouldn't close. The "closet" looked like a creepy killing booth. There is a CHAIN ON THE MAIN ENTRY DOOR!!!! Creepy. 
The furniture is so plywood.com! Come on! The thin, cheap, spring-in-your-back bed doesn't even fit the flimsy platform plywood bed. 
I felt like I was on a set of a scary movie. I literally slept with all lights on and all doors closed. 
My view: a fire escape although I asked for a view of Grant park. I needed to see civilization. Who would I scream at when the ghosts come?
The hotel: when people are present the place is not to creepy. But once you get up on the floors, after riding the original elevator up, where is everyone? And there's that creepy ol blood burgundy carpet and down this dimly lit hallway. 
The lobby is so fricking old. Again, this hotel reminds you of the abandon hotel on The Shining. 
What's good? Your on Michigan Ave, you have protection from the weather and the buffalo wings.

L'hotel si trova di fronte al grant park, quindi in una buona zona, tranquilla e vicino al centro storico (loop) e ben servito dalla metropolitana. La camera non era niente di particolare, ma comunque pulita. La stessa cosa per il bagno. La camera era dotata di wi-fi gratuita. Disponibile il personale della reception.
This hotel was clearly grand in it's day, but sadly that day has come and gone. Just the fact that it was older and not well kept wouldn't have been bothersome but it felt seedy

No AC this place is awful. Windows open only 3 inches. Bathroom tiles are drywall screwed to the wall and they used liquid nails for grout. Shoty work and unfriendly staff
The also lied and said no one was unhappy as they were getting complaints by phone in front if us.
Hotel resturant has poor quality food and bad wait service.

Our first time in Chicago couldn't have had a better location. The staff are wonderful, helpful and friendly. The accommodation is incredible sooooo much space !! The food is great but portions are way too big for us Brits !!! :)) one block away Grom main shopping street. 10 min walk (30 in the blizzard !!) from the Naval Pier. :D
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Hotel Chicago Downtown Lakefront

review_text: We paid $200/ night and not worth it. Very old, dingy rooms that they have tried to remodel best they could. Water slow to come out of pipes, rooms smell like Smoking Rooms from the 1960's. Look a little more North up Michigan Ave would be my suggestion. Dk

Terrible hotel. I couln't stay and had to fin another hotel in the middle of the night. The room was dirty with bugs in the bed and bathroom. Simply terrible and when talking to the manager I received a bad attitude. Do not stay here.

review_title: For the $ Best a value for the location.
review_text:
For those with a limited budget this is THE best value for lodging in Downtown Chicago, when you can book in the $80/nite range.
We've have stayed in some dives and we have stayed in some 5 Star places like Shutters on the Beach in Santa Monica, The San Maria Isabel in Mexico City, Penninsulas, etc. The Tremont is a 5 Star dive. It is a little rough on the edges but for the value and location it can't be beat.
The lobby has a very nice sitting area with nice leather chairs and couches.
Right next door is Ditka's which has a decent menu (on the spendy side though).
We stayed in room 1503 which was small but adequate. As we were out and about the town most the time, the room size mattered little. The windows were small but the room got good light in the day and has a nice view of Michigan Avenue. Cable channels were limited but the carried FOX (Rare for Chicago) a plus for us NRA members.
Room could have used a place to hang up stuff but overall a really suitable place. We've rated service average because we had really no interaction with the staff, though the limited interaction we did have was very nice.
For the value and location and condition of rooms our room at least was thumbs-up.
hotel_name: The Tremont Chicago Hotel at Magnificent Mile

review_text: This hotel is terrible.my room had 18in between the bed n the wall. Paint peeling, exposed wires. The L outside my window all night. They offer an upgrade but then were sold out of all upgrades because u can only upgrade if staying 1night.awful.....

Absolutely loved this hotel! Our room had a great view of the skyline and river. The room was spacious and comfortable, with loads of storage and a great bathroom. 
The beds were heavenly and the pillows were perfection. 
The location is great, just down from a bus stop and within walking distance to millennium park, navy pier, and Michigan ave (as well as Giordanos-for amazing pizza). 
Definitely coming back !!!

review_title: You can do better in Chicago
review_text: The web site describes a luxury hotel but it may have been that when it opened but not today. The lobby is dismal and the check in desk area is tight, not staffed well and in need of a major redo. The rooms are ok but as with the standards today are not up to a great room/ bath experience. The elevators have the most unusual way to get to your floor. You need TO get used to the lack of buttons in the cars. This is not a flagship property for this brand.

review_title: Worth a revisit, great location and quality.
review_text: The only thing I didn't think much of was the pricing in the restaurant. 30 odd $ is just too much for breakfast. Otherwise everything top noch.
Small restaurant in hotel serves a full breakfast. Decent, well air-conditioned rooms. Close to all downtown attractions and to 'L'.

review_title: If you like bad service and small rooms this is your hotel
review_text: This is the worst 4 or 3.5 star hotel in Chicago. I travel alot and can say they are not even good enough to be called a hotel. Front desk is poor on check in and rooms are a closet. Restaurant is poor service and valet will take over 20 minutes to get your car. Find another hotel so you can enjoy your stay in Chicago.

we got this hotel through expedia unpublished rate .. Was very sceptical at first after reading some negative reviews.. But was very happy once I saw the hotel. It was at a great location, feel of great old charming hotel with nice clean cozy room. Nothing could beat the deal, if u r paying a very high price and expect an upbeat classy hotel, then this might not be your best choice. I like the old woody effect. Hence I wud definitely give this a thumbs up...
hotel_name: The Tremont Chicago Hotel at Magnificent Mile

review_text: Very friendly staff. The rooms were clean. Many people in other reviews had multiple complaints; I found nothing wrong. Rooms were average size. They only had two elevators, but found that they moved fast and you didnt have to wait long to get on them. Furniture was outdated but added character to rooms. We enjoyed our stay there. Would definitely go back. It was in an excellent location.
This hotel needs an extreme makeover. It was incredibly disappointing. The location has a great deal of potential.
hotel_name: The Tremont Chicago Hotel at Magnificent Mile

review_text: The front staff are friendly and most are extremely helpful. My room was great and the bed was super comfy. Hotel is a mere 1 min stroll to the Magnificent Mile. Some great value restaurants nearby. Hop On Hop Off Sightseeing Bus has a stop at end of street so very convenient! Better than great value for money.
hotel_name: The Tremont Chicago Hotel at Magnificent Mile

review_text: I travel frequently for work and was very impressed with both the service and quality of rooms at the swisshotel Chicago. I did not expect as good a room as it was. Spacious, great view, quick elevators, friendly staff, great location. I can't say anything bad about this place. Room was on 33rd floor. Great view. Special thanks to the maid who came to my rescue with an ice pack after seeing me bang my face against an ajar door. Did not expect it. No bar fridge tho? Empty fridge that works . Again. Overall impressed and would easily stay again.

review_title: Not a 4 star hotel. Old outdated and in need of repair.
review_text: Disappointed with hotel. Room was not ready at checkin. Waited an hour with luggage. Room was old with outdated furniture and a small Zenith TV. Do they even make zenith TVs anymore? Tile in bathroom had cracked and holes were in shower marble. This may have been a 4 star hotel in the 1930s but today, I would rather stay at a nice motel 6. Definitely avoid unless you absolutely have no other options.

The first room was not what I had expected, but they were quick to satisfy my expectations, however the king-size bed was a little too firm for me. The room was clean. There was no coffee maker, and the requested bathrobe (listed as an in-the-room amenity) was torn and stained. Room service got ice for me, however I was a bit uncomfortable receiving ice into a questionable bucket. One morning, I had asked housekeeping to just leave towels and not to worry about the housekeeping, however she did some cleaning and trash emptying that lasted about five minutes while we were in the room! The location was great with easy access to the Magnificent Mile shopping and restaurants, and the train. The customer service was very good.

review_title: These are the worst beds in the Midwest!
review_text: After checking into the hotel, we were put in a nice room but our bed swooped in the middle. So, our butts were about six inches lower than out head and feet. We were moved to another room ( very small) where the bed was hard as a rock but a matress topper was put on (probably eight years ago) and was soft and lumpy between the people and still hard where you lay. Mind you I am paying over 200$ a night. Will be looking for a new room somewhere else to finish my trip.

I have stayed over 100+ nights in choice hotels this calendar year and the Inn was a surprising gem. The tripadvisor reviews scared me, but we were pleasantly surprised. The price was right. We were upgraded due to our choice diamond status, so we had a nice sized room and bathroom. Front desk staff was accommodating and professional. It was a find.
I am loyal to choice and they rarely disappoint.
hotel_name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel

review_text: Older hotel with small bathrooms but flat screen tv's and a good staff. Bartender was a snott.
hotel_name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel

review_text:
I spent one week at the hotel felix with my boyfriend!
We really had a great time! The hotel is very good located and the staff is so friendly! The rooms are very clean and really stylish! For us it was perfect!!

review_title: Why I'm unable to fall back to sleep at the Hotel Felix...
review_text:
Just after 2am doors are opening, slamming shut, people knocking on doors, voices IN the next room, TV noises next door. An hour later, what are these people up to with so many visitors? Worries me after my travel companion, my 13 year old daughter, Googled the Hotel Felix just hours ago and discovered there was a murder here in October 2011. A 31 year old suspected prostitute was stabbed to death in one of the rooms here. There is no clock or docking station in our room, the outlet to charge my phone is at the end of the bed on a 'desk'. Heating/cooling system is annoying, I'm either roasting or freezing as the vent is just over our heads and blows right onto you as you lay on the bed. 
First impression of hotel: Cute, small lobby; staff was not overly friendly or helpful; we were sent to the 10th floor, got off the elevator and the compact hallway was a bit confusing as we searched for our room- they must have doubled the number of rooms when the hotel was remodeled; I opened the door and was not prepared for what I saw - yes, I read comments before we left, but was in no way was I prepared for this... a room that fit a bed and very little space to walk around the bed; bed itself is comfortable but pillows are too small; bathroom was also minuscule with a sink that does not have enough clearance between faucet and drain to even wash hands; the view out our window, where do I start! Wish I could upload my photos from my iPhone now, I've never seen anything quite like it! And just don't know what to say about it other than it's absolutely terrible. 
Hopefully my neighbors will quiet down now, I really want to get back to sleep!

review_title: Great location and value for a somewhat tired hotel
review_text: Snagged an $88/night rate so I knew not to expect over-the-top. Clean room with comfy king bed. Wood furnishings are scuffed up but functional. Not much for amenities. Also a bit short-staffed as there was only one front desk clerk who also handled concierge requests (like if there was an in-house ice machine. We never found one.) the good news is the fabulous location. We didn't spend much time in the room!
hotel_name: The Tremont Chicago Hotel at Magnificent Mile

review_text: My friend and I enjoyed our stay here. We have all good things to say about it except the bathroom was small and I would have liked a microwave for popcorn. Other than that, great price, great location and comfy beds.
hotel_name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel

review_title: Wow, once in a lifetime experience.
review_text: Literally, will go there once and never again. Needs a major update (furniture, lighting, paint etc...) rid of the mildew smell throughout.. Perhaps an exorcism or two as well.

The pros:
Excellent location
Soft, comfy beds with updated linens
Nice bathrooms
Walking distance to everything on the mag mile
The cons:
Small lobby
Slow check in
Old televisions
Smallish rooms
Outdated corridors - need new carpet and lighting
The Whitehall is a throwback to the old days of Chicago. That said, the hotel could benefit from a renovation of the public spaces - the hallways especially. Just look old and in need of a fresh coat of paint, new lightning and new carpet. The furniture in the rooms (desk, armoire, headboard etc) are pretty old. The Chinese retaurant on the first floor has some decent choices. Room service was ok - they got my order wrong on a few occasions. Even with some of these drawbacks, the location cannot be beat, especially for tourists. The beds are very soft and comfy.

review_title: If you enjoy AC in July, don't bother staying here!
review_text: My husband and I went to Chicago with friends for a ling weekend. We booked the hotel through a travel agent, so we thought it woul be decent. We were excited when the cab dropped us off, so close to Michigan Avenue! We dropped our bags off before exploring the city ad turned the thermostat down in our stuffy, dirty corner room. We were surprised when we returned 10 hours later and the room was still hot. Neither of us slept solid that night as the room was probably 78-80 degrees, no exaggeration. The next day, we asked the front desk to send someone to fix our AC on 3 different occasions throughout the day. We returned for bed that night, again to a hot room. We asked again the next day and nothing was ever done. On top of that, the carpet and all interiors are old ad dingy. The shower tile grout was growing with black mold. The pictures you see posted are no exaggeration. Great location, awful hotel.
hotel_name: The Tremont Chicago Hotel at Magnificent Mile

review_text: Read other reviews. I'm in a king room. Very clean, adequate size, everything works fine. Starbucks right across street (room coffee always sucks anyway). Tv works just fine and there's a clock in our room. On the 7th floor facing an alley, but helps with city noise. Great blackout drapes and room stays cool. I would stay here again. I ALWAYS believe it's helpful to call hotels the day before and talk to desk clerk; check your room-ask for upgrade (especially if downing a whole week) notify if you have late check-in, & small chit-chat. That way they should know when you walk through door. Oh, do self park 2 blocks away and save $36 compared to $49! And a tip about shower... Let the water run in the tub so you pull water up to your room and you'll be fine.
hotel_name: The Tremont Chicago Hotel at Magnificent Mile

review_title: Beware if booking this hotel thru a third party site...
review_text: My husband and I booked this hotel thru Hotwire, approx 3 weeks prior to our stay. We arrived 1 hour before check in and told that because we booked thru a third party, our reservation was NOT guaranteed (even though we had prepaid $402.00 for 2 nights), therefore we would have to wait until check in time. After a conversation with the manager we were finally given a room. The rooms are very small and VERY antiquated. The night stand drawewr handles were dangling, the bed skirt was dirty, the sliding closey doors were rickety, the walls were very thin, we could hear coughing in the room to the left of us and the toilet flushing in the room to the right of us. The TV was small and required manual turn off and on, the remote only worked for channels and volume control. There were 3 old lamps in the room, each one required a little maneuvering to turn on and off. There were only 2 outlets in the room, and each one was loose from the wall. The bathroom was clean, but very small, with the toilet wedged under the sink (very awkward). The positive aspects of this hotel. The staff (minus the RUDE front desk clerk, who later wrote us an apology and slid it under our door, ( I'm sure at his manager's urging). Also the location is great, diagonally across the street from Water Tower Place, upper Michigan Avenue. I would not stay ther again.

review_title: Clean and neatly decorated, but very small.
review_text: The Hotel Felix was a very nice clean hotel with a good location. It was a quick walk to the Michigan ave, restaurants, and bars. It was decorated very tastefully and staff was very friendly. The only downside was the size of the room. The rooms were very small and left little space for luggage, but it was manageable. I would recommend using the parking garage across the street vs valet. Overall this hotel was very nice and I would stay there again, but kind of suprised that it was listed as a 4 star just based on size.

review_title: Great location, friendly staff, clean rooms, would recommend
review_text: Had a double room w nice river view. Room very clean, bed comfortable. Toiletries not the best, no conditioner provided so if you use it you should bring your own. Towels were fine unlike some other guests reviews. Separate tub and glass shower stall. Nice keurig coffee maker. Enjoyed my stay.

review_title: More a Hampton Inn than a Westin
review_text:
We arrived today, looking forward to a wonderful weekend of Christ,as shopping. The Westin location could not be better. Check in was quick and friendly.
That's where the positives end. The first room had a door that would not close. We were relocated to another room, that was much smaller ans had a lovely view of a brick wall from the building next door outside. A platinum SPG memb, we called down to ask again if there was a more suitable room. The front desk manager offered to send someone up with a key to yet another room. New waited a while and the key never came. The rooms are very old... with peeling wallpaper and old, worm carpet. Never the heavenly bed that we have come to know and love was worn and tired. It really did remind us more of a roadside discount hotel than a big city luxury hotel.
In the end, we left and crossed the street to stay at the Four Seasons. I am a loyal Starwood client, but think this Westin is past it's prime.

review_title: Another great time at the swissotel Chicago
review_text: Corner suite , lake and city view, courteous and accommodating staff as usual - only place we'll stay downtown Chicago plus they're green and reward you with half off nightly parking charge!

review_title: Great location, good value, will definitely be back...
review_text: I was extremely nervous after having read previous reviews. I had my cousin in Chicago to let me know her thoughts and she felt it was ok. I went with it and glad I did. It was right across from Grant Park (Taste of Chicago venue) and moments from the Navy Pier, Giordanos, Art Institute and much more. I was pleased.

My fiancÃ©e and I stayed one night here and decided we won't be returning. Great location but not worth almost $200 a night.. The rooms are just disgusting. Aside from the gross red carpet and wallpaper, the overall cleanliness was pitafull. Our comforter was stained, along with our pillow cases, oh.. Not to mention long black hairs all over in our sheets. WARNING don't even think to look under the bed pad or bed itself, you'll gag. Our shower was filthy as well nor did it drain because the drain hole was clogged with nasty hair, I showered in flip flops by the way so I wouldn't have to step in the tub! It's noisy because of the Metra and the paper thin walls don't help the situation either. I dont care if this hotel is 540 years old, most of the issues we had, had nothing to do with age. It has to do with lack of care and neglect. I would of paid an extra $100 a night just to feel comfortable.. We won't be returning.

review_title: Triple check your booking! They won't guarantee anything.
review_text:
Booked a twin room as I was staying with a mate. 
Walked into the room to find a tiny double bed.
Star said their was nothing they could do for me as they can't guarantee you'll get the type of room you book.
The hotel could not even be bothered to contact me within the three weeks since I booked to inform me that they did not have the room I needed. I see this as lazy and a total disregard for their customers!
I would not recommend or stay here again.

review_title: Musty, old hotel masquerading as a 4 star property.
review_text: Ok this hotel has the smallest, most unreliable elevators in town. It Isn't a horrible hotel. But it's not 4 stars room was small and dark. The bed was comfy but the bottom sheet was too short so you felt the dreaded mattress pad. The lighting was dim. There were not enough outlets for phone and computer and one more charger. Bathroom was updated with marble but ridiculously small. I thought the faucet in the tub was going to break off in my hand. Some of the wallpaper was peeling. The good news is that was 125.00 on priceline. Just too old and musty and those elevators scared me. Front desk and bellman were nice and helpful. Great location.

review_title: Wonderful old hotel in a good location but the terrible service overshadowed the good parts.
review_text: We got this hotel through priceline and expected the best. We checked in around midnight and most of the lobby and other downstairs rooms were closed off. We were not told about coffee in the lobby in the morning which would have been nice since there is none in the room. The first thing we noticed was how warm the room was and we called to have the air checked but no one ever came up. We also did not have a hair dryer and one was brought up. It would only work on low settings. We asked for another but did not ever get one. The light bulb by the bed was out and we made repeated requests to get another but never got one until the last night of our four night stay. The room was never cooler than 76 until the last night when it finally got fixed by the man who brought the light bulb! This hotel is very old and nostalgic and the room was very nice. But I would not go back because the service was so bad.

My wife had stayed at this hotel prior to our arrival last week and rebooked as a result of it being excellent last time out.
Upon arrival we were given a musty smelling room on floor 12 which given we were jet lagged sufficed for the night but on the proviso we could change it tomorrow. Carlos on reception was pretty helpful and wanted to make our stay good. 
We had luggage missing on arrival (who doesn't from Air Canada?) so went back to hotel around 2 pm the next day to change our room. We encountered Derrick on reception who was extremely rude and put out by this request. He persistently answered the phone whilst we tried to sort it out, which as a Brit, I find extremely rude as he should be dealing with one query at a time. Eventually, after much huffing and puffing he managed to change the room as his colleague had told us the previous night.
When we were relocated in the hotel, the room was much better and brighter with another window which helped. The room wasn't overly clean, but it is old, and I do make allowances for that. The bed was comfortable and the bathroom was fine.
The location of this hotel is excellent, but it is a bit tired and some members of staff have an attitude problem. I encountered Carlos and Fernando on another day and both were helpful and cheery. Derrick and Barbara were less so; they seem more intent on answering the phone than dealing with guests who are waiting for them in the lobby.

review_title: Be Carefull some rooms are extremely small!
review_text: I stayed in the hotel like for a week for me it was perfect since I realized they gave me a suite in stead of a regular room and I pay very little, some rooms are normal size and others extremely small make sure to ask for a nice room maybe they have available. The best rooms are the one in the CORNERS. The rest, so so. Have a nice stay .
hotel_name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel

review_text: A deux pas du Loop, un hÃ´tel sans surprise pour cette chaÃ®ne amÃ©ricaine bon marchÃ©.
Only a short walk to navy pier and magnificent mile made it a perfect location! Staff is super nice! I will definitely stay again next time I'm in the city!

review_title: A little noisy, but beautiful room
review_text: We stayed 1 night after using an online bidding website (so we didn't exactly choose the hotel). First impression was bad - girl at front desk was outside on her phone, so we waited a good 5 mins for check in (it was after midnight). She did upgrade us to a suite, which was nice. Beautiful room with 2 bathrooms, great bed, high floor so nice and quiet...until the yappy do down the hall started barking in the morning. I had no reason to ask if I was a pet- friendly hotel, but couldn't they all go on one floor so the rest of us don't have to hear? Otherwise a nice hotel - just too noisy for us.

review_title: Nice digs if you can get a deal
review_text: Pretty decent for a moderately-priced hotel. The furnishings are a little worn but overall the room was clean and quiet. Front desk staff were pleasant. The only issue I really had was that the bedsheets were really coarse and stiff, felt almost like tablecloth. Regardless, I would recommend this hotel, especially if you can get a good price.
hotel_name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel

review_title: Pay the extra money and get a nicer hotel!!!
review_text:
This was my first time here and it's ok..once arriving here the lobby was alright, I've stayed in higher end hotels in Chicago before but we were just passing by heading back to St Louis and my boyfriend and decided to stay overnight downtown. 
The rooms are small, no mini fridge or microwave to put your leftovers. The room is small and the bathroom is TINY!! The sink feels like it's in front of the Toliet literally! 
But what really got me was the hotel bed. Gross. They didnt even put a bed cover on. And the sheets don't even fit our bed they're a size too small and you can see the matters and end of your feet! DISGUSTING. this place is dirty, outdated and staff seem to have a stick up there @$$. Will never come back here again!!
hotel_name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel

review_text: Based on prevois reviews and the great deal we got from Travelzoo, we booked our stay here. The location could not be more perfect. A block from the mag mile, the CTA, and the gorgeous Ohio St Beach. The staff was polite, and checkin was very smooth. We hot in at 11am expecting to just drop our luggage off till checkin, instead our rooms were ready and we got to freshenip before we started our site seeing. DD, Strarbucks on the same block. Rooms were small no doubt, but it was a clean safe area, and we toured all day so the bed was all that mattered. Roof deck was nice, would not recommend appetizers. Short walk to beach, where we rented bikes and viewed the city from the lakeside bike path. We LOVED this. All in all would recommend and stay again.
hotel_name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel

review_title: Make sure all 3 elevators r working! Long wait with 22 floors!
review_text: Tiny rooms, tiny beds, tiny bathroom, tiny sink, tiny elevators. Clean, good value, not great for families, rude staff but we didn't have to deal with them too much
hotel_name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel

review_title: So nice had to stay twice!
review_text: Chose to stay here on two trips to Chicago! Great location...great view of the Willis Tower from the roof top pool! The staff are so friendly & welcoming. Clean, affordable hotel! Great for the kids. My daughter LOVED the outdoor pool on the roof! Definitely will be staying here again

review_title: Prehistoric! No coffee service in room?!
review_text:
Outstanding location for our shopping trip steps away from Michigan Ave and Water Tower Place. Felt safe.
Employees very accommodating except night clerk who was unaware that I could order just coffee from room service.
Hotel is marketed as European ...
Translated to....
Older, worn, tired etc. needs some Fresh paint and updates
No fridge for our leftovers, and
NO COFFEE Service in room
Complimentary coffee at 7:00 AM 17 floors down ! No thank you!
I sip my coffee in bed each AM for 15-30 before greeting world.
If you book a "room deal" here.. Take it, but by all means bring your thermos.

We booked this hotel to explore Chicago for a few days. We chose this hotel because of the price we found on Expedia and because of its proximity to the red line.
Check-in was a breeze and we made our way to the small elevator and got out on the 3rd floor. We entered our king room and immediately noticed it was in need of more light. We turned on every light in the room and it was a little better, but overall, the room could be brighter. Luckily, the room had central air with an easy to use thermostat, so temperature and A/C noise were not an issue.
There was a mirrored walk-in closet and a safe next to the bathroom. The bathroom had nice marble tile on the wall and a granite countertop. The sink was a bit tricky to use. I enjoyed the industrial strength toilet. The shower and tub were nothing special, but had a massaging shower head and good water temperature and pressure.
The king bed was comfortable enough and the pillows were numerous, though a little worn. The main drawback of the room was that it faced an alley with no view and they were doing work on the building across the way every morning, so sleeping in was not an option.
The room had an older standard definition TV and a mini-bar fridge that we were able to use for our own items. There was also a desk and a couple of armchairs.
Check-out was also a breeze and the bellman stored our luggage for a few hours before our flight.
The hotel was a good value and very convienent. Although it didn't have the finishes or the level of service of a four or five star hotel, I would consider staying here again.

review_title: Good, clean room. Great rate. Super location. Friendly staff.
review_text: Stayed 4 nights late July 2011 with wife and 2 college age kids. Friendly staff and responsive valet. Clean room. Decent beds. Small bathroom but clean. Not fancy but rate was lowest in mag mile area even without Hotwire. Great location 1 block from Michigan Ave. Bar in lobby and on rooftop thurs-sat. 7-11 and Dunkin' Donuts across street. With Ambassador East ruined by remodel this could become our Chicago go-to hotel. Been to more expensive hotels that were not as good as Inn of Chicago.
hotel_name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel

review_text:
I have lived in Chicago all of my life and had a friend visiting from out of town do I got the groupon for a king executive sweet at the Allerton. I have seen this building many times on Michigan Ave and was really excited about staying at the iconic Chicago hotel. 
Checkin time was at 3:00 and we showed up about 15 minues early and didn't end up getting into our room until after 4:00. The entire lobby was full of families waiting on rooms while the front desk people continued to check in a seemingly endless line of guests. I have been to many hotels and I know that checking time is hectic anywhere you go, but I don't understand why none of the guests were getting rooms. After about 30 minutes I asked what the delay was and the woman at the front desk unapologetically told me it would be just a few minutes. another half hour later I asked again and was given a room without any apology or explanation of why it took so long. 
Our room was on the 9th floor with a view of the rooms across from us and a fire escape. The sliver of a view of Michigan ave was hardly worth the waiting and cost of the room. The room was also not even close to what the website pictures showed. We had no couch or fridge which was in the room description on the website. 
I want to love this hotel so much but I was sadly disappointed during my stay. The bell people were unorganized and unprofessional, the front desk staff was unfriendly and rude, the only good thing I can really say about out stay was the location.

We stayed 4 nights in August. Wi-Fi is free if you're an SPG member, which is free to join. We didn't eat at the hotel restaurant, but there is a Cheesecake Factory right across the street, which is a way better value anyway. The rooms are basic, but clean and the housekeepers were more than willing to accomodate special requests (I left them a $5 tip each night and that probably helped). The location is a little north on Michigan Ave for sightseeing, but ideal for shopping.

review_title: Awesome hotel has great staff, quiet, clean, great location, beds are to die for.
review_text: Stayed here from September 6 thru September 9 2011. The room was not small I stayed in room 704 great view, quiet, very clean, great service. Staff was very friendly and helpful. The elate restaurant next door had great food and good prices. If you're going to Chicago and need to stay near downtown this is the place. Four blocks from Michigan ave very nice and trendy area where hotel is located. Whole food store a block away for snacks or food items. The hotel is new clean and great value. I can't wait to go back.

We stayed at the inn of chicago for 2 nites the hotel was great. Location was perfect 1 block from Michigan ave 10 minute walk to pier. Rooms are small but clean & comfortable. Only knock LOUD a/c unit. Would definitely stay here again. Big Catt
hotel_name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel

review_text: clean room, hotel looks older but well maintained. Location great for mag mile and navy pier.
hotel_name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel

review_text: I have stayed here a number of times and although it is a bit if a walk to the shops of Mich Ave, I cannot fault it! Absolutely amazing views especially if you get a corner room! The staff are friendly however I would admit that the breakfast buffet is really not up to much and is shamefully in the bowels of the hotel with no exterior views which is such a shame. Also the lobby can get very congested! But otherwise a very relaxing experience!

Wife and I just stayed at AllertonHotel Chicago on dec25, 2011. The room was a special groupon rate and it was a good value for location. The room was a superior suite and it was plenty big for such a older classic Chicago hotel. The building is old and shows signs of wear . Carpets could use a good cleaning or replace. The service was adequate. Nothing to write home about. We stayed at the Hard Rock last year and were much more satisfied. But in the end I would stay again just for location.

Good location ...is about it! 
The rooms are not soundproof. We were woken up every night of our 4 night stay by drunk kids in the halls at every hour..
The concierge only works until 4 or 5 pm.
Our shower nor our sink would drain properly....we were standing in a pool of water while showering.

It was our first trip to Chicago. I took my family for a mini vacation the front desk was very friendly they had great suggestions on what to do and were to go. The entire staff was very helpfull in every aspect we forgot a couple of stuff we called down and they quickly brought them up. Overall we had no complains it was a memorable experience we would love to go back. A very special thanks to those who made our trip a success Denise,Harold,Jeff. Thank you all!

We visited chicago during the labour day weekend and booked this hotel via priceline. N got 80$ rate . Although for that rate i had no complains whatso ever with location and room as the room was decent size n furniture was ok too. Bathroom was small but it was acceptably clean. The front desk staff was good n efficient . Our check in and check out both were prompt . Valet parking was 30 $ so we parked in adjacent parking lot ( with in/out privilage ) in 20$ . Breakfast is nt included . . Overall till that point it is satisfactory hotel . The issue i had is with housekeeping. They are not efficient enough . Even theey were worse than. 2 star hotel . On my 2 nd night they even didnt refill the towels , toiletaries and disposables . With very unsatisfactory cleaning. For that reason alone i would not recommend that hotel to any body else.

Got this hotel off of hotwire. It was the tinest room I've ever stayed in, no exaggeration. Also limited tv stations. Staff was friendly, everything was clean. However unless you are literally only going to be in your room for 5 minutes, I wouldn't stay here. It just wasn't comfortable and offered nothing special to make up for it.

I like this hotel ad what saves it is the location. An easy walk to the best areas of the city. It is safe ad the area is clean and nice. The staff is excellent. The restaurant is nice and the rooms are clean for the most part. The bathrooms are nice and clean as well. However, the rooms are loud! I travel often and this hotel has the poorest insulation both internal and external for noise. I would stay here again but request a quiet room. Otherwise wear ear plugs to sleep...

review_title: Cute place, good location, pleasant service
review_text: Stayed in a double queen room during the week. Staff was very helpful, they even printed out directions for me at the front desk. Doormen always available to hail a cab. The lounge was very comfortable for coffee and the newspaper in the morning. The bedding was wonderful and the hotel was quiet. My only complaint is the room was quite warm even after having maintenance "reset" the AC even though it was fairly cool outside and the room was too dark, with only a couple lamps. Overall, great stay for the rate we got.

review_title: Good location rooms are a bit out dated
review_text: Stayed here for a few days for work. The location is great on Ohio between michigan and st Clair, right off mag mile. There is no room service, and the elevators are inconsistent as they lights and indicators don't always work. The bathrooms are a little older and the window ac units are a little loud. However the rooms are clean and the service was very nice and friendly.
hotel_name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel

review_title: Extremely small rooms at a great location
review_text:
Good: 
Excellent location 
Clean rooms 
Nice terrace open for everyone. Great way to spend time after dinner.
Bad:
Rooms are the smallest I have ever seen. Next to only a very crappy hotel in Rome
The bathroom is very cramped. Cramped is an under statement. The wash basin / sink is suitable for maybe a small monkey. That thing is a joke.
hotel_name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel

review_title: Great location, very nice place and cheaper than most other 4-stars downtown!!
review_text: My wife and I loved it! The room was small but we weren't in there much. One of the best mattresses I've ever slept on!! We were on the 3rd floor and heard NO street noise. Nice updates!

The location is great close to everything 
nice top roof bar just steps from great stores, and train station.........
i will definetly be back.....
hotel_name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel

review_text:
The Allerton is a great hotel if you're going to spend most of your time out enjoying the city. The location is PERFECT, and the rooms are comfortable enough. There's relatively few onsite amenities (like a day spa), but there's plenty around the area. 
We had a few issues with our stay. First, upon arriving at the hotel at 4:30ish, we found our room wasn't ready. Second, we were supposed to receive two glasses of wine with our stay. We were slipped a coupon for these under our door in the middle of the night, which did us no good, because we werent going to start drinking before check out the next morning. (we should have received the coupon at check in.). For both issues the staff was helpful and accommodating. We received a phone call a half hour after arrival that our room was ready, and received a portion off our bill to comp for the wine.
In SUMMARY....
PROs:
1) LOCATION
2) kind staff
3) punctual room service
4) quiet, despite downtown setting (not much road noise at all)
CONs:
1) room service and parking are horribly expensive. 
KNOW:
1) the entrance is easy to miss (just east of Michigan Ave) and isn't much to look at. Check in desk is very lack luster, and oppressively warm (by fireplace). 
2) rooms are comfortable, but not luxurious. I found the decor a bit odd, but not distracting. Could use some updating. 
3) it's a little bit of a walk to the El, but there'll be hundreds of cabs at your disposal. 
We would absolutely stay here again.

The hotel was great! Their beds are amazing!! Nice large bathrooms. No free wifi in rooms, which sucked. Had to go down to the lobby, where everyone else was using the free wifi. And the lobby music was very loud. Great location, close to anything you could want. If you aren't a walker the buses run right on that street. Buses were nice and $2.25 for a ride which beats a taxi! I thought the hotel was a little expensive, but so is Chicago!!
Cleanliness can be better but acceptable. Rooms are small but the price and location cannot be better. (booked with expedia with flight package) It is right on magnificent mile.
hotel_name: Inn of Chicago Magnificent Mile, an Ascend Collection hotel

review_title: I've never experienced anything like my visit here.
review_text: this is the worse hotel stay that I've never experienced. Very tacky and non-accomodating. They made me feel like I was in their way. I've experienced better hospitallity in two star accomodations. I would never recommend anyone to stay there. I would not consider returning until they can get it together.

review_title: Tiny rooms, far from Michigan ave.
review_text: These rooms are so small you can barely move!!!! Also, very far from Michigan avenue. We have stayed in Chicago numerous times, by far the worst experience.

Stayed here for business in June - extremely convenient location for short walk to shopping and great dining. Nice view, very good service, and we got a great rate for a downtown hotel. Room was small, but very nicely furnished with modern decor, and plenty of room for a single business traveller.

review_title: Underwhelming boutique hotel that over promises and under delivers
review_text:
Yes it's boutique, if by boutique you mean cheap, individual and over priced for what you get.
Poor eslection of room service. No water in the room, plastic cups, no minibar or fridge, no kettle and the basic of amenities.
Rooms were never serviced before 4pm and then inconsistently. Sheets were not changed the whole week I was there. I had to ask for bathmats etc.
Good location, but this is not a luxury or boutique hotel. This is a "smart" budget hotel. 
Still think it was way overpriced for the ambience, size of rooms, quality of training/management.
Oh, and I mystery shop hotels for a leading luxury brand by the way!!

review_title: Chic Boutique Hotel in Great Location
review_text: Hotel Felix is a totally renovated hotel located in a wonderful neighbourhood. Rooms are rather small as are bathrooms. Lovely amenities and first class restaurant.

Location is fantastic, heat for shopping and enjoying a run down Lake Shore Drive. 
WiFi connection is really weak, room service is ridiculously expensive and rooms are only so so good. Staff answer your questions, but less than friendly.

review_title: A great stay for patients and tourists
review_text:
My husband and I along with our two children, 5 and 2, stayed here for a short weekend get away. It's very easy to get here by any mode of transportation. $10ish for a taxi from downtown, three blocks from pink line and four block to the bus that will take you to the museums. The neighborhood is quiet with great food just a couple blocks away. 
The front desk staff was great with directions and the shuttle driver will take you anywhere within about a mile of the hotel. They are all very accommodating and helpful! 
While there is no pool or great views this hotel is incredibly comfortable, clean and easy to get to. Our family will probably stay here again!

review_text:
Nice location, nice staff, clean room with updates.
Conference rooms are clean, carpet could stand to be updated. Fair warning - the elevators at this hotel are very very slow!

The renovation is beautiful, its very stylish, affordable, and the location is unbeatable. The staff was very friendly, albeit rather uncoordinated ( had to call 3 different departments to get our luggage taken down to our car)
The regular rooms feel a bit cramped so upgrade to a suite if you can, and dont expect a bathtub unless you ask specifically

review_title: Very close to Michigan Ave & historical, but also very dirty and old smelling except for the closet bathroom..
review_text:
I booked thru hotwire for 100, where you don't see the hotel. Bad idea! Customer service agent wasn't so nice at all, tried to be friendly to her (Yana) not happening.. I get to my room, Ned skirt dirty with white stains and ripped at the bottom. the chairs had Nasty dirty stains looked like urine and they were torn. The old zenith tv from when I was born in the 80s, had stains around the frame, the cabinet it was in one door was falling or leaning the hinge was broken and the other door had the knob to open cabinet missing. I understand historical, maybe that's why the furnitures wood was chipped. The bed had a mink cover to hide the rips and tears on the blanket, and not sure what else was meant to cover the tears on the sheets and a stain on sheet.. Ugh.. I'm thinking the plush pad was nice or was it one of those covers to so bed bugs can't get on top.. I didn't see any and don't plan on it cuz I'm checking out.. The bed shirt was ripped and had white stains that looked like they could have been easily washed out. The bathroom was the only decent thing, for the 1/2 I'm here I was ok sitting in there. It's like a closet tho, the toilet was right next to tub, no space between shower n toilet. If your claustrophobic don't go in there altho it's the nicest thing I saw so far.. 
For the price, not a good deal!!

I didn't even know they made hotel rooms this small. If you are traveling with something like a car seat, stroller, computer equipment, basically anything more than a few suitcases, you literally will have no where to put it. The room was clean and everything was in good shape...as I'm sure they are in any other hotel at this level. However, one night we called the front desk asking for a cork screw and they girl at the front desk said she'd be happy to bring it up to us. 40 minutes later we called again and a guy said that she tried to run it up to us but she couldn't find our room and then left for the night. And that he was the only one at the desk so he couldn't leave it so we had to go down to get the cork screw. Going down to the front desk is no big deal. Waiting 40 minutes for it because an employee "couldn't find our room" is completely ridiculous. The fact that no one called us saying that we needed to come down to get it because they "couldn't find our room" is inconsiderate and unprofessional. With so many nice hotels in downtown Chicago I will not be spending my money at the Felix again.

Accomodations were good. The faculty was very nice and the location excellent. With that being said if you wanna get a good nights sleep either buy some earplugs or avoid this hotel all together. The walls and windows are paper thin! There is a hospital nearby and the sirens will keep u up all night!! Signed sleepless in Chicago.

review_title: Not a shining star in Chicago
review_text: The concept is great but this hotel had awful beds, postage stamp size pillows, I asked for a duvet and was handed a ratty old blanket, the breakfast was minimal at best, not enough newspapers for guests staying at the hotel and finally.. a call to a taxi company outside 312 area code for 2 mins was a whopping $5.00. I'd take a pass on this hotel as usually a five star can be had for same amount 300. per night elsewhere

review_title: Stayed for a few weeks and would definitely go back
review_text: I'm not sure how anyone can criticize this place. We had a one bedroom suite and loved it. Free breakfasts which were great and free evening snacks and occasionally beer as well. The rooms are clean. It's next door to hub 51 which is a great restaurant and night spot. If you're looking for a fun night out you are in the middle of the river north scene. The weight room is nice and but for the loud kids the pool would've been great. The staff was nice. The one thing to try to avoid is parking because that costs about 30-45 bucks. Thats about a third of the room price so take the train from the airport and figure out how get there without a car. You won't need one once you arrive since you're in the middle of a great part of the city. Anyone who has bad comments probably doesn't really understand what a great deal this place is.

review_title: A gem in the big city!
review_text: This is the second time I have stayed in this location. The staff, service, location, and overall atmosphere was terrific! You cannot go wrong if you stay here!

review_title: I had a pleasant stay at the Westin.
review_text: I stayed at the Westin and attended a conference at the hotel, and it was a very pleasant stay. Check-in was quick and easy. The staff was very kind. The rooms were very clean and comfortable. The only thing was the room didn't have any toiletries upon arrival and none were put in the entire stay. I'm sure if I would have called and asked for some they would have brought them to me. The food service staff did an excellent job of feeding us breakfast and lunch at the conference. The location of the hotel is perfect. It is right in the middle of fabulous shopping and excellent dining. Overall, the experience at this Westin was great!

Sheets and towels had stains. Staff is condescending. Only thing going for the hotel is the location. But even that is lost with all the other options that continue to open in River North. Friday night we were kept awake by a band in the restaurant on the first floor. My 9-year-old actually asked for ear plugs.

I was very excited to stay at this hotel. I booked 2 nights through Priceline at $115 and $155 per night. Being 4th of July weekend that was pretty good for the city. 
When we arrived the staff seemed ok, asked to help with luggage. The front desk told us about the hotel restaurant and the morning coffee/tea hour. However, they couldn't even point us to the elevators. 
The elevators started the smallness of the trip. 4 people were all crammed in with small bags. Once we got to the room we realized how small that was and why they have to offer free coffee in the morning. The room had no coffee maker or even cups. It offered 1 small window without much light, a closet 
(if you can call that a closet) with a curtain as a door. The bed offered TINY pillows which my head fell off 
of all night. The air conditioner was very loud and the tv seemed to be hooked up wrong because it took forever to get it to turn on. The bathroom had only a shower with a curtain that barely covered the opening which let water spray all over the floor. the sink was so shallow water would splash out. I did enjoy the toiletries offered including makeup remover clothes and q-tips!
Here's the kicker. We got home from a game and tried to get into our room and neither key card worked. I had to go back to the front desk and tell them and his first response, "well, were they by any credit cards?" Seriously, no I'm sorry or let take care of that for you?!?! Where has customer service gone?
I want to be comfortable when I'm away from home and I was not at Hotel Felix. We will never stay there again!

review_title: 1-2 star experience at a 4 star price
review_text: The Elevators in this hotel made the entire stay miserable. They are old and incredibly slow. This may not seem important but when you are visiting for a night or two and spend literally 10 minutes waiting for an elevator, and another 10 minutes getting from the 20th floor to the ground, that's 15-20 minutes per ride or 30-45 per round trip- a complete waste of time. The benefit of this hotel is the location which is negated by the elevator issue. All of the guests complained about the same thing. The room was old and the decorating all different styles that didn't seem to match. The staff was ok but not overly helpful- not what you'd expect for a hotel this price. We left and went the James which was the same price for an amazing experience. Avoid the Allerton.

Wouldn't think of a better place to stay at. Everything is within walking distance, food, shopping, you got it all. Great value for money, and very lovely staff. Heavenly showers in bathroom not so heavenly, but otherwise , a fantastic property.

review_title: The westin on Michigan avenue is the perfect place to stay when visiting downtown Chicago.
review_text: I was so, so impressed. I spent one night to celebrate valentines day with my girlfriend, and left wishing that everyday good go as well as that day. The wonderful concierge Kira helped me plan a few extras -- including rose petals in the shape of a heart on the bed when we arrived -- and it could not have worked more perfectly. The room service staff had champagne and strawberries in our room just before we returned from the theater -- perfect timing. I would and will go back in a heartbeat.

review_title: Perfect location, friendly service, great value.
review_text: Hotel is an older building, but inside is very nice. Check-in was smooth as could be, they upgraded our room from 2 doubles to a queen for free. Would of went to king but there wasn't any available. Rooms are small but we aren't living In it Just sleeping so it was fine. Bathroom wasn't as small as some reviews made It seem but it is pretty narrow and long. Shower was great. Only complaint I have with hotel is the breakfast. $15 a person for the buffet and it wasn't good at all. Total waste of money, especially when there are tons of restaurants within a quarter mile walk. Rest of our 2 night stay was fabulous. Location was everything.

I would like to start by saying I have never written a hotel review before; however, I felt like I would be doing other travelers a disservice by not sharing my experience. My initial room was so small I had to go beg the front desk for a room with double beds, their only solution was upgrading me to a single bed suite with a pull out couch (which they charged me an additional 30/night fee for a 4 night stay) and told me to try again the next day to see if I could get into a double room. I tried the following day and then the following day but failed. I was stuck on the 6th floor facing air conditining units out one window and a brick wall out the other. Cell phone service was almost nonexistent due to this. The sink in the bathroom had cracks, the carpet smelt and the bed didnt sleep much better than the couch. I booked this hotel thru Priceline's name your own price which had this hotel classified as a 4 star, I'd say it's more closer to a 2.5 after staying 4 nights.
Hubby and I flew into town for a BEARS GAME and stayed for 3 nights. This hotel is in the middle of everything and we felt so comfortable and safe.

Booked through a third party reseller for a song for 2 nights and actually through the hotel for one night to arrive earlier than originally planned. The worst was going through the reseller honestly, because what they had booked would not have accommodated our party, though I had specifically made notations on the booking form for them. Thankfully we decided to leave a day earlier which gave me cause to call the hotel a couple of days before to see about the extra night. The reservation agent was a doll, squeezing us into the right sized room and correcting the booking made by the third party. She blocked our room so they could not be reassigned out and gave me detailed instructions on what to ask the front desk for at check in (we needed a rollaway). It was easy to find, cheery and helpful valets and bellman and check in was a breeze. Had seen a bunch of concerns around elevators - this wasn't anything to complain about. In fact, we noticed that on the second day, our room actually shared a wall with one of the elevator shafts. We didn't hear a peep. We LOVED the Allerton and wouldn't hesitate to return for our next Chicago stay.

I would probably refer to this as a micro- hotel. Everything about it is small from the rooms and bathrooms to the beds. Service was substandard and staff was not willing to work with us on travel changes such as accommodations. Other reviews are correct in that this should not be rated higher than three star.
First it took us thirty minutes to check in and we were the only ones there. When we got to our rooms they were the size of other hotels closets with no amenities. Stay somewhere else!

review_title: There has to be better for the price!
review_text: Stayed 2 nights very high priced. Not very clean, the smoke detector was missing from our room, the ice machine did not work. We had a 14th floor room over looking state street, not a good view, some perv on the roof of the building across the street looking at our window at night. Valet 48 a night??? I was not gonna use my car for 2 days, nice bellhop suggested a garage down the street it was 35 a day and not a nice place although my car was ok. It just seems like the hellhole are only willing to help if you pay. No one even offered to help load the car, but we couldn't tell them no when we were unloading. For about 80.00 a night this would have been so so, but it was more than double that so I say look elsewhere.

review_title: Great boutique hotel in a great location.
review_text: The lobby and bar area have an old hotel embiance that is relaxing but chic at the same time. All of the staff was extremely friendly and helpful. We upgraded to a king bed room from a full for only $25 per night!! This is well worth it, as the king room is much larger. The location is extremely convenient... Right by Michigan Ave shopping.

Great boutique hotel in the hustle of Chicago. No doubt the rooms are small, think European. But I'm in the city and not hanging out in the room all day. Free wireless and free computer access paid for themselves. Nice decor, staff was eager to please. I'd stay here again.

This hotel is in a great location on Michigan avenue for dining and shopping it's all on your doorstep but the downside is the rooms are small and if your in a room overlooking the avenue then you may need earplugs for a good night sleep ! The staff can be either great and very helpfull or sometimes quite the opposite.

review_title: Good marks from this Gold Elite Member, sans decent Wi-Fi
review_text: Great location. Close to everything downtown. A very personable and friendly staff. The rooms are smaller than the average Courtyard, but with a more contemporary design. A comfortable lobby, spacious cafe and in-property Starbucks (would benefit from the Marriott "Bistro" makeover). The Fitness Center has a spa, lap pool, sauna and ample equipment, but could use better lighting and air conditioning (this is shared with the neighboring residents). My only disappointment is the lack of in-room Wi-Fi (my first Courtyard without in years) and the lack of Wi-Fi bandwidth in the common areas (i.e., very slow). Enjoying our Thanksgiving weekend stay.

We enjoyed a 2 bedroom suite which was generously sized for a family of 4, with a large living room area. Plenty of restaurants and shopping very nearby including a couple of small markets. Easy walk to Michigan Avenue and Water Tower, a little farther to red line subway. Very slow elevators (apartment building conversion to RI?). Average RI breakfast. Front desk staff was very helpful, good suggestions. Parking is the only downside, expensive and lightly staffed valet service, sometimes a long wait for car. Overall great for families and walking visit to Magnificent Mile and Hicago.
Room was comfortable. Internet is wired only, a disadvantage for me. Restaurant was marginal and bar expensive and sparse. But the location is great for eating elsewhere. Value stay.

review_title: 5 Star..... If you are a Hobbit!
review_text:
Without doubt a wonderfully located historic and charming hotel which screams character. It's a shame it's more suited to Bilbo Baggins then a 6 ft tall Irish man with a suitcase and trolly bag. 
From the moment you try to get a lift to your floor you realise that this will be a cramped experience. 
I had a wonderful corner room with two windows, one looking directly down onto Mich Ave and the other looking straight at the Famous Water Tower, it's a shame I could have opened both windows at the same time from my bed, one with my toe and the other with my arm and control the tv at the same time. There was just NO room. My suitcase blocked the main door when opened and had to remain closed for the most part and flush against the wall, why they bother to provide a suitcase stand I'll never know. And as someone said in another review, you literally have to climb over the toilet to get in and out of the shower.... The shower is in actual fact the most spacious part of the room!
I ordered breakfast for room service. It was the Allerton and it consisted of 2 slices toast, 2 poached eggs, breakfast potatoes and 3 slices of bacon. I also had a tea and OJ. I expected the rather high charge of $34.50 (despite being advertised at $15.50) but what I had not expected was just how meager the portions were, as small as the room!
Then the lifts, tiny is not the word, even the doors are too narrow! The wait can be significant, I waited almost 10 minutes at home point. 
However the staff are friendly and professional and the location is just amazing!
I appreciate that the building is old and they are limited in what they do but I really believe that the rooms are just too small. Size is not everything, but it is in this place!

Stayed here for 3 nights following a 2 week trip around the mid west.
We arrived late on a Friday night to find a room with one bed which was not appropriate when sharing with my Dad! There were no other rooms available so we opted for a room with a sofa bed. This was not the most comfortable but did the job.
Location was great, parking was expensive at $48 a night and no free internet as we gotten used to at other hotels.

review_title: Great location but watch what you are being charged.
review_text: So my son and I were in Chicago for his 13 th birthday weekend. I have never been to Chicago and booked this hotel through priceline. Got a great rate and the location was great. The staff was very friendly and helpful. Like the reviews say the standard rooms are a bit small BUT really how much room do you need. The beds were a little bigger than a double. The only thing I would say about the room is that they need to change the carpet it was showing the wear. The only big issue that we had was that when we checked in I was told that there was a 75$ incidental charge that needed to be paid and I would get it back when we check out. That wasn't a problem however I checked my bank the next morning and saw that the woman who checked me in charged me almost 300$ not just the 75$. I was able to resolve it and the front desk was some help. I was a bit surprised however that the hotel didn't offer something for the huge inconvenience. It wasn't a small mistake. So when checking in be sure you are being charged the right amount.

We stayed here for Memorial weekend and the experience was incredible. We got the hotel very cheap thru an online deal. The staff is amazing. I don't understand why there are previous reviews complaining about the room size, i've stayed in far more little rooms. The size is perfect. The only complain is that Friday night we had a group of very noicy either teenagers or collegue students that kept slamming doors and shouting in the corridors but when we called front desk the staff was really concerned and addressed the situation quickly.
Overall tge experience was amazing will defenitly come back and recommend it.

... especially if you want to swing it. For the money paid, this has got to be the smallest hotel room I have ever stayed in. It's a grand total of FIVE (yes, 5) steps from the furthest side of the bed to the door of the room. The room is, including the bathroom, about the size of half my kitchen. I can't stress enough how small this place is!
I got out of the shower this morning and literally had to climb over the toilet to leave the bathroom. The bed itself is not suitable for two people, unless you both happen to be under 5 years old. 
The room was clean though, and the room service reasonable. Staff are friendly and genuine. 
The only problem was, having been inconsiderate and bringing a case when I checked in (how stupid of me) there was no place for the staff member to put the tray - I had to eat my meal sitting on the bed. I really cannot stress how SMALL these rooms are. 
Please don't come to this hotel thinking it's luxurious or in any way spacious. It's tiny, pokey, dinky, squashed and cramped. 
I would not stay here again - however if I lose my legs in a freak accident meaning I end up 30 inches shorter than I am now - I'd certainly consider it (as long as I didn't do anything daft like bring a bag, or clothes, or someone else).

review_title: Really large rooms with separate living area, mini fridge. and microwave!
review_text: The location of this hotel is perfect for a visit to NYC. It is centrally located in the heart of time square with easy access to the subway and all broad way shows! The service was outstanding and extremely accommodating to all our needs. We even decided last minute to stay a few extra nights and they were able to keep us in the same room! Daniel at the front desk was fun, energetic and provided good advice on dinning options and how to get around!!! Maintance and house keeping were very prompt when needed! If you are thinking of staying in time square this is the place to stay!!

We LOVED our stay at this wonderful location. My fabulous husband arranged for my 50th birthday celebration and it was the greatest suite we ever had. We stayed here two years ago and loved every minute! Thanks to Daniel for making special arrangements for us; for the extra kindness he showed made me a happy baby boomer. Will love to return again with my sister as she loved the views and spacious suites. Exciting !!!!!!

Got a tremendous deal from a hotel booking website so I can't complain too much. The location is great. Walking distance to everything. Rooms are small, hotel is older, walls are thin. You can't beat theocation though.

review_title: Convenient for conferences/conventions at McCormick Place
review_text:
I stayed here in December of 2011 for a convention at McCormick Place. Location couldn't have been better, never had to walk outside to get to the conference.
The room was nice, with a nice view of the lake (i was on the 30th floor, not facing the city). Overall, the room was clean, but there were minor things that would have made it better - what appeared to be a coffee stain in the carpet, some mior touchup in the paint in the bathroom. Also, the heating was finicky, although it worked fine overall (blew cool air when it reached temperature instead of shutting off at times). The iron looked hardly used, but could have used replacement.
The restaurants on site were pretty good, especially liked Shor. They a resort-priced, but right on target for what I've seen in Chicago price-wise.
There is a Metra station right next to the hotel, and the #3 CTA Train runs right in front ot the Hyatt to Michigan Avenue, so although the location isn't necessarily in the heart of downtown, it's very accessible with public transportation.
The service at the hotel was very good. Every staff member I had dealings with treated me very well, and made me feel welcome. I absolutely will stay he again when I return next year.
On a final note, the bed at this hotel was among the most comforatble I have ever slept in, including my own bed at home.
I highly recommend this place.

review_title: (half review) Good budget option in Chicago
review_text: First, I was here for a sleep study, so my room was arranged and paid for by someone else, and we were on the lowest floor. All in all the rooms are clean compfortable and no frills. On te two times I stayed there, the tub drained slow and the showerhead was leaking. (you get a nice movable showerhead, but the joints leaked). The WiFi is spotty. That said, if you're looking for a break on price, it's a good option in Chicago. You're between a drug store and a grocery store. You're in Greek Town and steps from Randolph St, so no shortage of great food, but you will need a super short cab or bus ride to access the other keyspots of Chicago, assuming you don't want to drive and/or pay for parking.

When we first arrived we delt with a very pleasant gentleman by the name of Curtis. He was very friendly and nice to deal with. That's where it ended. On the last morning of our stay my wife was leaving prior to me and went down to get a cab. Two cabs pulled up and proceeded to argue with eachother as to who was going to take her to the airport. It ended with one of them grabbing her bag from her and throwing it into the cab. We visited to hotel bar later in the night where the working door man came in multiple times to get drinks and actually made comments about the drinks not being strong enough. Not sure why the bartender would serve someone that was working but that's just me. The next night the same doorman was leaning on the front counter in front of multiple customers making it very awkward for us/ them to get to the front to ask questions or check in. The elevator requires a key to get up to your room which I do like but it would be nice if the key readers worked. I was only able to get up one time out of the five without having to visit the front desk to ask why my card wouldn't work. While in the room they have a lock on the sliding glass door that's great but it only locks when the door is slightly open so I hope you like the sound of the city while you sleep. In addition to that the thing that you would pull the curtains closed with broke off right in my hand. Very cheap! Overall my experience was less than satisfactory. I stayed at the Afinia for the week prior and this was a night and day difference. The Afinia was excellent!!! Very professional and very nice!!! My brother is the GM of a hotel for a major chain in the Colorado area so I have started to take notice of the smaller things while visiting hotels in other states. I am in no way an expert but I know what professionalism is and what it should look like. The crown plaza reminded me of a hotel 6!!!!!

review_title: A Hotel that ticks all the boxes
review_text:
A warm and friendly welcome greeted us on our arrival at the Casablanca Hotel. This set the tone for the whole stay at the hotel. The staff couldn't do enough for us- answering any questions regarding New York, booking dinner reservations or assisting with luggage. Our room was excellent. The room was very clean, well laid out and very comfortable. Breakfast was great and the free coffee 24 hours a day was very welcome. 
The location of the hotel is excellent- approx 20 metres from Times Square, which made the hotel an excellent base to explore New York from.
This hotel does go that extra mile.

review_text: Nice, clean rooms and very close to downtown and to the very cool Randolphe St. Checking in, checking out, storing bags, retrieving bags were all extremely slow and disorganized. I would stay again, though, and take my chances.

review_text: I stayed there for a couple of nights on a recent business trip to Chicago. I had got a great deal on Priceline. The staff at the reception were very courtious. Shirley, at the front desk, gave me an upgrade. The room was on the 28th floor and provided a magnificient view of the Chicago skyline. The food at the restaurant was good. The location was a bit off though - not exactly downtown where you could walk around. Otherwise, it was a pleasant experience.

review_title: A bit remote from the city sights, but happy with hotel overall
review_text:
First, I was a bit disappointed that the website did not provide instructions from the airports on how to get to the hotel by public transit. It is a convention center hotel, so most people will probably take a taxi or the airport express, but I wanted to save some money as I was not in a rush. So for those of you like mind, I can at least offer instructions from Midway airport.
- take orange line directly from midway airport. Buy a fare card for $2.50 (2.25 for train, .25 for transfer to bus) or you can get a day or multiway pass if you think you'll use more transit. Get off at Roosevelt and exit the station. You'll need to find out which direction is East (you'll be facing either north or south depending on which exit you use). Walk two blocks east to Michigan (passing wabash) and catch a number 3 bus heading south. In about 5 minutes, you'll get to McCormick Place stop (yes, the stop is actually named that). Cross the street and there you are 2.50.
As for the hotel, the service was extremely friendly (actually everyone is really friendly here... Chicago is becoming one of my favorite cities). I also booked a horseshoe hammond casino rate, and there is a free shuttle bus going there and back daily from the hotel (saving you about 160 bucks).
Free airport check in machines in lobby is great too. Food in restaurant was very good, although a bit on the pricier side.
Rooms very clean, but I have to be honest, a bit dated. The bathroom needs a makeover if the hotel is to compete with the trendier hotels like W etc. Also, the "closet" is basically a cubby hole covered with a curtain. That I have not seen before at a Hyatt. Also, rooms are not very soundproofed, so if you are planning to make "noise" be forewarned.
Also be prepared to take a cab to get to downtown or the city sights, if you don't want to figure out the bus options.
All in all though, a pleasant stay for a decent price.

review_text:
This is definitely one of the best hotels I have stayed in for value, service & location in New York
A real warm welcome from the staff when we arrived, we have a suite as our daughter is staying with us, lots of space in the room (502) with great wardrobe space. 
Coffee and drinks available 24/7 and a great snack buffet from 5.
Position is excellent you can walk anywhere from the hotel. Noise not a problem for us (but we did have windows closed!)
A real gem of a Hotel.

Just back from 3 night stay (Â£700 inc all taxes) and couldnt fault it.
As stated in previous reviews the location is perfect-simply walk out front door turn right and you are in the heart of Times square.
The room size is on par with other NY hotels so if room size is crucial to your decision then possibly explore suites at the larger hotels.
5-8pm signals happy hour at Ricks cafe with red,white and sparkling wine available to wash down selection of cheese biscuits and snacks. Continental breakfast (included in rate) more than sets you up for a busy day sightseeing in the city.
Complimentary bottled water in room is a nice touch, and free in room safety deposit is provided.
When we return we will definitely opt to stay here. Stayed at Sofitel (42nd st) for our 1st visit to NY but the added extras at the Casablanca combined with its overall charm make it a more attractive option.
Enjoyed my stay here & the gym us excellent! It's a HUGE hotel tho with all the convention stuff so be prepared to walk if you're doing a conference there!

review_text: Perfect location, friendly and helpful staff, great service and amenities. Super comfortable beds, and super quiet, when you step in off the street you almost forget you're in Times Square. Casablanca helped make a great first impression of NYC even better. We will be back.

My family stayed here after the hotel accepted a great Priceline deal (thank you for accepting Priceline, it helped us get to experience a Chicago trip when funds are usually an issue for us). The hotel definately exceeded our expectations. I saw the mixed reviews here and comkented to my wife that I couldn't believe that some people claimed to have such filthy rooms, etc. I doubt the hotel has a block of rooms that are kept dirty for some people. It is more likely that the people writing the reviews were blowing one small issue out of proportion. 
My family actually loved the location...close enough to downtown, the museums, and the 12th Street Beach, to be convenient and feel like you are "in the city," yet far enough to get a break from the noise, hustle and bustle. We came prepared to take public transportation, because we would not be paying through the nose for parking. The passes sold by the desk were wonderful to have available, and the number 3 bus was very convenient. We even walked down Cermak to get to the L station in order to experience riding the L train (red line). It was a nice 10 minute walk, and the neighborhood didn't feel unsafe.
If I am coming back, I would stay here again for sure (as long as my Priceline bids are still accepted!) Thank you! :-)
