The air conditioning wasn't working and it was awful. I tried calling the front desk multiple times and no one answered. I left messages and no one called back. I finally went down to the front desk and asked and they said it was back on and would cool down eventually which it didnt. I would never stay there again especially for how much it cost. Even the holiday inn has ac. Terrible

We were supposed to check into the hotel yesterday but upon arrival were told the air conditioning wasn't working. It was 92 degrees! Funny, when I spoke to the concierge two hours before our arrival, he didn't mention that small detail. We had no place to stay that night and it ruined our weekend. My kids were crushed.

My first time staying at a Holiday Inn and this was a pleasant surprise. The rooms were clean and kept up by housekeeping for the entire stay (and we had a large group over 2 connecting rooms). The bar downstairs was not too pricey but still nice. The views are great. We walked to all of the locations we wanted to go around Chicago from the hotel. Cabs were right outside for the few times we did need a cab. Free Internet. Food delivery options for late night ordering. The bathrooms do not have ventilation/fan so it did get steamed up easy.

review_title: Great value, excellent view, good for a quiet business trip.
review_text: I stayed with the athletic club because it was most affordable by far and fairly close (15 min walk) to my office. Location is kind of strange and sleepy since it's within a financial services building on the 40th floor. However, hotel was clean and very quiet. Decor was simple and slightly dated but experience was good. Staff is really nice an helpful. Would recommend for a tired business traveller.

We changed to this hotel on our second night here and really wish we hadn't! The beds are super hard...they don't offer any kind of breakfast unless you use the restaurant, two of the computers didn't work and the other one was in Spanish half the time. Not to mention they don't give you coffee! You can only get coffee from 5 am to 7 am.... Whoever heard of a hotel room not 
Providing a room with a coffee maker! Chicago has many good hotels.... Trust me and go find one of the 
better ones. It is also farther from downtown than we thought... Not very attractive scenery.... And did I mention the coffee situation :/

review_title: Save Money staying a few blocks away...priority benefits provided even with Priceline reservation!
review_text: My first time at this hotel...even though I booked on Priceline, I still got the free Internet and Priority welcome gift bag! Rooms are nice, staff was friendly. I had a great river and city view...and only a few blocks from Michigan Ave...easy walk.

review_title: Nice rooms if you don't want room service or coffee
review_text: My room was spacious with a nice sitting area and a small walk in closet. But, for me, this did not make up for the surly and incompetently slow device (front desk and restaurant). There are no coffee makers in the room and no coffee in the lobby when I went down at 8:00am. I had to wait for 20 minutes to get a cup of terrible coffee that was unfortunately cinnamon flavored. I was told I couldn't get room service because of some "groups in the hotel" even though this us suppose to be a 3 star hotel. I came here for work at Mercy Hospital but will stay at a different hotel next time.

review_title: Don't eat at the sports bar here.
review_text:
We just spent several hours getting a "quick" bite to eat in the sports bar in this hotel as we were afraid to go outside to find someplace else since this area of the city is not the best and the actual restaurant was not open. 
First, they gave my salad to my fiance with chicken on top, which I did not order. There was no creamy balsalmic dressing on it so I was waiting for them to bring that, and my fiance's salad was still nowhere to be found. Instead, they took my salad back and it took another half an hour for the rest of our food to come, including my correct salad. And not including the cup of soup I ordered. My fiance, however, had been given the wrong salad. Neither of us were given dressing this time either. So while we waited for that, the bartender went back to find out if my fiance could get the salad he ordered instead of the one he was given. 
He ended up just eating the wrong salad, and I was so hungry that I ate half of mine before we were even given dressing (blue cheese and italian; neither of which were what was supposed to come with my salad in the first place). No soup to be found. We asked for it again. I ended up being pretty hungry once I finished my salad, so while the bartender made up our checks I asked if I just wasn't going to have any soup. I was still hungry and about to work until 4am with a half-empty stomach for 12 hours. As we were leaving, my soup came out and I had to finish it in about 30 seconds.
The worst part was that the bartender was apparently supposed to pay for the kitchen's (frequent and bad) mistakes... she comped my fiance's salad and used her tips to pay for it, so we felt bad and gave her the money for his meal anyway. She definitely didn't deserve to be treated the way the kitchen was treating her, and after she spent three hours trying to get them to make our food, she shouldn't have to pay for it herself. 
I had been in the car since very early this morning driving to Chicago and now I'm sitting in my room, exhausted and upset instead of enjoying myself like I should be. At least I finally got to eat something. The front desk and bellhop were very helpful; just please get ahold of your kitchen. There wasn't even anyone else ordering food in the bar.

review_title: Hotel price good, nice location, but service sub-par ...
review_text: This was an okay hotel overall. Good points: good price with the car stay free package, clean overall (no bed bugs)! Location and views from hotel were good. Bad points: restaurant in hotel lobby is over priced. Staff wasn't very helpful, requested extra towels one morning but never received them. Also, the bell-hops weren't very helpful, a bit rude. Even though it was a good price, I probably will stay somewhere else the next time I'm in Chicago. I would recommend only because I usually have good experiences at Holiday Inn hotels. Maybe the staff just had a bad weekend ...

Stayed there on Sunday and monday nites. Checked into my room and went to open the curtains to look out window and saw a totally awesome view of the skyline and the chicago river. Its a little bit of a walk from Michigan ave though, say 5 or 6 blocks. I would definitely go back.
The staff was outstanding. The rooms were very large and the tubs to die for. I would recommend this hotel to anyone that appreciates great service.

review_title: Air condition in the room is too loud
review_text: Is you want to have a good silent night sleep this is not a good Hotel for you. They have this old air condition unit in every room that make a loud noise. Not a good Place to stay during summer in Chicago. They sent someone to fixed the problem But the guy said that he can't fixed it since all the air-condition unit in this hotel is too old. Location is good but at the end of a long day , I prefered to have a quite night rest.

Firstly the location is great. We had a view of Lake Michigan and Navy Pier. Only 2 blocks from Michigan Ave. The lobby was nice and modern. Rooms were old. Rooms looked like a motel with a few modern pieces like a flat screen tv. The bath tub had scuffs in it. For $350 a night, I expected luxury, but it was average. They need to make it "cool" like the W in New York and not an immitation. Oh yeah, spa pool was nice but gym needed upgraded. Overall- location was perfect but hotel was not up to my W Hotel standards.

Arrived very late on a Thursday night before the marathon but it didn't faze them. Got the lovely hotel within a hotel floor (the 15th i think) with included breakfast, etc etc. Lobby can be noisy and the wine bar service seems patchy but the restaurant is good and so is the bar. I was running the marathon and they offered a number of race services, free water and the location can't be beat, frankly. Clean, modern, friendly. Liked it.
Very accommodating to our request of room, very friendly, great service. Fantastic. Wish the beautiful lobby bar stayed open late. Great location, strongly recommend!
hotel_name: Doubletree by Hilton Chicago Magnificent Mile

review_title: Needs a thorough cleaning and updated air circulation
review_text: Stayed here for five days in November for conference. Floor dirty, the cleaning staff did minimal, the bar staff is responsible for upkeep of coffee supplies and apparently they are trying to use up decaf because as I used the regular, they kept replacing with more decaf. No service at all on the last evening. Air and heating unit is poor, no circulation in room and lots of scuff marks in hall and room.

Nice hotel with great view. We got this room through a Priceline bid for $75/night. The going hotel price was $169. The room was spacious and clean. Parking however cost $43 per 12-24 hour period. There is cheaper parking at Navy Pier for $20/24 hour. There is a magnificent cafe across the street from the hotel with excellent breakfast/lunch choices called West Egg Cafe. Much cheaper than the hotel's restaurant. Overall the hotel is within walking distance of all that downtown has to offer including Navy Pier.
hotel_name: Doubletree by Hilton Chicago Magnificent Mile

review_text: Rates, location, rooms and service are good. But the a/c units are ridiculously loud. The weather for the first week of October was just gorgeous in Chicago and the air conditioning was needed pretty much all week. The units sound and feel like a diesel truck is idling outside of your window. Couple that with the down filled pillows that offer no head support and I had some pretty poor nights sleep. But overall, I did enjoy my stay.
hotel_name: Doubletree by Hilton Chicago Magnificent Mile

review_text:
I really enjoy staying at Fairmonts and when business or personal travel took me to places with a Fairmont, that's where I usually stayed. The Fairmont Millenium
is a nice hotel - quite chic in the lobby. Unfortunately, it's just missing something. It doesn't have the same feel as other Fairmonts. I believe a big piece has to do with the service, and I'll recount some experiences below. Nothing terrible but not in line with the caliber a Fairmont is supposed to be. Overall, it's a clean space in an OK area. The Millenium Park is right there and a nice place to walk. You can also play tennis on the nearby public courts. 
So here are some of the negative service experiences:
1. Check-in - 2 people, both on the phone, so had to wait nearly 10 minutes for someone to help us. 
2. Arrived at our room to find keys didn't work. Had to go back down, wait AGAIN, only to find that we were given the wrong room number (714 instead of 602). 
3. Went out front to get a cab. Doorman asked if I needed a cab, I said yes, he blew his whistle, walked away and began a conversation with another employee. Cab never came and he seemed more interested in his conversation so I walked down to the street to grab one. 
4. Called the concierge to ask about the Adidas Fit gear. Was placed on hold. Kept phone on speakerphone while I shaved, brushed my teeth, etc., and he never came back on the line. 
5. When I did get someone in te line, I asked if they had sweatpants (it was 34â€¢ out), was told yes, they sent up shorts. 
6. When I went to check at the concierge desk, woman was on phone with what I assume was a disgruntled guest, as I could hear 
the person's tone - while she was just rolling her eyes. 
7. I had two packages arrive suing my stay. Was not alerted about either and when I found where to get them, it took about 15-20 minutes to get them. 
Overall, these are mostly small things. In and of themselves I wouldn't complain, but the overall customer service experience here is poor. It's akin to what I had expected at the Hilton I chose not to stay at. My conference was there, and based on the hotel and service, I wish I had stayed there.

The hotel was in the perfect spot..right in between Magnificent Mile and Navy Pier. It truly was the best value in the area. The hotel had been updated, but there were a few minor things that still need some work. Very modern decor as well.
hotel_name: Doubletree by Hilton Chicago Magnificent Mile

review_text: My stay at the south.loop hotel was delightful. Andrew at the front desk got me in my room early an fast. The only problem I had was with the heat n the room was not working but Ronald the maintenance man took care of that real fast an got me ice an cups for my guests. A big ups to Ronald. I will be back SOON.Thanks ssnnaakkee

review_title: Nice hotel, but got tired of the nickel-and-diming
review_text: The fairmont is a nice hotel. You certainly won't be disappointed with the accommodations or the service. The rooms are roomy, the restaurants are quite good (Aria came recommended by locals), and the spa/fitness center was more than adequate. My only complaint, as the title suggests, was what seemed like a hi level of nickel-and-dimming on some items. Internet costs $15, and if you have an iPad and a laptop, you have to pay twice. The fitness center was $10 per session. None of these are really egregious, but I couldn't help but think that a hotel of this caliber should do better. But would stay there again.

Stayed on January 6-9 and it was all I ever wanted in a hotel.
Quiet, I even asked if I was the only one on my floor, 9th.
The front desk, especially Ida, very knowledgeable, helpful, friendly.
Doormen friendly and great cab hailers.
Room was meticulous and more than enough tea and in room coffee, plus in the am, coffee/tea downstairs.
Great rates, especially in January :)
Would stay again.... and recommend to anyone.

review_title: Nice hotel, great location, easy access to shopping and restaurants.
review_text: We were in town for the Chicago Marathon and checked in on Thursday, before most other runners arrived. We were given a room right by the elevators and all we could hear were the elevators going up and down all night (and day, while in room). Thank goodness the windows opened and the weather was nice so we could drown out the sound. Otherwise, a nice room but, find out about your room placement to elevators!

review_title: Clean, Good Location/pay for parking and Internet
review_text: The front desk was very courteous and helpful. The room was very clean and spacious, with nice touches. The rates seemed reasonable until you pay for parking and the Internet. That is my only complaint. I would still go back, but know the extra charges.
hotel_name: Doubletree by Hilton Chicago Magnificent Mile

review_title: Good but not great. But still a nice place
review_text: Nice hotel. Very good quality snd high standard of device. Lobby looked great. Can't comment on amenities as I was simply in and out of the room. Had a corner suite. Big room but furniture was unimpressive. Sofa was worn in pretty bad in the middle. Doors etc were a little beat up. Beds were tiny! I think they were twins.stayed at the swisshotel the week before... Would go back to Swiss before doing fairmont again. Like I said... Good but not great....
I wished I had stay my first night in Chicago here, the rooms were large beds were comfortable and it was at a good location for shopping and the navy pier..
hotel_name: Doubletree by Hilton Chicago Magnificent Mile

review_text:
I was worried about our upcoming 5 day stay based on reviews on triadvisor. However, when I arrived I was relieved. I didn't notice any dirty carpet or peeling paint. We were on the 18th floor. Perhaps the floors differ (remodeling?) but I'm not sure what the fuss is about.
Check in went smooth and was time efficient. Concierge and doormen were always helpful. Restaurant (marketside) was fabulous with excellent service. We were the second room away from the elevator but never noticed any noise. Actually the place was pretty quiet and we often slept in past 9 am with no interruptions.
Great stay... Even better price. Great location. Couldn't have asked for more!
hotel_name: Doubletree by Hilton Chicago Magnificent Mile

review_text: A pretty standard Holiday Inn. A little tired decor, but comfortable beds. Away from the congestion of Michigan Ave, but close to everything you want to do. Get a corner king, as these are nice, big rooms.

I was here for work so didn't have a say in where I stayed. I was a little disappointed in this hotel. They charge extra to use the gym and there's a fee to use the wireless, which I wouldn't have minded had the whole place been a little nicer. Sheets had stains, shower never looked totally clean. This hotel has potential but housekeeping (and the tacky ''my spa" sign which deterred me from even trying the spa) would prevent any future stays. The location is great, but there are a ton of hotels nearby.

Check in=horrid
Service=incompetent 
Location=excellent
I stayed here for a conference. Parking was pricey, the first room I got was occupied, and pool was small and not well kept. If you get a great rate stay here. If you are deciding between two hotels, pick the other one. This is not what you should expect from Hilton.
hotel_name: Doubletree by Hilton Chicago Magnificent Mile

review_title: Had rooms booked here for my family wedding!!
review_text:
Really highclass hotel, great rooms and location, great price, well worth the price
I give this hotel 5 stars. :)
hotel_name: Doubletree by Hilton Chicago Magnificent Mile

review_title: Incredible location, and a historic character.
review_text: I love when I can find a hotel like this to stay in instead of staying at the conference hotel. That way I get a nice walk in at the beginning and end of each long session, and get to stay someplace a little more individual. The room was small, but fun to see how the designer works everything out in tighter quarters. I particularly liked the refillable water bottles and water filters in the hallway, and the mini library in the lobby.
hotel_name: Club Quarters Chicago -- Wacker at Michigan

review_title: Fantastic location, super affordable, and very friendly
review_text: My husband and I stayed here when we combined a visit to family with our anniversary. We aren't people who spend a lot of time in our room, but would like a comfy bed and clean bathroom when we want a break from exploring a city. Club Quarters far exceeded our expectations. The rooms were bigger than expected, the views were great, and the location was more than we could hope for. It was so nice to be in the heart of the city right when we walked out the door. We actually commented on how we felt bad for those spending 4 times as much on a room across the river, when we had the same distance to everything and the same view! In addition, parking was a breeze (and reasonable when parking for 24 hours) and it is convienent to the trains. We will happily stay here again!
hotel_name: Club Quarters Chicago -- Wacker at Michigan

review_text: This was my second stay at CQ, the first time was at the Adams location. Even though this location was a bit pricier, it was worth it for the great location. Though the rooms are small and no frills, ours had a great river view as well as a fridge and microwave. It's very close to a 7/11 , many restaurants and activities. The only reason I gave it four stars is that I found the bed to be uncomfortable and the sheets stiff. It would not deter me from staying here again.
hotel_name: Club Quarters Chicago -- Wacker at Michigan

review_text: I waited 1 hour to check in! There was a large restaurant convention in town, and the hotel front desk was clearly understaffed. I counted 22 people waiting in line ahead of me. The free cookie couldn't take the sour taste out of my mouth.
hotel_name: Doubletree by Hilton Chicago Magnificent Mile

review_text: We were very pleased with the holiday inn midway. The hotel is new or newly remodeled. Clean. Modern. Friendly staff. No complaints.

review_title: Great location and better alternative to the Hyatt
review_text:
Returned after many years. Very contemporary which I don't prefer, but I'm over 50.
Very good value-- but Gold Club is never a good value. Fairmont, you should get rid of that or make it more accessible. I've stayed in 4 Fairmonts and 9 days and I still don't get access.
Despite that, this is amgreatmhotel and it's a superb brand.

I finally registered on Trip Advisor just so I could say how much we liked this hotel. The room was spotless and the location can't be beat. We happened to have a view of the river, Trump Tower*, and the Wrigley and Tribune buildings. (*The Trump Tower, being itself a mirror, provides additional views to the south.) A problem with one of the elevators upon arrival was completely resolved by the time we got back from lunch, and even that wouldn't have mattered if our room hadn't been ready before noon (a nice bonus). Check-in consisted of a credit card swipe.
We never tried the restaurant on the premises but the aromas were good and the place was always packed.
hotel_name: Club Quarters Chicago -- Wacker at Michigan

review_title: Lovely, classy, but room service is ridiculously expensive.
review_text: My daughter and I spent three nights at the Fairmont in August while touring colleges. It's a lovely hotel with traditional features but a very modern lobby and spa area. The location is only a block off Michigan Avenue only a short walk from trendy shops as well as Millenium Park and the museum. Quite a walk from nearest el station, however.

We got transferred here fromthe Central loop location as there had been a flood. The staff were very helpful, sorting a taxi etc to aid in the transfer. 
Once at the Wacker location, check-in was simple and quick and after a slight hiccup with the lift we got to our room overlooking the river. The room was clean and tidy with all the mod cons that you need. The bathroom was compact and clean.
Overall, the location is fabulous and the hotel very good. The laundry was an adventure but a useful bonus as it's free!
hotel_name: Club Quarters Chicago -- Wacker at Michigan

Da para escutar a sirene das ambulancias,com o tempo voce acostuma com o barulho...Pedir comida no quarto e carissimo,cuidado!o pedido de 38 dolares acaba custando 100% mais devido a taxa de entrega.A coca cola sai 5 dolares mais taxa!O buffet do cafe da manha 3 adultos 70 dolares,va ao Corner Bakery Cafe que e na mesma rua,maravilhoso e 1/3 do preco.O Lobby parece uma rodoviaria e qualquer pessoa pode subir no elevadorv e ir para os quartos.O que vale no hotel e a localizacao!

review_title: Small rooms with Old TV and uncomfortable bed.
review_text: The rooms are very small and in top of that they haven put a plasma or HD TV. The bed move because the legs are not very strong. The rooms are not ugly but it will be nice to put a plasma TV.
hotel_name: Hotel Indigo Chicago Downtown Gold Coast

review_text: Good value, good location, relatively quiet. Workout room was excellent. Check in/out was efficient though staff seemed indifferent. About 20 min walk to midst of Miracle Mile. Had trouble getting service at the coffee shop on two occasions, and damage to fire suppression sprinkler in our room 1214 was unsettling.
hotel_name: Hotel Indigo Chicago Downtown Gold Coast

review_title: Great hotel with very nice bathrooms.
review_text: Not sure when they last remodeled this hotel, but they did a very good job. Rooms are quiet and have great features: dimmed lighting, comfy bed, nice shower, etc. Location on Michigan Ave. couldn't be better.

review_title: Quiet, Quaint, Classy, Chic, Romance with a Fireplace
review_text: Room was perfect for our minimoon experience! Loved it. Staff was average to slightly disappointing, but the room was Quiet, Quaint, Classy, Chic, Romance with a Fireplace!
hotel_name: Hotel Indigo Chicago Downtown Gold Coast

review_text:
My wife and I always spend an evening in Chicago to celebrate our anniversary. This year we chose the Blackstone. Very unimpressed. The service was adequate. The front desk clerk never said hello or asked how we were doing upon check-in. It almost seemed as if we caught her right before a break. We asked if our room was a lake view. She said we could upgrade for an extra $40. I suppose the room went un-used for the evening. Would have been nice to get the up- grade, but still had a nice view of the Willis Tower and Harold's Chicken Shack. Was actually quite loud, could here the "L" and emergency vehicles all night. The bed was ok- the pillows were horrible, too big and hard. The room was nothing special. Bathroom ser up kind of strange with slider door and no door on shower. Made for a chilly shower.
Probably will choose somewhere different next time, but I suppose for the price and location it served the purpose.

review_title: The rooms are small and have an old TV.
review_text: The hotel is nice and very clean and staff is very polite, what I didn't like is that if the room is small it should have a nice HD TV: Plasma or LCD. But the TV was very small. The rooms to be hones are NOT very comfortable.
hotel_name: Hotel Indigo Chicago Downtown Gold Coast

review_text: The hotel is a modern victorian classic. It's so chic and the perfect distance to all the fabulous goings on in downtown Chicago. Service was excellent. Workers are attentive and incredibly helpful. Loved the atmosphere and will go back!

This hotel is the most beautiful I have ever stayed in from the rooms to the elevators. We had a room on the 19th floor and a great view of the Sears Tower from our room. It is right near Soldier Field and close enough to downtown that you can walk most places but a cab is relatively inexpensive if you decide to do that. The rooms were a little on the pricey side but it is a great splurge.

review_title: Not the most family or Hotwire friendly hotel.
review_text:
My family stayed at the Indigo from 7/12-7/14. We got a fairly good deal through Hotwire, but realized that the deal was not as good upon check-in. Be aware that they will charge $30/night extra for a room with 2 double beds. Parking is $36 per night, but this is to be expected as the location is in the city.
Another note- if you have young children and they like to take baths, that is not possible here as there is only a shower in the bathroom.
Beds were comfortable and the Aveda products in the room was a nice touch. 
Location was good, with easy access to the subway station, Michigan Ave, etc.
Overall, i would probably not recommend this hotel if you have small children. Might be nice if you are looking to explore the nightlife and vast amount of shopping that the area has to offer.
hotel_name: Hotel Indigo Chicago Downtown Gold Coast

review_text: I have stayed here twice, both for the Rock and Roll half marathon in August... Could not ask for a better location so close to the start/finish line and all race activities The staff is very friendly and always helpful. Rooms are clean with decor that tips it's hat to a by gone era, but with modern amenities. Highly recommend!

review_title: Bellissimo soggiorno con vista mozzafiato su Chicago
review_text:
Una bellissima struttura, con una posizione molto centrale e con una vista sul fiume semplicemente straordinaria. 
Le camere sono spaziose, molto pulite e dotate di tutti i comfort. La connessione wi-fi e' veloce e performante.
La colazione viene servita al ristorante Italiasia, giu' nella lobby, ed e' principalmente "americana", con ampia scelta di uova, bacon, pancakes, french toast e muffin di ogni genere. 
Eccellente, e decisamente in linea con i prezzi.

Had booked on Priceline. Traveled with a colleague and needed two beds. That costs extra money here, making the Hotel a rather average deal, and unexpectedly pushing your price up when you have no option. Try your luck elsewhere if two adults not keen on sharing the same quite small queens bed travel together.
hotel_name: Hotel Indigo Chicago Downtown Gold Coast

review_text: As per regular Westin standard. Late night menu is very limited though, if end up checking in late.

review_title: Lives up to expected Westin standard
review_text:
I stayed at the Westin River North two nights in early September.
The main reason you choose a Westin is the heavenly bed, at least for me. And the name isn't preposterous: You just don't want to get up out of it!
The rooms are nice, I didn't have mich of a view but still: the rooms are nice, clean and are spacious enough. The bathroom didn't knock me out, it was ok.
Nice touch were the really friendly and patient concierge staff. They really helped a lot and gave great tips for sight seeing and Chicago-style eats.
Location is fine, but you do have to walk somewhat to get to anyplace of consequence. The only place right around the corner is the river, great for picture-memories.

review_title: A very hip hotel with friendly staff
review_text: We stayed for 3 nights recently and loved it! Beautiful refurb of old Ambassador hotel. Or room was by (a deluxe) with ok size bathroom. It is 'affordable' so lacked a few luxuries - shower cap, bathrobes, proper hairdryer, umbrellas... But we didn't mind so much. Breakfast in the Pumphouse was good and there's also a pastry/ coffee bar just off the lobby. It was absolutely mobbed on Fri and Sat night and v loud in the bar, restaurant and lobby - but we weren't disturbed by this up on the 12th floor ( room had great views too!). We've stayed at Sofitel Warer Tower before which is more expensive but not as nice! We'll be back at The Public again.

Stayed here six nights for a meeting. 
The hotel is nicely located on the river and has beautiful views over the river. We changed rooms to one with a view and it was more than worth it. After a hard days work we started our night with a drink looking over Chicago's loop.
Upgrade to executive club was partially worth the money. Breakfast was okay but wireless in room was hopeless. We had to sit in front of out door to get any reception. 
The room was nicely decorated but my wife's favorite are the heavenly beds. 
Worth mentioning is Westin's gym and especially it's manager, Sam Guiragossian! I find a good gym important in my travels. His is one of the best I worked out. Not particullary because of the state of the art equipment, but most of all because of Sam himself.
He gave me some excellent advice and worked with me three days and made a tailored program to achieve my goals. He even follows up on my progress. 
All in all we spent a perfect week in Chicago and the Westin made it even better

review_title: Slow Wifi, rude awakenings, and no bathtub
review_text: This hotel is historic, beautiful, and centrally located, but it's lacking in some basic services. Wifi is too slow for citrix or video streaming. I tried calling the front desk twice, and they referred me to the wireless company's hotline in Korea, but to no avail. Also, I didn't expect to have to put on the "do not disturb" sign if Im leaving at 9:30AM, but I should have. Housekeeping woke me up at 8:30, and a phoney "room service" slamming on the door woke me up at 9, and I didn't order anything. I think they just wanted me out. Just a side note, my room had no bathtub, which is important to me. Overall, I've had more pleasant and comfortable stays at the Holiday Inn, for 1/3 the cost.

I'm a soccer mom from the suburbs and I have to say that I found the chicness of this hotel a little intimidating. The crowd on Friday and Saturday nights was very young and well dressed...I felt a little frumpy. However, I was treated very well. The staff was very courteous and helpful. The rooms were small but had everything I needed. My only complaint is that the rooms were not soundproof. I could here my neighbors loud and clear. It's a great hotel...give it a try!

review_title: It was a very nice experience
review_text:
They updated the work out room and it was great. They have a trainer who I worked out with for a full hour at no charge! He was really good! 
The only thing I didn't like was room service food, but the food in the restaurant was really good.

I have stayed here once before and was not disappointed either time. This hotel is beautiful, every bit if it. The bar is elegant as well. The location is great. It's hard to write a review, except to say you will not be disappointed.

A colleague recommended this hotel because of it's proximity to major sites and to millennium park. I really do not have any complaints about the hotel. I really liked that we were able to take the train to ohare airport for $2.25! Give yourself 40 minutes for this ride.

review_text: We had a wonderful stay! The Westin Workout was our favorite part. The free personal training was top notch.
We stayed here for a wedding and would have stayed longer. Rooms are spacious, beds are comfy and clean. Ask for a room with a view of the river. Fun place to stay in chicago!
Enjoyed a great stay recently. Was upgraded as a Platinum to a great room. Had a great workout in the gym with the very friendly Westin Workout manager Sam providing assistance.
Great service, great location. Very friendly and helpful staff.

review_title: Walk to everything from this wonderful hotel with an amazing staff.
review_text: Stayed here for the NRA convention May 20-24. The hotel is in the middle of all you want to see, eat and do. The rooms are nicely appointed and cleanliness and service are at the top of this Westin's priority list. I must mention a few staff members that went above and beyond to make our stay so wonderful. Diana at the executive lounge, Diane at the concierge desk, Keith, David, and really all of the front door staff were fantastic. However, Alan the bellman really stole the show, making us feel so welcome and taken care of. His passion for his job and for people really shines through. I commend Westin for employing such exceptional staff members and for their outstanding hotel. This was our first trip to Chicago, it will not be our last and we will never stay anywhere but here.
Our stay was perfert for our St Patricks Day girls weekend. Walking distance to most everything we needed. Loved the view & location.

This hote is noisy with paper thin walls. Don't plan on sleeping if your neighbors are watching television.
It's too bad- the beds are great with luxurious down quilts and feather pillows and noise from every direction.
Good location-near Michigan Avenue and shopping.

review_text: What a great surprise this hotel was. The staff were nice and professional the suite that we stayed in was furnished with everything we could need or want. The housekeeping was mostly good, a few missed cleaning spots, nothing big though. Our only complaint is the "king" bed was two twin beds put together, very uncomfortable. All in all and wonderful three night stay!
hotel_name: Club Quarters Chicago -- Wacker at Michigan

review_text: This was simply a great place to stay. My room was spotless, comfortable, stylish, well appointed and...the endless, free purified bottled water is a sweet touch. Italian restaurant in lobby good. Location can't be beat. I'll be back.
hotel_name: Club Quarters Chicago -- Wacker at Michigan

review_text: This hotel was very small and the rooms were painfully small. The bed had to be pushed all the way against one wall and you could barely turn around in the bathroom. BUT, the location was excellent, there was unlimited, free bottled water, and the rooms were clean. If all you want is a place to sleep in a great location, the price here is right. Also, the pizza place downstairs, Bella Baccino's, is my very favorite. It was kind of a nice coincidence that it shared a building with this hotel.
hotel_name: Club Quarters Chicago -- Wacker at Michigan

review_text: Very happy with our stay. Nice place. Left car in lot for 8 days, no worries. Not cheap, but good lodging & safe parking

This hotel offers a great location close to shopping and sight seeing. You have Navy Pier .7 miles away and In the other direction you have shopping, the Hancock building, and House of blues is .65 miles in the other direction. you can walk to everything.
hotel_name: Doubletree by Hilton Chicago Magnificent Mile

review_text: My main message is two days without hot water in the sink. One day I can forget, but not 2. Otherwise the room was nice, with a good view of the lake. The room wad loud. That can be the luck of the draw, but a better hotel offers better noise insulation. The location of the elevators is odd and poorly marked. I'm not a fan of the constant drum beat music in public areas, but some people think that's cool.

review_text:

I went to get my room changed and was moved to a higher floor but a smaller room and equally as noisy. I asked to be changes to one of the quieter rooms and was told they were oversold. They still charged me full price for my downgraded room and offered no other concessions. 
I'd recommend the James any day over this hotel

review_text: Moderno hotel, bien ubicado, un poco mas econÃ³mico seria formidable!

review_title: Always a fun place to stay
review_text: My girlfriend and I stay at a lot of hotels, particularly Starwood. Whenever we come here, there is never a problem getting upgraded to the e wow suite (which is more of a homier layout than the on on lakeshore). The service is always great, the front desk is super friendly, and I have never had a problem with noise complaints (we have our friends come and hang out with us to pregame before going out). One of my favorite W hotels

This is our second stay at a W, and the thing we are beginning to see and appreciate about them is the uniqueness of the properties but the consistency of the level of service. It is a fun atmosphere but we were on the 10th floor in a courtyard room so the noise was no issue (beyond the L which you would hear anywhere inside the loop.) The rooms are small, but sufficient for the 2 of us. The complimentary hot chocolate is magnificent. All in all, the W was a great beginning and ending to every day on our vacation. Great service and a great facility.

Arrivati in hotel sarete accolti dalle storiche foto dei presidenti che qui hanno alloggiato e del governatore dell'Illinois, Barak Obama, che eletto presidente, tenne nelle sale di questo hotel il suo primo discorso post elezione. review_title: Great hotel in the financial district
review_text:
The w is located right off the el train so there is some noise, I am not the heaviest sleeper but I did not have a problem sleeping. The staff is great and they have partnered with Acura so there are free rides around the city if pre-arranged. 
Overall a great hotel!

review_title: WOW! Great stay. Solid value. wonderful location.
review_text: Wonderful stay. We had five rooms for family event, every room was spacious and quiet. Really enjoyed the service, very attentive and helpful, from front desk to concierges. The location was perfect for walking to Michigan Ave, 10 Pin, Willis (Sears Tower), restaurants (Lou Mitchels for breakfast!), Amtrak and CTA. Good room rates too. Ample towels, Bliss bath products, quiet heater (kinda cold in Chicago, free hot chocolate and gourmet cookies in lobby. We also liked livingroom lobby/bar for adult relaxation after kids were asleep. Thank you for great stay. Valet is pricey, might find lower rate at Sears tower but not sure. We will go back when visiting Chicago!

Great location on Michigan avenue, yet old and tired. Heat in room is so loud, hard to sleep. Needs a Shot in the arm. The staff is good though!

Very hip hotel. As you enter you feel like you are walking into a club. The place is very dim and the bar seems very busy. You have to walk passed all the people in order to reach the front desk. The rooms are contemporary feel. The valet overnight was overly priced at about $69/night, but all the valets in downtown chicago are outrageously priced. The location is a walkable distance.

Great location but rooms in need of an update as they are a little dated overall. However, bed very comfortable and tv was brand new.
Any requests to front desk where dealt with well. Bathroom a little small, not much room for two.
$15 for 24 hours wifi is steep. 
If i got a good rate, would defo stay here again.

Overall the intercontinental hotel in Chicago was very enjoyable. This is a great place to stay and the location was great. 
There is so much close by and being in the heart of downtown really helps. 
The only issues I had were. 
Paying for Internet. Seriously does anyone pay for Internet? I'm a priority club platinum member and I shouldn't have to pay for that. I can stay at other IHG hotels and not pay. 
Service - it was seriously average but with so much going on I can't really fault service but they didn't do anything to wow me. 
Value - the price was overwhelmingly expensive. I probably could have stayed at a different IHG property and paid less. I paid less at the intercontinental in new york.

review_title: Pricey but overall a good value
review_text: Good location, clean but dated. Very pricey and limited room service menu. Parking can handle a hi-top van. Noisy lobby, quiet rooms. Expect 500 a day all in.

review_title: An excellent and historic hotel in a great location
review_text:
This is a great hotel in a superb location. My room was difficult to fault and I slept well. I enjoyed breakfast and the bar. The health club and especially the pool are absolutely awesome!
I would recommend this hotel.
Small rooms, typical of the old building type. Great location. Uncomfortable bed & desk.

Very nice hotel-excellent service. Use the concierge-they are knowlegeable about the area and give great directionsm. Rooms are nice (we stayed in a 'spectacular' room. Walls are thin. It was in a great location for first time visit to chicago. We may have been expecting a little more to the room for the $.

review_title: Small room, but overall stay okay
review_text:
We stayed at the W City Center for the first time to attend a friend's wedding nearby over Labor Day weekend. The rate was great ($160/night), and with the hotels.com free night, we ended up getting a great deal. Even if we had to pay full price, the W would have been fine, given how economical the price was. 
The room was pretty clean, but the size was just too small - even for two people used to city living and close quarters. I would say the room was comfortably no larger than 12' by 10 or 11'. The bathroom was absolutely tiny, but the real inconvenience was the lack of sink or shelf space for toiletries, etc. Bliss products were great. The water pressure was fairly weak though.
My fiancÃ© (a fairly light sleeper) turned up the AC to create background noise that he hoped would drown out the subway train noise coming from not too far away. The W hotel brand in general caters to younger, trendy travelers, so the lobby that pounded Euro/techno music was no surprise. Still, it's not for everyone. 
The location is not ideal for the average Chicago tourist who wants to walk around the Mag Mile and Gold Coast areas and venture north. If we were not bound to the wedding and had options to stay elsewhere, I would have preferred the Park Hyatt or the Peninsula, which are my two favorite hotels in Chicago. The W is fine for a short stay if you are okay with cramped spaces and noise issues.

My stay in Chicago was wonderful, and the staff @ the W was definitely part of it. Especially Laurelin Hefter making me feel comfortable with a capital C. 
Thx,
Paul Nazari

Room- this was a standard Marriott hotel. Room was clean. Bathroom was spacious. 
Location- it was right by Midway Airport. It was in like a parking lot full of other hotels. There was a TGI Fridays in the lot. I didn't see much else within walking distance. My husband ate at the restaurant for breakfast and thought it was average. 
We stayed here for a wedding due to the location near the reception. If I come to Chicago as a tourist, I would stay downtown versus here.

A fun place to stay, but by day three we were sick of the hot pink lighting, club music, and disco lights! This place makes you feel like you're in an episode of "sex in the city!" The holograms in the elevators made us motion sick every time! Very attentive staff and friendly service. Quiet room with large TV.

I have come here for the last 4 years for 5 to 7 days for business. I am an Ambassador member and have always been upgraded. The last time, when I came for a night with my wife, I was upgraded but to a smaller room than earlier. I was thinking that perhaps it's time for a change but when I went down in the morning to tell the desk I was leaving the staff member at guest relations, closed her eyes, remembered my name and asked if I had a good stay. I told myself then and there I would come back.
I am glad I did, the check in was smooth less and while they did not have my upgrade in the system, when I told them I was ambassador, and here for 5 days, they efficiently and without fuss moved some reservations around without inconveniencing anyone and gave me a very nice suite for my stay (I am still here).
The new Michael Jordan restaurant is quite nice (I never ate in the hotel before) and the concierge last night gave us a wonderful recommendation for dinner.
I have read some people say the staff is unfriendly, I cannot disagree more - from bellman, to doorman to chambermaid it has been a wonderful experience.
I will be back!

review_title: Very modern and upscale place to stay.
review_text: We stayed in this hotel and it was marvelous. When I walked in I thought I was in an upscale lounge. I had to wait for my husband, so I relaxed upstairs on the second floor overlooking the entrance. The couches were plush, clean and extremely comfortable. After we checked in, the bed we so cozy I didn't want to get up, but we were in Chicago, so we had to explore. The night before check out, the concierge printed our plane tickets and had them waiting for us in an envelope at the desk. They also had the best cucumber water I have ever tasted!

review_title: Three star hotel with a 5 star location.
review_text: Great location on Michigan avenue. Hotel was as I expected based on the reviews I read from tripadvisor. The rooms are small. Too small. I think most people have grown accustom to larger rooms at any price level. Where the room disappoints there is nothing else about this hotel that wins you back. I should have stayed at ANY other hotel. I had friends who stayed one night at the inter and two more y the embassy suites nearby. Embassy was nicer.

Having stayed here before and having had a positive experience, I convinced my mom and grandmother to pay the extra money to stay in luxury.
The rooms are very small and a little old - but that's okay. The lobby, pool, and bar are beautiful and the staff is very pleasant.
What wasn't okay: my mom on her second night realized she hadn't done her normal hotel bed bug check (of course no bed bugs) and upon lifting up the mattress found a pair of men's dirty boxers. This is obviously disgusting. Maybe the cleaning crew got lazy or maybe this was just a once off - either way when she told the front desk about it their response was unacceptable. First they offered to give her a free upgrade upon her next stay at the Intercontinental Chicago (only) if they had an open rooms. After forty five minutes of complaining they agreed to take 25% off one of the two nights from her current stay.
I would probably still stay here again myself but I wouldn't recommend it to others - Id send them across the street to the Conrad instead.

This was my first time staying at a W hotel. If you haven't stayed in one before, I highly suggest! This place makes you feel like you're the only person that matters, they aim high to please and try to use your name whenever possible. Everyone at this hotel is exceptional. From check-in, bell boys, housekeeping, and concierge-they all impacted my stay. This is by far the nicest hotel that i have stayed at. Note that I a platinum at Marriott but chose the W Instead. The place is hip and trendy. As for the view, they have done the best they can with the space. I can't wait to stay at the W again!

Let me just say, I loved the bed, but maybe we didn't stay in the right room. I requested a higher floor and best view, but I guess there isn't a really good view at this location. The room was very nice but I couldn't understand the very small bathroom? Other than that, I really don't have any complaints. The staff was top-notch!

review_title: The W did everything they could to accommodate my family although their focus was business. My children felt special the entire
review_text: Laurelin assisted us with tickets, tours, reservations, and special treats for my kids. She was awesome, organized, energetic, and efficient! I suggested using the W concierge!

Stayed here 3x over the past three months. I travel a lot and my wife joins me when she can. Great location for shopping at Michigan Ave and State St. Short walk to Mellinium Park and right next door to the theaters. I love the location of this hotel. The food at the bar downstairs is excellent. 
Housekeeping and their supervisors can use some improvement. I had one really bad experience during one of my stays - the bed was made but the refrigerator had left over pizza, cereal on the floor, and to top it all an expensive Nikon SLR camera beside the television. How can these be missed?
I called for the manager who moved us to a different room. Manager was apologetic and gave me 2000 Marriott points. The damage was already done. My wife and I didn't feel comfortable during that stay. I really liked this hotel but will now consider other hotels in the area. I'm still not over that experience that's why I'm writing this review.

We stayed here on a Friday night before seeing a Saturday matinee at the Chicago Theatre which is literally kitty-corner from the hotel. Our room, 2504, was extra spacious and had a suite-like feel: king bed, sofa, desk, two floor-to-ceiling windows with partial views of the Lake, as well as a large bathroom with Aveda amenities. Swift elevators with short wait times. Very large lobby with plenty of seating areas. $129 rate which was excellent for a holiday season Friday.
Go the room through Priceline. Staff was pleasant. The room was small. Space for only one person to walk between bed and tv.

review_title: Non-smoking room didn't smell, feel or look like a non-smoking room!
review_text: When I arrived at the hotel, I was very pleased with the location. The lobby was filled with people; mostly what appeared to be a Virgin Atlantic convention. I was in line to check in and as my turn approached, the representative apologized and directed me to wait again for another representative because he was helping the large group. My initial thought was that it seemed a bit disorganized, but ok I will wait again. When I checked in, I requested a non-smoking room on a lower floor and 33 was the best they could do. Okay, off to the 33rd floor. When I got to my room, it seemed okay at first; however, the longer I was in it, the more I recognized the smoke. When I called the front desk, they apologized and said they were booked. I also told them again at check out. Their response was to write the room number on a piece of paper and that was it. No apologies, offers for a free cup of coffee...nothing. Very disappointing. From the outside looking in it was a great hotel; once inside the "non-smoking" room, not so much!

the HOTEL SAX is not a 4 star property IMHO, but it is hip and fun and clean... with friendly staff, good foodstuffs, superior location, comfortable beds... easy to like, especially if you enjoy the (in-house) HOUSE OF BLUES.

This was my second time here. The past time I was upgraded to a suite on the front of the building overlooking the river. It was fabulous. This time I got a regular room facing another building (I am a platinum member). The first night my door wouldn't work. After sending me up and down with 3 different keys they send a security guard. 2 hours later they opened the door and moved me. Upgraded me to a suite but it was on the corner of the building where the T runs, every 15 minutes from 5:00 am to midnight. It was so loud. The lounge was very nice. Had lots of choices. Lots of restaurants close by.

review_title: Good location, friendly staff. Enjoyable on the whole however read incident below.
review_text:
Good location at one end of michigan mile. Was there for a conference and concierge were helpful. Room was adequate. Had to pay for internet.
Had one unfortunate incident where my partner and cousin whilst sitting at the bar were abused by a drunken man, when I asked the barman to remove him, nothing happened and I needed to remove him myself....no apology was given, unusual to see no security present or available???

review_title: Dont sound ur money there, really not worth it trust me!
review_text:
Hello,
My thoughts on the W city center is basically that up to now it is the worst W hotel I've ever stayed at. Thank god we didn't spend much time in the room because really the more I was in there the worst I felt about having paid so much for that kind of quality. One comment would be to redo ur bathtubs! The room we stayed in #1222 had a shipped bath tub I really didn't feel food about showering in there. Another complaint is that there was no complimentary coffee in the room. This is the first time I go to a hotel and no coffee or tea is offered in the room. Then we went to the gym and half the machines were out of order and the rest of them were being used so we couldn't do our workout. Finally when we came back from shopping on saturday our room wasnt even made we had to call front desk to request to house keeper to come.Â So my complaints aren't about the staff they are more about the quality of the hotel. Knowing the W hotel reputation and having stayed at the W in Montreal and in new York I expected a certain level of quality but didn't get that at all... Im really disappointed but thank god for Chicago being such an extraordinary city cause we still enjoyed our week-end. Just couldn't wait to leave the hotel. We will definitely not risk it again.

review_title: Nice place, comment about walls are true....
review_text: We booked this hotel on priceline for two nights at a very good rate for downtown. Room was small, but ok for the two of two us. Bed was OK. Not great, but ok. Only complaint were the walls. Had a noisy room next to us on Saturday night from around 1:30-3:30. Could here every single action for 2 hours straight! Kinda ruined a night of sleep. Otherwise, Location was good. Walking distance to Michigan Ave and several restaurants/clubs. House of Blues. Would stay here again.

review_title: A good hotel, reasonable prices and lots around within a few blocks.
review_text: I stayed here for work for 2 nights in October and thoroughly enjoyed my stay. The check in was a breeze, the rooms were clean, the service was nice and the meetings space was well appointed. There are plenty of food choices either in the hotel or nearby, and as with Chicago, for less than a $10 can ride you can be to almost anything.

After reading a few negative reviews on trip advisor, I was a little cautious in coming here. From the second I stepped up to the hotel, I was greeted with amazing service from the doormen to the front desk. This uniquely charming hotel really wowed me in every aspect. The service was impeccable and the rooms were completely renovated with a modern flair. The location couldn't be better with it just being steps away from Michigan ave. my daughter and I had the best time looking at all of the recently installed Christmas lights, and being only a few blocks from American girl store. I highly recommend this hotel for their location, charming interior, and the best staff I have ever encountered.

Spent three nights at the Miilenium Knickerbocker and my review is :
Pro:
Nice location
Clean
Con:
Central heat/cool not able to control in room but dictated by central air system and outdoor temp
Couldn't get coffee before restaurant opened in morning.
Overall, average experience but the heating/air system for hotel worth a call to check out before you spend your money there.

Laurelin Hefter and Vanessa Lopez are excellent concierge staff, and work very hard to accommodate your needs during your stay. 
The gym at this property is woefully inadequate, bur Laurelin and Vanessa were able to establish a relationship with a gym across the street to provide me with a negotiated day rate. This gym was *much* better.
This property is good overall, but Laurelin and Vanessa are extremely responsive and attentive. I'll certainly stay here again.

review_title: Nice hotel, but what was going on in the lobby?
review_text: The hotel itself is excellent. Beautiful rooms with the normally overpriced amenities. The lobby area is trendy but it looks like the red light district down there. Something about women in there twenties hanging over men in there fifties just doesn't look right. Maybe I just don't know the city that well.

I was a little surprised to see that this hotel does not accept Marriott points for our stay. It was expensive fir what you get but overall a nice stay. I can't say that anything other than the location stuck out.
This was a nice hotel overall but the decor is a bit weird. Large rooms, right by the river.
We stayed after receiving this hotel via priceline. A great unique property with highly attentive staff! They bent over backwards to help us in every way.

review_title: Well-Appointed & in the heart of the city
review_text: Great place & unbeatable location. Harry Caray's right next door, House of Blues across the street, walking distance to everything. Great in-room amenities and fantastic vibes from the lounge areas.

Overall I can't complain about this hotel. The room was a bit small and the sink was in the room not in the bathroom which I didn't like. The bed was very comfie and the tv was large. There are great restaurants downstairs for all prices and tastes. This is about five minutes from millennium park and very close to the theatre district and the magnificent mile. Great location and good value overall.

Great location, friendly staff (with the exception of the valet over the phone) and trendy decor. Convent android application to communicate with staff. Overall an average quality hotel with modern decor. Very pleasant.

review_title: Great location and beds but what a terrible elevator!
review_text:
Some of the previous reviews are correct.
1-great location-its next to everything
2-big comfy beds but perhaps too big for the room size
3-worth it? Hmmmm well maybe for a groupon or priceline deal
4-cost of food. Probably not worth it but I thought breakfast was good. It's in the heart of the city by the lake so the price reflects what other better places charge. 
Other stuff-
FYI my partial lake view rooms translated into a view between two brick buildings which nearly abut the window, so do not pay up for that feature.
Lastly and most importantly their elevator is terrible. I doubt that can be fixed. 
Overall I recommend this place but not the elevator or the "partial lake" (mostly brick building) view
Spent the weekend inChicago with friends and loved hotel. Located right on mag mile and walking distance to many locations.

We decided to take a last-minute trip for Thanksgiving, and wanted to be comfortable for our family of 5 without spending too much. With the suites, free breakfast, and manager's reception (free drinks!) nightly this place covered it all. 
The location is perfect--walking distance to shopping, restaurants, and Navy Pier and one block from the subway for a quick ride to the museums. We packed a ton into 3 days. Highly recommend the city pass if planning to visit museums and attractions.
Don't hesitate to stay here. Very clean, newer rooms. Part of the reason we chose to stay here was for the pool, but we never used it. It looked pretty small, but I didn't expect much more.
Staff was extremely friendly, room was clean and had a beautiful river view!

review_title: Very upset by service and amenities
review_text: As a platinum Marriott traveller, I was surprised by the lackluster service I received from the staff at this location. Normally, I love Marriott and their service; however, in this case I was less than impressed by the level of service I received. Normally, as a platinum member I would expect extra amenities from a hotel I spend an exorbitant amount of money with...but after a long discussion with the front desk...I will keep my standard room (which is fine)...but will pay for parking and receive no additional breakfast or any other amenities. For my money and amount of travel time I'll choose Hilton because they treat me better. The renaissance is fine if you only need a room and don't care about customer service...otherwise don't bother!

Despite mixed reviews on this site, my stay here has been wonderful. The staff is courteous and helpful. Rooms are small but lovely. Meeting rooms were great and Internet was complimentary for our group. 
Arrived mid- morning, asked for early check in and a room with a view and was graciously given both!
Very good price Rooms were very clean and bed was comfortable. Close to michigan avenue (magnificent mile shops and restaurants). Would definitely stay here again.
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton Chicago Downtown / Magnificent Mile

review_text: Everyone was extremely helpful. Laurelin Hefter, at guest services, recommended an amazing restaurant (The Custom House) and even got an earlier reservation at our convenience. Highly recommended!

Four Points was a great choice to stay in Chicago. It is literally in the middle of everything, Michigan Ave, State St. And of course Rush St. The rooms were nice, considering the price per night, I expected a little more, but the staff, service, and location made up for it. The best part was after we checked out; they allowed us to keep our car in the parking garage until 6pm. With this extra time, we got in a little extra shopping before we left. We definitely be back when we stay in Chicago again
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton Chicago Downtown / Magnificent Mile

review_text: The location was awesome, but the service was horrible! If you are booking from Hotel Tonight app I'd stay at the Talbot Hotel! Really nice, cheaper, and everyone was so nice there! Also if you check in on Facebook at Sax twice don't bother with the "free upgrade" they just moved us to an identical room but it had a mini bar so you could pay them more money for snacks!

We booked a king room in the Historic Tower and were placed in a room with no windows, which I thought was weird. Room was on the 9th floor and at around 7pm there was a party in one of the ballrooms below are room and it sounded like the band was in our room. We could here every word of every song and this went on until 11:30pm. Called front desk and said there was nothing they could do. Did give us 25% off stay. Wouldn't expect a noise problem in a 5 start hotel. Not worth the money. Have had much better stays at cheaper downtown hotels.
Everything was clean and nice and in a great location.

review_title: Large room, attentive service and extremely quiet
review_text: We just returned from a Chicago weekend - a parent's escape from our children. The hotel location was fabulous with easy access to the L and sights. The room was clean and larger than some of the hotels we have stayed at in the city. I usually don't sleep well in hotels, but the room was so quiet, I slept solidly. The pool and exercise areas were fantastic with a spa-like feeling. We only ate at the Novo Bar once and found their small plates were reasonably priced. The nachos were a bit bland, but they were still a nice option for a light dinner. Overall, the hotel was great and we'd definitely return.

Realizing that the average person staying at this hotel may know what to do, it was confusing to us. There was a concert at the House of Blues next door, so right from the start, we didn't know where to go for the valet parking. The parking is EXTREMELY overpriced, $52/night. Are you supposed to tip everyone who helps you? I felt a little like fresh roadkill rather than someone trying to check into a hotel.
When we got to the rooms, it was a little disappointing. Everything looked like it came straight from a 70's yardsale..not belonging in a 4 star hotel. Honestly, I've seen MUCH nicer Holiday Inn Express rooms...at least we would have had a little fridge to put some drinks/snacks in. No coffee maker! That was a huge lacking element...guess they want to do that for you too. 
Overpriced. Not worth it at all!!

You won't regret. Exceent location, one block from the theatre district and in front of the riverwalk and the Trump Tower. Not on the MagMile but just a few minutes walk away. Very good size of the rooms. Nice lobby. Efffective (but not very friendly) staff. Very confortable beds. Relatively good price. We have a riverfront view room and the view was indeed very good. All in all we definatelly recommend and we would stay here again.

review_title: Magnificent hotel on the Magnificent mile!
review_text: The hotel is in a great location with numerous choices of places to shop and eat. The hotel staff members are excellent, friendly, and knowledgeable. The hotel is clean, and my room was perfect. There was a coffee maker, microwave, and mini refrigerator, and free bottled water.
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton Chicago Downtown / Magnificent Mile

review_text: This hotel at the tip of the Magnificent Mile had a great location, fantastic decor, and service to match! The rooms were smaller than most, but it was part of its historic charm. The concierge was knowledgeable and friendly to this first time Chicago visitor.

We stayed here for a girls weekend and thought it was very modern, hip, and chic. Check in was easy however parking is pricey at 52$. The room was decorated in what I can only describe as retro-chic but it was cool. The bathroom was roomy and the beds were very springy. In the lobby of the hotel is the Crimson Lounge wich plays new music and gets pretty busy during after hours club time. If you are registered at the hotel you can get in free. It was a good stay, but I would try something new before I went back.
I've stayed here on 2 separate occasions, with a large group both times. The rooms are very comfortable and clean, the location is fabulous, and the staff are beyond fabulous!
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton Chicago Downtown / Magnificent Mile

review_text: I am very impressed that an entire hotel is all two room suites. It's rare that u get this much room to spread out, relax and enjoy a hotel. The room was spotless. The front desk service was perfect. I am only here overnight so wont have any experience with the cleaning staff. Very central location only 2 blocks off Michigan near the river. Loads of shops and restaurants within a couple blocks. Great place. I will stay here again.

I would say this is a 3.5 star hotel. They remodeled the rooms nicely but it had a little bit of a musty smell and the elevators showed age. We got a decent deal via priceline and the location is good, although a bit of a hike to Navy Pier. Super close to the Cheesecake Factory though! Bed and pillows were awesome. We slept really well. Rain shower was neat but not practical. Perfect for a hotel! The hand wand can be on while the rain shower is on. Super stocked minibar. We did the valet parking because traffic was insane and we didn't see the self-park (it is on the other side of Michigan). In hindsight we would have parked the car ourselves to save the $. If you do the valet parking don't feel rushed because if you forget something, getting it out is a hassle because they park them a few blocks away. So overall we were satisfied with this hotel as a home base to explore Chicago. If you really like new places, try somewhere else.

The hotel is in a great location. Walking distance to many sights, as well as most trains. Decor can be a bit spare in the rooms, as the space seems a little to big for the objects that fill it. Otherwise, a good stay overall.

review_title: Very great hotel in value, location and quality.
review_text: I stayed for 4 days over a long weekend in this very well maintained hotel and was very happy with it. The location is close to everything downtown/the loop/the river/the magnificent mile etc. The hotel staff were quite friendly and accomodated us to our room even tho we arrived at 9am (official check in is normally at 3pm). The room on the 15th floor was very clean, pleasant, comfy and had a great view. Mini bar items looked expensive but mostly same cost as buying something at a lounge. Did not try the lounge or the restraunt below so dunno abt them. I did use the room service which came promptly and was good food too.

review_title: The Hotel Sax offers a great new trendy brand of hotels and yet still provides you with the comfort of being at home.
review_text: I've had the luxury of staying at 4 or 5 of the Thompson hotels & all of them have their own unique style. They all are in great locations that help for you tour the most popular areas of the prospective cities.

We stayed here while in Chicago for a music festival. We booked very early as most hotel room prices were $ with the big festival happening. Not a luxourious hotel by any means but perfect if your looking for a comfortable and practical stay. It's very close to restaurants (2 amazing deep dish places- giordanos and UNO) and right off the famous Magnificant Mile strip. It's an affordable, practical choice if you're staying in Chicago on a budget! My only problem: waiting a long time for guest services to bring up towels/extra soap.
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton Chicago Downtown / Magnificent Mile

review_text: Can't wait to come back. Great location and close to L. Will bring wife next time.
Excellent service and very friendly staff, worth the price! Location is perfect; having Trader Joes and Starbucks next door is convenient. Rooms are clean, I like this hotel!
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton Chicago Downtown / Magnificent Mile

review_title: awful, smelly, rude staff, 2 star dressed up....
review_text: stayd there july 22nd... room was smelly and outdated with a few new add-ons....room was small as hell.....no pool...$53 to park and they took forever to retrieve the car.......we had a bill of 250 left under our door for a weed smell??!!! which was false and obsurd!!! the whole hotel smelled of b.o( body odor) and gym socks...my hubby went the fu** off on them..pack our belongings and we checkd out.....so that foul odor was.ur hotel and.lack of.cleaning....stayd at avenue crown plaza on huron and luvd it...dont stay here the smell is dreadful and the staff are lying, under achiever, minimum wage working a*s pple( rude fu**s)...yes im still pissed

review_title: You will like it! It have all you need.
review_text: I really like this hotel, nice rooms, plasma TV, refrigerator, microwave, Gym, pool, big rooms... All you need.
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton Chicago Downtown / Magnificent Mile

review_title: Perfect for a family in a very convenient location
review_text:
Despite a very tedious check in wait on arrival, the service and staff since then have been fantastic. The rooms are great for a family being clean and spacious. The children have thoroughly enjoyed the complimentary breakfasts, trying everything from the freshly cooked omlettes to the make your own waffles. My husband and I have also appreciated the complimentary drink and nibbles in the early evening. The hotel is very centrally located for shopping and transport links. I would recommend a high room away from the lifts to minimise on noise from the atrium.
The pool is adequate if a little chilly and there is no changing room so you are required to traipse back to your room in your costume and towel.
During our stay there was free Internet access which I understand is a summer special offer but this is extremely helpful. 
Overall great value for money and highly recommended. The staff are all delightful and happy to help.
Stayed at the Knickerbocker for a convention. The staff was great, it's close to everything, had a great experience.

This is one of my favorite hotels downtown. It is in a great location, one block from tons of shopping on Michigan Ave, attached to a Starbucks, etc. They had a free business center, free gym, and a free pool. The rooms were spacious and Very clean. I will stay here again!
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton Chicago Downtown / Magnificent Mile

review_text: Stayed for a week at the end of June. Location of hotel is excellent, just off the 'magnificent mile' of Michigan avenue, right near the John Hancock building. Facilities were excellent and house keeping staff were very good. For two people the room would be excellent, though probably the only let down was the lack of free wi-fi for a fairly expensive hotel. The small fitness centre was modern and a bonus. The hotel is very nice

Just checked out of this hotel after a 3 night break. Lovely welcome when we arrived and we had a double comfy room which was large and well equipped. Large flat screen TV, a good hairdryer and good lighting. 
First night we were in a room and I could not sleep well as I was conscious of the noise from the ventilation system ( not sure if this was because of jet lag that I was sensitive to the noise) but when I went to the front desk at 6am Rachel and the night porter couldn't have been more helpful. The hotel was full but they arranged for a room change and for my bags to be looked after until the room was ready. Overall a good experience and lovely front of house staff.
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton Chicago Downtown / Magnificent Mile

review_text: Omg so I wanted to impress my lady and take her to a high class hotel somewhere she's never been before. Its Valentine day plus her birthday is the next day. So everything seemed fine of course as I'm giving the clerk the money and something told me not to use a credit card...glad I didn't because we went up to the room and it was super small but she liked it so that's all I cared about... so I sneak downstairs to ask them to bring a bottle of champaign up....now there service would be great if they weren't money hungry the first thing they said was the price and mind u we have a stocked bar in our room filled with liquor about the size of my thumb and wants to charge us for a 5th like amount but because its what she wanted we drank it... I can tell she felt bad me spending way more then I planned on because when we came back from our romantic dinner the champaign was there waiting..she wasnt even excited about it because she knew it costs me.... so I'm trying to make the best of my time so the next day were hungry of course and I am completely out of money except for her gift so she had to pay for our expensive breakfast...and u think this high class high dollar place would just give u breakfast...they don't care about anything but your money...and of course they rush u out of there like a bunch of jerks so I wanted to hurry up and get out of there anyway so we check out and I had to check my finances to make sure I had enough for her gift and I figured I have like 20 or 50 bucks left out of the 200 I had to put down for this room.....NOPE I had zero dollars and I didn't want to blow up because it was her birthday so I chose ti stay calm and leave...now we took her car out there and since we had to 50 bucks a day to park we going to use all the time I paid for..so we get back like 5 min late and they tried to charge us for a extra day....but wait this is where it gets good...the bell boy goes in to tell management and they tell us we won't charge u for a extra day but we noticed that u drank some of the drinks including water which was not free as well and u have to take care of this bill before we release your car..WHAT!!!! Now my lady is fuming hot she couldn't hold it in no more...they tried to hold her car hostage until this little ole 50 dollars was paid off...so we threatened to call our lawyers then she tensed up and said just give us the 50 dollars next week then...so needless to say we didn't.... they took enough from us we will never go back again...as far as I'm concerned that hotel and the management can all burn...yes I said it

The location of this hotel is amazing. You can walk the whole mag. mile and walk to millennium park and the art institue from here. There is a great little quick resaurant(leaven) around the corner and dozens of wonderful full scale dinner spots surrounding the hotel. The rooms are a little small, but very comfortable. The pool and hot tub were somewhat small, but a great courtyard is outside for warm weather sitting.
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton Chicago Downtown / Magnificent Mile

review_text:
Had a great weekend with my wife at this historic landmark in Chicago.
As a Diamond member with Hilton we were upgraded to a lakewiew suite on the 8th floor. complementary lounge access as well which was a joy due to the great staff. Breakfast in the lounge was great, however a bit puzzling with charges for drinks in the evening in the lounge.
Overall a great experience.

review_title: Gies to show, a great product does not make up for rude service
review_text:
While this hotel had comfortable rooms & great location, the only person I came in contact with that seemed to remember they are in the business of hospitality was the gentleman who served coffee in morning. 
Rude staff from checkin to checkout and every interaction between.

We booked through Hotwire. Got a great deal! When we arrived, we were helped by Avi. Because we needed a rollaway bed for our third child, he graciously upgraded us to a Junior Suite at no extra charge. He later called our room to ensure we were satisfied and see if we had any additional needs. Great service! In addition, the hotel is gorgeous, and right on the river, one block from Michigan Ave. Great location! Can't wait to go back!!
Very nice, clean rooms. Friendly, courteous, helpful front desk staff. A bit of a hike to Navy Pier to the conference I was attending. Would stay here again.

review_title: Nice hotel in an even better location
review_text:
This hotel was a very nice hotel in one of the best locations in the city. We were only a block away from the red-line and bus stops which were very safe and cheap. The only downside is that the lobby and eating area need to be upgraded they were very 90s looking. Overall I would stay here again.
P. S. There was barely no line at the free breakfast in the morning. So don't let that discorage you.

Fast check in
Rooms are good and clean
Location could not be better
Rooms with balcony available
Nice pool
Small fitness
Free Internet
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton Chicago Downtown / Magnificent Mile

review_text: The Hyatt is recently remodeled and very nice. The staff was extremely friendly and always helpful. The location is centrally located on the mag mile and we could easily walk to all there was to do downtown. Will definitely stay here again. Classy but not stuffy.

review_title: Do not book here- stay at the marriott!
review_text:
