review_title: Great with kids - service excellent - beds just ok
review_text: We stayed at the Omni for three night with our two sons (4 yrs and and infant). The room was clean although a bit small once the pullout couch was out and everyone was asleep. The baby crib was old and didn't look comfortable. Definitely bring your own pack n play. The employees were so nice and this hotel really caters to kids. Great location. Beds are just ok and would go for two rooms next time to have extra room, but overall a good value and close to all the action.

Buen hotel, bien situado, clÃ¡sico, pero bien conservado al mas puro estilo americano. Rincones y salones por donde no ha pasado el tiempo. 
Cama superconfortable para adaptarse bien al cambio de horario

My partner and I celebrated our birthdays and anniversary in NYC over the weekend. Lenny was so sweet and hospitable, as was the rest of the staff. The hotel is beautiful. It's dark and very chic and visually stunning. The location is golden. Just steps from Times Square, the tickets booth, the subway and great places to eat. The rooms are small. The showers are glorious! We probably showered 3 times a day each just because it was so luxurious. There were basic amenities in the room hair dryer, safe, mini fridge, iron, and that's all you need. The bed was so soft and so comfortable. The design was just our style. Not stuffy, not uncomfortable, just elegant and inviting. We definitely want to get back as soon as possible. I'm afraid to see the rates in the late fall, but I have to get back to our Sanctuary. Even though we were in the city for the "killer hurricane Irene". We never felt anything but relaxed and comforable the whole weekend. We will be back!

Was in town for one night stay had a very early flight arrival and the friendly desk staff had a room available for us at 8:00am! Great location easy walk to Mellenium park. Large room clean Free wifi. Did not eat free breakfast or use pool or exercise room during my stay.
hotel_name: La Quinta Inn & Suites Chicago Downtown

review_title: Great hotel, great location, great staff.
review_text: The staff make this hotel. Nothing is too much trouble. My only gripe is that wi-fi is charged, this is just not acceptable in a hotel of this quality and price.
Stayed here for One night for business. Great rooms, service, and value. The only thing that I was not happy about was that parking was $49 per 24 hour period.

Got a great deal on priceline and the location is fantastic - so close to art institute, millennium park, el stops. Beautiful hotel. Only complaint is that they charge for wireless - really should be free. Why nickle and dime?

Es interesante alojarse en uno de los edificios emblemÃ¡ticos en una ciudad donde la arquitectura es su mÃ¡ximo valor. la ubicaciÃ³n es perfecta en el meollo de los lugares turÃ­sticos. La piscina del hotel es preciosa y estupenda para nadar unos largos. Hay gran variabilidad en las habitaciones segÃºn el ala del hotel donde te alojes. lo peor el climatizador muy ruidoso y los extras como mini bar y wifi son muy caros.

Beautifully appointed lobby and rooms. Great staff and great location off Times Square area.
Our room was very small (not unusual for NYC) and the bathroom was incredibly tiny. However, the room is very clean and you have control over the air conditioner : )
I would definitely stay here again.

Just got back today from our weekend away at the Affinia. We came down for the Magnificient Mile Lights Parade on Michigan Avenue last night. 
We had a junior sweet (husband, daughter and myself). It was really lovely with the modern decor. There was plenty of room for us to move around. We loved that there were two levels, and my daughter certainly made sure that the upper desk level was her domain to play in. We had spectacular city views looking right down the street. 
The bed was really wonderful and comfy to sleep in. My daughter had the pull out sofa which she said was good. Breakfast in our room was really great too! 
The nice thing was that we walked right up to Michigan Avenue for the parade and afterwards had dinner at American Girl which is about 1 block away. The Disney store is also right around the corner so my daughter had a dream weekend! 
This was my second time at this hotel and will book again!

We were able to get this room for half price through Expedia. I still paid as much as the Microtel we stayed at two nights previous. I was excited to be staying so close to the Magnificant Mile and all that is Chicago. My first disappointment was the parking. The hotel charges $49 a day for parking. We were able to get it directly across the street for $40. Once at the room, I was impressed with the layout. However, upon further examination I realized that there was no microwave and I had to unload the alcohol from the fridge so I could put in a couple cans of pop. There was no fan in the bathroom, water spots and cracks on the ceiling, and the bathtub tile needed re-grouted. When I bathed I found a yellow spot on my towel. The coffee maker makes coffee, but has no way to keep it warm and as I mentioned before, there's no microwave. The continental breakfast for two is $24 more AND Internet is an additional $10. The final problem I found with the room was when I found the heating/air conditioning unit the filter was completely clogged. Luckily I'm not sensitive to dust. I found this hotel completely unacceptable. My husband says that this is common in large cities. I'm sorry, but I expect MORE from an establishment on the Magnificent Mile, not less.

review_title: Still under construction.. But the let down is the service
review_text:
Stayed for 5 nights end of June and don't let anyone fool you, was told by construction workers that they would be lucky if done by the end of September. Only major issue with this (if u are made aware beforehand) is that the only elevator is a service one (very very slow) and it is in constant use by staff and construction personnell meaning plan on waiting 10+ minutes every time u want to use it. I would have had staff using the stairs but service as a whole was not good.
Asked on wed for them to fix the safe in room.. Asked again thursday (twice), again on friday. Each time they were appalled that 'no one' had done anything but no individual could be bothered.
Asked for a restaurant reccomendation from concierge and they simply brought up a 2 page zagat print out off the internet and suggested we try phoning some of those to see if any availability.
Was twice woken at midnight by staff knocking on our door when they had in fact been called to a different room.
I would happily forgive the construction if staff did something when requested as opposed to chatting amongst themselves.
Location good and room fine for the px range.

review_title: Excellent hotel - can't wait to come back
review_text:
Stayed here on a weekend getaway. Excellent location just off the mile. Room was very clean and nicely furnished. Right after arriving at out room, the staff arrived with a bed, bowl, towel, treats and clean up bags for our dog. The staff is very professional and courteous. 
Only drawbacks are the sirens from the nearby fire station (not really the hotels fault) and the pillows were a little hard but with 6 types to choose from, we will try again until we find the right ones.

review_title: Very good but can be noisy
review_text: Everything was very good, the room was small but clean, location and lobby are amazing. But the walls are thin, you hear clearly through the walls. Thanks god our neigbors did not watch tv at night.

review_title: A grand old hotel. I wish I could say as much for the staff.
review_text: We stayed at the Palmer House this weekend for the first time in a long time. The hotel is a grand old lady with great architecture and art but the staff lacks a lot. Our room was not supplied well, we had to request soap the second day, they wanted $10 to use the fitness center, internet access was $20 per day, the concierge argued with me and the executive lounge was crowded, filled with kids, the food stuck in a small room and crowded with people. I booked my room through Price line and even though I'm a Diamond in the Hilton Honors program everyone took great pride in telling me how thatdidnt do anything for me when I booked my room through them. They wouldn't even allow me to get credit for any incidentals. It was great incentive to not spend a dime in the hotel I didn't have to spend. All in all I can tell you that given a choice I will not stay at the Palmer House again. I wouldn't recommend anyone else stay there either. There are plenty of other great hotels in Chicago.

One of the best locations in Chicago right by the river. There is a seven eleven near by for late night movie rentals (DVD player in room) and for the people who dont use room service for everything. Very clean room and large bathroom with water fall shower head. All of my needs were met and I enjoyed the Hoyt restaurant and bar downstairs. The fitness center was very impressive as well. Bring your work out gear to get a work out with a great river view. My only complaint was no fridge or mini bar but a few buckets of ice fixed that.

Great hotel in great location. Stayed here 4 nights. Really fast and friendly staff, lovely rooms and absolutely massive too. This hotel is pretty great for shopping as your almost right on the bridge at one end of the magnificent mile.
Never ate here so can't judge food.
Staff were really helpful although one was trying to hard was obviously new and was telling us innacurate info.
Only downside was smell in bathroom. 
Would def recommend though.
Business trip. Some of rooms small and noisy, but overall pleasant stay. Room 18_218 was away from train and larger than most.

We stayed at The Palmer in 2006, pleasantly surprised to see the rooms beautifully renovated in 2011. Gorgeous decor, extremely clean, courteous staff, perfect location. Had a great time! Lack of free wireless is a bummer, but it's available at the cute coffee shop next door!

review_title: Great location - but very noisy room!
review_text:
This past weekend, my husband and I departed for a three night trip to Chicago. Our hotel of choice - Hotel 71. While sometimes I book our rooms through sites such as priceline and expedia; I choose to book direct for this trip in order to ensure we would have a nice room with a great view, etc. We paid 246 a night, which I thought seemed a tad high for this place, but I was willing to give it a shot. 
We had a superior king room with the river view. 
The good: very spacious room, beautiful view, double vanities, lots of countertop surface to set things, comfortable bed.
The bad: paper thin walls and tiled entry into room made noises throughout seem very loud and it was difficult to get a good night sleep. Couple this with hammering and the constant sawing from a chop saw for two mornings in a row across from our room made the beginning of what was suppose to be relaxing weekend away from construction noise (my husband and I both work in the construction field) not so relaxing. The jack hammering as we waited for the elevator in the lobby and other various noises from the room above ours we thought finally warranted a call to the front desk. 1000 spent at this hotel on room and parking. I never did get to awaken a single morning there peacefully. And how did they offer to make this right? A free breakfast on Sunday. Sunday, I couldn't wait leave. 
I really wanted to like this place and write more about some of nice features. However, the lack of sleep has proven me grumpy and very disappointed. I probably won't stay here again and most likely will not recommend this place to our friends that frequent Chicago quiet often.

I feel the rooms in this hotel are desperately needing an upgrade. As well as being tiny, the interior is dreary and the walls seem as thin as paper - I was lucky enough to be able to hear conversations and televisions from nearby rooms until late into the night.
More of a hinderance was the lack of wireless internet in the rooms. Being told that they had no wireless routers left without an apology was frustrating - especially when one of the few perks of Hhonors Gold is free Internet access. 
On the plus side I guess the gym and the gym staff were nice, it's just a shame about the Internet when I had some work emails to send (luckily Starbucks saved me).

review_title: Great location, amazing lobby bit run down
review_text: This hotel is old and the rooms show it. We however had a great time due to the hotel's location which meant we could walk everywhere. The lobby was also great place to have a drink after hard day of sightseeing. We stayed in executive level and the extra service there was good.

review_title: Cannot praise this hotel highly enough.

review_text: Good place for a night stay. Room was good.old styled. Downside- CRT tv . Also the person at reception was a bit rude . I recommend the hotel
We had a corner room with a fantastic view looking down the river. The location right off Michigan Ave. is perfect - within walking distance to everything. Very reasonable rates.

review_title: Very nice for a city hotel for our price.
review_text:
We stayed in August for 4 nights with a two year old. The hotel was clean, friendly, spacious, and perfect location. We booked using Priceline so didn't really have a choice. Was very pleased with the whole experience! We paid $120 a night. They offer an upgrade ($20 more a night) at check in. We didn't take it and honestly had no idea what an upgrade would be needed for. They provided a pack-n-play for our daughter and a room big enough for all of our things.
A side note we didn't know this before we booked but Batman- The Dark Night had a scene filled there.

review_title: A hotel as welcoming as it is beautiful.
review_text:
I love this hotel. A landmark Burnham building with all the fine Arts and Crafts movement details.
But it is the staff that makes this place so special. Very friendly and accommodating.
Yes, there is noise from the L. But that is a given anywhere in the Loop where the sound bounces off the tall buildings. Earplugs work fine for light sleepers.

review_title: Very poor value for the price!
review_text:
I am in Chicago for a business conference and the Palmer House Hilton was one of the block hotels reserved. If you are looking for a hotel with beautiful common areas in a decent location, but very little else going for it, you have found the right place. The common areas and ballroom are stunning but the amenities and guest rooms are mediocre at best and certainly not worth the 200+ per night that you pay. Take note that even though you spend a fortune for this hotel that the gym is not included. You still pay a daily rate per person if you want to use the gym. Internet use will be charged at a daily or hourly rate depending on where you use it and if you want wireless you have to request a wireless bridge.
I recommend spending your money elsewhere.

review_title: Great hotel in a great location.
review_text: We spent a week here in late July and could not have been more pleased. The room was very clean and well appointed with a great view of the Chicago River and downtown. The staff was courteous and helpful throughout our stay and the location couldn't be better. I would definitely recommend this hotel!

Hotel location is perfect. Value for money was good thanks to expedia offers. The room was large and clean, and the bed very confortable. Unfortunately if you have a room facing north the noise can be unbearable. we were given a room at the seventh floor where a humming and beating noise from the air conditioners of the adiacent buildings was impossible to bear. we asked for a replacement room and were given a much more comfortable one, less noisy but still on working days, trucks loading and unloading stuff in the next building were making lots of noise starting from early morning. they should install soundproof glasses in the rooms.

review_title: Great place to stay in downtown Chicago.
review_text: Stayed here over the weekend while running the Chicago urbanathlon. The hotel is in a great place near Grant park and Michigan ave. You can walk everywhere. Rooms were not the most modern i've seen but still very nice. I will definitely stay here again.

review_title: Para quedarme cada veqz que este en New York
review_text: El hotel es como lo musetran en las fotos. La habitacion que nos dieron estuvo excelente, limpia, espaciosa, y bien aislada del exterior. La atencion excelente desce el primer momento y muy corteses en general todos los empleados. El ambiente es muy cool y la ubicacion magnifica, al lado de times square. El desayuno es super bÃ¡sico con fruta y cereal, nada extraordinario. Volvere al hotel en mi proxima visita sin ninguna duda.

Second visit to Hotel 71 for annual shopping/sightseeing trip to Chicago. Upgraded to river view (corner) room for nominal fee and WOW! What a view! Located on 33rd floor, downtown Chicago at our feet, large room, somewhat smallish bathroom, but very comfortable. Mirrored closet doors came off tracks and we informed front desk, but problem wasn't fixed when we checked out. Walls somewhat thin, Lollapalooza attendees next door very loud! Hotel security called and immediately quieted the situation. Thank you, Hotel 71 for another great Chicago experience!!
Fantastic experience at this downtown gem. Well worth the price to have a huge room in the heart of the city. Other boutique hotels claim to be the best, but Hotel 71 is the real deal.

Spent couple nights while on business. Upgraded to suite, but nothing worth writing home about - extra space was nice I suppose.
Location is great - block off Michigan and near millennium park right at Wabash/Madison station.
Staff was very friendly and helpful. Hotel was clean and well maintained. The rooms and decor were very uninspired. Room had very little natural light and internal lighting was too soft and incandescent. With high ceilings and fully lit still seemed a little like a funeral home.
Key rarely worked, toilet broke, iron broke. Too many hotels in area to get a bad review

Great hotel in the middle of all the action. Amazing view of the river. Very short walk to access water taxis and river walk. Short walk to the Navy Pier. Great in house restaurant with street level seating. Great for watching the city going by. Rooms are nice. Valet parking right at hotel is very convinient.
It was our first stay in Houston and loved the Embassy Suites. Rooms are huge and clean. The staff was great. The best was the breakfast and the cook to order omelettes. Excellent value overall.

review_title: Great hotel in the heart of downtown
review_text: This hotel was excellent! The service was great. I had a problem with the safe in the room and they sent someone up within 10 mins and he fixed it. Superb location for bars and amazing food! And in no time flat you can be at millennium park enjoying great music! I would recommend this hotel to anyone

review_title: Modern, clean, accessable, I will Definitly stay here again.
review_text: I stayed here for two nights and was very happy. The rooms were very modern and very clean. The hotel has a restaurant in the lower level called Ada's, that wasn't too pricey for a large city and my breakfast was good. The location is awesome if you are a shopper with all the majors retailers being one block over. The subway/El/train lines are all at your disposal as well. If you are into sight seeing or the art scene, you are within walking distance of Chicago's art museum, their amphitheater, the Willis (formerly Sears) tower, and are in the heart of what Chicago calls The Loop. The hotel staff was friendly and helpful when asking for information and directions. I felt very safe and comfortable in this area and hotel.

review_title: A lot of room...for little money
review_text:
Let me start by saying that I'm incredibly impressed by how spacious our room was! We had a room with 2 double beds. The height of the ceiling really made it feel grand. The bathroom was also surprisingly large, which is plus. Often in big cities you have to give up space if you want to save a little money, but this wasn't the case at the Silversmith! 
Some people are complaining about the noise from the train. I don't know where their rooms were, but from our room we barely noticed. Every now and then we'd hear what sounded like a gust of wind, but that was it. Actually, the sound was rather soothing.
Other people have commented on the "outdated" furnishings. With an emphasis on solid wood and an earthy color palette, the design of the hotel recalls the Arts & Crafts Movement of the late 19th and early 20th century. This is very appropriate considering the building's history. If you're a history/design/architecture person like I am, you'll really appreciate it. Otherwise, I can see how some people might simply write-off the furnishings & fixtures as "outdated."
There are many things I liked about this hotel. Our room had a nice closet so we were able to hide all of our bags & luggage away. I think it always makes a room look unnecessarily cluttered, so having a closet is great.
The room was very clean. Each day we came back to our beds neatly made. The sheets and bedding are comfy, and there are plenty of pillows. 
The refrigerator came in handy for storing leftovers. Cold pizza in the middle of the night? Yes, please. 
The price and the location of the hotel can't be beat. The 'L' train is only a few steps from the door, and there are also several bus stops nearby. The hotel is within walking distance to Millennium Park, the Art Institute, and dozens of restaurants. If you like to eat late, there's a pub just down the street that serves food until 2 am.
There's one minor thing I didn't necessarily "hate," so I'll be brief. When you walk in, you have to take the elevator up to the 2nd floor to get to the lobby & check-in desk. The doormen are nice though. The ground floor smells like garbage, not sure why. Don't worry, once you get up to the lobby, it doesn't stink anymore.
Overall, I was more than satisfied with the Silversmith. I will definitely stay there again.
An unusually configured Enbassy - no atrium. Only negative is undersized and understaffed breakfast line.

Stayed here for a friend's birthday, got a great deal by bidding on the room. The staff was courteous and it was only blocks from the subway and Michigan Ave shopping. It is also right next to my favorite pizzeria, Gino's East. Only complaint is they did not have a pool.

review_title: A Fair Price, A Great Value Hotel
review_text: We stayed at the Silversmith for 6 nights. Location was great for getting around Chicago on public transportation, employees were always helpful, the hotel and room were clean, bed was comfortable, room/suite was spacious and the price was fair. We would gladly stay again.

review_title: Sehr zentrales Hotel mit entsprechenden Preisen
review_text:
Das Hotel ist perfekt um NYC zu erkunden oder shoppen zu gehen (Macys und vieles mehr ist max. 5 Gehminuten entfernt). Das Empire State Building ist keine 5 Minuten entfernt und je nach Zimmer bereits zu sehen.
Zum Hotel selbst: die Zimmer leider etwas klein aber modern ausgestattet mit Safe, Flatscreen, Minibar, Mikrowelle und Kaffeemaschine. 
Das Personal ist nett aber leider nicht unbedingt kompetent, wir haben unsere Koffer an der Rezeption zur Aufbewahrung abgegeben und als wir wiederkamen standen sie nicht abgesperrt in einem Raum sondern mitten am Empfang.

review_text: I was in need of a nice hotel in the heart of the loop and I found it. It's is a tiny place with a magical feeling. The price was a little high, but we were very happy with everything. I jus wish I could have stayed longer.

Tutti molto gentili e pronti ad aiutarti. ci torneremo sicuramente e lo consigliamo a chi come noi vuole girare New York a piedi. La camera piccola rispetto ad altri hotel ma molto funzionale. review_text:
Our experience was good and met our needs for a one night stay in Chicago. We did not opt to park near the hotel. Parking rates in Chicago are crazy and we have a good spot. We parked and walked everywhere during our stay and the location was good. We walked to the Shedd Aquarium and Charter One Pavillion. It was also close enough to walk to good restaurants. 
Service was OK. Nothing stands out and nobody seemed too interested in us. This stands out to me as unimpressive while the hotel itself was very good.

Internet speed unacceptable... cannot get my work done. Rooms are underwhelming. Laughably small TV in a big suite room. No glasses. No mini bar. No bottles of water. Service completely lacking on check-in... never greeted or offered help from curb to room. Would not stay again.
I checked in an was given the executive suite! Beautiful on the 35th floor. Food in restaurant was good and room service good. They serve illy coffee!! Amazing staff

Just finished a short one night stay in downtown Houston at the Embassy Suites. This location is far better then any Embassy Suite I have stayed at in the past. It is a new property and it shows. I only hope Embassy Suites continues going this direction with future properties.
My only complaints are the lack of a lock for the bathroom door and fact that self parking is not an option. I am not a fan of paying $28 for valet parking when they do not offer any other option.
Overall I would stay there again in the future.

We booked this hotel, for a very reasonable rate, thinking that this was a typical hotel, with valet parking because they were located downtown Houston, we were above shocked when realized just how extravigant this hotel was!!! And the service was above and beyond exceptional!! From the moment we pulled up to the valet, who are all beyond polite they make you feel like royalty, to the receptionists at check in, to the bellboy, my family and I didn't want to leave, although our stay had come to an end, but rest assured, my husband I are already planning our next trip, where We will definately not stay anywhere else.

We booked 10 rooms on Priceline not knowing what we were gonna get. WOW... not your small stuffy Chicago room that we have all stayed in before. Walk into your room and your met with a good size desk/ work area. To the left is a large bathroom. (Which is the size of some other places whole room) to the right is a sunken (3 steps) bed room area. Some rooms have 2 full and others had a king with a pull out sofa. Key to a good night sleep is 6 differant pillows to pick from. A must is the roof top bar! If you have any questions ask Victor at the front door.

Very nice hotel in a perfect location on Superior and close to Michigan Ave. Right next door to Ginos East and they give you passes so you don't have to sit in line which is very common at Ginos. Hotel is very clean and room was awesome. Had a standard king room on 22nd floor and it was perfect. It is next to the hospital so there were sirens from time to time but that's common in any big city. 
Rooftop bar is nice with great views of the city. We only had an appetizer but CHouse restaurant looked like a great spot as well. 
Staff was very helpful...got our room ready early so we could take a quick nap. 
Would definitely recommend this place for all travelers to the windy city. We got a great deal on priceline as well....ended up about $100 night even after taxes! Can't beat that in Chicago!! Thanks for a great stay Affinia.

Just stayed at the affinia and we were really pleased with location for getting around Chicago. The service was fantastic, advice on where to go and how to get around were very forthcoming and helpful. Rooms were very large and very well maintained

We stayed for 2 nights at this hotel. When we first arrived the rooms were very nicely decorated and seemed clean. One of the double beds seemed to be defective. It caved in the middle like a taco. We decided to give it a try but by the morning we realized she couldn't spend another night on the bed. When we went down to request another room in the morning they said that they were full and they could provide us with a cot at no extra charge. Really I didn't pay that money to sleep on a cot. I asked them to look at the bed to see if it could be fixed. We arrived back 3 hrs later and the front desk said they didn't know if it had fixed. When we went to the room it still was the same. Also the windows are paper thin so it felt like I was sleeping on the street because it was so loud. You could hear the dumpsters bring emptied at 4 am. Then there was the 7am wake up call I didn't request. When I told her that she said wrong number and hung up. There was a gas main break infront of the hotel so we had to wait 3 hours to get back in and then there was no heat or hot water till 7pm. The gas main break was at 9 am. When speaking with the staff they were less then helpful. When we were finally leaving they got us a taxi but took 5 dollars from the driver so she could have the fare SO TACKY! I will never stay here and I will tell everyone I know to NEVER stay there.

Devo dire di essermi trovato molto bene in questa struttura che vanta una posizione davvero strategica e a un passo dalla metro.Inoltre camere molto spaziose e pulizia accurata.Struttura dotata di business center e connessione wi-fi gratuita e molto veloce.Staff molto gentile e disponibile.Devo dire una buona struttura a New York considerando un prezzo non cosÃ¬ eccessivo.
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn New York West 35th

review_text: Favorite hotel in Houston by far. The staff was extremely nice...Esp the lady serving breakfast. The breakfast was very good and our room was very clean. The bed was extremely comfortable. Will definitely stay here again!!!
The staff was friendly and helpful. The room was really comfortable. It felt just like we never left home.
A 5 minuti da time square a piedi! Stazione della metro sotto l'ingresso dell'hotel. Struttura nuova. Camere pulite. Vista sull' Empire!
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn New York West 35th

review_text: This hotel is the best hotel I have been to yet. Hotel Staff are very helpful. Especially Hereasie and Daniel. They offer the best customer service. They will help you with everything you need. Rooms are clean. Breakfast is good. Paulette the breakfast bar employee is very nice and attentive. I will definitely be back.

review_title: Will definitely stay at this boutique hotel again!
review_text: Cute hotel with fun amenities including milk and cookie buffet in the evening and breakfast in the morning. Slept in so didn't do the breakfast. Enjoyed the area right in the middle of downtown. Convenient coffee shop open early & late at the first floor. We stayed during the holidays do there were parties going on. Only big downfall during our stay was that the main floor and elevators reeked of fish. Hotel needs better ventilation for their restaurant. Other than that, had a very pleasant stay.

Service at the hotel was outstanding and it is the best hotel we've stayed at in downtown Houston. Comfy bed and modern rooms. We were disappointed in the quality of the breakfast buffet this past weekend. We also had to have them re-clean our room. However, we were still very pleased with our stay and would stay there again.
Room was a little small, bit very comfortable. Was only a one night stay...so worked out great. Would stay again. Very good value.

Comfortable hotel in striking distance to ball park and convention center in. downtown Houston. 
Nice boutique feel despite size.
When staying downtown I always stay at the magnolia for their service and quality.
We stay here every couple of months. It is close to everything. They have great ammenities.

This hotel truly feels like a getaway! It's clean, friendly, and offers fantastic service and food. The milk and cookies at night are a perfect way to unwind and the free breakfast is delicious, plentiful and varied.

review_title: All the necessities and then some.
review_text: The hotel was quiet, my room was spotless, the free hot breakfast was tasty, and the service was impeccable. I won't stay anywhere else in Houston.

I think this place has been severely overrated on trip advisor.
First, the good points... As noted by others, the staff are friendly and helpful. The courtesy transport to/from the airport is convenient and welcome. Although it has some major weaknesses, it is reasonable value for Chicago. There is a Giordano's within walking distance, which is great for Chicago style pizza. The location is what it is. Relatively easy to get downtown, but takes a while.
Now... the less good. First, the rooms are fairly ordinary. Very small, with a small double bed. The bathroom is tiny. The shower curtain only covered half the shower, consequently water went everywhere. The rooms were also dingy. We had a room on the second floor, up the back, so very little light got in. All in all a fairly miserable atmosphere.
Second, our room was not clean to the degree expected. Although the bathroom etc was clean, the carpet felt and looked as though it could do with a good thorough stem clean. It felt dirty to walk on, and I noticed hair on my socks after walking around in the room.
Third, the breakfast was average at best. No-where to sit, we gave it a miss after the first morning. If stale dunkin donuts and cold breakfast sandwiches appeal to you then you may like it...
Overall, I can't recommend this, although the staff are very helpful. If you do stay, give breakfast a miss and ask for a room that faces out in the open for light.
This hotel is georgeous. Everything from the lobby to the rooms to the bar. First class all the way. Expect to pay Chicago loop prices for rooms and parking.

review_title: When in Houston, I'll never stay anywhere else.
review_text: Perfection. Why add anything else? Oh...50 characters? Ok..perfect, perfect, perfect, perfect, perfect, perfect. Get the point? Oh!! Perfect!
My wife and I had a great weekend, the hotel is in a great location and is as nice as anywhere I've ever stayed before!!!

review_title: Good value and very helpful staff
review_text: This hotel was in a great location for us and was a great value. The room had an overwhelming smell of cleaning products, but the staff was incredibly helpful, going out of their way to find info for us. I would definitely recommend it for value and convenience for people who are in town to see Chicago, rather than a fancy hotel room!!

review_title: One of the best business Marriott I have stayed in
review_text: I am a platinum member with Marriott and this is one of the best. Gorgeous rooms, bathrooms and incredible gym. The service was awesome and staff is very friendly. Very cool lobby bar.

I stay here a lot and figured I would give an update to my first review which was basically useless. This hotel is in a great location. It is clean, modern and service is great. Bring earplugs if you are a light sleeper- the sound proofing in this hotel is not the best. You will ample road noise and sirens for the emergency room, you might also hear other guests talking or partying in rooms nearby. I will continue to stay here because it's walking distance of where I need to be. There is also a decent gym, but I could not find any disinfecting wipes for machines. Yuck!
We have stayed here many times and have experienced a significant drop in the service quality during this trip including having our room given away to another guest and a maid at our door at 8:15 am.

I was most impressed by the staff at this hotel, the service was more than I have come to expect at a large chainnhotel. This hotel is located in a part of downtown surrounded by offices, so the "neighborhood" gets very quiet and empty when the business day ends. I had a room with 2 queen beds, it had a decent workspace and enough room to move around comfortably. My room faced in to an open outdoor space, no view for me, but it was quiet.

This is a great hotel! The staff is friendly, we especially love the breakfast hostess, Ismeta. She is just wonderful to everyone! Great location and reasonable, especially considering breakfast and dinner come with the room. Rooms are clean and well equipped. We will definitely be back!
hotel_name: Residence Inn Chicago Downtown / River North

review_text: Seven of us stayed here on our way for a two week vacation. We stayed at the beginning of the trip and then two weeks later. Our first stay was great! The staff went above and beyond in getting us what we needed, even going out of their way to drive us in the shuttle to Union Station so we wouldn't have to drag our bags to the L station in the pouring rain. They did this for no charge. Unfortunately, when we came back two weeks later, the lady at the front desk questioned our registration because she said it had been made under my late father's name and my mother's credit card only had her name on it. She was extremely rude and when I informed her we had stayed here two weeks previous with no problem, she still questioned how we could prove we made the reservation. I was fired up by this time and informed her we had been on a train for 36 hours, it was almost midnight and we did not need this unnecessary hassle. She yelled at me informing me she had been at work since 7 am. Big whoop, lady... That's your job and questioning people who had stayed there previously and treating us like we were common criminals who would come in with 5 other people ALL Senior Citizens as well. Get a grip! She then proceeded to lecture us on how we would never be able to stay at any hotel under those circumstances... Also untrue. My father has been dead for 18 months and my mother and I have been traveling extensively since then and I can assure you, no hotel has EVER questioned our proof of identity. All our last names are the same! She was hassling us over two initials. Although I doubt I would stay in this part of Chicago again, she ruined what would have been an otherwise glowing review until that night.
Quality and value that is hard to beat. Clean, with great staff and location to match.
hotel_name: Residence Inn Chicago Downtown / River North

review_text:
When have you ever went to a hotel and had the front desk charge your card for the room without stating the room rate? Well they did that here and then showed us the price we paid afterwards, we were immediately frustrated because the rate was $20 more at the front desk then paying online and they didn't care to fix this issue and it was their fault since she failed to let us know the price. I know that it's only $20 but I could have paid for that online and if they were more courteous we may have stayed an extra day, but they weren't and we opted for just the one night.
We ordered late night food in our room and although it was nachos and a grilled cheese sandwich, for some reason it took 50 mins!?! Like really 50 mins and $60 later for crappy food seems absolutely ridiculous. 
The morning we left, we called for a luggage cart and to have our car brought up from valet. We waited and waited, 20 mins later we called and they said it'd be a couple mins, finally he showed up and when we got down to the valet, you guessed it, our car was NO WHERE in sight!! Wow 20 mins waiting around so that we could wait some more, now if this was a weekend, I wouldn't have had such an issue but this was Friday morning and we had a meeting we needed to get to, which we were now running late for! I'm sorry, but that is unprofessional and being a hotel in downtown Houston, they should be better at this!

Rooms are great! Housekeeping has many OCD personnel as all our cords were neatly wrapped & tied every day. Our things on the sink area were placed orderly on a washcloth for cleanliness & our things in the shower were lined up neatly on the ledge. The tub was a small swimming pool! Ha-ha! My shorter adult daughter was not allowed to go in without a lifeguard. Within several minutes walking to many sights & amenities. Florentine restaurant on site, with Iron Chef Todd Stein, has food to die for! Friendly and helpful staff at all times.

Spent our anniversary at the Magnolia last night. Checked in a few hours before official check-in time without any problem. Hit the roof-top pool for some pre dinner
 R & R. There was a guy running drinks and food to guests. Received a complimentary bottle of champagne from the front desk for our anniversary. Hooked up with the valet guys for a ride to dinner and back in the hotel's suburban. Ordered room service coffee pre complimentary breakfast. Every single hotel employee we saw and spoke with was extremely professional, friendly and happy. The attitude of the entire staff made our stay really nice.
As a plat Marriott member, we were treated like kings. Definitely the best chicago hotel for Marriott elites, at least. For the rest of y'all, see what you're missing out on.

review_title: Good service, great location for work
review_text: No wireless Internet connection but a very comfortable suite and breakfast restaurant. The staff were friendly and very accommodating. Good spot in Chicago.
hotel_name: Residence Inn Chicago Downtown / River North

review_text: Great hotel, great location! The rooms are great as is the service. This will sound stupid, but the hotel parking garage is intimidating. I really like Marriott family hotels more so than others. They are clean, well decorated and comfortable. What I hate is that wireless is not free.... Stay here for the location, service and comfy rooms!

Stayed for two nights for business in October 2011. Location was great, rooms were clean, fitness facility was solid and the staff was quite helpful. 
Will return on future trips to Chicago.
hotel_name: Residence Inn Chicago Downtown / River North

review_title: Best downtown hotel by a mile.
review_text: Centrally located within walking distance of all downtown attractions. The Strip package was an awesome deal and was extremely romantic. The late night cookie bar was a nice bonus and the morning breakfast was terrific. The only complaint I had was the cost of the parking charge compaired to other overnight options in the area. This was Houston, not DC or NYC...

review_title: Wonderful decor and a relaxed atmosphere.
review_text: I would enjoy the opportunity to be able to stay again
Wonderful experience. Knowledgeable and friendly staff!

Was in town for the Chicago Bulls playoff game. The hotel was beautiful and the staff went above and beyond to provide exceptional service, i.e. allowed me to check in early due to the early game time. The room was clean, spacious and the bathroom was awesome! Room service was quick! I will defn stay here again whenever I come to Nashville!

We stayed here with 2 dogs and our 2 year old. It was great. The staff was so friendly! It was stylish, very clean and roomy. We had a one bedroom that had every thing we needed! They were so nice to our dogs. There was also a great free breakfast evey morning. The only bad part was the parking. We had a trailer and suv. It was going to be $160 for 2 nights parking. We parked 3 blocks away and still payed $120.
hotel_name: Residence Inn Chicago Downtown / River North

I stayed from 18th-20th in july the rooms were nice service was great they did everything i asked for, location is awesome its right next to the famous garretts popcorn, coach,burberry,etc. I loved this hotel the breakfast was great , it is about 8 blocks from the navy pier i would recommend this to anyone who is looking for a hotel with a great location and prices

review_title: Comfy room with an affordable price, great service.
review_text: We stayed at this Hotel because we were attending a wedding in town. We really enjoyed our stay and wish we could. Have enjoyed all the hotel had to offer. The room was spacious and clean, nice mini bar area with wine glasses and bottle opener. The bathroom was big as well and had nice lighting for applying your makeup... with sadly a lot of nice hotels don't. They offered a free breakfast buffet full of all the stuff you could ever want to eat. We would come back her anytime we are looking for a hotel in the area.

The hotel is in a nice spot. You can walk to most shopping areas and restaurants. Loved that it had free breakfast and Internet. I put 4 for service because anytime I called guest services, most of the time they sound annoyed. Like "why is she calling again!" Otherwise, I would stay here again.
hotel_name: Residence Inn Chicago Downtown / River North

review_text: Everyone was very friendly. Hotel was very clean. Overall experience was excellent!
It's a beautiful hotel and very relaxing and romantic! Can't wait to return!

Stayed here to attend trade show in Chicago. Rooms excellent size and slightly upgraded on usual Courtyard style. Always find this chain good for the business traveller but it would be agood choice for the tourist too as very central. Nice classy bar for business meetings but did not eat there as many good restaurants all around.

Just returned from Houston and 3 nights at the Magnolia. The location of the hotel is good. Close to restaurants and freeways. It is uniquely appointed in the lobby and the room. The rooftop pool was a hit with my teen. I called ahead to arrange a massage (I wrenched my neck on a roller coaster). The front desk had a RMT literally waiting for my arrival. The price tag was steep but it turned out to be a vacation saver... The therapist was nice. The beds were amazing !!!!! And the guys out front.... Were wonderful. Now for the areas I wasn't happy with. Apparently there is a free breakfast buffet. Was never told that and therefore never got to it. No one told us about free bedtime cookies. The pullout had no blankets and we waited forever for them. The front desk staff wasn't very friendly or helpful.... In fact, I felt they were a little standoffish. The staff, except the guys out front, weren't that friendly. Very disappointing.... Cause if they were, this place would be off the map for me. The hotel appears to cater to business folks.... Maybe that's why it is not very friendly. Oh....forgot to mention..... Room service is very very good. The wings were the best.

My girlfriend and I stayed the night and walked a few blocks to watch the Astros game. The hotel offered a nice- sized comfortable room with a great garden tub. The room was one of the quietest I've experienced. The breakfast buffet was one of the best I've seen in years. The staff was friendly. I'll definitely stay here again any time I'm in Houston.

I like Marriott hotels, but this one was better than most, still. The staff was very helpful and extremely friendly. Felt like tips were not expected and genuinely appreciated. Location is great just one block off Michigan. Highly recommend this facility.

review_title: Good but the extras blow out the budget!
review_text:
Room rate was great! Got a queen room, very small... But that in itself was ok. 
It was the extras that killed it! Parking ($33 if self park, $42 if valet), tip the concierge, tip the valet... Blew out the budget! 
Great location just be aware of the other costs that's all.

We have stayed at many residence inns and this room was very small in comparison. Requests for towels, etc. Required a second telephone call and more than an hour for the request to be met. The reason we gave service a 3 was due to Brita (spelling ?). She is at morning breakfast and is wonderful. She had a very contagious, cheerful demeanor. The rest of the staff could take a lesson in customer service from her.
hotel_name: Residence Inn Chicago Downtown / River North

review_text:
We came to Houston downtown to spend half day as a part of our roadtrip. Early in the morning somebody broke into our car (parked in public parking area in downtown) and stole our belongings from car. We had to go to service for replacing window. We needed to stay overnight in Houston and searched hotels on Tripadvisor. This was the only hotel had %100 recommendation of reviewers. We took the advise and called hotel. The front office staff (Daniel) was so kind and helpful. Room was perfectly clean and organized. (it was better than 4 star hotel in Florida; we stayed last week) Everthing we needed was available. I found a nice looking basket in the bathroom for dirty towels. I hate to use hotel towels, because people throw used ones to dirty - wet floor, step on their shoes and we as
next customer use them. For me basket was an example of their approach to maintain the hotel.
Breakfast was great, hotel staff was very kind and helpful. I want to thank Tripadvisor reviewers and hotel staff for such a pleasant stay on a bad day for us. Don't go to an yother hotel, this place is a gem.

My husband and I spent three nights at the Magnolia and absolutely loved it! It is very clean, with friendly staff, and the food at the Magnolia Club and in-room dining is awesome!! We will definitely be back!

If you have business in downtown Houston, the Magnolia is the place to stay. For the price of the room, you get free beer or wine in the evening, free cookies before bed, and a quick good breakfast the next morning. All of this aside the rooms and The common areas are first class as well.

review_title: Willows made first stay in Chicago wonderful!
review_text: My girlfriend and I stayed at The Willows for 3 days and had a wonderful experience. The friendly front desk staff was very accommodating and helped us find our way around a new city. The room was very nice, bed was comfortable, mini bar was priced reasonably and the people couldn't have been nicer. We will definitely be staying here again!

We stayed here because it was very close to the baseball stadium and were very pleased with how helpful the staff was. They went out of their way to help my father replace items he had forgotten at home - even driving him to the store when he was in a time crunch. The cost of parking here is high, but not that much more than other houston hotels, and in our case dad can't walk far so the valet service was well with the money. The free breakfast was also much better than I expected. I'd definitely stay here again.

As far as location, this is about as good as it gets. Less than 2 short blocks to the Magnificent Mile, 3 blocks from Lake Michigan, right on the bus line. Pretty building, very clean. Incredibly helpful and friendly staff. Breakfast is fine, no bells and whistles, but suitable. This is not a fancy, 5star hotel, but a 2 star hotel that is well run. My only complaint is the bathroom lay out (tight) and the view of ... nothing. Request a street side view.

review_title: Hip decor and location + hop-to-it service = happy stay in Chicago
review_text: My daughter and I fell in love with Chicago and plan to return as often as we can. We'd be crazy to stay anywhere else. The hotel sparkles, and so does the staff. In our ninth floor room across from the elevator we were never disturbed by noise, rarely had to wait for an elevator, and enjoyed the Navy Pier's fireworks display while sitting in bed! Sparkles!!

review_title: Great service, location, rooftop view and cookie buffet!
review_text: Always enjoy every aspect of this hotel. Would definitely stay again and recommend to anyone.
I was here for a business trip. The place was lovely. Great boutique hotel. Wonderful service. Nice decor. Fantastic room. Very comfortable beds. Lots of room to work.

review_title: Great hotel at a great value
review_text: Everything was excellent; proximity, service, value, and quality. I would stay here again.

Had a girls night out and the location couldn't have been better. Staff was friendly and helpful. They allowed us to check in early. We had decided to get a cot for the room and the delivered it with 5 minutes of making the request. My friend who slept on the cot is 5 months pregnant and said she was very comfortable.

review_title: This is the place to stay!!
review_text: We have just recently travelled round the world on a tour and this is the most impressive hotel we have stayed in yet!!very comfortable quite room with comfy bed,excellent Location, free wi-fi, laundry, free coffee ..breakfast and dinner with wine/lager.. This place rocks... Giving it a 5 star on my books.. And just a five minute walk to the subway for travellers coming from the airport like us.
hotel_name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown

review_text:
After reading the reviews I was very excited about this hotel, but upon arriving I was underwhelmed by the offerings.
First the positives:
The hotel has a great location, easy walk to Michigan Ave. the breakfast was very good and the fitness center was above average for a hotel. The breakfast was organized well and was less chaotic than ones I have experienced in the past at other hotels.
Second the negatives:
Probably the most annoying thing was the heat in the hotel. At times it felt like a sauna, even in late December. The hotel only has two elevators, which for a good size hotel meant long waits for one. The evening dinner was a bit much and very crowded. Maybe a smaller reception would have made sense, instead of a free for all Old Country Buffett style dinner.
Even with the outstanding positives, I'm not sure I would stay here again.
hotel_name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown

review_text: Great rates and rooms. just blocks of Mich ave great breakfast also has small supper Mon- Thursday
hotel_name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown

review_text: We stayed 1 night at the Magnolia. Overall the stay was great, but the only downfall we had was the thermostat. It took a while for the room to cool, but even with this problem we would return. There was something unique about this hotel.

review_title: Great location, great staff, great choice....
review_text:
My wife and I have just stayed at the James and we were incredibly impressed. The staff were all very helpful, kind and friendly. The rooms were beautiful and housekeeping did a great job of cleaning every day and turning down in the evenings.The bar staff were friendly and knowledgeable too! 
During our stay in Chicago, we ventured in to some of the local hotels e.g. Allerton and Sheraton and although they were both tip-top, we believe that due to its location, amenities and quality of rooms and public areas, the James has to be the winner!!

The location is great and rooms are spacious and clean.
The staff working is great and make you feel at home! Been there 3 times and will for sure return.
Great Hotel.

Very nice property with a good downtown location. The rooftop pool and fitness center are superb and the doormen/shuttle drivers are excellent. Skip the included and abysmal breakfast (sunny d and dried brown omelets) and you'll be much happier.

review_title: Stay like a king, pay like a pauper
review_text: Friendly, helpful staff. Clean, quiet room. Super comfortable beds. Convenient to downtown hotspots. *The* place to stay after a baseball game, night on the town, special occasion, or themed pub crawl!
We loved everything about the hotel. Definitely a must in Chicago.

review_title: We will return to the James!
review_text: We had a very nice stay and found the staff very friendly and helpful. Rooms were nice and location is very convenient to shopping on Michigan Ave.

Stayed 5 nights here. It was actually our second choice but became our first choice for these reasons (1) Located close to public transportation - 1 short block to the Redline subway line and 2 blocks from a bunch of bus lines (2) 2 blocks from the Magnificent Mile - not too far from Water Tower Place (3) comfortable neighborhood - lots of restaurants nearby and it felt pretty safe (4) Connie Wilson (? On the last name) in the dining room always greeted us warmly and watched over us wonderfully - she had the most wonderful countenance and was so helpful! (5) the dining room was handy for breakfast. We had dinner there one night - a nice break from eating out especially the night it rained - grabbed salad/side dishes in the dining room and warmed up leftover Giordano's in our room (6) all the staff was quite friendly and helpful. I'd stay there again and recommend
hotel_name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown

review_text:
We stay regularly at The James.
The service is top notch. 
As for those who complain in other reviews I am quite surprised since we have never experienced anything negative in the many times staying here. The rooms are clean, the location is perfect and they arrange all things to run like a boutique hotel should. We truly love this hotel. The doormen are knowledgeable and courteous.

review_title: Great location, clean room, comfortable vibe and helpful staff.
review_text: Very pleased that the James was in the centre of things yet not on the main street. Staff gave very good recomMendations for dining and sightseeing. Rooms were a good size and very clean. Would definitely return.

I stayed 7 nights in a corner king room in September with my boyfriend. I booked a serene king room through a third party website at 50% off. I emailed the hotel and asked if I could upgrade to a corner king and I would pay the price difference (corner king was not an option on 3rd party site). The hotel responded quickly and upgraded us at no charge. 
Check in was quick and the receptionist was friendly...I think her name was Blair. Our room was on the 14th floor with beautiful views all the way up N State St. Floor to ceiling windows on two walls, flat screen tv, VERY comfortable king bed with excellent quality bedding, mini bar and safe. The bathroom was beautiful also with, as previously mentioned, had a glass wall in the shower, overlooking the bed. If that's not your thing there is a curtain which can be pulled across the glass for privacy. Bathroom products were good and the room was spotless every day.
It is a non smoking hotel so I spent quite some time outside the hotel! The door staff were so friendly and helpful, in particular Caesar and another young male.
The hotel has a bar which was nice for a quiet drink. I also went to Vertigo, a bar on the rooftop of the hotel, which on a Friday night was busy, fun, and lively. Crowd was mostly 20s - 30s. It also has a restaurant called aja but I didn't eat there.
The location is fantastic EVERYTHING is within easy walking distance: mag mile, John Hancock tower, willis tower, navy pier as well as an abundance if bars and restaurants.
I would defiantly stay at this hotel again. The decor is boutique/modern/funky. I loved it.
1 minor complaint...Dana hotel...sort the elevators out!! You have to insert your room card before pressing the floor number, it often took 4-5 attempts before it would read the card. It got a little annoying. But apart from that a perfect hotel, location and atmosphere.
I had a wonderful time staying there for my daughter's wedding. Everything was excellent.
Wonderful stay, great service. Lobby bar and meeting room were great for our wirk meeting-

review_title: Not so good service...but excellent rooms
review_text:
First let me start off by saying that overall I thought the hotel was great as far as the rooms were concerned. It is a really beautiful hotel and it has the best bathroom that I ever saw in a hotel. Please check out my pics from the hotel. Now to the bad stuff. Initially I was going to purchase my stay from expedia as they had a great deal that made the rooms 50% off from the price on the hotels website. When I called reservations to ask a few questions I was informed by the manager that he could price match expedia's rateÂ 
and he added notes to the system about giving me a complimentary upgrade to the next size up from the room I had purchased. As you can imagine I was very pleased. So on the day of arrival the front desk clerk tells me that they dont have anymore rooms to upgrade meÂ for free, so then I proceeded to ask for the $20 upgrade which the reservation manager told me to say. The girl goes to the back office (I assume to ask the onsite manager if she could give me the upgrade) but when she returns she simply says that she cant do it. I was given the smallest room on my first night. I went straight to my room and called reservations to verify how many upgraded rooms were actually available and guess what they had plenty. At this point I now know that they were just unwilling to give me an upgrade because they saw what I had paid for the room in the first place. I called the reservation manager to see what he could do and he promised he would fix it that night. Well he didnt. The next morning I called him again and he acted shocked that the problem had not been fixed. He claimed that he would have the onsite manager contact me. At this point I had lost all faith in him and I went down to speak to the manager myself. They finally sent the assistant manager out to speak with me. After she heard my story she disappears to the back office along with both front desk clerks and the property manager (who by the wayÂ 
never came to speak with me). I assume they spent the next 20 minutes discussing what to do with me. Finally the assistant returns. She at least didnt try to BS me and she admitted that they didnt want to give me an upgrade because they saw how much I had paid for the room. I then explained to her that I was there for a seminar and it was the first year this seminar happened but what willÂ happen when I return home and complain about the service that I received there? The following year when more of my co-workers return to houston for the next conferences the hotel would potentially risk losing business because of their crappy service. The assistant then gave me the upgrade and the rest of the stay was fine.Â 
The amenities were very nice...the cookies and milk were a nice touch to the end of the day. The two free cocktails in the evening were very nice as well. Breakfast was pretty good. The first morning I wasnt impressed but the next day the omelettes were really good. The complimentary car service was a nice touch, although you might not want to ask them for a ride during their busy check out time around 11am because they pretty much ignore you and make you wait an hour for the car service.

On the ground floor you have a great bar, lobby a fantastic restaurant & on the roof another bar with fantastic views great music & friendly staff. It's centrally located to cafes shopping & all other clubs & restaurants what more could you ask for. The rooms are large & very clean with the nicest sheets on the bed. The staff are very very friendly & accommodating

review_title: Location, room size, service and value are all outstanding
review_text:
This hotel has a fantastic location, right in the heart of downtown walking distance to all attractions and the best restaurants and bars. Despite being on the busy Michigan Avenue the room was very quiet and being at the front had a great view.
The room was unbelievably big for a city centre hotel with a good size bathroom, a bedroom, and a large lounge with kitchenette sofa and desk. They also all have washer/dryers which is a great touch.
The staff are all very friendly and helpful. Breakfast is included and is quite passable.
The bes thing about this hotel though is the price you get all this for, it is an absolute bargain.
Great staff, great location. Hotel is very upscale and modern. Room service Was the only real let down. Over 1 hour to deliver and the order was wrong. Very hard to communicate with the staff.

Booked on hotels.com with a great price. Celebrated my wife's birthday. Called the hotel after booking and asked for high floor. We got the top, 25th floor. Great city view. I didn't know the 26th floor had a night club. The music was loud in our room, bass booming. Ear plugs saved the night. So ask for a room no higher than 24 th floor. Club was cool but we didn't want to be clubbing all night. 
Interesting room lay out with glass wall shower view into the room. 
Easy walk the near north shopping yet traffic was light. Used the valet parking.

review_title: Will come back here next summer
review_text: I come to Chicago every summer for my research for these couple of years and used to live in the city. I have stayed at several other hotels but this is the hotel I will use from now on. The door persons and front desk staff were always pleasant even late hours after midnight. The room was somehow outdated but kept cleaness. All the dishes were put in the dishwashers everytime we came back to the hotel. Breakfast and welcome supper with beer and wine were available although I stopped going to breakfast since it lacked the variety after three days. The room was just cozy and comfortable, just the right size for two people. I loved two flat tvs in the bedroom and the living room since my fiancee usually stays up later watching tv. We stayed ten days there and do not any complains but the two things. One is the elevators. They only had two elevators fir the size of the hotel and one time I waited for exact twelve minutes. The other one is we found there was no one at the door at 4 in the morning one time. The door was wide open and anyone can walk into the building. One guy came back from outside. I thought it was a bit strange although it is located in river north, relatively well patrolled area in Chicago. I also want to add that I liked Connie and Tony among the staff. They were always pleasant no matter how busy they seemed. I love the hotel and we will be back next summer for sure!
hotel_name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown

review_text:
So don't expect the Four Seasons and you'll be satisfied that you left with the best possible value for your dollar. Rooms are showing signs of age to be sure, but nothing I could not deal with for a couple nights. 
Pros
Location. - we took advantage of the block walk to Michigan as well as to the CTA red line (best way to museums via bus130 transfer). Plenty of restaurants and groceries nearby. 
Cons
Madhouse in dining room for breakfast. Have patience and you'll get a decent breakfast as part of your hotel rate. I did not try any of the dinners with all the great restaurants in area. 
Rooms need refreshing. Mostly in bathroom/closet area.
hotel_name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown

review_title: One of my favorite hotels except for hassles with key cards not working
review_text: Great hotel overall with interesting rooms and bathrooms, good service and a great restaurant. Had meetings there as well and it worked out well. The key cards were a complete hassle though. Everyone complained that at some point they no longer worked in elevator and/or room.

review_title: A very good buy for your buck spent
review_text: I have spent a very good time in this well placed hotel. The staff is friendly and the service is good. The front desk employee 'Loreena' is very efficient and extremly forthcoming when it comes to helping out customers. She is the good soul of the front desk. Rooms need some freshen up and the hotel needs an additional elevator.
hotel_name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown

review_text: We can't say enough about the Comfort Suites. From the moment we got there, the service was excellent. Everyone was helpful and informative. Our room was beautiful ~ we had several views of the river, plus a complete kitchen and living area - including a washer and dryer. The bathroom is small, but it was so clean, the floor shined. When we were ready to leave, one of the guest ambassadors, David Kavaliunas, helped us load our packages and take them to our car. He was extremely helpful and concerned that we had a nice visit wth them. And we did. We would highly recommend Comfort Suites to anyone who wants a relaxing, enjoyable visit to Chicago and wishes to stay along Michigan Avenue.

1:The phone in living area not working( not fixed during my stay).2:sink in bathroom not drainig water, 3:electrical plug not working in kitchen and finally 4:It was raining and when i reached the hotel in the evening second day of my stay i saw water was dripping from ceiling.
I called reception ( David who was very nice and helpful during my stay) he transfer me to night shift head ( Gaven) and he said there is no maintanence at night and he can not do anything rxcept move me to 4th or 6th floor. I refused to move due to increase noice from street.
 In the morning i went down and inform reception (Eileen) and she promised to either solve the problem or move me to another room in high floors. Around four o'clock I went back to the hotel and she told me that all problems were solved.
Telephone still not working. Plug still not working. Sink Drain was fine and finally water was not dripping any more but ceiling was still wet ( no more rain during my stay to check if it was really fixed).
Other negative points:
No enough space in restaurant to seat specially in the peak time for breakfast. 
Lobby very small and ugly.
No door between bedroom and kitchen.
Room service was not proper:not cleaning the floor whole my suay(6days) and they did not put shampoo and tissue box in the bathroom for 3 consecutive days. I called David for shampoo the third day at night and he sent for me one.

review_title: A Great Find In This Property
review_text:
What a great boutique hotel! I probably wouldn't have come across it except the price was right. Very hip, trendy and has a great sky bar that most people don't even know about. Rooms were modern and I loved the wood floors.
Ate at the restaurant Aja and that was very good as well. I absolutely would stay here again!

I stayed in The James for 2 nights. I was looking for a smaller design/ boutique hotel as I wanted to avoid the standard choices like Hilton etc. Hence, I ended up in The James which made a good impression from the website and the reviews. 
However, it was a very big disappointment. The overall impression of the hotel is that it's already a bit "worn down" and needs a make-over. Despite having booked a kingsize room including a confirmation from the hotel, I was put in a double twin room. Apology of the hotel was very standard and they didn't offer me anything to make up for it despite an upgrade to a room at an additional rate of more than 250 USD a night. 
Up in the room I was shocked from the poor design and the general layout of the room. It wasn't up to design hotel standards at all and I was rather disappointed. However, this might be rather a matter of personal taste. 
The broken window, the broken a/c, the loud noise from the street despite being in 11th floor and the dirt on the flow however aren't a question of personal taste. This was just unacceptable. I complained immediately at reception, however, they couldn't offer me an alternative room. An engineer came to fix the a/c. He didn't really succeed. It was extremely loud when switched on, has only one fan speed and when you switched it off it got hot in the room very quickly (although outside temperatures were in the low 60s). Moreover, the street noise was very loud and you could hear the traffic during day and night. 
Furthermore the walls of the room rather reminded me of a cheap youth hostel instead if an upscale hotel. You could clearly hear when the people on the neighboring room were watching TV or just closing the curtains. The maids on the floor also were very noisy and you could hear them talk from 7am in the morning. Doors and walls are just very thin and just seem to serve as a visual and not voice protection.
In general the staff was rather arrogant and not very helpful. 
Having travelled the whole world and having stayed in countless 4 and 5 star hotels, this experience was one of the more disappointing ones. Clearly no recommendation.

review_title: Rooms not clean, showers impossible to use
review_text:
My wife and I recently stayed here for a week on business. It has great location, being near downtown and the Galleria. But the room was not cleaned properly. We found a bottle of rotten milk in the ice bucket (along with melted ice). The shower used to be a bathtub (with the bathtub removed, so there is no soap holder. This made it impossible to shower or shampoo our hair. Plus, there was black mold in the shower. 
Other hotels in the area cost more, and now we know why.

review_title: Great location and great service for a great price!
review_text: We stayed at the Magnolia for a weekend getaway. My fiance and I were attending an NBA game, and the hotel shuttle ( a luxury SUV) drove us to the game at the Toyota Center, and also picked us back up after the game. The staff was very friendly, and the room was beautiful. Would definitely stay here again, it's our new favorite hotel!
Great central location. Everything within walking distance. Friendly staff. Nice workout facility and spa. Enjoyed my stay very much

I stayed here for a hometown visit in June. I cannot say enough about this hotel. It was stylish, clean, and the staff was super helpful and accomodating. Also, the location was perfect for taking advantage of all the great Chicago shopping and restaurants. I will definitely be staying here again for my next visit this fall!

review_title: Beautiful ambiance, wonderfully accomodating, efficiently located in downtown Houston, perfect for business travel, great valu
review_text:
Beautiful ambiance, wonderfully accomodating, efficiently located in downtown Houston, perfect for business travel, 
great value for the cost and still high class- loved it!

review_title: Great hotel, probably too hip for families.
review_text:
We stayed here with our 4 month old for 3 nights between moves (we are locals) and had a very goodstay, very courteous bellmen, I found the check-in staff to be a bit 'snooty' but all good. 
Our room faced a building with professionals working-make sure you pull the blinds I am certain they can see everything. 
Loved the snack bar options! 
Great area with lots of restaurants to choose from - their restaurant onsite was fabulous.
If driving and want to save on hotel valet parking there are cheaper options in a lot across the street. 
Try the frozen yogurt across the street - so yum.

Hotel davvero carino, non esattemte nuovissimo ma curato nei dettagli. Shampoo,balsamo,crema corpo....cookies sfornati alle 4....wifi gratuita etc...
Personale accogliente.
Un po' lontano dalla metro....la cosa migliore (soprattutto con i bagagli al seguito) Ã¨ prendere il bus 76 e scendere alla fermata clark/diversey.
Difetti: le finestre delle camere non si aprono!!!! E l'aria condizionata Ã© (come ovvio negli States) regolata per riprodurre il freddo polare. Per fortuna nelle camere Ã¨ totalmente regolabile.
La colazione Ã© abbondante ma servita nella hall dove 24/7 c'Ã© caffÃ© e thÃ© a disposizione quindi, se non so vuole bere caffÃ© all'ingresso....bisogna portare il vassoio in camera (il che ha anche i suoi lati positivi)

We had an enjoyable time at The Wit Hotel. Friendly staff and knowledgeable "experience architect" concierge Sean Patrick Wagner who was very helpful. We had breakfast included in The Wit Package at the State and Lake Restaurant that was awesome!

review_title: Nice bathroom, worn room and inconsistent (and unprofessional) staff
review_text:
I was truly looking forward to my stay at theWit, but was left dissatisfied, particularly because of a subpar staff. 
The good: i stayed in a king suite-1202 (intrinsically tied to the bad described below). the room was nice (nothing spectacular) and the bathroom was beautiful and moder-nice tub, great shower, awesome view, large, etc. The toiletries were beyond the quality of other Hilton brand toiletries. The tv was large and (thankfully!) wasn't controlled using lodge net (those who travel know how annoying/slow lodge net is). The iPod doc would have been great had it been functional (missing electrical plug). Unlike other reviewers, I found the elevators very fast and efficient. Finally, the fitness center was large (for a boutique-like hotel) and had good, new equipment. 
The bad/ugly: There are better hotels in Chicago for a lower price, and all that I've stayed in have a more professional staff. The staff was inconsistent, inattentive and unprofessional. Examples:
1. I had numerous large holes in my fitted bed sheet (thereby exposing the mattress) and had pillows that smelled like feces. In spite of notifying the hotel concierge and housekeeping, the bedding wasn't changed and neither were the pillows. I woke up with a terrible rash on my face and need to see a doctor (on Chritmas, no less!). 
2. The staff was particularly crass late at night...cursing in the lobby, discussing inappropriate and insulting topics, not greeting guests, etc. 
3. I was yelled at by staff for trying to use the side lobby door at night. 
4 Check in was annoying and slightly degrading. Although the hotel was rather empty, I had to practically beg to get an upgrade to a nicer room (as a Hilton gold member, this was disappoingting considering Marriott and Starwood readily upgrade me based on my gold statuses, and theWit had plenty of upgrades available for the night). The manager (I'm assuming) came to the front desk and allowed for the upgrade, but it was like pulling teeth with them (at one point I had to mention the it is Hilton policy to upgrade if available...concierge floor or not). So much for hhonors!!! I'm 2 stays away from diamond..this solidified my decision to focus on other chains that actually care about loyalty). 
Overall, I wanted to love this hotel, but didn't because of the staff (and i NEVER have complained about the staff in any of my other reviews). If you're looking for simply a nice bathroom and hip bar, this is a great hotel. But the rooms are "worn" in spite of this being a new property. The staff is mediocre at best and from my experience, doesn't care about the customer.

Stayed here for one night on a very busy weekend - the hotel is very central just off Michigan Avenue which makes it ideal for exploring Chicago when you only have limited time. However, there are better hotels in this price range a few blocks further away which would be preferable for a longer stay. The room was nice, not spectacular. The bed was very comfy though.

I stay at Comfort Suites all over the US. This one was a treat. I appreciated the huge room, full kitchen and spectacular views. My husband and I have stayed at the comfort inn not too far away which is also nice, but claustrophobic compared to this lovely place. The front desk staff was gracious and the valet parking came off without a hitch. My only complaint was breakfast: far too crowded to enjoy. Great stay!
Very nice hotel , very friendly staff and very well located

Having checked out of the pokey holiday inn we found this and what a find. Fantastic room, excellent service, free cycle hire. The bar was full of people full of themselves but isn't every big city ? After realising we could afford to stay there, the staff were very attentive. Would stay again if in chicago

Our family had the pleasure of being at the James the week before lalapalooza. It was quite busy, yet the staff was friendly and helpful the entire trip. It us to be noted that this attitude and atmosphere is no doubt a reflection of how it is ran by Patrick Hatton. As the general manager he has this place running smoothly. We will definitely be returning as we do every year. As everyone has mentioned this place is clean, priced well and is perfectly located. This is the place to stay if you are picky about cleanliness. Thanks for making our family trip enjoyable.
