This is one of the loudest hotels I have ever stayed in. The customer service was horrible. When I called to ask about moving to a room that was quieter they told me I shouldn't be hearing anything. It is in a convenient location but so are many other hotels in Chicago.

review_title: Great location, balconies, and top floor.
review_text:
Standard upscale hotel with small (20x10ft) rooms and still comfortable. The rooms are chic and probably best suited or honeymooners and couples. 
Overnight, valet parking is pricey at $38/night. The showers are nice along with the view. The beds are comfortably soft and pillows huge, but not best for long, back-enduring walks around the loop. 
Nearby is Magnificent Mile, shopping, 3:00am bars, and plenty to eat. Please note the rooms Do Not cool below 70F although the thermostat promises better.

The Wit is in a wonderful location for tourists and business travelers. The property is fairly new an kept up well. The room was definitely one of the cleanest I've stayed in. Modern feel to the hotel and the rooms. Nice bathrooms and generous amenities. My only complaint is that there was no coffee maker in the room. When I asked about coffee I was told "we serve breakfast on the second floor" in a condensing manner. There is a Dunkin' about a block an a half away. Also, I asked to borrow an iPhone charger and they wanted me to leave my phone with them at the front desk to charge. I thought the coffee and charger factors were rather petty for such a nice hotel. In any case, the $120 rate was, I felt, a great deal and the location is hard to beat.

Dana is unbelievable value for the price. Location for shopping is terrific . Concierge is very helpful. The door people make you feel very welcome!!
The little touches make the stay more comfortable.
The spa is excellent value and the gym has ultra modern equipment allbeit a bit small.
Will definately stay again!!
A great hotel for a romantic night, or to celebrate a wedding. Don't count on excellent breakfast, but the rooms, and appearance of the hotel are very nice.
Great long weekend in the windy city! I will be back!

Let me start off by saying that I am an employee at a Choice hotel. I know what guests expect from a hotel staff and the hotel itself. I was very happy with my stay here. I only stayed for two nights, but didn't want to leave! 
Location: It was smack dab in the middle of everything. Navy Pier is a five minute bus ride away. The train station is literally a thirty second cab ride away. There is tons of shopping and food choices within walking distance. The water taxis and Wrigley Building are less than a five minute walk away. The Walgreens and Subway next door made it easy to save money on quick meals and drinks to keep in the room. 
The Rooms: While the common areas are somewhat small, the rooms are huge! It literally felt like I had my own apartment in the city. They must have been apartments back in the day, as it is an older building. I had already expected the smaller areas, as it's a hotel in the downtown area, where everything is cramped. Imagine my surprise to walk into my room! I was placed on the 11th floor and had a corner room facing the water. Beautiful! The rooms are also very clean and included all the necessities, including a fridge, dishwasher, microwave, cooking utensils, and stove. The cleaning staff even washed my dishes for me! 
The Staff: Professional, friendly, and quick! They made sure to get my two rooms close together even though I forgot to request that. They even held our luggage for us for a few hours on the day we checked out, so that we could go to a couple museums before we left. 
The Value: I paid an employee rate, so it was worth the money a thousand times over. I know these rooms usually go for a couple hundred. Worth every penny! The breakfast is great. If you're looking for location and value, stay here! 
The Cons: The building has 26 floors and you may have to wait a couple minutes for an elevator (there is two of them), but not really a big deal. The breakfast area is small, but also just a minor detail. 
All in all, I had an awesome stay and will definitely stay again if I come back to Chicago!

We stayed at the fairfield inn over memorial day weekend and enjoyed it very much. The location was excellent, price was good, and hotel was Clean and modern. The free breakfast was nice. Plenty of selection. 
The only negative is that some heavy rains caused a leak in our room so housekeeping came and put a large, noisy fan in our room to dry it. A minor inconvenience but had to mention it. Also, I wish there was a pool. My 3year old son would have enjoyed that. 
Overall, we had a good experience.

After reading good reviews about I booked a 5 night stay. Checked in late bit called early in the day to assure we'd have a roll away as well as the pull out sofa for 2 teens. They somehow had us booked for two rooms instead. Got that sorted out and arrived around 10 pm. Checked in and waited for our luggage... Finally went down and got it ourselves. The room was a little grungy, furniture shabby, and discovered a suspicious stain on the duvet cover. Ewww. Called for a new duvet cover which was delivered and unceremoniously handed to me. FYI it's kinda gross to have to change the duvet cover in a hotel. Next day tried to iron a dress for dinner and the iron didn't work. Called for a replacement, waited a while, called again and was brought another iron which also didn't work. Third time was a charm. Oh boy. Too bad we paid in advance. Won't be staying here again.
hotel_name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown

review_title: Grate hotel. Even better people. Top notch concirge service from Mandy Bates.
review_text: Really enjoyed my stay. Very friendly people. I have no problem recommending them to friends.
Excellent base camp for magnificent mile. Rooms are modern, well equipped, but small. Possibly overpriced though. If booked with discount could be reasonable value for money

Stayed at The James based on reviews from this site and one other. Showing teenage son Chicago for first time, my umpteenth visit to the windy city. Also attending 2 music festivals in the area. Front desk upgraded us to a junior suite right away, probably due to lack of 2-bed room. First room we were given smelled as though the previous guest was very sick and was given a new room right away. Consulted concierge first night regarding music festival next day and was given a very negative review of the festival and discouraged from attending--all I wanted was directions! Next morning asked for directions to 2nd festival from concierge who seemed put out to speak to a "mom" type and was given directions heading the opposite direction from the venue. Called manager on duty who responded with a comped taxi to the venue, but unfortunately this didn't entirely solve the problem and actually made some things worse. After this last straw, we used our IPad and IPhone to help us find our way around rather than consulting the concierge desk. This is probably a fascinating hotel for the average high-roller, expense account wielding guest, but I can't recommend it for tourists, even though the location is perfect for downtown. Won't stay again.
It was a very good hotel, the manager jackie frank is a great assest to the company, it was a very wonderful stay for me and my family

review_title: Terrific place to spend time in Chicago!
review_text: This hotel has a great location. Only 15 minutes or so to all major sights (walking time). Staff is very helpful and friendly. Front desk answered all our questions. Rooms are clean and spacious. Breakfast has a good variety of food choices. Thanks to Connie for making our last morning so enjoyable! We will definitely stay here again.
hotel_name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown

review_title: HÃ´tel correct mais trop bruyant et petitdejeuner insuffisant
review_text: Correct pour le prix mais les bruits de voitures et avions dÃ©gradent l'ensemble (pas de double vitrage).

We stopped in Chicago after a trip to Costa Rica. We stayed there from June 30-July 3.
The James has two things going for it. The location and their employees. The rooms are clean and comfortable with a modern twist but very small bathroom and no closets. Waiting for a small cramped elevator wasn't the best but for a chic hotel with ultra "cool" people, it brought back memories. Our view was of a side of a building. A Hugh plus is the location. Doesn't get better. Great breakfast place across the street, shopping, short walk to.heart of the city. Scott, the tall concierge made our trip(hope the name is correct) . He sent us to a superb family run restaurant by the University. Maid service excellent as was front desk. Rates good for two nights, expensive for a Saturday.

I'm visiting from the UK so don't know what the Wit chain/concept was; the tripadvisor rating at time of booking was way up.
The rooms are clean and well appointed look very nice but still
Have coperate feel.. Roomservice excellent And front desk too.
The main problem with this hotel is that it feels like a giant nightclub with bouncers on the door and roped lines forming in the small foyer at night. You can come in late afternoon and find a DJ spinning decks. The whole raisin d'Ãªtre of this hotel seems to be this theme.
As a hotel guest you feel you are there as a supporting activity!
On the first night with Jet lag they assigned me a studio suite below the roof night club. I might as well have been in the club! The front desk was very sweet and gave me a free nights stay for that night and I got moved.
Another dissapointment is the breakfast arrangement in the bar which has a fixed very heavy menu with no buffet in a dark dingy atmosphere, again clubby. It also
Lacks any substantial quiet lounge area for guests
I have stayed in cool hotels before but I really didn't like the concept here 
Having said that once inside my room I was happy

I travel for a living. The staff really makes you feel at home, and everyone greets you. It's great because if you're a priority points member, you get even more perks. The rooms are always clean, and the hotel seems like it would cost more. I've paid more at other places and have much less quality and friendliness. I'll stay here every time I work in Houston. Plus, it's convenient to restaurants, bars, shopping, etc.

review_title: This hotel impressed my family so much that we will always stay at a Homewood suites wherever we go.
review_text:
I don't know where to begin. When we arrives we were greeted by Sami and Jonah. They were greatly helpful to us and even offered to store our roof rack away so that we could park locally. They both had great attitudes and always asked how we were and what they could do for us everyday that we saw them. 
 The front desk ladies were great too. There was a mixup on the dates that was sort of my fault since I'm the one who scheduled us. I had called in and asked them to change the arrival date and it did not get changed. This seemed bad at the time bc the hotel cancelled our reservation and charged me for two nights. However, the front desk reversed everything and got us back in a room lickety split. 
 The house cleaners did a great job. I never noticed that they had been there but I could see the clean sheets towels and surfaces. 
 The only negatives I had about the hotel had to do with our bathroom. There is no entrance from the main space so I had to walk through the bedroom where my son was sleeping to get to the bathroom. The tub didn't drain well, the light flickered and the tub needs those safety traction stickers on the bottom. My child slipped in the shower. 
 When I complained to the front desk they offered me a free nights stay. 
 The pool and gym were ok. 
 The best part of this hotel was the complimentary food. This saved us so much money and the food was of good quality. They did not try to skimp on it. The waitress Connie, i think, was awesome. She remembered us everyday and helped us get our table just the way we liked it. When something happened or someone was ill, she asked about us the next day. When there were problems with the meal she had them fixed immediately and made sure we knew when it was fixed. I was impressed with the service from a hotel employee. She could have been less helpful and attentive like other staff I have seen before but she chose to be great.
hotel_name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown

review_title: A very nice well priced hotel that is exceptionally determined to make your stay 5 star.
review_text: Well located clean friendly and amenable. We enjoyed our stay and will return there for all future stays in houston. Well worth the money.

The location and service at this hotel is great! Carlos at the front desk was a great help along with everyone else. Everytime we needed directions or recommendations they were so nice and willing. They offer breakfast every morning which was nice. It is served till 10am which was great ,even at 9:30 they were still bringing food out. The rooms are nice and large. We were across from the elevators which was not a problem at all. Overall this hotel is great for the price and location we would diffidently stay they again !

review_title: Bad Service - Poor excuse for a business-grade hotel
review_text:
Was there recently for one night for a conference. 
Tried to check-in at 5:30pm (the published check-in was 3pm), they said my room wasn't ready, where as others coming after me were assigned rooms. Was given a dummy door key card and asked to chill in the lounge on the 32nd floor and that they would call on may cell as soon as the room was ready. I chilled there until 8pm, no call, so went out for dinner. Came back at 9:30pm and asked if my room was ready. The gal said of course yes and give me a key. When asked why no one called me, she just shrugged. 
No, my troubles did not end there. I went to the room and opened the door only to find someone else in the room. Came back to the lobby, then they apologized and gave me another room. I said I was not going to walk-in on somebody else again, so they sent someone with me to open the new room. For all my "trouble" they reduced my bill by about 40%. It was definitely not worth the trouble they put me thru. 
Very bad experience.

SchÃ¶ne suiten..wunderbare betten..toller Service.
Absolut gute Lage an der magnificant Mile..nahe am Hancock Center..Water Tower..und zu saemtlichen Shops.
Super netter Service.
Am besten am loyality Programm des Hotels teilnehmen dann gibt es jeden morgen 2 getraenke und einen kleinen smoothie vor die zimmertuer.

review_title: Great location and rooms, a few faults though
review_text:
The hotel is really well located for exploring Chicago being less than half a mile from the Magnificent Mile and Millenium Park. We stayed in a King Spa Room on the 10th floor which overlooked the river and didn't suffer from the noise issues other people have mentioned. The room was a good size with a huge bath tub and separate shower. The staff were really friendly and helpful.
There are some negatives though. Housekeeping was a bit hit and miss with basic things like toilet rolls not replaced and one day the room didn't get cleaned at all. You shouldnt have to phone up and remind them to do these things when you're paying over $300 a night.
The room is pretty pricey so you would expect it to have everything you need. However, toiletries in the bathroom weren't enough for 2 people and there was no bath gel provided which, given the bath is the main reason why you'd book the spa room, this seemed a bit tight. The hotel seemed to charge a lot for things other comparable hotels would provide for free such as web access and bottles of water. Also, there's a $25 restocking charge for the mini bar even if you just take one item out of it.
We ate in the hotel restaurant and the first time our waiter was brilliant, very accommodating and helpful. The second time however the service was poor with the waitress bringing out our main courses 5 mins after bringing out our starters and trying to cram them on the table, and forgot to pick up our drinks order from the bar so we had to fetch them ourselves. Didnt eat there again after that.
It's a great hotel but for the price there probably are better places to stay.

Terrific suite hotel in a great location. The corner room was very spacious for our group of 5. Wonderful views of michigan ave and the river. We took the train to chicago, walked the few blocks to the hotel, dropped our bags off hours before checkin and went shopping. Staff was very accomodating with their secure storage room for luggage, quickly bring us extra bedding and towels, and storing our bags again after check out until we were ready for the train again. The kitchen area was nice to refrigerate our leftovers and enjoy cocktails before heading out for the night. The hotel corridor and elevators are not the best, but can be overlooked since their purpose is only to get you to and from our room and the lively downtown. This is our new favorite place since the price can't be beat, location was ideal for train station, millinium park and shopping.

review_title: What ever happened to pleasant customer service, at least a smile?
review_text: It was very disappointing experience. We had expected better being an SPG member. When we walked into the room, it smelled like smoky bar. We'll can't really fault the hotel but instead of offering us a room, they offered to ionize for about 40 minutes. Having a child with us, we insisted on a different room. There was some confusion with the bellman and the front desk, and when the bellman came he was very unpleasant. He ragged about it and was in a hurry, and barked out directions to us to follow. We took a "nice" tour of the back of house and frieght elevators. We did not feel like guests. We went to the Java bar and our server was not very happy also, does anyone smile at this hotel? We are really sorry to have bothered these people on our vacation.

We went with Homewood based on reviews on trip advisor. They were right. The Service was spectacular. Starr went out of her way to make our experience great. We arrived at 8 am and though our room wasn't ready she found other, better options that allowed is to get in right away and start our fun. Location is amazing steps to plenty of bars, restaurants and the red line. The Bellman were great too. We WILL be back. Great value.
hotel_name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown

review_text: I booked this hotel through Hotwire and didn't know where I'd actually be staying before putting in my credit card information. I must say I was pleasantly surprised! The room was comfortable, very clean, and had everything I needed including free wi-fi, a small fridge and a microwave. The beds were very comfy. The hotel staff was excellent, especially the concierge, Mandy. She wentout of her way to make both of my stays at that location free from worry. The housekeeping staff was excellent and friendly. The bar staff was also very accommodating. If there were any downsides to this property it would be the pool. Even though it was clean and well maintained, the location near the busy highway caused for a noisy experience. Since I'm not much of a pool person anyway, I was not bothered by it enough to reduce my rating. I would definitely stay at this lcation on a return visit.

I stayed here with a few friends, the hotel is excellant. The rooms are superb with some great views. The hotel staff are helpful and friendly. The roof top bar was good in Jan and will be even better in the summer.
One to recommend

review_title: Great location, service & breakfast for the price
review_text: Not a four star but great location if you're a tourist. Included breakfast is very good. Front desk has been friendly and helpful. Rooms a bit dated but clean, beds comfy. FYI, if you need a wine bottle opener bring it with you. They're not in the otherwise well furnished kitchens and you can't get one from the front desk...also hard to find to buy locally! We finally found one at 7-11..

We stayed 4 nights over thanksgiving holiday wweekend. The location is good, great service and friendly employees. We had a slow valet experience but were compensated by complementary breakfast. Overall it was a great vacation and we would stay here again

I was incredibly disappointed with the hotel. Staff was not friendly. Additionally we asked for our room to be cleaned and on arrival back from our wedding, the room was not. It was a complete embarressment. Valet was rude in the morning when we couldn't find our ticket and just watched us with our bags. When I checked in they had canceled our entire reservation and not the one night requested. It was a complete waste of our money. Not worth the stay! The sick part was I was there for my wedding night and no one of staff bothered to say ANYTHING! How obvious is it when you are standing there in your dress?! The hotel is cute from the outside but rooms are small and overpriced. You are better off going down the street to another hotel.

I loved everything!! The rooms pool lobby and all other things were great!The only things I didn't like were u had to pay for internet and there was no complimentary breakfast but otherwise a great place to stay

Booked a one night midweek stay a couple weeks prior to our trip. The TA reviews were once again spot on and helpful. The suite was large and had a view of Michigan Avenue. There was a spacious sitting area with a chair, sofa, flat panel tv, and work desk. The kitchen was equipped with a frig, small stove/oven, microwave and dishwasher, coffee maker and all pots/ pans and utensils needed to cook and eat a meal with. The sink had a large counter that accommodated two barstools for dining. The bedroom also had a wall mounted tv, roomy closet, a stackable w/d and iron. The bed was comfortable and a choice of feather or foam pillows. The bathroom is small but not an issue for us. We did not partake in the breakfast downstairs but the room was full of folks who did. It offered the standard fare both hot and cold. We would indeed stay again at this hotel if we return to Chicago. It had easy access to transit and shopping. The front desk was helpful and printed our documents when the guest printer was out of ink. If you are looking for clean and affordable, the Comfort Suites is a great option.

review_title: Beautiful hotel, friendly staff, great location.
review_text:
I visited the Crown Plaza for a meeting recently and was sincerely impressed with the property. The decor was modern, well appointed and very clean. The staff was accommodating and professional, the concierge was more than helpful with recommendations. 
I have worked in hotels and events and consider myself a hospitality snob. I can honestly say I was impressed and would recommend this property and it's great location.
Rachel
EventCraze
Owner

review_title: Pay just a little but get a lot!
review_text: I'm sitting on my uber-comfy king sized bed as I write this review. My cheesecake is staying fresh in my in-room fridge and I'm going to eat the rest of my dinner after warming it up in my in-room microwave. Just a short walk to the Mag Mile this is a gem of a hotel...convenient, clean, comfortable, close, and courteous! Anyone who complains about street noise clearly doesn't know what it means to be in a world class urban area. Paid very little and got a lot!

Yes, close to fire station but a good central location for shopping and good eats. Room was clean and staff were friendly and helpful. Good free breakfast on 2nd floor. Parking is $40+ but they were prompt in getting our car. I would stay here again.

review_title: Great location and service!! Big rooms
review_text: We couldn't have been happier with our stay. Close to red line and shopping. Huge rooms, and best of all service with a smile. Thank you most of all to Toni at the front reception desk for being so warm and welcoming. You really made our stay!!!
hotel_name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown

review_title: Great Hotel - But they lost my package
review_text: This is a really nice hotel in a great location. The staff is outstanding and the hotel is neat and clean. They did lose a package that was never found but verified delivered. I was out of luck on that one as the staff called and were at a loss on what to do. They have a nice fitness center that does not open early enough in the morning for early birds. Shulas, the restaurant downstairs is really good with great vibe. Pricey but does have a happy hour. Rooms were clean and updated. Usual amenities, no free Internet.

Just stayed 3 nights at The James. Pleasant and helpfull staff (the concierge gives out excellent suggestions for restaurants and other activities). On a rainy night, when taxis were hard to find, we got a ride to our restaurant with the complimentary car. Thanks to Craig, our very nice driver. 
The rooms are more minimalist in decor but inviting. Super clean. The bed is so comfortable. And it's only a few steps from Michigan Ave. 
Do get a mojito at the lobby bar (part of the steakhouse situated in the hotel).

The service is solid and it is a large, grand hotel, but there is something lacking. The rooms are slightly drab and the lighting isn't great, but they are quite comfortable. No complaints, but it wouldn't be my top choice for hotels in Chicago.

I was thre couple weeks ago and this is one of the best hotels I have stayed at...The service is very good..everybody is so atentive and friendy...the location is just perfect,you have everything around in downtown are walking distance...It is definily my first choice when I go bck to Chicago....

This was my first visit to Chicago, and I had made some requests prior to arrival (early check-in, high flr, view). All of these requests were easily accomodated. We were greeted by a trainee who obviously had already looked at our requests and voiced them to us ( I believe her name was Cynthia). We loved the river view that we had. The restaurant staff was amazing! We came ten min before lunch ended and they still treated us so nice. The next morning during breakfast, we were welcomed back. It was very impressive that they remembered us. Keep in mind, we were there while they had a large convention or something going on. We didn't spend too much time in the hotel, but those few interactions were wonderful. 
It is also in a good location if you like walking to the Mag mile and Mil Park. We did have to cab it to the nearest train station, but it was not much.

Everything about The James breathes Class, from the moment you enter it at it's terrific downtown location to the time you leave. How can an entire staff offer such superb service in so unobtrusive a manner? The rooms, particularly the Loft in which we stayed, are unique, everything is prompt, and The Prime House restaurant has a succulent menu. Their front desk folks can direct you anywhere in the city and offer opinions if you need them. Like I said, a Classy hotel.

review_title: A dissenting opinion - not the greatest
review_text:
My family stayed here without hesitation based on really great trip advisor ratings. This was not a terrible property, but it was not up to the level of most places I have stayed in Chicago or places I have stayed based on trip advisor with no where near as good ratings.
The positives were: staff was freindly and helpful, location was exceptional particularly if you plan museum grant park type stuff. There are a fair number of decent dining options right near by. The room we had (a suite for family of 4) was entirely functional, and had laundry and kitchen in room. The breakfast is about what youd see at most any Hampton or Holday Inn - but crowded the days we were here. No real complaints about any of this.
But this place has some serious drawbacks. It is very cramped throughout (though less so in the rooms proper) the elevators are very small, often stuffed to capacity during our stay and often slow to arrive. The view from our room was awful, but we knew that coming in and this did not bother us much. The lobby is not hideous but rather follows the very small, even claustrophobic, and drab theme of the whole place.
The basic problem with this place besides that it is cramped is that it feels quite long in the tooth. Hallways are kind of puke green with traces of a bad paint job on hardware fixtures. Loose door knobs and carpet well toward end of usefully life. Dated wallpaper and furniture. Our room did not feel all that clean and had a very soft lumpy mattress. I found somebody
s gummy bears between the headboard and the mattress when the remote fell in there.
This place has location and basic functionality, but other than that feels like a low end property and not worth the hundreds per night we paid. I was not aghast but I wont stay here again, either.

I stayed here on business in April and was looking forward to it based on the photos online. Overall, sadly, I wasn't impressed...while the service hit the mark, the quality of the room was below the mark. I've had far better experiences at a similar price point at several other Chicago properties within the same area.
It wasn't horrific. Like I said, the service hit the mark...fast and polite check-in, helpful doormen and bellmen, desire to serve. Very well done on that front. The gym, while in a basement, was complete with a great range of equipment. The bed was quite comfy.
But there were issues. The rooms are glorified IKEA. Totally cheap furniture that was badly worn. Chips in the coffee table, hinges broken, scuff marks, etc. And the room had no desk! While that might be fine for a leisure traveler, it is annoying for a business traveler. Rooms also had a barren look..all white, no wall hangings, brown carpet. I love modern design, but this place was put together on the cheap and the result is that it is showing wear and tear very quickly. 
Lobby is also a "scene." Not to the point where you don't feel welcome as a guest, like at some places, but combine the cramped quarters with the noise and I didn't find it very relaxing.

review_title: How did they get it so wrong?
review_text:
What appears to be a lovely, well designed hotel is simply a facade for a badly run hotel, that, in my opinion should only have three stars. 
To be honest we did no have any complaints with our room, except for s noisy air conditioner and a poky bathroom, with a tub designed for a toddler, not a five foot six woman of average build.
The general upkeep of the common areas left a lot to be desired, it took 48 hours for housekeeping to vacum up plasterboard scattered on the carpet on the level 12 lift lobby, and only after we complained.
However what annoyed us the most, the breakfast vouchers and the $14 dollar limit plus tax and tip allocated to each guest. What a load of rubbish, that gets you a coffee and some eggs, not even a juice, and if you want tea that will be $6. I have travelled all over the world and never experienced such a ridiculous system, that not even the staff could explain it properly and still managed to get wrong twice. In addition, if I paid for breakfast with my hotel reservation so why am I then charged tax again, when it is already charged for in my room rate? Clearly this hotel is all about income revenue, and not about customer experience, otherwise why would you? Perhaps they need to learn from more successful hotel chains, I am just grateful we are not staying with the James in NYC.

review_title: In a few words... Very Underwhelming
review_text:
I have spent the last month traveling around Europe and Canada and was truly disappointed with this Sheraton property. On arrival we were treated to hundreds of people attempting to check in for a conference. I am traveling with my elderly mother and so far had no issue with getting twin rooms. Even though we requested a twin room they were unable to accommodate our request due to the conference. The front desk advised there was no option other than a fold out bed. 
After finally checking in we had to battle the elevator lobby to get to our floor. It took at least 5 minutes to get into an elevator. This has continued every time you want to leave the hotel or return you are bombarded with a wall of people that are Attending the conference. I have had to help my mother on numerous occasions to get in and out of the elevator safely due to other guests who push and shove to get in and out of the elevator.
I would have to say the rooms are very tired and dated, not the standard of Sheraton nor upto the price paid. Having stayed in similar rated hotels in Canada and Europe, this hotel is underwhelming. Like other tripadvisor reviews we were treated to hairs throughout the bathroom...not clean at all.
I would never recommend this hotel. To this end we decided to check out early and find another hotel that provided a better standard and could accommodate a twin room.

The plus:
Great location; beautiful design of the room which was quite big; Nice view over marina city from the 12th floor; silent (for Chicago!) room. Excellent valet service (expensive but difficult to do without if you have a car).
To improve:
Unbelievable that an hotel of this category does not offer free wifi whereas every basic motel does!
You have to be on a high floor to avoid noise from the El but not to high to avoid the huge noise from the skybar on 27th floor (12th is perfect)
The skybar is a great disapointement: overcrowded at all times; presence in the lobby and elevators of screaming crowd of overdressed and ridiculous girls wearing high shoes they don t know to walk with:-) funny to see but rapidly annoying for hotel guests

review_title: Great location, good service, needs updating.
review_text: Stayed here over the weekend with my kids to do some shopping and sightseeing. Booked my reservation via priceline and then called the hotel directly to inquire about requesting a room with two double beds as I know priceline can't guarantee a certain room type. Was promptly told by the operator that I was booked in a king room and there was nothing they could do since the hotel was sold out. Ok fine, I know sometimes that happens with priceline.... However, when I went to check in, I inquired again about the two double beds and the girl at the desk said there were several rooms with doubles available and even asked what floor I preferred. Made me feel like the first person I talked to didn't even bother to check. We had a room on the 17th floor. It wasn't a river view room, but the view was ok nonetheless. What I did notice immediately was that the room looked very outdated and a bit dingy. The window treatments and wallpaper were particularly in need of an update. The bed and bed linens were nice though. Very clean, and they were all white, including the comforter, so that's a plus. The beds were also quite comfortable. Once we got settled, we ordered brownie sundaes from room service. They arrived promptly, but the brownies were stale tasting and there was hardly any ice cream with them. For $40 for 3 sundaes, I would've expected something delicious. The hotel also does have a large fitness center and a pool, which we didn't utilize, but I'm sure my kids would have loved it if we had the time, and many downtown Chicago hotels don't have pools. Overall, our stay here was nice. The location was excellent and very convenient to Michigan ave shopping and navy pier. The hotel was listed by priceline as a 4 star, which puts it in the category with the Four Seasons and the Ritz.... I would give it more like 2.5 stars in comparison to those properties. The accomodations were adequate for the purpose of our trip, but if you're looking for something upscale, this isn't the best choice.

review_title: Great location but is it a hotel or nightclub?
review_text: The location of this hotel is great walking diastance to everything worth seeing and the train directly to O'Hare airport. Nice rooms and friendly staff. My only issue with this hotel is on thursday,Friday & Saturday nights they have a night club on the 25th floor and preference to the lifts are given to the non guests going up to the club. I along with other guest waiting to get back up to their rooms had to 10 mins before I questioned the priority with the security. The other was being stopped each time I re-entered the hotel as security were preoccupied with stopping persons from entering the the hotel via the wrong entrance for the club. Would I stay there again yes probably.

review_title: Nice room, good breakfast... Views to a narrow dark alley
review_text:
Good hotel, free wifi, excellent breakfast you can pick up on your way down, big rooms. We were satisfied. 
Only drawback, there is a rage number of rooms without a view, just offices in front, no light during the day.

review_title: Wow what a hotel! Stay here, play here.
review_text: I have stayed in many hotels in Chicago and this is my new favorite. Hip, clean, fun, beautiful, Eco-friendly. Great location, close to Millennium Park, Michigan Ave and the River. Awesome ambient nature sounds in the halls. Service was outstanding and made us feel special. ROOF is the best rooftop bar in the city and it is on top of this hotel! This IS a trendy hotel but friendly and a great value. Stay here, play here!

This hotel should be called the Amalfi Experience. This is an unpretentious hotel that does everything to make you feel comfortable from the doorman to the front desk. Service is the best. The location is perfect. The beds are extremely comfortable with a selection of pillows to suit anyone. This is my favorite hotel IN THE WORLD!

I have stayed at this hotel twice this year and they never disappoint! If you are looking for clean, spacious rooms located right on Michigan Ave for a great price then this hotel is perfect for you. Thanks Comfort Suites for a great stay!

I have been to a lot of hotels around the world, but by far this place tops in service. The staff are so friendly, they go out of their way to make your stay great... Add free wifi, pop corn and 24 hour free coffee service, and nice breakfast. Would definitely come back again.

review_title: Balcony Suites and Bang for Your Buck!!!
review_text: My husband and I stayed at the Comfort Suites on Michigan Avenue for our 5th Wedding Anniversary over Memorial Day weekend. We had a huge suite with an AMAZING balcony overlooking Michigan Ave and the Chicago River. We were welcomed by the super-friendly and helpful staff (Gavin, David, Steve, Aes and Aaron were the best!) and couldn't believe how spacious our room was. We had a full kitchen (dishwasher, microwave and a stove) AND a washer and dryer in our room! We were in walking distance to everything we wanted to do. Stay at the Comfort Suites if you want to experience the magnificence of Michigan Ave without the pretension!
Good location (close To baby pÃ­er and Michigan Ave), excelent staff. Got a Great price because of a medical meeting (US$ 300). Wonderfull view from the Room. An excellent bed, like other Sheratons.
Every employee I encountered was very professional and made me feel like my stay there was very important.

Hotel was clean, spacious, good location and good value for money. Only criticism I would say is that it's right next to the fire department, therefore can be a little noisy at times, certainly not enough to stop me coming back.
Overall, very good.
Stay here when you go to Chicago. I have been to many, and this one rocks!

Stayed 1 night. Great service. The minibar in the room has sensors so don't remove anything unless you're planning on paying for it. You can request a fridge if you need it. We didn't read the warnings and got charged. Front desk was nice enough to reverse charges. Staying at the hotel gets you to the front of the line for the Roof which is nice. Really cool bar/nightclub but drinks are expensive. $14 for 1 mixed drink and beer was around $6. Cookies at check in are delicious. Location is perfect. All theaters and State street shopping are a few steps away. Potbelly's and Wow Bao are just across the street. Didn't try restaurant so I can't comment. I did order fries from room service and they came on a very nice tray.and tasted great. Had a great time and overall I loved the hotel.
Modern room, nice new. Hvac was broken but manager gave us a bottle of comp. Sparkling wine.

The Wit experience is truly awesome and just what I was looking for in a great value boutique hotel in a great location in Chicago. From a simple check-in to the upgraded King suite with an amazing view to the genuinely friendly staff. I give. It 5 stars and when I am in Chicago, I will stay at The Wit. Great job, everyone!!

During a recent visit to Chicago, I stayed at the Amalfi and found it to be a very pleasant experience. The location was terrific and very close to many great restaurants and obviously Michigan Ave. I'm a stickler for cleanliness and this hotel passed my test. I look forward to a return visit again later this year.
Stayed here in connection with a conference. Very nice hotel.

review_title: Not the newest but certainly value for money
review_text: We, family of 4, stayed here for 5 nights and loved it. The decor is a little dated and the hallways were uneven but we didn't stay here for the decor! The location is perfect, in the middle of the mag mile and close to CTA buses and trains, restaurants and grocery stores. Didn't use any of the facilities like pool, laundry or fitness so can't comment. Breakfast was great and only crowded on our last day for some reason. Kickback meal at night was adequate and free so who's to complain! All day tea and coffe in lobby available and very handy. Popcorn in room was a winner for our 2 kids, 8 & 14yrs. No room safe but we didn't have a problem, just locked up our valuables in our cases each day. Fast check out service great, didn't have to go to the lobby at all! Doormen very helpful and were prompt and helpful with my few requests, even after I forgot to tip them, sorry boys! Would def stay here again for convenience and free food and highly recommend to anyone who wants value for money and isn't after just aesthetics!
hotel_name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown

review_title: It's an OK place for a couple of days.
review_text: Hotel is ok. The lobby is on the 6th floor. Service is spectacular. The building itself is not magnificent; the orange bed cover is tacky and feels weird on the body. Location is excellent. Restaurants (PF Chiangs and Joe seafood &Steakhouse) are a block away. Nordstrom and Bloomingdales are both conveniently located for your shopping urges. I would recommend this hotel to travellers with kids in tow and budget conscious people however if you have the dough to splurge, Marriott Hotel is just around the corner.
hotel_name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Chicago Downtown

review_text: Stayed here for one night. This is a cute boutique hotel. Small and cozy. Close to the Chicago Theatre and many other attractions. My only complant is the breakfast... Mini bagels and mini coffe cakes, apples, yogurt. Not what I expected for breakfast. But overall it was a nice stay.

review_title: Good but a wee bit noisy
review_text:
Despite having to change our travel plans at the last minute due to the ash cloud, nothing was too much trouble for the helpful staff at this location.
Only minor gripes was external noise from the nearby fire station and late night revellers at the weekend.
Everything else was very good. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay and wished it could have been longer.
location was good. Parking is very expensive. Breakfast and staff was excellent.

review_title: Not if it were the last hotel on earth!
review_text:
The room itself was fine and comfortable(very peaceful), but the customer service by the so-called, concierge or "experience something or the others" left much to be desired. First, I arrived and the doorman walked me to the desk. I was not greeted with the usual "Hello, welcome to...". Instead, I got, "Your name? ID?" No, "hello", no "welcome to the Amalfi Hotel," just plain old poor customer service from the very beginning! That left a very bad taste in my mouth, but I decided to let it go and see how the rest of my stay was. 
The next day, I had some questions about suggestions on where to go to eat dinner. We were looking for any restaurant that was Chicago-based, not the usual chain hotel, and moderately priced. I went downstairs and was confused as to which one was the concierge, since in normal hotels, the concierge was separate from everyone else. But, at the Amalfi, there are two desks with hotel staff and by the door is the podium where the doorman stands. Well, I thought for sure the one at the podium was the actual concierge, due to the fact that anyone who stood there was always so pleasant and attentive. Just in case, I asked the ladies at the desk where I could find the concierge. They replied that they were! One of them was the lady who originally checked me in. So, I tried my luck with the other one, instead. I explained what I was looking for, in terms of restaurants, and lo and behold, she couldn't think of any restaurants to recommend to me! She said she lives on the South Side of Chicago, so she doesn't know the restaurants around there very well. Ummm, I'm thinking that if you are a concierge, then whether you live there or not, you'd still make it your business to know things like that! So, the other lady gave me a few names of restaurants, instead. 
Then, I decided to order in one night and proceeded to call and ask for restaurants that delivered and I was told that I could order room service, which would come from a nearby restaurant. I did not have a menu in my room, so her solution was to read me the menu over the phone, line by line! After much annoyance, I asked them to send someone up with the menu, which she seemed annoyed to have to do!
Also, I noticed when we would go out for the day and come back, they would never say, "Good morning" or "Good Evening" when they saw us. That's what I am accustomed to at other hotels. My friend was so annoyed by this that one evening she passed by and then turned around and pleasantly said, "Good evening!" The response was a confused "Good evening," as if they were wondering why she said it!
The other employees were quite pleasant, especially the doormen! They always greeted you warmly and asked you how your day was going!
Housekeeping was ok, but after I left the room one day, I had to return because I forgot something. When I got back to the room the housekeeping cart was holding the door open, but the maid was not in the room! So, anyone could have gone in our room and stolen something.
The continental breakfast was fine and I liked that it was on every floor.
The wireless service was awful!!!!! My iPhone would not work properly the entire time I was there. Once I left the hotel, it was better!
The manager ended up calling me(bill issues) and we spoke about the customer service at her hotel. She apologized for her staff, but failed to offer a reduction in the bill! $20 off would have been a good gesture.
Two weeks later, management was still calling me regarding the conclusions I'd made regarding their employees. I was annoyed that it seemed as if the 2nd manager that called wanted me to change my mind! After 2 weeks, one two many phone calls, & much aggravation, management decided to credit my room for one night, split between my friend & me! Funny how they managed to do that, but never fixed the original discrepancy! I had to mail my friend a check for my half of the room, since they charged her for the entire amount & never fixed it, even after all those phone calls! (sigh)
Maybe it's because I am from Florida, which is a state that caters to tourists, that I am used to a higher level of service. That being said, I have traveled all over the world, as far as Japan and Ghana, and have received better service!
Overall, there are many hotels in the downtown area, so don't waste your money on this one!

The hotel was very well located if you want to enjoy Chicago without having to use your car. Parking in/out privilege was a must, though pricy fee a little bit. Service was great, 2 complaints: breakfast lack some imagination, it was average. Swimming pool was dirty the first night we got there and our eyes and skin suffered. The rest of days, they changed filters and it was good.

review_title: Huge hotel with service of Ã  'hotel de charme'
review_text:
Perfect service (Thanks Amanda for all hour help)
Friendly staff
Nice and clean rooms
Great fitness and pool
Good location
Great lounge
We will come back!

Stayed at the Amalfi Hotel for a girls' getaway weekend. We all loved it. Clean rooms, great service, and we loved the happy hour! Saved us a lot of money by enjoying our cocktails at the hotel before our dinner reservations. We would definitely stay here again!!

I'm from the south and expected to meet very blunt and unfriendly people, wow was I wrong.
Every one was so nice and helpful,I will definitely will return!

review_title: For better value and service...stay somewhere else.
review_text:
Stayed four nights, but only because we paid ahead and had to stay. Room did not seem clean. Stains on bed linens, old carpet, drab decor, very old bathroom. Overheard guest at front desk check-in one day state that the room she just checked in to had used soap and open shampoo in the tub. Apparently not cleaned. Our bathroom seemed to be from twenty or thirty years ago and badly in need of update to make it more useful and cleaner. Bathroom in our King room had VERY limited shelf space and no vanity. Single, freestanding wallmount sink without vanity and TERRIBLE yellowish lighting made it difficult to do hair and apply makeup. Old, ratty towels completed the experience. In bed area, there was limited space reminiscent of a "larger" room I occupied once in London. So, by typical American hotel standards-tiny. The room had one useable, and accessable electrical outlet outside the bathroom and one inside. Super small, overpriced mini bar fridge was actually warm! 
Parking was expensive and valet seemed to be the only "easy" option. The top side valet staff was the only personable and hard-working staff in the place. 
Room service was OK, but typically over priced and hard to accommodate in the small room. And you may require this service, since the only casual dining in the hotel seems to close up early.
Alarm clock in our room was complicated, but the one in our travel companion's room was fine. 
Bathroom lighting has two options, full on or full off, and with the light switch outside the door - sure to wake and confound you in the middle of the night. 
View from 25th floor was very nice and the bed was comfortable - I'll give it that much.
Overall, I was terribly regettful that we did not stay somewhere else. There is no shortage of hotels in Chicago and I'm sure we could have done better.

This hotel is quite amazing. Great location; it's right next to the water tower with lots of shopping to be done within the vicinity. Many eateries and attractions are nearby making it very convenient for first time visitors. The rooms are beautiful and well-appointed with quality furniture and decor. Granite accents embellish the room with a modern touch. Bathroom is ginormous with deep soaking tub and shower. Even the toilet has a separate room!
Staff at this hotel are very pleasant and friendly. Karen, the chef concierge, was extremely helpful and knowledgeable. She definitely made our stay very enjoyable.
So stay here! It's a gorgeous property with great customer service!

My daughter and I stayed in a Park Suite for four nights. From check In to check out our every need was not only met but was anticipated. We were addressed by name each time we encountered any staff members throughout the hotel. Our room was always kept clean and was extremely comfortable. We used the laundry service for overnight dry cleaning and it was returned the next morning as expected. My daughter used the spa and was very impressed with their services and their products. I used the gym and pool. The equipment was all updated and functional. The locker room was extremely clean and well stocked where robes and slippers were provided. We lunched at NOMI on their outdoor terrace. The food and service were excellent. I would like to compliment the management on their staff and services. I anticipate ( and look forward to ) another visit to he Park Hyatt Chicago in the future.

review_title: Superb location near the important stuff.
review_text: It's a Hyatt, so you expect it to be great. It is a bit overpriced, but, there is value. The concierge was good, and the location is unbeatable. They have a variety of complimentary beverages 24 hours a day. Found housekepping a bit unresponsive--had to ask for somethings 3 times to get it done. You can walk to the Hancock Tower and a plethora of excellent restaurants.

Stayed here for a quick Chicago weekend. Nice hotel extremely nice staff. Very helpful. Great view of the lake and river. 2 blocks to Navy Pier and 2 blocks to the magnificent mile.
Staff was very nice and you felt they genuinely wanted to help you and make sure you had a great time and stay 
Would stay here again in a second.

I normally use Tripadvisor as a valuable and honest resource and have yet to be disappointed. Unfortunately I had to stay at this hotel due to a conference. I must say I was a bit disappointed. I really didn't expect very much and I got just that. Most of the employees I encountered were not very friendly nor hospitable. Certainly not an atmosphere of "above and beyond". More like "I'm here to collect a paycheck". There were two exceptions... Lanelle or Lanette (sorry-not exactly sure which) was very friendly and seemed genuinely invested. She cared if I enjoyed my stay. She is a housekeeper. Sandra at the front desk made an effort and accommodates my special request, which was refreshing in comparison. The rooms are dated and dingy which would have been easier to overlook had the staff been more pleasant. Great location and views. All in all, a little more concentration on true guest service and hospitality would have made a difference. Which is my point... This hotel does not stand out. No DIFFERENCE. Given another chance, I would use TA to find location, view, better rooms AND hospitality.

review_title: Luxury and location w/ all the little extras
review_text: We had a wonderful stay. Ideal location to shopping, restaurants and public transportation. (red line 1 block away) Beautiful lobby and friendly superior staff from the front desk to the maids. Hotel offers complimentary house car drop off within a few miles of hotel (upon availability ) rental bicycles, running maps. By far one of the best service have experienced at a hotel. Complimentary gourmet coffee, expresso, teas in lobby were a nice touch. Nightly turn down service, w/ little added extras like maid arranging sinkside items into organized formations, folded clothes that were on a chair, maid saw us coming in one night and offered us. ice and water. We had a beverage before turning in for the night on the rooftop patio bar, and the host brought me a shawl because got a little chilly. Very impressed and hope others notice as well.

review_title: A grand house full of hospitality.
review_text: From the beginning till the end a pleasure. We stayed in a park view suite. It was clean and complete in regard to amenities. From here we had access to most everything the 'Magnificent Mile' has to offer (including a built in Armani boutique). The fitness room and spa were great. What a pleasure!

review_title: Beautiful hotel with magnificent location and view!
review_text: Staying here for a meeting. I was amazed at how upscale this hotel is. Perfect location within walking distance to everything. Around the corner from Water Tower place and Rush street. Hd dinner on the outdoor patio at NoMi and loved the scene and food. Highly recommend!

Sheraton is a nice hotel. No doubt about it. The location isn't all that great. Michigan Ave is where everything is at.
Pros - 1) Nice hotel. 2) AMC theaters, Walgreens, & Dominick's (a local grocery store) is within walking distance.
Neutral - 1) Michagan Ave is a 10-15 mins walk.
Negative - 1) Pillows... HORRIBLE!!! I had to stack all of my pillows on top of 1 another to get a decent sleep. 2) Not a lot of variety of restaurants within walking distance in my opinion. (However, the hotel will give u a list of restaurants "in the area" and ones that deliver.
Overall the stay is good. Not many things to really complain about.
Side notes - 1)If you're looking to be in the heart of things in downtown get a hotel off of Michigan Ave. 2)If you're gonna stay @ the Sheraton (or off of Michigan Ave stay) eat @ Yolk. Wonderful breakfast!!! Not expensive. Big portions. However, the restaurant can be extremely crowded depending on what time u go. They close @ 3 (the one off of Ohio street does @ least). 3) Public transportation is not like NYC. Didn't see a lot of stops/subway entrances by the Sheraton. However... Please save yourself some money and take the L (their public transportation system) to O'Hare airport. It literally gets you to the airport. Real simple. Simple as can be. & the hotel has a print off of how u get there too. 4) Free wifi and touch screen computers on the floor below the lobby. So no need 2 buy Internet service in your room unless you have too.

Great location - walking distance to some top attractions such as Michigan Ave and the John Hancock Centre.
Lovely comfortable, clean rooms. 
Friendly and helpful staff - I was given a free upgrade to a suite! 
The breakfast buffet in the LB bistro was AMAZING.
I could not really fault this hotel to be honest!

review_title: The only bright spot during a bad trip
review_text:
I stayed at the Park Hyatt for a meeting in Chicago. I was sick (sinus infection) and I lost my wallet with my ID, credit cards, ATM cards and cash. I was miserable. The Park Hyatt employees helped me get cash (so I didn't feel helpless) and I went home early. The day I flew home my wallet was recovered but the person didn't want to take the time to mail it. I told them to drop it off at the park hyatt. When the park hyatt received it they called me and mailed it to me express! Thank you! :-)
My room was awesome! I looked down on the water tower. I would definitely stay there again!

review_title: DO NOT STAY HERE during the reconstruction if you want to sleep/rest!
review_text: I was awaken by hammering and sawing at 6:23 AM. They apologized profusely and sent up a fruit & cheese tray. They said the contractors were not supposed to start until 9AM and promised it would not happen again. The next morning at 6:20AM... again with the hammering. Don't stay here until the construction is over. BTW... my duvet smelled like smoke on Day 1 and the shower head was off and blasting water in not a good way. I must have the lemon room, #905.p
Spent 2 nights there - great staff and Lovett room. Location can't be beat. Would definitely stay there again

Me and my husband went for our one year anniversary. We had a great view of Navy Pier as well as a great view of the lake. We had great customer service when we checked in and anytime we needed a cab...we were greeted. The room was very clean and very spacious. Bed was extra comfortable.

review_title: Top hotel, bit pricey, but worth it. Make plans to stay at The Burnham.
review_text: Off the beaten path, as it's located in the Loop just catty corner from Macys on State Street. The Macys is the old Marshall Fields main store that has the windows at Christmas with the big tree inside. The Burnham rooms are decorated so lovely, very clean. The lobby and restaurant The Applewood are wonderful too. The building was one of the original skyscrapers in Chicago, a converted office building. Top notch, stay there when you are in Chicago.

The hotel is pleasantly situated, right by the river (odd floor numbers had river views on our floor) which has a very nice riverwalk alongside it, but as a base for sightseeing it's slightly out of the way: no subway stop close by, five minute walk (with kids) to the magnificent mile and not close to good dining options.
The hotel itself is very nice - the "iPad tables" in the lobby were a hit with the kids but obviously in much demand (they only have two). The hotel pool and sundeck were nice and they were welcoming of kids there. The "Chicago Burger Company" restaurant was overpriced ($8 for a single cheeseburger) and absolutely not worth it.
Rooms were fine although the plumbing was extremely noisy. And we had the obligatory inconsiderate 1am "corridor shouters" (ie thoughtless people who come back to their rooms shouting all the way down the corridor, presumably after a drink or two). 
We got our rooms discounted via hotwire.com - happy under the circumstances.

Great hotel, perfect location, wonderful staff and comfy beds.
Bathroom was not my favorite. Small towels and no shelf in shower for products. But clean and nice with Aveda products.
Stay on floor 7 or higher...facing State Street for best views.
The rooms are clean, staff friendly and helpful, breakfast was good, convenient to trains, Michigan ave, restaurants. Will definitely stay again.

I have nothing but good things to say about this hotel. From check-in being fast and efficient (thanks Leighann) down to the guys at the door (sorry I didn't get your names). Breakfast was good with good choices offered.
Wonderful, room and view!!" Great staff, awesome ammenties! We will make this hotel our downtown stay destination evetytime we come into town! Love staying here.

This hotel had a great location right on michigan ave. Walking distance to the magnificant mile, bus station, and only a few blocks from millinium park. And a great view out our window! The hotel was clean, room was big with full kitchen. And we got a great rate!

Met a friend for the weekend and we wanted a place to stay near everything. The rooms were very nice. My friend was able to check in early. I had called to request early check in and the staff member very helpful. The breakfast was great as well. We walked everywhere but the el stations were close if we needed them. I would highly recommend.

review_title: Nice hotel and a great value.
review_text: The Hampton Inn Majestic is undoubtedly the best Hampton Inn I have ever stayed at and overall a fantastic value. It feels like a boutique hotel and is in an excellent location. The room was very clean and I'd certainly stay here again. Why not 5 stars? This hotel is lacking in any sort of amenities (besides free contintnal breakfast in the small lobby) and is missing some of the finer touches (only 2 small and scratchy bath towels and 2 hand towels a day, the staff at ground level will sometimes sit by the door and not greet you or assist you with opening the door, etc). Still the pluses far outweigh the negatives and I highly recommend staying here for on a visit to Chicago.

This is a good hotel with great service in a good location. The rooms are small but not intolerable. The hotel is clean and the beds are comfortable. The bathrooms are small and lack some modern must haves such as a curved shower curtain rod. The restaurant on site is good and fairly priced. I would stay here again based on the price. Anything over $175 is too expensive for this hotel. It is purely a value stay for a day or two.

review_title:
Stellar location Lovely Service
Rooms....not so nice!
review_text:
The RC FS is located on top of Water Tower Place..just hop on the elevator and you are immediately transported down into
the shopping center! If shopping and people watching are your thing...look no further for the perfect hotel!
My early arrival was noted and honored. Room service breakfast came exactly on time. 
Now...the not so good. Room service delivered a cheese and fruit platter in a cardboard box inside a brown bag....no tray to eat it on and just a very strange way to have room service. Turn down was not even apparent until I discovered the bed pillow in my closet. The bed was messy from me lying on it and had not been smoothed out, the drapes had not been drawn and no mint, no weather update, nothing.
There was no book of services in the room, so I had no idea what the hotel offered.
The premium King room bathroom was wonderful but the room itself felt like a nice Holiday Inn ....bland, not luxurious nor special.
I am a hotel DIVA, I admit this, I want perfection! 
I may try the other FS next time I head to Chicago.

review_text: Attended large professional meeting here. Meeting facilities were fine. Hotel and room clean. Service was professional and friendly. Dining options in-hotel were very limited: basically Shula Steakhouse or room service. (Chicago Burger "in hotel" was shut down.) A bit of a walk to best shopping and restaurant rows; other hotels have more convenient locations. Slow Internet. Would not choose for a personal stay.

Stayed at this property for a conference. It is downtown Chicago, so nothing is cheap.
The property is in good shape and the staff helpful. You are close to the lake and right on the Chicago River. There are plenty of things to do and eat close by.
There are a lot hotel properies in the area. Unless you are hooked into Starwood Rewards, I think it is worth checking around for pricing at other hotel properties.

We visited Chicago over Thanksgiving and were very pleased with all aspects of the hotel. The only crunch was driving down Michigan on the Friday after Thanksgiving! Total traffic madness made us question why we planned this then, but upon arrival we were delighted to enter the lovely lobby on the 12th floor and very pleased with our suites. Great location, great attention to detail and very polite staff.

review_title: Great location, my alternative to the four seasons when I bring the kids.
review_text:
Location, location, location. I like being close to oak and rush streets. Close to the boutiques, barneys, the lounges and restaurants on rush/division. I statyed in a junior suite with my wife and two kids. The sofa bed was great, believe it or not. It had a down feather top, etc. Kids loved it. The price was okay as I prefer the Four Seasons down the street, which is more. But with kids in tow, the Sofitel seemed more kid friendly. Of course, the Sofitel is a notch down, but it's still nice. I would go back again. 
The service was okay, not fantastic. I had to call housekeeping to make up the sofa bed. While it was worth it, it did take a little while. The restaurant had an awesome butternut squash soup but my Madagascar shrimp salad was just so-so. The shrimp was not fresh but the flavor was good. I avoided the shrimp after the first bite. 
The room was clean and new. Bed was comfortable as mentioned in other posts. A very nice stay. 
I would suggest the hotel improve it's workout facility. It was cramped and not well ventilated. I expect more from a four star hotel. Sadly for the kids, mo pool!
Overall, we would go back again. Price point below Four Seasons and location is just as good. Cheers.

This is a fine hotel with wonderfully appointed rooms. The concierge was very helpful in directing me to a store where I could finish up my holiday shopping. A couple negative things were not getting my wake-up call (desk clerk apparently didn't get it entered) and a small housekeeping issue. I'll be back.

review_title: Only one place to stay in Chi-Town!
review_text: Sofitel is perfect. Smart, snazzy, great bar and restaurant. Bernard, at the Concierge Desk is the best. And the lobby smells wonderful! Highly recommend.

My husband and I stayed at this hotel from Dec 28 through Jan 3. In our opinion, it's the best location ever! It's just a 2 minutes walk from Millenium Park and The Art Institute, next to lots of good restaurants and shops, and the subway and buses just on the corner. Very good complimentary breakfast, making us skip all the lunchs. The staff: very good people, always prestative, goog humor (something we think it's also importante). We'll definetilly returning to this hotel next time in Chicago.

Great location!!! Great lake view.
Excellent fitness room and spa. The staff is really helpful. Rooms are clean but not really modern looking. 
The restaurant is fine but nothing special. There are bunch of better restaurants in the area. If you love to shop, this hotel is a play for you. You do not need to go out in order to get to the mall. It is in the building. 1-8 floor is the mall, 12 th floor is the lobby for the hotel. Enjoy!

The hotel was clean and inviting. The room was nice and the bathroom was very large. The location was great. We were able to walk to most shopping areas without a problem. It was our anniversary and the concierge helped my husband book a very wonderal and quaint italian restaurant for dinner. We will definitely return. I can't think of anything negative about this hotel.

Everything was wonderful!! When we checked in, Sean Murphy asked us about our occasion. We told him that it was our anniversary. Later that day, we received free chocolate covered strawberries and drinks as our anniversary gift and handwritten card from Sean. Everyone was friendly. Location of the hotel is great too. I highly recommend this hotel.

review_title: Great location, room service at 3 am
review_text: We have stayed in many Chicago hotels and really enjoyed the Ritz Carlton. It is attached to the shopping mall water tower and a half block from Michigan Ave. We could see Navy pier from the window. The service was excellent from the doorman to the room service at 3 am. It's kind of wierd that the lobby is on the 12th floor. The gym is on the 11th and seems like the basement but is very well equipped. They even had a flat iron for me. I felt totally pampered! As usual, like all good Ritz's, you can check out at 12 and then spend the day at the spa or gym and then shower and get ready for your flight. No problem!

review_title: All over the globe Sofitel will always be my number one choice.
review_text: I stayed at this hotel in August 2011. When I got out of the car a fine gentleman introduced himself to me and welcomed me with a kind smile. He gladly held my bags for me. When you walk in the lobby you feel so welcome. The lobby is beautiful lots of soft seats around. The front desk staff were very helpful and always welcome you by your last name. I was kindly upgraded to a suite. The hotel provides guests with a business centere located on level 2 with free Internet. If you want WiFi you have to pay a small fee. The room I was given was very large with all the trimmings. Such as a fully stocked mini bar and refreshment center. Complementary Evian water by my bed every day. Large windows with a great view of the John Hancock building. Blinds and curtains that are controled by a switch. 2 large plasmas one in my room the other in the lounge room. Housekeeping knew I was the only male staying in the suite so they stocked my bathroom amenities with male products by Herems Paris. Bathroom was beautiful large anti fog mirror bathtub was a bit small. However the handheld shower was very luxurious. Marble bathroom can't go wrong. The room came with slippers and a oversize bathrobe. Sofitel are known for there amazing beds and Chicago water tower did not go wrong here. The beds were amazing so soft and luxurious make for a fantasic way to get over jet lag. The rooms were cleaned everyday re stocked and newspapers left outside. I would give this hotel a 9 out of 10 the location is great the staff are great the hotel itself is unlike another. I will come back.
Great service as usual. The best place to stay in chicago. Beat value of the high end properties

review_text: Overall great location, good service and perfect location for a short walk to Michigan ave or even the goldcoast neighbourhood. Had a tasty breakfast via room service one morning and went to the little cupcake store around the corner, which was amazing. Well worth the little money it was to stay here.

We loved this hotel. Terrific service and a very short walk to the 900 shops and restaurants. The desk service was terrific and it had a great gym. Rooms were very comfortable and quite spacious for Chicago. Huge bathroom with great toiletries. We will be back!

Steps from American girl store and water tower. Great location and kid friendly. The kids made cookies with pastry chef in kitchen and later had a visit from candyman! Rooms were very nice, restaurant was good. Value was good with third night free.
