Il possÃ¨de la triade Wifi, piscine (extÃ©rieure cf photos, trÃ¨s agrÃ©able par 35Â° dehors) et PDJ gratuit (pas inoubliable mais pratique, le tout pour 140 â‚¬ Ã  quatre, que demander de plus ?
Les chambres ont deux lits doubles, un peu Ã©troits Ã  quatre, mais nous avons couchÃ© en famille sans problÃ¨me. La dÃ©co est passe-partout, il y a la fameuse grosse clim un peu bruyante des hÃ´tels de chaine. Enfin, le service est OK.

review_title: Second stay, staff much friendlier, still room to improve
review_text: The location is great, next to Penn and Drexel. Train station right out the door. Upgraded to club floor ($20 with elite status), both breakfast and pre dinner snacks a bit sparse for a club lounge. Housekeeping needs some improvement, left dirty dishes, did not make up the rollaway. Room service pretty much limited to oriental. Speaking of rollaways, still at $30, too much in my opinion for a pricey hotel. On the good side, clean, comfortable room and lobby. The hotel just lacks a "personality", hard to explain, but hopefully makes sense.

My wife and I stated for 3 nights-we went for a well reviewed hotel. We were not disappointed. Good location, super-friendly staff. Chris, one of the doormen- gave fab customer service, as did Vanessa on reception. Traffic noise was a bit intrusive, even on 17th floor, but hey, it's s big city. Would stay again.

This was our second stay here. We remembered it as an average airport hotel, but wow has it ever gone downhill. The common areas were the filthiest I have ever seen in an American hotel and I have seen a lot. Dozens of used dirty cups and empty bottlescovered the floor of the second floor lounge and hallway. So much crumbs ground into the hall floors that they literally crunched with every step. The pool was murky with gobs of hair floating in it. At night children and adults were running and screaming in the halls into the wee hours. Some guys were smoking pot in an elevator. While the hotel cannot control the quality of the clientele it attracts, it needs to have adequate cleaning and security to deal with the problems. Now they clearly do not. As we checked out a man was complaining about the filthy conditions and the woman at the desk said "the cleaners don't get here until 10 and it takes them a while." She didn't seem to care at all.

review_title: close to the airport, nice staff - but needs renovation
review_text: I would agree to people posted on this hotel before. This one needs some renovation. The rooms are definately used and even they are clean you feel a bit uncomfortable. Not the Marriott level I'm used to. Other than that it's a good place, free parking, very close to the airport, downtown is less than 30mins by car, so is King of Prussia. The hotel pool is also nice-indoor but with glass walls so it's nice and bright. Overall a good place with a very friendly staff.

Either renovate this place or shut it down Starwood. The Sheraton brand is being destroyed everyday you leave it open. 
This place is about even in quality with a cheap motel. Our room had a broken air conditioner. And when we called to have it fixed we were told the engineer had gone home for the day. It was cooler in the hallway than our room. 
The computer that was to offer free wi-fi flashed a message that it couldnt connect to the Internet and constantly self restarted. 
The room was noticably worn. Walls marked and wall paper patches and visible seams. Mold on the popcorn ceiling in the bathroom. 
A make shift closet door that you might find in a dorm room. 
They try to hide the years of wear and tear with a new shower curtain rod and marble on the sink. But when you really look at the place is no better than a cheap motel. 
We are Starwood members and the value of this property in terms of points or cash spent is really a rip off. 
This is our second stay here only because our daughter is attending Penn and we are Starwood members. But we will be going back to the Hilton after this experience.

Spent New Years Eve here with Sean n Eric at the complimentary wine hour, greeted ny Na`te at guest services, great info from concierge Abigail and what a location and cool boutique hotel. Did I mention hot chocolate break before the Mummers' Strut on 1st? Only hotel I"d recmnd in Philly! What a great surprise weekend for my wife.
hotel_name: Hotel Palomar Philadelphia - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: Central location but with a few flaws
review_text:
We loved the location, it was right next to the 42nd st subway and u could literally catch the train to anywhere in ny from here. The only negative comment I have about the location is that it was a few places down from the ny parole office And can get a bit dodgy at times ( especially at night) 
The staff were very nice particulary the barman and housekeeping staff. The front desk were also very pleasant but a bit inexperienced at times and couldn't assist when we asked about local restaurants and businesses. 
The rooms werevery clean and the soundproof windows blocked out alot of the noise from outside.
The one thing about my stay at this hotel that hindered myenjoyment factor was that room had no fridge and no coffee or tea making facilities. 
Overall a nice stay but not overally memorable.I probably wont stay here again in the future due to the lack of amenities and the hotel being so close to a few unattractive shops i.e the parole office and the adult store.

Just spent 10 nights at The Distrikt Hotel and it was fantastic! Great friendly service, very convenient location and yummy drinks in the bar by Leo. Definitely recommend this hotel for anyone going to New York. 
Haley - Sydney, Australia
I was picked up from the airport by your driver Steve. He was very funny and polite. The ride was nothing short of a good one, definitely an excellent experience!

review_title: Definitely staying here again on another trip to Philly
review_text:
I really liked my stay here. It was a lot better than I expected. The room was pretty basic but nice. They could upgrade the tv to a flat screen. We did have an issue on the second day with flies. That's my only complaint. The location was convenient for me--not as far away from the city as the airport but close enough to be extremely reasonably priced. Truly in the heart of all of the stadiums but I'm not a sports fan. 
Overall I really like this hotel and I will be staying there again on future visits to the City of Brotherly Love.

I was in town for the cancelled Phillies post season games and because we could not cancel after the loss we had to keep our reservation... We were very relieved and satisfied with the check in process GOLDIE was the girl who got us to our room and gave great directions to Oregan Diner...

Stylish and clean hotel very nicely located. Only two things were bad, the free WiFi did not work on Android devices and there were no minibar in the room.

I truely enjoyed my stay at this hotel I visited a while ago and its a beautiful change the renovations are great as well as the staff I felt very welcomed.I would like to give a special thanks to front desk clerk Tyrene shes deffinitly a star that lights up the front desk keep up the good work she went above and beyond the duty of just an average checkout wish there were more people like her.i will visit again.
i would like to commened Adam Tinkler and Demotus for their excellent customer service skills and the desication they showed me to making my stay as peaceful and pleasant as possible. Thanks Guys.

Hostess Goldie is very gracious and very informative. I'm a night owl and she always helps me out in whatever. With a kind smile she out of towners feel at home.
 Thanks goldie
 Thanks Holiday inn

This was an amazing hotel! The staff is the friendliest hotel staff that I have ever experienced. I live in south Florida and go to all of the nice hotels in Orlando, and the Distrikt Hotel beats all of them! The maid is very kind, the check in is polite, the elevator is extremely fast (never waited on it more than 30 sec.), I WILL be back at this hotel. The room was larger than I was expecting too. We got a room on the 11th floor which was just high enough to have a view. Also their maintenance staff is very kind and professional (I accidentally clogged the toilet with a bar of soap... Long story). I would 110% recommend this hotel to everyone!!

We like to stay here when we go Phillies games. We had some computer issues when booking the rooms... and they helped take care of that without stress. We got a parking pass for the game too. Location great, staff was very helpful and priority card got us late checkout...2:00. Wonderful stay. We will stay here again and recommend to a friend.

This hotel is especially perfect if you're attending any event at the sports complex in philadelphia. It's only about two blocks away, very well maintained, and very nice without being overly expensive. Have stayed twice for events at the Wells Fargo Center, had great experiences each time, and wouldn't stay anywhere else!

review_title: Faultless, you must book this hotel!
review_text:
Stayed at the distrikt for four nights in March and loved it. Excellent location, just outside the bustle of times sq but close enough to the subway and in a central location.
Seen a couple of concerns about the street the hotel is on. Personally I can't understand this one bit. Street was perfectly safe.
Room was top notch - large, clean with great views. Staff were all helpful and knowledgeable. Great value for money in a modern beautiful hotel.
We couldn't recommend this highly enough. Don't have any doubts about booking. First class all round.
We booked this hotel on Priceline by naming our own price and got a great deal. The room was clean, staff was extremely friendly, beds were comfortable. We really enjoyed our stay.

review_title: Good place to stay if you're going to a game but...
review_text:
My kids and I stayed here when we came in to see a Phillies game. The place was dated and the rug and was stained. 
My biggest problem was that the tv wasn't working properly. I called them at 3:30, then again at 8:00. Finally at 10:00 I went down and spoke to the manager. The maintenance guy couldn't fix it so at 11:00 at night we had to move to a room 7 floors away. 
To the hotel's credit they did credit me $30 for the inconvenience. 
It's walking distance to the park and easy on/off the highway.

review_title: Proche du bus pour le centre ville... En 30'
review_text:

Great location, excellent value, terrific city view, clean, quality everything. The manager and staff were very helpful, excellent customer service.

review_title: Outstanding service, stylish & spacious, right price!
review_text: After researching tripadvisor for Nyc hotels, Distrikt's reviews best matched my needs. I expected Distrikt Hotel to be a new hotel in a good location with a cordial staff. I can honestly say that Distrikt Hotel far exceeded my expectations!! The rooms are stylish, roomy & comfortable, location is excellent especially if you want to be near Times Square without the noise, and the staff is outstanding! Staff is very helpful and sincere in their efforts. Since I've been in customer service for many years, I always appreciate service from employees who take pride in their work.

review_title: Great location, new and clean hotel!
review_text:
My husband and I had a wonderful stay here. We got a great rate on a room, which was pretty small, but definitely clean and pretty chic. The staff was extremely friendly, and made up for the few amenities the room lacked, like a coffee maker, microwave, or fridge. Our room had strange heat (if it wasn't blasting, it was freezing) but overall we enjoyed our stay!!
The hotel was also close enough to all the touristy sights (times sq, rockafeller ctr) but far enough away not to be super busy or touristy. It is right off of 9th avenue, which is filled with delicious and generally moderately priced restaurants.

Stayed here at the beginning of December with my wife for a weekend vacation to NYC. The staff is very friendly and helpful. We liked the location; very close to the subway station with the AC and E trains. Also, the hotel is located within walking distance to many tourist destinations; times square, shopping, theaters.

The Distrikt is a fabulous trendy and sophisticated big city boutique spot with wonderful accomodations and service. Given it's location in the center of the fashion district just 4 blocks from Time Square with reasonable safe parking right next door and subway access within a few minutes walk I was pleasantly surprised at the cost. Me and my teenage daughters wanted the real NYC experience and definitely found it at the Distrikt. I will be recommending this place to my clients and friends and plan on traveling there from my home in Boston as often as possile. F. Burkholder

review_title: Old hotel in need of renovation
review_text: Wouldn't recommend this place unless you have no other options.

Saw a mouse scurry across our floor, which completely freaked me out. Took 20 minutes to check in at 8:30 PM on a Wednesday. Staff was relatively helpful, breakfast was okay, but hard to get past the mouse sighting!!

review_title: Nothing makes a weekend stay in Philadelphia more satisfying than seeing all the sites and coming back to stay in such a wonderf
review_text:
My boyfriend and I recently stayed at the Comfort Inn Downtown while in Philadelphia touring the city over the Thanksgiving weekend. I have been a loyal customer to Comfort Inn and their sister hotels for many years as I get great customer service and exceptional value. 
My stay at the Comfort Inn Downtown has left nothing wanting. The staff was curteous and knowledgeable. They helped provide transportation and suggested places to see and eat. Ms. Alicia Olcese, a manager on duty, was especially helpful in providing extra necessities for my room and by providing a wealth of information about the city. She is definitely as asset to the company and a positive example for the employees on her shift.
The room was clean and welcoming, especially after touring the city all day! The cleaning crew did and excellent job of providing fresh towels and toiletries and were curteous.
Overall, I'd give my stay at Comfort Inn Downtown 5 stars for customer service, cleanliness, location, comfort and affordability. I will certainly recommend this hotel to anyone planning a trip to Philadelphia and indeed return there myself if ever in the city again!

The hotel was a good value and worth its value, however its location was perfect. I say this because our room had a beautiful view of the Ben Franklin Bridge and it was especially interesting that it changed colors at night. We also saw many interesting things on the river. Also, the hotel was in walking distance of everything having to do with Independence National Park! Beautiful and a nice walk, we definitely got exercise in.

We stayed here overnight on our way home to Fl. It looks a bit scary in the lobby at first glance, like you're in some sort of dive. However, the staff is very nice and the rooms are just fine. Not luxurious, but clean and comfortable for weary travelers. The view from our room was of the bridge- quite spectacular- we were on the top floor. The hotel is only 6 blocks from the Bell. We took the free shuttle there and walked back. Warm breakfast, usual fare but good. Would stay again.

L'hotel si trova a pochi blocchi dalla City Hall ed Ã¨ praticamente in centro. All'arrivo ho trovato una cortesia che non Ã¨ comune, fidatevi! Mi hanno dato un upgrade della camera e tra sorrisi vari mi hanno regalato la colazione e in voucher per un bicchiere di vino presso il ristorante/bar annesso all'hotel.. una sciccheria!
Le camere sono in stile moderno e contengono 2 accappatoi 'maculati' che sono meravigliosi. 
La colazione continentale offerta Ã¨ raffinata e minimalista. 
In definitiva un hotel da scegliere tra i migliori che abbia visto in giro nel suo insieme (e di hotel ne ho visti parecchio in tutto il mondo!)
hotel_name: Hotel Palomar Philadelphia - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: Nice hotel but realy, no wifi in the rooms?
review_text:
Lobby was very nice and up to date. It was the only place besides the bar that you can get wifi. I could not believe that a hotel at the airport did not have in room wifi. Very disappointing. 
Rooms were clean and they had nice bathrooms and flat screen TVs. The bar is nice and the food is good. Great service and I loved the sweet potatoe fries. It is extremely close to the airport. Easy access for early morning flights. 
I would only recommend if you need to stay at the airport. Otherwise the lack of in room wifi and hi price would push me away.

We stayed here the night we flew in and the night before we flew out. We had our own folding bed for our baby but had asked on the reservation for a crib. Each time when we checked in we were told we'd have a crib in the room. Never did. The first time we called down and were told they'd bring it right away. After 15 minutes we unpacked our bags, set up our own and called to cancel the crib. The second time we stayed it wasn't as late getting in so we received one after about 20 minutes after we called down to say there was no crib in the room as we had been told. The crib that was brought was broken an we had them get us a new one (which came faster). However getting in so late and leaving so early, we'd stay there again if the circumstances were the same.

Was stranded at Phila airport again so I pulled out the phone and had them pick me up to be honest I thought the place would not be that good being that close to the airport, boy was I surprised. Everyone was very friendly the bar was great and breakfast as well. I found a new great place to stay when I am in Philly. Special thanks to Tyrone who went the extra mile

I read the other reviews before staying here and was expecting some problems but on the contrary it was awesome!
At check in the guys were very friendly, I asked for a king bed which they said no problem. I had booked this on priceline and sometimes you get 2 queens in the worst spot and can't change, but not today.
Next parking, I was expecting it to be very confusing but the check in staff explained so clearly what to do it was eAsy... Don't get me wrong, it's slightly complicated and if you don't listen you will be driving around saying 'where do I go? What do I do with these 3 tickets...' it also costs $20 a day, not the best since other airport hotels are free but Philly parking, especially center city, expensive.
The decor in the hallways and rooms could be updated for sure, it's like alot of hotels, nothing special, but the rooms ARE spotless, I checked, bathrooms, dated but exceptionally clean.
We stayed 2 nights and the other person I was traveling with had a 6.30pm flight and asked for a late checkout... They gave her 4pm at no charge, this, was awesome.
It's not a real Starbucks in the lobby store, they just brew Starbucks coffee but, it tasted great and the service from the staff excellent. I was prepared not to like this hotel, it was actually very comfortable. It's right AT the airport - attached by a walkway. I didn't hear one plane by the way! My flight departed at 6.15am and it was so good to be right there and have that little extra time that early in the morning. Recommended.

I've stayed here multiple times this year on business and found them to be consistently great with providing a high level of customer service. Only negative I can state is that the rooms are old and rather tired. Otherwise very good.

Great overnight stay before grabbing a flight. This Marriott is attached to the B terminal and you can take a quick van ride to the other terminals. 
Staff is friendly and efficient and the rooms are standard Marriott. Nice, clean and updated. 
The lobby has a great restaurant and bar called The Riverbend (I think). Good food and service. 
Only complaint I had was a weak air conditioner. Very happy overall.

review_title: Nice place but not so great service
review_text: We stayed there on our wedding night because we had aneatly morning flight. Desk staff was courteous but we got to the room and the key didn't work. Once we got a key that worked we saw the room was very clean and well kept, but we never got the room service we ordered. We ate at the restaurant the next morning which was actually pretty good compared to what we would have gotten in the airport. All in all not too bad, but could have been much better.

Overall I thought this was a decent hotel if you need to spend a night close to the airport.
Pros:
Free drink tickets were great.
Room was nice
Bed was comfortable
Airport shuttle was great and timely
Breakfast was nice
Cons:
Service at the sports bar was painfully slow.
Room was well soundproofed internally but the exterior wall seemed to let in a lot of noise from cars passing by. I normally am a pretty heavy sleeper but I found myself awake a couple times from the noise.
Overall I would stay again if I needed to spend the night close to the airport. 
As a sidenote, I didn't use the pool but it did look really nice.

review_title: Ok for airport stay but poor quality for a hilton
review_text: As a diamond member was very unimpressed. My bathroom should have been cleaner, room service breakfast was cold and did not taste good, got conflicting info on hotel shuttle - though drivers were excellent -and air conditioner was extremely loud. Will not stay here again. If good rate, stay at Marriott in the airport, or there is an aloft next to this property.

Secondo anno che provo questo hotel e giudizio sempre ottimo. Posizione, vista, camere, tutto al top. Purtroppo forse un po caro ma ne vale la pena. Il letto Ã¨ esageratamente comodo e le stanze spaziose. Ricordatevi di chiedere la vista verso il fiume! Ristorante buono/ottimo ma non al top come l'hotel!

Stayed one night. Great service, but the hallway and rooms were worn and need an upgrade. Everything was clean as best it could be. Really good location for airport access. Good stay and fly rate. Wouldn't stay more than one night.

review_title: Great location is worth the price
review_text: Typical Marriott hotel with tastefully done rooms, small but comfortable. Mattress was extremely comfortable. Location is key being directly connected to Terminal B. Staff was very polite even with a large group due to cancelled flight. Definitely recommend, but price is premium.

This is where I usually stay in Philly and probably log in 10 over nights a year or more. It is a medium priced hotel and is an older property. The place got a complete facelift, including bathrooms, awhile ago. It is located at a convenient hub of roads to the west of downtown. Access to Manyunk is great. Parking is free as is the wireless. The hotel has a small rental office in the back if you need a car or van. The eighth floor is executive level and the rooms include refrig and microwave along with access to the lounge which is has a stocked refrig and other food treats. If you need anything as for Jack Smith at the front desk. He is the best!! This is home in Philly to me.

Clean, tidy, convenient and cheap. The perfect combination for an airport hotel. 
If you want a resort or full service facilities go somewhere else. 
Perfect for my needs. I'll be back.

review_title: Unique rooms and great public spaces.
review_text:
As an SPG Gold, I received rooms on the SPG floor (i.e. free bottled water), a free drink at the bar, and a free jot drink in the morning. 
Staff was helpful and friendly on both stay and surprised me with the best service I've seen at a Starwood property. 
Rooms facing the runway can be a bit noisy, but it wasn't an issue once the flights died down for the night.

review_title: Not only are the beds extremely small but the business center in the lobby charges to use the computers to go on the internet!
review_text:
I am very disappointed with this hotel. Just as it seemed that hotels were starting to value their travelers this hotel is going in the opposite direction! No extras here. If you don't have your own laptop to access the Internet (which some hotels do charge for premium services). This hotel even charges to use the business center in the lobby. No printing-just accessing the Internet us going to cost you 3.00 and then an extra per minute charge. 
Not much else good to make up for the nickel and diming here. Way to take advantage of the travelers to Philadelphia ! Thanks Hilton!
Excelente hotel;acho apenas que nÃ£o deveria ser cobrado pela internet

review_title: Don't get caugt up in the modern look!
review_text: Has a nice look. Rooms could b better. No room service. Shuttle doesn't run as advertised you have to call it. Waited at airport for 35 min when it's supposed to run every 20 min. Cleaning staff is poor my room was left dirty
Best staff, location is perfect. Always clean. I love staying at the aloft in Philly. Such a treat.

review_title: Would come back if ever in the area
review_text: This hotel was great! The hotel staff when checking in was very friendly and helped us with all of our questions. They sent up an aero bed right away when we requested one. The hotel had a cool design and my family loved it. Even though it was a small touch we loved the hair & body products they supplied and liked that the shampoo, conditioner and body wash were in dispensers in the shower. A great way for hotels to go green, no more tiny bottles! Although the hotel does not have a restaurant it's two sister hotels which are just steps away have two different restaurants good for an easy dinner. Also features a great pool and workout facility.

review_title: My frustration went in peace once in my room
review_text: Airport hotels have a pretty bad rep. So my expectations weren't very high. Stock in phila because of the snow, no choice and from that point sparkles from the reception at the front desk to room service and finally my room. Spacious, clean, beautiful bathroom and extremely comfoable

This was a comfortable place to stay if you have business in the area. The hotel feels a little on the older side but still clean and comfortable. Noise wasn't too bad. Wish I had time to check out the gym and other amenities.

review_title: Clean, fun, trendy hotel near the airport
review_text: I stay here quite often for business trips and I really enjoy my stays. The fitness center is great, and the bar is too. Good beers on tap! IPAs! And the bartender Rebecca is wonderful. Good conversation and great service!

review_title: Worst, dirtiest, smelliest, Hilton in the US.
review_text:
Last year alone I stayed around 90 nights in Hilton hotels. I have been in the majority of Hilton branded properties in the US. 
The Philadelphia airport property is so bad I scarcely know where to begin. The shuttle bus to the hotel took over an hour to pick me up. I watched as the Sheraton busses went past dozens of times before hilton's bus finally showed up. The bus should have scared me off. It was filthy, smelled bad, and the air conditioning didn't work. 
Entering the hotel I immediately noticed the smell of old rot. There are chunks of the ceiling falling and dangling down ready to fall. The staff was pleasant, but when I got on the elevator there was a new unpleasant odor of powerful cleaning solvents on top of a nastier rotten smell than the lobby. 
Getting off the elevator on my floor, the corridor smelled worse than the lobby or elevator. It smelled like musty dirty laundry which must be thrown away as it can't be washed clean. This is not a subtle odor but a pungent stink you cannot escape. 
My room was slightly better in aroma than the corridor. Slightly. It also had chunks of plaster falling down in the bathroom and above the room's window. The towels were a dingy color. 
I went to the vending machine on my floor to get a bottle of cola and it smelled as if someone had been urinating in the corner repeatedly for a long time. The smell was as bad as anything you'll encounter on Bourbon street in New Orleans. As bad as the rest of the place smelled, this was an order of magnitude worse and made me gag.
I was originally planning to stay four nights at the Hilton. I checked out after one night and moved across the street to the cheaper A-Loft which still had dirty hallways but smelled clean and had no signs of decay like the Hilton. 
I would not recommend this Hilton to an enemy. Unless your sense of smell is disabled and you don't mind rotting filth, stay far far away from this Hilton. I am AMAZED that Hilton allows this place to use their name and logo.

review_title: Dirty room, stained sheets, rude staff, deceptive booking agent
review_text:
We called Aloft's reservation line and were told we were going to get a room on a high floor with a balcony. After waiting 30 minutes in line to check in, we were given a room on floor 2 and told they had no balconies. The staff did nothing to clear this up, not even a sorry.
We walk in the room to find the carpet totally stained and the sheets with large yellow stains. The front desk moved us to another room but were not nice about it. The next room had clean sheets, but the carpet was still stained. We gave up and went downstairs to their cafe/deli thing for food. What do you know? The sandwich makes us sick.
If you're looking for what appears to be a 90s hotel in terrible condition but filled with low quality ikea furnishings and a ghetto club downstairs, by all means, endure the rude staff and bodily fluid stains and enjoy your stay at Aloft!

review_title: The sinking feeling of the first, sharp whiff of cigarette when entering the non-smoking room
review_text:
After locating the epicenter of ciggie smoke to the bathroom, minor consolation was achieved by leaving the exhaust fan on. The next revelation was the concavity that characterized the queen bed. The regular nocturnal door slamming throughout the night drove home the salient qualities of the mattress. 
The one thing that I was pleased about was our early return to the hotel after dinner. As the parking lot was just about full when we returned at 9:00pm the prospect of remotely parking our car in the adjacent neighborhood(?) was not inviting.
Lovely hotel with good facilities in an excellent location. The pub downstairs is fantastic!

Why does Priceline keep sending me to these terrible hotels? 
Rooms are large, much larger than in other hotels. But it's a dump. Dirty toilet, super loud heater that over heats some of the room while the rest is freezing. Smells of cigarette and pot smoke. Yuck. 
But I have 2 32 inch samsung flat screens so I couldn't give it one star.

review_title: OK but nothing special for a Crowne Plaza
review_text:
The location is good - walking distance to area museums and attractions such as the Franklin Institute. Wireless internet is fast.
However, none if the rooms come with fridge unless you pay $25! Why does the Crowne Plaza, a supposed high end hotel, nickle and dime me?
The onsite cafe is good for coffee and pastries but the restaurant, Elephant and Castle is an overpriced disappointment. No breakfast included here.
For tech geeks bringing their own video toys like a Roku, Sling, or media player, the small, lame, outdated 27" CRT television has no inputs whatsoever (RCA, HDMI, etc) so you're stuck with the Lodgenet junk. On the bright side, the wireless was fast enough to stream Netflix which, at the time of this review, was not blocked.

We were there because of work at the Convention Center. Not real handy. Biggest complaint, very bad Internet access. We also had problems with the AC. The staff at the breakfast buffet was great and took very good care of us.

Albergo ben tenuto, camere vivibili anche se non pulitissime.
DisponibilitÃ  parcheggio per auto un po' caro (34$ a notte).
Personale adibito a auto e bagagli decisamente insistente e fastidioso.
Buona posizione (centralissimo); quartiere tranquillo e poco rumoroso.
Non Ã© prevista alcuna penale in caso di cancellazione di prenotazioni (se effettuate per allungare il soggiorno previsto).
Il ristorante attiguo, Tavern 17, offre un menu ridotto ma di buona qualitÃ .
Abbiamo soggiornato al radisson durante l'uragano irene, agosto 2011.
Il personale Ã© stato molto attento e cordiale; la struttura era ben organizzata e ha trasmesso sicurezza e protezione ai clienti. Hanno messo a disposizione acqua, torce e quanto fosse necessario in caso di inconvenienti indotti dall'uragano.

Arrived to the hotel way before checkin time. Expected to still be treated with some welcoming hospitality. Instead it was almost like we were bothering the gentleman at the front desk.
Overall it was a positive experience. The hotel is walking distance to the Terminal market and even to the visitors center and the historic sites surrounding it. If my pregnant wife can do it, so can you! Otherwise there are plenty of bus lines with regular schedules that run down market. Tip: if you plan on busing it, buy some tokens at the many newsstands up and down the street. 
Also within walking distance to high end shopping on Walnut.

Habitacion no muy grande, pero bonita.
Cama expectacular.
Bar en el hotel muy agradable.
Ubicacion muy buena

I got stuck here on a hotwire deal you get what you pay for. They rooms were so small about the size of a cruise ship cabin. 2 twin beds did not realize I was in a European hotel. Access to the lobby was difficult either a slow elevator or a stair case that winded through dirty hall ways. Room was clean and location was good but won't stay there again

Ever since I was a kid I've dreamed of visiting Philly. Finally, aged 36 I lived my dream and ran those Rocky steps. I would personally like to thank the staff at Crowne Plaza for a pleasant vacation. Coming from the UK, we found the location tremendous,all in walking distance of the city's main attractions and those famous steps.
Extremely courteous staff, who were always available to ensure our stay was memorable.
Thoroughly recommend the Elephant & Castle for your meal... Bang On! As we Brits say.
I am very much hoping to return to the City early 2012.. I have no hesitation in choosing CP again. I'd like to book direct as opposed to using a travel agent. Would love to hear from you Bob. See you next trip.

The good: good location for business in downtown Philly. Free managers reception with beer wine and cocktails. Free hot breakfast. Rooms are big. I mean studio apartment big. With microwave, minifridge and wetbar. The bad: the place badly needs a fresh coat of paint and some new furniture. Not to say it isn't clean, but it looks worn. Tip: if you need a beer or whatever after the manager's reception ends skip the on property TGI Fridays. There are several pubs very close by with more charm and better beer.

We stayed here for the Philly marathon the night of nov 19. Our stay was short but our overall experience was decent. Very thing seemed really clean and the beds were quite comfortable. There were two labeled choices of pillows which I thought was great and convenient.
Location wise this was a great spot. We didn't do much tourism because of the race, but our locatin to restaurants was great. We were also a short walk from the marathon route, and we got to watch our runner in 4 different spots and walked back to the hotel at the end of the race.
The one draw back on race weekend was the check out time. The race started at 7am, and most runners finish in 4-5 hours, meaning 11am or noon. Checkout was at 11am, and cost extra to get a later time. We had two rooms, one with spectators and one with our runner, so we extended the time on one room so she could wind down after the race. The 11am time was really inconvenient because we barely had enough time to see the finish, find our runner and get back to the hotel for 11... And she happens to be quite a fast runner. It would have been nice if the hotel extended checkout time for race day oly.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Hotel Historic District Philadelphia

review_title: Nice room, good location and value
review_text: We spent one night here. The check in staff was super- maps, resto directions, taxi help. The room was very clean- only about 12 rooms to a floor in an odd shaped building, but we had nice views from the room. We walked to dinner and there were parks nearby to enjoy. Quiet at night. Breakfast was typical for an E-S. We would recommend!

review_title: Safe location, clean rooms, friendly staff!
review_text: I had to be in Philly for an extensive period of time & stayed here at Holiday Inn. I always felt safe here. The staff was always accomodating, the rooms always clean, & the hotel is in a great location to walk to many different places. The food in the bar was always fresh and hot, though it did take a little longer to get the meal. Breakfast is either from the menu or the buffett. Try To stay in a higher room, 7-8 th floors-great views if you can face the bridge! Have a great stay! This is where I will stay when I return to Philadelphia!
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Hotel Historic District Philadelphia

review_title: Great location but older and worn facility and staff charged me almost $500 for a free stay
review_text:
The hotel is convenient to the historic sites as well as restaurants and bars on Market street. The facility is not remarkable; it is your average suburban HI. The bathrooms have been partially redone recently but the mattresses seem very uncomfortable. 
Front desk staff seems clueless. I was using my Priority Club points (literally all of them) for a free rewards stay but they still charged my credit card $465. Now I have to deal with the hassle of disputing it.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Hotel Historic District Philadelphia

review_text:
Spent two nights here with spouse during weekend visit. Short walk from Market East SEPTA stop from Airport.
Check in was quick and easy. Received room on 8th floor looking west towards downtown.
Room nicely furnished. Bed comfy and linens very nice.
Quiet area. Starbucks 1 block east on Arch. Easy walk to Independence sites, Constituition Center and much more.
Would stay here again.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Hotel Historic District Philadelphia

review_text: I just checked in today. The receptionist was so rude. One of the elevator showed signs of potential fire and they stopped it. Then I asked him that it would be safe to use elevator. He replied to me, " you could use stairs if you want." in addition, He did not say sorry about the inconvenience due to the problem with the elevator.

Simply put it's a very dirty unkept hotel. Lobby furniture is very warn. Make your way up to the rooms and the hallways are very dirty with day old room service trays and unvaccuumed. Door to my room was very dirty and damaged. You can see in the pictures the curtains had stains in them, the pillows had holes, refrigerator was in terrible condition, and the safety latch was completely broken off. Finally there were exposed pipes with cobwebs on them in the room. When holiday inn remodeled they obviously missed this hotel. My suggestion is look elsewhere for a much cleaner hotel!
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Hotel Historic District Philadelphia

review_title: Not up to Embassy Suites standards!
review_text: We recently booked a stay at this hotel for five nights - we only stayed one night. The air conditioner did not work. They sent someone up pretty quickly to fix it. The bathroom door was broken and the ceiling was molding with parts of it falling down. I was afraid to put the kids down on the floor because it was dirty. The nice cheese plate that was advertised when I booked the room online was obviously on the fridge too long - the nuts were mushy!! This experience is not what I have come to expect from embassy suites!

I have stayed at this hotel on several occasions. The staff are incredibly kind and helpful. I travel for work and have stayed in many different chains, at many different price levels, and I seem to always come back to this one when I am in Philadelphia... Thank- you to the staff for another great stay!
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Hotel Historic District Philadelphia

review_title: Highly recommend for traveler with kids
review_text: We stayed there around 7/9-11, got the stay and play package and we got a two room suite. Great walking distance to museum, and short driving distance to zoo, touch museum, downtown and pretty much everywhere, the breakfast is buffet style and good variety of food. A little crowded on Sunday morning but overall it was good. Internet is charge per device though, if you have touch, laptop or iPad you could be charged three times. The room was clean and spacious, mini kitchen but no plate or any utensil. We really love it here and will stay again very soon

I stayed at the Hilton garden inn about 3 weeks ago I was visiting a friend in the city who lived near by great location right in the heart of Chinatown the reading terminal market has to be one of the best places I've been to in my life my room was nice and cozy although I didn't care for their "sleep number beds" the front desk was awesome especially on young lady Janika extremely pleasant very informative a smile that can light up a room people like her is why I continue to come back to different hotels. I will definitely be staying here again
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn Philadelphia Center City

review_text: We stayed here one night & I'm glad that was it. The light switch on our bathroom was filthy and the room had a terrible smell to it. It was ok for a night but I wouldn't recommend it to a friend.

review_title: Great for staying in historic downtown!
review_text: This place is right in the middle of historic Philly! My friend and I were able to walk to several bars and cool restaurants within blocks of the hotel. The next day we just had to walk around the corner to Ben Franklin's burial site! A few blocks from that is the Liberty Bell and Independence Hall! Perfect location for seeing Philly history! Will book again!
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Hotel Historic District Philadelphia

review_text:
First I should say that as a 27 year old making a teacher's salary there's no way I could've afforded to stay here unless a friend I was with got us a discount through her work. So things that impressed me about this place may not be so impressive to people who are used to staying at such a pricey hotel. 
This place was very easy to find; it's right off the Benjamin Franklin parkway a few blocks from the art museum, city hall, and love park. We heard from friends that it cost $35 to park at the hotel so we found a nearby lot on Arch St. that was only $27. The rooms (which would ordinarily cost around $300 a night) were awesome. They had a spacious living area with a tv and seating for 6 as well as a kitchenette area, nice bathroom, and separate bedroom with two queens. Our view was the best! The rooms ending I'm "03" look straight down the parkway at the art museum. 
To top it all off they provided complimentary beer and wine during happy hour and an extensive complimentary hot breakfast the next morning. My only gripe is that the tourist attraction magazine in the room was from the previous month so all of the events listed had already occurred and when I asked the front desk for a current copy they said housekeeping had received themand hadn't yet put them out. I'm still not sure why I couldn't have one. 
Definitely stay here if you can afford it!

International traveler who's stayed here many times. Along with the single beds, small rooms, rude staff and no breakfast here's some stories for ya. I've been woken up by a jackhammer doing construction on my outside wall at 7am and no one cared. I've had a not working AC unit and 2 times the fire alarm has gone off after midnight or at dawn for 20 minutes and again. No one cared. The owner of this hotel should be ashamed to even call it a 3 star hotel. The only reason anyone is here is because of priceline.

I chose the hotel randomly with little research and I'm glad it worked out. The location was very ideal, the room was clean and large. The view was non-existent but I was too busy sleeping on the comfortable bed to care.
I was able to check I early...i think they understood how tired i was and rather than have me wait for my room to be ready, they moved me to an available room with two queen beds (and I was just one person)...I thought that was kind!
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn Philadelphia Center City

review_text: I was in Philadelphia for the marathon this weekend, I got to the hotel fairly early and surprisingly my room was ready when I got there upon check in I was greeted with a warm hello I dnt remember her name but she's the only woman with blonde hair, she gave me plenty of information about the hotel amenities and a nice little gift bag with the essentials I needed to get through the race. Very unexpected I thought it was a kind gesture. When she asked what kind of a late checkout I needed I was really stunned because most hotels don't honor that and to top it off we had special marathon keys that will be an excellent keep sake. The Hilton Garden Inn went beyond the call of making sure the guest come first I was extremely pleased with my stay and I look forward to coming back. My room was nice and comfortable and i was greeted with a hello and smile by almost every staff member. Great job Mr. Williams
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn Philadelphia Center City

review_title: Great location for the business traveler.
review_text:
Staying in downtown Philadelphia is a great location for banking and general business people 
In addition to a close proximity to the Convention Center, the hotel is close to all major medical facilities, and Historical Attractions.
The staff, dinning and cleanliness are excellent.
The hotel is a bargain for the location.
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn Philadelphia Center City

review_title: The warmth of a family run hotel with and upscale and modern twist.
review_text: What a great experience. The rooms are small, but nice with very smart use of space. The service is genuine and great. They are simply nice people who make an effort. The lounge has great hot chocolate and coffee and the restaurant looks really nice. Overall, super clean and organized and a great value. Steps away from soho, little italy and the best shopping and eating this city can offer.

review_title: The Pearl is a gem of a hotel!
review_text:
We stayed the last week of November for the tree lighting. The hotel is in an excellent location for walking to theaters. The Book of Mormon is across the street, Chicago is adjacent, Sister Act is 4 blocks. The proximity to the theaters cannot be stressed enough. 
And here's the "gem" part--the rooms are quiet! Once you retire to your room, the noise of the area stays outside. The beds are comfy and plush. There is a coffee maker in the room and continental breakfast (consisting of oatmeal, bagels, pastries, cereals and fresh fruits) is served during generous morning hours. There is also a hosted happy hour although we were never back in time to enjoy it. Service is excellent and friendly!

Parking is 49.00 for 24 hours. Don't pay more than 129.00. Great cleaning people, however bed bugs are hard to compete with. The hotel thrives on location, has a tiny refrigerator and microwave only. Room service is 20% for service. Its desperately in need of renovation!

Central , good service , clean !
But tried to change room- smaller ( stayed for 2 weeks). I did not Get a smaller room - and i feel they did not try ! 
But everything else was excellent !

review_title: Great, friendly staff with a wonderful location for sight seeing!
review_text:
Stayed overnight and arrived after visiting the Philadelphia Museum of art (fabulous) and Eastern State Penitentiary ( not up my alley).
We arrived tired and hungry but the we checked in quickly, and when we arrived in the room, the hotel clerk, (Frank I think) called to see if we were happy and needed anything. The room was wonderful, great views of the city! Only complaint was that breakfast had no fresh fruit and the coffee tasted instant. We left in the morning for a full day of sightseeing and the bell clerk kept our bags for us. They were most accomodating including allowing us to leave our car with the valet for 2 hours past the time. I will stay here again.
If you like the Embassy Suites there are no surprises here; rooms are typical Embassy rooms. The staff here is the hotel's best asset; everyone is extremely nice and helpful.

review_title: Don't stay here, just pick any other airport hotel
review_text: I wish I could say I was exaggerating, but altogether and with manager escorts, I had to go back to the front desk 7 times to get a working room key and a room that wasn't already occupied. The carpets were stained in both rooms I saw, one light didn't work, one phone was broken and the second couldn't get a dial tone, the shower door isn't sealed so water leaks all over the floor, the soap holders were loose on shower wall letting soap fall out, and the list goes on and on. The hassle of acquiring a room is a huge deal and everything else just makes it worse. Don't bother coming here, just go to the much newer sheraton suites, sheraton four points, or aloft down the road. I guarantee you the free breakfast and managers evening reception is not worth it. I should have checked trip advisor before I stayed, with only 59% recommending the hotel, there's a reason and I found it.

My husband and I both travel on business so we stay at a lot of hotels. We both thought this was The worst hotel experience we've ever had. We only stayed her one night on HHonors points on our last night of vacation because we had an early flight and wanted to be near the airport. the hotel was horribly understaffed. there was only one clerk at the front desk and a ton of check ins. My husband tried to print our boarding passes and the business center printer was not working. He waited in the front desk line a second time for help and it took forever to get help. We arrived in the evening and needed to get our daughter to bed. there were no linens for the pull out bed in the room. when I called down to the desk they said it would be 30 minutes before they could send someone up!!! are you kidding me??? So my husband went back downstairs, waited in the line again. the security guy ended up bringing them up shortly after. There was a huge group of people there for a family reunion. they were going in and out of the pool getting the floor in the lobby, elevators, and hallways all wet. There was only one employee trying to get them to stop (we found out later he was the food and beverage manager). the group was really loud and were letting their children run everywhere in the hotel. There was a sign up that asked everyone to be quiet after 10 pm. This was NOT enforced at all. My daughter could sleep in the living room area on the pullout bed because the noise in the hall was so loud. She ended up having to sleep on the floor in the bedroom part with us. She was crying at one point because she was so tired but couldn't sleep! My husband called down to the desk many times throughout the night but the problem was never solved. Then in the middle of the night, loud music started blaring near us. Again, calling did NO good! The desk staff sounded annoyed that we kept calling!!! We were talking to another couple the next morning who had the same issues. They said "oh well, if the hotel tries and the guests won't listen what can they do?". You can kick them out that's what! And if they give you grief call the cops! I hope that group business was worth it to them for all the other guests to have a miserable stay. I want my HHonors points back for that stay! We left for the airport the next morning exhausted instead of rested. The only good thing about the stay was the breakfast.
Breakfast was amazing! Clean and upscale. The only negative was that the sofa bed is unsleepable! Springs hurt so bad to even sit on. Was pricy, but happy with our stay other than the bad sofa bed.

This is to let readers know that despite the pro forma response post from this hotel (Sorry we could not provide you with the amenities you expected -- like a clean room!!! -- we will reach out to you to make it right), the hotel has not contacted me. So it's dirty and they lie. Just thought you all should know.

Stayed for two nights because I was running the marathon and the hotel was extremely convenient for that purpose. Close to everything we wanted to do. The room was perfect (and a bit oddly laid out) in the sense that it was clean and quiet. Would definitely consider coming back.

We are currently staying at the Windsor Suites as family of three. When we checked in the lady at the reception seemed to be unhappy that she had to serve customers, beside the room number she said nearly nothing and spent quit a lot of her time on the phone during chekin. When we went to the room we got nearly depressed as it was more like a box then an apartment. Asking at the reception for a room matching the hotel description we were threaten like dump, stating that all rooms are equivalent. The fire rescue plan told something different, and today we had the chance to get a look of another (single) guests room which was about 50% bigger. At least we now understand the different ratings here. Having a room towards the street is quit spacy, having a room to the backside is horrible. With the "no service" reception this is a "no recommendation"!

I have no complaints at all about my stay here and would definitely recommend this hotel. Nice, clean rooms, friendly, helpful staff, convenient location to a lot of walkable places. Would stay here again if I ever get back up that way.
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Independence Park Hotel

review_text: Huge rooms with kitchen, dining table, loads of storage - after stayIng in tiny manhattan rooms this place was MASSIVE!! the decor could do with an overhaul (was a bit 'Fresh Prince of Bel Air'), but it was nice and clean. The pool on the roof was basic but fine, shame the sun wasn't out!! Had some great food in Philly (tapas in Bar Ferdinand in thd Northern Liberties, Mexican in El Vez), will be back hopefully!

My family (husband,10 yr old son and myself ) spent 4 nights at the Windsor. Everyone was very nice and helpful from the front desk to the engineers. If we asked for something it was always there within 10 minutes
The hotel is within walking distance to quite a few historical sites also. The only thing we didn't like about the location was that everything was closed by 6 pm so you had to go out of the area to find something at night. But all and all it was a nice stay and I would book there again.

review_title: Watch out for bad location and fees, fees, fees!
review_text:
yourself a favor and don't stay here. Â This hotel is far removed from the parts of the Old City that anyone would want to visit. Â It's basically on an island between the river and I-95. Â Unless you really like long walks to get to restaurants or attractions, you'll end up with a cab ride every time you leave the hotel.
Parking is $38 per night. Â Internet access is $10 per day per device! Â So if you park your car and want to use our laptop and iPad you will spend $58 per day on top of your room rate.
As to be expected in a high rise hotel far from non-hotel restaurants, the room service is very expensive- we spent $46 on an appetizer, a sandwich, and ice cream. Â The food was mediocre, but at least it was served promptly.
The hotel had other problems. Â The tv had to be turned off and on three times to get a picture. Â When the picture appeared it was a fuzzy analog screen without even the local comcast sports channel to watch the 76ers. Â I was put on hold each time I called the front desk, sometimes for several minutes at a time. Â Wen I called the manager I was ushered into voicemail. Â In the bathroom, the water ran out of the shower and covered the floor with water every time we showered.
I'm sure this place is fine for conventions and perhaps huge tour groups but do not stay here for personal travel.
hotel_name: Hyatt Regency Philadelphia at Penn's Landing

review_text:
Stayed here on a business trip. The hotel is certainly expensive. ~$300 for the room, 25 for overnight self parking, 6 to use the computers in the business center (hotspot wifi in rooms- not free), 17 for breakfast buffet... It adds up. That being said, the location is great. Convenient off and on to 95 without having to drive though the city. The staff was extremely helpful, courteous, and professional. An odd note- after parking in the garage, you walk into the on-site Avis rental center with a few disheveled employees lounging around. Since those are the first hotel employees you meet, it starts your stay on a sour note. 
The restaurant on-site is terrible for lunch (expensive and tasteless food) but breakfast is decent. 
Overall, a pretty good hotel run by professionals.
hotel_name: Hyatt Regency Philadelphia at Penn's Landing

review_text:
This is a fine and comfortable hotel. But it is a $10 cab ride away from anything and everything you want to see, do or eat in Philly. 
The rate was good and it sure beat staying at the airport when everything else was sold out, but I'd rather stay closer to the action next time.
hotel_name: Hyatt Regency Philadelphia at Penn's Landing

review_text: Walking distance to historic sites biggest plus. Parking is such a hassle, and expensive, they should offer valet for free.
hotel_name: Hyatt Regency Philadelphia at Penn's Landing

review_text: What has happen to you omni.I ck in with my family for two days of pure hell.if it wasn't the bellman trying to hustle my wife along with another cab driver where they have a special relationship with or waiting 2hours for pillows or the overflowing toliet from above our room or replacing the drywall nextdoor or the family with the teenage daughter screaming bloody murder or the manager hanging up on me when I complained.no housekeeping service.the noise from the street was overwhelming I was dreaming thought I was outside camping.the attitude from the staff was unfriendly made u feel as if you uncomfortable.i will say your saving grace is Aj your GM nice guy offered my family a free night but I didn't want to extend this nightmare.I will say the lobby was cozy with the fireplace very nice.I think for a omni this is just horrible I will stay with another brand in the future.
Located on Penns Landing. Near historical sites. I would stay here again.
hotel_name: Hyatt Regency Philadelphia at Penn's Landing

review_text:
I stayed at this hotel due to work commitments not by choice. It is situated outside the city centre by a busy road network. If you don't get a room not facing the water you'll experience a lot of noise-I managed to change my allocated room but had to wait 45 minutes to do so.
Also I'm disgusted that in this day and age hotels still charge for wifi-shame on you Hyatt hotels! The only positive is the restaurant: expensive but reasonably good food. The breakfast is good value for money. This hotel is ok for conventions but once the sessions are finished it's definitely time to get out of this hotel as soon as possible. Disappointing...
hotel_name: Hyatt Regency Philadelphia at Penn's Landing

review_text: I was a little skeptical when this hotel was revealed. But for the rate what a value. Great location clean exceeded my expectations. Parking was more than the price listed on the web site. Overall great stay.
hotel_name: Hyatt Regency Philadelphia at Penn's Landing

review_title: The hotel is a little away from theMain street
review_text:
The location is not far from the center but is not close aider. 
I did like that the HD TV is very big and have very nice channels.
This hotel is right besides the embassy suites.

Spent one night with two children. Good location. Had to walk a bit to the old city. Great view of Delaware. Very clean rooms. Rooms a bit on small side. If you park your own car in the garage it is a bit of a hassle to get to the hotel.
hotel_name: Hyatt Regency Philadelphia at Penn's Landing

review_text:
The Independence Park Hotel was a last minute stop on our drive back to New York, and it was a stop to remember! It is a quaint little place, almost blink and you'll miss it, but once inside its quite grand and welcoming. The warm tea and cookies in the lobby gave it an old world feel that my family and I enjoyed. The room was clean and well decorated, housekeeping staff very friendly.
And talk about location! Literally everything within footsteps for tourist attractions and restaurants! We will definitely try to return and stay for a bit longer next time!
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Independence Park Hotel

review_title: If you're going to Philadelphia, don't stay anywhere else.
review_text: The location is THE best in Philadelphia for seeing everything in the historic district. The staff,helpful and professional. We did not eat in the hotel, we have 2 children and the hotel restaurant is more for the older set. The rooms are beautiful and spotless. Our had a gorgeous park view with a bridge view as well. The bus tours are around the corner, everything is so easy to get to even with 2 children and a pram. For parents of young children...go to the Franklin Institute and the Please Touch Museum. review_title: Great hotel and location, skip the valet parking.
review_text: Stayed for 1 night on our vacation. Hotel location was fantastic, historical sites were as close as across the street. Hotel staff at check in were friendly and helpful. Only downside and reason for 4 stars instead of 5 was the valet parking. We paid the extra $10 over self parking for the convenience, but after waiting on the street for almost 30 min for my car (they first brought the wrong car) I wondered why I was paying a premium to replace a 2 min walk to the garage with a 30 min wait.

This hotel is In Society Hill, the most historic neighbourhood. It is right by independence hall, liberty bell, US mint, Carpenters and many other attractions. As this was our first trip with our 4 month old it was perfect. We around and then come back to the hotel if need be, which we had to several times esp as it was so hot.
It is a very kid friendly hotel, as they let had an extra sofa bed in the room.
The rooms were spacious and clean. The bathrooms were very clean and big.
They provide valet parking or you can Park in the garage which is right by the hotel and very convenient.
It also has a restaurant which is fairly pricey but has good desserts.
So the bottom line is it has a fabulous location. If I go back, I would definitely stay there again.
Room was small but we had a great time.. Breakfast was good.. We will visit again

review_title: Disappointing compared to past Sofitel experience but great location
review_text:
A disappointment compared to previous Sofitel experience.Â 
I stayed at the Sofitel in DC on Lafayette Square in March and had an exceptional experience. The room was luxuriously appointed and the restaurant provided a delicious and satisfying breakfast with friendly and attentive service.Â 
The same cannot be said about the Sofitel Philadelphia. The room was drab and uninspired although the bed was extremely comfortable. In DC, I was charmed upon returning to the room in the evening to find the bed turned down with classical ambient music playing on the stereo. The housekeeping staff in Philly were not so attentive.Â 
Breakfast in the morning was overpriced and underwhelming, and I'm pretty sure we never actually received the selection of pastries that were supposed to accompany our breakfasts. The "Philly breakfast," called the "American breakfast" on the room service menu, was tasty but small for $21 and the wait staff took their sweet time attending to us.Â 
These are petty concerns, yes, but when you are paying for a stay at a luxury brand-name hotel it's not too much to expect a high level of treatment and consistency from location to location.Â 
One thing Sofitel has going for it here though is location. It's very close to major shopping and dining areas.

The location of Sofitel at Philadelphia is wonderful. Â There are lots shops and restaurants around, and a great coffeehouse (Lacolombe) is just a few blocks away. Â For around $200 a night, the rooms are spacious but old, have really thin walls, and old windows that let all the street sounds in. Â The front staff are great but the concierge was not optimal. Â Overall, a three star experience.

review_title: The hotel rooms, installations, and service was good but due to the ILMUNC conference, the elevator access was limited to such a
review_text:
I traveled to the hotel as a chaperone for a group of students participating in the ILMUNC conference held at the Sheraton Center City Philadelphia this past January. Our experience with the hotel rooms and service was good. The high point of our stay was one concierge, Ms. Mastrobuoni, who was exceedingly helpful with a number of arrangements we needed to have made. She was always very patient, attentive, and informative and she went out of her way to be helpful. 
On the other hand, the low point of the visit was the fact that at times, we would wait for an elevator so that we could come down from our floor for 15 minutes or more. On one occasion we even resorted to walking down more that 24 flights of stairs after we had waited for an elevator for 25+ minutes only to have five completely full ones stop and go on. Because we were participants in the conference that caused the elevator congestion, we were able to tolerate the inconvenience. For those who were not part of the event and were unwittingly affected by it, however, the experience must have been unacceptable. For the future, the hotel management must engineer a system for running their six elevators that circumvents such a degree of disfunction. One final moderately disconcerting feature of our trip was when, upon our checking out at 3:00am to catch an early-morning flight and asking at the front desk for help confirming what we thought were the directions to the airport the desk attendant replied, "I wouldn't know, I don't drive," and nothing else. It is understandable that any one employee may not be able to accommodate our need for directions and we cannot fault her for not knowing. It would have been more appropriate, however, had she then done something to help us find out such as call in another staff member on duty or look up the directions online. 
 Overall, I would recommend this hotel, but be sure to ask in advance if there they will be hosting any conferences and, if you are driving, secure your directions with the concierge well in advance and do not rely on front desk personnel to be helpful.

Also, we had a problem with our room the first night--the Heating/AC unit was super loud. It sounded like there were squirrels trapped in it! We had to keep the TV on all night to drown out the noise. When we spoke to the front desk the next morning they promptly changed our room (to a larger corner room) and gave us free breakfast the next day! I would definitely stay here again.
