We love this hotel! My parents and I stayed two nights here recently and it was pure heaven. To start, we arrived at 12:30, and even though check-in was hours away, they accomodated us in a matter of minutes. The valet staff were prompt and nice. The overall Spanish ambiance of the hotel was spectacular and bewitching. We loved our immaculate, plush suite (519) and sitting downstairs in the Cork Bar taking in all the architectural features and people watching over frozen margaritas. Don't miss the delicious room service breakfasts or the Paella Valencia at Las Ramblas downstairs. This is also the BEST location I've ever stayed in on the Riverwalk, minutes from everything but nice and quiet at night. We'll be back, you can bank on it!

review_title: It's the best hotel I've stayed at!!!
review_text:
They have the best service
Very very nice employes and the best clubs in SD club 207 and club float with the best VIPs and the best hosts

I was a bit thrown off by the neighborhood, but once you are inside the hotel you are ok. Room was clean. The beds were comfortable. I have a super sharp sense of smell and room smelled clean. Hallways clean and lobby is pretty and front desk staff is friendly. A bit noisy outside, not the prettiest view from outside but we were overall very pleased with this little hotel
Clean rooms, great service and good rates. Smart decision.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Diego - Mission Valley

review_text: This place was way over rated and not worth what we paid. The roof top pool was not included in the $200.00 per night stay. There was only 1 cup of coffee. Breakfast started at $10.00 for strawberries and whipped cream. Front desk staff was rude. This was not the ideal weekend get away for my husband and i.

review_title: Hip, rocking hotel in a great location.
review_text: What a great location in San Diego, this Hard Rock personifies the name by being hip, trendy, fun, and overall a great time. If you want a quiet get away this place is not for you but if you like action and nightlife this place is #1.

review_title: Safety and service aside, this hotel would have been the hotel for us while we were looking for a permanent place to stay here i
review_text: My wife and I have both been assigned to San Diego recently (since late August) as part of our company's expansion. We initially stayed at Residence Inn in a 2 bedroom suite for 3 weeks before deciding to move to Staybridge Suites in Mira Mesa, with similar amenities and accommodations. My wife and I initially thought that value wise it gives more bang for the buck. But just after one night we already had a scary and disappointing experience. First when we were getting ready for work, the closet door which should at least be 50 lbs heavy, fell on our 3 yo son while he was closing the thing after getting a pair of socks. We were scared s#*t upon realizing what happened. But when we realized it was just his toe that got hit, we decided to call the operator to send in the maintenance guy to fix the closet. Our son recovered and looks fine to me. However, when we came back to our room later that day, the house keeping did not exactly do what was supposed to be done, which is to clean at least the floor and replenish the coffee, soaps, shampoo and conditioners in both rooms. At least the house keeper took the tip we left at the table. So far it's disappointing now we're thinking of moving out by Friday.
hotel_name: Staybridge Suites San Diego - Sorrento Mesa

review_title: Not what I expected from Hyatt
review_text:
Except for RESTRAUNT Manager, staff was less than friendly. Due to poor weather, river walk was not option so we stayed at hotel for several meals. First was disaster, did not get what was ordered. Manager invited us back for free breakfast. Second meal was better, but no attention to details. Every table needed service, salt/pepper/sugar etc. Breakfast was best meal but tables not serviced Real issue was last day. With weather warmer, she asked if she could go on patio to sit in sun and read. Was told she could only go out if she ordered food. So she said ok. Then told also had to order a drink. Also agreed. Still it was like this was a major issue. 
Will stay else where next time.

The lady working the front desk was less than friendly upon check-in. My husband was outside trying to drop off our car and he had to call me only cell when I was checking in because the valet told him we were not on "the list." Shouldn't the valet have called the front desk if this was an issue rather than my husband having to call me and then me having to tell the lady at the desk the issue? Later on, when I went down to get our car, I approached the valet who was having socializing with another valet and I literally had to stand there and wait for them to finish their conversation before they would even acknowledge me. That night, back in our room, when we pulled out the sleeper sofa for our little boys to sleep, the sheets were dirty! There was even a pubic hair 
on the sheets and stains on the 
pillows! I called the front desk and
 it was a total of 30 minutes before
 we finally had a clean bed. Keep in
 mind I had a 4 year old and 6 year
 old who were exhausted from 
traveling all day. The dirty sheets
 were such a turn off that I was 
grossed out the rest of our stay. I 
will say, the hotel is very pretty. 
We enjoyed the hotel restaurant 
(kids eat free all day!). Dinner was 
decent (not 5 star by any means but still good) and so was the
 breakfast buffet with lots of options
 including fresh Belgian waffles and omlettes made to order. There was a bit of traffic noise outside our room but luckily I brought our white noise machine and cranked it up full blast to drown out the noise. If your staying here on the weekend I would really try not to stay near the lobby area. The noise from the bar got kind of loud on Saturday night. 
Next time we come to San Antonio we will probably not be staying here.
Both Eli and Derrick were great ambassadors for the HR Hotel! It was an awesome b-day experience.

My family and I stayed at the holiday inn mission valley a month or so ago. This was not a pleasure trip as my husband was having surgery bit come time to leave we didn't want to go. The staff was very friendly and helpful. They brought up a fridge by us merely asking if it was possible. My kids needed help logging in on the wi fi and the lady at the front desk was a henipus and got that job done. I fedinstely will stay there again even if it is way out of the way. Way to go to all your staff. Beth holt
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Diego - Mission Valley

review_text: I had the pleasure of staying at the Hard Rock in October during a short business trip and it was amazing. From arrival to departure and everywhere in between, they remembered my name, made me feel like a VIP. Adam in Mary Jane's was exceptional. Jeremy, one of the managers, went above and beyond to get my suit pressed in time for a meeting. Nobu was rediculously incredible, the jalapeÃ±o sashimi is to die for - the crowd and the vibe in 207 was perfect, not what I'd expect in San Diego. My room was spotless and comfortable. I even had someone help get me a cab at 5am, which the valet made seem easy (I knew it wasn't). I can't wait to come back, this is the ONLY hotel in SD I would ever stay at or recommend. These dudes get it right, very impressed - like a Four Seasons but way more approachable and relentlessly cool.

If you want to be in a perfect location in San Antonio, this is the place! It is along the famous Riverwalk (the river flows through the lobby). The lobby was undergoing renovation when we were there (Sept 2010), but the rooms are not dated and appear clean. Our room was perhaps the 15th floor with a wonderful view, looking directly at the Alamo (literally, the Alamo was 300 feet straight ahead with a completely uninstructed view). I simply asked politely for a room with a view when checking in, no extra charge (granted, it was a quiet weekend). Street parking can be found near the hotel free (at least on the weekend). Directly in front of the hotel, there are about five unmarked parallel parking spots. There are no signs, and it seems everyone thought it was for loading/unloading. However, the hotel has a U-shaped driveway under the building on the Lobby level, so these parking spots are literally free--and it's the best parking at the hotel (way better than parking in their parking deck!). You can save nearly $30 per night by parking on the street, right in front of the hotel since no one seems to know the secret about the unmarked parallel parking spots!
Overall, highly recommended hotel. The newer hotels (like the Grand Hyatt) cannot beat this property simply because of it's excellent location! With the river going through the hotel, you cannot get much closer to the Riverwalk...and with the Alamo directly facing the hotel just a block away, San Antonio's most famous attraction could not be closer!

Stayed here for 3 nights in late May. Room was well planned with plenty of space for 2 adults and 4 kids. View overlooking the pool was welcomed. Nice breakfast with lots to choose from. Pool and bbq area were very clean and quiet. Checked out early and they had a to-go beakfast bag ready for each of us. Excellent. Shops right next door and food court also. Great location
hotel_name: Staybridge Suites San Diego - Sorrento Mesa

review_title: A fake plastic watering can, for a fake Chinese rubber plant.
review_text:
My wife and I were planning a trip to SD and wanted to stay a few nights in the Gaslamp Quarter. We originally wanted to stay at Hotel Indigo, but we waited too long to pull the trigger and the rates went way up, so we went with the Hard Rock with some apprehension based on the good reviews.
Well, big mistake. The hotel is packed with trendy 20 somethings and plenty of older folks trying to act like they are far younger than they actually are. It is SoCo, so I guess fashion is important everywhere, bur this trendy hotel and it's guest have a very plastic feel. 
Overall, the room, location and service are all up to par, but the atmosphere is too cliche for me. 
Lest the reader get the wrong idea, I am 40 and have an abnormal love for rock and roll, so I thought it would be fine. The wall art and collectables were cool, but the scene was too much. Maybe I am just getting old . . .
This was a great, cool hotel with fantastic night life and restaurants nearby! Definitely coming back...

review_title: Best hotel I've ever stayed in!
review_text: The beds are awesome, the staff is amazing and makes you feel like a rock star, and I love all the memorabilia! Breakfast at Mayjane's was amazing as well. I want to go back already!

review_title: Fun place to go stay at !
review_text: It's an exciting place to go . The mangers will take care of you. With my exspericne I had !
Eli in VIP check in is a tremendous asset to the HARD ROCK. My Favorite place to stay in San Diego.

We were at a different hotel, and left to stay at this hotel.
Better location. Better bed. Better staff.
Just a block from the beach, near a beautiful park, there was plenty of parking very close to the room.
Jim Silver, the manager, was very gracious and friendly. Everyone we met was warm and friendly.
This hotel is a great value. Very clean, basic, wonderful, attentive staff. Nice unassuming hotel when you don't want to pay Hilton prices.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express San Diego Airport - Old Town

review_title: Comfy beds, great showers and very clean
review_text:
Nice location, close to great restaurants and bars.
The double showers heads make the shower experience very special.
We strongly recommend.

I booked this room thru expedia, pictures looked nice. Well when we arrived I realized that this used to be called comfort inn, that I reluctantly stayed at a couple years ago. I felt deceived, for one, the pictures were not from this property and our room was advertised as a queen bed, it was a full. The room themselves were clean and remodeled, but the bed & pillows were so uncomfortable. We went to sit in the jacuzzi one night and there were about 7 employees (still in their uniforms) drinking 40oz beers. I definitely don't think $120/night is worth it. Find another place.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express San Diego Airport - Old Town

review_text: I had a great time at this Hard Rock. The rooms are well done and clean. It's in a perfect location in the Gas Lamp. There are good restaurants and a fun atmosphere.

This hotel is located at the beginning of the Gas Lamp District. It was in the perfect spot and the room was clean and very comfortable. The view was of the parking garage and the stadium, so not the best. Had a great bar in the room with snacks and other things to make your stay, but they were ridiculously over priced. $4.00 for a snickers. Lol. And you could get one downstairs for 99 cents. Was disappointed that we couldn't use the pool or even see it because they use it as a club. But overall enjoyed our stay and would stay there again.

Overall, my stay at this worldmark was ok. So, I'll list my pros and cons
Pros: this worldmark is nestled perfectly between San diego's two main attractions, sea world and the zoo so the drives were pretty short; there are a couple restaurants like el torito just steps away from the property; the rooms were relatively clean
Cons: the view from our room was of the rocky, uninteresting hill side and from the living room was the trash dumpsters and the back of the Radisson or something; a long walk from the elevators to end of the hall rooms; rooms seemed tight and cramped including the kitchens and bathrooms; there was a bulky heater of some sort in one of the bedrooms and the living room that is extremely loud and disruptive
My stay at this worldmark , to say the least, left a lot to be desired

The check in was something out of the stone age. Room smells like urine and lysol. Bathroom still had hair in the shower, dead ants on the wall and no way to stop the bathtub if anyone is brave enough to sit in that DISGUSTING tub. We were supposed to be here four days, checked out after one night. The "hot" breakfast they speak of is bread that you can toast.

My husband and I stayed here for 5 nights. Our first night was ok, but with the train noise, we asked to move to a room that did not back onto the rail tracks. The new room looked fine but my husband woke up with bites/lumps on him after the second night. We haven't experienced bed bugs before so didn't know what they were. We thought it was hives (as he has itchy welts all over him) but after antihistamines proving to be ineffective he looked for other causes. It wasn't until our last night that we suspected bed bugs. We couldn't initially see anything in the bed / mattress, but when we looked the next morning we saw them!! 
We informed staff, Arthur was very apologetic but didn't know what to do/say except sorry. We were initially sent away without any offer for a refund / compensation. 
I went back (after other guests had left the reception area) to again express how angry we were, and that we potentially have to throw out all our possessions / luggage and / or pay for laundry for our entire bag's contents (we live in Australia) and won't be home for another 3 weeks.. Arthur by this time had called his manager to get approval to reimburse us our final nights stay. 5 nights for the price of 4 in a bed bug infested room.. Tital room cost $330 And consequently have to throw out our clothes / shoes / luggage and replace them: total loss of luggage / clothes $800-1000. I really don't think the reimbursement of $100 for our final night was sufficient do you? 
Stay away from this place or at least check that they have successfully managed their bed bug outbreak! 
I am sorry to have to write this but as a traveller I would expect the same feedback from others out there.
hotel_name: San Diego - Days Inn Harbor View / Airport / Convention Ctr

review_text:
I stayed at the Crowne Plaza San Diego for 2 nights for a conference. I got the club value package which included a free breakfast and nightly drinks. A big plus was free in and out parking. 
The rooms were very clean, but a bit dated. The hotel restuarant was convenient and had excellent service, but the cuisine leaned towards coffee shop or cafe vs fine dining. There is an excellent steakhouse across the street, though, if that is your preference. There is also a wonderful onsite spa. 
The staff was excellent on all levels, and the value and personal attention more than made up for any minor detractions. The stay was a top notch value for the price, which was considerably less than others in the area. A great stay whether for business or pleasure.
hotel_name: Crowne Plaza Hotel San Diego - Mission Valley

review_title: A good Monday through Thursday hotel!
review_text: I stayed here with my husband for the week of my sisters wedding! The room was nice, the gym was awesome, the cucumber lemon water was great! Then Friday rolled around, the day of my sisters batchelorette party and I got home late from partying to find a club in my hotel and pretty much in my room with how loud it was! I was on the 5th floor and should not have been able to hear that if the walls had been made soundproof as they should have been. The club proceeded to party til the wee hours of the morning through Sunday night! Then it was also upsetting to find out I had to pay $20 to enter the pool at my hotel! The staff was very insistent that I needed a room card to enter the hotel and get through it. I had to show it five times just to get to my room, what a hassle!! So in conclusion it is a good hotel only on the week days!

My wife and I spent 4 nights at the Hard Rock, and I can honestly say, it is one of the best hotels we've ever stayed in. Hip atmosphere, decor and rooms. May possibly be the most comfortable hotel bed I've ever slept on. There is rock memorabilia everywhere, including the handwritten lyrics to "While My Guitar Gently Weeps", in Mal Evans handwriting and notations wriiten in by George Harrison. For this Beatles fan, it was practically Holy Ground!
The customer service was outstanding - everyone we came in contact with was friendly, helpful and totally guest focused. And one of the coolest amenities I've ever received at a hotel, the use of a Fender TeleCaster at no charge!
The location couldn't be better, right at the entrance to the Gaslamp District and one block from Petco Park. Just a 5 minute walk and your in the stadium. Dozens of restaurants within a few minutes walk of the hotel, although the hotel has restaurants for all tastes. I especially liked sitting at the poolside bar enjoying a cocktail, a plate of pita and hummus and the beautiful weather.
I will say, over the weekend we seemed to have a run of loud, obnoxious drunks yelling in the hallways until the wee hours, but that may have been an unusual occurence for all I know. However, it was such a minor annoyance, it probably wasn't worth mentioning, but be aware...:)
Overall, a terriffic experience, and I would go out of my way to stay at a another Hard Rock Hotel.

Excellent location. Only spent one night here but my pillow smelt funny, I should've asked for a new one but it was late so this is partly my own fault. However everything else was adequate and price reasonable.
hotel_name: San Diego - Days Inn Harbor View / Airport / Convention Ctr

review_text:
Elevator near room . Bell kept going off
every floor.
hotel_name: Crowne Plaza Hotel San Diego - Mission Valley

review_text: They were extremely rude and unprofessional. The rooms were dirty so many things were broken. There was a blood stain on my mattress!

Very nice rooms updated and clean. Nice pool area. The property is spread out over a large area do be prepared for a little walk. A bit confusing they way it's set up. Pool very nice. Room service very limited for kids easy walking to old town
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Hacienda Hotel Old Town

review_text: This is our regular hotel for when my family is in the San Diego area. Has been for a couple years now. I go to college in san diego so whenever they visit me, we stay here. It's clean and pretty well kept. The staff is friendly and will do their best to fix any problems you may have with the rooms. For the price it's definitely worth it!
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN PLUS San Diego / Miramar Hotel

review_title: Ruined the last days of our honeymoon - poor service and lack of care for customers
review_text:
We stayed for three nights in a $399 a night float studio, described on the website as on the pool deck with a private terrace. The room was small and the carpet was "crunchy" as if it had been wet and dried an number of times. The private terrace was 8ft by 6 ft wi wicker sofas over looking a large blank concrete space with cheap astroturf on it. 
The sofas were full of cigarette holes and each morning were hosed down with a strong bleach solution, is meant the cushions were wet all day and couldn't be used and at the terrace smelt like a public toilet. Each day we have to replace the cushions and reset the terrace ourselves - the cleaning teams didn't return to do is.
When we did use our "private" terrace for the first few days we watched engineers and members of staff from the hotel setting up tables, bars for an event just at the end of our terrace - not very private. 
On the last day of our honeymoon from 8 am there were people outside our terrace setting up an event - we were blessed with listening to the staff shouting to each other and we caught to catch up on all their personal gossip as they chatted away - again not very private. At 3 pm the event started and 200-300 people in party mode appeared at the end of our private terrace (which had a rope place across the end - not sure if this was to keep us in or them out). They had a great time firing t-shirts out of air canons drinking and eating. 
My wife got upset when guest continually approached us to ask if they could join us on our terrace - some didn't bother asking we found one guy happily sat on the terrace chatting on his mobile phone.
So overall really poor. We don't have a problem with the hotel hosting great event but we booked our room 12 months in advance and they knew we were on honeymoon - it wouldn't have taken a genius to work out the two things are not compatible and to have offered us a different room - even a downgrade would've been better!
We spoke to the hotel on the friday and at checkout ultimately they just offered platitudes and seemed to think it was our job to offer them a solution to our dissatisfaction. The guy I spoke to was nice enough but he was more interested in getting a complaining customer out of his lobby than really dealing with the problem. In the end they waived the resort fee and gave us $130 off the bill - but they just didn't get the fact that was inadequate - this was our honeymoon - ultimately they didn't care.
We had various other service issues with unreturned concierge calls and it was a disappointing end to our honeymoon.
I would not stay here, the location is good but use the Hilton or omni - they are in the same place and have proper hotel service standards. Don't get a suite and don't believe the descriptions of the rooms and facilities on the website.

I recently stayed at the Days Inn on Ash Street in San Diego, room 414 to be exact. As soon as I got into the room I sat down on a chair next to the round table and it nearly crumbled into pieces. The outlets are completely worn out and will not hold the prongs properly. The power went out in the room numerous times. But the big one was on the last night of my stay...at 2:15 am water began dripping from the ceiling all over the room. My luggage was soaked and so was the bed. We obviously could not sleep, so we checked out early. When we told the "professional" at the counter what was going on, all he could say is...."sorry, should I charge the rate to the card on hand"? He didn't try in any way to make it right. Trust me, stay somewhere else. This place sucks.
hotel_name: Days Inn San Diego Downtown/Convention Center

review_text: I must share with you all everyone at this hotel was so polite n willing to help. I truly enjoy my stay and coming back in the future. Yasi was the best!!

review_title: Great customer service, but no fridge!
review_text:
I am a frequent traveler and this is by far the best customer service experience I have had. 
 When I first checked in, I was greeted by Bob. He was extremely helpful and made checking in a breeze! He was extremely personable as well which really set the tone for the rest of my stay.
The resort itself is set up more like an apartment complex than like a standard hotel, so it took a few minutes to get your bearings straight on where everything was located. 
The room was very nice and clean. I had a king bed that was comfortable and the room had a separate vanity from the one in the bathroom. My only negative about this hotel is that there was not a mini fridge in the room... this made for a big dissapointment after ordering extra sushi to go from a nearby restaurant.
At checkout I was helped by the multi-tasker extraordinaire, Kirk! Everyone at that resort really was attentive and helpful and truly seemed to appreciate my business there. I would highly recommend this resort.
hotel_name: DoubleTree by Hilton Golf Resort San Diego

review_title: Best hotel in San Diego, trust me.
review_text: The hotel was much better then I expected. Great service, clean rooms, fresh smell, great pool deck. Very modernized. They even upgraded me to a suite at no charge. My room had a view straight into Petco park. The hotel is much bigger and nicer then it looks in the pictures you'll see online. The hotel is right in the gaslamp area, lots of action at night.

review_title: Everything you want in San Diego except the ocean
review_text:
Just stayed three nights for a training at PPH. The room is spacious and well planned out. Note: no fridge.
The staff is friendly and helpful all hours. 
They have fantastic chocolate chip cookies.
The golf course is pleasant and peaceful (I did not golf though). Mulligan's bar and grill has a great happy hour menu. Can't beat the burger and fries for $5, and really good potstickers, chicken quesadillas, and Caesar salad. 
A wonderful fitness center with a lap pool away from the rooms. A seperaye family pool for families with kids near rooms.
Rooms have balconies with table and chairs and room service.
Great room rated. Major chain stores nearby, a grocery store across the street, and excellent freeway access right where the 15 and 56 meet. A straight shot over to Del Mar for ocean dining and more.
hotel_name: DoubleTree by Hilton Golf Resort San Diego

review_text:
What dump, bed linen is two sheets with a blanket in between, there has to be a 1/4 inch gap around the door, ac dials "all broken" per maintenance man, so room is either ice cold or steamy hot.
Area it is in is a dump, it is 6:00 am and the trash truck is emptying the bins.
Well at least no shootings.

review_title: Just an okay hotel but red flags initially everywhere.
review_text:
First, some things that us question our choice: We arrived for a long stay around 10pm on a Friday and the lobby main door was locked... we had to use a bullet proof "night window" to check in (like a bank would have in a not so nice part of town). After feigning hearing issues with her behind glass, I asked to be let in the lobby and was let in and saw security camera monitors were pointed at every possible corner of the grounds. We got a room on the 3rd floor and the automatic door facing the hall to the rooms was broken. We had to walk all the way around the outside. We get to the elevator and its "down for maintenance". I went back into the lobby and asked for a first floor room or second floor at least and she gave us one. 
When we got in the room though we were pleasantly surprised. The room looked updated for the most part with a nice granite counter outside the bathroom, counter height refrigerator and microwave. Horrible outdated tv though and ours had a loud screeching sound until it got warmed up. Bathroom was unbearably small. You had to step in and go behind the toilet to close the door. Outlets were lacking too. My husband and I both use our cell phones as alarms and want to plug in our phones next to the bed but there were not outlets anywhere near it. I had to unplug a lamp on the other side of the room. Beds and pillows were comfortable. 
Breakfast was blah but I wasn't expecting much from continental. Lo and behold, something else was broken! There are two Belgian waffle makers and one was out of order so we waited a very long time for our turn. Cereal, pastries, toast, coffee, etc. Every piece of fruit I got was a little past prime. Nothing to rave about.
Overall, for the money, great deal and adequate for short hotel stay.
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN PLUS San Diego / Miramar Hotel

review_title: Great hotel at a great location.
review_text:
Me and the family stayed here last Thusday night and had a great experience. The hotel is in the perfect location. The staff from the valet, to the front desk were nice and very helpful. 
When I checked in, the front desk lady, sorry I bad with names asked if we wanted to upgrade to a suite and after reading other reviews on how great the suites were I did. 
The room was large for the four of us. It was clean, modern and had a very confurtable bed. 
Since my wife and I were traveling with out two kids, we did not go to the bars and Nobu Restaurant that were in the hotel. 
I would stay again at this hotel.

review_title: Don't stay here if you need to work.
review_text: The hotel is okay. It has some positives but there is a reason why it has an 80% recommendation. Thin walls, sound echos in the hall and from outside. I could hear 3 different conversations not occurring in my room. Internet straight from mid-1990's. No wifi in the rooms and an ethernet connection that is molasses slow. Tried to work, couldnt. Tried to download a movie. After three hours, only 6 hours more remain. Not great accuracy of information about hotel services from central reservations.
hotel_name: DoubleTree by Hilton Golf Resort San Diego

review_text: Had a wonderful stay. Loved the free breakfast wonderful location. Asked the staff for directions for whale watching and ended up taking me and picking me up. It made my trip so worry free.
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Hacienda Hotel Old Town

review_text: This place is a dump. It is old and falling apart, from the closet doors to the furniture. Don't let the entrance or lobby trick you. The rooms, towels and exterior need alot of maintenance. There are too many other hotels in the same proximity to choose from.
hotel_name: Crowne Plaza Hotel San Diego - Mission Valley

review_title: It's a motel for the budget minded traveler
review_text: It was decent. The room remodel is a step up from what it use to be. The location is great! Just minutes to almost any major tourist spot and quick access to the free way. I'm not a fan of the faux wood floors in the rooms, I though they looked dirty. The reason I gave a low score on service was the front desk employee who checked us in was rather unhappy and one of the days the elevator was broken so our room never got cleaned (I needed towels and more cups). I would stay here again... You can't have high expectations for leads than $70 a night in downtown SD.

review_title: Best hotel service in San Diego
review_text:
Mr. Kruvi 
The best Hilton Hotels I have ever stayed at. The staff is amazing. Actually you guys set the standard for others to follow. Every single person that I have come in contact with has been outstanding. As a matter of fact I have highly recommended your hotel to every one of my coworkers. Please express my appreciation of the fantastic service I receive from your hotel every time I stay with you. The Double tree is my hotel every time I come to San Diego because of your the people. From the front desk to the pro shop, house keeping and the restaurant.
 Every single person genuinely cares about making this hotel the best. The Doubbletree is the only hotel I consider when coming to San Diego
hotel_name: DoubleTree by Hilton Golf Resort San Diego

review_title: Ottimo hotel..camere grandi e pulite..posizione perfetta!
review_text: Sono stato in questo hotel per 4 notti...la camera con due queen bed era grande e pulita...il servizio in camera Ã¨ stato effettuato ogni giorno anche se la camera veniva lasciata libera solo il pomeriggio...alla reception sono stati molto gentili e ci hanno lasciato fare il checkout anche fuori orario...la posizione Ã¨ perfetta...10 minuti a piedi da gaslamp il quartiere centrale di downtown con tutti i locali e ristoranti...appena a 1 minuto dalla freeway 5 con la quale si puÃ² andare a pacific beach in 15 minuti...vicinissimo anche all aeroporto...davvero consigliato!
hotel_name: Days Inn San Diego Downtown/Convention Center

review_title: A fabulous place where you really experience the life in San Diego!
review_text: A vibrant place where the nightlife in San Diego is.. For fun loving people.. Hard rock hotel is the place to be! Great place with great service too.

Definitely get what you pay for. Cheap price = cheap quality. I was afraid for myself and my family to sleep on the beds. We got two rooms with two queen beds each, they both had an odd smell to them. One beds blankets, sheets and pillows had hair all over them. One bed had what looked like old blood stains on the sheets and mattress cover. The heater blew cold air and the fridge was useless, it didn't close all the way. Not to mention the shower water was freezing then you'd get the water right and it would burn you. Never staying here again !!!

review_title: It makes you feel like home!!
review_text: I appreciate the stuff who appreciated me, and I appreciate the HRH members who are taking the time to focus on me out of thousands that stay and returning my emails... Really means alot to a customer, thanks!

Arrived on a Saturday via Amtrak from L.A. Got to Motel and went to check in. The girl at the front desk was not very friendly. Almost like she did not want to be there. The room was nice and clean. It was good size room, but the bathroom was kind of small. Like others have stated the Motel is next to the San Diego International Airport runway. Which means there will be some noise with the planes. But I can sleep thru almost anything so it did not bother me at all. I stayed at this Motel for 2 nights. Price was good, room was clean. Over all expierience good.

review_title: So sorry I didn't check reviews first
review_text: Very noisy. They recently replaced all the carpeting with laminate and you could hear EVERY footstep overhead. Unfortunately the people upstairs paced through the night. Watching the planes come in was like watching a horror movie of a plane crash. Every time one came in I got the urge to run.

When they said this hotel was close to the airport I didn't realise they meant under the flight path within a stones throw of the airport!
Let's get a few things straight... Yes you are going to see and hear planes, but they are not flying all night, intact around 11 they stop until about 7:30, so it does not affect sleep!
Also there are trains, but they are similar timescale!
Motel clean, rooms large, plenty of parking! Short drive to gaslamp and Balboa! We were her for four nights! No problems!

Liked the fact that it had a mini kitchen on it, very close to freeways, however,no customer service. We were two minutes late for breakfast (because no one informed us about their hours) and we were not allowed to eat there. It is good for the price, just any questions you may have ask them directly.

The Hard Rock San Diego is in the best possible location in San Diego. There is a lot to do and see all within walking distance. Staff was excellent and hotel & rooms were very clean. I've read other reviews saying that it was very noisy. Our room was on the 8th floor right by the elevator & we couldn't hear a thing. Can't wait to visit again!

review_title: Best hotel to party and relax at the same time
review_text:
I had my bachelor party at the Hard Rock San Diego. 
The hotel and the staf fis amazing .The pool pary was unbelievable.The people were beautiful.The bars of the hotel are great
Everybody has to experience that vibe. 
Can't wait to go back again : )

This the hotel for a good time around fun people. Pool scene is the best in San Diego. And location is perfect for a Padres game or hanging out in the Gas Lamp. Just so you know, this is not the place for children or a quiet stay.
I love the rooms they are awesome and spacious comfortable bed worth the price

What a horrible place. 
Here are a list of reasons why you should not stay at downtown San diego lodge:
1) On check in I had to pay more money than expected because the hotel added on extra tax plus I had already paid for the first night as a deposit which they apparently said I hadn't (even tho it had come out of my bank and I had it on my reservation papers). So i had to pay again. 
2) our first room had a faulty lock and they only way we could get in was to ask reception to let us in. we slept with our cases and a bedside table against the door as we backed onto a road and didn't feel safe with a faulty lock. 
3) we switched rooms because of the lock and because a group of lads next door were up all night fighting and banging on doors. Both rooms were dirty, the bathrooms especially. They were in the middle of a revamp and there was dust everywhere, wires hanging out the walls, no curtains in our second room and the air conditioning unit had half the front missing 
4) there was no hot water. 
5) the cleaner stole my shampoo and conditioner then admitted it to the manager when I confronted them (altho the manager was lovely and gave me some money to buy more)
6)one member of staff (receptionist) was rude and wasn't very helpful altho I couldn't fault the manager. 
7) it's not good value for money. 
If your a group of lads looking for a place to kip after a night out then this is the place for you, altho a premier inn is just as cheap and a damn sight nicer.

review_title: Horable esablishment with blood, roaches, bums
review_text: The hotel was under what looked to be some construction, we were told we were getting an upgraded room, but there were dirty raisers in the bathroom, bottle caps in the ac, roaches in the sink and on the floor.... and when we brought all this to thehotel mgr he said, what's the problem? We had to fight to get a full refund....

review_title: Recommend for anyone looking for a great deal and a comfortable stay
review_text: The room size was adequate and had a fridge, microwave and even a safe. The management was courteous and professional. We have stayed at other locations in San Diego and this is one of the better deals we found. The hotel is a bit older and has some minor repair issues but nothing of great concern or diminshed quality. It was easy to get to sea world, beaches or anywhere in town from this location. This was the best value for that price range in san diego

This place was pretty bad. I had some very sketchy stuff happen to me while staying here, someone banged on my door at 1:39am and then a creepy dude called our hotel rooms phone at 2 am asking how I was doing. Then I called the front desk and they said they didn't call my phone but someone from out side the Hotel could have.. Not normal and the place was a dumb filled with sketchy people.
hotel_name: Howard Johnson Express Inn - San Diego

review_title: The customer service was excellent and very helpfully at at times
review_text: The employees were very friendly, and helpfully at all times of the day. The only bad thing out of the trip was the shuttle service to the begging of the marathon race, other than that inconvenience everything was excellent!!!

review_title: Awesome place to stay with an incredible staff!
review_text: Great, fantastic, wonderful! They really know how to treat their guests.

review_title: Most Epic Mid Week Party Ever
review_text: I have stayed at the Hard Rock San Diego before so when my 30th birthday came around there was no question as to where I was going to stay. I reserved a Rock Star Gold Suite and it was perfect for the pre-party as well as the after party. The pool was awesome and the servers were very patient (we had a group of about 15 people and after the drinks settled in we were a little loud). She was also pretty hot. The entire staff was really attentive and they were also polite, even when they had to cut off one of drunk friends in the group. I will be staying here on my next trip to San Diego, that is for sure.
A unique experience, Definitely will return. The service, the people, the location, the unique rooms, the vibe I give it an A+++++.

review_title: Clean, basic, perfect location, great price!
review_text: It's not the ritz but for $40 it was just what I needed! Great location, nice staff, super basic, but I'd come back especially in the summer so I could get in one of their awesome pools.

review_title: No hospitality value but ok area
review_text: Long line to check in with an 16 year old front desk clerk. Make sure to keep yourself busy as You hear everything in rooms along side and above. Nearby diner is average but very friendly. Overall blahh but on an tight budget it works.

Pretty mediocre hotel. Worst part was the sagging matresses. Woke up with a terrible backache! The hotel could definitely use some upgrading. Only reason we were there was because we bought on hotwire. Won't do that again!

We booked our room and I wad leery to stay here with the reviews I read. First the front staff were rude when we arrived early and asked about checking in early. He abruptly told us no our room will not be ready until 3:00. I wanted to cancel then but my husband wanted to stick it out. We took our son to the beach to kill time. We returned at 3:00 to check in and our room was in the back. HORRIBLE parking. We struggled to park our crossover as did others we noticed. Our room looked clean enough, carpet is gross. But we have a bathroom sink that leaks and a light over the vanity that turns on and off by itself. There was mold on the ceiling above the shower. This is our first night of a four night stay let's see if we make it.

review_title: Disappointingly ill equipped, overpriced, and noisy
review_text: We rented the 2 bedroom, 1 bath suite for 3 nights. While the panaromic ocean views from the balcony were beautiful, it did not make up for the lack of service, the noise that we had to endure 2 out of 3 nights, or the general uncleanliness of the suite. The kitchen was lacking basic equipment like paper towels, dish soap or dish cloths, and maid service never cleaned our kitchen at all. Both days we came back at 4 pm and the rooms still had not been cleaned. There was loud banging all night from the kitchen/bar below, and pounding music 2 out of 3 nights well past 2 am. The shag carpet was disgusting, and the wifi did not work well. The towels were old and stained, and they didn't provided enough until our last day. They tried to charge us $479 per night, way over the quoted rate on the phone. After getting no sleep the first night we complained, and they immediately reduced the rate $100 (to the originally quoted price). After the last night of noise and having to phone front desk to complain, they took another $80 off the total bill. A nice gesture, but does not make up for the lack of sleep we experienced on this trip. I'm all for retro hotels, but under no circumstances would I recommend this one to friends. One note: the maids, when they did finally clean our rooms, were friendly and did the best job they could under the circumstances.

review_title: By far the best hotel in Gaslamp!!
review_text: Self contained, u will not need to leave the hotel!!! Great food, amazing drinks, excellent nightlife...all in the hotel!

This hotel was the most nasty hotel I have ever stay at! I should have left as soon as I walked into my room. The place was very run down and was way over priced. The next day when I woke up, my bed was infested with bed bugs and when I talked to a manager he tried to pretend like he didn't even know what bed bugs looked like. So I caught one in a cup and show him, still he acted like he didn't know .

review_title: Great location--do not get the handicapped room!
review_text:
PB is a great place to stay--that being said, at the Surfer we were assigned the handicapped room, which apparently is the only non-balcony room at the hotel! Since there is no air-conditioning at these hotels by the beach, that meant we had to leave our windows open, and though it provided little comfort (room was on the corner so there was no cross breeze), it was scary since the room was on the first floor. We met two couples who had been broken into at other hotels, so it was a little scary (not to mention extremely hot and humid). 
We tried unsuccessfully to get a room change--apparently no one else wanted that room either! Ugh!

We were going to be in town for one night and found this location for a cheap price through AAA. We requested a non smoking room, as I walked in thru the door the nasty odor of smoke smacked me in the face. I immediately turned on the ac and left for a night out in town hoping the smell eventually would go away.
 I came back and it was still the same, I was so fed up That I gathered my belonging to check out. I expressed my concerns to the receptionist at the front deck and she offered to upgrade my room. I wa so disgusted, there was no way I was sleeping there. I requested a refund but she told me that because I checked in at 4:00 pm and it was now 12:00 am she couldn't do it. I gave her the keys and walked away. Never will I ever stay here again and do not recommend it, spend the extra cash for something decent.
hotel_name: Heritage Inn - Sea World San Diego

review_title: SEEDY! This place hasn't, been quality for a long time!
review_text: We stayed for four days. the elevators creek,doors don,t shut properly. Doors at the end of the building have no locks so are not secured at night. the spa is a joke still only one machine no sauna steam room etc. The key failed to work 1/2 the time. The window on our room did not close completely so we heard whistling all night. thank God we did not have bedbugs but the mattress was very hard. the clock was broken and the firealarm box was hanging off the wall. This is the kind of place you would send someone you really didn't like and wanted to have them suffer!

We brought our 15 mo baby nervously but the room and hotel,mid week, was quiet, clean, and safe. The staff was helpful and very friendly. We stayed in a king suite and had plenty of room. to avoid charges we brought our own pack n play and microwave. But they can provide them on request. strongly recommend staying here.

Stayed in a Woodstock suite. Beautiful room with a great balcony overlooking both the pool and Gaslamp Quarter. Service was impeccable. Ate 3 times at Maryjanes. Food is terrific. 
The rooms are very comfortable and spotless. This is one of my top 3 favorite hotels.

Having stayed at the Hard Rock inVegas I was expecting the same uber cool hip vibe and although the hotel is very modern and cool in decor its very small and cramped. I reserved one.of only 6 float studios which boasts that you open your patio door to your private poolsude cabana. I opened my patio door to no pool or even a pool view just a large area covered in astro turf set up for a wedding. The tiny pol area is on the other side of a wall about 50 feet from my patio. The only view I had was of the backside of the V.I.P. cabanas my room was also right next to the service entrance so I had the joy of seeing people filter in and out all day long for almost 300.00 a night I would have expected much more not to mention they charge you 34.00 a day for parking. My suggestion is to stay at the Omni and come party at the Hard Rock these rooms are definitely not worth the price!

review_text:
Poor no sorry , very poor . Dirty broken rooms . Holes in room walls , lights that flicker , well wifi is a differant kind . Cause it says we got it but it don't work , 
Everything about this place is poor . Why ! How ! Is this place still trading , don't please don't do it . It's a hole !

review_text: This resort was not as nice as the pictures I paid for the room to relax which is supposed to come with upgrades when available yet our room seemed like the least place you wod want to relax. First the carpet was badly stained the matresses were terrible uncomfortable. My fiancÃ© sat in the chair and when he got up he had all kinds of dust all over him. The bathroom was okay but part of the bathroom door had looked like someone kicked it and a corner of the inner door was unpainted and looked like it had not been repaired. Oh also the actual door to the room had a trick to shutting it you had to pull and slam very ghetto. Next our tv remote did not work we called and they said someone would be right out but Boone showed up until an hour n half later. The wifi connection was slow and overall our stay was terrible the only nice person we encountered was the bar tender but the bar that was supposed to be open until two closed at ten go figure.

When we opened the door we were greeted by the lovely smell of mold and dust. The carpet was in bunches and had huge disgusting spots all over. The bathroom sink was literally falling off the wall!! I was nervous staying here with my family. The first night was horrible for many reasons. One: the smell. It was horrid. Two: the 10:00 curfew only applied to guests. Local teens and bar hoppers were allowed to party till 4. Three: we were right next to the ice machine and people needed ice at 3 am keeping us awake. 
The second day I attempted to find another hotel but many were booked full. My wife went to go check us out of this nightmare when I was out looking for better hotels. They offered to upgrade us to a better room at no cost. We accepted. Room 2 gave my three year old a rash on her face when she laid down in the chair!! The towels had hairs all over them and it was still run down. Plus we couldn't use the hot tub due to it being filled with drunken teens. 
The little mini mart was nice during the day at night its a different story. We went in to get ice cream and a young lady offered to give me oral if I bought her a bottle of booze, I had my 5 year old daughter with me!! I could not believe it! I told the front desk and they told me she is always there on Tuesday nights. They didn't even care!! This is a shady and dingy hotel!
This place is horrible for families. I wouldn't recommend it to my enemies!! DO NOT STAY here!! It should be condemned!!

This was my first time staying at the Hard Rock hotel. I was very pleased with the quality and cleanliness of the rooms. The location of the hotel was awesome as well. It was right next to the ball park and also right in the gaslamp so it was convenient for is to watch the game,get dressed and go out dancing right after the game. The only downfall I had was the expensive valet parking they had buy all I did was park in the parking structure next to the hotel which was literally right next to the hotel.

There is a electric stove in the room but since the room is wired all off one gfi circuit you cant even use the stove with all the appliances and lights off. Then the desk clerk was not helpfull at all, so if you want to pay for a broken room go for it. Its hard not to use expletives in this review,morons had to wire this place.

200 paying guests from across the country staying for a week for a wedding. Worst management. When asked if they wanted to please their customers, manager on duty replied "only to an extent". Wouldn't waste your money or precious vacation time. Very disappointed.

Weekday getaway brought us to Kona Kai. Gorgeous property, beautiful location, impeccable service. Pool & spa are right on the water, steps to a private beach. Check in was fast, friendly and made me feel at home. Looking forward to coming back, I can't imagine choosing a different resort at the same price.

review_title: I've stayed in better places in remote villages of Kenya
review_text: Probably one of the worst experiences of staying in a hotel ever. First, bring some sleeping pills...the walls are so thin that you can't sleep. Second if you ask the front desk a request, it more than likely will not happen (asked to be in a room next to my family a week ahead of time and that did not happen AND asked for my room to get cleaned one day only to come back at 7pm to find it not done)

Looked nice online great location. Checked in rooms were a little dated for the price but what the heck it's near the beach do be it. I am relaxing on the patio and hear my daughter and wife scream. I run in the room just in time to see no less than 15 huge roaches scurry offy pillow. We pack up and go to the front desk to cancell our room and the front desk person acted like it was no big deal no apology nothing. After 3 days of my funds not bring released I called to speak to the general manager and he almost accused ms of lying he said they couldnt find any roaches. A few friends and I stayed here for the Fat Tues Mardi Gras. To our surprise our suite balcony was right over one of the entrances, the view was amazing! Everything exceeded our expectations.

review_title: Time to re-think your rules and regulations. You fail!
review_text: I would have to say the management does not know how to run the pool. You don't let 20 kids under the age of 14 take over the hot tub then tell the adults they have leave.

review_title: Nice,but didn't live up to its hype
review_text: This hotel was a nice stay for us,the area is great.you can walk to a lot of places in point loma.try staying in room 126-134(even#) the terrace leads right to the pool. The website made it look like a fun happening place with luaus and hula dancers. When we stayed their was nothing going on.it was like a ghost town.the fees are bad.parking $15 and gym use $10.

Over all OK for the price $50.00 a night for 4 nights. As for location, it is Not close to the Gas Lamp District or the Convention Center or Balboa Park...San Diego ZOO. You have to get a Taxi, to get to those places. I took a jog from my hotel to gas Lamp, as I said" it took longer then I expected. Even jogging to the Convention Center, boy what a boring jog, until you finally get to the back of the convention center, where all the activies are. 
Back to the hotel room. Room was ok. Highlight was mini refrigerator, microwave and no bed bugs. the room did smell moldy and the carpet was filthy, so keep you shoes on unless you want to see you white sox Black. There breakfast was simple, cereal,Danish and orange drink. There Ice maker, the only one in the whole hotel Sucked. It took forever to dispense Ice....argg. Overall you pay for what you get. Probally would not stay here again, unless it's really really Cheap price $.

review_text: Me and two friends stayed here for a convention. We were told it was in walking distance, but quickly decided that we would not be walking. There really isn't easy access to much unless u drive or take a cab. The rooms are old and dingy. Even though the maids seemed nice and came in each day. We had a big ant problem the whole time we were there. Honestly we didn't spend much time at the room unless we were sleeping... But we kept the door double locked while we were in there. If you are looking for cheap and don't care, this hotel will do. If u are looking for comfort or clean, book elsewhere.
