We went to Austin for the football game and met up with family at this hotel. They had chosen the place to stay. I will stay there every time I go to Austin. It was so nice. The bed was incredibly comfortable, everything was clean, lots of room to visit with family and many extras in the room. Close to every place we wanted to go. Definitely would recommend.
hotel_name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Austin-Arboretum / NW

review_text:
Nice setting in the live oaks off Mopac.
Clean. The nightly hospitality snack was obviously prepared with pride and attention to detail...get there early if you like that sort of thing.
There is not an ice machine but you can turn on your ice maker in the fridge if you will be there a couple of days. Plus the staff keeps bags of ice in the frig in the lobby convenience shop.
If you are on the second floor, some of the rooms are easier to access from the back door which opens straight onto that floor.
hotel_name: Homewood Suites by Hilton Austin-Arboretum / NW

review_text: Whenever partner and I go to Austin this honour hotel of choice. Her its a bit far north, but the service.and rooms are TERRIFIC . If the folks at Marriott want to showcase a hotel for how it is done right, this should be their choice.

Great location if you need to be downtown. Extremely over priced considering there are other Marriott properties minutes away. This is a hybrid design with courtyard. Two separate desks that have as much communication between them as the middle east.
hotel_name: Residence Inn Austin Downtown / Convention Center

review_text: Not the best Marriott I've stayed at. Small lounge area, couldn't check in till almost 4pm. Pool and jaquzzi was freezing for and indoor pool. Also the floor was so dirty in the pool area and no towels. Overall okay...
hotel_name: Residence Inn Austin Downtown / Convention Center

review_text: Great location in downtown Austin. Stayed on a business trip. Staff was great to work with. Had to book a block of rooms and make some last minute changes. Couldn't have been more accommodating.
hotel_name: Residence Inn Austin Downtown / Convention Center

review_title: A lovely hotel reflecting the city's history.
review_text: Just stayed for a week at the Steinhart. Everything was wonderful - from the front desk staff to the location. Rooms are well apportioned and beautiful - reflecting the city's Victorian history. Just a few blocks away from the Powell and Mason/Hyde cable cars. While others have commented re: proximity to the Tenderloin, it was not an issue and front desk staff was very good at showing us where not to go. If you are staying for a longer vacation and the idea of having a bit more space and a kitchen appeals to you, this is a wonderful place to stay.

Close to Union Sq, this has an old world feel about it. One small elevator, adequate but not generously sized rooms, and the feel of an old (but nicely renovated) building, channeling a literary vibe. Just as long as you don't expect a fancy (soulless) modern hotel, you will love the very friendly and helpful staff, the social happy hour in the lounge, and Max the pug.
hotel_name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text:
Good stay, great value but small rooms and please update the showers! 
You won't go wrong here great location too!
hotel_name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text:
We stayed one night at the Harbor Court and found it to be a very nice place to stay. The staff was friendly and the furnishing/decor were very stylish. The location worked out well for us.
We stayed in their queen suite which has nice views of the Bay Bridge and floor to ceiling windows that let plenty of light in. Overall, the size of the room for a suite was small, but that is expected in the smaller boutique hotels in San Francisco.
Everything was very clean and comforting. They even put out milk and cookies in the evening. We would definitely stay here again.
hotel_name: Harbor Court Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text:
We stayed at Inn at the Opera for 6 nights in October 2011. What a fantastic hotel. The reception area is lovely and open with some vintage touches. The elevator is gorgeous inside the walls are lined with red velvet and classical music is played. The room we stayed in was a perfect size. The two of us were more than comfortable. We had a very comfortable king size bed, a flat screen tv a large fridge with freezer section and a coffee maker. All the staff were very professional and very helpful. They really went above and beyond. Check in was extremely fast and whilst we were checking in our bags were taken to our room.
The hotel is a stones throw from the opera house and the city ballet. Its also a very short walk to lovely bars, shops and restaurants. The F line street car is a 5 minute walk away on market street, the local bus to golden gate park is round the corner and the red tour bus stops right outside the hotel. We didnt eat in the hotel restaurant but the food smelt gorgeous it was very busy with locals every night. Breakfast in the hotel was very good and it was free, good variety of bagels, toast, fruit, eggs and a variety of fillings, tea and coffee also available.
We stayed here as part of our Honeymoon. We were treated to a lovely bottle of red wine in our room which was such a nice touch.
We would definitely stay here again if we visited San Francisco.

Got an amazing suite here for 99 dollars. Awesome room with living room.....kitchenette....dining table....comfy bed. Close to ballet and opera house and great restaurants. Bart isn't too far either...great breakfast. Would absolutely stay again..BTW avoid the standard rooms, I heard they are small as broom closets

This hotel is very nice because of its union square location, friendly staff, and its atmosphere.The location is great, it literally is steps away from the mall, multiple bus stops, the powell street bart, the cable car, Cvs pharmacy for grocerys and snacks ,and bunches of resteraunts. The staff is so helpfull and kind all of the time even in the middle of the night, they can reccomend clubs, restaraunts, things to do, and they even have different colorful drink shots each day that you can try for free. At the hotel its so quiet and calming as soon as you walk in the door, just what a hotel should be.

At our arrival we were a bit scared as to what was ahead for us. The gentleman at the reception was sleeping. He kept repeating himself and well just seemed a little out if it. Fortunately, other than this our experience at the Abri Hotel was great. Beautiful hotel located about 5 minutes from Union Square. The city trolley is also 5 minutes away and it takes you to the port where you can see Alcatraz, walk 5 minutes from there to Fishermen's Wharf to enjoy some seafood. Hotel is clean, good price, great location and overall a pleasant place to stay.

review_title: A quiet, comfortable little gem in San Francisco.
review_text: The rooms are lovely, clean and the beds are comfy. Service is personal and attentive. The neighborhood has a good variety of small, delicious restaurants in walking distance. In fact you can walk easily to a number of bus or street car stops to get anywhere in the city. If you want a smaller hotel that caters to adults, you will love this place.

review_title: Old World Charms...but rooms need to be updated
review_text: Staff, service and location are why you come to the Ritz in SF. The rooms are clean and comfortable, just need to be updated in this competitive market yes, it's expensive, but don't be shocked or complain, as you knew it when you picked the place. Top notch staff will keep you coming back.

review_title: Excellent hotel close to Union Square, Nob Hill and Cinatown
review_text: This is our 2nd visit to the Rex (from the UK). Hopefully that provides good endorsement. The best factor is it's location - a 2 min walk from Union Sq. Its second best feature is the complimentary glass of wine you get each day (Merlot was excellent). The service is great, we asked to move rooms, which was easily done. The rooms are air-conned, clean and a decent size. The bed was comfy enough. Free wifi throughout the hotel is a bonus. Would certainly go back.
hotel_name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: Stayed there for 2 nights. Very nice and modern rooms, friendly service and good location.

review_title: Wonderful hotel on the edge of the city financial area with Bay Views
review_text:
I was surprised by this little hotel, wonderful staff and a easy place for everyone to find, walking distance to the Ferry building and to the financial district at waters edge. 
The room was well appointed with large falt screen, wi-fi and a one of the most comfortable beds! This is not your standard large business hotels, so if you want something a little different where you could explore the city but walk to the waterfront Ferry Building and jump on a ferry to Sausilto or walk to embarcadero center this is good option
hotel_name: Hotel Vitale, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: Tiny but clean rooms in central location.
review_text:
Arrived to friendly service, unfortunately rooms not available before 3pm. A little tough on people arriving on long haul flights so keep in mind. 
The rooms are tiny but newly refurbished and kept very clean. Water pressure at times a little weak, but generally fine. Hair dryers supplied are the type that singe rather than dry hair, so bring your own or buy a cheapy (if yours won't work properly on US power supply) from the Walgreens a block away as I did. 
Unless you enjoy looking over air-conditioning ducts, ensure you book the more expensive bay view room type. 
The staff are very friendly and helpful. If they don't have an answer, they look it up on the PC whilst you wait. 
The location is fairly nice - a few minutes walk from Embarcadero BART so you can get there very easily and cheaply from the airport. Being at the far end of the financial district means it is nice and quiet with little or no street sounds. Plenty of cafes and restaurants about as well. It's about a 20 min walk to Union Square or walk 2 mins to Market and jump on a tram (cable car). 
All in all, a nice, quiet, clean place to stay. I would go again.
hotel_name: Harbor Court Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: Great for what it is - a downtown, non-luxury, boutique hotel.
review_text: I am a frequent guest at the Abri and I continue to stay there for many of the reasons others have mentioned: location, rate, and service. This is not a resort nor a spa - it is a downtown hotel in a major city. If you want shop and be near BART, MUNI, or even cable cars and don't want to spend a fortune then Abri is a smart choice. I travel for business and being close to public transportation and a wealth of food choices is paramount. Abri, as well as the other Larkspur properties, will not win any records for Internet speeds, but the wifi is free and more than enough for file transfers, browsing and email. The rooms on 5 can be a little musty (moreso than the 4th floor), but they are further away from the street. If you have stayed in a hotel in Chicago or NYC, the street noise is typical. If you are exting peace and quiet in a city hotel, then you definitely need to request a quiet room away from the street or stay at a larger hotel that can get you further away from the everyday hustle and bustle. Abri acknowledges the noise and does their best to compensate with fresh ear plugs and eye masks nightly. The adjoining restaurant is always busy (that's a good sign) and has happy hour pricing until late on Mon and Tue. It is noisy, but never rowdy - definitely a wine and cocktail crowd and while busy, is fine for those traveling with kids. The staff make a noted effort to get to know their guests and make them feel welcome. The evening complementary drink in the lobby is kid friendly during the week and adult only on the weekends. The suites are very spacious yet cozy with seperate spaces for sitting a sleeping. The TVs offer hookups for your own devices for movie watching if you brought your own. Their is comp coffee, tea and newspapers in the morning in the lobby (as David will be certain to remind you of as you exit). There is also a large selection of snacks and electronics for purchase in the lobby should you get hungry or forgot your charger. As someone mentioned, there are pan handlers out in front frequently - the staff does their best to move them along, but unless you stay on top of the hill at the Fairmont or somewhere else away from the busy shopping district, that is unfortunately the norm for San Francisco and should be expected. Having stayed at many Larkspur properties, I prefer the Abri based on the hospitality of their staff and their proximity to shopping, food and public transportation.

Great hotel with a great location. Free fresh baked warm cookies and milk every night! Coffee, tea, and hot chocolate in the morning. Close to local fresh food market on Saturday's. Short walk to pier 39 and rail cars. I would definatley stay here again.
hotel_name: Harbor Court Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: Great stay, although some staff lacked enthusiasm
review_text: I stayed here for 6 days. It is a great little place. The rooms are well sized. It's located in the Marina district and had a partial view of the Golden Gate Bridge. Vince on the front desk was absolutely lovely and there was another lady that provides good service. Sadly there was another man on the desk that lacked enthusiasm. Other than that it was fantastic!

We spent one night here before flying out to Portland. After spending a very disappointing night at a Kimpton property I booked this based on other reviews. We had a water view room. It was beautiful. Upon telling the desk clerk of our anniversary we were sent a bottle of wine. A nice touch. Location to the Ferry Building and restaurants was perfect compared to our creepy stay at the wharf Kimpton. The staff was great. We will definitely seek out other Joie de Vivre properties in our future travels.
hotel_name: Hotel Vitale, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: Quaint and classy in San Francisco
review_text: The Inn at the Oprah is a wonderful place to stay. The rooms are clean and neat and all a person needs. The only detraction I have is the area where the the Inn is should be better advertised to the patrons so they know what is within walking distance. The service is 5 star and the restaurant is great. Give this hotel that is off the main path a chance and you will be pleasantly surprised.

review_title: Character hotel in great location with free wine!
review_text: There is nothing corporate about this hotel - every area has a quirky character, from the library bar to the corridors and rooms. It works. It's also in a great location, close to the shops of Union Square and the cable cars to Fishermans Wharf. On top of that, there's free wifi in the rooms and a free glass of wine every night. We booked early and got a great rate, but I would recommend this hotel to friends even if they had to pay a bit more. I'd also recommend a trip to the Ferry Building where you can buy delicious food and drink, including wines, cheeses, bread and coffee.
hotel_name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: I would definitely come back to Orchard Garden Hotel. The staff was very polite, the rooms are very clean and comfortable, and the location is perfect! It was our first trip to SF and we felt as if everything was within the walking distance from the hotel. Chinatown is right next door, Union Square is right around the corner. Would definitely recommend this hotel!

review_title: Spacious rooms but not the best views.
review_text: Lovely amenities and walking distance to downtown highlights. Not impressed with views for the price.

I stayed here for four nights in a suite. My kids were delighted by the two bathrooms and two TVs. The staff are friendly and helpful. I would recommend the hotel to all nut those with young children.
A very nice hotel, with a lovely and always smilling personnel, all garnished by an Excellent restaurant (Americano).
hotel_name: Hotel Vitale, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: Hotel is very clean. Staff is on point. Location is nice. But like other review said bring some soap bar is smallest I've evere seen. taxes on valet are high but that's not there problem add almost 6 bucks to 40 dollar parking. Enjoyed my stay great value!!! Will be back

review_title: Great value in a great SF neighbourhood.
review_text: I just spent a really enjoyable weeklong stay at Inn at the Opera. The staff were all exceptionally friendly and helpful. I stayed in a Ballet suite and found it to be spacious enough for my needs. Very clean and quiet. The hotel is also conveniently located to public transit and the trendy Hayes Valley neighbourhood. I have made many trips to SF and this has been my most enjoyable stay.
Very friendly staff and helpful. Couldn't ask for better service

review_title: Another lovely stay at the Ritz
review_text: Spent two nights on the club level and loved it but what's not to love? As others have mentioned it's a great location, within walking distance of both Chinatown and Union Square; and a cable car ride away from Fisherman's Wharf. Valet is steep at 60-something so next time may try some of the parking tips mentioned in other reviews. Service was impeccable except for the plates and wine glasses left outside our door all day.

I was given the smallest room in thd hotel on the first night (1 foot of walking space between the wall and the bed). The next night I was given a much larger room when I told then I was going to change hotel. The night clerk refused to change my room the first night.
Good location for the bart and Civic Center. 
Not a bad hotel.

I stayed at the Orchard garden. During oracle. The hotel is very clean the location is great. And the best quality that this hotel has is the staff. Thank you ms joy Zamar. You are the reason I will returned to this hotel. You went above and beyond. Legendary service thank you.

Stayed at Hotel Rex for 4 nights at the beginning if a honeymoon road trip. The front desk staff were excellent and kindly gave us free champagne and breakfast for 1 day as a honeymoon gift. 
The rooms aren't huge but are very well decorated with lovely bathrooms and huge tv's. 
The hotel is really central and is very handy for union square and the shopping facilities - a bit of moneyed area so be prepared to spend. 
Couldn't fault this excellent hotel and would definitely stay again if I went back to SF.
hotel_name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text:
Stayed there for 10 days with my with in sep 2011. Hotel very well located with plenty of restaurants and cafes around, just two blocks from union square. The room is large, clean and the staff very helpful.
Would come back! Higly reccomended.

I arrived in San francisco with a sinus infection. I called the hotel to find a local doctors office and they referred me to one who was 4 blks away from hotel. Btw great doctor. We used the Bart system and got off 1 stop 2 early on a one way street and walked 5 blks to doc office. So after doc apt. I called to make sure there would be a room available. She said to me they were sold out the night befor and she would do here best to have a room ready. Well we got there at 2:15 and we were informed that there wasn't a room ready and if we wanted to check in the room that was ready was a "superior king" & it would be 30$ more. I only paid for it cause I felt near death. Basically I felt ripped off when I opened the door to my "superior" room. I didn't have the energy or time to sit and wait for my regular room rate. If you get a good price book it just don't get suckered in to the upgrade. Also wifi never worked. But on the other hand it was a very clean room. Not much wow factor but comfortable. Staff was very helpful and nice, not counting my check inn. Great location and I even made it to our cruise to Alcatraz which was really cool.
All in all it was ok.

Brilliant stay was upgraded to executive suite at front desk on checkin as it was our honeymoon. Tasteful decoration, spacious room, great bar with complementary red wine, had a really good burger here of all things! Would recommend to any couple visiting SF as the central location is brilliant.
hotel_name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: Wife and I usually stay at the Grand Hyatt when we are in SF but decided to try the Rex instead to save a little money. Â We are glad we did. The staff was polite and helpful, our room was clean and comfortable with all of the expected amenities, and was reasonably quiet considering the central location. WiFi was included, our bed was warm and cozy, and the shower had lots of hot water with good towels. The free glass of wine in the evening was a nice touch. We decided to forego the valet parking and stowed our car in the Union Square garage instead, Â a short walk from the hotel, which saved us even more. If you go, please say Hi to Maximo for us; he will be in the lobby in the morning.
hotel_name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text:
Spent three nights in this great city center hotel in March. The key about the hotel is it's location and the fantastic staff really.We walked a couple of times to Fishermans Wharf (easier walking there than back!) in about 35 mins which was a great way to explore the lovely city. It's situated right in the city centre so close to many central restaurants and bars and a short walk to Chinatown and the Italian district for sone nicer restaurants.
The rooms are good,comfortable and clean but nothing that will blow you away. Happy hour at the bar provides you with complimentary wine and great service from the bartender who was full of cool tips and chat (cant recall his name but he gave us some amazing tips on where to go for drinks/food so thank you!). 
Nothing bad to say about this hotel,would recommend it and would stay again for sure if I went back to SF.
hotel_name: Hotel Rex, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: Nice hotel in a good spot
review_text:
The service was wonderful. Always cheerful and very helpful. This is quite important to me. The hotel is nice, but the tv had a very bad picture. It was an "off" brand. I'm not usually in the room much, so not hat big of a deal to me. If coffee is important in your room, you may want to bring your own or head out, as it's quite awful. Starbucks is almost across the street :) I also had a very difficult time with wifi reception in my room. I did accidentally lock my belongings in the safe without my code entered and they responded almost immediately to assist. Take note, the safe functions completely differently than any others I've ever used. Our friends did the same thing in their room. Valet is quite expensive, $40 per nt., but I'm sure parking is at a premium. We didn't need our car at all during our stay, as so much is within walking distance and there is a good bit of public transportation. Located right outside of the entrance to China 
Town.
The bed was quite comfortable and we would choose this hotel again.

Had a great experience. The staff was very helpful in everyway. The staff helped us find our way around the city. The room was on the small side but very nice. The mattress was so comfortable. Very glad we chose this hotel especially since many of the comparable hotels didn't have AC. The lobby was nice and quiet. The only negative comment would be about my reservation. I paid over the phone upfront because they matched priceline.com. When we got there they had my info but not my room set and it didn't show I paid. Luckily they had a room and I verified with my credit card that I wasn't charged. Make sure you call before you get there to verify you have a room even though you have a confirmation number. The location was great, close to everything.

The hotel was located in an ideal spot.close to pier 39 fishermans wharf and giants ballpark.very seductive open rooms,with mirrored wall next to bed!only problem I had was the tremendous taxes and fees added to room/parking. Paid over $60 for parking and room taxes. Ouch!......once you get past that you surely will enjoy your stay here!
hotel_name: Hotel Vitale, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: I love this hotel and it's staff
review_text: This is the 2nd time we have stayed here. From the doormen (cute hats!) to the waitstaff the service is wonderful and accommodating.

We just recently wrapped up a five day, four night stay at Hotel Monaco. The hotel was quite charming, with a great wine bar at night and coffee bar in the morning....make sure to attend both! The location is right on the edge of what I would call the perfect location. Three block walk to Union square where you can pick up the cable car line as well as many double decker tour buses. Nob hill is just a few block walk up Taylor street and is great. I do not recommend waking south of the hotel as the neighborhood transitions pretty quickly from good to sketchy. But as long as you stay north you will be in walking distance to Union Square, Chinatown, Nob Hill, etc. The hotel staff is great and the rooms are very charming. We would stay here again. I was very glad we did NOT stay by Fisherman's Wharf as that location is extremely touristy and crowded. 
I recommend checking out Alcatraz (book your tickets EARLY), Muir Woods, Sausilito, Napa Valley, Chinatown, Fisherman's wharf and the financial district.
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text:
Despite having received a nice room upgrade upon check in, the rest of the stay was downhill. 
First off, when we arrived at the porte cochere to check the car with the valet, we were immediately approached by a bellhop, presumably to take our luggage and port our car to the garage. The bellhop had a different idea. Rather than assist my female companion with her luggage, he stood at the trunk of the car engaging her in a battle of wills to see who would ultimately extract the luggage (2 standard size suitcases). To her credit, she waited him out and he begrudgingly lifted the luggage out. I was wrestling with the duffle bags in the backseat while this exchange took place. 
We then were directed to the check in area where we were greeted by a friendly face. Our check in was handled professionally but unremarkably. There was no escort to our rooms. Nor were we offered any sort of refreshment at the front desk. 
I arrived at my room to find it in proper order. Average cleanliness and adequately maintained. The furniture showed its age (couch was worn in areas and chairs were slightly stained). The room contained a nicely stocked mini-fridge and Bvlgari toiletries (strongly scented and more feminine in smell). The pillows were just right, the mattress worn and covered with what I presume to be a bedwetting preventive cover which sounded and felt like a pamper. It crackled through the night and detracted from the sleep experience. My companion confirmed her mattress was similarly fitted with said pamper so I conclude all the beds have this deplorable feature. 
After check in, we decided to check out the spa for a massage. The spa facilities are small and the lockerroms more gym-like than spa-like. Massage rooms are average. We agreed to meet up in the pool/hottub area after the treatments. To my dismay, after receiving a relaxing massage, I exited the locker area to the wet area to be confronted with 5-6 children under the age of 5 screaming and running around. The children were attended to by a grand mother who yelled not less than 25 times "no running! Last warning!". The children did not heed warning and continued their misbehavior. Spa staff did not intervene and at least attempt to maintain a spa-like atmosphere. Our massages were shot and we decided to bail. The hotel should simply call this area the pool area/daycare for lazy parents. It is not a spa atmosphere in the least. There are no "adults only" wet areas in the hotel. 
We then had dinner at The Dining Room (the hotel restaurant). We each selected the chef's tasting menu. The food was outstanding; service was awkward with long delays between courses. The entire presentation took more than three hours. The length of service is less of a critique and more of a warning to plan your timing accordingly. 
I encountered several staff who were at all times friendly and professional but who lacked refinement. (not addressing me by name, no anticipation of needs, etc). The one exception to this criticism is who I believed to be the head bellman I encountered when checking out, who was outstanding.
Overall my treatment during the stay was on par with a Hyatt or Marriott; entirely disappointing for the cost and expectations.

For USD98/- we got a double queen size bedded room. Rm Is so spacious n with ajoining room accessible via a interlinking door, it is really the best accommodation for a family of four. The beds were comfortable, toilets were clean, nice n big LCD TV with a spacious area for a coffee table and 2 chairs. Only gripe is that the hot water in the shower is bit too cold. 
Location is good, walking distance to the crooked part of Lombard st. and the fisherman wharf . A cafe at the Chestnut St offers good bagels breakfast. Long queue quickly formed after 0900 on a lazy Saturday morning. Cab ride to the airport cost $48/- . Excellent stay. Friendly receptionist named London starts yr day on a happy mood.

Definitely highly recommend this hotel. 
Great rooms (only complaint is pillows were too soft, but that is a personal preference), fabulous location- walking distance of union square, with cable car stop just outside the hotel (just literally around the corner) and its the cable car line going to fisherman's wharf and Lombard street (uphill) or union square (downhill).

review_title: Awesome for your super rich grandma
review_text: Small room, stuffy, lame, smells and looks like your grandmas house. Nice pool and location.

review_title: Small and clean with excellent staff
review_text: The staff at this hotel go out of their way to make your stay comfortable and they are what make this hotel. Nice rooms in a convenient location. Good breakfast and a comfortable bed. We felt very welcome here from the moment we arrived.

I would recommend this hotel, if you are looking for something a little different. Rooms, while on the small side, are beautifully furnished and spotless.
Staff are friendly. Continental breakfast is quite good and served in a lovely dining room.

The castle inn is a pretty good find really. It has an excellent location - you can walk to Fisherman's wharf easily, it's really close to the crooked street and the cable car is a couple of blocks away.
The included breakfast is really fairly basic but better then a lot I have encountered. The rooms themselves are good - pretty-much motel room stuff like you would expect. Overall I think it is a good value place.
Wonderful boutique hotel in good location. Charming interior. Happy hour with complimentary cocktails. Good beds, not too soft. Would recommend and go back.
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: Nice hotel, nice bar, people that work there are nice, location is near all the fun locations bars, restaurants, trolleys, the only thing and Its not about the hotel but be warned as soon as you leave the hotel people called San francisco artists will ask you for money handouts, help. I live in Texas we call them homeless, drug addicts, scum smelly people. Thank Nancy pelosi your town needs real help, but the food 4 stars
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: We stayed here for five nights in mid September. Staff were friendly and attentive. Rooms comfortable but old style non flat screen television was a surprise. We had an surprising experience finding blood smeared on the bathroom wall near the light switch one evening upon return. This was cleaned off the next day by housekeeping and apparently attributed to the air-conditioning engineer. Difficult to judge if The Orchard is good value compared to other hotels in San Fran but it is not grand value.

review_title: Great value for money and great location!
review_text:
The great thing about this hotel is the location with the free parking for clientele. It's located near most of the main attractions, fishermans wharf, the golden gate bridge and the crooked street. Union square is around 10 min cab ride away.
The rooms themselves have decent amenities and are very clean so you can't go wrong with the overnight stay.
The staff are really helpful who immediately upon arrival showed us first timers to San Fran where to go and where not to go.
All in all I would definately stay here again on my return visit.

Always a great place to stay in SF. Special attention to nontoxic materials were used in the design, healthy bath products, and a nice interior design. Great breakfast cafe across the street on the corner too.
Solid Kimpton Hotel in a great location. The rooms are good with many extras to make you feel at home. The staff is very helpful.
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: Slightly wacky, couldn't fault much. Instant hot water in the evening would have been nice. Apart from that, a very good hotel.
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: Booked through expedia based on reviews and were not disappointed. Booked in for 9 nights and were given a suite room which was fantastic, plenty of space. Breakfast was fine, simple fair but plentiful, only negative was having to clear the tables. Loved the sherry and cookies when we managed to get back in time. For me, a great location, close to japan town and filmore st restaurants and only a fairly flat 20 min walk from union square.

review_title: Love this place! And it has private garages! Totally cute, live all the flowers!
review_text: This place is wonderful, i think they must have been apartments at one time. My friend and I met in Sf ( me from Wa, her from Az) with our kids( 5 kids)the hotel we had booked tried to double our rate, so we left, and found this little jem! It's private, quiet, clean and we had a little kitchen and a garage!! The rooms are on the second floor and the balconies are dripping with flowers! Just lovely! Reminded me of melrose place( I know I know). I am a cheap skate, but I'd definitely stay here again!

The location of this hotel is simply great! Get a waterfront room and stay on the 5th floor or higher. The bar/restaurant is loud and popular Weds-Fri...so keep that in mind if you like that or may not. The bed linens, towels, pillows, robes and toiletries are awesome, but the beds are hard ( hubby loved it - me not so much). The honor bar selection is great and so is their in room dining ( which is 24 hours). We'd stay here again in a heartbeat!
hotel_name: Hotel Vitale, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: We stayed for 3 nights on a recent California holiday and this hotel was the perfect place to spend our last few days before returning to the UK. Upon arrival our check in was quick and efficient with very friendly staff. The porter who took our bags to the room was lovely and remembered our names each time we passed him in reception. He put the bags in the room, made sure we were happy with the room (Alice in Wonderland Suite which was superb) and gave us lots of helpful information about the area. Every afternoon they offer free wine in the lounge along with free back and neck massages (although we never managed to get a massage as the queue was very long). The rooms were very, very clean and ours had a separate living area and huge bathroom. The breakfast we had paid for on top of the room was very basic though, just some fruit and either toast or a croissant so this was slightly dissappointing and the quality wasn't great. In the evening the bar was packed and the bar men were excellent and really friendly and professional, although it is quite pricey. Overall this is a great hotel. Location is perfect for all the sites in San Francisco and the customer service and amenities arenoutstanding. Highly reccommended.
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: Wonderful boutique hotel in great location!
review_text:
We stayed at the Hotel Vitale when the other hotel we had booked was not up to par. This is a wonderful hotel with the most comfortable beds, Egyptian linens and soft comfy pillows. It was very quiet and in an excellent location on the Embarcadero. There are plenty of restaurants, the Ferry Terminal shops are right across the street and the area is very safe. It is not cheap but you get what you pay for. The only negative is that parking costs $48 per night. 
I would not hesitate to stay here again or recommend this hotel highly.
hotel_name: Hotel Vitale, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: Absolutely loved this mini apartment on Lombard. Ask for a room in the courtyard to avoid the sounds of the road when you're trying to sleep at night. Close to pier 39, and some great restaurants. If you drive in to San Francisco, the Marina provides garages under your suite to park your car. Forget staying at high priced hotels downtown. I know, I stayed at them too! You get a full kitchen with dishes and two lovely windows that are proped open welcoming you for your stay. I can't wait to go back and stay here again.

review_title: Nothing special and it doesn't worth to stay.
review_text:
It was a standart, low level city hotel.
Rooms are spacious but some of them ( maybe half of them) have no city view. If you like backyard view and garbage containers it's ok :)
Aaand the most important detail;
If you want to use hotel parking and valet service, they are charging usd 45 for one night!! (including tax). no comment, you can guess what i thought about them.
So, recalculate the actual cost of room.
But, the location was perfect. Next to the cable car station and one minute walking distance from union square.
I think you have options...

I've stayed her twice and was pleased both times. The rooms are full of antiques, the concierge is friendly and the building is charming.
The free breakfast is adequate, but I cut them some slack after I receive my free sherry and cookies in the evening.

After several nights on our road trip in boring, conventional chain hotels, what a wonderful surprise the Queen Anne was! the decor was wonderfully over the top - draperies, overstuffed sofas, antique and repr dark wood furniture, wood paneled walls hung with tapestries - it felt like visiting a rich if somewhat eccentric maiden aunt. The staff were friendly and went out of their way to be helpful. The room wasn't huge But adequate and the Gilchrist & Soams toiletries were a nice touch. Breakfast was good and having tea and coffee available in the guest lounge 24 hours a day was appreciated. It was lovely to end each day with a wine (the hotel happily provided a corkscrew and wine glasses) in front of an open fire. 
I sreally liked the ambience of the Pacific Heights area. A bus stop at the door makes it easy to get round town and the restaurants and bars of Japantown are a short walk away. 
Loved everything abut this place!
This was the perfect place for a quick stay in The City. The rooms were clean, the staff was friendly, and the location was perfect! Right between Union Square and Market Street!

Stayed here for 2 nights following a week of so so hotels. Couldnt be happier. The rooms are charming and cozy, with the most comfortable beds ever. The location was great and everyone at the hotel goes out of their wAy to be friendly. I would definitely stay here again. Hotel has a great vibe.
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: Everything here is wonderful from the staff to the amenities to the location to the adorable rooms, even gave us a gift of champagne for our honeymoon
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: My partner has said it all in earlier review. She was right! I just want to add "all round excellence"!!! Keep room 808 ready will return for sure. Shout out to Jay who sorted us shuttle to sfo at last minute

review_title: Amazing hotel in a great location
review_text: Great hotel and service. Amazing location. No complaints. I would stay there again.

Complimentary Continental breakfast, cheese and wine in the afternoon, & Internet. We weren't expecting it.
We were able to check in early. This is an older style hotel. It was comfortable for a us (couple). The toilet is a slow flush on the 8th It took ages ....
Great location to some dining facilities. Worth walking around the hotel and to union square shops. Close to the cable cars. You will want to use it to go to the pier and see the crooked street. San Francisco is a great city.

review_title: If the staff changes, don't trust them
review_text: This hotel is in the heart of the city, you'll love it. The current staff is wonderful, Damian is the manager and made our group of 15 welcome and caterered to our very needs. Great bargain compared to other hotels. Food was great but the dining room is a bit expensive but you have many choices bc youre in SF. I felt like a king!
A great Eco hotel, beautiful room, fantastic location and helpful/friendly staff. Highly recommended.

Visited for a week and enjoyed our location. Waking distance to everything. Front desk staff were nice except the concierge. I've stayed with them previously and it's the same guy over and over who is irritating and not helpful. One more thing, when getting dropped off by a friend the parking attendant gave us problems parking in their lot to unload our items.

Stayed here twice and absolutely love it. Great location, friendly staff and lovely rooms.
The Wine Hour is a must!
Recommended to all friends and family.
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text:
While the location is good, the hotel rooms are dated, the walls are extremely thin and the customer service is pretty average. Having stayed all over the usa during our holiday in hotels that cost as much as or less than this I wouldn't consider this a three star property. Some of the two star properties we have stayed in have been nicer, with better customer service and a nicer breakfast for less money.
If doing this again I would stay in a chain hotel like holiday inn or best western.

This hotel is in a good location. The hotel is small and has basic services. The hotel rooms are large and bathrooms are updated. The hotel room furniture and television are dated and worn. We found the bed to be hard, and didn't sleep well. Our last morning, the staff woke us up at 7 am by calling the room to ask of we ordered room service. For location, I give the hotel a 3. Otherwise I rate it an average 3.

Arrived to a room at 83 degrees despite thermostat set at 65. I called down and ...eventually someone came to confirm it really was quite hot. 3 hours later and after significant perspiration (no offer to exchange rooms) maintenance fixed the fan, but NOT the AC and declared it fixed. By then it was night and I had opened the window.
The next day my wife arrived to....82deg after a long flight and hike. After 3 hours they finally agreed to just give us another room. My wife forgot my phone charger while moving all my unpacked luggage. So I called from the new room's bathroom after finally realizing the new room's phone did not work. They had already put a guest in the room with no AC and never really looked into finding my charger until 2 days later at my insistence.
Cheap wine at 5pm and good coffee in the morning is nice, but does not make up for poor facilities and a lack of true service. This hotel presents the worst aspects of a chain without consistently providing the best details of a stand alone.
To be fair, the location is great, Walgreens is across the street, and the daytime desk/door are friendly.
PS Don't walk south at night. San Fran has some very real risks in the wrong neighborhoods.
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: Reality is way too different that their photos. Terrible room!
review_text: We reserved a king suite but end up with a room like a cell. The bathroom has nothing but a small sink and a tub. we were just so disappointed that we paid almost 300 dollars for a room of a cheap hotel. The decor is terrible compared with the elegant photo of the king suite they use on the website! We ll never stay there again!

Was originally booked in across the road but indifferent staff, and women of questionable repute in the foyer, and a horrible room resulted in an unhappy spouse! So u walked across the road to the Monaco which was the complete opposite. Nice staff nice room clean civilized no hookers! What's not to like more expensve but we did get what we paid for!
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco San Francisco - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: We stayed here for 4 days and it is a fantastic hotel,very well placed and very clean... Very attentive staff,one of the best hotels iv ever stayed in

review_title: Over priced considering other rates in downtown
review_text: We love the location as it is one block from where our son lives and close to parts of town we like to visit (presidio palace of fine arts, Filmore street). However we also stayed here in July and there has been a noticeable decline although more expensive. The rooms are still comfortable and clean and the city view is great, staff is very friendly and helpful but the continental breakfast 6 months ago was fruit pastries juice hard boiled eggs erc and now consists of dry pasties and coffee. They ran out of everything yesterday about halfway through. Overall the hotel seems in a little need of attention. I sad about this as everyone is so nice and things are clean but to pay $179 a night when there were many many options near union square for $ 89-120 means we will have to think twice before staying here again.
hotel_name: Laurel Inn, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: very nice hotel in financial district with modern amentities
review_text:
very good business hotel
clean convenient
great views
good service
Brilliant location, great rooms and good service. Can't go wrong, spend a litle more and stay here.

review_title: Rooms disappointing, bar and service great.
review_text:
With limited room availability in SF when we arrived, we ended up picking the Clift and a 'studio suite' for about $345++ (=$400 nett not including breakfast) which was described on their site as a larger, more luxurious room. The room was indeed reasonably spacious, but decor was very sparse. The only item it seemed they had spent some money on where the curtains, everything else was very basic. The bathroom was small, with an institutional feel to it (not the good kind). 
The hotel's saving grace is the excellent location close to Union Square and a couple of great breakfast places (Taylor Street Coffee Shop, Dottie's), plus the concierge and front office staff is excellent. The bar is great also, and really gets hopping on the weekends. 
Would not stay here again, despite the pluses mentioned.

review_title: Excellent customer service but overpriced for facilities.
review_text: The location is okay, staff & customer service is excellent. Car parking is slow & ludicrously expensive. The rooms & small & old & painting them a funky colour does not hide this or justify the price! The restaurant isn't great & food & drinks are expensive.

I enjoyed staying at this hotel. It was in a good location. They provided bikes for free. The service was good and the room was spacious and comfortable. It felt an older style hotel- for memory lavender carpet and pale blue walls. It was good value. We chose to stay in a bigger room. Hugh Hackman was staying there as the theatre was right next door.

We've stayed here four times over the past year and have always had a great time! The hotel staff are very accommodating and attentive to detail! The location is close to the Montgomery BART stop, China Town and North Beach. We'll be back!
Very lively hotel. Rooms are comfortable and breakfast was excellent. Ideally located. Will definitely return. Visually impressive decor.

review_title: Good location no special honeymoon treatment
review_text: We stayed for 5 nights for the start of our honeymoon in September 2010. We had booked a deluxe King room and didn't get offered congratulations on being newly weds nor an upgrade. Still this was made up for later on in our trip. Great location, cool bar but would try somewhere else if visiting again.

review_title: Well located business class hotel in SF
review_text: I've stayed at a number of business class hotels in SF and this one is likely the best value. Located in Chinatown/Finacial District, you are walking distance to the Muni and Bart for mass transit. Chinatown offers all manner of interesting things to see. Union Sq and Embarcadero are both close. Ask for a Bay View room when possible.

review_title: Not quite as good as it makes out to be.
review_text:
I wasn't to impressed with the Clift. It's quite pricey and you get very little for your money. The rooms while advertised as Â minimalist in my opinion are stark and un-welcoming. The bathroom was old fashioned and a bit dowdy and was not in keeping with the style of the room. it's nowhere nearly as trendy in the rooms as they make out.Â 
Little things like not providing glasses for your mini bar drinks or charging massive fees for wireless really get up my nose.Â 
On a positive note the bedding and mattresses are to die for and I had three good night sleep. Â The location is great and the rest of the hotel is pumping! Â The staff are all very friendly and polite also.Â 
All in all, it gets a three star from me just because I've stayed in much better for Â lower cost.Â 
A final note, on completing the survey the manager was kind enough to write a note back taking on board some of the concerns.

review_title: Love this place, a true Morgans Hotel... 1st class
review_text:
Upon our arrival our room was not ready, so they upgraded us! The location is a few blocks from Union Square, & close to everything. We borrowed the Clift Hotel bikes & rode all over the city... to Sausalito & back! The concierge folks were very attentive, assisted us w/ our car rental & restaurant recommendations. 
Room was spacious & comfy w/ great city views!

review_title: Top location, mixed decor and mediocre service.
review_text:
We stayed at The Clift after a recommendation from a friend who had lived in the city. Found a great multi day rate on Expedia. We traveled to San Francisco for a conference and spent some leisure time afterwards.
We were impressed by the plushness and fresh feel to the rooms, even at this entry level - lovely toiletries, nice fluffy towels and comfortable mattress. Our room faced the inner courtyard, but was still light and sunny.
The decor of the lobby and dark lifts don't match the upper floors of the property, although did add an ambience. Perhaps slightly too dark during the day.
The service was always swift, although perhaps too much so. No personal touch, we weren't asked how our stay was upon check out and when asking questions seemed to get rushed responses; as if the front desk staff had something better to be doing. When I enquired about staying longer the receptionist picked up the phone and told me to speak to reservations, who put me on hold - I didn't wait and subsequently stayed elsewhere for 3 more days.
Porters only seemed interested if you were getting a taxi, perhaps for the commission from the taxi drivers? We weren't offered with help with our bags upon check-in, even though there were few people checking in.
Overall, we enjoyed our stay, being so central to many of the major sights, restaurants and public transport was a big bonus. 
Would highly recommend a visit to the bar Bourbon & Branch, just nearby the hotel.

The beds are okay but the bathrooms are too cramped with absolutely no counter space. The lobby is dark and they are more concerned with their nightclub than their guests. No one opened the doors and valet was awful. I will not be staying with them again.

Stayed a total of seven nights at the Clift good location close to union square great door staff and friendly manager , concierge good , some of the reception ladies not so friendly 
Do not walk in area behind hotel it's not great 
Definately try the farmers Market at the ferry building , thurs and sat
Friday evening food fair at fort Mason and the bars at haight and dogpatch a trio to mission is also a must

review_title: construction site beside it is noisy even at night, better if you stay closer to union square, this one is in Chinatown.
review_text:
This hilton is situated in Chinatown, you have to walk a few
Blocks to ride the cable car; the street is one way and there is a bus at the front of the hotel going to fisherman's wharf but not going back. It would better staying somewhere closer to Union Square.

review_title: A really stylish hotel. Beautiful rooms, a lovely cocktail bar, the redwood room, do book a table for drinks, it gets busy !
review_text: We were on the very top floor, with a very clear view 2 ways across the city. We will certainly come back and really absolutley loved our stay. It was our final night before going home from our honeymoon and was perfect place to be to say goodbye to San fran and the USA.

1st August, Check in.
- I was told there were no rooms with king side bed so they asked me if I was ok with taking a room with a queen bed instead... Ok, no problem. The room was a disable room with no bath. The room stunk of cigarettes. Ok, I called the reception and asked why they did not told me the type of the room in advance... No answer, instead when i asked if someone could help me move my stuff to the ither room they were giving me, they said that if I wanted to change room I had to take all my belongings and bags dowstaies from the 23rd floor and wait till someone was available to help...
1st August night time: I could not sleep all night due to a constant noise of the trucks loading and unloading material thru the night. I called the reception at 4 am and the only thing they were able to say was that SF was a big city and noise from the outside had to be expected!!! What? I asked to change room nxt morning.
2nd August: change of room, ok.
3rd august: room service, dinner delivered stone cold!
5th August: breakfast, they charged me 17 USD for a continental breakfast that tasted like ----! The pastries must have been from the day before as they were soft and a bit sticky besides the fact the did not taste right, the coffee was ok but the pineapple was mauldy.. Yak!
9 august: no hot water for 2 hours from 5 till 7.10.
9/10 august: nobody picks up my laundry and I'm asked to bring my dirty cloths down to the reception!!! So I'm waiting in line with other guests just to drop my laundry off... 
Oh dear! 3 more days to go and I will be happy to be out of here!
Just book another hotel please, the service us bad and the facilities even worse!

Paid for room w king bed over 1 week ago. When arrived room given had 2 doubles. Front desk states their are no king or queen beds available at this time! Not disclosed at time of reservation made. Beds are hard as a slab. Room very hot, no AC, poor ventilation. Found band aid wrapper on floor. No outlets for cell phones & computer by the night stands. All outlets are at desk being used for lights & TV. The Super 8 very nice and would recommend.

review_title: Seriously give this one a miss!!
review_text: Coming into our 4th month of a year ling trip around the world we have stayed in many many of the cheapest roughest places going! This one is way up there with the worst! To be fair the room isn't to bad, although incredibly basic, it's not a hotel... I'd even question calling it a hostel. The most alarming this about it all is the neighbourhood, full off junkies, homeless mental patients (which I know fellow travellers not from the USA will find this commen in most states of America) but this area is really in the thick of it!! But also not far from the nicer areas if you don't get robbed on the way there! We can't comment on the breakfast as we missed it, although free tea and coffee was good and the wifi wasn't bad either, genrally I wouldn't recommend staying here! Oh and I just forgot the "bathroom" was an absolute disgrace!!! (and was shared between a floor of 40 rooms)

This place smells, looks cheap, feels like Crap, sign says no parking 4-6pm, so we missed the sign and got our truck towed, made us pay the parking ticket costing us 450$ for nothing. I'm being very Honest, This hotel is the worst ever been in my entire life. And will be forever. I will never spend my money here. This hotel clearly fails any hotels ratings. I am very angry with this peice of Crap. I hope no one never sleeps here so this can go out of business.
The only attraction is the free parking. We did not want even want to take shower after we saw the condition of the room.

review_title: I would pay a little more to stay somewhere else.
review_text: Questionable stains on the carpet. Lamps, the fridge, and the microwave were not plugged in and had to be moved across the room to be plugged in to sockets. Thin walls. Half a block from a bar; there were drunks walking around and screaming till 3 in the morning, and the sirens didn't help from the cops trying to clear them off the streets. The only plus was that it was about two miles walking distance to fisherman's wharf, golden gate park, and the palace of fine arts- but if you're not a big walker and you could stand to spend $20/night, I wouldn't bother with this place.

review_title: Good value but at a price!
review_text: We stayed 3 nights in this very centrally located hotel. It is in a safe area but the room was so small we had to juggle suitcases to fit in. The shower drains smelled bad and the shower head was so low I had to bend over to wash my hair. If you are not at all fussy this is a good hotel. Free parking is a plus.

review_title: Bery good hotel but unconinient location
review_text: Location with lots of bums nearby because of the shelter for homeless. therefore these person can be mostly avoided if going to the downtown along hyde street an not ellis. Very nice rooms and very nice view from the breakfast room which is at the top floor. Free wifi internet and good showers. But personal did not let us leave our bikes at the garage and it was very pity and not good for us.

review_title: Great place to stay in the city
review_text: Hotel is centrally located in downtown San Francisco. Clean, comfortable rooms at a reasonable price, with a great breafast and a staff always willing to help. What mre could you ask for..

The Mithila is not as horrible as some of the reviews make it out to be. It's in a great location that is slightly away from the noise of the city and is a perfectly fine place to br based in San Francisco. 
 One thing to take note of are the paper thin walls! You can hear absolutely everything (like a neighbours VERY loud snoring) from your own room! Not great for light sleepers, also tv only had about three channels. On the positive side though the unlimited free wifi was a nice extra.

We pulled up to front of hotel prostitute approached our vehicle...witnessed a drug deal right on steps of entrance...and watched a man with an exposed knife walking towards our vehicle...all during 2 minutes in broad afternoon daylight!!!!!! Needless to say we had no choice but to stay elsewhere. Was booked through booking.com (another horrible decision) and alerted them immediately of the situation. 6 days later they said they can't help get a refund and closed the case. On top of that we were double charged for the room we never chked into, almost $400 later...no resolution with management being a bunch of crooks! If you value your life and money do yourself a favor and book elsewhere. Travelocity puts their customers FIRST!!!!!!
hotel_name: Americas Best Value Inn & Suites Union Square

review_title: What a crappy place. Dirty, smelly, gross.
review_text: Had to stay here because nothing else was available. What a pigsty. Absolutely horrendous. There was a prostitute next door...the toilet and shower had to be shared...NEVER told us this. Would not give our money back. The prostitute smoked marijuana and it filtered into our room...there were roaches in the hallway...it was just bad. The area was ok....so we only came in to pass out...avoid.

review_title: There are better places for the money
review_text:
The 80$ room is tiny, the towels are small and the place stinks. But my complaint is the service, specifically the woman that runs the place.
In the morning, before checking out, I went for a walk. It came to 1045, I was 30 minutes away, and I didn't know what time check out was. I called, she said 11, I asked if I could be a little late, and she said fine, no problem. I got back to the room, and she had taken all of my stuff out and put it in a storage closet. I hadn't packed and it was strewn about. I couldn't find my dirty clothes. I asked her where she put them and she took offense at my 'accusing' her of stealing my dirty socks and underwear. Eventually the guy shampoo vacuuming the room (reason they could not wait 15 minutes) suggested I look in the trash, by which he meant the dumpster out back. There it was. Why would she do that? I hate giving people like that my money.

review_title: If you're a degenerate...you hit the jackpot!
review_text: For $273.00 a week you can rent a poorly cleaned room with a private bath replete with roaches, brain fried residents that tweek, yell and trip through the wee hours of the morning. The rooms are small, the carpet filthy, the comforter looked to have a thousand cigarette burns in it, the blanket had a giant hole in it and the surrounding area crawls with tranny hookers. Only stay here if you are desparate. No tv and spotty internet.

review_title: Nice hotel, area could be better.
review_text:
The hotel is nice and clean. The staff is friendly.
Rooms are nice beds are nice.
Downside.. Walls very heary.
Breakfast is good.
People saying the area isnt good. Its true. But its realy funny as people say they are from a big city and arent afraid but basically cr*p their pants walking to the trolley.

If you look like "oh grab my wallet" they smell it.

Nonetheless i can imagine people not realy happy about it. But nothing will happen.

Location is excellent. Rooms were old but still in good shape. Service was outstanding. If we are ever in San Francisco again we will come here. Oh, and don't book your room over the phone. The room would have been 50 bucks more through the phone reservation service.

review_title: Not just bad but ruined my trip!
review_text: I won't add the same information about the disgusting room. Agree with all those comments. It was the nightclub level noise that blew me away. The club below was so loud- blaring music til way past three am. Unbelievable thFat this hotel charges anything to stay here. It's 545 am and traffic noises are loud enough to wake me. I am so tired, that there is no way I can enjoy my only day in San Francisco and that sucks! I'm so tired I feel like a toddler on the verge of tears. Thanks, embassy hotel and hotels.com

review_title: Great value and walk to the opera!
review_text: We were pleasantly surprised to find the room (506) was quiet, clean, "newish" furnishings, large closet and bath with interesting tile, firm mattress with NO bedbugs (we checked), and although we were next to the elevator, we could not hear it in our room. Walls NOT thin, windows have screens and open. Didn't use heat so not sure about that. Safe didn't work. No frills (iron, fridge, coffeemaker etc), but we carry out own. We will definitely return for events in the area and stay here. Great value and safe feeling walking toward Van Ness.

As I write this I am sitting on the most uncomfortable bed. My head is pounding from the lack of sleep my husband and I got last night. Springs from the mattress were poking me all night, pillows were as hard as rocks and there is the most annoying knocking sound coming from inside the walls. All night! We are going to ask to change rooms and hope that helps. If not we are leaving and finding a room elsewhere! 
Another thing, walls are paper thin. Could hear a drunk girl in the next room over singing at 4:00am. Awful night. 
I need a nap.

review_title: Still recovering from the bed bug bites
review_text: Stayed 5 nights week of October 2nd. First impression was of a small room with tired carped and no ac. Conveniently located but would not recommend because of the pest control issue. Unacceptable in the 21st century. SF tourism should remove hotel license from such establishments until they do something about it. Tarnishes SF's reputation.

review_title: Good location but a very average hotel.
review_text: The location is great with easy access to all the sights but the hotel itself lacks anything that adds to your stay. Everything is OK but nothing is great. Charge for wifi and bar and food options attached to the hotel are appalling.

We booked this hotel at the last minute as we drove into the city late.
At first we thought the hotel was a bit run down but service was okay and it was in an okay location to union square.
After the second night and noticing a few bite marks on me I started to become concerned.by the third day I was completely covered in bed bug bites,and I have never been so itchy in my life.
I'm not being a drama queen but this hotel pretty much ruined my holiday for the next 10 days as I dealt with these stupid bites.
When we checked out I told the front desk and got a 'ohhh well we have your details so we'll get in touch...' but two weeks later still nothing.
There is nothing good about this hotel except the free parking.

review_title: Mediocer hotel in middle of downtown
review_text:
For people wanting to stay in the downtown area this has a good location. If you come by car beware that this hotel only offers valet parking for $34. And the nearest parking garage charges aprox the same. The rooms are somewhat less then basic;.no safe, no minibar, old tv etc. As mentioned by others WiFi is not included so you pay $9,95 per 24 hours and it does not even work. We have not been able to log on once. Finally the location is nice in terms of downtown but you will have to overlook all the bums in this area. 
Ps. No breakfast possible because there is no bar or restaurant with the hotel.

I stayed there in August for 4 nights and was completely satisfied. The room furnishings were showing their age and things you find in more modern hotels (such as a TV) were missing, but the room was clean and everything was in good working order. The view was not really that -- about 3m to the next wall if the hotel. The location is very convenient though. There is a nice coffee shop next door and a large shopping centre on the other side. Bus, metro and cable car stations are about 3 minutes walk away. Would stay there again.

review_title: We knew it was a risk but everyone else was booked
review_text: Other reviews were correct. The best thing we can say was that it offered off-street parking within view of our room.

review_title: Average hotel, past its prime- Little to love, little to hate.
review_text: This place feels a bit tired. The location is the best thing about it. Bathtub seemed dirty, but it just might be age on the vinyl. Walls were a little thin, but typically for a drywall building. An old tube tv in a armoire, lightly chipped furniture, and black/white tile seems to hint at the need for an update in this hotel. This place is fine for a night, probably comparable to a Howard johnsons or an older Holiday Inn. This is a really strange designed space, wide hallways and elevators, bathrooms in the hallway, but rooms are average size (or a little big by San Fran standards). This feels like it could have been an apartment building, a dorm or a retirement home. It has the past polish of the type of place sold with time shares-good at the start, by quickly diminishing. There was a constant leaking sound in my room, but I couldn't find the source. The front staff were rather indifferent about my check in and the room was generality cold and without character. I've stayed at $13 guest houses in Cambodia and 5 stars in NYC. This place is in the middle, fine but nothing to write home about. With so many great place to stay in sf, I'm not sure this is a great choice. My room was less than 100, so you do get what you pay for. For $25 more, I'd go boutique hotel and get some type of charm. For conference goers, Moscone is very close, but prices spike when the conferences meet. Very average overall. Little to love, little to hate.

review_title: Good value at a good location
review_text:
We: Middle aged couple and adult Son (21)

Hotel located conviniently and in walking distance to Market Street and Cable Car (California St, China town)

Negative: Some faint but disturbing music beats during the night.

review_title: Interesting location, friendly staff, better than the plastic HInn but don't epxpdect luxury
review_text: Good location ... Helpful staff ... Great place to eat across the street .... Interesting early morning stroll
Rooms are old, outdated and mine smelled like mothballs and smoke. Service was non existent... Breakfast? Your best bet is to go to Mel's diner. Not worth the $90.

review_title: The guy at the front desk hit on me & insulted my girlfriend! A nexus for nuts?
review_text:
This place was chosen on the basis of price & on that count it's a pretty good deal. Physically, the rooms are fine; on the old end of the spectrum but that's fine, as it is neat & clean. 
My problem was with the people. After finding street parking my girlfriend & I were walking towards the hotel when we noticed a pair of angry, drunken, screaming teens. In summary: please reconsider staying here. It's got some bad mojo going on for sure!

This isn't real fancy, but good location, really nice helpful staff, location good for kicking around san Fran. About $8 cab fare to all main areas of SF. I would stay again.

If you are adventurous and fan of the tv show "man vs wild" and want to sleep in this hotel at all cost don t read the following review cause it might spoil surprises and ruin your experience. If you are a simple traveller just looking for a place to rest while visiting SF, I beg you to read this before choosing this hotel.
First, for the record, I picked up this hotel by default since I booked it few days prior to my arrival during high season (august) so I had not so many options to choose from. I was looking for a cheap, or should I say "not too expensive" hotel not too far from major city's attractions. 
The pros:
- Good location: a few blocks away on foot from union square where you can take cable cars or other transportation
- Cheap, at least cheaper than other hotel in the area, although it's still a total ripoff. The nightly rate was like 70 bucks on week days and 125 (!) for the week end.
- The room was clean for the most part except some cigarettes burns on the bed cover and holes in walls
- Parking is free. Note that hotel management declines responsability for any damage done to your car or any goods stolen. Park at your own risk ! (please refer to the cons section for more details about security issues)
- You might want to do a one-night stay to have an idea of what it s like to sleep in a very bad hotel. Any other hotel will then seems 5 stars hilton class afterwards.
Cons:
- Bad location: although this hotel is not far from union square, its location is far from being desirable unless you don t fear to be mugged or robbed. One sentence from our taxi driver sums it all: "it's a rough neibourhood". You got it, homeless and crackheads are wandering in this area so you'd better not walk at night alone. You can tell that security is an major issue here by the number of video cameras installed in this hotel (a lot)
- THE NOISE: unless you like to party or don t need to sleep more than 2 or 3 hours this is gonna be also a major issue for you. If you want to experience what it s like to sleep in the street than it s ok. If not, be prepared for endlessly hear cars honks and engines roars, people talking, screaming, laughing, yieling or spitting like you never hear it before. The sound experience is pretty amazing, it s like cars or people are actually in your room. Also when other people from adjacent rooms of the hotel use the bathrooms it actually makes more noise than when you use them ! Unbelievable... I guess the walls of rooms are made of cardboard or paper. It makes sense since this hotel is more like a motel and the building seems not to be made of solid stones or concrete. Hopefully this motel will not survive the big one (earthquake)
Anyway I m not a deep sleeper but I m used to sleep in not so quiet environment. But here I think I spent the worst night ever of my life, I might have slept like 1 or 2 hours max only because I was exhausted. I think scientists should definetly use this hotel to do some research on acoustics and echo chamber
- Wireless internet is complimentary but unusable. It s like you are back 15 years ago at the beginning of internet. I could hardly send an email with my smartphone. Luckily there is an Apple store in SF
- Guys at the desk were friendly as prison wardens (sorry for the wardens)
To conclude don t book this hotel unless you have no other choices. Try to book early another hotel even if it's not as well located. Taxis or buses are fast and cheap and there are other great areas besides union square or the classic tourists-traps like fisherman's wharf. Valencia or the Mission districts there are great restaurants there.
Hope this helps.
This hotel smells like urine everywhere. It has a horrible room service and a very noisy place. Never say at this hotel!!!!!!!

review_title: Great flavor of downtown for a reasonable price
review_text: I stayed here after a show at the Warfield. As a bay area native, I really appreciate the location, good and bad. It's within walking distance of almost everything. Kinda seems like a party hotel for broke young kids... So if this is your thing, it's all good. Far from clean, but charming. You'll want to get drunk before laying your head down here. Overall, it was perfect for my purpose.

I Heard About This Hotel Online. The Pictures Looked Amazing. 
Our Stay Was For 2 Nights. The Cleaning Service Was Average. You Have To Pay $25 A Night For Parking And You Need To Leave A $50 Deposit Each Night. 
If You Don't Mind Bums & Human Bowel Movements Outside Your Hotel Then This Is The Perfect Plc To Stay.

We always stay at the cova when attending events at the bill graham civic auditorium, because late night cabs on busy nights are hard to come by, and the cova is in walking distance. The staff is friendly, parking easy, rooms clean. What more do you want? The tenderloin sucks, but come on that's not the hotels fault. And you really shouldnt be looking for a hotel restaurant, this city has some of the best food in the country.

review_title: It's ok, great location but full of weird people on the street
review_text:
It's in market street, close to the Cable Car and the F bus, which are the main way of transportation for tourist people.
The street is good located but it's full of homeless people, you don't have to feel afraid, they are in their own business and they aren't going to tell you anything.
The staff was kind and helpful and the reception is open 24 hours. They have parking lot, it's 25$ per day, which is cheaper than a public parking. The parking is really strange and the neighborhood a little it more difficult than the hotel one, but we didn't have any problem.
The room was fine, clean but old and small.
Briefing, its an option, not bad but neither the best in the city, we took because no other choice but it wasn't a bad experience

Cheap is the only plus point I would say. Neighbourhood is terrible. You can hear people screaming and lots of sirens at night. Day time, many homeless as well as jobless people loiter around. Even local tour guide also not feel comfortable.
Everyday they serve doughnut, coffee and tea as breakfast. Free wifi is only true when you are at lobby and each floor waiting area. But guess what, no power point over these places. Tried access from room, you would give up quickly when the connection always broken!
Twin bed is smaller than normal queen size standard. Washing basin have hot and cold water separated and not mixed for better balance. Queky sound when walk on floor or take elevator, smelly carpet and shaky elevator...funny is, you have to leave your room key every time you go out. Their room service will only take care their stuff, not even fold your blanket if you got one. They can enter your room even you have do not disturb sign hanged on door knob.
Luckily I'm just here for a week trip, no impact for its no visitor policy and its high parking fee. But what surprising me the most is, they can act friendly to you in normal time, but when you ask for help, they said not their responsibilty. I would rather they tell me politely they need to charge instead of saying this is not their responsibility!
In summary, I don't recommend this 'hotel' at all and I swear no more next visit if I were to visit San Francisco again.

review_title: Nice but in a sketchy part of town
review_text: The hotel is very nice. It's beautifully decorated but some of the gym equipment did not work. Although the Internet is free (a rarity in San Fran) it did not work in any of the rooms....only outside next to the elevator. It's also part of town. Lots of homeless, drug addicts and prostitutes. Oh not to mention the trannies and drug dealers.

review_title: Hotel barato e bem localizado. Barulhento mas perto de tudo.
review_text: Este hotel cobra pouco e oferece o basico necessario. Faz parte de quem paga pouco, exigir pouco. Para san francisco, o preco e qualidade sao compativeis. Vale pelo preco, mas precisa ter muito estomago para aguentar o barulho e o entra e sai constante do hotel. Vale a estada, pelo preco pois o quarto Ã© suficiente e limpo.
There are half the number of parking spaces than there are units. Street parking in the area is almost impossible.

Hotel che ha bisogno di un restailing completo soprattutto per la biancheria sembrava pulita ma lenzuola di colore grigio e piene di buchi coperta con righe di sangue.
