review_text: Over priced...terrible customer service, definately doesn't deserve the hotel title. I've travelled all over the world and this has to be worst hotel I have EVER stayed in. Please book elsewhere as you will be disappointed

review_title: Better alternative for the same price
review_text:
I had an awful experience with someone at the desk front. At the check out, he refused to give me a receipt for the luggage storage and started to yield. 
Moreover, the price is quite high for the quality of the room. The breakfast is also very disappointing.
Positive points: the 50's atmosphere of the hotel and the ladies at the desk front who are very nice and helpful, in contrary to the men.

if you are looking for the Hyatt, Best Western or even Motel 6 in this hotel...keep looking. From the "traditonal" male mentallity front desk man...who checked in a male customer before me "a female" even when the man walked in after me to don't bring anything bigger than a backpack or you won't be able to fit in the elevator, you won't be able to bring your bicycles, they do not have any where to store them and don't expect to watch any tv other than local channels. Granted this building I over 85 years old, it wouldn't take much to make this a quaint and nicer hotel....I would not recommend this hotel....I stayed because there wasn't any others to chose from in this area.
modest but clean and well priced rooms in the heart of downtown. Good service, highly recommended.

We would have never stayed in a place a shady as this if we hadn't already booked over the phone in a last ditch effort to find an affordable hotel. They do have free garage parking, which is very limited & open for the homeless to rummage through the dumpster. The signs warning against vehicle vandalism & break ins didn't seem to ease the comfort levels either. They seemed to be in the middle of a cheap renovation, which didn't help things much. We were awakened every night to what sounded like the dumpster being wheeled out to the street for garbage pickup. The overall area of the Motel is what some would call "the ghetto". Lots & lots of homeless & beggars. Not really a kid friendly part of town. All in all, I guess the lesson we learned here is, you get what you pay for! I wouldn't recommend to anyone I know :(

This place was very affordable for downtown San Francisco. The rooms were very nice and the staff was courteous..only downside is the police sirens throughout the night..but that is to be expected considering the location. The neighborhood is nice too.

This hotel is located near everything. I was quite surprised on how inexpensive it was considering we were so close to everything. Rooms were clean and staff was extremely friendly. Thanks Diya & Ricky for the great customer service.

Last minute trip. I don't know SF at all but it's near the interesting spots so I figured I'd give it a try. 
Not clean at all. Poor maintenance. Clerk put me next to a room with 4 children under the age of 5. 
The carpet was stained and had a thick layer of dirt in the corners. 
Baseboards were covered with accumulated dust/dirt/shmutz and couldn't even see the color of the paint. 
Clerk balked at refunding but reminding her it was American Express was enough to change her mind. 
Don't chance it.

review_title: Rude, smelly, dirty & smelt like last nights curry!! Don't bother.
review_text:
This place is basic and is run by a rude indian family. It is cheaper than other places but you get what you pay for. 
Parking very limited, Internet and breakfast may as well have not been advertised.
Definatly consider something else.

review_title: Average hotel; no Internet and no breakfast.
review_text: Rooms were OK, fairly clean and included fridge and a microwave. The value seemed pretty good for San fransisco (alot cheaper than the other hotels)... However the wifi connection was so slow it was impossible to use the Internet. There isnt enough parking for all guests so you either have to double park everyone or park on the street. The hotel advertises breakfast (I think I saw 2 types of cereal when we checked in and that's pretty much it... No seating) Hotel staff were unfriendly and bordering on rude. The hotel is however in a good location for nice restaurants, bars and some shopping.

Stayed here one week for oracle week I had a wonderful time room was excellent and clean over looking the front Geary street. Lots of restaurants and was walking distance to my conference. Over all this is a good hotel in a five star location and the staff was very helpful in answering all my questions I sure will return next year for oracle week.

I didnt expect much going in-i read the reviews before booking. We were just concerned with getting a nights sleep. I was disappointed to have an extremely uncomfortable night. The room stunk so badly of of years of cigarette smoke we left the door open. The lights didn't work on the first night and we couldn't get hold of anyone in reception to fix the problem. The motel looks like it could do with a complete renovation, and i wouldn't rate it'd chances of standing up in an earthquake. The woman in reception was overly aggressive when checking in and made me wait until 3pm despite a notice on the wall clearly stating check in was from 2pm. The best feature was the location, which is close to the Marina Triangle, although the traffic noise won't be to everyone's liking. Worst of all was the price, $200 per night when booking through hostel world is outrageous when I think it is worth $80 per night absolute max. Overall not a great experience.

review_title: You get what you pay for.. Worth it.
review_text: Well, at first sight, I was weary about staying. It looked rundown and pretty empty.. we got 2 nights without checking out the rooms first and I was honestly expecting to walk into a smelly room, dirty sheets and even dirtier unkempt bathroom.. But I was surprised at how decent the room looked.. fancy by no means, basic stuff.. But everything was functional.. Only thing that bummed me out was the noise, I have insomnia and being close to the road didn't help much but it does quiet down at night. Overall is a safe, economic stay.

Me and my friend just wanted an inexpensive hotel for a weekend in san francisco. We didn't want to blow our budget that could be used to shopping eating and drinking in the city. With the price we were paying we were grealy surprised at what we got! Our room was comfortably fit for just the 2 of us and and very clean. We loved the brick wall, the vintage-looking bathtub and the real coffee they provide! The staff was very helpful always with a smile one there face, they recommended some great places to eat nearby that were delicious. The location was a perfect distance to the downtown area were we wanted to be.All in all our weekend getaway was a success, would definetly stay here again.

We scored 3 nights here for $80 a night! Different to other reviews so needless to say we got a bargain. 
My husband and I stayed here & yes the rooms are small & hot but the cleanliness of the room over ruled the size issue. We ended up sleeping with the window open & thankfully it was Nov so not a hot day at all.
The breakfast was very suitable, tea, coffee, fruit, juice, toast & bagels. Perfect start to the day. 
Staff were friendly & spoke fluent English so I'm not sure what the problem was with other reviewers. 
I have stayed in many different styles of accommodation and have travelled a lot and found no problems with this hotel. 
Location was perfect! :)

We arrived at the Dakota hotel (sister hotel next door) and were moved to the Fitzgerald (no idea why). Check in was easy and staff welcoming. Rooms are clean, VERY small and hot but fine for a base to explore the city. No wardrobe and barely any storage space so bare this in mind. Tv only has 12 channels but wifi is brilliant. Location is amazing, central to everything, safe area and quiet at nights. Free breakfast is great, simple bagels, fruit, coffee but a cheap and yummy way to start the day. We took the airport shuttle to the airport and is only $9 and runs every 30 minutes. I thought it was a little pricey for the space and amenities but the location is worth it and nowhere is cheap in San Francisco! I would definitely stay again if on a budget.

review_title: Not the nicest, but clean and good location.
review_text:
We booked this hotel at the last minute on expedite, which didn't really leave us much choice. We needed something close to the Fillmore that wasn't super expensive. Luckily this was only a short drive away. However, it was a short trip so I can't speak to its proximity to any other tourist spots.
The hotel is small and can be easily missed on Lombard. Hotel parking is limited and street parking is a nightmare. We parked in a no parking spot next to the ice machine and the desk guy swore we wouldn't be towed, thank goodness we weren't.
The rooms were also small. We had 2 doubles, mini fridge, microwave, iron and ironing board and some hanging space. There was a small flat screen with very limited channels. The room was a bit dark even with the curtain open.
The bathroom was also tiny and the towels were thin. It had a skylight which made the room super bright, but the light allowed you to see the many flaws. The tub was poorly installed with giant seams along the walls that weren't properly called, the curtain rod was hung crooked so it didn't fully close, and the floor of the tub was so slippery I almost fell the dirt time I got in.
For the one night we were in town, it worked for our needs, but I would have liked something a bit nicer for $161+ tax a night. Guess that's the price you pay for booking the same day.

review_title: Great beds, cool details in the hallways: Whitcomb wins in my book.
review_text:
I liked this place. The bed was comfortable, and there were pillows of difference thickness to choose from so I found my perfect choice. The tall ceilings and dark wood trim in the hallways made me feel like I was in a European villa. But the updated bathroom and amenities made it feel like a Marriot. 
 I stayed here for the AGU meeting and it was perfect. It's cheaper than the union square places (which are ridiculously marked up), but it's just as convenient. It's also right at a BART stop. There is a Chase and a Starbucks right down stairs for those who like those conveniences. I ate at the restaurant attached to the hotel all week because the food is good and the hostess is super friendly. I also saw the mayor there.

review_text:

Minutes away from lots of shopping malls and museums, around the corner from city hall, and the hop on hop off bus tours stop right there.
There is a mediumly shady stretch of market street which can can be a little intimidating to walk through if you are alone.
My trip to San Francisco was as a tourist, Hotel Whitcomb was a good experience, and I can see myself staying with them again for future trips.

review_text: For my 21st birthday I desided to book a room of 2 beds one room. Oh no they gave me 2 ghetto looking roach rooms okay you don't even have your own bathroom you have to share it! After my girlfriend & I came back from clubbin we played music on our phone veryyyy veryyyy low like seriously the person in charge came to my room about 3 times to turn it offf what the hell I payed 300 for one night! Even before I. Entered the room I wanted a refund. Guys keep searching!

A downtown motor inn with free parking that is within walking distance to cable car route, local restaurants and bars. The rooms have been updated and it seems that the exterior is in the process - railings are being painted, room doors definitely need it. This is a motor inn with free parking, that is hard to come by in the city. The rooms are average size, not much room to maneuver around the beds but sufficient for a short stay.
Other reviews (and maybe the website?) said they offer a continental breakfast, but we were told No by the guy working at the front desk, who couldn't tell us where the nearest coffee shop was, since the restaurant adjacent to the inn didn't open until 7:30. 
There is a Starbucks one block down Van Ness, on Polk (take a left)

review_title: Old and tired in unsafe area.
review_text: Stayed in this hotel for one night while in San Fran on business. The hotel looks ok in the lobby but all other areas of the hotel are in major need of an update. The corridor areas smell damp and the rooms for what is supposed to be a 4star hotel are very poor. The bathrooms look like they have not be done up in 30years and there is no mini bar or even tea and coffee making facility. The worst thing about the hotel though is the area which is unsafe especially at night. Would never stay here again, truly terrible.

My husband and I stayed here in September for our honeymoon as part of a 3 week trip of the states. 
The reception area and bar are beautiful with wonderfully helpful staff. The lady concierge was extremely knowledgeable and funny. On her advice we found a jazz club called Biscuits and Blues and had a great night.
I acknowledge that the rooms are by no means "plush" but I think they are full of character and 100% value for money. 
The area is in the tenderloin district, which is not a fancy area but the transport links are outstanding! The metro and tram stop directly out of the front door, and I recommend making full use of them. They are so cheap and efficient. Purchase a travel card from the tourist centre nearby and it will save you a fortune.
Yes there are a lot of homeless people but a polite "no" when being asked for money was often greeted with a "thanks, have a nice day".
There is a cafe across the road that we had breakfast in everyday. I can't remember what it is called (its directly aross the road from the hotel and on the left) but it looks like you would never want to eat there, but you should. The staff were helpful and it is where the local builders eat!
All in all I would say this is a great hotel, great location and great value for money.

It's a shame the way "Hawey" front desk staff treats customers, rude, disrespectful.
This guy, treated us very disrespectful and rude when I was trying to get a second room key. The way he was asking us what we needed was very rude. 
I had to asked him to stop talking to us that way.
Tipically, his answer was "sir.. I'm trying to help you" to which I answered, yes but you don't have to talked to us in that sarcastic and rudely tone. 
He finally gave us an extra key. Without activating it.
When we came back to the lobby. Another front desk staff helped us. This guy Hawey came back to the lobby asking the other employee with a sarcastic smile." what happened? It didnt work? Walking away without apologizing. 
Obviously They don't know what the term "Customer Service Mean"

Old. Poorly maintained stairs to room. No amenities. Pricey for what you get. Parking spots are ruled so narrow that cars barely fit. Staff has little or no knowledge of the city. No way I would stay here again.

The staff of this hotel is more or less friendly, but the hotel is seriously lacking basic hygiene standards. The hallways smell mouldy and are covered by carpets that should have been renewed ages ago. The carpet in our room was the same: greasy and dirty, a haven for microbes! Behind the bed there were towers of dust. The grossest thing of all was the bathroom however: a rusty bathtub, cracks in the walls and ceiling, mould and filth everywhere!
This hotel claims to be a sophisticated and clean place, and it charges according fees, but it is in fact disgusting, dilapidated and fails to meet the most basic of hygiene standards. I stay at simple two star motels all the time, but none of them ever were as off-putting as the Whitcomb.
I wouldn't recommend the Whitcomb to anybody and wouldn't stay here again even if they paid me $100 a night!

Since British Airways has this hotel at the top of the recommended hotels list, it was to be experinenced. BART from and to SFO International was $11 per person one way.
Check in was rapid and friendly, just take care to put your valuables to the safe at reception - no room safe boxes. And prepare to wait to access the safe at certain times.
Housekeeping was perfect, the beds and linen clean and comfortable. 8 pillows per sleeper! AC units were old style, every room had their own, and rather noisy but efficient.
Hotel appeared safe despite of the wandering street people around the neighbourhood.
The hotel restaurant had very expensive breakfast prices - as well as the across street diners - $50 was barely enough for two people. Price difference with equally conveniently located Hilton or Hyatt was thinning off quikly during our stay of one week.
Subway across the street is open 24/7 and offers nitebites for the hungry party animals heading back to the hotel.
And do get yourself the 3 or 7 day MUNI pass to travel around - $26 for the 7 day pass is a bargain. Those are available at 5'th and Market, the SFO Tourist Info Office.
All in all, a pleasant stay!

review_title: In the center of everything for cheap!
review_text: Although the room wa not te most spacious, and we got attacked by mosquiotos, it was in the epicenter of SF! We were able to walk to union square, Chinatown, little Italy, and fisherman's wharf(if your up for a 20 min walk)!!

review_title: Beautiful hotel in the heart of SF.
review_text: Wonderful service and staff. I highly recommend this hotel if you are staying in SF and want an authentic 1920s SF experience.

review_title: Easy to get around , affordable, comfy pillows
review_text: Harvey at front desk made our stay the most pleasurable and Keith is an excellent bartender.
We stayed here so that we could join the holiday fun on union square- the price is really reasonable- location is great- rooms are a little small but clean and comfy.

review_title: Appalling flea-bag in a sketchy neighborhood.
review_text:
We booked the hotel based on the location convenience to BART and Powell Street. Big mistake. While the hotel receptionist was pleasant and helpful in checking us in early, we got stuck with a smoking room (which I specifically did not order) because all other rooms were booked. Turns out, the room was also located smack dab over a very loud night club playing dance music at full volume until 3 am (room 202). The supposedly recently renovated rooms are dingy with torn curtains and a cheap coat of paint applied over clearly patched 
walls. The sink & tub were cracked and damaged, the carpet stained in numerous places, the furniture chipped and worn and the "street scene" is typical of the Tenderloin's sleazy rep. Since we were only giving up frequent flier miles, we got another cleaner hotel in Oakland(!?!) so we could get a good night's sleep. If all you care about is location or low cost (by SF standards), then stay by all means, but as the film Midnght in Paris points out, cheap is cheap...

review_title: Good hotel. Location is not great
review_text:
Clean.
Nice staff.
Big old hotel.
Good value
Not a great location.
Room on end of corridor was noisy due to close proximity to elevator and ice/vending machine.

This Hotel reminds me of a lot of hotels and small/cheap hotels geared at young people in Europe. It's not exactly in a good part of town, but SoMa is in the beginnings of a revival and this hotel is a good representation of that. I stayed in a queen room in the main building on the 2nd floor. The service is great, rooms are as clean as you would expect for a 3-star hotel, and the overall feel is young and unpretentious. 3 bikes are available for free from the front desk. The attached Sidebar restaurant/bar is convenient but closes pretty early.

review_title: Didn't really see a strong Eco friendly push even though that is the premise of their brand.
review_text: Not in a great area but quaint. Rooms were small but standard for San Fran. No amenities. No breakfast or lunch available. Probably would not stay again.

review_title: Worth the discounted value (but not the actual retail value)
review_text:
Pros 
- great proximity to union square. Straight bus from union sq to the wharf and pier areas. 
- breakfast is free; but no warm food
Cons
- location might be a bit dodgy; try not to go west of he hotel. Everything on the east (towards union sq) is okay
- room kinda reminded me of my apartment in my poor undergrad days in Boston. Lil bit dingy but livable once you get used to it. 
Overall: try to understand that most hotels in e area are really expensive so you won't have much of a choice. For the money that you pay, you get decent accommodation. Dont expect the Hilton (which is just a block away) and you won't be disappointed.

The hotel is located in a very busy intersection. But also it is right next to presidio park and the golden gate bridge. Public transport is ok, within 20 minutes your at fishermans wharf with a trolley bus. The room is decent and the owner is step by step investing. We had an new mattress and motion activated lights. But some defects such as a shower that didn't keep the temperature, heater that smelled terrible and bed linnen that did not fit the bed size. Oh yes, and a refrigerator that was a freezer. It costed us all our fresh food. :)

review_title: Don't get tricked by booking this hotel - bed bugs!
review_text: Hi, we stayed here for 2 nights. We overpaid due to being in San Fran on busy weekend. Paper thin walls and ceiling. I've never experienced bed bugs before but now have itchy red bites on my arms, legs and torso so I'm guessing they are bed bugs!

The day we arrived we took the elevator and got trapped. When they finally got us out they told us it was because we were 8 people even the elevator had a sign of limit of 12.
At least my room smelled a little to feet
One of my friends got some kind of rash we think he got bed bugs, kindly the manager offer to pay for medication. Still that was really gross

Location is the best!! For the price it was the best we could find

So I move to a new room, the next morning I notice I have a bunch of bites over me so I go to the front and tell them and they were very rude about the situation. Didn't want to give me my money back and just ignored the problem. I leave the next day coming home to Florida and the bites are getting worse. So I go to my doctor who tells me I have scabies:( this is from staying in a dirty hotel(Monarch) which now I am suffering with bites all over my body and face. I am depressed and highly upset about this it will now take a least a month for everything to go away and be back normal hopefully. Please do not waste your time and money staying there u will regret it!!!.

I would never stay at this hotel again!!! The service was horrible, not friendly at all. The room was small and the smell was awful. I got maybe 2 hours of sleep due to the noises outside and people talking outside and in their rooms ( we were on the 6 floor ). In the middle of the night, I smelled cigarette smoke in my room. The floors were squeaky and I heard the people next to me flush their toilet. The beds were very uncomfortable and the pillows were very flat. There were bums outside the hotel. When I checked out, a lady was complaining that there were bugs in her room!!!!! To me, this hotel is not even worth paying $80 for.

review_title: Comfortable place to sleep when up for an event
review_text: We arrived and parked in a pay lot around the corner on O'Farrell for $20 overnite. We planned to walk till we left so that was fine. Waited a Few minutes till mgr arrived (pkg a car?) and he was friendly enough. The first room we were given had not been cleaned so we called down and got another across the hall, 608, 2 doors from elevator was fine. We heard another guest request a different room away from the elevator, which was typical for this era of hotel, slow, clunky, noisy and not level. But it worked. It was unseasonably warm, so we left windows open all night and were not awakened by noise. Overhead fan was helpful. No bedbugs detected or felt. We come to SF often to go to symphony so like to be able to park and walk and this worked for us. Extremely busy wkend with marathon and we paid $117 including all tax thru booking.com and this was very reasonable for the season. We would return for a quick overnite again.

review_title: Fantastic service for a great price!
review_text:
I stayed at Hotel Whitcomb over NYE and was shocked when I walked into my very clean, large room with queen bed! For $69 online! It was luxury after a long hall flight. The staff were happy to help with maps, bags and new keys when they stopped working.
It is easy to walk from the hotel down Market St to Union Square or catch a trolley car right out front.
At the end of my stay my flight was cancelled. The staff at Hotel Whitcomb accomodated me at the sane low price and calmed me in a time of distress.
A great place to base yourself when in San Francisco

review_title: A little gem in San Fran!!
review_text:
After reading the reviews we were slightly worried but honestly it is fine. We liked the quirky hotel. Very close (5mins) the Powell street train station which you can get to directly on the BART from the airport $8.10 each way and 30mins. The room is basic but we had a reasonable sized room, comfortable bed, fridge, bath/shower, towels and clean. The front desk staff are so nice and very helpful. We had breakfast on a morning which made us laugh the first day of 3. Breakfast is an orange, doughnut, squeezey yogurt and hot drink, not the breakfast of champions but filled a hole! 
Downsides - there are quite a lot of homeless people near the hotel but they don't bother you if you don't bother them, we always felt safe. To be honest San Francisco has a very high homeless rate, much more than we expected. Also the windows as single glazed so it can be a little noisy through the night. 
Positives - great location for getting to and from the airport, clean and tidy rooms with everything you need, 5 mins walk from the start of the Powell tram station ($6 single or you can get a day pass $14 which includes buses and underground too) shopping centre 5 mins walk, lots to do in the main street. 
We walked from the hotel up through china town, great, through little Italy, up telegraph hill fab views over San Francisco then over to Lombard street and finally down to Fishermans wharf which is brilliant and lots to do. We caught the tram back. The walk took approx 2.5 hrs with stops but so worth it and you can stop off along the way. 
Highly recommend Alcatraz and book early at pier 33. Pier 39 is great for viewing and kids and there are seals in the water. 
Any way overall we liked the hotel, more than we thought. Just walk around the homeless and you will be fine and dandy. Great if you're on a budget and traveling around 
Finally it's very easy to get to Candlestick park for the football from this location!
Cool old building loved elevator. But it is the tenderloin remember. Steps away from everything

We stayed at the Comfort Inn by the Bay for just one night and it was exactly what we needed. Clean room, nice hot shower, wifi, free breakfast, car park and the location was great. Would recommend to all.

Eravamo preparati ad un salasso arriavando a SF nel weekend... e invece questo hotel e' stato una piacevole sorpresa! Servizio cortese, ottima posizione per esplorare il centro, parcheggio gratuito (considerati i prezzi dei parking di SF e' una caratteristica quasi unica!) e camere (e bagni) ampie e molto pulite! In effetti alcune stanze possono risultare un po' rumorose, ma e' un inconveniente parzialmente superabile chiedendo una stanza che non affacci sulla Van Ness!

The service is absolutley horrible I watched a tour bus pull up.... about 40 senior citizens got out no one there to help them with their bags or the door so I stood there for 30 min and helped them ...after I went to the desk and they told me it wasn't their job ...[--] pathetic

review_title: There are better hotels for this price
review_text:
After checking in at Bay Landing($159+tax) on our first night in SF and at Westin market street($169+tax) on the second night, our hotel expectations were pretty high so we were disappointed when we checked in at comfort inn - which actually cost more than the first two hotels at $189+taxes. I booked these hotels online so I figured the location must be the reason for the high rate but Westin has a better neighborhood than this and a few minutes walk to embarcadero
Here are other gripes:
1. One of the front desk clerk was curt and unfriendly when we were asking if we could deposit our bags early, enough to make me want to cancel my reservation, unfortunately I would have forfeited the fee for the first night so we just let it go (FYI at bay landing they let us leave our bulky luggage in their storage room while we explored the city)
2. Price for the room is not worth it even with the free breakfast and free wifi. Definitely not worth the $200 total I paid online - I have yet to see if the safety deposit box fee is true when I check out later
3. Smell of the room is what greets you when you first come. It smells of old cabs with damp carpets. They need to recarpet the room and change the AC. It's 5am now as i write this and I can't sleep because of this smell - can't wait to check out of here.
Will not stay here again

review_text:

Having never been to San Francisco I was worried about where to stay. This turned out to be a very good location in a wonderful neighborhood. The prices were good for the rooms. Although not very big, the room was very clean, the service was good and there was breakfast as well. Good pick.
This hotel does not provide guest with parking lot. And the china security guy is rude and has problem articulating his thoughts. Overall very poor service. DO NOT RECOMMEND ANYONE TO STAY HERE

I'm sure there are better hotels in san fran. They have no microwaves the fitness room is small and has a broke thread mill. Plus lots of homeless at night and police station right around the corner stops u from sleeping well
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway

review_text: Simple and old hotel! Lot of history, beatiful and chique corridors and rooms. Very clean. Low pressure on the water, windows not in the best shape, no ice buckets avaiable! The location is awesome!

Wifi was advertised as complimentary yet reception wanted to charge me $10 per day. We ordered a junior suite which supposedly had more space and a seating area....well we def had the extra space...an extra room in fact but no additional seating area as expected. Ice machine did not work. The fans in the room where phantom fans, as their lights went on and off on their own while we were trying to sleep and we had to turn them off completely. The room, however was newly furnished.

review_title: Great value, have reasonable expectations before you arrive.
review_text:
This is a very large Holiday Inn by comparison and therefor you can receive a great deal. For the time of year I was in San Fran the rate I got was very good. 
The rooms are clean and functional. The bathroom was not great but surprisingly a good size. I found the staff friendly and helpful. There seemed to be a lot of security to access the parking garage and therefor you had to carry your room key with you EVERYWHERE you went. 
My only true criticism was the EXTREME noise produced by the ac unit in my room. Thank goodness the weather in SF is very mild and there is very rarely a need for the ac to be constantly blowing. 
I would stay again for the value.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway

review_title: Great location but not so great service and very old furniture.
review_text: Stayed here for 5 nights for the Nike Women's Marathon. The room was in bad repair. One of the beds constantly creaked and the desk drawer was broken. The carpeting was absolutely disgusting! Having stayed at other Holiday Inn locations, I was very surprised. They need to update this location. The restaurant looked dark and uninviting so we never ate there. Basically, the only good thing was the view and the location. Oh and don't expect the guest services to call cabs for you as they may tell you what they told me, just go on the street in front of the hotel and get the cab!
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway

review_title: No A/C, not worth the money
review_text: The rooms have no A/C and the rooms smelled very musty. Being that they have no A/C you must sleep with the sliding glass door open where everyone that walks your room can see you and of course it can be very noisy because doors are open. Service was slow but our bell man was very good. Would not recommend this hotel. Not worth $197.00 per night at all.

review_title: Nice hotel but very expensive parking
review_text:
We were booked here as part of a fly drive tour therefore had a car with us. We didn't need the car to get around in San Gransico so parked it up in the hotel car park which was a total rip off. We had to pay $38 per day plus tax therefore our two night stay cost us over $85 even though we arrived in the afternoon on our arrival day and left very early on our check out. The discount for guests was next to nothing compared to none resident parkers. 
That said the hotel location was very good-local transport straight outside and the Van Ness/California cable car stop on the corner so excellent for getting around. The room was clean and looked very nice (obviously a newer room having read some previous reviews). The fridge in the room was a bit loud but ear plugs blocked that out. 
The gift shop assistant was lovely-very helpful and friendly. Make sure you go to her for a free map and guide advice when buying the MUNI pass. 
Overall-would not go back with a car, but without the parking fee, would recommend.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway

review_title: Generally good but wasn't happy with maintenance
review_text: This hotel felt more like a boutique hotel than a Best Western - I think that's a good thing. Love the fact that it's in an old restored building with lovely windows and a temperamental elevator - I recommend the stairs. Reasonable breakfast included. Arriving jet lagged from Australia I wasn't thrilled to have a toilet that didn't flush but could get it to work by sticking my hand in the water down the back and pulling the broken bit up. I reported it first thing the next morning. Was shocked when I returned the next evening and it still hadn't been fixed. "Sorry, it was on the list but the maintenance man didn't get to it." You are joking. Makes you wonder what else was on the list if a non - flushing toilet doesn't make the cut. My only option was to switch to another room. So I did

review_title: Great Service from Front Desk Employee, Ken
review_text:
After a long flight from the east coast, I was greeted by the front desk employee named Ken. It was the best service I've ever received at a hotel. 
Unprompted Ken offered advice for what to see, where to eat (affordably), and even directions for how to get to my afternoon meeting, even leaving me with a map!
Great employee at a great place!
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway

review_text: Forse un pÃ² scarno ed essenziale, ma a parte la colazione c'Ã¨ tutto e il prezzo Ã¨ ottimo e le camere sono pulite. Ottima l'ubicazione, a 10 minuti a piedi da Union Square. Alla reception sono un po` sgorbutici... il parcheggio si paga a parte, 7 dollari a notte. L'auto la parcheggiano loro per voi. Detto ciÃ² Ã¨ un albergo nel quale tornerei sicuramente per un uso solo dormire come Ã¨ stato il nostro.

Luxury boutique hotel? Duluxe room? On what planet???!!! Seriously shocked that they can get away with charging more than 70 bucks a night, let alone $190!!! the only good thing was its a comfortable bed with nice linens. Otherwise waaay out of line on price, totally low class (the dirty pool is surrounded by astroturph and i have seen college dorms that look nicer) and they couldnt pay me to reccommend this hotel to anyone. Not good

The rooms are very old. Could not tolerate the smell in the elevators, they always have excuses for your requests. The staff do not care for your inquires about the city of SF. High value of mony to provided services. Any way the location is great if you want a good access to SF.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway

review_title: Not a family friendly hotel. Very noisy during the night.
review_text: This hotel is far from friendly and welcoming. We were given a room near the pool as we has children. Sadly that is also the smokers area and the room stank. The noise during the night was awful. When I mentioned it to reception staff they said there was nothing they could do and I should have mentioned it at the time - what, get the children out of bed and pack up our things to move to another room? Don't think so. No effort made to make amends and reception had the most patronising of attitudes. Car parking is also the most expensive in the entire area. All in all, a very unpleasant experience.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway

review_text: ....small scruffy room, seedy foyers and decor, noise, staff that were useless until we checked out early, expensive parking, and a very unhappy wife! - who booked it incidentally!

I stayed here for work and was pretty dissapointed. Whatever you do don't do business with the gift shop they won't return anything for a refund and the one ladies is very rude its like dealing with shady people on the street. The hotel allows them to rent that space from them and they shouldn't . Breakfast buffet isn't a great selection and they don't have a brunch. The bathroom was run down and windows dirty in the bedroom. San fran has so many options chooses a different one
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway

review_text:
I booked La Luna earlier this monto because the city was booked solid for numerous conventions and I needed to be within the city limits for work. 
The room was reasonably clean, I found parking both nights, and service was helpful, but the street noise was crazy loud and the pillows were all rock hard. Good location though.

We spent two nights here in August, we had a car and this meant that this hotel was perfect for us, we were very close to pier 33 for our Alcatraz tour, we headed back to the room after and then headed towards union square, the hotel is on Lombard so keep driving and you get to the long windy road!
The golden gate bridge is convenient from here too!
A clean and friendly hotel with a nice set of shops, delis and 
restaurants on nearby roads! Made our stay very pleasant, would stay again!

review_title: Not a place I would stay at again
review_text: I think the bed was the only nice thing about it. The elevator never seemed to work. There were all of 5 tv channels to watch and the bathroom was blah. The toilet made me think I was in some public restroom and the towels were made for a 6 year old

It was a great location and I got the room for $100. I thoroughly enjoyed the stay for the money. If I had payed the $190 normal price my review would have been different. Overall I seriously enjoyed my time.
The only complaint was the absolute rip off restaurant. The breakfast was about $16 for some sub par food. If they get their breakfast down to a decent price I would thoroughly re coment staying there
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway

review_text: Literally, the wallpaper was peeling off the walls in my room, mold on the exterior facing wall, the windows looked like they had not been washed in ages and they didn't seal tightly so they whistled....I can go on...I'm staying her this minute and can here the person in the bathtub next door...every little squeak and splash ... What an absolute DUMP... Id leave now but the whole area is booked solid for the marathon tomorrow. Spare yourself
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Golden Gateway

review_text: The motel is well located but the breakfast was really poor, just coffee, juice and greasy snacks. The owner made us feel under control during the breakfast. In particular she didn't allow us to bring two trays in our room with the breakfast, explaining us that she didn't have enough trays for the rest of the motel guests. You can feel the stinginess of the owner noticing the old fashioned furnitures of the room and the shabby aspect of the bad linen, however the room was clean.
Staff are rude. Location is full of criminals. Room noisy. Parking pathetic.

We stayed here for three nights, having booked ahead to ensure somewhere to sleep for the nights in Sf. On arrival, the reception staff seemed ill at ease and really uncertain of how to welcome us. As a matter of fact we learned more from the parking lot attendant, Gilbert who was great with city info. The rooms are nice, very modern, but 
on day three of our stay it looked as though our room hadn't been serviced at all, an unfinished cup of coffee I'd been drinking was left, sheets on bed were not changed, a used drinking glass was exactly where my husband left it. As we booked this room in a hurry, we didn't get time to read the trip advisor reviews, we probably would have booked elsewhere if we had. We ventured out for a walk ( on our first night) blissfully unaware of how the area was swarming with poor unfortunates. We didn't walk far, believe me. We also asked the lobby staff for info on how to get to the nearest cinema and she didn't have a clue, and was more interested in talking to the maintenance guy on her walkie talkie as a get out clause. All in all I give this best western one star out of five.

review_title: Excellent location but that's about it
review_text:
Location is excellent, no doubt about it. The hotel is quite old, they should change the carpets, and they should give complementary bottled water inside our rooms. No amenities too such as toothbrush and combs.
I know I maybe nit-picking but I have been to too many SPG hotels and unfortunately except the location, this is not the place to stay.
I wanted to go to gym and they wanted to charge me, so I decided not to go simply I have never paid to go to the gym as hotel guest. So, I might have to say that this is going to be my first and only stay at Westin St. Francis.

Went here for a cocktail to check out the Westin for our next trip to SFO. The male bartender the evening of Dec 29 was arrogant and rude to us and the people next to us. I complimented him on the drink he made for me and he made a surly remark. Then he proceeded to insult one of the other staff and then asked our bar stool neighbors to put away their cell phone because they were distracting other guests which they were not. Not a very good impression to portray to both guests and potential guests.

Not the fault of the hotel or it's management, but people are jerks--they hold loud conversations in corridors during "quiet hours". The layout of the hotel is such that you hear all these inconsiderate @**holes in your room. Do NOT stay here if you value your sleep.

Boutique style. Cute rooms. Proximity to neighbor makes you able to hear when they come and go. Location is not very central to tourist areas. Hotel lacks air conditioning and the only window that opens, only opens 3 or so inches. The cool air was great but the noisy street blow provided a night of broken sleep.

review_title: Nice hotel, friendly and very helpful staff, pretty central but bad area.
review_text:
We stayed at this hotel for 4 nights during a recent trip to America. It's a lovely wee hotel, rooms are basic, especially the bathrooms, however they are clean. Staff are excellent and very helpful. Hotel is fairly central, easy to walk to shops and union square. 
Really not impressed with the area though. Seemed to be worse during the day than night but I have never seen anywhere with that amount of homeless drunks in any city ever. Real shame as really let's this hotel down and even the city.

Sloppy hallways, carpets dirty, trash left outside rooms for days!
Visited for Christmas and should have spent a few bucks more for the Ritz or Four Seasons. Unless $50 more a night is a real necessity, steer clear!!! Great value but beware
Excellent location on Union square. Tbe hotel is huge. You want to be in the new tower, where the rooms are modern and nicer.availability of multiple conference and meeting rooms.

Ideal location for Union Square and one of the cheapest. Rooms are small but adequate and quiet and clean. reasonable mini-bar prices and free continental breakfast. Great bar attached with cheap prices and free hotdogs. Would stay again.

review_title: Superb location and impressive history, just a couple of seemingly easy details missed which left a bad impression
review_text: We had a week long stay on "points plus cash" which was a very good deal. We were upgraded to a superior room on the 27th floor with a view of Union Square and could see lots more especially whilst riding the lifts in the newer tower part which are glass and face the Square. Service and amenities in the hotel are good, except for the gym which desperately needs to be redesigned - simply moving the weights to the upper level and leaving the current weights area for stretching only would would solve the very awkward current layout. The single most annoying thing during our whole stay was something seemingly simple to solve - one night, someone had left some trash and a wine glass at the reception area on our floor just in front of the lifts. Unfortunately, these items were not only left there overnight but also for the entire next day! Further, even after I told the front desk about it, it took another 12 hours before someone bothered to clean it up. It literally would have taken them two minutes, and it is hard to understand how both housekeeping and room service could silly walk past and not clean it up. The hotel should have someone go from floor to floor simply checking for these type messes and clean them up, clearly this would be worthwhile because this incident has left a very bad impression with me and likely many others.

Had a very pleasant experience. :)
Was very impress with the way they pulled off making an older building looking fresh and fun.

We decided to stay at this motel because of the price and location. Checking in/out was smooth, rooms were clean although we are not fussy travelers. This is a two star hotel and it is exactly what we paid for, nothing more.

review_title: Charming hotel in a great location
review_text: Loved this place. A really lively lobby and fantastic concierge (bearded chap at the front entrance). Would definitely stay again.

review_title: Decient hotel, kinda seedy area but convenient location.
review_text: We stayed 1 week total. Very convenient location right in the middle of walking distance where we needed to be. That's what really helped us choose this place over others & super sweet decor pictures ! Staff was great upon arrival. Resturant was ok lil pricey. Bar was ok, hotel bar pretty common. Our 3rd day we had a friend visit for a few hours in the afternoon. He used the hotel parking, we went to our convention came back he paid for parking & left. The next day I was charged $40 for his few hours of parking. After debating with a few hotel staff & personally calling my friend who had paid for his parking to verify, the charges where taken back off. On our last few days there, I started to get a strange rash. I came home seen my Dr. He said it was bed bug bites. Big cities like San Fran are known to be notorious. It all went away within a week of trying not to itch. Lotsa benadril. Thank god we didn't bring any home. The walls where pretty thin so you can hear the others around you.(all night long) I was on 2nd floor by elevator. My hubby loved it. I wasn't thrilled coulda been better but also coulda been way worse lol. Great location most of the staff was great housekeeping super nice decient prices.

My friends usually books their rooms during the Southwest Chinese New Years parade. The trick is to find out what month and day the parade is and also what animal is the year of. Book a room face Powell street lower level as possible so you don't have squinting eyes afterwards. This way you get a room with birdseyes view for parade and moneys worth. Another option is too grab a table at macys cheesecake factory facing geary street. Now you must be there at least 5pm just to have a good view from above. Both location is good but I prefer macys because KTVU Channel 2 is right there in front doing the air broadcasting for local tv programs.

review_title: UbicaciÃ³n inmejorable, buen precio, algo justo en detalles
review_text: Aunque la situaciÃ³n, la atenciÃ³n y limpieza son excelentes, falta pulir algunos detalles. Las ventanas filtraban aire ( con el frio q pasamos en pleno agosto se notaba mas). Aunque habia agua caliente, costaba muchisimo regularla y la ventana del baÃ±o no cerraba bien. A parte de estos detalles, solo le encuentro a faltar un pequeÃ±o desayuno. El hotel esta casi perfecto, lo recomiendo!!
Ideal location makes this place a no brainier. I was with the family and everyone was comfortable. Lobby is always busy. Only complaint is the $35 charge for the rollaway bed.

review_title: Excellent place to stay for the value.
review_text: My wife an I stayed here while traveling the west coast for only one night. The AAA cost was just under a $100. We had a rental car so I paid an additional $25 to have it valeted. The rooms are a little on the small side but plenty big for my wife and I. It was very clean and comfortable. The location was great. We walked all over the downtown and rode the trolleys around too. There were many many different places to eat and drink within a short walk. The bar downstairs is very quaint too. Would definately stay here again.

review_title: Do not stay here if you want to sleep at night!
review_text:
This hotel(??) is TERRIBLE.
No customer service whatsoever.
The rooms are SO small but you will be out all day so doesn't matter so much but just be warned.
They have the noisest heater in the room and we asked to switch ours off but it's automatic for whole hotel so we couldn't turn it off. I had to take Valium to get sleep!!!! Everything is so run down too.
Good location. Terrible hotel.

We stayed for 9 nights, and overall we were quite pleased! Staff were friendly and helpful, and very welcoming! 
Room was small but very functional! Ensuite was basic, but clean. The rooms are cleaned daily, and although the room is basic and not decorated very well, we were pleasantly surprised! 
There is a drinks vending machine in the lobby, as well as an ice machine. Water is also purchasable from staff. 
The bed was okay, albeit a little soft for our taste, and there was extra pillows. The sheets were clean and well kept.
Couple of bad points though. No aircon was a pain, as it got very warm in a small room like that. Wifi is included, but didn't work very well (but when it did, was helpful to plan out our itinery). Walls and floors are thin! Our upstairs neighbours were.. Um.. Quite active and we got a full sound show when they were at their most active! Thankfully, didn't last very long ;)
Overall, a good hotel for the cheap price we paid, and the pro's far out weigh the cons! As long as you go with the attitude of 'budget' in mind, you'll do well!
This is one of the best hotels for travelers in a budget and lone wolfs. The Grant Plaza has excellent locations allowing for anyone to easily know San Francisco
I stay here when ever my husband has to be in the hospital. UCSF and St Mary's Medical Center are both with in walking distance. Staff is very friendly and helpful.

review_title: Great location clean and tidy, nice people good value
review_text:
We stayed for 5 nights and would happily go back again. We read the reviews before picking Grant Plaza they were varied between good and awful. Our conclusion is a lot is down to expectations a personal view. If you want a clean budget hotel in a great location which is clean and well run then it will be great. if you want lots of power outlets a large room with modern high class fittings then pay more as the Grant Plaza will only disappoint!
Again we wanted clean, inexpensive and a central location, had no intention on spending much time in the room as there are so many site to see, also we are not TV watchers

review_title: Belle camere, vicino al centro ma in zona brutta
review_text: L'hotel ci ha colpito per le sue contraddizioni: Ã© un bell'albergo, stanze stile inglese, ben arredato a 100 metri circa dall'info point e dalla partenza delle cable car con parcheggio nel retro (anche se costoso). review_title: Old hotel - not what I expected from a Westin hotel.
review_text: The location of this hotel in the middle of SF and on Union Square is excellent. The rest is not. The hotel is really big and old, but does not have much charm. The location is noisy and the rooms are not very well sound isolated. The beds are modern, comfortable bed as you find in other Westin, but the rest of the room was old and shabby.

Not money well-spent. One of the worst "high-end" hotels I've stayed at. Room walls paper thin. Hotel layout confusing. Poor dining options and in the most touristy unappealing part of SF.

We enjoy the stay
The location is perfect the staff very helpful, specially the morning lady who help us in many ways!
Everything is close by. Try to get rooms on the back, while they can be smaller they are quieter 
Enjoy!

review_title: You get what you pay for !
review_text: The hotel is not the greatest it's a very small boutique hotel with very small rooms but quite clean. San Fran can be expensive so this is one of the cheapest it's among alot of things but the area is quite rough at night and can be through the day but mostly at night. I couldn't stay here a week the rooms are to small but you know Its cheap

review_title: Redelijk hotel net buiten het centrum
review_text: Op zich prima hotel. Kamers zijn niet heel groot maar alles is aanwezig; douche, wc, wastafel, tv, koffie/thee zetter. Lakens en baddoeken zijn schoon. Je zit in de stad, je hoort dus het verkeer en of af en toe een brandweer langs loeien. Ook hoor je wel eens iets van de buren. Parkeren kost 20 dollar per dag en zit niet bij de prijs inbegrepen. Je auto staat dan wel met bewaking geparkeerd. Hotel maakt een schone indruk. Naast de lobby zit een hamburger rest. en bar waar je drankjes kunt bestellen. Locatie is ok, je zit op 5 min. van Union Square. Er zijn wel behoorlijk wat zwevers op straat, maar dat is in de hele stad valt ons op. We vinden het niet echt veilig 's avonds.. Maar dag geldt dus niet alleen voor de omgeving van dit hotel. Bediening/personeel is wat stug.

Have to say was alittle nervous about hotel from reading reviews, however upon arrival these went away!! The location is excellent right next to the BART line, Westfield shopping centre and 3 min walk from union square. Hotel staff was fantastic very helpful and nice, hotel room was clean and nice. Unfortunately homelessness is a huge problem in San fran so were ever u go u will meet them. Was never harassed by any homeless people at hotel. If anything the hotel area has the same amount of homeless people as any area of the city. Would highly recommend this hotel and would stay again!!!

We stayed here 3 nights and it was the first hotel of our vacation so we were hoping for a good sleep to recover from jet lag. But it was far from being a good welcome! We arrived at 10 pm and the first thing we saw was a shopping cart loaded with rags parked in front of the entrance door and several homeless arguing at the corner. Before arriving I had sent an email asking for a quiet room and for some help to organise a birthday surprise for my daugther:neither requests were fulfilled and the lady who opened the email did not even bother replying. In fact our room faced the street and the view was very bleak: homeless everywhere and people yelling unti 3 am.Â 
For the sake of truth, I must say that we were never approached by any beggar so the neighborhood might not be that dangerous, yet we felt uncomfortable, especially at night. When I asked for a room change, the receptionist informed me that all rooms with 2 double beds were on the street side (that is why she did not replay to my email...).
Beds were quite soft and sheets and blankets had several holes. The themed room just consisted of 5 black and white photos of old cinema and actors. The bathroom looked very tired, the sink had Â even some cracks and the wall were so thin that I could understand every word our neighbors said.
After a poor sleep, we were ready for the next disappointing surprise: breakfast! The choices were very limited: wholegrain sliced bread, bagel or waffle (none of them was fresh). The fruit selection consisted of red apples and bananas. You could help yourself with coffee but toÂ make tea, you needed to heat water in the microwave.Â 
The only good point is that this hotel is one minute to Market&Powell (by the way, the WEstfield shopping mall has a great food court, so bear it in mind if you are looking for a quick and cheap meal).

Check-in was hassle free. Staff tried to answer all questions and was helpful. Lobby and rooms are appointed nicely. Clean room and bathrooms; fairly updated rooms. Negative: someone caused a "prank" fre alarm while I was there, in the middle of the night, which forced everyone outside. It took about 30 minutes before we were back in our rooms. Also, at night, there are homeless people and others; the midnight atmosphere is not very safe. However, during the day, this hotel is central to transit and many sights. Overall, I would stay here again and simply ensure not to walk around the neighborhood alone in the middle of the night. Also: Movie buffs may like this hotel; each room is named for, and has still photos of, a classic movie.

If you are coming from the airport(SFO)by train then this is the hotel for you! ,it is so close to the train station and tram stop which is fantastic.the staff are very nice and helpful,the rooms are very clean and large.the only thing that may put people off is the amount of homeless people around the area but I did NOT have any problems while staying in the area.the shower is good but they need brighter lights in the bathroom....very dull/dark.the beds are very firm which I loved but the pillows are too soft for me.there is a burger king,post office,wallgreens and subway ALL ONE BLOCK from the hotel......FANTASTIC!!!!!
The hotel is close to market street, and bart is one block away. Very close to food, and the theater... great place to stay if your heading to or coming back from SFO.

We had a nice 11 th floor room. Watch for proximity to lifts as they are very noisy at night. Desk staff attentive and helpful. Location is around 15-20mins walk to a decent part of the city. We concur with other reviewers regarding a large number of homeless in this area. We did not leave the hotel at night on foot! Poor form in bar where we overheard waitress complaining to a customer about another customers lack of tips. She would do well to remember that many countries don't tip as a custom liken USA. When we heard that comment, we didn't tip either!

review_title: The Westin is a great historic hotel with the best location in San Francisco.
review_text:
The service was great from the moment we arrived at the airport. We were immediately greeted by the staff who helped us to our room. We had a room on te 28th floor with great views of the city. The location is excellent right at heart of union square. You can access everything you want by cable car or bus. Parking is quite pricey at 50 dollars a night. The hotel itself is a good blend of historic charm and modern amenities but don't expect things like breakfast or a pool. 
The staff was prompt and friendly for room service, valet, and concierge. Ms. Marichu Alvarez was a great ambassador for the Westin and made us feel right at home for our week long stay.

Marichu Alvarez is a terrific hostess! We were greated with such warmth and professionalism. Also we had Joy check us in at the front and she was equally professional and nice. Your staff knows how to show customer service with a smile! Good job!

review_title: The queen of hotels has seen better days.
review_text: Checked in for a Salesforce conference. Location is outstanding and the history of this hotel fascinating. But after that it goes down hill. The rooms while comfortable and bedding as always a delight, were worn and at best blah. Check in was efficient and the bar quite fascinating. Hallways were dirty and my overall impression is this place needs a work over.

The air conditioning in our room was broken during our stay--it took two calls down to the front desk to get anything done. Finally, two hours later they fixed it.half the lights did not work in our room either. The bourbon steakhouse at the Weston sucks too one of the waiters punched me--accident or not he could've hit the 2yr old in my arms!! Trying to leave, called the bellhop--nobody came!! We had to drag all our luggage & baby downstairs & not one hotel employee offered to help!!

My wife and I were celebrating our 34th Wedding Anniversary. Having never been to San Francisco or California for that matter I stuck to Westin, because we had never been disappointed. I started having second thoughts after the booking because of the reviews and ranking on tripadvisor. They couldn't have been more wrong. Not only was this the nicest hotel we have ever stayed in and we have stayed in some very nice hotels, but the staff from top to bottom were far and above the greatest we have ever experienced. A huge thank you goes out to the Westin Saint Francis for making this a cherished memory!

We stayed for 2 nights and had a wonderful experience. The greeting upon arrival was remarkable , as was the gorgeous corner suite with the heavenly bed! The location was perfect for seeing San Francisco our first time.
If you have a Moscone Center conference, then this is a fair choice considering the high price of the W and the rest. It's a 15 minutes walk through one of the sliziest streetsbof San Francisco

The room was nice, spacious and clean. Staff were friendly and helpful. We were warned to be careful going out after dark and it did seem like a bad part of town after dark. However, it was handy to be close to the Bart station and bus stop. The worst part was the $35 parking fee, but I don't know if that's standard for downtown. I'd stay here again regardless.

review_title: If not for rather small rooms, I'd give it a 5 all around!
review_text: Wonderful location, incredible food (from both room service and Oak Room dining), great lobby with free wifi, great bar food and wonderful service and, of course, location, location, location! Right on Union Square in the heart of beautiful San Francisco. Ok, it ain't cheap but nothing in SF is. Definitely worth the money. BTW, my last hotel was a suite on the Champs Elysee in Paris and this hotel was 10 times better. In fact, I was so annoyed by THAT hotel (Frasier Suites) I was moved to write a negative review. And it was twice the price of the Westin St Francis! I will always make the Westin SF my home away from home when staying in San Francisco.

review_title: Beautiful, historic hotel in a great location
review_text:
This is a gorgeous hotel that actually has quite a bit of history tied to it. They have displays in the lobby showing the history of the earthquake in the early 1900's along with pictures and memorabilia. They also have photos of famous people that have stayed there & a hotel channel that tells the history and famous people and the scandals they were mixed up in as a guest. 
The Clock Bar is very cozy. Go early to get a seat. After dinner, it gets packed. The bartenders are great, they had a diverse drink menu and eccentric crowd. 
We stayed in a deluxe tower room with king bed on the 19th floor. The front desk staff was very friendly and when I told them it was our first time in SF, they made sure we were assigned to a room with a great view. We could see all the way to the water even though we were in the heart of Union Square. We had a corner room with the bay window shown on the website as well as a side window. The room was just like the picture. It was huge with a large L-shaped hallway that led to the bedtoom. I don't know why they don't show the bathroom online. It's marble with a tub big enough to soak in and the normal Westin heavenly shower. We had a flat panel TV with plenty of channels. I really liked all the dark wood and beautiful crystal chandeliers in the lobby. It's very elegant. We found a great special online; three nights for the price of two, otherwise it would have been close to $350 per nt. for the room we chose. If I could get a similar deal, We'd definitely stay there again. Otherwise, it would be a bit pricey and we'd probably get a basic room there instead.
If you are taking one of the hop on hop off bus tours, they pick up right across the street. Very convenient!
Friendly staff. New modern rooms. Good restaurant.

Stayed here as final part of our honeymoon destination having travelled across USA for the last three weeks. Really looking forward to chilling out for 4 days. Arrived to protests and had a guy thrust a piece of paper at me on arrival. I refused to engage with him and he shouted at me 'don't you care?' got into the foyer to be greeted by staff saying ' hi welcome to hotel frank' my reply was that I'd had better welcomes to hotel! After putting our stuff into the room we decided to check out the area. Went outside via the bar and walked down street past protests on opposite side of the road. I did not appreciate being shouted at via a loudhailer 'that girl in the pinstripes shame on you' and then continuing to carry on their protest. As previous people have stated I have no problem with people protesting, however I do not expect to be embarrassed in the street just because of my (tour companies) choice of hotel. The pickets continued bang on 7am the following morning till 8am that day which again if you sleep at the front of the hotel like we did it is quite a rude awakening. The two layers of double glazing are not soundproof and fortunately I slept with earplugs from the flight. The protests run from weds to sat at various times. Fortunately we did not see them again and left on the Tuesday. We had a flyer pushed under the door explaining protests to which I did read however again this is something I don't want to be troubled with on my honeymoon! The staff at the hotel are part of the protests and I understand some of them are ex employees of the hotel. The rooms and location of the hotel are good, nicely decorated and our room was clean. Hairdryers iron etc are supplied. We had nothing complimentary from the hotel (unlike others) for choosing them to celebrate our marriage. The location is two mins from union square which is nice but it could be quite noisy due to refuse lorries and people in the early hours. The main thing that we felt let down by was the protests. Especially after I had spoken with Kevin about our choice of room prior to our stay. He mentioned nothing about the protests which was quite unfair. The least the hotel can do is to tell you about it so you are at least prepared if you still decide to stay. They could also supply earplugs too! I was prepared for the protests as I knew about them from talking to people in a town prior to SF and trip advisor. I would stay here again if the protests had been sorted out but whilst they continue I wouldn't dream of it. We tried not to let it impact on us to be honest and anyone elderly or with children I would not recommend it while the protests are being conducted. Outside of those times you'll be fine.google protests at hotel Frank for times and days of protests and fit your stay around them and you'll have a better stay :-)

My BF and I had the best time with thanks to Beck's Moter Lodge... Free/safe parking, clean rooms, short walk to all the bars and restaurants on Market and Castro and an even shorter walk back. I have read the negative comments about this place and most are off... This is not a fancy place but a very safe, clean, friendly and affordable MOTEL and next to the Castro. Can't wait to take my BF back!

review_title: In the world of "hit or miss," Pickwick is a miss.
review_text:
You know how go back and forth on a choice you've made because you're not 100% sure about it, and your gut is telling you 1 thing and you do the other? Follow your gut.
The Pickwick falls short in many respects. First let me be fair. I walked in not expecting the Waldorf. I read the reviews and thought I'd keep an open mind. The location is great. The front desk folks are nice.
Unfortunately, thats not going to be enough to make you stay here. Rooms are old and dated, even though there's a flat screen tv, which I think is hilarious. They have the old school alarm clock that you grew up with. Carpet that looks dirty. Ok bed.
But the cardinal sin of any establishment is that my wife shrieked when she found hair in the tub! And it wasn't hers. Really? This really happens?
The good thing is that this hotel makes you want to get up early and explore the city all day, just so you don't have to spend time in the room. Had we been in San Fran longer than 1 1/2 nights, we would've bounced. Whatever you think you're saving in money is lost in comfort. But hey, now we know!

review_title: One night too many in this dirty, stinky, loud hotel
review_text: I was excited to spend the weekend with my husband in san Francisco, but as soon as we checked into this hotel and got to our room, I was disappointed. I then spent the night and next morning trying to find availability anywhere else. I have been through Europe and stayed in some old, rundown hotels. I was shocked at the state of this place. Carpet and walls were dirty, bed was uncomfortable and bathroom looked like it was notncleaned after last guests left. Although the rates at this place seem reasonable, I would avoid it if you could.

review_title: Overpriced good rooms, poor service with horassing protestors and not eco-friendly
review_text:
Stayed for a week at this hotel due to a conference visit. For that purpose this location was great, but as a tourist I would rather have stayed closer to north beach.
Arrival was good and friendly and at first there was no sign of the protestors.
At one of the non conference days I planned to go biking the bridge. So I asked at the front desk what the closest location would be to rent a bike. He sent me all the way to the wharf. The next day I found out that there was a bike rental shop just around the corner. Very strange they did not inform me about that!
At the end of the conference there was still no sign of the protestors to me, although my girlfriend (who spent her days as a tourist while I was at the conference) ran into them. But nothing too bad and only targeted at the hotel and not at its guests. She said she could barely hear it in our room (11th floor).
After a long and exhausting conference I was looking forward to catching up with some sleep and relax all Saturday morning. Too bad that was when the protestors decided to protest at 7am. The continued screening the same monotonous thing over and over again. This time the must have tuned up their megaphones, because it was really loud, even on the 11th floor! I tried to ignore it for a while and get back to sleep,but that was impossible. So I called the frontdesk to express my frustration. They did nothing to apologize or make me less frustrated. They just said it would be over in 20 minutes. When I said I was not paying 300 dollars a night for this, they simply said that they'll let the manager contact me as soon as he/she came in. But I never got a call, neither a note or remark at checkout. Which I think is just poor customer service.
I have no good word for the protestors either. Sure they have the right to protest, but doing that at 7am in the morning in front of people who have nothing to do with that issue is just not right. I would qualify that as horasment! They were screaming for there jobs back. After this behavior I support the hotel for not taking these rude people back. My advise to the protestors would be that they'd better invest their time applying for new job opportunities, than keep stucked in their past. Get a life!
One thing that I also need to mention is that we got new towels every day, despite of the fact that the old ones where not on the floor and some signs stated that what was what you needed to do to get fresh towels. Not very eco-friendly!
The wifi connection also has room for improvement. Randomly we had to enter the wireless login information again. This was really annoying.
Had an amazing stay here, perfectly located for shopping and the cable cars. Room nice with a really comfy bed and some quirky touches. Staff extremely helpful and polite.

review_title: The little hotel in union square
review_text: Visiting SF for the first time hotel frank was pretty good. The staff were extremely kind and generous people. The resterant near the lobby had really good food, and had fast takeout. Warning if u are going to stay in a room with 2 double beds it is VERY squishy. Also, sometimes the bathroom stinks, but overall pretty average and ok.

review_title: Great one night stay near union square
review_text:
I came into SF last night for a conference and stayed at the Hotel Frank. Great location near union square (where I normally stay when in SF). 
I had the king room, which was very sizable for a boutique hotel off of union square. Big TV on the wall, nice desk, and clean and modern bathroom. Overall the hotel has a more modern feel, actually. 
I definitely recommend if staying in SF and you want a great location and nice hotel.

The hotel is reasonably centrally located but beyond this has little to commend it. The rooms are small, the bathrooms tiny. The decor is tired, you can see the walls and doors have been bashed by a thousand suitcases. The walls are paper-thin so you can hear the conversation next door as well. For the money- $250 per night there has to be better available.

review_title: Good hotel apart from the strikers
review_text: This is a great hotel and I would recommend it to anyone however on our first day on our way to check in we were accosted by labour strikers. These people continued to strike from 7am very loudly and we were on the 9th floor! A lie in was on of question!
