hotel_name: Laurel Inn, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: We stayed here on our honeymoon for 3 nights as part of our West Coast extravaganza. We arrived to hear protesters chanting somewhere only to realise it was directly outside or hotel! Outside were ex employees of the hotel which had been taken over a while back - these protests had been going on 8 months!! When we booked earlier in the year we were never told about this. We certainly did not expect to arrive on our honeymoon to jeers of "shame on you, dont stay here!" we were informed that this only happened in the afternoon on certain days for an hour. Not a problem we would be out anyway. However our front facing hotel room was party to another protest at 7:00 am on a sunday! Despite a couple of calls to reception that morning saying we had not been warned and it wasn't acceptable we were told the manager would call back. After it got to 11am we gave up and went out sightseeing as the lobby was to busy at this point to do in person and we didn't want to waste any more of the day. No one ever got back to us and when we went back the manager was gone again. In te end when we checked out we were told only the manager could authorise any sort of discount and he wasn't around. Again. Overall the hotel is located well for union square and shops, and rooms aren't bad. Unfortunately the service was extremely lacking.

review_title: Location, location, location and brilliant service
review_text: Stayed for 3 nights on the way to New Zealand. Jacquie greeted us on arrival - brilliant welcome, extremely efficient and offered useful advice for 1st time visitors to San Francisco. Location of hotel couldn't have been better - everything within walking distance. We were given an upgraded room - thank you Hotel Frank it made our trip extra special. Would highly recommend this hotel and the staff are brilliant. Thank you

review_title: Great hotel, initially put off by the "protests" but there was no need to be.
review_text:
We arrived at hotel Frank for the first night of our honeymoon. We had booked to stay here for 3 nights whilst staying in San Francisco before moving on to Las Vegas.
I think we were lucky with our room allocation, as when we checked in, the very friendly receptionist noticed that we were a honeymoon couple and made a few room changes. 
We ended up in a room near the lift, sort of on "a corner" of the hotel. The view from the window was non existent, just a fire escape, but the room itself was good, with a queen sized bed, funky decoration and lighting, good sized bathroom off a separate corridor within the room and a walk in wardrobe. 
All very clean and tidy.
The protests were a bit of a worry before we arrived, although it was explained to us by the receptionist who seemed to discuss it in a fairly light hearted way. Although I think she supported the protest, she said that they'd been doing it for a while and nothing was really coming of it.
We only saw them once on a bus tour which happened to drive by the hotel.
We ate in the restaurant below the hotel once, "max's on the square" which was nice.
Location wise, you couldn't beat it, with easy access to the local shops, restaurants, cable cars etc etc.

review_title: Great Hotel for Union Square area.
review_text:
I just stayed here for 4 nights and even though my flight was delayed by several hours the front desk staff was cheerful and helpful even in the middle of the night.
I read just before going that there were picketers. But I only saw them once and they did not bother us. But if you want to work around them, simply enter and exit the hotel by going thru Max's restaurant. It is connected to the hotel lobby and you don't have to worry about the picketers should you see them. Otherwise, while they were out the hotel had staff at the front door so we did not feel threatened or anything like that.
As for the room. My room was really large for the area. I had 4 adults staying in one room so I had a king size bed and a sofa bed. Even when the sofa bed was pulled out there was a 4 to 5 foot walk way between them. And to top it off there was a desk area completely away from the sleeping area. The hotel had everything including a hair dryer, flat panel tv, great lighting, refrigerator and a safe. The housekeeping staff was very accommodating, when I asked for extra towels and pillows they appeared within minutes.
The hotel is in a wonderful location. Just out the door to the left is the Cable car stop. Down a couple a blocks is the mall. Down one block and to the right is the Rrazz Room at the Nikko for nighttime entertainment. And one more block over is the Marrakech Magic Theater which is an amazing show and very kid friendly too if you need to do something with the youngsters.
Just about anything you can think of to eat is within a short and easy walking distance. Or if you want to go spend the day at Fisherman's Wharf just hop on the Cable Car. No need to use your own vehicle here.
Overall we liked this hotel very much. Excellent location. Decent part of town. Very clean and friendly. Only thing it did not have was free breakfast or a microwave, but that still didn't damper out stay. We'd stay here again if we ever were in this area.

review_title: Best hotel I've been to yet
review_text: This was a very nice hotel I loved the way the rooms were remodeled and that this building kept some of the originals in place like the windows. The overall stay was great and close to all the stores downtown and right in the prime spot for all forms of transportation I would go back there in a heartbeat. Only sad thing for me was the bath robes were to small but that's not a huge deal. Loved the stay and the employees were all friendly

Good location..
Rooms weren't the most amazing thing ever but had your basics.. 
Would recommend for a short stay - nothing like a honeymoon destination or anything!

review_title: Average value, decenct location...but don't pay full price!
review_text: Booked on Hotwire, so we got an ok deal, but I would never pay full price. Stayed Pride weekend, so considering the crowds in SF it was a good location. But beware of dirty bathrooms, over charges to your credit card and the loud construction north of the hotel. We are 50-50 to stay there again...and definitely not at full price. Recommended with reservations.

My sister, dad & I just stayed at the Mark Twain hotel in October 2011 for 3 nights. 
If you're looking for a nice hotel that is reasonably priced, has friendly staff and is in a good location then this is your place,.
I spent HOURS reading reviews for everywhere I stayed all over the states & promised I'd post honest reviews when I got back so this is one of them.
If you're an impatient person that nit picks everything & is never happy & expects gold when you only wanna pay silver then you may not like that SOMETIMES the lift takes about 1 min, or that the lift isnt MASSIVE.
Location is great, 2 shirt blocks to Powell st where the cable car line is, one block from Macy's & other awesome shops.. A nice restaurant downstairs, cafe next door that does a cheap breakfast.. Oh and free water & lemonade out of a dispenser type thing right next to lifts which is handy when you don't have any on you & dont necessarily want a whole bottle - haven't seen this at other hotels. 
Taxi from airport was about $65-$70 but the hotel organized a car for us on way back to airport which was a really nice, big car (for all our luggage!) which was only $45.. So enquire about that first.
The rooms were cleaned really well - as in you could smell the cleaning product which was fine by me.
The room we had wasn't massive - no room to spread all your stuff out but had a decent sized walk i pn cuoboard & we werent there to chill in the hotel room! 
Flat screen TV with lots of channels.
Noise was fine, didn't bother me - can't even remember hearing much noise... If noise is something that bothers you perhaps request top floor but wasn't an issue for me at all.
All in all, good hotel - I'd stay there again & definitely recommend it.

I stayed here the first weekend of November this year, so it was a very cold weekend. Once my friends and I got to the hotel, we were not let in immediately. We were left to wait out in the cold with all of out bags until a guest was leaving the building to let us in. The staff member that was sitting at the front desk saw us, but never made an attempt to open the door. When we got to the front desk, we paid for our rooms and went upstairs.
For my boyfriend and I, I booked the junior suite, which should have had a couch in it. Once we got to our room, to my surprise, we had a queen bed and a single bed, but no couch. The next day a few more of my friends flew in and were going to check into the hotel (mind you, they had their reservations booked weeks in advance). The same thing happened to them where the staff left them outside and did not open the door. The staff told them from inside that, "If they're guests at the hotel, they'd know how to get in." My friends were able to get in because a guest was leaving the building. Once my friends checked in and brought their things to their room, the keys they were given did not open their door. My friends went back downstairs and told the person at the front desk that the key isn't working and the hotel staff told my friends that they were completely booked. The staff had to call the manager to see what they could do. A few minutes later, a room suddenly was open for them to stay in. Not once did the staff apologize for this inconvenience to them. Then the next day, the room they booked had opened after the hotel called a locksmith to open the door. It would have been an inconvenience for my friends to pack all their stuff up just to move rooms again. Again, the hotel staff did not apologize for anything. And the hotel manager seemed to never be available to speak to them.
The last day of my reservation, I tried calling the front desk to request a late check out for my boyfriend and I. I called 4 times and let the phone ring for a few minutes. Check out is at 11am. I first tried calling at 8:30am. Then again at 9. Again at 9:15 and then 9:30. No one answered. Finally, I decided to go downstairs at 10am to request the late checkou. That is when I see 3 people behind the front desk just sitting and staring at the monitors for each floor. I asked one of the ladies about a late checkout and she told me it would be $20 extra to check out at 12pm. I mentioned to her that I've been trying to call the front desk for a while and no one has answered. She completely ignored that and told me I had to pay for a late checkout..only one hour for $20. Instead, I told her I'd be back after I got breakfast. I just ended up putting my bags in my friends room in the floor up from me that requested a late check out. It was then when my friend told me that he requested a late check out and didn't charge him or tell him there was a fee. 
Overall, this hotel has a great location and was reasonably priced for a room, but the service was horrible. The staff was not helpful nor friendly, in fact, some were quite rude. I'm from LA and I would have expected better service from this town, especially from a hotel that's been there quite some time. I will never stay at this hotel again. Great location, good prices, but everything else was terrible.

review_title: Easy access to Chinatown; centrally located
review_text: Situated directly across from the Chinese Cultural Centre and Chinatown, the hotel is convenient if you want/need to be close to this area. Otherwise select either Union Square or Fisherman's Wharf properties. The hotel seems a tad tired but otherwise the rooms are fine. Free wifi is a big bonus. Didn't try the restaurant although had a brunch there. Good quality food served.

review_title: Too expensive for what it offers
review_text: We went there last July. Nice bar and location but the rooms were a bit cheap looking and dark. Bathrooms were even more dated. Expensive breakfast and not free wifi were disappointing.

review_title: Good customer service when things do not work out as you expect!
review_text: Bit of a muddle with bed's was resolved well by the manager. Setting is what you would expect for the $ & would recommend it to a friend

review_title: Massive hotel in central location with very poor service
review_text:
My husband and I stayed there earlier on this month. The check in experience was dreadful, we had to ask to speak to the manager as they were offering corner rooms looking into a brick wall or close to the street where you can not sleep. After speaking to the manager we managed to get a decent room but for a +1000 room hotel is not good enough. 
The room was not cleaned until after 5pm, they charged for use of the fitness centre which looks like a dungeon. 
This is definitely a hotel I would recommend
I will never go back to this hotel ever,it takes almost 12 hours to get a fresh towel.Elevator too slow.Services less than poor....I rather stay in Motel 6 next time.Don't go there.

As a budget hotel (almost hostel, even though I paid U$ 140,00 plus taxes and fees= 161 - in November, the same room costs 55 bucks), they don't provide with almost any additional service offered by a regular hotel. Not even breakfast is available. 
Daily chambermaid service has an extra fee of 7 dollars. 
But the worst was to come: from the Booking website, they informed the rooms had air conditioner. When I entered that incredibly stuffy room I realized no air conditioner was available. And the clerk said that only 2 rooms of the hotel had it. How can they do it? It's a rip off. Bear in mind that my main requirement when booking a hotel is the availability of air conditioner. I'm completely disappointed. And nothing else was offered to make up for it.

review_title: Modern and clean hotel with personality and great service.
review_text: Clean room, strong WiFi, great service, awesome water pressure, comfortable bed. Lots of restaurant choices within a few blocks. Shopping is very close. I loved that they asked what type of room I liked (quiet, high floor, close to elevator, etc) and actually delivered on all my preferences.
Noisy, strange lighting, homeless folks wearing you out, conceited staff, room decor bought at Goodwill (seemingly), tiny bathrooms...felt like I was staying in a pornstar's dirty apt

The location was perfect. Several places to eat, walgreens, shopping all within walking distance. The room was clean and the bed was comfortable. 
The hotel staff were on strike and picketed infront of the hotel. At times it did make it awkward to enter and exit the hotel. 
My room had no coffee maker and no hair dryer which was kind of odd. But there was starbucks on every corner.

review_title: Reasonable comfort in a good location
review_text: Hotel Frank was fine. Very good location. Reasonably friendly staff, nice enough rooms. Just not outstanding despite it's boutique reputation. Also didn't help being shouted at by protestors outside the hotel, shouting "shame on you" when we came out of the door! What was that all about?!

It feels like your in a lunch box. The room is extra small. You can hear people walk by your room and I'm sure if you had a intimate night everyone would know....smh. This is definitily not a place for couple to spend there wedding anniversary. This place should be a hotel for shorts stays, like by the hour if you know what I mean. If your only going to use this room for only to sleep then all is good. Oh, and last but not least, there is no air condition or fan. Have at it

Can't fault this hotel for it's location- right in the heart of downtown. Rooms clean and bed comfortable. Bathrooms are tiny and ours stank to high heaven of garlic! Showers not particulary great. Check in staff not at all friendly and concierge didn't really seem to know much. 
Just got a very unfriendly vibe from the place.
Breakfast at lefty o'doulls v good though:-).

The Frank Hotel is perfectly located, just off Union Square. We were upgraded to a suite as soon as we arrived (thanks Jackie) and the room was massive. Decorated very stylishly and very clean too. We were recommended Lefty O'Doules over the road for breakfast and ended up going there for breakfast every day. Would also recommend the Mexican, el sitano (I think..) up the hill. It can get a little noisy in the hotel due to the usual hustle and bustle from union square and there was a demonstration by some protesters (including a maniac on a loud hailer) at 7am on Saturday. But this didn't really detract from a very enjoyable stay.

review_title: Cool scene in a cool town
review_text: Great location two blocks off union square. Room was big as we took the 29dollar upgrade offer via email. Only neg was could hear the service elevator through wall. Fortunately we sleep heavy after hanging in the bar and enjoying the people watching. Don't miss slanted door restaurant or Gary Danko both great and worth the money. Also get to muir wood early very limited parking. Breakfast at the hotel not great. Went up to a coffe shop on Taylor good fast and reasonable. Door man told us about it.

review_title: Nice hotel in a great part of town
review_text: We had no problems during our stay here. People were friendly and beds were extremely comfortable. Just down the street from Coit Tower and easy walk to Chinatown.

review_title: Affordable luxury in the very best location!
review_text: Our Valentine getaway was magical in the most beautiful city in the world and the only thing that could make it better would be to stay in a fabulous hotel. The Westin St. Francis on Union Square was the perfect hotel for intimate and splendid. The location is right in the middle of everything! and the staff is from another time - our comfort, relaxation and satisfaction were their only goal. Thanks to all at the Westin St. Francis for memories to treasure.

Overall a lovely hotel v cool and great bar but in this day and age why charge for Internet? Esp when 15 bucks a day Everyone knows this is a quick buck to take advantage of business accounts buy just puts me off staying in future.

review_title: Disappointed toward treatment of a loyal customer.
review_text:
I actually stayed in 2009, but I couldn't go back that far... I had the same dealings with NOISE as some of the other reviewers. 
Even with a non adjoining room, I could hear WAY too much noise . Even could hear the person next door PEEING in the toilet!!!
I will have to say that the management did move my room and offered me some compensation.
 But my REAL disappointment 
came recently with trying to book a second stay July 2011. I secured a decent rate for the room in January. A little over a month later, 
I thought I was going to have to cancel my trip, so I canceled the reservation, then 2 days later realized I could still go. Well the rates for July 2011 went up $115 per night. After several phone calls they would NOT reinstate my rate. 
I am now forced to stay at another hotel. 
They could have worked with me, but instead they followed text book policy, so now they lost a customer. I forgot about all the noise there. All the more reason I won't spend what they are charging now per night.

review_title: Pay extra for the W Hotel
review_text: I recently stayed here and it wasn't a great experience staying at the hotel. When we arrived at reception desk to check in we were told that out room wasn't ready. We waited and waited and waited and weren't in our room until after 4pm. I found it hard to believe that all the rooms were booked and there were no other rooms available. I regret not booking at the W Hotel.

review_title: Great hotel in the heart of Union Square
review_text:
Stayed three nights while attending a conference in SF. 
Great location, in the heart of everything. Rooms were ok ... I think the westins are moving away from their heavenly beds?! 
Pricey ... Reasonable I guess for the area. 
Bar and bartenders was a great experience.
Extremely focused on customer service. 
Would stay again. Stayed at the W right down the street a couple of years ago. Just can't deal with the continuous techno music. Lol

review_title: On going construction nearby. Stayed on 19th floor and could not sleep beecause of nearby location
review_text: Ovwerall great hotel and the chinatown is the added value; however they have a stupid 24/7 building construction near the hotel. I stayed on the 19th floor and could not sleep. The windows are not sound proof. Stay away because of construction

review_text: Clift delivered in every way possible. Staff, rooms, food, drinks were all on point. I would compare this with any property in the world. Perfection!

Stayed for 4 days at this Hotel and did not want to leave. Read mixed reviews before we went but was pleased to say that thus hotel was top draw.. Location could not have been better, staff were very friendly, rooms great. Would recommend this place to anyone..

This is a wonderful, well-managed and staffed hotel. My boyfriend and I stayed for eight nights and throughly enjoyed it. I would love it if they installed coffee pots in the room, but that's a small complaint. 
The hotel is apparently being boycotted by some union group. What a bunch of shrill losers.

review_title: Unique room, breakfast and service excellent!
review_text: Stayed for three nights, although room was over a back alley didn't really matter. The Irish pub next door ideally located. Room was spotless with everything you needed although a little small. Breakfast was scrummy for a continental, and service spot on, so helpful. Parking expensive, but seems to be the case in San Fran.

This is a nice hotel with different artwork in each room. The rooms were clean and you get breakfast which was great! My only problem is you get woken up very early from the noise in the alleyway outside. From garbage trucks at 4am, to glass breaking, to a guy throwing beer kegs around - its not the best sleep.

review_title: I can see how this wouldn't be for everyone, but I loved it
review_text: Amazing location especially for the money, funky vibe, can be noisy, but the cleanest hotel room I've ever seen! I found the front desk over three days to be very personable and helpful. The problem with less expensive hotels can be they aren't in great locations, but this is ideal to explore the city. The one thing I would say is I was surprised by the parking situation (you have to park in a public garage- a bit of a hassle and costs 30.00 a night which I didn't know on booking. That may be common in SF though, I don't know, and at 89.00 a night the total was still a great value in my opinion)

Petit dÃ©jeuner trÃ¨s correct.
I love this hotel- clean, safe and funky! the rooms are a great size and make you feel you are staying somewhere expensive! free wifi and breakfast and choice of rooms with or without bathrooms.

review_title: Not bad if you book with discounted prices
review_text:
This looks to me as an old hotel probably from the fifties that hasn't been updated in all this years. The rooms are small and beds are uncomfortable and really really small. Queens are almost like a single to me. Furniture is old and the mini fridge is locked on a night table but makes more noise than an old refrigerator. The rooms are still clean but you can't fight the age and dust on carpets or on the old curtains. Location is very nice
 It's conveniently close to Union Square and Bart station but be aware it's also close to a very bad neighborhood known as the Tenderloin so if you're not familiar with the city and decide to stay here you better ask which streets you're not supposed to walk into for safety reasons ... some streets close to the hotel are full of homeless people and junkies that might get aggressive if you don't give them money. But as I said that's not the usual for instance when coming from Union square. The best of this hotel is without a doubt its employees. Most of them are willing to help and would give you any information you might need. Also you have Internet usage for free on a desktop PC at the lobby. Wireless internet is available but it's too expensive. It has a restaurant but didn't eat there so I wouldn't know. In any case I recommend this hotel id you're familiar with the city and if you manage to find a promotional price online for staying here. For it's full price won't be worth it and you possibly can find better options.

review_title: Great hotel, great service, great location!
review_text:
I was a little hesitant to stay at the Clift after reading some of the reviews but am now glad I did.
The location certainly can't be beat and I loved the vibe of the hotel, it was fun, modern, and hip. As far as the bathroom size that so many people seem to complain about, well, I found it to be perfectly adequate and even charming as the size is a nod to the historical nature of the building. I have stayed in several historic hotels and the charm and knowledge that they are a landmark and a piece of history outweighs any thin walls or accommodations that don't fit in with our "super-size me" culture.
Thank you Clift for a wonderful stay, your friendly and helpful staff as well as the lovely ambiance and elegance of your hotel made for a very enjoyable visit! I will definitely be returning!

review_title: A hotel and art gallery in the heart of San Francisco - winning!
review_text: Great hotel. Great art. Great staff. Great location and value! As the mother of an art school student, I really appreciated the art in the halls and painted on the wall of our room. We will be back!

The hotel is situated in a great location; steps from Chinatown, close to all the public transport and a few minutes away from the shopping district & Market St. 
Although a small & old hotel, it's made interesting by turning the hallways into an art gallery. Even the rooms are uniquely adorned. 
There is really no luxury but the unique surrounding make up, especially since the room was always clean. The heating was a little bonkers causing us to leave the windows open resulting in mosquito bites...
Finally the free breakfast is basically muffins, toast, juice, tea & coffee served in a tiny room with stools for both the seats and tables. 
All in all it was interesting but been there done that...

review_title: Great location, service and overall experience
review_text: We chose this hotel as it looked different, quirky yet still comfortable, and it was all of the above and more. The complimentary breakfast bagels, muffins and coffee were a surprise but really yummy! The room was exciting to come home to after s day out exploring, and the location is great, right near trans, china town and the city centre, yet still quiet enough to get a good nights rest. Highly recommend! A unique hotel experience! Really is like staying in a gallery.

While lack of a/c is rerely an issue in SF. It was very warm during my visit making spending anytime in room impossible. Had windows pried open in the middle of the night. Noise was really bad. This hotel borders the tenderloin. Very decieving and dangerous location. Service and food in breakfast room , very bad. Too bad. I love the Warwick in Denver.

The room and bathrooms were very clean, and the art was beautiful. The staff is knowledgeable about the city and will help you get where you want to go. They also will let you in on the "locals" favs, you just have to ask. The wifi isn't super high speed, but it's about normal as most. Besides that, the hotel is awesome. It embody's the true San Fran experience.

review_title: Central location, a great place to stay
review_text: I stayed here in September 2011 for 4 nights with my husband. This hotel was great for us, central location, clean and a great price. I am surprised in reading some of the negative reviews as our experience was pleasant. Staff were helpful, assisted us with organising airport shuttle and we felt safe in this area walking the neighbourhood. One minor drawback was that our room faced the laneway and was a little noisy late at night. However, the windows were pretty good and blocked out most of the noise. I would recommend this hotel.

For my first trip to San Francisco, decided to bite the bullet, try to save some money and "Name My Own Price" through Priceline. Big mistake. Ended up with the Warwick listed as a 3-star hotel. I'm not sure of the expectations of other guests here, but anyone noting the Warwick as clean and helpful...really? I was determined to go against the bad reviews when arriving, keeping an open mind, but the hotel is a dump. The non-smoking rooms smell of mildew or something of that nature. The shower, when run at the normal pressure and speed, left a 2-inch deep pool of water for you to wade in, stains on the throw pillows on the bed, the armoire broke...complete disaster. After hours upon hours between Priceline and the property, we are receiving a refund for the two remaining nights that we WILL NOT be staying. If you're allergic to mold, you're going to wake up with a stuffed nose to enjoy in the morning. I'm positive after reading past reviews I'm not the first to experience these deplorable conditions and service. If you, like me, booked through Priceline and are unhappy, do not listen when they say things CAN'T be changed. There's a difference between CAN'T and WON'T.
What hotel doesn't have a manager on duty on a Friday night? To call this a 3-star hotel is an insult to the industry and the guests paying any amount of money to stay here. 
If you want a dirty hotel in a great location, this one's for you.

My friend and I stayed here during our West Coast tour of the US last month and this was our favorite hotel that we stayed in. The service was impeccable. The staff were helpful and very friendly. Our room was beautiful and fairly spacious. The decor was exactly to my house- I wanted to take the room lamps home with me! The location is excellent, too. What more can I say? Staying here was an absolute delight :)

Despite some reviews, staff were terrific in all cases. Room nuce and cant complain about that, cleanliness or the usual stuff. Location difficult to beat and it is oh so cool. 
However, it's not cheap and with high bar, restaurant and WiFi charges you could begin to feel somewhat fleeced. The latter in particular really should be included, at the very least in public areas. 
Lots of homeless in the area, which is not the Clift's fault, but an apparently increasing problem downtown.

Stayed only 1 nite but wished I could have stayed longer. This lovely hotel had the warm and friendly atmosphere. I was traveling alone but didn't feel uncomfortable. Great food at the restaurant. No hurry during dinner. Never felt rushed. Very pleasurable.

L'hotel e' un po' datato, ma comunque funzionale. E' pulito, la camera dove abbiamo soggiornato era giusta per due persone. Sei proprio in centro, a pochi passi da union square. L'unica pecca pero' e' il fatto che proprio girato l'angolo si trova il quartiere di Tenderloin, uno dei peggiori di San Francisco. Frequentemente si trovano barboni, anche se comunque gentili, nel senso che non sono invadenti e ti lasciano stare, non insistono. Confermo che la zona e' controllata dalla polizia, in ogni caso consiglio di non rientrare tardi la sera.

Overall we had a great stay! The room was cozy and clean. We loved the Victorian eclectic feel! We did however get some beverages stuck in the mini fridge because the key broke and the staff was unable to fix it. We did experience some strange happenings in our room, the light turned on in the middle of the night and the blinds opened one time by themselves, it was very bizarre. I definitely don't believe in That sort of stuff...but it was quite odd. However I never felt unsafe or freaked out. When we got home I googled to see if anyone else had experienced something similar there, and found no results.

review_title: Will come back every year to celebrate our anniversary
review_text: The hotel reminds me of a french hotel its decorated really cute and the beds are super comfortable. The people in the front were extremley nice to us ans you can't beat the location it was next to the mall whichwas a plus. We usually stay at the St Francis but they were booked but this hotel was much more cozier that we decided to stay there again this year for our anniversay

review_title: Best place to stay to discover daily life in San Francisco.
review_text:
Pros:
The staff (Rita and Jag) are fantastic!
The rooms are clean and the price is affordable.
Nearby Mall for shopping.
Quiet area.
Great Ocean Beach a few block away.
Easy access to downtown....great cental location.

Parking spaces are small.

review_text:

What makes the Nob Hill attractive is its location and the availability of (narrow) parking. Otherwise, this is a motel with 5 star pricing.

The rooms are large and comfortable. They are somewhat dated but that's to be expected for the price. Location was great and you could walk to most attractions within 30 mins. The immediate area felt safe and there was a nice deli and grocery store right nearby.

review_title: Good location, large rooms, free parking.
review_text: San Francisco is amazing and Nob Hill Motor Inn was a good base for the 2days we were there. Parking was free and easy. Rooms were big and clean (towels were a bit thin!). Breakfast was rubbish but there are loads of lovely places to eat in San Fran.

Close to Powell st cable cars and union square.
Room was good size, bathroom was clean. Plus there was FREE wireless Internet and computers in lobby (the Internet speed was slow though).

What a great find! I'm giving it four stars, not because it's a four star hotel. It's actually just a step up from hostel, but it is such a great deal for the price and location.Â 
Location: It's so close to Union Square, the BART, and great shopping and restaurants. The block it takes to walk up to the hotel is a hill. It didn't bother us though. But just a warning.Â 
Price: 88 dollars a night for a queen with a private bathroom. And on a holiday (Veterans) weekend!Â 
Room: Don't expect anything fancy. Its tiny with no view. But, it does have a private bathroom with a tub/shower combo. Our view was a white wall, but whatever...at least it was quiet =)

Hotel was in a great location about 30 seconds from the nearest cable car stop.
We stayed in room 315. Rooms are basic but clean and the bathrooms look like they have been recently refurbished. No strong smells, the hotel is a little musky but nothing like what the other reviews say.
All of the other hotels nearby charge our weekly rate for one or two nights so definitely a bargain. 
Ignore strip club you wouldn't even know it was there. 
Overall I would go back to The Grant Hotel.

To be honest, the smell of public areas is terrible, but once in your room, it is a clean small room, really what you pay for (cheap), and an incredible location.
We saw other comments abut homelss people and the night club next to the hotel. The truth is only car noises were anoying. You see homeless peolple all over the area, even outside the big hotels, and the night club is nothing to worry about.
Again, get some Glade from home and the hotel is great if you want to save some bucks.

review_title: Comfortable clean and convienient and good value
review_text: I stayed 3 nights and was very happy with the quality and comfort of the hotel for the price. Didn't eat the breakfast, the coffee machine was broken, but the computors in the lobby for Internet access were very convenient. It was a short walk to the tram stop and union square with lots of places to eat and chinatown down the road.

we spent 3 nights at the crescent during our recent visit to sf. the situation of the hotel is ok, but in my opinion not as good as many people write here. the room interior is also ok, but the size of it is just too small.
breakfast was a big disappointment. we stayed at motels for less than half the price of the crescent and got better choices...
the bar makes a lot of noise, but no wonder when the door is always open..
overall i have to say: too expensive for what you get and we will definitely not return

The hotel was super cute as I walked in, and there are a lot of out of towners checking in, our check in was pretty speedy and we were given a room on the last floor (only 5 floors) and given the corner room which was pretty quiet. The room was nothing out of the ordinary vary plain and a PLUS is the flat screen t.v. & the bathroom was very clean, another plus is the in room safe. We wish they could have updated the mattresses because the springs were worn out and but after a long day of San Francisco, just getting back to a warm bed and resting my eyes was great. The breakfast I knew would be nothing out of this world, but coffee is $3/ cuo at Starbucks so I'm not complaining if it's free and with a delicious pastry ( muffins, doughnuts, croissants, and chocolate croissants ) and you can get more than 1, the bakery they get these pastries from, is excellent. Oh and they have boiling water all day and night, so I made myself a cup of tea each night. Ask for a refrigerator if you want to keep anything refrigerated which is what we did. 
The hotel is walking distance to the cable cars, which is great SF experience, and bus stops/ Bart station. I bought a muni pass and took public transportation everywhere. The best shopping is within walking distance and if you take any tours, the hotel is a pick up location. Found some great eateries nearby and whenever you need something ASAP, the walgreens is a block away. Even realized some pretty good nightlife is nearby, Ruby Sky, the bar at Clift hotel, and plenty of bars.
Would I return to this hotel, probably yes! Great price for overall stay. Wish they just updated their mattresses, kinda hard.

review_title: Great location with lots of character.
review_text:
The Crescent is exactly like I expected with the added bonus that it was close to everything. It is an older hotel so it has many of the quirks like a slow elevator that really only accommodates two due to weight limits. We were on the 8th floor and down was not issue but we waited for the elevator to go up. 
There is no AC so we had windows open which was fine for the room temp but did make it noisy. 
This is not a modern hotel, but if you want character (it looks just like posted pictures) and location, give it a try. 
We were a couple of blocks from Chinatown, Union Square, and Nob Hill. A safe neighborhood all in all. There were tons of great places to eat.
Breakfast was fresh and plentiful. We skipped it and walked down to one of the amazing French bakeries. 
We would stay here again.

review_title: Great price for a great location!
review_text: Walking distance to China Town and Union Square. About 1 mike walk to Fisherman's Wharf. Easy walk there but take the cable cars or bus back up! Coffee and pastries for breakfast, free Internet access on nice new macs! Very clean! We switched to a bigger room after two days and they let us check in at 10 am! I highly recommend this hotel for people on a budget!

Charming, unpretentious little hotel just blocks from Union Square and Chinatown. Our bathroom floor was clean enough to eat on-I've never seen a cleaner room. Very quiet, although our room was at the very rear. It's my new place to stay in the city.

Had a great four night stay here with special deal thru travelzoo.com. Included free WiFi and daily $10 food voucher. Easy access to cable cars, BART, and Muni. Friendly staff and nice breakfast in the restaurant adjoined to the hotel. And no bedbugs!

review_title: Nothing flash but in the best location!
review_text: This hotel was fine. It was clean, it was literrally across the rd from the wharf and the stff were extremely helpful and friendly. Im used o staying in 5 star places but because my partner partner and I were travelling around the USA for 7 weeks we didn't want to blow the budget out. Anywhere in Fishermans wharf is expensive so no matter where u stay it's going to be pricey. We stayed for 3 nights and it was about $575. Its older but other then that no worries at all!

review_title: Classy, chic, clean, close to attractions.
review_text: After reading reviews here, we went for it, and requested a room above the fourth floor. We got a top floor room, which was the cleanest and most attractive room ive seen for less than $ 300. We walked a few short blocks to union square, walgreens, transportation, and starbucks. Theres a convenience store next door, and its close to chinatown which means great food can be delivered. Free breakfast was fantastic and healthy. Wasnt overly noisy, unless youre used to the country or a light sleeper. Elevator is not slow, and no noise from the bar on higher floors. Excellent shower, high ceilings, dimmer lights, soft bedding, quality toiletries.

review_title: Hip, excellent value and very central
review_text: Perfect if you are looking for an alternative to dreary chain hotels, but definitely for those who want more urban edge than quaintness. Got a fantastic deal by booking direct with hotel and will definitely go back.

Thin windows = cold rooms and loud street noise. One pilllow did not have pillowcase, which other pillowcases are questionable at that. Tiny rooms, but typical for SF. Boutique for sure, with prices to match, but not quality. Loved the bathroom.
It would have been rated lower but the staff was excellent. Sometimes with Priceline you et what you pay for.

Have stayed in Warwick San Francisco every year for 7 years. Still has the charm if a quality boutique hotel, however service is not the same. You wait a long time for your car, rooms are not maintained as they used to be and food quality has gone down a bit. Still a great place to stay if you want an alternative to the big hotels on the Square.

The only good thing about this hotel is its location. While checking in the front desk staff was not only rude but dint give us any directions on where the elevator was or that we need to use the key card to access it. No information was given by her about amenities . She dint even say have a nice stay. The room was average. Have stayed at better quality hilton rooms.

This hotel was a last minute choice for my family and I, as the hotel we had booked for our SF stay proved unsuitable. The service we recieved on arrival was excellent. Staff did their utmost to get the four of us ( my wife and me with our two sons 8 and 10) into a suitable room. They found a room with a king bed and a single, which was adequate, but not ideal. The room had no refrigerator, but a call to the service desk had one sent up later that day. The room was clean and the rate was reasonable. The location of the hotel is just a short walk to Fishermans Wharf and all of the attractions of that area

This hotel is in a great location within walking distance of Fishermans Wharf, Restaurants and public transport. Friendly and helpful staff. We would recommend this hotel to anyone travelling to San Francisco.

We stayed at this property for one night and it was great! The location is just far enough that the cable cars and other loud sounds don't bother you, but close enough to walk to Ghiradelli Square and the Wharf! Debbie the concierge is absolutely AMAZING, she genuinely cares about her job and guests. Alicia at the front desk was very welcoming, friendly and helpful. All in all I would definitely recommend this property!!!

review_title: Run don't walk from this hotel.
review_text: I am a Hilton Gold member, check in was easy and fruit basket was left in my room. Morning breakfast wasn't very good. Location is bad if you are attending a convention. Last day of checkout, the cleaning lady tried entering at 800am while I was sleeping then again at 9:00am. So much for sleeping in....

Rhe location was gr8, hotel clean, staff friendly and helpful!
Room was quite noisy from street noise and could hear other guests no matter how late or early they were returning to room talking, although they were really loud, also hear people in room above us wAlking around. Disappointing that bar shut at 930pm and no evening meal although breakfast wasn't brilliant, toasters didn't work and food cold .

Affordable, yet simple hotel in a relatively expensive city. Good location - a couple of blocks from muni and Bart stations and union sq. Room simple but clean - bathroom toiletries add nice touch. Stayed in a room which looked out onto geary St. Was really quite noisy - and this could definitely pose a problem for light sleepers. Good free wifi and two computers available (but no printer). Comfortable bed and good shower.

review_title: Great place for a weekend trip.
review_text: Place was clean and service was great. It was relatively centrally locate to places to eat and public transportation. Parking was also pretty reasonable. Would stay here again on another weekend trip.

3 blocks from wharf . Good sized rooms and well stocked bathroom toilitries. Room opposite beer garden with people sitting outside the window. Had to keep curtains closed. Decent breakfast but no fresh eggs. Reception unhelpful and no postage stamps available.

review_title: Good central location with well appointed rooms
review_text: Only stayed one night but this hotel served it's purpose well. Rooms were well decorated clean and individually appointed. Admittedly the street outside had it's fare share of down and outs but not unusual for a major city. The central location was ideal.

review_title: Great location-comfy beds-free parking..what else could you want??!!
review_text: My boyfriend and I stay here for 2 nights. We loved the location. The room was very clean and the bed was very comfy. The parking is free but limited. We parked and took transit everywhere. You could walk 3 blocks to to Van Ness(a main road) and hop on a bus that would take you to anywhere in the city you wanted to get to. If you dont mind walking you could walk to union square. It took us 20-25 mins. I wouldn't recommend walking down Eddy rd though. There is a coffee shop approx 6 blocks up Van Ness called "Philz". I got the best cup of tea I've ever had. My boyfriend loved his coffee. We went there every morning.
hotel_name: Days Inn San Francisco Downtown/Civic Center Area

review_title: Excellent value for money, good location
review_text: Excellent value for money! Location is close to major spots to see. Free parking, free Internet, qualified and friendly staff. It is not a five star hotel, but you also don't pay like for a five star hotel. Over all the Buena Vista is a very good deal. I stayed in my life in several hundred Dollar 5-star hotels and cheapest motels and this place is definetly a worth every cent. I booked over booking (dot) com and paid in Dec. 2011 $65 + tax per night.
It's on lombard street so you hear traffic in your room all night. Garage only fits about ten cars. Most uncomfortable bed I have ever slept in.

We stayed at this hotel in October and were very happy with it. It is an older hotel, but it is kept very clean and the bathrooms have been upgraded. The location is excellent, walking distance to Fishermans Wharf. We were three women and we felt very comfortable walking around this neighborhood after dark. The free continental breakfast is only pastries, fruit, juice and coffee (which is what a continental breakfast is) but it was enough to grab and leave the hotel in the morning. The desk staff was helpful explaining bus routes and other directions. I recommend using public transportation, even these drivers will help out with directions! Overall for the value, I would definItely stay here on my next visit.

review_text: Location is great, and that's a huge plus. Yes the rooms are small, I'm 6ft 4, and when you add bags from you and your partner, its snug at best. The bed is small too. If you like swinging cats, maybe it's not for you. In all honesty though, you don't come here to stay in the room or for a luxury stay. It's perfectly adequate to sleep in, nice and clean to freshen up, and nicely located to get out and see San fran. Plus let's be Frank, it's cheap! You can hear the nightclub, but if you are not shattered from a day exploring, what have you been doing? All in all it's good, clean, cheap hotel in the city centre.

Estuvimos en Agosto, durante 4 noches. La primera de ellas, perfecta, pero luego llegaron las noches del jueves, viernes y sabado. 
Habia fiesta en el Pub y la sala de fiestas del primer piso y la musica y el ruido eran insufribles. Retumbaban los radiadores y los espejos en las habitaciones, por la musica que sonaba en le sala de fiestas. Ademas, algunas parejitas,
se subian a los pasillos del hotel a darse el lote, discutir, o simplemente a descansar en las escaleras a las habitaciones. Total, la decoracion esta muy bien, aunque es un hotel viejo reformado, pero si tenei que pasar un fin de semana, no os lo recomiendo.

I quite enjoyed my stay here. I was in town for a convention at the Hilton, which is literally around the corner and twice the price. Although the rooms were a bit on the small side, the beds were comfortable and my roomate and I found the hotel to be really enjoyable. Being right downtown, it was somewhat loud, but that is to be expected. Everything you need is within walking distance. The staff were great and very helpful. I would definitely stay here again!!

This hotel was amazing and we'll definately be back. We arrived after a delayed flight due to the weather and we were upgraded to a junior suite, which was a gorgeous room. On the small side but had everything we needed and was tastefully decorated. 
The hotel is above fusion bar, voted in the top 35 bars in the world and we saw why. It was fantastic. 
The hotel offered a complimentary breakfast which was no frills but fine.
It is also in a great location. Close to everything you could possibly want to see!

My husband and I stayed at Hotel Fusion mid-September 2011. I chose the hotel due to the photos online, general reviews, and location. I wish we spent more money to be in a nicer hotel. 
Check in went well and the front desk allowed us to check in at 10 instead of 3.
Upon first inspection of the room, it appeared trendy and clean. Which it is...but its one of those places you just always feel dirty!
Our view was to other buildings ... almost a courtyard of concrete...and the exhaust fan from a restaurant was spewing greasy air into our room. I had trouble sleeping due to the odor and wanted to switch rooms but my husband wasnt bothered by it so we stayed put.
You can hear everything in the halls, outside, and in the rooms surrounding your room.
 The bathroom is clean but ladies, good luck seeing yourself in the mirror. There is one flouescent light above the mirror in the whole bathroom. Not conducive for putting on makeup and getting ready. The shower has a steady stream of water until the pressure suddenly changes and starts sputtering out in varying temperatures. 
The location is clutch right in the center of Union Square. We were right near everything!
Save your money and stay elsewhere, you might regret booking this hotel like I did!

review_title: Modern very central safe and secure
review_text: Had a single room with a single bed,but quite comfy. Tea and coffee making equipment,fridge,safe,iron and board,fridge,flat screen tv with lots of channel.Window looked out on nothing. Thin walls so you don't want noisy neighbors if you want to sleep,I was lucky. Breakfast was provided,do it yourself stlye. a room on 5th floor had trays,paper plates tea and coffee,milk,instant oats,raisin bread,croissants,danish pastimes apples and oranges.Take it back tok your room to eat.Worked well enough for me until a huge group of mature French tourists arrived and had huge appetites and ate everything one morning,and I was up there at 7-30am.I alerted front deskm and it was soon restocked. Staff very friendly,room and bathroom ver clean. Fluffy big towels. Union Sq. Powell St Bart,Muni and cable care turnaround right outside the door. Free fast wi fi.

We enjoyed our stay at SW hotel. Great location for us right in the middle of Chinatown and walking distance to great restaurants, city centre and Fisherman Wharf. The room was very clean and decor of the room was tasteful. Wifi was great, very fast. Only negative was the $28 per day parking and no coffee making facilities in the room.

review_title: Depends on whether you plan on hanging out in your room or one of the most lively neighborhoods in the city...
review_text: Let me start by saying that I gave the location a 5 for one reason only: I came to SF to eat and play in North Beach! This hotel is perfect for you if you are looking for the same and don't plan on spending much time in your tiny room. There is a parking garage below (an annoying $27) but if you've ever circled this part of the city looking for parking you'll pay it and think nothing more while enjoying a sidewalk meal and trying to interpret exchanges in Italian between octogenarians then sipping your second dark and stormy while (re?)reading Howl at Vesuvio then strolling mere steps back to your room. It's a clean room in a fun part of town... What more do you want?

Would definitely recommend this hotel. Location was spot on for us, bordering Chinatown and North Beach so loads of restaurants close by, and 10 min walk to Union Sq. 
Rooms were ok size (good for central SF), service was excellent

review_title: Poor service, very small rooms, smelly
review_text: Average neighborhood, poor service on checkin-not helpful at all. Rooms very small and have a poor odor. Would not recommend.

This hotel is really value for money. Its main drawing point is the location - we walked everywhere: to Union Square, Chinatown, North Beach, Coit Tower, The Embarcadero... It's a great place to stay if convenience is your main issue. 
The people at the front desk are really nice, the toilets are a little old but still clean, the rooms are on the small side but then again it's not like you'd get a huge room for $60/night, the elevator is a classic and I loved riding it.
Overall, if you are looking for a place to stay in San Fran on the cheap, and one that is centrally located, this is it! I would definitely come back to this hotel.

Can't beat this location especially for the price!!! Close to the Powell st cable cars so easy to get to fishermans wharf, union square only one block away for great shopping!
Yes the hotel is old and a little outdated and does not have modern (alot more expensive) luxuries. But if u haven't got lots to spend it's great plus rooms and bathroom were clean

I am stunned this hotel has anything but very positive reviews! Extremely friendly/helpful staff. Room was very clean (but do remember...this is a European style old character hotel) & absolutely perfect location. I would stay here again in a heart beat!

I stayed for 2 nights, the welcome was very friendly and the room was clean with fresh linen, towels, toiletries etc.
I was travelling alone with a full sightseeing schedule so I wasn't too fussed on creature comforts, my girlfriend turned her nose up a bit when we had a Skype video call (the hotel's free wifi was a bonus) so gents it's not somewhere for a romantic getaway. It has a bit of a university halls of residence feel to the place (people coming and going at all hours in varying states of drunkeness) but as a base for sightseeing it's unbeatable.
The price was very reasonable and with it's excellent location I would definitely stay again.

review_title: Great value for price in an excellent location

We took a room with shared bathroom. It was next to our room and it wasn't bad as I thought..overall we had a great stay and I recommend this hotel to anyone who doesn×³t want to spend a fortion on an hotel.

This place is friendly, has more amenities than a typical courtyard and is walkable to a lot of downtown, moscone center, chinatown and union square attractions. Very nice fitness center for a courtyard. Contemporary urban vibe and happy staff. Great value.

Stayed at this hotel on a quick trip to San Francisco. It is located 2 blocks from Fishermans Wharf, so convenient to that area. It is also very close to the Cable Car and the F Trolley stop if you want to get to the main part of downtown at 5th and Market. The hotel is clean and the staff is very friendly and helpful. We actually got to the hotel at 10:00 in the morning and they allowed us to check in. We asked for a late check out for 1:00 and they didn't hesitate to grant it to us. If you are a preferred member, the biggest down side to this hotel is that they do not have a club. They compensate for this by offering a free breakfast and a free cocktail at the bar. It is a nice substitution, but doesn't completely make up for no lounge.
This area of town can be noisy. With it being two blocks off the main drag for Fishermans Wharf, it is minimized somewhat, but can still be a bit loud since a SFFD station is located right next to the hotel.
Bottom line: If I wanted/needed to be in this area of San Francisco, I would stay here again without hesitation.

Picked this location for proximity to downtown area. Staff very courteous. Had an episode of excessive noise from neighbor one night and hotel staff dealt with issue promptly. Good restaurants nearby. A short walk to Union Square, but a bit of a hike to other parts of town. Bar prices for beer excessive in my opinion, even for a big city. Overall I would stay here again.

review_title: Perfect hotel to see all of San Francisco!!
review_text: This may be the friendliest Marriott I have ever stayed! From the housekeepers to the valet they all smile and say good morning (afternoon) how is your stay? It is walking distance (or cable cars at the wharf or Hyde st) to absolutely everything ( pier 39, Lombard st, union station) yet you off the wharf do you don't get all the tourist traffic. We accomplish all the sites we wanted in two days with the help of the friendly conceige at the Marriott. Important point: this is not the Fairmont, Mark Hopkins etc of Nob Hill. Stayed there before and yes it's nice but THIS is the practical and best value hotel for your money. Only complaint $54 parking and you don't need a car, daughter said the roll away cot was uncomfortable

review_title: Excellent hotel in the heart of San Francisco
review_text:
The view from the street isn't much, in a very touristy part of Powell Street, but the hotel itself and the location are excellent. 
Helpful staff, clean, well decorated and run. Recommended.
tiny rooms. woke up with bites and told mgmt. despite bites on leg and neck they said they had no problems. more bullying and condescending than courteous and helpful.

review_title: Lobby Bar is worth the stay!
review_text:
Love love loved the lobby bar/estaurant! Morgan was so cool, genuine and offered perfect advice on choices. She exemplifies authentic san franciscans!
Hotel a bit old once you get to the room. Typical san fr

Very nice hotel. Very convenient for cable cars and sightseeing. Nice bar, cafe in hotel. Starbucks is also very close by. Did not really enjoy Italian restaurant attached to hotel, food overpriced and quite rude staff behind the bar.

review_title: Not my Favorite CLV Property but...
review_text:
As always the staff was exceptional! Didn't really care for the location, and the room / suite showed signs of wear and tear. 
The Bar Adagio had the most personable Mixologist ever! The food was delicious. The Front desk is staff is fabulous. Wonderful turn down service with Champagne, Rose petals and soft music playing when we returned = perfection.

We visited SF from the UK on our honeymoon and pre-booked 3 nights at the Marriot on Fishermans Wharf. 
The entire hotel is incredibly tasteful decorated and striking.
Having flown for 11 hours, our king bed was heaven. So comfortable - hands down the best hotel bed I've stayed in and that says a lot given that we toured the East Coast in 2007. 
It is conveniently located and just a short manageable walk to the shops, bars and restaurants. A fantastic start to our honeymoon :)

review_title: Nothing special, expect more from a Marriott at this price.
review_text: I travel for business, so spend approximately 150 nights a year in a hotel. I understand value, have reasonable expectations for price paid, and do not expect phenomenal service from a mid level hotel. This hotel still underwhelmed. No real "issues" - just a rather gloomy entrance, rooms with a peeling tub (seriously Marriott????), and EXPENSIVE room service. They are a block or so from F Wharf - but no view, and for the price, I can do better elsewhere. IMO, do not stay in this area, instead stay elsewhere in the city and come to this area during the day. There are so many other great hotels....pick one and take the cable car to visit here.

review_title: Hampton inn without the free breakfast at Marriott prices
review_text: Stayed here for a conference and took my 18 year old son along. First the positives.Very good location- walk to fishermans wharf, north beach, china town if you are a walker. Concierge Pablo was excellent in booking tours, helping with general sightseeing, etc. Other concierge and front desk people also helpful. Hotel was clean. Now the not so goods. For the marriott name and price, hotel did not have the kind of service I'm used to from a Marriott. No real restaurant, though there is room service, no turn down service, room was clean but we had 2 double beds. Small for 2 people and bathroom was so small I banged my knees twice while trying to close the bathroom door . I'm only 4ft11.facility is low rise, only 4 or 5 stories, no good views. I'm not a snob and I like the Hampton inns for road trips. If you expect a Hampton inn type facility with a fancy lobby and bar then that's what this place is but at Marriott prices.
Great service and location. The size and decor of the rooms were great. Nice bar in the lounge.

For the price....its just fine. Locale cannot be beat. Poor internet svc and rooms need updating. Hallways seem dark and borderline scary. As a female traveling alone,would not return. Desk staff quite helpful!
We had a very nice stay at this hotel. We were 5 so we booked 2 rooms. Since the hotel is so centrally located some street noise is heard. Ask to get a room not facing the street.

review_title: Great location, Great Service, Pricey Parking
review_text: My wife and I stayed here 2 nights Friday, Saturday. This is great property in a great location. An easy walk to the Fishermans Wharf, bike rentals and all the water front shopping. We rented bikes for the day and rode to the Farmers Market which is located near Pier 1 about 3 miles from the hotel. We also biked the GGB and spent some time in Sausalito for lunch. We chose to tale the Ferry back to SF. This was well worth the 8.50 per person it was a great opportunity to take some photos of the Bridge and Alkatraz. This was are third stay at this Marriott and it was nice to see some of the same employees from the previous stays. The only negative was that there was no complimentary coffee in the lobby. All in all this is a great stay and we will be back.

That man made such a big impact... The person greeting at the door. I believe he was part of the crew that valets the cars. The hotel was clean, well put together, even the bar soap in the shower .. Nothing I've had before.
I already recommended the hotel :)

review_title: Great for a night but definitely wouldn't be honeymooning here...
review_text: My husband and I & kids aged 12,10, 9 had booked 3 nights but changed to 2 after the 1st night. Let me begin with the positives; good location, big room & the staff were fairly accommodating. complaints would be parking lot-specifically homeless people "living" under our car, restaurant is seriously understaffed and the lack of space in the bathroom. We paid about $210 per night which

review_title: Nice hotel in a great location.
review_text:
This is my forth stay at this hotel. The fact that I keep coming back has to say something about the hotel.
It's a quality hotel in a very good location.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_title: 5 mins from union square, great stay!
review_text: Lovely hotel for our busy stay I'n San Fran loads to do so diddnt spend much time I'n the hotel but was a great base to explore. The staff pointed us I'n the direction of some lovely restaurants and a lovely piano bar at the top of the Wyatt so were very helpful. Very clean and tidy hotel with great service!

This hotel has two separate buildings. On our first of three nights, we were in the annexed building in a room with two double beds. The room was mostly clean; only complaint regarding cleanliness was that there was a bit of hair remaining in the bathroom. The wallpaper was peeling at the corners in the room, and the room fixtures seemed dated. The double beds were incredibly uncomfortable; neither of us slept well. At our request, we switched to a room with one king bed in the main building. The room seemed much more modern, and the bed was marvelously comfortable. The location is *very* touristy, but it is a convenient "home base" for visitors.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_title: Great location to visit Fishermans Wharf area
review_text: Stayed over Veterans Day weekend. Standard HInn rooms, a nice place to crash after a day exploring SF. skip overpriced breakfast and head across the street to Joanie's or walk a block to The Buena Vista. Parking is $40 a night, but you won't find cheap parking anywhere in SF. Convenient to Fishermans Wharf, Marina, Fort Mason, and North Beach - one block to Cable Car
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_title: Fine, but no better than that.
review_text: I was a bit disappointed with the Villa Florence. The room was fine but tired, the bathroom was cramped and old fashioned, the TV was poorly set up. The staff were friendly enough. It was OK, but nothing special, and really quite expensive.

review_title: Relatively cheap and close to the wharf and local transportation.
review_text: We spent 2 nights at this hotel. Window rooms facing the bay can be a bit noisy due to the F-line trains going by every 7-15 minutes, but are otherwise pretty nice for a Holiday Inn. Plenty to do nearby. We highly suggest the USS Pampanio submarine and crab at the Grotto
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_text: This hotel is a great location, but the rooms and hotel itself has a lot to be desired. We were put on level 7 (top level) and asked for a quite room as its our honeymoon tour. The room is quite loud even though it's facing the back, the tv is ancient with it being impossible to change channel, the aircon/heater is also ancient wall unit that takes about an hour to warm up! The bathroom is tiny and the shower is in the bath! There is a shower curtain, I didn't know they still existed! The staff are friendly and the local great but the room is very over priced and very very dated!

We stayed at the Adagio for seven nights. We arrived tired from the Uk but check in was a pleasure. The guy( tall European guy) should be royally paid by Hotel Adagio, he was informative, efficient and caring, knowing exactly the right pitch for the client. 
We had a very large room on the tenth, the bed was extremely comfortable and the bed linen was good. As advertised there was an iPod dock, free Internet, coffee machine, alarm clock etc, all making our stay easier. The room was clean but not sparkling, a very through clean would be welcomed. We had loads of hanging and drawer space, were able to stash the suitcases in the wardrobe area. The bathroom hAd had a make over and was adequate but not fantastic the towels were ok only. 
The location is brilliant for travelling around San francisco, it is on the edge of the Tenderloin but don't let this alarm you, you'll see homeless people but it felt totally safe. 
The reason I give the hotel a five is the reception staff, they were always helpful and knowledgeable, I don't like fuss but love efficiency and every request was efficiently dealt with promptly. They added to the ease of my holiday

review_title: Very nice with a few flaws
review_text:
I stayed in the annex which is just around the corner, and I thought a slightly better location than the main building. My room was spacious, clean, and quiet. The bed was comfortable and I had excellent sleeping conditions. Bathroom facilities were better than average, furnishings were in good condition. No fridge or microwave, old-style TV with HBO among the 35 channels. Denny's in the building open 24 hours, and you're a short walk from dozens of restaurants, Trader Joe's, and Safeway.
My biggest disappointments: the free Internet was very slow at all times during my 3 day stay. It reminded me of dial-up, or "borrowing" somebody's wifi from out the hotel window. Also the 2 elevators in the annex are inadequate for the traffic. 
If you like the bustling touristy Fisherman's Wharf area you're right in the middle of it. If you prefer the center of San Francisco you are a short ride away on the historic trolley cars of the F line that stops a half-block away ($2) or ride the cable car that's 2 blocks away ($6).
Try to avoid bringing a car to San Francisco...who needs $3.50/hr parking meters and $45/night hotel parking? 
Even though Fisherman's Wharf was not my favorite part of the city, I'd be happy to stay at this hotel again. I do wish they'd fix their Internet.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_text: I was treated awfully at this hotel and turned out on the street simply because I did not have a credit card as security. I had ample cash to pay for the room & leave a deposit but apparently that wasn't good enough. I was reduced to tears by the whole situation but the bureaucratic a-hole at the front desk was unmoved.

review_title: Charming Hotel, great location and great price.
review_text: We stayed at the Andrews this past weekend and really enjoyed this older charming hotel. Comfortable bed ( better than a many of the 4*s we have stayed in lately. Awesome shower, in terms of hot water and pressure. Nice continental breakfast served on each floor. General Manager and weekend day woman working the front desk were very pleasant and helpful. The restaurant downstairs was great with really friendly staff all the way throughout the restaurant. Would definitely stay here again for a couples weekend!

The moment my wife and I walked in with our backpacks we were given the once over look by the staff at reception as if we weren't good enough for their hotel. And no we were not poorly dressed.
Perhaps I should have reminded them they are a mid range hotel at $140 a night and not anything above.
The room we had was a dogbox and the smallest I have ever stayed in. Breakfast???? So they call serving a few muffins, pastries and fruit breakfast?? I don't think so.
Then to top it off our room rate jumped from 140 to $389 per night for the same room all because there was some stupid conference on in town. The hotel thought it was a great opportunity to rip us off obviously and did so.
A few weeks later I returned to San Francisco and needless to say I stayed elsewhere.
I passed on the thought a dogbox room, snobby staff and being ripped off again.
They think they are better than they actually are.

review_title: Great location and service but very historical building
review_text:
Stayed for a weekend, when checking in staff was very friendly and helpful. Excellent service! 
The hotel itself has a very historical vibe. The room is def not luxurious or modern. The trash wasn't properly emptied when we arrived. Not impressed with the room.
The location is great for the price, walking distance from downtown where all the really nice shopping areas are, Chinatown, and it took us an hour and over some hills but we walked to fisherman's wharf and the crooked street in one day. The have a quaint complementary continental breakfast on every floor every morning.

We select this hotel based on its location and it was an excellent choice. We arrive in the afternoon after a long day on the road, checking was quick and easy. They asked if it was our first visit to SF and when we told them that in fact it was, they upgrade us to a junior suit. The also gave us a couple of bottles of wine on the house when we told them this was our honey moon. Very good reception service!
Our room was really good, big bed, all extras and some very good toiletries :)
It's within 5 minutes walking of union square and all attractions with plenty of restaurants near by. I will really recommend it, will also book it if I come back!

review_title: The good and the bad. The right fit.
review_text:
Spent three days and got exactly what we wanted.
Great:
Got in around 9 am and there was a room ready for us. Ended up being a king with a view of the brick wall which we didnt mind.
The location was great for public transportation and getting to all the tourist highlights. Bars were close too. 
Liked the lobby and room decor and athmosphere.
Bad:
The walls are a bit dirty.
There was a hole in our sheet.
No laundry bags.
Towels weren't changed daily.
Could hear hall noise.
Random notes:
Do not go to the tenderloin. Saw feces on three occasions.
Found a $100 behind our tv. Returned it to front desk.
Conclusion: good for middle expectations. Hip option if you arent looking for a chain. We would reccommend it.

review_title: Everything you need except space and a bathtub.
review_text:
This is a very adequate hotel in a decent location near Embarcadero. This hotel is fine but, I don't believe it should be rated three and a half stars, which Priceline does. I give it three only because of the amenities.
Very small room, but everything we needed in it. Ours had a queen bed, desk, microwave, refrigerator. The bathroom is small with a shower but, no tub.
My complaints: the toilet kept running after flushed, a light bulb was burned out, and the grout in the shower floor seemed dirty. 
Regarding the service, they were friendly but gave us bad information a couple of times.
The upside: free water on each floor, secure floors, a bar/restaurant next door which is accessible through the hotel, and access to free internet and printer.

An older hotel with smaller rooms, but it has a great feel to it. Located near Union Square, it's close to everything. Rooms are clean and service is very professional. Would recommend to travelers on a budget.

The room is huge, well, at least for San Francisco standard and the price I paid. I stayed here twice in a week and one time I got a king size room and one two queen size room. Both rooms are big, probably over 300sqf. The hotel is about 7min walk to Union Square where all the shops are but you will see a lot of homeless on the way. They don't attack you though. The rooms I had are very clean, but the carpet in the elevators smells really bad - they should definitely consider changing the carpet there.

review_title: Good hotel in a great location
review_text: Thought this was a really good hotel. We stayed in the part on Beach Street which looked a little newer than the main building. Clean room, housekeeping did a great job and were very friendly. Hotel is in a great location so we were able to get to all the usual tourist spots easily. No issues with noise or other guests. Can't comment on the Denny's restaurant as we wouldn't choose to eat their food anyhow but I guess you get what you pay for in there. Definitely recommend hotel.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_text: This hotel is in a great location for a lot of popular tourist spots (Alcatraz, Pier 39, Ghiradelli Square, etc) but it is NOT worth the price. It is a little run down, our bathroom was dirty (hair on the floor, water spilled on the counter) upon our arrival and the room smelled really bad. Several of the staff members were VERY rude when we asked them questions or needed something. They act like tourists are a huge inconvenience to them and definitely won't go out of their way to help. The restaurant is VERY overpriced although our server (Lorene, I think her name was) was very nice & helpful. Don't waste your money, stay somewhere else.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_title: U get what u pay for
review_text: This hotel was fine.....I payed $100/night in San Francisco. The front desk staff was awesome, it was clean, the rooms were small. I was in SF for a conference, I spent no time in the room. Ok for business, not for a romantic getaway.
