review_title: Good, budget hotel near Union Square
review_text:
We stayed here for 2 nights in late April. The rooms are pretty small and the bathrooms, particularly the showers are tiny but it was all fine for 2 nights - you couldn't really unpack or spread out! Breakfast is laid out on each floor from 7am and they have small pastries, fruit, juice and coffee - enough to keep you going. The area was fine, best to walk left on exiting the hotel towards Union Square and walk along Post St. We took a taxi from SFO to the hotel, it
cost 45 dollars including tip. The staff were pleasant but you had the feeling they'd rather be somewhere else, and who can blame them in such a great city.
I love the location! The rooms are a little small but they are clean. The hotel is well maintained and overall good value.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_text: We were staying in the second building on beach st which we actually preferred. Denny's restaurant was in the lobby and was great value for money and very convenient for breakfast. Rooms were clean, with a choice of pillow. Guest laundry was a bonus as well. It was only a short walk to either cable car turn around and pier 39 was only minutes away. Lack of fridge in the room was the only negative in what was an enjoyable stay.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_title: If you enjoy a goodnight sleep, then don't stay here.
review_text:
Pro: location and that's pretty much it.
Cons: Small rooms with even a bathroom the size a closet ( not a walk in closet)
Paper thin wall and no concept for insulation- its currently midnight and I'm hearing the guy next door on his laptop talking to whoever he can get a hold of. They also have a club on the 21st floor that you hear until they close. They just renovated the club, they only left out the noise reduction part.
Poor customer service
Internet is 10 a day but parking even for guests is 55 bucks (and for 55 bucks it takes over a half hour to get your car).
No ammenities for the customer like a coffee
Save your money and stay at a Holiday Inn than here, at least there you will not be reviewing your hotel when you should be enjoying a goodnight sleep.
I wouldn't recommend it to my enemy.
hotel_name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text:
Stayed for 3 nights as part of a Cosmos/Archers/Globus coach trip called Western Wonders. 
Hotel was in a great location with many amenities within walking distance. The staff were very helpful, it had free wifi if you were a Kimpton in touch member. 
Our room was huge, the bed comfortable but the bathroom was tiny. The view of Macy's from the 12th floor was great at night. The windows are single glazed and street noise could be heard. Other visitors and reviews mentioned not to have a room on the top 3 floors due to the noise from the Starlight Lounge on floor 21 as there is little or no soundproofing. 
All In all a good stay and would stay again.
hotel_name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: Great location, good service, very nice room
review_text: We enjoyed a 3 night stay in a deluxe room on the 17th floor and didn't experience any of the negatives that others have suffered. The location is excellent, making access to the sites and best eating precincts easy via cable car or just walking. The view was really nice but you could hear some outside noise at night. This didn't bother us.
hotel_name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: We stayed four nights and got a good deal on Priceline for the room. The rooms are small, but the hotel was built in 1928 so that is expected. The room and hotel were both very clean and the room was decorated nicely. The location is perfect for touring the city. It is very close to Chinatown and North Beach and the Cable Car stop to head to the wharf is right out front! Great stay and would definitely stay here again.
hotel_name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: Good service, comfy bed, clean room, SF charm, old quirky hotel.
review_text:
The most important things were done well:
Clean room.
Comfy Bed (soft cotton sheets/duvet).
Free Wi-Fi in rooms.
Good (and fast) room service.
Secondary things were quirky:
Ice machines were broken on several floors, but they would bring ice if you called.
Valet garage was offsite, so service was slow getting in and out.
Bathroom was tiny and the tub overlay was badly chipped.
Would stay again for a great rate, $125-$150 seems about right on Priceline. Remember, parking is about $50/night.
hotel_name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: It was our 1st time in San Fran & I would recommend the Holiday Inn to everyone.. Steps away from fishermans wharf & a few blocks from the cable car. The staff were all very pleasent and helpful, free Wi-Fi & couldn't complain about the room at all, it was spacious & clean! Was very happy with our stay and if we get a chance to go back there would be no question as to where I would b staying!
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_text:
I missed my plane to Thailand and got stuck in San Francisco for 2 days! I was very upset about that before I got a room at this hotel! They made my stay in SF so special ! Leif, the concierge , was the best ever! He managed to put me in ease with my unexpected adventure, and advised some awesome things for me to do in those two days! He was so sincerely interested in me having a great time, it's was very touching and I appreciate it a lot! Sorry, it's took a few months for me to wright a review, but I do have a greatest memories of my stay at this hotel because of the people and the service! I wouldn't even try to find the better place to stay next time I am in SF! And, by the way, I didn't have a change of clothes with me, so, they did my laundry and gave me a beautiful animal print oversized bathrobe to use! (at no charge!) maybe I looked too pitiful!? I loved this hotel and people working there!
Special thanks for Leif! He turned my trouble into the unexpected treat!!!
hotel_name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: Bad experience I wish I had picked somewhere else:(
review_text: This hotel is poor. The only thing it has is it's location. We were given a smelly room right across from a very busy nightclub with noise and music until 3/4 am. When I spoke to the manager she acted like a robot and offered to take my car park fee off? She said if I had called the desk during the night they may have been able to fix it??? Don't stay here!
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_text: Old hotel could tell it has been newly remodeled. Great location in Union Square across from awesome diner.
hotel_name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: Perfect location, small room good service. Average value.
hotel_name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: We stayed here for 3 nights. Had a room overlooking road and were woken up at 2am by the bin men so asked to change rooms the following day to a courtyard room which was alot better. Good location for fishermans wharf, quite a basic hotel but you don't spend much time in your room in Sanfransisco as there is too much to do
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_title: Walking in the doors, the lobby is jaw dropping and the service is refreshingly exceptional!
review_text: We loved it here! The staff is great, the rooms are spacious and very clean. I would recommend booking in advance for good prices and staying here for a couple of days!
hotel_name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: Stayed here for 4 days, would definitely use again if I return to San Francisco. It is in walking distance to fishermans wharf and plenty of restaurants. It is round the corner from where u catch the bus loops tours which was great for us. The hotel was very clean and nice room, nothing special but as long as it was clean that was all we wanted. Didn't eat in the hotel as weren't really there, restaurant looked nice but did seem bait over priced for a holiday inn.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_text: Great location so they get two stars. Stayed in room 1133--extreanly small and right next to the elevator. I was up the entire night--worse hotel night sleep ever. When I asked for a room change they gave ms ear plugs. Really ear plugs....
hotel_name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text:
We Were ther recently. Was crowded and they put us on "annex" across the street and was strange.
Prices are little higher but correct as a Holiday Inn can be
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_title: Un hotel muy caro para dormir...
review_text:
El hotel en general esta en muy buenas condciones:sus habitaciones son muy limpias y de muy buena caliidad,el problema son sus servicios,el restaurante solo sirve desayunos de mediana calidad hasta las 10 a.m. Y el resto del dia esta cerrado.el bar cierra a las 11 p.m. Asi que si quieres tomarte un trago o una cerveza despues de esa hora tienes que salir del hotel o simplemente irte a dormir..el costo del estacionamiento es un verdadero atraco,mas de 50 dolares por dia...en fin, creo que los 316 dolares que pague por habitacion por noche (sin incluir el estaconamiento) no valen con mucho la calidad del servicio que recibimos..en el courtyard.  Companias hoteleras estafar a sus visitantes..

review_title: Perfect location and excellent customer service
review_text: Just finished a two night stay. Chris who works at the front desk was quite helpful during our stay. Hotel is lively and scala's downstairs has amazing food. Would stay again!
hotel_name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: we were visiting from uk, were greeted by friendly staff. rooms very large and bed comfy. very clean. free own internet avail and free internet computers with printers anytime. concierge helpful. pool area nice and clean bit cold in may but we used it , towels provided. bar ok but closed early and not used much. restaurant bit pricey but plenty of eateties within minutes. great hotel.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_title: Poor excuse for a remodel, awful service
review_text: I LOVE Kimpton hotels. This hotel is a disgrace to the Kimpton Family. Though calling ahead several times my room was not ready as promised. Upon arriving I could not get a valet, then was not even offered bell help. The room was dreary, my window was so filthy they covered it up. The workmanship of the remodel was unacceptable and the bathroom was dirty. My early arrival/day in san Francisco was ruined. Luckily a room opened up at Hotel Palomar a "real" Kimpton hotel. I promptly moved. Thanks for ruining the beginning of my short weekend away. Remodel should be used loosely. The staff from curb to check out was disgraceful.
hotel_name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: It's not the Hilton but it's not bad
review_text: For the money you save by not staying at a bigger name hotel, you can take a lot of tours and have plenty of change left for nightly sundaes at nearby Gihradelli's. Very clean rooms, great locale, and friendly staff. No regrets for staying here from this traveller!
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_title: Perfect for a first trip to San Fran
review_text:
Came here as part of our tour of California and what a way to start!
Right near Union Square, Chinatown and the cable car route. Perfect.
The staff were incredibly friendly and held a wine reception for guests every evening.
The room had real character - and that's not code for falling apart! It really felt like you were in SF and not some bland hotel that could be anywhere in the world.
Very clean, decent sized room and great value for money.
Would definitely stay here again. Thanks so much for an amazing stay.

Come in alte recensioni di cui sopra, ho trovato il Clift un bell' albergo di design se ci si limita al piano terra. Camere e bagni piccoli e neanche ben curati (vasca scrostata). Essendo luogo cool la sera si trasforma in disco bar; o vi aggregate alla mischia o ballate nel letto! Mi aspettavo di meglio

Threadbare notted rough sheets with terribly uncomfortable spring mattress.....no water, ice or coffee available for room. Superficial clean, but noticed so much dirt behind bed while plugging in the fan. Desk men were very, very polite and helpful with dinner suggestions. Good location. Would not stay there again. Laura from Pittsburgh.

review_title: Nice, clean place. Great for those driving.
review_text: Nice, clean and comfortable rooms. Free parking is good for those who drive. Location not exactly the most convenient.
free parking, decent rates, clean rooms, noisy street but its close to a lot of tourist spots, good area versus union square dowtown area. greayt value and great service.

review_title: Very nice hotel, friendly staff, conveniently located
review_text: First time I stayed here and was very surprised at the location, cleanliness of the rooms, friendly and helpful staff. Buses close by. 28 or 43 takes you to the presido or golden gate. One block away take bus 30 to Pier 39, north beach, Chinatown and union square. Great shops and restaurants within blocks In each direction I will stay again

Was drawn to Hotel Del Sol due to its reviews, but I honestly must have been at a different hotel! First it was not very clean -- cobwebs, spots of who knows what on the walls, trash under the pull out couch. The pool and pool area was nasty! Secondly, it was very small -- our room was billed as a junior suite -- that was a joke! The bathroom door hit the toilet when opened. There was virtually no drawer space. According to my children, the pull out coach was like sleeping on metal. Thirdly, the NOISE--between the drunks yelling up and down the street and it sounding like our upstairs neighbors were in the room with us- we were barely able to sleep. I guess the only good thing was the free parking but would have preferred to pay for parking and stayed somewhere closer to Fisherman's Wharf or on that direction! Also made a complaint to the hotel and have never heard back!
hotel_name: Hotel Del Sol, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: Great hotel if you have car
review_text: Stayed here 3 nights, we were overall happy with it, the free parking was the selling point for us as parking fees in SF can be ridiculous, the continental breakfast was also very good. The location is the only downer being a 15/20 min walk from fishermans wharf, if you dont like walking hills then get a cab :) when we went the weather was great high 20's just touching the 30's (90f) so the walking around was hard but we are young so managed it :)
hotel_name: Hotel Del Sol, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: A nice motel if you're traveling with kids...
review_text:
We stayed for 3 days in the family room with 3 kids. They had a blast since there were games, movies, books, toys, and the decor in the kids room was very appropriate for them. For the adults though, the mattress was not so good, the covers and linen was not hotel like but I guess more like in a cheap motel. The towels were cheap, the main room was crowded. Parking was also a problem. The in building parking was always full and had to park across the street, raining and all as it did those 3 days. The service was not bad per se. The people were very friendly but just there were not many services, no room service, bell boys or valet as in a hotel. Location was very convenient. 
I would recomend it to a large family as ours if you don't mind the precariourness of the ammenities.
hotel_name: Hotel Del Sol, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: I've never driven in SF and was a little nervous about it. It was super easy to get to the Hotel, and to park. We used muni for most of our stay which was fine, good busses nearby, plus my 7 and 5 yr old walked to Fisherman's Wharf once (not back!). My kids LOVED the hotel. They spent a lot of time in the pool, and loved the breakfast and cookies and lemonade. I liked that when the knob broke on our shower it was fixed immediately, and the room was very clean. Staff were very pleasant and accommodating. This place is a lot brighter and more family- oriented than other Joie De Vivre hotels we have stayed at- maybe not the place for a romantic getaway- but otherwise terrific!
hotel_name: Hotel Del Sol, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text:
We had a wonderful stay while at The Del Sol, the room was clean, a little on the small side but just right for a couple. The bright colors are refreshing twist from the rest of the city and everytime we entered the enclosure it really did feel like an oasis. Few downsides, our door would only fully close if you slammed it hard, I'm sure other hotel guests didn't appreciate our coming and going. Also location was at times a challenge, it's a great walk to both the wharf and golden gate, but taxis were a constant challenge even If you called the company directly. Muni the public transit was actually the best way to navigate the city, it was efficient and affordable, with only the occasional crazy. The staff was very
 friendly and the small breakfast served featured great muffins and juice. Overall a great stay!
hotel_name: Hotel Del Sol, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: Hotel del Sol offers a fun stay in a dynamic neighborhood.
review_text:
Stayed here for a few days and enjoyed it very much. The location in the Marina district is close to restaurants, bars and cafes. The price includes breakfast of pastries, yogurt and hot drinks. The front desk staff are very helpful with arranging transportation, recommendations etc. Free parking is available which is rare in SFO.
Rooms are very clean with an emphasis on green living. Oh, also a heated pool and kid friendly and spend some time in the hammock!
hotel_name: Hotel Del Sol, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: This is the perfect getaway, shopping and family hotel. We go to the city with another family, twelve of us, this this was the perfect venue. Close to shopping, the cable car, testifies at Union Square. Everyone was nice and helpful,from the valet, doorman and front desk. The bar next door even reopened for us for a late night libation...so so fun. We also were able to be our crazy selves in the lobby lounge area. This will now be our annual go to hotel for the holidays!
Typical of the chain. Great service very accommodating staff, perfect location. The rooms are not large, but they are well appointed.

I can appreciate a boutique hotel, and as such did not mind the more 'historic' size and ammenities. What I do mind, however, is propaganda. The Kimpton Group choses to publish an make available its magazine 'Life and People'. The magazine pushed a liberal progressive agenda that would make FDR blush. No expense was spared to publish and deliver this garbage, unfortunatey upgrdes were not made to provide a comfortable room. The bed was a tiny torture machine.

review_title: Great location, but way too noisy.
review_text: The first room we were given was on level 2 facing the street - which was very noisy. Within 5 minutes of arriving I went back to reception and the quickly changed me to another room on the same floor facing the back - the downside this time a really noisy kitchen fan and a bad room configuration - tv was immediately on the left. I was then moved to level 4 in front of the lift and was presented by the noise of people coming in and out of the lift. Overall a really lovely and clean hotel with very accommodating staff, but the quirkiness of it being an old building with a bad layout doesn't work for me. Walls, doors and windows paper thin so don't expect a good nights sleep unless you bring earplugs!

review_title: Brill location and value for money! Would defiantly stay again!!!
review_text:
Stayed for 6 nites in November, had a great time and would defiantly stay again! Hotel is in brilliant location, could not be better and loved everything about our stay! 
Did not have a problem with the size if our room as we has too much fun enjoying San Francisco to be sitting in our room. Was fine for 2 people and our luggage. 
If we get the chance to return we would def stay here again! 
Loved the handy baskets in the room to take to the shower. We had shared bathroom rooms and never once had a problem with waiting for the bathroom. 
Would recommend this hotel to anyone who would rather spend their money on seeing the sights of this amazing place rather than a room.

review_title: Brilliant hotel, amazing value for money!
review_text:
We booked this particular hotel more because of the low cost rather than recommendations, the location or anything else and was pleasantly surprised by the quality of the hotel, the service and it's location.
The room was fairly basic but modern, comfy and the perfect base for a couple sightseeing around San Fran.
The staff are friendly and there is the nice added touch of free coffee and muffins in the reception each morning.
I would stay there again and recommend to friends!

review_title: Fantastic location and a great price. Valet parking a bit pricey.
review_text: Stayed here for one night and perfectly located right near Fishermans wharf and right near the cable car terminus. So when you've finished at Ghiradelli Square, Fishermans Wharf and Pier 39 you can catch the Cable Car to Union Square, Market Street or Chinatown. You can then catch the F line back around the esplanade back in a loop. Breakfast was included in my bill and was excellent buffet style. Room was nice, bed was king and roomy. I had the executive suite (upgrade) which had a sitting room. My only issue was that an occasional table had cup 'rings' on it where it hadn't been wiped properly from the previous guest. A bit unusual for Hyatt. Rest of the room was to Hyatt's normal high standards. Valet parking seemed expensive at $45 which was added about 30% more to the overall room cost. If you dont need a car then there are plenty of options to get around, but connection to airport would be a challenge from this lcation only using public transport. Would definitely stay here again.

review_title: Great location for a reasonable price.
review_text: The hotel is in an excellent location, just steps from Union Square. The rooms are small, but comfortable. Having the shared bathroom wasn't as bad as I thought it would be. The BART stop is right around the corner (Powell St. stop). The building is old and you seem to be able to hear everything like people going down the stairs and doors opening and closing. Nonetheless its definitely worth it if you plan to be out and about in the city.

Just checked in today, used lobby restroom while my husband was checking in. While walking down the hallway the strongest urine smell hit me! Not a great first impression. Got worse, the bldg is old and looks it. Not like most kimptons. Don't use this hotel!!

review_title: Buono in generale, poco chiara la questione dell'addebito della prima notte
review_text: L'albergo Ã¨ buono, abbastanza centrale, pulito, stanze spaziose, ed il personale disponibile, non ho capito perchÃ© addebitano la prima notte prima di andare e poi al pagamento fanno pagare il totale e non la differenza. Al momento i soldi del primo prelievo non li ho ancora riavuti e sono andato via da 10 giorni

I have stayed here twice now in the last couple of years and have enjoyed it on each occasion.The hotel is ideal for exploring the city with good bus and cable car services a short stroll away.The rooms may be a little small but they are clean and comfortable,the staff are always friendly with a great front desk,would look to stay here again if I'm ever back in San Fran.
hotel_name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text:

hotel_name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: Great location near good restaurants. Very accessible to Muni transportation. Has heated pool, hot tub and workout room. Staff is very helpful. Go to concierge for help about local attractions and restaurants

A musty, old unrenovated hotel, not up to the Kimpton's usual boutique standards. It's on the Tenderloin (read: dodgy) side of Union Square. The real problem is that the place is old and badly in need of renovation. Our room was small and cramped. It smelled strongly of perfumed disinfectant, but not enough to disguise the disgusting odor of cat-litter box, which never abated. Not a bargain at price.

Having been to the Hyatt in Australia I had high expectations coming to this one, unfortunately the level of quality and features was very disappointing . The room lacked the following :
1- no mini bar fridge ( useful when you want to store your own drinks and food )
2- no iron included 
3- tv reception on many channels was bad
4- no bath, just shower
Final verdict, I would have chosen holiday inn express opposite it for half the price as I stayed in there last year so could compare the 2

review_title: More than Comfortable in Great Location
review_text: We stayed here on our first night in CA before heading north to wine country. The rooms were very clean, staff was friendly and helpful, and the bed was just what we needed to rest up before our vacation. It was a bit pricy, but worth it.

Get room 819 if able best room in hotel
Close to everything making a great central starting point
Small rooms at about 120 sqft
Close to BART and other public transportation

This hotel is centrally located in downtown San Francisco and is convenient to shopping, great restaurants, and transit. We were amazed at how quiet the room was, considering staying in downtown. The hotel staff is very friendly. If you are looking for a quaint, neat, and affordable place to stay while in San Francisco, certainly give this hotel a try! I will definitely stay at this hotel again in the future!

The staff were fun and extremely helpful. The wine reception at night they do is a blast! Its in a great location, we went to some great restaurants and union square is only a 10 min walk. The hotel is unique and clean and overall is excellent value for money. Only downside is slow wifi that drops.
hotel_name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text:
Fun staff. Wine in the evening. Way too expensive.
If you follow the street to the north a Saturday night. You can find a party or happening.
hotel_name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text:
The staff was very friendly and helpful. Couldn't do enough for you. Our inroom coffee pot did not work and within 15 min it was replaced. 
Only issue was in the bathroom. They ask you re use your towels but there is only one hook and no towel bar to let them dry! Also the in ceiling shower head was a little enemic. 
Would definately reccommend

review_title: Not Worthy of a Four Star Rating
review_text: This hotel was a big disappointment. The room was drab, depressing, and smelled like a cat litter box. The view we were lucky enough to get was of a wall and old pipes that were noisy. The water was luke warm and the toilet cluncked ever few minutes. Room Service dessert was sub-par and not at all worth the price. Worst, upon check out we were unable to use the public guest living room area while waiting for our airport shuttle due, to a private meeting. Had to stand in the small lobby area near the door for a half hour. Staff did not offer alternate seating arrangements and were less than friendly. Very uncomfortable and will not stay at this place again. The best part of our stay here was the check out....do yourself a favor and stay somewhere else!!!
Made our stay in San Francisco very pleasant nice hotel in a good location shortish walk to union square bit longer on the way back and very friendly staff
hotel_name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: If your after the generic feel of the average hotel, this is not the hotel for you. It has a lovely old feel to it, all be it abit noisy. One thing it lacked was a bar! It's set in the prime area of San francisco- the pictures you see of a steep hill with cable cars on it is at the end of the road! At the bottom of the hill is the subway which is so easy to use, and the buses to places such as the golden gates bridge go from the next block. Also the cable car stop is at the bottom of the hill (Powell street). Only thing I would say is that the area is not suitable for those with walking difficulties as the whole of San francsico is exceptionally hilly.

This hotel is centrally located and makes it very easy to get around the city. It is very close to the pier and cable cars. The rooms are clean and comfortable. The bathroom in our room was a bit awkward as the door opened into the room. There was also no ventilation in the bathroom which made it difficult to use after a shower. There are lots of places to eat in the area (Scoma, Ghirardelli, great happy hour at the hotel bar).

review_title: Fine for a single person short stay
review_text:
Attended a convention at Moscone Center and The Mosser was conveniently close by a block. Easy BART access from both SFO or OAK since the Powell station is half a block away. Loved the central Market St and Union Sq locale. Adjacent to the much pricier Kimpton and Marriott hotels. Overall the age, ambiance and size of rooms reminded me of those old Ivy League college dorms ... shared baths, narrow halls, creaky narrow stairs, slow elevators and cool urban vibe.
Desk staff were all very friendly and helpful. Housekeeping kept the place tidy although the beige and brown checkered carpet throughout made the place feel dated. Furniture also showing some wear. This place is a step above a hostel.
The Deluxe Queen I reserved was the size of my children's bedroom at home. Smallest hotel room I've ever slept in. If my spouse joined me we would have found it too cramped. Barely enough room for the queen platform bed and one easy chair by the bay window that overlooked the small side street. 
Happy I reserved a private bath. Good sized soaking tub and shower. But smallest sink ever .... just like a tiny sink in a camping RV. Couldn't wash my face without dripping water onto the floor. Had to be careful when brushing my teeth.
Room itself was well insulated from street noise. I was in room 609 and only heard the AM trash truck. 
There is no air conditioning but opening the single window and activating the ceiling fan permitted sufficient air. Doing so allowed in lots of street noise unfortunately.
Would I return? Yes if I was traveling alone and looking for rate under $200 in downtown SF near a central BART station. Its an adventurous hotel to try if you're willing to give up space and certain conveniences like a gym, pool, and large public lobby.

We were shocked by the size of the hotel room, we'd never seen a room in the States so small. Two average sized suitcases just about filled the floor space.
The hotel however was kept spotlessly tidy and clean and the bed was very comfy. We were on the back but my other half said she found it too noisey, it didn't bother me as afterall it is in the middle of a city.
We didn't realise when we booked that we'd have to share the toilet/bathroom facilities with the rest of the corridor though it was never a problem as we were always up bright and early.
Disappointed there were no tea/coffee facilities in the room.
If we were ever to re-visit we would ensure we had a room with an ensuite.
The coffee and muffins served each day in the lobby are extraordinarily poor. The coffee has no taste and the muffins are heavy and stodgy (yuk!) and everdays like groundhog day... same coffee same muffins. After day 1 of 4 I couldn't bring myself to attempt them again I just watched the other guests faces as they tackled them.
Locationwise if you want to shop you are slap bang in the middle of everything (fall out of bed & your in Bloomingdales!). You could not be more perfectly placed.

review_title: Comfy bed, clean room and good value!
review_text: We have eaten at the resident Saha Restaurant several times (lots of great vegan options) and this trip decided to try the hotel. We have enjoyed the wine reception before while waiting for our table in the restaurant, and this time we were legit guests! Staff extremely friendly and not trying to ferret out who is legit or not and that makes for a generous spirit in the place. Nice lobby with fireplace and couches. Our room was large for SF, very clean and NO SAGGY BED. We slept great. We could clearly hear the guests talking in the next room and assume they could hear us. But we all went to sleep at the same time so no trouble there. One special touch is the water dispenser on each floor. I am picky about water and we believe this was reverse osmosis machine with both boiling and cold water. No need to shlep bottles of water to your room. This is a big thing to me. No street noise in our room 517. Extra blankets in the closet (we don't like pouffy comforters). I like the dispensers in the bath - seems less wasteful of resources to me. Coffee makes in room but I walked 5 blocks where there was local place Quetzal, Peet's or Starbucks. We will definitely return.
hotel_name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: Ideal location for first time San Francisco visitors!
review_text:
Just finished a 4 night stay and very happy with our choice of accommodations. Location is fabulous, 2 blocks to Fisherman's Wharf, all MUNI transit systems (bus, trolley, streetcar) within a block. Knuckle's sports bar serves a fabulous Cobb salad and with linens! Only downside, Internet was $10 / day so we visited our friendly neighborhood Starbuck's around the corner.
Our room only had a large shower which was fine for us but if you like to soak in a tub, would be disappointing.

review_title: Immaculate and convenient and an all star concierge staff
review_text: Arrived via BART which stops right outside the Hyatt Regency. As do the cable cars, subway trolleys and buses. Great views of the bay, excellent restaurants nearby. Try Sinbads for lunch, it needs updated but food is excellent and reasonable. Rooms are large and the cafe is excellent too, though pricey. I had a convention rate which made it affordable
I stayed in this hotel with my daughter and found the rooms very spacious, clean and accessible. The only negative comment I have was the lack of a universal socket for my laptop.
Good spot in Fishermans Wharf and close to transport and attractions. Friendly staff. Big, comfy bed.

My husband and I stayed at this hotel over a long Memorial Day weekend. Our flight was cancelled due to bad weather. The hotel was very accommodating about changing our check in and check out dates. The room is neatly decorated, not the biggest, but not teeny tiny either. It is perfect for two people.
Other positive things:
The hotel itself is quite cute.
They provide a wine hour with decent wines (I prefer white).
The restaurant is AWESOME, decorated swanky, and served some of the best food I had the entire trip.
The price can't be beat.
The iffy:
The neighborhood isn't the greatest, but is in walking distance of a lot of cool stuff and major bus lines.
Bring your own shampoo and soaps. I didn't care for the quality.
The music during the wine hour is um...creative.
I would recommend this hotel if you're on a budget, are going as a couple, and are open to walking around in different types of neighborhoods. If your the type of person who has to stay at a chain in the middle of the shopping tourist district, this isn't the hotel for you.
hotel_name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: Noisy, run down room and things taken from room.
review_text:
Unfortunately after a day out we returned to find our liquor had been taken, not just a little bit but two bottles at one litre each completly gone. I went straight to front desk and even thought they were most professional i got the feeling that it wasnt uncommon. I was required to call house keeping to enquire to what happened to them the next day and no one really seemed to concerned that someone had helped them self to it. The amount was credited against my account but still feel pretty disappointed that this happened.
 In regards to the actual room it is a very basic but acceptable room. As previously mentioned paper thin walls and we could hear everything the next room was talking about. Not just noise but clearly understand every word.
hotel_name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: Very bad service, disorganized & will never go back
review_text:
The service here is so low I have never paid for such place with such poor standards. It was like a hostel service not a hotel!
First after 22hrs flying they wouldn't check me in until they had credit card authorization, then they wanted cash for the room even though it was showing up as paid with my bank. Then the room was not serviced for 3 days - I had to call the front desk to ask for them to turn it down! Then after 22hr flight someone rang my room at 7am, then someone tried to open my door while I slept one morning saying sorry wrong room. 
Then my shower did not work on check in, the maintenance guy they sent spent 25mins with me in my bathrobe saying 'sorry it's a hotel built 70yrs ago. Then my room swipe card didn't work on last day & they seemed put out to get me new one!
Then on check out they wanted the initial credit card payment again! I was aghast by this stage that my credit card payment had to be fought for 3 times in 4 days.
Then my airport shuttle they booked is 30mins late, maybe not the hotels fault but again they have partner services that are unreliable.
Location & deco style was good, but since just accross the street is Marriott for only $10 more a night & this place has no hotel quality service - AVOID if you can.

I'm sure the price reflected San Francisco, but we thought it was over priced. They had the coffee maker in a drawer so we didn't know it was there. Paid $10 for room service coffee. Pool area was nice and quiet

review_title: Great location, very clean but in need of updating
review_text:
Fantastic location but dated.
Welcome to the early 80s, where large open atriums made for an imposing (yet somewhat impersonal) grand entrance. I stayed her for almost a week attending a conference.
The hotel is located in a great spot. You're a two minute walk to the main port in Embarcadero with access to ferries across the Bay and trams out to the world-famous piers. At the front of the hotel, you've got access to cable cars and other transportation options. Was easy to walk around given the central location.
Rooms are fairly large and bed was very comfortable. The bathroom was in need of some updating. Fixtures were worn and wallpaper feeling the impact of age. The room was very quiet (one advantage of an open atrium outside is that you don't hear the doors from your neighbours slam shut in the middle of the night) so good sleep. Room was very clean.
Service was great at reception, though room service was inconsistent. My room wasn't cleaned the day after I arrived (I was out of my room at 630 AM, so no issue with not having access to it). Reception offered a goodwill gesture for the inconvenience and offered to have it serviced (I'm a neat person so it wasn't so much about the room being dirty, but when you're paying a few hundred dollars a night, daily service should be expected!). Daily newspaper delivery was also supposed to be included in my rate. I think of the 5 nights at the hotel, I only received the paper delivered twice (other guests received theirs, so not sure why so inconsistent).
Overall, I'd recommend the hotel for the location and cleanliness. Hyatt should spend some money on updating the bathrooms and wall coverings, but overall a good product.

We stayed in an amazingly spacious suite on the 10th floor (huge for san francisco). The room had a large balcony with views over looking the bay bridge and Alcatraz. The staff was very friendly and accommodating.

We frequently go into San Francisco for overnight getaways from the North Bay and we have had very little luck finding a convenient, clean, affordable (for SF) hotel that we can stay at. Our trip last weekend changed all of that!
From the helpful concierges (I forgot my cell phone - Yikes!) to the beautiful holiday lights throughout the hotel we had a wonderful stay. The beds were super comfortable (a Hyatt standard) and their gym was filled with all of the Lifefitness equipment I could have asked for. 
All in all I was impressed for a 4-star mega-chain. No doubt we will be back. Thanks Hyatt for a great little trip!

review_title: Funny, friendly staff and Great rooms.
review_text:
We came here as the start of are road trip across california/Nevada and from as we stepped in the lobby after a 12 hour flight we felt right at home. The concierage was friendly and cracked a few jokes. Although our room wasn't ready when we arrived we were perfectly content sitting in a comfortable and warm lobby styled with middle eastern decor (to keep in style with the restoraunt located on the ground floor).
The room itself had character with some very interesting decor and decent size. I would reccommend asking for a top floor room because of the skyline rooms. The rooms are fairly quite however you can sometimes hear people in the hall. The room comes with the usual amenities (tea, coffee, phone) as well as high speed internet and plenty of sockets.
On our first morning we went to the hotels local restoraunt saha for breakfast. The service was fairly quick and friendly and the food was great however it is fairly expensive for breakfast costing us about $55 for three, furthermore they put an additional 20% service charge on top automatically which I thought was really not right. If you want a cheaper and more plentiful breakfast go to the golden coffee down a short walk east of the hotel on stutter street.
Overall a really great experience and a hotel I would defiantly visit again if I was in the area and to experience the great wine tasting in the lobby every night at 5:30 till 6:00.
hotel_name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text:
This hotel is perfect. The deluxe rooms inc your own bathroom which is well worth doing. The room size was as expected from other reviews but that was not a problem and neither was any noise (room 716). Consider asking for a room off the main street.Â 
The hotel seemed popular for young people and business.Â 
Other reviews said the hotel is dated but we didn't see this at all. We found it modern in style, clean and well presented.
Getting to the hotel from SF Int airport on the BART was very easy and the hotel is at the centre of the bus, tram, cable car network. Tip: buy a Muni pass (all buses, trams and cable rides inc but not the BART) for the time you are there, it was $21 each for 3 days. When you consider a single on the cable is $6 and the fact SF is so hilly you will use the pass all the time.

We usually stay in union sq or Nob hill but wanted to be closer to AT&T park and a change. After reading reviews here and checking rates decided to pay extra for a king with balcony bay view. It was well worth it--the room was large and clean and efficiently laid out with dressing area and closet off bathroom which was not visible from bedroom. So despite typical bland corporate furnishings the hotel lobby is dramatic and the room's view with doors that really open was wonderful. We watched ships come in, sea gulls stop by etc, equally enjoyable day and night with city lights as a backdrop. We did not pay for valet parking instead self parked and saved $30. Only downside was superbusy entrance two floors below lobby-- not even room to pull in and drop off guests on a busy Saturday. We skipped bellman too to get to reception desk sooner.

The reception is lovely but that initial experience was sadly not reciprocated once we checked in, where we were barely acknowledged and given no information whatsoever, or when we got to our room. The decor was tired and the bathroom cramped. Worst was the musty smell. We complained and were left shell shocked by the reaction or lack of from the receptionist. Fortunately the next morning, Kevin on reception was more than helpful and moved us to a much better room. Good location, but make sure you get a good room!

We arrived in San Francisco very early as we had to drop a hire car off so arrived at the hotel at 9am. There was no problem checking us in at that time. The check staff and concierge was really friendly and so helpful,we even thought they might moonlight as comedians. When the found out my partner was in the RAF they were so pleased to accommodate us,we were upgraded and given a free bottle of wine.
Our room was fantastic,was decorated really well and was quote quirky. Everything was really clean and looked great.
Our only downside were that the Walls were paper thin and you could hear next doors conversation at times. 
Location was great for mooching to union square, at night it could be easy to walk into a 'bad' district but the hotel staff are aware of this and advise you on a map where not to go. The area is not dangerous and we never felt threatened.
We had breakfast the day we arrived and were a little disappointed that they put on 20% gratuity automatically when it states in the menu that this is for parties of 6 or more, I don't mind tipping but I dong feel it should be automatic,if it's good service then I will tip.
We wish we had gone down for the wine tasting earlier on in the holiday as we didn't until the last day,it's great though and you get to chat to really interesting people.
We really enjoyed it and would definitely stay again!
hotel_name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: A website that my husband I were looking at advertised that Hotel Carlton was located in the Fisherman's Wharf area however it is actually in Nob Hill. But the area was great. Lots of little places to eat and somewhat off the beaten path which was nice. We did walk back to the hotel from Fisherman's Wharf one day and while it was a LOT of uphill walking it was doable. The hotel staff was incredible! They were so friendly and accomodating. Our room itself was pretty small but it was clean and the bed was comfortable. They also have complimentary wine at 6pm every night. We would stay there again.
hotel_name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: Need to get the right room!
review_text: the location is great, but you gotta get the right room wit bathroom, otherwise they'll stuck you into a locker room. If you manage to get a good room, everything is perfect, maybe except that other guests and trunkards are noisy at night...
Staff was great. Very helpful, one block from the wharf. Will definately say again
VERY helpful, friendly staff. Excelent location. Happy with everything.

We picked for price and got a good deal in location. Bus straight to union sq one block. Bus from down town stops in front. Bus from ghiradelli stops one block California cable car three blocks north. Good room. Restaurant over priced for breakfast. Go to golden coffee shop two blocks east. 
Fly next door has great garlic base pizza for $6 happy hour and scrimshaw beer is tops. 
Don't book tours here. They use Gray Line and very average job. Took us to Sutter Home on napa tour very disappointed. 
Polk street one block with good eats. 
This is a middle eastern neighborhood and the streets were very free of drugs and not many vagrants. Obviously no one messes with this area. Four blocks south was a whole other story. 
One perk is the free wine at 5:30. 
For the $ and a part of sf we would not have seen this was a really good choice
hotel_name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: Good value hotel, friendly staff, average location
review_text: Good hotel, clean room if a little noisy with daily rubbish collection. Not in best location as area was run down in comparison with most of city but easy to walk everywhere. We loved it because good value and in middle of all districts, so good base to see whole city.
hotel_name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text:
We had a conference suite which was very large and had a room with two queen beds and a room with a kitchenette, large table, separate full bathroom and sofa bed with lots of sitting area. This was more then comfortable for a family of five. 
The hotel is very well situated at the wharf and close to everything you would want to see - aquarium, boats, ferries to Sausalito and Alcatraz, and all the restaurants and shops. There is a good sports theme bar attached to the hotel, but the lobby is small and not much of an area to sit. 
The rooms are good size with large bathrooms and plenty of storage space. Overall, I was impressed by the hotel and the staff and I would definitely come back. 
The only beef I had is with parking. Valet is quite expensive at something like $45 per day, and self park is not on site. It is a block away.

I stayed here for 4 nights in October. After check in I went to my room and unpacked. I tried to put my passport etc in the safe and found it wasn't working. I went back to the desk and told them. I was told it would be sorted out a.s.a.p. After 3 more times of asking it still wasn't fixed! Mini bar was never stocked (again requested 3 times) I generally got a blank "what do you want me to do about it" look. Restaurant v.overpriced considering you are sitting in the lobby. Wifi is a joke. $9.95 a day and it is like dial up speed. 
To sum up Noisy, pricey & Rude. Never again!

Spent one night on business. Location great for tourists but not for people who have been to San Fran many times already, the area is a bit of a tourist trap. Rooms are spacious and beds comfortable. Flat screens with HD! My a/c didn't work, but wasn't a big deal. Attached pub/restaurant offered good food and happy hour beer prices.

review_title: Great hotel in good location from which to explore the city
review_text:
We stayed on the 16th floor in late September and found the rooms to be well appointed, spacious and have a great bay view balcony. Getting there from the airport was easy via the BART train which was great after a long flight. There is a well maintained/spec'd gym on site that was handy for early morning workouts.
The F line street car to Fishermans Wharf or the Castro was conveniently placed just outside the hotel lobby together with the cable car.
The only issues I experienced were lack of free wifi (we had to pay $10 for 24 hours) and very poor signal reception on the tele (later found out to be lose connections). Otherwise a pleasant stay.

review_title: Sorta cool, retro lobby, main floor
review_text: For a mammoth, less-than-new business hotel, the Hyatt Regency doesn't dissapoint. Cool lobby area with a 1970's feel. Rooms are exactly what you'd expect although the bathrooms really could use a serous update. Overpriced (at least the conference rate I got).

review_title: Convenient location and good facilities and comfortable rooms
review_text:
We stayd here for 4 nights in a standard king room. We were very happy with the hotel amenities such as the kiosk in the lobby for quick snacks and coffee, the convenience store and the laundromat for hotel guests only.
The hotel is in a great location close to fishermans wharf, Cable car stops, ghiradelli and pier 39.
The rooms are comfortable although the room we were in, 441, was located close to the elevators and we could hear people getting in and out. 
The only negatives things I would say about his hotel is that the room service menu is small and isn't 24 hours and the other thing is the air conditioner in the room. It was so noisy and kept turning on and off during the night which woke us ip several times. It didn't even coolnor heat properly no matter what setting it was set at.
I would stay hre again but I would make sure that I has had a room with a decent air conditioner as it really affected our sleep.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_text: This hotel is located within a few blocks of Chinatown, but if you walk one block the opposite direction, you will find yourself in the ghetto. Though the room was nice with a comfy bed, the front desk people were very unhelpful. Honestly, one of the best parts about this hotel is Saha, the restaurant downstairs.
hotel_name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: Great location, ok to lay your head
review_text: Arrived over labor day weekend in our rental car which was a huge mistake-San Fran is a nightmare to drive round and park in. Hotel was easy to find but could only recommend parking nearby at Â£34/24hrs!! This was on top of our room price. Hotel lobby was lovely with an open fire & free wine 5-6pm which was a bonus. Unfortunately our room was pokey to say the least & we couldn't open the curtains as we looked directly into someone elses room! Couldn't even see enough sky to decide what to wear in a morning! Plus points-room was clean & fairly quiet. Hotel is 5min walk to union square but, like all of San Fran, involves a steep climb. Reception staff were helpful.

review_title: Very good location and great ambiance
review_text:
this hotel in downtown san francisco has ver good looks and a feel of antiquity. The cable car runs in front of the road and is at walkable distance from union square.
Worth spending time here
hotel_name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: Stayed for 2 nights using points. I have stayed here several times before on business and had a nice room. Using points gets you the worst room that is not updated. Room was never cleaned until after 5pm when I called and a poor job was done. There were union protesters outside yelling until 11 pm so you would think management would go out of there way to have better service.

This place is a throw-back. Big atrium hotel, makes me feel like it's 1980 all over again. It has been kept fresh, not as tired as it's age. And you cannot beat the value or the location. I plan to return. thy to avoid rooms far from elevator,the walk can be long. Ask room location on check in.
The rooms are cute and stylish, with great bath tubs. They have very nice fire pits with comfortable sofa's around them. Parking is super expesive as with most main steam hotels.
Nice rooms, great location eight downtown. Nice lobby area.

This hotel has its unique charm. The hotel location is within reasonable walk to other attractions. It is a bit noisy during the night as it is located in bars area. The area is safe as long as you don't walk south toward the civic center area at night time by yourself.
hotel_name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text:
This I one of the best hotels i've ever stayed in.Â 
I love the intimate nature of it. The rooms are big enough with a large walk in closet. The decor is quirky and unique with a colourful bedspread and photos with the world traveller theme
Yes the elevators are small but in the olden style. To the person who though negatively of this, you really need to travel more.Â 
I loved the plastered wall of the world map Â Â 
The staff is the most funny and friendly folks. They are a riot and you can tell these guys love their job and meeting new people. Theo gave us an excellent overview of the city including board off the 'are you should not go to' on our map.Â 
There is free wifi in the whole building. Computers downstairs charge $4,95 for 40 mins but you can use it and their printers to check in.Â 
Also they have $8 continental buffet breakfast but there are plenty of places around. 
 The location is excellent. We were able to walk everywhere at most 20 minutes.Â 
Parking all day with in and out privileges is $20 across the street. But the hotel charges $30.Â 
For breakfast , the best and closest is Golden Coffee Shop two block south.
hotel_name: Hotel Carlton, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: This hotel is great, yes it is not the newest in the area. However when you have spent only $54 a night from Hotwire who cares. The location is excellent with an easy walk to everything.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_title: Great location, price, and very clean rooms
review_text: I went to san fran for 4 day vacation. The hotel was in a great location blocks away from everything at fisherman wharf and great value. The room was very clean and very nice the beds and pillows also were to my liking as everyone has different views on pillows and beds. The staff was very friendly and helpful. I left something of value at the hotel and they shipped it back home to me. we did not try the restaurant in the hotel. I would stay here again.........
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_title: Best deal in the heart of The City.
review_text: Booked a quick overnight stay at The Mosser. For the location, you cannot beat the price. Within walking distance of some of SF's best attractions, dining, and shopping, including public transportation. The rooms are on the small side, but I was upgraded to a queen suite for just $10. Very clean! I will definitely be staying at The Mosser next time I'm in SF.Free wifi is also a nice bonus.

Great location right next to the wharf. Rooms are recently remodeled so thats a plays. Parking is outrageous but I was able to find free sunday parking a few blocks south. Got the room for only $70 on priceline.

Il clift e' uno dei piÃ¹ belli che abbia mai visto ma quando rientri la sera tieni ben in vista la chiave della camera altrimenti il buttafuori non ti farÃ  entrare... GiÃ  perche oltre che hotel e' uno dei locali piÃ¹ frequentati di San francisco! Camere di categoria e ottima cucina...un tantinello caro ma ubicato vicino ad union square, piazza centrale di San francisco, da provare!

We stayed at this hotel for 4 nights in late April 11. The staff were very welcoming and friendly, particularly Tami who checked us both in and out on the front desk. We arrived at 9am and were very grateful to be able to access our room straight away. We requested a king bed but it hadn't been guaranteed and they weren't able to provide this, but the room was big and spacious, including the bathroom. They have coin operated laundry machines on each floor ($1.50 washer, $2 drier), they sell tide powder in the vending machine - it was great to be able to use this service. I swam in the pool once and the pool area was a lovely sun trap. They provide beach towels and the jacuzzi was very nice. We ate in the restaurant at 8pm on the Tuesday night - the food and drinks were fine but the service wasn't great - it was pretty busy but we ordered 2 cocktails which arrived 10 mins apart and my salad didn't have the chicken on it which I ordered - so I had to wait another 10
mins whilst my husband ate his meal - it didn't make for a relaxing dinner really. The waiter seemed more concerned with presenting an image of being very professional but actually could have paid more attention to getting our order correct. We took a town car booked through concierge to sfo airport for a flat rate of $55 including tip - it is $45 for a taxi so this was
well worth it. The area around the hotel is great, 10 mins to north beach, couple of blocks to the wharf, 15 mins (uphill!) to coit tower. We also stayed in union square for 2 days and much preferred the hyatt's location, it was all very relaxed and really helped you feel like you were on holiday. I'd highly recommend this hotel!

I've never had to write a review before but I need to warn fellow travelers. This hotel is the worst I've ever stayed in I've had better service and cleaner rooms at motel 6. This place is awful. The windows leak and are cold. I turned on the heat all day while I was gone and it was freezing cold when I got back. When I went to get management he came in and said heat is coming out. And I told him it had been all day and it was still freezing and he just walked out!! When we got here I asked about parking on the street and what the zones ment and they wouldn't tell me. Said I had to use the $30 parking garage. I thought it was my choice to park on the street. Weird. Batteries in t.v. Remote didn't work and to top it all off it is the dirtiest place I have ever ever stayed!! The floor looks as if it's never been vacuumed and the bathroom had actual dirt on the sink!! The comforter is ripped. It's sooo bad I begged my husband to take me home. But he said think of it as camping. At least if I was camping I wouldn't have payed this much and would have a warm sleeping bag. WORST place ever do not stay!! I guess groupon isn't always the best choice :(

review_title: Would have been happy if we did not upgrade
review_text: Hotel is nice and in a great location. if we had paid the base rate for the basic room it would have been ideal. We upgraded to a balcony regency club room. When we got to our room, it was small and basic. I actually thought for a second that were given the wrong room. The bathroom has no fan so expect a super humid room after you shower. Bathroom was basic but clean. The problem I had was the keys and the elevators. Our key took about ten to fifteen swipes before it worked each time. We dreaded going to our room! The elevators took forever and required us to swipe to get to our floor and guess what? That didn't swipe well. We weren't the only ones though. The elevator was full of people trying to get their cards to work. Very annoying. We asked for a new key but that still didn't work. The regency club was ok. I'm using the free internet to write this. Balcony on our room was not impressive. We got a corner room and could barely see the water. Like I said, had I not upgraded for an additional $500 I would have been happy.

For a price less than the SFO airport hotels, stayed at a gem of a hotel right off Union Square!
Beautifully renovated room, world class lobby, 5 star service.
Do yourself a favor. Was solo on a business trip, but plan to bring my wife back for some SF romance. Maybe another time with our four year old daughter and dog (Kimptons are pet friendly!).
hotel_name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: Tre notti al Clift durante un viaggio on the road in California...bellissima posizione vicinissima a Union Square camere sempre pulitissime e dotate di ogni comfort! Molto bella anche la hall ed Il bar Red Room molto alla moda e frequentato anche dagli abitanti della cittÃ !personale gentile ma molto distaccato Ci ritornerei!

Despite having to change room twice, staff here amazing! Food at knuckles great too, so worth a visit. Everything close to hand. Make sure you ask for room which looks out onto street; internal view is horrible and can be noisy on certain floors. All in all lovely hotel.

review_title: Good location to see SF, but really only 3 star hotel. Don't expect too much for your dollars.
review_text:
Although a Hyatt Hotel, this certainly doesn't live up to the quality normally associated with this chain. Staff are friendly and helpful, it's just the hotel is old and our room seemed dated. Pillows were all extremely soft feather style, causing both my wife and I to have stiff necks and headaches after the first night. Beds advertised as special were only double size. My booking form also said "marble bath" but that means the bench top, not the bath apparently after I enquired if we had the right room. After having stayed at wonderful (and same priced) hotels in Vegas, Reno, Monument Valley, and Tahoe, we were "underwhelmed" by what we expected to be a better hotel.
Maybe we should have chosen the Best Western or Holiday Express hotels right across the street. The Wifi is generally free at those places and they try harder to make you comfortable.

Good location. Service standard nothing to shout about. One particular elderly gentleman at the spressi lobby was extremely grumpy and rude. Rest of staff were fine. He was very rude on both occasions when I bought some after dinner coffee. And witnessed how exaperated another hotel guess waswhwn they tried to buy some wine.

review_title: The vintage is not a good year.
review_text: I recently stayed at the executive court vintage hotel. I don't understand this hotel - it's two blocks from the fashionable union square and close to several other boutique hotels. Yet the hotel is in need of major redoing. The rooms are old and musty, the showers and bathrooms very much in need of a facelift. This hotel has so much promise but fails to deliver.

I must admit I am a bit biased because I am a platinum Hyatt member for almost 10 years. I decided to surprise my wife with an impromptu trip to San Francisco is weekend and the highlight of the trip was our stay at the Hyatt. I have stayed here several times and the last time I noted that them rooms needed some refreshing. We had a small suite on this stay and the room was great, the service was even better! We had a slight problem with the tv and it was immediately taken care of by engineering with prompt follow up by the front desk. Everyone was very pleasant and our stay in San Francisco was enhanced by the staff at this great hotel. Can't wait to return.

review_title: A Great Time at the Drake
review_text: We spent four nights here and had a great stay. Everyone was very nice and helpful. Great service, the new rooms look great. Very happy with our stay here.
hotel_name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: Older hotel with recently renovated California styled rooms, location just minutes walk from the waterfront.
review_text: Good value for the money (got the corporate rate). Location is good. Easy access via public transportation.

I was a little concerned from reading a few of the reviews here but shouldn't have been. Check in went very smooth after a not so great flight and I was in my room in under five minutes. The room itself on the sixth floor had a great view of the Bay Bridge and Market Street. It was high enough up that I didn't notice any noise other than when the BART Protestors walked by. The front desk staff was helpful with answering questions and the concierge recommended some great restaurants in the area. Room was very clean and the cleaning crew did a great job each day. The only small issue I had was the bed was "lower" on one side than the other from being slept on and probably the mattress needed to be rotated. Overall it was a great stay and I would recommend.

Room was ok, fantastic view of the bay. Go to take a shower and there was hair all over the tub. Then, get in bed later that night and more hair (different color and length)! Suffice to say, no so happy with cleanliness of this hotel.

The Hyatt evidently has double beds rather than queen beds though the room was plenty big enough for queens. I would expect that a four star hotel would have queen beds. The water closet which held the toilet and shower was very small and cramped! Parking was much cheaper at the Stockton and Sutter garage $8 rather than the $57 the Hyatt charges the walk is just 10-15 min but worth it for the amount of money you save!!

review_title: Great location, but overpriced, and then parking extra!
review_text:
I took to work colleagues to Fisherman's Wharf between two projects (on in San Ramon and one in Houston). We stayed at the Sheraton.
Its location is very good, just two blocks away from the touristy areas - far enough to avoid most of the noise, whilst retaining the convenience of exploring on foot.
When we arrived, valet was helpful and parked our car - "included" we were told. The front desk was under-manned, and we had a longish wait to check in. As a Sheraton Gold card holder, I expected to be upgraded, but was not. But my room was nice, with the trademark Sheraton comfortable bed and bedding.
We paid over $200 a night to stay, and the hotel had the audacity to charge another $90 for two days parking. Outrageous - public parking on the same block was $10/day.
Do turn left outside the hotel for breakfast. There are three pavement cafes onthe left - we went to the centre one, and had a great experience. Just past those cafes is the streetcar terminus. It is a must to take this all the way to the other end of the line.
All in all, a nice weekend. But the prices left a bitter aftertaste.

review_title: Alarm sounded at night at 4am!! All guest went down . No staff around
review_text: The alarm sounded at 4am . All the guest went down. But there were no staff .after about 15 min, one staff came out and said false alarm.went back to room but can't sleep after that.i wonder what would happen if a real fire break out

review_title: Nice balcony rooms looking out at the bay. Unfortunately, room not clean.
review_text: It's a nice hotel. I got in late after checking in earlier to find smeared in hair in the ceiling, on the blow dryer and on the walls. Mold in the corners of the shower, stained ceiling tiles and at night the bed smelled like old man sweat. I called the front desk to have them apologize and offer me fresh towels??? Anyway, in the morning they removed my upgrade charge and offered me breakfast. Not bad. I wish they would have moved us though.

On arrival we pulled into the hotel and got a sales pitch on valet. After explaining we were just checking in the valet acted as if he was doing us a favor allowing us to leave our car there while we did this. Way to long a line with only 2 people at the front desk. 
Hotel charges $57 for overnight parking. They will say it's in line with their competitors but seems overpriced to me as I parked on the street a block away. 
Room had a nice view of the cable car but you cam hear every car and bus on the 5th floor.
Very nice bed with flat screen in the room. The lobby is beautiful. 
$25 for a roll away bed seemed too much a well.
Would recommend the hotel just for location. The staff could be a little more customer service oriented.

What a great location absolutely perfect!! We had the best time here! Room was great size and very clean!! It was a two min walk to pier 39 which was fantastic!! Easy access to bike ride to bridge and Alcatraz!! Sheraton had good cafe with breakfast foccacias for good price! We loved it thanks for ending our honeymoon on a high!! :)

review_title: Great location, shame about the rooms
review_text: Convienient location for tourist attractions everything in walking distance for us. Now to the rooms small, very old air conditioning equipment, low quality fixtures and fittings and our room had a stale smoke smell which was there all weekend. All in all you are solely paying for the location not the quality of the hotel

Excellent location and hotel is okay.
Will try other hotels in the area as the price paid could easily get a nicer hotel in the area.
