review_text: HÃ´tel bien dÃ©core , emplacement au calme et a la fois pratique pour les accÃ¨s aux diffÃ©rents endroits Grace au bus . le quartier est agrÃ©able avec resto et boutique
hotel_name: Hotel Del Sol, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: Great hotel in a great location.
review_text: Stayed at this Marriott for a 3 night pleasure stay and had a great time. The location can't be beat. It's right near a BART station, right near the cable cars, near any kind of shopping you can imagine. Would definitely stay here again.
All nice hotels in San Francisco are expensive. This one is a really nice hotel in a great location. Concierge was very helpful.

review_title: Great location, friendly helpful staff, comfortable beds!
review_text: My husband and I stayed here for a week's honeymoon after our Vegas wedding a few weeks ago. The receptionist ensured we had a nice room and the bed was really comfortable. The hotel is in a fantastic location and we travelled around this wonderful city using public transport links found near the hotel. The concierge was great and really helpful. The hotel was clean and bright and we would definately stay here again. Thank you Sheraton!

review_title: Ok for the wharf area...town is a few miles away..
review_text:
Spent 2 nights here,experience an earthquake..walk from elevator to room involved some distance along corridors.room ok, bathroom small.
Breakfast options of buffet(small dining area) or coffee bar...both not cheap but work out the same price in the end...better off going for buffet for hunger and coffee bar for speed. Staff friendly. Location...wharf is busiest during day, quieter at night...need to travel the couple of miles in cab or get tram into town at night, good location for Bay view and Alcatraz.I won't plan on going back, there must be better options (as an spg member)

First and foremost thanks to Jim at the front desk and Ryan in concierge. They provided the best service and were just great people overall. The hotel is beautiful, so big with everything you need. The rooms are a good size and very clean, also have amazing views. We will definitely be back!!! Marriot baby!!!

Just checked in here for three days...what a mistake...and three days to go! Started great with the very nice bellman and doorman. From there though, all downhill. The front desk clerk did not smile once during the check-in! I saw an advertisement at the counter for allergy free rooms. I inquired by asking about the allergy free option. The clerk replied only, "...yes, we have those rooms...". That was it. She didn't ask if we wanted an allergy free room! The room itself was ultra shabby...very, very, worn! Loose wallpaper, torn carpet, dirty, not what you'd expect from a hotel of this caliber! The location is great, but the staff and rooms leave you feeling ripped off. Never again!

I stayed here for a week. Newer my bed was changed. Can sit in lobby bar for hours but no one will came. Actually lobby bar personal unfriendly and quite slow. Cleaning service personal start to knock my door 8.00 at Saturday and did it every 20 minutes! 
Only one good thing about hotel is reception staff!
Never recommend this hotel to any of my friends

Dated hotel, dated rooms, no room service at lunch time. However, comfortable bed and quiet room you would expect from a Marriott. Decent place if all you want is a basic, quiet room in a decent location.

We stayed here on our last day in SF, and it was a good relaxing day. We added the Regency Club access ($35 ea, kids free) and enjoyed the view, coffee and snacks, massage chair, and Internet. Rooms are well appointed and clean! Beautiful lobby and next to an interesting MC Esher-esque like water fountain. Valet was $50+ per night and slow.

review_title: Biggest lobby for hotel that I ever seen.
review_text:
Beautiful hotel with extras then some. Check in here back in October while I had time to kill I went to get an espresso at Starbucks and play their nintendo wii system had fun with the bowling 3D game almost forgot to check in on time. This Marriott makes me feel safe at all times security personel are seen everywhere I turn to. My only complaint is the valet parking over $27 for a day of parking. Area is great again within walking distance of shopping and dining.
*Note their in room wi-fi is spotty at times. Sometimes it just wouldnt let you get page noting connection can not be found. Very annoying if you have email deadlines. Other than that I will return to stay again.

Just spent 3 nights at the Marquis. It is an enormous hotel with multiple meeting facilities and a top floor bar on the 39th floor. The hotel is clean but starting to show its age. Rooms have great beds and modern TVs. There's plenty of space as well. Similarly the hotel gym is a bit cramped and aging but the indoor heated pool was an excellent bonus. 
The hotel is located near businesses, restaurants and entertainment. Catering to conference attendees it is also quite noisy and bustling during the day. 
My main complaint was with the shower. The soap and shampoo were of a grade Motel6 managers would have found embarrassing to offer. By all means bring your own, though disappointing for the room price. The shower itself had weak flow. 
In all this is a Marriott. There may be better places but this is a reliable, clean hotel with a great bonus of a pool. OK plus.

review_title: Convenient location with easy access to public transportation
review_text: Located next to shopping area, Macy and Nieman- Marcus, it is an ideal place to stay on thanksgiving day. The store opens at midnight for black Friday. A movie theater is nearby. Muni at Powell St is a short walk away. Ditto for cable car. The corner room with double beds , 2541, has a decent view of skyline and distant mountain but not the ocean or Golden Gate bridge. The room is very spacious. The furnishing is just a typical Marriott standard in good condition but nothing special. Free Wi Fi and concierge lounge with gold member status. The breakfast is decent with some hot meal such as scramble eggs but no breakfast meat, fresh orange juice in addition to the typical continental items. Short cable car or Muni (F) from fisherman wharf .

We spent 2 nights at this property and enjoyed our overall experience. Jenn the concierge was helpful in landing us Giants tickets, a bus tour, Alcatraz and dinner reservations. She was always so pleasant and helpful. 
The room we stayed in, a 1 bedroom suite was spacious and very nice! 
Perfect location!!!

Comfortable enough but unremarkable. This is a bit of a classic 1970s style atrium hotel which is showing its age and in need of renovation. Rooms and bathrooms a bit tired, windows not double glazed so there is street noise. It is centrally located and quite convenient

review_title: It was more than I expected!
review_text: My husband and I just came back from a weekend in San Francisco. The first of many more visits to come! We booked our hotel and flight through Priceline. The deal was indeed a steal! The flight left in the evening so we got into San Francisco at night. For those who have never been to San Francisco in the summer, it does get cold, especially at night so bring a coat and wear layers! I came prepared and the weather was a nice change from Arizona heat. I had phoned Hyatt in advance to let them we were checking in late. We didn't rent a car because, hey! It's San Francisco! There's transportation available nearly every block. We took the BART station from the airport which let us off literally right in front of the hotel. A mere $8.10 fare. Check in was fast and smooth. A very kind, friendly, smiling gentleman asked for our name and instantly gave us the desired room and off we were to the 14 th floor. I walked in our room and I was blown away, there was an entry way, separate bathroom, vanity area and closet. Past the entry way and around the corner was our studio like room, large desk, lounge chair, flat screen tv, dresser, nightstand and king size bed. To top it all off we had floor to ceiling window/sliding doors and a balcony overlooking not only downtown San Francisco, but the bay, bay bridge and Ferry Building. Breathtaking! We wanted to get a quick bite and drinks and although the concierge desk was closed for the night, the kind gentleman at the Front Desk provided us a map and suggested a few places nearby that were open 24/7. The next day we were off sightseeing, first stop concierge desk; we asked where is everything and how do we get a Muni Pass (unlimited transportation pass for all buses, trams and trolleys), the very knowledgable and informative concierge whipped out a map and proceeded to trace streets and circle landmarks for best possible routes. He even color coded with highlighters for different routes and even asked if he should make reservations after our long day. As for the Muni pass he said to simply walk across the street to the Ferry Building and the store was the first store on the right once through the doors. So off we were to get coffee at the Ferry Building which also has the Farmers Market on Saturday, it was steps away from the Hyatt. We bought a Muni Pass and we were headed for Chinatown and Fisherman's Warf. After a long day we were still geared up for nightlight and got on the guestlist to an exclusive nightclub. We got back too late as concierge desk closes at 8 pm, no worries, we spoke to a lovely lady at the front desk for directions and she printed us directions from mapqwest. The next day we headed to the hotel's restaraunt for coffee and juice, we already had a Cafe in mind for brunch so we just had the drinks, the waiter was still very kind and even said he'd give us coffee to go at no charge. Off we were to the concierge desk to find a Go Car rental location. This time it was a different concierge from the other day but still jyst as pleasant and just as informative, he too whipped out a map and highlighted the best route to take. All in all our stay was wonderful. The staff was exceedingly helpful, very friendly and accomodating, as we checked out the nice lady at the front desked wished us well and suggested we use the computers to print our boarding passes. We would stay at this Hyatt again, for location, room, view and top notch staff!

Terrific hotel. The corner room with double beds and an abundance of windows made for a VERY nice four days. Being able to check in before 8:00 am after an early flight from LAX gave me a chance to make up for lost sleep. This is a TOP choice for SF. Recommend without hesitation.

Staff was great! The morning I was leaving the lady at the front desk (Margarita), helped me get my boarding pass. For whatever reason the computer was not letting me in and was taking forever. She tried many times also, but could not get it. She apologized and said I would have to get it at the airport. That was cool cause they were very busy and I would have some time when I got there to do it. I grabbed something to eat when she walked up to me and said sir, I got it for you! Now that was customer service. She didn't give up even while helping others. I hope Sheraton realizes what a great employee they have, that shows great leadership and service skills. I run a small airport and know all about customer service. Margarita would be a great asset to any company! I hope management takes a closer look at her and make her apart of the management team! My tip of the day!
Chris

review_title: Hotel cuts corners in odd ways.
review_text: A 3 room suite with 2 bathrooms, one with a tv, but the shower door is crooked and won't close. San Fran is known for great coffee but the in room coffee pot is a cheap monstrosity even Walmart wouldn't sell. The coffee in the restaurant downstairs is undrinkable. There are 11 different kinds of hard liquor in the suite but no tea. The room is gorgeous but i can hear every word from my neighbors tv, every noise they make, even when they drop their toilet seat. $300 for this?!

review_title: Overpriced, dark, worn room disappoints greatly.
review_text:
The Marriott is not playing fair. We paid about $360 for a room that was worth about $189. Marriott is banking on location, location, location, and they freely admitted to up charging because most hotels were at full capacity because of conferences at the Moscone. 
Our room was small and adequate. I expected more, and maybe I have grown spoiled after staying at the Ojai Valley Inn and Resort, the Grand, and Nemocolin, but yuck. 
I don't mind staying in a moderate place, but I hate feeling like I got overcharged gleefully.
Service is good. Kudos to concierge and housekeeping.

Spent the last three nights of August here. Has been almost twenty years since last stay. Renovations are nice. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Too cool to use the pool, but the fire pits were nice with the cool weather. 
Didn't use other facilities but did use wi-fi in the lobby area, as did
many other guests. Best thing is the location just two blocks from the Wharf and all of the activities, shops, and restaurants. For less expensive breakfasts we went to I-Hop across the street one block, getting a coupon on our Safeway receipt - Safeway is across the street - for a free breakfast, and Jack's Bar on Jefferson for just $5. We walked the area or rode the street cars for much of the day. A $2 fare let us ride to the Ferry Building to the Farmer's Market, then to the Castro District for exploration, and back to the Wharf. Got to the Giants game easily with public transportation. We had a great time and would gladly stay at the Sheraton again.

review_title: Paper Thin Walls Bring Down the Sheraton!
review_text:
My family of four recently stayed at the Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf on a weeknight in August and it was a mixed experience. 
The Good: Very nice lobby and common areas featuring wi-fi and outdoor firepits. Very good and prompt service from the valet, bellman and front desk.
The Bad: Rude service from the quick food service attendant in the lobby. A very bright and nicely appointed room marred by a leftover dirty sock from a previous night's guest and a few crumb-filled carpet areas where perhaps the maid's vacuum could not reach. 
The Ugly: Ultimately, the reason most guest go to a hotel is to get a peaceful and comfortable night of sleep. And this is where the Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf truly let us down. During the day, we heard kids running up and down the hall, their pounding footsteps doing their best to accurately reenact the SF quake of 1906. But at night, every noise -- each drawer slamming in the adjacent room, each child's jump off a bed, every door closing shut -- interferes with the very purpose of why we seek out a luxury hotel.
And therein lies the rub: Because the Sheraton Fisherman's Wharf hotel IS a luxury hotel with upgraded luxurious design, appointments and service. But if a guest cannot get a restful night of sleep because of the flawed original construction of the hotel, what good are those luxuries?

review_title: Nice Spot. Look Out For Parking Fees !
review_text: Nice location in the heart of fisherman's wharf. Parking a rip off at over $50 per nite.

review_title: Nice place to stay at the Wharf
review_text: This Sheraton was upgraded about 2 years ago. You can walk to the local attractions too. The staff takes good ca re of you. We enjoy sitting by the outdoor fireplaces too. The rooms are equipped well. We have stayed here multiple times. We plan to stay again. it is also dog friendly. 4.5 stars

Great hotel, great location, great service! The lobby atrium is beautiful and the rooms were very modern. We even had a balcony which I wasnt expecting! The top floor room for regency members has great breakfast, snacks, cocktail hour and is a nice space that overlooks the city and and bay. Would definately return!

review_title: Good specials and location but lost laundry let it down
review_text:
I had to stay here for 2 nights at short notice due to hurricane irene and managed to get a good last minute special on bookings.com
The location is great, very close to union square. Checkin took quite a long time as it is a huge hotel but they had very few staff on. Unfortunately my room apparently wasn't ready despite having requested early checkin before leaving nz but i could pay an additional amount for one that was... a common trick apparently. 
But my room did have a great view and was very comfortable and spacious. Free wifi in lobby was great. Very friendly concierge staff who were very helpful as i was trying to get through to airlines etc.
But the one black mark was the hotel losing my laundry which was quite stressful and they had incredibly bad followup for this issue for a hotel of this level and cost. I dropped my laundry down the morning the day before i finally could fly out before dropoff time and when i returned that night to find no laundry checked at the bellboy desk - for some reasom no laundry had been collected that day. While annoying that was fine and i was going to take my laundry with me but they indisted it could go through on the express service and be back at 2am ready for my departure at 5am. So based on their assurance it would be ready i left it only to wake at 4am to find no message as promised and upon checking at the counter was told it was still at the laundry provider with there no way it would have been done by then as I'd been promised. All very stressful for that hour! So i left my forwarding address and they were to ring once it arrived back to confifm but very poor followup snd i had to ring several times. It did eventually arrive but unneeded stress was not what i would have expected so i would question staying here again or at least using their laundry service!

We paid $279 per night and felt this hotel wasn't worth it. The chair in our room had buttons missing. Also the reading lamps above our beds were not working. We told the front desk in the morning but by the evening they still weren't working. We had to go back to the desk to find out the bulbs were on back order. Couldn't leave our room a message? For $279 per night, the amenities should be exceptional! If you want to park there, they charge you $55 per night over and above the $279! The parkade across the street is $30 per day which is marginally better. We had a room at the back of the hotel & the windows were filthy. They may have remodelled but the condition of the rooms does not match the price they charge! At the very least breakfast should be included. Won't stay there again!

review_title: Great base for exploring the area
review_text: Had 4 nights here in July. The hotel is quite contemporary and is equally lent to the business traveller as those with a family wishing to explore the area. The rooms are well appointed and the beds comfortable affording a good nights sleep. Hospitality and professional politeness are to a high standard with all staff being most polite and helpful. The location is superb from a tourist perspective with Pier 39 a few moments walk away, and plenty public transport options within a short stroll. We did not eat in as our holiday here meant much exploring and trying local cuisine. Sorry cannot comment on food. Two adults and two teenagers stayed here most comfortably. Most importantly, would we stay again? Yes.
Very central hotel clean and spacious , great beds.

The Shearaton is a really nice hotel. Check in was quick and easy. The rooms are clean modern and bright. All the beds have lovely warm duvets and were very comfortable.
There were cofffee facilities in the room as well as the usual ironing board hair dryer. There was an in room safe as well. Wi fi was available only in the lobby and cafe area
The swimming pool was small but clean and plenty of pool towels. 
There is a cafe which was nice a bit pricey but nice to sit outside next to the fire pits. 
The hotels location is brilliant walking distance to Fishermans Wharf and Ghiardelli Square.

Stayed for a week in sept. 
Lovely little hotel. 
Big funky bedroom and bathroom very colourfull. 
Good size comfy bed. 
Nice helpfull staff. 
No restaurant so you'll need to look elsewhere for breakfast etc. 
They do give you a cardboard box with an apple/orange, pastry bun and juice drink in the morning if you ask for breakfast. Not to filling tho. 
Walking distance to shops , Westfield center , Chinatown.

Really lovely hotel with great room and really nice modern bathroom with large walk in shower. Room was great, with TV and iPod/radio alarm. Nicely decorated and something a bit different. Location is just a short walk from Union Square and the trams, buses and BART (subway). Would definatly stay here again.

review_title: Not bad, just not worth remembering
review_text: Rooms are clean and the staff are helpful and friendly, it's just not as nice as the price tag would reflect. Good location and the facilities are nice enough, but it is lacking. Room service/restaurant is pricey considering the quality of the food. The best thing about the room is the bed. Very comfortable. I guess I just expected more for the price.
I love this place,everytime I check in ,I always get the best service,staff is very friendly,very professional.

Stayed here for a Conference. The front desk staff as well as every other staff person were Wonderful!
Very accommodating and friendly!
The rooms are very clean and updated. The conference rooms are large and the wait staff are wonderful! There are three sets of elevators to get to different towers of the hotel. All elevators were extremely fast. Never had to wait for the elevator. Swimming pool and hot tub very clean (indoors). There is a gym that is opened 24 hours per day. I would definitely stay again!

The hospitality at the Diva is on point. From the CEO Yvonne to the front desk and housekeeping, everyone cares about your stay and makes you feel welcome and important. The DIVA hotel encourages rest, relaxation, and sensuality (if you allow it!) The lighting is adjustable and strategically placed, the shades have images that stimulate your mind and the beds are seductive and ultimately comfortable. Great experience!

review_title: Good location but nothing else good about it
review_text: We were pleasantly surprised as we drove up to the Sheraton that the Dollar Car Rental was next door. The doorman was helpful and friendly. We waited patiently in the queue to check in and when called up to be served by NEXT we walked up to the counter. The women behind the counter was rude and barely talked to us. She said we had a twin queen when I said I thought we had requested a King she snapped at me and said no we had a standard run of house . As I had given her our voucher I had no reference to what we had,I asked to see the voucher and she said it says standard. We were put in a room that was a long walk from the front desk. It was not very sound proof. It was clean neat the bed area was a decent size but the bathroom very small and cramped. I had read reviews and had expected the small bathroom. We were woken every morning by trucks and loud motorbikes about 4 am. We didn't ask to be moved couldn't be bothered dealing with rude staff. The concierge was very helpful and friendly but then they are working for a tip and commission on trips they sell you. The location was handy to everything but there were plenty of hotels in a small area. I wouldnt recommend this hotel it didn't have a very good feel to it and by this stage of our trip we had stayed in quite a few places.

review_title: Great location for Staying in San Francisco
review_text:
Recently attends a business conference in San Francisco and stayed at the Marriott Marquis. The hotel was across the street from where I needed to be and was within a short walking distance from shopping, restaurants and public transportation. 
The hotel staff were the friendliest, politest and most professionals I have encountered while traveling.

My wife, daughter and I stayed at this hotel four four nights. First, the good. The location can't be beat, only a block and a half from Union Square on Geary. The room was reasonably spacious and clean. The Murphy bed in the two room suite was comfortable. The shower had good pressure and plenty of hot water, although if you are over 5'8", you probably will have to squat a bit to get under the shower head. 
The bad--I use hotels primarily as a place to sleep, and that was not easy at this hotel. The windows are not soundproof, and even on the 5th floor, between the sirens, trash trucks, and other street noise, sleeping through the night was an issue. Also, some people used the fire escape right outside of our room as a smoking/talking area on a few occasions, one of which started at about 2:30 in the morning, when some people, like myself, are trying to sleep. Not pleasant. 
If the hotel would spend some money on soundproofing, I might consider staying there again. Otherwise, probably not.

review_title: Great location, nice rooms, mediocre service
review_text:
The checkin process was smooth with a very helpful desk person as I requested a room away from noisy streets (thanks to Trip Advisor suggestion). I highly recommend this suggestion to others. The rooms were recently updated and very nice. The hotel location was great for everything- close to cable cars, street cars and the wharf. HOWEVER, we had problems with a door person that we asked for a cab one evening. He adamently tried to convince us that we needed to wait
 15-30 minutes for a cab, that most
 cabs didn't travel close to our hotel 
and it would be much easier to take 
a limo sitting on the corner for $30 
for a 1 mile drive to the restaurant.
 Cabs were everywhere of course.
 Really disappointed in this scam. 
Then we asked for directions from 
the concierge to AT&t Park-a common request. He neglected to mention an essential transfer which almost doubled our travel time and we were late for the game. Go to the hotel but don't trust the service.

review_title: Too many other good hotels to choose from
review_text:
I wish I could rate this hotel higher, but I had so many disappointments that even the location can't bring the rating up. It wouldn't take much to get this hotel up to par with it's rates, yet right now I say pass and book somewhere else.
I was in room 414 and i was constantly having dropouts on the wi-fi. It was a real drag since I had brought my new ipad for a test drive. The front desk said they didnt know what the problem was but I have a feeling it's a common complaint.
Before I checked in i called the front desk from my mobile phone and there was no answer. Then I dialed an extension for a manager and there was no answer. Then I left a message with the manager and never even got a call back.
The front desk staff was not very helpful in getting a cab. In fact, they did nothing even after seeing me in front of the hotel for nearly twenty minutes. 
On my last day the "Belman" said i could take a shuttle to the airport from vertigo and there were no other stops. In fact, the shuttle stopped three times to pick up passengers. 
I think there are other hotel options until Hiyel Vertigo gets their act together.

LOCATION -
This hotel is situated in the heart of the busy shopping area, opposite theatres and a short walk from union square.
APPEARANCE -
Easily missed from the outside. But looks nice.
RECEPTION -
Extremely friendly and helpful staff are a real credit to this hotel. Check in was very smooth and easy. And help was on hand to bring the suitcases to the room
THE ROOM -
We stayed in room 206. The room was very clean. The decor was very modern and contemporary. The bed was far too comfortable making it very hard to get up in the morning. It has a free safe. Good size tv. Only down points was the ancient and very noisy air con and the small bathroom which had a sink around the corner meaning you had to leave the bathroom to wash your hands. On a good note the shower was fantastic.
MISC -
There is a Starbucks attached to the reception for your morning coffee if you don't fancy making your own.
FINAL THOUGHTS -
A lovely hotel. Very comfortable and very welcoming. I highly recommend this hotel.

Nice location convenient to BART, bus, walking distance from Union Square. Lovely lobby and attractive rooms. Great Marriott beds and clean bathrooms. A good SF location for a safe and well run visit.

Nice hotel, very friendly staff, such a good location, close to all the good stuff. The rooms were a good size, very clean etc. The only bad thing i can think of is that you could hear the people in other rooms quite loudly, especially the people above - maybe a tip could be to ask for a room on the top floor, then you wouldnt hear the people stomping above.

We booked this hotel as our first stop in a 4 city tour.
The location is central but quiet, the check in was easy and the room was roomy & light.
No complaints except the lack of free Wi-Fi in the room although the free service in the lobby was really efficient.

review_title: Save your money, stay someplace else
review_text: This hotel is bland: no character, nothing outstanding about it except the pricetag. The rates are unreasonable compared with the many other hotels in the area, many of which are privately owned. The furniture is cheap. It's an ugly building. And what makes them think it's ok to charge $15/day for Internet access?

review_title: Just checked and already had to call housekeeping and maintenance!
review_text: Room is hot. A/C won't stay on. A/C vents dirty. Chair upholstery stained. Dismal, small room. Not what I expect for a Marriott at all!
A beautiful hotel that's only a 2 min walk from union square with plenty of options around for food and cheap drinks. Will definitely stay at next time I'm in SFO

I stayed here a few months back, first of all the location was great right by union square, alot of fun places around, pizza joint down the street pretty good. Starbucks right by hotel, wine shop down the street with very good wine selection, ruby Skye (night club) is less than a block away. will admit it was hard to find the place took about 3/4 spins around the same street since it's only a one way street,until we finally found the place. I met two different front desk clerks and they were both very helpful an always engaged conversation with us as passing the lobby into elevator. Also got valet and the gentlemen escorting my car to garage were always helpful. The room is on the smaller size as well with the bathroom also being fairly small but its decorated with a unique modern look to it, but come on it is sf most of the rooms are on the smaller side in this town. If the price is right stay here you will not be disappointed.

We checked in early and it wasn't an issue to the staff. Friendly, efficient check in staff and everyone we met though out the stay was excellent. Rooms will be good for another few years before they need a refurbish. I would only suggest that they take a look at some of the electrical sockets as they made static noise when being used. Also another concern was windows open so if you have children I see a real hazard!!! Everything was clean and as promised on the web site. Love the location and as mentioned, all the staff are 10 out of 10. WILL be back

review_title: Nice looking hotel in a great location
review_text: This hotel is not your typical looking hotel. It's unique, creative and urban. We rented the queen suite which was ample for three people. Felt like we were living in an apt in San Fran. Hotel was clean and staff were very friendly. Washrooms are a bit small but nothing to worry about as they are large enough for what you need them for. Bathtub water pressure was very low and the shower pressure was very high. Amazing location as you are right in the action of union square. A few homeless people around but it seems liken they are all over San Fran. Definitely a good price for what you get. Will definitely be back.

Diva is in an amazing location for Union Sq, transport via metro, bus and trolley. Hotel staff are very helpful. Rodney the concierge is great- he even let us use his phone to contact the airline when hurricane irene struck and our onward trip to New York needed cancelling and our flight rerouting. He was a sweetie. Gorgeous decor and toiletries too. Quirky blue lifts and blue jelly belly beans on the counter, see what you make of the roller blinds! We would go back

- Excellent location
- Comfortable, supportive, king sized bed
- storage space for luggage
- free access to in-room safe
- reasonable bathroom amenities 
- good sized writing desk for planning your day
- helpful staff (didn't call on their help much though)
- slightly noisy with ventilation ducting and noise from the corridors but acceptable still
- refurbishment work not a problem (carpet laying still when we arrived)
- near Union Square so some noise associated with proximity. Not too bad. 
Not a large room that we stayed in but we merely slept here. It puzzles me as to why people expect a tennis court sized room....are they coming to sleep and visit the city or stay inside the whole trip???
We would recommend this hotel.

review_title: Nice hotel, good location, cost reasonable.
review_text: Location is nicely centered in town. The renovation noise was hit and miss. Biggest challenge was getting the maid service to follow simple direction. Rooms were nice, bathroom on the small side but overall better than average experience.

Was a good place to stay, I maybe be going crazy but I found the staff in the Lobby area (food & bev) area were all a bit snobby and were almost speaking down to myself and other guests. The friendly attitude was lacking. The front office staff were far more friendly. The location is great for fishermans wharf. I would stay again. I'd like to see if they have friendly staff though!!!

camere microscopiche. accoglienza molto scortese. colazione inestente. avevamo prenotato per alcune notti ma dopo la prima siamo fuggiti altrove...e' un posto molto rumoroso e la colazione inclusa nel prezzo e' una vera presa in giro. Il signore alla reception nonne sembra tagliato per svolgere questo lavoro.

We spent 8 nights at the Kabuki over the 2011 Thanksgiving holiday. It's beautiful and interesting, with a wonderful koi pond in the courtyard, the sort of San Francisco spot where a priest heading to an interfaith breakfast crosses paths with a sloshed rock musician stumbling back from a nighton the town. It has character, and a great Japantown location, a lovely lobby and good rooms.
We found the service a bit slapdash, though: dirty dishes would sit in the hallway for days, it took repeated requests to get more coffee for the room, the housekeeping was on the desultory side. Recommended if you get a good deal on the price.
hotel_name: Hotel Kabuki, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: I love this place. Great location. I try to stay whenever I stay overnight in San Fran.

I have read all other reviews and just had to leave my own. I use this site religiously and tend to pass over comments about noise as my boyfriend and I sleep through pretty much anything. How I wished I had paid attention this time! Firstly this hotel is ideal location, lovely rooms and clean. But just like all the reviews say the parking is over priced, $45 + tax a night, and it is so so noisy. I am irritated that the general manager subtly hints at this being due to noisy people above. This is NOT the case. We were kept awake from around 4am both nights we were there until 6.30/7 from squeaky floorboards when anyone was apparently walking on the floor above. We were on the third floor and there are four floors. I am also irritated that the solution is to request a fourth floor room. Someone has to stay on the lower floors unless you keep these empty and just fill up the fourth. We mentioned it to the girl when we checked out and they charged us one night of parking instead of two.
Anyway, in summary yes the hotel is perfectly located, clean and generally a nice hotel. But that is severely tainted by the creaking floorboards which have nothing to do with noisy guests and everything to do with the materials used when building. If you stay here definately request 4th floor room only!!

review_title: Small rooms, poor service, great location & view
review_text:
We stayed at this bay front location for acouple of nights. Liked the view and location - slow(!!!!) service - did take forever fo check in, long lines , only 3 staff checking in. Had filled out eUpgrade day before arrival willing to pay $70+ ... Upon arrival a very unfriendly staff member fold me that only one suite is avail and therefore they request $150 additionally fo the already pays $ 225 - even worth. He was not apologetic at all - certainly NOT HyAtt standard ( I am Platinum member)
Our return had 2 glAsses and 2 towels - we were 2 adults/2 kids - we called 4 times f add glasses - one hr later we still had not received them. Front desk stated they are fully sold out and very busy. All in all. Very modern decor room, TV in bathrm mirror. SmLl shaped room due to triangle f families
Great bfst!
 Byt
Located in a very touristy area, the convenience is nice. A bit simple and outdated for a Sheraton. It is nice not having to taxi for lunch or dinner everywhere thought.

review_title: Good location, large rooms and close to lot of great restaurants, shopping and museums but parking is expensive and be sure you
review_text: The rooms are quite large -enough for rollaways but we booked through exopedia and were told we'd have a double wtih 2 queens but they didin't have that when we arrived (despite calling in advance). They said they would move us the second day but we settled in and just enjoyed the great location and all stayed together -it worked out fine. It was reasonably priced for Union Square and very convenient for walking to lots of things! There is also an alternative public public just blocks away

The pro's-location is great. Room is clean. Bed's comfortable. Food at restaurant was good. 
The con's-bathroom in double bed rooms are very small! Can be claustraphobic. The water pressure in the shower is horrible.

I'm staying on the last floor. Huge noise on the corridor and doors slam very early. The windows don't stop the traffic noise so if you want to rest...the room is very cold and the AC just sends more cold air even setting to 90 F. Bathroom is colder then a fridge !
We're paying a fortune this week in this hotel - 300$ per night - and they didn't even offered a breakfast or showed some concern.
When we arrived late at night driving the coast there was a parking space free where we parked, few minutes later vallet told us to take the car because that place was reserved and we had to go to a parking (payd, extra 18$/night). Room service ok, fast and efficient, but also pricy. Mini bar is locked and water until now never replaced.
In our country a hotel this pricy treats you like a king, offers you a drink at the bar, includes breakfast, the staff tries to see if you're OK, etc.
We don't recommend and will not stay here again.
hotel_name: Hotel Kabuki, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: Excellent location in the city with good communication to all tourist attraction and a friendly atmosphere in the hotel.
review_text: We are very content with our stay in hotel Diva. Good communication to all tourist attraction, walking distance to restaurants and shopping. Very helpfull concierge. Starbucks in the hotel for breakfast if you want.

I flew into SF and stayed here for 4 nights. The lobby area was nicely decorated, and the courtyard was gorgeous. I had a corner king room. The room was quiet , and beautifully decorated Japanese style, including a chaise lounge chair, flat screen tv, and 2 sliding doors that opened to a wrap around balcony. I enjoyed having both sliders open, to allow the crisp breeze in my room. The air conditioner did not work, but the weather was nice enough to just keep the sliding doors open. One suggestion, however, would be to have screens put in. There are no screens on the sliding doors, so I had to close them when going to sleep. 
The bathroom was very large, and included a traditional Japanese soaking tub, and staff left bath salts every night...a great way to end the day! 
I ate one morning in the hotel resturaunt. It was a bit overpriced at around 18.00 for buffet, but it was pretty good.
I walked the area around the hotel... Not much for shopping, and no American convenience store to be found. But, plenty to do down at the pier. I believe it was about a 10 to 12 dollar cab ride to get there. 
All in all, this was a nice experience in a unique hotel, and the soaking tub was a plus!
hotel_name: Hotel Kabuki, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text:
This place is nearby the worst part of town and it shows. There are homeless people and druggies everywhere. My friends and I made the mistake of walking to dinner. While trekking only 1 mile, we were approached by numerous street people, witnessed a woman urinate in the street, and found ourselves in the middle of a vulgar screaming match because some toothless woman punched a toothless man's pitbull as he walked by. Classy for a diva, right?
Enough abiut the neighborhood, the hotel itself reminds me of an apartment building. The bathroom is so small that the sink is placed in the sleeping area instead. It was clean but you can tell the building was old and they just hastily slapped paint on the walls to make it look hip. I don't plan on coming back. 
Stay away if you can.

Treated with the utmost care. Celebrating our anniversary and had special touches. Wine with cheese and crackers. Baggage check in. Amazing view of the bay! Most comfortable bed ever. High class hotel!

review_title: A very noce hotel in a good location that isn't too expensive.
review_text: This hotel is very nice. Clearly it is older but they have spent a lot of money on room renovations. The lobby is lovely with a nice little cafe and cute outdoor seating with fire pits. Nice touch. The service is good, not great but not bad. The rooms are clean and comfortable and the Housekeeping staff is amazing. Also the rooms are large so of you have a family staying it works well. You can walk to all Wharf attractions and the trolley stops right by the hotel. Also cabs are very easy to get. There are two grocery stores within a block so you can buy fresh food too.

review_title: Rooms are nice, location good. Service is poor and wireless is awful.
review_text:
Hotel room are actually nice. The service is poor - giving mis information, not capturing credit card at check in and calling at 10 pm to get from the guest. 
Wireless service is awful. I was only able to get connected at 9pm or later. Other guests had the same problem.
hotel_name: Hotel Kabuki, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: Beautiful views from 34th floor, but avoid shoebox room 3422.
review_text: Valet service is $50+ a night, very efficient considering small driveway. Check in was smooth and friendly. Both rooms were upgraded to SPG 34th floor. One room was large with sitting area, one room so small had hard time walking from bathroom to bed without banging into TV cabinet. Dual shower heads and Heavenly bed were wonderful. Not much street noise since on 34th floor. Free coffee for Gold/Plat members in bar in morning along with newspapers. Overall good stay.

review_title: Great room, great location, great bed
review_text: This is now our "go to" place in SF. The location for shopping, food and public transportation is perfect! The bed is cozy and perfect for a great sleep!
We looked at a "Japanese suite" today. Filthy, ratty, dark, bizarre layout. Unhelpful staff. Unattractive lobby. Everything worn out and tired. We fled. Don't stay here.
hotel_name: Hotel Kabuki, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: L'hotel Ã¨ situato on Powel St., in pieno centro, nei pressi di uno dei capolinea del Cable Car, di Market St. e all'angolo di Union Square. Praticamente il meglio per visitare il centro della cittÃ . Non mancano nelle vicinanze ristoranti e locali dove trascorrere la serata. Le stanze, comunque pulite e ordinate, sono anguste, come anche il bagno. Ai piani piÃ¹ bassi il traffico, che anche di notte non manca, si fa sentire. Il personale Ã¨ gentile e disponibile ed il servizio buono, anche se mi Ã¨ toccato riabilitare la chiave della stanza ogni sera. Attenzione ai costi del parcheggio. Carissimo.
hotel_name: Sir Francis Drake Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text:
Very nice rooms, helpful concierge, great location, overall a very nice hotel which we would recommend. However, the hotel restaurants were just OK, but were quite pricey (Mission Grill & 4th St Bar). 
Skip the hotel restaurants & visit Annabelle's Bistro just outside the hotel's main entrance for a MUCH better meal.

review_title: Good location with a beautiful view
review_text:
Checked in today and was given a room on 24th floor. Beautiful city view with partial bay view. Justin was very kind to give us free Internet access and arranged for such beautiful room.
However when we came back from dinner at 7pm noticed that the concierge desk was closed and all enquiries directed to front desk. So we decided to check the info on Internet ourselves as the front desk was too busy attending to guests checking in and there were only two of them. I think this is not fair to the front desk.
Overall the location is fantastic as there's hardly any homeless people hanging around here compared to union sq and it's next to four season hotel.

review_title: One of the best nights sleep
review_text: Normally stay at st Francis, opted for market due to availability...good move, not going back to st Francis..great corner room, great beds, great bar, buffet breakfast the usual banquet...only negative was the small gym...opted for a road run instead...central location, pleasant service.good choice

review_title: Great location just don't count on the concierge
review_text: Great beds and fabulous location with Bart nearby. Rooms were comfy and had a great view on the 19th floor. The downside was the concierge service. Although their food picks were often decent they were just incompetent at directions and most other types of information. Each time they gave us directions they were not only wrong but seriously underestimated walking times by a factor of 2 or even 3. They sold these poor fellow conference attendees hop on hop off bus tickets and told them the last bus was at 6Pm when in fact it was 5pm. Concierge service is supposed to be the top service source for a hotel and they were basically incompetent. Nice hotel, avoid the concierge service at all costs.

The Hotel Kabuki was fortunate to have a room for me in my moment of despair, however, staying there, I know why. 
Note: they do not serve room service or have an open restaurant in their hotel on Mondays or Tuesdays. Being in Japantown, the choices are sushi sushi or sushi. I don't like to eat sushi on Mondays. And it was raining in SF. 
#2 bad-no coffee in the morning! What?? Sucks. (I am writing this review because of this fact). 
The rooms felt dank, the plastic curtains kept out the light, but they are cheap and torn. The beds and pillows were stiff. The carpet was suspicious. 
Two redeeming factors: the shower, which was considerably larger than my bed, was amazing. The other was the demeanor of the staff. They were very kind and sincere. Too bad they have to deliver the news of no room service and no coffee. 
I have been a long time Joy of Life club member. This experience was anything but joyful. And definitely not worth the rates.
hotel_name: Hotel Kabuki, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: Great location, clean rooms and comfortable beds, no Internet and average service
review_text:
Location of this hotel is great - close to muni trams, muni buses, BART station, 5 min walk to westfield mall, union square, and cable car station.
Beds are comfortable and clean. The ergonomic work chair was really good and didn't give me any back pain. Our bathtub clogged a bit though but we didn't bother getting them to fix it because we were here for 3 nights only. 
Front desk not accommodating when asked for higher floors as well as late check-out. Concierge didn't know where the elevator is for the BART station - it was really hard carrying the luggage going down the stairs to the station. 
Great gym area! No pool at hotel. 
No Internet in room unless you pay $15 a day. No wifi as well in the lobby :(
We bought a flight + hotel package for our San Fran trip. I wouldn't pay regular price to stay at this hotel for an average level of service.

Good standard Westin / Starwood, no complaints. Two minutes from Bart (Montgomery), 25 minutes direct from the International Airport and very convenient for sightseeing / shopping. Good selection of restaurants and bars close by.
Perhaps biggest surprise was the number of down-and-outs hanging around the general area. No hassle but something to be generally aware of as a tourist exploring the streets.

Malgrado l'ottima posizione noln pensate di selezionare questo hotel se avete bisogno di pianificare nuove tappe del vostro viaggio utilizzando internet. Noi abbiamo fatto una vacanza girando per hotel e prenotando di volta in volta gli altri hotel. Qui non Ã¨ stato possibile, viene reclamizzata una high speed connection che non esiste. Per il resto la posizione sarebbe ottima anche se il rapporto qualitÃ  prezzo Ã¨ un po' elevato.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf
