hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_text: This business hotel near the convention center unbelievably has no wireless in the room. I stayed for business and couldn't believe this. Parking is outrageous at $58 a day. The rest was standard Marriott and fine. I live in the Bay Area and could have stayed anywhere in SF for this meeting so this was no great.

review_title: Great start to our honeymoon, great view to bay, and stylish smart hotel
review_text: We stayed for 3 nights at the start of our trip, and found it a great base, to explore San fran. Lots of great restaurants nearby and loads to do, shops on the doorstep the perfect start off location. We had a corner room on the 28th floor, with views to the bay, and great service. We had some great breakfasts at mels dinner round the corner, and a great dinner on our first night at annabelles bistro again a 5 minute walk, great local food, beautiful restaurant and fab service. We also went to credo for dinner, and that was about a 10-15 minute walk into the financial district, great food again would def go back!

review_title: TrÃ¨s bon hÃ´tel et emplacement idÃ©al
review_text: Nous avons passÃ© 3 nuits dans cet hÃ´tel trÃ¨s bien situÃ© Ã  10 minutes des Pier et du cable car. Les chambres sont propres et spacieuses. Excellent service. Petit dÃ©jeuner copieux sous forme de buffet continental et amÃ©ricain (21$). Parking sous l'hÃ´tel (40$). Le restaurant est moyen mais plein de bonnes adresses Ã  proximitÃ©.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn San Francisco Fishermans Wharf

review_text: My wife and I spent our 34th anniversary at the Westin Market Street. We booked our getaway based on recommendations from Trip Advisor and were very pleased with the result. Very central to cable cars, sightseeing and shopping. Excellent restaurants in close proximity. Very well appointed room, very quiet and comfortable. Valet parking was in line with other large US city hotel charges and very prompt. The concierge at the desk, Kim, was extremely knowledgeable about San Francisco and had extensive knowledge about a number of restaurants in the city. We had a problem with a cleaning issue with our room, but as soon as it was brought to the attention of the housekeeping manager, Susan, it was very promptly corrected. The breakfast buffet was very good and service was excellent. We very much enjoyed our stay and would not hesitate to stay there again.

I chose to stay at Columbus Motor Inn for my San Francisco visit, based on the many positive reviews on the hotel. I have to say that I was not disappointed. In fact, I very much agree with all the positive points written about it, as my stay there was very pleasant. The front desk staff, especially Joe, was very helpful. 
The room that I booked was a 2 bedroom suite, and its very spacious. The beds' mattresses are by Serta, as mentioned by the hotel in the website, most comfortable. Had no problem sleeping. The room amenities are great (picture big screen LCD TV in each of the bedrooms, as well as free high speed internet access and car parking. Also, there are free apples everyday at the front desk for guests to munch.
So, any areas to improve on or to note? Well, there is no fridge in the room, and I think the window panes are a little thin, as we can hear all traffic that pass by our room Other than that, it is now my favourite hotel in San Francisco, and I will stay there again when I visit San Francisco again.

review_title: If you get a good deal book it!
review_text: In the city of San Francisco this is a perfect location if you want to be out of the tourist hub of fisher mans wharf, which is only a 10 min cable car ride away. The service was what you would expect from the Westin, and the rooms were always clean and the double shower head in the bathroom was a nice touch, if you have problems getting in and out of a bath this is not the best choice. The bath is very deep and is a bit hard to get in and out of to use the shower. Over all would recommend to people who do not want to be on the wharf but still easy enough to get to.

review_title: Good Hotel w/Free Parking in San Francisco
review_text: This was our 2nd stay at this hotel/motel. This time was for our daughter's graduation. To be fair, this is really more of a motel, but the rooms are very clean, and the parking is free. Free parking in SF is virtually nonexistent, and considering you'll pay between $40 & $70 to park your car, this is a major savings. The location is very convenient to North Beach & Fisherman's Wharf for restaurants and sightseeing. Would definitely stay here again.

The hotel was great, room was nice and good sized. The location is great, right off Market street, within blocks of shopping and great food. Chinatown is about 7-8 blocks away. The F line and cable cars are within 2-3, bringing you to the Fisherman's wharf and Embarcadero. The service, however, was subpar. I was very disappointed with the service at the front desk. It was almost 5 minutes before we were even greeted. The lady that checked us in was not nice at all. The conceirge was great though. The guy was very knowledgeable, with lots if suggestions on places to see and eat. Check out was much better, very smooth and simple. I would definitely recommend coming to stay here if you are coming to visit San Francisco.

Great location and hotel ! Easy 5 minute walk to Fishermans Wharf and tram terminal, 10 minute walk to the Crooked Street and surrounded by bars and eateries. We stayed in room 315 a family of 5 (3 tennagers 2adults) and had plenty of room, 3 queen beds, 2 rooms !. The rooms have glimpses of the bay and views of some famous landmarks, 1 of the rooms has a balcony. Overall I would definitely stay here again, we loved it !

The Columbus Motor may not offer the best views from some of the rooms, but it is very reasonable for it's location. The desk staff were very helpful with directions to restaurants, sights, and bars. It has all that you need and a bit more. Flat panel Tvs, free parking and easy check ins made this a nice inn. I would definitely consider staying here again. A business center would be nice just for printing off boarding passes.

Stayed here on a vacation with friends. Was within a couple blocks of all the major San Francisco sights. Found out after we got to the hotel that they have a shuttle to the airport and have free parking. We took the BART and then a bus which dropped us off across the street from the hotel. Beds were comfortable. Bathrooms were a little old but still decent. Would definitely stay here again.

Next to Market Street with easy access to shopping and restaurants. Walking distance to Embarcadero and Sauselito. Modern Lobby with dark interior and comfortable sitting area. Outside patio bar. Rooms rather standard with a small bathroom but nice city views from the upper floors. We had a good deal for $180 for a deluxe room. Next time I would rather prefer the W hotel.

Can't beat the location which is next to Westfield mall. Check-in staff is friendly. However, we asked for a bottle opener to our room and the one we got was one without a lever which I could not use. Asked if we could get another one and was bluntly rejected. The concierge day and night shift staff gave contradicting advice on transport options to the airport... Overall frustrating experience....

review_title: Great hotel, great location, great city!
review_text: Great hotel, lovely spacious rooms with balconies, great service and more importantly a fantastic location in San Francisco. It's minutes walk from the Wharf and right on Columbus which is full of great bars and restaurants. Be sure to visit Trader Joe's just 2 blocks away and the cable car!

Stupott , London 
We stayed here for 3 nights in June. 
This isn't the newest of hotels or the best around but if you want value for money this hotel is great. You get to park for free a rarity in SF its a short five minute walk to Fishermans Wharf and about fifteen to the Alcatraz Ferry pier. The cable cars are close by and so is Lombard Street. The shops and restaurants in Fishermans Wharf don't seem to open until ten am but if you want an early feed mcdonalds seems to be the popular choice. Overall the Columbus motor inn is good value for money.

review_title: Great location, shame about the noise
review_text:
In hind sight we should have asked to be moved after the first night, but we thought our neighbours might be checking out! 
Initial worries over nightclub we overlooked unfounded as club only opens Fri/Sat and we stayed Mon-Thur, however the thin Walls mean noisy neighbours can be heard clearly and opening and shutting of room doors is very annoying. We were in a corner room between kids/parents (why they didn't offer them an adjoining rooms that the internal door could be used I don't know) and they were constantly going from one room to another!
Front desk staff were generally courteous and helpful and the hotel is in a great location for exploring the city with bike rental places close by and easy access to the cable cars and nonproblem exploring from here on foot. 
Reasonably priced compared to others in similar area but not for light sleepers!

review_title: Nice hotel in a great city
review_text: Nice, clean hotel not a lot of the bells and whistles of boutique hotels but convenient to Starbucks, BART, Chinatown. Clean rooms, nice service! Reasonably priced!

This hotel is so nice, they have a wonderful restaurant called "Ducca" in the hotel. It is very unique and good food. The staff at both hotel and restaurant are amazing, couldn't have had a better stay!

The overall stay was spoiled by the 48.00 plus tax(54.00 +) for 4 nights was unreasonable for the guests. I did not like that this was not diclosed so we were kind of disappointed. Also a view of the roof. I would expect a nicer view for all the money $$$ spent. I will
never stay at Westin again.

review_title: great location + excellent room and view
review_text: arrived 2 hours early for check in but they gave us a room anyway - corner room, 14th floor with great views of the city. staff was very attentive, called our Yosemite tour for us. Location is superb, right on the financial disctrict, a block from market street, there's starbucks, quisnos, subway, 7-11, mcdonald's. Bart station is just two blocks away and embarcadero is a 10-15 minute walk. The only con is you pay extra for everything else like breakfast, wifi, local calls etc. Otherwise I'd stay here again if the rate is right

Overall a solid performance that you would expect from a Westin. The rooms were nice and spacious, and location was good being only a short walk from Union Square. Service was only average - highlighted by a very slow check-in. Rooms were also on the expensive side - so hunt around for a deal. I would stay here again.

Rooms- clean
Staff- extremely helpful, especially the concierge
Service- very prompt
Rooms- updated and clean
Bar- amazing view!
Loved my stay!

We stayed here in SOMA at the height of the summer tourism season and expected a crowd. We got that and more. Not just touring families but swarms of businessman attending the convention next door. Swarms, moving in packs, ignoring everyone else, swamping the lobby, restaurants and sidewalks. An experience to avoid if you have small children or want to be reminded less of the drone of the business world. 
Staff are refreshingly personable under the circumstances, an amenity we always value highly. From bellman to parking attendant to sales, all showed commitments to individual and friendly service. Only exception would be the concierge lounge, which actually has no concierge, and even though designed to be an amenity, was anything but. Relentlessly overcrowded, this inadequate space is staffed with rude attendants who make you feel like you're imposing on them by being there. What could be a great respite for the frequent traveler here has become nothing but an extension of the chaos in the lobby. Big oversight Marriott!
Otherwise, just steps to cable cars, trolleys, BART, so about as convenient as it gets. Even so, next time I will trade being in the center of a whirlpool of businessmen for a less convenient spot that offers a rhythm other than full speed.

review_title: This is an ok hotel, bit tired round the edges, but great location, and nice theme.
review_text:
We stayed for a couple of nights. We loved the location Fillmore street rocks, great shops, bars and restaurants and japan town itself is fun too. We had breakfast at mels dinner a 15 minute walk away and at a great little bakery on Fillmore street so can't comment on that. The reason for the low score is the decor is a little tired. Great fun bathroom, japanese style and we liked the window panels, but it could have been cleaner.... Nice touch they gave us a bottle of wine for free as a welcome. 
We absolutely loved a bistro on 1950 Fillmore street florio, best ragu I've tasted ever, even after all my trips to Italy!
hotel_name: Hotel Kabuki, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: The design of this hotel is really interesting. Everything was very clean, with different little touches in the rooms that you wouldn't usually find in a hotel. It's great to be right in japantown, and it's only a short bus or taxi ride to other sights in the city. Staff were all very helpful, giving directions and advice about the area.
hotel_name: Hotel Kabuki, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: Rooms a bit worn & dated, but excellent location
review_text:
My husband stayed here for three nights during our anniversary trip. Fantastic location, with the rest of Japantown only steps away, plus a Japanese mall adjoining the hotel itself.
If we were going to stay here again, we would have specifically asked for a room with a view of the courtyard garden. Ours looked onto the street plus had more street noise than I assumed other rooms had.
Loved the Japanese decor of the room, but everything looked a bit worn/dated. There was a big tear in the tatami mat, for example, that the hotel had attempted to hide with a chair instead of replacing. Both the tub and shower had minor mechanical issues, but my husband was able to fix the shower head.
Despite the above, however, we very much enjoyed our stay. The location is stellar re: access to Japantown and an interesting neighborhood.
hotel_name: Hotel Kabuki, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text:
This is definitely a big, convention style hotel, the type that I usually try to avoid. However, the facilities are excellent. They have several restaurants and a full Starbucks right in the lobby.
Their fitness center is outstanding and it also has a full pool. You're right at market street so it's pretty convenient to get anywhere. Therefore, overall this is a good placento stay. Just realize that th,e lobby will always be crowded.

Floor to ceiling window, up high, view up the bay... Wow...
Asked for a high room with a good view when checking in - we were close to the top. Walked in the room and the view was amazing... NB if you suffer vertigo - get a much lower floor - or close the blinds.
Hotel location is great, eight near union square, trams are 200 metres away.
This was a great pitstop for 2 nights on our whirlwind tour of US & this hotel was comfortable & friendly.
5 stars because I ignored factoring in the service (or lack of) from the lounge bar in lobby. NB all other staff were amazing. But we usually are happy with ebbs & flows of happenings. Not demanding, just wanting good service but realise not everyone can be 100% all of the time.

review_title: Pleasantly surprised for a big-city Westin
review_text:
I am a Starwood Preferred guest but to date have not been impressed by Westins in popular tourist destinations like San Francisco. I was pleasantly surprised by this one. 
My husband had checked in to a regular king room then I joined him later in the trip. The check in lady was extremely apologetic that they couldn't then upgrade us to a better room or higher floor because they were sold out (btw we hadn't asked). I was expecting something tiny & dingy but the room was a good size and although only on the 9th floor we had a good view and it was still quiet. The bathroom was tiny but otherwise the room exceeded expectations. 
The location was great - right on the trolley lines and right around the corner from the shopping area. I would definitely book at this hotel again.
Recommend for business or pleasure. Excellent location. Service is great. Rooms are a little small but well appointed.

review_title: One of a kind hotel, great location
review_text:
I stayed here a couple of weeks ago for the weekend and had a great San Francisco experience. The hotel is low key and quietly cool, but with all of the qualities and high standards of the Kimpton chain. I loved the coffee in the AM (good quality organic stuff) and the cookies in the evening! The bathroom was spotless, great shower. The rooms are a bit small, but the hotel is in an old building and it was really quiet. I didn't get a room with a Bay Bridge view, but the view is yours the second you walk out the back entrance.
The location is great for a mini break. Very accessible to Union Square, the Embarcardero, AT&T stadium. Great food options at the Ferry Market Terminal for breakfast and lunches. There is a BART stop a few blocks away, along with cable cars and busses.
The only thing to watch out for is the taxi situation. Steuart St is a one way street and not much traffic, especially on the weekends. It was hard to just flag a taxi, concierge had to call them. Also, the hotel staff pushed the hotel town car option to SFO pretty hard--after explaining a couple of times that I wanted to take a taxi, they finally called one for me. It was a minor annoyance--town car was $45 (plus tip), a taxi is about $35.
hotel_name: Harbor Court Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: We stayed here and of all the hotels we stayed in our month long vacation in the US (which included New York, DC, Vegas, and San Fran) the Abri staff were by far the friendliest and most helpful. The hotel is in a great location only a few minutes walk from shopping restraunts and tram lines and has clean comfirtable and modern rooms with large LCD tv free wifi and charging for iphones.
We had a beautiful room, great view and a perfect location! The price was right and the staff was very helpful. We would definitely stay at this hotel on our next visit to SF.

We just checked out of the Westin Market Street, I was not impressed. Seems this Westin has not been updated as others. The room we stayed on was on the 21st floor but nothing special about it. Room seemed outdated for a Westin. The location was the best figure during our stay in SF.

Look if you're coming to SF on vacation to stay in your room the whole time this probably isn't the right place. The rooms are really small but they tell you that on their site, they give you the sq ft for each room, and when they say 164 sq ft they mean it. Our room was tiny but it didn't matter. We were only paying like $150/night in SF, that's a steal. We were mostly only in the room to sleep or get ready. If you can't find other stuff to be doing in SF, then get a life or pony up the extra scratch and book a luxury hotel. The Harbour Court nails it's demographic, young, hip, adventurous, budget conscious travelers looking for some amenities but nothing overwhelming. 
My wife and I had a great time. The location is the embarcadero which is great if most of your activities are up north but with all the public trans in SF it turned out to be easy to navigate the entire city from there. The staff is extremely friendly and were as helpful as they could be. I would absolutely stay at this hotel again. If you stay here and don't like the staff, something is wrong with YOU, trust me.
hotel_name: Harbor Court Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: Stayed here the day before thanksgiving and it was great. Had always wanted to stay here after living in Austin and always admiring the beauty from outside. Everything was great. The lounge was espescially nice. If you want and elegant and comfortable stay choose the Driskill.

The regular rooms are tiny. After placing two bags on the floor, you have essentially no open floor space. As a current resident of NYC, I am used to small spaces but this room is just too cramped. The other main complaint is the quality of the bed linens - every time I moved, it sounds like I was rolling around in a stack of newspapers. The location is great since you are near the Bay Bridge, ballpark, and some nice restaurants/shops along the Embarcadero. As with Kimpton hotels, you get the free lobby happy hours, so that is always a nice touch.
hotel_name: Harbor Court Hotel - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: Beautiful, historic, cozy hotel in a fun location with a super nice staff. Would love to go back!

This is a stunning hotel in the perfect location. We had a suite as there was 3 of us. Great size, but would the bathroom for the rooms with a sofabed were in through the other bedroom which was not ideal. We checked in to a street view room, but were offered a change if it was too noisy, which it was. We had a lovely room looking into a courtyard. Staff in the hotel and restaurant next door were excellent. Plus free tea/coffee each morning/ access to business centre and a drink each evening made this place perfect. Definitely check out the bar/restaurant next door.

everything about this hotel was amazing! i called at 8am to see if i can check in early and i was told that they have a room available so i can check in early. checked in at 9am, i'm very thankful. free upgrade from queen bed to king bed was also provided for free. the bed was very comfortable and there's a DVD player provided which was a real plus!!! the staff was very friendly and helpful. i'd stay here again.

review_title: There is no noise insulation in rooms backing onto Ellis street
review_text: I stayed in a room backing onto busy street. A night club went in until about 2.30am. Every word could be heard due to poor double glazing.

review_title: It was a like a dream.
review_text: Hotel was so comfortable! Beds-perfect. Rooms-big and beautiful. Lobby-luxurious. Location- really? SO MUCH FUN.

I loved the location of this hotel. Perfect if you have to walk anywhere as it is close to 6th Street and a short walk to the Second Street district.
The rooms are smaller than expected, but very comfortable. The beds are amazingly soft!
The one downside was that the room smelled a bit musty/smoky when I first went in. Perhaps this is due to the age of the hotel, but it would be nicer if the room was aired or a scented candle were used prior to guests arriving.

I was hesitant about staying here booked by a corporate travel agency. The lobby is like full of the Mad Hatter from Alice in Wonderland's fabrics and dark. Elevators (2) are super tiny and is like riding the Cash Cab with different coloured ceiling lights. Hotel rooms are super tiny smaller than rooms I've stayed at in Hong Kong (where real estate is tight). First room was a definite no go where bed was a weird twin and a half on a weird upholstered bed. Bathroom is a closet and can't shut the door and sit on toilet at same time. Rooms have a funky smell too. Upgraded to a king bed which is more normal but the other attributes remain the same, small, funky, weird smell. There are also Fred Flintstone random bathrobe in the teensy closet. Location is all right but at this price would rather stay at a chain hotel. Fact that it's pet friendly is concerned too as dirty pets may have been in the bed...ew. Stay away if you have chain standards. I even stayed at off beat hotels in China and they were bigger and not so weird and creepy.

review_title: Central location, historic value and an amazing deal made this hotel amazing!
review_text: The rich history, perfectly decored rooms and great deal we got made this centrally located hotel a highlight of our trip to Austin. If you are looking for the place to stay in Austin and want a step up without breaking your wallet this is a great choice!

review_title: This is not a 4 star hotel let alone 5 star!!!
review_text:
I booked this room as a vacation package for a friends 40th birthday getaway. The original package was 577.00 with taxes. The Driskill also charges 27.00 per night plus tax for parking and their main restaurant was closed for renovations.
I realized I was charged 368.00 for the first night, I spoke with the manager Michelle who argued that this was the proper rate. After producing an email that showed her what I was quoted, she still argued with me until I asked her if she didn't want to stand by my quoted rate. She finally said she would yet part of the package was an upgraded room which we didn't get. I received no apology, just attitude like I was wasting her time even though we were staying on the off season. Also, we were woken up by screaming girls in the middle of the night, which was so bad, the Austin police responded. I wish I would have booked at the W. I am sure the Residence Inn which is a couple blocks away is probably a better choice.

review_title: A great place for your four legged friend too.
review_text: Great place to stay with Fido too. Very dog friendly hotel ad with biscuits treats and water bowl upon entering. I had to bring fido here during the summertime and will do it again. Staffs are friendly and attentive all you need to do os pick the phone tell them what you need then consider it done. Its noisy during weekends so get the highest level as possible if not head over to walgreens and get earplugs rated at 33db level trust me you will need it.

I've stayed here once before on business, but this one was with the fiance. The whole vibe is a bit hipsterish, but there were plenty of middle aged average folk like us so we felt right at home. And welcomed - really. 
The staff were super friendly, start to finish. The room was not massive but it was comfortable. Bed was very comfy. Decor was definitely stylish but not overdone.
And we'll miss the free wine reception, which in December offered also a hot toddy as a "seasonal" alternative. Man, we loved the hot toddy, along with the welcoming fireplace where we drank it. People were hanging out there - it was quite festive. I'd stay here again.

review_title: Great Location, Lots of Charm, Standard Service
review_text: You can't beat the location in the center of all the Downtown Austin action, and the hotel's historic charm is well-preserved while remaining extremely well-kept. The service is adequate, though nothing special. I would recommend it for location and charm, but not to those expecting white-glove service.

This hotel is like a palace. Staff is helpful and happy. Weird but cute doll sized chairs were samples sales men selling furniture brought around... cute. Softest towels of any hotel ever! Seriously challenge me! Amazing food at cafe. Try cheese soup. Bed is luxurious and every care is put to details. Just a charming historical hotel in the heart of Austin
The Triton is a nice boutique hotel. Nice touches like the wine hour and fruit. Location is good next to China town and shopping. A good choice for an alternative to the larger hotels.

review_title: Great hotel for price and location!
review_text:
A great lodging choice located in the heart of the Fisherman's Wharf district. Only 1 block from Powell-Mason cable car line too. 
Hotel was clean, staff was courteous and efficient and is a great value for the location. 
Only thing missing that you might be looking for is a pool. 
Would definitely stay here again.
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf

review_text: Hotel's location is great, but there are better places to stay in Fisherman's Wharf. This hotel needs updating as the rooms show signs of wear. Also check your bill carefully as they tried to bill us $90 for parking, which was already included in our price and they were reluctant to remove the charge.
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf

review_text: Great home base for an Austin adventure. Amazing architecture and great interior deco. Concierge Emily Monroe was key to our wonderful stay.

review_title: Excellent hotel, really great customer service & great location.
review_text: Definitely one of the best hotels I ever stayed in. Really friendly staff that pays attention to your every need (they even gave us a free bottle of wine & upgraded our room for our birthdays). All in all, it was definitely the icing on the cake for a memorable stay in San Francisco.

review_title: It was great...til I encountered the bed bugs!
review_text: I have stayed in Kimptons before and when I come to SF i usually stay at the Palomar. As this was Pride weekend and I figured it would be pretty hectic on Market St, I went with the Triton instead. It's a great location right by the gate to Chinatown and an easy walk to the BART. I was given a king room and yes it was small but nice and even on the second floor the noise wasn't bad at all. I stayed two nights and during the first I could swear something was in bed with me. And sure enough in the morning there were bites. But as I'd been out at Fisherman's Wharf the previous evening I thought maybe it was mosquitoes. Last night however, I wasnt feeling well so I was in bed by 8. And within a couple of hours, I had loads of bites on my arms and legs and even my face. I went to reception and asked to move and as soon as I showed them the bites, they not only moved me, but moved me to a king suite. Great, if I wasn't now paranoid about bed bugs! I know SF is known for having a bed bug problem but I was really disappointed that even the Triton had them. That the receptionist didn't seemed shock at all is also really disappointing. In the morning when I checked out, a different receptionist commented on how few people tell them when they see bed bugs. Sorry, but that's not really much of an excuse for having them and not keeping your rooms clean! I will be contacting Kimpton as I think they need to totally fumigate not only that room but probably the whole hotel! Oh and maybe train the staff to not dismiss your bites as mosquito bites - that didn't sit well with me. So overall, a great location and fair service but until they fix the cleanliness problems I won't be staying there again or any other Kimpton. Shame really.

Good hotel, but a bit Noisy. Hear cable car, neighbour room people speaking and people on floor. Thin walls. Service ok if tipped ......
Good location on top with cable car stations in front
hotel_name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel

review_text:
Its a functional / large hotel. Old in places but the rooms are clean and it's good value for money.
Located on the edge of the dodgy part of town but as long as you stay on the time square side you are all good.
Lobby busy with people but the staff are efficient and friendly who are always happy to help.

Tuscan Inn isn't as nice as some other Best Western/Kimpton hotels, but it was clean and the location was nice. Easy walk to Pier 39 and the wharf. Not too far from public transport and lots of taxis around. The pizza room service they offered was mediocre, but there's a Safeway across the street and a Starbucks around the corner. The two-bedroom suite was cramped with small windows, but nicely decorated.
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf

review_text:
I have visited this hotel more than I can count for both business and personal travel. It is in the heart of everything that is San Francisco's downtown. With that said, everything that comes with a major metropolitan area including high crime, homeless and drug infested neighborhoods are all part of this cities layout. One tip for this area is to not pass Ellis st. (stay north of Ellis st.). Basic rule of thumb, exit the hotel onto O'Farrell and turn right.... Shopping, great food and local shops await. 
One consistent problem that I have at this particular Hilton property is the lack of respect for the "do not disturb" sign. They will knock, enter and call your room with complete disregard for your comfort and privacy. 
On a better note: the breakfast is always consistent. The counter and wait staff are always chipper and helpful. And once inside the property, safety is a high priority because the hotel always has a boat load of security on staff waiting to assist you around every corner.

Stayed with the family. The hotel has a nice driveway entrance. The hotel itself is at the top of nob hill. We found going up and down the hill actually enjoyable. The cable car line does go right by the hotel. The staff was not overly friendly. We had two beds in our room and it was rather cramped. The beds were pretty comfortable. Our view was over an ugly courtyard. I asked for a high floor as a gold member and was given one of the lower floors without explanation. Small bathroom with little privacy.
hotel_name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel

review_text: Amazing location atop Nob Hill with beautiful SF bay views, on intersection of 2 cable car lines, & Union Square shopping/restaurants only a couple blocks away. Pretty large rooms (by San Francisco standards), super comfy beds & nice lobby bar.
hotel_name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel

review_text: We used our Marriott points to stay here during out trip to San Francisco. We were immediately upgraded for free to a studio suite on the top floor without asking. The view was out of this world. You can see the bay bridge and beautiful skyline. We ordered room service for dinner and breakfast and everything was delicious! The hotel is right next to the fairmont hotel where the rooms cost 5x the amount but you still get the same great location and service for better value! There is a cable car stop right outside the hotel. Such a great and convenient location. The Decor was fresh and modern. The beds were super comfortable. Everything was top notch in my book. Aveda products are used here! Highly recommend this hotel. No negatives!
hotel_name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel

review_text: Small room for a family with only a small double sofa bed for the 2 kids to share. We found pier 39 a bit tacky and so location although great for fisherman's wharf was a bit wasted on us. If I were you I'd save money by staying downtown & just go to the wharf for a visit.
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf

review_title: This hotel was probably nice in the 80's!
review_text: This hotel is old. If you are expecting the decadence of hilton hotels as depicted in madmen, forget it. No safe in the room. Mini bar fridge was broken. Mirror in bedroom cracked. Wifi connection expensive with a very slow connection. I was awakened by the sound of banging pipes every morning. The lobby in front of tower 1 elevator smells like a garbage dumpster. The staff was friendly but not very helpful. And their doorman stands around and shoots the sh*t while you struggle with the door and your bags. I have stayed at motels and had a better experience. The restaurant was very good and the service there was excellent. Also, you can't beat the location.

review_title: Nice clean Hilton convenient to shopping and restaurants
review_text: We stayed at the Hilton after spending one night in a horrible "boutique" san Francisco hotel. The lobby was always busy, the hotel restaurant also with a line far outside the door. After having a light lunch here one day, glad we didn't spend time waiting in this line for breakfast. Mediocre food and service. Fitness center was decent, room service food very good but slooow. Overall, not a bad place to stay in the city.

review_title: Nice hotel, good location. Room is very small and no view.
review_text: Very close to the Union Square, this is a nice place to stay. The free wifi is very slow. The room is small but clean.

review_title: Great hotel in a great location
review_text: Great hotel in a great location. Â Fast check in. Â All around clean and quiet room. Â Could be a little more spacious but hey it's in downtown San Francisco!!! Â Very nice gym. Â Starbucks in the hotel a plus.

We stayed at the hotel the second weekend of October extending our adventure up the coast just before hitting Yosemite. The hotel had a great rate for the weekend booked the Monday beforehand. For me, this hotel is way too large and too busy. Reception was quite friendly, cordial, well informed and showed a genuine interest in accommodating us. The lines and wait were annoying buther service made up for the inconvenience.
The accommodation was SMALL, with our bags it was not comfortable, although being in a center city location we did not spend much time in the accommodation. The bathroom was nice ut the doors were these french styled closet doors which slammed loudly and did not afford too much privacy. Kudos to the bath amenities, I wanted to steal some extras from the Housekeeping Cart but did not see any. They were quite special, upgraded for sure and wondered if they had been locally sourced.
Be prepared to wait for anything you may want from this hotel. I will admit that everything utilized coffee, concierge and internet was truly good quality. I may be slightly jaded as my preference seems to wain towards something more personal than what I experienced with this hotel. With the pricing they provided intact, I would stay with them again.

Great location. 
Small room. Expected larger because of the brand name. There was a conference so check on that when you book. 
With my 4.5 and 1.5 yr olds. San Fran isn't for toddlers but they were trooper and the cleaning staff were very sweet. Tucked her blanket in the bed. Have us extra towels. 
Sink didn't drain. Shower didn't work. No room wifi. We r in 2011 right?
Anyway, the location is really great and I suppose it's the same for every hotel in a big city. 
Try the Olympic Cafe on Jones, around the corner. You could order two breakfasts which is enough for and the prices are great for the amount.

We stayed at the Renaissance Stanford from July 8-11th. The hotel is in a wonderful location with access to all the cable cars and short cab rides away from important San Fran destinations. Hotel was spotless, and the staff was courteous, especially the doormen. Their service was exceptional. We are Marriott rewards members and the only disappointment was the club lounge was closed for the weekend. It opened on Sunday evening. However for the inconvenience we were upgraded to a larger corner room with a lovely view of the city. Would definitely stay there again.
hotel_name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel

review_text: En apparence hÃ´tel trÃ¨s mignon et chambre grande et propre mais l'envers du dÃ©cor pas trÃ¨s trÃ¨s jolie... ProblÃ¨me de plomberie de tuyauterie, douche qui fuit, wc qui Ã©vacue mal! Isolation inexistante, bruyant comme si vous dormiez dehors! Accueil minable et prix pour le parking pour une nuit 35$, de quoi vous faire regretter la rÃ©servation. Ne recommande pas du tout cet hÃ´tel.
hotel_name: Hotel Kabuki, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: Tres bien placÃ© a Union square! Ideal pour visiter!
review_text:
Tres bon hotel en plein centre, belle chambre
Mal insonorisÃ© pour une chambre donnant sur rue.
Parking de l'hotel cher.
Great place to spend the weekend at while visiting San Francisco. Our room had a bad TV and we were offered another room or $50 discount per night! Can't be that!
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf

review_text: Internet was out but everything else was good. I would stay here again.

I stayed here for a convention in town in may. I'm usually one to stay at a five star hotel, but they were all full, and so I ended up at Baldwin. I wasnt sure of staying here but by night two I knew I had found a real gem! 
The staff here does anything, they really go the extra mile. What a great team. Location is perfect - so close to everything in San Fran and I loved being by china town and the shopping just two blocks away! I was able to spend some of the hundreds I saved by staying at Baldwin! 
It would be nice if they added a mini fridge or updated the elevators but hey, those are very minor complaints. 
Overall, if you are considering Baldwin and aren't sure - stop reading reviews and just book this perfect little hotel!!

Lovely central location but be prepared for the hill (tram not working the weekend we were there)! Paid extra for city view but just a street view, other rooms had internal view only. Food and drink there expensive but lots of lovely cafes within short walk for breakfast and free WiFi. Staff very helpful and friendly.
hotel_name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel

review_title: Nice hotel... On the top of a hill. Street cars can be loud if your window is looking out over the street.
review_text:
Nice place. Would stay here again but you will have to walk up (and down) a good size hill if you stay here. In union square/nob hill. Close walking distance (less that 1 mile) to some very good restaurants.
Next time I'll ask for a room away from the the main street. 
Do not eat at the hotel resturant. Bad food.
hotel_name: Renaissance San Francisco Stanford Court Hotel

review_text:
Grand hÃ´tel bien situe au niveau des transports (trams, mÃ©tro, bus au pied de l'hÃ´tel).
Notre chambre Ã©tait un peu vieliotte mais avec une belle vue sur le Bay bridge.

Stayed here for 2 night trip to SF. Location is brill you can walk to all the sites easy. Close to BART stations. Rooms clean and have all the amenities. Paid only 60$ a night, which in my experience is great value. Recommended !!!!

No complaints at all about the hotel. It is perfect to everything. Pier 39 and 42. Close to transport, cheap taxi from the airport. 
Room was a good size for San fran, air con was good, bathroom great and big, staff extremely helpful at all times!! Quick check in and out. Extremely efficient young male works on the front desk, he needs an award. 
Only downside is the restaurant next door, which offers extremely poor service at all times and has very rude staff. Avoid at all cost! We had vouchers for breakfast so went each day, we were no too concerned as we had booked room only so breakfast was an added bonus!
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Tuscan Inn at Fisherman's Wharf

review_title: Not too expensive in a good central location
review_text:
We stayed for 2 nights in room 903.
Some sound carried up from the street despite being 9 floors up and the shower was really noisy.
Apart from that, the room was clean, the bed comfortable and it's location was really central.

review_title: Great value in a great location
review_text: Old hotel, was very clean and nicely located. We could walk to union square in 5 minutes, china town in 1 minute, and to pier 39 in half an hour or less. North beach (little Italy) was a scenic walk through china town in 15 minutes. Everything was very clean. Bed was small and tv hummed, but was a good nights sleep with a cool view. All we wanted and more for what was paid. A great value.

review_title: Never again! This is just for older people, who don't have high claims to stay in a modern hotel.
review_text:
After staying in this Hotel for 4 nights:
In my opinion this is a very old fashion hotel located in downtown with many homeless people around.
The rooms are very small, especially the bathroom is euquippet with dark light and not much space!

review_title: Average hotel but in a good location
review_text:
Radisson Hotel Fisherman's Wharf
We are a well traveled English couple in our late 40's / early 50's and have traveled all over the world in the last 25 years staying in 2* accommodation to 5*. This is an objective review of the Radisson Hotel at Fisherman's Wharf over a 2 night period in September 2011.
We drove to this hotel from the Yosemite National Park and the Sat-Nav found the hotel without any problems. 
The check in was good, no problems, as was the check out. Our room reminded us of a budget motel style room in the UK, functional but nothing special. The bed was comfortable and the room had a big wide screen TV. that we never used. The windows were quite dirty and a lot of black mould was evident on them, however, the room itself was clean apart from this. The bed was comfortable and had an electronic adjustment feature. My wife seemed to like this but I could not see the point in it. The room had coffee making and ironing facilities, it also had a hairdryer.
The bathroom was clean, of a normal size and functional with the usual complimentary toiletries.
The hotel had what looked to be a diner style restaurant attached to it, however, we did not use this as a number of good eating places are very close by.
The hotel has no bar and we found this quite strange; we can never recall staying in a hotel before that did not have one. They did say that we could bring in our own drink and they would provide glasses for us. Again this is a strange policy as most hotels do not like you brining food or drink onto their premises.
The hotel has a fire-pit that is okay; it has a glass shield so it is not as affective as many we have sat around.
They have a small pool that looks okay but we did not use it.
Wifi, now you should know that this is a pet hate of ours. We feel that it is quite ridiculous in this day and age to be asked to pay for this service. It is our opinion that wifi access should be free in almost all circumstances, it's a vital tool for life in the 21st century and to charge for it when a facility is in place in a given location is just a ripoff. We are please to say that this service was offered free of charge, so well done to the hotel for this.
Parking. You park your car yourself and then pay for the privilege, quite unacceptable!!!
Location. This is the perfect location for a hotel as you have easy access to the local bars, restaurants and both sea and land trips. We went on a hop-on-hop-off open top city tour bus and also on an evening Alcatraz boat trip; both were very good and worth the money. We did book the Alcatraz trip in the UK and this was a good thing to have done. If we had not booked in advance for Alcatraz we would not have been able to go to the island due to the lack of availability.
In conclusion we feel that this is an adequate hotel that does what it says on the tin but nothing more. If you are just looking for a base to explore from and crash into bed each night then it will be fine for you, but do not expect any more than this.

Talk about being in the right place. This hotel could not be better situated. Pier 39 is just outside the hotel. Alcatraz tours are a short 6-7 minute walk away. Great view of Alcatraz and the bay. Comfortable sleep number beds, a super friendly staff. Couldn't be happier.

review_text: Spent a long weekend with my wife and teenage daughter. Great hotel with excellent location and attentive service. I would easily return as I prefer smaller, friendlier hotels with European service to larger American luxury brands. Favorite part was the breakfast served in the hotel restaurant. Highly recommend.

It was our first time in san Francisco. But we now know where NOT to stay. You could hear so much noise no matter which area of the hotel you're in. You pay tons for parking and cant even get a free bagel or coffee in the Lobby in the morning. There is no hot tub, the pool is tiny. It seemed as though I was in a retirement home when I went to sit by the firepit. I found a safety pin laying on the floor of our room, thank goodness we don't have children. If I were you, go to the Sheridan across the street. That's also the closest place to get a drink. Oh and I failed to mention, the morning we left I was sitting outside the lobby by the street and a member of staff asked me to move to another bench so he could sweep. Lol. What a horrible impression San Fran has made. We won't return or send anyone to the Radisson, maybe just our enemies.

I stayed here with my 21 month old twins and my husband for a 3 night visit back to SF, where we used to live. This is in the Marina, just down the street from our old house, so I know the area really well. But neither I nor any of my friends knew Cow Hollow Motor Inn had great apartments for rent, or a huge underground parking garage.
We arrived Monday early afternoon, and they already had our suite ready, which was great since our babies were ready for a long nap. We had recently stayed at 3 different hotels on the east coast, including the Ritz in Philly, and no hotel could get the cribs in our room prior to our arrival, so we were so pleased to find the pack n plays already placed in our spacious apartment. 
Parking is covered, copious and free. There is a key-guarded elevator that goes right up to our floor; unfortunately, it stopped working Tuesday night and the front desk had no idea until I told them Weds morning, and it still wasn't working Thurs morning, so that's why only four stars for overall. But the pros of this place far outweigh the cons. The one bedroom was bright and spacious, with a big living room with fireplace. It was furnished with a large sofa, comfy chair, ottoman, flat panel TV, window seat and a desk in the corner. There is a fully equipped galley kitchen and a dining area for two adjacent. The bedroom has a king bed, flat panel TV, and large closet. The bathroom is spacious but not luxurious. There are hardwood floors and nice area rugs. My only complaint about Suite 141 is that the bedroom fronts Chestnut Street, and is therefore very loud. The buses continue to run past 1AM and deliveries on the street start before 5AM. But it was fine for our family of four in terms of space, but I couldn't sleep even with ear plugs. The room cost $235 per night, and I found out Tuesday morning that the two bedroom, two bath next door (Suite 142) was available and only $50 more! We moved right away. This apartment has an even larger living room that fronts Chestnut, but that's actually a bonus, a dining room with table for four, and full size kitchen. The guest bedroom has a queen bed but no TV. The master is very large with a king bed, flag panel, large walk in closet. The two baths are a bit smaller than in the one bedroom, but not a problem. It also has hardwood floors, a large coat closet, great furnishings (antiques and big cozy chairs), and the bedrooms are in the back. Suite 143 is also a two bedroom in the back, and 144 is a one bedroom in the back. I would suggest just avoiding the Suites 141 and (presumably) 241 upstairs. This place is great with excellent, attentive service (except for the broken elevator), and we are very happy with our stay. We will definitely stay here again when we come back and would recommend it to anyone.

review_text: what a great value. The rooms were fun, great for me and my 9 year old daughter. the location was not that great, but we rode the bus and where we needed to all around town. The front desk staff and housekeeping staff was very friendly. the japanese mall just south of the hotel was very inexpensive. the restaurants were a good value. I chose this hotel for its price point in being in the trip advisor top 50 of 250 hotels in san francisco. It was a great choice. I would highly recommend hotel tomo.
hotel_name: Hotel Tomo, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: Stayed for 5 nights. Free parking was a great draw to this hotel. Rooms are big, clean, but can do with a paint in some places. Big bed. Shower ok, the light in the bathroom sometimes did not work but wait 5 minutes and it did. Location is ok, if you stand out as a tourist you may get hassled by the bums but just ignore them. Got to take part in a wine tasting event for free. Overall would defiantly recommend but don't expect the same luxury as the brand new Hilton it is as it describes a motor lodge.
hotel_name: Phoenix Hotel, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: Nice hotel, nice pool, nice service
review_text: Different (in positive way) from other hotels in vicinitY, helpful stuff.
hotel_name: Phoenix Hotel, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: Nice place, but loud at night.
review_text: I really enjoyed staying here. The location was fantastic and the staff was very friendly. Only issue was at night the club across the street was so loud it felt like my bed was in the center of the dance floor. If you aren't planning on going to bed before 1am I would definately stay here. I would suggest if u are traveling with children to see if there is a room not as close to the club, or stay somewhere else. Other than that, its a good price and very clean facility.

My wife and I enjoyed three nights in the Taj. Excellent location for Union Square and the surrounding shopping and restaurants. The room was fine, but not as large as some we experienced. Clean, tidy and good service.
We would return to the Taj again and again.

review_title: In the right place and good value for money
review_text:
San francisco 
Is one of the worlds city's that is a must see city with loads to do and see. But you do need a good week there to see the sites. A tram ride shows you apart of the city but got on you feet and walk the steets so mush to look at from the seven sister to the golden gate Brige with it views over the bay. Great restaurants for romantic nights out and for family to. Buy the travel pass great value for money and the public transport is next to none (great) for getting around to place you want to see most.
Just a basic hotel in a nice location. Parking is expensive. $40/day. Some road noise can be heard.

Hotel rooms have been updated with three sheeted bedding but could use a deep cleaning. Inside of windows are very dirty and thick dust on top of bathroom light. Toilet leaks and water damage "bubble" above the shower from room above.
No restaurant but IHOP adjoins downstairs. The wharf side of hotel is all tshirt shops and restaurants and packed with people. Not a respite hotel but location is convenient to wharf and cable cars. Fire pit on patio shown on website is very small and is in contained courtyard with no view to the outside. During our stay it was constantly used by people smoking which rendered it useless to our family.(supposed to be a nonsmoking hotel). concierge was thorough and on the mark. I'm recommending for location only.

review_title: Great location shame about the road noise.
review_text: Stayed here three nights. Arrived in town at 9.20am after long Amtrak journey and able to check straight in. Much appreciated. Brilliant location. Easy to get around town. Clean and comfortable. But noisy at night from the Beach street traffic. You can actually hear people talking on the street below. So, a recommendation with reservations.

review_title: Very cool place, but under construction and some very rude staff...
review_text: A very cool hotel- fun atmosphere, great art deco designs, and very clean. I would have given more points-however, the two major down falls are the construction going on all day (hard to relax by the pool listening to the loud drone of a drill), and while most of the staff has been very accommodating and kind, a young man at the front desk was extremely rude- had I not pre-paid for my room, I would have moved to another hotel. He was rude enough to ruin my stay here- and has caused me to seek recommendations for food, sights, etc elsewhere. A big disappointment for $150.00/night. No restaurant or bar on site either. Would have considered staying here again- but this being my first experience here- it is also my last. Shame...the property itself is great.
hotel_name: Phoenix Hotel, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: One of the best I stayed. All staff are just desperate to answer your questions and help you. Immaculate room service, food is irresistible, they do extra effort for cleaning, staff is happy and v courteous. Gives tough competition to 5 stars. I am defenetly coming again here.

Room smells like smoke. Yelling kids at the pool after 10:00pm. Roll away bed was promised and they did not have one. we are waiting now and I have spoken to management twice in last hour. Patients are running thin. Will never stay here again. Nor will I recommend to anyone.

This radisson is right on Fishermans Wharf, a great location. The hotel is a bit dated and pretty noisy. 
Our room overlooked the car park so we didn't have the street noise but we did have very noisy plumbing, or rather the rooms around us did. Each time the rooms next door or above used the toilet or shower we knew about it via a noisy pump and rattling pipes. Notma problem in the morning, but when late arrivals check in duuring the night you are going to be woken.
The reception staff and concierge were very polite and helpful and arranged us a car via Enterpirse, cheaper than direct with Enterprise.
Johnny Rockets diner is adjoined to the hotel so if you want a good burger then check thus place out. Great value for money.
Overall the hotel was ok. It was booked with our air operator so was at a reasonable price.

The front desk staff was super friendly. They really gave the impression that they wanted you to enjoy yourself and wanted you to walk away happy. Rooms were bright and funky think ikea. Very clean. It is only 45 min walk to fishermans wharf and 30 min walk to chinatown. overall it was a great experience!
hotel_name: Hotel Tomo, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: For $300 a night, I expected more than a room with a broken lampshade, dirty curtains and a ceiling that was intact. Granted I was dressed as a stay at home mom would be, but Nathan was uber cold and suspicious when I asked for additional room key.

I stayed for a conference for a few days. The staff was excellent, they never got tired of smiling, the hotel has everything you need and more. Thhe food was excellent especially for banquets, I would go again on leisure

Property is situated next to Hooter's and In and Out Burger. On our first night, (a Sat.) there were guys walking through the courtyard, yelling playing catch football. This was around 1:30 am. Then at 5:30 am the owner of the bicycle rental store, inside the courtyard began hammering. This lasted for about 30 minutes, and I finally called the front desk to request another room. The person working acted surprised that we found the hotel to be loud, saying that no one else had complained, and that the courtyard facing rooms were the more quiet rooms. After reading other reviews we decided to stay put since other rooms were just as exposed to the parking garage and garbage truck noise. 
One trick is to keep the ac unit running to block out courtyard people's conversation. Towels were flimsy and shampoo scarce. I agree with another reviewer that the hallways smell. However, the 2 queen beds and plenty of pillows, were very comfortable. Also, the 2nd floor bistro is very clean with nice breakfast options, but for the price, better to walk to the actual Starbucks at the back of the building.

review_title: A dated venue in a good location.
review_text: We went on my honeymoon expecting luxury. The hotel is dated and whilst it is clean and well maintained, it really did disappoint as a venue. Location though is great although we expected more rather than being situated between a set of dirty diners and gift shops. The gym was tiny and the pool small but we weren't really there for that though. A big disruption to me was the miserable older black lady on check-in desk, her name escapes me. Whilst I've put no as a recommendation, I would if there were no other decent alternatives.

review_title: Good location but hotel has other issues.
review_text:
Just finished 6 nights here. Whilst the rooms were clean and the location fantastic, they really could brush up in other areas.
Firstly we booked b&b for a family of 4 yet didn't get "vouchers" for our children. Wasn't too fazed as the breakfasts next door were nothing at all special, especially as you could only have a cooked breakfast. Great if you want to have a healthy start to the day... not!
Secondly this hotel has a real noise issue. Permanently people running around screaming. At times it felt like a youth club what with the hordes of teenaged here an taking over the pool and communual areas.
Lastly we didn't find it dissapointing to be told that if we wanted a drink the courtyard we would have to go to a 7/11 and buy drinks to drink there. I don't think we have ever stayed at a hotel of this size without even a small bar... My wife wasnt too excited at the idea of drinking wine from a bottle out of a brown bag!
Not an unpleasant stay but would not return as plenty of other options....

My husband and I stayed at this location for one night. We arrived after check in time, the room was ready, front desk was very helpful, and asked why were here? We let them know we would be going to the giants game that night and instantly he gave us a map and what transportion we could use and the times and fares , it was so nice to not have to figure that out! The room was very clean - shower super clean, which is a big ? For most hotels, overall we would definitley stay here next time we come to sf!!!!

review_title: Great hotel, clean and well maintained. Perfectly located to fisherman's warf.
review_text: This is a great hotel located in the heart of fisherman's warf. The hotel appears new and is well maintained and clean. The rooms are comfortable and quiet. The staff was very accommodating and friendly. Hertz and Avis are right next door. Paid $179.00 a night

The free wi-fi was annoyingly unreliable. The TV remote didn't work. Our reservation for adjoining rooms was not honored. The front desk staff barely spoke English and could not effectively meet our needs because of it. Don't waste your money at Hotel Tomo.

review_text:
Nice little hotel, very clean and close to Fillmore street which has great night life and a lot of restaurants.
I loved the room decorations with Japanese art twist.
hotel_name: Hotel Tomo, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_title: one of the best deals you can find in SF
review_text: this hotel is a total satisfaction for the rates it charges.. everything from the lobby to the rooms make you feel good about staying here. the rooms are spacious w comfy beds and are good design. located in the japanese district it really has a hip and distinct character.
hotel_name: Hotel Tomo, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: Hosts were awsome upon check in. Took our luggage up to the room, offered directions to various places,gave us a map etc. Room was spacious and clean. A little noisy, but is right on Lombard st and this is a big city! Walking distance to Fisherman's wharf and other areas. Great price, FREE parking.

Typical courtyard as far as the rooms go. Decent size room with a couch and desk. Rooms are clean. Within walking distance to the wharf. Valet parking is offered at $36/day. A parking garage is next door and is a few bucks less. We found it more convenient to use the valet service. Staff was friendly. There isn't a restaurant on site, but there is a bistro open in the morning for breakfast on the second floor. You can charge purchases to your room. We didn't find it too noisy, but you are in a city.

I wish when this was recommended and I had checked the reviews that I would have had some advance warning about the beds. We had a room with two (double?) Beds. They were the most uncomfortable things I've ever slept on! The room was quiet, but I couldn't sleep becausei was so uncomfortable. I'll pay the money to sleep in a better known hotel where comfort won't totally be sacrificed! I am not too sure how really clean it was either.
hotel_name: Cow Hollow Motor Inn and Suites

review_text:
It's one of the closest hotels to Pier 39 and the hop-off bus is just around the corner, but there were a few downsides on this property in my opinion. First, this hotel looks and smells quite old. The room card keys were terrible, and I had to spend my entire stay fighting with the door. There is no fridge or a sitting area in the room, so having the entire family eating together was quite a chalenge.
Taking these problems aside, the place was overall ok thanks to their staff. Our room was ready before check in time and the conscierge was very helpful arranging our airport transportation. Rooms were clean, and despite some reports about the noise, I didn't hear anything, not even the cars from the parking right under my window bothered me (my room was on the 4th floor). For breakfast there was an Ihop and a seven Eleven on the same block and a little cart selling coffee and snacks on the lobby. 
Would recommend only if you really want to be close to Pier 39.
Whilst the hotel is a little dated, the rooms are comfortable and the staff were amazing. It is in an ideal location just minutes away from Pier 39.

4 days in San Francisco on our self drive tour of USA. First impression of hotel/ room was OMG how old is this place and what no fridge in the room. However upon settling in it was quite appRent that this place is all about it's location. A stone's throw from Pier 39 and Fisherman's Wharf at your doorstep - certainly spoiled for choice when it came to dining out. Close to all the loop and tour buses. A real happening location. Forgive the rooms they are clean and comfortable. Save your taxi fare and stay at the Radisson.
Greatest hotel. Best prices. Everything perfect. not in center but idealy situed
great hotel with very nice people it makes you like at home next time i go to SF i will repeat the redwood inn thanks for everything. Dyenno and folks, Natal, RN, Brazil.

I always believe location is the key of any hotel. This hotel as well, it is quite near the famous fisherman whalf. The room is clean, and there are some gift and grocery store around. Overall very good!
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf

review_text:
- Carpark cost $45 per night... Plus tax/tip = $120 for our 2 night stay. The receptionist was unable to do us any deals on this and disputed the fact my friend had got a deal when she was there earlier in the year. 
- Breakfast's only healthy item was banana, the rest was pre-made junk food- burgers, omlete, cinnamon buns still in their boxes straight from the freezer. All the drinks were sugar based & syrupy. Never seen anything like it in my life. I'm a 42 year old qualified chef. 
- The view was the windows of an adjoining concrete block, we could see something of a view, but as we'd specifically requested a high level room with a view, this was a disappointment. 
- The room was clean and the hotel is in a good location for fishermans wharf, that's what you're paying for here and that's all you get.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf

review_text: We stayed an entire week here and were really happy with our hotel choice. The location is superb: a short walk from the BART which we took to/from SFO airport, a short walk to the cable cars, a short walk to the trolleys and buses on Market, and tons of restaurants in the immediate area. Our room was on the 16th floor of Tower 3 which is where the pool is. As big as this hotel is we never had to wait for an elevator for more than 15 seconds. Amazing!

As a diamond member. I have stayed at several Hiltons. The service I received at this hotel was first class. The room had a gorgeous view of the city and the bay. This trip was not for business but for a milestone birthday for someone special. The staff at the hotel made us feel right at home and was there to help us with any needs we might of had. Will definatly be returning.

review_title: Reasonably priced hotel in a great location!!
review_text: We stayed here July 4th weekend and really enjoyed it! Perfect location and the price was phenomenal. Don't think we could have found anything better at this price. Parking is pricey $52/day for selfparking but we drove to SF so we had no choice. It was nice to have our car with us though.

My husband and I have stayed here a few times over the years, but this time they really outdid themselves. Their concierge service is great. They have always pointed us to the right direction and hooked us up with everything from restaurants to hairdressers. I love the beds - They are super comfortable. You are almost always guaranteed a great view, no matter which side you are on. I like the fact that you have agreat bar - with a view - just a elevator ride away. Granted technology is not their forte - this is where their stars get dinged the most - but their managers are willing to go the extra mile to assist you! On our first night our room was great, spacious and quiet, but had absolutely no wifi signal (938), the manager removed the internet charges, and connected us to their Internet provider, while they were able to improve it a bit, the Internet was crawling! The next day the manager called to follow-up, which I thought was a nice touch, and offered to move us to another room closer to the wifi point. While the new room had a better view, it was also louder - closer to the elevator and ice machines - but the Internet worked like a charm! Fast an easy. If we were here for a night, fine, I can leave without Internet, but 4 nights would drive me nuts! In the end, I am glad we moved! We will definitely keep coming back! We love San Fran!
This is the worst place ever. It is filthy. If you go to San Francisco stay at the Fairmont which is across the street.

review_title: Nice hotel, not so nice area.
review_text:
The hotel itself was very nice. Wonderful service and clean rooms. This hotel is huge and the lobby was almost always crowded. The ro om was spacious enough for your family of 5. The windows could use improvement - we could hear everything on the street and the city never slept here. The neighborhood isn't the best - lots of homeless and beggers. It was hard walking with young children because the sidewalks were so packed. That said, it's central and easy to get to public transportation. 
Parking at the hotel is insanely expensive, but there are plenty of other garages for less. We found a valet one for $25-35/night. The valet at the hotel offered to point some out to us too.

review_title: Fabulous historic building, unique location, lousy service.
review_text: Whatever the gracious history of this hotel, it's in the hands of the Intercontinental chain now. The building itself is gorgeous and in an unbeatable location with great views. But its age does mean that the rooms are tiny, and other than a small lobby and a restaurant on the roof (the Top of the Mark, which is perpetually full of backpackers gawping at the view) there are no public areas in the building. Want a cup of tea? Forget it. You either have to line up for 30 minutes at the aforementioned Top of the Mark ( no priority is given to hotel guests) or order from the glacially slow room service. The staff happily suggest you use the facilities in a couple of nearby hotels - indeed, they give every impression of wishing there were no guests in the hotel at all, so they can get on with running a tourist attraction, which is sadly what this place has become. The rooms are tiny with very limited storage space (no drawers!) and dominated by a massive bed (v comfy) and huge TV (unfortunately providing the dreadful Lodgenet service). If you 're lucky enough to get hold of room service and they actually deliver your order, there is no space to sit and eat. On the upside, the room decor is recent, period-correct and stylish, with opening windows and smart marble bathrooms, and well looked after and clean. Noise from the cable cars might be an issue for some people but for the middle of a major city, the location is pretty quiet. There are the usual chain hotel corner-cutting annoyances - $15/day for 1mb wireless, a very mean allocation of threadbare towels and toiletries - and a general sense that, behind the scenes, things are not going well.

My first impression of the hotel was that it was showing some wear in the rooms. The wallpaper was starting to peel off the walls and the glue was showing through. Our first room had a hole punched in the wall through the paper. Having said that, upon closer inspection, I saw that the room and bathroom were clean, as well as the rest of hotel. Upon entering our room, Joseph called from the front desk to see how we liked the room. When I mentioned the hole in the wall and the peeling wallpaper, he immediately offered another room. As I was leaving to go downstairs for the key to the other room, I was met by a pleasant woman with a clipboard who asked to see what the problem was with the room. We moved into the next room and enjoyed the comfortable beds, clean rooms and towels, and friendly staff. The only complaint I have is the $45.00 fee to park the car overnight. While the valets were friendly and always offered directional help, I feel the price was steep--especially when you add it on to the cost of the room. All in all, I would not hesitate to stay here again.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf

review_text:
what a beautiful hotel. I have stayed in Intercontinental Hotels all over the world and this one is one of the best. Huge room and bathroom. Great service and room was very quiet. 
yes, it is not uber modern in furnishings or style but this is Nob Hill in San Francisco! an area known for classic architecture and style. 
elegant hotel with an amazing breakfast buffet, great rooms, great service, and great location.

The hotel is in a Great location from which to explore San Francisco. Â Close to the wharf and public transport.Â 
The accommodation is modern, clean, and well kept with helpful and friendly staff. Our room was fairly basic but nice and had a large double bed. Free wi-fi was included for use in the lobby area.Â 
The only real downside is the typical express breakfast, which at best is pretty poor. Finding a table to eat at can also be a problem.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf

review_text: Excellent location near all wharf activities. Breakfast buffet selection far better than most HIE. Only negative is the smaller room size.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf

As breakfast is not cheap in this area. Just a few blocks from Fisherman's Wharf. They were great in setting up all our tours for us. Would be my first choice when returning to the Bay area
