review_text: j'y ai sejourne 4 nuits avec mes enfants, accueil excellent, chambre impeccable, situation exceptionnelle. A conseiller lorsque vous souhaitez visiter San Francisco.

review_title: Great location - but offers less than most holiday inn express'
review_text:
I have mixed feelings about this hotel. Great location, with easy access to the bay, fishermans whalf and all the aminities of the city. 
The negatives are it offered so much less than other holiday inn express hotels. There was no coffee available throughout the day, no onsite laundry and the rooms were just so tiny. Just big enough to hold the kingside bed and little else. The bed was so hard and could not manage to get a good night sleep at all.
Breakfast was ok, but lines far to long no matter what time of the morning you arrive. I think it was down to poor placement of the pancake maker and toaster. It held everyone up, would be far better if these were placed in a different location.
Expect to pay $45 Per day for parking, cheaper parking lots available near by.
Overall good clean hotel, put lacking the little extras.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf

review_title: Excellent experience in an excellent location.
review_text: We booked this hotel through an online website and got a great deal. We stayed here for our honeymoon and weren't disappointed. The service was great. The front desk staff was very helpful and exceptionally kind. We felt welcomed at this hotel. I am sure that we got upgraded to a nicer room because we were about halfway up and right in the middle so we had an amazing view. It was so gorgeous out during the week that we were there so we even opened the windows up to get a great breeze in the room. We would love to go back. It was in a good location to get around the city and do some shopping.

review_title: Good central location close to BART and cablecars
review_text:
First, it is pricey. But given you are downtown San Francisco that is expected.
Room is nicely setup with high end furnishings. My only negative is tv is horrible. Picture is not high def and they stretch the image I.e. distort, to fill the screen. Granted, I was out mostly, but watching news and sports highlights is hard to view. Sorry, this is a pet peeve of mine.
Food is great and the views from the restaraunt are stellar.
15 walk to BART, but hill is quite steep. Very safe area for walking and shopping. Many high end, mid range and specialty shops, including Chinatown are close.

The Holiday Inn Express, not to be confused with the nearby Holiday Inn is a good, basic, clean hotel in a great location only about 4 minutes walk to Fisherman's Wharf and great places to eat, as well as the F MUNI line. In particular:
1. Friendly service at check-in.
2. Rooms are clean.
3. Bed is comfortable. I suffer from a sore back so I should know.
4. Breakfast is provided for free. It is basic, consisting of various cereals, fruit, coffee and tea, juices, pastries, eggs and bacon and other meats, bread, toast and spreads. Served between 6.30 and 8.30, get there early or you'll find it hard to get a table.
5. Free wifi is provided in the lobby. This had download and upload speeds of about 7mb/s. It dropped out sometimes on my iPad. Rooms also have cable Internet.
6. My room didn't have a fridge, but you are provided with an ice bucket and there is a free ice-vending machine.
7. Shower pressure is not high but it heats up quickly.
All in all, a nice experience. I was there from 21-25 September, 2011.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf

review_text: I stayed on a street room and the upside was you are right nest to metro and the down side is you are right next to metro , the train is SUPER loud I can sleep through anything but if your bothered by noise don't stay in their street rooms . We really liked the room it was nice and homey . The staff was quite friendly , and polite and helpfull the only down side was we ran into a pummeling issue with our bathroom sink and they assured us it would be fixed but it never was , so no sink for 2 day. Overall a truly awsome location and I will stay again I'll just be sure to bring draino.

I could not fault ocean park, found it on trip advisor. Like everything it is all about what you want to pay for and what you are looking for. I wanted a proper American motel and ocean park was perfect. Simple, cOmfortable and clean - with parking. The motel is a good 30 minutes on the very frequent muni and two good local cafes just around the corner. One upscale and the other not. Zoo and beach a short walk. Only drawback is taking the Muni late night back to motel is NOT for the fainthearted. My story is seeing the most amazing fistfight - real bare knuckle stuff take place over a seat. A bit scary but a highlight of the trip and something to tell the folks back home.

This was nice choice for San Francisco. Nice room and bed good parking.Although well outside city,tram stop (end of line-zoo stop) just outside so very easy to get into city and find way back. Tram Price seniors $0.75 regular $2 tickets last 90mins. My only gripe with motel is the advertised WiFi didn't work and this is obviously a common problem as there Is a sign up at the office which blames the lack of reliability down to the old building. Very annoying as we tend to find next hotel by using internet night before. However all is not lost as there is good cafe very nearby with excellent speed (they also provide power points ) and most of their customers were making use of this. Food mostly sandwiches were very good.

The Top of the Mark is a must see! Great live music and a fun atmosphere. The hotel staff was friendly and helpful. And while the rooms were beginning to feel a bit dated in terms of amenities, apparently they were in the process of upgrading the electronics and furnishings.

review_title: Great location, must pay for everything however.
review_text:
Enjoyed the location very central. Concierge were helpful and organised a tour to muir woods easily.
The room was on the small side and no fridge. Internet was outrageous 15 dollars a day and 10 dollars to use the gym! Front desk were abrupt and attempted to charge me for the gym even though I ddnt use it.
Great hotel with excellent service from start to finish. Club room lounge was also really nice to have. Great room, food and service whilst being made to feel very welcome.

The hotel is situated in a great location for shopping, with Macy's, Niemen Marcus and Barney's New York just blocks away. The Wharf or the Piers are within a mile or two away. The hotel is sophisticated ad the rooms are very clean. I was very impressed with the upkeep of the room. The rooms are small but didn't bother us as we were out all days.

review_title: Wanted to like this place, but just could not
review_text: Stayed here based on excellent reviews. Garage entrance was akward. Room was on 6th floor and we had many sleepless hours because of street traffic, revelers and pedestrian noise, sirens, and service vehicles most nights. Gym and pool were nice but the locker room was a mess with used towels all over the place. Elevators were clean and quite fast. They tried to sell me upgrades and Internet at check-in (declined), but check-out was easy.
Wear and stains on carpet. And why bother with a giant flat screen that has the most minimal non-HD tv? A joke. For the money there are MUCH better hotels in this neighborhood.

Got a good deal on Priceline. Hotel is older but has been refurbished nicely. Bathroom was fantastic. Upon checking in, the hotel desk attendant offered a complimentary refridgerator for our daughter's food. Quick walk to Union Square, BART, and good restaurants. Hotel Nikko does border the Tenderloin so be careful walking around.

The hotel is in a great location. We had a 3rd floor room overlooking North Point ..... no traffic noise. The family room was large enough for 2a & 2c and very clean. Although the breakfast was included the quality was poor. The coffee was great but the use of plastic cutlery & paper plates was not the best. Often large lines between 7.30 & 8.30.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf

review_text: First class hotel near all the city locations; embarcadero, Powell cable cars, Union Square, shopping, etc

review_title: Impressed by the building, disappointed by service
review_text:
Very impressive building right next to the cable car line, but one block (on the steep hill) from muni stop. 
Very small reception for a big, busy hotel, and staff seemed rather unfriendly. The room had only one robe and a pair of slippers for three of us and housekeeper did not even refill shampoo the 2nd day. 
Minimal service, big disappointment.

review_title: Best hotel I have ever stayed in
review_text: This hotel is wonderful. The outside entrance is beautiful and makes you feel like royalty. Greeting was personable. Front desk awesome every time and extremely polite. Wilson at front desk took care of us the whole week. We had club access which is worth it as we got bottled water, sodas, cocktails in the evening, hor deuvres, small breakfast and snacks all day. The location is great. On topof nob hill with great views. Cable cars that go to union square or fishermans wharf. Def recommend muni pass. The bed was extremely comfortable. Room average mostly. No complaints. Top of the mark awesome for a drink before dinner. Tuesdays they have free wine tasting and a movie which was so awesome. This is the best hotel that I ever stayed in and I travel for work so that says a lot. Highest level of service that I ever received in hotel.

review_title: Grand old hotel, for those who enjoy grand old hotels.
review_text:
Valet and check in went smooth. The hotel inside architecture is remarkable for it's era. Convenient walk to Union Square. 
The bed didn't provide a restful night of sleep. The comforter is heavy, the sheet covering the mattress slipped several times and the mattress was exposed. I could hear neighbors coughing in two different rooms through the walls and my immediate neighbor apparently had a bad dream because I heard his exclamation around 330am. I didnt hear any traffic noise because the room faced internal courtyard. Modern tv, few outlets by desk for my electronic gear. Service was attentive at front desk.

I was not impressed. Was sold a view and got none.
Asked for upgrade, had nothing?
Would not stay here again,

Enjoyed this hotel and would stay here again. Perfect location, impressive ambience, very clean, great service. Bathroom was very nice with separate shower and tub which is unusual for the area. If you're expecting a large room, you might not find it here (or anywhere in San Fran for that matter). We upgraded from a Queen to a King for a reasonable $20/night and it was perfect.

Subito dietro Market Street e abbastanza vicino a Union Square, per gli appassionati e' sulla strada per l'Apple store.
Moderno, molto curato, pulito con un buon servizio; la location puÃ² disturbare il sonno (in dotazione vengono dati mascherina e tappi per le orecchie), come in tutti gli hotel nel centro di grandi e trafficate cittÃ .
Parcheggio costoso, ma nella media
Ottimo rapporto qualitÃ /prezzo, lo consiglio
Hotel was clean, decor was very nice, room wad very nice but smaller. The only complaint I have is that the bed wasnt very comfortable.

review_title: Great location, a bit expensive for a holiday inn express
review_text: For a hotel in the heart of fisherman's wharf, you cannot really beat the value and the short walking distance to the big sites. I found it to be a bit expensive (compared to other big cities), but I guess that is normal for san fran. Service was fine, breakfast was normal holiday inn express breakfast (who doesn't like the cinnamon buns?), and the room was normal holiday clean.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf

review_text: Two staff members of this hotel that truly worked hard to enhance our experience in San Fransisco include Helga at the front desk and Ceasar Henjivar. Each went out of their way to help us find tickets to attractions that we wanted to see and Ceasar even came after his shift, to find us at a nearby lounge, to give us info on the vineyards we were planning to see. While our room was small, the warmth of these two individuals made our stay at the Mark Hopkins a wonderful experience.

review_title: Large rooms. Large bathrooms. Excellent gym and heated pool Excellent central location.
review_text: We had to wait 3 hours for our room. But the room is large and the bathroom also. Location is excellent. The gym and heated pool are wonderful.

review_title: Petit coin tranquille en plein centre ville
review_text:
Havre de paix dÃ¨s qu'on franchit la porte, piscine chauffÃ© au milieu de la cour intÃ©rieur,on l'on peut prendre le petit dÃ©jeuner le matin.
Le bÃ©mol pour nous a Ã©tÃ© le quartier et les rues a traversÃ© pour se rendre dans les avenues commerÃ§antes et touristiques...
L'hÃ´tel reflÃ¨te bien l'Ã©tat d'esprit de la ville de San Francisco, nous n'y regrettons pas notre passage!
hotel_name: Phoenix Hotel, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text:
Positives : great location to all the sites in the city. Excellent lobby and breakfast area.
Negatives : being in the city means crazy prices, nothing is cheap or even reasonably priced including here. Very small rooms, but clean. Old tube TVs with only fair reception. Expect more for the $. Also $44 just for 1 nights parking, alternative is to park 3 blocks away and pay $20. I went with the $44 for the convienence. I guess that's just the way everything is in the big city.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf

review_title: A fabulous hotel very conveniently located
review_text:
Very clean, good sized rooms with all necessary facilities. Service is excellent. 
Location is perfect for shopping, sightseeing or restaurants. 
We did not taste the hotel food at Ansu as there are so many options within a short walk.
EstÃ¡ situado en una zona tranquila pero con buena accesibilidad. Es limpio y el servicio muy agradable.
hotel_name: Hotel Tomo, a Joie de Vivre hotel

review_text: Close to the bustling city centre yet remarkably calm, the Palace Hotel truly is a remnant of a golden era. The dining area is a actually one of the main sites San Francisco! The rooms are spacious and have modern amenities. The staff is very helpful and competent. The only critique I have is that the valet parking is overpriced.

Great location but there's lots of street noise even on the top floor. Rooms are small but well-appointed. The bathroom had a huge window covered by white shutters on the inside and there was a thick layer of black dust all over them Yuck. Also lots of dust on the little bathroom lampshades.

review_title: Very expensive but beautiful hotel in a great location
review_text: Lovely decor with high ceilings & stained glass. The bar boasts a maxfield parish mural, & the ambience is of old world elegance. There is free coffee in the lobby early in the morning but not in-room. Gym was well equipped, pool blessedly uncrowded. However the bathroom was dusty, & the bellhop unhelpful. The price is way too high, but that's true of all San Francisco hotels.

review_title: This was the worst hotel experience of my life, and as a former SF resident, I can honestly say, any other hotel is better.
review_text:
1) arrived and the room we reserved was "dirty" so were downgraded for the night to a FILTHY room in the older building.
2) we booked this location, though more expensive then the Hilton across the street, for the refrigerator (needed for medication), which wasnt in the room. A very rude gentleman reluctantly brought one to our room after a lengthy phone conversation. 
3) D "just the initial" refused to call a cab for us, was very rude, and told us to go "find the bellman," who was no where to be found. 
4) When we complained to the manager, Robert, about how unimpressed we were with our experience, he stated, "well, I'm not impressed either," gesturing to my sister. 
In short, rude staff, FILTHY accomidations, no customer service standards, and false advertising on amenities. Hundreds of hotels in the city, pick any other.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf

review_text: What a fabulous hotel for a fabulous price! We were so pleased with our stay and will definitely stay again! It is in close proximity to Union Square, BART, and everything else that a first time tourist to SFO would likely look for. We have been to SFO several times before and our reason for this trip was for a conference. But we still had time to enjoy the city and walk around and see the sights, and our location at Hotel Nikko was so convenient. We will definitely come back - the value could not be beat and the accommodations were superb.
Great location, clean rooms, good buffet breakfast, can't go wrong staying here.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf

review_text: As a college student I could only afford the happy hours at the Top of the Mark and dreamed of the day I could stay there! Now, it was everything I dreamed it to be. Courteous, staid service, a clean room and comfortable bed and the cable cars and St. Pails from put window! Delicious brunch and impeccable service! I now have family ther and it will be my go to spot upon return visits. If you like a modern hotel this is not for you as it has a more refined elegance and history!

We had a great stay and the people working in the hotel are very friendly
Situation is perfect to discover the wharf and Frisco
We come surely back
Thanks
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites San Francisco Fisherman's Wharf

review_text: The nikko is well situated near to union square, rooms were ok but they were small, and nothing special. The worst thing was the fact you had to pay extra for everything- water in the room, use of the pool, wifi, and any decent tv channels! Parking was also extortionate at Â£30 for 24hours, though probably on a par with other SF hotels! Given the number of hotels in SF, I think we could have found better for the price!

review_title: This hotel is off the hook!
review_text: This hotel is top notch! From the front desk staff all the way to the Imperial Club folks! I have never encountered a friendlier and knowledgeable group of people than the staff at this hotel. And this is coming from someone that had experience staying at 5 star hotels throught San Francisco (namely The Fairmont, Hilton, etc.). The reservations dept is very prompt and responsive. You only have to wait for 1 ring and you immediately get a human being on the other end. That's right! A human being! Not some automated crap. And did i say you only have to wait for one ring nor would you feel that you have to call back again cause the phones (at the other hotels) would ring endlessly? Not at this hotel, that's for sure. Front desk is the best too! If an upgrade is available, these folks will not beat around the bush; you will get the upgrade outright and they won't make you feel like you now owe them something for doing so. Awesome, awesome, awesome!!! The Imperial Club Lounge staff are also top notch. Very professional. Really made us feel special. You don't even have to ask these folks for a cup of coffee. They will come to you and offer you one when you need it as if they can freakin read your mind! Will definitely recommend this hotel to ever single soul i know. Nikko, we will be back!

Der Besitzer ist recht stolz, dass er ein Hotel hat das im Art Deco Stiel ist und das schon recht alt ist. In das Hotel wurde sicher schon einiges investiert, in den letzten 10 Jahren allerding wohl eher weniger. Ob es sauber war kann ich nicht sagen, da in dem Zimmern nur recht schwache Lichter verbaut waren. Den Teppichboden wuerde ich allerding trotzdem mal austauschen. Da die Dusche keine Mischbatterie hat und die Temperatur das Warmwassers schwankt ist die richtige Einstellung der Dusche eine ziemliche Herausforderung. Ansonsten gibts entweder Hitze oder Kaelteschock. Das Hotel hat kein Fruehstueck. WLan hat nicht funktioniert, der Besitzer fuehrte das auf die robuste Bauweise zurueck. Ich wuerde mal sagen: Zu schlechtes oder zu wenig Equipment. 
Da wir die Stuite hatten, war der Zimmerpreis recht hoch und stand in keinem Verhaeltnis zum gebotenen.

We stayed at the nikko for three nights for part of our honeymoon and I can't say enough nice things about this place. Great location close to the Bart and cable cars. This is a very well maintained hotel with wonderful staff. The room was clean, modern and a comfortable bed. Would highly recommend!

My fiancÃ© and I found this online. We are actually here now!! We wanted a nicer hotel, something different than the Hilton or Marriott. Upon arrival, long valet line, rude valet people, rude check in clerk. They basically said our room was tiny and convinced us to upgrade for more money, gym more money, valet more money, business center more money, pool more money! All of this with horrible rude service!! Also it is on the edge of a shady part of town! We will never come back!

For such an old (historic) hotel it's nicely updated. The location is convenient for shopping and for access to Union Square, financial district, BART & transportation to Fisherman's Wharf. Room was basic but clean. Ours faced other rooms but from the 4th floor I couldn't hear much street noise.

Stayed at the nikko for 5 nights in Sept 2011 as the first leg of my honeymoon. Fabulous location for shopping at union square, 150m from the cable car turn around point where u get on it, restaurants in abundance, approx 1hr walk to fishermans warf. 
Hotel didnt have free WiFi, although the star bucks in the lobby does, and its quick even from outside, so no stress on that front. 
Didn't eat in the hotel, purely as there is so much locally. I would recommend the dim sum at the Chinese just over the road from the sbucks down the hill to gte right also the Indian buffet which looks horrific from outside about 100m up the road left from the hotel door was very good.....I live in bradford so believe me when I say its good! Also Lois diner is brilliant round the corner next to wallgreens.
The room was a good size with modern fit and finish, also the gym is excellent and well worth the 10 bucks per room per start usage, for the sauna and steam room alone.
Special thanks to Rick on the concierge desk, very useful guy who never got stumped by a question and was always keen to help.
Highly recommended if you are heading to san fran, I went to the raddison @ fwarf to meet a mate and frankly it was crap compared to the nikko and cost nearly 3 times as much. Also the warf is very tacky and full of tourists.....which generally I can not abide!
As an aside, I would recommend the alcatraz tour it was great (book online in advance though nearly half price!) Also get the cable car back from the warf not to it, the views are better in that direction and the Q was much shorter! Finally on the subject of parking, yes its a lot but not much more than the other secure options, and u can call from your room for your motor, so for me the extra few quid was worth the convenience, choice is yours!
In summary, not a bad word to say about the hotel, and would recommend highly for a city hotel in san fran at the price.

Our flight got cancelled at midnight on labor day weekend and Hotel Nikko was the only one that had rooms at 2am Sunday. The lady at the front desk was very efficient at checking us in. We got one of those rooms on the imperial club floor (22nd floor) - you need to insert your card key on the elevator to get to your floor. The room was huge with great views of the city and our only complaint was that there were too many doors at the washroom, at least 3 I think. The tv on the bathroom mirror was really cool. Be careful about moving stuff on the fridge, or you'll be automatically charged, call front desk if you need extra fridge space. The free breakfast was great with lots of choices - it's a $22 value and they will charge you $5 tip on your room bill. We paid a total of $300 for one night stay.

review_title: Lets you concentrate on your holiday
review_text:
Just spent three nights here and our stay was totally uneventful from an accomodation perspective. Perfect!
It's not often that an hotel gets it all right, but the Nikko just blended into the background perfectly, letting us get on with our holiday activities without a worry in the world.
The hotel is stylishly decorated and well serviced. The rooms are elegant and well equipped, and the service is invisible yet highly effective. Position is awesome - at the heart of it all in SF.
Would definitely come here again!

Sehr gute Lage, um die Ecke ist die Wendeplatte des Cable Car. Shopping Center und viele SehenswÃ¼rdigkeiten zu Fuss erreichbar. Die Zimmer sind klein, aber alles war sauber. Das Personal war sehr nett und hilfsbereit. Ã–ffentliche Verkehrsmittel sind ebenfalls in wenigen Minuten erreichbar.

From the moment we stepped out our car we were given the VIP treatment. All staff went out of their way to make sure everything about our stay at the NIKKO SF was top notch. Rooms were very clean and the beds were quite comfortable. The welcome cheese and cracker plate was a great touch. We also really enjoyed the Sunday brunch in the ANZO restaurant. We will be coming back!

This hotel offers excellent service, with large clean and comfortable rooms. The staff is courteous and helpful. The location is perfect as it is close to all forms of transportation including the Bart, Cable Cars, Streetcars & Buses. It's also very close to excellent stores like Macy's, Nordstroms & Barneys to name a few.

My wife and I stayed there for 1 night in august 2011. I am a star wood gold member and used cash+ points option to stay at the palace hotel. The hotel is very conveniently located right next to the Montgomery street Bart stop. The front desk was very nice and check in was pleseant. The room that we stayed in on the 8th floor was nice with beautiful high ceilings and has a very grand feel. This hotel reminds me if the waldorf in NYC. It has an old and royal feel to it. Like all fan Francisco hotels, the palace rooms are small but they are very nice. W had a very nice time. The staff is very friendly and you cannot ask for abetted location or a more beautiful lobby.

review_title: Sf is expensive, but this place is worth it
review_text: Let me start by saying I found a pretty good deal, I believe it was 110 a night so not like I spent a fortune here. Parking is another 50 bucks a day which is ridiculous, but unfortunately thats the way it is in sf. The good thing is there is so much within walking distance. Chinatown is just a couple blocks away. Tons of nearby restaurants and shopping areas. There is a cable car line RIGHT in front of the hotel which was great. Also the rooms here are very nice, clean as can be. The front desk people were polite and helpful enough. I would definately go back here if I could get the same kind of deal

review_title: Fantastic hotel: reasonably priced & great location!
review_text: This is a 5 star hotel, located in the center of the SF hustle and bustle. For the price per night, this represents the best value in SF! Everything was positive, and the only critism I have is the lack of free wireless internet.

This place is so overrated. Yes it's a great location. Maybe it's because I live in Las Vegas & I know that I can get a MUCH NICER room for half the price. The bed is very uncomfortable. The pillows are the smallest I've seen in a hotel. Cigarette burns on the toilet seat. Stains on the curtains. Dingy bathtub. The lobby of this place is 4-star. Not the rooms. The Palace should not market itself as a 4-star.
Good hotel, good location, excellent food - however if driving be aware that parking at the hotel can be over $50 per 24 hours - Ouch!

I stayed here for 2 nights in a double with my 16yo son.
The hotel is a smaller, boutique hotel - with a gorgeous lobby - quirky and welcoming.
As I've come to expect from a Kimpton, the service is always wonderful - welcoming and professional.
Location was convenient to union square and transport.
The room and bathroom were a little small, but a super rate and great service means I rate this hotel as exceptional value for money.

review_title: Elegant, stylish and on the right side of quirky
review_text:
Superb, richly appointed and generally lovely hotel within easy walking distance of Powell or Union Square. Pet-friendly and so are the owners- nothing like nuzzling up to a huge St Bernard as a welcome to SF.
Staff go out of their way to make you feel welcome with free wine and random lectures/activities in the early evenings. Superb restaurant/bar on the ground floor that's rapidly becoming a neighbourhood destination.
Rooms might seem a little small to those used to corporate monsters. But they're well appointed and have a good mix of modern convenience and period features. (Being a Brit, though,wouldn't mind a kettle.)
The 3* for location is because while the hotel itself is in a safe neighbourhood, one block over it gets quite iffy (it's quite obvious which way you shouldn't go). Ask door staff for directions or a cab anywhere.

We booked at the last minute so I was worried what we'd find and was pleased with what we found.
Hotel and rooms were quaint and well kept. No view and teeny bathroom but the location, cleanliness, and service staff make this a recommended stay.
Only significant gaps are no coffee maker in the room (although free in the lobby) and a horrible hair dryer (bring your own).

review_title: Outstanding!! Location and value was great.
review_text:
We stayed for one night, Friday night in July. We stayed in the deluxe king. It was room 358. It was spacious with an oversized room and very tall ceilings. This room faces market street. We had gone to the giants game, an easy walk for a capable person - returned to the hotel. We ordered a glass of wine in the pied piper which is in the first floor of the hotel. We took the glasses up to our rooms, cracked the window and put our feet up on the oversized window sill while we sipped our wine and listened to the sounds of the city. It was perfect. We were torn as we have two toddlers - should we sleep with the window cracked or closed ? We gave up sleeping in in favor of hearing all the wonderful sounds of the city. 
The hotel is definitely old but in such a cool way. You feel like it is something special. The staff does a wonderful job taking care of you during your stay. Each room has strong solid wood doors with a solid handle. We never once heard another guest in any direction on our floor. The room was so spacious we could have stayed there a month or more without feeling crowded. For anyone traveling with children the deluxe king room is plenty big enough for a roll away and a pack n play or two if you needed it. The bathroom and closet is small but I don't think it negatively impacts the room. And the showerhead more than makes up for anything you could possibly think was wrong. It is amazing. I might even call to find out what brand it is I liked it so much. 
There are three bakeries that serve breakfast within a block on market. The buffet in the hotel was $30 pp so we passed and went to Anderson Bakery for $13 for two people. Just a note - don't try to find breakfast in union square unless you want to eat at Starbucks because there aren't a lot of options. 
We stayed for one night to go to a giants a game. We wished we could have stayed many more. We will 100% for sure stay here the next time we want to stay in this part of SF. We thoroughly enjoyed the palace hotel.

review_title: Great location,small and clean rooms, charge you for everything
review_text: We stayed at Nikko over memorial week end.the location is great,close to shopping, restaurants. Rooms are v small, we had to pay extra 20 dollars plus taxes per night to be upgraded to a king bed but rooms are still small.u have to pay addition $ 10 to use pool which is ridiculous and valet is $45 plus taxes. Very expensive for an already expensive hotel. Very clean rooms and they gladly accommodate us with a complementary fridge for our baby's milk.

This hotel has the most character of any I have stayed in. We chatted to some charming fellow guests over wine in the lovely lounge. The fireplace in our room made it feel very romantic and the lift has to be experienced (original wrought iron). Convenient location too.
hotel_name: Petite Auberge a Joie de Vivre Hotel

review_title: Not a 'theme hotel' just a fantastic hotel with charecter with nice extras
review_text:
Stayed for 3 fantastic nights at tge PA.
Arrived early and was offered the room straight away.
Some would describe this as a french 'themed' hotel, but the quality, attention to detail, and the consistency make this far from a theme hotel. This hotel has charecter, from the rooms to public areas.
The rooms are fairly small, but not so small to be a problem...its a city hotel in the USA...therefore I would count the space generous compared to New York.
My room was next to the lift, which you could here a slight rumble, but nothing that was going to keep me awake.
The room and the public areas were clean. The furnishings were nice with a very comfortable bed...which is in the main what you have a hotel for...a good nights sleep.
Breakfast was nice, something a bit different to the normal plastic continental served at most chain hotels. Wine in the parlour was a nice touch served early evening for all guests.
Staff were friendly, and especially housekeeping who did a fantastic job, and were always especially friendly when we saw them around the hotel. The property isnt over run with staff, the main reception being at their sister property next door...don't be expecting bells and whistles reception with conceirges, bell hops etc...it feels more like your own country house in the peace and quiet. Hot drinks, soft drinks, water was all availible free of charge to help yourself to as you wish from the kitchen area...this to me is what a hotel is about...the nice little extras.
The hotel is in a good area, easy walking distance to downtown and public transport.
I would definately stay here again, whether business or pleasure and is quite possibly one of my favourites of all time.
A great hotel which I will highly recommend.
hotel_name: Petite Auberge a Joie de Vivre Hotel

review_title: Value for money but nothing special
review_text: Hotel decor tired and dated, staff very helpful tho and made all the difference especially the doorman and Angelique in Jaspers, location a little far out from the wharf for our liking but an enjoyable stay in an amazing city.

review_title: Traditional excellence in a city not known for tradition.
review_text: Had a recent business meeting at this Hotel. From the point of arrival I was greeted with a smile and an eager face. Everyone offered to help at any chance. I hope it is contagious. The room was not small and had to look hard to find any faught, maybe the air vents could use a little more attention. Food was great at our event and would have been happy to have had all there. The Bar was friendly and believe it or not, not too noisey. I have not stayed in a hotel this nice since London. If you can afford this one, you will not be disappointed. It is very convenient to the sites and for transportation. I took the BART to the airpoint since it was 4 steps out the corner door.

review_title: We have mice, but otherwise we're great.
review_text: Stayed there 4 days in October 2011. Had a bayfront room, small but nice. Typically what you'd expect in this area. Area was great, close to F line cable cars which will get you everywhere else. View from room of Bay Bridge was fantastic. Staff was friendly. Only one issue- I awoke to a mouse on my night stand eating a granola bar I'd left there. Also realized that unusual noise I heard during night was a mouse dragging a sticky trap to free himself. Ruined a good stay.

review_title: Kimpton standards as good as ever.
review_text: Good service, great location and clean, comfortable beds. Housekeeping staff very cheerful and friendly, same goes for concierge staff. Slept well, and was well rested to head out into the city every day. Be careful about wandering too far west into the Tenderloin if you're not used to stepping over people and the strong scent of urine, but union square to the east provides easy tourist access. The Serrano is a regular rest stop for us in San Francisco. Recommended without reservations!

review_title: Older hotel, but still in good shape.
review_text: Nice hotel; great downtown location. Parking expensive. Very nice staff.

My husband an I arrived at the hotel on Sunday, September fourth about 1 hour before check in. We parked in one of the 2 spaces they have out front. I went in to let them know we were here understanding that a room would probably not be ready. When I entered the small lobby and walked up to the desk the young lady behind the desk did not even say hi nothing she just looked up at me. I informed her of our stay and she told me there were no rooms ready. I said okay and asked about having our car parked and if we needed to access the car during our stay could we. She could not tell me where they parked the car and said they could only get it for us and it would take 15 to 20 minutes to get the car. We took our luggage out of the car and John (the only nice person) took our car to the unknown lot. We thought we would just wait in the lobby till our room was ready. After waiting only a few minutes Matt the manager called us to the desk to let us know a room was ready. We went to the room which had a maintenance man fixing a light fixture in the bathroom and a drilling noise that made the walls shake. I went back to the lobby to ask about a room without drilling and possibly not a maintenance man. The same young lady, Julia, was at the desk and told me there were no rooms without the drilling available for our stay. I asked to speak to Matt the manager. She told me to go back to the room and he would call. A few minutes later Matt called and said there were no rooms that did not have the drilling and not to worry as it only goes from 10 am to 5 pm. I told him we would leave then and he said fine to go ahead and leave as he could not help us. There were no apologies and no attempts to solve the problem.No I am sorry let's try and work this out. He just told us to leave. We gathered all our stuff, went downstairs and I told them how unhappy I was and that the room was not ready that there was someone in the room fixing a light. He could not have cared less and we left.
We went a few blocks down the street to the Inter Continental Hotel and we were in a bigger, beautiful and cheaper room in 15 minutes.
This was a birthday getaway for my husband and I which I mentioned at the Griffon and got no response. The Inter Continental sent up a lovely pastry selection with Happy Birthday wishes! What a difference in customer service and quality.

review_title: Small, but great location and extras
review_text:
So the Petite title of the hotel is definitely accurate, we booked the Cozy Queen room and it certainly is cozy! The room is tiny, and the hotel is upfront about this in the room descriptions. We stayed for two nights and found the location to be excellent, easy transportation access to get virtually anywhere in the city, and close to Union Square shops and restaurants. The hotel offers free wi-fi, breakfast and drinks/nibbles in the evening. A definate bonus for those wanting to save a few dollars. As for our room, we were unfortunately situated directly behind the reception/elevator, due to the age of the building you can hear plenty of squeaking floorboards etc. but I believe we had more than the normal amount as any guests leaving/entering would traverse past us or use the elevator as we were situated next to the elevator/reception. Saying this the hotel provided a machine in-room that provided ambient noise (think ceiling fan noise) which we found to be quite good at covering/distracting from other noises in the hotel. Not to post too many cons, but the bed was fairly uncomfortable, we found the mattress to sink in the middle and after staying at 4 hotels on this trip so far we would rate it as the worst bed we'd slept in.
Regardless of the above, we thoroughly enjoyed our stay, the extra amenities are great, the staff friendly and helpful, and the location was excellent.
hotel_name: Petite Auberge a Joie de Vivre Hotel

review_text:
Stayed at the Hotel Griffon for 3 days in a standard queen room last week. The hotel and room were very well appointed. It was not the smallest room I've stayed in, but not the largest either. It had an in-room coffee and tea maker. Biggest complaint was the lighting. Since the opaque window looked at four walls, there was very little natural light in the room. Otherwise, there were three small lamps. With every light on in the room and bathroom, it was still pretty dim.
No other complaints, though! Service was great! Location was FABULOUS! Within walking distance to everything. Peet's coffee and tea with fruit in the lobby every morning. Perry's Restaurant had a great patio area with a view of the Bay Bridge--happy hour too!
Overall a great stay. Would definitely stay here again!

The title is assigned by Kimpton, chain owner of this property and, sure enough, the property lives-up to its claim. The lobby is nicely appointed and service from check-in throughout is personable and excellent. Parking is a big pain but, hey, it is SF so expect it too be difficult and expensive wherever you go. The room standard room is long and lean but well-appointed. The restroom is right next to the bedroom which is convenient but offers little to the imagination if the fan is not turned-on. Super quiet room, which is impressive as is the view looking-up at Non Hill where we usually stay. The wine hour is hosted by the hotel in its lobby; cool to hob-nob but prepare to stand as seating is spare. The wine poured is typically bleh but Jasper's next door has a good bar selection though that costs. Overall this is a nice place to stay if you want to see how the other half lives as this is the Tenderloin District which, as those in-the-know know is not for the easily shocked or offended. 
Ghod theatre district and union square accesibilty but expect to pass a few interesting scenes along the way. Hey, you really want to go home without a uniquely SF story? If so stay somewhere else. But if you want a crazy SF story this is your pick.

review_title: A well located hotel with character
review_text: We found this great little hotel perfect for our needs: well located in walking distance to Union Square, complimentary wifi and a great breakfast. The staff was super friendly and the hotel has lots of character. Our room for instance had a little fire place.
hotel_name: Petite Auberge a Joie de Vivre Hotel

review_title: Beautiful petit hotel with very friendly staff
review_text:
Charming, kind of an Inn hotel, like home away from home. We got a nice room at the end of the corridor on the ground floor, which was very quiet and lovely, with fireplace.
Staff was so kind and helped us with everything we needed. Every day they offered a different kind of home made cake or cookies, at 18:00 - hot and cold drinks, wine.. 
If we will ever come back to SF, this is the place for us. Highly recommended!
hotel_name: Petite Auberge a Joie de Vivre Hotel

review_text: I'm a frequent guest of Kimpton Hotels, having stayed in about 15 different properties in the last 12 months. This one definitely rates as the worst of the Kimptons. The doorman didn't even make eye contact when I entered, my room is the teeniest I've seen, the elevator floor was splashed with water, the elite amenity was less than any of the other Kimptons have provided, and if this room was renovated I hope they paid the contractor minimum wage. I won't stay here again and am disappointed that Kimpton has this property in its portfolio as it does not meet their typically high standards.

Stayed in May of 2010, the hotel was under going some restoration and at first I was worried due to it looking shabby, however I couldent be more wrong, it was excellent all the way. 
Great staff helped me with some tour bookings, very friendly and good value for money.
Rooms were tidy and clean, the hotel is a brisk walk from nice locations and close to the BART. I'd stay again for sure!

review_title: Great hotel, great location, amazing service and a really great price!
review_text: Stayed at the Serrano for 2 nights during October in a trip to the us from Australia. After being in LA for a week before SFO it was amazing tO get to the Serrano and relax on the amazing beds, in the lobby on the oversized chairs. A great hotel with great service in a good location. Would return in a heart beat

review_title: My first choice when I am in Sf.
review_text: The customer service is excellent..the room is comfortable and big enough, the beddings were clean, thats the one I check first and the bathroom...the only downside is you have to pay your wireless internet with the price you pay per night...the location is the best because I can just walk around where I wanna go...
We have stayed in 3 different hotels in Union Square in the last 6 months and the Marriott is top of the list. I would absolutely recommend this hotel. You won't be disappointed.

review_title: A Great Choice for A Stay in San Fran
review_text: I stayed here for multiple nights recently with my family. It has a great location at Union Square. A starbucks is right across the street. There is obviously a ton of restaurants, bars and shopping nearby. It is a very close walk to Chinatown and not too bad to get to North Beach. The hotel is pretty modern and clean. We had a very large room with two beds. The beds were comfortable. The bathroom was well appointed. We had a nice view out of one of the windows. Although we were high up, we actually heard a good amount of noise from the street below at night. The concierge lounge is large with pretty good selections. The staff is friendly.

We were there for 5 nights last year. The room is very clean and the bed is very comfortable. The room service is excellen. No matter how dirty or messy I left the room in the morning, we was always welcomed by a clean and nice room at night. The location is very convenient too, it close to few big shopping mall. You can easily access alot of places by the cable car which just at the junction.

Nice hotel, great location and really friendly, helpful staff. Bathroom is a little small two women on a girl's weekend struggled sharing the vanity. It was a very minor convenience. I would definitely stay at this property again.

The room was nice but make sure you get a high floor. You will hear trash trucks early in the morning. The bellman just brought my bags in and set them down. He didn't help put them on racks or show me the room amenities. I found the nice coffee service in a box inside of a bathroom cabinet. The coffee pot is inside a bathroom cabinet too. Beware, valet parking is very expensive at least $50 night. So a cab might be cheaper. Overall nice hotel but just needs a little better service
hotel_name: JW Marriott San Francisco Union Square

review_title: Muy centrico, muy limpio, no muy caro para la zona. Lo recomiendo para ver San Francisco
review_text: El hotel esta muy bien. Sin lujos, pero sin defectos. El trato muy bueno, muy limpio todo, y la habitacion con lo necesario. Ideal para pasar unos dias y conocer la ciudad, ya que esta entre chinatown y union square. Buena zona. Muy centrico. Nosotros pasabamos por el hotel varias veces al dia a dejar las compras, descansar un ratito, etc,...

Loved this immaculately clean hotel, with incredible staff who treat you like royalty! Perect location with a great cable car stop right outside, Starbucks on the corner, great restaurants all around, wonderful shopping and cheap taxi ride to the wharf and Ghiradelli. Beds were wonderful and we wish we had a shower like theirs at our house. Try "Sears Fine Food" next door for a terrific breakfast.
Biggest pain in the butt to get to. Noisy and unorganized. Never will stay again. Tremendously overpriced. Rude staff.

review_title: Such fun! Great use of Starwood points.
review_text: We asked for a room with a great view if it was available and we got it. We also ask to check out later and got a 4 pm check out. Yippee! Pool, great with kids. Fun room!

review_title: Good location, but that's about it
review_text:
I really wasn't going to write a review about this hotel because we are loyal / platinum Marriott members. However, I think if you are looking for that "JW Marriott" experience, you won't find it here. The biggest problem here is street noise. We were on the 18th floor & could hear loud street noise morning, day & night. Staff was not very friendly (bordering rude), bellmen always seemed so confused & it was very hard catching cabs from this hotel. 2 good things: Darlene, the concierge, & location (walking distance to everything). If you are interested in a private wine tour in Napa, talk to Darlene. 
Good restaurants to try: lunch @ Four Seasons, Yank Sing for Dim Sum, Ozuma for sushi & Boulevard for dinner. Make reservations or you will be waiting...even during lunch.
We will not be staying here again. There is another / newer Marriott up the street on Powell that is a newer property. We'll that a shot next time.
hotel_name: JW Marriott San Francisco Union Square

review_title: A very comfortable, conveniently located hotel with very spacious rooms - why stay anywhere else?
review_text: I had the opportunity to stay at the JW Marriott San Francisco on August 25th. The hotel was beautiful, comfortable, and very conveniently located. I purchased a PURE room for the first time to see what it was all about. I typically suffer from allergies and hotel stays are typically challenging for me. This room made all the difference in the world and I was quite skeptical at first. They are basically hypo-allergenic rooms that have a PURE air filtering system that apparently can work wonders. I slept through the entire night and woke up feeling clear, rested, and very refreshed. I would recommend this hotel to anyone. It has a very understated luxury about it but was welcoming at the same time - nothing stuffy, just a very high level of service and quality.
hotel_name: JW Marriott San Francisco Union Square

review_text: Great location, very friendly staff and well appointed room... Would stay here again!
hotel_name: JW Marriott San Francisco Union Square

review_title: Gone Downhill - the 'WOW' has long gone.
review_text:
Having stayed here on several occasions since the hotel opened, I was deeply disappointed by this stay. On arrival no assistance was offered with luggage so we found our own way to the temporary check in desk. We discovered there were refurbishments of the ground floor and so the check in area was very disorganised. We stayed in a 'Fantastic Suite' which was very nice with great views, the only downside was poor water pressure so the shower is really only a trickle. Ordered room service as the restaurant was closed due to the refurb - wish we hadn't bothered as it arrived cold and was well below standard. On returning to the hotel late on Saturday night, we were greeted by a young guy who 'fell' out the hotel and vomitted on the sidewalk - a nice welcome back! The lobby area seemed to be filled with (very) young drunk people. Possibly the same that could be heard partying in the hotel in the early hours. The final annoyance was an argument/fight/screaming coming from another guest room in the middle of the night - but at least security did sort that. In general poor service, all style and no substance - just call the Whatever/Whenever service for a demonstration of that. The ineffective W management need to decide if it a nightclub with rooms attached or whether it is a hotel as advertised. After the weekend the hotel was much better but really, the staff need to stop being so 'cool' and drop the W-attitude. The staff need to realise they are actually 
hotel workers and that guests deserve the service we are paying top-dollar for (and which most of the great people in the industry are happy to provide). Avoid - there are now much better options for the price.

This is a fabulous hotel in an awesome Union Square location. Lots of shopping and restaurants nearby! Spent 3 nights here with some girlfriends and would definitely return. The staff was welcoming and accommodating. We were able to check in early since we came in on a red eye flight. They were also able to answer questions about different modes of transportation and directions to different locations. The lobby is nice and modern. The 
rooms are a good size and the beds are comfy! The cable car stop was near the entrance of the hotel too.

review_title: Awesome location, generously sized room, large windows, lots of light.
review_text: We love the central location, the friendly staff, the colorful appointments (cheerful), the light-filled room.

The W is always a great place to stay, no matter where. This hotel in SF was not the greatest location, not bad, but not as great as others; however, I do keep in mind that real estate is at a high premium in SF (but the NY locations are great). The rooms are great - appointed better than the Scottsdale, AZ location. The lobby is a welcoming area to relax with a friend over drinks. I love staying at The W's because they are always so stylish & elegant, yet very each one is unique with it's own "flavor".

Pretty standard Marriott rooms. Very clean and updated. In a good location. The service was outstanding...very welcoming and accommodating. Had great nights sleep.
Location was perfect for me. Close to shopping, transportation and dining options.

We stayed here for two nights during their free parking specials and what a sweet deal it was.
The hotel staff was excellent except for one instance where one of the staff on duty refused to give my pregnant wife the complimentary umbrella for temporary use because she wanted to save it for other guest...yes weird but true.
Barring this the stay was excellent. They upgraded us to a suite upon arrival and the room was exceptional. Their gym is pretty good and other than the one instance , their staff is very curteous. 
This hotel is within walking distance of the piers and the exceptional slanting door restaurant. Parking without the special is close to 50 bucks a day. 
I would stay here again

review_title: Very good hotel if you're wkng in Financial District and looking for comfortable bed.
review_text: Location is downtown, close to Financial District and as a bonus, about 200 yds from Punchline Comedy (after a long wk day the convenient laughter spot is welcomed). Easy walk to Little Italy and Chinatown. Ck in was smooth. Room was comfortable overall. The bed was very enjoyable. Heavy drapes kept out day ligh and cold from the large windows. Experienced the city mechanical sounds (sirens, car horns, trucks) if you're a light sleeper might need ear plugs. No pool but 24hr wk out center. Good amount of desk space and ample outlets. Really enjoyed the very quiet heater/air conditioning in room system. I'd stay here again.

review_title: Nice hotel, good location, great value.
review_text:
Came here during a weekend gateway with the wife. We had come here before when it was a Hyatt Place some 5 years prior. We had incredibly fond memories of our last stay, especially of the fantastic, awesome, mind blowing beds. At that time, the hotel was very obviously built in the late 80s, but the rooms were appointed well enough that the age didn't seem apparent. The bathrooms were dark marble, slightly older again, but well maintained. Some of the furniture was older, somewhat dinged for a 4+ star hotel. Still, none of it mattered once we got to bed. The bedding, the mattress, the bedroom was all amazing. It truly set the bar for all of our subsequent hotel stays to come.
Seeing the property change hands, we were encouraged to visit based on the incredibly good deal for the room type we booked (king suite).
Coming back, it was the same hotel, but different enough that it didn't feel the same. Lobby and elevators were pretty much the same, which was fine. The bar and dining area got fixed up, which was nice since it was getting a little long in the tooth.
Alas, after checking in we quickly rushed to the room. We were surprised to see a complete remodel (save for the bathroom), which was nice. The bed was comfortable, the layout logical, and the room was well positioned against the bay (from which you can see the Bay Bridge very well). The beds are NOT the same as the Hyatt Place beds. Not to be unexpected, especially since its now a 3+ star hotel. Still nice, but not the same. The showers in this hotel are awesome! We loved them and the bed. Overall very nice, very comfortable.
Being that its San Francisco, you will pay through the nose for Valet. This is not different anywhere else, especially anything near the business district.
Would come back again ...

review_title: Luxurious and well located. Lacking buzz but fine for business when you want quiet and to be left alone.
review_text: This hotel is comfortable, and perfectly suited for business. Quality food and room service, also convenient to meetings in downtown San Francisco. Only criticism is that my room service tray sat in the hall the entire afternoon and early evening, that seemed unnecessary and I should not have to call them to collect it. Also, very quiet, at least when I stayed, but this can be good if you want rest when you return to your hotel. I will definitely stay here again especially when visiting on business and if the cost is competitive relative to the other Starwood properties in the city.

I snagged this steal on Priceline and couldn't have been happier! Amazing room at a GREAT rate! The Financial District is probably not the best place to stay for touring the city but it's an easy walk to the Ferry Building and the MUNI.

review_title: Won't compare to other W hotels you may have stayed at
review_text: The hotel was missing that coolness factor that you find at many other W hotels. They were undergoing renovations to lobby during stay and perhaps that had something to do with it. Rooms are small with double beds. When I asked if we could get a room with 2 queen beds they said they didn't have any. It is hard to move around in the "spectacular" room and the decor hasn't been updated in a while. It would have been impressive in 1995 but not 2011. We orders room service that took an hour and a half. Also ran out of toilet paper as none extra in our room. The spot to catch a taxi wasn't the best and many times we were on our own to catch a cab.

review_title: Small and modern hotel with a great staff
review_text: My wife and I stayed at the W for one night in august 2011. I am a star wood gold member and stayed using cash and points option. The lobby is under construction and checkin is done in the makeshift lobby down the block next to the valet. The staff is cry nice and check in was fine. The were no phrases available which is always somewhat disappointing. Like most San Fran hotels, the rooms are small. The room we stayed in has a modern feel to it, and almost feels like I'm staying in someone's bedroom rather than a hotel. Not necessarily a bad thing, but deffenitly doesnt exude luxury. The hotel has free bikes that guests can borrow. The staff here is really nice and that is the reason why I would go again. Not for the luxury.

Just ran the Nike Women's 1/2 marathon and spent the night there pre-race with my family of 4. They were very accommodating, providing a kid size bed as they only had a king room available. The hotel is small but cozy.

review_title: Expensive for a couple of nights stay
review_text: Very last minute booking with hot wire.big race on so all cheaper rooms were booked.hotel is lovely,rooms are plush, towels and bed great.great location walking distance to fishermans wharf, Chinatown and union square.cant compain about any of the above but it was a bit expensive for a couple of nights just to sleep. Only downside no free Internet or breakfast but there are Macdonalds and Starbucks nearby.
Great hotel. They gave me a suite with sweeping bay views. Extremely comfortable room. They even provide an umbrella for those foggy/rainy San Francisco days.

Stayed here for an anniversary weekend. Loved the fact that it was in the financial district. Everything was sooo quiet while only being a short cab or walk away from the action. We loved the bed so much I have called the company they get their pillows from. 
I would suggest street parking which was plentiful vs the $50 they want to valet. 
Loved the room and the location. Would be happy to stay there again!

Everything from the room to the bartenders and even the Friendly breakfast wait staff made my stay very enjoyable. It was nice to have so much available all from one building. The room was awesome, I loved all the modern touches. Bed was very comfortable, and even the soap and shampoo was of good quality.

I stayed here a few weeks ago and had a really wonderful time. It is close enough to central SF but far enough that you are not stepping on homeless people. We had breakfast one morning and the manager was so nice to come check on us, she was sweet. Front desk was efficient and very calm despite it looking like a busy day. I called down for some qtips and they had them which was so nice, the last hotel I stayed in had none of the items one accidentally forgets. Overall 5 stars, would love to come back soon.

Nice Hotel close to the local MOmA, I recommend the corner rooms on upper floors, spectacular views. The bar downstairs is quite cool and gets very busy by weekend at night, with a nice young crowd. Definitely a good design place

review_title: $56 to park and $13 Internet! What a joke
review_text:
I understand that parking in San Fran is costly but $56 is outrageous especially when there are other lots that charge $30 and they don't have guests staying there. Plus when I need something out of my car it is a pain because I have to call downstairs and have them bring my car. Wait 10 min. Then tip the guy, get my item and then tip him again to take it back to the lot. Plus they charge $13 for Internet? That is a joke. How come other hotels can provide it for free? They had coffee in the lobby but if you wait until after 10 you have to buy some at starbucks. 
Other than that excellent room. Beautiful marble, beautiful view, LARGE room. A lot of electronic stuff that I would just assume replace with a coffee maker.

Great location. Good Service, loved the room decor 
We upgraded to a corner suite after having gotten N Awesome rate on pricline - will certainly b Back

review_title: Disappointing stay, will probably not go back.
review_text: This was our 3rd stay @ Le Meridien and probably the last. It appears to have gone downhill from our prior visits. If you are a single traveler, I would maybe still recommend, but not for a couple due to the limited room amenities. This visit we checked into our room and quickly headed out to an evening Giants game. We got back to our room very late and very tired after walking back from AT&T park. Upon showering we noticed there were NO washcloths. Also, there were only 2 bathtowels and they were exactly like the thin scratchy towels you got in high school gym class. To top it off, after showering we had to toss a coin on who got a robe as there was only one. Had it not been so late or had we not been so tired wanting to just go to sleep, I would have called for extra linens. Then, we found a pair of socks in the room, left behind by a previous visiter. YUK. Now we were thinking maybe the room had only been partially cleaned & they simple hadn't finished and that's why linens weren't re-stocked. Not a pleasant feeling. The next morning we showered again with no washcloths, dried with our still wet towels from the night before and made a point to let the front desk know about this mix up. When we did, I was shocked to hear that it wasn't so much of a mix up. The front desk stated it is now their practice to only supply one robe and 2 towels, but they had run out of washcloths! She did apologize for the leftover socks. She made no attempt to make any ammends. Our prior visits were not like this, previously you rcvd complimentary waterâ€¦ thick towels (and enough that you don't have to reuse a wet one in the morning) there used to be 2 robes...with all the competition in SF and a lot of unsold rooms, I don't think now is the time to cut corners. Or, if you are going to make changes like that, let the guests know at checkin by telling them something like 'in an effort to conserve, we no longer provide water and have limited the amt of towels, but if you'd like water or towels, please just ask & we will provide.' Just a thought.

review_title: Great Place to arrive in San Fran -location great and helpful service!
review_text: Super comfy beds, staff helped with bookings and car rentals and printing. 5 to 10 minute walk to Union Square (main shopping & transport hub) and Market Street. Very pet friendly, didn't have time to eat there so don't know about the food but everything else was great. Recent construction works were nearly complete but we didn't notice a thing. Not supermodern, more of a character hotel. Good price online.

review_title: Great quality but lacking certain needs for the price.
review_text: $29 for breakfast? C'Mon, there's am economic crisis! If I'm spending $300 a night, throw me some breakfast, continental at least...I'll be using my money in Europe where they cater towards the guest...
