Great location. Great views across Missisippi River. Spacious room. Friendly staff. Perhaps only criticism is lack of guest laundry.

Just got back from our vacation in Seattle. We stayed at the Belltown Inn and it was great! It was clean, and the staff was very friendly. The location was excellent and we could walk to everything we wanted to see. We are already talking about our next trip to Seattle, and would DEFINATELY stay here again!!

Stayed at the Springhill pre cruise for a couple of nights,while not the idea location for a couple of seasoned adults we were able to walk to most attractions with a little effort. They do have a courtesy van that will drive you go certin locations but it seemed the drivers were put out when you requested a pick up and were not very friendly at all. The hotel desk were very accomadating and went out of their way to help,all in all the staff were top shelf. They do offer a comp breakfast which was actually edible which is saying alot if you've been through a few of these The room was standard Springhill,large with separate sitting area and a couple of tv's. I would recommend this property without hesitation for the budget minded tracker or for anyone who does not want to pay Ritz prices to stay on the water front. By the way the bowl of suckers at the front desk were a welcome treat. Thank you!
hotel_name: SpringHill Suites Seattle Downtown/South Lake Union

review_text:
read amenities carefully. When it said ceiling fan, that was a big tip off. Front lobby is air conditioned. You think wow this is a nice place. We visited during a heat wave. We were given a fan and told to prop open our door. There is a dog park across from the inn. If the dogs aren't barking, the fire trucks and ambulances zipping by are noisy enough. could have sworn I heard gunshots at 2 am our last night.
If you're going to have an inner city establishment, get air conditioning so your guests have a restful evening.

Location great, walking distance to Pike's Place Market and loads of restaurants. Room was small, but had microwave and fridge. Worst part was the air does NOT get cold enough. Had to open the windows and then it was load with nighttime city noises and cars. Beds way too hard also. Hardly slept.

review_title: Great value, great service, great amenities....
review_text: We stayed at this hotel over a busy weekend and we were pleasantly surprised and pleased with our experience. At first we were disappointed thinking that our hotel was too far away from the sights we wanted to see and visit. But then we found out that the hotel offers a free shuttle to the locations we needed. Shuttle reservations are made through the front desk staff. Our next discovery was the guest laundry which was greatly appreciated. It is very inexpensive just $1.00 per load for the washer or dryer and that includes the detergent. The room was large and nicely appointed and the wifi worked very well. The kitchen area was small but adequate. We avoided the breakfast buffet after the first morning. The food was plentiful and varied; but it was just too crowded and hectic for our liking. If you are driving to the hotel it is a little tricky to find the entrance because of the one way streets. There is an overnight parking fee of $20.00 plus tax added to your bill at checkout to be aware of if you are working to a budget.
hotel_name: SpringHill Suites Seattle Downtown/South Lake Union

review_text: We picked this hotel because of its location to the airport and the indoor pool..no one told us at check in that there was a private party at the pool..when we saw signs stating it was closed, we tried to call the front desk for almost 20 min before we got someone to answer and they weren't real apologetic about the fact we couldn't use the pool..we also got charged twice for our room service but they did get that resolved..we also had neighbors who were loud all night but we never could get anyone to answer at the front desk..

review_title: Free use of 24 Hour Fitness, close to Capitol Hill and downtown
review_text: I have stayed here many times. Near downtown. Free use of 24 Hour Fitness across the street. Walk to restaurants of Capitol Hill and downtown. Rooms are spotless--and vacumed. Ask for a room facing away from I 5 or Yale Avenue (windows a little thin). Nice free breakfast--and no green bananas. Friendly front desk staff. Laundry machine on 2nd floor a plus.
hotel_name: SpringHill Suites Seattle Downtown/South Lake Union

review_title: Best value for location in Seattle!
review_text: Walking distance to Needle, Pike's Market, downtown bars and clubs, and waterfront path. Great b'fast, rooms, staff and value. All rooms have separate kitchenette and living room area. At front rooms above second floor have spectacular view of the sound.

This hotel was recently updated, vert clean, updated tv, bathroom was very clean and well-lit. For all you germaphobes out there, you will like this hotel. Service was very good, the front desk was approachable and willing to help. We stayed here with points so I'm not sure about the value of it, but our experience was very enjoyable. If we needed to stay near the airport again, we would pick this hotel. It's about 20 minutes from downtown. Ambience is wonderful!

review_title: Wow! What a great night's sleep!
review_text: I cannot believe how well I slept. It was quiet inside and out. The bed was extremely comfortable and you could actually adjust the room temperature without a huge effort. I was also very impressed that they had a special remote control for the (big) LCD that was designed so it could be easily sanitized. They also have enclosed parking and a reasonably priced breakfast buffet. The staff (front desk, maintenance and housekeeping) were all extremely friendly and helpful. I will definitely stay here again - for the money, it cannot be beat.

Wonderful helpful staff! I came in late and was leaving early and you took care of everything for me....I greatly appreciate you going the extra mile. Loved those hash browns early the next morning! 
Thanks for a great but short nights sleep! I will be back!

review_title: Well managed Hampton in a great neighborhood near the Space Needle.
review_text:
Nice Hampton in an eclectic neighborhood with great small restaurants and pubs. Walk to the Space Needle, Key Center and theater.
Well run hotel with a wonderful staff.
I had a suite which ranked with Hamptons best.
Well staffed breakfast area that was clean, friendly and well supplied.
The only complaint is the noise factor from the hallways and street. The walls are not well insulated but this is a small drawback from an otherwise great smaller Hampton Inn.

We booked a two bed room weeks before, got email confirmation from the booking agency/hotel and when we arrived they said there was a glitch in the system and had to stay in a one bed room. 
They gave us the room with a view of a scummy parking lot instead of a view of the space needle, which is why I booked it in the first place. When I called to switch rooms they said there was none available...and to take a breakfast voucher. Well, I didn't come for a breakfast voucher. I came to have my own bed with a view of the space needle.
Never again.

review_title: Fine but not as good as Doubletree nearby
review_text:
For the same price, you can get a much nicer environment at Doubletree. 
Pros 
* free airport shuttle, clean, winnable on priceline
Cons 
* nickel and dime costs for Internet, parking, king bed
* too few elevators

review_title: Not going back even if it was inexpensive ....
review_text: The Best Western near Seatac seemed like a good choice because I had to work at the airport but I was disappointed. The room was huge but terribly furnished, looked like stuff from Goodwill. The tiny TV was about a mile from the bed! The shower drain was mildewed. The continental breakfast was the only good feature. Service was adequate, nothing special.
Very friendly, clean and convenient. Bar / rest in hotel was surprisingly good. Would come back

I got the rooms from priceline. We were told since we got it from priceline we were assigned rooms with two double beds. We have to pay $10 to upgrade to a king room. I've won Hilton through priceline all over the country. This was the first time I hear this. I didn't argue with them. But it's surly disappointing.
Parking isn't cheap. Rooms are on the small side. They don't have a printer for guests as the doubletree next door does. Other than these, it's a OK Hilton hotel.

We arrived at Sea-Tac after midnight and was glad to see the hotel shuttle arrive a few minutes later. The driver was very helpful - even arranged a private car to take us into the Amtrak station the next morning at a better price than a cab. The room was very large and the bedding was the best. We were sorry we only had a few hours stay.

The staff are friendly for the most part. Be advised of the $50 per night pre auth to be put on your credit card. Everything has a price here. There is a much better free continental breakfast down the street at the Sleep Inn. The only way to get a free one here is to have enough HHonors points.

review_title: The best folks there were the evening valets
review_text: An airport hotel should never tell a late night arriving guest that they may have to wait several hours before their room will be ready and that they can wait at the bar....after knowing the guest has a pre seven am flight.

review_title: For the business traveler with a late check-in, be warned.
review_text:
I booked an overnight stay online for a layover. I informed the hotel that I would be checking in around 10:30 pm and would be leaving at 7:00 am the next day so I would appreciate a quick checkin. I arrived at 11:30 (delayed flight) and the representative at the desk told me there were no clean rooms, that he wasn't sure when there would be a clean room, and that I could just wait. I asked what he expected me to do and he informed me that I could wait a couple of hours in the lobby but he wasn't sure how long that wait would be. I informed the representative that although it wasn't his fault, I was a bit disturbed that I might not get a room until 2:30 in the morning and then check out at 6:30 am. He stared at me with a blank stare and shrugged. At this point I requested that they cancel my reservation (luckily a friend had checked in earlier and had a room in which I could crash) and he so kindly informed me that they would waive the late cancellation fee... Right. I felt horrible for the fellow late night travelers left stranded.... Not once did Hilton's representative act engaged or concerned. Moreover I would expect some sort of apology and perhaps an offer for coffee etc. While suggesting I wait 2-3 hours for a clean room at midnight. 
That being said, my friend's room seemed clean. The bed was comfortable and the proximity to SEA-TAC can't be beat-that is if you actually get a room.

review_title: This hotel makes a bad name for Hilton :(
review_text:
Stayed at this hotel for 4 nights for an event and I was less than impressed to say the least. 
The hotel is located by the airport and with little things to do near by with the exception of a few fast food places. 
The hotel staff are not very acccomidating. I had booked my room 2 months in advance and had requested a fridge but was declined one at check in. 
There were no working ice machines anywhere on the 2nd floor and due to the strange shape of this hotel it would take 10 minutes just to get sw ice. 
Internet will cost you $15/day and I find this unacceptable in 2011. When you're paying $120+ nigt the Internet should be free. There was no WiFi in the conference area either:(
The hotel restaurant is overpriced and the food is just ok. I'd eat elsewhere. 
If you need assistance the front desk staff lack any type of hospitality skills. I asked on arrival and my day of departure for a late check out (1.5 hours). I was given an extra 15 minutes or "additional chargers would take place". 
In conclusion, I would rate this hotel at a 3 star at the best and give it a 2/10 for value. Will not say here again.

Sono passato di qui con due amici per una notte. Che dire, la camera fantastica, super moderna, addirittura oltre al wifi, c'Ã¨ pure una porta Ethernet e varie porte per connettere pc portatile alla tv..Il bagno normale, ma dispone di una doccia stondata grandissima.. Insomma se passate di qui fermatevi... Zona centralissima e trenino dietro l'edificio. Claudio

How do these rooms not have mini fridges? Bar food was good. Did the fly n jet package. Buses run late during busy times. Overall I would say "meh". Two out of five. Oh yeah...place is kinda sleazy...watch out for ladies of the night coming and going.

For a 4 star hotel I am really disappointed. The pool and hot tub are closed. Apparently I was supposed to look on their website for this. The top floor lookout bar was closed. $15 if u want Internet. And to top it off only one elevator works of four so have been waiting 20 mins to go out.

review_title: 3 an a half weeks later and I'm still itchy!!!!!
review_text:
My family and I stayed here at the end of November. I almost always take my own soap and if I forget I go and buy it. This hotel claims they are 4 stars and their bath products are supposed to be from a well known spa so I thought "hey how bad can it be?". REAL BAD!!! My skin had an allergic reaction to this horrible soap and lotion and I scratched NON stop day and night for 2 weeks and am still itchy. I have been to 5 different doctors which included an allergist, a dermatologist and the ER!!! I was told my skin has severely reacted to something I have used which has caused my psoriasis to flare up like never before. AND The ONLY thing I have done different is use the bath products at this so called "4 star" hotel. In almost 35 years i have NEVER experienced skin problems even half as bad as i have since staying at the hotel. The staff was not helpful, parking was outrageous, security questioned us like we were trying to steal something, for the first time ever at a 4+star hotel I was charged for milk for my baby, the call button on the intercom from the parking Garage was not functioning so i had to Walk back into the hotel. I'm sure there is more but I can't think with the burning sensation around my eyes!!! Overall a HORRIBLE experience! Guess we should just stick with The Sheraton. 
Irritated beyond belief!
I have stayed here a few times. It is close enough to walk to dinner and shopping. Short drive to sight seeing. Very nice location and rooms.
Central location, clean rooms, friendly staff and went out of their way to help us organize tours and things to do.

Ok location. Syrupy sweet clueless front desk staff. Generous size rooms. You should get a prize for finding the front door. The address is on 4th Avenue, but the entrance is actually on Seneca. Valet parking looks like you are pulling into the building not a parking structure. There is NO self parking. They will direct you to a garage on the corner, but if you are travelling on business or accuring hotel points this garage does not bill to the hotel. Very dark rooms, as in no lights, not as in dark enough to sleep late. Many better options in the area.

review_title: Cheap hotel with a posh name!
review_text: The staff is really cordial and polite. If you stay here ask for a room that does not face te highway, because the windows are a single glass and it might be very noisy, specially during week mornings. The rooms are ok, but nothing extraordinary. If you have breakfast, maybe choose of the menu. The buffet has a lack of options and not as well prepared. Maybe choose somewhere else for the same rate.

It is what it is. I guess for near $300 a night (after the taxes and valet charges catch up with you) you would at least get some WiFi included with your stay. Not to mention that when you pull up the valet would be there to actually get your car, take your gas and there wouldn't be only two people to check in a crowd of thirty. The rooms are nice, clean, and stocked. There was a mini-fridge that did not charge you each time you opened it. Very easy access to the freeway, so this would be a good stop on your way north to Canada.

review_title: A really great deal in downtown Seattle!
review_text:
I was able to secure three rooms at this hotel via Priceline.com for about $100 ea. on a Thursday night. For a full service hotel in downtown Seattle I thought this was an excellent bargain. 
The rooms were very nice, clean and comfortable. The location is convenient and and easy walk to many attractions, museums and restaurants. I personally had a room on the 8th floor and thought that there was a bit too much road noise coming from the street. If I ever go back, I will ask for a higher floor. 
The bar on the 28th floor has an amazing view on a clear night. You don't want to miss it!
Hotel is old but the rooms were very clean and comfortable. The outside may not be pretty but there was nothing wrong with the inside. I would definitely stay here again.
We stayed four nights. Everything was perfect. No ice machine on the 26th floor.

review_title: HOW DID THIS PLACE PASS INSPECTION?!....
review_text: Me and my friend were looking for a cheap place to stay till the morning while we were out of town. I really wanted to stay in a nicer place but lack of money. We got our room, there were cigarette burns in the floor, not to mention the bed..... It was disgusting and the sheets were dirty. When we went to pull off the sheets THERE WAS A BUG CRAWLING AROUND IN THE SHEETS! we ran out of the room screaming. We left asap and got our money back thank god. Be aware in the parking lot there will be creepy people. Two black men tried coming to "chill" with me and my friend in our room. EW.

If your in it for a quick stay than this isn't your place,however, if your looking to get a piece of history then this is the place. I was a little skeptical on this place due to bad reviews and the overall look of the place. Truthfully, I thought I was gonna see a ghost and be freaked out and leave. But after staying here I have to say, if you sit down with the owner and learn about the place she will go it of her way to help you out. She mapped out the best places to check out in Seattle, named some good cheap places to eat AND she even upgraded the rooms for the same price. Btw i've never slept in a more comfortable hotel bed :-)

review_title: Not as close to sightseeing as online sites say.
review_text: Pretty average place only really worthy of a 3 diamond rating. my wife was annoyed with the concierge on multiple occasions because of snobbishness. expect to pay an extra 30 dollars on top of your room rate for nightly parking. as with most hotels now everything is an extra and costs money. for the cost we would likely stay at the fairmont or hyatt next time

Well I have stayed here before and it seemed like a real nice atmosphere. It did have it's problems but the staff were making sure it was safe place. Now I recently went back and it said it was under new management. They raised the prices. Not good as far as customer service,there was blood on my sheets and I found a needle in my room with my newborn child. Not Happy!!!! I also overheard a man talking about his room hving bed bugs. As soon as I heard that it was time to go! If you want bad services, drug paraphernalia, expensive rooms rates and bloodon your sheets this iz tha place for you.

This is a bad place. I had stayed here a few times before a.d had no issues. I saw a sign that said under new management and figured i would try it again, Bad decision. Room was not clean and had a very bad smell. They charged way to much for the room to begin with. There was dirty sheets on my bed and I even had someone walk into my room. I stayed 45 minutes and drove up the street to another HOTEL! Room was cheaper and ten times nicer. DONT GO TO THE EVERSPRING!

I am very familiar with the Seattle area and love the location of this hotel!! Very close to pikes market, west lake mall, the monorail, tons of other shopping and restaurants!! Low crime area with police force around so you feel pretty safe;). Great place to stay at an amazing price!!

LOVED:
- locaton; never more than 15-20 mins away from all attractions (shopping, space needle, pike market) 
- large rooms (including couch, desk, king size bed)
- hot tub, sauna and inground pool
- great service at front desk
- small balcony with patio door that opens
WASN'T CRAZY ABOUT
- noise (with a whole wall mde out of windows, very noisy even on the 15th floor!)
- tiny bathroom
Wouls definitely go back....and would try what seems to be amazing restaurant (Margaux)

If I was bringing a hooker back to some seedy hotel, this is where I would go. The rooms are about 12'x12' and the bed squeaks every time you move. No water glasses, tin tiny soap bars, and a broken smoke detector, add to the ambience of this fine establishment. The bathroom is about the size of a closet. We found a smoked cigarette butt floating in the toilet, in our non-smoking room. Shows exactly how much the owners care about cleanliness. I ended up paying for parking, since the underground parking lot was full. This feat of manueverig only took 20 minutes of my time, since the idiot at the front desk obviously did not keep track of anything. The tv in the room got all 4 basic cable channels, so I guess thats a plus. Only stayed here because all other hotels were booked. How the owners get away with changing $100 is beyond me! The best part of staying here was getting out of the room. Avoid this dump at all costs, unless you have some kinky hooker fantasy going on, or want to experience how people in communist Europe used to live.

review_title: DON'T STAY HERE UNLESS YOU'RE IN DIRE NEED OF A HOTEL!!!
review_text: This motel was absolutely disgusting. It looks exactly like where cops set up drug and prostitute stings. The ice bucket was stolen from the radisson hotel, it smells like a mix between dirty air conditioning and cigarettes. The bed is ridiculously uncomfortable, and the towels, let's just say I'm lucky I brought my own. The point is, don't stay here...EVER!

The hotel was fine. Nothing special and we had a less than lovely view of the highway. The hotel staff were very nice and I love that the provide Aveda products!. My only complaint is that the room was very cramped.

This hotel is very convenient in the centre of Seattle with friendly and courteous staff.
The rooms are clean and tidy but starting to show signs of their age and in need of upgrading.

I usually dont leave poor reviews but at first glance motel looked nice, location was nice motel looked updated...then we got a room with dog pee all over floor, my one year old crawled on it and her knees smelled like urine so my husband checked floor to see where smell was coming from and yes dog pee. Then at 11 pm someone was smoking pot in next room so bad it filled our room...and when I called front desk they said person might have marijuana card..like that made it ok? So at 11:30 at night I got to wake up 3 small kids and move rooms. I guess the final straw for me to where I felt I needed to leave this review would be the bed bug I found in my bed and the bite marks on my 17 mth old...i will never ever stay at this motel again. When I contacted corporate all they said was "sorry we didnt meet your expectations, we hope to show you we have improved on your next visit" sorry not happening I will spend the extra $20.for super 8 where they dont allow pot smoke in bed rooms and bed bugs in our bed.

Stayed here oct 17-19. Great experience!! Location, price and view! Sliding door opens to mini balcony but good enough. Can walk everywhere tho waterfront can be challenging coming back-- hill. Tho I am not a high maintenance person--I can read signs and figure things out. If I can't I will ask for help nicely!! If you have problems with the help anywhere touristy you are not asking correctly. Really--try it!!

Really thin walls. We could hear people in other rooms when they even were just walking to the bathroom. Could also hear anyone talking in the hallway and out in the parking lot clearly Random black hair in the bed, shower, and bathroom floor. Front desk seemed rude. Seemed like they were tryin to kick me out of the room the next morning after like 10am even though checkout isn't till noon. I know there are other hotels in the area with similar pricing. I would stay somewhere else next time. 
Breakfast wasn't too bad. Although the room was small and I think it made a lot of the guests grumpy.

I stay in Seattle quite a bit for business and thought I would try something other than the Westin. BIG MISTAKE!!! This hotel has been given 3 1/2 stars and in Chicago it would be lucky to get 2. For starters, the room was about 100 square feet, the furniture had to be for decoration because it was so uncomfortable to sit on. The bathroom was barely big enough to turn around in and the shower head was broken. Has anyone ever seen a window air conditioner in a 3 1/2 star hotel? I could hear everything my neighbors in the next room were saying and the traffic on the street started at 5am...bus route right outside. 
I have no idea how this hotel gt any good ratings but if you want luxury
 for the price don't stay here!!!!!
$45 parking per day. NO in-room coffee or internet. Ordinary rooms & beds. Heavenly beds are better @ Westin. Great location, walking distance to Pike Place and downtown shopping.
Great location, walking distance to all exclusive shops, restaurants, and Pine Street Market. Buffett breakfast was great tasting and variety.

When I spend 200+ dollars a night for a hotel room I expect to be treated well. The customer service in this hotel is lacking. And there is no coffee maker in the room. When I called the front desk at 1015 am I was told there was coffee in the lobby but only until 10, so no I could not have a cup of coffee. They said they could send up a coffee maker but they did not have any ground coffee. I stayed at the hotel 1000 a little less than a year ago and would highly recommend every to stay there instead. Better rooms and better/friendlier staff.

review_title: Very comfortable, gay friendy vibe. Would stay again.
review_text: Great location,excellent service nd comfort- a wonderful hotel.

We stayed in a room with two queen beds. With two teens in tow it would be better if they had rooms with one queen and two twins. Overall great. We stay here every time we have a SEATAC layover and will repeat.

Good location , fast check in although we were simply handed our room key I think it would have been nice if the desk clerk could have said " you are in room so and so floor etc 
The cd player didn't work 
lamp next to the bed switch was loose 
most annoying was the housekeeper knocking on the door at 9am we told her we were checking out at noon 
then at 11.15 she knocked again same person that was annoying !

review_title: Didn't live up to the hype, but just barely.
review_text:
My stay began Sunday and ended this morning. I was in corner room 2012. I found the check in staff to be quite pleasant, and they quickly helped locate the valet so that I could park my car; I was surprised that no one was at the valet station for several minutes after I arrived, but I did arrive late on Sunday so it wasn't a big deal. I was offered the customary points bonus or wine (I am a platinum level guest) and told about the gym (pretty nice compared to many other hotels). It was an easy checkin and a welcome experience after my trip.
The room was very nice, and during my stay the only complaint I have is that an awful lot of street and HVAC noise made it into the room. So much that I had a hard time sleeping on Wednesday night when the wind blew just right and made some noise at the window. I'm not sure what the solution is for this. The tv remote works flawlessly, and it was neat that there was a DVD player in the room - although I did not use it. I was very comfortable overall.
There was only one thing that marred my experience: the last interaction with the front desk this morning. I noticed that I was charged $45.14 for parking vs. The advertised $37, so I wanted to find out why. I asked the young man and young lady at the desk this morning about the discrepancy. I was told that the city tax had been included in the total, and that it was on the sign as $37 + tax. I told them I felt it was a bit like a bait and switch, but that I understood and felt that perhaps it would be helpful to have the tax as a seperate line item on the reciept - to avoid this issue in the future. There was some back and forth conversation about the tax, and I reiterated that I felt it should be a seperate line item, like other Starwood hotels in the area. In response, the young man smirked at me and told me that all the hotels in the area do it this way (they don't), and that it was 'clearly on the sign'. 
I am sorry, but at midnight on a rainy Sunday night it isn't clear, and I certainly don't appreciate being laughed at. As a former employee of the Westin Kierland I know the level of service expected by Starwood employees. This fell FAR below expectations. I felt stupid and insulted and like I told you as I walked out the door: I'll just stay at the Sheraton next time: the only issue there is that they're often full.
This can be fixed, which is why I am posting this review. Starwood hotels have been and will continue to be my first choice when travelling. I would recommend this hotel, but only as second choice to the Sheraton for business travelers.
Good location near airport, only few minutes drive. This ramada is off course no luxury but good value-for-money choice. Rooms r spacious and clean

I'm going to just simply describe what I feel needs fixing in this hotel. First my room TV, you need to turn it off and on several times to make it work. In other words it needs to warm up! Huh? Really? It's 2011 guys, not 1973. Channel selection, very poor no Travel Channel! Another huh? Shower, low pressure and definitely old school. Once you get it going it's takes time for the hot water to come out. Are we using coal chambers here!!!!
Food, breakfast Buffett, $18 bucks!!! Same menu, little no variety! For that much you expect more. Lastly, here's a hint? When you see your customers walk in the lobby, say hello!!! The women staff members here feel they're gods gift to men....really?

The hotel room is so very dark - it is the hotel's style but we found it depressing. There was plenty of wardrobe and drawer space for clothes.
The bar is located in space normally a corridor, quite off-putting. The bar furniture is very tired, I wouldn't want to entertain there.
The restaurant although highly rated and award winning was very quiet, we didn't try it as it was expensive and there is so much choice nearby at more affordable rates; including a Starbucks across the road for breakfast.
The hotel staff were helpful and polite at all times.
I feel sure for there are better choices in Downtown Seattle.

review_title: Querky, charming and a nice change from your average hotel.
review_text: Hotel Max was such a charming little hotel right in the heart of downtown Seattle. Within walking distance of everything you want to see in town. The rooms are a decent size and the beds are so comfortable! The nicest beds I've ever slept in in a hotel! Other reviews stated the bathrooms were small but ours was just fine. I stayed in room 420 which was a corner room with a good view of the city. It was creative and fun without being over the top. Great value for what it is and I will certainly be back.

review_title: Style and good value in Seattle
review_text: Clean, friendly, stylish and well-located with a decent restaurant and charming, helpful staff.

review_title: Great location and service, good price for the area.
review_text: I chose the hotel for location and price. I was extremely happy with the service during my whole stay. Staff was friendly, responsive and helpful. Location is extremely convenient. Rooms furnishings are not the newest, but that does not detract from the comfort, and it was quiet at night. I did not eat in the restaurant and cannot respond to negative reviews of that restaurant's prices, but I will note that nearby restaurants are all pretty expensive.
This hotel expresses an heir of entitlement through the expression of their rates with backing it up with substance. The accomodations were adequate but overpriced for the overall services delivered.

Well you are likely to get ripped off no matter what hotel you stay in downtown of any city, hotel max makes it an art. No free wifi (this really makes me mad, as every hostel and motel I've ever stayed in has FREE wifi... What a concept! No they want 12 bucks a day). Parking was 35 dollars per night. They bed was one of the most uncomfy I've ever slept on, the walls were paper thin and there was a screaming seagull's nest outside our window which made it hard to sleep and the shower was a super cramped cell (and I'm 5 ft 3 in) with a opaque shower curtain that made it almost pitch black in there. Save your money and get a private room in a hostel! The location was ok.

Have just finished a five day stay. A little concerned before arriving having read some negative reports on here. I found the hotel and staff excellent for a hotel in this price range. The courtesy bus collected me from the airport and when I arrived I had been upgraded to a King size which was extremly comfortable. You could hear the trafic on the interstate but it was not that load that it disturbed my sleep. Staff were very helpful whenever I had a query or request, and I managed to make waffles each morning with no problems. There is coffee in your rooms and if you need more there is coffee in reception 24hrs. The number 150 bus stop is just 5 minutes walk and a frequent service that takes you into Downtown. The hotel courtesy bus brought me back to the airport it was just a ten minute drive - will definately stay here again next time I am in Seattle

Right across from airport. Older building with an odd design, but the rooms are updated, clean and comfortable. 
Good wifi signal, fast enough for video. 
Decent fitness center w/full dumbbell set to 50 lbs. Several treadmills and ellipticals
If you don't like to walk with bags, get a room close to the lobby. I was in wing 4 and it was a bit of a walk and two different elevators to get to my room, but I the chocolate chip cookie gave me the energy I needed.

This feels like a wonderful place for very hip young people. Rooms were wonderfully appointed but tiny. Lighting in the bathroom was poor. Art on doors was wonderful but a bit disorienting. Bed was very comfortable.

review_title: Ask for a room away from the highway
review_text:
The hotel is right next to the highway. This makes it easy
 To find but the rooms on that side must be very noisy. Our room was on the inside overlooking the pool but away from the highway. The room was clean and what you would expect from this sort of hotel/motel hairdryer, fridge microwave 2 queen beds, linen was clean, bathroom reasonable modern and clean.
On our booking we requested a rollaway bed and blankets. It wasn't there on arrival so I asked at the desk and they said they would bring it up. It never arrived. I asked again the next day and then went back to reception, again and again. It got very late again and I had to but the children to bed so I went down to say not to bother but was told It was not available and never had been. I did feel this was bad service as they should have said when we checked in not had us waiting, and asking several times and waiting... Just say it is not available.
The breakfast was very nice, included with room rate. Waffles, pastries, cereals, juice etc
Area was kept clean and replenished right up to 9:30 finish
20 minute drive to downtown Seattle , 5 min to Airport
Shame it is so very close to the highway. A little further back would have been so much quieter.
It is OK for what it is- cheap, clean 1 night hotel

I opted for this hotel as my known and looked hotels were unavailable for my dates. Just booking the room online was troublesome. Wanted park and fly, followed the site's instructions of how to book, and was informed on arrival $25 more needed for parking. This after calling to verify at time of booking. Oh well, flight is soon, had good shuttle to Seatac. On return trip, despite putting note in original booking, and conversation with front desk on initial arrival, I called Days Inn for ride from airport, at 1 am as noted. Informed shuttle doesn't run after 11 pm! $20 more for taxi. Met with stale room adjacent to freeway, shower only functional because I have overhauled plumbing before, and knew how to hack it enough to deliver water. Left ASAP, found breakfast downtown.

review_title: Pleased for the price we payed.
review_text:
We booked our one night stay on Priceline after winning a bid for $75.00 for the night. Priceline says this hotel is a 4 star property, but it is not in my opinion. I would put it at a 3 or possily 3.5 star. Here is why... The room furniture was scratched and had gouges in the surface. The tiles in the shower were cracked. There were scuff marks on painted surfaces. To me 4 star is attention to those details. So the room itself was more like a 3. 
The service was a little better. When we arrived I had mentioned we were there for my wife's birthday, and they asked me if we liked Wine or Beer. I said I liked Beer but my wife doesn't drink. When we returned from dinner they had placed two bottles of beer and a bottle of sparkling cider on ice in the room. Very cool. That service bumped me up to probably a 3.5 overall. 
The pool and hot tub were nice we spent a couple of hours there. 
Didn't try any of their lounges or restaurants. 
As far as noise goes, I do have to say you can hear things pretty easily. Heard a vaccum running in the morning, toilets flushing, heavy doors shutting, hotel itself creeking in the wind, and occasionally voices. 
Have to say the residants in the condos across the way are very entertaining and some even seem to enjoy putting on a show if you know what I mean. 
The parking underneath is tight. Hard to navigate and didn't appear to be enough. We came back around midnight or so and had to go all the way down. 
Overall, I can't complain for the price we paid. I'd stay again for that rate, but wouldn't pay full fare to stay here.

We are military and were stuck in Seattle for almost a week due to a typhoon where we were headed ( Japan). This was not something we'd planed for. Over all the staff was super nice and the people of Seattle were really friendly. The only issues was TWO WEEKS after we'd checked out my card was charged TWICE MORE! almost $400 for a stay that was for 2 nights at $65.00 per night! I called and emailed the hotel with no response. I will now have to have my bank go after them for unauthorized charges.

Great place to stay. I'm partial to this collection of hotels. This is an older property, but it has been well maintained. The staff is friendly, helpful and very accommodating. You can't beat the location if your traveling for pleasure - right downtown and very near the waterfront. Beware -parking is expensive!

I had low expectations for this place but I was suitably impressed. It's good value for money, the rooms are clean, the beds are super comfortable, and I had a great night's sleep. We only went in to the city once, and although it's a 30 min Skytrain ride away (which I wouldn't like to do regularly), the station is a minute's walk away. There are also restaurants nearby and plenty of other hotels with restaurants. We ate at the hotel restaurant and it was really good.
This hotel is modern and funky with character. It is close to all the shopping and walking distance to the main sites. We got the train to the airport early morning and it was easy.

review_title: Great Hotel in a Great Location
review_text: My wife and I stayed here the night before our cruise. The hotel was very nice and was in a great location. It's minutes walking distance from Pike's Market and other great Seattle attractions. It's also conveniently located only a block from the transit system. The gym was really nice. They also offer complimentary transportation to the pier for anyone leaving on a cruise.

review_title: I will never stay here again
review_text: The room sucked, parking sucked and the service sucked. Do not stay here. It wasn't even worth $79 per night. I'll pay more to stay somewhere else next time.

review_title: Overall great hotel, service really needs attention...
review_text: A Christmas Spectacular...the lobby is stunning. The rooms are spacious and clean..yet the bathrooms are tiny. The service is on a downward spiral. We stay here yearly on business. I called the front desk twice for tissues as I was sick and a replacement iron as ours was horribly dirty and would not place it on my clothes. The hairdryer was broken and when I called the front desk for a replacement, the gal stated they had none...I told her I need one for an office party and one magically appeared. On our second night there, I asked the concierge for a dinner recommendation that did not include meat, and they both gave me one choice packed full of meat...no seafood restaurants, no Italian. I asked for an additional option, They Both Had Only One Restaurant To Offer......when they called for a reservation, it was booked. My husband and I walked around downtown on our own and found Local, and had shrimp. At The Spa you can always get a wonderful pedicure and the women are always happy and gracious. Overall, The Peabody is a wonderful hotel to experience at Christmas for the decor..the lobby is beautiful. The bar is happening and the bartenders work their tails off. On the other hand, I believe the staff could use a boost....we looked at other hotels in the area for next year and think we would go to The Peabody for drinks and the spa...

review_title: Wish I read these reviews before I stayed!
review_text: We checked in and the girl wasn't overly friendly, but that wasn't a really big deal to us. Went to our room and it was ok, nothing fancy, but it would do for 2 nights. The first night was fine, in terms of noise and quality of sleep. In the morning I woke up and not sure why, but decided to check trip advisor. I was shocked at other peoples stories and advice. When my partner woke up he told me that someone had knocked on our door several times during the night. We both decided to loose our money for the second night and leave. It was a good decision!

Posizionato in una zona malfamata, nonostante avessimo chiesto delle stanze non fumatori alcuni di noi si sono trovati in stanze talmente puzzolenti da non poter dormire. I cuscini erano impregnati di fumo ma il consierge non ha trovato nulla di meglio che piazzare un inutile ventilatore. La pulizia lascia a desiderare, cosÃ¬ come i servizi.

Each year I stay at the W Seattle at least once. In 10 years of traveling to Seattle, the last 3 have been with the W every time. The staff continues to be amazing, the accommodations are perfect, and the location is super convenient. I brought my wife this time and she was also very pleased...and my wife finds problems with every hotel so her positive experience is priceless.

We stayed at the W Seattle for four nights and had plenty of time to study this interesting hotel. First of all, the staff at the reception were not only unfriendly, but even snobbish. Same applies to the concierge that showed a similar level of (in)competence as the reception guys and seemed to be more interesting in surfing a bit on the internet than making a reservation at a restaurant... The hotel is definitely overpriced for what you get. I'm staying at Starwood hotels pretty often and in general appreciate the service and comfort you get. W Seattle was definitely a big disappointment and honestly doesn't merit to be called a "W" hotel at all. Beside of far too small rooms, the hotel's general business policy towards guests seems to be "grab everything you can and run!". Parking did cost more than in New York and Wifi rates were just a rip-off par excellence. Better go to the ACE hotel where you get for the same price a room twice as big and much more competent and willing staff!

We stayed on a BUSY saturday night. When we arrived 2 of 4 elavators worked (about 2pm). By 6pm only 1 worked! We were on the 9th floor and traveling with a baby so we waited 15 mins one time. next morning still only 1 elavator worked. This is the only negative thing I have to say. Shuttle service to airport was great! Room was clean and comfortable. Service was excellent.
From the famous duck walk to the location, service, atmosphere, all was great.

Located within a couple of minutes of the airport this is a large hotel that we thought was great value. No problem with aircraft noise really nice bar and lounge with sensibly priced good food. Recommended
Very accomodating... Great location, great recomendations... Great service = Great stay!

Stayed at the hotel in November for a business trip. 
Location: fantastic, a block from a light rail station, and walkable to great restaurants and sights
Gym: good size, has free weights, machines, and 10 or so cardio machines. Would have liked kettle balls and an ab machine. 
Service: great, very friendly and prompt. 
Rooms: got upgraded to the 23rd floor, so had a great view. Room was clean but some drawbacks: no hooks on closet door or behind bathroom door to hang anything, no outlets near windowsill couch, digital alarm clock would be better. 
Overall, loved my stay.

Pros:
* very nicely decorated, close to airport, 24hr shuttle, 12pm checkout, comfy beds
Cons:
* no free breakfast, wired Internet, pricey if you didn't win it via priceline

I stayed here because it was close to the airport and is in the Hilton family. The bed was SO comfortable!!! The staff was very friendly and definitely went the extra mile. I think I lucked out with staying in the main tower, as this is a huge complex! I got lost trying to find the coin laundry. The laundry area is nice, though. The washers and dryers have timers on them, so that helps. Room service dinner was okay. Not great, but not bad. Love the cookies at check in! I would recommend returning your rental car and riding back to the hotel on the shuttle as parking is expensive.

review_title: Perfect location for the price but VERY SMALL
review_text: I have stayed at Hotel Max three times and have been happy with each stay. The location is PERFECT! Right downtown! The only thing that I find negative about Hotel Max is how small everything is. The elevator can hardly fit two people plus luggage and the rooms are tiny. But they are very artistic and trendy which helps make up for the size.

We decided to stay here for three nights during our trip to Seattle. The checkin clerk was very friendly and said she would ensure we had a good view. We ended up on the 11th floor overlooking the airport and the Cascades. We had a balcony, the beds were super comfortable, room was a good size and clean. There are restaurants all around, plus two in the hotel. Shuttle to airport runs every 20 minutes. Great place and would definately stay again.

review_title: Nice rooms, near airport, long walk to room
review_text:
I stayed one night at this hotel as it is very close to the airport. Overall the rooms were nice and clean, comfortable bed, and good location. 
Two issues:
This is a big property so it is a long walk to some of the rooms. Not a big deal but could be for others.
The issue I had is that my wake up call came 1.5 hours early.

review_title: The only place I will stay when in Seattle
review_text:
I love this hotel. It is close to bus lines, the light rail, and all of the things that you want to see in Seattle. I can walk to Pikes Place and the Space Needle, or for $2.50 I can hop the light rail to the stadiums. For $4.00 I can take the light rail to the airport. 
The rooms are beautiful with floor to ceiling windows. You can get a city or water view and since the buildings are in the round you can see everything. I normally ask for a higher floor to improve the view and decrease the city noise. 
Staff are great. You must stay here on your next trip to Seattle.

review_title: Great service and location at this historic hotel.
review_text: Don't miss the chance to see the ducks parade off the elevator in the lobby.

review_title: Great Views, Good Service, Needs Remodeling
review_text: Our view of Puget Sound and the Space Nestle from our 37th floor North Tower view is hard to beat. The entire hotel though is a bit dated and run down. For the price, I want overall newer and cleaner.

This was my first trip to Seattle. I loved the views from the room and the bed was SO comfortable, heavenly. There were a couple times we had to call for things like bad creamer needed to be replaced, room service was there in a flash. We had a suite and the rooms needed a bit of updating (furniture a bit worn and one of the light fixtures was broken), but overall good size, spectacular views and very clean. I would return to this hotel again.

Stayed here with my 7 year old son overnight on our way to Asia. It was convenient and friendly. Clean rooms and love that they had room service. Prompt airport shuttle and amiable staff. Used the gym facility which was adequate and pleasantly unexpected in a hotel this size. 
Will be staying here again on our future sea tac layovers.

I brought my husband here with high expectations and was sorely disappointed . The whole place was run down - cracks in our bedroom window were selotaped together, service was shabby, fire alarm went off at dawn with no apology from staff when we arrived downstairs and noises from the water pipes while we tried to sleep. Save your money and go to a motel!

Just finished my first stay at a W brand hotel and was very disapointed. The bathroom was dirty with visible mold/mildew on the grout on the tiled shower. We were stiffed on our bathroom toiletries. When I tried to call housekeeping to request the missing toiletries the phone in the room didn't work. The walls are thin (there must have been a party going on in the adjoining room). The bed was uncomfortable and there were no extra blankets (with a lighter weight than duvet) or pillows to use. Also $11 for a room service milkshake? Give me a break! If the hotel was fancy enough to warrant a milkshake that expensive that would be a wholly different story. Do yourself a favor and stay at the hyatt or Monaco for a much better experience.
As an aside, I highly recommend the "Mod" pizza place around the corner, great pizza with great prices!

I have stayed at the Hotel Max twice, and had great experiences both times. Parking at the hotel is super easy and all the staff are very friendly and attentive. My only complaints are with the size of the rooms/bathrooms, but that only applies to the most recent stay. The first time I had a pretty big room, but this last time it seemed the room shrunk by half. At the end of the day this is not a huge problem since the room is really only there for me to shower and sleep in, if I were living out of it, that would be a diferent story. Overall great experience and I will defeinitely be going back. Ohh and I forgot to mention the location; it is perfect for the person(s) who want to see all of downtown Seattle (Pikes, Space Needl, shopping) and don't mind walking. One night of parking at the Max is cheaper than a few hours of parking anywhere downtown.

review_title: This place was probably pretty sweet 30 years ago
review_text: First impression: crappy. Dingy. Old. Stuffy. Overpriced. If you consider changing a few light fixtures hanging some newer art and adding flat panel TVs a "remodel" then you'll be right at home here. Not only is it dark and musty smelling, but the staff really knows how to make you feel like you're an inconvenience. When I booked this room, nobody bothered to tell me they charge hotel guests $20/night for the privilege of parking in the same hotel you happen to be paying to stay at. When I attempted to complain to Marc (head of the front desk, by the way) he pointed out that parking this close to the airport is at a premium and I should be happy that as a guest, I get a discounted rate. Non-guests have to pay twice as much, he pointed out. Yeah, but they didn't pay $180 a night for a room to begin with, was my response. Besides, if someone is looking for airport parking, I'm pretty sure they can park at the airport itself for cheaper. Now who's the sucker? That's right, me. The one who paid in full in advance and had no recourse but to tell them about the negative review I was going to write. I could tell Marc cared deeply as he pretended not to hear. Here's the deal, if you want a nice place, go to Cedarhurst. If you want parking, go to the airport. Either way, move along people, there's nothing to see here...

review_title: Westin preview of planned upgrades fantastic!
review_text:
Westin Seattle staff went above and beyond for our 23rd wedding anniversary. Upgraded to one of two new rooms with the same great Seattle Westin comfort and a nice new modern look. The rooms decor was the main change with slick lines and the bed moved from its corner location providing more space and a nice luxury feel. Westin Seattle sets a high bar because the old rooms while only a little tired, remain luxurious right up to this planned rennovation. 
I have been hard on the Westin Brand as a platinum guest of spg because of the lack of lounges and upgrade amenities. But this stay included this lovely room and a nice bottle of champagne arranged by the front desk team and was splendid. 
I recommend the Westin Seattle in any room and look forward to the completion of the upgrades which are cominh ahead of the typical timeline. 
I hope the Westin Seattle adds some of nice features like amenity lounges and complimentary platinum parking etc. that are nice treats at their sister Spg properties.

Major disaster averted thanks to Westin Seattle's super staff! 
 I raced to Seattle to give a talk after tending to a family major hospital operation. Technical materials and resources for my talk were, unfortunately, sent to my twin grandsons' birthday party while I received the boys' presents and party favors--not a good day, but funny! Concierge Richard sent a car to pick me up. Ms. Helms along with arranged a room where I could work to collect materials and meet with colleagues. Concierge Judy told me where to find replacement materials. The bell staff are great! They hauled boxes, taped them, Sorid, only recently hired, actually moved furniture to arrange the suite to meet my needs and the bellman on duty overnight taped my boxes and handled my Fed Ex shipment, packed my cab to the airport this morning and mailed the presents home.. Vardo at the business center reprinted my handouts and immediately rushed to help me drag my suitcase out to the curb when he saw me struggling down the hall. Thank you all! This one day whirlwind trip worked out because of you! It is what makes me such a loyal SPG fan! The staff even reminded me to remember to eat "to keep up my strength." I am literally old enough to be their parents! Thanks guys!!!

Reserve:
To keep back, to set aside, to retain or hold over for a future time.
When I make a reservation one month in advance for a king size room and show up at exactly 4 pm to check in, I expect to receive keys to my king size room. 
Instead, I was told that "we are really overbooked tonight," and I was sent to a queen room with no reduction in fees or other offers to compensate me for my inconvenience. 
When I asked what else I should do next time to ensure I get what I reserve, the answer from the very polite young man was, "I don't know."
There will not be a next time. Ever.
Peabody is an excellent hotel. Customer service was excellent and room was great.

review_title: Grand historical hotel that misses the mark on service.
review_text: I have never been to Memphis and just came from Nashville where we had stayed at the service focused hotel The Hermitage. Check in was unorganized, with long lines. The room was tasteful but dated. Hated the bedding. General lack of of customer first attitude. Bellman would come into elevators with the luggage carts when it was already occupied by hotel guests. I will say that the staff in the gift shop were very nice. The duck walk is a good draw but at twice a day and the fact that there are more non-guest and kids running around really detracts from the elegance of the hotel. Too many add on charges that bring no value.

I stayed one night last week in room 702. It was an executive king at the end of the hall and was lovely. Updated and refreshed. My only complaint was the difficulty I had finding the valet entrance and the self parking was a bit of a hike.

Staff was friendly and breakfast was good. HOWEVER, the bathtub had hairs from previous occupant, the toilet was a mess, the bath towels were not clean at all (one still wet from previous guest) and inside the ice holder was a gross unknown substance. 
Hotel manager was apologetic and let us leave with a refund.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites North Seattle - Shoreline

review_text: This is our first time to Memphis and its been awesome! The staff here has been awesome and friendly and very helpful. Had a carriage ride that was part of our package. The kids loved the ducks and the scavenger hunt. The rooms were very comfortable and the beds ohhhh so soft! The hotel itself is very grand and beautiful. While doing scavenger hunt we realized we felt like it may be a bit spooky. We thought of the shining movie...other than that the piano man was great in lobby, wine was great and we've enjoyed our stay very much. With the package we recieved 2 scrap books for the kids and a carriage ride plus 2 free kids breakfast buffets. We would definitley come back! We also strolled Beale street,civil rights museum and tomorrow hitting Graceland ...;)

Visiting Seattle Woodland Zoo with the family, decided to use this as a home base for the 2 night stay. After reading some bad reviews, we were ready for the worse case scenario but I was pleasantly surprised. Hotel staff was very friendly and was greeted with a welcome gift (something to do with the priority member perk?). It is an older building but it's kept clean and I didn't see any sings of neglect. My son really enjoy the pool and plenty of restaurant choices in the area. Keep in mind, this is not down town Seattle. It's 15-25 min drive to downtown. This is not a touristy part of Seattle but if value is your priority, you'll like it. One complaint, their breakfast can step up a notch.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites North Seattle - Shoreline

review_text: We just arrived in Memphis this morning and have already had a great experience at the Peabody. We had an early flight and our room was ready for us at 9am they even upgraded us to the club level for our 10th anniversary! We got to see the 11am duck march and it was very cute. Now if it would stop raining it would be perfect. Will update with more details later.

We had a wonderful weekend stay. The Peabody has a great location near everything downtown, a classy yet fun lobby bar, excellent rooms (one of th best beds I have slept on), and of course the duck walk which really was fun. I need to put in a good word for Linda Small, who was very helpful Friday evening in the 12th floor lounge. She is a gem.

Nice hotel with fantastic fitness center. That's all that can be said. The duck march was crowded and lame. The service was typical. Truthfully I'd rather had stayed across the street at the Holiday Inn.
After our stay at The Madison, we realized how great The Peabody is. If you are going to pay above $200/night per room, you might as well do it right and stay here.

review_title: The most enjoyable stay at a hotel I've ever had!
review_text: When I first entered the Peabody, I was speechless. The lobby was huge and very elegant. Check in was a breeze. When I got to my room I was again, speechless. The rooms were kind of small but they were obviously showing that this was truly a five star hotel. The feature I really thought was cool was that there was a TV in the bathroom. Very comfortable beds and either 40 or 42" flat screen. Not the best view on the side of the hotel I stayed in but I didn't really care. The swimming pool was indescribable! Now this pool was the most exquisite swimming pool I have ever seen. I really don't know how to describe it, but your mouth will definitely fall open when you see it. And oh, there's also a hot tub. The outskirts of the lobby was kind of like a mini street. It had a bunch of Peabody brand stores. Now as some of you may know, the most special thing about the Peabody is no doubt, the ducks. First, music starts playing. Then the elevator doors open, and five ducks waddle out in front of the duck master into the fountain in the middle of the lobby. They stay there in the fountain till five o'clock and then the duck master comes and the same thing happens, only they get on the elevator instead of getting off. They go up to their duck palace on the roof, which you can visit. You can also just take in the view of downtown Memphis. I'd say that this hotel is a Perfect business hotel. There are a lot of meeting rooms, even one on the roof. The location of this hotel is perfect and a few blocks from Beale Street. I would highly recommend this hotel to anyone.

Very appointed in the Peabody. Rooms are very small and NO counter space in bathroom. The room overlooked the air conditioning unit. The worst part was there was a rooftop party going on and I could here everything loud and clear even on the fifth floor. Try sleeping with music blasting. Stay somewhere else .

review_title: Watch the seaplanes come and go from your room
review_text: I recently spent 4 nights here with family and really enjoyed this hotel. While the room was rather ordinary the view was great from our 7th floor perch. A big flat screen was nice but beds that were a bit too soft for my taste. The location was excellent right across from lake union and very close the the tram that goes directly to downtown. I would stay here again if my travels were to bring me to Seattle again
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Seattle Downtown / Lake Union

review_title: Superior service, other reviewers correct about the beds.
review_text: Service level here amazed me. This staff could immediately interchange with the Ritz Carlton and no one would be the wiser. I almost want to tour their HR. This is a walking business location for me with free street parking at night. Marriott Waterfront though is my prime choice for personal sans vehicle stay.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Seattle Downtown / Lake Union

review_text: A heritage hotel was a nice clean hotel. The rooms had a little kitchen which came in very handy. Staff were very friendly and helpful. Close by everything. Spec needle is walking distance 15mins approx. Downtown is just a short monorail ride after a 10-13min walk.

review_title: Great overnight for cruise, but not handicap-friendly
review_text: This was a real bargain through Priceline and perfect for our late-night arrival the night before our cruise. Right near the airport with a free shuttle and a great concierge. Only complaint was that the room was quite far from check-in, which was a bit annoying for us wearied travelers and a challenge for a handicapped guest we saw. Not really an issue though considering the incredible rate and excellent customer service. We even enjoyed our little balcony and the nice breakfast buffet in the morning, great coffee - yum!

review_title: Nice if you don't mind being charged 18 dollars for a cup of tea
review_text:
Peabody is an attractive hotel. The lobby is always busy mainly down to the twice daily 'duck parades' (cute the first time, irritating stepping over the general public who are not staying at the hotel, after that). 
Our room was nice, a queen size, the bathroom was very small and not a full bath which I don't feel really suited the room size. 
I am overall impresses with the facilities the pool area Is great but watch out because like everything at this hotel they hide the little additional charges from you. The facilities are not free and we were stung about 12 dollars per day extra even if we didn't use them. Apparently we were told this on check in. Well aim fairly sappy, granted, but I know when I'm being shafted! 
After three days of burgers and chips I was desperate for a cup of tea. Called room service after checking the menu and seeing 6 dollars for a pot of small tea. It arrived with a bill of 18.95 dollars. Apparently 4 dollars for delivery and 8.95 as a 'service charge' is acceptable. 
Frankly I was less than amused and the Tea tasted like pee.

review_title: Horrible value, not worthy of being called a "hotel."
review_text:
I recently stayed for 5 days on business at the Nexus. The hotel touts itself as being remodeled and modern, yet they still have 20 yr old televisions in some rooms. The colors make it look like it was used as a drug dealer motel in Miami Vice in the 80's. And the Breakfast is sparse and of low quality. 
I stayed in one of the Hydrotherapy suites. Do not believe the advertising. It is a overgrown tub that you can sit in. They are noisy and keep you awake if your neighbors happen to run theirs at night. Oh, and they are all bottom floor suites. Worse yet, there is little privacy in the rooms, given only a piece of glass separates the sleeping area from the toilet. Also, the Nexus has a policy that only your bed gets made and towels changed if you stays less than seven days. No counters or toilet cleaned, nothing else. Maids are in and out in just a few minutes. 
The Nexus is nothing more than an old outside-door motor inn that has had a feeble attempt at remodeling on the outside. It is still a noisy, cramped, and cheaply furnished motel on the inside. For your $150, the are many newer hotels (the Nexus is a motel still) that offer much better accommodations and service.

Located in the heart of Queen Anne. Lots to do in this area. Easy acess to down town Seattle. Cab fare is only about 7 dollars to Pioneer Square from here. The rooms are cozy and as expected for a historical hotel. The service was friendly and very helpful. Price was good. Would definitely stay here again.

There was a Microsoft convention the week I stayed there, but usually this hotel averages $150-$160 per night after the $10 parking fee. That is high for just an average HIE that is not very new. The location is good, but there are not many amenities or restaurants within walking distance. The hotel is loud because the rooms do not have double windows. I brought my ear plugs, so I was able to take care of the noise issue for about $.99. I stayed in the 6th floor (highest level), so the rooms had very tall ceilings; therefore, it took forever to heat the room. I was so cold that the first two nights I had to sleep with my jacket on. I finally requested double blankets to the Latino mades. They were super nice, and they are really the only reason why I would consider coming back to this hotel. If you are driving an SUV you will have a hard time parking since the space is so so tight. Overall an almost below average hotel that is overpriced.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Seattle City Center

review_title: Very close to the space needle
review_text: The hotel was fair. It was were close to the space needle. If traveling on aurora ave, it is quite hard to get to
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Seattle City Center

review_title: Great place to stay if you're planning on seeing Seattle.
review_text: I booked this hotel through priceline as part of my first trip to Seattle. The location is perfect. It's right across from the airport and right near the train into Seattle. The rooms were spacious and I had a balcony (not exactly a great view but I wasn't staying in the Alps). There's tons of places to order food from in the area. The staff was great. The girl at the front desk (cant remember her name it was a different name she had glasses) was extremely helpful and very personable. She gave me tips on what to see and avoid in Seattle. I will specifically book this hotel on my next trip to Seattle.
hotel_name: Red Roof Inn Seattle Airport - SEATAC

review_text: We stayed here for three nights on a family trip to Seattle. It was clean, comfortable and the service was great. Nice hot breakfast included that changed every day, and free shuttle service into town to help save on parking. The only two negatives were that the pool was out of service while we were there, although it was a lovely flourescent green colour, and they had a full house the first night which made them run out of parking spaces on the property, so some guests had to park in a lot across the street.
Very nice Seattle center location, small rooms , very quaint older hotel, for the budget concious traveler. Many restaurants nearby. Public transit one block. No need to use your auto...

Truly the worst "hotel" I've ever stayed at! We came to see a concert at the key arena across the street. We reserved the room 3 months in advance and specifically asked for a parking spot. We showed up, no parking spot available. They sold them all off for concert goers. Customers? Forget them! Had to park 6 blocks away in an overnight parkade for another $20. Then walked back to "hotel" to check in. It gets worse. The room was nice (around 80 years ago maybe) looked like a low income housing/halfway house. Situated right by the staircase without even a deadbolt lock! Then we look at the matress.....really scary! But as we were already late for the concert we just said we'd stay the 1 night instead of the 2 we booked. The "help" at the front desk was pretty useless as well. She was the one who informed us that they didnt have a parking spot. Also, they advertise a continental breakfast. Went to the lobby and found some oatmeal bars and oranges. 
At the end of the day, I recommend no one stay at this place! It should be condemned! Very dirty and disgusting. The Mediteranian hotel is 100 times better!
A popular spot for the pre and post cruise crowd. Close to downtown and the Needle. Most attractions about a 15 min walk.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Seattle City Center

review_title: A budget hotel in a central location. No frills...you get what you pay for.
review_text:
I stayed here for 2 nights last week with my husband. We were in Seattle for the weekend and knew we would be out and about sightseeing the majority of the time so didn't want to spend a lot of money on a hotel we wouldn't really be using very much. We wanted somewhere cheap, in a good location.
The Sixth Avenue Inn fit the bill. It's a basic, no frills place where you get what you pay for. We had a double room on the third floor. Pros: great value, $200 incl tax for 2 nights. Nice, friendly and prompt service. Easy walk to Pike Place market and restaurants/bars etc
Cons: very basic rooms, cheap decor and fittings. Didn't mind this too much because it was expected, given the price. Also though the bedding was horrible. One sheet and a really light, thin scratchy blanket! I was freezing in bed and asked for an extra blanket. The heating in the room warmed the place up pretty well but when they promptly brought me the extra blanket, it was exactly like the one already on the bed! No duvets or comforters here, which I did miss.

Not what I expect from a holiday inn express. Vanity is in the main room which makes the use of it subject to others in the room, this is more of a la qunita type room than what I have seen from the express chain in general. The elevators here are beyond slow and the area in which they are in is a poorly designed congested spot near the pool entrance. The beds were cony but the frames felt like they could come apart at any moment and the four pillows were so used they seemed little more than functioning marshmallows. A convenient location with quiet rooms but with the above listed cons and a almost useless work out room, save your money and go next door to the holiday inn which we felt is in much better shape and a few bucks cheaper.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Seattle City Center

review_title: If you're looking for a great sports trip get a package from Hotel Nexus
review_text: 16 co-workers and I booked a Seahawks group package from the Hotel Nexus. For a very reasonable price we got a nights stay, tickets to the game, 2 free drinks from the restaurant, shuttle service to the stadium, and non stop ice cold fermented beverages on the shuttle and breakfast the next morning. The hotel is close to the north gate shopping centre and theres a starbucks and a mcdonalds across the parking lot. They even gave us a free ride in the shuttle after the game to the micro brew at the mall as the on-site restaurant closed at 10pm. Top notch customer service, everyone was really friendly. The rooms were not anything special, but they were clean and the bed had lots of pillows. While I wouldn't say this is my favourite hotel in Seattle I would stay again particularly for another sporting event package. Well done Nexus!

I've stayed here fairly often over the past 5 years, so I've seen the transformation of the hotel over the years. 
PROS: 
The rooms are clean and comfortable
The breakfast is good
Service from everyone is exemplary
Restaurant next door is superb
Microwave and fridge in the room -- YES!!
Room rates very reasonable for Seattle
Location is great -- just off the exit ramp from I-5, a few miles north of downtown Seattle
Elevator
CONS:
Can be a bit noisy
Don't count on having wi-fi service -- it's spotty at best, and super slow when you manage to connect. A lot of hotels seem to have this problem, so if having wireless access is critical to you, keep this in mind. They REALLY need to work on this. 
This remains one of my favorite places to stay when I have concerts in Seattle. For the money, it's a good deal.

On checkin we were upgraded to a 2 queen suite since I'm a priority club member and the room was available. For our 3 night stay that was very nice for our family of 4. The price is higher than what we usually pay for hotels but seemed comparable to those in the area. With the upgrade it seemed great! 
Breakfast is included and laid out in a manner that makes it fairly easy to obtain. Lots of choices to satisfy every family member. 
Location is only a few blocks away from Seattle Center and the free bus ride zone. Front desk was very helpful to us in figuring out busses to take to and from Qwest Field.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Seattle City Center

review_text: I don't give 5s unless things were exceptional... That said, this was nice place, centrally located. All of the staff was helpful and efficient. Breakfast was good and plentiful.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Seattle City Center

review_title: Great location if you're a shopper
review_text: The Hilton is located close to many malls and shopping centers. All the stores are conveniently located within walking distance. Staff was very friendly and helpful in providing directions to the various attractions. Rooms are decent, nothing spectacular. Grabbing a taxi from the airport to the hotel is expensive o I would suggest taking the metro or shuttle.
This hotel is great for a stop over. It needs a little updating in the rooms, but the price is right. They also accept pets which is a big plus, and it's super close to the airport.
hotel_name: Red Roof Inn Seattle Airport - SEATAC

review_title: Outstanding staff, friendly, calm and delightful. Very highly recommended. Will be missed when gone.
review_text: I am an individual who chose this facility for my lengthy stay without any prior knowledge, knowing that I would be able to move to any number of highly recommended places at any time. I chose not tonfor a number of reasons. I was amazed bynthe quality of the staff at all levels. They were consisitently kind and professional, and for my specific need, compassionate. And although I tried to minimize my requests, the few that I had were met with concern, ambition and dedication. I got to know my new friends on a personal basis and there are far too many to mention here. Many staff went above and beyond in meeting my needs. Now for the location, the only word being ideal for so many things. Surrounding neighborhoods are safe and surprisingly artistic. Daily Walks, or in my case wheeling in a wheelchair, were very enjoyable. People need to be aware that while the shuttle is there for your convenience, it is also important to know that the drivers have cruise ship obligations amongst others, so it is necessary to always be prepared to take a cab. They can almost always accommodate you with at least a days notice. Rooms were exceptionally comfortable and if anything was lacking, it was only a friendly phone call away. I would have preferred an ice machine on every floor, but this was only because I was unable to use the stairs and had to wait for a sometimes busy elevator. Overall I would highly recommend this hotel for the exceptional staff...all of whom should be commended, maybe in the form of a raise :). Highly recommended!

review_title: I'm getting too old to stay in such places
review_text: Photos on web (incl. TA) make it look a lot nicer than it is really. A big block warehouse of rooms has the feel of college dorm rooms that need work. Very friendly staff. Just okay for one night on a quick trip in and out of town, but I'm unlikely to return. I used miles and the old adage applies: you get what you pay for.

Location is excellent. Very close to everything. Problem is that it is an older hotel refurbished superficially. Carpet was put on rotting, humid hardwood floors and it smells awful. 
Beds were comfortable, but cleanliness of the bathroom was just average. 
You pay for the location. 
Free wireless internet is nice and all staff i interacted with were very helpful and nice.

review_title: Affordable hotel in seattle city centre, but awful experience with staff
review_text:
So, let's start from the pros:
This is place is in a good position, has a parking on the next door building (you have to pay extra, of course) and is below the average cost for a hotel in the city centre of Seattle.
Let's go to the cons:
Elevator was working intermittently, it happened that we sometimes had to wait for 20 min before we could use it, and once we used the stairs instead (bear in mind that we were on 7th floor). All the other guests had same problems, and complained with staff at the reception, but no one ever bothered neither sympathized about the situation. They were undergoing major repairs on the elevator, and they clearly should not have kept the hotel open meanwhile, especially considering the number of storeys.
Going to the rooms: our was small, not so clean, and the bathroom was microscopic, too. We could barely fit our suitcases on the floor. We could hear noise coming both from the corridor, and from the neighboring room, which was pretty annoying especially late at night.
It is true that we did not spend much on this stay, but next time I would rather pay 100$/night more rather than staying at this place again.

review_title: Some of the nicest service I have had!
