review_text: The hotel is a short walk from the link light rail (word of warning - the map makes it look flat ... You are in for a steep climb!) which makes it great coming from the airport. The service was great - from checking thru to checking out - I honestly have not had such welcoming people at hotels. The room is small so don't expect too much from that. Would definitely be coming back here

review_title: You could see the Space Needle and the next hotel's occupants...
review_text: Stayed here since it had a special hospital rate. Not sure how that is calculated but we didn't get the same rate, but still an okay value. They offered a free shuttle to hospital but anywhere else was about 10-15 bucks for a few blocks or to go to a Mariners game or to one of the popular piers. Located down town and just a few blocks from the Space Needle. A few more blocks to major attractions downtown. The ladies that checked us into the hotel were friendly and gave some good information about hotel and it's resources. The morning managers on the other hand were, not quite rude, but frustrating in trying to get them to give information such as shuttle times, wake up calls and checking out. The room is super small. The dresser drawers couldn't open all the way because the queen bed was occupying the same space. Found a random earring on the dresser. Uses deodorizers so if you're sensitive to extra fragrances it might be difficult but otherwise it was pleasant and not overly perfumey. Overall a fair price for an okay room in a great location I'd stay here again because of price and hotel/ hospital shuttle but am willing to spend a bit more for next time.

We stayed for 5 nights. We were on the 14th floor the first night with absolutely no view. We moved to the 15th floor the next day and the view was better
Bathroom is very small. The staff were not friendly. For the rate we paid, we were expecting better service than this. When we asked about free Internet and breakfast and etc...we were told rudely that we are not elite guests but they never told us how and explaint it to us. We felt that they only care about the elite guests
It's a great location but so are many other hotels around it. I won't stay here again

review_title: Comfortable hotel in a central location.
review_text: I stayed at the Sixth Avenue in for one night before a cruise. All the staff were so friendly--the registration desk, cleaning staff, and restaurant. The hotel was much quieter then I expected, given the age of the building and the fact that there were a couple large groups that night. And the bed was so comfortable!

Handy location and walkable to pikes peak Market, monorail for space needle. Hotel is 40 years old and rooms need upgrading. Air con unit in our room was very original and was so loud that we couldn't have it on at night, the toilet flush was broken and the shower control was missing parts. That combined with a very small bathroom and generally small room, made the price seem not good value.
The staff (front desk, bell boy, concierge) were all excellent- friendly and helpful.

Because there wasso much to see and do in Seattle, this place really was just a great place to park our car. Convenient to Pike's Place and restaurants, this hotel is a little expensive to use only for sleeping!
The staff was friendly and helpful and the room was clean, if tiny! McDonald's is right next door for a quick breakfast.

This hotel is pretty low priced but be prepared for a couple of things. Firstly the staff are kind of strange. The first was so desperate for conversation she wouldn't let me go to my room, the second tried to convert me to their own political ideology and would direct me to the nearest Starbucks as they were too corporate. The third wouldn't even raise their head to even acknowledge my existence. That coupled with the ancient decor and general dark feel of a prison with brown flaky walls made for a very interesting stay. Not horrible but I wont be going back.
hotel_name: Travelodge Seattle by the Space Needle

review_text: Located 2 blocks from space needle. This area is not central downtown so whilst it is probably quieter there's not much going on a felt a bit creepy - maybe just the time of year? Easy access to main downtown by monorail though which was good. Breakfast more than adequate. We didn't park so can't comment on that. Like all motels Walls a bit thin. If you need this area can recommend otherwise next find we would probably pay a bit more to be downtown
hotel_name: Travelodge Seattle by the Space Needle

review_title: Great location view and room with a view.
review_text: We stayed here due to a few reasons. The great deal we received through Clipper Vacations and for the location. We paid a bit extra for a better room because I like a nice view. The beds were amazing and we were close to shopping. Having to go to the lobby for wi-fi was annoying. For the room cost it should have been free. Busy hotel but the lobby is nice and big to accommodate everyone so you don't feel crowded. Fast elevators and friendly staff. We will be back.

review_title: Fine location and great pricing for seattle
review_text:
Stayed here for a few nights. Thelocation is handy to public transit. It's quite handy to explore Seattle by foot. It is much less pricey than the nearby more upscale hotels. The rooms are a little dingy and dated. I felt it was still worth staying here As opposed to the more pricey choices. 
Concierge was fine. Toiletries are fine. Lines are nice.

review_title: A very nice central place to stay
review_text:
Basically a nice place to stay
Love the double shower heads
The beds are hard but the pillows were nice ;-) 
I'd say they are slightly overpriced. I've stayed in much nicer places for the price. But overall it is the perfect location and it's clean and the rooms are spacious. No major complaints. be prepared to pay $25+ for parking!

review_title: We didn't even bother to unpack!!!
review_text: Upon arrival the first thing we noticed was the smell & the filthy carpets & this was in the lobby ! The room was minuscule with 2 beds squeezed into a space only big enough for one . My wife was horrified at the condition of this supposedly 3.5 * star accommodation . I wouldn't let my dog sleep in this dump . We felt it was neccessary to wipe our feet on the way out of the door . There is a lovely view of the local power station on the corner . You will need a pack mule to get to civilization ! Don't bother staying here uless you like wallowing in filth in 3rd rate accommodation .
hotel_name: Travelodge Seattle by the Space Needle

review_text: But the hotel is just ok. Rooms just ok. If it wasn't for the location...

review_title: Perfect location and very friendly staff
review_text: I agonized where to stay in Seattle. I usually don't stay in this nice a hotel, but I said, why not? I could not have been more pleased. The room was great with a nice view, large couch an a really big picture window'. Best of all was the location. The monorail to the Space Needle was right outside the door. Downhill stroll of 10 minutes to Pike's Market. Bus stops everywhere. The concierges were fantastic and seemed to remember where we had been and asked how it went. For a quick breakfast, McDonalds out the back door as was a great food court which had fantastic Thai food. It was a wonderful experience and I would stay there again.
From the moment I checked in to the moment I checked out, this was a great hotel with great customer service. Bathroom is a little small but I enjoyed my stay there and would choose it again.

review_title: Faded gem, in need of refurbishing
review_text:
This "classic" property was likely once a happening spot located right in the center of Seattle. Alas, it's small European hotel-sized rooms are showing their age. Despite a few modern conveniences like rain shower heads and older model flat screen TVs the rooms feel tired and worn. The bathroom in my room, 804, was tiny with a sink the same size as an airplane bathroom and the toliet is so close to the wall it is almost unusable.
We paid $200 which is a bit much given the age of the place and size of the room.
On the positive side the girl at the front desk was happy and helpful as was the doorman.

review_title: Great hotel very close to the airport and car rental
review_text: A good value hotel near the airport and car rental though parking isn't cheap. Staff are helpful. And also they give away good cookies to hotel guests.

Very close to Seatac, we were tempted to walk there from the airport. In fact, the free shuttle probably spends more time driving back to the hotel than it would probably take to just walk back across the street. 
The hotel is clearly old but Hilton has gone to some lengths to make it feel more up-to-date. It's obviously clean, although the further you get into the maze of halls the more the funky smell of "old" permeates the air. 
We utilized the free airport shuttle, which is handy, but did not use any other hotel service. 
The room was fairly quiet when other guests weren't talking in the hall. The bed was quite comfortable and free of bed bugs. 
The neighborhood has mostly fast-food or 'greasy-spoon' joints except for a nice looking Thai restaurant across the street. 
We would certainly use this hotel again as our layover sleeping arrangement on our way to and from vacations.

review_title: Decent, if you can get it cheap.
review_text:
We go to Seattle often, but this is our first time staying at this hotel. We got a deal through expedia that made it less than half price, so we thought we'd try it out. 
The deal made it worthwhile, but I don't think I'd stay here for full freight. The recommendations on here that decry the small rooms, smaller bathrooms, paper thin walls and slow elevators are accurate. The service was good though, very friendly. 
If you can get it cheap it is an ok place to stay. Don't stay here if you expect $225/night quality.

Not sure why so many people like this place. I was very disapointed, maybe that's because I'm used to the great service and great rooms at the Hotel 1000. Tried The W for wife's bday to find my room dirty (holiday Inn cleans their rooms better). The customer service was horrible. The front desk person was like a robott or on something. Kept asking me how I was doing

Biggest problem: my room smells. In fact, the room, the fridge, the hallway outside the room, and the elevator all smell bad and each in different ways. There was also a wet spot on my carpet, a stain on my duvet, and the bathroom light switches are grotty. I know different people have different standards, so for reference, in the past twelve months I've had 30 different hotel stays around the country, and this is the first hotel that seemed gross to me. This would be unacceptable at any price, and at this price it's an outrage. I tried to move, but everything is booked up for a conference.

Great centrale location, in middle of everything, great staff absolutely friendly and helping, a good 3 stars hotel. But room are hobbits-style, they r nice but very very small, first of all bathrooms. The worst? Breakfast. It's in close cafÃ¨: u receive a single pastry and a drink, just enough to go to have breakfast... elsewhere

review_title: Nice hotel, great beds, mixed staff.
review_text:
We checked in late Saturday of Labor Day weekend. We booked a very specific room type (king with pullout mattress), and my wife checked in very quickly. We got to the room, and discovered that we were placed in two queen doubles. Room was very high up with a nice view, but it wasn't going to work with the combination of young kids and two adults also traveling with us. My sister in law went down to front desk to see if we could get the situation resolved, but she was informed that the room type was not available that night. We were given vouchers for the breakfast joint in the lobby, and offered a crib. This still wasn't going to work, so I went down, explained that I had booked through corporate, and that we should be able to get the room type we booked. I offered to return the vouchers, and asked them to resolve. Within a couple of minutes I got the room I wanted (much lower floor, still a very nice view), and they let me keep the vouchers. Three different front desk reps, but eventually resolved. Housekeeping was exceptionally friendly, although we never got the towels we asked for on the second day. The concierge was helpful in getting a van to the airport on incredibly short order, although it was apparent she was frustrated with this last minute request. To compound the issue, my two very young children were having a break down in their very nice lobby, adding to nerves for us and the staff. However, once the van order came through, the concierge became much more relaxed, and even got got my kids a little snack to keep them calm. Outside of some of the frustrated looks I got from front desk and at first the concierge, every request was met without too much strife. I don't have too much travel experience with young children at nice hotels, but it seems this hotel is better catered to families with slightly older children and young professional travelers/couples. I can't help but shake the feeling that the reason we were changed in room type is because the room we booked was attached to another room (for closed 2 room suite upgrades). I've worked hospitality for 5 years in the past, so I know how these things go, but when you book corporate you should always make sure those room types are matched to a "T". Club members, then corporate, then walk-ins, then saver sites (Travelocity, Hotels.com, etc). Still can't complain too much since I got the room anyways.
The beds were very nice and incredibly comfortable. I sleep on a Temperpedic at home, and this plush spring mattress easily matched the comfort level we expect. Very nice sheets, heavy blankets, and soft pillows (I think the king had easily 9 or 10 pillows). Turn down service on the pullout sofa was prompt, and the room was properly stocked with toilettes and coffee. Floor was very clean, and the bathroom was spotless. The only niggle I had was that the widescreen TV only got standard definition signal on the cable channels and on demand. We would have purchased content, but it looked incredibly poor, so we decided against it. Ice machine was down the hall, nice tasting ice, and you beverages heard it from the room.
The hotel is slightly older (I'd say 30 years) but everything has been renovated. Quick elevators, clean hallways. The gym was nice and modern (although a little cramped) but the heated indoor swimming pool was great! Lots of towels out for guests, and a nice jacuzzi for the adults. 
The hotel is situated nicely in downtown, a short 15 minute walk from Pike Place. It's right next to the tram if you want to ride to the Space Needle. We walked there instead, took about half an hour.
There is a inexpensive drug store across the street, countless coffee shops, indoor malls, and a ton of awesome dive bars a short walk away.
I would highly recommend this hotel and will use it again should I come back to Seattle again. It's my second Westin chain experience, and now my second time for enjoying a Westin hotel.

review_title: Fine for couples unless you are overweight.
review_text: The bathroom is quite unique, i.e., the shower stall has a large slab of marble as most of one wall, the toilet is auto-flush, and the door is smoked glass. That said, while we were quite comfortable, for more than two people there would simply not be enough room, two could not be in the bathroom at once, and large people simply would not fit. This is a nice, boutique hotel in a great downtown location, close to everything, not to mention buses that go everywhere (downtown is quite parking-challenged )and light rail between the airport and hotel. Hotel staff were very knowledgeable and friendly.

Stayed here 2 nights. Good size room with large TV and sitting room area. Nicely presented rooms. We had a king size bed and slept soundly. Breakfast buffet has a good selection of fresh foods. Staff are very friendly. Hotel has laundry facilities, pool and fitness centre. Good location. Quiet area

review_title: Westin is a good hotel, but during windy weather the walls can make load squeeky noises which disrupt sleep.
review_text: The hotel (overall) is nice, it has large rooms, the staff service is good, *but* during windy weather the walls/floors make load squeeky noises, which were enough to disrupt my sleep, with the need to use earplugs. The week I stayed (for business) this happened a number of nights. I stayed on the 17th floor in the north tower, facing the space needle. My co-worker reported the same noises on the 23rd floor.
Our room was very nice and clean and had a great view. The hotel staff even provided us with a vase so that my husband could get me flowers from the nearby markets. We love the heavenly beds.

review_title: Wonderful and in the midst of everything
review_text: From shopping to dining the Westin puts you right where you need to be. The hotel is very nice, and the beds as comfy as they come.

review_title: Wonderful Hotel close to Boeing Field
review_text: I enjoyed my stay at this Hotel very much! The Staff was fanastic, the room spotless and very comfortable. The bed was great...I slept like a baby! Thanks to ANTHONY at the front desk for being so gracious! I am returning to this Hotel again later this week. I highly recommend the Georgetown Inn!!!

Not too far from downtown Seattle, great place to stay over night. Showers were hot and the water pressure was reall high. Check out by 11 and head back to Seattle for our weekend trip. I would definitely stay here again.

review_title: If you need to stay around Boeing field, this is it.
review_text: If you need to stay around boeing Field in Seattle you could do a lot worse. This Inn provides a continental breakfast and is located in the Georgetown area of Seattle.Ll rooms are second floor or above with the lobby on the main floor. I stayed on the third floor and the wifi was week but present. Not a lot of restaurants in the area so plan on driving. There is a Shell station across the street were you can by beer, fried chicken or the occasional jojo. The room was clean but dated. There was a refrigerator in the room. The room had a nice tv and was well lit. If I needed to be located in this area again I would stay here again. Thanks for reading.

review_title: Got what I paid for. I stayed for free, but wish I had paid for somewhere better.
review_text:
I got a room here with my mother while she wound up staying at the nearby VA hospital for a last minute emergency. They set us up here because of the shuttle service that goes to and from the hospital.
Pros: the rooms were clean, and through my mother's coverage, the stay was free. That's about it. 
Cons: there is literally nothing of interest and nowhere to go nearby. Not even a simple supermarket.
There's a couple of restaurants across the street that had decent food and prices, and a gas station with the usual ridiculously overpriced groceries. However, a lot of rowdy people loitered in its parking lot at all hours of the night, and shouted a lot. I wouldn't recommend wandering around at night, as the neighborhood looks a bit unsafe. There was also a starbucks. From what I gather, there's ALWAYS a starbucks nearby in this city.
Technically they have wifi, but their signal strength is so weak you have to go down to the lobby to guarantee you won't get cut off unexpectedly. The rooms however are all upstairs.
I informed the man at the desk, and he just said "yeah. I guess it's kinda weak. Depends on the device". Well it wasn't just my device, cause I heard him say the same thing to several other guests that I heard complain while I was in the lobby trying to get a signal.
Also, there were several large and nasty looking spiders I had to squish, in our room , the lobby, and the laundry room. Gross. 
In the long run I guess I can't complain much, since I didn't pay a dime, but after staying a few days, I kind of wish I had splurged on something nicer.
If I WERE paying, I certainly wouldn't pay to stay here again.

Stayed at the Westin Seattle for a business trip. The hotel is nice- room was great with an amazing view. The hotel is centrally located and just a quick walk to the public market. 
I would be happy to stay here again!

review_title: Parking in the alley and borrow WIFI from Courtyard Marriott
review_text:
We love the one bedroom suite. It is spacious and clean. The swimming pool is open 24 hours and we can swim late. The complimentary breakfast is great, although I can foresee problems when there are more people. 
We park on the side street which divides this hotel from the previous one. So we did not pay $10 a night. There are about 10 spots available. We also borrow Wifi on the side closest to Marriott's free wireless, which are at the swimming pool and the business centre.
We will visit again!
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Seattle - Tacoma International Airport

review_text:
My first complaint may not bother everyone. I like my room to get very cold. I'm an insomniac, and cannot sleep at all in a hot room with no air movement. The windows open about 4" on either side, but the drapes cover up that area of the window, so I'm unsure why they open at all.
My next complaint I'm sure would bother anyone. After checking out I discovered a used plate, fork and knife had been thrown on the hood of my car, along with other garbage. One of the reasons I choose to stay in an expensive hotel is that I believe my car will be safer there. Next time I'm in the area I'll be staying at cheap hotel with an actual functioning air conditioner and know that my car is just as safe there as at the Seatac Embassy Suites.
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Seattle - Tacoma International Airport

review_title: very nice housekeepers rude front desk nice drivers
review_text: They do clean every inch of the rooms but some old lady with short blond hair was been rude to here workers nd she was whistling loud and yapping on the phone opening doors with ppl inside Front desk is careless would expect them to be enthusiastic and cheerful bu just dnt care about customers theres one with black hair shes rude and taking her time reading instead the short one speaks little english and theres one with acne all over her face she checked me in a dirty room the housekeepers are great i was on the 6 th floor smoking room and my housekeeper was so helpful and had very good manners and she even said "have a safe flight" when i was walking out over all i would stay here only if i had no were else to go

review_title: Nice choice for the SEATAC area
review_text: After staying at the Best Western across the street for one night, we opted to look for nicer lodging. My wife got an excellent rate here so we gave it a try. The location is great for getting to and from the airport and is also very near shopping and several dining choices. The hotel is also about 12 minutes away from downtown Seattle. The rooms are clean and roomy, the staff seemed very nice and helpful. The business center was very convenient as I needed to print some tickets for a ball game. The breakfast is very good as well. The only negatives I can find are they charge for wi-fi and there is quite a bit of train traffic behind the hotel, so if you have a room on the back of the building ( like we did) there is some noise from the trains. And really, $10 for wi-fi, Boooo! We stayed in cheaper hotels that provide it for free.
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Seattle - Tacoma International Airport

review_title: Great hotel...10 min walk to the Space Needle.
review_text:
We got this hotel using Hotwire...great deal! 
It looks a bit older from the outside, but the inside is newly renovated and very clean. The desk staff was very friendly, and we were given a little bag with a bottle of water and microwave popcorn on arrival. 
Our room was new and had a fridge, microwave and flat screen tv. They also provided a few disposable plates/cutlery for the microwave...fantastic idea! 
We asked for a few extra towels as we had our two little girls with us...they were delivered to our room right away :)
We walked to the Space Needle and it took about 10 minutes. The hotel is on the other side of Aurora Ave (very busy road!) I wish the hotel was on the same side as the Space Needle, but oh well!
I've been to Seattle many times and have paid $200+ per night to stay at places like the Edgewater and the Monaco. I must say that this hotel is a FAR BETTER deal! 
We will definitely be back to the Holiday Inn on Dexter! Thanks!!

Our travel agent put us up here before our cruise. The hotel was beautiful and best part walking distance to all the touristy things. We had a great view - especially the Space Needle at night. I'd stay here again

I had such great customer service, from the front desk to the bell hop and especially the information desk! We were given great suggestions on what to do, what buses to take that were free, places to eat (she even made reservations for us). The rooms were very clean, the beds were comfortable, and I loved hanging out in the lobby (for the free wifi) and at the bar.
It was about an easy 10 minute walk to the convention center each morning. 
I would stay here again in a heartbeat.

review_title: Good for a short term stay
review_text: A bit of a walk to Pike Street Markets. Not many restaurants within walking distance. If you have a car it is easy to get around. I'd recommend for couples or the busy traveller.

We stayed there for 3 days (2 rooms). Both rooms were not cleaned at all for 1 day, after complaining they apologized and offered fresh towels! When we arrived we couldnt park on the curb for check in because the manager told us big buses would be arriving and we had to make space for them, the entrance was being painted so we couldnt park there either so we had to find a spot down the street. On our last day although you have to pay for parking, it was full, after asking where we could park we were told rudely to find a spot on the street, but there was no spot on the street, so we asked if we could park in the check in zone and were told we would be ticketed if we did. After getting a bit upset the person in charge offered graciously to take the charge for the parking off our bill as a solution, but we still had no parking space, after back and forth he wrote us a note so we could use the parking space of a parking lot 2 blocks away.... This would all not have been a big issue if the staff would have been friendlier but they were short in responses and acting like nothing was their problem. Too bad the service was like this, the hotel is nice and the location great but I would never stay there again! The emerald grill whish is beside the hotel and offers breakfast, lunch and dinner is great! The staff there was the opposite of the hotel staff! Food was good and people superfriendly!

Just returning from a quick road trip that took our family through Seattle. We spent one night at the Seattle downtown Westin. This hotel is in a great location within walking distance to many restaurants and shops. The room was clean and the beds are really comfortable. Downside is the cost to park at the hotel, but that's pretty much unavoidable in any big city and Internet is not free.

review_title: Not as nice as I expected
review_text: Very disappointed in the Internet, not even free in the lobby. Luckily, I had a room overlooking the Courtyard Marriott next door, who offer free Internet and have very good signal strength! The rooms themselves were awesome. Big and comfortable, great bed. Housekeeping did a great job. Prefer the breakfast buffet over the Embassy's line up, but it is a good trade off to get the cook to order eggs.
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Seattle - Tacoma International Airport

review_text:
Alaska airlines put me up in this hotel after a delay caused me to miss my connection in Seattle. The room was basic, but clean, felt like I was transported back to the 80's with the decor (even the lamps were glued to the nighstand). The night staff was courteous and helpful, check in was quick and she pointed out walkable restaurants. But, after going to bed at 7am, I was rudely awoken by very loud
DRILLING in the room next door at 10:45! Check out is not until noon! After calling the front desk she replied "you are checking out today anyways" so rude and not helpful! And the drilling continued!!! I would not recommend this hotel at
 all to anyone due to the rudeness of the morning front desk. Airline comp or no comp!!!

Attentive desk staff and we got a bigish room well appointed. Location is a short (maybe 15 mins) to city centre. Avoid Denny park unless you like mixing it with homeless beggars. Restaurant adjacent to hotel is handy and we thought prices were ok.

one the 4th floor facing the runway right next to the elevator . Very quiet. Firma beds and very clean. I was expecting mucho worse but nice place. Good breakfast. Gets crowded though. Front desk not very attentive . Parking good. very close to main terminal entrance . It got it for 80 .00 on priceline which was high.If you get it for less go for it.

review_title: Worst place I have ever stayed
review_text: Booked Executive Room TV did not work,no remote,Safe not working movies for the coffee room not as good as some basic rooms that I have stayed in. Booked in for 10nights and moved after one night nag going elsewhere my wife is withe and concurs with this view

We booked this for 4 nights while travelling in Seattle & British Columbia. We are a family of 4 & wanted somewhere we could make a sandwich & have breakfast so chose this with a kitchenette.There was a fridge & microwave & 4 plastic plates & no cutlery. 
It was very noisy from road traffic but on our last night a coach stopped outside our room around 4 am. It woke us with it's reversing hooters & kept it's engine running. After 30 minutes I contacted reception who told me they were sorting out. It did turn it's engine off after about another 20 mins but the noise from it continued ( ? The air con) until after we got up.
Really good cafe - restaurant great time speaking with the head Chef
Good location...horrible service, overcrowded, overpriced...would never comd back!

review_title: Good hotel but not up to par with other Westin locations!
review_text:
Although we got a great rate ($129) through Priceline for a last minute room on a Saturday night in June, I would never pay the average full price for rooms here (about $229 a night). The bathrooms leave something to be desired--something I judge a room by strongly. 
Room 1155 is right by the elevators which ding each time they stop at the floor. Understandably we were probably put in a "value" room since we booked through Priceline but I expected more from the Westin brand of hotels. 
The room also had an odd odor to it. 
The views are probably pretty fabulous the higher up you go and the room layout makes it so the beds face outward- a big plus at nighttime. Our tower had 44 floors, we were on the 11th. 
The room and hotel itself was good but I was surprised there wasn't more luxury to the rooms here.

We just stayed at the Westin Hotel and loved it. Good central location close to the shops. Free WiFi in foyer. We had a beautiful room over looking the Space Needle. The beds are heaven wanted to take it home with me!

Booked direct with hotel. Prepaid for rooms and stood on two seperate occasions. First time they overbooked and sent our family of seven,3 children,2 seniors,2adults to another hotel at 2 in the morning. It was a partying hotel with vomit in the elevators and lots of drunks everywhere. Very scary for children and old seniors. Next stay, checked in at 5 and our rooms were not ready till after 10 that night waited around with the kids and grandparents . Requested two doubles in each of the two rooms
did not get it. 7 of us, figure that.
.
.

review_title: Great hotel if ordered on Hotwire.
review_text: The hotel is great, and since Seattle is spread all over the place, the location is right off the highway. Expensive if you order online unless you do it through Hotwire. Cost me $85 instead of over $225 through Westin.

Location is very very good. Traffic noise not too too bad. No hot water 2 mornings out of 3. Kept saying boiler was not working. They did compensate with $ off our bill. However... their "blackout curtains" are nothing of the sort. They are way too short. At 6:30 am the room lights up like the Vegas Strip. But the hotel is one of the nicer looking Holiday Inns. Location is reallly nice. Hope they can fix the details like the curtains and hot water issues.

review_title: Everything you need with great service
review_text:
The room was clean and the beds comfy. The service was also very friendly and everyone was keen to help us. Being right next to the space needle, it's a brilliant location and very easy to find your way back to. It takes 5 - 10mins to get yourself on foot to the area around pike place market and the first Starbucks so that's great. I would say it's definitely worth staying here rather than a much more pricey place which is actually only 5mins from this hotel anyway.
The only down point was that I kept having to re-enter the wireless password on my phone so that was a bit annoying. Refreshing to have free wireless, though, so I can't complain too much.

review_title: Nice accommodations just steps from the airport
review_text:
The Radisson is definitely within walking distance from Seatac if you don't have much luggage. No need to wait on the free shuttle. 
The hotel is very clean and the lobby is quite large and very nice. We enjoyed time there.
The rooms are a very good size and comfortable. Amenities are pretty standard, and wireless Internet is free.
The front desk staff is quite nice, however they seemed to have a limited knowledge of the area. We discovered a number of restaurants within walking distance of the hotel (take a left out of the lobby for a Denny's, Jack in the Box, Taco Bell, Roaster's Ale House, and a very good Thai restaurant), yet the front desk staff knew of just two of them.
There is a complimentary shuttle, but it only takes you to the airport or to the light rail station. The hotel is 40 minutes from downtown on the rail.
Negatives: (1) The breakfast buffet looked quite good, but it is $13 per person so we walked to Denny's. (2) The Sleep Number Beds in the rooms are hard to work with and I thought they were horribly uncomfortable.
Overall, this hotel is very convenient to the interstate and the airport. The staff is friendly but not too knowledgeable. The rooms are clean and large, but the beds are not comfortable. Ultimately, we enjoyed our stay here.

review_title: Uncomfortable beds, otherwise ok. Nothing exceptional here.
review_text:
My company books us here when we overnight in Seattle. It's an easy walk to and from Seatac Airport and is surprisingly quiet considering it's location. The staff are pleasant enough, the rooms are clean, but the beds are not so good. They are the adjustable air filled mattress with two controllers to adjust firmness. I do not recall the brand, but you are supposed to be able to adjust each side of the bed independently from the other. Often the controllers do not work and it is very difficult to get a comfortable night's sleep. 
The rooms we stay in are always clean and are quite large and have a great layout. There is no fridge in the room, but the staff is quick to bring one up on your request.....unless they don't have any left if you arrive late in the evening as we usually do.
I can't comment on the cost because my company pays for the room and I do not see the bill.
I would not stay there if I was traveling for leisure, simply because I know there are rooms of comparable quality, but with more comfortable beds in other hotels nearby.

We walked to Pike's Marketplace. Restaurants are close by. Visited an awesome Nordstrom and the REI "mothership". The hotel was busy due to cruise ship traffic which changes the dynamic of the Marketplace too. 
Lots to do.

Very nice staff, nice workout area, great location. Wifi needs to be adjusted as I had to log in too often... The error should be keeping us on too long not cutting us off. But nice hotel in great location

review_title: Great place to stay if looking for a cheap weekend in Seattle.
review_text: If you're looking for a romantic weekend getaway...not the place. If you are looking for somewhere central and simple while visiting Seattle - it's perfect! I stayed here with friends for the New Years and found it clean, friendly, and a good value. There aren't a lot of amenities, but honestly of you're in Seattle you want to explore - not spend your days in the hotel room. This place reminded me the hotels you find in many European cities.I would recommended this place for friends looking to explore Seattle an young couples looking to get away without spending a lot. Best thing about this place...location, location, location. Plus, near a Link station so it ha easy access to the Airport.

After checking many travel sites I went online directly to this hotel. They had a special deal that was very hard to believe. I kept waiting for them to add hidden charges. It never happened! Every staff member we met was very friendly. The location was very good for walking around downtown. The room was small, but clean and well appointed. I could not think of anything that is lacking. We'll definitely return.

Delightful hotel in Queen Anne neighborhood. Close to restaurants, shops, public transportation and two blocks from Seattle Center. Clean, efficiently designed rooms and excellent staff. Microwave and refrigerator in room and Starbucks shop off lobby. Around the corner from supermarket and two blocks from 24hour drug store and supermarket. Parking garage on site-$15 per day- is very tight.

review_title: Value for ocation and staff can't be beat in all of Seattle.
review_text:
Just a short block or two from light rail station or your bus stop, leave your car at home when staying at this modest and terifically-priced hotel. Want to swim? The downtown ymca is a block away. Need a rare document? The seattle public library's behemoth main branch is directly across the street.
And the staff -- from front desk to bell captain to housekeeping -- go well above the call of duty. We accidentally left stuff in our hotel safe--including a passport needed in 2 weeks' time--and front desk employees FedExed it to us when we called and made arrangements, then housekeeping's Roberto followed up on it to make sure. The bell staff knows all there is to know about where to catch what bus line or train to wherever you need to go. What a terrific weekend they made it for us! And the price of the room left us money to splurge on other things, such as several of the nearby topnotch restaurants.

review_title: Are we at the right place?
review_text:
Hi Everyone, I hate writing bad reviews! But I have to share our experience at El Goucho. Imagine this, I am 6 months pregnant and thinking this may be one of the last shopping trips to the states from Vancouver, BC for awhile. We thought we would get all the baby clothes we needed for our soon to be arriving daughter. The sales were great! I highly recommend shopping in the US for kiddie clothes! 
My partner (who prefers the title husband :)), was driving and I was navigating. I was like 'oh no, this may be an adventure' when I first saw El Gaucho. It doesn't quite look like a hotel. We pulled up, no one was around to valet our car or greet us. That meant no help with our bags too. And no elevator! So a rather steep flight of stairs (not particularly great for pregnant bodies)! 
My partner made the several trips up and down. We got upstairs to a dimly lit reception area. The actual reception desk was off to the side so again could not see anyone but heard someone having a full on phone conversation about her previous evening and things like 'I can't believe what he said...' etc. Not the best welcome. Finally upstairs, we waited for her to notice us but didn't so we started talking to each other, she clued in and got off the phone. No apology. I asked if someone could valet our car. 'the person who does that doesn't start work until 6 pm so you have to do it on your own'. No apology. We got into our dimly lit room by way of a very dimly lit hallway. It was 4 pm and it felt like it was in the middle of the night. The colours were weird and I could see some sense of retro chic wannabe style going on but it was under done. The room was fine. Nothing to write to anyone about! The best thing was the bed. The lighting again was dim. The bathroom was tiny. The air conditioning too loud. We decided to change and head put for the evening. We came back to a more receptive front desk clerk but the ambience never got better. We stayed 2 nights and never saw another guest until we were checking out. One day, our key stopped working and we had lugged all of our shopping up the stairs and were exhausted! I left my partner with the bags and reported the issue to the front desk clerk, he said to try again after putting it through the machine. It didn't work again. I headed back again and he came to check it out this time. The front desk is on the same floor as the rooms. Given the lack of activity, it would have been nice to have him deal with it the first time, especially since he said this happens from time to time. On our departure, there were 2 clerks, our car was retrieved, and we were sent off with smiles and pleasant thank yous. I don't think either of us would opt to stay here again. It was fine, easy to get to Nordatrom Rack in downtown Seattle and places to eat, and also just enjoy downtown Seattle but there are better options. Our baby girl has been out growing her clothes quickly - so it was totally worth the shopping trip! 
The good points: it was clean, the bed was cozy and clean, the walk to the restaurants and shopping was easy. The not so great: the service, the odd ambience and the eery feeling about being the only guests was a bit like checking into a haunted hotel! 
If your stuck with limited options, consider El Goucho but if you have options, go elsewhere! It is nice to be greeted and welcomed, it is nice to have the option of valet, to have help with bags, to have an elevator, to have little touches that indicate that our choice to stay there was valued. 
Have fun in Seattle!

I changed my reservation to this when noticed on Google maps that my car rental Avis was across the street. You will have most departement stores very close by, and the station for the monorail out to the Space Needle (1962 World Exibition Event) is less than a block away. The Swedes have a word for a little hideaway where you may enjoy the best in life; smultronstaelle. The Westin Seattle is like Westin Galleria in Houston; Hasslefree!
I try to hold on to my money, but this was worth every dollar spent.

If you want a hotel right in midtown this is it. Close to Central Park, Times Square, Carnige Hall etc... Nothing too special, overall the room was clean, bed was comfy (no bed bugs). I booked one night for $96. I'd stay again but wouldn't pay over $150 a night.

Booked a Grand View room, 6 months in advance for my sister and I, and was supposed to have had Sweeping Views of Puget Sound and the Space Needle. When I checked in as a Starwood Member, I was told that I was getting upgraded to the Royal Suite. It was written on the card with my keys. We get to our room, which turned out to be NEXT to the Royal Suite. We walked in and we had a king bed and a city view! Went back downstairs to talk the check-in and was told they had NO rooms with that view I was promised available, due to being full capacity! They then got the Hotel Manager and after 2 hours of dealing with this they mysteriously found me a regular room with a view of The Space Needle! But, alas, NO Suite!

I have stated at this hotel a number of times, mainly because I will always know what I am going to get. I have stayed here for business and for pleasure - but have really found that there published prices are a little high for what you get and I have had a lot more luck getting a discounted price off of the several websites that do this. Â I like the fact that this hotel is comfortable which is why I will continue to go back. The heavenly beds are amazing, they are very accommodating to pets. The restaurants in the hotel are only ok, but the location is great and there area lots of places to go close by. The parking is very expensive, but so is life in a big city.

review_title: Great location, nice staff, thin walls. Great Value!!!
review_text: This was s great place to stay downtown can't beat the price, and an amazing staff and location!
Up to 15 minute wait for elevators, screaming baby next door and sub par rooms. Overall was well below expectations.

review_title: Plush extravagance with a breathtaking view
review_text: My husband and I stayed here to celebrate our first anniversary. We had a Grand View Room and a package that included room service breakfast and a 4pm checkout. It exceeded our expectations and was a perfect way to celebrate. The view from our room was spectacular, and it was amazingly comfortable. It was a lovely way to have a gorgeous view of our own city.

Enjoyed staying there on business. Beautiful room but it would be great if they provided bottled water and had the clock next to the bed instead of behind it. Walls are a little thin. The bed was comfy and the room was spacious. the place is mostly very nice and well run. Like the workout center and lobby bar.

We didn't want to pay too much but wanted a good location - and I am very happy with our choice. Yes the walls are thin, and it is an older building, but the bed was awesome, the room was clean and after a very long flight the shower was excellent. 
I guess it is an example of moderating your expectations. I didn't expect a fancy new hotel, so I'm not disappointed. I did expect a good bed and great location - and I'm not disappointed.

Overall had a pleasant stay, true the rooms including bathrooms were small but the overall experience was great! If you like more of a fancier place stay and are willing to pay for it then go somewhere else. The room, location, staff, and service is just what I expected and we were completely satisfied.
Thankfully we didn't have the issue of hearing our neighbors even though the hotel was completely full when we stayed :)

review_title: Don't know why the bad reviews- we found room to be clean and well-appointed.
review_text: Not sure why folks are so down on this place. Our room was very clean, nicely appointed. Yes, the rooms are a bit small, but if you are doing more than sleeping in your hotel room while you visit Seattle, there's something wrong with you. ;) I would recommend this hotel to anyone looking for a reasonably priced hotel, conveniently located.

review_title: Best Hotel in Seattle's Queen Anne
review_text:
This is one of the best hotels I have ever stayed at. It is not the most high-end, but the rooms are clean, the staff goes out of their way to be helpful, and the view from the roof top patio is unbelievable!
There is a Safeway right across the street, and some amazing restaurants down the block. 
Will definitely stay here again!
Hotel was clean, bed was super comfy. Rooftop deck has a beautiful view. Location was a little further from downtown & the harbor than we would have liked. Having a Starbucks in the lobby was great

review_title: Bad from the moment I clicked reserve
review_text: I've stayed a month at SPG hotels in the past year & never have gotten the flat-out crappy service I experienced at the Westin Seattle. I goofed my reservation & when I called to fix within a few hours, I was told they couldn't fix it -- called SPG who got them to. Next day reservation still wrong; more calls, assurances. On arrival, promise of personal service & room in North tower away from elevator turned into South tower directly in front of the elevator. They just don't seem as intent on taking care of loyal customers as every other SPG hotel we've stayed at. Despite ideal location, we won't be back.

My husband and I stayed here for 3 days on our trip to Washington. The hotel was just average. Nothing too special about it. There was a Starbucks in the lobby which was nice. Internet and in room coffee and water was extra. Location was pretty good but we still drove to most of the things we wanted to do.
Good location for the Needle and seafront. Clean and good service. Not a bargain, but good quality for the price.

review_title: Convenient to the major attractions is Seattle.
review_text: Convenient to the major attractions in Seattle. This is an exciting city with the best seafood any where. Atop the space needle is spectacular. Pike place market is a must see. The salmon and oysters are worth the trip. The hotel is beautiful with a great view.
hotel_name: Red Lion Hotel on Fifth Avenue Seattle

review_title: If you want to stay somwhere that in comfy and convenient to main attractions...this is your place
review_text: Me and my son stayed here for our first familt vacation. I didn't want us to be somewhere that would be crawling with drunk kids on spring break and thought Seattle would be a good spot. Yes, my school took our spring break later than others. This hotel was a good price and was located about a couple blocks from the Space Needle. The trip to get to Seattle was long and it was refreshing to have a room that was comfortable and nice. The monorail was awesome and Pikes Place was amazing. When I come back to Seattle w/o my son, because there was definately some places I wanted to go that is not kid friendly, lol, I will definately be staying there. The staff was nice, courteous, and helpful when suggesting where and where NOT to go. Also I met a fellow Louisianaian who works there and he we talked about home, so I didn't feel too out of place there. An added plus was the workout I got trekking up the hills with my son's stroller : )

We stayed here for a sunny weekend in Seattle and found the hotel to be everything we needed. It is on a street with a ton of great restaurants and bars, there is a Starbucks in the lobby for convenient breakfast, and it's easy to get to most of Seattle from here. We parked on the street which was a hassle but cheaper than paying $15 per day at the hotel. Our king room was spacious and clean and the staff were very nice.
Loved the clean rooms, friendly front desk, and location. We walked to the lightrail, three blocks from the hotel to get to the airport.
hotel_name: Red Lion Hotel on Fifth Avenue Seattle

review_text: This hotel is very clean and in a nice area of Seattle with some good restaurants and walking distance to the Space Needle. The staff were friendly. Our room was small but had a fridge and sink and was well worth it
We have found this Red Lion to be a hidden gem in downtown Seattle. It is surrounded by good restaurants and convenient to the 5th Avenue Theater. Good price and nice rooms.
hotel_name: Red Lion Hotel on Fifth Avenue Seattle

review_title: Perfectly placed to get to know Seattle city
review_text: Excellent position for visiting Seattle and very friendly hotel.
hotel_name: Red Lion Hotel on Fifth Avenue Seattle

review_text:
We - family of 3- stayed here a week and were very impressed. 
Complimentary breakfast and dinner. Free WIFI. Very close to Seattle Centre- no more than a 10mins walk; and, a 20mins walk to Pier 66 & 70. This is not a downtown hotel but makes up for far away location with great services.
Staff is courteous and helpful and will book packages for you at hotel discount. 
The suites are incredibly spacious and very clean. Our room was quiet but faced 2nd Ave. and not Western Ave. which is a major road. 
We booked online and got a very good rate. 
Zipcars are just around the corner also. Parking is availabe if you drive. Grocery store is a 5mins walk away. Laundry room onsite.

Our family of our stayed at the Homewood Suites in Seattle during the last week of August as part of a 10 day to Washington State.
We stayed in a one bedroom suite with king bed and a sofa bed, with a partial bay view...room was very clean and comfortable with room to spread out.
Location was great, near all the attractions, mins to the State Ferries and SAFECO Field.
Parking was secure under the hotel for $15 a day. Hot breakfast saved us a good deal of money and it was good quality. Fridge in the room was also a money saver for Cokes and snacks.
Rate was reasonable...we would come back here again!

Free wifi, comfy beds, nice big tv. I really hate the Terrace restaurant inside the hotel, it's food is bland and overpriced. The only hot food I liked in the breakfast buffet was the eggs with tomatoes and green onions. Bad service as well, no one came to our table except for once to ask if we wanted coffee, which we didn't, so they left and never came back. The only reason I even ate their breakfast was because it came with the room. 
I also had a gross experience, when we got there, there was a decorative throw on the end of the bed. Without getting into too much detail, let's just say someone had a really fun time on that bed, I guess after the maid had cleaned the room. Called housekeeping and they promptly came and replaced it and apologized. It was pretty nasty.
That being said, we usually end up staying here, we're a part of their rewards program, and every time we want to come down, they make us an offer we can't refuse.
hotel_name: Red Lion Hotel on Fifth Avenue Seattle

review_title: Great hotel. Stayed several times and would again.
review_text: I love everything about this hotel. Stayed several times. Great location. Nice staff. Big rooms. Great views. Not the cheapest in town and parking is a little pricey, but so central. Clean. Excellent with pets. They give you a doggie bag for your dogs with treats and the pet rooms are very well deep cleaned. Definately staying next time I go. Only rated value as 4 as it's relative. But great staff, cleaners and designers don't come cheap at the end of the day, so not a bargain but reasonable.
hotel_name: Red Lion Hotel on Fifth Avenue Seattle

review_text:
We stayed at the Red Lion pre cruise. We were upgraded to the Family suite it was a huge suite with two rooms, one room had a lounge and chairs and lovely furniture throughout it was good centrally located hotel. Good restaurant downstairs.
We also stayed at the Westin post cruise and loved it too.
Hard choice between the two loved the extra room at Red Lion but loved the bed and views at Westin. Location is perfect for both hotels and short taxi ride to pier.
Can't go wrong with either hotel just go for the best deal.
hotel_name: Red Lion Hotel on Fifth Avenue Seattle

review_text:
