review_title: Light rail system perfect to hotel
review_text: I forgot to add in our last review,and feel very important,that we took the light rail system from Sea-Tac airport for $2.50 a person within a couple easy walking blocks of the Best Western Pioneer Square Hotel. The light rail system was very clean and a pleasant 30 minute ride for $2.50! Took towncar from hotel to cruise terminal for $20. All worked great.
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Pioneer Square Hotel

review_text: My husband and I stayed 3 nights and enjoyed meeting the staff, was offered free umbrellas each day and the breakfast was outstanding! Definitely coming back.
hotel_name: BEST WESTERN PLUS Pioneer Square Hotel

review_text: Friendly staff. Good shuttle service to central Seattle. Good value for money. Norwegian family of 5.

Got a great deal under $100 for the Sheraton. 
The positive: Walk to Pike, Shopping, Convention Center. 
Free wifi in lobby. Room was basic but clean and satisfactory.
Great Coffee just down the street! (Monorail Codfee)
The negative:
Parking is $35!! At a lot a block away! Latte in lobby cafe was the worst I ever had. Lobby feels cold and uninviting. Pool and exercise area overlooking the city on 35th floor.
Overall, a good place if you don't want to drive. No wow factor, but worth the price. I would stay again.
Got great price on Priceline and feel lucky to have landed such a nice place in great location. Parking is expensive (43) but same as municipal lots nearby.

I was so impressed with the Paramount. I have stayed in many of the downtown hotels in Seattle and I have to say that the Paramount is one of the nicest hotels downtown. The hotel is very well kept and modern. The room had a great feel to it and was very good size. The bathroom was amazing. The best part was the bed. Probably one of the most comfortable hotel beds I have ever slept on. If you get the chance to stay at the Paramount don't pass it up. You'll be glad you did.

This is a gorgeous old building, with tons of history. Completely remodeld, the arctic bar was a great place to wind down. Viktor is a great bartender as well as a great host. He takes hos business serious and it shows.

review_text: My wife and I recently spent a night at this hotel. What a great hotel and the location is perfect if you want to be downtown seattle in the heart of things. From the moment you step in you know you are staying at a professionally run hotel. Everything works well and the rooms are great.

review_title: Convenient location. Don't get in a rush to check in though...
review_text: Really nice place. If your not a member of their rewards program though be prepared to be treated like chopped liver.

review_title: Just as Grand as its title!
review_text: I found my experience while staying at the Grand Hyatt Seattle simply pleasant. The check-in process was smooth even after arriving late. I typically don't order room service because of cost and food quality. In this case food quality was not an issue. it was actually good.

I gave it an overall four because of the restaurant. Its really overpriced for food that is just average. I only ate there once, and then went to other restaurants after.
But the rooms are lovely and so is the hotel

Yankees and mariners game was great and the front desk was busy, yet they still changed one of our rooms to a double queen from a king which was great service. Beds are great and the location is wonderful.

review_title: High rate and $40 parking fee per day!!!
review_text: Definitely a business expense hotel. Rooms nicely furnished but not enough plugs convenient for charging. Staff was okay. Expensive food options in hotel. Convenient to pikes market and shopping, but would not be my choice on a return. high room rate plus $40 a day for parking.

review_title: Great for business and leisure travelers
review_text:
Stayed at the wonderful four seasons for 3 nights for work and sightseeing. 
I've stayed at many different four seasons properties across the globe and this one is better than the average four seasons. 
The service is great. The front desk and lobby staff are super friendly and go out of their way to helpful. They made great restaurant recommendations (metropolitan grill was my fav) and assisted us in storing/refrigerating some food we purchased at nearby Pike market. 
The location is great - very close to the famous pike market and acquarium (great for kids). Seattle is a terrific walking city with lots of shopping choices and we found the four seasons to be a great home base to see everything. 
The room was very high quality and modern. Love the in mirror tv. Always appreciate the turn down service with complimentsry bottles of water. The housekeeping staff was invisible yet they always cleaned our room whenever we left the room, which is the way it should be. Had a nice view of the water from our room. Very nice room overall. 
The fitness center has pretty new equipment but not much choice. Nice views of the water from the treadmill. Pool was closed, outside only and pretty small. The spa was pleasant, and massage was good like most other four seasons spas. The locker room was a bit disappointing - small with a steam room but no sauna or whirlpool. 
Wifi Internet worked well but was expensive. Tv choices were great - even had nfl network. Had breakfast one morning and it was uneventful as the food was very average - you're better off walking to a nearby diner. 
Overall I would definitely recommend the four seasons Seattle to anyone traveling to Seattle for work or fun.

review_title: This is the nicest hotel I've in in many years - certainly in Seattle.
review_text: I loved the Sorrento Hotel. It has an old fashioned ambience - rightly earned given its history - with lots of beautiful wood paneling in the lobby and a wonderful arts and crafts fireplace mantel. Our room, actually a small suite, was cozy without being cloying or cute, with a comfortable bed complete with comfortable linens, which weren't too heavy, a pet peeve of mine. The bathroom was immaculate with no trace of mold, though both the toilet and shower were a bit balky, though the issues were quickly addressed by the staff. The staff well may be the best part of the hotel. They were professional, courteous and helpful, the very best staff I have ever encountered at a hotel in Seattle, and indeed at a hotel anywhere. We will definitely stay there next time we go to Seattle.

review_title: There must be better elsewhere for this price
review_text: Everything was averagely ok except for the staff which I found alternating between rude & unhelpful. The concierge was a joke & when I tried raising the issue of her rude unhelpfullness to the front desk, they just said, sorry about that but if you want directions you're going to have to ask her again. Perfect. I did come back later & get a different person who was more helpful after I basically demanded real directions. The first time around I was advised to, "take a bus". Ummmm, but which bus, from where, what stop, how much? I tried to ask her this & to write it down but she seemed so annoyed & it was like pulling teeth. Also, the first day the maids tried to come in at 7:45am & the rest of the time they stalked the room until I felt forced to leave so they would stop knocking every 20 min asking, how about now? The maid war was the most annoying aspect of the stay. The walls made of cardboard so you could hear every sound like it was in your room, the cherry.

I stayed here in a corner Elliott Bsy Suite with my husband and my son.
The hotel room was very nicely appointed, but I was not crazy about the color scheme, if I can be picky. The room was very comfortable and well-appointed, and very clean.
One thing that I did not understand was why they didn't put any heating vents in the bathroom. It was a very chilly day in Seattle, and the bathroom was always very cold.
Heated floors would have been a nice touch.
Other than that, I would highly recommend this hotel.

review_title: Worth every penny, we will be back!
review_text: We were celebrating our anniversary and the staff went out of their way to make our stay special from the moment we arrived! We will remember this weekend!

Recently stayed for 4 days, first the hotel rooms are just amazing! Had a view of the ocean which was great. I was here on business, but I would certainly return as a couple, top quality amenities, furniture, bed, and a huge bathroom. Location can't be beat, a block away from Pikes Market, great restaurants, bars, pubs all within a block or two Staff were all great and attentive, the morning coffee in the lobby was a nice touch. As for the the conference, the food was great! For a great "locals" bar, check out the Alibi Room in Post Alley, just under the hotel.

My wife and I visited the sorrento for the weekend recently. We arrived a couple hours before check in time but were checked in immediately and offered a very reasonable upgrade to a spacious corner suite on the 6th floor. The room itself was clean and comfortable with a complete entertainment system, 2 couches and a wet bar. They have managed to provide a modern vibe to a historic hotel. The hunt club restaurant was great, there were special events happening in the penthouse and inline music in the fireside room . Def Recomend this to anyone visiting Seattle

Great location close to Pike Place. Make sure you stay in the new building, but great hotel.

Kudos to Sara and Chris at the front desk. Chris went the extra mile to ensure we had a room that would work for my 86YO Mom. Earl the concierge was helpful. While the valet parking ain't cheap the in and out privledges help ease the sting. Check out the fab gym!

We looked at a range of hotels in Seattle but settled for the Sorrento and are very pleased we did. From the moment of check in, the service was fantastic with John in particular worth a mention for a level of service of you would normally only get in Asia. The location is the only thing you sacrifice in this property but the rooms size (significant), free wifi and courtesy cars at your disposal a major plus compared to the peer group. We used the courtesy car 3 times and each times the driver was willing to give a little guided tour and insight. The only small negative is that the towels are over leaned and the odour of bleach on them needs getting used to but it is rare to say that the only downside was overcleaning!! We would definitely come again.

review_title: Nice place to stay in downtown.
review_text:
Stayed here for a conference and had an excellent stay.
The rooms were huge, the bed was very comfortable, and the view was great.
Very conveniently located especially if you add going to the convention center.
There are excellent restaurants near by. I would highly suggest a visit to the "Tap House" which is just down the street.
Also did breakfast the Daily Grill down on the lobby level. The food was outstanding and the prices weren't too bad.
I would definitely recommend this place!

review_title: Very nice hotel, but avoid rooms near icemakers!!!
review_text: Really wanted to love this hotel because it has lots going for it, but we slipped away for a night only to be stuck in a room near an icemaker. Never has an icemaker been a problem for us before, but in this case it was right across the hall and sounded like a freight train. Woke us 4 times. Called front desk at 4 am to find out if it was broken. Was told "no" this was just "normal". On checkout next day staff was mildly apologetic. We'll "mark your record" to be away from ice machine next time--like we won't remember. Overall, nice hotel, but avoid rooms near ice machine like the plague.

review_title: Last minute reservation thru priceline! And it was great...
review_text: We needed a hotel at the last minute in Seattle and used priceline.. We were thrilled with our experience.. Beautiful room and lobby, good location and great beds! Slept soundly! Try Ruth chris's Steakhouse for happy hour... Just across the street! We would go back...
Stayed here for 8 Biggs and have no compliants. Good service and great location. Enjoyed using the gym, pool and hot tub every day too!
Rooms are nice....well appointed! Received a free upgrade! Ate at Art the hotel resturant....really good, but not super busy! Lounge was very busy though. Outdoor pool was great!

What does this Sheraton have going for it? Front desk staff, Concierge, house keeping staff, great gym, great pool, nice big comfortable rooms, comfy beds, nice views on upper floors, antique stores, aquarium, parks, REI Flagship store (large wall climb), shop till you drop shopping, new and used bookstores, Pike Street fish and flower market (Saturday a.m. is best), restaurants to suit any palate and outdoor paradise a short ride away. Take the really cheap fairy across the bay for a lunch or dinner. I took the Seattle Underground Tour with Gael in Pioneer Square. Most of Seattle burned down in 1889. She did a wonderful continuous "one-liner" schtick about the history of Seattle while walking through the bowels of the city. Fascinating! If you can't find something you like in Seattle, you would be difficult to please anywhere.

review_title: Great Staff, Beautiful Rooms, Wonderful Hotel
review_text: After a very long trip to Seattle, I was welcomed warmly by a very helpful staff and checked into an absolutely beautiful room. Even though I was there for work, this hotel was the perfect place for me to come "home" to and relax. I couldn't have been happier with my stay!

Good location, clean and tidy
I still struggle to understand why big hotel chains still want to charge for wifi in room

review_title: Beautiful historic hotel -- a comfortable and pleasant stay.
review_text: This hotel is a few blocks outside of downtown but is a great place to stay. The service was friendly and efficient, the rooms are nicely decorated, clean, and very comfortable, and the bar and lobby are stunning. We spent time downtown and in Capitol Hill and both were an easy walk. We did not eat in the hotel but Sugar, the cafe across the street, has the best pastries I've ever had.

We stayed here with a group of friends for the 4th of july weekend. The location of the hotel is perfect it's located near shopping center, market, and most of the other attractions! The hotel is clean, the rooms are nice the pool and spa are great! We also enjoyed the restaurant and the bar at the hotel called urbane we ate breakfast there every day and each day it was very good! The bar is also nice the the girl that runs it is very nice and very helpful! There is also a nice coffee bar there which has amazing mochas! Oveall I would recommend this hotel to everyone and would stay there again! Thanks

Beautiful hotel, comfortable, clean, hip. Location was great. We are comfortable walking the city, willing to walk more than the average, and we found it easy to access various tourist points in the city without transportation. We were lucky though ... No rain that weekend!

The service was execellent. The staff were very helpful. It was a fun lobby with a lovely fireplace. The front desk staff were super friendly and knowledgeable. I will stay here again. And you can not be in a better location.

Hotel Andra is a hidden treasure in Seattle. Located in an older but classy building, once you walk in the door, it's modern yet warm charm envelopes you. The staff is friendly and very helpful yet not obtrusive.
Our room this trip, a suite, was large, very nicely furnished and comfortable.
For the value, this place is a hidden treasure. Excellent restaurants nearby, valet parking and close to Pike Place and downtown, Hotel Andra hits a home run.

We loved the service and everything that makes the Alexis an outstanding hotel. We especially loved the concierge John A. He more then once went out of his way to provide us with transportation and even helping us with breakfast in bed. Ty again! We can't wait to go back.

The hotel and staff are great and very helpful. The hotel is about 7 blocks from most tourist attractions, but the walk is nice. Shopping and various restaurants are located right around the corner. There is a fridge in the room, but it is a minibar. You can request a fridge and the charge is $5. The rooms are very spacious and comfortable.

review_title: The best kept secret in downtown Seattle!
review_text: We stayed at the Alexis for a holiday party downtown and we were very impressed with the welcoming atmosphere, friendly staff, and even other guests in the hotel. The staff made us feel as though we were the only.ones staying at the hotel. They had a complimentary wine.hour that was incredible and we made quick friends with people staying at the hotel. The room was perfect and the bed very comfortable. I would recommend this place to anyone staying or visiting downtown Seattle.

This hotel was amazing, the location is awesome you don't really need to use your car because you are so close to everything like pikes place and the Seattle public library. The restaraunt is also great, try out the boka burger. The only gripe I have with the service is on check in the front desk attendant was very short with me, like she had something else better to do than check us in, but the rest of the staff was great. I'd go back again for sure.

We had the very best stay. It was the nicest hotel I have ever stayed, in terms of all around experience for adults and kids alike.
We especially liked the Wine and Wii hour every evening. A brilliant combination to make it fun for adults and kids alike.
hotel_name: Hotel Vintage Park - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: We stayed here for our first visit to Seattle just a couple of days before Christmas. I booked here after reading reviews. We were not disappointed. We were greeted with 2 glasses of prosecco upon arrival. Valet (Miles) took care of our luggage, showed us all room features, and answered any question we had. He brought us ice, iPod cables and two complimentary local microbrews as a welcome to the northwest. He even left a handwritten welcome note for us. Concierge Ben and Matty(?) made several reservations for us. They were both extremely pleasant and patient with us (we made a couple of changes), always made us feel that they were there to help us. Same experience in the hotel bar and restaurant, very pleasant staff. We had dinner, drinks and breakfast at Boka, I normally avoid the hotel restaurant. Seattle has great food choices. We enjoyed our 4 day stay and Hotel 1000 was a large part of that. When we come back we will definitely look to stay here again!!

This hotel does so many things right: Â glass of wine at night; great food (albeit only casual dining); Monday night at the movies (in the bar); coffee/tea in morning; free Internet wi-fi; beautiful architecture and interesting art; friendly staff; courtesy umbrella in the closet, etc.
One problem we had was getting heat in our room. Â  We changed rooms once and then 3 visits from the engineering (over 24 hours) before we got reliable heat. Â The front desk apologized, set chocolates up there really isn't a substitute for heat. I suspect we were just unlucky; I would certainly stay again. Â  What annoyed me was soap, shampoo, etc in little pump bottles. Â  It was nice stuff Gilchrist and Soames but the pump really did not work--what fun in the shower-trying get the pump to work.
Great hotel, beds comfortable, food from the restaurant Boka is not value for money very small portions with a big price.

review_title: Beautiful spaces and a wonderful, friendly sta..
review_text:
I adored this hotel, which I stayed in for a large conference. Smaller than the other conference hotels, the spaces were warm beaufiful, modern styles executed with warmth. My room was comfortable with plenty of space and microareas to inhabit. 
Public spaces: Coffee shop in the lobby has amazing coffee (yes, this is Seattle) with very reasonable prices (even cheaper refills!) and no feeling of rush. The fitness center was beautiful, with two wonderful facilities.
Staff: Helpful and engaging. 
Something special: Took a water aerobics class, which was great.($10)
I can't comment on cost because I had a confwrence rate.
This is just a wonderful hotel. I loved staying there.
This was a wonderful hotel.

Pool is ice cold,hot tub is more like pool temp should be,no robes in the rooms,rude front desk,average rooms.
We thought we would try this hotel out instead of the usual fairmont,never again!

This is a great hotel with a modern vibe. The hotel itself is gorgeous with a sleek, uncluttered look. The rooms are beautiful and well appointed with a fantastic bathroom. The lighting in the rooms enhances it quite a bit. I had a corner room with about 30 feet of wrap around windows- the whole hotel has an abundance of windows and natural lighting. The pool/spa is very nice and fosters relaxation. Overall, one of the better hotels I've stayed in and a great place to unwind after traveling

We've stayed at the Andra several times. We usually book a suite - for 2 adults / one chilld. The rooms are spacious, modern and clean with all the amenities youâ€™d expect - Comfortable bed and trendy dÃ©cor. The lobby area / lounge is busy in the evening. Cool atmosphere for pre-dinner drinks. The staff is friendly and professional. The restaurant â€“ Lola â€“ is good and always busy for breakfast. Good location - A short walk to Pike place Market, Macyâ€™s, Nordstrom , Niketown and many great restaurants. Windows could use better soundproofing, you can hear traffic noise even on the 8th floor.

review_title: Great hotel, great location. Breakfast - not so good
review_text: We had a suite on the 14th floor of the hotel. Wonderful room. Bar area, lounge area, separate wc, bathroom was fantastic. Tv in the mirror and rain shower were a nice touch. Tv in the lounge and another in the bedroom. Very clean. My only down side would be that breakfast was not complimentary, at this price I would expect it. We ended up eating in the hotel restuarant for breakfast in any case, it was really nothing special - potatoes were super salty and we had to ask three times to aquire all the necessary cutlery and condiments to the meal. The staff were very polite and proffesional. Just be careful about asking for reccomendations for local restaurants. There is obviously a standard response for one fish resturant but further questioning gleamed more choices and uncovered a gem (mortons). Overall a nice hotel but lacking in that final touch, it seems that if you want them to give you that little extra to make it a great hotel, it is gonna cost you.

review_title: Very nice hotel and great location.
review_text: This hotel is in a great location close to a lot of shopping and restaurants. I stayed in a room in the new tower. The room was so beautiful. Great beds, really nice bathroom, good TV. The bathroom could have been a little cleaner. Great shower. The hotel is large is it is very crowded and busy but the service was excellent. Great food. Free wifi in the lobby.

review_title: Great location but worst view ever
review_text:
We stayed in this hotel for just one night. This hotel tries very hard to be accommodating, from the friendly staff to the wine voucher they provide to guests who missed the wine tasting. 
But the hotel itself is old. We got two handicap rooms. They are slightly larger than regular rooms. But we looked right into the dark and ugly valley behind the hotel. Also, the chimney in the valley made a lot of noises. We had problems with the old toilets too.
This is a 4 star hotel. But it felt more like a crappy 3 star.
hotel_name: Hotel Vintage Park - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: Stayed there in may and loved it! Rooms are clean, good restaurant, fantastic location!
hotel_name: Hotel Vintage Park - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text:
Wonderful hotel, very clean, no complaints except no free WiFi. Amazed that I can get free Wifi at the Motel 6 in Dalton, Georgia but must pay or go to the lobby Srarbucks at the $170/night Grand Hyatt. 
Spotlessly clean, helpful and knowledgeable concierge, valet kind enough to store our luggage for 10 hours, and somewhat easy to find.
I work in Seattle from time to time and always stay at the Alexis. The service is attentive and personal, the rooms spacious and comfortable, and the location fantastic.
Bon hÃ´tel surtout avec la vue sur le lac. Chambres spacieuses quoique austÃ¨res

My wife and I visited Seattle on short notice and after a quick look on trip advisor decided to stay at the Alexis. The excellence started at the curb in front of the hotel with the valet parking and continued though out check in and then on to a truly awesome room ( the symphony suite) at a price that was a good value for money. A very well appointed room, large with comfortable furniture and bed, High ceilings, and was SPOTLESS. A truly relaxing experience. We will definitely stay there again and will look for Kimpton hotels in any city we visit.

review_title: Amazing treatment for a "nobody" - place was awesome.
review_text:
I cannot compliment this staff enough - I can't wait to save enough to stay there again.
I wanted to take my husband on a
"stay-cay-tion" - we live literally 3 blocks from this hotel but needed some in town down time. I wanted it to be super special. And the staff 150% was behind me all the way.
I arrived to champagne at the front desk upon check in - im pretty sure an across the board thing for everyone who checks in - already they had my stamp of approval.
They made us reservations at their restaurant, were ridiculously kind to us and always said hi, gave us a "how are things" and brought us towels and pillows within 5 min of our requests. The restaurant even made me an item that wasnt on the menu because the waitress happened to overhear me taking about my need for comfort food during this stressful time - they made me gourmet grilled cheese and tomato
soup, all with a smile and just because!!!!
Do yourself a huge favor and stay here. It's my philosophy that you get what you give - all I gave them was my business and a smile, and in return this staff gave us the world! 
Thank you to all of you who
Work there - I'm a low budget nobody who got celebrity treatment for no reason at all but that youre amazing at what you do!

Frequent traveler and stay in hotels around the world. This is one of my absolute favorites. The customer service is over the top, the location is perfect and the hotel tries very hard to make it a great experience. I will never stay anywhere else in Seattle. You can't go wrong with this hotel.

After 19 hrs in transit from australia, hotel 1000 was the perfect place to start our hols. It has everything a great hotel should have. We where so impressed, staff, cleanliness, position and the rooms are all great. Dont hesitate if wanting to stay in Seattle. You will be hard pressed to find better. Thanks for having us
Rapt.

review_title: Great location. Design over function. Service variable
review_text: The location is great ; near bars & restaurants, and a short walk to Pike's market etc but relatively quiet. Attracts stylish young guests . The room was lovely and spotless but sacrificed usefulness for looks. Example: akward & noisey pocket doors on the bathroom and a bed with a frame that juts out in a way perfectly designed to attack your shins. Service was mixed. When we checked in, the desk was rude and clueless. Luckily after a while, a manager swooped in and sorted things out. My rating would be much lower if that had not happened. Overall, I would not hesitate to stay here again but it would not be my first choice.

The room was very nice, free wifi, they allow pets which was nice to know for next time. We used priceline and this hotel picked up our bid so it was reasonable however the true cost is very high. But it was downtown Seattle and we were able to walk to pike market and safeco field pretty easily. 
The only drawback is the 34 dollar parking charge which is pretty steep. But the valet was nice and we were on vacation so whatever!
hotel_name: Hotel Vintage Park - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: This hotel is amazing. It's a little out of the way but not terrible! The rooms are lovely and on top of it its a Eco hotel!

This is a very nice hotel. Our king-size bed was very comfortable. The room was very clean and anything you may need was available in the room. It was very quiet. There was some city traffic noise but not noticable. After a long day of sightseeing it was great to come back to. Our only complaint was the cost of parking our car. I wish we would've not rented a car and took the train from the airport. There is so much to see in Seattle and great free transportation.

review_title: I have never written a hotel review before, but Hyatt at olive 8 is amazing I just had to!
review_text: My wife and I stayed at the Hyatt at olive 8 back in late July 2011. We were supposed to stay two nights leading up to our Alaskan cruise honeymoon. Delta screwed up our whole flight arrangement (never had a good experience with Delta) and we ended up running from gate to gate at our transfers and arriving in Seattle after midnight. Since we did not call to tell them we were going to make it they cancelled our room for the night. HOWEVER, when I called they were already on it. They put my wife and I up at the Hyatt regency around the corner in a big suite at no charge! They asked us to come back to Hyatt at olive 8 the next day with an upgrade over the standard king room we reserved. When we showed up they put us in one of their largest suites at no extra charge! Also, they left us a bottle of champagne on ice, some chocolates, and vouchers for free room service breakfast the next morning (it was delicious)! We were floored. Everything was fantastic. The room was the largest suite we had ever been in, and it was beautiful. Very modern and hi tech! Every person we dealt with at the hotel seemed to know who we were and all about our earlier cancellation. They were all so friendly. To top it off, being the cheap guy I am I noticed they charged me at the non AAA rate I reserved. Being the cheap guy I am I brought it up and hey knocked off an extra 100 bucks instead of the 25 I was expecting. I have never experienced such fantastic service at a hotel! I'm not sure if the hotel reads these reviews, but if they do I'm so sorry for taking so long to write this up. You guys helped our honeymoon be an extremely memorable experience. Thank you so much! We want to travel back to Seattle just to stay at this hotel! (won't be traveling on delta)
We stayed at Olive 8 for just one night but enjoyed every minute we were there! Beautiful hotel, amazing service, and great location!!! Can't wait to go back!
The hyatt is a reliable and good hotel from which you can easily wander through the lovely city of Seattle :-)!

review_title: Gorgeous accommodations but watch add ons!
review_text: First this hotel is grand... Location is great, Rooms are quiet and clean. Had club level suite with access to free food and drinks morning and evening! You will be able to park upon arrival and walk everywhere you wish to go! Now for the other charges! Parking 40.00 a day valet 30.00 a day self park in garage! Internet 15.00 a day and the market store has everything you wish but expensive as well! Would stay anytime again!

Excellent centrally located hotel.
The restaurant, 'daily grill', is very very good. Pleasant surprise for a hotel restaurant.

My wife and two teenage daughters stayed at Hotel 1000 for a long weekend visit to Seattle. We have travelled extensively all over the world and have not had a better experience anywhere. I have never seen happier or more helpful staff anywhere. The front desk staff, waiters, valets, everyone. Everybody working in this hotel gave you the feeling they had the best job in the world. Oh, did I forget to mention the great location, cool decor and wonderful restaurant? Stay there. You won't be disappointed.

My boyfriend and I stayed at the hyatt back in July (been meaning to write this review sooner!)
We were in Seattle for the long weekend and just wanted to get away somewhere that we could drive to. That being said we weren't expecting a whole lot. Especially when my boyfriend used priceline to bid. We were pleasantly surprised when we got the hyatt for the price we asked for. The hotel was so much more than we could have asked for. The room was a nice size with a comfortable king size bed. The view from our room wasn't great but that really just depends on what side of the hotel you're put on. The bathroom is huge, nice big glass shower and a large separate bathtub, double sinks as well. And the room was spotless both days we were there. The location is right in the downtown shopping area and not to far from the farmers market. Valet parking was quick and all the stuff we encountered were always smiling and happy to help.

We ended up being in Seattle at the last minute and The Vintage Park was available. I have stayed at other Kimpton hotels in the past and this was no exception. Great staff, clean comfortable rooms in a very good location in downtown. The room we had was small but we didn't spend much time here anyway. I like the fact that they are pet friendly and that there are benefits by being a member of their loyalty program which provides free items and services that would normally be expensive at other hotels in the same price range.
hotel_name: Hotel Vintage Park - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: Nice place but not worth the price
review_text: I recently came to Seattle for a conference and stayed at the Vintage Park. I was not overly impressed. The location is great and convenient to everything downtown. The restaurant downstairs was excellent, in fact the hotel staff should take customer service lessons from the restaurant manager. Rooms were small and a little dated, but I did get a good laugh from the leopard bathrobes. The nightly wine tasting is a nice touch too. Over all the hotel is nice but just too expensive. Another reco from a guy who just travels way too much, Joe Sloboda
hotel_name: Hotel Vintage Park - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: Very cool hotel! From the pictures on the walls to the warm cookies upon arrival this hotel is very inviting. The room we stayed in was a little small. But the ambiance more than made up for it. The location is within walking distance of pike place market. But is also located on some very steep hills. Bring some walking shoes!

review_text: Perfect location, service, and restored historic hotel. What a treat! A little loud but well worth it. Skip the car and take the metro to downtown from the airport. Loved every minute!

review_title: Too far from downtown. Neat building
review_text: We needed a room for our family (2 small kids) for one night. I used to live in WA, so was familiar with area, butthis is a newer hotel. Seafair was going on and rooms were a little tight in town. I got a room at this hotel through hotwire at a decent price, having used priceline and hotwire many times in past. So we show up after a long day of travelling at about 9:30 and instantly upon check in the guy working at the desk days " i see you booked your room through a third party site". I said yes. He said, well we cant accomodate you with 2 beds. Kind of haughty about it as well. Actually, on hotwire you can request accomodations for 4 people, and we did it at the sheraton thefollowing week. They ( sheraton) automatically had us in a double room without asking. So with "nothing else available" we had a room with a pullout sofa. It was fine but you couldnt really move around. Otherwise, the bar area was cool--absinthe! Sirens all night long was unpleasant. Restaurant juno for breakfast was ok albeit slow service. I wouldnt stay here again, too many better options around.

review_text: Nice room in a great location, but there are a lot of hotels in Downton Seattle that can say the same. Kind of a cold, sterile atmosphere. Obviously cater to conventions. Ruths Chris is always good, but the bar is not appealing. Walked in the rain to the Mayflower for a drink. Really irritates me that they charge for WI-Fi.
The rooms were nice and the beds very comfortable. The location is great. It's very easy to walk to many of the tourist attractions in the city, like the public market.

review_title: What we expected, and then some!
review_text:
Check out the clerk's hair! Am I allowed to comment about that? It has to take a long time to prepare that look... Awesome!
Animal print bathrobes, a comfy bed & walking distance from the best of Seattle!
Pricey, but a great location & a ton of fun!
hotel_name: Hotel Vintage Park - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text:
This is a very nice hotel downtown.
My family and I had a great stay at the Arctic Club. 
It is located several blocks from Pike and Pine but it is easy to get there day or evening.
The staff doesn't give advice unless you ask for it.
But the rooms and the hotel are great.

review_title: Unparalleled Luxury at a great price!
review_text: Hands down, this hotel exceeded my expectations! For a first visit to the pacific northwest, the Maxwell understands the essence of what it means to create the ultimate customer experience. We were greeted warmly by the staff at the front desk and they even allowed us to check in early. The lobby is spacious and elegantly decorated. The room was amazing. From the cozy bed to the sleek decor to the large shower, all our senses were engaged. We had time to use the pool and gym, although they were on the smaller side they were clean spaces which is always nice! My spouse and I are planning to take another trip to Seattle and we will be repeat customers. Thank you Maxwell for an amazing stay and intro to your beautiful state!

review_title: Special rooms, nice people, great hotel
review_text:
Top notch rooms with original art, super clean, exceptional location and great service. 
Ask for a room with a bath ... It's a unique set up (water fallsnout of the ceiling) and the rubber ducks are a nice touch. 
Great restaurant, busy bar, great people. 
Gym can use lots of work ... Other than that it is perfect

The Paramount was a nice surprise - classy and elegant without being over the top. When was the the last time that someone arrived at your hotel door with water and chocolates to welcome you? And in a hotel that is very affordable and nicely located. Friendly welcoming staff, clean, one of the best hotels I've stayed at in a long time!
Great room with lots of room, standard small bathroom with great shower. Only negative was the restaurant for breakfast, i don't expect to have to wait 20 min for a table.

Outstanding top floor gym is a treat. Some young staffers need polish, but try. Would stay here again for business or pleasure. If shipping boxes to hotel, be prepared for a charge and to pay $34 to park.

My boyfriend and I just stayed one night in the Sheraton. We were down for a Seahawks game and had previously stayed in the hyatt across the street. Obviously the Sheraton wasn't up to the level as the hyatt but overall we don't have really any complaints. 
Upon arrival they had us in a double bed room but we're happy to change us to a king bed room. The room was clean and a nice size. The bathroom was nothing special but clean. The Starbucks coffee in the room was a nice plus and we appreciate having wine glasses in the room as well. The pool on the top floor didn't have as nice of view as I thought it would. I didn't go in the gym area but it looked huge and full of nice equipment. 
We had forgotten toothpaste and the front desk was happy to send someone up with some, probably only took about ten minutes. 
If you're looking for someone really nice to stay I wouldn't suggest it but of you're just down a night or two and need somewhere to stay it'll do the trick

review_title: Great location if you're staying downtown.
review_text:
If you're staying downtown, location is excellent. Within 3 to blocks of the best of downtown shopping. Convention center? Right next door. Obviously renovated in the not too distant past, so rooms are in excellent shape with all the amenities you would expect for this price range, such as large bathroom with separate marble shower, excellent bed and recently updated furnishings. As you would expect from any Downtown hotel, this is oriented to business travellers. If you're looking for the romantic weekend getaway, however, there may be better options (Fairmont?). I gave it a 4 overall for service. Nice furnishings and updating are important, but really great hotels distinguish themselves with the calibre of their service, and that usually means the training of their employees. As a rule, on this point Hyatt is fine, but not great. And this hotel is no exception to that rule. 
 One word of caution - downtown is a little edgy at night for my liking. The people we encountered while walking around looking for our restaurant at 9 pm did definitely make us a little unconfortable at times. My wife will want to stay in Bellevue on the next weekend trip to Seattle, because of that. But that is obviously something that is a very personal preference.

review_title: There are other hotels near by with friendlier staff
review_text: Not nearly the quality of stay you'd expect for a Hyatt. Manager and staff and rude, and obviously dont value the guests. My advise is go stay at the Hilton or Roosevelt. Same quality hotels, but with much better staff.

After flying 20+ hours I was greeted with champagne on arrival, a small gesture that was welcomed and appreciated. 
From the photos I was expecting a bit more from the decor but it is nice and the hotel has everything you'd need plus more.

On a recent family trip (two adults, two boys 7 and 9 y/o), we decided to take a risk and stay at a "non-chain" hotel. We weren't disappointed! The staff was friendly and very helpful (even offering activity boxes with crayons, card games, Legos for the boys to use during our stay). My request for a room with a view was honored (we had a great view of the Space Needle nearby). The room was clean, the decor was refreshing, the hardwood floors (and potential noise issue) wasn't a problem. We didn't mind that there wasn't a restaurant in the hotel, as the hotel's location is near the Seattle Center, monorail, and lots of good eating options. The free parking was worth it alone!! The room rate was great. I can't rave enough about our experience; we highly recommend it!

review_title: They really don't care about their customers.
review_text:
We were really looking forward to our stay in Seattle. The hotel shuttle dropped us off our first night at their favorite restaurant (Anthony's), even made a reservation for us. When we got to Anthony's the restaurant had no heat. The outside temp was 30. We stayed anyway and the food was ok.
We called an hour later to have the shuttle pick us up and were told that since it was now snowing they would not pick us up and to find a cab. There were no cabs around and the Hyatt just said sorry. We started walking back when they called my cell phone and said they would meet us half way if we could get to a particular intersection, about a mile walk. We got there and made it back. The manager ran upstairs to stay in a guest room for the night and left the front desk clerk to speak to us. She said the manager had authorized 1500 points for our trouble (it takes 8000 for 1 night.) Never an apology from management, he just ran and hid. Plenty of better places to stay in downtown Seattle, where management care just a little.
When we planned our trip to Seattle I was 8 mo pregnant so comfortable beds were a must! This place not only has comfortable beds but excellent service!!!!

review_text: This hotel offers 4 star rooms, at a 2 star price. Free shuttle picked me up, and dropped me off, at the ferry terminal, the following morning. The bed, large couch, gigantic digital tv, which swiveled, and work desk, were great. Bathroom was huge, with waterfall shower. Good free breakfast. Nice indoor pool. Space Needle, in my face, through my window. Paid $80, via internet special. Worth full price. Will gladly stay again.

I have to say the charm of this hotel blew me away. The building was an old gentelmens club, that has been preserved and restored. The rooms although small make up for it with days gone by charm with modern amenities. The blue room doors were a hit with me. Its close to pike market, and we didn't need to rent a car. Seattle has a great public transportation system. The gem of the hotel was Angelo the bellman he was our go to guy. He really took care of us, and answered all our questions. Now, I did find a tank top behind the end table, when my watch fell. Honestly it would have been easy to miss. I had to move it to reach all the way beihind it. This in no way effects my opionion on the hotel. If you dont want the cookie cutter hotel. I highly recommend this one.

review_text: Loved everything about my stay, except CNN stations didn't work and I had to watch Fox News.
I am in our room now! Great location to everything, free fridge and wireless wifi, friendly staff. Only bummer thing was the parking fee. Would definately recommend!

review_title: It was the best hotel ever!
review_text: Everyone at the hotel was so nice and very helpful... If I ever go back to Seattle I will stay here again.

This is a good choice for Downtown Seattle.
Very well maintained and managed. My only minor complaint is some noise from the plumbing, also from the street and from an adjacent building's hvac system. Other rooms might not have this problem.
Be aware that Downtown Seattle can be a bit unnerving late at night when things get quiet and only the occasional passer by or homeless person wanders by.
Overall a good hotel very convenient for shopping.

If I could live here, I would. The Cedarbrook Lodge is stunningly beautiful - rain or shine. The stff is pleasant and welcoming. The accommodations are clean, well-appointed and the deep soak tub is super fantastic. Bathrobes included! The lodge gives you luxury status without the luxury rates. Amazing. It's been a year since my last visit and I thought the definitely earned another raving review.

I recently stayed here for a wedding. It was a beautiful Hotel . I loved the theme of the decorations which seemed to center around early 1900 mens atire and walruses. The rooms were clean, comfortable and once again really nicely decorated . It was close to everything! We took the link in from the airport and it was only one block away from where we got off. 
There is an awesome Resturant right across the street called the mimosa cafe! I'd stay at the is Hotel again !

review_title: Wine theme interesting and great local but....
review_text:
The front room of hotel is adorable. In the morning, it's completely busy and full of people checking out old school style. For whatever reason, to-go coffee cups are behind the front desk and because of the morning crowd not easily accessible. Remember to get yours when you check out. 
The room was fine. I slept comfortably. But the walls are thin. I could hear the phone and alarm in the next room over.
The lamp knobs require man handling to turn on and off in room 309. 
And the sink handles are also tricky to turn with wet hands. 
Interesting tiger robes and socks in closet. I never put that stuff on but some may like that perk. 
I wish there were water bottles available in the room but that said, they do have fresh cucumber flavored water in the lobby.
hotel_name: Hotel Vintage Park - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: Charming themed hotel with an antique feel and wino flare.
review_text: Love this hotel!! If it was cheaper I'd go every time. The lobby is like walking into the coziest living room ever. We had wine and brandy tastings by the fire in social, informative gatherings. Views were great of city, in a great location for pike place, theaters, and game day. My favorite Seattle hotel.
hotel_name: Hotel Vintage Park - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: Outstanding hotel. Staff was extremely helpful and courteous. It's a short walk to the market, the waterfront, and all the shopping at Pike and 5th.

review_title: Get bumped from our reserved hotel to the Alexis!! What a lucky move!
review_text:
The Alexis is a great hotel!! Nicely done rooms, we had a king spa suite, couldn't have been happier! Wine happy hour was great. Staff was very nice. 
Location is good, about 5-6 blocks from the Market, so good walking distance to everything. 
Highly recommend staying here!

The location is absolutely fabulous. Just a few blocks walk to the pike place market and surrounded by some great restaurants. We were there during the parade and it was a pain to try to get across the other side of town back to the hotel. We brought our little dog and there was a bed and bowls with a treat waiting when we arrives. The room was smaller than we expected but it was comfy and clean. We were on the 4th floor looking at other rooms and it was quiet and pleasant. I was a little bit confuse at first as there are 2 entrances. I'm not walking very well after a surgery and the Madison street enterance was not too friendly for me as there are only stairs and it is uphill walking to the front entrance. It is on the pricey side but overall it was a fabulous stay.

review_title: Nice rooms, service could be better
review_text:
The Maxwell has nice, clean, good sized rooms. No complaints there.
I found the service left a bit to be desired however. On check in at 1pm, we were flatly told that check in was 3pm. I appreciate that 3pm is the check in time. However most places are generally a bit flexible about check in time. Maybe they were 100% booked the previous night, but it would have been nice to have that communicated. We don't usually show up early for check in, but find that good hotels are generally accommodating on the odd occasion this happens.
There was also another strange guy working the desk at various times who was a bit creepy.
All that said, as other reviews note here, the rooms at the Maxwell are high standard and good value.

The Kimpton Hotel chain is one line of hotels you can always count on. They are each unique and very, very nice. The Alexis hotel is in a prime location for downtown walking. The room itself is very clean, modern, and they always have soft towels! I like the chain mostly because each room looks like it just came out of a decor magazine. They have great wifi too.

This place is at the edge of downtown and Belltown. Great location if you want to easily get away from the downtown touristy places. The hotel was renovated when the Andra took it over but you can see the bones of what it once was. The rooms are big and well appointed. Tivoli clock radios, couches, walk-in closet, wet bar. The only negative on the room is that the bathroom is pretty small. Remnant of the old bones I suppose. Service was good. Free newspaper and shoe shine. Lobby is nice with fireplace. Definitely recommend over any of the chains.

We love this charming boutique hotel. Very friendly & accommodating staff, very nice rooms, great location, even complimentary wine receptions. Also has one of Seattle's best restaurants & bars - Tulios.
hotel_name: Hotel Vintage Park - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: We spent 5 days at the Maxwell Hotel and found it to be excellent. The rooms were spacious and well appointed, the location a bit far from downtown but convenient to Queen Anne district and other resources. Free parking, free Internet and outstanding service especially from Justin at the front desk who we found to be extremely professional and helpful. We will use the Maxwell as our base for furtre travels to the Seattle area

Couldn't ask for a better location in downtown Seattle. 
Lobby is bright and fresh. Desk staff was very friendly and knowledgeable. There was a convention going on so it was pretty busy...but never felt crowded. 
Room was clean and seemed to have been remodel recently. I was on a high floor so I had a good view. Bed was comfortable and it had soft sheets and pillow cases. 
Best part (IMHO)...exhaust fan in the bathroom! Why don't more hotels have these?

review_title: Beautiful hotel. Great location. Walking distance to Pike's market.
review_text: Stayed two nights. Valet parked car and walked all over downtown area. Friendly staff. Nice, clean room. Expensive, but higher end place. Liked we did not have to drive. Walked to pikes market, shopping and waterfront.

review_title: Excellent hotel. Friendly staff. Easy free parking.
review_text:
Stayed 3 days with 3rd night free and got a free upgrade too which was very nice. Room was fantastic - little touches like free water each day. Don't know if I would pay for refrigerator in room as didn't use it much - only for toddlers milk and would be cheaper to buy carton each day. Breakfast was reasonable. Lobby/meal area was very comfortable and spent lots of time down then when toddler going off to sleep (watched by husband). 
Lots of restaurants nearby - 2 or 3 block walk. University type pubs and fast food mainly but probably something to suit most. Front desk provided lots of options for eating including delivery menus and delivered to room.
Only negative was that the free shuttle does not allow babies or small kids to travel without car seat and won't provide one. So unless you fancy carting one round all day, you have to use your car or take the bus. We used the buses each day and drivers were super helpful and nice. Just added an unexpected cost to our trip - cost was about 4.50 each way for 2 adults. We normally stay central to avoid extra transport costs and time travelling, but thought we would use the shuttle. Nevermind, the bus was interesting for a change. Also downtown was full of unsavoury characters - terrible homelessness etc which is sad to see. We were a little pleased to get put to the suburbs each night actually.
Overall great experience and ideal if you need to be near university or don't mind shuttle or buses to get downtown.

review_title: Nice play to stay in University district
review_text: We've stayed here multiple times when visiting family in Seattle. This is predictably a pleasant stay; clean rooms, friendly service, free breakfast and wifi. Only con's are the street noise (although location is convenient,) and it can be a bit pricy, although good for Seattle.

review_title: Great $$$, Super bonus for free parking, funky neighborhood, loved the art-deco decor!!! Would go back I'm a heart beat.
review_text: As above...nothing bad to report as long as you can walk a bit easy trek to dwntwn or monorail, sweet hotel, a treasure.

review_title: Clean, comfy, noisy, but read on for some tips and what to expect.
review_text:
Stayed here 3 nights. Our first time in Seattle and not realizing that being near the space needle does not mean you are near downtown. 
Location and getting around
The staff advised us the simplest quickest way to get downtown was to walk 5 minutes to the space needle. It is definitely NOT a 5 minute walk to the monorail! We are fit people and walk at a fairly fast pace. The best time we clocked from the hotel to the monorail was 10 minutes. The monorail has two ends; space needle at one end and a shopping centre that is a couple of blocks from pike place markets. There are no other stops. Each trip is $2 for the 1 mile covered. We discovered the bus as a better option. The off peak fare is $2.25 and you should always get a transfer which lasts 2 hours so you can make the most of the ticket if you want to return to the hotel or visit another area. There are two places we picked up a bus; 5th and valley or 1st and mercer. These stops are 2 or 3 blocks away; much closer than the monorail. 
The room
Unfortunately we were given a room right next to the elevator and with a stunning view of the car park across the road facing Roy street. As other reviewers have said it is very noisy from other rooms. You can hear everything. We had the added bonus of the dulcet tones of the bing bong of the elevator and the grand accompaniment of loud merrymakers until the wee sma's. And on a weeknight too! Then the early risers using the elevator from 5am continued to keep us alert so we wouldn't miss the continuing sounds of room doors slamming shut. We did mention to the staff each day that we were being disturbed by noise. I'm certain there was a family of elephants in the room above; running continually up and down the hallway to their door. The staff offered to contact the guests in that room if the noise continued past 10pm. We were also disturbed by passers by on the street who were often exuberant; probably due to having just been to a show at the key arena.
Wifi
Basically, it sucks. The only way we could get enough signal was to sit in the hallway behind out door. We advised the staff on several occasions and they blamed apple devices for the problem. 
Bathroom
I am really not a fuss pot but I do use a hair dryer and the length of cord on their dryers is impossible to be able to dry your hair unless you are prepared to have your nose stuck against the bathroom wall. The cord must measure about a foot and a bit long. The staff could not help with that either. All the dryers were the same, I was informed. Oh well. 
Beds
Very very comfortable. 
Business centre
This was convenient and you can print for free.
Great staff, great service! They really went the extra mile for guests. Beautiful location!
Great location for walking around to see sites, but don't stay here if you want rest and relaxation.
Wonderful boutique hotel experience. Gorgeous Icelandic decor. Restaurant on site, Lola's, is amazing and we ate there every day.

review_title: Not your typical hotel stay. In a good way!
review_text:
First off, I felt like I was on a college campus trying to find my room. Once I found it I was a happy camper. Wonderful, modern rooms with little details such as an easy chair and ottoman, wall mounted tv, two work stations and floor to ceiling windows. 
They have common areas with free snacks such as ice cream, yogurt, chips, candies and water. The newspaper was at the door each morning and the surronding grounds were beautiful. 
I was surprised there wasn't a refrigerator in the room and there was no bath tub just a shower stall. Also, the bathroom lacked counter space and places to hang the hand towels. 
The staff was friendly and we did eat in the hotel restaurant Copperleaf. It was a delicious and memorable meal. The Continental breakfast was good with plenty of selections and Starbucks coffee of course. We would definitely stay here again.

Got a great rate the day before our "get-away" weekend and will be back again! Beautiful serene gem of lodge. Played Bocce ball, lawn croquet, pool and walked the lush, peaceful grounds. The Haggen-Daz was a delightful addition!
Wonderful staff, clean, soothing decor. You feel like you're at a spa and not 5 minutes from a noisy airport.

review_title: The perfect stay to end our imperfect trip!
review_text: We stayed at the Maxwell Hotel after a long trip with our toddlers. It was perfect! From the cupcakes at check-in to the DVD player to the free wifi to the popcorn it exceeded my expectations. The location was perfect and we found walking to meals fun! Our suite overlooked the Space Needle, which was nice. The beds were so soft and comfortable. The room was chic and had all the modern amenities a travelling family needs. There is even a kids cart you can rent with games, coloring books, etc! The parking garage was being repaved but the hotel had a staff member out front directing patrons where to go to park. All the employees we encountered were super friendly and helpful. My only complaint was that whoever was staying above us sounded like a dinosaur with all of his/her stomping. That is the only negative I could come up with about the hotel! We will definitely be staying here again! Thank you Maxwell Hotel!

review_title: A lovely hotel with fabulous staff!!! Thank you for making our stay so memorable
review_text:
Last weekend my mum, my
Maid of honor, and I decided to drive down from Vancouver to shop for a wedding dress. We had not made a reservation in advance thinking we would find something when we got into town. I had stayed at the hotel 1000 a couple years ago and suggested we head over there as it is only a couple of blocks from pike place and has nice, modern rooms. 
We were greeted with a glass of champagne in the lobby while the Valets parked the car and brought the luggage up. We had a lovely room and decided to have happy hour in the bar.... After I skyped my fiancÃ© with the free Internet. We ordered snacks and martinis from the friendly bar staff and I went to talk to the concierge about making a dinner reservation (this was at about 6:30 on a saturday) Marty the concierge was fabulous!!! I explained what we were looking for and he had us a 7:00 pm reservation at an amazing funky Italian restaurant and the name of a bar we could go to after, that made custom drinks based on your favorite flavors and spices?! When we went up to our room to change for dinner our doorbell rang and it was Matty with a red rose saying congratulations on buying your wedding dress and he hoped we had a wonderful evening! We did! The hotel also has very comfortable 
beds - a real bonus! We checked out but left the car with the hotel which was no problem at all - they had even comped our parking when we checked in and when we picked it up from the valet in the afternoon there were three bottles of water in the cup holders for our drive home. Every little detail was taken care of and the staff really couldn't have made us feel more welcome. We will be staying with you again!!! I think all of want to recreate the weekend (hotel and restaurants le spiga and the baguette box) again with our significant others. Hopefully there aren't to many spelling mistakes as I have written this in my iPhone. 
Thank you!!!
We thoroughly enjoyed our stay at the Mayflower, the staff was excellent and the rooms well-appointed. My only hang up was the price, which felt exorbitant, yet unavoidable for the location.

To start Justin at the reception was extremely helpful and made sure we had a great room good beds on the top floor.
Room was spacious and clean.
Hotel nice atmosphere. Pool small but nice.
Location okay, very near to monorail.Ample parking when we were there,so easy with a car. Only disappoinment was, no sandwhiches left for breakfast, but there is coffee and cakes on arrival.

This hotel turned out to be perfect for the 4 of us. We had a booking at the Schaefer Baille Mansion on Millionaire's Row, but they overbooked us. Luckily, we found out a few days before the stay and found this hotel. We dropped by Schaefer Baille to collect our money and get free breakfast, and realized we were lucky to be at Maxwell. Good location. PiKe's Place is a bit of a walk but doable. Free parking and wifi. Nice snacks and coffee in the room. We booked the cheapest room thru Octopus (Japanese site was a bit cheaper) and it was comfortable for 4 people for 2 nights. We saw a family eating takeout food in the nice lobby tables one night and thought that had I known this I'd have gotten some nice roasted chicken from the supermarket to feast with my friends :)
They do sometimes offer 1 night free if you stay for 3 nights. Check that out.

The hotel was a little difficult to find but once we called the hotel and got some help it was ok. Check in was fast and friendly. The front desk clerk called our room to make sure we were able to settle in ok. The hotel doesn't have a restaurant which disappointing considering the expansive size of the lobby and sitting area.
I prefer that the shower stalk would have a shower curtain but the design is one where it is not required. The water pressure for the shower could have been better.

review_title: Super cool hotel, but missing a restaurant and bar.
review_text:
Stayed here on business. Not sure the exact cost for a room, but I'm sure it's on the expensive side. The rooms are very cool and contemporary and slightly different from the average layout. Loved the decor throughout the hotel and rooms. The A/C ran very good and the beds were very comfortable IMO. 
My only complaint is that there isn't a restaurant or bar in the hotel. There's all this extra space in the lobby with all this cool decoration it's a shame that it's only functioning for the ambiance of some lounge chairs. There is a cafe with a limited selection of cafe-style treats. All is not lost though, because your in walking distance of some great pubs serving their micro-brews and great food and there's some amazing restraunts around that are also within walking distance. 
Speaking of location, there are rooms that look out over the space needle and your within walking distance of some great attractions, including the EMP (experience music project) museum, which is a must see, because hey, you are in Seattle!
This hotel was very nice and located right near the center of town and transportation hubs. The room was big and nice. It wasn't cheap but probably avg $ for that location.

Great location but definitely not 5 star. Ver clean and modern and the boutique feeling. We were happy that it was close to to everything. You have to check out Brooklyn at happy hour time. Back to the hotel, the staff was very friendly and very attentive. The lounge next door is very nice and great to pop in after a long night. Overall we were happy and will return when we are in Seattle again.

We have been coming back for 8 years, would't stay any where else in downtown Seattle. Great service, warm and friendly. Lovely decor. Oliver's is the best martini bar around.
They go above and beyond to meet all your needs.
Staff was friendly...rooms were clean and large. Great location for downtown and the parking was great. The only thing it seemed to be missing was a hot tub.

We absolutely loved this hotel. The decor is beautiful, classy and hip. Parking was free!! Spacious room and rather large bathroom ( with a great blowdryer). Located a few blocks from the space needle and close to many theaters.

Nice hotel but certainly not a 5 star property. It's at best a 3.5. Location near airport but in a residential area. Not the best area for safety. Property well kept and people were kind but the location and amenties leave much to be desired.
Fabulous service, big comfortable rooms, leafy location, great food....and all incredibly a 5' shuttle ride from the airport. Highly recommended for business meetings.

review_title: Close enough to Everything and MUCH better than most !!
review_text:
We spent 4 nights at the Maxwell and quite enjoyed the room, the ambience and the people. We were greeted by Adriel, who checked us in and was extremely knowledgeable about the area and Seattle in general. The hotel is well situated just outside of downtown, a couple blocks from the Space Needle and Aeattle center, right across the street from Teatro Zinzanni and a short walking distance from a network of restaurants and a grocery Mart. The only thing better than the location, is the hotel itself. 
The rooms are spacious, clean and quiet and decked out with a big screen LG tv and a dvd player (dvd's can be borrowed from the front desk library). The hotel is
decked out with modern furnishings 
and great colours. The wifi Internet is fast, and the parking is not as 'limited' as noted in other reviews (about 100 stalls).
A fantastic find that will have us back.
NB- regarding the 'overrated' review below. I was at the front desk when the gentleman was there. He was treated with much respect and consideration, in fact I was impressed with how Jacob handled the situation. He found the guest another room quickly, and worked hard to satisfy a client that was simply looking for more.
Within blocks of the space needle. Very friendly staff. Comfortable beds and bedding. Sophisticated yet colorful decor.

We stayed here for one night right after our wedding before flying out for our honeymoon. The bad experience started at check in. We arrived in a limo in a tux and my bride in her wedding dress. The front desk did not acknowledge us nor ask if we needed any help with our luggage. After approaching the counter the gentleman was courteous and checked us in. We proceeded to check in however no bell hop was available so we proceeded to push the luggage cart to the other end of the property to our room. 
The room: We booked s suite through AAA. Overall the room was nice but there was tons of wasted space. The extra room did big add any usable space at all and from looking into the regular rooms they were a much better value and we liked them more. 
Room service: Food was pretty standard. Ordered a crab sandwich and the bread was soggy. My new wife ordered a chicken sandwhich and it was very good. 
The fire alarm: We were awoken at 3 am by the fire alarm going off in our building. Staff was clueless and totally unavailable. The fire trucks showed up and they proceeded to search the building with no fire found. The next issue was the alarm. The fire men were unable to disable it fully but they disabled the alarm sound at approx 4:15. The blinking stove light in our room however proceeded to blink every second until approx 6 am. At no time during this ordeal was any staff member available for questions nor did they let us know what was going on. 
After having a horrible nights stay we asked for a late checkout so we could catch up after thd fire alarm issue for 3 hours thd night before rudely we were told there was no late checkout by the front desk. I the pressed thd issue further and the manager begrudgingly allowed us to stay an additional hour. 
Overall there are nice amenities, the breakfast is amazing zng the Lou ge with snacks is a nice treat. It however does not make up for the lack of service we met at every turn. Based on the other reviews I hope our experience was just an anomaly.

review_title: Wish we allowed more time to stay longer
review_text: Simply very good, nice extra values. ( free water, ice cream, and yogurt)

Great hotel, couldn't fault it. Our room looked out to the Mississippi river. It's in a quiet but very safe neighbourhood but it is easy to get to Beale street and other downtown locations, it's a 10 min walk to the main street trolley and we paid 9 dollars for taxi back. Downtown memphis is quite rundown so this hotel is a good choice to stay.
Fabulous northwest lodge feel in a secluded airport neighborhood. Had dinner in the lounge. Bryce provided exceptional service and great humor. This is a special spot, I really mean it.

I just stayed there for 3 nights on a business trip. I will not be staying there again. The walls are not sound-proofed at all, so you can hear every little sound in neighboring rooms. I had an extremely noisy couple in the room next to me who kept me up until 4 am when I had to get up at 6 am for my work obligations. The bathroom floor and tub were moldy. My company paid for my stay in full ahead of time, about $400. I gave them my credit card up front for incidentals, and they put a $1600 hold on it and attempted to charge me for $800. Luckily, my credit card company alerted me to the unusual transaction. When I called the hotel to ask for the charges, they stated that they only did an $800 hold, which is still a lot for a stay already paid in full. It took a while to remove the $1600 hold. Luckily, my credit card company called me. Otherwise, I would have been mistakenly charged $800 of that $1600 hold.

review_title: Another top review, exceeded high expectations
review_text: I expected a top experience here given the prior reviews and these were all met or exceded. Friendly desk staff, spotless rooms and public areas, and courteous breakfast room staff. I appreciated that they still had coffee and food available even after the 10AM sign posted. Ample newspapers, and good free WiFi (I speed tested it at 6.5 download and 6.7 upload, quite good for public WiFi) made this lodging comfortable. Beds were comfortable, soft but very supportive. The hotel was full and I paid over $140, nearly the price of the Hilton in the area. We were alarmed when we got in at 1AM on a delayed flight and was told that the hotel was full. The night clerk seemed confused that we used the online check in at the airport that evening and we had the last room and room number confirmed in advance No problem, the surprised clerk gave us the keys, not expecting any more check-ins that night.
Loved it. Friendly, comfortable and convenient. Watched the sun set over the Mississippi every night.

We love the beautiful trees and enjoyed walking around the property. Breakfast items were all high quality, not packaged products. Homemade apple preserves and smoked salmon were the best. The young staff members drove the shuttle bus and were very warm and friendly. Highly recommended as a starting point for Mt Rainier since it is south of Seattle. Much better value than hotels in downtown Seattle, but not so convenient if you want a mid-afternoon rest at your hotel.

My husband and I are staying here now and we really like it. Great places to visit and go eat right in the neighborhood. Nice to have the parking for free! Also we lived the coffee and popcorn that was in the room. Beautiful hotel, big room!!
I truly enjoyed my stay here! Never have I seen such a friendly staff or cleaner rooms! The location was right next to many nice restaurants and the very cool North Market.

review_title: Rates are greedy for room sizes.
review_text: Perhaps if they knocked through two rooms to make one on each level you would have a normal sized room and the Lilliputian offering here. Fat people, those with more than carry on luggage or substandard agility can forget it. The location is great, granted. The breakfast excellent: granola and French toast world class. This is really what would be called in the UK a "restaurant with rooms" the designation "hotel" falling foul of the trades descriptions act. Staff were all fine. I agree with the consensus here which is visit bistrot and beacon hill but stay in a more orthodox hotel as Boston is small enough.

review_title: Expected more from the only Pan Pacific hotel in the United States...
review_text:
My wife and i stayed here during thanksgiving weekend 2011. The room was nice but did have some drawbacks. The major one was air leakage in our room. There was a beautiful view of the space needle from an angle but during the night, coldness emanated from the window area despite use of curtains. I set the temperature at 71 during the nighttime but upon waking found room temp to be 62f to 63f every morning, which was very cold and also drying on my sinuses. Hotel didn't have a vaporizer/humidifier for use which is not surprising. They did offer an air purifier, which is useless, and did not offer anything that would help or change of room. 
Other things that should have been there, especially for this caliber hotel and price range: make up/shaving mirror, jets in tub, scale, better toiletries/amenities in bathroom (they could learn a lot from other hotels like fairmonts around the States or especially the Langham hotels around the world).
Probably will not stay here again unless major upscaling is done. But they did have a beautifully decorated lobby and friendly staff. It was also nice to have Whole Foods nearby for snacks and drinks.

review_title: This is where you stay in Seattle !
review_text: Read all the reviews and settled on the Pan Pacific Seattle and was not disappointed. Will at the front desk allowed us to upgrade to a king deluxe corner room for $20 more and it was fantastic. Rooms are clean and very well maintained. Whole foods adjacent to the hotel didn't hurt either. Would we stay here again.... Definitely !
Great hotel and good location close to belltown and emp. Can walk taxi or monorail most places. I definitely recommend.

Great hotel strategically placed between Westlake and the Space Needle. Some rooms have the best views for New Years Eve fireworks in the city. 
It still concerns me that bellhops only bring your bags as far as the front desk.

Unbelievable as it seems I had never heard of this place but had "won" a nights stay from an auction I had attended so decided to spend the night while also attending a play in Seattle. It was absolutely fabulous! A bit pricey but well worth the money when you take into consideration the friendly can-do staff, very unique rooms and all the amenities that you receive.
