review_title: Great relief in time of need
review_text: My husband had a stem cell transplant stayed at hotel for 23 days. Did not have to worry about a thing. The free shuttle was a great relief. Took me to and from the hospital each and every day. That took a lot of my plate. Having a gym and pool was also a great stress reliever. Breakfast in the morning to start your day off is a welcome gift! Staff was friendly, helpful, and understanding. The hospital rate was also helpful. Thank you! Only thing I would change is to a have a Resturant in the hotel.
hotel_name: Hampton Inn & Suites Boston Crosstown Center

review_text:
Booked on the strength of reviews I found this Holiday Inn to be ok only. Staff were a bit distant, as is the location - although they provide a free shuttle to Andrew metro station, which is actually only 8mins walk away anyway. Town isn't too far, but it does take up time so bear it in mind. 
Rooms a little tired, lifts old and slow, but free breakfast, wifi, coffee all make it value for money.

My husband and I stayed at this property for a wedding for a friend. The hotel is wonderful! And is a GREAT location-very close to many attractions downtown Seattle. All were in walking distance. The staff was VERY friendly, and always spoke to us when we were coming and going. The free Starbucks coffee and nightly wine receptions were wonderful. When we asked about transportation back to the airport, they secured a town care for us that was less expensive than a taxi. The only negative I would have to say is that the housekeeping staff woke us up early everyday! The walls are really thin in the rooms. i could hear what my neighbors were saying. The beds were uncomfortable, and the rooms were slightly dated. The DM emailed me after my survey, and ssaid they are going to renovate soon. I would definitely stay here again in future trips to the area. I'm going to Chicago soon, and will definitely look at the Kimpton properties in the area! Overall it was a really nice place!
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: I loved this hotel so much I want to move in!
review_text: This was my first experience with Hotel Monaco and I was more than pleased. It was a little piece of heaven each and every day of my stay in Seattle. Loved, loved, loved my chitah bathrobe. The staff could not have more pleasant and helpful. My bed was like sleeping on a cloud...I will definitely be back
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: Typical Hampton Inn Property but Bad Location & Poor Service
review_text:
Typically stay at this Hampton Inn when the rates are reasonable (especially compared to other hotels in the city); however, this is my last time staying here. 
The property, rooms and typical Hampton qualities were all fine. Nothing to write home about but comfort level was there...
The location and service made me not want to return. This hotel is adjacent to Boston Medical Center...I'm not sure if it is a busy season or what but the ambulance/police/fire sirens are non-stop... all through the night/morning. If you need a 5 AM alarm... stay here. Typically I request a high floor but my arrival wasn't until 11 PM and I received a room on the 3rd floor... terrible. 
Additionally, the Wireless Internet wasn't working. When I called to ask if they would reset the router they said that it was my computer issue. Next, some random man knocked on my door without my request and offered to help against my protest. His suggestion was to restart the computer (thanks, because I didn't already try that). When that didn't work he gave me a number to call... so I can sit on hold and talk to your service tech. No, thanks. 
Never again...
hotel_name: Hampton Inn & Suites Boston Crosstown Center

review_text:
Supposedly built in a former bank- welcoming cheerful staff- room 607 is large with Queen bed, no view- good small bath with lighted shave mirror and hairdryer; good bath amenities- T V and purchase films, the latter expensive-
Avoid breakfast as it's too pricey; cross the street to the Seattle Brew or turn left to Starbucks- the hotel serves coffee in the Libby until 9 AM and has a 5 PM wine tasting with snacks which is free- only blocks from Pikes Place-
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: Amazing that a hotel with such comfort and amenities exists just seconds away from SEA-TAC airport. Was skeptical of the glowing reviews, now a believer.
Great place to stay except for the coffee in the restaurant... That is my only complaint...fantastic service
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text:
I added the $1 breakfast deal. In truth, the breakfast voucher is only worth $11 credit in the restaurant. I had egg whites, tomato, toast, juice, and coffee. The cost was $24! With my breakfast voucher I still owed $14... This was NOT a good deal. 
(the hotel did remove the full charge for the breakfast after complaining, but I did not use my other two vouchers for my other two nights stay after my first costly experiance). 
The hotel is great, the restaurant is not.
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: A super little place - staff were so helpful
review_text: My husband and I were stuck when our flight was cancelled because of hurricane Irene. The staff in the hotel were so helpful and friendly they made sure we were able to contact our airline etc. It has a great a location (backing onto a retail park with many goood stores). It is close to the metro and easy to find. Breakfast was good and plentiful and the warm cookies a treat in the evening. $5 transportation to the airport and the site seeing trolley stops every morning. A good little find

Came to Seattle for a football game. Hotel was perfect location close enough to walk yet also close enough to the city center. Loved the hotel we had a pet goldfish on our room throughout the stay, the staff was very accommodating . The only downfall was the bar ran out of our type of beer one night but that was completely stocked the next day!
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: Great hotel in a great location. We could only stay for one night, but will definitely be coming back! Great coffee at the kiosk in the lobby too.

We wanted to be close to pike place so this locale was great and valet was 24 hour access so we could go out to Ballard ave for dinner and hen come back later. Clean room and great experience overall.
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: Most comfortable atmosphere with exceptional staff.
review_text:
The Monaco is always one of our favorites. The staff is friendly and helpful and the rooms are very comfortable. It's central location is fantastic. 
You can rest assured you will have a wonderful stay in this Kimpton hotel.
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: The hotel is located a bit far northwest of downtown so walking was to town was not as easy as we had originally thought. Hotel was beautiful and service was exceptional. Our room was on the corner so was oddly shaped and a bit small. Bathroom opened up to room to observe downtown view. We got some great snapshots of both the sunrise and sunset. Starbucks (next door) and Whole Foods (downstairs)were very handy to have close by. Overall experience was nice. We would definitely recommend.

review_title: Clean near airport and the T.
review_text: Very clean good value , short walk to subway. Cons: no pool or spa and nothing around hotel to do or cab to. Not for family but great overnite stay.

We had a short stay in Boston and wanted something convenient and relatively inexpensive. This place fit the bill and I would not hesitate to stay here again. Love that the entire hotel is non smoking. The shuttle to mass transit was a nice extra. Our room was clean and comfortable ... but relatively small ( we chose a room with one queen bed). The hotel was in the middle of renovations when we stayed so parking was at a premium. Overall a good experience.

My fiancÃ© and I stayed in a King-sized corner room at Pan Pacific recently and were very happy with our experience. The staff is very accommodating - they happily met every request we made and were prepared with restaurant suggestions and directions. The only downside to the Pan Pacific is the price - it's a bit expensive so we were only able to enjoy the hotel for one evening. Also, the traffic is a bit noisy at night, but us certainly not bad. We definitely plan on returning... once we have some extra money.

review_title: Perfect if you can afford it.
review_text:
We stayed at this hotel on points and were very pleasantly surprised.
It has location (close to everything by foot and accessible to very cool electric trains if not), service, decor and an absolutely fabulous lobby where to chill. 
Rooms were clean and well equipped; if you are lucky, you'll get a room with space needle's view.
Bonus! Has a healthy supermarket below in case you forget anything or feel like an extra-healthy breakfast to offset your holiday over- indulgence ;)

We love kimptons and we enjoyed our stay here , but we wish Our dog was with us and that there was a pool or rooftop hot tub.. Wine hour is always great. The rooms were clean and modern but the beds were not so comfy. You are a few blocks away from the fish market and some great restaurants (Go to "list" for happy hour- half off great food and beverages inc. Wine bottles). Make sure you join kimpton rewards!
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text:
We stayed two nights at Maxwell at a great rate from their website. The service is great. We arrived early, at 11 am, and not only did they have a room but a free upgrade to a Space Needle view. The staff also gave good advice for restaurants and arranged someone to drop us off at the train station for free.
The room was very good and we had no problem with noise as mentioned in other reviews, but the hotel was not that busy. We walked everywhere and found the location to be ideal in a mixed residential / commercial neighborhood with lots of record stores and good food. It is about 1.5 miles to Pike Place Market but an easy walk we did 3 times.
Overall the hotel presents a terrific value with great service over the upscale chains downtown. I highly recommend for leisure travelers in the area.

review_title: Cool place to stay in a cool city
review_text: I picked this hotel based on its location and all the glowing Trip Advisor reviews. It did not disappoint. I emailed ahead and asked for a room with a view of the Space Needle and they came through even though the place was pretty full of folks there for a film festival. When we checked in, the gal at the front desk told us what was going on and said not to hesitate to let them know if it got noisy but we never head much even though we were close to the elevator. The location can't be beat. We really appreciated the coffee (and tea) machine and fridge in the room, as well as the free WiFi. Overall, a very hip but classy hotel.

review_title: Charming hotel. Great service. Excellent restaurant and good location.
review_text: We loved our stay here. The hotel is small enough to feel personal. The room had personality. It was not a sterile, big-city type of place.
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: Stay here you wont regret it!
review_text: Stayed at a four season hotel then moved to this hotel. Very clean rooms and friendly serive. I highly recommend it.
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: This is a wondeful hotel - great location - very clean and so friendly. Shane at the front desk really cares and that is rare - so many front desk people just go through the motions..... Last name....credit card... Not here - this is refreshing amazing care!
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: Double Tree quality but a little overpriced.
review_text:
This was the only area hotel I could find with rooms available for college move in week. Price was rather steep at over $200 per night. On top of this you pay $30 per day parking. Sadly it does not even include a free continental breakfast. 
There are positives though. The hotel is well maintained. I previously stayed here about 15 years ago and they have kept the property updated. The room was spacious and actually was a suite with a nice sitting area and a separate bedrooom. We were on a high floor with a nice river and city view. 
They do have a pool and exercise room but we didn't have time to use them. 
My only complaint is the high room rate with nothing extra incuded such as parking, breakfast or internet. 
While not a problem for us since we used our car the hotel is not near any T train stop. I suspect they will shuttle you to a stop but I didn't ask.

We had a weekend getaway and decided to stay at Pan pacific as I have really fond memories of this brand. Everything was excellent except the location is a bit isolated but having wholefood right below is totally awesome! Room was a decent size, had a good view at rhe space needle and the tub fits for 2 was awesome! It's much closer for you to walk to the space needle but if you are going downtown shopping, you would probably drive. I would say there's always room for improvement but I like this hotel and this is always the first few places I check when I go to Seattle. For the price of this place, it is a deal compare to a lot of downtown hotels but you are getting the same excellent qualities like those ones.

review_title: Good service, clean rooms, three criticisms...
review_text: We were happy to find a comfort sleeper instead of a spring sofa bed in the suite but it was too firm. the bed was very soft, but comfortable. The view on the Charles was pretty. The bathrooms lack a fan/ vent. The room was very dry. Our son knocked over a ceramic lamp shade in one of the hangouts, but since we were ordering food, they told us not to worry about it. Having said that, skip the tabouli- old and oily.

Worth the stay. It is right above whole foods so when traveling and just need a salad and quiet night after a busy day it is perfect. The staff is always very helpful and polite. Walking to everything in the city. And a 15 dollar cab ride to the best gelato in the western US: D'Ambrosio Gelato in Ballard on Ballard Ave.

I booked this lodge months before an anticipated stay in the Seattle area, based partly on a trip Advisor rating of 10 best places to stay in the country. When I arrived, I was told they didn't have a room for me. And got shuttled off to a Doubletree, to a room with a view of a parking lot. I am very disappointed!!

review_title: Less than expected for a 4 star hotel at well over $300 per night.
review_text: Seattle is expensive. We were prepared for that on our visit. We travel for pleasure about once a quarter and like to stay in the nicest places possible. We booked this hotel based on reviews from Trip Advisor. We paid rack rate of $305 per night plus taxes plus $39 per night for parking. We have stayed in mega suites in Vegas for less. My complaints are : had to request tea (coffee available in room but had to call and ask for tea), after returning to our room at 2pm after sigh-seeing, had to request housekeeping, no evening turn down service and my husband ordered 2 diet cokes from room service and it was $12. (no where within a mile to buy a diet coke) this hotel is identical to the Intercontinental in Atlanta we stay in for half the price. There is nothing wrong with the hotel except they don't miss an opportunity to price gauge its customers.

review_title: Incredible solitude and peace inside a hectic and busy urban experience
review_text: Laney and her boots, Joey and Elvis, and John and the gang made our stay very special. They are special!

Handy to Boston University, great view, wonderful little suite with hot cookies too. Tried to charge for internet which is free for gold members of their loyalty club. Really nice fitness center...would stag here again...great little breakfast too...
Decent hotel. Good location. Room size is a bit small but clean overall. Would definetly stay here again

review_title: Great location - friendly staff and great bar/restaurant
review_text:
I stayed here back in June but wanted to make sure I submitted a review:) this place was great. The staff were very friendly and helpful.
 I found that the rooms were nice, a little musty smelling but comfortable
I ate at the restaurant one evening and found the food and drink to be very tasty. 
There is a Starbucks just downstairs to the right (really convenient )
hotel_name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Boston - Downtown

review_text: We were given a free room upgrade, the room was big & very clean. We had a fridge in the room which was very handy for drinks. Bed was big & comfy. Bathroom was very nice, clean & excellent shower. Staff were very friendly & helpful.

The hotel is old and a bit dark, easily the worst Doubletree that I've stayed in. I was very disappointed to find that I not only received a ground floor room (my profile distinctly indicates I prefer upper floors), but my room doubled as a conference room, having a board table with about 8 chairs. The staff was friendly enough if I could find someone, as that was a challenge. Considering the rate I paid, I could have easily stayed at another property with a much nicer facility. I wouldn't recommend this hotel, too many other nicer places to stay.
hotel_name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Boston - Downtown

review_title: Good value, great service and great locale -- dated bathroom
review_text:
We stayed here for an overnight because we got a great rate -- under $200 for a Friday night. The service was excellent. The front desk was nice and very helpful and the bell staff were great. 
The hotel is walking distance to almost everything and very near the orange line T at Tufts medical campus. It's also only a 10-minute walk to Downtown Crossing.
The hotel is near the Boston Common, theaters, Newbury Street, Washington Street shopping and Chinatown. You can also walk to the North End in about 20 minutes.
The rooms are good sized for the city but the bathroom was a bit small and dated -- lots of cultured marble and a small toilet. BUT everything was very clean.
If you are in the market for a good location and a clean and comfortable room, I'd check this out. It's not luxurious, but it was a great place for the price. We will stay here again!
hotel_name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Boston - Downtown

review_title: Paid near $400 Inc taxes for a night for what?!
review_text: Stayed here one night at just over $400 for the night and can only assume that I paid that for the location (which was ok but not fantastic). Has a very tatty and old feel about it ... And the old is not quaint. It's in need of renovation. Rooms were old, grubby carpets, newest thing was probably the tv. I couldn't wait to leave. The service was ok and friendly, but if going to Boston, find somewhere else to stay!
hotel_name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Boston - Downtown

review_text: Our room with 2 doubles beds was small but adequate. Front desk staff was nice. THe lobby bar is awful and bartender was rude. I asked to watCh a game on espnU and he said cable messed up and no service. When I asked him where I could go watch a game he knew of nowhere, nor did anyone on staff. I finally found a close by pizza place that had espnU and saw my team Win big. I hate that a big hotel like this that caters to tourists offer so few channels and bar amenities. Staff can ve short and rude but that is a Boston thing.
hotel_name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Boston - Downtown

review_text:
We stayed at the Fairmont for thanksgiving weekend. The room was spacious, clean and in great condition. The lobby is very busy and can feel impersonal but we weren't looking for a personal relationship. All the staff we deal with were great and very helpful. The deal we got was fantastic through Expedia and I thought the stay was great value. 
It is also very nice to have access to a pool in the hotel.

Stayed there during family weekend because could not find a hotel under 300 per night and was a little worried...but ended up pleasantly surprised. Rooms were modern and clean, bathrooms were on the small side and needed renovating..overall great value.

review_title: Great place for a family to stay
review_text: My family stayed here mid-June. I cannot think of a better place to stay- location is ideal. Several blocks to the waterfront, several blocks to the monorail, Pikes, shopping. A short cab to Safeco. Very attentive to my entire family. Also looked like a good place to stay for the business traveler too.
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: Happy with our stay here, not a hotel with pizazz, but not a massive building, a comfy bed in a good location and at a relatively good price that reflects other uses of building.

review_title: Short of other Kimpton hotels, stay at the W across the street
review_text: Room was never cleaned, needed to request from front desk. Housekeeping woke us up on the day of check out. Overall, hotel was short of my typical Kimpton experience -- very disappointing. Just stay across the street at the W.
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: Staff seems preoccupied, did not feel welcome. Location is fine, rooms have thin walls so sleeping may be a problem. All in all an 'ok' place to stay in Boston.

Room was on the small end, but for the price and location not a bad place to stay. They have listened to previous reviews and added a shower caddy to help with the limited space. If you are staying for a few nights on leisure and looking for an area with good shopping, look no further. I would not recommend for business travel as there is no where to "set up shop." I would stay here again

Great location next to T stop. Arrived early and our room wasnt quite ready. But the gentleman at the desk offered us an upgraded room on a higher floor with a city view! All the staff were friendly. Very impressed overall
hotel_name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Boston - Downtown

review_text: My wife and I stayed here in jan 2011. Great location everywhere walkable. But subway next door if needed. Staff were incredibly helpful to us, and very friendly.
hotel_name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Boston - Downtown

review_text: We took a ten month and three year old and the hotel is chic yet kid friendly. Toy box with free toy upon check in and kids welcome bag help. About four blocks from Pike's place so an easy walk. We got a fish in our room to watch during our stay and there was a DVD player which came in handy. As usual of kimpton there was a helpful and amazing staff
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel

review_title: Nice place to stay in downtown Seattle
review_text: We stayed here when we spent the night in Seattle on our way to Alaska via Holland America cruiselines. Its in a great location downtown and offered us a great experience into Seattle on our first ever visit there. Highly recommended.
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: I stay here on business, once a month for 5 days at a time. Always a pleasure and NO hassle!
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: Love this hotel for business or personal travel. They had to replace the phone in my room and delivered a box of chocolates to apologize. Also love that Kimpton in touch program gives you a $10 minibar credit and free wifi.
hotel_name: Hotel Monaco Seattle - a Kimpton Hotel

review_text: Everything was perfect. We will definitely return!!!

Spectacular service from arrival to departure. Valet greets you with towel and water bottle after a morning jog. Great dining at shuckers. Easy location to all major Seattle sights. We even walked to game at Safeco Field

review_title: Reliable wi-fi would make it 5 stars across the board.
review_text: We stayed at the Fairmont Olympic Hotel for four nights around Labor Day. We were very happy with the hotel. The location is very convenient for the ball parks, for downtown attractions, and for the ferry system. The housekeeping staff was superb. Our housekeeper noticed one burned out light bulb in a multi-bulb fixture and had it serviced immediately. The housekeeping department was also very quick to clean the room upon request. Our 9th floor executive suite was right across from the elevators. We were pleasantly surprised to find that we heard no elevator or hallway noise. The room was very quiet. We knew from standing in the hallway that a constantly screaming baby was staying in the next-door room, but in our room we never heard it. The bed was exceedingly comfortable. The only bad thing about the hotel was the wi-fi, which was unreliable at best. We ended up using the ethernet connection. This was fine as wi-fi was included in our group rate but if you are not in a group you may have to pay for wi-fi, and it is unacceptable. The hotel could be characterized as slightly faded granduer, however, we found the very friendly and unfailingly helpful staff, the quiet room and the great location more than made up for the few scuff marks and dated decor, and we will happily stay here again.

We got this hotel on Priceline for a great deal. The hotel is right in the middle of downtown Boston. You can walk to almost anything. Great rooms and service. Parking was very reasonable. The bathrooms could be nicer / bigger but overall an excellent stay.

review_title: Lovely, grand hotel in excellent location, but privacy an issue in suite.
review_text:
The facility and amenities are lovely, and the service was topnotch. The location is terrific, and you can walk to many sights and excellent restaurants, BUT we were surprised and dismayed to discover that the doors between the bedroom and the living room were not solid. In the photos, they look like French doors with curtains, when they actually are just frames with sheer fabric in the center. This means that there is no sound barrier and the light coming through the sheer fabric leaves no privacy even for dressing. Although it would be fine for a couple, we had thought the suite would suffice for us and our college-age daughter, but it 
really did not work well.
I would caution others who might make the same mistake. We would have been better off in two rooms--either there or some place less expensive.

Stayed here for holiday while visiting family. Pricelined the place. Room was not bad. Parking is 32. Dollars a night. Valet is 45. Noisy neighbors kept us awake. You could sit in bathroom and here next room through the vent. Not a place I would recommend or stay at again.
My friend and I stated at hotel 140 lastnight. everything was great . The room was clean and spacious. The hotel staff was very welcoming and friendly and we will be back again.

We had reserved a suite room so that we would have a pull-out for the kids. When we got to the room, the pullout was broken, and in it's place was a loveseat-no pullout. Our room looked out onto a parking lot that became a party central at night, it didn't break up until 3 am. Also had trouble getting billed for the roll away that they offered to us.
hotel_name: DoubleTree by Hilton Hotel Boston - Downtown

review_text: Classic great hotel. Rooms are larger than most old hotels and it is wonderfully maintained. For the business traveler, the rooms are not as well designed as a more modern hotel but it is a classy place.

Hotel is beautiful. Many positives. Would stay again. Noise from street is loud. Other reviews mention same issue. Windows are old and do not block traffic sounds. Schucks Oyster Bar is great. Staff is top notch. If price is the major concern Fairmont isn't the way to go. If quality and location are your desire this is a winner.

review_title: A top hotel in a top location
review_text:
Our cruise ship stopped in Seattle so we stayed for four days so we could take in what Seattle had to offer a fabulous city, we loved the markets, the needle, the Boeing Factory, the Aquarium was awesome and the Olympic has the best Concierge in the world. 
An excellent stay, not sure of the cost per night as we were on a voucher but it was worth the money. So central to all we wanted to do. 
Top marks in every way.

Before i even start my review, I have to address the previous post "Nickel and Dimed." First, some of costs cited are not correct. Parking was $32. In-room wireless was $9.95. And there was free coffee in the room. Second, parking rates in Boston are generally very high. (My office building 100 yards from the Hyatt gets $38 per day, more if you stay overnight.) This is a hotel in the business area of the city and while we may not like the fees, they are pro forma in this type of hotel. If you do not want this, then choose a Hampton Inn type hotel or stay in the 'burbs and you will be much happier. 
I had a great 1 night stay at this hotel. Room was clean, spacious and very well appointed. Every staff person I encountered went above and beyond. I was there bc I had no power in my home for 5 days and I could not have found a nicer place to stay. There are many nice restaurants in the area and the theater district is steps away. The hotel is also on the edge of Chinatown, which does get a little iffy late at night. Just be aware of your surroundings and you'll be fine.

Hotel was decent though obvious that the hotel needs some updating in the bathrooms, public areas and elevators. Room was average size, good place for a conference. Very good food. At the right price, well worth it
Stayed three days. Room was dated. Bed was very comfortable. Service was excellent. William is a great concierge. I would stay again.

Stayed for one night. Great location but quality of room wasn't worth the price. Also no wifi; which I haven't experienced at any of the other hotels I sttayed at in Boston. Room service for breakfast was poor. Burnt soggy toast and tasteless homefries.
Not a bad experience but for the money you can do much better in the theatre district.

review_title: Nice location and very good staff.
review_text: The staff were very friendly and eager to help in anyway with directions and dining suggestions. Our room was very clean. The location is a short walk from the market and minutes from city transportation. I would give ten stars for this hotel on staff alone. We were very pleased with or stay.

Went to Boston for Labor Day Weekend. I could not have asked for a more perfect hotel. The location was smack in the middle of the city so I was able to walk everywhere. The concierge was so helpful as well. I was traveling alone so she recommended the best restaurants and hot spots for each night. She also directed me to various tourist attractions. I had one issue with the AC and I called the front desk. Josephine directed me to Sasha who had someone up to my room in 15 mnutes. They upgraded me to the business plan for the inconvenience. Josephine followed up by calling the room to make sure all of my needs were met. The breakfast was great, the hotel was clean, rooms were comfortable and the staff was beyond helpful. I would never stay anywhere else and once again Hyatt continues to impress me!

review_title: Love this place! A bit expensive and no wi-Fi! But, everything else is great!
review_text: Lovely hotel. Great service from the front door man, the receptionist, the restaurant and from the person getting a taxi. I will definitely come back here again. Plus, it is so close to the freedom trail. And, the downtown shopping area, Quincy market, shed aquarium. A big negative is that there is no wi-Fi!!!!!! Why can't this hotel just give it for free when I paid $400 a night.
Housekeeping doesn't come close to acceptable. Front desk is a bunch of lost youngsters without a clue, this place has lost its footing and should be avoided.

The hotel was very nice. We had a gift certifcate that we had purchased in a package at a school auction.
The rooms weren't anything spectacular. Just a typical nice hotel room.
The location was superb and we were able to walk everywhere we wanted to go.
Baker parking was expensive but very polite and let us leave our car for the day we checked out so we wouldn't have to move it to another garage.
Overall it was a nice fun weekend but I wouldn't pay the prices they ask for what you get.

review_title: A rained out sox game turned to an awesome trip to Bahston
review_text: Let me start this out by saying that we are a group of people who all work in the hospitality industry (in a small luxury hotel as well as a 4 diamond resort) who were traveling for a red sox game which unfortunately got rained out. Upon arrival we were greeted by a very professional and curtiorus staff that were friendly and genuinely interested in making sure that we enjoyed our stay not only in the hotel but in Boston as well. Not long after we got to the hotel we found out the sox game- was cancelled and the concierge staff jumped at giving us other options of things to do and where to eat. Edison the Front Desk Manager went out of his way to accommodate us. We forgot a camera in the car but Mike Collins who was part of the valet staff went out of his way to help us get the camera back and was very helpful with getting us to the nearest T station. Sam the bellman was also very friendly and always wanted to know how we were doing and how are stay was going. We will see you in August!

Rooms were great. Bed really comfortable but decor in bathroom somewhat dated. Location is good for exploring Boston. Gym and pool facilities good. 
Would expect free wifi in this class of hotel. Staff were efficient but not particularly friendly ( apart from concierge who was great)

This hotel is not a cheap stay by any means..and after paying a pretty decent nightly rate, they will nickle and dime you for EVERY little request that you may find comes standard in other hotels. ($15 room refrigerator delivery fee, $15 for one hour of internet in the business center, $16 for a crappy continental breakfast, self parking is over $30 per day, etc). The hotel does not have a shuttle service either. When asking the hotel staff questions, it seems each person will have a different, inconsistent response as well. Very discouraging. Good location& good if money is no issue.

metro a 5 minutes a pied (ou navette gratuite si vous le voulez) qui vous emmene en 12 min dans le centre de Boston. Hotel situe juste a cote d'une autoroute. pratique mais un peu bruyant mais sans plus. Bon compromis pour une famille de 4 personnes. Pdj correct. Parking gratuit. Il faut manger a boston centre, rien dans le quartier.

review_text:
Das Hotel ist am Rande der Stadt, besitzt ausreichend kostenfreie ParkplÃ¤tze und bietet ein gutes Preis-/LeistungsverhÃ¤ltnis.
Das Personal war sehr zuvorkommend und hilfreich bei Fragen jeder Art.
Zum Zeitpunkt unserer Ãœbernachtungen wurde das Hotel renoviert. Ich glaube, die alten und etwas verwohnten RÃ¤ume gehÃ¶ren nun der Vergangenheit an. Sie waren nicht mehr zeitgemÃ¤ÃŸ, genauso wie die alten RÃ¶hrenfernseher.
Das FrÃ¼hstÃ¼ck war etwas enttÃ¤uschend fÃ¼r HIE und schon vor Ende der FrÃ¼hstÃ¼ckszeit wurde abgerÃ¤umt.
Um die Ecke gibt es einige Restaurants, einen Supermarkt und das Boston General Hospital ist in 5 Minuten zu erreichen.

We arrived for a weekend stay at the hotel. The hotel is a pretty short walk from South Station, Boston's major transit station, and had an enjoyable walk over. We were checked in by a Ms Maggie, who was professional and did her job well enough, but it was a series of motions rather than an engaging conversation. The rooms are nicely decorated and we had a pretty view of the city; we had a two bed room. Everything was flawless; the housekeeping staff had paid a lot of attention of detail.
We went downstairs to the Concierge Desk, and were greeted by a Mr Mike, a Mr Stephan, and a Ms Susan. Each were friendly and extremely knowledgable. We had some pretty non-standard questions about the city and bars, but they were able to help us set everything up. A+ to all three individuals. They were also able to give us information for the tours we wanted to take, the places we wanted to go, and gave us suggestions for further exploring. As we headed out, Mr Steven, the bellman, was extraordinarily friendly and offered to help us find where to go and how to get there. He even remembered us later in the night when we checked back in -- they were doing a simple check for keys, which made us feel a lot safer --and he not only remembered us but remembered a joke we had made with him. Kudos to that fine gentleman.
We also had a chance to dine in the restuarant. For breakfast, which was an excellent buffet, Mr Andjul helped us and was extremely friendly and an excellent host. A better server could not be asked for, save for Ms Alyson, who served us at dinner. Both made enjoyable small talk, recognized us when we came back, answered our questions, and couldn't have been nicer. Dinner was spectacular, and I couldn't more gladly recommend the creme brulee.
Overall, we were blown away. The service was exceptional and memorable - hence why I can name names and give examples. The room was beautiful, the location excellent (it was only about 1/2 hour walk to anywhere we wanted to go) and the food fantastic. You couldn't find a better place to stay.

review_title: Worst customer service and shoddy rooms.
review_text:
Got this hotel on priceline. This property is definitely not 4 stars. I was ill and wanted to see if I could check in early. The first lady at the front desk rudely said check-in is at 3PM. She didn't even offer to check as I was coughing up a storm. 
So I came back to check-in at 3pm and the second associate was just as rude. I understand that she was having a bad day, but don't take it out on customers, like me.
I went to the room and found a tube TV. Is this circa 1999? Come on Hilton. 
Also, the room was really dusty and made my cough worst. The dust was soooo bad that I went to the hyatt ( I was scouring around the city to check in early because I was really ill) . 
Then when I went to check out literally after a few minutes I checked in, I asked to get a statement. The rude associate said she couldn't give me one. Even the manager was rude to me. 
This is the first and last time I'll support the Hilton brand and will make every effort to share this experience with everyone.

review_title: Modern comfort close to the Space Needle and Seattle Center
review_text: What a great room! Super clean and comfy! It's a bit far from Pike Place, but minutes away from the Space Needle. Wonderfully friendly and helpful staff. Would definitely stay there again. Be sure to head over to Peso's on Queen Anne for a scrumptious breakfast! Just ask the front desk to point you in the right direction!

We stayed at the Cedarbrook Lodge for the first 3 nights of our vacation and tour down to San Francisco via some of the Northwest National Parks.
The hotel was great - all we expected it to be - not disappointed at all. It has a great location close to the airport (although you'd never know, being secluded in almost a nature reserve); the shuttle to the airport and the Seattle transit were great; the free snacks, fruit and ice cream in the communal areas were really welcome; and the breakfast, if a little limited, was included and great quality.
My only slight complaint was the price of the restaurant/bar menu - very pricey.
Otherwise we had a great time and would definitely recommend / return!

Clean and comfortable. Good location near to Common and shopping. Quite expensive, but what really bothered me was all the potential extras. Fridge- $15, WiFi additional charges. The list goes on. I do expect to pay extra for certain things, but in this price bracket not everything. Would look for an alternative hotel nearby next time.

review_title: Good hotel but watch out for sneaky charges..
review_text:
We stayed here just after Thanksgiving and were given a massive room, which was pretty modern, clean and comfortable. The location is great and convenient for South Station and Quincy Hall.
My only gripe is that the hotel charged us $16 for using the mini bar when we never touched it. We were not told about this charge when we checked out and I only just noticed it on my credit card statement. To be fair to the hotel, they cancelled the charge as soon as I called but I didn't appreciate having to sort this out. Not what O expect from a Hilton and we won't be staying here again.

We stayed there from 7/5-7/10. We were on the 21st floor and liked our room. The hotel always smelled nice and looked clean. The staff we encountered were wonderful. We had 2 minor issues the day we checked in where our room keys did not work and someone had to come twice to fix the problem and there was a mixup where the person at the valet area left our luggage in the trunk of the car instead of bringing it up. Because of those things happening we were given a $150 voucher to use at the hotel restaurant. We liked all the meals we had at the restaurant and the 2 nights we did room service. We found the hotel to be pretty quiet as well. We had our dog with us and it is close to Boston Common so she had a nice place to do her business. A lot of attractions were in walking distance and sometimes if we were too tired to walk most cab rides cost about $10 from there. We would stay here again.

We stayed here for the 4th of July weekend. We booked through expedia and we got a good rate. I must admit I was a bit disappointed in the overall stay. Front desk checknin staff was not cordial or hospitable at all. Our room was small unlike other reviews. We were on the 22 fl but no corner, so be aware all the rooms are not spacious. Location was good as we walked almost everywhere. So to sum this all up, this stay was just ok, nothing special. We would not stay here again, but liking or not liking this hotel really depend on your individual expectations in a hotel.

review_title: Front desk lady lied to me, so did the hotel manager
review_text:
Today is July 1st 2011. I had to download the app to my iPhone and write this review, because I was so upset that I was lied to by the front desk lady, as well as the manger. When I confronted them with their lies, they had the IQs to create more blatant lies. 
I stayed at the corner room on the 16th floor, it was. Good size room with 2 beds. I asked for another rollaway bed, I had done this at the Marriott Copley square hotel where the room was much smaller. The front desk lady ( extremely unpleasant) said 'no , it's a fire harzard'. I knew it was a lie, because Boston rules And regulations should applied go both hotels. I asked for proof of of the rules, she could not provide. Her manager called , he said it was not Boston reggulation, but hyatt's policy, however, this is a policy he can not show me ( a customer), when asked why a hotel has some secret policy which is not open to customer, he again changed to another story, saying something like the maid does not want to have a rollaway bed because it is too crowded. How strange? I told him this room is 30% larger than the one I stayed at the marriot Boston, if it was not crowded at the Marriott ( they always brought the rollaway when asked) , why it should be crowded at the Haytt? Here's his answer: ' you can go back to the Marriott' 
So for those of you who've traveled around, here's your taste of the professionalism at the Hyatt Boston.
I am extreme upset, but this is the July 4th , leaving is not an easy option, my only choice is get on here to write my review.

review_title: Nice enough but not worth the money
review_text: Great location, big rooms but overall a bit disappointing especially for the price. Shower head was cheap plastic hose attached to the wall. Would not stay here again.

I don't know where the good service reviews came from. This place was possibly the worst hotel experience I've ever had. A co worker of mine and myself were just casually chatting in my room when security showed up and said they had received complaints. Complaints, plural? On two people? This was comical. Until this second time the security came, and said we were being evicted for excessive complaints. Since when does the word of some crazy neighbor mean eviction? I had to pack my bags and be escorted by security to speak with the manager, who talked down to me and didnt seem to care about my side of the story. Move my room if there was a problem, but dont threatened with police intervention when I state how ridiculous the experience was. This place is unprofessional to professional people and a horrible place to stay, I'm glad this happened because I will never stay at another hyatt again. Nice work customer service.

Simply terrible service at this high priced, poorly managed establishment. The rooms are pretty standard fair, not bad. Be prepared to be nickel and dimed throughout your stay and dont bother trying to request or discuss anything with their incompetent staff unless you enjoy talking with people who could care less about hospitality. 
There are plenty of options in Boston, avoid this place like the plague.

Easy access to tourism. Great jumping off point to explore the city. Rooms are nice but not amazing. Restaurant a little expensive and neighborhood is pretty abandoned on the weekend (during the day)
Would stay here again.

In ottima posizione per visitare a piedi Seattle e muoversi in ogni direzione. E' un vecchio albergo bello e con il fascino del tempo passato ma con le limitazioni che esso comporta: un ascensore unico e piccolo e una camera veramente piccola come piccolo il bagno e un numero di prese elettriche in camera insufficiente. Presente pero' la rete wifi gratuita. Buono il servizio e la pulizia possibilitÃ  di parcheggio cin servizio vallet.

I am a Kimpton Loyalty member and I am a loyal Kimpton fan. In a country that prides itself on its customer service, as an Englishman abroad I have to say that the service offered at their hotels in unsurpassed! This is my third stay at The Onyx in five years and to be greeted by name on arrival made me feel immediately at home! I don't leave until tomorrow, but I just wanted to say a huge thank you to both the Lauren's, Jon and all at the front desk, a particular mention for Kevin whom I met at the Nine Zero last year...quite superb at his job and real gent to boot! This had yet again been my home from home and a great one to come back to each day! Well done Team Onyx....you rock!!

review_title: Holy cannoli! I've never been treated with such amazing customer service!
review_text:
I booked our room through the Internet and put in a note stating that it was my 4 year anniversary. My husband and I arrived and were informed that we were upgraded to the penthouse room. That would have been more than enough for us, however we opened the door to our room and disscovered that it had been decorated with rose petals EVERYWHERE, chocolate covered strawberries, and a bottle of champagne!!!
The Onyx has clearly done their job in hiring the best staff in Boston. Everybody is knowledgable, helpful and extremely kind.
We didn't think it could get much better until we decided to order room service at 1am. After a very short wait, our meal arrived and we were told it was "on the house!!!". Really, WHAT HOTEL DOES THAT??? Oh, and by the way, the meal was fantastic!
If you want to be treated like royalty stay at the Onyx!

In general a very good hotel, great room, good location, wonderful pool and steam room. But be aware, if they give you a room with a connecting door you can forget about silence. The guy next door was just talking by phone and I heard him as if he was talking into my ear. they write everywhere in the hotel that you should keep silence. But instead of that they would need just to take care of the good noise insulation between the rooms. Another minuses were no sleepers for the pool, no keys in the pool lockers and several other detail. Well nevertheless in general we enjoyed our stay here, but it could be much better, usually you get better quality and service in Hyatt.

review_title: Great value. Perfect location for shopping and eating places. Breakfast buffet excellent staff very pleasant
review_text: Stayed here with my family of five and we were delighted. Rooms clean we were given free wifi because of a check in problem. Hotel attached to a great mall with plenty of restaurants.

This hotel was booked through priceline so it wasn't our choice, but what a find. They didn't have a king room for the whole 5 night stay but they offered us either the larger handicapped twin room or the choice of moving hotel rooms if we wanted a king room for 3 of the 5 nights. We opted to stay in the twin room for the duration. The decor was lovely and the room clean. The leopard print robes finished off the look perfectly. When we rang down on the first morning to ask if we had to collect the coffee from the lobby or did we order it to the room, a coffee machine was bought up and topped up daily.
The location of the hotel was great for easy access to the touristy areas and if you don't like to walk the T station is a 2 min walk away.
The staff were fabulous especially on our last day when we weren't quite ready to leave but had already checked out. The bar was closed but staff bought us coffees (for free) and called us a cab when we were ready to leave. Nothing was too much trouble.

review_title: OK hotel but in loud neighborhood
review_text: Our room was spacious and clean, but the beds were small (full rather than queens) and the noise from the street was disturbingly loud with ambulances passing by frequently through the night. The free shuttle bus was very convenient, but as a family with small children we would have appreciated more to have a hotel restaurant/bar and a nice neighborhood with walking distance to local restaurants. The breakfast was OK, access to the hotel by car is very convenient, free parking is great as well as free Wi-Fi. None the less, I will probably chose a different hotel the next time in Boston.

review_title: the club offers excellent value for the prize
review_text:
perfect location
great views
wonderful complementary breakfast
rooms are not big but very nicely remodelled

We stayed here nov 2011. There was 7 in our group. The first night we got there they had double booked us but couldnt have been more apologetic or accommodating. They upgraded our rooms, left a personal note in each room & a complementary basket of sweets etc. Hotel was extremely clean and staff were very friendly and hepful. Location is very central and close to every mode of transport. Would happily stay here again.

review_title: Best boutique hotel near TD Garden and North End
review_text: The Onyx is a great hotel. The staff is extremely friendly and welcoming. They remembered my friend and me after when we returned after a year! The location is awesome to see sporting events at the garden, just down the block. There are plenty of great restaurants and bars within walking distance. But you never need to go outside of the hotel if you don't want to. The hotel restaurant has fantastic food, the lounge has a very cool vibe and the room service is overly accommodating. They ran out of muffins one morning and instead of telling us we had to order something else, they had them delivered from a local bakery! Did I say I love this hotel!?! It's definitely my first choice on any trip to Boston. It should be yours, too. You won't be disappointed.

review_title: Excellent location, walk to shopping centers, Boylston and Newbury,
review_text: River view room is a bit small, but the view to Back Bay and MIT/Cambridge is so impressive that we don't want to close the drape. We came from Logan Airport using the shuttle bus and subway to Prudental station, then walk through the mall to the hotel, very convenient. Will stay again.

We've become Kimpton fans...we have yet to stay and not had a great experience...and the Onyx continued the trend. Absolutely no complaints...room was great, clean and comfortable....front desk staff was pleasant and knowledgeable. Did not eat onsite, but the lobby bar area was a great place to end the days adventures with a cocktail.
If this trend continues I may have to restrict our vacation travel to cities with Kimpton properties...;-).

Hotel muy bien comunicado con el aeropuerto, cerca del metro(T), "cercano" a todos los lugares de interes en Boston. Impecable limpieza y personal muy amable. Las hb son un poco pequeÃ±as pero muy comfortables (con frigorico de cortesia).

review_title: Great place for a quick tip to Boston
review_text: We really enjoyed our stay. Staff were helpful. Great location. Lovely room and bathroom. Love the leopard print bathrobes! Would definitely stay there again.

review_title: Posh downtown hotel with top notch appeal!
review_text:
Great downtown boutique hotel within walking distance to Fanueil Hall and the Garden... Also very close to North Station. They describe themselves as a luxury boutique hotel and I couldn't agree more!
The rooms are on the smaller side but the furnishings are beautiful. Much attention was paid to the small details. The bed was super comfortable- I slept like a baby. 
Service is excellent - everyone was friendly and hospitable and always more than willing to help with anything whether offering directions or recommending restaurants.

We chose the Sheraton for the location. We did pay more for a deluxe king and while the view was fantastic the room was dirty and very dated with no fridge or safe. Real shame! I wouldn't recommend this hotel.

review_title: Great everything except for the rooms....
review_text:
I stayed here with my mother last weekend. It was a good stay, the people were nice, and the room was clean. However there was no fridge or dvd player. 
Overall good stay but those two things were bummer.

Location is fantastic ESP since I was attending conference at Hynes. Very easy to access some of the prettiest parts of Boston also attached via underground walkways to Hynes convention centre and Prudential mall

review_title: Great location and very good SPG member lounge
review_text: Located in Boston's Prudential Center it's easy to access shops and restaurants without even going outside. The hotel is one of the better Sheratons with modern rooms (I was in a junior suite overlooking the Charles River and it was very spacious). Valet Parking is very expensive here $44/day.

Fantastic location.
However, bedroom was more like a student hall as it was rundown and had very dirty carpet.
Had a room close to main door which was quite noise.
They could defenitely refurb to offer the basic standards.

review_title: Spacious rooms and good value if you don't mind being out of the way!
review_text: This hotel was great value for money but you do have to get a bus and a subway to get into Boston and buses at night aren't very regular. The area felt a bit isolated and I wouldn't have liked to wander much at night. The room was spacious if a little dated and musty smelling. Service was good, we were able to check in early. Only a Chinese restaurant attached to the hotel but a nice breakfast diner just across the street. Nearby Cambridge has lots of nice places to eat.

review_title: Fab stay in beautiful Back Bay, friendly staff and cosy studios
review_text: A group of friends -11- in total stayed at Copley House for 5 nights. The staff are very helpful and friendly. Rooms are very cosy, charming and clean, nothing fancy but really convenient, affordable and clean accommodation in central Boston. Highly recommended for a group of friends!!!!

Staying at this hotel for work this week. The room we are in is crammed with old furniture so that the room seems very small. Disappointed that the negotiated almost 300 per night rate gives me a room with ugly flannel curtains, a tiny bathroom with peeling wallpaper, an industrial toilet and a shower that should have been replaced 10+ years ago. The drain looks rusty and the tiles are just beat up. The bed is rock hard. Wish there was a room fridge. Know they have them because our elevator stopped at a floor nobody had selected FULL of dorm fridges. (that was after almost tripping into a broken elevator hanging open bit not even with the floor level. 
The location works. Very close to the green line T stop at prudential and a nice mall with decent options for my non conference attending spouse. Can walk right into the mall from the hotel which is nice in the rain.
The room does not meet my expectations for a Sheraton and I have stayed at hamptons that are nicer. Super disappointed.

Chose this hotel for it being close to the garden for the bruins game. This hotel is close to everything and is great but once the game got out the noise level increased throughout the night with the bars in the area overall we had a good experience and would book for next bruins game
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Boston Garden

review_title: This Sheraton has seen better days!
review_text: The Boston Sheraton is in a great location. I used to stay there during the nineties when business took me to Boston fairly regularly. What a let-down. What is offered now for $300 is not much more than a Motel 6 experience: shoddy facility, dated rooms, poor service and management incompetence. Don't waste your money. Better choices are just around the corner.

After reading many other reviews on tripadvisor I was scared to stay here! However, I was pleasantly surprised. We had an early morning flight out of Logan and for $140 we could sleep there, take the free shuttle at 3am, and leave the car for a week! How can you beat that? Our room was on the top floor and we didn't hear anything outside of our room! The room was nicely decorated, had a flatscreen tv, and was clean. We were in a handicap accessible room and the bathroom was huge! We loved the shower! Also, stop n shop is right across the street in case you forget anything. The shuttle to the airport was on time..and actually was waiting for us, both ways! No complaints at all!

The room was extremely small, the bathroom door was one foot from the bed, there were dried 'splashes' of who knows what on the ceiling, there were boogers on the wall, the bathroom door had to be shoved with full body weight to close, the 'courtesy shuttle' was never on time or there were way too many people to fit in the van and you would have to wait another hour to be picked up. When you did get a ride it was terrifying, it was like they were driving for NASCAR. 
The walls were paper thin, I could actually hear the conversations in the next room. The train is behind the hotel and you got the joy of hearing it every fifteen minutes, and it was extremely loud. We heard doors to other rooms open and slam shut all night long. 
If you want to pay too much, lack of sleep, and be late to anything, stay here.
Very cold rooms but otherwise great stay! Great breakfast and friendly staff
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Boston Garden

review_text: We stayed here after a concert and it is a prime location to events at the td garden. The hotel is clean and the service was excellent. One minor problem was our AC didn't seem to work. Other than that the hotel is clean and a good price.

review_title: What do you compromise on, for value?
review_text:
This hotel is located close to the north end and all that is offered here...and that is quite a lot; little Italy, historical monuments and the Freedom Trail - well worth it. 
Although the rooms are really quite spacious and if you use them as we did, you can overlook some things - the slightly dated decor, dirty looking carpets and a rough looking location. 
As a value for money sleeping place it is ideal.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Boston Garden

review_title: Very close to everything, good value, not fancy but friendly and functional
review_text: Walking distance to North End (little Italy), holocaust memorial, Beacon Hill. Room was fine for sleeping, no view but large windows and lots of light. Breakfast was a bust, warm milk, not much selection. It was hot, and all hotels were asked to conserve power.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Boston Garden

review_text: My stay at this hotel was the worst! They placed me in a room right outside the elevator so all day/nite you could hear all noises! The bed was so uncomfortable it felt like i was on an elevation table. Every direction i moved i felt like the bed was going to collapse! The furniture and TV were completely outdated. The TV stoped working in the morning all we had was a frozen picture, couldnt even reset the TV! The only positive features was the large bathroom that was actually clean & the location of the hotel. For the money spent I would not stay again!

review_title: Friendliest and most accomidating staff I've ever seen!
review_text: We traveled to Boston from Colorado for my 3 year old grand daughter to have surgery. After being disharged from 5 weeks at the Children's Hospital we needed somewhere to stay while we made reasonable accomidations to get back home. We travel quite a bit and stay in many hotels, and never have I had the prompt, pleasent, high quality service that the staff at this hotel provided. It certainly was a pleasent suprise and made our very stressful stay much more comfortable than we had expected!
All of the staff was very helpful. Bret was extremely informational and helpful. Restaurant in the hotel is awesome, location was awesome! Highly recommended!

We stayed at this hotel for the Bruins Stanley Cup parade. From the front desk to the valet guys, the service was second to none. Geez, they even waived the 2nd day parking because the streets were closed and access to our car was limited. Clean rooms, great location, helpful staff = returning customers.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Express Hotel & Suites Boston Garden

review_title: Lovely room in a good location. Central to most routes.
review_text: Stayed at the Sheraton from the 22nd august 2011- 27 august 2011. When we arrived check. In was quick, explained that we had requested a fridge to store my two yr olds night time mlk and had asked for a king size bed and cot. The receptionist immediatley upgraded us to an executive suite at no extra cost. We were on the end of a corrider which suited us fine due to our loud two yr old. The old town trolleys stop outside the Sheraton and I would recommend this chain of hotels to anyone. Conceirge desk was a fantastic help.

review_title: Kimpton Onyx is a great stay.
review_text: I often stay at a Kimpton Hotel in various cities, second stay here. Love the location, staff excellent, rooms nice but on small side. I love this hotel chain for many reasons, including that they are all different but all excellent!

review_title: Dated but Okay for the price
review_text: This place was good for the price. Very dated but clean. A bit of an industrial cleaner smell in the rooms and the hallway. Further away from a t stop than what I would prefer but perfect for a visit to fenway.
hotel_name: Howard Johnson Inn Fenway Park Boston

review_text: We stayed in the hotel at the end of aug. Hotel is in a perfect location close to all,tour trolley's,malls,food courts and all important newbry street! Only thing is no fridge it would have been nice to bring bottles of water back and for it to be kept cool instead of gettin ice but other than that it was lovely,bed was super comfy by the way!!

We arrived a tad too early for check-in; the chap at reception was very accommodating and stored our luggage until check-in opened at 3pm. 
We checked in and made our way to the sixth floor. The room was a tad tired and dated. There was no wi-fi available in the room, to benefit from this you had to sit in reception. 
I approached reception to ask about a taxi to the airport. The lady suggested a minimum of $30 for a taxi. I asked if she knew of any other route or way that was cheaper. She asked me to leave it with her and she would call me in the room. Not long passed and the lady called; she could arrange a shuttle for $25 for the two of us. 
I am sorry that I can not remember that lady's name but I would like to say thank you for your excellent customer service. Thank you. 
As a one night stop over the hotel is okay, but not the same value for money as the other hotel we stayed in earlier in our trip was.

review_title: Great location at a better price than most.
review_text:
Small entrance that needs some work...however, the rooms are good, clean, and quite.
Location is great for touring the city.
Take urban adven Tours for great bike tours of the city...see Pell!

Stayed with 4 friends. It was two to a bed, and what a mighty squeeze it was! Not only that, even the walkway from one of the beds to the toilet was practically nonexistent. My friend who slept inside had to crawl over me when trying to get to the bathroom. After putting our luggage in there, there was hardly any space left to do much. Front desk was helpful enough though. There is no toilet on the first floor except a staff toilet in the basement though it was clean enough. Parking is also far away from the hotel. Hotel location is good though. I'll bear with it just for that but not if I want a pleasant time.

review_title: Nice rooms, great location, but no character
review_text: The Sheraton hotel is perfectly located. Restaurants, shops, tourist attractions. They are all nearby. Our room was on the 14th floor and looked clean, modern and fresh. View across the city and hotel pool. What disturbed us were the very noisy waterlines/plumbings. All day and night long. Last year we were on a higher floor in the other tower and the noise was a lot less. Most of the TV channels were horrible to view because of the poor transmission. What bottered us most was the staff at check in/out: not impolite, but cold, careless, uninterested. They really must hate their job or just don't care. The Sheraton wants us to rediscover Sheraton, but should start with their own front desk staff first. It would make a difference.

review_title: Great city nice room. Terrible service.
review_text: Everyone here just seems very annoyed in general with the fact they have people staying here. Wifi doesn't work in room, sorry. Overall so many better places to stay for less money.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Logan Airport

review_text: This hotel was clean and service was great but the rooms were small.

Stayed here for one night before an early flight. This hotel, although a Courtyard, actually had the feel of a full service Marriott. Restaurant and full bar serving decent food and individual TV screens in each booth. Several computers with printers in the lobby for boarding passes. Airport shuttle for your use. Free parking if you have a car, which I did. The surrounding neighborhood is fairly bleak, the closest gas a couple moles up the road and not much else around. But the rooms were large, very clean and the staff 
were very pleasant. The airport is 
about a 5 minute drive away. Overall I was impressed with the amenities here and the decent room rate. I wouldn't want to stay here as a base for a Boston trip but it's an excellent choice for the late arrivers or early departers to Logan.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Logan Airport

review_text: I've come to expect more from Marriott. Our room and bathroom were quite small. The PBS stream for the entire hotel was out for all four nights we were there. The GM was in the lobby and asked about my stay on the 3rd day. I mentioned that PBS was out and he was unaware. So was the Front Desk when we asked them about it on two occasions. Our first night, the fire alarm went off a 12:30. False alarm, thank goodness. Our room was typically not serviced until mid to late afternoon. Worst was on our last morning, we discovered black mold behind the curtains. It explained a lot of our breathing stuffiness. The manager on duty came up to inspect. They are taking this room out of service. They did offer me Marriott Rewards points for the trouble. All that said, I'd probably stay here again. It's very convenient to many activities, theaters, restaurants, historic sites, the T, etc. Our room didn't have a view but it was quite quiet.

I stayed here on business for 5 days. We arrived very early in the morning, and the front desk clerk was very accommodating in ensuring we all had a room. Nevertheless, it was not what I had requested. The staff was very professional and when i described my request made sure I got exactly what I wanted. The room was well appointed, the location was perfect for walking almost anywhere in downtown boston, and the concierge was very helpful! Thank younto the staff for making this trip very pleasant!

The location is located in the theater district of Boston. Subway station is 5-minute walk away. Chinatown is 7-minute walk away.
Services at front desk is average at best. Be aware that if you stay at the lower levels, you will hear the noise and bass coming from the clubs downstairs and nearby. It is kind of annoying. Also, the wall is so thin that you can hear people talking next room clearly.
The only good thing of this hotel is its location only.

There is nothing really wrong about this hotel but the decor is s bit dated. There is a strong smell of air fresher in the corridor but I can imagine that this is use to cover up the original bad smell. Staff are nice though

Stayed here to save money since all of the hotels in downtown are super expensive ($300 and up). Its about a 10-15 min drive from the main attractions in the city. It's a quiet, clean hotel, a great value for the money. Here are some of the perks:
- Free wi-fi!
- Continental breakfast complimentary. Includes waffles, pastries, juices, coffee, yogurt. 
- Free parking
- complimentary coupon book including coupon for free fudge at Phillips Candy House next door, a free beer and free clam chowder at the restaurants next door. 
- Free airport shuttle and shuttle to the subway every 30 min until 11 pm
- Lots of huge, fluffy pillows on the beds. 
I really enjoyed staying here. The staff is friendly and attentive. Its no fancy hotel, the decor is outdated, and the elevator is a little questionable, but if you dont care about that, it's a great place to stay and save money!

We stayed at the ramada inn for an overnight stay prior to flying out of Logan airport the next morning. First we had to bring our vehicle on the other side of the hotel to park it for the week ( which worried me a little) and then we had to bring our luggage through two heavy glass doors to get to the most unsafe elevator I have ever been in. There was no inspection sticker inside it either. The moment we stepped
Onto the third floor there was a strong odor that smelled like urine. The hallway had a large stain on the carpet where I assume the source was. Of course we were placed in the last room at the end of the hallway. 
On our return from our trip we had to wait about 50min before the shuttle picked us up after I had called and they stated about 20min. Apparently the driver was in route to come and get us and was called back to the hotel to bring a crew to the cruise dock before coming to get us!!!!
We will never stay here again!!

If you can get a deal on the price it is a good value. Centrally located and convenient. Don't pay full price though because they charge for virtually everything. Small rooms are clean and comfortable.

The hotel is in the theater district across from The Wang theater. The Boston Common is a short walk and the Boylston Station T. The front office will give you a list of attractions and directions. The front desk was very helpful, we were given an early check in, a late check out and switched rooms.
The hotel has very small rooms, however it is reasonably priced. We were able to get a larger room upon request. Do ask for a corner room on a high floor. The hotel is old but the location and price are a good trade off.

review_title: Good value for money but there was a bit of a commute..
review_text:
My partner and I stayed at the Ramada and found it was good value for money. However, it might be worth spending a bit more to stay closer to the city as the commute limited what we could do in the centre of Boston.
There were good points about the hotel. Firstly the shuttle was good and always on time. We also used this do get from the airport, which saved us about 35 dollars. We also used this everyday to get to the T and the shuttle drivers were generally helpful and informative. Breakfast was also surprisingly good - there were eggs, bagels, muffins and waffles everyday and this was all complimentary.
The rooms were sizable but were quite outdated in their decor. We also found the locks on the door were a bit dubious. However they were clean and offered everything we needed.
The only downside was the area the hotel was based in. There were quite a few facilities in the complex - there is a bowling alley which did reasonable food. There's also the Freeport tavern which does dinners and brunch, but we did find this to be quite expensive and preferred the food in the bowling alley. There was a supermarket, pharmacy and bank in walking distance which were useful also. In regard to other dining places and bars, there were no others which meant our nightlife was somewhat limited. 
If I was to stay in Boston again I would pay the extra to stay closer to the city, but this was a good value option as we were on a budget.

review_title: Within walking distance of North End nightlife, but value for money lacking
review_text:
We arrived on a weekday night from New York for a quick trip. The area surrounding the hotel can be perplexing if you haven't been to Boston before -- we weren't sure whether it would be safe to walk around as it got darker. 
Our room was directly off the elevator, which isn't ideal if you're looking for a consistent night's sleep. It was smaller than average, compared to chain hotels of similar scale, and had two double beds. Decor was, overall, somewhat dark, though the bathroom was modern and updated. 
Something about the hotel just didn't feel right. Perhaps it was the sub-$200 price tag attached, lowered significantly by joining the hotel's email list, but not enough to make it worthy.

My family and I spent 4 nights here in July at the beginning of a 3 wk holiday. Found hotel to be v good value. Hotel is old but v clean and v good continental breakfast and fantastic management who were on hand overseeing their brilliant COMPLIMENTARY shuttle service at all times. During our 5 day stay we did so much and we did not spend one cent on transport which meant a great deal. The shuttle bus brought us from airport to hotel on the Monday. We took bus tour of city next 2 days and the tour bus picked us up each morning at hotel and dropped us back each evening. Next day we got hotel shuttle to JFK station where we picked up another free bus to JFK museum. On the Friday we got hotel shuttle back to airport for our flight to NYC. On a couple of occasions I saw management outside the hotel checking times of shuttles and on one occasion when shuttle was delayed in traffic I saw management organise passengers in a managers car and brought to airport by car. I was amazed by this efficiency and at the time commented how Ireland had a long way to come in promoting tourism. I would definitely go back and since my return to Ireland have recommended it already..... Saying by no means plush but free transport outweighs seeing Boston. So unusual to go to a city particularly the states and not spend a cent on transport. We also loved the choice of restaurants nearby and unfortunately didn't get time to avail of the bowling next door. Collier family, Ireland.

The point of a hotel is to sleep. No soundproofing here. Ambulances, crowd noise, horns, and slamming doors (they are designed this way) all night for several days. I was on the second highest floor so that does not help. Colleagues on other floors with the same problem. Room is small with a pedestal sink. There is a tiny shelf for toiletries not over the sink but over the toilet - you can guess what happens. The breakfast is OK but it is exactly what is offered at Residence Inn for free except you can get made to order omlettes. For $14.95, does not seem a good value. The staff was friendly, courteous, and prompt throughout the hotel. I am a regular Marriott fan but would not return to this property.

review_title: Hole in the wall with small rooms.
review_text: The location of the Onyx Hotel is very good. It is convenient to the North End and The Garden. Other than that, this hotel is pretty average. A small unimpressive lobby, tiny guest rooms and no vending machines do nothing to help the cause. We had reserved a room with two doubles. When we arrived we were told the room category we had requested was over booked. Since we had booked through a third party website we had no recourse. They provided us with a rollaway bed. When the person delivered the bed they pushed it in the doorway and didn't even offer to help us set it up. If you are looking for a bare bones hotel in a good location then this is the place for you. If you are looking for luxury accommodations, stay away.

Based on the previous reviews, we were apprehensive about staying in this hotel. However , we were placed in a room away from the street so there was very little noise even on Friday/Saturday night. Room was somewhat smaller but had king size bed and desk, no fridge and only stand up shower. This was sufficient for us. Room and bathroom was very clean and decor was modern. Location was 1/2 block from the T and close to several very good restaurants. Only about 3 blocks to Boston Common and Chinatown. We did get a reduced rate on priceline so did not pay retail for the three nights we stayed there. I would recommend this hotel and would stay there again.

review_title: Friendly staff and close to transportation
review_text: I very much enjoyed my stay there. It seemed more business focussed, but it was worth it for the price. The hotel is about a 5 min walk to the train station and a 15_20 min ride into the downtown area. There was also a free airport shuttle, and the driver was very friendly and gave me great advice for my travels.
hotel_name: DoubleTree Club by Hilton Hotel Boston Bayside
