review_title: A historic hotel in the middle of Kenmore Square around the corner from Fenway & many restaurants!
review_text: This is an old, but clean & comfortable hotel. It's easy to find. There's a T station right down the street (which is how we traveled), but plenty of parking nearby if you choose to drive. Fenway is a walk around the corner. We hit Boston Beer Works for dinner, always delicious! We have stayed here before in one of the smallest rooms, which is fine if you're heading to a Sox game and aren't planning to spend hours in the room. This time we had a 2 bedroom apartment with a living room, small refrigerator & microwave. Great if you have 4 or more people! The hotel has an interesting history. Babe Ruth was a frequent guest & it is said that the World Series scandal involving Shoeless Joe Jackson was set up at Buckminster! Expect some noise such as sirens in the middle of the night...you are sleeping on a main intersection in the middle of Boston, but it's bearable. And if you have a room like we did, it's worth a little noise to be able to peek out the window & be staring directly at the iconic Citgo sign!

review_title: Nice hotel, nice views, not close to much for tourism.
review_text:
We stayed here over the Labor Day weekend and really enjoyed it. The room and the staff were great. The view over the harbor was pretty good (also looked over a large empty parking lot and abandoned office building).
Our only issue was that you had to take the subway (station was close by) or a cab to any of the "tourist destinations.

This hotel at a walking distance of the main attractions: Boston Common Park, Beacon Hill, The Freedom Trail... You don't need public transportaton at all. It is nice and clean, the beds are very comfortable and the bathroom spacious. It is a good idea to get a room + parking package. My only objection: no wifi access in the guestrooms.

review_title: Too far out for convenient sightseeing without a car.
review_text:
Excellent pickup from the airport after calling. Check in fine even late at night. Surprising though that all Hilton Honors members do not receive free internet and bottled water at check in!
Room a tad on the small size. Beds very comfy with triple sheets. Nice toiletries with fragrance but not enough to set off an asthma attack. Carpet grungy with permanent marks on it .. needs changing. I did not want to walk barefoot on it!! Old school wall unit A/C that works well but noisy! 
Just a couple of minutes walk to the JFK/U Mass T station red line so easy to get in to town .. just takes a little time.

review_text: The rooms are clean, and I've never slept better than I did on their bed. The hotel staff is very friendly and helpful, and the courtesy van from the airport was on time. If you use the transit system, it's a 5 minute walk to the station. If you're looking for new and luxurious downtown, this hotel is not for you, but if you're here to see the sights and get the most value, it's a great place to stay.

review_title: Great location, just a little old
review_text: I had a dulux queen room. It was all I needed. Modern bathroom, cable tv, window (with a view of a brick wall, but didn't matter as I only slept there an didn't need a view). It was clean, well maintained. Building was a bit dated but I believe they are refurbishing. The location is fantastic. Right near Kenmore station so its easy to get around. Only issue was the price of the room - it was very small so it seemed a bit much to pay as much as I did, but I guess I was really paying for the location which really makes up for it. I'd stay here again for sure.

review_title: Good accommodations with spacious hotel rooms in downtown Boston
review_text: We spent the 4th of July weekend here because the hotel indicated they could accommodate our party of 6 in one room. We were very impressed with the size of our room. We had lots of space for everyone and our luggage. We had a great big closet to hold most of our things. Because this is a Courtyard Marriott, they did not have concierge, full service dining or room service - which was fine with us since we knew this when we booked. A really nice touch was the free morning coffee they made available in the lobby every morning and also the fresh drinking water in the afternoon - it may seem like a minute detail, but trust me when I say that my kids loved coming back to the hotel after a day of sightseeing to help themselves to citrus or cucumber water. The location was also great as we walked almost everywhere. We never needed our car. The hotel also gave great recommendations for nearby dining. We were never disappointed. The fitness center isn't very large, but I never had a problem finding free equipment to workout. I only wish they had a pool.

Just checked in here and let me say this place is disgusting-I'm here with my mom and we requested double beds, didn't get them. Got to the room and it is tiny-no room to even put a bag. Hot as heck and when icalled for a temperature adjustment they offered to being up a fan. It's dirty everywhere inclunding curtains and floor-which is the only place we can put our bags. I'm going to try to find an alternative but please learn from our experience and do not stay here!!!!

We booked three months ahead for two connecting double rooms plus fold-away in one. Didn't get it, in fact rooms were on different floors (we're a family)! Rooms were not cleaned until late in day, glasses were not replaced, etc. The one good aspect was the beds were very comfortable. Staff were very 
friendly but we won't be back.

This hotel is a joke. It is on the side of a hill, we could barely get out of the car because of how steep the hill we had to park on. The htl staff called us (my mom and I) in the middle of the night saying to us that there were complaints that our room was being too noisy....we were asleep, it was 1:00am. There was noise from outside but it was not us. After being startled at that hour we were awake for a few hours. I asked the next morning if they made a habit of calling their guests in the middle of the night without checking to see if they had the right room, they insisted they checked, which of course we know that they couldn't have because they would have seen that our room was dark and quiet. Please check your windows to be sure they are locked ours we both unlocked, this place is basically a motel. I would never stay there again and would recommend that no one stay there.

I was a little hesitant to stay here based on the reviews I read, but I was quite pleased. We arrived early and wanted to do some sight seeing, so the front desk held our luggage for us until check in. The cookies were delicious and the bed was comfy. If you are worried about the wallpaper or furniture, you are probably spending too much time in the room!

review_text: Decent hotel near Boston College. Clean rooms. Don't be put off by the lack of curb appeal. Friendly staff, good breakfast, ideal for college visits.

review_title: Pleasantly surprised! Great place to stay in Boston!!
review_text:
My family and I had been on the Cape for a week and wanted to stay in Boston for a couple of days to explore . I choose bw terrace inn because of the reviews I read, location, and price. It exceeded in all categories! Rooms were a little dated, but clean, staff was friendly, but we didn't see them much. The
 T station was about a 5-7 minute 
walk and was super accessible for us small town peeps :). Loved the
 fRee parking as I found everywhere out east had parking fees. We did the aquarium and museum of science packages. What an awesome deal! No lines to wait in, and let me tell u there was a huge one! We ate one night in the city at Cheers :). But the other we stopped at the Thai place Bamboo on the walk back from the T station. Great food and fast! My only thing I wasn't terribly pleased with the free breakfast eggs were awful but my taste I guess.

review_title: Aging hotel but clean and friendly and very noisy! (walls are paper-thin)
review_text:
Pros:
- staff are very friendly and helpful
- rooms are clean
- free Doubletree cookies
- free shuttle is handy for airport users and those using rail at South Station
Cons:
- rooms are old (wallpaper is coming off in some areas)
- walls are paper-thin; can hear conversations in the corridor and other rooms very clearly - as if there was no wall at all
- bathroom is like a sauna (very poor ventilation)
- wifi is $13 a day
- business centre is old; keyboard was broken and computers are slow
- breakfast is very average
hotel_name: DoubleTree Club by Hilton Hotel Boston Bayside

review_text: Hotel had very small, very out-dated rooms. Windows are locked closed. Air conditioning inadequate. Bathrooms are poor, with only shower and small sink. Above all the beds were bad And television was off to the side of the room, hard to view from bed. This hotel is way overpriced for what you get.

Very small rooms, no wireless Internet, bathrooms were small. If you are taller then 5 feet 8 inches, you will have to duck down to get your hair wet. Shower heads are low. No bath tubs. TV are small. Plus 40 dollars a day to park your car. They do have hard wired Internet. They do not have safe in a room. Shame on you Marriott. Should atleast have a wireless Internet.

review_title: Good, the location is that matter
review_text: If you look for a priceless hotel in Boston, I think is the only acessible option near than Copley Square and Kenmore Sq. My tip is that you ask for a room with a outside window, to get some fresh air, instead of internal rooms. It makes difference!

No bellman, so you'll carry your bags up a short flight of stairs. Efficient and polite desk staff. We had a two bedroom suite, with teeny bedrooms and a large living room with a couch, table and chairs, a refrigerator and a microwave. The very small TV's are similar to two I just gave away to goodwill, but color and there is cable. All the furniture, carpets, bedspreads need updating, but everything was clean. Linens are clean and white but not at all luxurious. Think of a well-run Days Inn in an old building, that;'s what it's like. There is no room service, but a nearby Uno's will deliver myriad yummies, and there are several very good restaurants within a block. 
The continental breakfast is just that, nothing fancy. I heard people saying, "What? Only pastries, toast, juice and coffee--what kind of breakfast is this?" My answer: it's a continental breakfast, dummy. If you read the hotel description and the reviews, you will know what you're getting. Boston hotels are expensive, this one is well located, clean, and well-run. Works for me.

review_title: Excellent location if you are going to a Sox game!!!
review_text: I love the Buckminster. Rooms are small but very clean. Thisclose to Fenway park which I love. Would totally stay here again!!!

review_title: Only reason to stay here is convenience to MGH
review_text: Do not eat at the first floor restaurant. Some of the most horrendous food that I have eaten in my life. Very convenient to MGH. Standard room. Staff can be a little rude.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Boston at Beacon Hill

review_title: Great hotel in a nice location
review_text: We just arrived home from a wonderful stay at the Boston Sheraton. Loved that it was attached to a large mall with restaurants and stores. It was also a departure point for the famous duck tours and a trolley stop on the beantown trolley. It has a T stop (prudential) and an Amtrak station (back bay station) that are in walking distance and all indoors. Loved the pool with the retractable roof too. Would definitely stay again.

review_title: Awesome time in the shadows of Fenway Park
review_text: This is going to become my new home away from home! Stayed here for four nights in early July (including July 4th). Check in was easy, got a double room on the 6th floor. So close to Fenway Park (major plus for a huge Red Sox fan) that I felt I could throw a baseball onto the Green Monster from my room!! There's a Uno Chicago Grill in the same building, plus more restaurants close (or, for those who prefer fast food, a McDonald's over the road and Popeye's next door), and an awesome burger joint called uBurger just a three minute walk away. Kenmore T station is right there as well. Room was exactly what I needed - comfy bed with a good shower (and good toiletries as well). Looking forward to going back!!!

I've stayed at this hotel a few times and it is always my first choice when going to Boston, especially to see a Sox game. It is walking distance from Fenway and even has window views of the park. The service is always amazing. The front desk staff are friendly and accommodating. I even forgot my camera and they had it shipped out to me that same day!! As for the price you can't get hotels for this cheap anywhere else unless they are trashy. The Buckminster is NOT! It is old but its charming. I love it and will use it every time!!

review_title: Pretty nice hotel but had problems with the bathroom
review_text: This overall was a nice hotel but the bathrooms had mold on the ceiling which should have been taken care of right away. Otherwise the pool was pretty nice espcially when they open the roof and you can hear the sounds of the city. The bedrooms were pretty nice overall.

Checked in today for conference.
Room smaller than a studio. No wifi in room. Have wired internet but cant use because t here is no ethernet cable in the room.
Smallest bathroom ever. pretty much brushing my teeth over the toilet. Have to be careful stepping out of the shower otherwise my foot would be in the toilet. Closing the door makes it too claustrophobic.
Pool smells like feet and hasnt been cleaned in awhile.
Very disappointed at sheraton
Great hotel, great location, great view, brand new! We realy liked this hotel, close to the metro, easy access to most important places to visit...

review_title: Over priced and rooms need major updating!
review_text: While this Holiday Inn had a very friendly staff, I was disappointed with the quality of the rooms. The rooms are dingy and the decor is stuck in the 70's.Rooms aside, the hotel is in a good location...about a 15 minute walk to Quincy market and 20 minutes to the Harbor. This hotel is not worth the nightly rate of almost $300!
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Boston at Beacon Hill

review_text: We visited the hotel father's day weekend. The staff was awesome, and very friendly. The views of Boston from our room and the Club Room were beautiful. The location was awesome, close to the subway and dining!

About five years ago I was on a round the world trip and stayed here for the Boston leg. When looking at hotels this time I looked all over Boston. But this was the cheapest I could find. Sure it's not the best hotel but let me tell you that it is good value for money. Being single is sometimes a pain when you do a lot of travelling. This hotel is in prime location less than 5 minutes from the Grayline tour office- good cos I had some tours booked. 
The breakfast was ample - bowl of cereal, bagel and cream cheese and filtered coffee, brilliant. 
Sure it had quirks like a sloping floor in the bathroom but hey I did not expect 4 stars (if you want a complaint from me read my other review about Maltese hotel).

review_title: Lower your expectations and enjoy the prime location
review_text:
The Milner sits in a perfect spot in central Boston, theatres are around the corner, shops and attractions all just a few mins walk away - it's hard to resist the draw, especially when you see some of the rates they offer. 
It is however nothing fancy, it's old and tired, but breakfast is free, wifi free in the lobby, in room coffee and bottled water, and I slept well on clean dust free bedding.
Arrive with low expectations as I did and you'll not walk away disappointed. And be aware the rooms are all diff sizes, singles are small, some doubles are too.
very bad attention at the from desk for the manager and personal del hotel.they no give back the money after I decide no stay in the hotel.they went to very route.

The room was really small but I came to see Boston and didnt spend much time in the hotel. I was traveling alone and it was close to restaraunts and the subway. Good price for the location. I would not stay here again if I was with someone. The room was too small. But if youre looking to save some money and have a safe place to keep your stuff you should check it out.

The only good things about this hotel were: a) the free wifi - even though speeds on our iPhones were in the range of old 56k modems; b) the location was close to two of the trolley tours stops. 
For the price we paid (~$150) we would've had the Hilton back home. 
I guess the location (upscale Boston area) is what affects price at this hotel. 
The hallways smelled really musty; it was horrible. The rooms were really dated, with small old Zenith TVs and tiny bathrooms where the paint was chipping all over the ceiling. Not to mention the size of the bathrooms: you had to slide yourself between the toilet bowl and the countertop just in order to close the door! There was about 1/2" clearance between the door and the front of the toilet bowl. 
Also beware: parking is ridiculously expensive at $40 per day. That's what lunch for two costs in an average restaurant! Impossible to park in the smaller streets as they are reserved to residents of the area. If you're lucky and you find a spot, you can park on the main street for free on Sundays.
Would probably book in another location and get better value for money. Book somewhere in the outskirts near a subway station; you can get around for $1.70 in the subway system.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Boston at Beacon Hill

review_text: This is a great hotel for location as you can get any where riding the T (Boston Subway). It is a more economical hotel but a tired one. The beds are fine so you get a good night sleep but the walls are paper thin so you can hear everyone inside and out. The bathrooms are small. Boston us expensive and this hotel is cheaper. At least there is a Starbucks across the street.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Boston at Beacon Hill

review_title: Boston Milner Hotel is in a good location, but over priced for what you get!
review_text:
We (husband & wife ) stayed there for 1 night, Oct 2, 2011. We paid $195 for a double bed, hard & uncomfortable. The room smelled like cleaning fluid & ventilation was horrible. We had to open the door & turn on fan. We'll be in Boston next week & will stay elsewhere. 
The saving grace is it is centrally located, near the Boston Commons & China Town. The staff was pretty friendly especially in the dining area.
If you want to stay in the heart of Boston for a buck it's the right place. My room was very clean and had everything I need, breakfast in the lobby with free Internet. Great great location!!!!
We enjoyed our stay at this hotel. Great location, friendly staff and comfortable room. Will return!

The constitution inn was a nice place. The location was good, right near the ferry to long wharf. It's only $1.70 ea and brings you right downtown by the aquarium. 
Price was very good. Rooms were nice enough, nothing fancy but we didn't spend a lot of time in the room anyway. I did like that they had a mini fridge and microwave in the room. Beds were comfy, bathroom was a little bit small but clean.
The biggest downfall was the elevator was sooooo slow. Would stay here again.

We stayed here with a group and had SO much fun! It is a beautiful Lodge with clean rooms, a great tub/shower, and very comfortable beds. The living rooms provide a place to gather and lots of free snacks! The breakfast was wonderful. We spent a lot of time playing pool in the bar, where we had the most joyful staff serving us and interacting with us. Our shuttle service was prompt and pleasant and it was just an overall WONDERFUL stay! We stay in Seattle every few months, and this will now be our ONLY choice. What a fun time!
Great location. Close to Orange and blue t line. Close to newberry street and fenway. Beds are comfortable but the bathrooms need updating.

review_title: This hotel is good, but could excellent under new management.
review_text:
A fantastic hotel with 'some' excellent staff (Ted & Mike). The room was excellently appointed (Room 322) although the constant hum of the air conditioning unit mounted somewhere above the room was very irritating!!!
The cocktails in the 'Little Bar' were excellent:)
We enjoyed Great food in Paulette's Restaurant 2 nights running.
Things went well until during a storm we had a power cut. In theÂ Morning fire exits were the only way of exiting building but with no lighting this proved a highly dangerous decent.Â 
Having made our way to the restaurant (Admittedly we didn't expect a full breakfast) we found the Manager and staff in a state of shock, heads in hands waiting for power to come on...Â 
No effort had been made to lay on the most simplest of breakfasts - although milk and cereal were in the kitchen NO emergency torches were available so the staff refused to serve. Equally despite coffee shops having power less than 2 miles away no effort was made to bring in coffee. Poor / No organisation in the face of adversity!!
In summary a great hotel that could really blossom under Management that really cared about customer service and satisfaction .

I recently took a trip to Boston with my husband. We booked our hotel not really being familiar with the area. We ended up in Charlestown which is right outside the main Boston area. As soon as we got off of the airplane in Boston we kind of stood around looking at each other wondering how we got to our hotel from the airport. I finally picked up the phone and called. Kelly, the woman working there and on the other end of the line, was extremely helpful and detailed in her instructions on how to get to the hotel the cheapest way possible. Instead of a $25-$35 cab ride, we spent under $8 getting there via subway and train.
As far as the hotel goes, it is definitely nothing fancy. If you are just looking for a place to rest at the end of the day, then this hotel will work. If you are looking for 5 stars, then you're in the wrong place. The review before mine was dead-on. Our room made me think of an old dormroom. Our view left something to be desired but like I said, if you just need somewhere to sleep at the end of the day, then this place will do.

This room is horrible!! We were below the executive breakfast lounge and at 6:30 am we could hear all the noise of tables and chairs moving above us until we had to get up from misery!!! Nice hotel but stay away from this room!!

review_title: Un po' fuori....ma dipende da quello che si deve fare!

review_text: The Chandler Inn Hotel was the perfect getaway for my husband and I. The staff was so nice and very helpful. The room was beautiful... Very modern, no frilly flowered pillow shams or ugly wall hangings. The bed was super comfy, the best sleep I've had in a long time. The bathroom, while tiny, was very clean and I love the marble walkin shower. We were close enough to walk to nice places to eat, close to the T, and awesome deal with the parking garage... Half off with validation. I got an awesome rate, $99 winter special with an extra 10% off for booking non-refundable on their website. We will stay here again and again.

L'albergo ha un discreto rapporto qualitÃ  prezzo, c'e la possibilitÃ  di optare per avere compresa nel prezzo la colazione o l'aperitivo serale. Le camere sono confortevoli e pulite anche se i colori ( rosso e nero) lasciano un po' a desiderare e ricordano un' atmosfera un po' ..boudoir.... in compenso la clientela e' assolutamente normale e il personale gentile. E' vicinissimo allo stadio dell' hockey e consiglio , se possibile, di andare a vedere una partita. La fermata della metropolitana e' vicina per cui si raggiunge il centro citta' in 10 minuti.

We stayed for four nights while our daughter had surgery at childrens hospital. The hotel was nice but way overpriced. The room was spacious and adequate. I was charged 10 dollars extra a day for a rickety old fridge. I needed it for medical reasons and told them so. They replied that it was their policy to charge for the fridge even if it was for medicine!! No other hotels have ever charged for a refrigerator ever!! Next to some world premier hospitals to boot!!!

Bett sah aus wie benutzt. Nach Aufforderung wurden 5 neue Kissen gebracht und das Bett gerichtet. Keine Minibar. Bauarbeiten aussen, daher Fenster nutzlos (keine Aussicht). Die Lage des Hotels ist sehr gut, der Preis stark Ã¼berzogen.
Der Concierge ist gut informiert und hilfsbereit. Insgesamt wÃ¼rde ich das Hotel nicht noch einmal wÃ¤hlen.

Stayed here with my son (12 yrs old) for 2 nights. Staff were very friendly & room was very nice and spotlessly clean. Location was good for the money I paid. Very close to cafe deluxe which is def well worth a visit and within staggering distance!!! I'd def stay here again.
Great hotel. I highly recommend this place. Great views of the harbor plus theres ferry service right in front of hotel.
hotel_name: Hyatt Harborside at Boston's Logan International Airport

review_title: Excellent location and a very good Grill
review_text: This hotel has a great view of the city and if you need airport access it is perfect. The shuttle service is handy and access to the city view water taxi or subway is very easy. The. It surprise was the quality of the food in the Grill. Excellent and imaginative choices. Service was impeccable and particular praise for Bill at the bar. Great value. Thanks
hotel_name: Hyatt Harborside at Boston's Logan International Airport

review_title: The front door guys most helpful! They are what made this hotel excellent
review_text: My girlfriend and I spent the weekend in Boston and got to visit this beautiful city. Although the check in staff was basically non existent and not all that helpful. What allowed us to give a higher rating then we would have otherwise, was the guys at the desk when you walk in on the left. They were the most helpful, had great tips on travelling around the city and the fastest forms of transportation. Bobby Stone and his colleagues really exemplified the meaning of customer service and hospitality. If it wasn't for them this hotel wouldn't be any different from a Motel 6. We especially found it an inconvenience that wi if was not included when most other hotels, Starbucks and even McDonalds provide complimentary wi if to their customers.
hotel_name: Hyatt Harborside at Boston's Logan International Airport

review_title: Fine for 1 night for a wedding - but overpriced
review_text: Don't get me wrong - this is a nice, new hotel with many amenities, including (expensive) valet parking and good service, but I think for its location and usual purpose, it was WAY overpriced. Even with a wedding block discount. The wedding was held inside the hotel, and it just felt very canned, like there could've been weddings going on in all the other conference rooms at the same time. The area around the hotel is definitely growing and someday may be more of a destination like downtown Boston, but I think until then, I'd rather stay downtown for the money. What was good was that everything is almost new so it's very clean and modern and the room was very nice!
hotel_name: Hyatt Harborside at Boston's Logan International Airport

review_text: My family and I stayed here for 5 nights to see the sights and catch up with friends before the holidays. The hotel is in a great location for the airport and car rental but be prepared for a short drive into the city. There are no restaurants within walking distance from the hotel but dining at the hotel was pretty good with plenty of choice and a kids menu. The hotel is very clean with spacious suites ideal for families. My kids especially enjoyed the indoor pool. There is a nice breakfast buffet served daily with many options and the early evening reception serving snack foods such as cheeses/ crackers and even some warm appetizers which was great. The only downside for us staying here was the $32 valet parking per night fee, which we were aware of when booking but still quite expensive. Overall we would stay here again.

review_title: Excellent view, but need to pay wifi
review_text: I stayed for one night, bed is extremely comfortable, but just one disadvantage - I need to pay for Internet, which is not good for business travel.
hotel_name: Hyatt Harborside at Boston's Logan International Airport

review_title: Good value and easy for park stay and fly
review_text: We stayed here the night before our flight out early Saturday am (3 am). Room was clean and no issues with noise etc. quick walk to blue line station so we went in to the city for drinks-north end. Then back to the hotel for a bit. We then walked over to Rino's for dinner. About a 15 minute walk. We checked with the desk to see if they could put a duffle bag in the car with our cold weather clothes. No problem. We gave the desk the bag the next morning. The shuttle was there at 3 am and off to the airport. When we got back we just called them and a shuttle was there in 10 minutes and our car was waiting with the duffle bag in the car. This hotel was about $100 less than the Hyatt down the street (who also does a park stay and fly) and the service was just as good and the rooms were fine too!! Would definitely use them again before an early morning flight!
Worst management I have ever experienced. Will never return nor would recommend to even my worst enemy.

review_title: Excellent view, but need to pay wifi
review_text: I stayed for one night, bed is extremely comfortable, but just one disadvantage - I need to pay for Internet, which is not good for business travel.
hotel_name: Hyatt Harborside at Boston's Logan International Airport

review_title: Great for an overnight near the airport.
review_text: Great for an evening arrival from the West Coast. Wish I would have booked the rental car a day later to save the $32 parking fee as the hotel has a free van to/from the airport.

We spent a night during a slow period on a Vacationist offering. We had a very pleasant Junior Suite that was pleasantly furnished with working fireplace. There is a menu of woods available that are delivered and lighted by the staff with 20 minutes notice. No extra charge. The bedroom was equally pleasant. The bed was nice but not the best I ever climbed into. The bath was marble, nice with a deep tub. The shower did not work, but I mentioned it to the front desk upon checkout and they eagerly assured me that it would be taken care of promptly. The hotel feels old line, not contemporary, but our room was comfortable; the heating/AC worked well. There were signs of wear and tear which would have been more objectionable at full price.
Now to the bar. It's great. Not cheap, but it is comfortable and is one of the best I've found in Boston. We did not eat at the hotel so I can't comment. But the staff, with one exception, were very pleasant. The exception, one front desk clerk, but the hotel does seem to be trying to counter some of the bad press.

review_text:
Bien situe au pied de bacon Hill. IdÃ©al pour visiter Boston a pied. PropretÃ© trÃ¨s moyenne, due en partie a immeuble vieillissant. En dessous des autres hÃ´tel de la marque en raison du prix (325$)...
piscine trÃ¨s agrÃ©able apres une journÃ©e de marche.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Boston at Beacon Hill

review_text: They have a ferry that goes across to downtown Boston. Great way to take pics of the Boston vistas.
hotel_name: Hyatt Harborside at Boston's Logan International Airport

review_text: Decided to stay near the airport the night before our flight after dropping off our rental car. It was so convenient as Avis, and most of the other hire companies were walking distance of the hotel and there is a free shuttle to the airport. The rooms were a good size, even had a microwave.

review_title: They made sure our stay was a "10".
review_text:
My husband is a frequent business traveler.Â  That said, he does his best to stay in Starwood properties whenever and wherever he can.Â  Late August my daughter and I traveled with him to Boston.Â Â UponÂ our lateÂ arrival we were greeted by yourÂ Welcome Office Agent, Noah Dinerstein.Â  It had been a long trip and we were every bit the weary travelers.Â  Noah exercised just the right amount of humor and vowed to make our stay a "10".Â  We got to our great room, dropped our bags, and left to get a bite to eat.Â  When we returned, Noah had left spa slippers and a special Bliss Savory snack.Â  Small gesture to some- but my daughter loved, loved, loved the special treatment.Â  It gets better.
My husband hit his wrist watch on a door leaving the building the next morning.Â  Doing so, he lost the bezel onÂ the watch.Â  When your doorman saw me and my daughter looking around in the lobby and outside, HE also began to look.Â  Then he contacted the head of loss prevention to make him aware of the missing bezel.Â  I was most appreciative.Â  I was then offered a car service to Copley place.Â Â We declined, preferring to take in the sights on foot, but thanked everyone for their patience and generosity.
Â My only regret is that it has taken me so long to post this positive review. So many times we are far too quick to point out negatives.

We stayed in the Junior suite over looking the Commons. The fireplace added to the room's elegance and romance. The King bed had a Down Comfortor which made the bed super comfortable. The staff was nice, friendly and helpful. The morning we checked out they had actually forgotten to put our luggage in the trunk. We did not notice and drove away to Cambrigde for breakfast. They notified us and immediately drove it to us at the restaurant we were eating at....Now that's service!

I take certain pride in being a Starwood platinum guest, and I assumed the W Boston would be the same way. I checked in with my wife and they upgraded us to a spectacular king with wonderful stains on the bedspread. We ordered room service the first night, the menu had like 5 options, but the food was delicious, I'll admit that, especially the fries. We walked back Halloween night when the Nor'easter hit Boston and asked the doorman to enter, he literally made us wait outside in the sleet until we could find our room key. 3 minutes later, when we produced our room key, we were granted access to the Mecca that is the W Boston, covered in sleet. Besides the fries, this hotel has no legs to stand on. 
 - platinum Starwood guest

review_title: Great Location, clean, quiet, breakfast a big plus
review_text: Assuming you can get a good rate, this is an excellent place from which to base a Boston excursion. The rooms are clean, spacious, and comfortable. Breakfast (included) has omelettes, pancakes, waffles, fresh fruit, bagels, coffee, bacon. Sausage, and oatmeal. Anyone complaining about the breakfast is out of their mind. It is a short five minute walk to the subway, and you can be anywhere you want to be within 30 min

review_title: Great place for a short stay, if you are visiting your kids at any of the Boston colleges, or just visiting the city for it's hi
review_text: I have stayed at the Taj Boston on my two visits to the city in September 2010 and 2011. It's a classy property, with excellent service and very dedicated staff, who even remember your favorite tipple! After a whole year! Great concierge! There's never a problem getting good advice and reservations at the city's best restaurants, sports and cultural events.

Un hÃ´tel Pas trÃ¨s beau au premier abords mais on y dort bien, le prix de la chambre est pas trÃ¨s cher. IdÃ©ale pour visiter Boston Grace a son emplacement (trolley a proximiter pour visiter la ville avec un guide + dÃ©but du freedom train tout prÃªt) 
Nombreux restaurant a cotÃ© pour tout les goÃ»t ( chinois, fast food, italien...)
Un petit dÃ©jeuner bon avec la possibilitÃ© de se faire des gauffres certaines fois.

I stayed at the Midtown hotel for 5 nights this previous week, I must say that I was attracted by its location as much as anything. 
On arrival I was greeted by a very friendly concierge who offer to assist me with my baggage upon arrival. Check in was quick and easy and I was directed to my room down the hall. Some people may be put off by the long corridors, to me it was not bothersome. 
I arrived in my room to find it very clean, spacious and well equipped for my stay. With a 32 inch HD tv to compliment the room I felt right at home. There is ample room to hang clothes and store them in drawers which I found very useful. The room had a fantastic view of the Prudential center and Huntington Ave. All in all I was very impressed with the room.
The staff at the midtown were simply AMAZING! I had a minor issue in my room one morning and within 30 minutes it had been sorted, I must say Ron who works on the front desk is a rock star, he and all the staff made my stay simply fantastic, so help with everything, from finding places to eat, to advice on what to see and to organising my travel back to Logan Airport, it was all made so simple for me!
I will certainly be returning to the midtown in the future, thank u guys!
