Al nostro arrivo siamo stati accolti freddamente dalla receptionist di turno...che pronti via ha voluto la carta di credito ed i documenti, e ci ha dato senza troppi salamelecchi le chiavi della stanza (n.414). La struttura Ã¨ d'epoca (secondo loro) ma per alcuni tratti direi piuttosto vetusta, molto usurata, ma ben manutenuta. Purtroppo la stanza aveva 2 french bed che per una coppia non rappresentano certo una comoditÃ  (o si dorme ognuno per conto proprio in letti separati o si dorme insieme appollaiati in un letto da 1 piazza e mezzo). Inoltre al primo risveglio abbiamo avuto l'amara sorpresa (siamo infatti arrivati alle 21,30 col buio) di constatare che davanti alle 2 finestre della stanza c'era un bel muro del palazzo adiacente (a circa 2 metri) il quale non consentiva l'ingresso della luce del sole in stanza e nemmeno di vedere il tempo atmosferico all'esterno! Pulizia ineccepibile. All'esterno della porta della stanza continuo via-vai anche durante la notte, notevolmente fastidioso. Uniche note positive la vicinanza al centro della cittÃ  (10 minuti a piedi dai Boston Common) e la colazione (inclusa) onesta, decorosa ed abbastanza completa. Comunque lo sconsiglio.

review_title: Bon camps de base au coeur de Boston
review_text: IdÃ©alement situÃ© mais chambre trÃ¨s basiques et bruyantes. Convient bien pour juste y dormir et visiter. Petit dÃ©jeunÃ© dÃ©cevant. PropretÃ© impeccable.

review_title: A wow place to stay, very cool
review_text: Our first stay at a W. They upgraded us to a wow suite and it was definitely wow. Service was first class with everyone going the extra mile to make or stay prefect. The lounge has a fantastic buzz about it as folks just drop in for a drink.

We arrived around 9am, hoping to store our bags until check-in time, but we were pleasantly surprised to find that our room was ready. This allowed us to check-in, and relax a bit before heading out to see Boston.
The complimentary breakfast featured a wide selection, but we thought the dinner menu was a little overpriced. 
There is a shuttle to the airport, and the hotel arranged transportation to the cruise terminal.
There's not much in the way of restaurants close by, but there is a pizza place, Santarrpio's, about three blocks away that is highly recommended, although we didn't go there.
The hotel is about a five minute walk from the intercity train station.

review_title: Four star hotel on the edge of Boston Common
review_text: Nicely renovated classy hotel. Excellent location on Boston Common. We attended a wedding here in July. Fantastic food and service.

Located just outside the town center between Chinatown and Back Bay, walking distance to many restaurants and tourist attractions.
Rooms were good. Recently renovated. Carpet could have been a little cleaner but standard level of cleanliness.
A little pricey, but better value than many. Would stay here again.

review_title: Modern cute room with closet-sized bathroom
review_text: Just arrived & very surprised to see that the bathroom is actually the size of a small closet (with an actual closet door). The room is decent but definitely NOT worth the price!!

Located next to Logan airport, the view of downtown Boston over the water from the hotel can't be beat. Just a short water taxi ride gets you downtown, and free airport shuttles get you to the airport, which you can't hear despite bordering on the runway. I have stayed twice now, and will contine to use it when flying in and ouy of Boston to enjoy those spectacular views. I will however opt out of the restaurant for dinner given that there are much better options just across the water via a nice water taxi ride. Note that on my value rating, I do have a corporate rate I enjoy.
hotel_name: Hyatt Harborside at Boston's Logan International Airport

review_title: Great location nice room but not worth the price
review_text: Taj has a great location within walking distance to lots of attractions room was nice but didn't offer anything to stand out from other hotels in this price point
I woke up several times due to noise. The front desk was in no way helpful and had no fans.
hotel_name: Hyatt Harborside at Boston's Logan International Airport

review_title: Excellent experience in every way possible. Would highly recommend this property over any other hotel.
review_text:
I am a platinum Starwood member so I have stayed at plenty of W hotels across the country. The W Boston is no exception to the excellence this brand stands for. I was given a free upgrading to a lovely and spacious room. Everything from the front desk to room service was perfect. 
I can go on and on about all the details that other hotels wish they could claim. This is one of the finest W's that I stayed at, plus make sure to sign up for the Spg loyalty program. 
Stay at this hotel and see why the W experience is like no other. Afterwards, please write your review.

Great location! Spacious and comfortable rooms. Be sure to book one with a city or park view. Excellent service, friendly and efficient staff. One of the best hotels I've stayed at. 
One not unimportant detail:wifi is not free....most hotels in Europe, even 2 or 3 stars ones, offer free wifi to their clients. Seen the category of the hotel, free wifi would add to to the high quality services offered by this great hotel

review_title: Perfect Boston Hotel - location, rooms and service
review_text: I have not stayed in this hotel since it was a Ritz. My wife, son and I were in town for a visit to Children's Hospital. We had a lot of anxiety about the trip and the hotel staff took great care of us. From check in, to room service and the concierge, everyone was there to make our stay comfortable. We even got the use of the hotel car service on our trips to the hospital. The rooms were very nicely decorated and clean. Our room had a nice view of Newbury St and the Public Gardens. Location doesn't get any better. We are going back later this week and look forward to another great experience.

Stayed the weekend at the W for the first time and loved it. We have stayed at several Boston hotels and this one is now at the top of our list. Clean, modern and fun. The room was great, modern furnishings, plenty of room and great amenities. The "screen" between the bedroom and bathroom is really cool. The staff is very friendly and helpful. Location is great, plenty of restaurants and bars in the immediate area. A short walk gets you to Newberry St. or the Prudential Center. Loved it, we will stay again anytime we travel to Boston without our kids.

review_title: A good place to stay when visiting Boston.
review_text:
We were going to be in Boston for an evening, and wanted to check out the tourist spots, etc. 
We found all the downtown hotels to be way overpriced. So we decided to stay at the Embassy Suites at the airport. It was considerably less expensive. 
The room was clean and nice. The breakfast the next morning was good. 
It is only a $2 subway ride to downtown. To get to the station is only a 5 minute walk from the hotel through a park. We came back to the hotel late and felt very safe with this walk (we did encounter a skunk, though).

Great van drivers, great view, nice help. Noisy air conditioning, plugged toilet that took four calls to be fixed by a very nice maintenance man. A generally worn bathroom with no towel racks and not a watersaving toilet. Nice but ridiculously priced lunch and dinner menu. Really nice servers at breakfast. Pay 9.95 per day for wi-fi (how bush is that) but still really nice restaurant personnel, concierge and van personnel. The fish rots from the head. This corporation is very inconsistent and we are really annoyed with this experience.
hotel_name: Hyatt Harborside at Boston's Logan International Airport

review_text: The hotel was very lovely. It was also very clean and the service was very nice. Like!

review_title: Small rooms, but very clean and comfortable.
review_text: I was in town for a quick over night stay. A longer trip I would probably want a hotel with more space, but the price and cleanliness are great.

We have recently returned from a two week trip to the States. We spent 4 days at the Taj on the recommendation of a friend and we were not disappointed. This hotel prides itself on first class customer service and even by American standards it was exceptional. 
The rooms are spacious and very 
nicely decorated. The restaurant 
served excellent food and the staff were delightful. We enjoyed a drink in the bar most evenings and again found the staff attentive and friendly. The same could be said for the reception desk, doormen and maid service. But the real jewel in their crown is their concierge desk - NOTHING was too much trouble. Every restaurant they recommended was spot on as 
was the recommended unofficial tour of Harvard. Thank you to all
at the Taj for making our first trip 
to Boston so memorable.

review_title: Much better places to stay in Boston
review_text: The only plus for this hotel is that it is the only SPG in downtown. Apart from that,staff is fairly arrogant and they charge for absolutely everything. As an spy Platinium me member they did have the kindness to offer me a (very) small bottle Pf water for the room. Impressive! Don't even get me started on getting in the hotel at night when there is a long line of people waiting to get in the bar... Finally, this is the only SPG property where they offered me 500 points if they didn't have to clean my room! Most amazing part of this was that the check-in girl would not take no for an answer.

review_title: Great hotel for easy access to the airport.
review_text:
This hotel is really close to the airport and offers agree shuttle bus to the airport, car rental and the T stop.
The view across the bay is spectacular and for plane spotters, the rooms at the rear provide unparalleled views of the runways.
Parking is outrageously priced at $34 per day!
There are better value hotels in Boston but for easy access to the airport this is hard to beat.
hotel_name: Hyatt Harborside at Boston's Logan International Airport

review_text:
My wife and I stayed here over our anniversary on a month long trip through NYC, New England, Canada and the east coast. The hotel looks nice enough and has lot's of "wannabes" trying to act cool at the bar and lounge. We were put on the 14th floor in the corner suite that we booked after I refused to stay on the 4th floor where they tried to put us upon check in. Even on the 14th floor, the noise on the street was ridiculously loud being graduation weekend in Boston. The room itself was large, but the "soaking tub" which we booked it for barely held one (petite) person. One whole side of the room was windowed, but the curtains had to manually drawn each night which was a right hassle which involved climbing over the couch to complete the chore properly. The staff were a tad arrogant, and that included the 4 guy's acting as doormen who simply just stood outside the hotel chatting and doing stuff all, and looked like they were in pain when asked to do something. There was no free wifi in the room (the only hotel on a month long trip that didn't offer it for free) at $350 odd a night I thought this was pathetic and super scummy of the W. Each time my wife and I had a drink in the bar, our room was charged $50 on top of the drinks amount as a "deposit", this took a week to be refunded to my credit card which was unacceptable as we had numerous drinks down there prior to going out and the "deposit" totalled $400. All in all there are loads of better hotels to stay at in Boston that will be of a higher standard at a cheaper rate and without the arrogant tosser's that seemed to frequent this 
establishment.

very convenient location for the hurried business traveller (close to airport, rental cars, subway, and shuttle-connectet). 
As expected, you get proper service, rooms, etc, for the price of the room. Except for three week points:
- indoor swimming pool is too children oriented, and, high on chloride
- internet works very bad (I have noticed this before a couple of times with the same ISP "hhonors" in other hotels)
- this is me, but I hate not to have natural orange juice in breakfast buffet (otherwise, great!)

I travel heavily for business. AmEx Platinum services has good Fine Hotels package so we tried Taj instead of Mandarin or Charles.
Great location, pretty nice hotel. Felt nickel and dimed at each turn, starting with getting a few aspirins from the concierge ! ($3, please). 
Canceled return reservation and switched to Charles Hotel this week.

review_title: Nice room, great for AM flight, but . . .
review_text:
Really, no Restaraunt?
At 6:30, on a Tuesday the only place to eat was the bar, with a 30 minute wait? Is it really too much to expect a major brand airport hotel, booked full, to offer actual food?
The burger was okay, but the wait was silly as was the noise level.
Room was quite nice and very quiet.
Access. To terminals A and E is good, for C and D it's faster to take the shuttle.

Well located hotel.Very nice rooms.Sensational,comfortable beds.
Walls were thin but noise not too much of a problem.
Wi-fi should be free

We have stayed at This hotel twice now and both times were for flying out the next day. It Is nice to be close to the airport for when you fly out the next morning. They have a shuttle service that transports from the hotel to the airport. We have not run into any problems with the shuttle service.

This hotel is located near the airport but within walking distance of the T line also they have a free shuttle that picks you up in the train station. The breakfast bar is excelent they offer something for everyone from omelets to fresh fruits. The employees are very friendly.

We recently stayed here to utilize the Park n Fly option. The stay was fine, service was good with valet but returned from a 2 week trip and the valet pulled up with my car and says "here you go", and I find a HUGE dent in the driver's door with the paint peeling off and damaged handle that was not there when I left it with the valet. There's no way the valet did not notice this damage when retrieving my vehicle (unless he did it). Beware of parking here. At least there was absolutely no argument as to the liability for damages and the manager is helping to take care of the cost with my local body shop, something that I'm not sure would happen with a lesser hotel. Clearly once the valet takes your keys they should be responsible. What a hassle to deal with this after a long trip and have to interrupt my work schedule with this.

review_title: Great place to stay if visiting Boston
review_text: Following on from other reviews for this hotel, I was on business recently from the UK and found this hotel met all my requirements and expectations.great place to base yourself and the hotel staff were always willing to assist in making my visit as pleasant as possible. Would definitely recommend both from a sightseeing, business perspective with excellent transport links to the city.

review_title: In the heart of it all
review_text: Stayed with another family and they gave us a suite and adjoining room. Great!

Stayed here for a conference in the hotel. The location was excellent for walking but spent most time in doors. Overall, everything was good and would stay here again for another conference.I would look elsewhere for a vacation stay.
This hotel is in the perfect location for both work and play. There is a big 24 hours supermarket just across the road from the hotel. Service staff are all extremely helpful.

review_title: Great shopping with a conference hotel attached!
review_text:
I stayed here for a conference so didn't have a choice on hotels but was pleasantly surprised by both the location on top of two high-end shopping centers (Prudential Center and Copley Place).
Rooms were standard but clean and the housekeeping staff always greeted me with a smile and hello when I passed in the hallway.
Concierge lounge on floor 28 was small with standard appetizer and breakfast fare. They did have crab cakes one evening which ended up being dinner for me that night.
Location is just 3 blocks to Copley subway stop so great for using public transport around town.

Checked late in the evening ahead of an early AM flight. My wife and I were both quite disappointed by the service at the front desk. Guy clearly didn't care about customer service. Considering I'm a diamond member, i wonder how others who aren't elites get treated. Hotel was convenient though.

My wife had stayed here before so we elected to stay here on layover while in transit from Paris to Minnesota. We booked the hotel on Hilton Honors points so cost was not a factor. Our room ( slight bay view on 7th floor) was nice bu nothing special. My daughter told mevthe pool was quite good. However: room service was slow, and the food was a disgrace. Parking prices ($38 per night) are insane even for Boson. Finally, in world where free wifi is rapidly becoming expected by clients, at this hotel Internet is available for a fee. I have stayed at numerous Hiltons and sadly report that this is one of my least favorites. The only outstanding aspect of this hotel is it's proximity to Logan.

As a 24 year elite member of Marriott I have been in a lot of Marriott Hotels around the globe. I had never stayed in this hotel, so this is my first impression. I was put on the Concierge level. One very big gripe I have when a hotel has a lot of convention guests like me during this visit, is that they close the Concierge Lounge and all services associated with it from FridY pm until SundY pm. We are business people at a convention. We are paying the rate, but not getting the service we are paying for. I could care less about the fact the wonderful personnel who take care of the Congierge Lounge need a break on weekend. Use it to train others. The least you can do is to open it and allow access to coffee and soda pop and water. Is that too much to ask, cheap hotel owners?
Now that that's over, know that the location is superb, particularly for shopping and getting to the Hynes without going out in the elements.
The fitness, swimming,spa area has been renovated and is greAt. The rooms are just OK and haven' changed much in the last decade. One of my other peeve is the lack ofnsheets and blankets. You get a comforter which seems to work very well for my spouse, but I have to throw it off as being too hot about 4 times a night. That is why I really stay away when I am alone on trips from Marriott's and got to the lower brands, as they are more comfortable regarding bedding for men who tend to have a very different temperature desire when sleeping.

My memory was that the Eliot was an all-suites hotel but our room (perhaps because it was from hotels.com?) was very small and definitely not a suite. The decor was lovely and the bed comfy, but the hallway needed vacuuming. My morning coffee came pretty quickly but cost $14.00. The location was good and the stay was fine but w/out the suite there is just nothing special about the Eliot (as an expensive but not super-luxurious) hotel. I'd still pick it over a big chain but might explore other boutique offerings (or 9 zero or the W) when I return to Boston.

I stayed here last week and the cost of one night would have bought me a carribean cruise. Simply outrageous that this property would charge this amount. The food was also overpriced and it was not a high quality. Basic expensive pub grub. I recommend using hotwire when staying at Logan. You'll save a fortune for the same type of rooms.

stayed here for a first time visit to Boston for a football (soccer) game at Gillette. Very close to Fenway, station etc, taxis are right outside and is about ten minutes from quincy market.
Parking is easy on site too.
Staff, service and rooms I found were all excellent and would def stay here again.
Thanks

review_title: Great location but you should get more for the money.
review_text: Great location but on arrival the room had items from previous guests. After paying over $300/night they wanted to charge an extra $15/day for WiFi access. Why can you get free access at Motel 6 and not at the Hilton?

review_title: Designed with meetings in mind but in a mall in the centre of town!
review_text:
A large (but not quite anonymous) hotel with everything the business and tourist traveller needs - including an ok sized indoor pool. Rooms are clean but not large, nine lifts service guests with the first five floors devoted to meeting, eating or heating (exercising)!
Very convenient for all the usual outlets and the transfer to the airport via the 'T' is easy enough. Would be happy to stay there again

dieses Hotel haben wir in guter Erinnerung. Das Personal ist sehr freundlich und gibt gerne Auskunft. Wir haben uns lÃ¤ngere Zeit mit ihnen unterhalten. Das Hotel und die Zimmer sind einfach, aber sehr ordentlich gehalten. Die Zimmer sind sehr groÃŸ, die Betten gemÃ¼tlich. Man kann anscheinend irgendwo dort frÃ¼hstÃ¼cken, wir haben aber in einem Bistro nebenan gefrÃ¼hstÃ¼ckt. Man hat W-Lan. Die Anbindung an die City und wichtige Stadtteile ist gut, man ist mit dem Auto/Taxi im Nu in der Stadt, es gibt ganz nah einen Bus, man kann auch leicht zu FuÃŸ gehen. Ich glaube, dass man sogar zu Wasser hinkommt. Ja, einen Uferspaziergang sollte man auch unbedingt machen, das ist direkt am Hotel.

review_title: Hard beds, crabby bartender and no parking
review_text:
We stayed at the Eliot on 10/27/11 for 3 nights. Our original trip for our friends wedding to Mexico got ruined by Hurricane Rina so we (veryyy last minute) decided to take a road trip with another couple that wasn't able to get to MX. We tried the "unpublished hotels" option on Expedia. It guaranteed us 4 stars and within the immediate confines of Bean Town. Fine, we got 4 stars and within the confines of Bean Town but we also got an extremely hard bed, a weird shower with only 1 door that let the cold air in and water on the floor, a crabby and cheap (with the alcohol) bartender, and nooo parking. We spent $60 on 3 drinks and 1 ended up being a double because the bartender poured less than half the glass. My fiancÃ© asked for more and he said he'd have to charge us for a double. Go figure?!?! We're guests at the friggin hotel!! Either way, we wish we had been in Mexico and not in cold, rainy, snowy Boston. 
We would recommend the hotel if you're middle aged and stuck up. The Eliot is definetly not a place for a young hot couple looking to have a laid back and fun weekend. If you're looking to spend lots o' $ and get no perks (not even free wifi or a continental breakfast) stay there. One more thing.... Breakfast will run you about $25 per person. We opted for Dunkin Donuts and Mike's Diner while we were there. Hope this helps.

Stayed for 2 nights. Great location with easy walk to transportation system in Copley Place. Rooms well proportioned with nice bathroom. Bed very comfortable. Great views from 26th floor room. Lobby service adequate but impersonal.

review_title: Location is great, but rooms are expensive.
review_text: We stayed here for two nights and got a good deal via priceline. It was conveniently located about a block from the T subway as well as to some great shopping and easily accessible to good restaurants. Old town trolley tours also has a desk in the lobby so that was easy to book and get on/off the trolley. The room was clean and comfortable and we had nice view of city. However, I would not have paid their regular price of $299/night as there was not much included such as free internet or breakfast. Even the "bath and body works" shampoo/cond./lotion doesn't make it worth it.

review_title: Nice location but expected a little more
review_text: Great location for visiting Boston. Expected a little more. The property was slightly older. Couldn't turn our thermostat below 68, but they did send someone to help open our window. We were on a high floor with lots of noisy teens who woke us up. We called and Hilton sent security right up which was nice. Great pool and hot tub!

The rooms are big - 2 rooms in my 2 stays. He service is amazing and friendly. But the decor?? I'm not a huge fan of traditional/charming/new England. I like modern and refined. This hotel is the former!
Service, however makes it a top choice. I will return.

This was a wonderful hotel in a good location. It was a block from Newbury Street, and within walking distance of many of the historic sights and Public Gardens Our suite was spacious and well appointed. Service was excellent. This was a real treat.

review_title: Overall a good place to stay
review_text: Ok I wouldn't say this was the best hotel I ever stayed in but it is a good place. If I had to split hair I would only say the older woman who checked us in could of been a bit friendlier. But I would recommend this hotel.
Loved the location.could walk to Fenway. Subway was conveniet. Their breakfast was very good. Their staff was very helpful. First time to Boston and would definitely go back here

I stayed here for five nights for work. Beds were comfortable and my room was super clean. Housekeeping staff was very friendly and kept my room sparkling clean. The water pressure wasn't great, and the water quality made my hair dull. Freebies in the bathroom were great. I loved the lotion. If you ate not a gold club member they do charge $12.95 a day for Internet. Rooms aren't cheap, discounted rates was $229 plus tax. Request a room on a high floor. There are sine good views. Concierge desk left much to be desired. visited it three times and got lousy advice from two concierges that seemed bothered I was asking. The third time I needed to buy a stamp and the act of making change perplexed this woman. She short changed me by 16 cents but I was in too much of a hurry to even argue with her. The concierge desk was very disappointing and actually the front desk interactions were not great. So in short, good rooms with comfy beds in a great location.

My husband and I stayed in the Eliot in march, we were blessed to be given a room upgrade but even without this the hotel is truely first class! Beds don't let you get up to easy in the morning, they are so comfy! Location wise the hotel is perfect. One evening of our stay, i was unwell and arrived home before my husband, the staff noticed and asked if everything was ok, and then asked my husband if i required a doctor! Brilliant attention to detail. Overall, we can not wait to go back!

review_title: An Hilton?? It should be called a motel!
review_text: At this price you would expect nicer rooms not a old designed room with no bar, no light extinction automated, etc... The restaurant (if we could call it so) is very bad and the waiters are not nice at all. For the breakfast the buffet is small and potatoes were not cooked! Oh I was about to forget the 32$/day for a parking were you park and get the car by yourself!

Just stayed here on a combined work and play trip. The Eliot is always my first choice in Boston. I stayed in a double bed suite with my kids. Kids are always welcome here and there was plenty of room. There is a huge walk in closet to store all of your stuff. Wonderful living room space with a tv and computer. The bathroom is very small, but has a glass walled walk in shower. I love the location of this hotel. Newbury Street is just one block away. You can catch the T station there. There are plenty of dining, shopping and sightseeing options all within walking distance. The wonderful running trail on the Charles River is just a few blocks away. A word on the staff - always pleasant, extremely courteous and helpful. There is always a doorman to help you out. Just top rate staff at all levels. Would and will stay here again.

Boston Marriott Copley is an excellent hotel in the Back Bay. Hotel staff were attentive and pleasant. Room was large and beautifully furnished view were of historic Back Bay and Copley Square and with an high price mall with Ferragamo Cristian Dior shopping boutiques. Champions a great sports bar and lounge with at least 40 TVs and the ultimate 200" HD projection screen a superior place for sports viewing with friends or family

Stayed at this hotel after being recommended it for its location. It IS in a great location but for the money there are a lot of other hotels in the area. The room was an average marriot room. It was quiet and clean and perfectlty...average. 
I wouldn't go back for one reason alone. The hotel desperately needs more elevators. Each time we knew we had to go for an elevator we knew we would be waiting. My guest even had to use a bathroom in the starbucks bc the elevator took so long...and when he came back....I was still waiting for the same elevator.
Do your research and stay in a hotel in the same area but not here.
Rooms are small. Hampton inns have larger and more comfortable rooms. Very disappointing.
We stayed here our last night before returning home from a trip to Boston. Everything about this hotel was first class.

review_title: As airport hotels go ...... One of the best !
review_text: Having stayed in airport hotels around the World, this is up there with the best. Good location, with Terminals A and E accessible by a connecting walkway. And great views of the airport. Most airport hotel bars are either empty or full of very tired business people, but here the bar was as lively as any in a downtown location.

Stayed 2 nights on the back end of an east coast trip to experience Boston with the kids over 4th of July. This hotel was busy! We were able to check-in early, which was nice. Rooms were smallish, but didn't spend much time there. Staff was very helpful...a trainee was checking us in and seemed bit confused, but then someone came over to help her and all was good. Right across street from Duck Tour check-in, which we had reservations for. Shopping/restaurants in both Copley Place and Prudential was steps away and convenient with the kids. Loved the Vineyard Vines store there too!
Concierge was helpful and recommended a good spot for fireworks viewing so we didn't have to sit all day on our blanket! Gave us good directions to walk to Fenway too. Parking was expensive, but expected. Next time, we'll plan to return car to airport after check-in and take short T ride back.
Overall another nice Marriott property.

review_title: The Eliot hotel is a fresh and unique.
review_text: I come from a city that knocks down old buildings to put up newer ones. I've stayed at the Eliot everytime I've been to Boston. I enjoy the decor of the hotel. It's very French and unique. Very personal to each guest. The staff is more than helpful and accommodating. The location is perfect for walking or grabbing a cab, restaurants in and around the area.... provides touch screen computers to each room. It's very unique.... I love it! I took a photo of the snow, it was shoveled about 10 feet high :) absolutely an amazing experience.

review_title: Pleasant surprise for an airport hotel
review_text:
Let's face it. Airport hotels exist primarily for overnight transients. They are not dolled up for the tourist trade...unless, of course, the airport is also near the touristy areas of the city. That is certainly not the case with Boston's Logan airport. 
But the Logan Hilton was a fabulous surprise. From its lovely towering lobby to its spacious, well appointed rooms and it's pleasant staff, the only downside it that this is not a downtown hotel.
Hotel excellence is all about attention to detail...and these guys get all the details right!
One note... Careful before dining in the Publick House restaurant. While the food was decent, the prices were outrageous. It would be cheaper to take a taxi downtown and eat in a nice restaurant!
The beds and pillows were too soft. I suffer with lower back discomfort and this bed made me very stiff. I could barely stand up in the mornings. If you have back problems, stay away.

The Eliot is next door to the Harvard Club at the corner if Mass and Comm. I have always stayed closer to the common, but I enjoyed the proximity to the bike trail on the Charles River (3 blocks away), and the proximity to Newbury and its cafes (1 block away). The room was spacious and relaxing, although the bathroom was quite small. The service was attentive, but unobtrusive. I did not eat at the hotel, but I did eat at the chef's other restaurant Toro, and it was great. I will definitely come back. It is a relaxing retreat in a busy city.

Amazing location ...clean rooms , close to the train station and connected to prudential building thru a sky bridge . We dids not have any meals in the hotel so cannot comment on food . We visited the harbor area thru train which was very short ride . Theatre district is nearby and lot of nice touristy stuff around . Indoor Pool was nice and small ...my kids had a great time . They have starbucks on site so you don't have to go far for your morning coffee . I would recommend a stay here definitely.

Perfect for Seattle Center exploring, clean,comfortable beds, huge lobby w chic furnishings, pool, free parking which is unheard of in Seattle(most hotels charge $40+), also free bike rentals. 
I live south of city but stay here when I am n town late for shows, parties etc. I have recommended this to numerous out of town visitors who loved this place. 
Note it is not right in hub of downtown but a long walk or short cab. It is however right next to the Space Needle. Right out front door in all directions are great restaurants, pubs, coffee shops and stores. The Duck tour is super close too. 
We really like this place. Only quirk is showers are walk in with no shower door and rooms only average size...but u are there to explore great city of Seattle!
(Walk to.these places : cafe lladro for espresso, Crow for casual gourmet dinner, Dicks for a cheap burger, McMENNAMINS for craft brew and pub food, and Tolouse Petite for breakfast, lunch, dinner or famous huge happy hour.

review_title: Very clean an well laid out hotel. Close to tourist attractions and local transport.
review_text: Does lack a restaurant but plenty of options within 10 minutes walk.

review_title: Very nice hotel in a good location
review_text: This hotel is very well located for tourism or business in downtown Seattle. It's smart, friendly, and well appointed. No complaints.

Very impressed ... Quick check in ... Polite employees ... Nice facilities ... Attached to Copley Mall ... Good fitness center with plenty of cardiovascular, pool, jacuzzi. Comfy beds ... Roll away for 3yr old son came right away. Coffee maker and fridge in Rm. Very easy for family travel ... Can catch duck boats right outside, sky observatory in mall (great views of city) and Top of the Hub Restaurant (also in mall) excellent food & service with great view. Only bummer ... No shuttle to airport. Overall great hotel.

New hotel with all the modern amenities. Nice pool and jacuzzi along with gym. Parking is one the expensive side at 40 a night. Must walk to the t stop a couple of blocks. Attached to the convention center. The are has gone through major revitalization over the last ten years. Mostly new properties and a revamped seaport blvd has new bars and clubs. Be somewhat cautious on busy nights. Room walls don't do the best of keeping out sound.

This hotel is tired. Lobby is worn out especially the furniture. On sat nite city bar is closed at 7 pm and there in no restaurant for a complete meal except the Irish pub. Hallway rugs are food stained, looks like a frat party happened here.

The location is great if you want to be in the harbor area. Rooms are very expensive by most standards but the services like the restaraunt are very limited. The "full service restaraunt" offers the same menu as the bar, both of which are limited. Rooms are large and clean with flat panel HD TV/display.
Internet is free in the lobby bar restaraunt area but 12.95 or 16.95 for wired/wireless in room at $350/night for the room, they should provide internet free.

I stayed here for a conference. The front desk staff was very efficient and professional w/checking me in and out. The room was clean and spacious. The king-sized bed was comfortable.
The housekeeping staff cleaned the room well and replenished the toiletries but did not leave the breakfast order form for the next morning. Oh well... The coffee in the room was not very good. Starbucks is downstairs though. 
All in all, it was a good stay.
This hotel is too close to the fish market and the smell is quite strong. It's also a bit far from a subway station and the center of town.

review_title: A great hotel in the fantastic Seaport district -near the new spots and handy to all the rest!
review_text:
We stayed here just one night -we got a great rate to start with and hit a free upgrade to a city/harbor view -the room was super clean and basic. Very quiet. Breakfast was very good, typical city prices but a good value for the location-and very good service.
This hotel is right in the middle of all the new restaurants at Seaport-literally-all the new(er) places are a very short walk-and then there's the ever-changing scene on Biston Harbor with so much boating action.
I definitely recommend this hotel!!!

Really, really lovely hotel. Lobby was great. Staff was attentive. Room was clean and comfy. Especially loved how well appointed the room was - plugs where you need them, stylish furniture, etc. Great location, right next to YUMMY restaurants. 
Only complaints are small ones: The bathroom floor was a bit slippery. Should have gone with the natural travertine, instead of the polished. And, the bed wasn't the most comfortable I've ever slept on... but I'd go back.

As much as I looked forward to staying at a Westin, wow, so far not impressed at all. We arrived at 5:45pm and our room would not be ready for an hour, huh? We had to check our luggage w the Bellman ($) went to the bar to wait ($l and 1.25 hours later we have a hideaway bed or half-parlor as it is called, as this was all that is available. Huh? We have a reservation and we don't have a room? There is one pillow so we ask for another ($ tip) and our "room" will be available tomorrow AM sometime. Huh? They said the hotel is sold out? We booked a king (have documentation) and they said we have 2 double beds!

review_title: Nice clean & close to lots of waterfront shops & restaurants
review_text: New clean spacious room with great views of the city and the waterfront. Check in was a bit slow due to understaffing. I was in town for 5 days on business and found the hotel easy to get back to from various points around town. Not enough coffee supply in the room, but after I requested more they made sure to keep me stocked.

I stayed at this hotel for a week long convention and it was great! The wifi worked perfect all over the hotel, the indoor pool is fantastic to swim a few laps, the gym is also very nice! Also the location is excellent if you are attending the convention center plus the train station is within walking distance.

It was about a $20 taxi trip from the airport.
We arrived at 10:30 in the morning on Friday, they had rooms available to check-in; however, we were given a room that overlooked the roof of the convention center. I don't think so! So, went back down and requested a room change. Orlando was able to fulfill our request, but we couldn't get into a room until 3pm. 
So we purchased tickets from the concierge for the old town trolley and rode that tour and enjoyed the sites until 3. 
They had complimentary luggage check-in at the front desks.
We'll definitely come back! All Westins are our favorites!

I stayed one night with a friend in july 2011. Everything was immaculate.. Fresh, clean room, beautiful lobby with restaurants & bars, the front desk staff is quick, efficient & friendly. The valet staff are amazing! I forgot the gentleman's name, but he was so personable & helpful- he got us a great spot on a free shuttle into the part of the city we wanted to go that night. When we cam back to the hotel he was joking with us, remembered our names.. Just an excellent fellow with great customer service skills.. It makes your stay better :) South Boston is beautiful, I wish I could have stayed longer. Great hotel & staff!

review_title: Stay at the Seaport hotel instead.
review_text:
I was able to compare this hotel and the Seaport Hotel (1 block away) in the same week and the two are very different and here's why:
This Hotel has a very modern but 'cold' feel as you walk in. And what's with the glass orbs behind the desk? Even the lobby bar has hard plastic seats whereas the Seaport has tons of squishy seating in there huge lobby area. 
I think my biggest gripe with this hotel is NO WIRELESS! And you have to pay $16 a day for wired access-- c'mon even Super 8 has Free wireless and for $300+ a night, a staple these days is expected. And yes the Seaport has free wireless and its pretty fast (8 mps). 
The Seaport's restaurant is much more quaint and the staff is friendlier. Again, it felt like I was in a cafeteria with it's modern decor in this hotel's restaurant. 
Even though they are almost next to each other, the Seaport has the better location-- seems to be in the center of it all versus the Renaissance on the 'end' surrounded by parking lots and busy roads. 
But in the end it's the little things like built in shampoo on the shower walls, little shoe polish sponges, robes, $80 cheaper per night, live jazz and a 7 Eleven across the street that makes the Seaport Hotel a clear favorite in my opinion.

review_title: Adequate lodging in a great city.
review_text: Let me preface this review by stating we got an excellent deal on priceline. We paid $170 when the cheapest rate I saw anywhere else was $340. We were put in a low floor handicap room, which I understand, but the roll in shower was terrible. Flooded the bathroom everytime I got in. I feel gyped out of their heavenly shower experience. The concierge staff were all friendly and informative. The desk clerk was lukewarm at best upon check in. Parking is pricey, so be prepared or find an alternative like parking in a suburban t station and ride the trains in.

We stayed here for 3 nights. Lovely clean hotel. Porters were very helpful and plenty of staff about. Did find in a bit far out but that would not put me off staying again. Some great eateries in this area. It was a shame that there was no free Internet in the rooms. You would think now a days you would get it.

Like most Westins, you have very nice decor, very zen, very clean. The price is what brought me here. The location is a bit far, so walking was a bit much. WHat we saved on the room, we ended up spending in taxis. We did enjoy the pub in the lobby and the breakfast restaurant. It was more by necessity than choice given that others were too far away.

review_title: Albergo molto carino e in posizione strategica
review_text:
Struttura molto caratteristica all'esterno, atmosfera urban-casual all'interno!
Quartiere tranquillo e gradevole, a pochi minuti da zone centrali per shopping e vita notturna.
Buon livello di pulizia, arredamento moderno e piacevole; bagno piccolo ma funzionale.
DisponibilitÃ  bevande calde gratuite e self-made in reception.
Personale disponibile e attento ad eventuali difficoltÃ  linguistiche.
DisponibilitÃ  di parcheggio convenzionato a meno di 5 minuti a piedi.
Facilmente raggiungibile dall'autostrada.
Zona leggermente rumorosa.

review_title: Decent hotel in best location in city!
review_text: The hotel is in the best location, close to T stops, walkable to Fenway, the Common, river, etc. Even a grocery store across the street! Great fitness center too! But rooms are dated, old, not 100% clean so it's a bit of a let down. Hopefully, you are out exploring and then too tired to notice when you return!

review_title: Great service, great location, beautiful hotel can't wait to come back.
review_text: We were celebrating my boyfriends 50th birthday and decidedto go to Boston. He grew up in Boston and wanted to show me around. We took the silver line from the airport and arrived at the hotel in no time. We arrived prior to our 3pm checkin time, but room was ready. The check in process was flawless and our Guest service agent Joseph Boikess was fabulous. He really went out of his way to make our stay memorable. HE noticed during our checkin im process that we were there to celebrate my boyfriend 50th birthday. We made it to our room with a great 11th floor view of the city. We got situated and went into Boston. We were out all day and made it back to the room to find a note from Joseph Boikess, with some bubbly and snacks. I couldn not believe his thoughtfulness. It's rare to find an associate make a connection like this. This hotel has a great staff. They are friendly, knowledgeable, and professional from guest services to housekeeping. The accommodations with the heavenly beds and showers are so comfy. Whirlpool and pool was a nice plus after a long day of sightseeing on foot. The location of the hotel is so close to the airport, public transportation, and Seaport area. Walking distance to a happening area of sportsbars and restaurants. Will stay here again. THEY KNOW WHAT CUSTOMER SERVICE IS!!!

Our third time to the Charlesmark and owner gave us complimentary drinks for anniversary to start...right outside is the Boston library, Newbury street and the Prudential Center. Cannot beat the location...rooms are on the small side but you are in heart of the city and the staff is great. Love this little nugget.
This hotel was very reasonably priced. The rooms were very clean and well decorated. Staff were nice and helpful. Great stay!

review_title: Small Boutique Hotel in a Awesome Back Bay location!
review_text: The rooms at CH are small but modern. The bathrooms are uptodate - no bathtub just a shower. Our room (both times I stayed there) had a small couch that was a pull out so that was fantastic for when my sister stayed with us one of the nights. The bar downstairs is nice enough for a quick drink before you go out or when you return from a day out of either shopping or sightseeing. The location in Back Bay is unbeatable with plenty options of shopping or sightseeing adventures. I have stayed on the top floor and the room was spacious and lovely! I also have stayed in the smaller standard rooms mid floors and they were also lovely just small. The staff was friendly and upon our arrival we did get a free drink at the bar. Great bargain in a fantastic Back Bay location.

Only Internet connection in rooms is Ethernet wired connections, no cables provided. Can't use my wifi iPad except in the lobby. They do have a large lounge, which they cleared out at 3:00 to set up dinner service. TV has very few HD channels. Rooms are fine, location is great, but I could pay $150 less and get wifi and breakfast. Marriott should be ashamed of this property.

Very well located. Rooms are big but cold. Beds are ok. The bathroom in my room was old and needed some refurbishing. 
Nice staff at the breakfast. 
A very big hotel with nice facilities but a product of mass consumption

Excelente cafÃ© da manhÃ£, exceÃ§Ã£o para o cafÃ© preto, estilo americano, ralo... Happy hour com comidinhas e refris grÃ¡tis... Quartos grandes, com cozinha. Limpo, bem arrumado...

Excelente hotel y extraordinaria ubicacion a 7 minutos a pie de estacion del metro

This is a great new luxurious hotel. The hotel is very convenient to the subway and to old town trolley. The star bucks in the hotel is convenient as well. The room is luxurious and had a great view of the harbor. Overall this is a great place to stay

review_title: Beautiful Hotel. Ran into a few service issues though.
review_text:
Check in was fine. When we got to our two room suite about 9:30pm we were settling in when I made my way over to the other room and found that the door was open. The lock was in the door jamb and had been intentionally propping the door open. As if that wasnt strange enough, there was a piece of paper towel jammed into the peephole on the same door. 
I checked the rest of the room to make sure nobody was inside and called the front desk. There was not very much concern on the other end of the phone. Security never showed up to the room. 
I gave up on the unsecured room problem, as my wife was trying to take a bath. Only too find the tub would not drain at all. Luckily the other room in the suite had another bathroom and she was able to rinse off in the tub/shower there with no problems. I decided not to call back down to the desk about the tub. It was getting late and we were tired. Since they didnt seem concerned about an unsecured guestroom, Im sure an issue with the tub wouldnt 
matter.
Other than that, the hotel is beautiful and the rooms are what you would expect from a Westin.

Conference hotels can be perfunctory pit stops or the highlight of the trip. The roomy, clean and beautiful room I had was an oasis. The bed was fantastically comfortable, as I've come to expect at westins. Great products, sheets, robe, lighting- loved it. Rate was fair for a conference rate, and I was actually surprised that it wasn't more. Bistro in lobby was only food experience- service was slow and food was super salty. Hotel service express, however, was responsive and got an a+ from me, so that's why I gave 4 stars for service instead of 5. What a nice break from the tired business hotels I'm often stuck in. Particularly loved the new Westin blue channel with continuous, gorgeous, simple nature videography. Super engaging and relaxing. Location is perfect if attending a conference, but there doesn't seem to much around for someone who might be using this as a base for a Boston visit, a possible minus for others. It's not far from the historic center and is close to waterfront and my room had view out to harbor, plusses.

review_title: Would be all 5's except for internet access
review_text:
I just stayed there because I got a great AAA rate. I usually stay in Brookline to see my daughter but this was a lot less than Courtyard there. Everything was fine except for the Internet access. I did not like being attached to the desk in the room and I sure did not like not being able to use my iPod in my room. Also it got so crowded and noisy with everyone else in the lobby and Starbucks using their laptops etc.
Other than that it was really nice. Especially when I had asked for early checkin (at about 11:30 am). That was wonderful.

review_title: Comfort and friendly service at the westin hotel
review_text: The Westin hotel at the waterfront is only a 15-20 minute drive from the airport. It is located in a beautiful section of the city. Just a short walk away to the many good fish restaurants on the waterfront, this hotel is located next to the boston convention centre which is so convenient for those attending conferences. Like all westin hotels, the cleanliness and comfort of the rooms is worth noting. The friendly staff at the front desk, and both the women concierge offered valuable information for our "touring" and "dining" experience. The hop on hop off bus picks up and drops off at the westin hotel each day. That was so convenient for 2 our days in Boston. I highly recommend this hotel. Enjoy the Starbucks in the hotel for an am coffee and treat as well!

I typically select Marriott for the great predictable offerings. This is an aging property so that could explain the lack of WiFi above the first few floors and the painfully slow elevators to the concierge level on 28. That does not explain the sloppy housekeeping service in our room or the indifferent concierge. My colleague tried to get assistance with dinner reservations and was offered PF Chang or Cheesecake Factory rather dismissively when she asked for seafood suggestions. When I asked for directions to the Museum of Fine Arts, he waved in the general direction without looking up and mumbled "more than six blocks, less than ten" in response to my inquiry as to how far it would be to walk. Hardly a friendly welcome. Nice wine for a fee, weak snacks, but great breakfast in concierge level gathering area. Next time I must attend a meeting at this hotel, I will stay next door at The Colonnade. Too many nice spots in Boston to spend this much money here.
Very nice hotel that has a mall attached to it. The mall is nice and big and has many restuarante options. The rooms are nice. The pool is also pretty large.

review_title: Only stay if you get at discount
review_text: Glad to hear others had a good experience but our fridge didn't work and they told us they didn't have any to replace it and $12 to $18 night for wi-fi and $32/night for parking.

review_title: Spacious and luxurious rooms, so so location
review_text:
We stay here overnight with a voucher from our credit card company so it was essentially free. That being said we did think the room was a great value. The room was spacious and very clean. The lobby bar was very cool and there was a Starbucks attached. The buffet breakfast was awesome!
my only complaint is that the location on the waterfront meant we had to take cabs into Back Bay but the value was worth that inconvenience.

Typical large Marriott hotel. Room average size and small bathroom which is typical for the older Marriott's. Fitness center very good with an indoor pool. Nice lobby with a Starbucks. They gave us a nice $10 voucher for Saturday breakfast as a platinum member. Buffet very good at Champions.

review_title: Cracking location but an empty feeling
review_text:
The Club Quarters sits in an enviable location smack bang in the centre of Boston's financial district - it's a doodle to get anywhere from here, south station is a couple of mins walk and it's a 15min max bus ride to the airport from there.
Checking in and out and the feel of staying here is somewhat odd, you actually don't need to speak to anyone at all if you know how to use the machines, and I did feel like I wasn't really a guest, more a client. But then again, it is a business hotel. 
That said, the room was spotless, comfortable and had a power shower, coffee maker and great bed. Coffee also to hand in the lobby lounge, and next door is the Elephant & Castle pub serving meals and a fantastic cooked to order breakfast menu. 
The walls are thin however, and I was forced to move rooms at 1am due to neighbour noise (group party) but once in a quieter spot I slept like a log. It's good value for the location, but if you prefer to be treated like you're a guest you may not like the experience.

3 night stay for a conference. It really is an old fashioned 'grand hotel' w/ all amenities. Had to switch rooms b/c paint fumes w/o hassle. Right next to green line T stop, also close to Boston Common.
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_title: Attended a meeting here. Left a bit to be desired.
review_text: Attended a 4-day meeting here. The conference staff seem to not know how to feed a crowd of 400 efficiently. The food was good but one had to stand in line and wait a long to be served from the buffet. Most of the breakout meeting rooms are long and skinny, making slides hard to read from the back. The Imperial Ballroom is gorgeous.
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_text: 1 night stay for us after a concert - fun because we both attended college in Boston and never went into the Park Plaza. Room was clean but tiny and parking is either really expensive or a pain - we chose the latter by attempting to find street parking and drove around for an hour in rush hour traffic. It ended up working out for us though! Loved the hotel and all of its history.
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_text: I stayed at the hotel during a business trip. All the expenses were payed by the company, so I cant say much about the price. What I can say though is that the room was bettet than expected and the service was excellent. People at the rest and front dedk were great. I specially remember Mike who I met at the front desk but also saw him at the rest. Always very attentive and making sure I was having a good experience, he even took my breakfast to the room when it wasnt his responsability only to make sure it wasnt delayed.

review_title: Mike at front desk goes extra mile to help.
review_text: First time staying here. Unloaded bags out front, checked in, and when going back to park car it was dead. Mike S at front desk got jumper cables for me, called AAA, and even waited 30 mins after his shift to make sure tow truck arrived. Couldn't have been nicer, very impressed.

review_title: Very classy, not expensive, good location
review_text: The Silver line bus from the airport stops 2 minutes from the hotel. Very new, very classy. Upgraded our room for a higher floor with big windows for free. Starbucks coffee in the room. Nice, new, designed rooms. Very good gym with treadmills and pool for free. Downtown is in 15 minutes walking distance but the bus is at the corner. The staff is helpful and polite. Try the Barking crab near the hotel!

There is a major building project going on right in front of the hotel and it is running all night. The noise is a major issue, but that hasn't stopped CQ renting out the rooms and offering me, wait for it, Ear Plugs! Despite sometimes iffy room cleanliness in the past I continued to stay here as it is good value for money, but this is probably the last straw.....

review_title: A historic structure in a historical American city
review_text: The Boston park plaza boast of history. However the rooms and the foyers need need carpets and decor. Furniture too needs replacement. Bedding was comfortable and sleep quality is good. The room needs better sound insulation . restaurants on site are good.
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_text: Stayed here for 2 nights found this hotel very central, the staff on the front desk were alway's helpful, our room was very comfortable, had a good meal in the Elephant & Castle next door, we enjoyed our stay so much we are bringing friends over from the U.K next year

Comfortable bed especially for someone traveling alone, could be a squeeze for two. Good desk space and very comfortable chair. Not overly fancy but I like that.
Great filtered water help yourself with supplied bottles, nice lounge downstairs. Staff helpful and not in your face, Irish pub on ground floor noisy inside but really good cheap food. Biggest downfall for me was thin walls, but didnt prevent me sleeping well. I'll come back!

review_title: Great location! Nice room and friendly staff
review_text: We had a great stay here for a few nights in October. It's a small hotel on Newbury in a great location. The staff is friendly and the hotel is quiet for the location. Our room was in the back on the alley it was quiet except for the trash truck in early am. We didn't mind because its expected in the city. I'd definitey stay again. We actually extended our stay by one night.
Stayed here after a concert and had a pleasant stay. Clean and good service.
hotel_name: Residence Inn by Marriott Boston Harbor on Tudor Wharf

review_text: This is the second time I've stayed here, because every other hotel was sold out or a small fortune. I tried to save my company a few bucks. I didn't love it last time, when the room I checked into wasn't clean and I didn't love it this time when the room I checked into had two bathrooms - super weird and creepy. I asked to change my room, the manager first told me to shut the second bathroom door, before accommodating my request. All this place needs is a few renovations, including new bathrooms and new room doors and maybe it wouldn't be half bad. And it might not have seemed as bad if I was traveling with somebody, but being a woman traveling alone, this place is two for two in terms of creeping me out. In the future, I'll definitely book in advance when I can and stay at the Westin or Back Bay Hotel.
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_text: Stayed here with my family (I usually travel for business). Staff was very friendly and helpful. Good local knowledge of attractions and transportation options. They offer nice breakfast buffet options. The only downside could be the location; the hotel is in Charlestown (which has some charming streets). This puts the hotel a little far from most Boston attractions, especially for families with small children. I plan to stay here on my next visit to Boston.
hotel_name: Residence Inn by Marriott Boston Harbor on Tudor Wharf

review_title: Over priced hotel, but great location.
review_text:
Stayed here two nights for $500. The room was nice size...2 queen. It was clean and comfortable, but tile in bathrooms were cracked, paint was peeling off boards. The room stayed warm and we could not get the air condition to work- room 1040. We ate the Sunday buffet for $25 a person. It was tasteless... I have had a better breakfast at Hampton Inn for free. The front desk was not friendly. I asked to speak to the concierge and the girl at the front desk did not know one existed! Ha!!! The one redeeming quality is that it is in a great location to sight seeing. 
I will look elsewhere for my next stay.
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_text: This hotel has such a old feel. If you are into modern this hotel isn't for you.
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_title: Great building and location but not much heart.
review_text: The room was comfortable and stylish and the location speaks for itself. However the staff were chilly and overall it was more like a hotel without a dining room than somewhere I would call a b&b.

review_title: Very disappointing and overrated, but great location... Keurig was nice.
review_text:
Hotel is in a great location, but for the supposed quality and history of service the hotel advertises, we were very disappointed and discouraged from ever staying here again. First thing we noticed upon arriving is there are an unusual amount of hidden fees that are standard in most hotels of this supposed quality. Things such as shuttle :
- service to and from the airport is $17 per person.
- Internet connection is $11 per day to have in your room, and it is strictly from a ether port connection. NOT WIRELESS! iPads, blackberries, or any other modern Internet device is unable to be used.
- If using the business center to access the Internet, you are charged $7.95 for 15 minutes and there were only 2 working older, computers that are on an unsecured connectiion.
- Room service was adverstised as 24 hours but ends at 11pm. 
-Trying to reach the front desk or anyone else for that matter to address a concern was difficult. Phone would ring with no answer.
- Alarm clock did not work, and was not replaced per our request. 
- No express checkout. 
Great location, historic, but does not keep in step with what the moderate traveler has come to expect from a hotel of the supposed caliber at this price point. Very expensive for such little amenities and low service. Would not recommend !!!!
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_text: Stayed for 1 night in a bay window view room. The rooms are excellent, best bedding by far during our 3 week USA holiday. Location excellent with walking distance to many attractions, shopping & dinning. Breakfast was perfect, eggs and also fruit & oats. This was the second most expensive property we stayed at, NYC was the most, well worth the price. Highly recommended & would stay again if in Boston.

review_title: Clean, smoke free and excellent value
review_text:
We stayed here for 2 nights in July for a mini getaway to boston and we were not dissapointed! We love having the small apt feel. Clean and smoke free is what we always look for and this fit the bill. Comfy beds, flat screen tvs in bedroom and living room a big plus! Nice views of the harbour.
The complimentary full hot breakfast was great. The location was just right. Away from the hustle and bustle of downtown but not too far. My sister even got a free blackberry charger from the front desk, left behind by a previous traveler. They had 2 boxes full of chargers! Good to know since this is something people forget to pack sometimes. Parking is a bit far and pricey. Overall we were satisfied with our choice.
hotel_name: Residence Inn by Marriott Boston Harbor on Tudor Wharf

review_text:
Nice place on the harbor near the TD Garden. Finally a Marriott with a good breakfast rooms were clean and nice, staff was great. 
Two negative points, but not so bad that I would not recommend this hotel. One, they have spotlights that light the outside of the building. One seemed to be focused directly on my side window. It was so bright that the shades would not keep the light out. I could almost read at night on my room with the lights off. 
I also had ants in my bathroom.
hotel_name: Residence Inn by Marriott Boston Harbor on Tudor Wharf

review_title: Great Boston hotel for families with little ones.
review_text: We stayed here for 3 nights with our 18 month old and 3 year old. The one bedroom king room worked perfectly for our family. The kitchenette even had enough space for our pack & play so the little guy could have his own area. The location is requires some walking to get anywhere besides the USS constitution and harbor area, but that was ok for us. We enjoyed walking around the harbor area and seeing the boats. We even took our breakfast out there one morning. The breakfast also worked great for us and was the typical res inn spread. We made use of the inroom dishwasher and the coin-op laundry on our floor.
hotel_name: Residence Inn by Marriott Boston Harbor on Tudor Wharf

review_title: Hidden Gem/Great Location/ best Value in Town!
review_text:
I stayed here for a week in August and I am coming back for sure! This is a no frills Marriott, an amazingly great value, a short walk to the North End, Rose Kennedy Greenway and Fanuel Hall. The staff was fam
Ntastic and the condo like feel makes it like a nice vacation home. He breakfast and evening snacks were great! I can't say enough for this place and I am usually a hotel snob staying in Five star hotels. Dog owners-- there is an awesome dog park right next door!
hotel_name: Residence Inn by Marriott Boston Harbor on Tudor Wharf

review_title: A high priced "motel" with little to no customer service.
review_text: This Marriott is an embarrassment to the chain. As a frequent traveler and a Marriott elite level customer it is clear this property and it's personnel have been ignored. The hitelis dirty, the beds are horrible, most items in the rooms are broken or un disrepair and the staff, all of them and consistently, the rudder and least helpful I have encountered. Truly out of character for this chain. A huge disappointment.
hotel_name: Residence Inn by Marriott Boston Harbor on Tudor Wharf

review_text: Wow, this is my favorite Ritz Carlton I have been too!

review_title: Modern amenities with old Boston charm.
review_text: What a great staff and location! We were very pleased with our room and the friendliness of the staff. We were upgraded our second night (because we decided to stay another night) to a king suite. It had amazing views and was spacious. Kelly & Carlos were terrific! Would highly recommend to anyone who appreciates colonial charm rather than a "cookie cutter" hotel chain.
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_title: Great value, off the beaten path
review_text: The pros of this hotel are many: large room, fabulous harbor view, fine service from front desk and car valet, good value despite high $35 daily parking charge, and a surprisingly good hot breakfast. The only con is the location at the former Navy Yard in Charlestown. About a 15 minute walk to the "T" at North Station or a cab ride to get anywhere. Only one good restaurant within walking distance, but several only a 5 minute drive away in the North End. But even the location has positive aspects: beautiful, quiet surroundings in an historic setting far from the chaos of downtown.
hotel_name: Residence Inn by Marriott Boston Harbor on Tudor Wharf

review_title: Good location, more conemporary than other RC's.
review_text: Great location and typical Ritz service. Smaller and more contemporary than the RC's I've stayed at. Close to all that's good about Boston.

review_title: Great hotel! Unless you have a car...
review_text:
Even though this hotel shows up in most hotel sites as located in Cambridge area, it's actually within walking distance from the old town and downtown Boston. It's located right next to USS Constitution and has a great view of the Boston harbor. The only inconvenience of this hotel would be parking, which costs $32 per day for valet at the hotel. There is a public parking right in front which costs $22 per day (outdoor, 1 min walking distance) and an indoor parking which cost $20 per day(3 min walking distance). 
Everything else other than parking is great! Every room is a suite with fully equipped kitchen and they even do groceries for you if you stay long.
One of the things that I liked most about this hotel is the complimentary breakfast which includes amazing self served waffles and English muffins. Be sure to try it if you stay here.
hotel_name: Residence Inn by Marriott Boston Harbor on Tudor Wharf

review_text: Clean, roomy, nice service. Nothing special. Just a good vanilla hotel.
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_title: SchÃ¶nes Business-Hotel, etwas weit weg von der "Altstadt"
review_text:
Das Renaissance Waterfront liegt leider nicht direkt an letzter, hat aber dennoch Comfort und alle Annehmlichkeiten, die ein Urlauber verlangt.
Parken ist recht teuer - es empfiehlt sich auf einem der fuÃŸlÃ¤ufigen AussenparkplÃ¤tze zu parken. SupermÃ¤rkte und Restaurants sind nicht in direkter NÃ¤he, das Herz von Boston ist in ca 10 Minuten (bei Verkehr) mit dem Auto zu erreichen.
Die Zimmer sind komfortabel, ruhig und sauber. Wir hatten Blick auf die Industrie und den Flugverkehr, nicht schÃ¶n, aber bei unserer Rate gab es keine MÃ¶glichkeit auf ein Upgrade.
Obwohl es fernab der Stadt liegt, ich wÃ¼rde ausserhalb einer Messe sicherlich nochmal dort einkehren.

review_title: No HD TV - are you kidding me?
review_text: I'm here for business, the Stanley Cup finals are on TV - but the picture in my room is terrible there is no HD, but the TVs are LCDs. I called house keeping, they sent up a technician to tell me they only have HD on a Few channels. This is the Ritz?????

review_title: Nine great nights in the Garden Suite!
review_text:
Aloha!
I stayed for nine nights (August 27 - September 5, 2011) in the Garden Suite (423) with my parents, two kids and my daughter's roommate. The suite was absolutely gorgeous, clean, comfortable and the hotel has a central location.
We all found the front line employees to be friendly and accommodating. Breakfast was served on the 15th floor in the Towers Lounge and on weekends in their lobby restaurant.
Our suite had two bedrooms, kitchen, three big screen TVs, a living room and a terrific outdoor garden area that served as my remote office while checking email and answering voicemail.
This was our favorite suite in all of Boston and we have stayed at some pretty nice hotels in this city. Mahalo to the staff at the Boston Park Plaza Hotel. We at planning our next visit again soon!
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_title: Perfect location for first-time visitors+awesome showers!
review_text: We "named our own price" on priceline and lucked out with this hotel! Walking distance from North End and all of downtown Boston. It's also 1 block away from subway "the T" so you can get anywhere. The rooms were spacious, beds comfortable, and showers were AWESOME. Our only complaint was that they didn't have free Internet.

review_title: What kind of a fancy hotel does not have a fridge and free Wi-Fi
review_text:
I get it! This is a fancy hotel. It is super clean. The room is quiet and usable. I had a room with 2 washrooms. My issue with this place are:
1. For this price, I should be able to get free Wi-Fi in my room or at least access to Internet via LAN. Instead, they want tmw to hang out at their lobby with the rest of the universe.
2. It has no fridge. Again, I am paying premium price for a premium hotel. Where is my fridge.
3. The gym is closed. They want you to go to a public gym somewhere and pay another $ 15 per use.
Seriously, if I had known, I should have stayed at the Hilton, intercontinental, Sheraton, etc...
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_title: In general it's a good hotel.
review_text: I've stayed for 8 days but the last two days my electronic key was disabled and it was a long time waiting to fix it. One of their emplyees said that the system system is old and need to be replaced.
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_title: Historic hotel rooms need to be updated
review_text: I stayed in this hotel for a conference. I was amazed to know all of the history behind it. However, it has not been updated. The bathrooms are awfully small and out dated. Beware! The elevators ate scary.
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_text:
In general, the hotel rooms are roomy, modern and well kept. A manual climate control is also a huge pro these warm weeks.
Friends of us on the third floor reported a very good nights rest everytime, yet we were given only a very little rest thanks to our fellow guests on the sixth floor.
The first night, the adjoining room was filled with drunk guys arguing till 3.30 pm. We kept calling the service desk, but they didn't come up themselves before we threathened just to leave the hotel the next morning. After that, the guys were quiet (somewhat).
The second night, there seemed to be a wedding reception across the hall after midnight. This time, we didn't wait till the service desk did something aboit it and send these people downstairs ourselves.
In short, the hotel is allright. Yet the superthin walls are your curse when confronted with ignorant fellow guests. Also service could be way more pro-active

I had the opportunity to stay at your hotel this year and my staying there was great. I felt like being at home, the hotel was clean, everyone was very nice but there was one employee in particular Mr. Felix Hernandez, who was very helpful with all of my questions and concerns about the hotel and the city of Boston, since it was my first time visit there. I want to congratulate you guys for having such an amazing employee. Thank you for the wonderful experience. On my next trip to Boston Â I'll make sure to stay there again.
Sincerely, 
Ricardo Gomez Bejarano.

I recently stayed at the Westin Waterfront and the staff were incredible! From the door men to the waiters.. everyone was very welcoming. Deborah the concierge went out of her way numerous times to make our stay unforgettable. She could not have been sweeter. The rooms were very nice and there was so much to do in Boston even in the cold weather!

Nice lobby
Rooms slightly tired and traditional
Bell staff and porters very helpful
Location is the best thing about the hotel

review_title: A nice place to stay in Boston.
review_text:
Great location literally across the street from Fanuel Hall. This is a nice boutique hotel. Rooms are good size, well equiped and furnished (great big tv). Bed very comfortable. Front desk staff seemed on the ball and provided good service. They boast about their restaurant but honestly- there are so many places around the corner or across the street at Fanuel Hall, not to mention that the North End is a 5 minute walk, I'd recommend trying local fare. 
I come to Boston twice a year for a meeting which is held at this hotel and I look forward to the stay.

review_title: Perfect place to stay in boston
review_text: Amazing location and a very cool classic hotel. Walking into this lobby quickly reminds you how hotels use to be. Staff is friendly and took care of any requests I had. Since I am a low maintenance person I didnt have significant interaction with staff. Check in and out staff friendly ad were the door men. Rooms very comfortable and the bed is amazing to sleep in. Pillows were perfect and the a/c worked like a champ. Rooms were clean and quiet. All in all a great place to stay and good value
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_text: The Park Plaza Towers is an elegant Boston landmark with an interesting history. The hotel is perfectly situated with easy access to city parks, public transit, and the shops and restaurants of Newbury St.
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_text: The staff was lovely and very cordial. Great decoration and location. The restaurant choices were good although it could benefit from a green tea choice on the menu. What I didn't like was the dark tiny room and paper thin walls. We were constantly woken up by hallway noise and our friends stayed across the street at a much nicer hotel for $85 a night less. We won't be back to this hotel.
The staff is wonderful and really go out if their way to make sure your stay is enjoyable. It is centrally located to several attractions which makes it easy if you don't have a car.

Excellent hotel for location and nothing else. Located next to Boston Public Garden and close to the metro station and shopping streets. Rooms are small and my carryall bag was missing in the room on my last day, and did not realize until I was looking for it at the airport.
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_text:
The hotel is nicely situated near Back Bay Station where we arrived from New York. 
The staff member at check-in was very welcoming. She checked us in and immediately advised us that we were welcome to come down to reception to enjoy some complimentary wine. 
The location of the hotel was wonderful, it was within walking distance of many attractions and restaurants. Even the Duck Tours were just 2 minutes away. 
The room was more than adequate, if I was to be a tad critical I would have liked a wee kettle in the room. But that is me being hyper-critical. The hotel does offer coffee and tea in the reception area. 
I would happily go back to this hotel, and currently looking to return for a wee holiday. Thank you for a nice time.

We booked a double room with two double beds and were given a free upgrade which meant we had separate bathrooms! The beds were really comfortable and the heating/cooling system worked well (we find the systems in some places are quite bad). Breakfast buffet was expensive but there is a Bon au pain next door which is better value. 
This hotel was located at the bottom of Boston Common. It's about a 20 min walk to Quincy markets but was 2 mins from the Boston Common and Boston Park and is close to Cheers and shopping at Newbury St and Copley Square! This was great for us! Staff incorrectly tried to charge us for a breatfast but it was removed without question when we informed them of the error. Would stay here again.
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_text:
Arrived and there was a huge line for check-in. No Priority Club or Ambassador check-in either. Same issue upon departure.
Upgraded to a very nice suite with a lovely view of a rooftop! 
It's one of those places that does certain things really well and then let's themselves down on the simple things like having no staff in the Club Lounge during the 'quiet' period (middle of day) so if you happen to go in, you will find dirty tables, nothing in the fridges etc.
