Not what I expect of an InterContinental branded hotel, especially given the price per night.

L'albergo appare sin da subito di classe e la stanza meravigliosa: una suite sull'angolo dell'hotel, elegante, confortevole e pulita. Ottima posizione anche per cercare ristoranti per la cena. Da consigliare soprattutto per coppie.
L'atmosfera e' d'altri tempi...pare di essere in una dimora bostoniana dell'epoca del tea party.

I stayed here for 3 nights on business, it's a great hotel. I travel in the US on business and sometimes do these reviews. Firstly it's close enough to most of Boston, but not to close to noise etc. Easy to get around and the silver line from the airport is a 2 min walk. I get expenses so could use any mode, but this is quicker and easy. 
The hotel is stunning, it should not be anything but 5 stars on tripadvisor. The bars, lobby and rooms are great. I'm in a river view, which is pretty big and a great bathroom. The gym and pool are great. The staff are all helpful, couldn't do enough. I can't rate the room highly enough. 
Sushi is very good, as is the bar. I would stay here again, and will.

I really like this place. I have been here for several months (I came to work) and it's been a very nice experience. 
Mike Squadrito specially makes an effort to make it comfortable to everybody.
Marco Hernandez

review_title: All what you get is the location
review_text: Rooms are very small. Staff not helpful at all. My shower was broken. I asked for a fix, they use tape to tie the shower head to the wall, really?
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_text:
My husband, 4month old and I booked this very lady minute and arrived late at night - we had a nice friendly welcome by check in staff and bellman offered quick food suggestions and umbrellas as it was pouring. As we had one of their last rooms we had 2 doubles but it was fine and beds were very comfortable and absolutely loved the blackout curtains (I took a photo of them as I loved the rooms decor) as it gave us a great night sleep. The only annoying thing was there was no place near the sink/mirror to put my makeup bag to get ready. 
Overall staff were really accommodating holding our bags the entire next day after also providing late checkout so our infant could get in a good nap. We stay in hotels all over the world frequently and service matters most to us so we were appreciative. 
Good location for shopping at prudential center.
Aimed at business customers on expenses. But does this v well. Good food and service, nice ambiance, excellent functions facilities, great location

review_title: Like eating a Subway sandwich for 500.00
review_text: Had to haggle for a room under 700.00. No shampoo no hairdryer. I called multiple times for a toothbrush and finally got a "free" one after contacting the manager. Sterile and cold but clean.

We stayed here 4 nights in April. We got a great deal through Priceline so it was a great value for us. Check in and all the staff were great, friendly & helpful. Our room was one queen bed, great linens and super comfy. Our bathroom was updated and clean. We had a small desk as well for our laptop. As in older hotels, the walls were a little thin and you could hear your neighbors. However, we were unaware that a HS Prom was being held here and when a large group of giggly girls moved in next door, you could not miss a word they were saying. We called downstairs, and the staff sent someone up immediately to talk to them. Apparently we weren't the only ones to complain because when we called again a half hour later to move us, they advised that they were already moving them. 
Location can not be beat here. Great restaraunts surrounding the hotel. And in walking distance to all the sites! Loved our stay here and would recommend it to family and friends.
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_title: Well worth it...location was great, comfortable, and accommodating.
review_text: We would definitely stay here again. The king edge room was fantastic...beautiful, comfy bed, and nice size. Location was excellent. Rooms were clean and view was nice. All around great hotel!!

review_title: Great location but rooms are small
review_text: We stayed at Copeley Sq over the weekend and found it to be located conveninetly to everything. The Duck tour boarding point is down the block, the visitors center is a 20min walk, which is also where the Freedom Trail begins, which is a must if you want to take in the history of the city. The mall is also a block down, and has an abundance of stores, including the top high end brands. The Xhale restaurant downstairs of the hotel had great breakfast (roughly $40 for two). The miniBar was lively and had a good vibe and good drinks (roughly $10 a drink). The bar also has an outdoor seating which appeared to be very popular since it was always to capacity, whether due to its own accord to the great weather that weekend. The only negatives were the expensive vallet ($45/night), the elevator not working 75% of the time during the 2 days we were there, and finally, the room was tiny. We staid in a king delux, and felt like we were in Alice in Wonderland, with the room being so small. Our initial reaction was 'where's the rest of it?'. If you're the type who likes to spend time time in the room during your stay, then it may be worth looking elsewhere. Otherwise, the bed was comfortable so the room serves its purpose if that purpose is just to crash at the end of a long day.

review_title: Daily wine tasting puts this hotel at the top of my list
review_text: The room was great - nice bed, good shower. Staff was outstanding! Perfect location with a Trader Joe's nearby! We could walk anywhere or hop on the subway. And the wine happy hour at 5 each day just made this hotel perfect.

review_title: Exactly what we like in a hotel - one complaint.
review_text:
My husband and I stayed here as the "overflow" hotel forour conference being held at the nearby Marriott. A very good choice at a renovated historic hotel. We usually don't stay at the conference hotels anyway, just to get a little separation from the intense networking.
I read other reviews and made a point to tell them I am 7 mos pregnant and request a non-smoking king at a higher floor (avoid noise from street and club in hotel). They accomodated nicely putting us on the top floor. Staff was pleasant and helpful... love the Asian housekeeping staff... they kept asking me how I was feeling. Good business printing service. Had breakfast in hotel one morning - a bit pricey but good. Husband liked nightly wine tasting. Great location. Bellman suggested car service reseration at check out since we stored bags for the afternoon - great price and on time. 20mins to Logan - at peak hour. 
One complaint: internet was annoyingly slow. Not sure why. Would absolutely stay again if internet is fixed.
This has to be the cleanest hotel I have stayed in. Excellent service and great attitude. The rooms are a little small but very comfortable.

review_title: Best meals at a week long conference ever.
review_text: Staff is amazing. All of the amenities great. I was here for a week long conference and my experience at this hotel was so good I can't wait to come back.
Always stay here when I go to Boston for business. Great rooms, service, bars, and the gym. No complaints at all!

review_title: The lobby is beautiful, yet that is where the beauty ends.
review_text: I am writing this review while sitting in my bed on my third night at the hotel. It has been snowing this weekend, and though both of my windows are securely closed, I am feeling a strong freezing breeze blowing on me. The closed shades are actually blowing away from the window. The wall in front of me has poorly painted-over patches, the ceiling dips down, again poorly painted in order to cover the cracks. This is far below what one would expect from the hotel rating and price. This is a Starwood hotel, and as a Starwood Meeting Planner member, I am quite surprised at the state of this room. After reading numerous reviews, and also knowing a couple who held their wedding at the hotel (and who felt that the hotel serviced their event wonderfully), it seems that there is a vast difference between the quality of many of their rooms. Aside from the front desk and wait staff, I found the majority of the hotel employees to be rather cold and put out if asked for assistance. I am a very pleasant, patient, and cordial person when interacting with staff, and was surprised by poor customer relations I was met with. Absolutely no complementary breakfast (and I'm only talking about coffee and toast) is provided, and I must admit that the $10 price tag for a bowl of cereal actually made me laugh, shake my head, and walk away. If you are a business traveler with an expense account, and manage to land a good room, then this hotel could be okay. Otherwise, I would avoid it completely. I would also avoid the $46 a day valet parking, and simply drive around the corner to the parking garage (the same one that valet parks your car in) and pay the $30 a day general rate. When we pulled up and asked the doorman where we could park, he really pushed valet. When we stated that we would prefer to park ourselves, he completely dismissed us, turned and walked away. Wired Internet access is available in rooms for $11 a day (slow connection) and $13 a day (advertised as faster), and wireless is only accessible in the restaurant. (bring a long extension cord because of the few outlets available for power, only one socket is located anywhere near to a table. This can also apply to the hotel room, as sockets are limited there as well.) Lastly, in the evening (9pm) it took several minutes for the water temperature to come up to a luke warm level which was still too uncomfortablly cold to shower in. All in all, I will never stay at this hotel again, and will certainly avoid ever using the hotel in conjunction with any conferences and events that I hold in Boston.
hotel_name: The Boston Park Plaza Hotel & Towers

review_text:
Mike es un excelente persona y cuida a los clientes y siempre esta atento a las necesidades de uno.
Gracias.
This hotel has a great location. Two blocks from South Station/Amtrak and the Children's Museum. A short walk to the Aquarium and Quincy Market. Take the train to Boston. You will not need a car.
This was a great place to stay.The staff was professional and friendly. The rooms were very comfortable. There are many nice touches...wine hour and in room offerings.Great location.

review_title: Best bathroom ever, great service, perfect location
review_text:
I had the pleasure of staying at the InterContinetal for two nights in June during a conference at the nearby convention center. Very comfortable, though compact for a king room. 
The bathroom was the best laid out floorplan I've ever seen. Large walkin shower, huge separate tub, with shutters opening to the bedroom letting in natural light. 
Short walking distance to the North End, close to the T, and right on the canal. Very convenient. Concierge helpful and kind. 
I have no idea how much it cost, as it was on the company, but i highly recommend it.
The hotel was clean as a whistle. We had a really large room with a huge window facing the Boston harbor. It was actually very luxurious.

review_title: Just got back from Xmas overnight
review_text: I went to Boston to see my kids overnight...hotel and city were very quiet but the room was clean...hot strong shower in the AM...thought my tv remote was dead desk delivered one in 3 minutes. Very friendly staff. Room is spacious for city room if you think it is small stay in NYC, they are small. Love the water bottles and Keurig coffee in the AM. Elephant and Castle is a nice comfy welcoming place to get a bite and a drink. Would stay again !!!

My husband had a business trip to Boston so I tagged along. His work had put us up in a nice hotel but after his work was done we decided to stay a few days at a hotel we could afford. I was a bit hesitant about staying in the financial district however after looking at map we booked our room because it didn't seem far from the hub of things. In fact Club Quarters is practically in the middle of things. Depending on what your looking for if course. It is a minutes walk from part if the freedom trail. The hotel staff was very friendly and helpful. The room was very comfortable and clean. Overall this hotel worked out perfectly! The restaurant downstairs was really fun also! If your in Boston on a budget or even if you aren't I highly recommend this hotel!

review_title: Great hotel, perfect for our needs
review_text: Overall, a really good hotel, especially for the price. Used the valet parking as other reviews indicated self parking was difficult to get to. Overall service was very good, all staff were friendly.

Booked via hotwire. After getting a small room with two seemingly small doubles my husband requested another room saying it was our anniversary. We got a wonderful upgrade to the club floor including breakfast and an evening cocktail. Nice location 5-star. I think I just prefer small touches of a boutique hotel

We stayed at the intercontinental for the Boston marathon. Im sure hundreds of other runners did too as we saw them bustling about the hotel. It is a beautiful hotel, but the staff were not willing to meet our needs for a late checkout following the marathon. We will not stay here again and will likely advise others looking for a hotel for the marathon to stay elsewhere. A late check out is an essential need for a marathoner post race.

Had a lovely stay in this hotel for new years. Really conveniently located in the back bay of boston. Great value. Only annoyance was...checkout was noon. Housekeeping knocked on the door every half hour from a little before 9am till we left at noon. Clearly when I told them to come back after 12 it didn't register. Other than that which really put a sour taste at the end, this hotel and the staff were awesome.

I would highly recommend the Intercontinental. The room was beautiful and very spacious. Housekeeping and room service staff were accommodating. The one word of caution would be to avoid the concierge for restaurant suggestions - they recommended a place that they were affiliated with and it was not "moderately" priced as we requested nor the type of gourmet we were looking for. The spa, however, was incredible and the massage was probably the best I have ever had! And, the lobster benedict we ordered from room service was phenomenal.

review_title: Great location, service but the walls are thin
review_text: This hotel seems great at first because of the great location and great service and the cute hotel dog that everyone can touch but when you are trying to sleep you nearly feel like if the people in the next room are speaking right next to you. The hotel was built in 1912 so I'm not very surprised. Apart from that everything at this hotel is great.

review_title: If you'd like to feel like royalty, book a room at the Fairmont Copley Plaza Hotel.
review_text:
I have traveled all over, and who knew my favorite hotel I've stayed at was less than an hour from where I live. I booked a room for a night on the town of Boston and I have never been treated so well. 
 The room was immaculate, the staff was friendly and very helpful, dinner & breakfast the next morning in the Oak Room were both delectable... I truly have nothing negative to say about this beautiful, historic hotel in the heart of Boston.

review_title: Business Hotel ... Geht aber auch mit Kindern.
review_text:
Neues Hotel, modern und verkehrsgÃ¼nstig gelegen. Zimmer sind Klasse mit groÃŸen Fenstern und einem teils tollen Blick in Richtung Wasser.
Ich frage mich nur immer, warum bei solchen Hotels der Internetzugang noch mal teuer bezahlt werden muss. KÃ¶nnte eigentlich schon im Preis drin sein.
SchÃ¶ner Pool und Fitness Bereich.

Perfect location for walking around and seeing the city by foot. Tons of restaurant choices, tours, and sights within a few minutes walk, and a beautiful room to top it off. They were very accommodating to an early check in and late check out, great customer service. Would highly recommend!
Always stay here given the opportunity. Phenomenal location, nice staff. On the pricier end however, but it's worth it.

This is my favorite place to stay whenever I'm in Boston for business or pleasure. The beds are extremely comfy, the rooms are clean, and I love the complimentary bath soaps (odd thing to look forward to, I know). The staff can be a little snooby sometimes, but nothing outrageous. Wonderful location, and if you don't feel like wandering out of the hotel for food, there are plenty of options in the lobby. There's even a walkway to the Copley square mall, so you don't have to venture outside on blustery days - more dining options and things to do -bonus!

If you are going to stay in Seattle, this hotel offers everything right outside its doors..the Market, the ferry, restaurants, and many things to do and see. The only thing I was missing was a fireplace in the room to warm up from checking out all that Seattle has to offer. The staff was great and the view from our room was fantastic.

The staff provide excellent customer service. This stay was a return visit & they took the time to personally recognize me by providing me breakfast & a personal thanks. This is above and beyond many hotels. Of course the beds are Heavenly, no pun intended. Also the workout center is awesome & location great, especially of you are a shopaholic, you just walk from lobby to the mall. I shall return @ you should too. Pt of ref: I'm a Platinum in Marriott & SPG, Diamond in HHonors & Diamond Delta. Travel lots.

review_title: One of the finest luxury hotels in Boston.
review_text: Had a wonderful 2 night stay here. Service was excellent. Hard to imagine how this hotel could improve. Will definitely stay here next time I am in Boston.

review_title: Amazing boutique hotel, super service, can't beat location!
review_text: We LOVED this place. Having been to Seattle several times, this was our first visit to IATM. First, I have to say that Katie at the front desk was extremely helpful with sleeping arrangements for our children, after we had a slight snafu with Expedia. She also helped us arrange transportation and reservations during our stay. What impressed us most was that she accepted total responsibility when 2 drivers appeared to pick us up at the airport. Long story, but she handled it like a total professional. That's rare, usually they blame a co-worker. As far as the room, SUPER comfortable bed, beautiful elegant bathroom, very nice mini bar selections (our kids love to snack from mini bars!). Location can't be beat. Literally a few steps from my favorite bakery at Pike Place - La Panier. Forget Starbucks and head there for the best cappuccino! Also one block from a huge Nordstrom Rack. Best shoes ever! Bell service, housekeeping service (including turndown) A+++. Can't say enough about how we loved this place, and can't wait to return.
Good hotel with easy access to harbour side activities. Some good views from the upper rooms. Pleasant bar that was not too noisy but had some atmosphere. Excellent decor in lobby atrium area.
Perfect location to Quincy Market, Aquarium, the North End and Logan. We always stay here when in Boston and since the remodel it's even better than before, which is hard to believe.

review_title: The only place we stay while in Seattle.
review_text: This will be short as I watch the sunset into the water and mountains from the 5th floor deck, While sipping a glass of red wine. I believe this is our 3rd or 4th stay, and will always be our choice while visiting Seattle. Couldn't ask for a better location - to my right is the sunset, the neon PUBLIC MARKET sign just to my left. Smell a meal being prepared down below. Rooms are very tasteful, beds quite comfortable. Service from the staff has been consistently good during each visit. I appreciate that they are friendly, personable and helpful. Our partial water view is very partial, but I may be splitting hairs. Great place to stay. Now, back to that sunset...

Having lived on Boston not too long ago I prefer the Long Wharf over any other. Super close to aquarium, harbor, Quincy Market and even North End. Never need the T from here. Legal Seafood and other nice places are literally at your door. Rooms are three star but view and location are five stars. Restaurant is good for breakfast but pricey and we'll skip next time. Fitness center is nice.

Although our room was spectacular I have to report that a pair of earrings disappeared from my room while I was having breakfast. The concierge staff were not concerned and the only thing they did was pointing me to a phone to contact lost and found dept. The room maid obviously did not find anything and barely spoke English.

The hotel was very well positioned, with regards to the downtown area. Close walking distance to the light rail, which we caught from the airport. The room was very clean. The service also great. The only negative was the loud air conditioner. The street noise was minimal. For a first time in the US, it was a great place to start the journey.

review_title: Location was awesome! T-station was right outside our door!
review_text: Access to freedom trail and T-station for transportation was excellent. You are only 2 stops on the T from the airport. Very easy to get to. My only complaint is that the guy at the front desk talked me into eating at the Marriott restaurant when I said I wanted clam chowder and I was going to go to Legal Seafood. The Marriott clam chowder was not that good. But otherwise I really enjoyed my stay and would recommend it.

Having been to New York last year I didn't think the experience could be matched. I was wrong Boston is a fantastic city and the Westin Copley was a fab place to stay. We were greeted by warm friendly staff. Our bags were kept free off charge whilst we went to explore( we were early for check in). The hotel is on the corner of a very clever network of shopping malls, including a Starbucks only seconds away from the hotel lobby. Complimentary wifi in the lobby. I liked the fact that you could use a stand alone computer in the lobby to check in for return flights hassle free and without cost. Thank you Westin for a fantastic stay in a brilliant city

review_title: Good location and hotel, but overpriced.
review_text:
Stayed here during a business conference we had and the rate for the room was high, but I guess it's typical when you stay at places and locations like this.
The room was very nice, clean and comfortable. Of course, the Internet price is not free and are charged about $10-12 for 24-hour period.
The meeting room they stuck us in was very tight and just not the best.
The location is close to many restaurants and a fast food joints too. Only thing I experienced at the hotel was the bar and it was nothing special, but pricey for the drinks. 
The hotel is close to a super market and the subway. We were able to walk to the Cheers bar from here, but it was a good walking distance.
Overall, I would not stay here on my own dime, but for business travels it works if you want to pay a lot and not get any free stuff out of it. 
It was close to a mall or shopping area, but I did not explore that.

review_title: I wish I would have spent more time in my room.
review_text: Hotel is newly built, for Boston standards, at least. Hotel is in a great location yet away from all the hustle and bustle of the city. If you are lucky enough to get a room with a Harbour view, the serenity is spectacular. I wish I would have ben able to spend more time there. The mattress quality was excellent. The size of the bathroom rather large. The hotel is split in to two buildings. Try and stay in the building where the lobby and the restaurants are. If you can't, it wouldn't be the end of the world. Breakfast in the outdoor patio is a great way to start the morning, except in winter!
We loved being at Pike Place Market. The hotel was a gem...including the French bistro downstairs. The croissants for breakfast were amazing.

This is a very nice hotel in a good location. Convenient to Subway, restaurants, sights. We had a deluxe double plus rollaway for family of four and it was fine. Nice bathroom! I would stay here again if visiting Boston!

review_title: Affordable suites in a perfect location
review_text:
We stayed here with our 3 year old right before Christmas. We always try to stay in suites so we have somewhere to go while our son is sleeping. The suite at this hotel was spacious and quiet. I did wish there was a mini-fridge in the room, though. 
The hotel staff was great. We arrived at 7:00 am after a long redeye flight, and we were able to check into the room immediately. At one point, the battery in our door lock died, and when it took more than 5 minutes to fix, we were given free breakfast vouchers for the next day. Then when our car rental place closed early on Christmas Eve, the front desk helped us try to find a place that was still open and had vehicles available. 
The location is perfect. Copley Square is just a few T stops from anywhere you want to go downtown. We got week long T passes, so we hopped on even if it was just for one stop. There is also plenty to do within a few block radius of the hotel. 
We will be back the next time we are in Boston!
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Copley Square

review_title: Great location and hotel, best place to stay in downtown Seattle.
review_text: We travel to Seattle several times a year and since our first stay at The Inn At The Market my wife will not stay anywhere else. Best location and staff. The rooms are spacious and have an understated elegance.

We recently got Ames hotel through a priceline bid. We were a little nervous of how "fancy" the hotel looked since we were traveling with our 3 year old. The room was beautiful and very modern. We had a queen bed and we were upgraded to a king bed for free quickly since we had our daughter with us. The location was perfect for us. We walked to the aquarium, childrens museum, and fanuill hall within minutes as well as the T. The people at the front desk and the concierge are among the nicest and most helpful people I have encountered at a hotel. They quickly printed out directions for us and made dinner reservations. If I had to say anything negative the only thing I would say is that I could hear a lot of street noise at night even on the 7th floor but I don't sleep well anyway. My husband slept right through it. I would highly recommend this hotel!

Perfect location on the waterfront with great views of Boston harbor. In the North End with some of the best restaurants. The history of Boston is at your front door. 
 The rooms have everything you could ask for and the staff is friendly and eager to help.

This was out first stay in the north end area of Boston. We had planned to visit the New England Aquarium and chose this hotel because of the proximity being within walking distance. We were able to check in early at 11am. Our room was very clean and comfortable. Lots of great places to choose from for dining, coffee and scenery all within walking distance. The staff went above and beyond to make our stay comfortable by sending someone out to purchase a heating pad when they no longer had one available.

review_title: Wonderful stay as expected, a little far from main attractions
review_text: Luxury is as expected. Check-in staff and concierge were top-notch. Staff remembering check-in notes about anniversary was a plus. No coffee in room, even upon request was a let down. $10 pot of coffee is a bit steep. Could have more working plugs in this day and age. Pay for internet is a bit passe. Amenities were a bit stingy. No refills or replacement after use, even though I had stayed for 3 nights. Location is a little far from the main attractions, so you will have to take either a tour or learn to use the subway. Management handled security well despite the raucous outside from the July 4th celebrations. Express check-out was painless.

Hotel has a youthful feel, partly due to its lively bar; but also due to its energetic staff and modern decor. 
The hotel is difficult to locate, there is no signage out front and the door staff are scruffy and without uniform.
Inside however it thankfully changes. Good decor, excellent staff. Although, bathroom was a little dark. Hotel has a small boutique feel.
Solid hotel for business or a weekend break. I would return.

Terrible place to stay in the summer. There are large outdoor bars on both sides of the hotel that you can clearly hear from the guest rooms. We were on the top floor (7), and could hear the din of the crowd above the noise of our air conditioner. We're in our late 30s, and it still disrupted our sleep. The noise doesn't quiet down until about 12:30 or 1:00am. Big disappointment. I'd stay elsewhere if I were you
We stay in a lot of hotels in Seattle, but this is our favorite. The location is great. The service is great. Love it.
Probably the most accommodating hotel my wife and I have ever visited. location, service, friendly people, the best consierge ever,and on and on. Would go back in a heart-beat!

review_title: Great hotel in a great location!
review_text: I had a great stay at this convenient hotel. The rooms were clean, nice, and the staff was great.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Copley Square

review_title: Phenominal location and good quality hotel.
review_text: If you are lucky enough to stay here for a reasonable rate take the opportunity to do so. Rooms are quiet, clean, well appointed, clean, nicely decorated, clean, sizeable, clean, and with a great view.

review_title: Absolutely first class on the world class scale
review_text: We spent ten wonderful days in this hotel. I would single out the unfailing friendiness of the staff and their dedication to service.

Nice room, excellent staff, BUT the subway noise is just too invasive. You cannot sleep with the noise unless you normally live under a flight path in a busy city. Trust me, look elsewhere if you need a good night's sleep. and if you don't believe me and book anyway, don't say you were not warned!

Great time. Clean hotel. Very friendly staff. Subway access right outside the door which goes everywhere. 
Will stay there again!

The liberty hotel was an old jail that was renovated to be a modern hotel. Our room had an amazing view of the Charles river. The nightlife in the hotel was very happening but the hotel rooms were very quiet. Location was great! Next to the red line stop and Charles street. It was a short walk to Boston commons and fennuel hall. Only negative was the hotel restaurant, clink, had awful service. Very slow and they gave us the wrong food.

We stayed here for two nights as part of our summer vacation. This place is beautiful and in a wonderful, safe part of the city. I worried a bit that it wasn't very close to the T, but it was a very short walk (10 mins) to the nearest station. And the walk is enjoyable too. We walked along the harbour and through a beautiful park to get to the Aquarium and the T is right there. A three minute walk will put you on Hanover Street where you'll find lots of restaurants and shops. 
Our room was upgraded upon check in to a harbour view. Very nice. 
The rooms are a little tight. There is no space for a cot. The bathroom however is spacious and had a wonderful soaker tub and a separate rainforest shower. 
As for the staff, we were mostly treated very well. The front desk and especially the guys at the front door were very friendly and helpful. The only negative came from one guy in the lounge. My husband and I just returned from an afternoon Red Sox game, still wearing our ballcaps and t-shirts. We sat down for a drink. I felt a bit unwelcome there. Don't know if there was a dress code, or if he was a Yankee fan. Other than that, do not hesitate to stay here. I would love to come back, and hope to in the near future.

review_title: Great location, staff was a bit rude, under renovation, jackhammers start at 7am
review_text: Poor wine selections, staff seemed too busy to be nice, didn't get the type of room we requested. Great location, rooms were freshly renovated and clean. Easy walk to all kinds of food and tourist attractions

I had a flight delay, and it was the airline that put us up in this hotel. I felt that I could ready enjoy it, as I didn't hace to pay the bill. The bed a queen size & was wonderful & the way it was dressed with lots of pillows & cushions. 
The room was so large that I have stated in smaller sites in 5star hotels.
The mini bar, was nit just overt priced like other hotels, it was extortion, & I refused to indulge. 
Should I have the misfortune to have to return to Boston I would happily stay there.

review_title: excellent service leads to excellent stay
review_text:
One of the best cared for of the courtyard properties. The front desk was excellent in every way. Thanks for the great stay.
This is a great hotel if you want a major brand in a great place, but you want more of a specialty hotel feel.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Copley Square

review_text:
We stayed in a Deluxe Corner King room. We were on the 4th floor
It was obnoxiously loud the first night! I read a few other reviews that mentioned it being noisy, but I had no idea it would that bad. We've stayed in other cities this big before, but this is the loudest it's ever been. A white noise machine would really have helped! We were traveling with a baby, and I don't know if the put us there as opposed to a higher floor to keep from disturbing other guests or what. Our room was above the large patio area of the Woodward restaurant which becomes a large, loud bar area on the weekends. We were there on a Sat & Sun night. Sunday night was better, but there were might be a hospital near by because we heard many sirens that night as well. 
Other than the noise, we loved the hotel. It has a very tendy, modern vibe. It was surprisingly a very child friendly room. The bed was very low, and I liked that the room had hard wood or faux wood floors. You can't beat the location. You are about a 5/10 minute walk from Boston Common on one side and the North End on the other. You're even closer than that to Quincy Market.
If you can help it, don't drive in Boston! There are tons of tunnels close to this area, and it's very east to get turned around. 
We had room service for dirr and lunch one day. The food is from the kitchen of the Woodward restaurant, and it was good. We also walked to Mike's Pastry one morning for cannoli. It was amazing, and you feel a little less guilty about it after all the walking you do in the city. 
The only other warning is that there is a big homeless shelter right next door to the hotel. The people stay in that area in benches aok around the hotel. We saw them get in a few fights in the two days we were there. I wouldn't have felt comfortable walking around there at night.

This place was awesome. It was very clean and the staff was wonderful. I loved the rooms and they were quiet! No hearing your neighbor or people in the halls. The location was perfect, right next to train stop, trolley tours and aquarium. Acrossd the street was Quincy market to shop. I will come back here again every time.

review_title: Wonderful boutique hotel in the heart of Boston!
review_text: We took a chance with a last minute reservation through the "HotelTonight" app (very good btw). The Ames exceeded our expectations in every category. Clean, spacious and beautiful room and bath. The staff was very friendly esp. the concierge who easily determined the best places to dine near our venue. The bed was so comfortable that I did not want to leave. The bathroom is very cool (!) with the shower wall made of glass which overlooks the bedroom (if u keep the sheer curtain open)... Definitely will be visiting the Ames again...

The hotel is unique. Beautiful inside, the room was nice & cozy. The bathroom was perfect!!! There are lounges & restaurants in the hotel which was convenient. Had the view of the river & fireworks through my own window! Loved it

This hotel is gorgeous! And what a great place to people watch! We stayed in the jail section. They said it might be loud at night, but we didn't hear a thing. Didn't even have to drive into Boston. We took the bus to south station, then hopped on the red line of the T, and the hotel was right across the street.. Within walking distance of the north end. We ate at the Clink restaurant which was excellent! I would absolutly stay again!!

We've stayed at the Inn at the Market before and always loved it. This time we were in town for just one night. The Inn was still as cute and well located as always. But I must admit to feeling that maybe it is a bit overpriced. With the Four Seasons next door now, the Inn has more competition than it used to. I also found the bellman completely unhelpful. But that's probably an aberration. Overall, still nice. But next time we may opt for the FS, whereas in the past the Inn has always been our first choice.

review_title: Modern hotel with central location and great service
review_text: This is by far one of my favorite hotels to stay at, not only in Boston but anywhere. I travel to Boston for work but have also chosen this hotel when traveling on my own dime. Rooms are a good size and decorated well. Comfy beds, great shower. The staff is friendly and helpful if you need directions or recommendations. You also great great bath products and on occasion I've been surprised by cookies and milk delivered to my room!

I stayed in room 627. The bathroom was from the 1940's. There was no heat duct in the bathroom and the temperature was probably 60 degrees. The closet in the room was even colder. 
I called the management inthe morning and they sent a portable heater to the room. They said its an older building and they will be doing some remodeling. Sorry for the inconvenience was their position. When blow drying my hair, the circuit breaker blew out. 15 minutes later they reset it. Again, sorry for the inconvenience, however now I was running behind schedule. As an accomodation, they took the breakfast charge off the bill.

The converted prison is an architectural marvel combined with excellent service makes this establishment stand out ! If you like The W style of lobby bars then you will never look at a W in the same way once you see the w/e scene at The Liberty.
It's a must and will be repeated.
Great value, location, and standard. Call first to make sure that there is no construction going on outside. I'm laying awake because 24 hour construction is happening outside my window. So loud!!!!

Location: Â Shopping arcade with high-end retail connects this property and others to the Hynes Convention Center. Â Located in the heart of Back Bay, the Westin is also close to several T (subway) lines, the Boston Public library, and some great running and biking trails.
Accommodations: Â Very nice rooms with breathtaking views from the higher floors. Â Great beds. Â The clock radios have iPhone docking stations so if one forgets the plug-in charger, no worries!
Service: okay -- not great! Â I checked in to find pubes in the bathroom and a room phone with makeup on the receiver. Â The breakfast buffet had good food but the service sucked just about every morning. Â The servers were so slow with drink refills that I had to refill my own juice and water two mornings in a row. Â And, for $20 the buffet should include an omelette station, it doesn't. Only my 15 percent conference discount made the price tolerable.
Lastly, I want to commend management for keeping the hotel guests apprised of developments during the little East Coast Earthquake. Â The tremor caused the all but one of the hotel elevators to shut down making my 33rd-floor room tough to access after lunch. Â The manager sent no less than three voicemail blasts to guests during the afternoon, the last of which let guests know when all elevators were back online.
Overall, a pretty nice place, I would stay here again if I needed to be close go the convention center.

I am Diamond with Hilton Honors and spend on average over 40 nights a year traveling for business. This hotel has it all. Great location and outstanding associates. Very helpful and friendly. Will be back when I am in Boston again. Sorry Hilton.

review_title: Great location if you want to be by the water
review_text: Gym is awesome as recently updated. Conciege lounge has good view but food is not great. Legal Seafood is very close. Great service and would stay again. View from my room was awesome.

review_title: Really beautiful lobby, nice room, GREAT location!!!
review_text: Happy to be staying here. We have stayed in many hotels in Boston and liked most of them. The Long Wharf is great because of the location to so many attractions. We ate next door at Chart House and it was fantastic. Nice clean room, plenty of space, even a little waterview from the room. Very happy.

Totally NOT a 4 star hotel. No idea how they got that rating. Location is good, everything after that is downhill. 
Service was abysmal. Lots of 'not my job' going on. 40 minutes for bags to be brought up, room never cleaned consistently, always took @ least 3 people pointing to figure out how to get car from valet, etc, etc, etc. 
I began to refer to it as the Holiday Inn. It is a solid 2-3 star hotel. Way overpriced. Add to that 46/per night to park and you have a stay at the Westin. 
Not sure who they paid to get the 4 star rating, but let's hope they treat them better they treat the guests.

Travelled to this hotel for a meeting. Arrived in the evening pouring rain & no one there to open the door. There was a doorman there every other day. Very old and historic hotel. Beautiful foyer. Rooms are consistent with the period hotel. But door frames need to be painted Bathroom was very small (had a $500 Suite) with very little counter space. Compared to similar Fairmont properties the bathroom was less than I expected likely consistent with the age of the property. Dog barking in the next room concerns me about the cleanliness of the carpets if pets are allowed. Hotel staff very curtious. Excellent location for shopping. Oak Room restaurant nice atmosphere. Average Food. Overall nice Hotel but overrated.

review_title: DO NOT STAY HERE BED BUGS
review_text: I stayed here for 2 nights. After the first night I had a small few bites I thought maybe I was allergic to something. After the 2nd night the bites were everywhere. I told mgmt. They brought someone in and they confirmed it was bed bugs. All we were offered was our $ back after having to throw away our stuff because we didn't want to bring the bed bugs home.

Can't tell you what a nice place, super people and great location the Ames is. From the front desk to the maids and everyone in between were just great. The rooms were a thing of beauty, and squeaky clean. And finally, the location, oh my God. You are right on the Freedom Trail in the heart of it all. Kudos Ames, you made us all very, very happy!

review_title: Clean & modern, great location for tourists
review_text: taking the MBTA from the airport is a bit complex with 4 different segments. It is do-able, but with suitcases, we chose a taxi for the ride back to the airport. Modern, clean, convenient, expensive.

review_title: Great location, personalized service expected in a boutique hotel.
review_text: Great location, hotel and staff do a great job incorporating that into their service. Friendly and excited. Very refreshing and relaxing.

What a unique, memorable, nostalgic place! Everything from the exterior to the interior was incredible. The history of the place is both sad and intriguing. Clink was great. Rooms/service/food was phenomenal. There isn't even a need to go out at night to find nightlife, because on the weekend the place is hoppin'. Definitely worth checking out!

Room was small. Window facing Mass General Hospital wall. Bathroom dusty. Towel shredded at seams. Molton Brown shower toiletries attached to wall, difficult to dispense, disassembled. Shower floor plastic and slippery. Matress quality inferior. Waterproof mattress cover made bed uncomfortable. Champagne was nice and after hours happening and vibrant but if you are looking for quality accommodations, not worth the price.
Lobby was ridiculously loud at night (rap group performing one night). Hotel rooms were just okay, although the view/location was very nice.

review_title: Great location, nicely appointed rooms with good views!
review_text: Had great view of Copley Plaza, Charles River to Cambridge and downtown skyline. Great location in the heart of Back Bay, Boston. Excellent choice anytime, but especially in the winter or spring when Boston weather can be harsh and unpredictable. Hotel is connected to the Copley Place Mall which also connects to Prudential center. Able to get to either Green or Orange line T stops without going outside, as well as many shops and restaurants within the malls, or use as passage way to travel several blocks while protected from the elements. Great starting point for most of your tourist ventures and easy to find your way back to from anywhere you go.
Loved the Fourth of July fireworks right from our room. Walk to mall and Copley Square. Even close enough to Charles River. Best Boston experience we have ever had!

Location is excellent. Close to Quincy market, lots of restaurants, bars and coffee shops. Bed was so comfortable, my wife didnt want to get up in the morning. Lol. Would have been nice to have a coffee maker in the room, there was 24hr coffee in the lobby, but it was cold and old. Good thing there is a starbucks a block away. The main stop for the trolly tour is steps away and we used it to get a feel for the area. I would recommend that as well. ( old town trolly). There is a lot to see in the area.

review_title: Superb location and room for the price.
review_text: Ideal location and spacious comfortable and pleasant room made for a great stay in Boston. Cleaning staff were lovely, reception staff efficient but a little lacking in warmth. Overall one of the best hotels we've stayed in. Wouldn't hesitate to recommend it.

While the lobby is a bit of a scene, once you wade past all the party-goers, behind lurks a great hotel. Interesting history and architecture, a great vie of the city, convenient location, stylish but not uber-trendy furnishings, and I will never forget that water pressure blew... Nearly blew me out of the shower - love it!

review_title: Great hotel, reasonably priced, excellent central location
review_text: This hotel is perfectly located to access all of the city centre's attractions. It is only a few minutes walking from the harbor, north end restaurants and Boston common. There is a great bar attached to the hotel and the staff are friendly and attentive. At less than $200 per night, we would recommend it highly.

The Langham is a nice enough hotel, in the old federal reserve building. The room we had was pretty small and had no natural light. I was surprised at how easy you could hear the people next door and in the hallway. Service was great and everyone really went out of their way to make sure our stay was good. Overall, a nice place to stay but the design and decor was a little too old school for me.

We stayed here for five nights, the room was tight on space but quite luxurious and cosy with a good view, we were on the tenth floor. The hotel itself is very opulent and historic but the best thing about it is the location- right on the freedom. Trail and a stones throw from Boston common- brilliant.

review_title: Hidden "gem". location and staff, enough said.
review_text:
Frequently travel to Boston for work. Prior to my recent two night stay, I had never used this hotel. Moving forward- I'll only stay here.
Location- perfect nook right in the heart of the city. So surprised at proximity to just about everything Boston has to offer. 
Staff- They don't make them like this anymore
Added bonus: complimentary beer (good beer!), upon returning from a long work day. It's the little touches as such that put it in my category of a "gem".
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Copley Square

review_title: Great location, friendly staff, unsatisfactory room
review_text: Great location. Staff was very friendly. We stayed in a bi- level room with a pullout couch for the kids. The room decor was outdated and a bit musty. The room faced the street and the noise at night made sleeping difficult-- the rooms just don't seem well insulated from the noise. We checked out early and went to the four seasons instead for just a bit more money. Perhaps the other rooms at the Inn are better. We were disappointed.

review_title: The mist wonderful hotel for our wedding night!
review_text: Our day was perfect, and due to an unexpected family friend at your hotel named Wade we arrived to a fabulous room with a huge deck overlooking the market with a full water view unlike another found in Seattle. We would recomend this hotel to everyone who is looking for the best! Great location, best Seattle view, excellent service and thoughtfulness. Also, the bed is so comfy, my husband wants me to find out where we can buy one!

We stayed at the Copely Westin for a conference. It was convenient to most everything, including downtown - subway, walking, cab. Rooms were very nice - spacious, clean, well decorated. Loved the single brew starbucks in the room! The only complaint is the honor bar in sensors. They went off easily and I was charges for things I didn't take, but the front desk quickly removed them from my bill. Great overall stay.

My wife and I were able to stay here recently for our 3 year anniversary. I emailed ahead asking for some recommendations for dinner and the concierge got us awesome reservations at the top rated (trip advisor) seafood restaurant. Nina, you rock!! Thank you for your help too!! My wife loved the room and the view. Only problem we had which was quickly resolved was a $200.00 charge for smoking in our room. But I think it was a room next to us and the charge was quickly reversed. This hotel is central to all you want to see and do in Boston. Cross the street to the T and awesome food within walking distance. A great experience with awesome staff. Look forward to coming back.

This is our second visit to the Courtyard Copley Square. The second stay was every bit as good as the first we were even welcomed back. We asked if it was possible to have the room we had last time but it was taken but the desk clerk got us an identical room on a different floor. The Copley has definitely become our hotel of choice for future stays.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Copley Square

review_title: Our Best Stay Ever in Boston
review_text: We found the Courtyard Copley by chance we usually stay at the Long Wharf location but they were sold out. The front desk offered Copley as an alternative. We didn't know what to expect but we found to our suprise that although small the hotel was very comfortable and the staff very friendly and helpful. The location was unbelievable and although not on the water had as many local attractions as that area. The rate we paid was a little high probably because it was a last minute booking. The agent did note that they always had specials online that are usually a lot better. We will give the Copley another try on our next visit if we an get a good deal.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Copley Square

review_text:
Checked in today and I am floored by how dirty the rooms are.
My room is missing a picture on the wall, the decor and wall paint is not very modern, and the carpet is disgusting!
My husband and I reserved a king room and when we checked in we were given double beds! We complained and apparently the hotel is fully booked. 
I am very very disappointed in our room and the hotel. The room is not a room in a luxury hotel but more like a 3 star hotel.

The Inn is a very comfortable and stylish set of apartments. Â Located in a quiet area of Back Bay it's a 10 min walk from the train station and 2 mins from the subway.
Our family of 4 adults stayed for four nights in one of the two bedroom apartments. Very Nice! Â The main living area has a large lounge, chairs and dining table. The main bedroom was large but the second bedroom was a tad too small for our two sons 18 and 20 YO. The trundle bed was also, a little two small for our 6'6" 18 YO so he slept quite well on the lounge. The second bedroom is large enough for teenage or younger children and even has its own cable TV. In fact both bedrooms and the lounge room have a TV each. Â That's Â right three TVs!
The kitchenette is small, with a two plate hot plate, a microwave and a small oven. There is no dishwasher and not a lot of room to wash up and stack drying dishes. Â It would have been nice to have tea towel to dry things. Â The full size fridge allows you to stock some nice wines cheeses from the nearby markets. Although the kitchen is small we successfully cooked a few meals but as an alternative, there are loads of restaurants and cafes nearby.
The sole bathroom is an excellent size with good lighting.
Security and access is controlled by an access code for the front door and apartment. This means that you can access the apartment at any time after the office has closed.
Tom and the staff in the office were more than helpful and even assisted with some maps and tour stuff.
The exercise room and laundry facilities are ample for the accommodation. We were grateful for the business centre as we had some work matters come up that needed attention.
There is a convenience store across the road and the Prudential centre for more in depth shopping is in the next street.
We will definitely stay here next time we come back to Boston.
Top notch, top drawer, upper crust. Name the superlative, it applies. Beautiful property. Super classy.

My husband and I just had a wonderful 5 nights stay at the inn at the market when we were in Seattle. We will not stay anywhere else ever in Seattle. For the location, the atmosphere and the service I can frankly say it can't be beat. I wake up each morning and open the curtains and see the mountains and the market vendors loading their stores and smile. The service is also very good. We went to pioneer square, bainbridge island with a wonderful ferry ride, Fremont, Ballard and university village. It's so welcoming that I cancelled the Alexis to stay here 2 wks later when we take our flight back home. That tells a lot. î—

review_title: Special Birthday cup cakes for Steve Nordstrom
review_text: The Hypnosis bed is comfy. The location is perfect to the pike place chowder, number one place to eat in trip advisor. Walking distance to Washington State ferries, Bainbridge and Bremerton Island. Light Rail is $2.50 from sea Tac airport. Overall a good Birthday gateway.

I've stayed at Liberty every three weeks for the last year. Good points: excellent location, Â professional and friendly staff, one-of-a-kind charm (former jail!) Not-so-good: Very fashionable and loud place on Friday and Saturday nights, lots of beautiful people to wade thru on your way to the elevators.

review_title: Quiet in-room, but noisy lobby every night of stay. Large bathroom but small counterspace.
review_text: This is my 4th stay at this hotel. I still find in-room to be quiet. You can't hear your neighbors but you can hear people out in the hall. The lobby becomes a party place after about 6 pm so be ready to fight your way out to the front driveway if you are going out at night... Even during the weeknights. On Friday just before lunch, it took about 20 minutes to hail a cab for me. I was 4th in line. I ended up having to raise my hand to hail it myself cuz the whistle they use wasn't very effective. The front design of the building could be better, but I love the large bathrooms, the separate bathtub/ shower. And the quietness and the aircon of the rooms is heavenly after an extremely hot and muggy day. Room service was fast our first night, but that was the worst pulled pork sandwich ever--- pork was dry, they added ham and pickles so it was too salty, the bun was reversed so the sauce drained right off the meat and onto my shirt, and the pork was NOT marinated. Also the sweet potato fries were NOT that sweet. No more room service for the rest of our stay. But all other services were done well.
My wife and have just enjoyed three lovely nights at the langham Boston the hotel is clean and very comfortable bed only week point was the concierge Who did not know much about the city

review_title: Very cool hotel, well situated with good roms and facilities.
review_text: We stayed just two nights here and we wished it was a little longer. The hotel was really easy to find from the station, just short walk through a pedestrian only park. The aparments were very stylishly done, with pretty much everything you could want. We didn't see much of the staff but when we did they were helpful and polite. It was perhaps a little expensive, but it did have a lot of character and quickly felt like home.

I have been staying frequently at this hotel for the last two years. I consider it to be my home away from home while I am in Boston. My company used to book my travel for me but now I call or email the hotel directly. The service is as personal as you wouldn't believe and its obvious that the staff and management take pride in their property. I meant to write a review a long time ago so this is for my freinds at Copley from Mr IHRD see you soon guys.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Copley Square

review_text: I would just like to give a shout out to the two Justins they never forget my name. No matter how long since my last visit. This time I was with my wife and we were celebrating 35 years together and we got a nice bottle of white wine to start off our evening. The staff didn't have to do anything but it is typical of the service I have come to expect at this hotel. Thank you.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Copley Square

review_text: Enjoyed our stay immensely at the Courtyard Copley the weather was terrible but the hotel had free hot coffee every morning and warm apple cider and cookies in the evening which the kids loved. The staff were very friendly and helpful. Will come back in the spring and hopefully see more of the city.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Boston Copley Square

review_text: You can't beat the location, the room and amenities are comfortable and is a part of history.

review_title: One of a kind hotel in Boston!
review_text:
Everything was just perfect,
The first day we came in we desided to prolong our stay for another night.
The Nespresso coffee machine at breakfast was a wonderful surprise, ouner was very nice and helpful. We even drove all the way to Matouk factory store to buy those wonderful towels we had in the room!!
We will deffinatly recommend this lovely place for anyone going to Boston, and if we ever back to the USA and to Boston, ST Botolph is our place there:)
Beautiful hotel, convenient location, big rooms! One block from Quincy Market where there is shopping and lots of restaurants, and close to the aquarium. The views from the hotel are awesome!

It is very easy to find a more expensive hotel in Boston, but there is no hotel better then The Inn. Rooms are spacious' comfortable, clean, fully equipped like a home. The location is great as you are right by the subway and within walking distance of some of the best restaurants in Boston. WiFi was good and every morning you can avail yourself of the complimentary breakfast with the best espresso you will get anywhere. Stayed here for five days and could live here and be very happy and comfortable. Don't even think about staying anywhere else if you can get a reservation here.

Wonderful check in/check out experience. I checked in online, so they had my room packet ready upon arrival. I was in my room in less than 2 min. The room was tiny (see pics) they should not put a king bed in such a small space. I definitely could not stay there for more than one or two days I would have went crazy. The food both catered at the conference and at dinner in the lounge was very good. I stayed for a conference so the rate was reduced, but the regular rate is just ridiculous I would never pay.

review_title: Great location and beautifully designed rooms!
review_text: We booked through hot-wire and received a great rate given how nice this hotel was. Our room was adequately spacious. We enjoyed our stay thanks to a helpful and friendly staff and an ideal location in the centre of Back Bay-close walk to many of Boston's major highlights! I'd stay here again!

Lovely grand dame type hotel, restaurant worth visiting, beds &linen top notch, rooms a bit on small side & though our bathroom huge only one small handbasin & elderly difficult to use shower!
Location really quiet but near to sights, etc. All the staff happy to help in all departments, we had a lovely time here
This hotel is very nice in a great location very close to the aquarium and Faneuil Hall and it's shops. My only complaint was the noise at night with workers below on the street.
The standards you expect ofmvci plus more. Everyone so helpful and friendly, nothing was too much trouble. Just needed a change in the weather..snow in october!
Great room, good room service food, decent bar, but a little pricey. It was also further that I thought it would be from the convention center. Overall, good experience

review_title: Remodeled, Clean Rooms, Great Service, Central Location in Downtown Boston
review_text:
Stayed here for a conference the last week of March. The hotel has been remodeled, and the rooms, and the public areas look wonderful. My room was on the 32nd floor with a great view of downtown Boston. Request a high floor, you will not be sorry. The hotel is located in Copley Square, and is easily reached off of I-90, Amtrak is right across the street in the Back Bay Station, it is also next to the Green T and Orange T lines, so getting around town is simple.
The room was very clean, new carpets, furniture, wall coverings, large HD TV, in room Starbucks. My room was a junior suite with a king bed, and a day bed that turned into a pull out for the kids.
The food was great, had room service about 4 times, very prompt, under 30 min delivery every time. The restaurants were very good as well. I ate in Turners which is seafood, as well as The Palm. Each let you charge to the room so I could get triple SPG points.
Not much on the downside other than parking is valet at $40 per day, the bathrooms need a little better lighting, and the bell men will not let you use luggage carts to take your own luggage out to your vehicle. I guess they really want those tips.... Minor stuff though.
I will always stay at this hotel when in Boston.
Great central location. Good service. Rooms are small. Even the deluxe room was very small. The bathroom is very small.

You cannot beat the service or the location of this hotel. I always try to stay ar a Westin just because of the coma inducing beds But this time the bed was not up to the usual standard. Second the room was too hot. I turned down the temp. To 60 but still no luck. 
The service is worth the stay. I would go back despite the things I ran into during this stay. Great value and great service

review_title: Fantastic historic structure with best location in Boston for vacationers!
review_text: I traveled to Boston for vacation with my 8 yr old son during the heart of summer. Historic facility in a city in which your surrounded by history! Subway is right outside your door! Faniel Hall right next door! New Kennedy Greenway and Harbor right out the front door! Use the pool at the Marriott Long Wharf, visit the observation deck, gameroom, movie room, and bfast room! This rare "urban" Vacation Club also functions as a Hotel, and is a winner. I only wish Marriott would build more "in city" Vacation Clubs!

review_title: Historic Hotel in a Great Location
review_text: We stayed in the Parker House because it is such a famous place and because it has a perfect location for us. It is within easy walking distance to the Quincy Market area, the North End and Back Bay, as well as to the transportation hubs of North Station, South Station and Downtown Crossing. Our room was attractive enough, if a bit dated, but it was so small. The bathroom was claustrophobic and we had a view of a very tall wall, i.e. We couldn't see the sky. The lobby and other public spaces are grand but somewhat dreary. A freshening up is in order.

review_title: Nice hotel in good location. Expected nicer room.
review_text: I booked this hotel through sniqueaway and paid 140 a night for Friday and Saturday stay. I would have thought that the service, amenities and rooms would have been just a little higher-end for how much the rooms go for at regular price. The hotel is in a very convenient area- just a short walk from Back Bay station, the Prudential Center and nice shopping streets. The rooms are pretty small. The photos make it look larger. The shower is an older-style tub vs the shower enclosure I was expecting. Bed is comfy, tv is big (but very few basic channels). I would stay here again if I got a good deal- but even for the 140 I paid I would rather stay at another hotel I like, such as the Ames, if there was a special.

review_title: Great city, great hotel, great location
review_text:
Really happy with the Back Bay hotel, lovely rooms and a good base to explore the city. Freedom trail walking distance one way and Pru center etc shops the other way.
Free coffee in reception when we visited and free bottled water in the rooms both very handy.

I really dislike paying a lot of money for a hotel room...but location and elegance at the Parker House really made our stay in Boston that much better!
I booked through www.booking.com and got a good rate for a 4 night stay and double bed room. (no hassles at all on checkin) The room was a tight fit for the double beds with absolutely no view, but it was extremely clean and SUPER comfortable! A single bed would have made for a perfect size room!
For our last afternoon, they had no problems holding our bags till our departure in the early evening! (Extra sightseeing!!)
We really enjoyed our stay!

My wife and I booked a room for her birthday. When we entered the gorgeous lobby we will filled with excitement. We were surprised when we checked in that we were upgraded to a suite!! It was awesome! We were overlooking an old church on the freedom walk. Our sitting room had a nice tv, couch, desk, an being a corner unit had two windows overlooking two streets. The bedroom was very cozy and the bathroom was perfect.
The bar downstairs was fun and the restaurant was good. You must stay here.

Stayed in this Boston landmark hotel for a conference which I attended. The service was impeccable at this hotel. The staff was highly attentive and yet unobtrusive. The hotel's restaurants had wonderful old world charm and the menu items were both varied and appetizing. Highly recommend this hotel.

The day of check in the hotel was able to let us check in early. Olivia @ the front desk was fabulous knowing it was one of our birthdays she made sure we had champange and boston cream pie! The traditional room is a great price and big enough for 2. The location is supurb, we walked to everything. The only bad thing is my truck was damaged in the valet garage. Not a little ding a huge dent!!!! But overall the Omni parker is a great place. We will stay here every time we visit Boston. Just to update...the Valet manager called today 9/11/11 to appologize and he was very nice! It means alot to me.

review_title: Great location, wonderful staff, very nice rooms and lots of extras.
review_text: First of all this was one of the few hotels in Boston who not only advertised a military rate but actually honored the offer. Fantastic staff who responded with light speed. Very nice room, heated towel racks and nepresso coffee a nice perk. Had lunch at the hotel on our first day. Over priced and the quality just not there. Clam chowder lumpy, seemed to be thickened with corn starch or from a can and not adequately mixed. So bottom line is great hotel, wonderful staff, fantastic rooms just eat elsewhere.

review_title: I'll stay here on my next visit
review_text: I love this hotel. Great location and staff. The rooms are well appointed but they are small. The hotel has a nice downstairs bar (Cuffs) that serves decent food, esp the burger.

review_title: Great look, staff, location, but small room, and expensive
review_text: The Parker feels plush and looks fantastic. Classic high end hotel, with if the walls could talk vibe. Has modern conveniences, but not designed for them. Room with 2 double beds is small, with tiny dresser and desn crammed in. Small bathroom with doll sink. Clean, very comfortable beds, perfect location, centered around all the big attractions and walks. High price does make you think twice at $250, but Boston not cheap anyway.

I travel often to Boston for business and always stay at the Lenox Hotel. However, this last trip was booked with short notice and the Lenox had no vacancies, so I stayed at the Back Bay hotel. My trip was for 10 nights, so I booked a deluxe king - smart move. The room was spacious, the closet with plenty of room for all my clothes and the bathroom - equipped with dual shower head and heated towel rack - was just enough to make me feel at home. 
Service from the front desk, maid service, bellman and valet were always with a smile. 
Location is easy to/from Logan. Walking distance to lots of bars & restaurants and just a couple blocks to the green & orange lines and the Amtrak station. 
For my next trip to Boston, I'll definitely be staying at the Back Bay Hotel...my new Boston favorite!!!

review_title: Great location; good service; aging hotel
review_text: The Parker House has a great location for exploring Boston and staff was generally good Biggest downfall is the tiny bathrooms (older hotel) so if that's not an issue for you, go for it.

Great front desk and service staff. Nice rooms well appointed , several mirrors but no decent lighting near the mirrors. View from the observation deck is amazing.
We attended the presentation of Marriott's new program and found the salesman loud, talking down to those present and completely unprofessional and high pressure,not at all like anyone we have met in 24 years with Marriott!

review_title: Loved the party atmosphere with a heavy touch of class
review_text: Stayed at Liberty with my girlfriend for a weekend in May to celebrate her bday. Champagne on check in, beautiful lobby, ideal location in Beacon Hill right along the Charles, across the street from a T stop - what more could you ask for

review_title: A pleasant surprise in down town boston
review_text: Built in 1857 and tastefully restored this hotel is a cool place to bring a family - I write this note from the hotel bar ;-). We chose this place because virgin atlantic cancelled our flight home, due to the evil "irene" storm come hurricane come tornado. I would definately return but next time minus the kids.

review_title: Wish I could have stayed longer
review_text:
The Back Bay was the perfect hotel at the right price for a two night stay in Boston. We booked through Hotwire and only had to pay $279 a night which was a nice deal. The service provided exceeded our expectations with the helpful doorman taking our bags up to our room and the friendly front desk staff. The room we had was great with comfy beds, modern touch to it and a large clean bathroom WITH HEATED TOWEL RACKS! 
The complimentary bottled was a nice touch. Our room however was across from the construction site but the windows kept the noise out so that was nice. 
Overall a great hotel in a great city and a place to definitely stay at again in the future.

We stayed here at the last minute as a result of price line.com. We found everything first class. The location is perfect for sightseeing and shopping, the staff is both knowledgeable and courteous, and the room had lots of amenities. It even had a light sensor in the bathroom and a heated towel bar. The cuff restaurant had great drinks and a terrific late night menu We loved our experience, and never for one second did we feel like second class citizens as a result of our price line reservation. Special thanks to Sandy, Maria, Heather and Amy for their helpful suggestions, and many thanks for the late checkout! We will be back!
Arrived tired after flight from UK and were greeted with politeness and friendliness by all. Great location, free coffee on Sunday mornings and the best pillows I can remember, will definitely return

review_title: Fab location - hotel not so great
review_text:
I was here for 9 nights as part of a business trip to the US. When I checked on I was given room 759 which was tiny, very dark and cramped and looked out onto a brick wall. It was also very noisy. I asked if I could move and was given room 1028 which was almost twice the size, bright and airy with a view towards the harbour and much quieter.
The room itself was fine but the public areas of the hotel are dark and dowdy. I know the hotel is old but it just feels lacklustre.
There are coffee makers in the rooms and if you sign up to the loyalty programme you get free wifi and a choice of drinks delivered to your room each day with a newspaper. For a few extra dollars you can have a bagel, muffin or croissant which is a nice touch.
I found the food in the restaurant to be bland and expensive. There are some amazing restaurants nearby which are much better.
The location of the hotel is brilliant. 5 minutes walk from Quincy Market, 10 minutes from the Harbour and 2 minutes from Boston Common and the Park Street T stop - brilliant! There are other hotels nearby and I would probably choose one of those in future.

After glancing the high rating and shelling out $400 a night for a last minute trip to Boston I was extremely disappointed with this hotel. It is NOT a top rated boutique by international standards.
Check-in was crude and transactional, the rooms feel outdated with shaggy carpet and an empty bar fridge (except comp water). Internet is free which was a plus.
I treated this hotel like a $400 a night hostel and got out first thing the next morning; the staff were much more helpful on my departure.

review_title: Old Police Station but you can't tell!
review_text: Hotel was nice but not what I had expected for four stars. Everything was nice and new and good location but close to a fire station which I heard sirens several times in the middle of the night. The rooms and restaurant were nice.

We stayed at hotel for our anniversary and couldnt have been happier. The room was large and immaculate. Service was efficient and courteous. This was the perfect location for us as we were doing the Jimmy Fund walk the next day. We were in such close proximity to great restaurants and shops, it was perfect. Cuffs was a good place to end our night. Would stay there again!

review_title: Comfortable well equipped hotel in good location for tourists to Boston
review_text: We stayed 1 night for excellent price in large single room; comfortable quiet hotel, well appointed, very traditional - maybe a little staid . Don't expect a young or noisy crowd. In room dining and entertainment good. Perfectly pleasant and a very good location for old Boston. Suit adults travelling alone or in groups, or families with small children.

Excellent location downtown Boston. Efficient and quick service. Good quality breakfast Restaurant is elegant and quality is good. As a family of 4 adults we were given a too small room. After the first night they readily gave us a larger room with no additional charge.

review_title: Awesome location, large, clean rooms, noisy halls and street
review_text: Great location if you don't plan on renting a car. Walked to Aquarium at the harbor in about 10 minutes. Right on Freedom Trail and new Boston Common. Large, nice rooms. Helpful staff. Only complaint was the noisiness. Both street noise and hallway noise were so loud it seemed like there were no walls at all.

Being in the heart of Boston is great! Love the location of this hotel! However the rooms are really tiny, mine was dark since the only window had an ac unit in it and face a brick wall, and it was impossible to find free plugs to charge my laptop and phone. Make sure to call the front desk for a powerstrip! 
If you are driving beware parking through the hotel is $42 a night.

Love, love, LOVE this hotel!!! I was a little concerned to start staying in a double bed room with 2 adults and 2 kids, as we usually book a 2 bedroom suite. Of course we usually go to Orlando or some other place where space is not an issue. This location has to be the BEST in Boston!! It is located in the center of everything! The room was small but remember you are staying downtown, I am sure all the rooms are small. We have been fine in our room. The beds are super comfy and the rooms are very clean. This hotel has so much history, Boston creme pie, Parker house rolls, and many more amazing things. The concierge are AMAZING!!! Helped me with a great running path, down Beacon street, next to Boston Common, the capital, Cheers, and down by the Charles River. It was fantastic!!! Also recommended all of our restaurants every night. Sorry tripadvisor concierge at Parker House is better!! :) This is a great place to stay with kids or a couple. They actually do have some rooms with bunkbeds for kids, if the double bed room is too scary for you. Do not look elsewhere book here NOW! I promise you won't regret it!

Overall our stay was good
Love the hotel 
Especially the location
Love the staff i couldnt say they re extremely friendly but they re good enough
Love the room
An love the lobby it looks cozy
The only thing that was bad is the toilet, i couldnt flush the watet
Seems like something wrong happened but we re bout to check out so not a big issue

Walk to everything, very centrally located. Clean rooms, helpful staff. 24 hour coffee in the lobby with REAL half and half! Great breakfast restaurant next door! They could change the window shades in the room to something that keeps the light out better. There is even a stereo system in the roo with built in speakers, and even a speaker in the bathroom!!

Had to check our bags with the valet on checkout day as our flight was later. Went back to claim them and they only had three of the four .the one that was missing had our most valuable items ( computer, business checks, keys, airline tickets, signed Red Sox memorabilia , clothes and more). No real concern or urgency was exhibited and obviously their security is lax. I wouldn't feel safe there ever again

First time I. Boston. Location was good I walked everywhere including north end. But I am fit although no more then 1.5 miles anywhere. Everything was top notch. Very european feel but rooms bigger. Lots of sports channels for the guys in the room. Comfy bed. Great pillows. Water at times was not as warm as I like but no big issue. They have this nozzle in shower that squirts water straight out at waist level. I took this as a bum washer.
