We loved the rooftop which overlooks the Mississsippi River (beautiful view), there are tables that you can sit at and a mini bar to order drinks. The hotel also has a bar downstairs that makes some of the best Long Island Teas I've tasted. They offer a nice turndown service and they leave chocolates on your pillow. The Madison Hotel is southern hospitality at it's finest!! Can't wait to go back!!
A beautiful hotel with lovely rooms. Great staff. Nice bar and restaurant.

This was really not what we expected, the floor in our room hasn't been cleaned prior to our arrival. The pictures on the Internet show rooms that are much more appealing than they actually are in reality, the bed cover on my bed had food rests on it... The breakfast is ok, the pool was closed, the only good things about this place are free wifi, free parking and bus stop in front to easily get to Baltimore without taking the car.
hotel_name: Days Inn Baltimore West, Security Blvd

review_text: Nasty odor. Stained bathrooms. Unclean floors. Bed seemed unclean I ended up sleeping on the top of all the covers with a hoodie on. Worst of all--- NO TV REMOTE!

My husband and I stayed at the Madison for a little "escape from reality", and were blown away by the exceptional service and accommodations! The facilities, the restaurant, the service, and the staff are all wonderful. Although we considered our decision to stay at the Madison somewhat of a "splurge", it was worth every penny. I will definitely stay there again and look forward to it!!

review_title: My second stay topped the first!!!
review_text:
Kumar and Rookman were excellent!!! I love those guys!!! Customer satisfaction GUARANTEED!!! Even when under pressure they smile joke and have a good time. Courtesy and respect are understatements! I won't stay 
ANYPLACE else....UNLEESS they run the place (smile).....This New YorkGirl has found a home awayfrom home!!! Sukriya!!!!

review_title: Simply not worth the money, there is better one block away.
review_text: First of all I live in Memphis. Number two I like staying in nice hotels. I've stayed in great hotels all over the world. The Madison is simply not one of them. I stayed there to attend the 4 th July celebration on the roof. The party on the roof was over priced, 96 for two people for hamburgers and hotdogs and BBQ beans that were undercooked. Drinks were available but for an additional price. The view was nice, the band was good but the food sucked! But that would be ok if the room was ok. But it's not. The room is small, the decoration tacky. They call it European meets southern class. I call it cheap and tacky. At 255 a night it should be a luxury room, not a Hilton style room with cheap furniture. The Peabody just two blocks away does it right. A beautiful lobby, pleasant rooms and great service. The Madison achieves none of that and over charges you as if that will make what they are giving you become nice. The people were helpful in making my reservation but I just can't get past the poor quality of the room. Stay at the Peabody. No hear the Westin is nice! But forget the Madison, simply not worth it. Zero elegance, pretentious without a reason to be pretentious, expensive without the luxury, what exactly is it worth? Go elsewhere, there are plenty of better places that deliver what they say they are going to give you. This is a hotel that would have you think they are a boutique hotel but give you Hilton style and expect you to be impressed. Forget it.

I am so dissapointed, we got a basic room for $255, this is well over what I should be paying. The bathrooms are nice but the room is tiny and the view is pathetic. I tried to call for room service...phone line busy. Called the front desk...busy. My husband had to use his cell phone to call the actual hotel and order us something to eat. I am surprised by the high ratings this hotel has received from tripadvisor...if you want great service, this is not the place.

We are still waiting after 3 hours for someone to fix the toilet. The staff is worse than indifferent, they lie. Promised a room change, did not happen. Now waiting on the shuttle driver to come back and bring a plunger. The folks here no no care about their guests. Stay away!

review_title: Door is open in the middle of sleeping
review_text: I was sleeping an somebody open the door. When i do appeal to front desk, employee said it is not a big deal. What if it happened to women, she could have heart attack.

The Ramada is a very nice hotel I call it my home away from home the pricing is very affordable.and the rooms are very clean and comfortable I love staying there if I could I would stay there all the time if anyoneis in baltimore and want someplace nice byt cheap stay here
Spent 4 nights, paid $250. Nice and clean rooms. The staff were friendly. I guess they were Indians. Got small shops near by.

Were at this hotel right now, I mean motel, I have never stayed in a place with the ironing board, hangers & ice tray in the bathroom, I'm in total shock, never again, hotwire needs to remove this place off of their website!!

review_title: I agree about Murphy, the bartender
review_text: I visited the Madison the first week in June. I've been coming to Memphis in business many times and the last few visits I've been staying at the Madison. One thing I have come to appreciate about this hotel is the friendly staff. Most of all, I want to mention Lisa Murphy, the bartender. She has made me hang out in the bar a little too long many times and simply been a great person to get to know.

review_title: The best service I have ever had at any hotel !!!!
review_text:
I recommend this hotel to anyone who is going to visit the baltimore area! John Hopkins university is directly across the street, it is in a great location. Rooms are nice, and clean!!! And the service is by far superior than any other hotel my husband or I have stayed..... 
The general manager, personal helped make sure our stay was as comfortable and best as it could be, thank you Steve!!
Also the room service was delicious because the food was directly sent up from the Alizee, (hotels full service restaurant).

review_title: Good for proximity to Johns Hopkins + Taxi vouchers
review_text: I spent a week here while a family member was at Johns Hopkins Hospital. Pros include: free taxi vouchers to/from hospital, new hotel, nice design for price range, clean rooms, can request quiet room facing a back street, tavern with decent food, free breakfast, rooms with microwave and fridges, can walk to little Italy and shopping. Cons: some desk staff don't know how to handle the vouchers, a Saturday night had only one person at front desk and it was a zoo, walls between some rooms are thin, the breakfast is pretty cheap-it could have been a step up for the price of rooms, parking is prohibitively expensive. Tip: leave your car at JHU hospital parking, get parking vouchers from hospital, and use hotel taxi vouchers to shuttle back and forth.
hotel_name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Baltimore Downtown/Inner Harbor

review_text: Stayed a night in a one bedroom. Room was spacious and clean. The heater didn't warm up the bedroom as much as the living room so we had to keep the bedroom door open to let the warm air pass freely. Was also a very loud hvac unit. Breakfast was good. Lots of food options closeby.

Stayed at the Residence Inn White Marsh while in town for Baltimore Grand Prix. While the air conditioner was very loud, the rest of the hotel was surprisingly nice. The outdoor pool area with fireplace, basketball court, and game area were well kept. The breakfast was one of the best free buffets outside of an Embassy Suites. Our room was a nice two room suite with newer furniture and Josh, the Front Desk Guy, was super helpful in fixing a room issue. For whatever issues the hotel had previously, it appears to be well run now. Enjoy your stay, you'll be pleasantly surprised.
Beautiful rooms, friendly staff and great views from penthouse terrace
The room was nice and clean, location was perfect. Parking cost to much and thank god I am only here for two days.
hotel_name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Baltimore Downtown/Inner Harbor

review_text:
We stayed 10/22 through 10/23 2011. The Homewood Suites and Hilton Garden inn are in one building and share a check in desk. We were in Baltimore for just a night in an extended stay suite, but the suite was just what we needed. The 1 bedroom suite had a full kitchen and a seperate sitting area. The size was good with a pull out couch in the sitting area. Excellent for 2 adults and a 7 year old. The couch could use some updating and the dresser in the bedroom was a bit scratched up. Free hot breakfast including breakfast burritos and standard continental fare. We didn't leave hungry in the morning. The Maryland Athletic Club is in the building and guests have access with your room key and photo id. My husband and son utilized the pool and enjoyed. The hotel was so quiet I felt like we were the only guests on our floor.
The location is the best thing about the Homewood Suites. Whole Foods, Starbucks and a 24 hour CVs are within a block along with several restaurants. Little Italy and Inner Harbor are within 5 minutes. We had plans in Fells Point, which was about a 20 minute stroll.

Nothing went right, from check in to the toilet, and shower, several attempts to correct issues needed. Have to say it showed no sign of being a Hilton hotel. Room smelled like mold too. Some days are just like this, but most hotels try a little harder to remedy their nightmares!

review_title: I would stay at this place again in a heartbeat!
review_text: After reading reviews I was a little iffy about this place, but aside from the stairs, I loved the building, the room, and the staff. Especially Becky working evenings. Don't let the bad reviews scare you away. Its not cookie-cutter, but it is charing and very unique. And it was clean! A huge requirement for me and my crazy OCD.

the place is a once grand Victorian style hotel. Yes it needs updating, but I hope they never do any major renovations because this place is an amazing deal! For $54 a night, friday and saturday, we got a huge bedroom with a very comfy bed, an even bigger living room/dining room/ kitchenette room and a small, very dated bathroom.
Yes, there was mildew in the caulk, but everything else was clean. And I work for the health depth and am very paranoid about bedbugs right now but found no signs of them.
Staff was very helpful.
I thought the neighborhood was beautiful - a huge gorgeous church across the street and plenty of beautiful architecture all around. 
We're walkers so we walked down Charles street and explored the restaurants on our way down to the inner harbor. It was about a 20 minuete walk. I never felt unsafe, even at 1 am. We were just starting a 9 day motorcycle trip. We parked our bikes for free in the bank parking lot and they were not touched-saddlebags are only secured with zippers and there were no issues.

Good service......could be better though..the cleanliness and responsiveness of staff to issues bothering customers should be improved with a view to retaining and sustaining the existing customer base and loyalty as well as attract new customers.
Very nice suite , nice to have the kitchen and whole foods next door. Close to everything in inner harbor. Water taxi across street or close by foot

The price of the hotel was probably only good thing about this hotel. I had a terrible room, the tv had 3 working channels. The WiFi was terribly slow, and the air conditioning did not work. The service wasn't bad, just the hotel wasn't in the best condition.

Stayed here on my way through from PA. This Quality Inn was nicer than most I have stayed in, and can't beat the location. A lot of others in Baltimore were very high priced, and this one was a much better deal, location, and seemed to offer everything that I needed while visiting the city. Quick walk to the Inner Harbor area as well. I will stay here next time I'm in Baltimore.

review_title: Don't let the lobby fool you.
review_text:
When I first walked in and saw the out dated lobby, and somewhat dirty, I got a little discouraged. But the staff was exceptionally nice. And showed no frustration dealing with out of towners when we asked 'tourists' questions. After we got on the elevators everything went up from there (pun intended). The hall ways were nice and clean. The room was great. The door was a large, heavy, wooden door which made us feel very protected. Everything was very very clean. You could definitely notice that they put a lot of care and effort into making you have the best stay as possible. 
I appriciate the very nice, safe, and clean stay. 
Will be returning :)

What a wonderful surprise this hotel was...a hidden jewel. Arrived with very low expectations from view of the lobby but that view changed rapidly. The staff was very impressive and friendly. The rooms are very unique and pretty large. Enjoyed the continetal breakfast and chatting with the manager. Added plus is the location of the hotel, great eateries, lounges and museums close at hand. Great place and looking forward to returning!

From our first greeting to our departure, the service here was amazing. Every person we encountered had a ready smile and was eager to help us. For our daughter's birthday, not only did the staff set up restaurant reservations and limo pick-up, they surprised us with a tray of chocolate-covered strawberries and non-alcoholic champagne, champagne flutes and a birthday card signed by the staff. A manager took care of a return of a defective umbrella purchased in the gift shop; the gift shop was closed and he personally took care of a refund. The staff of the concierge lounge was incredibly pleasant. The doormen were friendly and helpful with directions or getting transportation for us. We have stayed in many places all over the world and seldom have experienced this level of service. For that alone, we would absolutely return to this hotel.
hotel_name: Baltimore Marriott Inner Harbor at Camden Yards

review_text:
The staff were very kindly. We had very pleasant stay at the Rodeway Inn. When we arrived, we were warmly greeted by the staff. Inner Harbor is very close. (15min walk or there is also free bus to center city)
Breakfast was good. We really had a good time in Baltimore. If I get a chance, i will go to there again!!!
:-)

We needed a safe, clean place to stay for our spring break trip. This hotel isn't the Hilton however it doesn't cost that much either. It is a great value plus it's close to so many things. If you are traving to see the inner harbor, Orioles game, Raven's game, or the aquarium, this is the perfect place to stay. Plenty of food places close by and their free breakfast was very satisfying. We will definitely stay here again. Front desk staff was very friendly and informative. Thanks for a great stay!!

I selected this hotel because of the rave reviews and free parking, but both were disappointing. I booked a king room for my husband and I, and upon our arrival, we found ourselves in a room with 2 double beds. When I asked the woman at the front desk about the mix-up, she was less than apologetic, telling me that the hotel was full and we couldn't be moved to a king room and that the double rooms were actually better because we had our "own fridge." That would have been a real perk if we had any need for one, but we didn't. The free parking was full, so we had to park a ways up the street and walk with our bags. When my husband asked for a toothbrush, he was told they were all out; the guy behind the desk never suggested the possibility of the Rite Aid up the street. The hotel is a 5 minute drive from the Inner Harbor, and is located in a questionable part of town. On the upside, the beds were comfortable and the room was clean, but I would not recommend the Hotel Brexton. The pricetag does not equate the quality.

review_title: Near inner harbor, in downtown. Rough looking neighborhood.
review_text: Would not recommend taking ur fam here. Rough area. Nice hotel, big room, clean, good service otherwise.

We arrived to Hotel Brexton after 2 days at a high-end hotel in Washington DC. What a wonderful place to end our trip! The staff was very friendly and allowed us to check into our room early. They were very informative about things to do and see, as we had a few hours to kill before the concert we were seeing. 
Our room was spacious, spotless, the bed was perfect, and best of all- great pillows! Pillows make all the difference for me and I spent two prior sleepless nights on rock-hard pillows. These were amazing! In fact, I took a short nap when we arrived to test them out. 
There is a garden terrace where we had drinks after the concert. Hotel Brexton is beautiful inside and out and has so much more charm than some of the chain hotels in the Inner Harbor. Worth the short drive to the main attractions of Baltimore just for the experience! We will stay here whenever we visit Baltimore.

Stayed at hotel for business conference. Service, rooms and location great! Complimentary wi fi with my rate and room had mini fridge. Enjoyed the 10th floor concierge lounge, excellent breakfast choices and great early evening reception. Walking distance to major attractions. Starbucks two blocks up the street. Hotel lounge was nice as well and received good service with nice wine and beer selections. I had a beautiful view from my 8th floor room and no problems with noise.
hotel_name: Baltimore Marriott Inner Harbor at Camden Yards

review_title: Disorganized stay at an ok hotel
review_text: Let me just say that next time if we can't stay at the Hampton Inn, we will stay at another hotel chain. We stayed here for my birthday weekend and had no idea it was a Baltimore vs NY. They overbooked at both sides of the joined hotels and the service was deplorable. We requested a crib a week before we got there, had to ask again at checkin. An hour later, no crib , 3.5 hours and 4 calls later we finally get the crib. My son had an accident so we needed a new top sheet and comforter- couldn't get it because apparently they don't have enough linens! When they finally did the guy pounded on the door and tossed them at me when I opened up the door. So we made our own bed. Next day, no housekeeping until nearly 4 and when they did come they left the dirty stuff half in the room, half in front of the room. We got no hand towels or wash clothes. I call down and apparently they don't have enough towels to go around because of how booked they are. When I got a hold of the front desk manager she did offer to return a small amount of the points we used to stay but it didn't even equal 1 nights points it costed to stay. Parking cost us 64 bucks which is ridiculous! Honestly it really messed up my birthday weekend and I am considering writing corporate. I'd find another place to stay which is a same because it is a nice hotel with a great location.

Location is good, but they really need to finish renovation. Carpet in rooms needs changing ASAP. Pumping in bathrooms needs work from bathtube water backing up to old shower head. No vanity space in bathroom. Bed and linens were nice, public parking is ok.Room rate is reasonable.
hotel_name: Tremont Suites Hotel and Grand Historic Venue

review_text: The hotel Brexton is the best hotel I've ever been to. It's smack dab in the middle of Baltimore. It has the best walking distance and the staff is very friendly.

review_title: Room mix up, but great location
review_text: Stayed one night to go to a baseball game, front desk said it was a 15 minute walk to park, took us about 40 minutes to get out of park and walk home. Hotel was clean and fresh. Had booked a panoramic view room, but when we got here, there were not any. Front desk gave us another room without the view with a discount. Breakfast was ok, garden inn next door, looked better. The hotel is hooked to a health club, that is very nice!

What a pleasant surprise - a bit of the old and the new. The front portion of the hotel is the hotel, the back portion is an old Masonic Temple. You need to check it out. A good experience overall. Food was good, rooms were good. Only issue was cost of valet parking...other than that a good experience. Never knew it was there...
hotel_name: Tremont Suites Hotel and Grand Historic Venue

review_text: I attended a conference at the Mt. Washington Conference center and stayed in the rooms. This is a great place for a M-F conference when you want to focus on the conference. Mt. Washington Village is a short walk down hill and the light rale is also. But there are no child oriented activities on site other than a pool table and ping pong. The staff was fabulous - super accomodating to me as well as my family. The rooms are small but clean and have a little deck. Housekeeping stopped me in the hall twice to ask if my room was acceptable. Everyone was super friendly!! I would com back for a conference or short get away!!

I stayed here for a 5 day business trip. The rooms are fastidiously clean, elegantly decorated, and furnished with nice extras like iPod players and flat panel tvs. EVERY employee I met was kind, courteous, and accommodating 100% OF THE TIME. They recommended a lot of places to eat for us that were within walking distance of the hotel, and their suggestions never failed us. It was a more like a vacation than a business trip!
Unique boutique hotel. Every room is different, it's cozy and the staff is professional, friendly and very helpful!!!

This hotel had the most friendly people working there and they have the best deli awesome sandwiches I think it was fifty to be exact and the rooms where so spacious and comfortable I can't wait to go back
hotel_name: Tremont Suites Hotel and Grand Historic Venue

review_text:
We stayed here for a night last week. Had a room with two double beds. Beds were fine. The carpet in the room was filthy. The stand that the microwave was on looked about to collapse and was obviously a very cheap piece offurniture. Nothing felt clean. The room did have free wifi. The man who worked at the front desk was very kind but the woman was standoffish and 
never smiled. Fells Point seems like a party destination and I would stay some place else next time in Baltimore.

review_title: Exceptional! Top to bottm world class service provided here!
review_text:
We recently attended a wedding at the adjacent Tremont Grand and stayed in the hotel. We were delighted with the service, from the valet attendant to the front desk and everyone we encountered. Never in all of our travels have we enjoyed a hotel stay as much. FIVE stars for terrific service and beautiful accomodations.
Also, if you need to plan an event choose the Tremont Grand...this was the BEST wedding we've ever attended. Food was amazing and we wish we received such caring service everywere.
hotel_name: Tremont Suites Hotel and Grand Historic Venue

review_text: The best part of my stay was the valet guy, Matthew Morin, that met me when I first arrived. I had gotten off track on the trip and ended up somewhere in town I probably should not have been. I pulled up to the hotel in relief, he greeted me and could see on my face that I was stressed. He told me not to worry because I had made it. He took care of my parking and my bags. After I arrived I realized I had grabbed the wrong charger for my phone. I was running back and forth from the hotel to the parking garage to charge my phone. I saw Matthew on one of those trips, told him what I was doing and he told me to wait that the hotel has a bag of chargers. He helped me go through the bag until we thought we found a match, but to no avail. I thanked him for his efforts and walked to my car for my phone. By the time I returned to my room he was on the phone to tell me he found the pieces I needed. I appreciate everything he did to help me out. He went above and beyond and it should not go unnoticed. I work for Citi and was in town for training and Matthew Morin made my trip excellent. Thank you Matthew!
hotel_name: Tremont Suites Hotel and Grand Historic Venue

review_title: Good location, good value for the price.
review_text:
1. Â Located about 3 miles from John Hopkins Hospital.Â 
2. Â Accessible Jr. Suite was comfortable. Roll-in shower. Easy to maneuver in wheelchair. It has 2 queen size beds - I would recommend 1 bed. Kitchette is a great addition-microwave, frig, toaster, sink, dishes etc. Small table.Â 
3. Â Staff - extremely pleasant to deal with. Very very friendly & helpful.Â 
4. Â You can see the holes in the ceiling of the bathroom where the renovations were done. It is an older hotel but has and continues to be renovated. That was the major complaint we had...you could hear them drilling at 9am in the morning.Â 
5. Â The restaurant did not have a large selection of items. There is a deli on the premises which does have a great selection of sandwiches, prepared foods, etc.Â 
6. Â Overall, not a bad hotel. I would recommend this hotel.
hotel_name: Tremont Suites Hotel and Grand Historic Venue

review_text: Excellent hotel in the middle of lots of little taverns! Water taxi across the street. I would recommend a room with a balcony!!
Great choice for downtown. Close to Inner Harbor shops. Great value. Clean rooms, friendly and helpful staff.
hotel_name: Hampton Inn & Suites Baltimore Inner Harbor

review_title: Very nice hotel in a great city.
review_text: Stayed for the weekend with friends, no complaints.
hotel_name: Hampton Inn & Suites Baltimore Inner Harbor

review_title: Greatly located....view of an abandoned building
review_text: Just arrived and everyone was friendly. The room smelled old, like no one's been in it awhile. We went to the window to check out the view. We have a view of an abandoned building. Oh well, we fixed that by closing the drapes. So far so good.
hotel_name: SpringHill Suites by Marriott Baltimore Inner Harbor

review_text: This hotel is perfect if you are attending an event at the convention center or visiting Baltimore and the Inner Harbor. Hotel is very clean and decor is updated. Nice flat screen TV in the room. Staff is very friendly. Valet parking is pricey at $32 per day, but that should be expected in the downtown business district of a big East Coast city. I highly recommend this hotel. Check out Peters Pub around the corner for dinner and drinks.
hotel_name: Hampton Inn & Suites Baltimore Inner Harbor

review_title: Awesome hotel! Great location, free hot breakfast, wonderful room!
review_text: This hotel is located only 2 blocks from the Inner Harbor so it's very easy to walk everywhere. We even walked to Powerplant in heels which wasn't bad at as all. You are also near the Harborplace Mall. There is a parking garage one street up from the hotel for $20 instead of paying $32 for valet. The rooms are great. We got the one king bed and sofabed so the room, if you wanted, could really sleep 5. Free hot breakfast consisted of oatmeal, waffles, cereal, scrambled eggs, sausage, bagels, english muffins, asst juices, and coffee. Get there before 9:30 to get the waffles. Nothing bad about this hotel, we will def stay there again!
hotel_name: SpringHill Suites by Marriott Baltimore Inner Harbor

review_title: This hotel is dated, smelly and and in need of an overhaul.
review_text: If you want cheap then this is it but if you want cleanliness then look somewhere else. Terrible odors and outdated decor. A little scary for me. Dont know how I made it through the night.
Great location and large suites, the early eighties furniture didn't matter because it was clean and spacious. One downfall is valet parking is too expensive.
hotel_name: SpringHill Suites by Marriott Baltimore Inner Harbor

review_text: Rooms were clean and spacious. The employees are nice, helpful and efficient. The breakfast was ok, for free. It's a converted bank so the rooms are not what you normally get with a suite, there is no way to close off the living area from the sleeping area. The old vault in the basement is neat to see. The wifi connection was bad.
hotel_name: SpringHill Suites by Marriott Baltimore Inner Harbor

review_title: Love the location and historic architecture.
review_text: Second time staying in this hotel. Love the building and location. Staff was very helpful. Only knock on the hotel is the limited parking means you have to valet, which is time consuming. I've stayed at the Residence Inn next door and they have the same issue, so I'm not blaming them. Just give yourself 15 minutes padding before you have to leave.
hotel_name: Hampton Inn & Suites Baltimore Inner Harbor

review_title: Old style but worth the money
review_text:
Got it for business stay for one night on Priceline for $50. Very well recd on arrival. Greeted well by the front desk staff. Asked for a corner room thinking I'll get room w view and many windows but was disappoited to find a view of the alley and a small window. Room appeared very old but w character. An old CRT TV on a desk and very old looking carpet. Sleep number bed worked well but also very old. BR also very old looking. The location is nice and they offer free
Shuttle to hopkins on designated times. Also for $3 there is a shuttle to go around the downtown place of choice. Overall will be happy to come here again if o get it for the same price esp due to the front desk staff.

review_title: "Hospitality" is something that "Harbor Magic" is lacking a great deal of.
review_text: I will only say one thing: find someplace else to stay and take a cab to Fells Point. This hotel missed the mark on too many things to list. Everything from the service to the pillows all need improvement to be worth the hassle we went through.

Great location to inner harbor - friendly staff especially bell hop Jared. Hampton inn across street allows Springhill guests to use pool. Nice perk. Worn furniture in room. Great Internet and breakfast. Noisy at night on 3rd floor.
hotel_name: SpringHill Suites by Marriott Baltimore Inner Harbor

review_title: Great location, nice size rooms, friendly staff, but housekeeping was less than par
review_text:
Went to this hotel after reading several of the reviews. Upon our arrival we were greeted by valet, whom told us the outrageous rate. We decided to park there anyway, as to find a cheaper location was not worth it. When we got to our room we found it to be VERY large and roomy for 2 children and 2 adults. It was cleaned and well decorated. The price was a steal for what we received. We usually pay between $300-450 a night for a hotel and we did not get such a BIG suite like this! The hotel is literally 2 blocks from the Inner Harbor. We did not need our car for the entire stay! 
Now, for the disappointment; after returning from the Inner Harbor, we came back to our room to see the garbage not emptied, the bed not properly made (they just threw the comforter over the wrinkled disheveled sheets!) the air was turned down to 60 degrees; I guess she wanted to make sure she was comfortable doing a half job, because we were FREEZING! There were four people staying in this suite and she only left two towels and no washcloths or hand towels.
When we arrived initally we only had three towels and had to ask the front desk for more. The breakfast was not worth getting up early for (served between 6-9am). the waffles was the only thing good, everything else needs a little work. The last night there we ask the front desk for information. She was busy on a personal call and gave us false information as a way to shoo us away.
I expressed my concerns to the front desk and she offered a discount on one nights stay to compensate for the inconvenience. However, I still wanted to talk to manager who was not available until the next day.
 I did call Jason, hotel manager and left a voicemail and he PROMPTLY returned my call. He apologized and asked if there was anything he could do. I told him no we already received an adjustment for our stay, but thought it was very important that he knew about housekeeping, because it could make or break a hotel LITERALLY! He agreed and stated he was having a meeting with them at 11:30am that morning. One thing I notice about this manager is he takes the comments seriously and goes to lengths to try to correct the problem as I read from the many reviews.
Overall, I would have easily gave this hotel 5 stars, but just couldn't based on the little mishaps! Nevertheless, do visit this hotel if you want space, and easy access to the Inner Harbor!
hotel_name: SpringHill Suites by Marriott Baltimore Inner Harbor

review_title: By far the best place to stay!
review_text: We had our Family Reunion here July 2010. Don't bother to rent car. Everything is in walking distance and the clean buses are free! A 3 story shopping mall is connected to the Mall. There is a covered walkway, above the street that connects to the Inner Harbour! The hotel is excellent, friendly staff, clean rooms, great resturant. A perfect getaway for each family member!
Don't expect super luxury, but what is offered is excellent by people with a smile

review_title: Very Good Place to Stay, Above-Average, Not Exceptional
review_text: The hotel is very nice, helpful front desk, attentive maid service, nice rooms. I would certainly stay again, but I save a "5" rating for truly exceptional places with special and/or unique features (eg waterfall showers). This hotel is very nice, but not extraordinary.

review_title: Grand hotel but in need of a face lift
review_text: Probably once a grand hotel of a bygone era, but not now. Located just a few blocks from the inner harbour, a 10 minute walk. There are a number of homeless people around the hotel, which can make you feel a little uneasy walking around at night, so we avoided going out and about in the evening. The room was adequate, but the bathroom looked in need of an update, as the wallpaper was peeling and there was some mould and it could have been cleaner! The bed was very comfortable. The adjacent coffee bar in the hotel was a bit tatty. Overall, an ok hotel, but don't expect top class luxury. Really needs an overhaul, as lots of alternative smarter hotels and it will be left behind if no improvements are made soon!

review_title: Good location good value business hotel
review_text: Excellent location, free wifi, lots of eateries nearby. Would definitely consider staying there again on business or with family.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Baltimore Downtown / Inner Harbor

review_text: bad customer service when they are in a bad mood, some smile when talking amongst other employees then shift to sarcastic smirk the instant a customer approaches. honestly, save yourself some money and stress and go to a dufferent much more updated hotel, one with staff that enjoy working with their customers.

Terribly overpriced. I have stayed in top Marriot resorts for less per night. This room wasn't even a nice Courtyard. The bathroom only had a shower, no tub. Parking is 23 per night. The fitness center smelled.like must.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Baltimore Downtown / Inner Harbor

review_text: We stayed here for one night on August 26th, while dropping our son off at school. Especially liked the location near the Little Italy section. The rooms are very clean and comfortable. Indoor parking lot attached to the hotel ($23) per day. Free wifi is always a plus. The staff was always posting notices in the lobby informing everyone about Hurricane Irene. Have stayed here in the past and will stay again.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Baltimore Downtown / Inner Harbor

review_text: We stayed here for a weekend and the location is great. Fell's Point is an awesome place for bar hopping and the restaurants are good. The price is a bit pricey, but Baltimore isn't cheap. Not bad, would stay here again.

review_title: Pricey but clean and well appointed
review_text: The location can't be beat if you're in town for an Orioles game at Camden Yards or to see the Inner Harbor. For the price, its not a bad value. Rooms are clean and modern. Beds are fairly comfortable. Our weekend rate came with free breakfast at the Watertable restaurant which was pretty good and had good views. The hotel is located across from one of the harbor-related malls which has chain restaurants like Unos and Cheesecake Factory and right on top of a large indoor mall. It's within a short walk of the aquarium, the stadium and other inner harbor attractions. If you have kids or like to swim it has a very nice indoor pool. There's a coffee shop with in lobby that sells Starbucks and a well-appointed workout room. (There's also an actual 'Bucks in the downstairs mall under the hotel for the purist.) If location, cleanliness and convenience is a priority and you're not on a tight budget it's a good choice.

review_title: Surprisingly great bargain priced hotel in a great location
review_text: I booked here based on the price and proximity to the convention center, It was about a half or a third of the convention recommended hotels. Because of that, I expected Spartan accommodations, but instead got a charming hotel, nice lobby, spacious rooms and free (albeit pokey) wifi. There is a restaurant in house and the staff at hotel and restaurant are ULTRA courteous. Right across the street from the convention center, a block from the light rail from the airport and a few blocks from the inner harbor restaurants and attractions. Wonderful. Gives me a whole new perspective on Days Inn.

Booked for two nights as I was attending a conference at the Sheraton which is a block away. The rate at Days Inn was a third of the Sheraton.
The check in process was quick and friendly and we were provided with information about the immediate area. 
The rooms are functional and may not be as nice as more expensive hotels but they are clean and spacious. There was a nice big HD television, a fridge and microwave but the best thing of all is that they have free wifi for guests.
As this was a work related trip could not have asked for more.

They have charged my credit card four times for a fee... I have called five times.. They politely refund my money and then recharge my card again... Maybe they were hoping I didn't pay attention to bank statements.

review_title: The best thing about this place is the scalding hot water!
review_text: Checked in on a Friday night. Sleep number bed was ok but be warned it isn't for everyone. Room was tiny, maybe we got stuck with a small room because we used an Internet booking site? We never received shampoo, called to have the blinds dusted because they were nasty and to have tissue replaced. We are still waiting. Spent a day out in the city, came back to a toasty room. We had the AC set on 60. Front desk told my husband that our room was one of the lucky rooms that was having the AC worked on for next weeks guests and we should have received written notice. We are still waiting on that too. My husband went down to get a new room, which we had to request, and we only got s king sized bed again because he refused to accept one with a double bed for three people. No one offered to help us move rooms even though I saw bellman help other families with their luggage all day. Our new room is larger and comes with what appears to be dog food on the floor, hair all over the bed spread, and a broken remote for the tiny TV. It is yet to be determined if our room will cool off before we check out tomorrow. Our new room has mold covering the shower curtain and tile. If safety is a concern, dont stay here. You know the neighborhood is dangerous when the mcdonald's two blocks away closes at 8:00 pm. In this case historic does not equal nice.

review_title: A great value in a terrific location
review_text:
I was in Baltimore for a conference that was being held in the nearby Sheraton, but it was booked, so I ended up at the Days Inn Inner Harbor. What luck! All week fellow participants where complaining about the Sheraton, and I got to rave about the good deal I had gotten at the Days Inn. A far superior stay at half the cost.
Service at the front desk was friendly and helpful. Rooms were clean and well maintained, with comfortable beds and in room amenities such as microwave and refrigerator. The bathrooms are small and the vanity spartan, but the desk space and lamps were set up well for work in the room. Definitely one of the nicer Days Inns I have visited. And the location is convenient to everything downtown and at the harborfront. I would highly recommend for the cost conscious business traveller.

Stayed here recently on business. Room was large and very clean. Cannot beat the location for visits to Camden Yards, harbor area and other sites. Lots of good restaurants nearby. Staff was very friendly and helpful. Would stay here again.

review_title: You get what you paid for.
review_text: I went to Baltimore on a 3 day business trip back in June 2011. When I arrived at 9:30pm, I was warmly greeted. I went to my room and it was very clean. It had a nice tv, comfortable bed and the usual toiletries you would expect at a hotel. It also had an iron/board and a blow dryer. My favorite part was that I got free wireless Internet. I've been to places where I paid more for my room and had to pay $12/day for Internet. The pool & hottub was not the best set up (inside), it was very hot in the pool room. I only stayed for a short period of time cause I couldn't handle the heat any longer. Outside the pool room was an outdoor patio, very nice. It was nice and close to the galleria for shopping and the harbor for wonderful food and scenery. Great location, nice staff, clean and right next to a cvs and whole foods. I really enjoyed my stay.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Baltimore Downtown / Inner Harbor

review_title: Perfect place to stay in Baltimore
review_text: If you are visiting inner harbor, this is by far the best place to stay. For the location, you can't beat the cost. The staff was very friendly & accommodating and the rooms were at the utmost cleanliness standards. It has a lovely indoor pool and the restaurant within the hotel was fabulous. Grand slam, renaissance!

review_title: Perfect location right in downtown Inner Habor of Baltimore with everything within walking distance.
review_text:
We, a family of 4, stayed 5 days and 4 nights. We had breakfast in the hotel, not included with the room but very reasonably priced, every day. We also had problems with our safe and shower head, but once we called the front desk, everything was fixed quickly and the staff were amazing. Parking is attached to the hotel, but not included in the room, with in and out privileges. We parked the car when we arrived and did not move it until we left. We visited the science center and the aquarium as well as having a weekend function at the Baltimore convention center. Everything was within walking distance and I think the Days Inn was the closest hotel to the convention center. The room was your standard room with two double beds, microwave, fridge, safe and iron and hairdyer. The pool is outside, between the hotel and parking garage and was a little cloudy, but our son went in everyday and had a blast.
We found the Days Inn to be the best value for our money and would stay there again when in town.

review_title: U don't have to leave the hotel for anything
review_text: The hotel has an indoor pool that's adjacent to it's clean hot tub. The Lobby has a sexy bar n lounge area am Internet cafe. A chess lounge a reading Area and it's connected to a three story mall. Plus has it's own restaurants that overlook the harbor. Across the street is the inner harbor that offer shows restaurants boat rides and more shops

review_title: Great hotel, great location, great customer service! !!!
review_text: My daughter and I tagged along with the hubby to Baltimore. He came here for a conference for 4 days. During this time,we had to use the fax machine to receive and send faxes. The front desk staff were great and patient with us in helping us. Room was great. Housekeeping was good. I love the fact that the hotel is attached to a mall and you can use the overpass to get to the inner harbor rather than crossing the street. I would come back to this hotel again. Great customer service!!!

review_title: Nice Hyatt, just needs more rrstaurants
review_text: Exactly what you'd expect from a Hyatt; great staff, great room, and fantastic location, but with only one restaurant with a limited menu, you are forced to dine outside. This probably was no big deal a couple of years ago since it is so close to the Inner Harbor but with many venues closing there, having a nice meal is a bit of a chore.

Staff is very friendly and gracious. All in all, I don't really need that much in a conference hotel, and it served the purpose just fine. A few things I didn't love:
toilet seat in bathroom is peeling. It's made of plastic and the top layer is clearly worn down.
My window leaked air like crazy, so I had to run the heater, despite the 50 degree temp outside.
Squicked out by the visible insect glue trap under my bed. Saw no bugs, though. Yay!
In room coffee- yes! I guess they ran out of stirrers because I had a pen wrapped in a napkin next to the coffee pot for the purpose.
Linens are old and pilled- especially the pillow shams.
My remote control was filthy, numbers worn off, and only flipped through three channels.
While none of these things are really a big deal in the grand scheme of life, they added up to be disappointing. The most unforgivable part of the stay was that the coffee shop downstairs in the lobby ran out of coffee lids and put a soup lid on my $4 cafe mocha. You are a convention center hotel, and you should not be running out of coffee lids while your hotel is full of convention attendees. At 8 am, I'm trying to eat and run, and now I have to worry about dumping a latte on my business attire? C'mon!!!
Overall, it's fine, and people were so nice. But the rooms are dated and I do think that management needs to bring it up a notch for the money.

I got my room for $85 Off priceline. The room online is $280. It was a nice clean room just like the hotel pics show. It did not have a view. They said that would be an extra $40. Parking is $28 for overnight. Its location is great. It has a walkway over to the harbor and there is shopping everywhere. I would not have been happy paying $280, but for the deal I got, I was very happy! Priceline is the way to go!
Delivered what I expected. Stayed on 10th floor, had a great view of the harbor. Floor was quiet at night and room was clean.

review_title: Great hotel in a great location
review_text: We stayed there for a conference and had a harbour view room. The hotel is located in a mall and just across from the inner harbour area of Baltimore so there is plenty to do and numerous places to eat. Only complaints were that we asked for new sheets for our infant's pack and play three times before they brought them and the pool was only opened mornings and evenings. Club lounge was alsO

review_title: It s in the best location, right on the inner harbor
review_text: Stayed for two nights in very big and beautiful hotel located on the harbor and my room had a stunning view of the inner harbor. The rooms had everything someone would need: an oversized and comfortable bed, a big bathroom and a flat screen satellite tv. There was also wi-fi connection, but it s not complementary. The only glitch was that in the room it was a little too warm, while in the hallways air conditiong was running at full power. The bar on the second floor had a large variety of drinks and breakfast was very good ( you could choose either buffet or service at table). A pedestrian bridge was made for this hotel to reach the inner harbor thus avoiding to cross the highly trafficated street. Want to go to baltimore? The hyatt it s a no brainer.
Walking distance to stadium but it's easier to take the train. Was there for U2 show in June. Great base. Close to good restaurants & bars.

Hotel was clean and price was not horrible. The waterfront restaurant is good, and the hotel is in a great location. Downside staff was rude at check in, and whenever you had a question they did not know the answer and offered no alternatives. Has business center but rips you off at 3 bucks per minute to use computer. Internet was over priced and for what you pay should be included.

We were visiting Johns Hopkins and this hotel is within minutes of the campus. The check-in was pleasant and quick. The rooms were clean but dated. We didn't use service or other amenities. Restaurant was terrible but I'll write another review for that.
Outstanding location, great beds, incredible views of water, food was very good... Loves the Starbucks in lobby and great buffet brunch

review_title: Great location but some service and room condition issues.
review_text:
Front desk service was very good. The bathroom had mildew in the shower and the room furniture was stained with who knows what. The location is awesome. Housekeeping never cleaned the room, we called but they never showed up. 
We have stayed at several Hyatt properties, while this had a great location, the stay was only so so as compared to other locations. Hyatt has been hit or miss over the last few stays.

review_title: Good location but not the best Hyatt
review_text: Hyatt Baltimore is good but I've stand in better Hyatts. while they have done some renovations the hotel still feels a bit dated. obviously fake plants decorate the lobby. the food in the restaraunt is okay but won't dazzle. our room on the street side was noisy but had a great view. the service is very accommodating.
We stayed here last night on a whim to Break up a trip home from the beach. The service was incredible, the bed was comfortable and the location was perfect. Will definitely stay again!

Meredith, our concierge/check in person/ wine opener, was our 1st entrance to the wonderful staff of the hotel. Location is fantastic, near to all that is fun in inner harbor Baltimore. Street noises are a little noticeable, but the overall experience was very good.

review_title: One of the best hotels in Baltimore!
review_text: I really loved and enjoyed my stay in Brookshire Suites for a month when we had our training last March in Baltimore. I can say that everything is perfect for me, strategic location, cozy rooms, good customer and room service, great food and drinks at the cloud club and unlimited free internet access! I felt very pampered during my stay here and definitely will go back to this hotel if given another chance.

Stayed at the Hyatt for two days. The location as others have said is great. The hotel I am sure when first built was amazing - It needs attention now.
I used to be a maid a resort and am therefore very picky about the details that make a difference. We walked on the room was warm and musty
 We stayed for two days with the AC set to 60 and the room was only comfortable at night - when we weren't moving around. This was disappointing since is was 100 degrees out. 
We booked on priceline and charged $30 more a day for a king bed and Harbor view. If I had know that I would have bid higher with the hope a getting a newer hotel.
The pool is postage stamp size. When we went to look out the window at the view in our room - the settee was stained
 The carpet was stained with some red substance. The shower has mildew ib several place counter was dusty. The wallpaper was peeling under vanity and dust and hair accumulated in the room corners. The tissue holder was not polished and has fingerprints on it - yes I'm picky.
Last they should not charge guests 30 to park. I would try a different hotel when I return. Yes everyone was smiling and said hi -

review_title: Nice hotel but bring own pack and play
review_text: I had a business conference here and extended the stay to visit nearby family. Like many hotels, wireless was extra. We had our baby with us and asked for a crib and fridge. Despite being requested at the time of reservation, we had to call down once we arrived. Both were brought to the room...the fridge worked fine. The crib was an old wobbly pack and play. On the positive side, they provided baby shampoo and lotion.

We stayed @Hyatt Regency for a night before out trip to DC. This hotel is in a beautiful, accessible location to the Inner Harbor. Also, we cannot stop talking about the customer service (150%) in this hotel!!! Staff was extremely helpful and w more than willing to facilitate our stay!!! Words cannot describe our satisfaction at this hotel!

review_title: Probably the best staff we've experienced
review_text: Most pleasant, professional, & well-trained front office my wife and I have come across and we're in the business. Room was spacious and clean with a picturesque view of Baltimore. Breakfast was plentiful and tasty. Only hiccup was young lady who worked overnight who needs to take a lesson from the wonderful day staff. Word of advice from someone who began on the desk - don't tell a guest that something is "really not my job" ever. She was young but the attitude diminished what was a terrific evening. Overall a top hotel in our book!

review_title: I would make reservations here again without a second thought.
review_text: I stayed here as a relative underwent treatment at Johns Hopkins. The room was nice and the bathroom had a large countertop for items when getting ready to go-a small thing but it annoys me to have to try to balance my make-up, etc. on the back of the toilet or tiny countertop. The staff was friendly and professional and they offered the best hospital rate I found. The only downside was being from out of state, I was dependent on public transportation or the hotel shuttle. The shuttle was often in the 20/30 minute "late" time frame they made clear in the instructions due to traffic, etc. However, that is beyond their control and the shuttle drivers were all friendly and professional as well. I heard from some that the neighborhood was less than desirable, but I give them kudos for turning that beautiful old bank building into a beautiful, modern hotel.
The hotel was very clean & so close to harbor, even had a sky walk to get to the harbor. Great views with a quaint pool on the roof. If your going to Baltimore stay here.
Very nice rooms. Awesome hot breakfast, with omelettes made to order. If you are a light sleeper like me, remember to ask for an inside room. Covered parking under the hotel.

Stayed for one night with my 8 year old for an appt the following day at Johns Hopkins. There was no parking. I did find an empty spot in the lot, but was I couldn't park there because all the permits were taken. The clerk suggested I park on the street. I was hesitant, but he assured me it would be fine. Imagine our surprise when we came out in the morning to a smashed window. Nothing was taken because I didn't leave anything, but we were an hour late for our appointment and the hotel refused to pay for the window. They refunded our room, but it was being paid for by a study we were in anyway. Now we are out almost $300 to fix our window. The hotel manager, Mark, would not help us other than giving us a refund on our room. I would definitely not recommend staying there. This is a huge inconvenience to us because we have to get the window fixed and obviously, financially it's not fun either. My 8 year old is now very anxious for her appointment as well, because of this mornings happenings.

These poor employees, great service in a poorly maintained and in need of updating building. The breakfast in the cloud club was good, the lobby was nice, but my room was very lacking. The electrical outlets were falling out of the wall, bathroom tiles were black (not too sure if it was mold). Air conditioner was failing, quit in middle of the night.

review_title: It's me and my girlfriend's new spot!
review_text: I really enjoyed the whole place. And Kenya at the front desk was especially helpful! The valets were pleasant and helpful and the accommodations were pleasing. A good experience.

This was more like a homeless shelter. It actually does house displaced people for the Baltimore area. There were panhandlers in front. Garage was creepy. Located on a dark street you had to get out of your car to open door. Breakfast is dormitory style. Maybe because this hotel is also used as a dorm for a local college. The help at the front desk were pleasant and cordial. However this is not a place for me. I travel to Baltimore at least every 6 wks so I know for the money, there are better places.

Okay so I see some reviews on here that are negative. Maybe, I stayed at a good time. Lol The only thing I have to say is some off the staff aren't to friendly that work on the floor and in the dining area. They can be rude. Also, the smell in front of the hotel is bad. It is a cheap stay compared to other hotels. The breakfast was good. You can't want to much for the price. The room was clean and the bathroom was nice. Wifi threw the hotel that's free. Close to downtown with free buses.

The staff at this hotel is excellent. They were helpful with everything that I needed (cabs, directions, etc.). This was my first trip to Baltimore and they made it much easier. Convenient to John Hopkins hospital (just a 7$ cab ride). If you are interviewing there, call ahead, they have a great deal.

review_title: Beautiful old hotel but service left a lot to be desired.
review_text: We stayed here because a wedding we were invited to was in the neighborhood. The staff did not go out of their way to be helpful. 2 out of the 3 nights we had really loud neighbours in the room next to us. The valet was often not out in front and we ended up waiting a long time to get our car on a couple of occasions. it is a beautiful old hotel with a lot of charm. It would be great if the service could be as charming as the building.

review_title: Very nice, great jumping off point!
review_text:
I stayed recently at the Baltimore Hilton for a bachelor party. 
Although we didn't spend much time at the hotel, it was very nice. The staff was friendly and professional. 
The room was very clean with a nice sized tv, but the view was the most memorable point of the room. We had an amazing view of Camden Yards.
It's about a 20 min walk the inner harbor area, shopping malls, and so much more. 
I would go back in a heartbeat.

Stayed here for business for four days. Rooms are spacious, beds comfortable, with nice views on the upper floors of the Inner Harbor, downtown skyline, and Camden Yards. Location offers easy access to Convention Center, Inner Harbor attractions, etc. But there are not many food and drink options beyond sports bars in the immediate vicinity.
And that gets to my main complaint. It is strange to be in an upscale Hilton property with no coffee shop, a poorly stocked and understaffed lobby bar, and a restaurant that is across a skyway from the hotel proper. Needing to walk several blocks for a decent cup of morning coffee is a real drag on a business trip. 
Otherwise a fine stay. But with lots of other options in the area downtown, not sure I would choose it again at the price point.

review_title: Wow. Great place to stay. Very professional staff, excellent restaurant with in house chef.
review_text: I would stay in this hotel again without hesitation. So close to the airport, super convenient shuttle service. The staff was so friendly and helpful. The restaurant was excellent, and their in-house chef was great. I recommend upgrading to the top level club, worth every penny.
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton BWI Airport

review_text: This hotel was a great value as I booked it through Pricline and only paid 59.00 per might for Easter weekend. Unfortunately, there were a few very strange quirks. One, they had no heat because they had switched the system to a/c the day before we arrived and the room was cold the first night. The location is a bit sketchy, being about one block from a kind of run down neighborhood and about six from the ballpark, which was fine bit the hotel comes up on Google as right near Camden Yards. The street is also one way and you cannot park in front to unload and check in. There is underground parking but you have to check in and get your key to access it, making arrival a bit of a challenge. The staff is very friendly though a bit undertrained. I booked a room with two beds and was given one with one calefornia king. When I complained I was told there were no more rooms and nothing was done to try to rectify the situation. I should note that I was told that there is no guarantee you will get the room you book when you go through the web, and I got a GREAT price so I can't complain too much. The hot breakfast is great albeit basic, fine for me b/c I am not a huge breakfast person anyway and more substantial then at most other hotels, even more expensive ones. Another great thing was it is right across the street from he Baltimore Bassilica, so I was able to take my nephew to Easter Mass and it was conducted by the Archbishop of Baltimore! I also should note, do mob pay for the "movie deal" because it is misleading. It says it gives you 80 movies to choose from but it really just gives you a few Starz channels. Overall, a good value bit needs some improvement. Sent up extra blankets and pillows and the bed was fantastically comfy.

At first glance, the hotel seemed more "dated" than our liking. Quickly, the knowledgable and friendly staff made me feel so comfortable. It was one of the front desk staffs first day...I would have never known had he not mentioned it after checking us in! Thanks very much for the "non" hotel, homemade breakfast too!
My 3 boys look forward to our return! 
One suggestion, maybe pillowtops...

review_title: Wonderful rooms however the staff is simply mean.
review_text: I would stay here again but I would not plan on eating the complimentary breakfast. The wait staff acts as if they get paid on how little people eat. All I wanted was some coffee, and I was yelled at in front of other people when I went back for a second cup!

Got this hotel on priceline for 1 night before a flight home from BWI. Hotel looks nice enough, front desk staff was friendly, but the soundproofing between rooms is nonexistent. It's midnight and I've spent the last 2 hours listening to the family in the next room as I try to fall asleep. They do not actually seem to be talking all that loudly, but it sounds as though they are practically in the same room. At least my kids finally managed to fall asleep despite the noise. All in all, I can't recommend staying here - at least not if you actually want to sleep.
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton BWI Airport

review_title: Great place to stay before flying out!
review_text:
Have stayed here twice for 1 night for early am flights out of BWI. Very convenient. Staff are responsive and friendly. The shuttle drops you off right where you need to be and you can leave your car parked in their lot for up to 7 days for $30 while you are gone!
Rooms are clean and comfy. Main lobby area also clean and newer looking. The hallways to rooms show their age. 
It's nice to unwind in the downstairs bar after arrival. 
Will be back!
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton BWI Airport

review_title: Great location, nice room & wonderful view
review_text: Very happy with our room. It was clean, nice sized, and had a great view.
Rooms were great. Customer service better than average. But after paying premium for wireless access, the network wasn't available in on-premise meeting rooms.
This hotel was great..the rooms clean and modern and the staff was wonderful!

review_title: Very clean, friendly, rooms just a bit small.
review_text:
We stayed here with our 4 month old and had trouble with space as we had both a stroller and a portable crib to squeeze in. So, factor that in when I say room was a bit tight. 
We had a neat view of the Baltimore baseball stadium. I enjoyed having the free city shuttle bus stop right outside the hotel, 
very convenient. A nice, very big lobby made the hotel feel spacious. Lots of conferences are held here as it ajoins to the Baltimore convention Center which also was the reason for our trip. Solid 4 star, no real complaints here.

We have stayed here many times. The staff makes an effort to remember you, the room views are fab, the rooms are above average especially on a cleanliness level, but another high note is that the hotel restaurant "Oriole Grille" is much better than most hotels. Of course, having Morton's downstairs does not hurt either.

Again a very typical stay at this hotel. Iv reviewed it before and really no difference this time round. Very friendly staff, clean rooms, good location for Baltimore and this time I managed to connect to the wifi in the room no problem!
It may be nothing special but it's nothing bad either!

Obviously you don't expect much from an airport hotel but....when I arrived at 1 am, there was a long line waiting to check in and only one hostess handling it. This is a major international airport and when I booked, they assured me that they were fully equipped for 24 hour service to accommodate passengers at all times. The room was clean. But it was boobytrapped with multiple alarm clocks going off at 4,5,6 am. Not kidding, and yes, this is highly unpleasant after a very late arrival. Finally, service was poor. They shut down room service at 12 am- though I had read online that 24 hour service was available.
hotel_name: Four Points by Sheraton BWI Airport

review_title: Arrived at 6:30 and our room isn't ready!
review_text:
All week I looked forward to attending the NBA Conference with my husband and celebrating my birthday tomorrow and our 21st wedding anniversary on Thursday while staying at the Hilton. We arrive tired but looking forward to heading to our room and then going out to dinner. Upon arrival we were told not only was our room still not ready at 6:30 pm but they were unable to let us know what time our room would be available. Unbelievable! So my husband and I wait outside while our luggage lingers in the lobby and an hour later we receive a call that our room is ready. We collect our keys head upstairs open the door and our room has two double beds. We're a married couple celebrating an anniversary. My husband calls the front desk they forward our call to the managers Voicemail I express my frustration with the service we've received thus far and requested that he calls us back. No response.
This quality of service from a Hilton Hotel is unacceptable.

Sheraton is paying top dollar to improve their hotels and brand... but they need to work on customer service and staff professionalism too. Multilple bad encounters with staff. Everyone seemed irritated to assist us.

Has received too many bad reviews. Not bad at all. I am guessing, they worked on it and improved. It's clean and decently maintained. You get what you pay for. Staff is courteous and helpful. It might be on the edge of safe part of town, but I had no trouble walking from the convention center to the hotel at 11 pm in night. Don't go into dark alleys, that's true for any city! I always asked staff if walking to such and such place at a particular time would be safe. they were helpful.

Super clean, lots of shops and restaurants within walking distance 15 min from the bay. Bed was oone of the most comfortable ever. Lots of pillows. Staff was exceptionally friendly. Small pool. No complimentary bfast...
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn Baltimore / White Marsh

review_text: I stayed here as a side trip to a college reunion in Annapolis. My fiancee has never been to Baltimore, so we took advantage of this hotel's excellent location to see Baltimore. It is a block away from a public-transit hub, including the light-rail line to BWI and various bus lines to major attractions not already within walking distance (e.g. Fell's Point). Found this hotel on Hotwire & got a great rate. Service was prompt and friendly. Can't beat the free Internet. Only downside is that its restaurant is overpriced for breakfast

This hotel really needs a Face Lift. The hotel may have been a 4-Star hotel twenty years ago. The lobby is great but when you hit your room you have just step into a twilight zone. The furniture is miss placed in a out date room from the past. The staff was friendly and very helpful.

It does what it aims to do as a bog standard Sheraton but there is nothing particularly special about this hotel.
Rooms are comfortable and contemporary. My TV had a terrible reception on it however and no room service menu was in my room which simply list them some extra revenue cos it motivated me to just go out and eat. I also couldn't log onto the wireless from my room, when I rang down I was told that it must be a fault with my laptop!!!! However neither my laptop nor iPhone could connect from my room but both worked fine in for the free wifi in the lobby!
The pool is no bigger then a hot tub so don't expect to be doing laps as a work out, just stick to the cardio facilities or weights equipment.
Otherwise this is a nice hotel which is very nicely located by the inner harbour!

I am currently here with my 7 y.o. son. I read ALOT of reviews on Inner Harbor hotels before choosing this one. 
Good-
Location. Not right on the water. Your views are other hotels and office buildings. Crossing the street to get to inner harbor, shops, aquarium, etc a little tricky. Alot of road work/paving going on in the area. 
Cleanliness. Room very clean as well as hotel lobby, pool, gym. 
Pool. VERY small 3-4.5 ft in depth kiddie pool. My son loves it! Lifeguard on duty too which is unusual (but nice!) for hotel pool. 
Gym. Modern, clean, great equipment. 
Bad-
Hotel shop. Not well-stocked and very expensive. 
Breakfast. Didn't eat the food so can't speak for quality. $20 for eggs and $17.50 for oatmeal seems a bit ridiculous. 
GREAT-
So far all staff have been friendly and warm and helpful.

Continued.... And to top it all off... Forgot to hang the darn "do not disturb" sign on door last night.... Hotel staff knocked, loudly I might add, at 8:15 this morning to find out when the heck we were leaving so they could clean the room.

Overall a great hotel. Our room was a good size, looking right into Camden Yards. Room was clean and staff was super friendly and helpful. Even though there were tons of kids in the hotel, we were not disturbed at all! 
My tiny complaint is that the bathroom didn't allow a place to hang towels so they could be reused. Being Eco-friendly and only staying for 2 nights I didnt really need new towels but there was no place, besides back of door which didn't fit 2 towels or allow them to dry, to hang the towels. A towel rack is really all I can say that would have added to my overall experience.
Overall a great stay!

We enjoyed our stay, we booked with priceline and got a good price. After reading the reviews we asked for the South tower and was on the 24th floor. We checked for bed bug evidence and found none so that was good! No tub, but not an issue for us. The worst was the crack in the window and the single pane glass which allowed ALL noise from outside to be heard! Also the pillows were too soft and went "flat". The service was great although alittle slow when requesting clean towels. They stored our bikes for us and it was a nice ride to inner harbor. Self park is cheaper and we could get to our car with no problems! No free wifi or continental breakfast.
Stayed here during the 4th of July. The hotel was wonderful, staff was pleasant and the bed was the best bed my husband and I had ever slept in. Super clean hotel. I would stay here again, for sure.
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn Baltimore Inner Harbor

review_title: Only two things make up for this hotel experience - the gym and the location.
review_text: Once you figure out how to navigate your way into the driveway without being slammed by turning traffic, it's pretty much downhill. You then need to find someone to park your car and forget about help with your bags. There is a look of relief on the attendant's face when you say you'll handle it yourself. There is a continual line at the registration desk where 2 people try to help you while answering phones. Our room was average size. I turned down the comforter to crawl into bed and the sheets were dirty with what I can only describe as "body fluids". I went down to the lobby to talk to someone about it and there was a woman there demanding to see a manager about the filthy comforter on her bed. tried to do laundry. 2 washers don't work. I have to carry laundry to washer in adjoining hotel. No apologies - no assistance. Breakfast buffet so-so. Coffee earns always empty! Hotel is in great location to inner harbor sites and restaurants. The attached gym is THE best I've ever seen in a hotel
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn Baltimore Inner Harbor

review_text:
Was here for a conference, so most of my review is based on that experience. The conf space was awful--bad AV, bad configurations, bad sound, bad temp, bad noise carryover, bad equipment. 
The food was completely under-whelming. Not bad, but not good.
The staff was mixed. They were super friendly but not terribly good at their jobs. Friendly is great...but so is competence.
The hotel room was okay. Not all that well-appointed though (i.e. no plugs where you need 'em, like on the desk--HELLO!!-- old clock radio, instead of one that plays/charges an iPod, etc.).
The valet drained my battery, so I waited 30 mins for my truck. They helpfully informed me that 'it happens all the time here.' So apparently they don't learn...
Lastly, the restaurant in the hotel had great food but the WORST service, so skip it.
Skip it all, really.

rom the first phone call that I made to the Sheraton Baltimore city center hotel I encountered problem after problem. The staff that received my initial reservation was unclear on the terms, which led to me having to pay a higher rate then first quoted. Secondly I was not told that the reservation was non-refundable, not that I intended to cancel, I just wanted the option available to me if it was necessary. Thirdly, a day after I checked out I was charged an additional $50 because I was told that they did not charge me enough at the time of my initial checkout, and then the staff was rude to me when I called to question why I was charged more money after checkout.
 Overall I would probably never stay at the Sheraton Baltimore city center ever again, and I am unsure if I would stay at another Sheraton property again if this is an example of the service that I would receive

I stayed here because I had to for business. Do not ever stay here if you can avoid it. The reviews are not exaggerating about the lack of cleanliness. The carpet is disgusting. My colleague's carpet has a huge red stain next to the bed. The walls are covered in black marks. The curtains are covered in dust, as is all of the furniture. The bathroom had hair & dust all over the floor & the shower smells strange (and there is hair on the walls). The bed is terrible & I made the mistake of pulling the top sheet off the duvet. There is a ton of hair & dust & fuzz balls in there. 
The staff is nice enough but nothing can make up for how filthy & run down this hotel is. It is impossible to relax when you don't want to touch anything. Stay somewhere else.

We stayed here one night just passing through. The hotel appears fairly new. It was spotless everywhere we looked. Quick, easy check-in and -out. The room was 'right-sized' for our needs, and well appointed. There is an Ikea store across the road and the furnishings in the room look like they could have come from there. The only issue--and this is barely worth mentioning--is there was no exhaust fan in the bathroom. Leave the door open a bit and there's no problem. The breakfast is standard Fairfield, but once again the breakfast area was kept spotless and the quality of the food was just a little better than I've experienced at other Fairfield inns. 
Easy access from I-95, and a gas station, mcdonalds, and taco bell are within walking distance. White Marsh town center is across the road with plenty of other eating and shopping choices.
I highly recommend this hotel.
hotel_name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Baltimore White Marsh

review_text: We arrived at the hotel around 3pm and waited a hour and a half to check-in & secure our room! There were at least 80 to 100 people standing in line to check-in as well. We were told this was due to large groups arriving at the same time and rooms not being cleaned!!

Good stay, requests all met. Was here for a graduation, perfect location to shopping, food, and highway. People were friendly, room clean. This was actually my 2nd time staying here. If I need to return,I'll stay there again.
hotel_name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Baltimore White Marsh

review_title: Jada and Kevin are major assets!
review_text:
We were pleased with the hotel but were amazed by Jada and Kevin. Jada welcomed us like we were old friends and gave us advice as to some of the local attractions. Kevin had a good conversation with us after Crabby Hour. 
The Peir 5 Hotel was upscale but not stuffy just the perfect place for our weekend get away.

review_title: Nice lobby but rooms need a face lift
review_text: Although the hotel provide a nice location for getting around town, it appears the rooms (at least those in the north tower) need a little help. Once I checked in and received wonderful customer service, I made it to my room only to see several signs of a worn out room. Although surrounded by windows, the curtains were torn, the desk was broken, the phone was disconnected and the space was quite small. Don't get me wrong, the hotel is trying...the restaurant has a nice bar and staff goes out of their way to provide good service. All and all, for one might on business, it was alright. However, if I was on vacation I would probably stay elsewhere.

Hotels seem to undervalue the need for Internet access. We travel with an iPad and a laptop, and use them for different projects, and rarely at the same time. This hotel charges $13 per night and insisted that it is "Sheraton policy" that it be charged per machine, not per room. There is no free wifi in the lobby, only four computers that can be used, if available. The manager very reluctantly waived our second charge the first night. Not very smart for an expensive hotel in a struggling area
Aside from some small issues such as; no free continental breakfast, no pool and poor tv channel selection, pretty accommodating. Very friendly staff and excellent location.
Went there for business, staff was amazing as usual. Hotel looks great and location is perfect. Highly recommended and will return soon.

review_title: A botique hotel located in the Inner Habor with nice looks and little substance.
review_text: The hotel is cute in that Ikea-eqsue so-called botique style. Most surfaces such as door, railings, etc are painted with cheesy faux finishes. Our room was on the third floor and the air conditioner was insufficient for August summer heat. House keeping did not clean the room when we returned in the late afternoon. Overall the location was great but the service and very warm room dissapoints.

I have taken my family to Baltimore the last couple of years (kids 2 and 5) and wanted to try a Harbour Magic Hotel. We tried the Pier V and we loved it.
