hotel_name: Hyatt Regency Washington on Capitol Hill

review_text: The hotel is within walking distance of union station and the Capitol building. We stayed in the regency club which was nice but the rooms although comfortable require a refurbishment as do the whole floor. The carpet in the corridor is stretched and old as it the entire finish to the rooms. Saying that we still had a great stay and would probably stay there again. It is a 20 min easy walk to Chinatown where there is a great Italian restaurant called viapiano which is great.
hotel_name: Hyatt Regency Washington on Capitol Hill

review_text: What a dump. For $30/night, you get smelly roach-infested rooms. Also, this "hotel" has some sort of contract with the government that allows homeless women and their kids to stay there. These women are rough-looking and the children are unruly. The staff is horrible...the skinny black guy with glasses used the "f" word a few times when I asked him he name of the manager. Worst hostel experience EVER!!

You get what you pay for! I stayed here because I had a discounted rate, the hotel was noisy, people had their t.v. up loud and talking past 1 a.m, you could here the noise from outside as if the Windows were up. I just decided to move out to a more expensive hotel so that I could get some rest. I moved to DC from out of town and all the Motel 6 I have stayed at were great this was the worst.

review_title: Great location and good breakfast, but bed comfort and service need improvements
review_text:
The hotel is steps away from the Capitol, making it very convinient to it and surrounding places. However, their service from valet to front desk to restaurant was mixed. Valet was not courteous. Front desk was accommodating and helpful, but had some difficulties with recognizing my Hyatt Platinum. The restaurant service was sometime slow, while their food was very good to excellent. 
The rooms and amenities were good, but the bed was a bit too firm and not as comfortable as usually encountered at other Hyatts.
hotel_name: Hyatt Regency Washington on Capitol Hill

Very nice hotel in great location. Short walk to White House. Staff was very accommodating. Parking is expensive and garage can fill easily requiring using a garage near by. Rooms and bathroom on the small side but not unusual for a city location. Pool was small but nice. Would definitely stay here again.

We had booked 4 nights here through a private travel company. We arrived by taxi, and drove through some pretty scary looking slums to arrive at this dump. The lady at the front desk who checked us in was friendly and helpful but that's where the positives ended. Our room was on the ground level right next to the vending machines and washing room which was one big noise the whole night. There were shady looking guys sitting in their truck in the car park right by our room the whole night, constant yelling and talking from outside right through the night, the walls were paper thin. After about 2 hours sleep and a few bed bug bites (yup I'm not kidding!) We used the internet in the lobby to book a room for the next 3 nights in DC at the Courtyard Marriott and checked out straight away. We told the man at the desk we didn't feel safe there and he didn't even seem surprised. We asked him to call us a cab so he got on the phone and told us 15 minutes. We went outside and this rusty old car pulls up with no sign of any company name, no meter no ID badge. He told us he would take us to where we needed to go for $15, I told my partner that I did not want to get in the car with this guy so we told him not to worry, we'd get another taxi which lead him to swear at us and accusing us of wasting his time after coming all the way there. Luckily there was a taxi getting gas right next to the hotel so we got a ride with him. Was just not the start to my time in Washington that I was expecting, it was terrible service, grotty rooms and not safe at all.
Awesome location, nice rooms and even good food at hotel. There isn't any where to eat after 11 but hotel bar offsers a pretty good menu.
hotel_name: Hyatt Regency Washington on Capitol Hill

review_text: Found through hotels dot com and will definitely return. Clean room, good price, helpful staff, great location for Dupont Circle or the zoo (walked to both). Don't pass this place up!

review_title: Not a four-star- just a tired hotel that the great employees work to keep afloat.
review_text:
This Hyatt does have a great location and lobby is still wonderfully classic to its time. But the rooms need to be updated as do the floor hallways- carpets and curtains, both. It was time for the mattress on our double bed to be replaced- one expects better from any four-star hotel these days.
The food was great though, even I'd very expensive. The service in the bar was below average, but all the folks in the dining room were great.
I wouldn't return, but the experience wasn't horrible.
hotel_name: Hyatt Regency Washington on Capitol Hill

review_text:
Big, big disappointment.
Location good but that's where it ends.
Overpriced rooms, overpriced shop and very overpriced bar.
Bar staff rude and request tips. 
Lots of guys hang around outside hotel requesting money, ciggarettes etc.
Shower power poor. No in room safe. Old fashioned rooms. 
Generally not a friendly place.
hotel_name: Hyatt Regency Washington on Capitol Hill

review_title: Really cool neighborhood for those who like to be outdoors
review_text: This location is in a really neat area. The cab ride from the airport took us through the forest primeval...gorgeous parks and creeks, etc. I was there for a conference and didn't sightsee much, but did not the convenience of a nearby metro station (Woodley Park Zoo Metro)

review_title: All you can expect from a well run 3 star hotel. Fantastic location.
review_text: We enjoyed our two-night stay this April. The location is walking distance from Union Station, Capitol Hill, national Botanic Gardens and all Smithsonians. No safe inside room. No mini bar or fridge either. Excellent value for a three star. Parking outrageous price at 41 per day!
hotel_name: Hyatt Regency Washington on Capitol Hill

I went to this hotel to getaway for the weekend when I got there it was a fast check in.but the front desk agent were quite rude just a liltte bit but overalll my stay was ok.
hotel_name: Comfort Inn & Suites New York Avenue

review_text: We got a suite for the family if 5. It's clean, updated bathroom, a comfortable temperature, quiet and spacious rooms, and good value. The breakfast was good and staff attentive there. Also had helpful staff at front desk got us a discount by getting a Comfort inn member number so we extended to 3 nights. Staff also got us a free shuttle since we didn't realize the regular shuttle hours were finishing. Shuttle driver really nice Extra pillows promptly delivered. We had a great first experience the last week of August in Washington.
hotel_name: Comfort Inn & Suites New York Avenue

review_text: Great facilities, good location, wonderful place to stay will consider this over a hotel anyday. Much better atmosphere for family holidays.

review_title: Clean and comfortable rooms with the best breakfast buffet ever.
review_text: The rooms were clean and comfortable but could of been a little more luxurious. The breakfast was outstanding. It was a buffet with every breakfast food known to man. Pancakes, waffles, eggs, omlets, fruit, dessert, hash browns, and bacon. There was a swimming pool and a fabulous gym. If you're in Washington DC stay there.
hotel_name: Hyatt Regency Washington on Capitol Hill

review_text: Great location, staff, and rooms. The Woodley Park area is really nice and has good restaurants. Hotel is within walking distance to the Metro.

review_title: Very underwhelming, unwelcoming and poor service.
review_text: Had to call for different pillows and towels were like sand paper. Also the service was so poor and un accomodating for large groups. Terrible place for a conference.
This hotel was fantastic. Good location next to the metro. Lots of restaurants near by. Have to try the quesadillas at harrys pub in the hotel. Very nice and friendly staff. Thank you marriot

review_title: Recent renovation but not near union station
review_text:
I checked on google maps before staying at the hotel so knew it was about 2km from union station.
The hotel has a shuttle which was running every 20 minutes or so until 11pm.
The area around the hotel is not nice but with the shuttle I did not see it as a problem as the trade off is much better deals than the central hotels.
I was told by the taxi driver that the hotel had been recently renovated an you could tell, the shell was still the same but the bed, fridge, microwave etc were all new looking.
The staff were helpful on the few occasions I had questions.
hotel_name: Comfort Inn & Suites New York Avenue

review_title: Location does not make up for the poor service and overall shoddiness of this hotel, will never stay here again.
review_text: Picked this hotel because of the location and proximity to the metro line, what a mistake. In short this is a run down hotel that was likely built in the sixties without any obvious real renovation effort. Room is muggy and smells of mold, furniture is outdated and cheap looking, towels are thin and ratty, overall has the feel of a larger motel 6. The icing on the cake was the service, or rather the lack thereof. Left the room at around nine am, returned at ten pm to find that the room had not been cleaned at all. Called the front desk which offered no apology or remedy. Dont waste your time or money on this place, there are many other options at this price level.

Great hotel for a conference. Excellent gym open 24 hours to guests with room key. Very few frills or extras. If you are used to a newspaper at your door in the morning you won't get it here. You won't get a single thing you don't pay dearly for. Rooms comfy with mini business center, flat screen TVs and lights that actually illuminate the room! Restaurants extremely expensive and even the coffee kiosk charges $3 for a weak cup of Java. But they handle conferences well as far as crowd control. Very vigilant security. Definitely not for a family vacation. Located in an OK restaurant area. Took the Metro from Reagan Airport without problems.

review_title: Great hotel for business meetings or for vacation in DC.
review_text: Location is great and dining on site is wonderful. Staff is very helpful. Very nice experience.

Largest hotel in DC, very impersonal. The room was small and pretty standard. The gym has many defect machines and old weight equipment. Very expensive room service, and I travel all over.
Not convincing.

This was a great hotel, I read the reveiws from this site about the location, but that is greatly over shadowed by the service and up keep of the hotel!! The manager was very nice and accessable, as we called on her a bit much! The shuttles run very frequent and the breakfast was pretty good! I would like to thank the whole staff there! Thank You!!
hotel_name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Washington, DC/New York Avenue

review_text:
Positive points v clean, nice area not far to dupont circle, restaurants nearby on 17th st, no probe with wifi.
Negative points decor in room a bit tatty and could do with an update/refurb, thin Walls and doors which had gaps at the bottom, sink 
in room. 
Some may find shower room on the snug size as it literally looks like it was built in a cupboard and shares with the wc.

Two of my electronic chargers were stolen throughout my 2 week stay. On the second day of my stay my daughter's Ipad charger was stolen and on the 6th day my Tmobile cell phone charger was stolen out of my room. Don't leave your chargers out in the open, please hide them in your suitcases, because housekeeping will steal them.
hotel_name: Georgetown University Hotel and Conference Center

The Quincy is sadly let down on 2 fronts:
1. Noise - we had front facing rooms on floor 8. There was almost constant noise from early each morning - largely due to a garbage truck stop directly across from the hotel. The Quincy does not have good sound proofing (the windows opens unusually for a city hotel). It is fair to say that it is probably the noisiest hotel I have stayed at.
2. Heat - we stayed in Nov and found the rooms heated to an almost unbearable temperature. The air con is old and useless - our only remedy was to open the window and suffer more noise.
The above is a shame as the staff were unfailingly friendly and the location is good. Unfortunately though, a hotel that fails to provide a good night's sleep is not fit for purpose - by checkout after 3rd night, we were tired and desperate to leave.

review_title: Stay elsewhere if at all possible.
review_text: With the exception of two staff members, the entire hotel staff must have learned their hospitality as guards in a war prison. The facility itself is dated, uncared for and not comfortable. I was there for two weeks and lock on my door had to be reprogrammed everyday! This was a common problem for other guests as well. Yet the old guards from Stalig 13, I mean hotel staff, insisted I was somehow doing something wrong. The owners obviously refuse to see or impliment the required upgrades to make the hotel welcoming and comfortable.

Would not return : except the excellent location, nothing worth it : not so clean room (dirty tissues under the bed side table from the previous host : eww!) and bathroom, no free wifi in the room and not even in the lobby (are we in 2011?), none hotel in room stationery, breakfast restaurant overpriced and food not great.

Have stayed here over the years and always regarded it as a great value that left me totally satisfied - rather like good comfort food. On recent stay found it still a good value, but loosing the quality that made that value special. Both business center CPUs are ancient and were out of order; the van service was slow to respond; front desk staff seemed burned out and was indifferent. Still not bad, but could so easily be better.

Good location, excellent house keeping / service, dangerous place (cockroach in elevators, unclean and slippery hallways). I had a fall after slipping onto something greasy outside the elevator and nearly injured myself. I don't think I will ever go there again.

Rooms are good size with separate living room, kitchenette, and very small bathroom with tub/shower. 5 min walk to Foggy Bottom metro stop & GWU Hospital. Kitchen has full size refrig/freezer, 2 electric burners, coffee maker, dishwasher, & microwave.
Beds comfortable, nice showerhead, & currently free Internet with Hilton Honors member. Few of front desk and bellman very friendly-some not so much. 
No sit down restaurant in hotel but they have breakfast room service. Not a lot of restaurants nearby and many closed on Sundays. 
Elevators incredibly slow most of time. 
Nice hotel for area.

Very convenient location to the foggy bottom metro but the staff not very attentive - every night we had to request extra towels - we stayed as a family of four and we were given 3 towels every day of our 6 night stay. In room coffee maker was broken.

review_title: An well-worn hotel with a great location with acceptable amenities.
review_text: An OK hotel showing it's age a bit. Great location in Georgetown. Walk right out the front door and catch the "Circulator" city bus for a buck! From there you can go to the Metro or Union Station for trains. The hotel has everything you need, it's just showing some wear.

I was very sceptical about staying here after reading some very negative reviews. Thankfully, I was pleasantly surprised at the quality and cleanliness of the rooms. It is basic but this place is not advertised as a luxury hotel. The rooms are clean, the beds are comfortable and there were no bed bugs. The front desk staff, the concierge and the shuttle bus driver were all pleasant and helpful. The location is great, Georgetown is a beautiful place. The walk to M Street and the National Harbour is easy - there and back. You will need to use transport to get to the National Mall and Smithsonian institutions. I was happy to staying away from central DC as it was quiet at night and felt safer than some areas downtown. I would recommend this hotel.

I stayed here for four nights and fount it quite pleasant. It is centrally located and the staff is helpful and friendly. The rooms are clean and comfortable however, I would recommend against staying on the second floor as the noise from the bar downstairs can be distracting. The noise woke me up several times during the night an I wish that the staff could have addresses this, but I guess that is out of their control

review_title: Dirty sheets, dirty carpet, old furniture, loud refrigerator, uncomfortable bed. Avoid this hotel.
review_text: Dirty sheets, dirty carpet, old furniture, loud refrigerator, uncomfortable bed. Avoid this hotel.

review_title: Great stay in an outstanding location
review_text: We stayed at The Quincy for a week of sightseeing. Our room was comfortable and clean, and the staff were all friendly and helpful. Bed was especially comfortable. This hotel is within a couple of blocks of the Farragut North AND Farragut West Metro stations, which gives you access to multiple subway lines (red, blue, orange). Lots of places to eat nearby. White House is only a 20 minute walk away. The hotel is in a busy downtown area, and you will hear street noise - as other reviewers have noted. But we found it to be a good value in DC, and we loved the location.

review_title: Terrible customer service--overbooked and left our family with no place to stay
review_text: After traveling for 13 hours our family arrived this evening at dulles and had to go directly to the emergency room with our youngest child. We called the hotel to let them know we would be arriving late only to find they had overbooked and sent is to a hyatt who we came to find out also was oversold, so now we are driving 40 minutes in a taxi to a hotel in Maryland, with a ver sick child. I think this is immoral and sickens me that people do business this way.

review_title: Staff and location compensate for less than average room
review_text:
4 adults and two children traveling so we booked their only 2 bedroom suite.staff were excellent, full of lots of info, maps, shopping tips etc. It was very large room, which staff said was renovated- it was not! Settee was scagged and chair looked dirty, very large table ( seats 10) was marked and old. The carpet by the bathroom was soaking wet and smelt damp. I kept shoes on all the time as it didn't feel very nice. There was only 4 place setting of cutlery, despite being large room. No cooker, just 2 ring job, one of which was broken. No grill or toaster so breakfast was difficult. Tea towel looked dirty.
Very old tv, on off switch broken, also air con- is very old, either freezing or warm.
I never write reviews, but I was disappointed with room. Being very close to metro/ walking distance to sites and the lovely staff helped make up for rest of issues.

My husband and I have spent New Year's Eve the past two years at the Georgetown Inn. Love the location in the heart of Georgetown, and the room decor is very different than the standard chain hotels. We look forward to returning next New Year's Eve.

This place was extremely disgusting even for the price considering the prices of other hotels in the area. It would be fine for the price if the service was even just okay. We ordered room service and the person on the phone hung up after us placing our order without allowing us even a second to ask questions or giving us the price. The front desk is also extremely rude and unhelpful. Although they claim to be 24 hours they rarely answered the phone and when they did they seemed bothered and extremely rude!

review_title: A great deal pleasant stayGreat deal. Very pleasant. It is what it is.
review_text: It is a step back in time. But it is actually a perfectly fine budget choice. It is clean, the staff is very helpful. Still having trouble with key machine but they did everything they could to help while it was fixed. Bathrooms were very clean. LOVED the coffee shop. It was like 1965. If you are looking for Ramada inn or Hilton donâ€™t bother. Quiet and safe part of town. The river setting is nice and the seafood shacks at the end of the river walk are a must. As a man business travelled it is perfect...or for a family it's great. For a couple where she wants to feel pampered. No way. They clearly try hard. I'll bet anything the bad experiences were commensurate with attitude.

review_title: Recently, stayed here and had an item mysteriously "vanish" from my closed carry on luggage. Confined it was " borrowed" by hous
review_text: Lock everything...even it you think "nobody" would 'borrow' it...and why the hell is there no room safes in this hotel?

review_title: Our experience at the hotel was extremely enjoyable.
review_text: The hotel service did everything to accommodate our needs. They were also very helpful in providing us with entertainment, food, and events in the area.
Great customer service, shuttle took us right to our destination, and we will definitely stay here again! Thank you for a flawless experience!

Me and my friend decided to make a random, spur of the moment trip to DC. As far as rooms were concerned we wanted as cheap as possible without compromising our sense of security. We were surprised to see how much we got for our money. The building felt as though it were part of history yet had a modern style to it. We were able to see both the Capitol and the Washington monument from the room. Our concierge, Ray, was very informative in helping us navigate through the "to-go" places in DC. His direction definitely made the trip memorable. This hotel was definitely a good buy. It's half a mile to the Capitol. The only downfall is there aren't too many things within a couple-block radius.

I was very impressed with the courteous staff. They were both well groomed and well mannered. As a tourist to the state, they took the time to give me directions, car services, tourist attractions as well as pointers on where to enjoy nightlife. The hotel has a shuttle service which takes you to the "Mall" which is where all the government attractions are, very convenient. 
My bed was extremely comfy and my flat screen t.v was huge. I had an amazing window view of the Capitol. I also enjoyed the fact that hotel was a "go green" conservative hotel. The hotel lobby was beautifully decorated where it had a vintage/classy wall paper theme but all the furniture accents were modern an chic. I really could go on and on but my point is that I had an enjoyable stay and will be staying there again and again.
The room was beautiful & the view of the Capitol &have monument was gorgeous. Will definitely go again.

We arrived at the Hotel Harrington expecting very little as we had seen the other reviews, 
They were correct. We were greeted with a sweating obese man shouting at us. The rooms were diagusting to say the least, the toilet hadnt been flushed and there was ice cubes, white "stuff" (spunk) in the loo. it was vile! there were lower body hairs in the bath and the sheets were stained with purple marks and ripped around the ages. 
When we asked to borrow a hairdryer the reply was " you should have brought your own" and they were just as helpful about the broken air conditioning.
However the location was great! there were many liquor stores and the night life was wwild and loud all around the hotel which kept us entertaine as we tryed to spend as little time as possible in the rooms.

The rooms in this hotel have not been renovated in about 50 years!!
The air conditioning bareley worked and it is another old classic place going down the drains. The service is terrible and will make sure to tell you it's not their fault even if it's the maid service. Spend the extra money and go somewhere else or stay outside the metro area.

review_title: Great, but out of the way.
review_text: This is a great hotel, the only thing that let's it down is it's location. Slightly outside the Capital it is approximately a $10 taxi ride which can be a bit of a hassle if you've had a long day. Apart from that everything about the Capitol Slyline is fantastic! I arrived two hours early and my room was ready to occupy, the rooms were very large and the beds were the most comfortable I stayed in. This is a fantastic place to stay in DC.

review_title: Decent stay for a short time frame
review_text: We stay there for an impromptu stop in DC to see the sights and it was decent. I didnt care for the late evening registration female, she was cold and dismissive. I was also annoyed that the charged us $25 for parking in darkest and dingy lot. The room was cozy and comfortable but agree that they need much upgrades. The free shuttle was also annoying because it doesn't follow an accurate schedule and you end up waiting longer time than expected. But it's manageable and I would stay there again for the price.

review_title: Great location, nice staff, poorly kept rooms
review_text: Stayed at this hotel for one night in Oct 2011 because of it's convenient location near most of the major attractions and metro stations. The rate was cheap for DC but then again you get what you pay for. The room appeared clean but very outdated, run down and in desperate need of upgrades. This actually made the room feel dirty. The doors and walls are not sound proof so you hear everything. The bed was very springy so every time my husband turned in his sleep I would bounce. You get a few very very tiny bars of "facial" soap but no shampoo, conditioner or lotion. The tv was old. The antique A/C vent with rod above the bed hadn't been cleaned in ages and had a build up of dust and possibly mold on it and the ceiling around it. The thermostat with visible electrical wire tacked to the wall was antique and looked like a building code violation; it didn't work either with controlling room temp. The hotel staff was courteous. I personally wouldn't stay here again since the few extra dollar savings wasn't worth the overall experience.

Old hotel. Daggy and basic rooms, but was very clean, had a comfy bed, and on the doorstop of the Mall. Compared to other hotels we researched, was the cheapest, and did the job... Just dont expect a new, fancy room! Would definatley recommend if you just need a comfy bed to sleep between sight seeing.

review_title: Good base at the right distance of the national mall
review_text:
If you are looking for a good base of operations for scouting DC, the capitol skyline is a very good choice.
The rooms are pretty big and well kept. The promotional staff immediately took us to the map and not only showed us where the monuments were, but was also right on telling us where the nightlife spots and the finest restaurants were.
Another pro is the swimming pool. Cons are actually the breakfast served, which was very poor value for the money to be paid. Do not take the breakfast!!

review_title: Great location for Mall, bad location for crime!
review_text: My two daughters and i stayed here for 5 nights and overall the hotel was decent. It was close to many of the sites. It was in a bad neighborhood (near Anacostia- worst area for crimes) and I wouldn't recommend being outside the hotel at night. The manager gave us a good discount on parking in their garage! The decor is cheap but works. The hotel has a complementary shuttle that drops off at a few locations, first come first serve and is useful. Throughout the night you wake up to sirens, due to the police station right by. I didn't spend time by the pool but I could hear loud music coming from it that sounded like a bunch of loud, drunk people were hanging around. We would recommend this hotel for the location near the national mall, but caution people for the unsafe area, and not for families especially with young kids.

review_title: I do not recommend this hotel.
review_text: We stayed 3 nights and although it is walking distance from attractions, we were warned by locals to not leave the sight on food as it is not safe. The ac did not work at all and it was unbearably hot in our room. We asked for another but were told they hadnt switched from heat to ac so there was nothing they could do. When we walked out of hotel, we were immediately approached by bums asking for money.

I read the reviews of this location on my flight from Florida and was a little worried since we had already paid for this location. Upon arrival my wife and I were greeted at our cab and in our room in 10 minutes. It is true this is an older hotel. However there is a lot of character to the rooms and lobby. I travel weekly to high end hotels and would have no problem staying in this location again. Our room was clean, there was hot water, and the staff was very nice.
Dave Loiseau was excellent and accommodating! We would look out our window and be eyeline with the Nation's Capitol. The prices were fair and the service was prompt and friendly.
Great hotel if you're not looking for too fancy. It is a block from Georgetown and only a couple of blocks the other direction to the mall. Good service, great location

review_title: Good enough but a little pricey!
review_text:
Gorgeous hotel near Foggy Bottoms/GWU Metro. Clean and nicely decorated. Weird bathroom arrangement with the sink in the main room with bath and loo in the bathroom. 
The hotel is lovely, but $200 a night is very expensive. I'd stay again, but shop around websites for a better deal.

review_title: This gem of a hotel is perfectly located and exudes old Washington charm
review_text: Spent a night here with my teenage daughter. I grew up in the area and it felt like coming home. If you want slick, this isn't for you. If you want easy comfort, a helpful staff, and great location, you can't beat the Melrose. Lots of great eateries within walking distance, from pubs to haute chic. A deli a few steps down Pennsylvania Avenue is a good bet for breakfast and snacks. I read so-so reviews on Expedia and found the Melrose undeserving. I highly recommend this DC classic.

review_title: Solid hotel at a great value
review_text: Yes, this is an older hotel that could use some updates. Is it perfect? No. Checked in at 2:45 pm and was told there were no rooms available - then it'd at be at least 30 minutes for my room to be completed. After forcing them to check again, a room suddenly became available. The rooms themselves are quite spacious for DC - though the walls are very thin (heard everything the people next door were saying and got both of their wake up calls). In spite of the above, I'd still recommend this hotel based on location and, most importantly, price. It was literally hundreds of dollars less than the Westin just a few blocks away. I would stay here again in the future. Again, very solid hotel for this price and area of DC.
This was a very nice visit home away from home great front staff very very caring, restaurant was closed but they had a shuttle service for near by restaurant love this place
This is truly a great place thanks to Dave,Kimberly, and Jackie. They truly made this a memorial vacation we will never forget you. Also love the beds great location

review_title: Great hotel to rest your hat
review_text: The Melrose Hotel is a great value. It's not right in the heart of the action, but a cab ride to any place that is was less than $10 (including from Union Station). We walked only a mile to the Lincoln Memorial (took only 25 minutes). Our room was huge - the AC worked great and the staff was awesome (we forgot toothpaste and called down to see if there was a gift shop, which there wasn't, but instead they brought us up a complimentary tube in about 5 minutes). The small hotel bar - the Library Bar - was very reasonable and quaint. For the money, you can't beat it.

I stayed at this hotel while attending a meeting that was occurring there. Overall, I found it to be quite comfortable. 
The beds are great! The other room furnishings are reasonable for a hotel of this category. I didn't use any of the other hotel amenities. Parking was expensive but comparable to other hotels in downtown Washington DC. I did enjoy being within a safe walking distance of a number of excellent restaurants. All of the staff were extremely polite and efficient.
hotel_name: The Westin Washington, D.C. City Center

review_text: The hotel can be a little tricky to reach by car as you try to exit from Thomas Circle on a one way street. Room were normally sized and fully acceptable. Has a good meal in the restaurant that has some imaginative dishes. The only problem was the front desk which couldn't cash a $20 bill. Unbelievable that a hotel of this size could cash a 20. They sent me to the gift shop which wouldn't give me change unless I bought sometime. I finally got change from the doorman. Imagine, the doorman has more cash in his pocket the the front desk. But, on balance, it was a good room and I got a good nights sleep.
hotel_name: The Westin Washington, D.C. City Center

review_title: Excellent (if low rate and you are comfortable walking)
review_text:
Stayed here for one Saturday night on a holiday weekend with my SO and small dog. We live locally, so drove in to relax and see the sites and pricelined the room for under a Benjamin. Parking is EXPENSIVE - around $40-50 a night. No charge for my dog. 
Hotel common areas were nice, clean and standard for this type of hotel. Staff (valet, front desk, etc) were very friendly. Room was well-sized with comfortable beds. Not 4-star all the way, but very nice. The hotel rooms mostly face the lobby in a courtyard fashion, which is...interesting? Not bad, not good. It is quiet, but no view. No real natural light. We didn't mind bc we slept in a little better than usual, and when we wanted to see DC we went out! 
The location was good - walkable to many areas of the city if you enjoy walking. We walked to dinner on N 14th, walked to the Mall and the Int Spy Museum, etc. Not across the street from a major site, but close enough. There is a 24 hour CVS very close, so we loaded up on drinks there to put in the fridge.
Would stay here again, but via Priceline or another amazing rate.
hotel_name: The Westin Washington, D.C. City Center

review_text: This hotel was great - good location, nice rooms, nice lobby. The rooms were quite nice with a chaise lounge chair and an arm chair. Great bed & bath per usual with Westin. My room was an interior facing the atrium, be sure to pull the curtains as the window shade does not block light/images. I enjoyed my stay here very much!
hotel_name: The Westin Washington, D.C. City Center

review_text:
Our experience started out with rude front desk staff who were understaffed and could not make any decisions. There was no manager onsite to assist and the valet and the engineer were assisting and offering advice in customer service. The woman at the desk tried to give us extra charges that were not made known in advance or in writing. 
The rooms are oddly shaped. The bathroom door in my room would not open all the way as it kept hitting the toilet. There was barely any room to get ready in there. My friend's room had a large bathroom and a small bedroom. The tempeture in the room got very hot despite it being on the coldest setting and the only recommendation was to open the windows and turn off the air. 
The historic charm was nice and the location is good (except for parking). I probably would have rated the hotel higher if the staff had been friendlier and helpful. There are many other hotels in the neighborhood with better service.

Stayed for one night during our trip to Washington DC. The location worked fine for walking to the bigger tourist attractions, e.g. the White house. Some good restaurants were close to the hotel as well.
If the main attraction for your trip is the White house, the Washington monument and so on, you might want to stay at a hotel further south. But the walk down to those attractions was a nice way to see some more of the city.
Parking was no problem, but cost around 40 dollars. Wifi was available in the lounge.

Although getting to this Westin was a bit confusing due to the roundabout street systems of DC, I cannot commend this location enough! From the moment I walked in the door I was treated like royalty. The staff was friendly and knowledgable. I was given a beautiful guestroom overlooking the skylit atrium. Whenever I phoned guest services, I was greeted by name in a manner that could not possibly be more accommodating. I would go so far as to say this Westin has been one of my best experiences ever as a SPG Member; rivaling even some of the W's I have stayed with. When I next return to the DC area the Westin DC City Center will be my first choice for a first class stay!
hotel_name: The Westin Washington, D.C. City Center

review_text: For the price, one would've expected better. But this regular chain hotel does not stand out in any way except for cleanliness and location.
hotel_name: The Westin Washington, D.C. City Center

review_text: Stayed on the Starwood preferred guest floor. Top level with a fantastic view of the flags and waterfalls on Dupont Circle. The view at night was spectacular. The hotel accommodations made our stay extremely pleasant .
hotel_name: The Westin Washington, D.C. City Center

review_text: This hotel is in a wonderful location. It's close to the Smithsonians, Holocaust Museum, and the metro station is underneath. You never have to leave the buiding to ride the metro! There is a mall underneath with lots of restaurants-McDonalds, Starbucks, Au Bon Pain-- a CVS drug store, and a sporting goods store. The restaurants were perfect to get a quick breakfast. The rooms are older but nice. It had comfortable beds with very luxurious bedding. Our room had a balcony with views of the Washington Monument, Lincoln Memorial, and the Capitol--gorgeous at night!! I would definitely stay here again!

My daughter and I spent four nights here for a work/ vacation and the Westin didn't disappoint at all. The hotel is excellent and the staff even better. When we we checked in we were given an unusually large room however there was little natural light. The staff immediately set to work to arrange a new room. The smaller "preferred view" room was full of natural light and worked out great. I can't say enough about the staff. Everyone was friendly, helpful and courteous. About the Starbucks, it is really one of those limited service ones and you're better off going out to any of the numerous Starbucks in the area. Dupont Circle is a short walk north and if you have a chance, sample the best gelato on earth at Pitangos on P and 15th. Yes we did go there twice.
hotel_name: The Westin Washington, D.C. City Center

review_text: The hotel was very nice but not convenient for walking to the attractions. Had to catch a cab, which became costly.
hotel_name: The Westin Washington, D.C. City Center

review_text: Seems like I stayed at Motel 6 or even worse! Tiny rooms, old TV from 1990, no breakfast, over priced valet parking, and drum roll... No WiFi!! Ghetto hotel.. Stay away.. Many other better hotels nearby...
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Washington DC \ Dupont Circle

review_title: Lots of potential,but not up to standard.
review_text: This has the potential to be a great place for families. However, the owners really need to invest in some updated wallpaper,artwork, and most importantly, a clean and useable kitchen area. There were old crumbs still on the appliances when we got to the room. The cabinets are just disgusting. They are very dilapidated and filthy. One cabinet was so dirty inside that previPus guests had drawn their initials in the dust/dirt. Would stay here again if we heard the hotel had done some cosmetics/ cleaning.

Keep in mind that parking is 42 dollars for valet and 40 for self park, for every 24 hours you are here. There are no other viable options to park so you are stuck.
Rooms are old, and in need of upgrades, although it is for the most part clean.
Breakfast is not included, nor is any type of coffee outside of your room.

If you enjoy a cold beer, good food, sightseeing, and comfortable beds then this is the place for you! I stayed here for seven nights and had lots to do each night without spending too much money. The local bars are walking distance just as most of the monuments and major attractions. I would suggest this place for government personnel as they provide you with a complementary breakfast buffet with lots of options. Like to run? The monuments and the Mall are a perfect distance away...
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Washington - Central / White House

review_text: The Georgetown Suites are located in a fun, safe & tourist friendly part of DC. The rooms are generously sized however, the kitchenettes could use some renovating. The Georgetown location is perfect for walking to restaurants, shopping, etc. It has a young, college crowd feel.

review_title: Nice place to stay. Good rooms.
review_text:
The hotel is a little too far away from the metro (during hot wheater). The rooms are excelent. Great beds Bathroom is not big, but good. 
The people at the reception are no rocketscientists. I speak rather good English, but have to ask all the time everything twice. 
The lobby needs a quick make over. It is really old fashioned. The elevators are a real drama. 
The people at the restaurant need a course for better service.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Washington - Central / White House

review_text: This hotel was in the best location, the best value for the money and I would highly recommend it. Within steps of all the monuments and museums and if we didn't feel like walking there was always a cab there for us. Room was clean, bed was comfortable and we got the view of the Patomic which was a nice bonus. Hotel was going through some remodeling but we didn't have any issues with noise or dust. Staff was very nice and the restaurants in the hotel were good. I would stay in this hotel again!
Good value but the charge for Supposedly high speed Internet of $10.95 a day is a real rip off! It is slower than dial up!

We stayed at the Hamilton Crowne Plaza for a short sight seeing weekend and were pleasantly surprised by how convenient the location was. We could walk to all the main tourist attractions and we were also a stone's throw away from some decent clubs. The room was small but well formed and clean with traditional decor. The food in the restaurant was excellent. Be sure to check out happy hour downstairs in the bar area - prices are reasonable and the finger food delicious!

Construction until midnight both nights I was there. Called and complained to shift manager and she said there was nothing she could do. Rooms are old and outdated. Beds are uncomfortable. Only thing going for it is its proximity to the National Mall.
I stayed at the hotel last year. It's a nice hotel, in a good location, and had a good price. You can walk everywhere, and it's a good walk to the Metro.
hotel_name: Holiday Inn Washington - Central / White House

review_title: Great location at a great price
review_text: Within walking distance to the National Theatre, White House, etc. The room was just fine even tho it the view was office building windows since we weren't there to be in the room except to sleep.
The staff was friendly. Its about a 10 minute cab ride from Ronald Regan National Airport. Also , it's about a 5 minute walk to the Smithsonian and about 10 minutes from the National Mall.

Centrally located. 
Clean and good buffet breakfast with more than normal healthy options. 
It's a pretty standard Westin experience but I had two complaints: 
1) Our room wasn't ready upon arrival despite trying to check in at 3:30pm with check-in time at 3pm. 
2) The sheets weren't high quality- they were rough- which is unexpected for a chain that prides itself on the heavenly bed.
hotel_name: The Westin Washington, D.C. City Center

review_title: Great hotel in a great location.
review_text:
My wife and I travelled to the DC area for a family event. We wanted to go into the city specifically to see the Smithsonian and other downtown museums. The Holiday Inn Capitol looked like it was in a good location and it turned out to be great! Just a block from the Air & Space Museum and a short walk from the American History, Natural History, and other Smithsonian museums as well as the National Gallery of Art and the Holocaust Memorial Museum.
The room was very clean and the hotel service was very good. The hotel restaurant was excellent, which is good because there are not many other places to eat in the area. Prices were reasonable, portions were large, and the quality was excellent. In addition to the restaurant and bar they have an express counter which serves light breakfast and lunch items.
Hint: For lunch get a sandwich to go from the hotel express counter and skip the museum cafeterias as they are quite pricey (double the cost of a lunch to go from the hotel).

review_title: Great location for a fun night on the town
review_text:
Ideal location, courteous staff (ask for Innocent- he knows EVERYTHING there is to know and do in the DC area) and clean rooms. Just know that parking is impossible
In this area! The hotel provides valet though

We stayed here for 2 nights & on arrival got upgraded to one one the king suites. Firstly, after traveling with kids for 3 weeks it was nice to get 2 separate rooms! The room was massive, clean & very comfortable. Location was excellent....literally across the street was the Space museum which was fabulous. We only had 2 nights but technically 1 full day to do Washington. We contemplated doing a tour but decided in the end to do it ourselves & walk - we did all the sites including Arlington cemetery which is a must too but u will need to catch the train out. The museums are fabulous. We loved Washington it's a beautiful city. One tip don't use supershuttle from the airport.....we didn't have to wait for the shuttle to fill up we were the last to be dropped off after everyone else which was painful!!!

We stayed here this past weekend for a wedding and were not too impressed. Parking was valet and $37 a day! It also took forever to find someone to park it and to retrieve the car for us. They definitely don't have enough people working there. Also, the fire alarm went off while I was rehearsing at the church and my husband had to run down 8 flights of stairs with our 4 month old son only to be told once he'd reached the lobby that they were just testing the system.
Great historic hotel which was also an amazing value for the location. A short walk from the red line but uphill if you use the Dupont circle stop. Elevators are small, but work just fine.
We really enjoyed our stay here.... it was everything we expected, and more.

This hotel is very old and needs to be updated really bad. Our room didn't smell like some of the others, but it wasn't the cleanest. It was extremely loud all night too. Location is good, but definitely not worth it. Stay somewhere else!

This hotel is ideally suited to sightseeing and everywhere is within walking distance. Although right beside the Metro we didn't use it and walked everywhere - or cycled. There are very few shops in Washington but there is a CVS right beside the hotel. If looking for real shopping I'd recommend taking the bus -the Circulator - to Georgetown which is only 30 mins away and worth a visit. The bus costs $1 each way from Union Station ! 
Staff in the hotel were very friendly and we also liked having the choice of a restaurant or take away breakfast. This was our second time in the hotel and we'll choose again if lucky enough to get back to Washington.

This hotel was perfect for a brief stay in Washington as it was close to the train and the hop on hop off bus stopped right outside. A 2 min walk to the Smithsonian Air and Space museum with the Capitol just up the road. Rooms were comfortable with a choice of pillows and an on site guest laundry was a welcome bonus. Good bar/ restaurant in the lobby and Starbucks on site were very handy. Staff were very helpful.

review_title: If you ever wondered what it would be like to stay at your rich, eccentric aunt and uncle's house, this is the place!
review_text: A very cool place, but definitely not for everyone. When I'm staying there, I feel more like I'm staying with family. Very relaxed, always interesting.

I truly had a good time at breakfast. The staff was very attentive and the omelet chef, Brian, was not only an excellent omelet chef but a friendly, delightful asset to Embassy Suites. He made my morning, my day and my weekend. Thank you
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Denver - Downtown / Convention Center

review_text: We chose this hotel for the location to Air and Space, which was good. But everything else not so good. The food was the worst we have ever had and we are not picky when it comes to food. The breakfast buffet was included with our room but it was so bad we walked out. The only thing worse than the food was the service. The waiter could not speak even one English word, so he was completely unable to get us drinks. We asked the front desk for directions to restaurants and they told us that were on the wrong side of town for food. They said the only place would be a McDonalds right down the block but they would not recommend walking there at night! The room was clean enough but the bathroom had some broken fixtures. I would stay here if all you are concerned about is location to the Air and Space museum.

We hade two nights there. Rooms are big, even for people can sleep in a room.
Easy parking.capitolium, whitehouse , lincoln memorial in walking distance.

When we checked in we found a half drank bottle of water and a pair of socks left on the floor. We also thought the room had a refridgerator. When we told the front desk they apologized sent up a fridge and paid for our wi-fi for the duration of our stay. Very nice place and close to the metro.

We recenty stayed at Hamilton Crowne Plaza and really enjoyed our stay. We checked in well after midnight but called ahead to let the staff know we would be late and they were very accommodating. Clean rooms, great views, great location. Our room (Single King) was slightly cramped especially in the bathroom but overall very nice and well decorated. Some friends of ours also stayed in the hotel and had some problems with their air conditioner but were promptly switched to a different room, given a discounted rate, and given complimentary breakfast at the hotel restaurant with no questions asked. Concierge was very friendly and helpful and had great advice (be sure to ask for Innocent- he was great!). Overall excellent and relaxing stay.

Great location for 1st time in DC tourist;good value for money;great little extras offered priority club members;fabulous restaurant with outdoor verandah offering views of the park and the quirky things you see in a city;didn't eat anywhere else;wonderful staff;minor niggle: no fridge but this may be the norm in the US(we are from Australia)
Literally seconds away from M street. Great value for the location. My recommendations at the highest level
Thought it was an upscale boutique hotel, but was disappointed. Service people were very nice and location was great, but rooms were just lacking a bit...a bit rough around the edges and outdated.

Stayed on business trip recently for a week and generally thought it was a good hotel. Breakfast was great except for stupid system for queuing for hot food! Staff friendly but as always, v keen on getting tips!!! Rooms good quality and large but some look into the building which is not so great so ask for high floor looking out on street. No great criticisms or outstanding experiences particularly.
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Denver - Downtown / Convention Center

review_title: Location great - food less than average-Noisy and crowded
review_text:
The location is great , one block from popular kid friendly museums like American Indian and air and space. Also you can see l'enfant metro stop from the hotel room but You also can see and hear trains on three tracks, passenger, cargo and metro at all hours.
It's very noisy and crowded with lots of kids but we stayed with kids so did not mind so much. 
 Food is mediocre and overpriced for what it is. Food service staff is impersonal and unfriendly- there may have been a language barrier but it took over an hour for just a salad to be served even though the bistro was packed with servers.
 When served the dressing was forgot which took another ten minutes. Check came without a pen and it took another ten minutes before I gave up waiting and asked the front desk for a pen so I could charge my room. It is after I had already made it clear to the server that we wanted to go to the pool before it closed and had changed by salad order to go. 
 The front desk wanted me to wait so they could talk to the server but I told them I had two restless kids 
Who had been wanting to go to the pool and finished their soggy overcooked Buffett food an hour earlier and just to charge the room.
 We finally made it to the pool at 9:30 and of course the lifeguard chose to close early on a saturday night so we had 15 minutes of swimming. 
 When walking down the stairs because the elevator was packed, it was a safety hazard due to wet concrete stairs from all the wet guests that was wet several floors 
down. 
 We had a nice suite though it was dark and showed it's age.
 Parking is 30 a day. There is a small strip just to the right of the lobby that is free from Friday night through the weekend that we discovered the last day.
 There is a convenient cvs two doors down with limited hours- closed Sunday- open until 6ish other days.
 There are also cheap food options next to it ( quiznos, wall street deli, mcdonalds)
 Overall, it was what we expected for a holiday inn and the convenient location was a nice surprise. Service could have been better but they were perpetually busy this weekend with guests and long lines and the weariness showed. We are holiday inn platinum elite members so have stayed at many hotels in the chain.

review_title: Perfect location to stay for a family trip to Denver
review_text: Was so happy to stumble on this very new Embassy Suites when looking for a place to stay for the RnR Denver Marathon. Rooms are the standard Embassy Suites layout and great for families. Furnishings are nice and new. The location is an easy walk to the 16th Street Mall and directly across from the convention center. Breakfast selection was great and the kitchen was very clean. My only negative comment is that the beverage area would get very crowded and it was difficult to get around, but it wasn't a big enough problem for me to give them any less than a 5 star review. It was also a bit unusual to have to ride the elevator to the check-in desk, but again not a big deal - especially since I had read about it before I arrived and the elevators were quick.
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Denver - Downtown / Convention Center

review_title: As barney would say super dee duper!
review_text: Excellent hotel. Would definitely stay again. Excellent location to the convention center.
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Denver - Downtown / Convention Center

review_text: Just checked out after a 7 night stay. The location to Smithsonian and The Mall can't be beat. This is perhaps the downfall also of the hotel. Because of the location, they know they will get bookings so everything else does fall slightly. It's pretty much the minimum to get by. No-one or no service went beyond that. One guy in the restaurant Charles was downright rude which spoiled the other staff who were fine. It's not a bad hotel by any means but it's not outstanding either

review_title: Excellent stay, excellent hotel, excellent staff
review_text: Had an excellent stay. Great service and friendly and helpful staff. I had the best omelet ever and the host for breakfast was very friendly and helpful. Loved it!
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Denver - Downtown / Convention Center

review_text: Everything is included at this hotel and 24 hours. Great happy hour and awesome breakfast, can't beat a cooked to order egg white omlet.
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Denver - Downtown / Convention Center

review_title: Good value, location and helpful front desk.
review_text: The location, and the price compared to the other hotels in the DC area is what made this my pick. The front desk was really helpful. I came back from a day of sightseeing with my girlfriend and we were both very tired. I went to the front desk, asked for any recommendations for dinner that could be delivered and they gave me this great Chinese food restaurant menu that delivered to my room. The breakfast was good. It came with eggs, sausage, waffle maker, yogurt and many other amenities. The room was good for what we needed, and I had a good experience at this comfort inn.
hotel_name: Comfort Inn Downtown DC / Convention Center

review_title: Luxury without the usual price tag!
review_text: I was very impressed with this hotel! I shared a room with 2 co-workers as we were there for a business convention (which was RIGHT next door!). We had 2 beds & yet it didn't feel crowded in the least. We each had our own sink & mirror, it was clean & looked brand new, & amazing city & mountain views from rooms & from most areas in the hotel. The free breakfast far exceeded my expectations (omelets cooked to order were delish!). Plus there's a nightly complementary happy hour & appetizers. Security measures & location were also unbeatable. Only complaint I have is a very small one: computers & Internet in business center were painfully slow. I will definitely go back!
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Denver - Downtown / Convention Center

review_text: Beautiful decor, large, comfortable rooms and really nice complimentary breakfast. Would definitely stay here again.
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Denver - Downtown / Convention Center

review_text: Was pleasantly greeted. Found the room to be standard, clean, orderly. Relativley quite floor.

review_title: Happy I did my homework- satisfied.
review_text: I took plenty of time to surf the Internet for hotels in the DC area. Many hotels I searched were booked or too expensive for my budget. I ended up booking the hotel through the 1800 reservation line. The operator was rather pushy to book the room at the first rate given to me (ie 179 and 280 respectively for my 2 night stay- after about 3 different rates and offers I was finally quoted 179 promo rate for each night. Compared to other hotels rates I was satisfied and booked it. I chose for the rate, hotel pickup for Old Town Trolley, and location to the Smithsonian Air Museum- a short 2 blocks walk away. Yes it is in the business district which does shut down early and can feel a bit deserted - but I was fine with that. CVS , smaller food businesses , quiznos, McDonald's and Starbucks are all a short walk right in the same block on C Street! I was aware of limited food options so no surprises for me. Less traffic down C and 6th, less pedestrians. It was actually quite nice! Yes the rooftop pool is on the small size and only 4 1/2 feet deep. Life guard was on duty supervising each time we went. Room was clean and a convenient size for 2 doubles- roll away bed fit fine. Refrigerator cold! AC cold!bathroom had a nice long vanity counter- plenty of towels! Did my homework and requested room away from the train side and Nicole accommodated us!! Court yard downstairs was a pleasant for being in a big city. Ordered take out wings from the Bistro and they rocked!! The little Deli prices were not that high at all!!! Doughnut 1.00 muffin 1.25.... All staff I greeted especially at the front desk and housekeeping , the bistro, pool, were friendly. I did not like the fact that it appeared the in room microwave was removed from atop the refridge and when we inquired were told it was 10 dollars to get a microwave brought to the room. Also did not like missing the Old Town Trolley shuttle pickup for our nighttime monument tour - paid 11.50 for 4 for a cab to Union Station. Realized the next day by happenstance that it picks up at hotel 6 st side and not at C as I would have expected. Overall pleased with my stay- I did my homework and was happy knowing about the hotel and area before I got there. For those reviews that seem to complain about the lack of food choices , well the metro is only a couple blocks away! Thanks for reading this lengthy review!

First of all, this was me and my family first trip to Washinton, DC. I feel that the location might be the best in the city. The cost is well worth it. The staff was very helpful. Something I liked was how a member of the bell staff(Darren) acted as our concierge, since the hotel doesnt have one. He recommended some good restaurants, printed directions, and even talked sports with me while I waited to be helped at the front desk. These things help put our family vacation over the top. Grade "A" Service!!!!!!

Just spent 2 nites here. Front desk & hotel staff excellent for info about the city. The tiny pool on the roof was stuffed with over 50 people. It was 4th of July weekend, so there was a large # of kids there. Over all an excellent location(2 short blocks to the park). I would stay here again.

review_title: Great if you have business nearby
review_text: If you happen to have business nearby this is a modern, clean hotel with friendly staff. I've only been here for business and I'm not sure if this would be a great location for a tourist. Certainly there is no "nightlife" nearby. Comfortable beds, good breakfast.

review_title: Clean rooms in a quaint setting with construction noise across the street
review_text:
Construction is going on across from the hotel which may be annoying to some people. However, we tried to be optimistic about it and viewed it as our wake up call each morning since we had to get up early to see the sights anyway.
Rooms are extremely clean and the bed was one of the most comfortable beds I've slept in. Drawers in the dresser were broken though and one almost fell on my feet when pulling it out to use it. I complained about this to the front desk and they never fixed it nor did they follow up with me to give me an explanation. 
Value on the hotel varies to which night you stay. One night I paid 315 while other nights went down to 119. Overall, it's a good place to stay if you are looking for a small quaint boutique style hotel away from the crowds.

The hotel is in an excellent location for visiting the smithsonian museums and the Capitol building. It's also a block away from a metro subway stop, L'Enfant Plaza, which has four lines I believe.
The staff are polite and efficient. The hotel has two restaurants, a Starbucks, and a deli of sorts. There's also a gift shop with some snacks, cigarettes, soda, etc.
The only criticism i have is the room needs a bit of refurbishment. The arms of the desk chair were worn out and small pieces would come off when you touched it. The wallpaper in the shower was a little rough.
Overall a good stay.
The hotel is 20 min walk to white house so location is good staff very friendly and helpful and the restaurant in hotel very good would go here again if in washinghton

Staff - Terrific A+
Location - Very Convenient
Room - Slightly disappointed. Smelled of cigarette smoke. Must have been a smoking room at one time. Bed was a little uncomfy too. All other aspects were excellent.

review_title: Great old hotel with a lot of character, large rooms, and friendly professional service.
review_text: This great old hotel has a lot of charm with big rooms that have a bar, living area, several windows with good views, and service that is excellent. Free wi-fi and free bottled water in the room are a nice bonus. The hotel is equidistant from two metro stations - approximately a 15 minute walk. They provide earplugs to avoid the city's noise but we found them unnecessary even on a Saturday night. We love this hotel and would return without question.

'Cramped' is a word that sums up this hotel. From the small recepion area, the tiny bar with a limited menu, to the very compact rooms.
I made the mistake of ordering breakfast to be delivered to my room, and this really influenced my view on this hotel. On Day 1, breakfast didnt arrive as the menu card was still hanging on my doorknob despite having Been placed there at 11 pm. The next morning breakfast arrived ( i had made a point of talking to the front desk beforehand) but although I was provided with a cup and a jug of milk, the coffee I ordered did not arrive. Third time lucky? Afraid not, on Day 3, the coffee arrived but without the croissant I had ordered?
Otherwise, I guess its an average hotel for DC. Does the hob but no more.
hotel_name: Renaissance Washington, DC Dupont Circle Hotel

review_title: Nice hotel and great stay downtown if you have kids with you
review_text: We were a little surprised that the website said nothing about the $30.00 a night valet parking charge. However the rooms were nice and we had a king suite meaning my husband and I could have a little privacy while my kids watched TV in the main living area and slept on the sofa bed which was comfortable. There was some noise in the atrium area and hallways which woke my son up. The free breakfast is amazing. So if you are in Denver and are traveling with children and want to be downtown where all the action is, stay here.
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Denver - Downtown / Convention Center

review_text:
My mom and I came to DC for a mother daughter vacation. We were hoping to relax and see all the sights. The trip has been a nightmare so far. Our first room was across from the service elevator and ice machine. The train tracks were right behind our room. The floor was also filled with children on a trip who shouted and slammed doors all night. Needless to say we did not sleep well. When I woke up in the morning I found dead bedbugs in my bed. When we informed the staff of this they moved our room but did not even apologize.
There is also not many restaurants nearby and the hotel food is very overpriced for the quality. 
We would switch hotels but apparently the room is nonrefundable and we spent a lot of money to stay here.

Hotel un Po vecchio ma di altissimo livello ... Stanze enormi .... Come delle suit ..... Le due cose (negative) bagno non modernissimo e distanza dalla dupont station stazione della metro 10 minuti a piedi, non e' tantissimo ma dopo una giornata intera a camminare avere l'hotel vicinissimo alla metro vuol dire !!! ..... Ciao a tutti Jacopo
Rooms and everything was nice but it is very noisy due to the outside AC so are you a light sleeper don't choose this hotel.
hotel_name: Renaissance Washington, DC Dupont Circle Hotel

review_text:
We used our Starwood points to book this hotel and chose it by the location. We stayed in the W times square several years ago and didn't really like that one so weren't expecting much. We were however delighted by what we saw upon arriving. Bright open spaces beautifully decorated. Very cool! Checking in we were early but were told our room would be ready in just about 30 min. It was suggested we go up to the bar area called "point of view". What a spectacular view it was. We were so excited to see the white house, Washington monument and many other sites. 
Room still not ready but Jeff compensated us with suite upgrade and bottle of champagne. He extremely helpful and attentive throughout our stay. Jon, the concierge was also very helpful with the resturant reccomendations and advice for getting around. Weekend got really busy with weddings and parties at POV. Thought we'd hear music blaring but even being on the 7th floor it was quiet. 
Several things I would like to see improved are bellman/doorman services. They don't have anyone helping with this. Had to flag down our own taxis. Not what I expected at the "W". 
Our dining experiences were hit and miss. One room service meal was excellent but most of the others were lukewarm and lacking. The Sunday brunch was terrible and over priced. Very disappointed!

review_title: I was so pleased with service.
review_text:
We spent five days in DC. Each time we came back to the hotel, we we're cheerfully greeted. Each time we needed anything, the staff immediately took care of it. The hotel restaurant was a little pricey, but excellent food. The doorman was a tremendous help with sightseeing.
there were a few drawback ks but definitely overshadowed by the wonderful service. The location was close to tranportation and for $10 the doorman can set you up with a very comfortable sedan ride to downtown DC.
I would stay at the Park Henley in an heartbeat.

review_title: I think I'm fairly hip, but not hip enough for this hotel.
review_text:
Stayed for 2 nights for business. It was LOUD. My room was on the 9th floor and while I couldn't hear the nightclub on the 11th floor, I think the guests in the room above mine were having their own nightclub in their room. Really? On a Tuesday night? 
Pluses: comfy bed, very clean, terrific restaurant, Bliss products, great shower, fabulous rooftop bar
Minuses: the noise (see above), fresh paint smell in my room, alarm clock that I didn't set woke me up and I struggled to figure out how to turn it off. 
So, even though there were more pluses than minuses, I can't overcome the noise issue. Maybe it's not hip, but I really value being able to get a good night's sleep in a hotel, especially when traveling for business.

review_title: Elegant, excellent customer service, excellent.complimentary breakfast, great place to stay!!
review_text: I was very impressed by the service and accommodations! My husband. and I were visiting from Chicago for a convention. The accommodations are striking, the customer service from everyone was the best I've ever experienced. The complimentary breakfast had an omelette station, fruit, danish, oatmeal, granola, cereals, toast and bagels, bacon, sausage, pancakes, scrambled eggs, french toast, yogurt, potatoes.....INCREDIBLE!!!!!!! Additionally, there is a complimentary reception every evening including unlimited cocktails/beer and snacks. The housekeeping service was excellent, taking care of our requests. We were there for 5 nights, and the excellent service remained constant throughout!! Also, GREAT location!!!!!!!
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Denver - Downtown / Convention Center

review_text: This is an excellent business hotel, centrally located in the dupont circle area and within walking distance to many attractions, restaurants, bars. The rooms are a bit boring, but impeccably clean and the service is great; breakfast buffet is overpriced and with limited choices; m brasserie has decent (and expensive) food- pleasantly surprised; there is also illy coffee shop serving excellent expresso; overall, a convenient chain business hotel, but a bit overpriced ( internet should be included when you pay 289 per night for a standard room) and lacking character.
hotel_name: Renaissance Washington, DC Dupont Circle Hotel

review_text: Unbelievable experience. My wife and I celebrated our anniversary at the W and had an amazing experience. The staff was fantastic. Cody with managment was extremely attentive to our questions and went above and beyond the call of duty. Cody helped make our anniversary the special day we had anticipated.

review_title: I have never taken the time out to do a review but....
review_text: I was nervous after reading reading the reviews here. But let me tell you there are a lot here that are wrong or was there.on.a off day. Yes the rooms are not super sized but well appointed. But what was worthy of my time to write this was the service we received from the time we walked in. We couldn't even go for a stroll without first being wished a pleasant stroll. The valet guys are awesome, and the gentleman who helped us to our room waited patiently while my husband searched for a another parking alternative. Who does that anymore with a smile??? This will be my only choice when visiting the area. Customer service wins here.
hotel_name: Renaissance Washington, DC Dupont Circle Hotel

review_title: Airline pilot review.. A must read..
review_text: The hotel itself is great! Wonderful rooms. Great location... The staff on the otherhand is much to be desired.. I have had two people now come into my room with the front desk thinking I am checked out at 9am.. And the housekeeping staff continuously coming in with the do not disturb sign on the door telling me I have checked out.. I talked to the manager and she dud not seem to really care as it took 20 minutes for her to call my room.. The rooms and facilities are great but I would recommend the hyatt instead.. I have stayed there as well and have experienced the same amenities with a much more experienced/seasoned staff for the same price as you would pay here. Very unprofessional.
hotel_name: Renaissance Washington, DC Dupont Circle Hotel

review_text: We had an amazing time here! When you're there, ask for Cody. He knows everything about DC and took care of everything for us.
Great location and I like the new design of this embassy suites hotel. We use this brand a lot and this is one of the best. Staff are still trying to impress and were very friendly. Will recommend.
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Denver - Downtown / Convention Center

review_text: We got a great rate on priceline. I was nervous do to the negative reviews and would never have booked otherwise. Well it was wonderful!! Great service, clean room, great location. King room a little small but so well laid out and great bed. No view and a little noisy since we looked out on the acs but still slept great for bed was so comfortable and we smelled great from the products.
hotel_name: Renaissance Washington, DC Dupont Circle Hotel

review_text: Great new embassy suites. Service staff excellent. Good food and happy hour.
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Denver - Downtown / Convention Center

review_text: Great location near where I was doing business. Friendly efficient staff. Disappointed having to pay for wifi in room and $7.50 for 15 minutes on Internet in business center seems excessive to me when needed to print from Internet email No coffee in room but available in lobby in morning. Recommend with limitation
Had a great time at the W! Great location, great staff, great bar! Morning coffee in the lobby was a huge bonus! There are so many great restaurants nearby...you'll love it here!!

review_text: O horÃ¡rio de check in Ã© muito tarde, as 15h. Mesmo assim, quando cheguei Ã s 15h 15min, meu quarto ainda nÃ£o estava pronto.
