hotel_name: Hyatt Regency Denver At Colorado Convention Center

review_title: Beautiful space in a modern new hotel.
review_text: This is a fantastic hotel that feels brand new. The rooms are decorated beautifully and are really spacious. Breakfast is cooked to order. They have a wonderful indoor pool area and a great gym. This is the place to stay on downtown Denver. We will be back!
hotel_name: Embassy Suites Denver - Downtown / Convention Center

review_title: Not a four or five star experience
review_text:
I was checking in as an spg gold member for an 8 day stay at the W. My wife and son was going to be joining me later for the fouth of July celebration so I had booked a room with two queen beds. I was offered an upgrade to a suite for an extra $150 which I said I would consider for when they were arriving.
The room I got was indeed with two queen beds and with the usual cool W layout, but not really clean (e.g. hairpins in the sofa, hairbands on the floor) and with a view to a wall maybe 10 yards away. Not what I expected for $600 plus taxes per night.
Then my family arrived and the upgrade was now $200 plus $30 for a roll away as there would only be a king bed in the upgraded room. I kindly declined the offer....
When I learned that my son would not be allowed on the hotel's roof top on the fourth (while my wife and I would be welcome for a fee of $250 per person) I decided to find another hotel in town.
JW Marriott just around the corner from the W is by my scale better value for money. Not cheap and of course not the hip boutique style decor, but we got a great room on the concierge level overlooking the Ellipse and the Washington monument. And that's for about half the price of the two queen bed room with a backyard view at the W.
The bar staff and the bellman at the W are nice and smiling folks for sure, but it does not make it up for such overpricing. Neither for business nor for leisure travel.

Stayed at the Grand Hyatt for two nights. Staff were pleasant and helpful. Room had a king size bed and still space for 2 comfy club chairs and table for a glass of wine before bed or reading the newspaper in the morning.

Location, location, location... Staff was amazingly friendly and helpful. Rooms clean, bed a bit lumpy, but comfy. Walls just a little on the thin side. Little noisy at night. Within walking distance to most sights in DC. Brealfast buffet a bit of a rip off at $20 adult $10 for kids. Learned the hard way. Great little deli in the hotel. $20 for breakfast for the 3 of us. Will stay again on next visit to DC

review_title: Convenient location, friendly staff, kid friendly and clean!
review_text: We stayed in The Washington Hilton for one night, and found it to be super clean, close enough to the DuPont Circle Metro(5 minutes downhill) with a very friendly and helpful staff. The room was clean, especially the bathroom! The kids loved it, so did we!

review_title: Club upstairs blares music until 2:30 am so don't stay there if you want to get any sleep.
review_text:
We stayed here after a wedding as a rare treat. The club music upstairs kept us up most of the night. When we complained they allowed us to switch rooms, and the hotel staff says this happens every weekend. For the prices they charge - worst experience. Have had much better luck at budget hotels. Will NOT be back.
And the see through showers - seriously?

review_title: Great for conferences, but shower at home
review_text: Good food for conferences, firm bed, but low flow shower heads and NO HOT WATER. Had to resort to taking showers at night. Pathetic, and I was on the alleged executive floor.

Stayed at the hotel initially for a conference held there but decided to stay on for a few extra days holiday and sightseeing. The room was small but very well decorated. The sheets had some marks and holes but it didn't really bother us. There is a long walk from the lifts so ask for a room nearer the lifts and on a high floor so you get the view. I would have preferred a room on the front to get the view of the monument etc but the view out of the back over the local houses was lovely if you like architecture.
The restaurant for breakfast is pricey but normal for DC and most of the staff are lovely. Our service at check-in was brusque but efficient but a colleague of mine had the best service ever - the lady even booked cinema tickets for us! 
The free wifi area in the lobby can get crowded and they play music too loud for you to concentrate and work but there is no wifi in the rooms. There is broadband in the rooms but on cable only and ridiculously expensive.
The one major issue was the service at check out. This took four gos and I expect it is still wrong. I needed to split the costs and admittedly it was a little complicated but the attendant wouldn't listen to me, dismissing my concerns that he had understood properly. Sure enough at final check out there was complete chaos to the point where we almost missed our shuttle to the airport!
I would stay here again as it is a great location but I would only go when there are special rates.

Last minute trip to DC and decided to check this hotel out. It was a short stay but the location was perfect and walking distance to many attractions and restaurants. The room was very clean and spacious. The bed was perfect I did not want to get up actually I wanted to take the bed with me. The Hyatt exceeded my expectations. I recommend this hotel.

Well situated and nice clean rooms. The gym is basic but there's some freeweights. Breakfast was very good too. It can get a bit noisy at night. Nightclubs and hotels don't generally mix well and here's the proof. Bar prices are too high and there's also no free wifi in rooms, just in the lobby. iPod docking station in rooms is nice touch. Staff very friendly.

I've stayed at a lot of hotels in my life time and let me tell you, for the price, this has been by far the best one. The price can't be beat at $99 a night. Yes u have to pay $35 a night for parking, but all hotels u do in Washington. The service was great. Asked for a top floor room and was put on the 11th floor in a hypoallergenic room (didn't ask for that so that was a plus). Hotel was close to everything (all within a mile or less walk). Metro was accessible from right under our hotel. The only thing I would have to complaine about is that they did not have Happy Hour on Saturdays during games (they block most of them in your room so that u have to go to the bar to watch them). Also if u need the Internet over their wi-fi, you will have to pay a pretty Penny, but that shouldn't be a deal breaker. All in all I would recommend this to anybody.

review_title: Large business hotel with efficient check in and out system
review_text: Short business trip. Room clean and comfortable if a bit dark and gloomy. Friendly and helpful staff.

Great stay very clean. I liked being in walking distance of everything. We were right around the corner from China town. Where there was plenty of resturants and stores for shopping. The walk to the museums and memorials is a little hike because they are so spread out. Pay to ride the double decker bus is great.
Stayed here for conference. Hotel nice but rooms small and average. Overpriced. Would pay $150 not $280

I stay there often in part because of how friendly and capable the front desk staff consistently is. Overall management keeps the hotel running and appearing well. Only catch is major fluctuation in the rates, precluding me staying there even mor regularly

I stayed there for 5 nights, for a conference. There was no wifi in the room! And in lobby the connection was so bad. I have Mac book air and iPad, so the only way I could connect to the Internet was wifi. I actually had no access to the Internet in the hotel and that was really annoying! 
Room service knocked the door everyday at 8:30! And let knocking till wake you up! That was also really annoying!
Compared to what you are charged, service is not acceptable.

review_title: Every aspect of a two night stay was miserable
review_text: I have never felt the need to write a review but our experience at the capital Hilton was so bad I am compelled to do so. My husband who is a Hilton honors member hosted a conference there this weekend for 20 people and was embarrassed by the treatment and service in all aspects.

The Washington Hilton is a decent hotel thats been recently updated. Double bed rooms are very small and housekeeping services is inconsistent. Hotel food is okay and this Hilton has plenty of conference room space for all your meeting and event needs. For the business/transient traveler it's in a great location with a rite aid at the corner, restaurants and the ever popular Adams Morgan party scene all in walking distance. It's located in the high end Dupont Circle area and nearby shopping.
I would return just because of the location alone.

Stayed for 4 nights while on business. My wife joined me and enjoyed the convenience of the location (walking distance to museums, shops, restaurants, subway, etc...)
Rooms were clean, staff were great and the buffet breakfast (made to order omellettes) and happy hour put it over the top!
Terrific value! Would stay there again and definitely will...

review_title: Great hotel, excellent staff, great nighttime bar!
review_text: I love this hotel! I stay here every year when I attending the AUSA conference in Washington DC. I suggest you come here than anywhere else.
The hotel really made my stay enjoyable and relaxed. I will be back soon. This is truly a great hotel in a great location of Washington, DC!

Attended. 200 person conference here for two days in October 2011. Very good location for NW side of DC. In heart of business district. Lots of good places within walking distance. Nice facilities. Very large room with large sitting area. Small
Bathroom. Small kitchen. I had a regular room booked so u don't know if they are all large like this or if u was upgraded and not told but room was huge and very nice. Many 
Meeting rooms makes for great place for smaller conferences. Pricey rooms and food but that's DC.

review_title: Lovely hotel in good location. Small rooms, quite expensive.
review_text: My family and I stayed at the Washington Hilton for several nights. It is lovely and in a safe, accessible neighborhood. The Metro is only a few blocks away. A cab ride to The Mall is about $17. I was put off by a few things, thought. We chose to upgrade to the Executive floor (top floor) to have the breakfast and snacks available to the family. In total, the room was about $400 per night. The room was very small, the 2 double beds took up nearly a the space. Interestingly, they advertise that the beds are queen sized, but are definitely not. when I called the front desk to ask about the size, they initially said that they were queens, but eventually conceded that they were smaller than a "traditional queen". The bathroom was also small, but fully functional. I guess I just expected a liitle more space for the cost of the room. The linens were nice, service very good, hotel lovely, and I guess the size of the room and beds are my only complaint. No recycling containers, either. One other expense that I thought extreme was overnight parking @ $37 per night.

review_title: Good hotel but you need to hail own taxi
review_text:
Very spacious rooms and nice american breakfast (not for vegetarians). white house is within walking distance. Everything else is reachable by metro.
Only down is the taxi system outside the hotel is totally chaos, and nobody from the hotel seems to care. Be prepared to hail own taxi in the street.

Fab hotel and duping circle nearby which has nice restaurants/atmosphere. We spoke to the chap on the 'tours' desk on our afternoon of arrival to enquire about hop on hop off buses etc. They must have a deal with grayline and so we were sold 48hr tickets for that company. We were told buses came every 20-30 mins - this is not so!!!! Unfortunately we only had 2 full days in Washington and therefore waiting almost an hour both mornings for the bus, we wasted much time. The bus doesn't seem to have a schedule and turns up at the hotel sporadically! The second day we gave up waiting after 50mins and went for the metro instead. 
Being English, we like tea! It was great that there was a drinks machine in the room - we had 1 tea bag on arrival (lots of coffee). When we asked for a couple more tea bags on our second day we had a very rude response and were told we would have to pay!
Final note re service, on check out (when we needed to head into town for our train) service was slow and we got the impression the staff were ignoring the queue of guests and not even attempting to speed things up/apologise for the long wait etc.
It does sound as though I'm moaning, I don't usually write reviews etc but found them useful when organising our USA trip.
This is a fab spacious clean hotel, just requires a little better service - especially for Hilton!

We had a nice big corner room on the 5th floor. The down side of that was the noise from traffic all night. The room also had a musty smell like wet towels. Big living space, good closet space but very small but adequate bathroom. Overall, fine but not wonderful.

Loved the service there especially from the front desk when I was checking in. I had great service from everybody and love the fact that there was a Starbucks right inside the lobby. I really appreciate Aris for valleting my car even though the garage was full and for his great service. Looking forward to coming back this year.

review_title: Good location, not so good room!
review_text: I came here for a one night stay and I must say the location was pretty convenient. We walked to the Verizon center. Unfortunately the room stunk of ciggarette smoke and completely turned me off. I called the front desk and asked if I was mistakenly put in a smoking room. I was told no and was also told there were no available rooms to move me to. The stench was so strong I had to sleep with the windows open. I got a deal on hotwire for the room for 90 dollars and wouldn't pay a cent more to stay here. Also be aware that parking will run you $42 a night!

review_title: Great hotel, great location, great stay
review_text: Stayed for two nights to explore D.C. and got a good deal through a travel website. This hotel is in an excellent location, you can literally see the White House once you leave the front entrance. Staff was very polite. Our room was huge and very clean. The only con is that they don' t have a parking lot and valet parking is $42 a day. However, there are several spots around for self parking that are not cheep but ways cheeper than valet parking. Would definitly stay here again!

We stayed here for the Labor Day weekend. The hotel is pretty nice. Rooms are the usual big size split in to living room and bedroom. 
Breakfast was good with a wide selection, but weirdly there was no bacon! Very disappointing. 
Worst aspect of our stay was the pool. It was infested (and I use that word on purpose) with children. We were not able to enjoy the pool at all, and that had been one of the reasons we'd chosen the hotel in the first place. The hotel should instigate adults only times. There is also an evening managers cocktail hour where you can get one drink on the house. A nice idea in theory, but the reality was a queue of 25 sorry looking people all lined up waiting for a freebie - not in the least bit glamorous! To make it even more naff they do not hold this event in the restaurant or bar area, but in the atrium that mainly serves as the breakfast area. We only took part one evening. It wasn't our cup of tea.

review_title: Overnight stay at the WP for business
review_text: Arrived in the pouring rain via a credit cardless DC cabbie (remember to carry cash!), probably about 30 minute drive from Reagan airport. Check in staff friendly and efficient. Foyer not inspiring but the place seems as though it has undergone a recent refurbish in 21Century chain decoration. When I arrived in my room it was really hot and I ended up turning off the heating because the room didn't cool when the AC was dropped to the low 60's. Weird arrangement with the bathroom where they have partitioned the bath and toilet by subdividing the old bathroom and the basin is in the room 'outside'. Water didnt drain from the bath at the rate the shower was filling it. Room was neat an modern and for once a hotel got it right with FREE Internet and 2 bottle of water, none of the $5/bottle gouging!

We were so pleased with our stay at this hotel. The suites are perfect for a family and they are well maintained and clean. The evening 'manager reception' is a wonderful way for both adults and children to have a good time. And, the hotel amenities, especially the pool, are a plus. I would absolutely stay at this hotel again. It is a great value!!

I stayed here for two nights over Labor Day weekend. I consider myself a tough customer as I travel a lot, more and more to the DC area. The Washington Hilton surprised me with outstanding service and and one of the best stays I have ever had within the Hilton family of properties.
Upon check-in I was acknowledged as a gold member and upgraded to the 10th floor executive floor. This allowed access to the lounge each day for complimentary continental breakfast, dinner time snacks, and free nonalcoholic drinks. Also had a private bar.
The room was terrific and bed very comfortable. I had an issue my first night with water noises and Zack at the desk immediately offered to move me once security checked it out. No hassles at all and done very professionally and politely.
I had occasion to eat at The District Line (TDL) twice during the stay. Sunday night dinner on the beautiful terrace, and Monday morning. Both meals were very good! Be warned it gets breezy on the terrace!
For such a historic hotel....I was amazed the rooms were so modern. Elevators were great and all of the staff really were wonderful!
My only recommendation is to install wi-fi on the guest floors. In today's age of iPhones, iPads, and others a wired connection doesn't always work. I was pleased to find complimentary wifi in the lobby and Executive Lounge.
As for location it was in the DuPont Circle area about 4 blocks from the metro. I walked most of the trip but had no issues getting a cab at the front door twice.
Do some research on this place, it's home to the Correspondents Dinner, National Prayer Breakfast, and hosted all Presidents of recent history. It's also the site of Hinkley's assassaination attempt on President Reagan in 1981. It was eerie to be standing on the same patch of driveway!
I will DEFINITELY be returning to this location!! Thanks for a great stay!!!
I stayed at this hotel for business and it was so easy to play after work. The White House, Washington Monument, Smithsonian, Dupont Circle, and Capital are all within walking distance.
The hotel was very clean, comfortable and I felt safe while staying there. It had a good location and was easy to find.

review_title: Nice hotel in a safe neighbourhood.
review_text: I stayed in this hotel 2 years in a row. I like the location, the olympic seize pool and the safe neighbourhood. But.... Be advised that It can be very noisy here. Last time we stayed there was a congres and these people liked to talk very loud, also after midnight. Even when they got ice from the icemachine at 02:00 they were screaming to friends who were in the room....

review_title: One of the best hotels I have stayed in
review_text:
First to
Mr Eversley J. Lewis
In-Room Dining Captain
We Love You
VIP rooms
Hotel
Staff
Everything 
Fabulous!!!!
Nicole Smith, Pamela Prince & Jessica
Westchester County, New York

Stayed here Labor Day weekend. Nice hotel and easy to get to. There are parking garages that are cheaper than the hotel valet ($42) but good luck getting in to them. The rooms were nice and beds comfortable..... for the price booking directly through Hilton.com it couldn't be beat! Close to Washington Monument and the White House.... not to far from there are the Smithsonian museums. Nationals park is 3.5 miles from the hotel so its best to drive.
There are Starbucks on every corner and a subway. Many upscale restaurants close.. so if looking for something cheap Subway is about it. A mile away is Hard Rock Cafe. There is also a CVS right around the corner.
Overall would stay at this hotel again....

The staff at the reception were surly and unhelpful. While the rooms are spacious, they are humid and malodorous. The entrance is under repair but there are no bellmen to offer help even during a rainy day.

Since Washington is an eminently walkable city (weather permitting), the West End is an ideal location. You can walk to the multiple organizations around Pennsylvannia Ave., companies on K str and Connecticut Av. You can also walk to restaurants in Georgetown and the Du Pont area. And if you go further away, the Foggy Bottom Metro station is a 5 minute walk away. No need to suffer Washington taxis. If you are a runner, you have easy access to the National Mall, Rock Creek Park and the C&O Canal towpath. Unbeatable!
The Embassy Suites format has it's own advantages, if you don't HAVE to stay in a big-name hotel. Rates are lower, and you get a suite, including a good size desk, handy if you need to work at the hotel. There is a good breakfast buffet, and a good gym as well.
So, why not 5 stars? That's for perfection, and there are some shortfalls at this hotel. In my experience, staff were inconsistent. From a friendly "Welcome, Mr ..." to an attitude of "the answer is no, so what's your question?". My room, in spite of being non-smoking had been smoked in, and you have to crawl under the desk for access to the electric outlets. As often happens, that last bit to reach perfection is difficult.
The bottom line: It's a good option for business trips to Washington DC.
Perfect spot. You can easily walk to every spot. Hotel is clean and updated with REAL high speed Internet. The only thing I'd complain about is the noise made by the air condition in the room.
Close to everything. Very good service and clean. Resturant neebs more choises

Centrally located between Chinatown and the white house this hotel is the best place to stay. Very clean and well kept. Easy to get to by foot, car or metro. The metro center has an exit leading to the hotel. Multiple places to eat in the hotel and large room service menu.

Stayed at this hotel last weekend with my husband and three children. Loved the two room suite with two queen beds - very spacious! The happy hour was wonderful after a day of sightseeing and before going to dinner. Every night they changed the snack which we all enjoyed - fresh veggies and dip, pretzels and chips and salsa and cheese another. The breakfast was a amazing - crowded I have to admit but not to the point of being unbearable. There was a great variety of food and plenty of seating available. The service at this hotel was incredible and I would net hesitate to stay again. The metro was about a 5 minute walk but we found that the amount that we paid for the metro down to the attraction area was the same amount we paid for a cab so after the first day we took a cab. Loved our trip to DC and Embassy Suites was a major factor.

Paid the price I thought was very Reasonable and in a cool location. Yes lots of traffic In the area but that's part of the experience. Also not sure but I might have paid for parking which is dumb if so but otherwise was a perfect place

We were here in aug and stayed a couple nights. Hard location with a 2 year old but any place would be. Koi feeding was great. Most of the tips from Kevin were square on. Go to the concierge and get his quick tutorial. The cab across town was quick to my conference and the zoo was a quick drive. The front page restaurant wasn't really kid friendly, while they did have a kids menu we had to ask for it. We have an 8 and a 2 yr old. Breakfast and free drinks were great but there are a lot of stairs. Rooms were nice and clean. Great visit.

This hotel is conveniently located near the White House and major attractions. My room was rather small, but clean and comfortable; while housekeepking was diligent in keeping my room nice and clean. Best of all, no bedbugs!!!!
Clean and new, stylish and cozy! Good service. Good restaurant.

Heavy smoke smell in nonsmoking room thru ventilation system ruined our short stay.
Room is small. Remodeled bathroom okay.
Safe in room.
Would not choose to stay here again.

We recently stayed @ the Washington Plaza and LOVED it! The hotel staff was top notch! The room and roomy bathroom was attractive and modern. The weekend breakfast Buffet was a steal @ $15 coffee and juice included with custom omelets too! Great location as well and lovely pool. We can't wait to go again!

review_title: Very nice hotel with great location.
review_text:
The hotel is very very nice. It has a beautiful pool. Food was very tasty. It is walking distance to all of the sites in D.C.
The price was high but I guess that goes with the location. We were allowed to leave our car there while we toured on our day of departure. That save us parking & searching for a place to park. Would stay there again.

review_title: Good location near the White House and other attractions.
review_text: The room was comfortable but was on the small side. Staff were friendly and helpful; the restaurant was good and service very good - the duck especially. Be aware that room prices vary greatly in DC depending on which day of the week you stay. Weekends are best price but Sunday is more expensive. Good location in relation to the map etc although some might say it is too far to walk. We are walkers!
Very nice staff. Great breakfast. Great rooms and love the Managers reception.

review_title: Beautiful Historic Hotel with a 21st Century Touch!
review_text:
I stayed here during a US Department of Education conference and paid the government rate of $183 per night. 
The hotel was absolutely beautiful. I liked that each room was just a little different in its layout and design. It gave it character. The bar was lovely. Dark wood panelling lined the walls. A very classic, rich look. 
I only had one breakfast at the restaurant. It was a $20 buffet with fresh fruit, made to order omlets, meats, etc. 
There IS free wifi if you sign up for their select guest loyalty program. That also gets you a free beverage delivered each morning: coffee, juice, tea, etc. they so have in room coffee makers. 
Across the street is a great little restaurant called Open City. Give it a try!

review_title: Dated hotel in a great area
review_text: This hotel looks like it's stuck in the 80s and never been renovated. I got a double room on expedia just for myself and I immediately noticed a musty smell in the hallways and in my room. The room itself was tiny and the bathroom so small the door barely closes. I noticed a lack of attention to detail in the cleanliness. Would say skip this place unless your company is paying for it and you have a nightly cap!

review_title: You can see the White House
review_text: Walk out of the front door look to your left... White House & Washington Monument! So happy with the location. The room was nice. Staff was helpful with directions & recommendations. I hope to return soon.

Nothing terribly wrong, just not great. Lot's of other choices at similar price.
Room on arrival smelled like a gym locker room. To their credit manager on duty upgraded us to a suite immediately. 
Lobby bar service was quite good, housekeeping adequate. Executive Level breakfast lounge was poorly serviced and dirty all 4 days of our stay.
Overall the hotel just seems a little tired, not up to Hilton's typically higher standards.

review_title: Loved it! Very surprised for my last minute weekend getaway!
review_text:
Stayed here for a quick very last minute weekend rendezvous and the hotel was perfect. The room was beautiful and spacious for the two of us, and very clean. Ismail at the Front Desk was very helpful! 
The parking structure was a little confusing, but pay close attention and you'll be fine. It is >$30 a night so plan when you're figuring out your cost.
The location was convenient and we enjoyed the closeness to eveything. I will be back!!

review_title: Excelent location, best friend of White House and ambassie's avenue
review_text: You can do everything on foot or taking the metro. All things will be easy because the location is the best. And if you visited DC on summer, even the swimming pool you can enjoy. The room is ok, with a LCD TV, and the gym center was quite good. It's a big hotel, with large halls, but not crownded. The front desk should be more careful with foreigns, because I had problems with deliveries and attendance. Istead of this, go through, it's a priceless place ;)

Stayed early July. 2 adults and a teen. The hotel was lovely with everything you need well taken care of. Very friendly servers at the delicious breakfast buffet. Happy to poach an egg on request. Easy walk from the hotel to The White House and we then walked to The Lincoln Memorial through WWII and Vietnam Memorials. Took a cab back, very reasonable. Can't wait to go back to explore more.

review_title: Gorgeous modern hotel in great location!
review_text: We stayed here in august after getting a $99 deal through expedia. The hotel was well worth it - beautiful luxurious modern room with a lovely bed and bathroom. It is a very large hotel in a safe area of the city, close to lots of restaurants and bars (and a really great Wholefoods!). The staff are lovely. The rooms may be a little small, but we barely were there other than to sleep. We easily walked to the White House. Nothing bad to say!

review_title: Elegant spacious old time Washington DC
review_text:
Elegant old fashioned hotel with outstanding service. Our room was spacious and well appointed. The bed was outstanding.
The only problem was a slightly musty smell. Also the hotel doesn't have tea or coffee in the room. You have to buy tea and coffee at the Starbuck's in the lobby

review_title: A memorable experience with a staff who is willing to help!! :)
review_text: I want to Thank this hotel for a experience that will last a lifetime. The hotel staff is exactly what I would expect out of a hotel in a city like D.C.! I stayed at this hotel for a conference and had workshops all day and got in my room with my friends later in the evening about 12:00. I was ready for bed, But there was an issue with our room. I called the front desk and explained the issue. They connected me to the manager right away and I explained it again. He was very kind and courteous and sent a very kind fellow to help us move our luggage from our room in what I guess is the new part of the building to the older main building. The manager moved us from the newer part and up to the top floor of the main building where the rooms are much more Spacious and I believe are cleaner. Thank You to the manager, and kind staff for making my stay at the Omni a memorable one.! I hope to come back. I love to travel and this hotel is at the top of my list.! It's a little pricy but is very worth it.!.! God Bless.

review_title: Clean, large, budget friendly, and good location for you DC stay.
review_text:
My entire family stayed here the first weekend in November 2011 to attend a graduation. Hotel room was very large with a full kitchen and changing room. Hotel is in walking distance to the mall which was awesome. We arrived early with our luggage and was able to store our belongings until check-in at 3pm. Only draw backs were the lack of restaurants close by, some outlets didn't work, and a slightly musty smell in the room initially. My parents had a microwave and we did not. Also I needed 2 double beds and they charged extra but my parents only reserved a single for $20 less a night and ended up getting a double for the price of a single. I felt a little cheated when I knew what they got for cheaper. My parents drove and they had to pay $36 per night for parking which was a bit extreme.
All in all I would stay at this hotel again. It was in a nice quiet area but still close to the momuments, clean, classy, all for budget prices. Had a great weekend staying there!

The room is like a SUITE FOR A KING. the service is excellent. the price is not so expensive (i paid 119$ a night) there's a very nice swimming pool, a gym, internet everywhere, restaurant, bar, there are also some computers if you need to print something (i had to print my boarding pass for my flight). the only problem that i can found is that you have to walk for 10 minutes to get to the first subway station..but is not so much!
I'm from italy and unfortunally I stayed there for only tree night.
Stayed for two nights and had a package that included breakfast which included about every typeof breakfast food I can think of and more! Also enjoyed the self check in and check out facilities.

review_title: Don't stay here unless you are quiet as a mouse and leave at dawn!
review_text: Check in was ok except that we booked two doubles and ended up with a queen. A quick trip back to the front desk solved that. The room we ended up with was ok, nothing fancy. We had a few friends that also had a room at the hotel so we ended up in one room just chatting and listening to some music at a reasonable volume around 5 pm. Not even 15 minutes later security came up to tell us that there was a noise complaint. We left the room and went on with our plans for the night. The next morning we received a phone call around 10am from housekeeping asking when we were going to check out so they could clean the room. Check out isn't even until 11. Needless to say we won't be staying here again.

review_title: Single mom with 11 year old son love DC!
review_text: The outdoor pool was fabulous! Very refreshing after touring the sites and museums all day. Pool staff was very friendly and courteous. Rooms were clean and our room had a view of the pool. Closest metro is .3 miles away. Bring your walking shoes! Make sure you have a safe in your room because some of the rooms don't have them. Complimentary bottled water each evening was great too. I got a king superior room for 129$ a night so for location, amenities and value, I think this place is great. Next door is the Donovan House that has a rooftop pool and loud music. Bring earplugs if you are a light sleeper - Thomas circle had lots of traffic 24/7!

review_title: Very good service, convenient location, at a reasonable family rate.
review_text: We were looking for a room for a family of 4 and found a great deal on the Beacon's website that included parking. Room on 6th floor with small kitchen was fine for a short family stay. Staff was responsive and courteous. You can find jazzier and more updated hotels, but the quality and service were better than expected for this price in D.C.

review_title: Perfect but swimingpool has too much chemicals
review_text: Nice hotel in good location. Staff is helpful and prices are acceptable. Unfortunately beautiful swimming pool has too much chemicals! Almost poisoning. Coninctivitis you will get for sure. I would come back here for sure but never yse the pool again
Travelling from New York we found this hotel absolutely perfect. Swimmingpool, good air condition and very good space in our rooms and a very good restaurant.

The location is great, and the pool area is nice. There is a lifeguard on duty during the day. I only have 3 complaints:
1. Sheets are not soft
2. Room cleaning was not thorough during my week stay-dirty dishes left in room and bed was not fully made each day.
3. Very noisy at night if you are in a room facing Thomas Cir and pool. There are parties and entertainment at the pool bar, and outdoor cooridor access adds to the noise.

review_title: The large atrium amplifies noise tremendously. I felt as if my room opened out to a noisy train station. Check-in was slow, exp
review_text: The large atrium in the hotel amplifies noise tremendously. I felt as if my room opened out to a noisy train station. Check-in was slow, express check-in was nonfunctional, room service took forever. The rooms are not easy to access if you're not close to the elevators because the halls stretch on forever.
There is construction going on next door which makes for early wake up. Easy access to Metro and good location. Spacious rooms which are great for kids.

review_title: Well worn hotel, service leaves much to be desired
review_text: This hotel is well worn and in major need of renovation. Carpet inside and out of the room is filthy and in poor repair. Breakfast was a mob scene with no control or direction from staff. Kids enjoyed feeding the fish. No assistance with food allergies. The front desk staff was awful. Lomg walk to the closest metro. No one ever answered the phone, barely smiled, and everything I asked seemed as through I was bothering them. As a top tier Hilton honors guest, I was horribly disappointed.

Stay here one night to go the nationals game, hotel in very good neighborhood away from down town but it suit us best. Hotel lobby look very grand, 2 double bed room is very roommy had a parkview wing, farest from the lobby. 37 inch TV, mini fridge,2 free bottle of water. Bed is very comfortable wifi in the lobby, no self park. Velvet for 33 dollars a night. I sign up for their loyalty program, got a free inroom Internet and free beverage in the morning, milk and cookie and backpack for kid, Wolfgang puck coffee and tazo tea in room 
The not so good
Bathroom show wear and tear but no mold, wall is. Dry thin I can hear next door conversation.

review_title: Broken thermostats in all rooms and poor house keeping!
review_text:
I have stayed at the Washington Hilton a few times before The time I thought I just had a room where the a/c doesn't kick in so they gave me a new room but the other room had the same problem! Every time I have stayed here the thermostat goes up and then goes down giving you sweats and for a second you're cool throughout the night it tends to be very uncomfortable! I thought maybe it's just me.. maybe I don't know how to work it so I called for help and waited for an hour (probably bc the elevator is close to a half a mile from the room!) he came in, fiddled with it, and left not a changing a thing! It is most uncomfortable when the temperature in your room is blowing out heat when it is 81 degrees outside and all you want to do is come into a cool room. 
I didn't receive room service the first day so I also gave that the benefit of the doubt thinking that I may have left too late out of the room but the next day I didn't receive room service either so I called it in and they said they ll take care of it but when I came back to the room the room looked like just the bed was made and sloppy at that! The used coffee bag was still in the coffee machine and no toiletries were replaced in the bathroom and the towels were still wet and on the floor! the garbage was still on the table! This is not my idea of staying at a "Hilton" hotel! What happened to comfort and luxury? I'm really surprised that the company is not on top of this and I just warn you that you will deal with this if you stay here! Its definitely annoying!
What an awful experience!

The location is very convenient. Less than a mile walk to most Smithsonian museums and not much further to the White House, Capitol etc. There are also many restaurants in the area that you can walk to and it is only a few blocks from the Verizon center. The only down side was that our room was right on K street but it was on the 8th floor and the street noise was still very, very loud at night. Couldn't beat the price though, it was $80 per night between Christmas and New Years. I would just suggest an inside facing room to avoid the noise.

review_title: Beautiful and covienient location but small rooms.
review_text: The Beacon Hotel is located just blocks away from many fantastic sights in DC. Rooms are clean but very small! Was here in fall and wonder if it would be cold in the room due to all the windows. Resturaunt is okay but very over priced!

The location of the beacon hotel is hard to beat. Convenient to the Mall and monuments, Georgetown, Adams Morgan, etc. Staff is friendly and helpful. Hotel bar has great happy hour food and drink specials. Sky bar is also fun for a great view of the city. 
Downside is that the nearest metro is in Farragut square, about 5-6 blocks away. Also I was there during a season change. Two days were in the 70s, two were in the 50s. When I inquired about our 65 degree room, I found out the building's heat was on standby. The staff sent up the last space heater, which I was too paranoid to leave on over night. Not a huge deal but an inconvenience.

review_title: It's was the epitome of average
review_text: Overall this hotel was ok. Being on the circle was difficult for walking with a group of children. It was clean but not overally so. The room was nice space wise but I'm a bit spoiled with having not to ask for enough towels for each member of our family and basic toiletries. We arrived around 6:30pm and had to wait 20 min for valet service. I went to check us in while my husband waited. My six yr old , eight yr old and infant were waiting patiently on line until they took three people ahead of us!! I mean really I was standing in plain sight. 30 min after arriving we were checked in and wanting food and there were very few options that didn't involve an hour wait. Its ok if you need space for not much money but I won't be staying again.

review_title: Second time there - will go back again
review_text: Service really good. Near to metro. Has everything you need. Sign up for free stuff with select guest programme.

review_title: Not what I'm used to for a Marriott
review_text: We stayed here both for business and pleasure for 5 nights. The lobby has lots of comfy places to hang out, which is good because it's the only place you can get free wifi in the hotel, otherwise it's $12.95 a day! The rooms are average with basic fixtures and decor. The bed was comfortable and we had plenty of pillows of many shapes and sizes. Water pressure was also good, however the toilet was always running slightly, which caused some noise at night. Speaking of noise there were several nights where we were woken up by people yelling in the hall. After the second night we complained, they told us we'd have a free night. Very nice and unexpected, since we were able to sleep the majority of the night. Although, we did have to remind them on checkout that they'd offered it. The gym however is great with lots of updated equipment, an endless pool, sauna and steam room! By far one of the best I've seen offered at no charge. Service was good for the most part but there were quirky breakdowns. For example, the last day when we were leaving I went to fill up my 12 oz water bottle with some water they had in canisters with lemon and limes in it (nice touch). Then one of the staff came over to stop me and said I could only use the plastic cups, and the water was not meant to take with you. Really! I spend 5 nights and can't have 12oz of water? It wasn't a terrible place and the location for business is great. But I won't stay here again.

We agree with all that we have read. Start of our two location hol to USA. So much to see. Try the diner on the corner for breakfast. Lots of restaurants in area - weird Italian with Indian waiters. Hotel a.c. was noisy but always looked forward to going back to hotel. Definitely sign up for select guest morning tea was great as was choice of room an upgrade. We has huge corner room an only paid Â£70 per night for the room great value. Use the hop on hop off bus an spans some time in Georgetown.

I stayed here for a short business trip. I selected this location because of reputation (stellar), proximity to Metro (station at end of block), and price (good deal for this historic property). The staff provided outstanding service, as one might expect. After a long flight and metro ride from Reagan National, I was greeted and checked-in within 5 minutes. There is free printing of boarding passes in the business center in the lobby. The fitness center is huge; there are ~10 treadmills so no waiting even at peak times, exercise bikes, weights, complimentary earbuds in case one forgets to pack those, etc. My room was a corner room with a great view, and it was very clean. Bathroom space is tight, but I expected as much in a historic property. Overall, excellent accommodations in DC!
hotel_name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel

review_title: Fantastic hotel, great location, highly recommended!
review_text: Stayed here two nights in August. Location is perfect for walking to all monuments, white house etc. Safe area, friendly helpful staff. Spotless room with it's own separate kitchen! The only thing that sorta stinks is 30.00 per day parking (valet) but they do not charge the day of checkout. I would stay here again in a heartbeat! CVS right next door for snacks, drinks etc. An excellent value and super clean place. The location is absolutely perfect for walking to all attractions and not worrying about parking or traffic. I will stay here again on our next trip!

We were booked for hotel Capitol hill but due to some goof up we were rebooked for homewood suites by expedia at the 11th hour. But all is well that ends well, for an expensive city this hotel is value for money, rooms are well equipped a nice kitchenette two tvs, u get to see what u want, good toiletries and good evening spread with beer n wine, bf is good too and at an affordable rate

We stayed at the Washington Hilton while it was being renovated and as a result got a very good rate for our room. The renovations were not invasive and the staff were helpful. We had breakfast in the hotel one morning which was quite expensive but very nice. The rooms were clean and comfortable. The hotel was about a 10 minute walk from the nearest underground station which was cheap and easy to use. We also explored other districts nearby such as Adams Morgan where we ate in a great pub with live music called Madams Organ.

Instayed here for a conference. Even so there is plenty of connection for tourism. Near Chinatown, there are plenty of restaurants near by, as well as shopping if you need an extra this or that. The Gallery Place metro is very close, and right outside the front of hotel is the circulator bus which will take riders straight to The Mall, or Georgetown, and points in between. Tip: the metro is fast but the circulator is more scenic. Plus, the metro doesn't go directly to The Mall and Constitution Ave, whereas the Circulator does.

review_title: A Grand Hotel in a Surprisingly Good Location
review_text: When we first arrived here we were slightly concerned at how far from the centre of DC we were, however on walking to the Metro (2mins) it only took a few stops to find ourselves in the centre. The hotel and room were very spacious and comfortable with a great dining room. The additional use of the pool was also nice, considering the heat in DC in August.

Went to DC for our 5 yr wedding anniversary. The plaza was an excellent choice for our stay. We were upgraded upon arrival without us asking - even though I did and was informed it had already been taken care of. We were allowed to check in 3hrs early, and given a courtesy call within 15 minutes of arrival asking if the room was suitable. The room, bed and linens were extremely comfortable. We were even delivered bottled water without our request. 
It is a short walk to National Mall, Metro, Chinatown etc... 
The staff was very helpful, attentive, and friendly. The staff at the plaza paid attention to the small details that made the stay wonderful and a trip I wont ever forget.
I've stayed in many hotels and for the value the plaza is #1 on my list.
Great location for sights In Washington. Tourbus Pick-up right outside hotel. Not a kids hotel
hotel_name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel

review_title: Lovely hotel close to the tourist sughrs
review_text: Great hotel located within easy walking to the whitehouse, washinton monument, Lincoln memorial & GW university, as well as a metro stop close by. Staff were helpful & the room was very nice & also had a kitchen. Only complaint was wifi only available in the lobby.
Good location, able to walk to all main sights and museums. Clean room, comfortable bed

review_title: Great location and price- close to everything and staff was very friendly!
review_text:
We stayed two nights at the plaza to do some sightseeing and visit friends. The McPhearson metro stop was only a few minutes away which made getting to the cherry blossoms a breeze! We also too the metro to Arlington- 10 minute trip! 
Overall location-great, price-great, rooms- good but small and no fan in the bathroom (?!)

O unico defeito eh que o hotel eh Mais ou menos bem localizado...da par fazer tudo a pe mas cans um pouch mesmo pq Washington eh tudo muito espalhado. Para o meu gosto esse hotel vale muito a Pena...naotenho nenhuma reclamacao os quartos Sao execelentes .....

review_title: Very grand - but think about whether it's worth it!
review_text: This was an expensive hotel! But it didn't feel like we were getting much for the price. Breakfast was not included, they were stingy with toiletries and the in room coffee was terrible. But the hotel itself is stunning, so if that's important, go for it!
hotel_name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel

review_text:
L'hotel Ã¨ situato in posizione davvero startegica, sia per i viaggiatori business (vicinissimo a tutti gli uffici governativi) che per i turisti (a pochi minuti a piedi da tutti i principali monumenti). Le camere sono decorose ma rispetto al prezzo di scarsa qualitÃ . Colazione costosa e mediocre, altrimenti potrete farvi un fast breakfast presso la caffetteria situata nella hall.
Strategico ma nella zona ci sono molti altri hotel che a prezzo minore offrono di piÃ¹.

I do quite a bit of travelling and I must say this is the most friendless helpful staff I have ever encountered, especially Nicole!!
The bathroom tub tile did have some mildew, but I am being picky. I would recommend this hotel!! In fact, going back in a month.

Wow, a word not powerful enough for my stay. 1st class all the way. Kudos to the staff for an unbelievable stay. Spent some great nights in dc thanks to some unbelievable recommendations. Management was ready to help at anytime. Thanks.

Where to begin...first they advertise they have air conditioning but this is seasonal. I was told to open a window. So you can throw out the temperature control they also say they have. The room door is gaped at the bottom, so between the that and the paper thin walls I could hear everything through the nite. My TV had basic cable but the signal on higher channels was very snowy, suggesting bad cabling or signal strength. The room itself had very little decor or atmosphere and smelled like my old biology lab. I choose this hotel because it was very cheap compared to others in the area, there is a reason why. They also tried to charge me for my room key. Steer clear of this place at all cost.

review_title: Beautiful hotel in the heart of Downtown DC
review_text: This hotels offers everything. Location, service, bar scene, meeting space and great accomodations. The staff is so helpful. They will help you find anything you need. Great hotel to stay in while visiting Washington, DC. There are tons of restaurants nearby as well as tourist sites.

We spent four days here. Nice room, comfortable and quiet. However, we noticed torn sheets that don't stay in place and need replacing. Pillows that are small and uncomfortable. These small points are expected at lesser hotels---not historic, iconic properties such as this with a four star rating.
We noticed dirty baseboards throughout. Unacceptable to Marriott's usual high standards
The location can't be beat. Easy access to museums and restaurants. And a very accomodating staff. Kendra and Derek were especially helpful.
hotel_name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel

review_text: The location, ambiance and rooms are good. Little bit old, but goood place to stay. Room window seals had empty water bottles that had not been picked up. You need to use vallet parking or facility nearby.
hotel_name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel

review_text:
We recently had a great stay at the Omni Shoreham. There were 6 people in our group, using 3 rooms in total. The hotel was clean and pleasant and the staff were friendly and helpful. Our room, which was quite near the elevators, was quiet due to the room layout, which included a small hallway. Unfortunately we experienced a little of hurricane Irene during our stay and our room, which faced the rear of the hotel was fine, however both the couples with us had to move rooms due to leaking window frames from the constant rain at the front of the hotel. I am only mentioning this as when my parents had to move rooms, the member of staff who came to check out their complaint indicated that this has happened before as the windows in the hotel need repairing/changing. The hotel sent my parents a basket of fruit & cheese as an apology for the room change which was nice of them. However It is a shame that a lovely old hotel needs repairs that would appear not to be forthcoming. 
Having said that, this did not affect our stay, what I can say for certain is that there are many lovely rooms at the Shoreham!

We arrived at the hotel on July 2nd with our children for a three night stay. We arrived early and our rooms were not ready which is understandable. Our bags were stored so we could start sightseeing. When we arrived back at about 2:30 neither of our rooms were ready. We sat in the lobby for almost two more hours until our room was ready which was over an hour after check in. This was upsetting especially since we have three children under the age of 10 and had been travelling since 2am. There were no apologies for the inconvenience. We finally got out bags 20 minutes later with a gift for the long wait. It turns out it was a welcome amenity for guests of the wedding taking place the next day. The people at the front desk were confused when we returned the gift bag. It wasn't a great start to the trip and didn't get better. The fire alarms sounded around 2am and we had to rush three scared children six flights of stairs to the front of the hotel. I understand things happen but was a bit disappointed when other guests indicated this happened two nights earlier. It appears there was a known problem that wasn't fully taken care of. As another reviewer mentioned the alarms went off again as they were resetting them but my children weren't able to go to sleep until close to 4am.
The rooms were nice and the grounds and pool were beautiful. The staff at the pool were not attentive and we had to go get our own orders while others were being provided pool side service. Housekeeping was spotty at times and dirty towels weren't removed from the shower which makes me believe little attention was paid to the bathroom.
The location was nice as it was close to the metro and restaurants. Not sure this would be my choice for a hotel for my next visit to DC.

Situated within walking distance to many famous sites such as The Mall, the White House, convention centre and the metro. Complomentory breakfast every day and complimentory dinner weekdays Mo-Fr. Free wi-fi great grocery store just two blocks away. I highly recommend this hotel.

Our stay at the Washington Plaza was the best of our month long trip. We booked two double rooms and could leave our room doors open as there was another large security door enclosing both rooms.
All the staff were wonderful and extremely helpful (this hasn't been the case in other hotels so far).
The hotel was very clean and all amenities perfect. The restaurant menu could have been a bit more extensive as we felt it was more like a cafe.
We were able to walk to the majority of places of interest, unfortunately we came during a heat wave so needed at times to catch a taxi which were plentiful and cheap.
Only disappointment was the 
reflecting pool was empty as the area was under reconstruction.
Would definitely stay at the Washington Plaza again.
it was under
The staff is fun and pleasant. We loved it and will be back soon again.

I called twice prior to checking in and both times the person on the other end of the line was very rude and short with me. When I arrived the valet couldn't explain to me how to self park/find the hotel's deck. At check in, the man was again rude and when I asked a question about parking seemed annoyed. When I got into the room I was disappointed, to say the least, the room has a space for the mini fridge but no fridge, also there is no safe. I called down to ask and they said it was intentionally not there but they could deliver a fridge to the room. How ridiculous not to have it there in the first place?!? I've been waiting 30 minutes and still no fridge has been delivered. For all the hotels in the area one should not have to suffer through the stat here especially considering the nightly rate. Choose elsewhere, I wish I had!

This hotel, having played host to numerous presidential inaugural balls, traditionally knows how to impress, and it does still. The reception rooms are magnificnt and look recently refurbished to a high quality. The hotel shows no sign of being past its best and still has the potential to wow even the pickiest of guests (me) especially at the reasonable rate we were able to secure. Very favourable first impressions with efficient check in and friendly, courteous staff. Our room was almost a mini-suite, with a dual aspect and comfortable beds. The air conditioning leaked and the shower didn't do the luxurious bathroom justice but otherwise a very comfortable stay. Liked the Avida products too, although I would have liked a bath and an iPod docking station would have been good. Overall though a great stay in a lovely hotel which still manages to combine finery, character and quality.
hotel_name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel

review_title: Clean hotel, lots of amenities, but noisy, noisy, noisy
review_text:
My spouse had a business obligation that placed her at this hotel, so I got to tag along. We parked on the street at a meter since I was unclear of where to go. We entered the lobby which was huge and had a Starbucks, cafe, bar, restaurant, and plenty of seating scattered around. We checked in and the clerk told me how to get to the parking garage. I was happy to hear that I was to leave me car in the garage as long as I needed to after checkout.
The room was spacious, with a comfortable king bed, widescreen tv, and full bath. The remote on the tv did not power it on, but did work to change the channels. I thought we would enjoy a restul night's sleep, but being on a lower floor facing the street didn't allow us to get to bed early nor sleep in late. The lobby area seemed nice, but it was also too noisy for my taste to be enjoyable. The staff at this hotel was competent, but not as warm and friendly as the staff at the M Street location.

review_title: FOR THE SAKE OF YOUR MARRIAGE...AVOID THIS PLACE
review_text:
Staying here now (July 8, 2011). Requested hypoallergenic bedding prior to arrival (a few times) and it was not done, which means we called to request it. Several hours later...done. Next, we changed rooms once because the construction across the street started before 6:30am. Again requested hypoallergenic bedding, but this time we stayed away all day doing activities. Came back at 8:00pm...no hypoallergenic bedding. Called housekeeping three times and waited over an hour for bedding to be changed. 
Now the other part of the review: it is an average hotel at best. Rooms are just kind of old. The place is so big we often waited 10 mins for an elevator. The only saving grace was the restaurant in hotel called Cure (really nice). Bottom line is if we were not staying here for business (needed to be near the convention center) there is no way I would ever darken the doorstep.

review_title: Good Hotel, but a bit Worn
review_text:
This hotel is very nice and located in a great location about 6 blocks from the National Mall. The only
complaints I have are related to some "just average" housekeeping and the fact that the hotel rooms could use some updating(i.e. a lamp shade in our room was torn and new carpet and paint would make a big difference). Overall, the hotel is a great value, but this hotel is closer to 3 stars as opposed to 4 stars--because of its need for updating.
Great location, with helpful staff. Only negative being the wifi charge if you exceed 2 hours per day usage.

review_title: Excellent choice - great staff - very pleasant rooms
review_text: Hotel is in great location and excellent value for money. Staff very friendly and helpful. Rooms are clean and pleasant. Wireless good but you have to pay. Hotel is great choice for business or holiday stay.

review_title: Lovely hotel with just a few drawbacks
review_text:
Overall we had a very enjoyable 4-day stay at this hotel. It is a beautiful facility with a rich and interesting history, which to me was a particularly relevant thing to consider when visiting DC. The down side - our room was pretty small and not quite what I was expecting. I book hotel stays through a popular discount service, and in the past I've been blown away by the quality of the rooms I get. I think most hotels recognize that these services are used by frequent travelers, so they might spoil you a bit. This time, I felt like I got what I paid for. Can't complain, but certainly not super-impressed. 
Other considerations - the air conditioning in this older building is very loud. Might disturb some sleepers, but i didn't mind the sound. It's just a "whrrrr" ... not jarring. And, yes, the parking is atrociously expensive! Look for off-site long term parking if you have a car. The Metro stop is just steps away, so you shouldn't need a car during your stay anyway.
Staff was great, attentive and professional. Food was also very good and the atmosphere was enjoyable. A good choice for a DC visitor.
hotel_name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel

review_text: The price drops during the weekend for a reason -- the services elite rewards members expect vanish on the weekends. No one offered a bellman, doorman or anything except the housekeeping lady who offered a small pack of candy one night. You will not be pampered here despite the $500+ a night pricetag.
hotel_name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel

review_text: I recently stayed at the Mayflower Hotel to attend a conference being held at the Hotel. Our room and bath were fine. The Lobby Bar was less than acceptable. The service was poor and they ran out of popular liquor. The conference facilities were acceptable and the food decent, but the service good have been better.
hotel_name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel

review_title: Good value, hotel, rooms, staff all fantastic. Ventilation issues persisted throughout stay, but overall a pleasant experience.
review_text:
I stayed at the shoreham from Dec 22- new years. It was a great experience with only a few hiccups. I would definitely stay again.
The night we arrived we we given a room that we didn't like, smelled funky and it was right next to the elevators, ice machine, and a service area. We are a member of the omni rewards program and the hotel probably should have known not to place us there since our profile requests a quiet, high floor, away from elevator - but they fixed the situation quickly when I asked for a different room. Sometimes I wonder if it is a hidden policy of Omni, or hotels in general, to try and place people in the worst rooms first, because I've found myself asking for a different room on more than one occasion and not just at this hotel. Anyway the problem was solved quickly by the front desk who gave me a choice of rooms on different floors. We chose a corner room on the same floor an the staff had no problem with our desire fir another room, which made us feel good because although we didn't like the first room, we also don't like to complain.
Continuing on, the next night the hotel had many airline employees staying with them and one of the stewardesses was placed next to us (the layout for the shoreham is two corner rooms on either side of a suite). Unfortunately, the stewardess decided to ignore the fact that we were on a non-smoking floor which caused the entire wing to stink like cigarette smoke. This was a problem. I had my wife and baby with me and none of us can stand to be near a cigarette. I find it infuriating to have to breath in cigarette smoke, especially when I am paying for the room and the airline employee is not. In any event, I called the front desk who promptly sent up two engineers and security to check for smoke. The two engineers immediately confirmed the smell of smoke, but the security denied smelling anything. That security failed to acknowledge cigarette smoke was upsetting as five people had already determined that someone was indeed smoking on the floor. To make matters worse, it was midnight when the smoking took place, so switching rooms was pretty much out of the question.
When I inquired what would be done about the smoking I was told that security could not go around knocking on every door to see who was smoking, and at this point I had to let it go. I was extremely irritated, but I understood somewhat the perspective of the hotel in that they could not be 100% certain who was smoking. I would have liked to see the hotel take a more serious stance on their non smoking policy, but as it is, if someone is smoking on a non smoking floor the shoreham will only investigate the issue in the morning once housekeeping can enter the room. From my perspective, a non smoking health professional, this is unacceptable.
Realizing there was nothing that could be done, I thanked security for responding so quickly (which they did) and went back to my room. The shoreham has windows that open about 2-3 inches which is a big plus for me. I called down to the front desk to ask that two bottles of water be sent to my room because of the smoke and the front desk said that they do not usually provide water to guests unless they are platinum level guests. I reminded them that we were on a non smoking floor and that the water would certainly be appreciated. An hour later two bottles of water arrived. This was the second night at the hotel and at that point I was seriously considering leaving the next day. I expected more considering that I'd be staying with them for nearly two weeks.
The next day I inquired what would be done about the smoking and was told that the person that think responsible, the airline employee, was leavin that day. This was true and there was no other smoking issue for the next ten days. However, there was another issue with exhaust coming up through the elevator shaft and filling the entire wing with some sort of oil or diesel exhaust fumes. It was completely unbearable and my wife elected not to take a shower and simply leave for the day because she didn't want our 1 year old to breath it. I agreed completely and we alerted te concierge to the problem on our way out. If I had to guess I'd say that someone in the delivery area of the hotel left there truck engine running very near the service elevator, either that or there was a malfunction with the HVAC. We left for four hours and when we came back the problem was solved. I did not inquire about the cause.
Every morning we had breakfast at Roberts restaurant. The buffet was exemplary, although the menu was the same every other day, there was more than enough variety in the large buffet to get through one week without eating the same thing. Fresh fruits, pastries, eggs, potatoes, sausage, bacon, warm bread, yogurts, delicatessen items, cheeses, salmon, waffles, french toast, cereals, granola, and omelettes on the weekends - breakfast was fantastic and the service was consistantly excellent even though the staff rotated. Breakfast was not cheap, but it was good. I'm glad that the breakfast included a 16% gratuity because the staff deserves it. Overall I found the breakfast to be a great time and thank you again to all the servers for their unfailing charisma and service.
The hotel is quite lovely, we decided to walk around a few mornings after breakfast, to let our baby walk and to explore. I was surprised how expansive the hotel is. We wandered around for at least an hour, taking our time to let the baby walk, and were quite impressed with the size and build quality of the hotel. The shoreham is sound proof and feels like a solidly constructed building, dining rooms and ball rooms are very large and nicely furnished. There are what seems like and endless number of different rooms throughout the ground floor (the beatles, movie stars, musicians, and many presidents have been inside the shoreham for one reason or another) and the hotel retains an old refined feeling without coming off as dated or needing work. We occasionally met an employee or two and never had anyone treat us as though we didn't belong there. In fact, we were always treated with exceptional kindness and warmth and never felt out of place, from the valet to the housekeeping and all in between, the omni shoreham shines with the quality of it's personnel.
On one occasion we wandered far away from where anyone was staying and found a piano. I played the piano for my daughter for at least 20 minutes and no one bothered us. It was a lot of fun. We walked outside to look at the grounds which are impressive, but I was too cold to stay outside long and there wasn't really anything to see in December. Landscapers were working and the pool was closed so we didn't explore much outside.
The front entrance and reception area is beautiful. The ceilings are high and there are many chandeliers. There is plenty of furniture and I never sought after a comfortable seat if that is what I wanted. All of the front staff are appropriate and available if you want to talk, but not oppressive or intruding if you just want to sit and read or look around at the beautiful scenery.
Outside of the ventilation/air quality issues, the shoreham was a total win for us. We are grateful for a largely pleasant stay and while tree is room for improvement in enforcing their non smoking policies, I would stay at the shoreham again and recommend it to anyone visiting DC.
Joint the Omni rewards program is necessary to enjoy the hotel to it's fullest. It allows you complimentary beverages at arrival and every morning at any time you specify. It also provides free wireless Internet and is free itself so it should no be passed up on. There are other perks to be had, but if you aren't staying twenty or more nights in one year then those are the major things you'll enjoy from it.
The valet parking is 28$/night. Parking in DC is strictly enforced and there is not much option besides parking at the hotel. The valet was run very well, very professional, and although I didn't like the price I did like the service. If you plan your trip ahead of time and have flexible dates you may find packages which include breakfast am parking for as little as 125$/night. The shoreham is an excellent place to stay while visiting DC. Other Omni properties I've visited are Massachusetts and Virginia.
Our best to the staff of the Shoreham in this new year,
Mr. O'Brien & family
