The last minute I had to take my son to washington d c. It was hard to find a reasonably priced hotel in the location I needed. Hotels.com showes the Morrison-Clark Inn. It was a little hard to find but the valet parking really was great. I had a large historical room and a fine clean bathroom. For the price it was awesome. This staff is awesome. I will stay there again.

review_title: No nickel & diming at Embassy Suites Chevy Chase Pavilion
review_text:
Every employee we encountered at Embassy Suites was extremely friendly. The check in process went very smoothly. The staff was able to offer great suggestions for restaurants and activities based on our needs (girl's getaway). We were all very impressed.
Housekeeping was thorough and very honest...we left tips out each day but they didn't take them. I hope they share because we just left a large tip at the end of our stay. It was nice not to have to beg for towels like you do at some hotels. 
The cocktail reception was great. It gave us an opportunity to relax and plan our evening before heading out on the town at night. Bartenders were also friendly. 
The breakfast put this place over the top in terms of value. We all miss rolling out of bed and having someone else make our breakfast. :-)
Location was very convenient. It was nice to be in such close proximity to so many shops and restaurants. I suppose the metro was convenient too, but I prefer cabs. 
Thank you very much for a wonderful stay!

The location of the hotel above subway, within the mall and across shopping and food is ideal for families with children and teens. It is so convenient and safe to get around. Breakfast was very generous with a full buffet spread, so was the manager's reception with free drinks and finger food and board games. Our queen suite which came with 2 queen beds and a sofa bed was spacious and comfortable for 5 people. The only imperfection was that there was no complementary bottles of water in the fridge like we normally would have at other hotels/motels/apts. 
The best way to sightsee and visit the museums/monuments is to take the hop on/off or old town trolley because they stop near the site. A subway will arrive further and you will have to walk a fair bit. However, note that the subways do not travel as regularly or frequently on sats and Sundays due to maintenance, so the wait can be 20-30 mins. Also, do not take the last trolley which is at 530pm because it is likely to be full since everyone is heading back. Our group of 10 was stranded in the cold and had to find our way back.

We booked 3 nights here through a booking engine. Arrived here late at night and the staff were friendly and welcoming. We requested a quiet room and it was very quiet. There were toiletries in the bathroom and the shower was hot. The room was a little dark and you couldnt watch the tv while in bed. The bed was comfortable and the location was good. Its a few blocks from the metro and one block from the circulator bus that goes to Union Station or Georgetown. The staff were helpful and gave us maps and local information. We would stay here again.

Friendly, helpful staff. Breakfast chef patient and good. Only complaint is how difficult to get a taxi..
Hotel called for us since there is no taxi stand...but still no luck. Red line metro right at hotel if you're heading into the district.

My family and I stayed here when my brother ran the army 10 miler. Everything was fantastic. There are several stores and restaurants on location. The free breakfast and managers reception is a wonderful treat. My only complaint is that the staff tended to enter our room without knocking when delivering items or housekeeping. Well, they would knock but not give enough time to answer the door. That was unnerving. Beyond that, everything was perfect.

We just came back from a six night stay and my family adored staying here. My wife and I have 8 year old triplets and the two room suite was unbelievably helpful. Being right above the Metro was an easy way to get around the town. The kids adored the breakfast bar and the happy hour Shirley Temples and board games. And the rooms were plenty spacious. In fact, we even invited a friend of the kids' from school who had recently moved to the DC area for a sleep over the night of hurricane Irene. we all slept right through the storm and didn't need to leave the mall the hotel is attached to grab dinner. My kids specifically asked to come back to the hotel some day. So a total success.
Boy is this place ready for a fix up - worn out and boring.

review_title: Our experience was both good and bad.
review_text: This is a lovely boutique hotel. However, we were not comfortable with many aspects of our stay. The bed that we had was worn out and we rolled toward the weak center of the mattress each night. The espresso maker in our room was great except that they had no non-decaf pods and the desk clerk shrugged when we asked why. The breakfast in the common area appeared to be gratis but was so not. We were surprised to see a rat in the courtyard of the hotel. Here is our advice: stay here only if you must, and expect nothing but a good bathroom and desk. Even the tv channels were underwhelming.

review_title: Great service! Great location! Only minor gripes.
review_text: My wife and I stayed here as our last night out before our child is due. The valet service was professional and courteous. The desk clerks were extremely helpful and were more than happy to make accommodations for us - we asked for a room with a view, since the king suites only have a view to the interior of the building. The first room they moved us to was next to the elevator and housecleaning room. But after asking for another room they had no issue with moving us farther down the hall. The hotel is well maintained. My biggest complaints were 1) the cable was awful. The channels were snowy and when we rented a movie, it looked like we were watching an old VCR. 2) the AC was a little loud, due to vibrations in the ducting. I would have expected a little better considering the location and price. Overall I would recommend this hotel.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Washington Convention Center

review_text: A friend recommended this hotel for its convenience to the metro. Yes the convenience is there. The metro is right beneath the hotel! Awesome. I am greatly disappointed with our reception upon our arrival though. We entered on the lower level entrance and we were met by No One! The valet/bellhop desk was unattended(front desk advised us that they do not staff the area on weekends) . With numerous bags and two small children in tow this presented a problem. I can deal with schlepping my bags to my room If only I could find a baggage cart ! The front desk promised to get one down to the lower level but one ever came. The rest of the hotel was typical embassy suites fare. I could have done without the black stained and ripped bedspread though! No apologies were offered for the lack of service at the bellhop area nor for the bedspread even though I showed great patience and had a pleasant demeanor. The 25 dollar/day parking at the hotel brought my bill north of $200 for each day that I stayed there. Not great for a run of the mill Embassy Suites.

review_title: Great location but the room was filthy!
review_text: I booked a room for my parents to spend a good anniversary celebration. Booked a non smoking room and when checked in around 3:15 pm,, room was not ready and they checked us in a smoking room. My mom had allergic reaction and asked front desk to change room immediately but hotel only offered to keep out for about 3 hours and they will spray the room!!!

I usually stay here when in DC for business. It is comfortable, clean, and just a block from the Gallery Place - Chinatown metro, so it's easy to pick up the red, yellow, or green lines all over town. Also, just a block or two from some of the best restaurants in DC like Zatinya or Rasika. Gordon Biersch is right in the lobby too. Only markdown is that while they updated the shower head and faucets, the tub itself was pretty war torn (like putting lipstick on a pig). All else is great.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Washington Convention Center

review_title: Euro sized room and poor A/C in room
review_text: Great location. Staff very friendly and helpful. Entire property was well appointed and very clean. (This hotel is in an old renovated back...check out the vault room downstairs.). My only complaints are (1) the room was very small. I felt like I was back living in Europe. (2) the air conditioning sucked. We couldn't get the room to cool below 72 degrees even though the thermostat was set at 65 and it wasn't very effective at dehumidifying the air.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Washington Convention Center

review_title: Great location, great room - would happily stay here again
review_text: Fully agree with the other recent reviews. Found the front desk staff to be rather indifferent (no acknowledgement or even a smile when returning to the hotel) while housekeeping was first class. Good size and well equipped room was a little tired although bathroom and kitchen was modern and required no updating. Be prepared to wait for the elevator on occasions - they are old and seemed a little temperamental. Can't comment on the restaurant as we didn't use it. Menu did seem pricey, though. Handy laundry facilities in the basement along with only vending machine (poorly stocked when I used it). Yes, Internet was slow but usable for most things. W

review_title: Perfect choice--especially between Christmas and New Year's
review_text:
The Mr.and I stayed here for four nights--we had a ridiculously inexpensive deal and that was our reason for the trip to DC. Everyone was very kind and hospitable--the staff offered a very reasonable upgrade on a suite and we accepted it. Our visit was perfect!
With so many choices, I admit we never had a meal here. Our maid, who we never saw, was excellent--and left us extra coffee--it was clear we did not drink the decaf--having travelled extensively--that has never happened before...
A note...we parked on the street over night- and fed quarters to the meters when we went to nearby dinners--don't be a minute after 7am--our minute's delay cost us 25.00

review_title: A hotel with such class and simplicity all surrounded by a beautiful city!
review_text: I have nothing bad to say about this hotel. Ive stayed here for birthday affairs and just beacause affairs..the rooms were always well cleaned, the help was exceptional. The location is perfect! I will be plan to be there again soon enough!

I love staying at this hotel. The staff are just so friendly, great atmosphere and I always get a great room. I would certainly recommend this hotel for your next stay.
Try it out and you'll see what I mean.

review_title: Really cool neighborhood and convenient to the metro.
review_text: I recently stayed with my two daughters for a girl's birthday weekend. The rooms were spacious and the hotel was located in a quaint neighborhood. Everything was in walking distance or a short cab/metro ride away. Staff was friendly and professional. I would stay there again!
Just left the St Gregory and I must admit it is more then what posted online. The staff are wonderful and very helpful. The hotel is very clean but needs to upgrade the TV. Will be back
I found the service to be great. Mr. Haddock upgraded me to a suite and I appreciated the extra room. Krispy Kreme was only 5 minutes away ....
Starting with the staff,in one in particular( Wilver Cupido ) was very helpful, friendly, professional .I would recomend the stay to anyone looking for a great place to stay while visiting the city.

From the moment I arrived at the hotel I received exceptional service. The doorman greeted me with a warm smile and was so attentive to assist me with my luggage. As I entered the hotel I felt like I walked into a vintage paradise with a twist of Marilyn Monroe. The lobby had a beautiful decor and everyone was so polite and professional. The staff at the frontdesk were very friendly with their ever caring conversations. I was upgraded to an amazing suite that was by far more than classy. Even though my stay was brief, it was the perfect remedy of relaxion. The St Gregory is more than just a hotel, it was a home away from home.

First this hotel is very clean and the staff are the best. From the moment we arrived we were treated like royal. The doorman was very helpful, the front desk upgraded us to a suite for $20. It was worth every penny. Thanks to the entire staff for making our reunion great.

Ok, I can't add much to what's already been said, this is an incredible hotel. Here's the thing though: the towels are amazing; big, soft, absorbs every drop of water. Also, suite upgrade for super cheap, when we were there on an already cheap priceline-ninja rate!
I can't recommend this place enough. Ask them for an 8th floor suite.
Buen hotel, muy limpio, buena relacion precio valor. Inmejorable ubicaciÃ³n
HÃ´tel top, situÃ© Ã  5 minutes de Dupont Circle. Rien Ã  redire, mais j'ai profitÃ© d'un tarif trouvÃ© sur un site de discount Internet de 110$ la nuit.
Hotel Was good for it's value. Bed wasn't very comfortable at all and the room wasn't anything spectacular. But it is in a great location and was clean.

review_title: Nice hotel but not sure about 4 star ratings
review_text: Nice hotel in a good location but not sure how it gets four star ratings on some services. Rooms were clean but are in need of some updating especially the beds. Beds were not comfortable at all and pillows had no support. I guess because of business travelers they can charge $300 to $400 a night but not worth it in my opinion. Good but just not 4star.

review_title: A quintessential Washington DC hotel in one of the best locations in the city...
review_text:
I stayed at this hotel out of necessity because the hotel at which I normally stay was booked. I was surely impressed by the staff, their friendliness, and genuine warmth. Make sure you get the double rooms or the upgrade suites, however. The regular rooms are quite small and difficult to become comfortable:otherwise a great stay. 
Make sure to have a drink at the bar:lovely, intimate, colonial appointed space.
hotel_name: The Fairfax at Embassy Row, a Starwood Luxury Collection Hotel

review_title: State Plaza: pernottare sÃ¬, colazione no.
review_text:
L'hotel Ãª situato in una posizione comodissima per visitare Washington; si trova infatti in posizione baricentrica rispetto alle diverse attrazioni della capitale. A piedi si possono raggiungere la casa bianca, i musei, il Lincoln memorial, il quartiere penn, ma soprattutto lo State Plaza Ã¨ vicino anche al Washington harbor e a Georgetown (i movimentati quartieri ricchi di negozi e ristoranti in cui Ã© possibile fare shopping e cenare) che si animano mentre downtown di sera si svuota. La camera era spaziosa, con cucina annessa (datata di frigorifero e freezer, fornello, tostapane,stoviglie per 4 ospiti), il bagno piccolo, preceduto da un anti bagno. Nella stanza c'era anche la cassaforte e la connessione ad internet gratuita (wifi solo nella hall). Il personale alla recepiton era molto disponibile e gentile. Non avevamo la macchina,per cui non avevamo problemi di parcheggio. La sorpresa negativa Ã© stata la colazione, principalmente per tre motivi: 1) l'offerta dei cibi proposti era ben lontana dagli standard americani (poca scelta: o il caffÃ¨ o il succo o il latte portati dal cameriere e non alla spina; mancava il cheese per il bagel sostituito da una crema con aglio e cipolla, non c'erano marmellate e spesso le fette di pane da tostare non venivano riassortite); 2) per raggiungere la zona colazione, situata in un'altra ala dell'hotel, bisognava attraversare un garage chiuso, che fungeva da deposito dei cassonetti di spazzatura dell'hotel e della cucina. L'aria era irrespirabile e il garage andava attraversato in apnea perchÃ© l'odore era veramente sgradevole (gas di scarico+spazzatura+cucina= un aroma terapia da far schiattare) 3) il personale addetto alla colazione, a parte un ragazzo americano, non chiedevano mai se desiderassimo ancora del caffÃ¨ o altro.
Concludendo: la posizione Ã¨ ottima, le camere buone, la colazione insufficiente (la peggiore mai incontrata durante i nostri 6 viaggi negli States). Consiglio: vale la pena pernottare; la colazione potete prepararvela in camera acquistando i prodotti nel market aperto 24 ore su 24 che si trova subito fuori dall'hotel.

Nice hotel, but to be expected for the price. Not very satisfied with the room, good bed, but no closet, no place to put my suitcase and no minibar. And expencive breakfeast. Will not stay here again.
hotel_name: The Fairfax at Embassy Row, a Starwood Luxury Collection Hotel

review_text:
The Fairfax is a small European style hotel that competes with the Jefferson and the Hay Adams. It is enjoyable to stay at despite some draw backs. As the name implies, it is just off DuPont circle and surrounded by embassies. This makes it a fun neighborhood to walk around in. 
The hotel's lobby is quite small but there is a nice bar a few steps off the lobby that serves as a meeting place. The front desk staff is insanely good. They went above and beyond on every issue. Not the phony Ritz Carlton concern. I really felt they took ownership of my problems (both of which were of my own making). The same is true of the bellman, and this is the kind of hotel where you feel awkward if you don't use a bellman, plus there are a couple of staIrs to get to the elevator.
I would recommend you try to avoid a queen sized bed, even if you are a single. The queen rooms are tiny and the bathroom is silly small. It is so small that there is no place to put a waste basket and, I suspect, anyone over six feet tall would be unable to comfortably sit on the toilet. 
There are three things that drive me nuts about hotels as a frequent business traveler, and all three are present at the Fairfax. First is the lack of electric sockets. The only socket is in the lamp on the tiny little desk. So if you use that for your laptop, you have no place else to plug in your phone (and in my case, a CPAP). To access another socket requires moving the bed and unplugging a lamp. Would it kill hotels to supply a power strip?
The second is the tiny little print on identical looking bottles of shampoo, conditioner, lotion and body wash. Most people dont wear glasses into the shower.
The third is paying for wifi (although the Fairfax's charge is cheap at $9.95 and the wifi is pretty fast).
I had occasion to eat breakfast in the 2100 Prime restaurant (used to be The Jockey Club), lunch in the bar and dinner at 2100. All were excellent and not too expensive by Washington standards.
But, all in, the quality of the people who work at the Fairfax exceeds any of the other problem, and I look forward to staying again
hotel_name: The Fairfax at Embassy Row, a Starwood Luxury Collection Hotel

review_text: Our family of 4 stayed here for 4 nights. The rooms were very nice and the bathroom was very large. The hotel is in a wonderful neighborhood surrounded by beautiful brownstones and next door to the Embassy of Indonesia . The staff was especially friendly towards our two children. A special thank you to the doorman Ahmed who quizzed our son on the historical sites in Washington. All of the staff made us feel welcome. It is so convenient to the metro and lots of great places to eat nearby. I highly recommend the Fairfax to anyone planning to visit the DC area. We will definitely stay here again on our next visit!!!
hotel_name: The Fairfax at Embassy Row, a Starwood Luxury Collection Hotel

review_title: Very classic hotel with friendly service
review_text: Very classic and traditional decor. Not my style, but the service is warm and friendly. The amenities include toiletry kit and Remede products. The location is close to the metro, and walking distance to many good restaurants.
hotel_name: The Fairfax at Embassy Row, a Starwood Luxury Collection Hotel

review_title: perfect place to stay in dc
review_text: excellent hotel - friendly and helpful staff & beautiful room - especially the bathroom.
The location is excellent. Service was friendly, attentive and helpful. Food at the Biersch restaurant is nicely done, and so is the beer. I'll be staying here more often when I'm in DC.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Washington Convention Center

review_title: Excellent value. Perfect for quick business trip.
review_text: Had an event at Reagan building and found this place at a great rate. Staff was very friendly. Would stay here again.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Washington Convention Center

review_title: The service is exceptional; they are really at your service!
review_text: The hotel was clean, friendly staff and nice lobby area. Great location.

review_title: Great place, don't understand bad reviews
review_text:
We stay in 4 star hotels all the time and this place is up to par. Don't understand bad review of july 5. Our water preassure and air are fine. And I hot flash on a regular basis. To be fair, it unusually cool outside too. 80 degrees. Yes, the service is great, feels close to four seasons. I have had much worse hotels at 4 star level, including one in honalulu that was an spg prop. 2 miles from national mall, so metro works. Great neighborhood, beautifully gardened, landscaped. 
We're happy with our last minute hotwire purchase. ;)
hotel_name: The Fairfax at Embassy Row, a Starwood Luxury Collection Hotel

review_text: We pricelined our room for 1 night and we were surprised at how the hotel was classified as 4 stars. Our room had an old-hotel Best Western feel, with old carpet, tube television and foldaway bed and foldaway wall, I think the room is part of a suite because behind the wall is the next room. The bathroom was really clean however, the subway tiles in the bathroom was a nice touch. We kinda didn't have hot water to shower and my husband wasn't happy with the rough towels. We were offered free continental breakfast, so I appreciated that. It consisted of coffee, oj, 1 croissant and 1 muffin-it was just enough for me since we were going to have brunch at blue duck tavern, I was happy with the free coffee! All in all, it was just an OK hotel, I wouldn't pay more than 100 dollars per night. Its fine for a 1 night trip in D, but not longer. However, I thnk there are other hotels in the area or near DC that's preTty decent for much less

Very conveniently located between the Mall and Convention centre. Just opposite corner to the Spy Museum. The room we had was a bit cramped and had a peculiar layout where it felt like stepping in to the bathroom when the door was opened. Building is an old bank and a vault door remains as a feature in the breakfast lounge. Rooms were clean but not high standard. Breakfast buffet only Sunday, but the Spy Bar is just across the street if you get fed up with the meager choices at the hotel.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Washington Convention Center

review_text: The location is great. It is a block away from the metro. It is a nice walk to many of the monuments and musuems. The room is small but bed is comfortable.
hotel_name: Courtyard by Marriott Washington Convention Center

Valets qui vous salue en vous ouvrant la porte, des attentions que l'on apprÃ©cie. Chambres propres et confortable. Lit trÃ¨s confortable, et air climatise efficace. Wi-fi gratuit et fonctionnel. Excelente Hotel, limpio, bonito, buena ubicaciÃ³n, los empleados son muy amables

My husband and I recently celebrated our tenth wedding anniversary. Although we live in the District, our weekend "getaway" was at the Fairfax. It was a lovely experience; the room, staff, and restaurant were all top notch. 
The doorman and bellhop were very friendly. The front desk clerk, Josh, was kind enough to send us a complimentary bottle of wine and handwritten note. Housekeepers were always smiling in the hallways and the turndown service was a nice surprise. Breakfast in the Jockey Club was delicious.
We're looking forward to returning next year.
hotel_name: The Fairfax at Embassy Row, a Starwood Luxury Collection Hotel

review_title: Excellent location, clean rooms, and a Starbucks in the lobby.
review_text: This hotel has the best location if you want to tour the DC monuments. Good restaurants, close to everything. Tv and movie images not very good though. Not the Ritz, but then you don't have to deal with all the tipping, either.

review_title: Way overpriced, outdated rooms look like something out of 1970's
review_text:
When I arrived the staff was less then happy to greet me. Gave me a room on a lower level close to 1/4 mile away from the front desk. The room has not been remodeled in decades. The hallways lined with dirty carpet and tacky wallpaper should have been an indication that the room was going to smell like a musty basement and a dirty ashtray. They did upgrade to the flat screen TVs but didn't bother to update anything else. 
There is no way I would ever pay 300/night for this hotel ever again.

Well I stayed on the 12th floor of the this hotel with spectacular views of the washinton monument. The room was comfortable and very clean. I purchased the room and breakfast package which I loved,the breakfast was great. I loved the service.

Stayed here due to the hotels close proximity to the DC zoo. The pool was nice with a great pool bar where the kiss get drinks for free. The hotel lobby was so gorgeous but the room service was gross. Do not order from room service. Also the AC was loud but despite that will definitely stay here again.....

review_title: Nice hotel but stay away from the pool!
review_text: The hotel is nice and centrally located, but the pool area is a real desaster. In all my years of travelling around the world I haven't seen such a poorly maintained pool. I refused to go into the water or even take off my shoes! If you are going to stay at the hotel, leave your swim gear at home...

We sent 5 days at this hotel and couldn't have been happier. The hotel was glorious, clean, rooms large and comfy. We had 2 rooms, 1054+1053. They were located in the back and were extremely quiet. The rooms were off the main hallway so we never heard people coming and going. Maid service was great, check in was quick and everything we ask for was met. We. had apps on the second floor, our server was terrific, very attentive and made our evening enjoyable. The location of this hotel is close to eveything. White house 3 blocks away
 Metro red and blue line very close. Dupont circle 3 blocks up. Surrounding area very safe. Lots of places to eat, Mortons across the street,ask about specials and they will offer u a set price for $55. Well worth it. Includes everything. Enjoy your stay we sure did.
hotel_name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel

review_text: Think twice to stay here if you are international traveler. Concierge is rude and I woukd even think, racist. Twice we asked if they knew where we could take a sightseeing tour. Concierge answered only "YES" and turned around!!!! Very different treatment had northamerican guests. This is UNACCEPTABLE for me. I stayed at a Renaissence Hotel in Zurich and had the best experience, but here in Washington DC, the worst concierge service EVER!!

Ornate hotel. The room are huge with plenty of room for a rollaway cot. Bathrooms are very large with a stall marbled shower and a tub shower. The service people were great - many have 20+ years with the hotel. Location is very convenient to metro. Beautiful mezzanine bar area. Price for rooms is steep, but found ours on Priceline. Only downside is no pool.
hotel_name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel

review_text: Wow! Amazing hotel, nice location, beautiful gardens, excellent service, delicious food. The conciage was very helpful, arranged trips and made great suggestions to me for shopping and eating. Away from all the crazy busy town, nice food and shops just a brisk walk in to downtown. Highly recommended!

review_title: With so many options in DC why slum it here?
review_text: Cookie cutter hotel room that would bore you even if you were on a business trip. With so much to see and do in DC you can do better for price and location in other hotels. Rude check in staff sealed the deal that this is not the place to go for a fun experience in our nation's capital.
hotel_name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel

review_text: The reviews that I read about this hotel were spot on. The staff is beyond friendly. The presentation of the room and the meals were fabulous. Its location is very convenient when traveling to the Smithsonian and the monuments etc. I do wish that the pool cafe/bar kept later hours to 11pm rather than 9pm though. Housekeeping could perform more rounds and clear room service from the hallways in a more reasonable time. Overall this hotel was a pleasure and I'll definitely stay here in the future.

See my review under Embassy Suites.....wound up here in a two room Junior suite. Beautiful lobby, tastefully decorated rooms that were modern, yet classic, well appointed and had great finishes.
The 1331 lounge was great for unwinding with each booth having its own large LCD tv. 1331 had good food and attentive wait staff. 
All in all great location, good lounge, excellent rooms....the whole family was happy!
We stayed here with our two children. The quarters were a little cramped, but the location was quite good. And the elevator was a little weird. I think for two people it would be great.

Absolutely wonderful hotel! The staff and service was amazing! We arrived at 9:30am and our room was already ready for us to check-in. We were happy that we didn't have to leave our luggage and could spend then day sightseeing. The rooms are comfortable, large, and very quiet. This was the first hotel I've stayed at in a long time that I didn't need earplugs.
This hotel is a renovated old hotel and I love the details that show the history. The only downside is a narrow bathroom with a pedestal sink and a shelf as counter space. I made do just fine, but it is on the small side.
The pool really does feel like a resort in a city. It is super nice and I enjoyed spending a few hours poolside.
With hotels charging for everything these days. It was refreshing to be an Omni Select Guest member and receive free wifi and morning beverage service.
Hotel is in a great location - close to great restaurants and the metro.

Location good , Shop next door for groceries etc very handy worth big points if staying a few days , don't need a car , the touring redline buses stop there. Which are a perfect way to see Washington highly recommend. There are two Red line companies one has just bought the other line so you can get on any but they do have different stops be ware..one free washing machine on level 3 it's at the very end of corridor...could be a cue . wifi downstairs only

Location is great. Rooms are large. Staff is fine. The place is really worn, however. The walls are very dirty, towels are old and thin, bathtub vinyl bottom is peeling off, furniture extremely worn. In room coffee terrible, not even a teabag or two. Just spend the money to update! Could be a great place.

review_title: Charme von gestern zu ueberteuerten Preisen
review_text: Duchaus luxuriÃ¶ses Hotel zu leider voellig ueberteuerten Preisen. Das Hotel ist gut gelegen und die Anlage generell schon sehr gediegen aber leider stehen die Preise in keinem Verhaeltnis zum Komfort. Fuer ein kleines Zimmer, das ich eher als renovierungsbeduertfig bezeichnen wuerde, habe ich ueber 700 $ bezahlt. Der service ist sehr gut und das Personal sehr zuvorkommend aber die Zimmer leider seit einigen Jahrzehnten nicht mehr renoviert worden.
hotel_name: The Mayflower Renaissance Washington, DC Hotel

review_title: Good location but no ability to choose heat or ac
review_text: Picked this hotel because of location, good reviews, and decent price. When I arrived, I discovered they have central heat and ac. The choice of heat or ac is made by the university. It was 70 degrees each day but we could only get heat. The staff suggested we sleep with the windows open. This seemed like an odd suggestion for a $200+ per night hotel. We checked out the next day and moved to the Westin. Would not stay here again.
Found the hotel to be well priced and a pretty good location close to the white house. Breakfast was extensive and good value.
hotel_name: Residence Inn Washington DC / Vermont Ave.

review_text:
Wonderful location - 2 blocks from Dupont Circle stop on the red line. Lots of great restaurants and bars within a few blocks. We are at Vento (next to hotel) and Urbana (across the street) and both were very good.
Very good service - I used points to stay but we ended up needing am extra night. The front desk staff was very helpful. I also ran the Cherry Nlossom run and both guys at the desk clapped for me when I came back - so nice!
The rooms are a bit older but clean and functional. Kitchen includes coffee maker, full fridge/freezer, microwave and stove. Bathroom is basic.

review_title: Couldn't be happier with value and location.
review_text:
The rooms have plenty of space for me and my 2 children to spread out. The in room kitchen complte with stove and full size fridge make it a nice time or money saver for making meals and snacks. There was a very comfortable queen size bed and a fold out couch. Additional bed I believe is available for a small price, but 4 people could easily fit. Large flat screen tv and free wi-fi in the room, and they provide a complimentary real breakfast of biscuits and gravy, waffles, eggs, sausage, as well as a wide variety of other goodies.
There is a pharmacy/mini grocery downstairs for most needed food items. Less than 10 minute easy walk 4 long blocks) to White House and walking distance to museums and other attractions. 
Got an EXCELLENT rate on Priceline under $100 and parking was $25 a day (all hotels seem to charge as much as $45, so reasonable).
We had a wonderful stay!!!
Only downside is no pool, and need to plan ahead for dinner of not using kitchen since restaurants are further away in the evening except pubs.
I was very very very happy with this hotel, and strongly recommend it for families.
hotel_name: Residence Inn Washington DC / Vermont Ave.

review_text: Great location to see dc. Here for mcm was perfect. Hotel nice but rooms snug. Price reasonable.

review_title: This hotel is great value, clean, good breakfast, roomy, excellent service.
review_text: I would rate this in my top two or three big city hotels I have stayed in when you consider everything. The studio room easily accommodated 3 adults, a rollaway, and six suitcases. The bed was comfy, service impeccable, good breakfast. The doorman even ran down the street in traffic to try a find a van sized taxi for us when we were leaving. My mom is the pickiest person I know and she gave it an A+ on cleanliness. Halls also very clean. Only ding I would give is it is not super close to train, but still had no problem getting everywhere we wanted to go. When you go to DC, do your homework. Metro's trip planner on their website rocks. Not so much on app.
hotel_name: Residence Inn Washington DC / Vermont Ave.

review_text:
-rooms well presented and clean
-hotel was excellent for those of us at George Washington Univ. And Medical Centre, walking distance 1 block
-great location for the Metro, Watergate and Kennedy centre 
-staff were helpful 
-resturant had an excellent menu and good value for money pre-theatre dinner 3 courses $32
Only thing I would suggest is that if there is more that one of you staying in a room make sure you all register, my wife did the booking in her name and went shopping, when I got back and my room key did not open the door they had no record of me to let me in !!!!! Even though we had registered and had 2 keys allocated. Staff sorted it out but it took time.

Great location close to Gwu and Georgetown 
Located in a quiet area but close to metro and other sights
Very nice suite with a kitchenette 
Will stay again

We decided to spurge on our trip to DC and stay at the closest hotel to the Smithsonia museums. 
Aside from the initial hassle at check in because our room was not ready, AND the person we were dealing with apparent lack of customer service skills... After speaking with manager, Quinn, all was made right and the rest of the stay was pretty nice. 
The only other hassle, which normally would not be there was add security at the front door. It was a bit insulting at times to be questioned about being a guest at the hotel.

When staying in DC, location is very important. 
I found this Marriott to be a great marriage between location and value. Since most people have different expectations of their hotels, it is best to boil things down to a couple of pearls. 
Location and value. 
You will find both satisfied here

I cannot say enough about the location of this hotel. It is close to the metro with numerous bistros, pubs, and fine dining opportunities all within walking distance. Our suite overlooks the square and the amenities (such as the kitchen and LARGE walk-in closet) make it a comfortable home-away-from-home while exploring the beauty of D.C.

We stayed the weekend of the tenth anniversary of 9/11 and were very pleased with our accommodations. It was our first trip to our nation's capital and we had a wonderful time. The hotel was nice, clean and had a great view of the Washington monument. We are planning to return in the fall to the hotel

Nicely located in the middle of all DC sites and convention center. Staff was very nice, rooms were clean with the usual amenities of this class of hotel. No free Internet in rooms. Gym opens late for early risers. Starbucks in the lobby. Nice restaurant onsite, with a happy hour.

I would recommend others to stay in this hotel as it was conveniently located at the beginning of Georgetown. It was a short 15 minute walk to the Lincoln memorial and 1 block from Trader Joes. The kitchenette was clean and convenient for us and there were good eateries in the area - Thai Coast, Roti meditterranean Grill across from the metro, and it looks like they are building a Whole Foods right next to the metro stop! We even tried the hospital food one night - cheap and good, and a good variety.
They charge for plastic bags at all areas in DC so bring your own recycleable bags. The Circulator bus was convenient to get to Union Station and is only $1 from the corner of 22nd and K Street. It is also a short walk to Georgetown or catch the Circulator bus. Again, very convenient and clean hotel.
Valet parking and drop off are curbside so not a lot of room but the doormen and valet staff were very friendly and efficient.

review_title: Great Location, Friendly Staff, Nice Rooms
review_text: My husband and I stayed here for three nights on our first east coast trip and I don't think we could have found a better place. We did rent a car while staying because the Metro is so convenient, but this hotel is right in the thick of all the things we wanted to visit so we were able to walk everywhere. Check-in was easy, even with us arriving early due to flight schedules. Our room (I requested an upper floor) faced the quiet courtyard so we never had any street noise. While not a huge room, it was clean and the furniture comfortable, especially the bed! Nice Linens and great pillows! The bathroom was clean with granite counters. We were able to get a decent rate through one of their discounts so make sure you check them out before booking. We will definitely be back!

Used this hotel only if you have money to burn. Rooms are small, no refrigerator, and if you don't mind paying $19.00 for a breakfast buffet then go ahead and stay here. The only good quality of this hotel was it's location and the Maryland crab and corn soup at the Fire & Sage restaurant in th hotel.

We stayed three nights in a king suite. A little on the small side but well equipped and nicely decorated. The entire hotel has been recently renovated in an Asian influenced theme with extremely bright colors. Everything in the room worked properly except for the outlet in the bathroom.
The hotel was quiet, staff attentive and friendly, and complimentary breakfast just what we needed each morning. The Chinatown metro stop is about a block and a half away and there are several restaurants and bars of all varieties within walking distance. Overall, we were very pleased with this hotel choice.
hotel_name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Washington, DC / Downtown

review_text: We got the breakfast and loved it. You can take a very nice buffet or order from the menu. We could pass by the tacky food courts at the museums.

I stayed here for just over a week while I was at a very long conference for work. The room was excellent - very clean with a lovely comfy bed and pillows. 
It's in an excellent location for conventions as its only a 5 min walk from the convention centre, but is also close to various bars and restaurants. 
In the room there is also a microwave and a fairly spacious fridge so if you want to buy things from the local Safeway and bring them back rather than eating out that is also a possibility. 
Breakfast is buffet-style with a pretty good selection of food. The hot food varies daily. I was very pleased to see that fresh fruit was available every day as well as cereal, pastries, waffles etc. there were also freshly baked cookies in the evening if you get there at the right time. 
The staff were all pleasant, welcoming and helpful without being overbearing (something I appreciate as a Brit!). 
If I had to make one small complaint it was that the rooms were too hot for my personal liking and the air conditioning unit was very noisy when it kicked in. This left me in the eternal quandary of whether it was better to not sleep because I was too hot or not sleep because the air conditioner was making a right royal racket! When I was tired enough I generally managed to get to sleep whatever the conditions, however if you're a light sleeper you may find this difficult. 
Overall, this is a good hotel if you're on a budget. Much better than a travel lodge etc. Don't expect to live in the lap of luxury but if clean, comfortable accommodation is what you're after this will do just great :)

review_title: Great location and service, could be little nicer for $$$.
review_text: The location is perfect if you need to be by Capitol hill. It's near a metro stop so that's great. The rooms are nice but the hotel is a bit old looking with a blah feel. The service at breakfast and the hotel staff was VERY helpful and nice... Top notch service.

This hotel is clean, stylish, has very friendly staff, and is very environmentally conscious. Breakfast has all the artery cloggers as well as fruits. Hot tub temperature is just right; pool water a bit too cold.
Our family used to make day trips to DC. In the future we'll more likely stay here.

review_title: Good jumping off point for seeing DC sights
review_text: Spent 2 nights here while touring DC. We loved the location near the sites downtown and along the Mall. The metro is accessible at the hotel's doorstep so you can really get anywhere. The room was comfortable and nice - our only concern was noisy plumbing at night and hearing noise from the hallway. Would stay here again.

I spent one night here at the Fairfield and it was a great experience! The front desk clerk was very nice and helpful. The bed was large and very comfy. The flat screen tv had a few good channels including USA, TBS and HBO. The location is great! It is two blocks from Chinatown so my boyfriend and I just walked up the street to Clyde's restaurant for dinner. I did not take advantage of the continental breakfast and we arrived too late to hear the live band that plays. Overall good hotel.
hotel_name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Washington, DC / Downtown

review_title: Great location, nice rooms, and nice breakfast options
review_text: I'm not sure what upset a previous poster, but I like to find clean, modern hotels for lower prices in good locations. And that's what I found here. The rooms were updated, large, and had everything we needed. We had a room facing a church which had bells every half hour. We only noticed it in the evening before dinner so I think it stops by bedtime. Honestly, it's not that loud and I thought it was nice. I definitely felt like I was in the city. On the flip side of that, I never heard street noise nor traffic. So I'll take bells chiming over that. I found the staff friendly and professional. We ate breakfast one morning there. They have a great set-up that I would like to see the Hilton chain copy. They have bagels, pastries, boiled eggs, juice, etc. And they have in a fridge breakfast sandwiches to heat, cups of diced fruit, water, etc. Whatever your culinary challenge is in the morning, you can find something here. This is a solid choice for the moderate market. 20 minute walk from Union Station, 15 minute walk from the White House, and 10-15 minute walk to the mall. We found it to be a good base right near a subway stop if you need it.
hotel_name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Washington, DC / Downtown

review_text: Stayed here in August for the Jill Scott and Anthony Hamilton concert. Great proximity to the Verizon Center. Smaller rooms but that's to be expected with a Fairfield Inn. Overall I would surely recommend this hotel. See I live in Northern Va and I parked on the side street without paying cause I know there are a few spots near judiciary that don't have meters and I didn't get a ticket for these two days and one day was a work Monday. It's a chance to take if you don't want to pay for their parking.-which is on the street as well.
hotel_name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Washington, DC / Downtown

review_title: I'm sure they'll be rated more stars in future.
review_text:
Stayed in Sept for 3 night. remodel of hotel makes this place shiny modern. Started in suite but moved to queen room. You do notice differences between the two categories even though it's only 20 dollars difference. suites have a fridge, microwave, good views, double TV, automatic window shade open/close mechanism, roomy bathroom. Queen room seems cheaper all around.
other pluses:
- proximity to everything. can walk to metro station. lots of asian food options
- good breakfast although wish there were hot items instead of microwaving a sausage biscuit
- water available all day
- can sit in breakfast area at any time and watch the flat screen TVs
minuses:
- no room safes
- no fridge in lower category room
- sitting area for breakfast gets really crowded
hotel_name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Washington, DC / Downtown

review_title: Excellent Location, but is the price worth it?
review_text:
As mentioned, the Marriott Metro Center is close to the Metro. The elevator down to the station is right outside the front door. However, at $189 (special APA rate), I'm not sure it was worth the money. I know that parking was not T $38 per night!
On the plus side, the service was good. The cocierge was always willing to help and provided excellent recommendations. The lobby was attractive and the free ice water was appreciated as we came in from the heat!
Negatives included the cleanliness of the room. Our son found an old water bottle and a half-eaten cake under the bed. Good thing we were watching him! Also, the drawer to the armoire was broken, so we couldn't use it (the bottom had fallen out). When we got in the room and turned the sheets back, the duvet cover was ripped. Finally, the walls are very, very thin and every time someone came in or out on our hall, we were woken. Swimming pool is only one depth, 3 1/2 feet?
In summary, if you don't have a car and family with you this is your place. If you do, I would look for a more family friendly hotel.
I made arrangements for a small group of seasoned travelers, a tough crowd. All were pleased with the rooms, location and especially the service.

Heerlijk hotel. Ruime kamers, iets gedateerd, met keukentje, sanitair prima. Perfecte locatie om Washington te bezichtigen. Dicht bij metro Foggy Bottom. Je zit zo in het centrum, maar ook zo in Arlington. Zeer vriendelijk personeel en je kunt er prima ontbijten. Rustige en vriendelijke buurt. Op loopafstand van Kennedycenter.

Stayed here on a tip from a friend from July 5-13. The 1800 number could not help us but we ended up calling the Marriott directly and talked to the Manager, he was a great help as to our reservation. Totally made our trip with his service. The location you can not beat, only two blocks from all the spots you would want to see. The metro is on the corner and is a transfer station so if walking isn't your thing the metro is right there. A decent gym and pool, we used both and although the pool is only 4 ft deep it was refreshing. The starbucks in the lobby made mornings a snap. There are all kinds if places to eat within walking distance. Fast food mcdonalds gas three loctions less than a block away in each direction. We found Capitol brew company a great place to eat and relax plus kid friendly. The only thing I wish we would have had in our room was a fridge. No big deal but we had to use the ice bucked to keep drinks cold for the next day. It was hot as heck in July the a/c didnt skip a beat. We could hear the doors close of our neighbors room. The marriot need to put stoppers on the doors so the don't slam, but when you have been walking all day, sleeping sound won't be a problem. We walked to the mall just about everyday and took less than 10 minutes to walk there. Great time and would suggest this location to all you won't be disappointed.

review_title: Location, service, quality all in one place
review_text:
We had a great experience at this hotel. I was nervous when we arrived and our room was not ready early because my husband is a platinum member, but we had nothing to complain about once we got in, other than a pool that could use some attention to its chemicals.
The rooms are lovely, albeit small. The beds are great with a variety of pillows and nice linens. Housekeeping does a great job. The workout facilities are wonderful and the breakfast buffet left us wanting for nothing. We found everything we needed in the gift shop and didn't think the prices were out of line (didn't need much, though). 
Again, the location is fabulous. We were able to turn in the rental car and walk everywhere.
We had an issue with one of our phones and maintenance was there within 5 minutes if our report of it.
Oh, and they let us check out late due to a business call.
Location is excellent. Rooms are a little small & so are the bathrooms. Concierge is very helpful.
Spent two nights in this hotel with my family. Perfect location, walking distance to main POI. Bike station near the hotel. Will recommend the hotel to my friend.
The title says most of it. The location is right behind the Library of Congress - real close to Capitol Hill. It's not a bad walk to the National Mall, either.

review_title: Wonderful hotel in great location. Great staff!!
review_text:
My (14 y/o) son and I spent four nights here in the beginning of June. My ONLY complaint was that I wasted money on ear plugs. Yes DC has a very active EMS system, and yes you are across from the hospital, but we very rarely heard any sirens after sundown. Also 99% of the sirens were responding to calls not transporting to the hospital. My point is, you'd likely hear the same amount of sirens regardless of where you are. 
PLEASE don't let the fear of noise deter you from choosing to stay in this wonderful hotel. 
It's not a glamorous hotel, it's a business hotel. It couldn't have been better for us. Spacious, clean, and a full kitchen. Trader Joe's was a couple blocks away and a large CVS was behind the hotel. It's in a great neighborhood too. We saved a fortune by preparing our own meals a few times. And the refreshing citrus water provided to guests in the lobby was a special treat when returning from a long day of sightseeing. 
We couldn't have been happier with this hotel. Wish we could have stayed even longer.

We loved this hotel! The location was superb, quiet and only a couple blocks away from the Metro. Free breakfast was included with our stay (which was located in a different bldg--odd); nevertheless, it was a great stay at reasonable rate...would most definitely stay here again!! We were also able to park on the street right by the hotel for FREE!
The only complaint I had was no curtians besides the sheer to block the sunlight in the morning. Not a dealbreaker, of course.

review_title: Great location for touring DC without a car.
review_text: Great location....close to the Metro and walking distance to good restaurants.

We stayed at the Washington Court for 4 nights/5 days and it was perfect! We arrived in DC at 9 a.m. We went to the hotel expecting to just leave our bags until check-in at 4 p.m. We went to the desk and let them know we were there to leave our things and the staff immediately checked to see if a room was available. It was and we were able to get in the room before 10 a.m. This was a great beginning to our stay there! The room itself was great for our family of 4 and the girls loved the lobby! We were close to everything and walked to Union Station for the metro, trolley, foods, and shopping everyday. We would stay here again for sure!
hotel_name: Washington Court Hotel on Capitol Hill

review_title: A great hotel with impeccable service in the heart of DC
review_text: This is a true 5 star hotel. Very clean with great facilities. Amazing pool and gym. Service was the best I have experienced in a similar sized hotel. Beautiful food in restaurant and great atmosphere. Rooms are ok sized with smallish bathroom. Great value at conference rates.. Would be a bit pricey at rack rate. Would stay here again..
I woke up to bed bugs. It was the most disgusting experience in my life. The on duty manager was very apologetic but that didn't change the fact. I have pictures

I was really impressed with the Hampton Inn. Location is very good and my family enjoyed walking to all the monuments and museums which are all well within trekking distance. Service in the hotel was first class and staff are certainly motivated to go the extra mile for guests. Rooms were first class and spotless. Breakfast was really fantastic with the staff again going the extra mile. One of the best city hotels I have stayed in and the best Hampton Inn by a mile.

review_title: An excellent location that provides a an exceptional place to work and sleep.
review_text: Washington DC is hot and humid in summer. Having a location that provides a Metro stop and some of your destinations within a quick walk (one that won't have you sweating before you see anything) is gold. Being able to have breakfast before you start means you get going earlier in the day and being able to come back to deliciously cool rooms, a refrigerator and microwave and comfy bed keeps the weather from draining away the vacation fun.

review_title: Nice hotel but Terrible house keeping!
review_text: The room was nice and the concierge & valet parking attendants were excellent!! The overnight parking is very expensive ($33 a day). The bathroom was not clean very well when we checked in. There was hair on the floor and the toilet was not very clean at all. We did not make a big deal out of it we decided to speak to the cleaning people and told them to make sure they cleaned the toilet the next day. They still did not do a thorough job of cleaning the toilet at all. There were visable stains on the back toilet and the inside. For a "new" hotel the toilets should not look so dirty and dated. Before you fully check I would advise you check the bathrooms to make sure it's thoroughly cleaned before you get settled. Also, the buffet breakfast area is very tight so I suggest you come down for breakfast very early. The hotel is in a great are but you have the occasional homeless and old drunks around the next corner but they won't bother u at all. It's very close to the train and the megabus depot!
hotel_name: Fairfield Inn & Suites Washington, DC / Downtown

review_text:
Great location downtown
Fine service, superb ameneties
hotel_name: Washington Court Hotel on Capitol Hill

review_text: I am a Marriott Rewards member of over 10 years. I have stayed at Marriotts an average of 15 stays per year. The hotel is in a good location. Friendly staff. Average lobby. But.... Most overpriced Marriott property that I have stayed at. It is definitely not a great value. The rooms are average in size. The decor is not as modern as you would expect for a JW property. The bathroom is very small. I would not recommend this hotel to business travelers. There are much better choices at a lower price in DC. It does not help that I am here during the Cherry Blossom Festival. Paid $500 per night for something that is probably a $200 to $250 value.

Quasi vicino alla metro ma questo hotel e'davvero costoso (115 euro x una notte piu'30 per il parcheggio) e non offre neppure la colazione. La stanza e'grande e ha un cucinotto con frigo micro tostapane e l'occorrente x farsi il caffÃ¨. Forse e'una buona soluzione per chi si ferma in cittÃ  qualche giorno e quindi puÃ² organizzare di cenare in camera altrimenti il servizio cucina e'inutile e non giustifica il prezzo della camera. Non ci tornerei.
Excellent location and excellent staff. Rooms ae spacious, well maintained and very clean.

We stayed one night here, first thing I do is check for bed bug evidence, when seeing the mattress looked New and not a sighn of them anywhere I could relax and enjoy our stay. We had taken our bikes and they stored them for us. The only cons that we had was the expensive parking, wifi and no continental breakfast. But service was great, we would stay here again! Perfect location to bike around mall ect.
hotel_name: Washington Court Hotel on Capitol Hill

review_text:
Whilst moving a chair to better location in our room we came upon a dead mouse in a trap.after ringing reception to vent our concern we were meet
 with a Luke room response.they sent up a cleaner to remove the trap but said these had been placed in rooms by a pest company and they did not know where the traps had been set so they had no knowledge to check.whilst the rest of the trip was good,the accommodation,breakfast etc the front desk were not.

review_title: Perfect location to transportation and sights.
review_text:
I have never been to DC before so I was uncertain where to stay. Each day we could walk to most of the sights. If not, we could walk one block to the train. We were able to avoid paying high cab fares as well. We could walk to good bars, restaurants, a small grocery store or CVS.
The room was very clean and comfortable. An exhaust fan in the bathroom would have been nice. The breakfast buffet also helped save cash.

I stayed at the Washington court hotel in July of 2011. I herd they had upgraded and I was looking forward to my stay. When I checked in the first shock was the parking fee for my car...$43.00 per day!!! I thought that was outrageous and taking advantage of their guest. But I would have to chock it up, then I checked into my room. The view was beautiful of the Capitol but the room was smaller than I expected for the price which was $199.00 per night. The rooms had some were on it such as mold around the tub and water stain over the bed as if there was a leak that had been fixed but they didn't bother to repaint the ceiling. I decided to cut my trip short and pay the $75.00 early check out fee rather than pay another $142.00 for the room & parking. The whole place seem like they plan to get you for all your money including the restaurant,and the gift shop. The hotel was in a very convient location but definitely NOT worth the money.
hotel_name: Washington Court Hotel on Capitol Hill

review_text:
We, family of 4, stayed here for 5 nights a week before Christmas. Our first night there the concierge tried VERY hard to get us to purchase tickets for the hop on hop off tours, got the feeling he would get a kickback if we paid through him, cash only. 
Not knowing the area, we asked the concierge for advice about the best way to get to the white house and the only option he suggested was catch a taxi, however, after some self guided research we worked out it was less than 2 miles walk so opted for this much cheaper option and saw heaps more on our beautiful 20 min walk! In the end we didn't buy the hop on hop off tour and were SO glad we didn't because you REALLY need to see Washington on foot and the hotel is so close to everything you'd want to see and if it's too far for you to walk, take the train, it's really cost effective and very efficient! It's also an option that was never mentioned to us at the hotel, it pays to do your own research and it's disappointing that the concierges never once suggested the public transport option. The breakfast was always nice and adequate and the Brekkie staff VERY friendly and helpful. Pool small but my kids enjoyed the daily swim. Fitness also small but you can usually find some time when it's empty and you have the place to yourself. Laundry was typical hotel laundry. Overall, great hotel but didn't think much of the concierges. Would consider staying here again unless I could find a place with same value closer to museum strip, however, I didn't mind the walks to the monuments and museums.

review_title: Needs to do more to charge a five star price
review_text:
First the good points: great service, all the staff were delightful, kind, helpful and genuine. In addition the hotel has a great location, perfect for walking across Washington. The hotel is also a pretty building with some fine public rooms. But the downside is the bedrooms. We paid for a higher quality room, which while large was dark and rather gloomy - making you feel that it had all seen better days. The room was not that clean, with dirt in the entrance to the room which stayed for the whole three days we were there. It was also the type of hotel where room service trolleys stayed in the corridors for hours and hours.
All in all, despite the staff we felt it was very poor vakue for money.

During our stay from December 26-28th we made the best choice by picking the st.regis as our hotel for our vacation. We booked this hotel through our platinum amex and the accomodations and service exceeded our expectations! My husband planned this trip since I had never been to D.C before and we wanted our 3.5 month old daugher to share this memory with us also. The entire staff at this hotel makes it a wonderful place for a first time visit. From the bellhop who greeted us by name, the bartender who educated us about the hotel and D.C history, the front desk who helped with room upgrades, the concierge who mapped out the town, and all the friendly butlers who brought us everything we needed... 
The rooms are gorgeous and very classy. Our first room was amazing but it didn't have a bathtub that we needed for the baby, so I called the front desk and the manager, ertug ersoy came up immediately to show us other other options for rooms with a tub.. he moved us to a larger suite and we are so grateful for his genorosity. The room is luxiourious and spacious. I would definitely reccomend this hotel to anyone traveling to the D.C area..its steps away from the white house and very close to other famous monuments and museums. WE WILL BE BACK FOR SURE !!!!!
The rooms are unacceptably small for the price. The bathroom is tiny. There is no place to put your toiletries! There was only a shower. The room itself was a cracker box.

review_title: When is a Hilton not a Hilton?
review_text:
If you stay in a budget hotel you expect budget services and so roll with the punches if things aren't quite right. In fact you half expect to have some things go wrong, but not at the Hilton.
It has the Hilton name but not the Hilton standards. Its a shame as its a new Hotel and has the potential to be excellent to maintain the reputation.
Whilst disappointed we are not unhappy as there are still some great features, such as the excellent room sizes. Â Our room, fortunately was overlooking the inner courtyard, with it's sunny aspect (even for December). The nearby corner hosts a very comprehensive supermarket, providing the opportunity to stock the mini bar fridge or purchase a micro wave meal.Â 
It's location is amongst a new government office development and there are unfortunately very few restaurants within walking distance. There are however some fast food/cafe style eateries near the entrance. Alternatively you can visit the supermarket and choose a prepared or frozen or pre cooked meal. Seeing that these choices were not appetising we decided to dine in on the first night. Â The "in room" dining is conveniently, the same as the restaurant, which we thought would allow us to relax in our room after a day of travel. The meals arrived quickly but the portions were small and very salty. The room service tray remained uncollected for24hrs. Â The next evening we tried the restaurant but again found the meals to be sub standard. Â The calamari was served covered in an excess of bread crumbs and in pool of oil and the mains again were salty. Â  Our table was opposite the kitchen and I had the misfortune to witness the kitchen staff serving the food with their hands after scratching their nose and adjusting their hair. Â Food that was accidentally dropped on the cook top or serving area was quickly placed on the plate. Not very hygienic! I am not sure if this was why my son vomitedÂ during the evening. Â So for the rest of our stay we bought food from the supermarket, which surprisingly turned out to be quite OK.Â 
In the previous Hiltons on this trip all the staff were refreshingly cheery and enthusiastic but it seemed that some of the staff here were under pressure or just unhappy about something. Â In particular the restaurant staff just seem to be going through the motions.
The in room entertainment is limited, with quite few of the published channels not displaying. When my son asked the front desk what was wrong, we got a shrug of the shoulders and a comment "it's just like that, they fade in and out". He then asked do they have DVD players to use to watch some rented movies we again got a shrug of the shoulders.Â 
There is metro just around the corner but we chose to walk the 20 minutes to Capital hill and 30 minutes to the white house.
Some hotels cater for all guest types, but I would suggest this hotel best suits the business traveller and the young adults that need a place to crash after hitting Ibiza nightclub across the road.Â 
All up comfortable room but if we stay in Washington again we will try elsewhere.
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn Washington DC/US Capitol

review_text: The rooms are very, very small. It's a cracker box.

review_title: Great stay in a great hotel
review_text: Stayed 2 nights to attend the Army/Navy game and was very impressed. The hotel still feels very new and is very clean. Rooms are large and the bathrooms very nice and spacious. The hotel is a bit of a drive to FedEx Field, however, if you were visiting DC for sightseeing, there is a Metro stop about a block away. The hotel is also very close to Union Station and there are a few restaurants to walk to. Price was excellent for the services received, however, there is a $30/night charge to valet park your vehicle.
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn Washington DC/US Capitol

review_title: Brand New - Great Location and Value
review_text: Brand new, large, nicely-appointed rooms. Near Capitol, museums and Union Station. $30 to park overnight. Harris Teeter grocery on the same block. Convenient location and good value compared to other hotels on the hill. Some sort of nightclub across the street. Saw long lines of people but no problem (never heard) the noise.
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn Washington DC/US Capitol

review_title: Great location, great service, average rooms
review_text: If you need metro access and have business on Capitol hill this location is ideal. The staff was super helpful - happy to give late checkout and very pleasant. The rooms were tiny - and I was told I had a nice room. But the price was reasonable and for a work trip it was fine.

review_title: Classic, full service hotel, w/great service and home-away-from-home feel
review_text: Title says it all. This is my 'go-to' hotel for trips to DC - especially, when I'm traveling on Amtrak. Rooms are joce, clean and quiet, service is great, location is perfect for Capitol Hill visits and the pub downstairs is super. Reminds me of the nicer non-chain hotels in the UK - lots of charm
Great Location, very charming, very clean. I really liked the hidden TV in the mirror. The beds were super comfy and the sheets were very nice. Loved our stay!

review_title: Great stay for a great value!
review_text: Excellent service, staff, extra comfortable beds, spotless, great location near union station and all for a great value!!

I went with my parents at the end of July, partly to celebrate my graduation from college. I was very excited for this trip. I had been looking forward to staying at the St Regis. The valets were very nice however they were difficult to understand. Then the gentleman at the check in desk was very rude. He treated us very poorly and gave us a terrible description of our choice of rooms. When we got to our room and looked out our window, our "view" was of a brick wall and air conditioners. One of our beds was a pull out couch for which we did not have pillows. They had to go get pillows for us. The sleeper sofa was also terribly uncomfortable (and this is coming from a girl who can sleep pretty much anywhere). The best part was the tv in the bathroom mirror. Also the gentlemen who eventually got us the extra pillows for the sleeper sofa mentioned that they always put chocolates on the pillows when they turn down the beds. We never experienced this. I know that it's a little thing, but I can't help but wonder why we didn't get any. We were paying for the same service as everyone else. Overall I found this hotel to have the most horrible service I have ever experienced. I always knew people in DC were rude. I just didn't think that was how hotels were toward paying customers...
What a beautiful hotel. Right next to union station and close to the capital. So easy to get to and so easy to get everywhere else! Definately recommend! Rooms were beautiful!!

The Madera hotel is staffed by courteous and helpful staff. Centrally located just south of DuPont Circle and a Metro station.
Bathroom is a bit small otherwise this would be rated 5/5

review_title: Hotel is in great location and has cute clean affordable accommodations perfect for quick weekend sightseeing.
review_text: This Irish themed hotel is a quaint escape from the bustling streets outside. We were catching a tour from union station (which is across the intersection) so the hotel's location was perfect. The room was small, but cozy. The bathroom tile looked warn, but everything was super clean and tidy.

When I was booking a hotel for a recent DC weekend through Starwood I was excited when they had a points and dollars offer. Rarely does St Regis offer that and I always love the St Regis experience. but there was nothing to love about this St Regis. When I arrived I was told they had a great upgraded room for me (I am Starwood Platnium) but this room was dark and luckily I opened the curtains to an interior view of the air conditioners. Thanks St Regis. When I went with bellman to ask for another room it wasn't clean so I waited an hour in the bar where I bought my own drink 
The new room had a view of K street but there is nothing special or interesting. A square of a room..the door opens right into the room, the bathroom dark with poor lighting 
The reception desk is parked in the middle of the lobby on the path to the elevators. It seemed you were always in someone's way on the way to the elevators. But the concierge is tucked back in an alcove. The staff was cold and impersonal, except the bell staff
Am I the only one tired of hotels telling me I should save the environment by hanging my towels while they blast the air conditioners. Please!!

I recently stayed at the Madera for a girls night. The room was very spacious and even with 5 women there was plenty of room. The location is very close to shopping and restaurants/bars as well as embassy row. I also highly recommend eating in the adjacent restaurant, Firefly.

I spent two nights at the Phoenix Park to attend a meeting taking place at the hotel. The room is seriously tiny. It us so small there was no room for both a desk and a desk chair. Fortunately the bed was so close I could sit on the bed and type in my computer for short periods of time. The room was so tiny I could not put my briefcase down without having to step over it if I wanted to walk around the room. Internet is supposedly free but my computer detected no wireless and the LAN line was broken. The channel selection on the TV wad so limited i actually watched CNN. On top of that, the room smelled as if someone had recently smoked in it.

Me and my family stayed at this Hotel for one night. We are Hilton Honors Diamond Member, so we automatically got put on an executive floor. The hotel took us a little while to get to, but that was user error. We basically got everything discounted ( wifi, spa, breakfast) since we were executive. I really enjoyed this hotel & would defenitley go back. (:
hotel_name: Hilton Garden Inn Washington DC/US Capitol

review_text: I stay in mid range hotels and this is the best value I've been to. Great location and well priced room service. My room was a little small but adequate for my needs. I like the old fashioned decor. Would recommend.

I needed to find a hotel in DC, near the Capitol, on short notice for less than $157 per night. I was able to book online the same day for only $129 with the AAA discount. I was skeptical, but happily surprised. Fantastic location across from Union station, super convenient to the Metro and the room was really nice. Very comfortable King bed, huge fluffy towels, bathrobe, and fantastic service to boot. This is a historic hotel, with plush, traditional furnishings and old world charm. The Dubliner restaurant on the Ground floor was great too. I will definitely stay here when I return to DC!

review_title: Great experience all around at Madera again.
review_text: DC is a great town with many great hotels. I choose Madera because it is consistently comfortable. The staff is always courteous & service-oriented. The location near the Metro makes a big difference in ease of getting around. I also like that Madera has character; it's not like your typical chain hotel. Parking is expensive, but seems on par with DC rates. Free street parking is available on weekends.
I was on crutches during this visit to DC and the staff couldn't have been more helpful - they always are!

review_title: Great value for location, but nothing else!
review_text:
I stayed at this hotel VIA an Amtrak vacation package for 4th of July weekend. It is a perfect location as we were directly next to the union station and walking distance from the Capitol and other hot spots. Our room was kept clean but bathroom was tiny.
However, if it wasn't for the convenience of the location to everything we wanted to do. I would not stay here. None of the belhops even offered to help my sister and I with our bags. No greeting as to how we were doing or did we enjoy our stay. But most importantly the big hole in our bathroom ceiling that no one decided to patch.
I guess when you pay or convenience you can't expect good service or the best hotel all the time.

My husband and I needed a break from our daily routine in Texas so we took a trip to D.C.. After reading reviews on different websites we chose Hotel Madera for us, and it was the right choice. Upon arrival we were greeted by friendly staff members which gave us a right at home feel. Our room was clean and spacious. The location was outstanding being a block from the Dupont Circle and a short walk to Georgetown. Breakfast was delicious but just a bit pricey. Only con about the hotel is parking, valet is readily available but can get pricey really fast. Overall we will be staying at Hotel Madera for our future DC trips and we will be recommending it to our friends and family as well.

My wife and I have visited twice in the last year. From the start Ertug the front desk manager took AMAZING care of us. from our platinum upgrade suite, so we could hv the extra room for the baby he already had the crib in the room upon arrival. which was amazing after being in the car for 10 hours. 2nd time was just a date night for wife and I again another suite.massage therapist already in the room with the dozen roses ordered. looking forward to next weekend for our anniversary it has become our thing to get a date night away from the baby order amazing room service and I believe we have started a great tradition. Its started with Ertug and that first experiance..

review_title: Great hotel and a very good service.
review_text: One great hotel. Lovely and very exquisite room. I simply love the furnitures - very classy. You will feel privileged staying at this hotel. Service is excellent and I have no complain. Location is perfect. The staffs are all very professionals and very helpful. I only stayed for one night and wishing for more. Highly recommendable.

review_title: Making our anniversary all the more special.
review_text: From the wine tasting to the impeccable service to the tasteful decor, this hotel made our wedding anniversary an extremely special occasion. Kudos to the staff who were very accomadating and knowledgable about their city.

Das Capitol und die Union Station (Sightseeing-Busse) sind in Gehdistanz, das Hotel befindet sich in einem ruhigen Quartier. Das Zimmer ist jedoch schon etwas in die Jahre gekommen und das Bad viel zu klein. DafÃ¼r ist der Preis zu hoch. review_title: The Madera is the friendliest Kimpton in which I have stayed.
review_text: From the moment I arrived, I was greeted like an old friend. Fernando D'Tapia went out of his way to make me feel at home. The whole team was friendly,relaxed,yet professional.
